q: On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations (UN)? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, shortly after independence. The UN itself came into existence on 24 October 1945.

q: Where is the headquarters of the OIC and how many members does it have? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has its headquarters in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and 57 member states. It was founded in 1969 at Rabat after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.

q: Which is the largest continent in the world? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Asia is the largest continent by both area and population.

q: What is the longest river in the world? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is traditionally regarded as the longest river. The Amazon carries the most water.

q: What is the official currency of Japan? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Japanese yen is the currency of Japan. The yuan is China's, the won is Korea's and the ringgit is Malaysia's.

q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the capital of Hungary? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Budapest, on the Danube river, is the capital of Hungary. Vienna is Austria's capital, Bucharest is Romania's and Prague is the Czech Republic's.

q: Jahangir Khan is world-famous for which sport? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Jahangir Khan is a Pakistani squash legend who won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986 and six British Open titles in a row.

q: Which country is the world's largest crude oil producer (2025/2026)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The USA has been the world's largest crude oil producer since 2018, ahead of Saudi Arabia and Russia.

q: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan in the Khyber region? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad region in Afghanistan. Khunjerab connects Pakistan with China, Bolan lies in Balochistan and Lowari lies between Dir and Chitral.

q: What is the factorial of 4 (4!)?
What is the negative of iota (i), where i is the square root of -1?
f: Negative means multiplying by -1, so the negative of i is -i.

q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated on 27 December 2007? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: She was killed after a rally at Liaquat Bagh in Rawalpindi.

q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Khadija (R.A.)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Hazrat Khadija (R.A.) was the daughter of Khuwaylid bin Asad of the Quraysh.

q: Who married two daughters of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), one after the other? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Hazrat Usman married Ruqayyah and, after her death, Umm Kulthum, so he is called Zun-Noorain.

q: On which river is the Mangla Dam located?
f: Mangla Dam was completed in 1967 on the Jhelum River near Mirpur, Azad Kashmir.

q: What does the word 'Ahzab' mean?
f: Ahzab means the confederate parties. It refers to the tribes that besieged Madinah in the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

q: Which is the largest port of Pakistan?
f: Karachi Port is the largest and busiest port of Pakistan.

q: When was the Eiffel Tower built (completed)?
f: The Eiffel Tower in Paris was completed in 1889 for the World's Fair.

q: Ayat-e-Bir (the verse of righteousness) is in which Surah?
f: Ayat-e-Bir is verse 177 of Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (People of the Cave)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Quran mentions the dog of the People of the Cave, who stayed at the entrance of the cave.

q: Hazrat Hajra (R.A.) was the mother of which Prophet? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S.).

q: Which female companion of the Prophet (PBUH) narrated the most Hadith?
f: Hazrat Aisha (R.A.) narrated about 2210 Hadith, the most among women.

q: What is the capital of Somalia? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia.

q: Who was Bulleh Shah?
f: Bulleh Shah (1680-1757) was a famous Punjabi Sufi poet buried in Kasur.

q: Who was the second Khalifa of Islam?
f: Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (R.A.) ruled from 634 to 644 CE after Hazrat Abu Bakr.

q: Who is known by the title 'Abu Hafs'? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Hazrat Umar (R.A.) is called Abu Hafs because his daughter was Hazrat Hafsa (R.A.).

q: What is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir?
f: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin took over in 1948 after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.

q: In which year was the Simla Agreement signed between Pakistan and India? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

q: On which date was the 2024 general election of Pakistan held? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The general election for the 16th National Assembly was held on 8 February 2024.

q: Synonym of 'Eminent': (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Eminent means famous and respected within a field, so distinguished is the closest word.

q: Between which leaders was the Simla Agreement signed in 1972? (Repeated in 6 tests)
o: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
f: It was signed at Shimla on 2 July 1972 by Pakistan's President Z. A. Bhutto and India's Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

q: In which year did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: After the 1971 war, East Pakistan became Bangladesh on 16 December 1971.

q: What is the antonym of 'gracious'?
f: Gracious means courteous, kind and pleasant, so its opposite is rude, meaning impolite or lacking consideration for others.

q: Where is Masjid an-Nabawi located? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Masjid an-Nabawi was built by the Prophet (PBUH) in Madinah after the Hijrah. It is one of the holiest mosques in Islam.

q: In which year were Pakistan's first general elections held on the basis of adult franchise? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Pakistan's first general elections on adult franchise were held in December 1970. The Awami League won a majority of seats in the National Assembly.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib passed away? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born around 570 CE and lost his mother at age 6. His grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who then cared for him, died when he was about 8.

q: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a joint project between which two countries? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: CPEC is a joint development initiative linking Gwadar Port in Pakistan with Kashgar in China's Xinjiang region through road, rail, energy and infrastructure projects.

q: What does the word Pakistan mean? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Pakistan combines the Persian and Urdu word pak (pure) with the suffix -stan (land). The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Dasht River located? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Dasht River flows in southwestern Balochistan through the Kech and Gwadar areas towards the Arabian Sea.

q: In which year was Bengal first partitioned by Lord Curzon? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal on 16 October 1905; it was annulled in 1911.

q: K2, the second highest peak in the world, lies in which mountain range? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: K2 (8,611 m) stands in the Karakoram Range on the Pakistan-China border.

q: Who founded the Dawn newspaper in 1941? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Jinnah launched Dawn in Delhi in October 1941 as a voice of the All-India Muslim League.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Allahabad Address? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Iqbal gave the Allahabad Address on 29 December 1930 at the annual session of the All India Muslim League and proposed a separate Muslim state in north-western India.

q: On which date is Pakistan Air Force (PAF) Day celebrated every year?
f: PAF Day is observed on 7 September to honour the role of the Air Force in the 1965 war, the day after Defence Day.

q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population?
f: In the 2023 census Punjab had about 127.7 million people, the highest of all provinces.

q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by area? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan's land area.

q: What is the total area of Balochistan province?
f: Balochistan covers 347,190 square km, the largest province by area; Punjab has 205,344 and Sindh 140,914 square km.

q: The Arabic word Jihad literally means: (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Jihad comes from the root jahada, meaning to strive or exert effort, especially in the way of Allah.

q: The Islamic act of washing the face, hands and arms, wiping the head and washing the feet before prayer is called:
f: Wudu is the minor ritual ablution required before Salah; Ghusl is the full bath and Tayammum is dry ablution with clean earth.

q: Over how many years was the Holy Quran revealed to the Prophet (PBUH)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Revelation began when the Prophet was 40 and continued for about 23 years, 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

q: Which Surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah?
f: Surah At-Tawbah (Surah 9) is the only Surah that does not begin with Bismillah.

q: In which of the following expeditions did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) NOT personally take part?
f: At Mutah (8 AH) the army was led by Zayd bin Haritha while the Prophet stayed in Madinah. He personally took part in Badr, Uhud and Khandaq.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of -2?
f: The reciprocal of a number x is 1/x, so for -2 it is -1/2, because (-2) x (-1/2) = 1.

q: Change into active voice: The wires have been cut by someone.
o: Someone has been cutting the wires.
f: Present perfect passive (have been + past participle) becomes present perfect active (has/have + past participle), with the agent as subject.

q: An act that is obligatory (compulsory) in Islam is called:
f: Fard (also called Wajib by most jurists) is a duty commanded by Allah, such as the five daily prayers; neglecting it is a sin.

q: Which religion was spread peacefully in the subcontinent by the preaching and teachings of Sufi saints?
f: Sufi saints such as Khawaja Moinuddin Chishti and Baha-ud-Din Zakariya spread Islam through love, tolerance and good character.

q: Choose the antonym of the adjective MEDIATE (acting through an intermediary, not direct):
f: Mediate (adjective) means indirect, acting through an intermediary; its opposite is immediate, meaning direct with nothing in between.

q: At which place was the Simla Agreement between Pakistan and India signed in 1972? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Simla Agreement was signed at Barnes Court (now Raj Bhavan) in Shimla by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi on 2 July 1972.

q: How many degrees of comparison (degrees of adjective) are there in English grammar?
f: The three degrees are positive, comparative and superlative (for example good, better, best).

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan took office in August 1947 and served until his assassination in October 1951.

q: What was the occupation of Mother Teresa?
f: Mother Teresa was a Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950 to serve the poor and the dying.

q: What is the meaning of the name Al-Fatiha?
f: Al-Fatiha comes from the Arabic root f-t-h (to open) and means The Opening, as it opens the Quran and every rakat of prayer.

q: What is the capital of Nepal? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.

q: What is the meaning of the word Furqan?
o: Criterion (that which separates right from wrong)
f: Furqan means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood; it is a name of the Quran and of Surah 25.

q: A quarter of 10% of 120 is: (Repeated in 8 tests)
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one quarter of 12 = 3.

q: In which year did Osman I declare the independence of his Ottoman principality from the Seljuks (traditional date)?
f: Osman I broke away from the declining Seljuks and declared independence in 1299, which is the traditional founding date of the Ottoman state.

q: What is the currency of Brazil? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Brazil uses the Brazilian real (BRL) as its currency.

q: Which Companion recited verses of Surah Maryam in the court of Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi, who wept and refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraysh.

q: Which Prophet (A.S.) was swallowed by a fish? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Hazrat Yunus (A.S.) was swallowed by a big fish and prayed 'La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz zalimin' (Surah Al-Anbiya).

q: Which people lived in Khyber (Khaybar) at the time of the Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Khaybar was a Jewish settlement near Madinah, conquered by the Muslims in 7 AH (628 CE).

q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Gilgit is the capital and largest city of Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: In which Surah of the Quran does the full Bismillah appear twice (once at the start and once inside the Surah)?
f: In Surah An-Naml, the Bismillah is at the start and again in verse 30, in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.

q: Who is the current Foreign Minister of Pakistan (also Deputy Prime Minister)? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar is Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, in office since the 2024 government formation.

q: A brother is 3 years old and his sister is thrice his age. How old will the sister be when the brother is 11 years old?
f: Sister is 9 when brother is 3, so she is 6 years older. When brother is 11, sister is 11 + 6 = 17.

q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, ?
f: Gaps between letters increase by one each time: A+2=C, C+3=F, F+4=J, J+5=O.

q: Approximately how many Muslims were martyred in the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhud?
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, among them Hazrat Hamza (R.A.), the uncle of the Prophet (SAW).

q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
f: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 in Bombay, with A. O. Hume as a key founder and W. C. Bonnerjee as first president.

q: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: The treaty was signed on 19 September 1960 in Karachi, with the World Bank as a mediator.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed between which two countries?
f: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Nehru in 1960; it gave the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to Pakistan.

q: What is 9 divided by 81, in its simplest fraction form?
f: 9/81 = 1/9, because both 9 and 81 are divisible by 9.

q: Which animal is the national animal of Pakistan?
f: The markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.

q: Which flower is the national flower of Pakistan?
f: Jasmine (Jasminum officinale) is the national flower of Pakistan and also appears in the national emblem.

q: On which date is Pakistan Day (Pakistan Resolution Day) observed every year?
f: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution was passed at Minto Park, Lahore, in the session of 22 to 24 March 1940, and Pakistan Day is observed on 23 March.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg; Malala won the Peace Prize in 2014.

q: How many colours are there in a rainbow?
f: A rainbow shows seven colours: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet (VIBGYOR).

q: Who is the current President of Iran? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Masoud Pezeshkian has been President of Iran since 28 July 2024 and is still in office in October 2026.

q: Which was the first Ghazwa (expedition personally led by the Holy Prophet) in Islam? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Al-Abwa (also called Waddan) took place in Safar 2 AH; the Prophet led it himself and made a peace treaty with Banu Damra without fighting.

q: The Durand Line separates Pakistan from which country? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Durand Line (1893) is the roughly 2,600 km border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan (after the 25th Amendment)? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: After FATA merged into KP, the 25th Amendment reduced NA seats from 342 to 336 (266 general, 60 women and 10 non-Muslim seats).

q: Which Chinese 4.5-generation fighter jet was inducted into the Pakistan Air Force in 2022?
f: The PAF inducted the Chengdu J-10C (AESA radar, 4.5 generation) in March 2022 at Minhas Air Base.

q: Who is the current Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Field Marshal Asim Munir is Chief of Army Staff and, since December 2025 under the 27th Amendment, also Chief of Defence Forces.

q: Which team won the 2022 Asia Cup cricket tournament? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by 23 runs in the final at Dubai on 11 September 2022.

q: In which year was the Quit India Movement launched? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee.

q: Who led the Quit India Movement? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Gandhi launched the movement with his Do or Die speech in Bombay on 8 August 1942.

q: What is 5% of 80?
Solve using the DMAS rule: 2 + 2 / 2 = ? (Repeated in 8 tests)
f: Division comes before addition (DMAS), so 2 / 2 = 1 and then 2 + 1 = 3.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 17th?
f: 17 - 1 = 16 days later; 16 = 14 + 2, so two days after Sunday is Monday.

q: Who wrote the book Friends Not Masters? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Friends Not Masters (1967, Oxford University Press) is the political autobiography of President Muhammad Ayub Khan.

q: Which was the first major battle fought between the Muslims and the Quraysh of Makkah? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, was the first large-scale battle between the Muslims and the Quraysh. Earlier expeditions such as Abwa were only raids without fighting.

q: Who was elected President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) in September 2026?
f: Dr Najeeb Naqi Khan of PML-N was elected the 25th President of AJK on 24 September 2026, winning 32 votes against 13 for PPP's Latif Akbar. The post had been vacant since the death of Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry on 31 January 2026.

q: Who moved the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution on 23 March 1940? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: A. K. Fazlul Haq, Chief Minister of Bengal, moved the resolution at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League and Choudhry Khaliquzzaman seconded it. Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presided.

q: Adolf Hitler was the dictator of which country during the Second World War? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Hitler led the Nazi Party and ruled Germany as Chancellor and Fuhrer from 1933 until his death in 1945. He started the war by invading Poland in 1939.

q: Which is the highest peak of Pakistan?
f: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is the highest peak of Pakistan and second highest in the world.

q: Choose the synonym of WILD.
f: Wild means living in natural state, not tamed, so Untamed is the synonym; Tame is the opposite.

q: What is the rank of Pakistan in the world by population (2026)?
f: After India, China, the United States and Indonesia, Pakistan is the 5th most populous country (about 255 to 260 million).

q: According to the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by:
o: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
f: The 1956 Constitution had a President elected for 5 years by members of the National and Provincial Assemblies; Basic Democrats were used in the 1962 Constitution.

q: Who was the British Prime Minister at the time of the partition of India in 1947? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Labour leader Clement Attlee was Prime Minister (1945-51) when the Indian Independence Act 1947 was passed.

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (Rightly Guided Caliphs) were there? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: They were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them).

q: The nisab of zakat on silver is:
f: Nisab of silver is 52.5 tola (about 612.36 g); 7.5 tola (87.48 g) is the nisab of gold.

q: Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim conquered it in 712 AD?
f: Raja Dahir of the Chach dynasty was defeated and killed at the Battle of Aror (Rohri) by Muhammad bin Qasim.

q: In which year was the Sui gas field discovered?
f: Sui gas field in Balochistan was discovered in 1952; commercial supply to Karachi began in 1955.

q: In which year was the film Jinnah (starring Christopher Lee) released? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Jinnah, directed by Jamil Dehlavi, was released in 1998.

q: In which Ghazwa (battle) was Abu Jahl killed? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Abu Jahl, chief of the Quraysh, was killed at Badr in 2 AH (624 CE).

q: Who is the current Chief of the Naval Staff of Pakistan? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Admiral Naveed Ashraf has been Chief of the Naval Staff since 7 October 2023 and was still serving in 2026.

q: Which national airline did Pakistan privatize in December 2025 (won by Arif Habib consortium)?
f: On 23 December 2025 the Arif Habib-led consortium won 75 percent of PIA with a bid of Rs135 billion.

q: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
f: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded on 10 December 1901, five years after Alfred Nobel died.

q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's total area is covered by Balochistan? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Balochistan covers 347,190 square km, which is about 43.6 percent (nearly 44 percent) of Pakistan's total area, making it the largest province by area.

q: Who introduced the Basic Democracies System in Pakistan in 1959?
f: President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies Order in October 1959. Union councils elected Basic Democrats who later formed an electoral college.

q: What was the official designation of Muhammad Ali Bogra (1953 to 1955)?
f: Muhammad Ali Bogra was the third Prime Minister of Pakistan, from 17 April 1953 to 12 August 1955, appointed by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad.

q: Nelson Mandela was the leader of which country?
f: Nelson Mandela led the anti-apartheid struggle and became the first democratically elected President of South Africa in 1994.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 25th be? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: From the 2nd to the 25th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks + 2 days, so Tuesday + 2 days = Thursday.

q: Which tree is the national tree of Pakistan?
f: The deodar (Cedrus deodara), a cedar of the northern mountains, is the national tree of Pakistan.

q: Which narrow strip of Afghan territory separates Pakistan from Central Asia (Tajikistan)?
f: The Wakhan Corridor in Afghanistan's Badakhshan province lies between Tajikistan to the north and Pakistan to the south.

q: How many traditional (basic) senses does a human being have?
f: The five traditional senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

q: In which year did Pakistan and China sign the border (boundary) agreement? (Repeated in 4 tests)
f: The Sino-Pakistan boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963 in Peking by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Chen Yi.

q: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International located?
f: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 and its International Secretariat is based in London.

q: What is the derivative of cos(theta) with respect to theta?
f: The derivative of cos(theta) is -sin(theta); the derivative of sin(theta) is cos(theta).

q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Muslim army at Badr (2 AH) had about 313 men, against roughly 1000 of the Quraysh.

q: Abdullah bin Ubayy was the leader of which group in Madinah?
f: Abdullah bin Ubayy was the chief of the hypocrites (Munafiqeen) of Madinah, who pretended to be Muslims while opposing the Prophet (PBUH).

q: In which year did the Khilafat Movement begin? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 under the Ali brothers and others to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.

q: In which year did the Soviet Union (Russia) invade Afghanistan?
f: Soviet troops entered Afghanistan in late December 1979 and withdrew in February 1989.

q: The border between Pakistan and Afghanistan is called the: (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Durand Line (1893) is the international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan, about 2640 km long. The Radcliffe Line is the India-Pakistan border.

q: Hazrat Hafsa (R.A.), a wife of the Prophet ﷺ, is called Ummul Momineen. What does this title mean?
f: Ummul Momineen means Mother of the Believers and is the title of all wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Hazrat Hafsa was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (R.A.).

q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I)?
f: Chagai-I was five simultaneous underground tests at the Ras Koh Hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998. A further test (Chagai-II) followed on 30 May.

q: Global warming increases mainly due to the rise of which gas in the atmosphere?
f: Carbon dioxide is the main greenhouse gas released by burning fossil fuels. It traps heat in the atmosphere and raises the earth temperature.

q: On which date was the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution passed? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed at Minar-e-Pakistan (Iqbal Park), Lahore, on 23 March 1940 at the All India Muslim League session. It is remembered as Pakistan Day.

q: Choose the synonym of CANDID.
f: Candid means honest and straightforward in speech, so its synonym is frank.

q: When the actual words of the speaker are reported exactly as spoken, inside quotation marks, it is called:
f: In direct speech (direct narration) the exact words are quoted. In indirect speech they are reported in the reporter's own words.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: Aslam looks forward ___ meeting Ali.
f: The phrasal verb is look forward to, meaning to wait with pleasure for something.

q: Who led an army with elephants to demolish the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant?
f: Abraha, the Abyssinian governor of Yemen, marched on Makkah with elephants and his army was destroyed (Surah Al-Fil, 105). Abdul Muttalib was the Prophet's grandfather.

q: In which year did Choudhry Rahmat Ali first use the word Pakistan (pamphlet Now or Never)?
f: Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in the pamphlet Now or Never, published on 28 January 1933 at Cambridge.

q: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah take place? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Prophet ﷺ migrated from Makkah to Madinah in 622 AD, which is year 1 of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

q: Which is the third largest city of Pakistan by population?
f: In the 2023 census Karachi, Lahore and Faisalabad (about 3.69 million) are the three largest cities. Rawalpindi is fourth.

q: Lyallpur is the old name of which Pakistani city?
f: Lyallpur was named after Sir James Lyall and renamed Faisalabad in 1977 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.

q: According to the Quran, Allah created the human being (Adam A.S.) from:
f: The Quran says man was created from clay (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:12). Angels were made of light and jinn of smokeless fire.

q: In which year was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated?
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution declares Islam as the State religion of Pakistan?
f: Article 2 of the 1973 Constitution states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

q: Where is the headquarters of Interpol located? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Interpol (International Criminal Police Organization) has its General Secretariat in Lyon, France.

q: Which is the largest bone of the human body?
f: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest, largest and strongest bone in the human body.

q: On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
f: The UN General Assembly admitted Pakistan (with Yemen) on 30 September 1947 by resolution 108 (II).

q: Which Mughal emperor built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore?
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Aurangzeb between 1671 and 1673.

q: General Qamar Javed Bajwa, former Chief of Army Staff, passed out from the Pakistan Military Academy with which Long Course?
f: Bajwa was commissioned on 24 October 1980 in the 16th Baloch Regiment after passing out with the 62nd PMA Long Course. He was the 10th Army Chief (2016 to 2022).

q: In which Hijri year was Ghazwa Tabuk fought? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Ghazwa Tabuk took place in Rajab 9 AH (about October 630 CE) against the threat of a Byzantine attack. It was the last and largest expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which agreement ended the 1965 Pakistan-India war? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, with Soviet Premier Kosygin mediating.

q: Who was the leader (Fuhrer) of Germany during World War 2? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Adolf Hitler led Nazi Germany from 1933 until his death in 1945. Mussolini led Italy and Stalin led the Soviet Union.

q: What is the capital of Pakistan?
f: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan. Karachi was the first capital and Rawalpindi served as the temporary capital in the 1960s.

q: On which date was the United Nations officially founded? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, which is celebrated as UN Day. The Charter was signed earlier on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco.

q: On which date did the United States declare its independence? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, celebrated as Independence Day in the USA.

q: Who is the current Chairman of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) of Pakistan?
f: Nazir Ahmad Butt became NAB chairman on 4 March 2023 and received a three-year extension notified from 6 March 2026.

q: In which year (Hijri) did the Battle of Karbala take place?
f: The Battle of Karbala was fought on 10 Muharram 61 AH (10 October 680 CE), where Hazrat Imam Hussain (RA) was martyred.

q: Who coined the name Pakistan?
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name in his pamphlet Now or Never, published on 28 January 1933.

q: In which year was the War of Independence (against the British East India Company) fought?
f: The War of Independence of 1857 was the major uprising against British rule in the subcontinent, ending Mughal rule.

q: Which prophets raised the foundations of the Kaaba (as stated in Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 127)?
f: The Quran says Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House (Kaaba) in Makkah.

q: Before the change of qibla in 2 AH, towards which place did Muslims pray?
f: Muslims first prayed toward Bait ul Maqdis in Jerusalem, then the qibla was changed to the Kaaba in Makkah.

q: What is one third of one fourth of 120? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: One fourth of 120 = 30, and one third of 30 = 10.

q: Who was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity by Sarojini Naidu?
f: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title for his role in the 1916 Lucknow Pact between Congress and the Muslim League.

q: What is the capital of Cuba? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.

q: How many archers did the Prophet (peace be upon him) place on the hill (Jabal Rumat) in the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Prophet placed 50 archers under Abdullah bin Jubayr on the hill to guard the rear of the Muslim army.

q: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A.) was related to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as his:
f: Umm Kulthum was the Prophet's daughter and married Hazrat Uthman (R.A.) after the death of her sister Ruqayyah; he is called Dhun-Nurayn.

q: Who is the President of China (as of October 2026)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Xi Jinping is President of the People's Republic of China (and General Secretary of the Communist Party). Li Qiang is the Premier.

q: A train runs at twice the speed of a car. The car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km will the train cover in 30 minutes? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: In 30 minutes the car covers 60 km, so the train covers twice that distance in the same time: 2 x 60 = 120 km.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 10 years old? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now. Ali needs 6 more years to reach 10, so the sister will be 12 + 6 = 18.

q: In which year was Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, assassinated?
f: He was shot on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh (later Liaquat Bagh), Rawalpindi.

q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
f: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan; Punakha was the old capital until 1955.

q: The kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of which country? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The kiwi is New Zealand's national bird, and New Zealanders are nicknamed Kiwis.

q: What is the meaning of the word idleness?
f: Idleness means the state of doing no work or being lazy; its synonym is laziness.

q: In which city is Baitul Muqaddas (Masjid Al-Aqsa, the first Qibla of Muslims) located?
f: Baitul Muqaddas (Al-Aqsa Mosque) is in Jerusalem (Al-Quds), Palestine; it was the first Qibla of Muslims.

q: Ahmad is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ahmad is 10 years old? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Sister is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmad needs 5 more years to reach 10, so the sister will be 15 + 5 = 20.

q: Which Prophet (A.S.) opposed the tyrant king Nimrod (Namrud)?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) debated Nimrod (Quran 2:258) and was thrown into the fire, which Allah made cool and safe.

q: How many times is the name Muhammad mentioned in the Holy Quran?
f: The name Muhammad appears four times: 3:144, 33:40, 47:2 and 48:29 (Ahmad appears once, 61:6).

q: What is the officially announced range of Pakistan's Ababeel ballistic missile?
f: ISPR announced the first flight test of the surface-to-surface missile Ababeel in January 2017 with a range of 2,200 km. It is capable of carrying multiple warheads (MIRV).

q: In which year did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Al-Khalid (MBT-2000) was developed jointly by Pakistan and China, and the first batch entered Pakistan Army service in 2001. The improved Al-Khalid-I was inducted in 2020.

q: Which country hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
f: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar, the first Arab country to host it; the final was played at Lusail Stadium on 18 December 2022.

q: Which country won the FIFA World Cup 2022? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Argentina beat France 4-2 on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the final, winning its third World Cup.

q: In which year was the first census of Pakistan held? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The first census of Pakistan was held in February 1951; later censuses were in 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023.

q: What was the relation of Abu Talib with Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Abu Talib was a son of Abd al-Muttalib and so the paternal uncle of the Prophet; he took care of him after the death of his grandfather.

q: Hazrat Musa (AS) was the son of which person?
f: Islamic tradition names Imran (Amram) as the father of Hazrat Musa (AS) and Hazrat Harun (AS).

q: What is the life between death and the Day of Judgment called in Islam?
f: Barzakh is the intermediate stage between death and resurrection, based on Surah Al-Muminun, verse 100.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 18th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 18th is 16 days. 16 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2, so Monday + 2 days = Wednesday.

q: Who wrote the lyrics of the National Anthem (Qaumi Tarana) of Pakistan?
f: The lyrics were written by Abu al-Asar Hafeez Jalandhari, while the music was composed by Ahmad Ghulam Ali Chagla. It was officially adopted in 1954.

q: Hazrat Bilal (R.A.) was the slave of whom before he was freed?
f: Bilal bin Rabah (R.A.) was a slave of Umayya bin Khalaf, who tortured him for accepting Islam. Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.) bought and freed him.

q: What is the full name of the PSL, the Pakistani cricket league?
f: PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the professional Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan, started in 2016.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The IMF headquarters is at 700 19th Street NW, Washington, D.C., USA.

q: What is the capital of Iran? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.

q: What is 90% of 70?
If the 26th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 4th day of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days; 22 = 3 weeks + 1 day, so the 4th is one day before Sunday, which is Saturday.

q: What is one quarter of 120?
f: 120 divided by 4 = 30.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the partition in August 1947?
f: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947) and oversaw the partition. Lord Wavell was his predecessor.

q: Who was the first child to embrace Islam? (Repeated in 3 tests)
f: Hazrat Ali (R.A.), the young cousin of the Prophet (PBUH), is the first child to accept Islam.

q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah, the Mother of the Nation (Madar-e-Millat), die?
f: Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967.

q: What is the LCM of 4 and 8? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: 8 is a multiple of 4 and the smallest common multiple of both numbers is 8.

q: Zabihullah (the one offered for sacrifice) is the title of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Ismail (A.S.) is known as Zabihullah, the son Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.) was ready to sacrifice at Allah's command.

q: On which night was the five daily prayers (Salah) made obligatory for Muslims?
f: The five daily prayers were prescribed during the Isra and Miraj journey of the Prophet (PBUH), when 50 prayers were reduced to five.

q: Who was the head of state under the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1962 Constitution gave Pakistan a presidential system in which the President was both head of state and head of government; the post of Prime Minister was abolished.

q: What is the currency of Russia?
f: The official currency of Russia is the Russian ruble (code RUB), issued by the Central Bank of Russia.

q: In which year was the One Unit scheme implemented in Pakistan? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The One Unit scheme merged the western provinces into West Pakistan in 1955 (Act passed 30 September 1955, in force 14 October 1955) and was ended in 1970.

q: On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed?
f: The UN General Assembly declared 15 March as the International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan and the OIC.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of France (as of October 2026)?
f: Sebastien Lecornu was appointed Prime Minister of France on 9 September 2025, resigned on 6 October 2025 and was reappointed on 10 October 2025; he was still in office in October 2026.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 28th be?
f: From the 5th to the 28th is 23 days; 23 = 3 weeks + 2 days, so Friday + 2 = Sunday.

q: In 2020, Kashmir Highway in Islamabad was renamed as:
f: In August 2020 Kashmir Highway was renamed Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris on the first Youm-e-Istehsal.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 15th be?
f: From the 1st to the 15th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so the day is the same: Monday.

q: In which district of Punjab is Rohtas Fort located?
f: Rohtas Fort was built by Sher Shah Suri near Dina in Jhelum district and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.

q: Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty (1960) on behalf of Pakistan?
f: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by President Ayub Khan of Pakistan and Prime Minister Nehru of India, with the World Bank also signing.

q: In which city is the Pakistan Navy Headquarters (Naval Headquarters) located?
f: Naval Headquarters was shifted from Karachi to Islamabad in 1975 and is located in Sector E-8, Islamabad.

q: What is 40% of 60? (Repeated in 1 test)
If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 15th day of that month be?
f: From the 3rd to the 15th is 12 days; 12 = 1 week + 5 days, so Sunday + 5 days = Friday.

q: Complete the series: 1A, 2D, 3H, ?
f: Numbers go 1, 2, 3, 4. Letters A, D, H, M move forward by 3, 4, 5, so the next letter is M.

q: Train A runs at 60 km/h and train B is twice as fast. How many km does train B cover in 30 minutes? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Speed of B = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.

q: In which city did the Quraish tribe live?
f: The Quraish were the ruling tribe of Makkah and guardians of the Kaaba.

q: In which year was the first Round Table Conference held in London? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The first Round Table Conference began on 12 November 1930 in London. The Congress did not attend.

q: Who started the Faraizi movement in Bengal?
f: Haji Shariatullah founded the Faraizi movement in 1818 to make Bengali Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam. His son Dudu Miyan later led it.

q: Which companion served the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for ten years?
f: Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A.) served the Prophet (PBUH) for ten years in Madinah, starting as a boy.

q: Iran, Turkey and Pakistan formed which organization in 1964? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: RCD was founded in July 1964 by Iran, Pakistan and Turkey for economic and social development. It was replaced by ECO in 1985.

q: In which year did the UN General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
f: The Declaration was adopted on 10 December 1948 as resolution 217 A (III) in Paris.

q: Which is the national bird of Pakistan? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The chukar partridge (chakor) is the national bird of Pakistan.

q: Choose the synonym of JUBILANT.
f: Jubilant means feeling or showing great joy, so joyful is the closest meaning.

q: Choose the antonym of GLORY.
f: Glory means great honour and fame; its opposite is disgrace or shame.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah leave the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah resigned from the Congress at its Nagpur session in December 1920 because he opposed Gandhi's non-cooperation movement.

q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, ?
f: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10: gaps of 2, 3, 4. Next is 10, which is J.

q: What is 90% of 80? (Repeated in 1 test)
If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th be?
f: The 1st, 8th and 15th are Mondays. The 12th is 4 days after the 8th, so it is Friday.

q: What was the relationship of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was the Prophet's paternal uncle. Both were also nursed by Thuwaibah, so he was a foster brother too. He is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.

q: According to a hadith in Sahih Muslim, which voluntary (nafl) prayer is the best after the obligatory prayers?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) said the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is the night prayer, which is Tahajjud (Sahih Muslim).

q: Who conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD?
f: The Umayyad general Muhammad bin Qasim, nephew of Hajjaj bin Yusuf, defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh.

q: In which Ghazwa were about 70 Companions martyred, the largest number in any Ghazwa?
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud (3 AH), including Hazrat Hamza (RA). Far fewer were martyred at Badr (14) and Khandaq (about 6).

q: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
f: Japan's name Nippon or Nihon means sun origin, so it is called the Land of the Rising Sun.

q: Which continent is the coldest on Earth?
f: Antarctica has the lowest recorded temperature on Earth, minus 89.2 degrees C at Vostok Station on 21 July 1983.

q: On which date is Pakistan Air Force Day observed every year? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: PAF Day on 7 September commemorates the role of the PAF in the 1965 war. Defence Day is 6 September.

q: On which Prophet was the Injeel (Gospel) revealed? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Tawrat was revealed on Musa, Zabur on Dawood, Injeel on Isa (Jesus) and the Quran on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

q: How many general (directly elected) seats are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Of the 336 seats, 266 are general seats, 60 are reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslims. Before the 25th Amendment (2018, FATA merger) there were 272 general seats out of 342.

q: How many sons did Prophet Muhammad (SAW) have? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The Prophet (SAW) had three sons: Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyib and Tahir) and Ibrahim. All of them died in childhood.

q: Who started the Civil Disobedience Movement in British India?
f: Gandhi began the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the Salt March.

q: In which year did the Civil Disobedience Movement begin?
f: The movement began on 12 March 1930 when Gandhi started the Salt March.

q: What was the main event that opened the Civil Disobedience Movement?
f: Gandhi marched from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi in 1930 to defy the British salt tax and salt monopoly.

q: Who led the Salt March (Dandi March) of 1930?
f: Gandhi led 78 followers about 387 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, starting on 12 March 1930.

q: In which year did the Non-Cooperation Movement begin in India?
f: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 and called it off in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

q: Who launched the Non-Cooperation Movement? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: Gandhi launched it in 1920 so that Indians would withdraw cooperation from British institutions.

q: The Swadeshi Movement began as a protest against which British decision?
f: The Swadeshi Movement (boycott of British goods) started in 1905 against Lord Curzon's Partition of Bengal.

q: In which year did the Swadeshi Movement begin?
f: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905 and the boycott of British goods was resolved on 7 August 1905.

q: Which brothers were the leading figures of the Khilafat Movement?
o: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali
Liaquat Ali Khan and Ghulam Muhammad
Hakim Ajmal Khan and Dr Ansari
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and Maulana Hasrat Mohani
f: The Ali brothers, Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali, were the central leaders of the Khilafat Movement (1919-1924).

q: The Khilafat Movement was launched by Indian Muslims to support which institution? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: After World War I, Indian Muslims tried to protect the Ottoman Caliph and the Ottoman Empire's territory from being broken up.

q: Which two leaders led the Home Rule Movement in India?
o: Annie Besant and Bal Gangadhar Tilak
f: Tilak founded his Home Rule League in April 1916 at Poona and Annie Besant founded hers in September 1916 at Madras.

q: In which year was the Home Rule Movement launched in India?
f: Both Home Rule Leagues, of Tilak and of Annie Besant, were founded in 1916.

q: Martin Luther King Jr. is associated with which movement?
f: King led the nonviolent American Civil Rights Movement in the 1950s and 1960s and gave the 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963.

q: Who led the Civil Rights Movement in the USA?
f: Martin Luther King Jr. was the best known leader of the nonviolent Civil Rights Movement in the USA.

q: What did the American Civil Rights Movement mainly demand?
f: The movement fought racial segregation and discrimination against African Americans and sought equal civil rights.

q: Who led the anti-apartheid struggle in South Africa?
f: Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison for resisting apartheid and became South Africa's first democratically elected president in 1994.

q: What did the Suffragette Movement demand?
o: The right to vote for women
f: The suffragettes, led in Britain by Emmeline Pankhurst, campaigned for women's suffrage (the vote).

q: From which country did Pakistan buy Gwadar? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958; it became part of Pakistan on 8 September 1958.

q: Which is the most populated city of Pakistan?
f: Karachi is the most populous city of Pakistan; the 2023 census counted about 20 million people in Karachi division.

q: Who presented the Fourteen Points in 1929?
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at the Muslim League council in Delhi in March 1929, in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: What was the relation between Hazrat Musa (A.S.) and Hazrat Haroon (A.S.)?
f: Hazrat Haroon (A.S.) was the brother of Hazrat Musa (A.S.) and was made a prophet to help him (Surah Maryam 19:53).

q: How many gates (doors) does Jannah have?
f: A hadith in Bukhari and Muslim says Paradise has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.

q: The Liaquat-Nehru Pact (Delhi Pact), signed between Pakistan and India to protect minorities, was signed in which year?
f: The Liaquat-Nehru Pact was signed in New Delhi on 8 April 1950 by Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru. It guaranteed security and equal rights to minorities in both countries.

q: Attabad Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan was formed due to a:
f: A massive landslide on 4 January 2010 blocked the Hunza River near Attabad village and created the lake. It also flooded part of the Karakoram Highway.

q: Choose the synonym of SPONTANEOUS.
f: Spontaneous means happening naturally without planning, which matches impulsive. Planned, rehearsed and deliberate mean the opposite.

q: The ancient Indus Valley site of Harappa is located near which city of Pakistan?
f: Harappa lies in Punjab, about 24 km west of Sahiwal, on a dry former course of the Ravi River. Mohenjo-daro, the other major site, is near Larkana in Sindh.

q: Who is the Chief of the Air Staff of the Pakistan Air Force (as of October 2026)? (Repeated in 1 test)
o: Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu
Air Chief Marshal Mujahid Anwar Khan
f: Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu has led the PAF since 19 March 2021, and his tenure was extended by two years from March 2026, to 2028.

q: Who is the President of France (as of October 2026)?
f: Emmanuel Macron is serving his second term, which ends in May 2027. Sebastien Lecornu is the Prime Minister, not the President.

q: How many articles did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan contain?
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles, 13 parts and 6 schedules. It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated on 7 October 1958.

q: Who wrote the book Mein Kampf (My Struggle)?
f: Mein Kampf was written by Adolf Hitler (vol. 1 in 1925, vol. 2 in 1926) while he was in prison after the failed Munich Putsch.

q: Ghazwa Tabuk (9 AH) was undertaken by the Prophet (PBUH) against which empire?
f: Tabuk was the Prophet's last expedition; he marched against the Byzantine army gathered near Syria, but the Byzantines withdrew and no fighting took place.

q: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) connects which two cities?
f: The N-10 Makran Coastal Highway runs along the Arabian Sea from Karachi to Gwadar via Ormara and Pasni.

q: In which year was the State Bank of Pakistan inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan on 1 July 1948 in Karachi.

q: Which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH) is known by the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah)? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) gave Khalid bin Walid the title Saifullah, traditionally after the Battle of Mu'tah.

q: The Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act), which introduced separate electorates for Muslims, were passed in:
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, after Secretary of State John Morley and Viceroy Lord Minto. It gave Muslims separate electorates.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his Allahabad Address, presenting the idea of a separate Muslim state in north-western India?
f: Iqbal gave the Allahabad Address on 29 December 1930 at the annual session of the All-India Muslim League.

q: Who is the current President of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
f: Asif Ali Zardari is the 14th President of Pakistan, in office since 10 March 2024. Shehbaz Sharif is the Prime Minister.

q: Which letter comes immediately after M in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs ... K, L, M, N, O ... so N follows M.

q: Kaleemullah (Kalimullah), meaning the one who spoke with Allah, is the title of which Prophet? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Hazrat Musa (A.S.) is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly (Quran 4:164, 7:144).

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army after independence in 1947?
f: Frank Messervy, a British officer, was the first C-in-C from 15 August 1947 to February 1948. Douglas Gracey succeeded him and Ayub Khan was the first Pakistani C-in-C in 1951.

q: The word Mantaq (Urdu) means:
f: Mantaq is the Arabic and Urdu word for logic, the science of correct reasoning.

q: Harappa, in Punjab, Pakistan, is the type site of which ancient civilization?
f: Harappa gave its name to the Harappan or Indus Valley Civilization, a Bronze Age civilization, first excavated from 1920-21.

q: The tribes of Aus and Khazraj, who became the Ansar, lived in which city?
f: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later called Madina. They became the Ansar (helpers) after the Hijrah.

q: What is the formula for the circumference of a circle with radius r?
f: Circumference = 2 x pi x r = pi x diameter. Pi r squared is the area.

q: Ali is 9 years old and Hareem is twice his age. How old will Hareem be when Ali is 13?
f: Hareem is now 18. Ali needs 4 more years to reach 13, so Hareem will be 18 + 4 = 22.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is four times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 10?
f: Sister is now 4 x 5 = 20. Ali needs 5 more years, so she will be 20 + 5 = 25.

q: If yesterday was Saturday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
f: Yesterday Saturday means today is Sunday. Tomorrow is Monday and the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 26th of the same month?
f: 26 - 14 = 12 days later. 12 = 7 + 5, so move 5 days after Sunday, which is Friday.

q: Ali walks towards the north, turns left and walks 5 m, then turns left again. In which direction is he facing now?
f: Facing north, a left turn gives west. Another left turn from west gives south.

q: Akbar was born in 1980 and Aslam in 1987. Bilal is elder than Aslam but younger than Akbar. What is the order from eldest to youngest?
f: Akbar (1980) is eldest and Aslam (1987) is youngest. Bilal is younger than Akbar and elder than Aslam, so he is in the middle.

q: Choose the synonym of BRAVE.
f: Brave means ready to face danger without fear, which is the meaning of courageous.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to DISTURB.
f: To disturb is to interrupt or trouble someone, which is the meaning of bother.

q: Choose the synonym of NIBBLE.
f: To nibble is to take small gentle bites, as dictionary.com defines it.

q: Choose the synonym of MEDIATE.
f: To mediate is to step in between two sides to settle a dispute. Dictionary.com lists arbitrate as its synonym.

q: Which pillar of Islam was made obligatory for the Muslims on the night of Miraj?
f: The five daily prayers were prescribed during the Isra and Miraj journey, the Prophet PBUH brought them back for his Ummah.

q: In which sport is the word 'love' used for a score of zero?
f: In tennis a score of zero is called love, probably from the French l'oeuf (egg).

q: 24 January is observed every year as the International Day of:
f: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January International Day of Education in December 2018, first observed in 2019.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan during the 1965 war with India?
f: Ayub Khan was President from 1958 to 1969 and led Pakistan in the August to September 1965 war.

q: What is the product of two negative integers?
f: A negative times a negative is positive, for example (-3) x (-4) = 12.

q: The square root of a negative number is called:
f: No real number squared gives a negative value, so the square root of a negative number is an imaginary number (for example, the square root of -1 is i).

q: The book 'India of My Dreams' is attributed to:
f: India of My Dreams (1947) is a compilation of the writings of M. K. Gandhi, compiled by R. K. Prabhu.

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 took place in which city?
f: British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd in Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, Punjab, on 13 April 1919.

q: PEMRA, the body that regulates private TV and radio in Pakistan, stands for:
o: Pakistan Entertainment and Media Regulatory Association
Pakistan Education and Media Research Authority
f: PEMRA was set up under the PEMRA Ordinance 2002 as the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority.

q: In which Chinese city did the first cases of Covid-19 appear in late 2019?
f: The first Covid-19 cases were reported in Wuhan, Hubei province, in December 2019.

q: The Rowlatt Act, opposed by Indians as the Black Act, was passed in which year?
f: The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) was passed on 18 March 1919.

q: How many seats in the Senate of Pakistan are reserved for non-Muslims (minorities)?
f: After the 18th Amendment, one non-Muslim seat is reserved for each of the four provinces, 4 in total.

q: Who wrote the text of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as scribe? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: According to Sahih Muslim, Hazrat Ali (R.A.) wrote the treaty at the Prophet's dictation.

q: How many sons did Hazrat Yaqub (A.S.) have?
f: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S.) had twelve sons, the ancestors of the twelve tribes of Bani Israel (Asbat).

q: Who was the foster sister of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Shaima bint al-Harith was the daughter of his wet nurse Halima Sadiyyah.

q: World War II began on which date?
f: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, which started World War II.

q: On which date is the Independence Day of the USA celebrated?
f: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776.

q: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with China?
f: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang, China.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the ancient site of Mohenjo-daro located?
f: Mohenjo-daro, a major Indus Valley Civilization city, lies in Larkana district of Sindh.

q: In which year did the social worker Abdul Sattar Edhi die?
f: Abdul Sattar Edhi died in Karachi on 8 July 2016.

q: Which is the largest source of fresh water on Earth?
f: About 68.7 percent of Earth's fresh water is locked in glaciers, ice caps and permanent snow.

q: Which force opposes the motion of a moving body?
f: Friction acts between surfaces in contact and opposes relative motion.

q: In which sport did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal (Rome, 1960)?
f: Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the men's hockey final at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

q: The legendary boxer Muhammad Ali belonged to which country?
f: Muhammad Ali (Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer from Louisville, Kentucky.

q: The family tree of Prophet Muhammad PBUH goes back to which Prophet?
f: The Prophet PBUH descended from Hazrat Ismail (A.S.), son of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.), through Adnan.

q: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S.) was the son of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S.) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (A.S.) and the grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S.).

q: According to Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age to be elected President of Pakistan?
f: Article 41 requires the President to be a Muslim, at least 45 years old and qualified to be a member of the National Assembly.

q: Change into passive voice: Ali wrote a letter.
o: A letter was written by Ali.
A letter has been written by Ali.
Ali was written by a letter.
A letter is written by Ali.
f: Simple past active becomes was/were plus past participle: A letter was written by Ali.

q: What was the name of the US military operation launched against Iran in 2026? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: Operation Epic Fury was announced by US Central Command on 28 February 2026. The US said its aims were to end Iran's nuclear weapons ambitions and weaken the IRGC.

q: Which three countries signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in August 2026?
f: The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was signed in Mecca on 7 August 2026 by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. An armed attack on any one of the three is treated as an attack on all.

q: How old was Fatima Jinnah when she died in 1967?
f: Fatima Jinnah was born in July 1893 and died on 9 July 1967, so she was 73. She is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: The parliamentary committee that prepared the draft of the 1973 Constitution was headed by:
f: Mahmud Ali Kasuri headed the Constitution Committee that drafted the 1973 Constitution. The National Assembly passed it in April 1973 and it came into force on 14 August 1973.

q: Which of the following was NOT a daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA) and a wife of the Prophet.

q: Who is the Supreme Leader of Iran as of October 2026?
f: Mojtaba Khamenei was chosen Supreme Leader by the Assembly of Experts on 8 March 2026. He succeeded his father Ali Khamenei, who was killed in strikes on 28 February 2026.

q: On which date was the Battle of Plassey fought?
f: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 in Bengal. The East India Company defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, which began British power in Bengal.

q: Which country has the largest population in the world?
f: India passed China as the most populous country in 2023, according to UN estimates.

q: How many Articles does the Constitution of Pakistan 1973 contain? (Repeated in 2 tests)
f: The 1973 Constitution has 280 Articles, arranged in parts and schedules. Amendments have inserted and omitted some provisions, but 280 is the standard number asked in tests. The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles.

q: The Battle of Solferino (1859) inspired Henry Dunant to found which organisation?
f: Henry Dunant saw the wounded after the Battle of Solferino in 1859 and wrote A Memory of Solferino in 1862. The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863.

q: The valley of Mina, where pilgrims stay and stone the Jamarat during Hajj, is located near which city?
f: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stay in its tent city and stone the Jamarat there during the days of Tashriq.

q: Marvi is the heroine of which famous Sindhi folk tale of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai?
f: Marvi is the heroine of the Sindhi tale of Umar Marvi, told in the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai. She is remembered for loyalty to her homeland and people.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Islam?
o: Submission to the will of Allah
f: Islam means submission or surrender to the will of Allah. A Muslim is one who submits to God. The word is also linked with peace.

q: Which name of Makkah is mentioned in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:96) as the place of the first House of worship?
f: Bakkah is another name for Makkah, used in the Quran (3:96) for the first House established for mankind. The Kaaba is in Makkah.

q: Which institution conducts the population census in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) conducts the census; other agencies only help with logistics and security. The 2023 census was Pakistan's first digital census.

q: On which date did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan and become Bangladesh?
f: East Pakistan became the independent state of Bangladesh on 16 December 1971. The 1970 election results and the political and military crisis that followed were key causes.

q: In which Ghazwa was Hazrat Hamza (RA), the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), martyred?
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred at Uhud in 3 AH (625 CE). The battle took place near Mount Uhud, north of Madinah.

q: What was the main effect of the 18th Constitutional Amendment (2010)?
o: It devolved many powers to the provinces
It made Pakistan a one-unit state
It created the office of Chief Martial Law Administrator
f: The 18th Amendment, passed in 2010, strengthened parliamentary democracy and devolved many powers to the provinces. It also inserted Article 25A (right to education).

q: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
f: Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India from August 1947. Pakistan's first Governor-General was Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

q: How many National Assembly seats are allocated to Punjab (336-member house)?
f: Punjab has 173 NA seats: 141 general and 32 reserved for women. The 336-member house has 266 general, 60 women and 10 non-Muslim seats.

q: For about how many years were the Madani revelations sent down?
f: Madani revelations came in roughly the 10 years after the Hijrah (622 CE). The whole revelation period was 23 years.

q: On what date was the Tashkent Declaration signed by Pakistan and India?
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 after the 1965 war. Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the talks.

q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objectives Resolution on 7 March 1949 and the Constituent Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949. 7 March is only the day it was presented. 23 March 1956 is when the first constitution came into force, and 14 August 1948 is the first Independence Day.

q: Choose the synonym of INCESSANT.
f: Incessant means continuing without stopping, so ceaseless (never stopping) is the synonym. Occasional, intermittent and brief all describe things that stop or happen only now and then, so they are opposite in meaning.

q: In which district of Balochistan did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests on 28 May 1998?
f: The five tests of 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I) were done in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai District, Balochistan. Kharan was the site of the single follow-up test on 30 May, and Gwadar and Turbat were not test sites.

q: On which date did Fatima Jinnah (Madar-e-Millat) die?
f: Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967 and is buried next to the Quaid at Mazar-e-Quaid. 11 September 1948 is the death date of Quaid-e-Azam, and the other dates are wrong mixes of these days and years.

q: Who led the Aligarh Movement?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Aligarh Movement after 1857 to bring modern education to Muslims, and founded the MAO College at Aligarh. Iqbal was a poet-philosopher, Jauhar led the Khilafat Movement, and Salimullah Khan hosted the founding of the Muslim League in 1906.

q: In which year of Prophethood (Nabuwwat) did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madinah?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year after the first revelation. The 10th year was the Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn), the 11th year saw the first meeting with people of Yathrib, and by the 15th year the Prophet (PBUH) was already in Madinah.

q: What is the capital of Belgium?
f: Brussels has been the capital of Belgium since 1830 and is also the main seat of the European Union. Antwerp is a large Belgian port city but not the capital, Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands, and Geneva is a city in Switzerland.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: The fridge is ___ the kitchen.
f: We use 'in' for something inside a room or enclosed space, so the fridge is in the kitchen. 'On' is for surfaces, 'at' is for a point or place, and 'into' shows movement, so they do not fit here.

q: Rearrange the letters PHELTANE to make the name of an animal.
f: PHELTANE has the letters E, L, E, P, H, A, N, T, which spell ELEPHANT. Antelope, Panther and Leopard need letters (like O, R, D) that are not in PHELTANE.

q: In which Hijri year was Hazrat Usman (R.A.) martyred?
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A.) was martyred in Madina on 18 Dhul Hijjah 35 AH (656 CE) when rebels besieged his house. 23 AH is the martyrdom of Hazrat Umar (R.A.) and 40 AH is that of Hazrat Ali (R.A.); 30 AH is wrong.

q: The value of cos 0° is:
f: On the unit circle at 0°, the x-coordinate is 1, so cos 0° = 1 (same as sin 90°). sin 0° and cos 90° are 0; -1 is cos 180°; 1/2 is cos 60°.

q: By the power rule, the derivative of x^n with respect to x is:
f: Power rule: bring the power down and reduce it by one, so d/dx of x^n = n x^(n-1). For example, d/dx of x^3 = 3x^2. x^(n+1)/(n+1) is the integral, not the derivative; the other two forget the n or add to the power.

q: The kangaroo is the national animal of which country?
f: The kangaroo is the national animal of Australia and appears on its coat of arms (since 1908) with the emu. New Zealand's symbol is the kiwi bird, South Africa's is the springbok, and Papua New Guinea's is the bird of paradise.

q: In which year did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation in the Cave of Hira?
f: The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira in 610 AD, when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 years old. 570 AD is his birth year (Year of the Elephant), 622 AD is the Hijrah to Madina, and 632 AD is the year of his death.

q: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects (2025), which is the largest city in the world by population?
f: The UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025 report ranks Jakarta (Indonesia) first with about 42 million people. Dhaka is second, Tokyo has dropped to third, and New Delhi is fourth.

q: How many Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
f: The Holy Quran has 114 Surahs, starting with Surah Al-Fatiha and ending with Surah An-Nas. 30 is the number of Paras (Juz), not Surahs; 113 and 116 are wrong counts.

q: What is the full form of NATO?
f: NATO stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance formed by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington on 4 April 1949. The other options change one word (American, Trade, National) and are not its real name.

q: In which year did World War II end?
f: World War II ended in 1945: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan formally surrendered on 2 September 1945. 1939 is the year the war began; 1944 and 1946 are wrong.

q: Which community benefited the most from the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
f: The 1905 partition made a new province, Eastern Bengal and Assam, with a Muslim majority (about 18 million Muslims to 12 million Hindus), so Muslims got more jobs, schools and political weight. Hindus opposed it and started the Swadeshi movement, and the Sikhs and British traders were not the main gainers.

q: What is the upper house of the Parliament (Majlis-e-Shoora) of Pakistan called? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The Parliament of Pakistan has two houses: the Senate is the upper house and the National Assembly is the lower house (Article 50 of the 1973 Constitution). A Provincial Assembly is a provincial body, and the Council of Common Interests is not a house of Parliament.

q: The OIC (Organisation of Islamic Cooperation) was founded in 1969 at the first Islamic Summit held in which city? (Repeated in 1 test)
f: The OIC was founded on 25 September 1969 at the first Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque. Jeddah is its headquarters (from 1970), not the founding city; Lahore hosted the 1974 summit, and Cairo is wrong.

q: In which Hijri year was Ghazwa Khaibar fought?
f: Ghazwa Khaibar was fought in 7 AH (628 CE), soon after the Treaty of Hudaibiya, and Khaibar was conquered by the Muslims. 5 AH is Ghazwa Khandaq, 6 AH is Hudaibiya, and 8 AH is the Conquest of Makkah.

q: Which international body brokered (helped negotiate) the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 between Pakistan and India?
f: The World Bank helped Pakistan and India negotiate for about nine years and is also a signatory of the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty. The UN, the IMF and the Commonwealth were not the brokers of this treaty.

q: In which cave did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation (Wahi)?
f: The first revelation (the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in Cave Hira on Jabal-al-Noor near Makkah in 610 CE. Cave Thaur is where the Prophet (PBUH) hid with Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) during the Hijrat; the other two are wrong.

q: Ayat-ul-Kursi is a verse of which Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Ayat-ul-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne) is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah, the second Surah of the Quran. It is not in Surah Al-Imran, Surah Yaseen or Surah Al-Ikhlas.

q: The Sindhi language is mainly derived (through Prakrit) from which ancient language?
f: Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language; its base comes from Sanskrit through Prakrit and Apabhramsha. Arabic and Persian only added many loan words later, and Turkish is not its source.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of students is present?
f: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%. 80% would need 1200 present, 13.33% is the absent percentage, and 87.5% would need 1312.5 present, which is not possible.

q: In which year was the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament?
f: The Indian Independence Act got royal assent on 18 July 1947 and created Pakistan and India as two independent dominions. 1935 is the Government of India Act, 1940 is the Lahore Resolution, and 1946 is the Cabinet Mission Plan.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution declares Pakistan a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution says Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Article 2 makes Islam the state religion, Article 2-A makes the Objectives Resolution part of the Constitution, and Article 3 is about ending exploitation.

q: What is the date of birth of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
f: Quaid-e-Azam was born in Karachi on 25 December 1876, which is a national holiday in Pakistan. 11 September is the date he died (1948), and 9 November 1877 is the birth date of Allama Iqbal.

q: Which Companion stayed with the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Thaur during the Hijrat to Madina?
f: During the Hijrat, the Prophet (PBUH) hid for three nights in the Cave of Thaur with Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.), who is called the Companion of the Cave (Yar-e-Ghar). Hazrat Ali (R.A.) slept in the Prophet's bed in Makkah, and Hazrat Umar and Usman (R.A.) were not in the cave.

q: Choose the antonym (opposite) of CRUDE.
f: Crude means raw, rough or not processed, so its opposite is refined (polished, processed). Raw, rough and coarse all have nearly the same meaning as crude, so they are synonyms, not antonyms.

q: The Badshahi Mosque, built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb, is located in which city?
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Aurangzeb in 1671-1673 and stands opposite the Lahore Fort in the old walled city of Lahore. Delhi has the Jamia Masjid of Shah Jahan, Thatta has the Shah Jahan Mosque, and Multan is known for its shrines, not the Badshahi Mosque.

q: What was the real name of Titu Mir, the Muslim freedom fighter of Bengal?
f: Titu Mir (1782-1831) was the popular name of Syed Mir Nisar Ali, who fought the British and Hindu landlords and built the bamboo fort at Narkelbaria. Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement, Dudu Miyan was his son, and Syed Ahmad Barelvi led the Mujahideen Movement.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) spend his last days and pass away?
o: In the house of Hazrat Khadija (RA) in Makkah
In the room of Hazrat Aisha (RA) in Madina
In the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA) in Madina
In the house of Hazrat Fatima (RA) in Madina
f: During his last illness the Prophet (PBUH) stayed in the room (hujra) of Hazrat Aisha (RA) next to Masjid-e-Nabawi, passed away there and was buried at the same place. Hazrat Khadija's house was in Makkah, and the Prophet stayed with Abu Ayyub Ansari (RA) only after the Hijrah.

q: Christians wrongly call which prophet the son of God?
f: Christians call Hazrat Isa (AS), Jesus, the son of God; the Quran rejects this and calls him a prophet and servant of Allah (Surah Maryam, Surah Al-Ikhlas). Hazrat Musa and Hazrat Ibrahim are not called son of God by Christians, and the Quran says some Jews (not Christians) said this about Hazrat Uzair (AS).

q: Which is the highest polo ground in the world, located in Pakistan?
f: Shandur Polo Ground on the Shandur Pass between Chitral and Ghizer is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world (the Roof of the World). Deosai is a high plateau and national park, while Babusar and Khunjerab are mountain passes, not polo grounds.

q: Change into passive voice: They will play cricket.
o: Cricket would be played by them.
Cricket will be play by them.
Cricket will have been played by them.
Cricket will be played by them.
f: In future simple passive the form is will be + past participle, and the subject they becomes them, so: Cricket will be played by them. The other options use the wrong verb form (play), the wrong tense (would) or the future perfect tense.

q: Fill in the blank: He wished he ___ rich.
f: After wish we use the past subjunctive for an unreal or imagined situation, and the correct form for all subjects is were: He wished he were rich. Is and will be are present and future forms, and was being is wrong for a state like being rich.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q1) What will be the next number: 13, 15, 17, 19, ?
f: The series goes up by 2 each time, so after 19 comes 21.
r: Tip: first check the difference between neighbouring terms; a constant difference means an arithmetic series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q2) What will be the next letters: BC, DE, FG, ?
f: Each pair starts two letters after the previous pair: BC, DE, FG, then HI.
r: Tip: write the letters as numbers (B=2, C=3 and so on) to spot the jump between groups.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q3) Subtract 7 from 25+3. If the answer is 10 then write X, otherwise write Y.
f: 25+3 = 28 and 28 - 7 = 21, which is not 10, so the answer is Y.
r: Tip: in condition questions, do the arithmetic first and only then choose the letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q4) Airplane is to Air as Whale is to:
f: An airplane travels in air, and a whale lives and travels in the ocean.
r: Tip: in analogies, name the relation (here: moving thing and its medium) and apply it to the second pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q5) Saleem was born in 1947. He is 21 years old. His brother was born in 1965. What is the age of his brother?
f: Saleem is 21 in 1947 + 21 = 1968. His brother was born in 1965, so he is 1968 - 1965 = 3 years old.
r: Tip: find the current year from the first person's data, then use it for the second person.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q6) 4+3=8. If the answer is right then write X, otherwise write Y.
f: 4 + 3 = 7, not 8, so the statement is wrong and the answer is Y.
r: Tip: check the statement itself; the printed total is a claim you must test.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q7) If sow is to seed then reap is to?
f: A farmer sows seed and reaps the crop, so the object that matches seed is crop.
r: Tip: in analogies the second word of the pair is the thing acted upon; sow acts on seed, reap acts on crop.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q8) 8, 10 and 6: divide the largest number by the difference of the two smaller numbers. Answer = ?
f: The largest number is 10 and the two smaller are 8 and 6, whose difference is 2. So 10 / 2 = 5.
r: Tip: identify the largest and smaller numbers first so you do not mix up which ones to subtract.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q9) Tight is to Loose as Hard is to:
