f: Loose is the opposite of tight, so the opposite of hard is soft.
r: Tip: if the first pair are opposites (antonyms), choose the opposite of the third word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q10) Fish is to swimming as Snake is to:
f: Fish swim; a snake crawls (it moves along the ground without legs).
r: Tip: this is an animal-and-movement analogy; match the animal to its typical way of moving.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q11) Which word does not belong to this list: Foot, Inch, Yard, Acre, Mile?
f: Foot, inch, yard and mile measure length, but an acre measures area.
r: Tip: an acre is about 4047 square metres; in Pakistan land is also measured in kanal and marla.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q12) Cat is to Kitten as Dog is to?
f: A kitten is the young one of a cat, and a puppy is the young one of a dog.
r: Tip: animal-to-young analogies use the special word for the young of that animal (calf, lamb, cub).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q13) Which one is different from the others: Ship, Bus, Train, Car, Truck?
f: Bus, train, car and truck travel on land, while a ship travels on water.
r: Tip: group items by where or how they work, then pick the one that falls outside the group.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q14) If Light is to Eye, then Sound is to?
f: The eye senses light, and the ear senses sound.
r: Tip: sense-organ analogies pair a stimulus with the organ that detects it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q15) Which is different in the following: Lion, Wolf, Leopard, Lamb, Tiger?
f: Lion, wolf, leopard and tiger are carnivorous predators, while a lamb is a gentle animal that eats plants.
r: Tip: carnivores hunt other animals, herbivores eat plants; this split is common in odd-one-out questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q16) Which one of the following is different: Mile, Kanal, Marla, Acre?
f: Kanal, marla and acre are units of land area, while a mile is a unit of length.
r: Tip: one kanal equals 20 marla, and a marla is about 272 square feet.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q17) Hand is to Touch as Nose is to?
f: The hand is the organ of touch, and the nose is the organ of smell.
r: Tip: the five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch, each tied to one organ.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from others: Shirts, Boots, Coats, Trousers, Necktie?
f: Shirts, coats, trousers and necktie are clothes worn on the body, while boots are footwear.
r: Tip: look for the item that belongs to a different category (footwear versus clothing).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q19) Easy is to Light as Rough is to:
f: Easy and light both mean not hard or heavy to deal with, and rough is closest to hard (a rough surface feels hard and coarse). The paper's answer key gives Hard.
r: Tip: when the analogy is not obvious, look for the option that is the antonym of the third word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q20) Which of the following is different from others: Plate, Dish, Knife, Spoon, Sugar?
f: Plate, dish, knife and spoon are utensils, while sugar is a food item.
r: Tip: separate objects used for eating from things that are eaten.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q21) One third of one half is equal to?
f: One third of one half is 1/3 x 1/2 = 1/6.
r: Tip: the word 'of' between fractions means multiply.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q22) Hot is to Burn as Cold is to?
f: Excessive heat makes things burn, and excessive cold makes things freeze.
r: Tip: this is a cause-and-effect analogy; ask what the extreme does.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q23) Which number will come next: 6, 11, 12, 11, 18, ?
f: Take alternate terms: 6, 12, 18 goes up by 6, and the other terms stay at 11, 11, so the next is 11.
r: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q24) Which is different from others: Whisper, Shout, Sing, Tell?
f: Whisper, shout and tell are ways of speaking words, while singing involves music and a tune.
r: Tip: look for the action that uses a different skill from the rest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q25) Which one is different from others: Selfish, Dishonest, Foolish, Ugly?
f: Selfish, dishonest and foolish describe character or behaviour, while ugly describes physical appearance.
r: Tip: separate qualities of character from qualities of looks.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q26) Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to?
f: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in jail.
r: Tip: the relation is 'confined living thing and its place of confinement'.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q27) Which is different from other: Radius, Diagonal, Diameter, Circumference?
f: Radius, diameter and circumference are all parts of a circle, but a diagonal belongs to polygons such as squares and rectangles.
r: Tip: circumference = 2 x pi x radius, and diameter = 2 x radius.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q28) Which number is out of order: Four, Eight, Ten, Seven, Twelve?
f: Four, eight, ten and twelve are even numbers, while seven is odd.
r: Tip: check parity (odd or even) first when numbers are written as words.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q29) What comes next: 62, 31, 34, 17, 20, ?
f: The series alternates between halving and adding 3: 62/2 = 31, +3 = 34, /2 = 17, +3 = 20, so the next step is 20/2 = 10.
r: Tip: when numbers rise and fall, check for two alternating operations.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q30) Which one of the following is different: Cow, Goat, Sheep, Horse, Buffalo?
f: Cow, goat, sheep and buffalo are milk-giving farm animals, while a horse is not kept for milk.
r: Tip: think about the main purpose an animal is kept for.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q31) Which number will come next: 1, 4, 10, 22, ?
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12, which double each time, so the next difference is 24: 22 + 24 = 46.
r: Tip: if differences keep doubling, the series follows a doubling-gap rule.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q32) Which is different in the following: Speech, Lecture, Oration, Sermon, Gossip?
f: Speech, lecture, oration and sermon are formal talks given to an audience, while gossip is casual talk about other people.
r: Tip: formal versus informal is a common basis for odd-one-out questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q33) If A is to E then C is to?
f: A to E is a jump of 4 letters (A=1, E=5), so C (3) plus 4 gives G (7).
r: Tip: convert letters to positions to find a fixed jump.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q34) Which one is different in the following: Petrol, Oil, Water, Spirit?
f: Petrol, oil and spirit are flammable liquids, while water does not burn.
r: Tip: flammability is a quick test for fuels versus other liquids.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q35) Write the number that comes next: 5, 3, 6, 4, 7, ?
r: Tip: when the series zigzags, look for two alternating operations.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q36) Nib is to Pen as Blade is to?
f: A nib is the writing part of a pen, and a blade is the cutting part of a knife.
r: Tip: this is a part-to-whole analogy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q37) Which number comes next: 3, 8, 14, 21, ?
f: The differences are 5, 6, 7, so the next difference is 8: 21 + 8 = 29.
r: Tip: when differences increase by 1, the series is built from consecutive added numbers.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q38) Which letters will come next: BY, CX, DW, EV, ?
f: The first letters go forward B, C, D, E, F and the second letters go backward Y, X, W, V, U, so the next pair is FU.
r: Tip: one letter moving forward while the other moves backward is a classic two-track pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q39) A cake is cut so that one piece, which is half of the cake, is twice as large as one of the other pieces. How many pieces are there?
f: One piece is 1/2 of the cake, and each other piece is half of that, 1/4. The remaining 1/2 makes two pieces of 1/4, so there are 3 pieces in all.
r: Tip: draw the fractions out; the pieces must add up to one whole.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q40) Which is different in the following: Violin, Piano, String, Cutter, Banjo?
f: Violin, piano, string and banjo are all connected with music, while a cutter is a cutting tool.
r: Tip: the key word here is the category, musical instrument versus tool.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q41) Which number comes next in the following: 5, 9, 8, 12, 11, ?
f: The pattern is +4, -1, +4, -1, so after 11 comes 11 + 4 = 15.
r: Tip: write the differences between neighbours to find repeating operations.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q42) December is to October as June is to?
f: December is two months after October in reverse, so go two months back: June gives April.
r: Tip: count the months in the first pair and apply the same step.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q43) Which number will come next: 20, 15, 18, 13, 16, ?
f: The pattern is -5, +3, -5, +3, so 16 - 5 = 11.
r: Tip: alternate -5 and +3 gives two interleaved series: 20, 18, 16, 14 and 15, 13, 11.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q45) Which number comes next in the following: 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 22, ?
f: The pattern is multiply by 2, then add 1: 2x2=4, 4+1=5, 5x2=10, 10+1=11, 11x2=22, 22+1=23.
r: Tip: if the numbers jump up and then up slightly, test alternating multiply and add.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q46) Laugh is to Cry, so Weep is to?
f: Cry is the opposite of laugh, and the opposite of weep is smile.
r: Tip: antonym analogies pair opposite feelings or actions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q47) Add all even numbers and divide it by its middle number: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
f: The even numbers are 4, 6 and 8, which add up to 18. The middle number is 6, so 18 / 6 = 3.
r: Tip: with an odd count of numbers, the middle one is the one with equal numbers on both sides.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q48) Which number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
f: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42.
r: Tip: these are products of consecutive numbers: 1x2, 2x3, 3x4, 4x5, 5x6, 6x7 = 42.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q49) Tobacco is to Pipe as Coal is to:
f: Tobacco is burned in a pipe, and coal is burned in an oven.
r: Tip: the relation is a material and the container or device where it is burned.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q50) Which number comes next in the following: 3/4, 6/8, 12/16, 24/32, ?
f: Each fraction doubles both numerator and denominator: 24 x 2 = 48 and 32 x 2 = 64.
r: Tip: all these fractions equal 3/4, only the numerator and denominator are scaled.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q51) If 2200 hours is 10 o'clock in the evening then write the answer as 4, and if not then write 5.
f: 2200 hours in the 24-hour clock is 22 - 12 = 10 in the evening, so the statement is true and the answer is 4.
r: Tip: for 24-hour times after 1300, subtract 12 to get the pm hour.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q52) The next number in the series is: 120, 108, 97, 87, 78, ?
f: The differences are -12, -11, -10, -9, so the next is -8: 78 - 8 = 70.
r: Tip: when differences shrink by 1 each step, continue the pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q53) Finger is to Hand as Toe is to?
f: A finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot.
r: Tip: part-to-whole analogies are solved by naming the whole that holds the part.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q55) What will be the next letter: A, E, I, M, ?
f: Each letter is 4 places after the previous one: A(1), E(5), I(9), M(13), then Q(17).
r: Tip: convert letters to numbers to see equal jumps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q56) If L comes before P then write 5, otherwise write 4.
f: In the alphabet L is the 12th letter and P is the 16th, so L comes before P and the answer is 5.
r: Tip: alphabet position questions are easiest if you remember A=1 up to Z=26.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q54) Which is different in the following: Ounce, Pound, Ton, Maund?
f: Ounce, pound and ton belong to the same Western (imperial) system, while the maund is a traditional South Asian unit.
r: Tip: a maund is about 40 kg in Pakistan today (37.3 kg in the older system).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q57) List is to Last as Fist is to?
f: List becomes Last by changing the vowel I to A, so Fist becomes Fast.
r: Tip: when the words look alike, compare letter by letter to find which letter changes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q58) What letter comes next in the following series: A, C, F, J, ?
f: The letters are at positions 1, 3, 6, 10, whose gaps are 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5: 10 + 5 = 15, which is O.
r: Tip: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 are triangular numbers.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q59) Triangle is to Prism as Circle is to?
f: A prism is the three-dimensional solid built from a triangle, and a sphere is the solid form of a circle.
r: Tip: 2D-to-3D analogies pair a flat shape with its solid.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q60) Which word does not belong to this list: Less, Depart, Abate, Decrease?
f: Less, abate and decrease all mean to reduce, while depart means to leave.
r: Tip: look for the word whose meaning is not shared by the others.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q61) Tomorrow is to Yesterday as Thursday is to?
f: Yesterday is two days before tomorrow, so the matching day is two days before Thursday, which is Tuesday.
r: Tip: count the day gap in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q62) If 6 and 5 make 10 then write A, otherwise write B.
f: 6 + 5 = 11, not 10, so the condition fails and the answer is B.
r: Tip: evaluate the arithmetic, then pick the letter that matches the condition.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q63) If W precedes X then write the answer as 5, otherwise 6.
f: In the alphabet W comes right before X, so W precedes X and the answer is 5.
r: Tip: the alphabet order is ...U, V, W, X, Y, Z.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q64) Which number comes next: 6, 12, 9, 16, 12, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 6, 9, 12 (adding 3) and 12, 16, 20 (adding 4). The next term is 20.
r: Tip: when numbers go up and down, split them into odd-position and even-position series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q65) A watch reads half past nine. The minute hand points toward North. In which direction does the hour hand point?
f: At half past nine the minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand lies between 9 and 10. If the minute hand (6) points North, the clock is turned half a turn, so the 9-10 position (about 3) points East.
r: Tip: turn the whole dial so that the minute hand matches the given direction, then read the hour hand.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q66) What will be the next number in the series: 5, 8, 9, 16, 13, ?
f: Odd-position terms go 5, 9, 13 (adding 4) and even-position terms go 8, 16, 24 (adding 8). The next term is 24.
r: Tip: when a series mixes slow and fast growth, it is probably two interleaved series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q67) Bright is to Dim as Clear is to?
f: Dim is the opposite of bright, and vague is the opposite of clear.
r: Tip: antonym analogies: find the opposite of the third word in the answer options.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q68) P is to L as N is to?
f: P is the 16th letter and L is the 12th, which is 4 places back. N is the 14th, and 4 places back is J (10).
r: Tip: letter analogies depend on the fixed jump between the first pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q69) What will be the next number: 11, 21, 40, 77, 150, ?
f: The differences are 10, 19, 37, 73, and each difference is double the previous minus 1. The next difference is 145, so 150 + 145 = 295.
r: Tip: when each term is roughly double the previous, check for double plus or minus a small number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q71) Write the fifth last letter of the alphabet.
f: Counting from the end: Z (1st last), Y, X, W, V (5th last), so the answer is V.
r: Tip: the last letter is 1st last, so the fifth last is the 22nd letter (26 - 5 + 1).

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q72) Write the 4th letter before W, as counted from the end of the alphabet.
f: Going back from W: V, U, T, S, so the 4th letter before W is S.
r: Tip: the letter 4 places before W (23rd) is the 19th letter, S.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q75) If three oranges cost Rs. 9, how much will it cost to buy four and a half dozen?
f: Four and a half dozen is 54 oranges. One orange costs 9 / 3 = Rs. 3, so 54 x 3 = Rs. 162.
r: Tip: find the unit price first, then multiply by the quantity; one dozen is 12 items.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q74) Write the next letter in the series: A, C, D, H, K, ?
f: The letter positions are 1, 3, 4, 8, 11, with gaps +2, +1, +4, +3, so the gaps are +2, +1, +4, +3, +6, and the next letter is 11 + 6 = 17, which is Q.
r: Tip: when the gaps themselves form a pattern (here pairs rising by 2), write them out.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q77) Write the next number: 10, 30, 50, 80, ?
f: The differences are 20, 20, 30, 30, so the next difference is 30 (then 40, 40): 80 + 30 = 110.
r: Tip: repeated differences like 20, 20, 30, 30 are a common pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q78) NECESSARY CUSTOM TO TRADE ROAD DEVELOPMENT. If one word is omitted from the above, the others could be arranged as one sentence. Write the second letter of the word to be omitted.
f: Without the word CUSTOM the rest forms the sentence 'Road development necessary to trade'. CUSTOM has U as its second letter.
r: Tip: try dropping each word in turn and see which remaining set makes a sensible sentence.

q: (Forces Academy Test 1 · Q80) How much distance will you cover in 3 and a half minutes if you are moving at the speed of 120 km/h?
f: 120 km/h is 2 km per minute, so in 3.5 minutes you cover 2 x 3.5 = 7 km.
r: Tip: dividing km/h by 60 gives km per minute.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q1) SICK is to SACK as LICK is to:
f: SICK changes its vowel I to A to make SACK, so LICK becomes LACK.
r: Tip: in word analogies compare the letters one by one to find which letter changes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q2) What letter comes next in the following series: B, D, G, K, P, ?
f: The gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: P (16) + 6 = 22, which is V.
r: Tip: letter gaps that grow by 1 each step are very common.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q3) What number comes next in the following series: 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
f: The differences are -10, -8, -6, -4, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.
r: Tip: when the differences fall by 2 each time, the next one is also 2 less.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q4) If 4 is more than 9 write 2 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
f: 4 is not more than 9, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.
r: Tip: check the condition first, then write the answer for the matching branch.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q5) Students go to school because:
o: They want to be away from home.
They want to tease the teacher.
f: The main purpose of school is to gain knowledge; the other choices are minor or silly reasons.
r: Tip: in reasoning questions pick the most general and sensible cause.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q6) What number comes next in the following series: 18, 13, 9, 6, ?
f: The differences are -5, -4, -3, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.
r: Tip: shrinking differences mean the series is slowing down.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q7) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Car, train, aircraft and ship are machines with engines, while a cart is pulled by an animal or by hand.
r: Tip: the Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q8) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: February, December, June and September are months, while Monday is a day of the week.
r: Tip: February is the shortest month, with 28 days (29 in a leap year).

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q9) What number comes next in the following series: 49, 36, 25, 16, ?
f: These are squares in reverse: 7 squared, 6 squared, 5 squared, 4 squared, so next is 3 squared = 9.
r: Tip: learn the squares up to 15 so square series are quick to spot.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q10) NORTH is to SOUTH as EAST is to:
f: South is the direct opposite of north, and west is the direct opposite of east.
r: Tip: the four opposite pairs of compass directions are north and south, east and west.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Brother, uncle, son and grandfather are male relatives, while a sister is female.
r: Tip: check gender first when the words are family relations.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q12) Girls wear glasses because:
f: The usual real reason for wearing glasses is weak eyesight.
r: Tip: in cause questions choose the practical and most common reason.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q13) In a group of 50 players, 30% play hockey and 80% play cricket. Are there any who play both hockey and cricket?
o: One cannot say without further detail
f: 30% of 50 is 15 and 80% of 50 is 40. Since 15 + 40 = 55 is more than 50, at least 5 players must play both.
r: Tip: if the two groups add up to more than the total, they must overlap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q14) What number comes next in the following series: 40, 30, 35, 25, 30, 20, ?
r: Tip: two alternating steps make a zigzag series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q15) Engine is to Car as Cell is to:
f: An engine powers a car, and a cell (battery) powers a torch.
r: Tip: this analogy links a power source to the device it runs.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q16) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Tennis, hockey, cricket and football are outdoor games, while billiard is an indoor game.
r: Tip: split games into indoor and outdoor groups.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q17) If 7 and 6 make 19, write 5 as your answer, otherwise write 3.
f: 7 + 6 = 13, which is not 19, so the condition fails and the answer is 3.
r: Tip: do the sum first before choosing the branch.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Huge, great, fat and big all describe large size, while small is the opposite.
r: Tip: look for the antonym among a group of synonyms.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q19) What number comes next in the following series: 62, 32, 30, 16, 14, 8, 6, ?
f: Terms alternate between halving plus 1 and subtracting 2: 62 to 32, 32 to 30, 30 to 16, 16 to 14, 14 to 8, 8 to 6, then 6 halved plus 1 is 4.
r: Tip: in mixed series test each pair of neighbours for different operations in turn.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q20) If Arza is older than Munir and Munir is younger than Javaid, then Arza is:
f: Munir is below both Arza and Javaid, but nothing links Arza and Javaid directly, so their order cannot be known.
r: Tip: two people both older than a third cannot be compared with each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q21) If Asif is 12 years old and all boys over 10 are hockey players, then:
o: It is not sure that Asif is hockey player.
Asif is likely to become hockey player.
f: Asif is 12, which is over 10, and the rule says all boys over 10 are hockey players, so he is one.
r: Tip: when a rule says all, apply it directly to anything that meets the condition.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q22) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Mango, lemon and orange are fruits, while tomato is generally treated as a vegetable in cooking.
r: Tip: botanically a tomato is a fruit, but in everyday classification it is a vegetable.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q23) Women go to market because:
o: They have plenty of spare time.
They don't want to stay at home.
f: The practical purpose of going to a market is to buy things.
r: Tip: choose the reason that is the real purpose, not a general opinion.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q24) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Two, four, twenty and fifty are even numbers, while five is odd.
r: Tip: parity (odd or even) is a quick odd-one-out check for numbers.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q25) What number comes next in the following series: 27, 20, 14, 9, 5, ?
f: The differences are -7, -6, -5, -4, so the next is -3: 5 - 3 = 2.
r: Tip: differences falling by 1 give a smooth decreasing series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q26) What letter comes next in the following series: J, H, F, D, ?
f: Each letter is 2 places before the previous one: J, H, F, D, then B.
r: Tip: going backward in the alphabet by a fixed step is as common as going forward.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q27) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Yard, foot, mile and kilometer are units of measuring length, while length itself is the quantity being measured.
r: Tip: one mile is about 1.609 kilometres.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q28) Forests are useful because:
o: They help in building the economy.
f: Forests supply timber and other resources, so their main usefulness is to the economy.
r: Tip: Pakistan observes Tree Plantation Day to promote more forests.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q29) NEAR is to FAR as CLOSE is to:
f: Far is the opposite of near, and open is the opposite of close (shut).
r: Tip: close can mean near or shut; the first pair tells you to use the antonym of the word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q30) What is the area of a square which is 8 feet long?
f: The area of a square is side times side: 8 x 8 = 64 square feet.
r: Tip: perimeter adds the sides, area multiplies them.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q31) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Cup, mug, glass and jug are containers, while a drink is what goes inside them.
r: Tip: separate containers from their contents.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q32) If 5 is subtracted from 30, what would be the square root of the remaining?
f: 30 - 5 = 25 and the square root of 25 is 5.
r: Tip: remember the perfect squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100.

q: (Forces Academy Test 2 · Q33) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Sword, knife, fork and axe are sharp tools or weapons, while a cup is a container with no sharp edge.
r: Tip: look at the main property (sharp or pointed) shared by most of the items.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q1) Which of the following is different from the rest?
f: Unearth, discover, find and locate all mean to come across something that already exists. Invention means to create something new.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q2) What number comes next in the following series? 2413, 2420, 2434, 2462, 2518, ?
f: The differences are 7, 14, 28, 56, doubling each time, so the next difference is 112: 2518 + 112 = 2630.
r: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q3) Which one is different from the rest? Cow, Hen, Duck, Bull, Mare
f: Cow, hen and mare are female animals, while bull is the only male.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q4) If Shoe is to Foot then Helmet is to ____.
f: A shoe is worn on the foot and a helmet is worn on the head.
r: Tip: in analogies, first state the relationship (here, worn on) and then apply it to the second pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q5) What number comes next in the following series? 3, 10, 4, 17, 5, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 3, 4, 5 (plus 1) and 10, 17, 24 (plus 7). The next term belongs to the second series: 24.
r: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences. The answer key lists 26 here, but 24 is what the pattern gives.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q6) Which one is different from the rest? QS, EH, IL, MP, AD
f: In EH, IL, MP and AD the second letter is 3 places after the first. In QS the gap is only 2.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q7) If the second of the following numbers is added to the shortest number and divided by the third number, what will the answer be? 2, 14, 4
f: Second number 14 plus shortest number 2 is 16. Dividing by the third number 4 gives 4.
r: Tip: identify the numbers by position first (first, second, third), then apply the operations in order.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q8) What is the next number in the following series? 4, 8, 24, 96, ?
f: Each term is multiplied by 2, 3, 4 and then 5: 96 x 5 = 480.
r: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q9) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Town, city, village and township are all human settlements on earth. Heaven is not.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q10) March is to 31/3 and June is to ____.
f: March has 31 days and is the 3rd month. June has 30 days and is the 6th month, so 30/6.
r: Tip: months with 30 days are April, June, September and November.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q11) Which one of the following is different from the rest? Infant, Adult, Child, Newborn, Baby
f: Infant, child, newborn and baby all describe young ones. Adult is a fully grown person.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q12) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Separation, split, divide and gap all involve parting. Union means joining together.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q13) What number comes next in the following series? 63, 3, 44, 0, 91, ?
f: Each pair is the first digit minus the second digit: 6 - 3 = 3, 4 - 4 = 0, so for 91: 9 - 1 = 8.
r: Tip: when a series mixes two-digit and one-digit numbers, try operations on the digits.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q14) What letter comes next in the following series? E, J, N, Q, ?
f: The steps are +5, +4, +3, so the next step is +2: Q + 2 = S.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q15) Which one is different from the rest?
f: Kabul, Delhi and Dhaka are national capitals. Karachi is not the capital of Pakistan.
r: Fact: Islamabad has been the capital of Pakistan since 1960s, before that Karachi was the capital.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q16) My mother is your brother's sister. What am I to you?
f: Your brother's sister is your sister, so my mother is your sister and I am your nephew.
r: Tip: in relation puzzles, translate each phrase into a simple relation one step at a time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q17) Kamal is older than Jamal, Jamal is older than Hussain, Hussain is older than Waqar. Who is the oldest?
f: The order is Kamal, Jamal, Hussain, Waqar from oldest to youngest.
r: Tip: write the names in a line from oldest to youngest to check ranking questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q18) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: High, great, fat and big all suggest large size. Small is the opposite.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q19) What will come next in the following series? 2, 4, 8, 14, ?
f: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8: 14 + 8 = 22.
r: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q20) What will come next in the following series? 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
f: The differences are 10, 8, 6, 4, so the next difference is 2: 6 - 2 = 4.
r: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q22) Which one is different from the rest?
f: Relationship, kinship and friendship are all human bonds. Spaceship is a vehicle.
r: Tip: words with the same ending may still belong to different categories, so check the meaning.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q23) Akmal and Jamal are brothers, Anjum and Ajmal are their sons. What is the relation between Anjum and Ajmal?
f: Anjum and Ajmal are sons of two brothers, so they are cousins.
r: Fact: children of two brothers are called paternal cousins.

q: (Forces Academy Test 3 · Q24) Which one is different from the rest? Oxygen, Sulphur, Silver, Zinc, Protenium

f: The sky is above the earth; a ceiling is above the floor, so the pairing matches.
r: Tip: in analogies, state the relationship in a sentence first (above / below, part / whole) and then apply it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series: D, G, J, M, P, ?
f: Each letter moves forward by 3: D, G, J, M, P, then P + 3 = S.
r: Tip: a constant gap between letters means a simple arithmetic pattern; count the skipped letters carefully.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q9) Which number comes next: 43, 33, 38, 30, 34, ?
f: The changes alternate and shrink: -10, +5, -8, +4, then -6. So 34 - 6 = 28.
r: Tip: if the numbers zigzag, look at the differences between neighbours; they may form two separate patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q10) A trader invested Rs.2490 in a business but he had a loss of 100/3 percent. What was he left with after the loss?
f: 100/3 percent is one third. A third of 2490 is 830, so he was left with 2490 - 830 = 1660.
r: Tip: 33 and one third percent is the same as the fraction one third, which makes mental maths easy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q11) Iqbal, Asif and Mahmood are standing in a row. Iqbal is standing in front of Mahmood. Asif is standing behind Iqbal. Mahmood is standing in front of Asif. Who is standing in the middle?
f: The order from the front is Iqbal, then Mahmood, then Asif, so Mahmood is in the middle.
r: Tip: draw a quick line of positions and place each person as the clues are read.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q12) Teachers are respected because:
o: They look after their families well
f: Teachers are respected mainly for their service of educating children and shaping society.
r: Tip: in reasoning questions choose the cause most directly linked to the role itself.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q13) Which letter comes next in the following series: D, H, M, P, U, ?
f: Split the series into two: D, M, U (gaps +9, +8) and H, P, then W (gaps +8, +7). The next letter is W.
r: Tip: in alternating letter series, separate the odd and even positions into two sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q14) A meal always involves:
f: A meal by definition consists of food; the other items may or may not be present.
r: Tip: choose the item that is essential, not just commonly present.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q15) Three shareholders earned a profit of Rs.900 in their business. One got 20% of the profit, the other got 45% of the profit. How many rupees were the share of the third?
f: The third gets 100 - 20 - 45 = 35 percent, and 35 percent of 900 is 315.
r: Tip: subtract the given percentages from 100 first, then take the remaining percent of the total.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q16) OCTOBER is to NOVEMBER as SUNDAY is to:
f: November is the month that follows October, and Monday is the day that follows Sunday.
r: Tip: time-sequence analogies usually ask for the next item in the cycle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q17) SICK means the same as:
f: Sick and ill are synonyms.
r: Tip: a symptom such as fever or cough is not a synonym; look for a word that can replace the original in any sentence.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q18) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, E, I, M, Q, ?
f: Each letter is 4 places after the previous one: Q + 4 = U.
r: Tip: A, E, I, M, Q, U steps by four; the vowels A, E, I appear because 4 happens to land on them early.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q19) Travelling at a speed of 120 km/hour, how much time would be taken to cover a road that is 24 km long?
f: Time = distance / speed = 24 / 120 = 0.2 hour, which is 0.2 x 60 = 12 minutes.
r: Tip: remember time = distance divided by speed, and convert hours to minutes by multiplying by 60.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q20) In a class of 100 students, 40% failed in English and 70% in Urdu. Were there any who failed both in English and Urdu?
f: 40 + 70 = 110, which is more than 100 students, so at least 10 students must have failed both subjects.
r: Tip: if the percentages of two groups add up to more than 100, the groups must overlap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q21) Which letter comes next in the following series: R, O, L, I, F, ?
f: Each letter moves back by 3: R, O, L, I, F, then F - 3 = C.
r: Tip: a series can run backwards through the alphabet; watch for a constant negative gap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q22) Kalam lifted 20kg more than Kalim. Shakir lifted more than Kalim. Sabir lifted less than Shakir. Is it possible that Shakir and Sabir lifted the same amount of load?
f: Sabir lifted less than Shakir, so they cannot have lifted the same amount.
r: Tip: a statement using less than or more than rules out equality directly.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q23) If Aslam is taller than Hafeez and Hafeez is shorter than Mani, then Aslam is the tallest:
f: We know Aslam is above Hafeez and Mani is above Hafeez, but Aslam and Mani are not compared, so we cannot tell who is tallest.
r: Tip: a conclusion is certain only if every comparison needed is stated in the premises.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q24) Which number comes next: 2500, 500, 100, 20, ?
f: Each number is divided by 5: 2500, 500, 100, 20, then 20 / 5 = 4.
r: Tip: when numbers fall fast, test division before subtraction.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q25) What is different from the rest?
f: Swim, walk, run and gymnastic are physical exercises or movements, while game is a general term for a competitive activity.
r: Tip: look for the item that is a broader category than the rest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q26) NEAR means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of near is far.
r: Tip: avoid synonyms such as close, which mean the same thing, when an opposite is asked.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q27) Which number comes next: 92, 46, 48, 24, 26, ?
f: The pattern alternates: divide by 2, then add 2. 92 / 2 = 46, +2 = 48, /2 = 24, +2 = 26, /2 = 13.
r: Tip: alternating operations (divide, then add) are common; test each step separately.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q28) All birds have wings. Some insects have wings. X has wings, therefore it is a bird?
f: Having wings is shared by birds and some insects, so X could be either; we cannot conclude it is a bird.
r: Tip: from all A are B you cannot reverse to all B are A.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q29) What will be the area of a rectangle that is 16 feet long and 12 feet wide?
f: Area = length x width = 16 x 12 = 192 square feet.
r: Tip: area is length times width, while 2 x (length + width) is the perimeter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 7 · Q30) ARMY is to SOLDIER as NAVY is to:
f: A soldier serves in the army and a sailor serves in the navy.
r: Tip: in this analogy the second word is the ordinary member of the first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q1) Which letter comes next in the following series: S, Q, N, L, I, ?
f: Gaps alternate -2, -3: S to Q is 2, Q to N is 3, N to L is 2, L to I is 3, then -2 gives G.
r: Tip: alternating gaps in letter series repeat in pairs; list the gaps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q2) Which number comes next: 28, 19, 12, 7, ?
f: Differences are -9, -7, -5, so the next is -3: 7 - 3 = 4.
r: Tip: the differences decrease by 2 each time, a typical second-order series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q3) Three oranges cost Rs.6. How much will 1 and a half dozen cost?
f: One orange costs Rs.2. One and a half dozen is 18 oranges, so 18 x 2 = Rs.36.
r: Tip: find the unit price first, and remember a dozen is 12.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q4) AGREED is to 157224 as GEARED is to:
r: Tip: repeated letters, like the two E's, must give the same digit.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q5) NARROW is to WIDE as THIN is to:
f: Narrow and wide are opposites, and the opposite of thin is fat.
r: Tip: first decide whether the relation is synonym or antonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q6) WAR means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of war is peace.
r: Tip: the opposite of war-like states such as conflict is peace, not merely happiness.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q7) Which of the following is different from the rest?
f: Yacht, steamer and ship travel on water, while an aircraft travels in the air.
r: Tip: group items by the medium they operate in (land, water, air).

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series: X, T, P, L, H, ?
f: Each letter moves back by 4: X, T, P, L, H, then H - 4 = D.
r: Tip: count backwards carefully when letters step down.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q9) Which number comes next: 229, 222, 37, 32, 8, ?
f: The numbers fall in pairs by 7, 5 and 3: 229 - 7 = 222, 37 - 5 = 32, so 8 - 3 = 5.
r: Tip: the amount subtracted shrinks by 2 each pair (7, 5, 3).

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q10) What is the area of a rectangle that is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide?
f: Area = 6 x 4 = 24 square feet.
r: Tip: perimeter would be 2 x (6 + 4) = 20, a common wrong answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q11) If Ahmed is older than Kamal and Kamal is younger than Imran, then Ahmed is:
f: Both Ahmed and Imran are older than Kamal, but Ahmed and Imran are not compared directly.
r: Tip: two people both above a third cannot be ranked against each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q12) Sun gives light because:
f: The sun is a star where nuclear reactions heat gases so strongly that they glow and give off light.
r: Tip: the sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q13) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, Z, B, Y, C, ?
f: Two series run together: A, B, C going forward and Z, Y, X going backward. After C comes X.
r: Tip: when letters jump from the start to the end of the alphabet, think of two interleaved series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q14) A mother is always (?) than her daughter:
f: A mother is always older than her daughter; the other qualities may differ.
r: Tip: choose the quality guaranteed by the relationship itself.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q15) Which one of the following is the smallest?
f: Comparing the values: 0.073 is less than 0.1, 0.73, 7.3 and 73, so it is smallest.
r: Tip: compare decimals place by place; more leading zeros means a smaller number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q16) Tail is to ANIMAL as Beak is to:
f: A tail is a body part of an animal and a beak is a body part of a bird.
r: Tip: part-to-whole analogies pair a body part with the creature that has it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q17) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Crow, parrot, owl and sparrow are birds, while a lion is a mammal.
r: Tip: check class (bird, mammal, fish) when animals are listed.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q18) Which letter comes next in the following series: H, J, K, M, N, ?
f: The gaps alternate +2, +1: H to J is 2, J to K is 1, K to M is 2, M to N is 1, so N + 2 = P.
r: Tip: write down each gap and look for the repeating pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q19) A man had a wife, two sons and their wives and two grandsons. How many were they in all?
f: Man 1 + wife 1 + two sons 2 + their wives 2 + two grandsons 2 = 8.
r: Tip: do not forget to count the man himself in family-count questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q20) HIGH is to LOW as COWARD is to:
f: High and low are opposites; the opposite of coward is brave.
r: Tip: the opposite of coward is brave, whereas strong is a different quality.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q21) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, G, H, N, O, ?
f: The gaps alternate +6, +1: A to G is 6, G to H is 1, H to N is 6, N to O is 1, so O + 6 = U.
r: Tip: alternating large and small gaps usually mean two linked patterns.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q22) A man bought some chairs for Rs.3500 and sold them for Rs.5500. He earned a profit of Rs.100 per chair. How many chairs did he buy?
f: Total profit = 5500 - 3500 = 2000. At Rs.100 per chair, the number of chairs = 2000 / 100 = 20.
r: Tip: total profit divided by profit per item gives the number of items.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q23) PERMANENT is the opposite of:
f: Permanent means lasting for ever; its opposite is temporary.
r: Tip: changing is similar in idea but temporary is the true antonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q24) Which number comes next: 130, 81, 45, 20, ?
f: Differences are 49, 36, 25, which are 7 squared, 6 squared and 5 squared. Next is 4 squared = 16: 20 - 16 = 4.
r: Tip: differences that look like perfect squares (49, 36, 25, 16) are a clue.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q25) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Pear, orange, banana and apple are fruits, while potato is a vegetable.
r: Tip: classify by food group when a list mixes fruits and vegetables.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q26) NEVER means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of never is always.
r: Tip: seldom is only close to never, but always is the exact opposite.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q27) Which number comes next: 19, 10, 15, 7, 11, 4, ?
f: Take alternate terms: 19, 15, 11 fall by 4, so the next is 7 (the other series 10, 7, 4 falls by 3).
r: Tip: for zigzag series, separate odd and even positions and find the next term of the right series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q28) SKY is HIGH as EARTH is:
f: The sky is high and the earth is low by comparison.
r: Tip: in this analogy the second word describes the position of the first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q29) A man bought 2 dozen eggs at the rate of Rs.10 per dozen and 36 eggs at the rate of Rs.12 per dozen. How many rupees did he pay in all?
f: Two dozen at Rs.10 cost Rs.20. 36 eggs are 3 dozen at Rs.12, costing Rs.36. Total = 20 + 36 = Rs.56.
r: Tip: convert everything to dozens before multiplying by the rate.

q: (Forces Academy Test 8 · Q30) A person who flies an AIRCRAFT is called:
f: A person who flies an aircraft is a pilot.
r: Tip: captain is a rank, while pilot is the name of the job.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q1) Which letter comes next in the following series: B, E, G, J, L, ?
f: The gaps alternate +3, +2: B to E is 3, E to G is 2, G to J is 3, J to L is 2, so L + 3 = O.
r: Tip: alternating gaps of 3 and 2 repeat; add the next gap in turn.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q2) Which number comes next: 34, 24, 16, 10, 6, ?
f: Differences are -10, -8, -6, -4, so the next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4.
r: Tip: differences that shrink by 2 each step form a second-order series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q3) If you can buy 4 pencils for Rs.6, how many can you buy for Rs.18?
f: Rs.18 is three times Rs.6, so you get 3 x 4 = 12 pencils.
r: Tip: use ratios, because tripling the money triples the quantity.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q4) DERANGE is to 4371563 as GRAND is to:
r: Tip: build the letter-digit table first, then translate the new word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q5) DANGEROUS means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of dangerous is safe.
r: Tip: threatening is a synonym, not an antonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q6) DARK is to NIGHT as DAY is to:
f: Darkness is associated with night, and light is associated with day.
r: Tip: this is a characteristic-of analogy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q7) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: House, hut and villa are specific types of homes to live in, while building is a general term for any structure.
r: Tip: spot the word that is a general category rather than a specific kind.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series: C, F, H, K, M, ?
f: The gaps alternate +3, +2: C to F is 3, F to H is 2, H to K is 3, K to M is 2, so M + 3 = P.
r: Tip: write each letter as a number and list the gaps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q9) Which number comes next: 30, 27, 24, 21, ?
f: Each number falls by 3, so 21 - 3 = 18.
r: Tip: a constant difference means an arithmetic series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q10) If pencils sell at Rs.10 per dozen and the price of one sharpener is Rs.2, what will be the price of 24 pencils and one dozen sharpeners?
f: 24 pencils are 2 dozen = Rs.20. One dozen sharpeners = 12 x 2 = Rs.24. Total = Rs.44.
r: Tip: convert to the unit used in the price (dozens) before multiplying.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q11) If March comes before April and April comes after July, write 6 as your answer, otherwise write the last letter of the month that comes at the end of the year.
f: April does not come after July, so the condition is false. The month at the end of the year is December, whose last letter is R.
r: Tip: check the condition first; both parts must be true for the first answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q12) If Anwar is a student and all students are lazy then he:
f: All students are lazy and Anwar is a student, so Anwar is lazy.
r: Tip: a universal statement (all) applies to every member of the group.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q13) Which letter comes next: Z, W, T, Q, N, ?
f: Each letter moves back by 3: Z, W, T, Q, N, then N - 3 = K.
r: Tip: count back three places in the alphabet each time. (This question is handwritten on the paper as number 13.)

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q14) How many letters of the word CENTRAL are also found in the word DISCOVER?
f: DISCOVER contains C, E and R from CENTRAL; N, T, A and L are missing. So the answer is 3.
r: Tip: check each letter of the first word against the second, one by one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q15) Twelve years ago Akhtar was half of his present age. What will be his age after 12 years?
f: If x is his age, x - 12 = x / 2, so x = 24. After 12 years he will be 24 + 12 = 36.
r: Tip: set up a simple equation instead of guessing ages.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q16) RED is to BLOOD as WHITE is to:
f: Blood is red and milk is white, so the pairing is an object and its colour.
r: Tip: this is a colour-association analogy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q17) MAN is to MASCULINE as WOMAN is to:
f: Masculine is the adjective for a man and feminine is the adjective for a woman.
r: Tip: match the type of word, here an adjective.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q18) Which letter comes next in the following series: D, F, I, M, R, ?
f: The gaps increase by 1 each time: +2, +3, +4, +5, and the next is +6: R + 6 = X.
r: Tip: gaps that grow by one each step are a common letter pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q19) A family consists of a man, his two wives, three daughters, four sons and their wives. How many members are there in the whole family?
f: Man 1 + two wives 2 + three daughters 3 + four sons 4 + sons' wives 4 = 14.
r: Tip: list each group and add; include the man himself.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q20) FAST means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of fast is slow.
r: Tip: quick and speed are synonyms, so they cannot be the answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q21) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, B, I, J, Q, ?
f: The gaps alternate +1, +7: A to B is 1, B to I is 7, I to J is 1, J to Q is 7, so Q + 1 = R.
r: Tip: pairs of consecutive letters separated by a big gap are a classic pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q22) If three is subtracted from 12, then what will be one third of the remaining?
f: 12 - 3 = 9, and one third of 9 is 3.
r: Tip: follow the order of operations given in the sentence.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q23) BOTTLE is to CORK as BOX is to:
f: A cork closes a bottle, and a lid closes a box.
r: Tip: this is an object and its closing part.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q24) Which number comes next: 11, 6, 7, 3, 5, ?
f: The changes follow a pattern: -5, +1, -4, +2, -3. So 5 - 3 = 2.
r: Tip: when the differences alternate in sign, look at the sequence of subtracted and added amounts separately.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q25) Which group of letters is different from the others?
f: ACBC, XZYZ and JLK(L) follow the same pattern of one letter, one ahead, one in between, repeating the middle one; MCPO does not follow it.
r: Tip: compare the position patterns inside each group, not the letters themselves.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q26) FOOT is to LEG as HAND is to:
f: The foot is attached to the leg, and the hand is attached to the arm.
r: Tip: this is a body-part connection analogy.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q27) Which number comes next: 18, 13, 9, 6, 4, ?
f: The differences are -5, -4, -3, -2, so the next is -1: 4 - 1 = 3.
r: Tip: the differences decrease by one each time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q28) INFANCY is to CHILDHOOD as ADOLESCENCE is to:
f: Stages of life follow in order: infancy, childhood, adolescence, then youth.
r: Tip: the sequence of human life stages is infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q29) What number when multiplied by 3 gives one less than 10?
f: One less than 10 is 9, and 9 / 3 = 3.
r: Tip: work backwards by dividing the result by the multiplier.

q: (Forces Academy Test 9 · Q30) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Sing, call and speak are all ways of making sounds with the voice, while hear is a way of receiving sounds.
r: Tip: separate actions of producing from actions of receiving.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q1) Which letter comes next in the following series: D, G, K, N, R, ?
f: The gaps alternate +3, +4: D to G is 3, G to K is 4, K to N is 3, N to R is 4, so R + 3 = U.
r: Tip: alternating gaps of 3 and 4 repeat in turn.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q2) Which number comes next: 81, 64, 49, 36, ?
f: These are perfect squares in descending order: 9 squared, 8 squared, 7 squared, 6 squared, and next is 5 squared = 25.
r: Tip: learn the squares up to 20 to spot these series quickly.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q3) If apples are sold for Rs.15 per kg, how many grams can you buy for Rs.6?
f: Rs.6 / Rs.15 = 0.4 kg, which is 400 grams.
r: Tip: 1 kg equals 1000 grams, so convert at the end.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q4) TRIP is to DAY as CALENDAR is to:
f: A trip is measured in days, and a calendar is measured in a year.
r: Tip: this is a unit-of-measure analogy; match the unit that the object covers.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q5) CLOCK is to DAY as CALENDAR is to:
f: A clock tracks the hours of a day, and a calendar tracks the days of a year.
r: Tip: a clock tracks the day, a calendar tracks the year.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q6) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Smuggle, cheat, steal and bribe are illegal or dishonest acts, while selling is a normal lawful activity.
r: Tip: look for the lawful item among a list of crimes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q7) A person who writes poems is called:
f: A poet writes poems.
r: Tip: Allama Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan, is a famous example.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q8) Which letter comes next in the following series: C, D, G, J, K, ?
f: The gaps are +1, +3, +3, +1, then +3: K + 3 = N.
r: Tip: when no single gap repeats, list all the gaps and look for the cycle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q9) Which number comes next: 14, 10, 7, 5, ?
f: Differences are -4, -3, -2, so the next is -1: 5 - 1 = 4.
r: Tip: differences falling by one each step lead to a simple next difference.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q10) What will be the third angle of a triangle whose two angles are 45 degrees and 60 degrees?
f: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees: 180 - 45 - 60 = 75 degrees.
r: Tip: the angles in any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q11) If day before yesterday was FRIDAY, tomorrow would be:
f: If the day before yesterday was Friday, yesterday was Saturday and today is Sunday, so tomorrow is Monday.
r: Tip: count forward from the known day one step at a time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q12) People buy food because:
f: Food is a basic need of the body, so people buy it because they need to eat it, whether or not they feel hungry at the moment.
r: Tip: when options overlap, the key answer is the most general and necessary reason.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q13) Which letter comes next in the following series: B, E, F, J, K, ?
f: The gaps are +3, +1, +4, +1, +5, so the next gap pattern gives K + 5 = P.
r: Tip: letter gaps that interleave +1 with growing gaps (3, 4, 5) are a common pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q14) Clouds are formed because:
o: Chemical changes take place in the atmosphere
f: Water from the seas, rivers and land evaporates, rises, cools and condenses into tiny droplets that make clouds.
r: Tip: this process is part of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q15) If mangoes sell at Rs.12 per kg, how much can be bought for Rs.768?
r: Tip: quantity equals total money divided by the price per unit.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q16) TRIANGLE is to PRISM as CIRCLE is to:
f: A prism is a triangle extended into three dimensions with the same cross-section, and a cylinder is a circle extended the same way.
r: Tip: the key sheet gives sphere here, but a prism has constant triangular cross-sections just as a cylinder has circular ones.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q17) RECEDE is to PROCEED as STOP is to:
f: Recede and proceed are opposites, and the opposite of stop is go.
r: Tip: recede means to move back, and proceed means to move forward.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q18) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, W, B, V, C, ?
f: Two series run together: A, B, C going forward and W, V, then U going backward.
r: Tip: interleaved series run in turn, one forward and one backward.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q19) If one dozen pencils can be bought for Rs.15, how much will 72 pencils cost?
f: 72 pencils are 6 dozen, so the cost is 6 x 15 = Rs.90.
r: Tip: convert the total number to dozens first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q20) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Ankle, knee, foot and toe are all parts of the leg, while the tongue is in the mouth.
r: Tip: group body parts by the area they belong to.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q21) Which letter comes next in the following series: B, E, H, K, N, ?
f: Each letter moves forward by 3: N + 3 = Q.
r: Tip: a constant gap makes this one of the easiest letter series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q22) Which figure represents the smallest amount?
f: Comparing decimals: 0.09 is less than 0.9, 1.1, 3.1 and 10, so it is the smallest.
r: Tip: a decimal with more leading zeros after the point is smaller.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q23) EXTRAVAGANT means the opposite:
f: Extravagant means spending too much, and its opposite is economical, spending carefully.
r: Tip: the key sheet gives miser, but economical is the matching adjective, and wasteful is a synonym of extravagant.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q24) Which number comes next: 48, 24, 12, 6, ?
f: Each number is half of the previous one, so 6 / 2 = 3.
r: Tip: halving each time makes a geometric series with ratio one half.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q25) A bird does not always have:
f: Every bird has wings, eyes, feet and a bill, but not every bird builds or lives in a nest all the time.
r: Tip: the key sheet gives a bill, but a bill (beak) is a defining feature of all birds, so a nest is the best answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q26) BEGIN is to END as NORTH is to:
f: Begin and end are opposites, and the opposite direction of north is south.
r: Tip: the four cardinal directions form two opposite pairs: north and south, east and west.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q27) Which number comes next: 42, 30, 20, 12, ?
f: Differences are -12, -10, -8, so the next is -6: 12 - 6 = 6.
r: Tip: these numbers are products of consecutive integers (7x6, 6x5, 5x4, 4x3, 3x2).

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q28) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Stem, root, branch and leaf are parts of a plant, while the tree is the whole plant.
r: Tip: look for the whole among a list of parts.

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q29) Which number is missing in the following series: 98, 70, ?, 14
f: The series falls by 28 each time: 98, 70, 42, 14.
r: Tip: find the common difference from the two known neighbours (98 - 70 = 28).

q: (Forces Academy Test 10 · Q30) BAIT is to FISH as GUN is to:
f: Bait is the thing used to catch a fish, and a bullet is the thing fired from a gun to hit a target.
r: Tip: this analogy links a tool to what it is used to capture.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q1) Which letter comes next in the following series: A, B, F, G, K, ?
f: Positions in the alphabet are 1, 2, 6, 7, 11, so the steps alternate +1, +4, +1, +4, +1. Next is 11 + 1 = 12, which is L.
r: Tip: when letter gaps repeat in a cycle, write the letter positions as numbers and look at the differences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q2) Which number comes next: 54321, 4321, 321, 21, ?
f: Each term drops the first digit of the one before: 54321, 4321, 321, 21, then 1.
r: Tip: if each term looks like a shortened copy of the previous one, the rule is removing a digit.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q3) CLOSE is to OPEN as NEAR is to:
f: CLOSE and OPEN are opposites, so the opposite of NEAR is FAR.
r: Tip: first name the relationship (opposite, synonym, part of) in the first pair, then apply it to the second.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q4) MEDICAL is to 5132768 as DECIMAL is to:
f: From MEDICAL = 5132768: M=5, E=1, D=3, I=2, C=7, A=6, L=8. DECIMAL is D3 E1 C7 I2 M5 A6 L8, which gives 3172568.
r: Tip: write the letter-to-digit code under the first word, then read off the second word letter by letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q5) If 12 is divided by 3, what is half of the result?
f: 12 divided by 3 gives 4, and half of 4 is 2.
r: Tip: first do the division, then take half of the answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q6) HERE is to NOW as THERE is to:
f: HERE refers to place and NOW refers to time at the same point. THERE refers to a place, so its matching time word is THEN.
r: Tip: place and time words often pair up: here/now, there/then, where/when.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q7) TRANSPARENT is the opposite of:
f: TRANSPARENT means you can see through it clearly. The opposite, not clear to see through, is HAZY.
r: Tip: eliminate options that are synonyms first, as CLEAR is here.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q8) Which letter comes next: C, E, H, L, Q, ?
f: Positions are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17, so the differences are +2, +3, +4, +5. Next is +6: 17 + 6 = 23, which is W.
r: Tip: if differences grow by one each time, it is a second-order (quadratic) pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q9) Which number comes next: 11, 6, 7, 3, 5, ?
f: Split into two series: 11, 7, 5 (differences -4, -2) and 6, 3, ? (the second series continues with differences -3, -1). So 6, 3, 2.
r: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q10) What number when subtracted from 21 will give 15 as the answer?
r: Tip: the missing number in a subtraction is the larger number minus the answer.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q11) Men wear shoes because they:
f: The real purpose of shoes is to protect the feet from injury, dirt and weather.
r: Tip: for common sense questions, choose the most basic and practical reason.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q12) Birds fly because:
f: Wings are the physical feature that makes flight possible. The other options are possible motives, not the cause.
r: Tip: not all birds fly; penguins and ostriches have wings but cannot fly.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q13) Which letter comes next: U, S, Q, O, M, ?
f: Each letter goes back two places in the alphabet: U, S, Q, O, M, then K.
r: Tip: a constant step backwards in the alphabet means counting down by the same number each time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q14) Water becomes ice because:
o: We want to have cold drinks
f: Water freezes into ice when the temperature falls to 0 degrees Celsius or below.
r: Tip: water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius (32 degrees Fahrenheit) at normal pressure.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q15) If the numbers 16, 2, 27, 9, 7 are arranged from the smallest to the largest, what will be the middle number?
f: Arranged in order: 2, 7, 9, 16, 27. The middle (third) number is 9.
r: Tip: with five numbers the middle one is the third after sorting.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q16) Who was the first king of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan has never had a king. Quaid-e-Azam was the first Governor-General, not a king.
r: Tip: Muhammad Ali Jinnah was Pakistan's first Governor-General, and Liaquat Ali Khan was its first Prime Minister.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q17) Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: OBVIOUS, CLEAR and APPARENT all mean easy to see or understand. DUBIOUS means doubtful.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out words, find the three that are synonyms and pick the remaining one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q18) Which letter comes next: Y, S, N, J, G, ?
f: Positions are 25, 19, 14, 10, 7. The differences are -6, -5, -4, -3, so next is -2: 7 - 2 = 5, which is E.
r: Tip: shrinking differences (6, 5, 4, 3, 2) are common in letter series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q19) PIOUS means the same as:
f: PIOUS means deeply religious and devoted to worship.
r: Tip: a pious person is devout, while innocent means free from guilt.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q20) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: WRIST, KNEE and ELBOW are body joints. BALD is a condition, not a body part.
r: Tip: check whether three items belong to one category (here joints) and one does not.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q21) Which letter comes next: H, J, D, F, L, ?
f: Letter positions are 8, 10, 4, 6, 12, then 14. Within each pair the step is +2 (H to J, D to F, L to N), and the pairs themselves start at 8, 4, 12 (steps -4, +8), so the pair that begins with L ends with N.
r: Tip: if one step repeats (+2) between neighbours, the rest of the pattern is in how the pairs start.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q22) Twelve years ago Afzal weighed 50 kg. Every year he gained 2 kg. What is his weight now?
f: In 12 years he gained 12 x 2 = 24 kg, so his weight now is 50 + 24 = 74 kg.
r: Tip: multiply the yearly change by the number of years before adding to the starting value.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q23) DINNER is to NIGHT as MORNING is to:
f: Dinner is the meal eaten at night, and breakfast is the meal eaten in the morning.
r: Tip: the pair is meal and time of day.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q24) Which number comes next: 100, 64, 36, 16, ?
f: The terms are squares of even numbers going down: 10 squared, 8 squared, 6 squared, 4 squared, so next is 2 squared = 4.
r: Tip: learn the squares up to 20 to spot such series quickly.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q25) SCARCE means the same as:
f: SCARCE means in short supply, which is the same as RARE.
r: Tip: scarce and rare both describe something hard to find.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q26) DELICATE is the opposite of:
f: DELICATE means fragile or easily broken, so its opposite is STRONG.
r: Tip: choose the opposite of the main meaning (fragile versus strong), not the opposite of a side meaning.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q27) Which number comes next: 256, 64, 16, 4, ?
f: Each term is divided by 4: 256, 64, 16, 4, then 4 / 4 = 1.
r: Tip: check ratios as well as differences when terms shrink fast.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q28) The speed of sound is faster than the speed of light:
f: Light travels at about 300,000 km per second, while sound in air travels at only about 343 metres per second.
r: Tip: this is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q29) A man earned Rs. 28 and saved Rs. 7. What percent of his earning did he save?
f: Percent saved = 7 / 28 x 100 = 25%.
r: Tip: percent = part divided by whole, times 100.

q: (Forces Academy Test 11 · Q30) MILE is to LAND as KNOT is to:
f: A mile is a unit of distance used on land, and a knot is a unit of speed used at sea.
r: Tip: one nautical mile equals 1.852 km, and a knot is one nautical mile per hour.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q1) Which letter comes next: C, E, H, L, ?
f: Positions are 3, 5, 8, 12 with differences +2, +3, +4. Next is +5: 12 + 5 = 17, which is Q.
r: Tip: when the gap increases by one each time, add the next larger gap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q2) Which number comes next: 35, 19, 11, 7, ?
f: Differences are -16, -8, -4, so the next is -2: 7 - 2 = 5.
r: Tip: halving differences point to a pattern of repeated division by 2.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q3) The average cost of bananas, oranges and apples is Rs. 30 per kg. If bananas cost Rs. 10 per kg and oranges cost Rs. 45 per kg, how much do apples cost per kg?
f: Total of the three prices = 3 x 30 = 90. Apples = 90 - 10 - 45 = Rs. 35 per kg.
r: Tip: average times the number of items gives the total.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q4) TRAVEL is to 45936 as LATER is to (code: T=4, R=5, A=9, E=3, L=6 as in the printed number):
f: From the code T=4, R=5, A=9, E=3, L=6. LATER is L6 A9 T4 E3 R5, which gives 69435.
r: Tip: the printed code has five digits for the letters T, R, A, E, L, so match each digit to its letter in order.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q5) LATE means the opposite of:
f: The question asks for the opposite of LATE, which is EARLY.
r: Tip: read the question stem carefully; here it asks for the opposite, not a synonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q6) FISH is to SWIM as BIRD is to:
f: A fish moves by swimming, and a bird moves by flying.
r: Tip: this is an animal and its mode of movement.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q7) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: TALL, LARGE, HIGH and BIG all express greater size. SMALL is the opposite.
r: Tip: look for the antonym among a group of synonyms.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q8) Which letter comes next: A, D, I, P, ?
f: Positions are 1, 4, 9, 16, which are the squares 1, 2, 3, 4 squared. Next is 5 squared = 25, which is Y.
r: Tip: positions of 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 are perfect squares.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q9) Which number comes next: 1440, 240, 48, 12, ?
r: Tip: dividers that fall by one each time (6, 5, 4, 3) are a factorial-style pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q10) A train travels 6 meters in 1/4 minutes. How much distance (in meters) does it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 5 minutes contain 20 quarter-minutes, so the distance is 20 x 6 = 120 meters.
r: Tip: convert the time into units of the given interval and then multiply.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q11) Copper is cheaper than gold because it is:
f: Price depends on supply and demand, and copper is much more abundant than gold.
r: Tip: scarcity is the main reason precious metals cost more.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q12) People go to a doctor because:
o: They want to see sick people
It is pleasant in the clinic
f: The purpose of visiting a doctor is to get treatment for an illness.
r: Tip: choose the answer that states the real purpose.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q13) Which letter comes next: R, M, I, F, ?
f: Positions are 18, 13, 9, 6 with differences -5, -4, -3. Next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4, which is D.
r: Tip: write letters as numbers; the differences shrink by one each time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q14) We go to the cinema because:
o: Cinema halls are good to look at
f: The direct purpose of going to the cinema is to see films.
r: Tip: the best answer states the main purpose, not a side reason.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q15) If a pencil costs Rs. 10 per dozen and one sharpener costs Rs. 3, what will be the cost of 24 pencils and one dozen sharpeners?
f: 24 pencils are 2 dozen = 2 x 10 = Rs. 20. A dozen sharpeners cost 12 x 3 = Rs. 36. Total = 20 + 36 = Rs. 56.
r: Tip: convert everything to the same unit (dozens or single items) before adding.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q16) HIGH is to LOW as BAD is to:
f: HIGH and LOW are opposites, and the opposite of BAD is GOOD.
r: Tip: EVIL is a synonym of BAD, not the opposite.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q17) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: WEAK, UGLY, SLOW and DULL are all negative qualities. BRIGHT is a positive one.
r: Tip: sort the options by positive and negative meaning.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q18) Which letter comes next: B, D, G, L, ?
f: Positions are 2, 4, 7, 12 with differences 2, 3, 5, which are consecutive primes. The next prime is 7, so 12 + 7 = 19, which is S.
r: Tip: if differences are not simple, check whether they are consecutive primes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q19) A man earns Rs. 20 for producing 40 units of work. For each unit produced over 40 he is paid at 1 1/2 times his regular rate. How much will he receive if he produces 52 units of work?
f: Regular rate is 20 / 40 = Rs. 0.50 per unit, so the overtime rate is Rs. 0.75. For 12 extra units he gets 12 x 0.75 = Rs. 9, so the total is 20 + 9 = Rs. 29.
r: Tip: find the regular unit rate first, then apply the multiplier to the extra units only.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q20) CLOCK is to TIME as THERMOMETER is to:
f: A clock is an instrument that measures time, and a thermometer measures temperature.
r: Tip: the pattern is instrument and the quantity it measures.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q21) Which letter comes next: A, C, F, H, ?
f: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 8 with alternating steps +2, +3, +2. Next is +3: 8 + 3 = 11, which is K.
r: Tip: alternating steps repeat in a fixed cycle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q22) A man earns Rs. 2400 per month. He pays Rs. 1500 for office rent and Rs. 200 is spent as office expense. How much tax does he pay if the balance is taxed at the rate of 5%?
r: Tip: tax applies only to the balance left after the deductions named in the question.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q24) Which number comes next: 11, 12, 10, 13, 9, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 11, 10, 9 (going down by 1) and 12, 13, 14 (going up by 1). The next term is in the second series: 14.
r: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q25) EYE is to SEE as NOSE is to:
f: The eye is the organ used to see, and the nose is the organ used to smell.
r: Tip: the pattern is organ and its function.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q26) BACKWARDS means the same as:
f: BACKWARDS means in the reverse direction, so REVERSED is the closest match.
r: Tip: FORWARDS is the opposite, not a synonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q27) Which number comes next: 99, 80, 63, 48, ?
f: Differences are -19, -17, -15, so next is -13: 48 - 13 = 35.
r: Tip: differences that fall by 2 each time form a second-order series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q28) WHEN is to TIME as WHERE is to:
f: WHEN asks about time and WHERE asks about place, which is SPACE.
r: Tip: question words map to concepts: when is time, where is place or space.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q29) If Azam can ride a bicycle 300 feet while Akram runs 200 feet, how many feet can Azam ride while Akram runs 300 feet?
f: Azam covers 1.5 feet for every foot Akram runs (300 / 200). When Akram runs 300 feet, Azam rides 300 x 1.5 = 450 feet.
r: Tip: find the ratio of the two distances and scale it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 12 · Q30) MULTIPLICATION is the opposite of:
f: Multiplication and division are inverse operations, so DIVISION is the opposite.
r: Tip: addition and subtraction are also inverse operations of each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q1) Which comes next in the following series: E, GH, JKL, NOP?, with each block one letter longer and one letter skipped between blocks (the last block is NOPQ)? What is the last letter of the fourth block?
f: The blocks are E (1 letter), GH (2), JKL (3), NOPQ (4), with one letter skipped between blocks (F, I, M). The completing letter of the fourth block is Q.
r: Tip: in block series, count how long each block is and which letters are skipped.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q2) Which number comes next: 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, ?
f: The steps alternate +1, +2, +1, +2, so after 7 comes 7 + 1 = 8.
r: Tip: repeating step cycles like +1, +2 are common.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q3) If a boy can run 2 feet in 1/10 seconds, how many feet can he run in 10 seconds?
f: In 10 seconds there are 100 intervals of 1/10 seconds, so the distance is 100 x 2 = 200 feet.
r: Tip: divide the total time by the small interval to find how many intervals fit.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q4) HAPPINESS is to 415537299 as SHAPE is to:
f: From HAPPINESS = 415537299: H=4, A=1, P=5, I=3, N=7, E=2, S=9. SHAPE is S9 H4 A1 P5 E2, which is 94152.
r: Tip: build the letter table from the long word first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q5) BIG means the opposite of:
f: The opposite of BIG is SMALL.
r: Tip: LARGE is a synonym of BIG, so it is a trap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q6) SEEING is to PICTURE as HEARING is to:
f: We see a picture and we hear a song, so the object of hearing is a SONG.
r: Tip: the pattern is sense and the object it perceives.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q7) FLAT means the same as:
f: A flat surface is a level surface, with no slope.
r: Tip: INCLINED, UNEVEN and OBLIQUE all describe slopes or bumps, so they are opposites.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q8) Which letter comes next: KLMNO, LMNO, MNO, NO, ?
f: Each term drops the first letter of the one before: KLMNO, LMNO, MNO, NO, then O.
r: Tip: if each term is shorter by one letter, the rule is removing the first letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q9) Which number comes next: 15, 35, 55, 75, 95, ?
f: Each term goes up by 20, so 95 + 20 = 115.
r: Tip: constant differences make an arithmetic series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q10) Add all the numbers in the following series and divide the total by the highest number: 2, 5, 4, 8, 7, 6
f: The total is 2 + 5 + 4 + 8 + 7 + 6 = 32. The highest number is 8, and 32 / 8 = 4.
r: Tip: add carefully in pairs to avoid slips.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q11) If yesterday was WEDNESDAY, tomorrow would be:
f: If yesterday was Wednesday then today is Thursday, so tomorrow is Friday.
r: Tip: tomorrow is always two days after yesterday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q12) The Sun rises in the East because:
o: The Moon revolves around the Sun
The Earth rotates from West to East
It always comes up on that side
The Earth revolves around the Sun
f: The Earth spins from West to East, so the Sun appears to rise in the East.
r: Tip: day and night are caused by rotation, and the seasons are caused by revolution.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q13) Which letter comes next: E, G, J, N, ?
f: Positions are 5, 7, 10, 14 with differences +2, +3, +4. Next is +5: 14 + 5 = 19, which is S.
r: Tip: if the gaps grow by one each time, keep adding the next bigger gap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q14) Games are played:
o: They help us in keeping good health
We like to compete with others
There is nothing else to do
f: The most important reason is that games keep us physically fit and healthy.
r: Tip: choose the most meaningful reason among the options.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q15) If the numbers 12, 2, 27, 11, 7 are arranged from the smallest to the largest, what will be the middle number?
f: Arranged in order: 2, 7, 11, 12, 27. The middle number is 11.
r: Tip: sort first, then take the third of five.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q16) GIFT means the same as:
f: A gift is also called a present.
r: Tip: PRESENT is also a word for the current time, so watch for context.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q17) IRON is to HEAVY as FEATHER is to:
f: Iron is a heavy material, and a feather is light.
r: Tip: this analogy links an object to its typical quality.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q19) What will be the third angle of a triangle whose two angles are 30 degrees and 80 degrees?
f: The angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so the third angle is 180 - 30 - 80 = 70 degrees.
r: Tip: the three interior angles of any triangle always sum to 180 degrees.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q20) YOUNG means the same as:
f: YOUNG and YOUTHFUL both mean in the early part of life.
