r: Tip: BABY names a person, it is not an adjective like YOUNG.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q21) Which letter comes next: B, D, G, L, ?
f: Positions are 2, 4, 7, 12 with differences 2, 3, 5, which are consecutive primes. The next prime is 7, so 12 + 7 = 19, which is S.
r: Tip: if differences are not simple, check whether they are consecutive primes.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q22) In a school out of 200 teachers, 45% are more than 50 years old and 65% are married. Are there any who are unmarried and below 50 years?
f: 90 teachers are over 50 and 130 are married. These groups overlap by at least 20, but it is possible that all 70 unmarried teachers are over 50, and equally possible that some are below 50. So we cannot say for sure.
r: Tip: when data gives only percentages of overlapping groups, the minimum overlap does not fix the unknown group, so CANNOT SAY is common.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q23) INDUSTRIOUS means the same as:
f: INDUSTRIOUS describes someone who works diligently, which is HARD-WORKING.
r: Tip: industrious comes from the Latin industria meaning diligence, and should not be confused with industrial.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q24) Which number comes next: 2, 8, 26, 80, ?
f: Each term is 3 times the previous term plus 2: 2, 8, 26, 80, then 80 x 3 + 2 = 242.
r: Tip: if terms grow by about 3 times each step, test the rule multiply by 3 then add a constant.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q25) WHEEL is to BICYCLE as LEG is to:
f: A wheel is a part of a bicycle, and a leg is a part of the body.
r: Tip: LEG is also a part of a TABLE, so use the body-part sense for the closest match here.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q26) Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: TRIANGLE, PARALLELOGRAM, SQUARE and RECTANGLE are made of straight sides and corners. A CIRCLE has a curved boundary and no corners.
r: Tip: a circle is the only common shape with no straight sides.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q27) Which number comes next: 130, 118, 107, 97, 88, ?
f: Differences are -12, -11, -10, -9, so next is -8: 88 - 8 = 80.
r: Tip: differences decreasing by one each step give a simple second-order pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q28) DOUBT means the opposite of:
f: DOUBT means uncertainty, and the opposite is certainty, closest to CERTAINLY.
r: Tip: DUBIOUS is a synonym of doubtful, so it is a trap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q29) If a 20 feet long wire is to be cut so that one piece is 2/3 as long as the other piece, how long will be the shorter piece?
f: The pieces are in the ratio 2:3, so there are 5 parts in total, and each part is 20 / 5 = 4 feet. The shorter piece is 2 x 4 = 8 feet.
r: Tip: turn a ratio of 2 to 3 into 5 equal parts of the total.

q: (Forces Academy Test 13 · Q30) CLEAR is to DIM as NEAT is to:
f: CLEAR and DIM are opposites, so we need the opposite of NEAT, which is DIRTY.
r: Tip: when a pair is opposites, pick the antonym and reject synonyms like TIDY.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q2) Which one is different from the rest?
f: AC, CE, EG and GI each skip one letter and the second letter of each pair becomes the first letter of the next. II repeats the same letter, so it is different.
r: Tip: in letter pairs, compare how the second letter relates to the first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q3) What will come next in the following series: E0 V, E1 W, E2 X, E3 Y, ?
f: The subscript goes up by 1 each time (0, 1, 2, 3, then 4) and the letter moves along V, W, X, Y, then Z.
r: Tip: when a term has two parts, find the rule for each part separately.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q4) What will come next in the following series: 47, 40, 34, 29, 25, ?
f: Differences are -7, -6, -5, -4, so next is -3: 25 - 3 = 22.
r: Tip: if the gap reduces by one each time, continue the reducing gap.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q6) What will come next in the following series: 2, 3, 8, 63, ?
f: Each term is the square of the previous term minus 1: 2 squared minus 1 = 3, 3 squared minus 1 = 8, 8 squared minus 1 = 63, and 63 squared minus 1 = 3969 - 1 = 3968.
r: Tip: fast growth in a series often means a squaring rule.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q7) Which letter comes first alphabetically among the letters of the word MOTHER?
f: The letters of MOTHER in alphabetical order are E, H, M, O, R, T, so the first is E.
r: Tip: write out the letters in alphabetical order to find the first or last.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q8) If FACE is coded as 6135, then ACE is coded as:
f: From FACE = 6135, F=6, A=1, C=3, E=5. So ACE is 1, 3, 5, which gives 135.
r: Tip: the printed word options for this question do not fit, since the answer is a number code.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q9) Which one is different from the rest?
f: YARD, FOOT and KILOMETER are units of length. LENGTH is the quantity being measured, not a unit.
r: Tip: separate the units from the quantity they measure.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q10) HEAR is to EAR as CLOSE is to:
f: Removing the first letter of HEAR gives EAR, and removing the first letter of CLOSE gives LOSE.
r: Tip: check for hidden words made by dropping a letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q11) SOW is to SEED as REAP is to:
f: We sow seed, and we reap the crop.
r: Tip: GRAIN is only one kind of crop, so CROP is the best match for the pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q12) TIGHT is to LOOSE as HARD is to:
f: TIGHT and LOOSE are opposites, and the opposite of HARD is SOFT.
r: Tip: DIFFICULT is another meaning of HARD, so it is a synonym, not an opposite.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q13) Which word does not belong to the list?
f: BLACKSMITH, TAILOR and MASON are skilled manual craftsmen. A PROFESSOR is an academic.
r: Tip: split professions into manual trades and academic jobs.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q15) BIRD is to CAGE as PRISONER is to:
f: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in a cell.
r: Tip: the pattern is captive and the place where it is kept.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q16) Which one is different from the rest? 24, 48, 510, 611, 1130
f: 24, 48, 510 and 1130 are all even numbers. 611 is the only odd number.
r: Tip: check even or odd and divisibility first when numbers are listed.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q18) What number comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
f: Differences are +4, +6, +8, +10, so next is +12: 30 + 12 = 42.
r: Tip: these are products of consecutive numbers: 1x2, 2x3, 3x4, 4x5, 5x6, then 6x7 = 42.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q19) FINGER is to ELBOW as TOE is to:
f: The elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm, and the knee is the matching middle joint of the leg.
r: Tip: map the arm to the leg to find the matching joint.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q21) SINGLE is to DOUBLE as ONE is to:
f: SINGLE means one and DOUBLE means two, so the number matching ONE in the pair is TWO.
r: Tip: the pair moves from a count to the next count.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q22) Which one is different from the rest?
f: PLEADER, MAGISTRATE, JUDGE and ADVOCATE all work in the legal system. A COOK does not.
r: Tip: group the options by profession field.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q23) BOOK is to TITLE as MAN is to:
f: A book is identified by its title, and a man is identified by his name.
r: Tip: this pair links a thing to the label that identifies it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q24) Which word is out of the list?
f: COW, GOAT, SHEEP and BUFFALO are cud-chewing animals that give milk for human use. A HORSE is not a ruminant.
r: Tip: ruminants have a four-part stomach and chew the cud.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q25) Write the next number in the series: 1, 4, 10, 22, 46, ?
f: Each term is double the previous term plus 2: 1, 4, 10, 22, 46, then 46 x 2 + 2 = 94.
r: Tip: if terms roughly double, test multiply by 2 and add a constant.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q26) Which word is out of the list?
f: SPEECH, SERMON, LECTURE and ORATION are formal addresses to an audience. GOSSIP is casual talk about other people.
r: Tip: separate formal speaking from casual speaking.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q27) A is to E as C is to:
f: A is the 1st letter and E is the 5th, so we move forward 4 places. C is the 3rd, and 3 + 4 = 7, which is G.
r: Tip: count the number of places between the first pair and repeat the same jump.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q28) Write the next two numbers: 5, 3, 6, 4, 7, 5, 8, 6, 9, ?, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 (going up by 1) and 3, 4, 5, 6 (going up by 1). After 9 comes 7 from the second series, then 10 from the first.
r: Tip: in alternating series, split the terms into two separate sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 14 · Q30) What number comes next: 3, 8, 14, 21, 29, 38, ?
f: Differences are +5, +6, +7, +8, +9, so next is +10: 38 + 10 = 48.
r: Tip: differences that grow by one each time make a second-order series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q1) Which one of the following is different? A. MNO, B. STW, C. XYZ, D. EFG, E. BCD
f: MNO, XYZ, EFG and BCD are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. STW skips a letter (S, T, then W).
r: Tip: in letter-group questions first check whether the letters are consecutive, then check gaps and direction.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q2) Which one of the following is different? A. EVU, B. RHI, C. OLK, D. SHG, E. HSR
f: EVU, OLK, SHG and HSR all end with two letters in backward alphabetical order (V U, L K, H G, S R). RHI ends with H I, which goes forward.
r: Tip: compare the direction of movement inside each group, not only the letters themselves.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q3) Which one of the following is different? A. PQO, B. KJL, C. UTV, D. SRT, E. FEG
f: KJL, UTV, SRT and FEG each go one step back then two steps forward (-1, +2). PQO goes forward then back (+1, -2), so it is the odd one.
r: Tip: write the step sizes between neighbouring letters, as in +1, -2, to spot the odd group.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q4) Which one of the following is different? A. LLMN, B. UUVW, C. CCDE, D. GGHI, E. RRRS
f: The others repeat the first letter twice and then follow with the next two consecutive letters. RRRS repeats its first letter three times.
r: Tip: count repeated letters as well as the order of the alphabet.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q5) Which one of the following is different? A. Boy, B. Girl, C. Woman, D. Lady, E. Female
f: Girl, woman, lady and female all refer to the female sex. A boy is male.
r: Tip: in word odd-one-out questions look for a shared category such as gender, material or function.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q6) Which one of the following is different? A. Picture, B. Painting, C. Photography, D. Poster
f: Picture, painting and poster are finished visual items. Photography is the art or process of taking photographs, not an item.
r: Tip: separate objects from activities or processes when finding the odd one out.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q7) Which one of the following is different? A. Tobacco, B. Pipe, C. Cigarette, D. Cigar
f: Tobacco, cigarette and cigar are all made of tobacco. A pipe is only a device in which tobacco is smoked.
r: Tip: ask what each item is made of or what it is used for.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q8) Which one of the following is different? A. Stationary, B. Eraser, C. Pen, D. Paper
f: Eraser, pen and paper are all items of stationery. The word given, stationary, means not moving and is a different word.
r: Tip: stationery with an e means writing materials, stationary with an a means not moving.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q9) Which one of the following is different? A. Feathers, B. Hair, C. Grass, D. Wool
f: Feathers, hair and wool grow on the bodies of animals or birds. Grass is a plant.
r: Tip: classify by origin, such as animal, plant or mineral.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q10) Which one of the following is different? A. Circle, B. Square, C. Triangle, D. Hexagon
f: Square, triangle and hexagon are polygons with straight sides and corners. A circle has a curved boundary and no corners.
r: Tip: a polygon needs at least three straight sides.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q11) Which one of the following is different? A. Leprosy, B. Typhoid, C. Vomiting, D. Asthma
f: Leprosy, typhoid and asthma are diseases. Vomiting is a symptom, not a disease in itself.
r: Tip: distinguish a disease from a symptom of a disease.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q12) Which one of the following is different? A. Silver, B. Mercury, C. Gold, D. Iron
f: Silver, gold and iron are solid metals at room temperature. Mercury is a liquid metal.
r: Tip: mercury is the only metal that is liquid at normal room temperature.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q13) Which one of the following is different? A. Live, B. Die, C. Exist, D. Be
f: Live, exist and be all mean to have life or being. Die means the opposite, to stop living.
r: Tip: look for an antonym hidden among synonyms.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q14) Which one of the following is different? A. Hard, B. Stiff, C. Unbending, D. Flexible
f: Hard, stiff and unbending describe something rigid. Flexible means able to bend easily.
r: Tip: three synonyms and one antonym is a very common pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q15) Which one of the following is different? A. Sports, B. Teem, C. Game, D. Team
f: Sports, game and team all belong to the field of games and play. Teem (to be full of) is unrelated.
r: Tip: teem and team sound alike but have different meanings.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q16) Which one of the following is different? A. August, B. September, C. October, D. November
f: September, October and November all end in the letters ber. August does not.
r: Tip: September to December get their names from Latin numbers (septem, octo, novem, decem).

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q17) All the rivers have? A. Towns, B. Bridge, C. Banks, D. Fish
f: Every river, without exception, has banks on its sides. Not every river has towns, bridges or fish.
r: Tip: choose the option that is always true, not just sometimes true.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q18) ABD is to CBA as QRT is to?
f: ABD to CBA: first letter +2 (A to C), middle letter unchanged (B), last letter -3 (D to A). Apply this to QRT: Q+2 = S, R stays R, T-3 = Q, giving SRQ.
r: Tip: compare each letter position separately to find the shift for that position.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q19) What number comes next in the series: 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, ?
f: Each term is the sum of the next two terms (13 = 8 + 5, 8 = 5 + 3, 5 = 3 + 2, 3 = 2 + 1), so the next number is 1.
r: Tip: a series that falls can be a Fibonacci series written in reverse.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q20) What is the smallest even number (counting zero as an even whole number)?
f: Zero is divisible by 2 with no remainder, so it is an even number, and it is the smallest non-negative even number.
r: Tip: some tests consider only positive numbers and give 2, but the key for this test counts zero.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q21) What do you find once in a year and twice in a week?
f: The word YEAR contains the letter E once and the word WEEK contains it twice.
r: Tip: riddles of this kind are often about the letters inside the words themselves.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q22) Train is to track as bus is to?
f: A train runs on a track and a bus runs on a road. Both pairs show a vehicle and the path it travels on.
r: Tip: in analogy questions state the relationship in a sentence, then apply it to the second pair.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q23) If 8 men out of 10 are bald, how many out of 1000 are not bald?
f: 2 out of every 10 are not bald, which is 20 percent. 20 percent of 1000 is 200.
r: Tip: work out the complement (not bald) first, then scale up.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q24) What comes next in the series: 1, 2, 6, 12, 36, ?  (multiplying by 2, then 3, alternately)
f: The multipliers alternate x2, x3, x2, x3: 1x2 = 2, 2x3 = 6, 6x2 = 12, 12x3 = 36, so next is 36x2 = 72.
r: Tip: if neither the differences nor a single ratio fit, try alternating operations.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q25) Arrival is the opposite of? A. Reach, B. Departure, C. Away
f: Arrival means coming to a place and departure means leaving it, so they are opposites.
r: Tip: reach is a synonym of arrival, not an antonym.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q26) 6 is to F as 11 is to? A. K, B. L, C. M
f: F is the 6th letter of the alphabet, so the pair is number to its letter. The 11th letter is K.
r: Tip: remember A=1, E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20 and Z=26 as quick anchors.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q27) Aslam is four times as old as Ashraf. If the sum of their ages is 60 years, how old is Ashraf? A. 48 yrs, B. 12 yrs, C. 72 yrs
f: Let Ashraf be x, so Aslam is 4x and x + 4x = 60, which gives 5x = 60 and x = 12.
r: Tip: 48 is Aslam's age, so check which person the question asks about.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q28) If 1/8 of a number is 6, what is the number? A. 14, B. 48, C. 42
f: The number is 6 x 8 = 48.
r: Tip: to find the whole from a fraction, multiply by the denominator.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q29) Which one of the following is a prime number? A. 7, B. 8, C. 16, D. 12
f: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. The others are even numbers greater than 2, so they have more factors.
r: Tip: 2 is the only even prime number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 15 · Q30) 32% of 25 is? A. 16, B. 8, C. 4
f: 32 percent of 25 is 32/100 x 25 = 8.
r: Tip: 25 is one quarter of 100, so 32% of 25 is 32 divided by 4 = 8.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q1) What number comes next in the following series? 11, 17, 23, ?
f: Each term increases by 6: 11, 17, 23, so next is 29.
r: Tip: check for a constant difference first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q2) What number comes next in the following series? 23, 19, 15, 11, ?
f: Each term decreases by 4, so next is 11 - 4 = 7.
r: Tip: a constant negative difference gives a descending series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q3) What number comes next in the following series? 6/11, 5/10, 4/9, 3/8, ?
f: The numerator falls by 1 each time and the denominator falls by 1 each time, so after 3/8 comes 2/7.
r: Tip: in fraction series treat the numerators and denominators as two separate series.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q4) What number comes next in the following series? 1/3, 5, 1/7, 9, 1/11, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: the fractions 1/3, 1/7, 1/11 and the whole numbers 5, 9, and the next is 13 (add 4).
r: Tip: in alternating series split the terms into two separate sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q5) What number comes next in the following series? 8, 4, 16, 8, 64, ?
f: The pattern is divide by 2, multiply by 4, divide by 2, multiply by 8, divide by 2: 8/2 = 4, 4x4 = 16, 16/2 = 8, 8x8 = 64, 64/2 = 32.
r: Tip: when the pattern repeats an operation every second step, find it first, then follow the other operation separately.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q6) What number comes next in the following series? 3, 5, 3/5, 7, 11, ?
f: The terms come in groups of three: the first two numbers and then their fraction (3, 5, 3/5), then (7, 11, 7/11).
r: Tip: mixed series of whole numbers and fractions are often built from repeating groups.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q7) What number comes next in the following series? 2/31, 3/52, 4/73, ?
f: The numerators go up by 1 (2, 3, 4, 5) and the denominators go up by 21 (31, 52, 73, 94), so next is 5/94.
r: Tip: work out the difference of the top and bottom numbers separately.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q8) What number comes next in the following series? 93, 2, 73, 1, 63, 3, 33, 2, ?
f: Subtract ten times the number that follows: 93 - 20 = 73, 73 - 10 = 63, 63 - 30 = 33, 33 - 20 = 13.
r: Tip: in interleaved series one set of numbers can control the change in the other set.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q9) What number comes next in the following series? 1/2, A/B, 3, C, 4/5, D/E, ?
f: The pattern is number pair, letter pair, number, letter, so the terms run 1/2, A/B, 3, C, 4/5, D/E, 6, F and the next is 6.
r: Tip: when numbers and letters are mixed, follow the numbers and the letters as two interleaved sequences.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q10) What number comes next in the following series? 34/65, 23/54, 67/98, 45/?
f: In every fraction the denominator is the numerator plus 31 (34+31 = 65, 23+31 = 54, 67+31 = 98), so 45+31 = 76.
r: Tip: compare the top and bottom of each fraction with each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q12) What number comes next in the following series? 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, ?
f: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 2+1 = 3, 1+3 = 4, 3+4 = 7, so next is 4+7 = 11.
r: Tip: this is a Fibonacci-type series where each term is the sum of the previous two.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q13) Which one of the following is different? A. Young, B. Lovely, C. Beautiful, D. Handsome, E. Pretty
f: Lovely, beautiful, handsome and pretty all describe good looks. Young describes age.
r: Tip: group words by what they describe.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q14) Which one of the following is different? A. Month, B. Season, C. Year, D. Day, E. Week
f: Month, year, day and week are fixed units of time measured by the calendar. A season is a part of the year with a particular climate and has no fixed number of days.
r: Tip: the four seasons are summer, autumn, winter and spring.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q15) Which one of the following is different? A. GHI, B. JKL, C. NOP, D. QST, E. UVW
f: The others are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. QST skips R.
r: Tip: check for a skipped letter in letter-group questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q16) Which one of the following is different? A. Green, B. Red, C. Dark, D. Yellow, E. Brown
f: Green, red, yellow and brown are colours. Dark describes shade, not a particular colour.
r: Tip: dark and light are shades that can apply to any colour.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q17) Which one of the following is different? A. Camel, B. Ox, C. Horse, D. Donkey, E. Mule
f: Camel, ox, horse and donkey are natural animal species. A mule is a hybrid, the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.
r: Tip: a hinny is the opposite cross, a male horse and a female donkey.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q18) Which one of the following is different? A. Hand, B. Arm, C. Body, D. Wrist, E. Fingers
f: Hand, arm, wrist and fingers are all parts of the arm. Body is the whole that contains them.
r: Tip: whole versus part is a common way to make an odd one out.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q19) Which one of the following is different? A. Hot, B. Steam, C. Water, D. Ice, E. Vapour
f: Steam, water, ice and vapour are forms of water. Hot is only a quality.
r: Tip: water exists as solid (ice), liquid and gas (steam or vapour).

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q20) Which one of the following is different? A. Square, B. Line, C. Triangle, D. Circle, E. Rectangle
f: Square, triangle, circle and rectangle are closed shapes enclosing an area. A line does not enclose any area.
r: Tip: a closed shape has an inside and an outside.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q21) Which one of the following is different? A. Little, B. Rare, C. Less, D. Inferior, E. Few
f: Little, rare, less and few all refer to small quantity or amount. Inferior refers to lower quality.
r: Tip: separate words about quantity from words about quality.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q22) Which one of the following is different? A. RUS, B. FHG, C. MON, D. QSR, E. TVU
f: FHG, MON, QSR and TVU all follow the pattern +2, -1 between letters (F+2 = H, H-1 = G, and so on). RUS goes +3, -2.
r: Tip: write the jump between each pair of letters to find the common pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q23) Which one of the following is different? A. ABCACB, B. NOPNPO, C. RSTSTR, D. GHIGIH, E. KLMKML
f: In the others, three consecutive letters are followed by the same three with the last two swapped (ABC ACB, NOP NPO, GHI GIH, KLM KML). RSTSTR repeats the letters as S T R, which is a rotation instead.
r: Tip: compare the second half of each string with the first half.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q24) Which one of the following is different? A. TSUS, B. NMOM, C. DCEC, D. HGJG, E. RQSQ
f: TSUS, NMOM, DCEC and RQSQ all follow -1, +2, -2 between letters. HGJG goes -1, +3, -3, so it is different.
r: Tip: the third letter in each group steps forward by 2 from the second letter in the other groups.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q25) Which one of the following is different? A. Play, B. Cricket, C. Swimming, D. Football, E. Child
f: Play, cricket, swimming and football are all sports or games. Child is a person.
r: Tip: look for the item that is not an activity.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q26) Which one of the following is different? A. Two, B. Double, C. Pair, D. Three, E. Couple
f: Two, double, pair and couple all mean 2. Three is a different number.
r: Tip: check whether most words share the same number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q27) Which one of the following is different? A. STVU, B. HIJK, C. IJKL, D. OPQR, E. EFGH
f: The others are four consecutive letters of the alphabet. STVU has the order S, T, V, U, which is not consecutive.
r: Tip: look for a swapped or skipped letter.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q28) Which one of the following is different? A. Kingdom, B. State, C. Province, D. Citizen, E. Country
f: Kingdom, state, province and country are territories or political regions. A citizen is a person who lives in one.
r: Tip: a place and a person are different kinds of noun.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q29) Which one of the following is different? A. Run, B. Flow, C. Swim, D. Fast, E. Move
f: Run, flow, swim and move are verbs of motion. Fast is an adjective or adverb describing speed.
r: Tip: look for a different part of speech.

q: (Forces Academy Test 16 · Q30) Which one of the following is different? A. DBC, B. MLK, C. ONM, D. CBA, E. ZYX
f: MLK, ONM, CBA and ZYX are each three consecutive letters in backward order. DBC is not in a consecutive order.
r: Tip: check whether groups of letters run forwards or backwards.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q1) We read newspaper because: A. It is a good hobby, B. These give us knowledge, C. One learns how to read, D. These are motivating, E. These help us to get job
o: These help us to get job
f: The main purpose of a newspaper is to inform, so the best reason is that it gives knowledge.
r: Tip: choose the most general and direct reason in cause-and-reason questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q2) Which statement is correct? A. A son is always better educated than his father, B. A son is always more healthier than his father, C. A son is always younger than his father, D. A son is always less tall than his father, E. A son is always wiser than his father
o: A son is always better educated than his father
A son is always more healthier than his father
A son is always younger than his father
A son is always less tall than his father
A son is always wiser than his father
f: A father is by definition born before his son, so the son is always younger. The other statements may be true sometimes but not always.
r: Tip: the word always makes a statement false if there is even one exception.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q3) If clock A goes faster than clock B and clock C keeps time with clock A, then: A. C is slower than B, B. B keeps time with C, C. C is faster than B, D. B may be faster or slower than C, E. B and C keeps time with A
o: B may be faster or slower than C
B and C keeps time with A
f: C keeps the same time as A, and A is faster than B, so C is faster than B.
r: Tip: replace equal items with each other and the comparison carries over.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q4) 2 is to 5 as K is to?
f: The step from 2 to 5 is +3. Moving 3 letters on from K (L, M, N) gives N.
r: Tip: when numbers and letters are mixed, apply the same step to both.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q5) Parents give education to their children because: A. Children want it, B. It is a custom, C. It gives them better chances in life, D. It makes them obedient, E. It gives employment to teachers
o: It gives them better chances in life
f: The real purpose of education is to improve a child's opportunities and future.
r: Tip: pick the reason that best explains the underlying purpose.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q6) TIME is to EMIT as 4375 is to?
f: EMIT is TIME written backwards, so reverse 4375 to get 5734.
r: Tip: a reversal pattern applies equally to letters and digits.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q7) Which one of the following is different? A. South-West, B. North-East, C. North-West, D. East-West, E. South-East
f: South-West, North-East, North-West and South-East are the four intermediate (diagonal) directions. East-West is a pair of opposite cardinal directions, not a single direction.
r: Tip: the four intermediate directions lie halfway between the cardinal points.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q8) Which statement is correct? A. Two is equal to the difference between three and four, B. Two is less than the difference between three and four, C. Two is greater than the difference between three and four, D. Two may be less than or greater than the difference between three and four, E. None of the statement is correct
o: Two is equal to the difference between three and four
Two is less than the difference between three and four
Two is greater than the difference between three and four
Two may be less than or greater than the difference between three and four
None of the statement is correct
f: The difference between three and four is 1, and 2 is greater than 1.
r: Tip: calculate the quantity in the statement before comparing.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q9) Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. House, B. Mountain, C. River, D. Forest, E. Sea
f: Mountain, river, forest and sea are natural features. A house is man-made.
r: Tip: natural versus man-made is a common category split.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q10) STUN is to NUTS as POTS is to?
f: NUTS is STUN written backwards, so POTS reversed is STOP.
r: Tip: spelling a word backwards often produces another real word.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q11) About the word FLOWER which one of the following statement is true? A. O comes after L and E, B. E comes before R and W, C. L comes after E and before F, D. W is in the middle of R and L, E. None of the statement is correct
o: O comes after L and E
E comes before R and W
L comes after E and before F
W is in the middle of R and L
None of the statement is correct
f: In F-L-O-W-E-R, L is 2nd and R is 6th, and W is 4th, so W lies between L and R. The other statements fail, for example E is after O and W.
r: Tip: write out the letters with their positions before checking each statement.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q12) EF is to DG as JK is to?
f: E-1 = D and F+1 = G. Apply the same to JK: J-1 = I and K+1 = L.
r: Tip: letters moving outward from the centre form a mirror-like pair pattern.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q13) If a man goes 10 yards due north, then 10 yards due east, then 10 yards due south, then 10 yards due west, then: A. he is South of his starting place, B. he is north of his starting place, C. he has back to his starting place, D. he is south east of his starting place, E. he is west of his starting place
o: he is South of his starting place
he is north of his starting place
he has back to his starting place
he is south east of his starting place
he is west of his starting place
f: North and south cancel out, and east and west cancel out, so he ends where he began.
r: Tip: equal and opposite moves on each axis cancel.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q14) What number when taken away from 12 gives 3 less than one-third of 27?
f: One-third of 27 is 9, and 3 less than 9 is 6. So 12 - x = 6, giving x = 6.
r: Tip: break wordy questions into small steps.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q15) Even is to Uneven as Violent is to: A. Aggressive, B. Friendly, C. Responsible, D. Sadest, E. Unkind
f: Even and uneven are opposites, so we need the opposite of violent, and friendly (gentle) is the best match. Aggressive and unkind are similar to violent.
r: Tip: identify whether the first pair is synonyms or antonyms.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q16) Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to: A. Chains, B. Court, C. Freedom, D. Cell, E. Police
f: A bird is kept in a cage and a prisoner is kept in a cell.
r: Tip: this is an object and its place of confinement.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q17) If A is as tall as D, C is shorter than A, B is taller than D, then: A. A is taller than B, B. C is as tall as D, C. B may be taller or shorter than C, D. C is shorter than D, E. B is shorter than A
o: C is as tall as D
B may be taller or shorter than C
f: A and D are equal in height and C is shorter than A, so C is shorter than D. Also B is taller than D, so B is taller than A as well.
r: Tip: substitute equal items and chain the comparisons.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q18) 1/3 is to 9 as 1/2 is to:
f: 1/3 becomes 9, which is the square of its reciprocal (3 squared). The reciprocal of 1/2 is 2, and 2 squared is 4.
r: Tip: try squares, cubes and reciprocals for pairs that link a fraction to a whole number.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q19) SPHERE is to CIRCLE as CUBE is to: A. Cuboid, B. Angle, C. Square, D. Point, E. None
f: A sphere is the three-dimensional form of a circle, so the matching two-dimensional form of a cube is a square.
r: Tip: the question prints SRHERE, which is a typing error for SPHERE.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q20) If L is to 1, T is to 2, E is to 3, R is to 4, add up the digits for the word LETTER, divide the total by 5 and give the result as your answer.
f: LETTER = L1 + E3 + T2 + T2 + E3 + R4 = 15, and 15 divided by 5 = 3.
r: Tip: write each letter's value under it before adding.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q21) (2/4) is to (1:2) as (18/24) is to?
f: 2/4 is reduced to its simplest ratio 1:2, so 18/24 in simplest form is 3:4.
r: Tip: divide top and bottom by their highest common factor, here 6.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q22) Which of the following words has P but not A, has E but not D, has C but not L, has O but not I? A. Possible, B. Police, C. Pagoda, D. Pocket, E. Please
f: POCKET has P, E, C and O, and has no A, D, L or I. Possible has no C, police has I, pagoda has A and D, and please has A.
r: Tip: eliminate options one condition at a time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q23) What number when added to 14 gives 12 less than 30?
f: 12 less than 30 is 18, so 14 + x = 18 and x = 4.
r: Tip: compute the right-hand side first, then solve.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q24) People smoke because: A. They get pleasure from it, B. They want to show off, C. It is a fashion these days, D. It makes them social, E. It is good for health
o: It is a fashion these days
f: The most common reason smokers give is the pleasure or relief they feel, driven by nicotine. Smoking is not good for health.
r: Tip: smoking is a leading cause of lung cancer and heart disease worldwide.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q25) Three men A, B, C are standing in a row so that A and C are standing to the left of B, and B and A are standing to the right of C. Who is standing in the middle? (the paper prints A and B in the first part, which is a typing slip for A and C)
f: A and C are left of B, so B is last. B and A are right of C, so C is first. That leaves A in the middle: C, A, B.
r: Tip: draw a row and place each person using one clue at a time.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q26) Which would be the middle letter if the letters of the word SUBORDINATE are arranged in an alphabetical order?
f: The 11 letters in order are A, B, D, E, I, N, O, R, S, T, U. The 6th (middle) letter is N.
r: Tip: for 11 items the middle one is the 6th.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q27) Nazar is 2/3 times younger than his elder brother. His brother Rab Nawaz is 21 years old, what is the age of Nazar?
f: Nazar's age is 2/3 of 21 = 14 years.
r: Tip: 7 is one third of 21 and 14 is two thirds, so read the fraction carefully.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q28) People buy cars: A. To sell them at profit, B. So that they reach places quickly
o: So that they reach places quickly
f: The usual purpose of buying a car is transport, to reach places quickly and comfortably.
r: Tip: choose the most common, general purpose in these items.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q29) 63 is to 9 as 71 is to?
f: 63 gives 9 as the sum of its digits (6 + 3 = 9). So 71 gives 7 + 1 = 8.
r: Tip: the digit-sum relation is common in number analogies.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q30) FOUR is to ELEVEN as THREE is to?
f: FOUR means 4 and ELEVEN means 11, which is 7 more. THREE means 3, and 3 + 7 = 10, which is TEN.
r: Tip: convert number words into numbers before looking for the rule.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q31) COMPARE is to 7324615 as OPERA is to?
r: Tip: build a letter-to-digit table from the given word first.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q32) If A is greater than B and B is less than C; then: A. A is equal to C, B. C is greater than A, C. A is greater than C, D. One cannot say whether A is equal to, greater than or less than C
o: One cannot say whether A is equal to, greater than or less than C
f: Both A and C are greater than B, but nothing links A and C directly, so their order cannot be decided.
r: Tip: two items that are both bigger than a third cannot be ranked against each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q33) If the following are arranged in order of size, what would come in the middle? A. Book, B. Word, C. Chapter, D. Sentence, E. Paragraph
f: In increasing order: word, sentence, paragraph, chapter, book. The middle one is paragraph.
r: Tip: sort the full list first, then pick the centre item.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q34) Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. KOOL, B. LOOM, C. NOOS, D. MOON, E. WOOX
f: In KOOL, LOOM, MOON and WOOX the first and last letters are consecutive in the alphabet (K L, L M, M N, W X). In NOOS, N and S are not consecutive.
r: Tip: look at the outer letters when the middle letters repeat.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q35) You should not tell lies because: A. People will not trust you, B. You will always be found out, C. It is bad to do so, D. Truth is bitter, E. You will be punished
o: You will always be found out
It is bad to do so
f: The basic reason not to lie is moral: it is wrong. The other reasons are consequences that may or may not follow.
r: Tip: the answer that states the principle is better than one that states a possible consequence.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q36) What letter group comes next in the following series? JKLMNOPQ, JKLOPQ, JKPQ, ?
f: Each step removes the middle letters: JKLMNOPQ, JKLOPQ, JKPQ, then JQ.
r: Tip: look at which letters disappear from the middle at each step.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q37) If B and C are at equal distances from A, B is south-west of A and A is south-east of C, then: A. C is north of B, B. B is south east of C, C. A is north west of B, D. C is south west of A
o: B is south east of C
A is north west of B
C is south west of A
f: Put A at the centre: B is south-west and C is north-west (since A is south-east of C) at the same distance. So C lies directly north of B.
r: Tip: draw a quick compass sketch with A at the origin.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q38) Which one of the following is different? A. Teacher, B. Patient, C. Lawyer, D. Doctor, E. Medicine
f: Teacher, patient, lawyer and doctor are all people. Medicine is a thing.
r: Tip: check for person versus thing.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q39) Which one of the following is different? A. Lion, B. Wolf, C. Cat, D. Goat, E. Tiger
f: Lion, wolf, cat and tiger are meat-eating (carnivorous) animals. A goat eats plants.
r: Tip: diet is a useful category for animal odd-one-out questions.

q: (Forces Academy Test 17 · Q40) GREEN is to GRASS, CLEAR is to: A. Crystal, B. Light, C. Dark, D. Close, E. Tone
f: Green is the typical colour of grass, and clear is the typical quality of crystal.
r: Tip: this analogy links a quality to the thing most known for it.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q1) Re-arrange the letters ARTGN and find the middle letter.
f: ARTGN rearranges to GRANT, whose middle (third) letter is A.
r: Tip: unscramble the word first, then count to the centre.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q2) Which country is this, re-arranged: MERYGAN?
f: The letters of MERYGAN can be rearranged to form GERMANY.
r: Tip: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q3) What is the last letter if DASAL is re-arranged?
f: DASAL rearranges to SALAD, so the last letter is D.
r: Tip: try common words that use all of the given letters.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q5) If the 7th of the month falls 2 days preceding Sunday, then what is the day which follows the 21st of the same month?
f: Two days before Sunday is Friday, so the 7th is a Friday. The 14th and 21st are also Fridays, so the day following the 21st is Saturday.
r: Tip: dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q6) How many letters are there after K and before T in the following series: AABKMXJTTC?
f: Between K and the first T come M, X and J, which is 3 letters.
r: Tip: read the series positions and count only the letters between the two markers.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q7) If three days later the day after tomorrow is Friday, then what was yesterday?
f: The day after tomorrow is today + 2, and three days later is today + 5. If that is Friday, today is Sunday, so yesterday was Saturday.
r: Tip: add up all the day shifts to find the offset from today.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q8) If 25th December is Sunday then 25th January will be?
f: There are 31 days from 25 December to 25 January and 31 = 4 x 7 + 3, so it is three days after Sunday, which is Wednesday.
r: Tip: reduce the number of days to the remainder when divided by 7.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q9) If 3 days after tomorrow is Wednesday, then what will be the day before yesterday?
f: Three days after tomorrow is today + 4. If that is Wednesday, today is Saturday, so the day before yesterday is Thursday.
r: Tip: find today first, then move backwards.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q10) If 15th of February in a leap year is Sunday, then what will be the 15th of the next month?
f: February has 29 days in a leap year, so 15 March is 29 days later. 29 = 4 x 7 + 1, so it is one day after Sunday, which is Monday.
r: Tip: a leap year has 366 days and a February with 29 days.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q11) Arrange BROTHER in alphabetical order and then indicate the letter left of the middle letter.
f: In alphabetical order it is B, E, H, O, R, R, T. The middle (4th) letter is O and the letter to its left is H.
r: Tip: with 7 letters the middle is the 4th.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q12) Which letter is next to the middle letter between H and P?
f: From H to P the letters are H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P (9 letters). The middle one is L, and the letter next to it is M.
r: Tip: count the letters including both ends before finding the middle.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q13) It takes two minutes to boil an egg. How many minutes to boil 5 eggs together?
f: The eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so 5 eggs together also take 2 minutes.
r: Tip: some questions test whether a task scales with the number of items.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q14) Amjad is taller than Asif, Akram is taller than Amjad. Who is the shortest?
f: Akram is taller than Amjad, who is taller than Asif, so Asif is the shortest.
r: Tip: write the names in order of height to see the shortest.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q15) If Ali is brother of the son of Salman's son, what relation is Ali to Salman?
f: Salman's son has a son, and Ali is that boy's brother, so Ali is also a son of Salman's son. That makes him Salman's grandson.
r: Tip: work from the innermost relation outwards.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q16) X and Y are brothers, B is A's brother but A is the mother of X, what is B to Y?
f: A is the mother of X and Y, and B is her brother, so B is the maternal uncle of Y.
r: Tip: your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mama).

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q17) A husband and his wife have five married sons who have two children each. How many total family members are there?
f: Husband and wife are 2, five sons make 7, their five wives make 12, and 5 x 2 = 10 grandchildren make 22.
r: Tip: do not forget the daughters-in-law when counting the family.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q18) Today is Maria's birthday, one year after today she will be twice as old as she was 10 years ago. How old is she now?
f: Let her age now be x. Then x + 1 = 2(x - 10), so x + 1 = 2x - 20 and x = 21.
r: Tip: the key sheet shows 22, but checking the equation gives 21.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q19) A man walked 1 km towards south and then turned right and walked another 1 km, in which direction is he?
f: Facing south, his right hand points west, so after turning right he walks west.
r: Tip: facing south, right is west and left is east.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q20) Time on Ali's watch is quarter to three. If the hour hand is pointing towards east, then where is the minute hand pointing?
f: At quarter to three the hour hand is almost at 3 and points east, while the minute hand is at 9, exactly opposite, so it points west.
r: Tip: the 3 and 9 on a clock face are opposite each other.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q21) A man walked 10 m towards east and then 5 m to North and then 10 m towards West, how far is he from the starting point?
f: The east and west moves cancel, so only the 5 m north remains. He is 5 m from the start.
r: Tip: opposite movements cancel on each axis.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q22) If London is to Thames then Lahore is to ____?
f: The River Thames flows through London and the River Ravi flows by Lahore.
r: Tip: the five rivers of Punjab are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q23) If K-2 is mountain then Gobi is ____?
f: K-2 is a mountain and the Gobi is a desert in Asia, mainly in Mongolia and northern China.
r: Tip: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q24) Which one is different? Camel, Donkey, Bull, Mare
f: Camel, donkey and bull are general or male animal names, while a mare is specifically a female horse.
r: Tip: the key for this test chose mare as the odd one.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q25) If a = 3, b = 4 and c = 5 then a squared + b squared + 2abc = ?
r: Tip: follow the order of operations and do the product 2abc before adding.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q26) Smile: Glad then Sadness: ____?
f: Glad is a word that goes with smile, so a word that goes with sadness is gloomy.
r: Tip: this analogy matches a thing with a word of the same mood.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q27) What comes next: 7/49, 6/36, ____, 4/16?
f: Each fraction is a number over its own square (7/49, 6/36, 4/16), so the missing one is 5/25.
r: Tip: look at how the denominator relates to the numerator.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q28) What is 30% of 30?
f: 30 percent of 30 is 0.30 x 30 = 9.
r: Tip: 10 percent of a number is that number divided by 10.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q29) If straight: Curve then decent: ____?
f: Straight and curve are opposites, so the opposite of decent is indecent (rude).
r: Tip: the first pair tells you the relationship is antonyms.

q: (Forces Academy Test 20 · Q30) Which is different: Triangle, Rectangle, Square, Circle?
f: Triangle, rectangle and square are polygons with straight sides. A circle is a curved shape with no sides.
r: Tip: look for curved versus straight edges.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q1) Orange Line train is working in which city?
f: The Orange Line Metro Train runs in Lahore.
r: It is Pakistan's first metro train, opened in 2020, built with Chinese cooperation under CPEC.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q2) Which article of the Constitution of Pakistan gives freedom of speech?
f: Article 19 guarantees freedom of speech, subject to reasonable restrictions.
r: Article 19-A gives the right to information.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q3) Which article of the Constitution of Pakistan gives the right to education?
f: Article 25-A makes free and compulsory education a right for children aged 5 to 16.
r: It was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q4) Which one of these is a greenhouse gas?
f: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, so it is a greenhouse gas.
r: Methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour are other greenhouse gases.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q5) In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the Muslim League?
f: Jinnah joined the All India Muslim League in 1913.
r: He had earlier been a member of the Indian National Congress, which he left in 1920.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q6) In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy, as commonly given in Pakistani notes?
f: Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan, and Pakistan's first embassy and ambassador (Raja Ghazanfar Ali Khan) went to Tehran.
r: The sheet says Iran; some sources give other countries, so treat this as the standard exam answer.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q7) Which is the largest dam of Pakistan?
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus is the largest earth-filled dam in the world and the largest in Pakistan.
r: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum is the second largest.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q8) Which is the highest military award of Pakistan?
f: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest gallantry award.
r: Nishan-e-Haider was instituted in 1957 (applied from 1947) and was first awarded, after death, to Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed for his action in July 1948.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q10) Which country is the largest exporter of oil in the world?
f: Saudi Arabia exports more crude oil than any other country.
r: Saudi Arabia is the largest exporter of crude oil, while the United States is now the largest oil producer, followed by Russia and Saudi Arabia.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q11) In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) founded?
f: The SCO was founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai.
r: The sheet says 1999; the predecessor Shanghai Five formed in 1996 and the SCO itself in 2001. Pakistan joined in 2017.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q12) What is the capital of Cuba?
f: Havana is Cuba's capital and largest city.
r: Santiago de Cuba is the second largest city.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q13) Which is the second highest mountain peak in the world?
f: K2, also called Mount Godwin-Austen, is 8,611 m high, second only to Everest.
r: K2 is the highest peak of Pakistan and lies in the Karakoram range.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q14) Who built (rebuilt) the Grand Trunk (G.T.) Road?
f: Sher Shah Suri rebuilt and extended the old road from Sonargaon to Peshawar.
r: Sher Shah Suri (1540-45) rebuilt and extended the old highway from Sonargaon in Bengal towards the north-west; the name Grand Trunk Road came in the British period.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q15) The Karakoram Highway starts from which city on the Pakistani side?
f: The KKH (N-35) begins at Hasan Abdal and climbs to the Khunjerab Pass.
r: It links Pakistan with China and is called the Friendship Highway.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q16) Who was the adopted son of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him)?
f: Zaid bin Haris (Haritha) was adopted by the Prophet before prophethood and later freed.
r: Zaid bin Haritha was freed and adopted by the Prophet before prophethood, and he is the only companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:37).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q17) In which month was the Battle of Badr fought (17 Ramadan, 2 AH)?
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
r: About 313 Muslims faced roughly 1,000 Quraish.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q18) Which prayer is offered at the time of a solar eclipse?
f: Salat al-Kusuf is the special prayer for a solar eclipse.
r: The prayer for a lunar eclipse is called Salat al-Khusuf.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q19) Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
f: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva.
r: It was established in 1995 and replaced GATT.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q20) Where is the headquarters of Interpol?
f: Interpol's general secretariat is in Lyon.
r: It was earlier based in Paris.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q21) Which is the longest river of Europe?
f: The Volga, about 3,530 km, is Europe's longest river.
r: It flows through Russia into the Caspian Sea.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q22) Which is the largest river of the world by volume of water?
f: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.
r: By length the Nile and Amazon are close, and the Nile is traditionally called longest.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q23) Which is the smallest bird in the world?
f: The bee hummingbird of Cuba is the smallest bird, about 5 to 6 cm long.
r: Hummingbirds are the only birds able to sustain backward flight.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q24) Which is the smallest country in the world?
f: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square km.
r: Monaco is the second smallest.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q25) Who was the first lady governor of Pakistan?
f: She was appointed Governor of Sindh in 1973, the first woman governor.
r: She also founded APWA, the All Pakistan Women's Association.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q26) Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: Sir Frank Messervy led the army from August 1947 to February 1948.
r: He was followed by General Douglas Gracey; Ayub Khan was the first Pakistani C-in-C in 1951.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q28) Who is the author of the book Mein Kampf?
f: Hitler wrote Mein Kampf (My Struggle) while in prison in 1924.
r: The first volume was published in 1925.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q29) Who wrote Hayat-i-Javed?
f: Hali wrote this biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
r: Hali also wrote Musaddas-e-Hali.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q30) In which year was the movie Jinnah released?
f: The film Jinnah was released in 1998.
r: Christopher Lee played Jinnah.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q31) Who directed the movie Jinnah?
f: Jamil Dehlavi directed the 1998 film.
r: Jamil Dehlavi directed the film Jinnah (1998), and Akbar S. Ahmed co-wrote the screenplay.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q33) What is the capital of Portugal?
f: Lisbon is Portugal's capital.
r: It lies on the Tagus river.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q34) What is the capital of Chile?
f: Santiago is the capital of Chile.
r: Valparaiso houses the Chilean parliament.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q35) Who was the founder of fascism?
f: Mussolini founded the Fascist movement in Italy in 1919 (Fasci Italiani di Combattimento) and became Prime Minister in 1922.
r: The Fascist movement became the National Fascist Party in 1921; Hitler later led the Nazi Party, a German variant of fascism.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q36) In which year did the Russian Civil War start (as commonly dated)?
f: The Civil War followed the Bolshevik revolution of 1917 and lasted until about 1922.
r: Sources differ: some date the start of the Russian Civil War from the Bolshevik takeover in November 1917, others (such as Britannica) from 1918; it ended around 1922.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q37) What is the opposite of the word tamed?
f: A tamed animal is domesticated; its opposite is wild.
r: Domesticated and feral are other pairs.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q38) The 38th Parallel line lies between which two countries?
f: The 38th parallel was the dividing line between North and South Korea after 1945.
r: The present border (DMZ) follows the 1953 armistice line, which only roughly follows it.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q39) Which line forms the boundary between Canada and the USA?
f: Much of the Canada-US border runs along the 49th parallel north.
r: The 49th parallel forms the western and central part of the Canada-US border; the Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q40) The boundary line of the Rann (Run) of Kutch is also known as?
f: In the Rann of Kutch dispute Pakistan claimed that the boundary ran along the 24th parallel line, so this is the line linked with the Rann boundary.
r: A tribunal in 1968 largely rejected Pakistan's claim to half of the Rann; the Sir Creek boundary at its western end is still disputed.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q41) What is the meaning of the word Pakistan?
f: Pak means pure and stan means land.
r: The name was coined by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q42) In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
f: Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah in 1757.
r: It laid the base of British rule in Bengal.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q45) What is the name of Pakistan's cruise missile?
f: Babur (Hatf-VII) is Pakistan's ground-launched cruise missile.
r: Ghauri and Shaheen are ballistic missiles.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q46) Which is the highest battlefield in the world?
f: The Siachen Glacier battlefield lies above 5,000 m.
r: It is in the Karakoram range.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q47) In which city is Pakistan's largest nuclear power plant (K-2 and K-3, 1100 MW each) located?
f: K-2 and K-3 Hualong units at Karachi are the largest reactors, each 1100 MW.
r: The sheet says KANUPP-Karachi; KANUPP (K-1) was Pakistan's first power reactor, from 1972.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q48) Who wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob?
f: Ali bin Usman Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh, wrote it in Persian.
r: His shrine is in Lahore.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q49) In which city is the Golden Gate Bridge located?
f: The bridge spans the Golden Gate strait at San Francisco.
r: It opened in 1937.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q50) Who was the founder of modern Turkey?
f: Ataturk founded the Republic of Turkey in 1923.
r: He abolished the caliphate in 1924.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q51) Where were the modern Olympic Games first held (1896)?
f: The first modern Olympics took place in Athens in 1896.
r: The ancient games were held at Olympia, Greece.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q52) Who was the first man to walk on the moon?
f: Armstrong stepped on the moon on 20 July 1969, Apollo 11.
r: Buzz Aldrin followed him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q53) What is the currency of Russia?
f: Russia's currency is the ruble.
r: One ruble equals 100 kopeks.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q54) What is the currency of Turkey?
f: Turkey uses the Turkish lira.
r: Its code is TRY.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 1) In which year was the War of Independence?
f: The War of Independence broke out in 1857.
r: The British call it the Sepoy Mutiny.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 2) In which year did the Urdu-Hindi Controversy begin?
f: The controversy began in Banaras in 1867.
r: It pushed Sir Syed towards Muslim separatism.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 3) In which year did the Aligarh Movement (MAO College) begin?
f: Sir Syed founded the MAO School/College at Aligarh in 1875.
r: It became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 4) In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
f: A. O. Hume founded the INC in 1885.
r: W. C. Bonnerjee was the first president.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 5) In which year did the Partition of Bengal take place?
f: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905.
r: It was annulled in 1911.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 6) In which year was the Simla Deputation sent to Lord Minto?
f: The Simla Deputation led by the Aga Khan met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.
r: It demanded separate electorates.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 7) In which year was the All India Muslim League founded?
f: It was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906.
r: Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted the session.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 8) In which year were the Minto-Morley Reforms introduced?
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 granted separate electorates to Muslims.
r: It is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 9) In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed?
f: The League and Congress signed the Lucknow Pact in 1916.
r: Jinnah, together with Tilak, was the main architect of the Lucknow Pact.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 10) In which year did the Khilafat Movement start?
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919.
r: Ali Brothers led it.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 11) In which year was the Simon Commission appointed?
f: The commission was announced in November 1927.
r: It had no Indian member.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 12) In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India?
f: Stafford Cripps came in March 1942.
r: The Muslim League and the Congress both rejected it.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 13) In which year was the Simla Conference held?
f: Lord Wavell held it in June-July 1945.
r: It failed over Muslim representation.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 14) In which years were the general elections of undivided India held, before Partition?
f: Elections were held in the winter of 1945-46.
r: The Muslim League won almost all Muslim seats.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 15) In which year did Pakistan gain independence?
f: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947.
r: The Indian Independence Act was passed in July 1947.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 16) In which year was the Nehru Report published?
f: Motilal Nehru's committee issued the report in 1928.
r: Jinnah's 14 Points were the response.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 17) In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present the 14 Points?
f: Jinnah announced them in March 1929.
r: They answered the Nehru Report.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 18) In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
f: Iqbal gave the address on 29 December 1930.
r: He proposed a Muslim state in north-west India.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 19) In which years were the Round Table Conferences held?
f: Three conferences were held in London between 1930 and 1932.
r: Iqbal attended the second and third.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 20) In which year was the Government of India Act passed?
f: The Act of 1935 introduced provincial autonomy.
r: It was a main source of the later constitutions.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 21) In which year were the Indian Provincial Elections held under the 1935 Act?
f: Provincial elections took place in 1937.
r: Congress formed ministries in most provinces.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 22) In which year was the Lahore Resolution passed?
f: It was passed on 23 March 1940 at Minto Park, Lahore.
r: A. K. Fazlul Haq moved it.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 23) In which year was the Day of Deliverance observed?
f: Muslims observed it on 22 December 1939 after Congress ministries resigned.
r: Jinnah called for it.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 24) On what date did Quaid-e-Azam die?
f: Jinnah died in Karachi on 11 September 1948.
r: His mausoleum is Mazar-e-Quaid.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 25) On what date was the Objective Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly?
f: The Objective Resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan on 7 March 1949 and passed by the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.
r: It became a preamble to the constitutions of Pakistan.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 26) In which year was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: He was shot at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
r: The park was renamed Liaquat Bagh.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 27) In which year was the Bogra Formula presented?
f: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented it in 1953.
r: It proposed a two-house legislature.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 28) In which year was Pakistan's first Constitution enforced?
f: The first Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956.
r: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 29) In which year was the first Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
f: Iskander Mirza and Ayub Khan imposed it on 7 October 1958.
r: Ayub Khan removed Mirza within three weeks.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 30) In which year was the Second Constitution of Pakistan enforced?
f: Ayub Khan's constitution came into force on 8 June 1962.
r: It created a presidential system.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 31) In which years was the first Indo-Pak war fought?
f: The war began in October 1947 and the UN-brokered ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949; it is usually called the 1947-48 war.
r: Many books call it the 1947-48 war.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 32) In which year was the second war between Pakistan and India?
f: The war was fought in September 1965.
r: The Tashkent Declaration ended it in 1966.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 33) In which year did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh?
f: Bangladesh emerged on 16 December 1971.
r: The third Indo-Pak war occurred that year.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 34) In which year was the Third (current) Constitution of Pakistan adopted?
f: It was enforced on 14 August 1973 under Z. A. Bhutto.
r: It is the present constitution.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 35) In which year did Pervez Musharraf resign as president?
f: He resigned on 18 August 2008.
r: Asif Ali Zardari succeeded him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 36) In which year was the second Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan handed over power to Yahya Khan in March 1969.
r: It lasted until 1971.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 37) In which year was the third Martial Law imposed in Pakistan?
f: General Zia imposed it on 5 July 1977.
r: It was called Operation Fair Play.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 38) On what date was Z. A. Bhutto hanged?
f: He was hanged in Rawalpindi on 4 April 1979.
r: He was tried in the Kasuri murder case.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 39) In which year did Zia-ul-Haq hold his referendum on Islamization?
f: The referendum was held on 19 December 1984.
r: It was meant to give Zia a five-year term.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 40) In which year were the non-party elections held under Zia?
f: Non-party-based elections took place in February 1985.
r: Junejo became Prime Minister afterwards.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 41) In which year did Z. A. Bhutto appoint Gen Zia-ul-Haq as Army Chief?
f: Bhutto promoted Zia over senior generals in March 1976.
r: Zia overthrew him in 1977.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 42) In which year did Muhammad Khan Junejo become Prime Minister?
f: Junejo took oath on 23 March 1985.
r: Junejo took office as Prime Minister in March 1985 after the party-less elections and was dismissed by Zia in May 1988.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 43) In which year were the first general elections of Pakistan on the basis of adult franchise held?
f: Elections were held in December 1970.
r: The Awami League won a majority.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 44) In which year were the general elections that brought Benazir Bhutto to power held?
f: Elections were held on 16 November 1988.
r: The PPP won most seats.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 45) In which year were the general elections that brought Nawaz Sharif to power held?
f: Elections were held in October 1990.
r: The IJI won.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 46) In which year did the general elections that gave Nawaz Sharif a heavy mandate take place?
f: Elections took place on 3 February 1997.
r: In 1997 the PML-N won a heavy majority (about 137 of 217 seats) and, with its allies, a two-thirds majority.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 47) During which years was Benazir Bhutto Prime Minister for the first time?
f: She served from December 1988 to August 1990.
r: She was the first woman Prime Minister in the Muslim world.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 48) During which period did Nawaz Sharif hold his first government?
f: His first government lasted from November 1990 to July 1993.
r: He resigned under pressure from President Ghulam Ishaq Khan.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 49) During which years was Benazir Bhutto's second government after the 1993 elections (the chart gives 1993 to 1997)?
f: Her second term began in October 1993 and ended when President Leghari dismissed her in November 1996.
r: The chart says 1997, but it ended in 1996.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 50) During which years was Nawaz Sharif in power the second time?
f: His second government ran from February 1997 to October 1999.
r: General Musharraf removed him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 51) Which government removed the presidential power under Article 58(2)(b) through the 13th Amendment?
f: The 13th Amendment of 1997 was passed by Nawaz Sharif's government.
r: The chart writes 58-26; the clause is 58(2)(b), which let the president dismiss the assembly. It was restored in 2002.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 53) On which date did General Musharraf become President?
f: He took oath as president on 20 June 2001.
r: He replaced Rafiq Tarar.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 54) In which year did General Zia die in a plane crash (the chart says 1989)?
f: Zia died in the C-130 crash at Bahawalpur on 17 August 1988.
r: The chart says 1989, which is wrong.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Exam World 55) On what date was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
f: She was killed at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.
r: A suicide attack in Karachi on 18 October 2007 had targeted her earlier.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q27) Which princely state is described in standard Pakistani textbooks as the first state to accede to Pakistan (October 1947)?
f: The Nawab of Bahawalpur signed the agreement with Pakistan in October 1947 (accepted on 9 October), and textbooks name Bahawalpur as the first state to join.
r: Khairpur acceded at about the same time (early October 1947). Junagadh's ruler announced accession in September 1947, but India took over the state in November 1947. Kalat joined in March 1948.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Sheet Q32) In which year was the famous Urdu autobiography 'Shahab Nama' by Qudratullah Shahab published?
f: Shahab Nama was published in 1987, shortly after the author died in 1986.
r: Qudratullah Shahab was a senior civil servant and writer who worked closely with several Pakistani rulers.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 1) Which Sahabi carried the letter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to the Persian emperor Khusro Parvez?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abdullah bin Huzafah Sahmi (RA) with his letter inviting Khusro Parvez to Islam.
r: Khusro Parvez tore up the letter, and the Prophet (PBUH) is reported to have said that his kingdom would likewise be torn apart.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 2) In which reforms of 1909 was a separate electorate granted to the Muslims of India?
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, gave Muslims separate electorates.
r: Separate electorates were the first formal recognition of Muslims as a distinct political community; Lord Minto is called the Father of Communal Electorate.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 3) In which year was the Simon Commission announced and sent to India?
f: The all-British Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 and reached India in February 1928.
r: Indians boycotted it because it had no Indian member; Sir John Simon was its chairman.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 4) Which major party was absent from the First Round Table Conference held in 1930?
f: The Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference (1930-31) because of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
r: Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference in 1931 after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 5) In which year was the Wavell Plan made?
f: Lord Wavell put forward his plan in 1945 and it was discussed at the Simla Conference in June 1945.
r: The Simla Conference failed because Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on Muslim representation.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 6) In which year did the Dawn newspaper begin publication as a daily by the Quaid-e-Azam?
f: Dawn became a daily newspaper in 1942 in Delhi under the guidance of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
r: Dawn was first started as a weekly in 1941; it later moved to Karachi after independence.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 7) Who was the first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan?
f: Martial law was imposed in October 1958 and General Ayub Khan was made the first Chief Martial Law Administrator.
r: Iskander Mirza, who imposed martial law, was himself removed by Ayub Khan only 20 days later.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 8) Who was the first elected Prime Minister of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister in August 1973 under the new Constitution, and is counted as the 9th Prime Minister of Pakistan.
r: Bhutto had earlier served as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator from December 1971.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 9) Who was the first recipient of Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in the 1948 Kashmir war and received Pakistan's highest gallantry award first.
r: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti received the Nishan-e-Haider for the 1965 war.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 10) In which year did the Hindus of Banaras raise the Urdu-Hindi controversy?
f: The Urdu-Hindi conflict began in 1867 in Banaras when Hindu leaders demanded Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu in courts.
r: This conflict convinced Sir Syed Ahmad Khan that Hindus and Muslims could not work together politically.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 11) In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan given the title of Sir?
f: The British government honoured Sir Syed with the knighthood (Sir) in 1888.
r: Sir Syed was made a Companion of the Star of India (CSI) in 1869 and knighted (KCSI) in 1888.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 12) How many Muslim members were in the Simla Deputation that met Lord Minto?
f: The deputation led by Sir Aga Khan comprised 35 Muslim leaders.
r: Some notes give the year as 1905, but the Simla Deputation met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 13) By which other name is the Government of India Act 1919 also known?
f: The Act of 1919 followed the report of Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State) and Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy), so it is called the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
r: It introduced the system of dyarchy in the provinces.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 14) In which year was the Khilafat Committee formed?
f: The Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after the First World War.
r: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 15) In which year did the Khilafat Delegation visit England?
f: The Khilafat Delegation led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar visited England in 1920 to plead the Caliphate cause.
r: The delegation failed to change British policy, and the Treaty of Sevres was signed in the same year.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 16) On which date was the Quit India Movement launched by the Congress in 1942?
f: The All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August 1942.
r: Gandhi gave the slogan Do or Die, and the main Congress leaders were arrested the next day.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 17) Where and when was Liaquat Ali Khan born?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was born on 1 October 1895 in Karnal (East Punjab, now Haryana).
r: The note gives 1889, but the accepted year of birth is 1895.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 18) On which date did President Yahya Khan dismantle One Unit (West Pakistan)?
f: One Unit was dissolved on 1 July 1970, restoring Punjab, Sindh, NWFP and Balochistan as provinces.
r: One Unit had been created in 1955 by merging the provinces and states of West Pakistan.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 19) On which date was Mangla Dam inaugurated?
f: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was inaugurated on 23 November 1967.
r: It was built under the Indus Basin Water Treaty of 1960.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 20) On which date was the Lahore television station inaugurated?
f: Pakistan's first television station opened in Lahore on 26 November 1964.
r: Pakistan's first TV station opened in Lahore on 26 November 1964, and colour transmission began on 25 December 1976.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 21) In which city were the Gandhi-Jinnah talks held in 1944?
f: Gandhi and Jinnah met at Jinnah's house in Bombay in September 1944.
r: The talks were based on the C. R. Formula (Rajaji Formula) and ended in failure.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 22) How many general seats did the Awami League win in the 1970 National Assembly election?
f: The Awami League of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 general seats, all but two of East Pakistan's seats.
r: Counting reserved women seats, its tally rose to 167 of 313 seats.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 23) On which date did Bangladesh come into existence?
f: Pakistani forces surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and Bangladesh emerged as an independent state.
r: Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971, which it celebrates as Independence Day.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 51) The Battle of Yarmuk was fought between the Muslims and which power?
f: The Battle of Yarmuk (636 AD) was fought between the Muslim army and the Byzantine (Roman) Empire.
r: Khalid bin Waleed commanded the Muslim army, and the victory opened Syria to the Muslims.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 52) Which angel will blow the Trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement?
f: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Trumpet to announce Qayamah.
r: Hazrat Azrael (AS) takes souls, Mikael (AS) is in charge of rain and Jibrael (AS) brings revelation.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 53) Which Caliph established the Police Department in Islamic rule?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA) set up the police department (Ahdath) along with many other state departments.
r: Umar (RA) also started the Hijri calendar, the Diwan (treasury register) and the system of provinces.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 54) In which year did the Mughal emperor Jalal-ud-Din Muhammad Akbar die?
f: Akbar died in October 1605 at Agra and was buried at Sikandra.
r: The note gives 1606, but the accepted year is 1605; his son Jahangir succeeded him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 55) What is the officially accepted height of Mount Everest, as announced by China and Nepal in 2020?
f: In December 2020 Nepal and China jointly announced the new height of 8,848.86 metres.
r: The note gives 8841 m, which is wrong; the older accepted figure was 8,848 m, and K2 is 8,611 m.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 56) Who is regarded as the fifth pious Caliph (Khalifa-e-Rashid) by many scholars?
f: Umar bin Abdul Aziz, the Umayyad Caliph (717-720 AD), is called the fifth pious Caliph for his justice and piety.
r: Umar bin Abdul Aziz (reigned 717-720) is popularly called the fifth Rightly Guided Caliph, though this is an honorary title.
