q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 57) About how many active soldiers does the army of China (People's Liberation Army) have?
f: The PLA has roughly 2 million active personnel, the largest standing military force in the world.
r: China's army (PLA) has about 2 million active troops, and India's army has about 1.45 million.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 58) If A = (2, 4, 6) and B = (1, 2, 3, 6), then A - B equals what?
f: A - B has the elements of A that are not in B. Both 2 and 6 are in B, so only 4 remains.
r: B - A would be (1, 3), because those are the elements of B not in A.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 59) Israel is the title (another name) of which Prophet?
f: Israel means servant of God and is the title of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) (Jacob).
r: The Bani Israel (Children of Israel) are his descendants through his twelve sons.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 60) In which year was the Treaty of Severes (Sevres) announced?
f: The Treaty of Sevres was signed with the Ottoman Empire in August 1920.
r: It was replaced by the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 after Turkey's war of independence.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 62) In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
f: Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, while still being a member of Congress.
r: He presided over the Lucknow Pact session of the League in 1916.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 63) What does the Swadeshi Movement mean?
o: Boycott of foreign (British) goods and use of local goods
f: Swadeshi means one's own country; the movement urged people to boycott British goods and use Indian-made goods.
r: It started in Bengal in 1905 as a reaction to the Partition of Bengal.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 64) On which date was Bengal officially divided in 1905?
f: The Partition of Bengal was announced in July 1905 and took effect officially on 16 October 1905.
r: Lord Curzon was Viceroy at the time, and the partition was annulled in 1911.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 65) In which year did the Chaura Chauri tragedy take place?
f: In February 1922 a mob burnt a police station at Chauri Chaura and killed policemen, so Gandhi called off non-cooperation.
r: Chauri Chaura is in Gorakhpur district of Uttar Pradesh.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 66) On which date was the Day of Deliverance observed by Muslims in 1939?
f: Jinnah called on Muslims to observe 22 December 1939 as the Day of Deliverance after the Congress ministries resigned.
r: The Congress ministries had resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 67) The Pirpur Report of 1938 was about which subject?
f: The Pirpur Report listed the injustices against Muslims during Congress rule in the provinces (1937-39).
r: It was prepared under Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur for the Muslim League.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 68) In which year was the League of Nations founded?
f: The League of Nations came into being in January 1920 after the First World War.
r: It became ineffective by 1939 and was formally dissolved in 1946, replaced by the United Nations.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 69) The Battle of Waterloo in 1815 was fought between Napoleon's France and which side?
f: At Waterloo the British army under Wellington, with Prussian help, defeated Napoleon Bonaparte.
r: Waterloo is in modern Belgium; Napoleon was afterwards exiled to Saint Helena.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 70) Which is the most populous country in the world at present?
f: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, with over 1.4 billion people.
r: Some notes say China, which was true until 2022.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 71) The KGB was the intelligence agency of which country?
f: KGB stands for Committee for State Security, the main security agency of the Soviet Union from 1954 to 1991.
r: Russia's present agencies are the FSB and the SVR; the CIA is American and Mossad is Israeli.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 72) In which year did Russia sell Alaska to the USA?
f: Russia sold Alaska to the United States in 1867 for 7.2 million dollars.
r: The note gives 1878, but the correct year is 1867; the deal was called Seward's Folly.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 73) In which year of the Hijrah (AH) was the Battle of Uhud fought?
f: The Battle of Uhud took place in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD).
r: Badr was in 2 AH and the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq) in 5 AH.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 74) Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, real executive power lies with whom?
f: The 1973 Constitution created a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the chief executive.
r: The President is the ceremonial head of state, although the 8th Amendment later shifted powers temporarily.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 75) Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Armed Forces?
o: Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
f: The President of Pakistan is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces under the Constitution.
r: The President is the constitutional Supreme Commander of the armed forces; the 27th Amendment (November 2025) created the post of Chief of Defence Forces.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 76) On which date was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot dead on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
r: The park was renamed Liaquat Bagh after him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 77) Which was the first country to recognise Pakistan?
f: Iran was the first country to accept and recognise Pakistan after independence.
r: Afghanistan was the only country to vote against Pakistan's UN membership in 1947.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 78) How many sons and daughters did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) had three sons (Qasim, Abdullah and Ibrahim) and four daughters (Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima).
r: All sons died in childhood; of the daughters only Hazrat Fatima (RA) outlived him.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 79) For how many years did the British rule India, counting from 1857 to 1947?
f: 1947 minus 1857 gives 90 years of direct British Crown rule after the War of Independence of 1857.
r: Direct Crown rule began in 1858; counting from the war of 1857 to independence in 1947 gives about 90 years.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 80) Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
f: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan served as Pakistan's first Foreign Minister from 1947 to 1954.
r: He also later served as President of the UN General Assembly and a judge of the International Court of Justice.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 81) On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
f: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, as its 56th member.
r: Pakistan and Yemen were admitted to the United Nations together on 30 September 1947; the UN itself was founded on 24 October 1945.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 82) From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD degree?
f: Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany (his thesis was completed around 1907-08).
r: His thesis was The Development of Metaphysics in Persia.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 83) In which year was the Nehru Report presented?
f: The Nehru Report was drawn up by a committee led by Motilal Nehru in 1928.
r: Jinnah responded to it with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 84) In which year was the All India Muslim League founded?
f: The All India Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka.
r: The founding session was presided over by Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk, and Nawab Salimullah Khan of Dhaka proposed the party.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 85) Which angel brought Wahi (revelation) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Jibrael (AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
r: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira with the words Iqra (Read).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 86) Which gas is commonly used to extinguish fire?
f: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and does not support burning, so it smothers a fire.
r: CO2 extinguishers are suited to electrical and oil fires, but not to metal fires.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 87) What is the total area of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan covers about 796,096 square kilometres.
r: Balochistan is the largest province by area, making up about 44 percent of the country.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 88) How many seats does the Senate of Pakistan have at present?
f: After the 25th Amendment (merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018) the Senate was reduced to 96 members.
r: The notes give 104, which was the number before the 2018 merger.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 89) How many seats does the National Assembly of Pakistan have at present?
f: After FATA's merger the 6 FATA seats were abolished, so the National Assembly now has 336 seats (266 general, 60 women and 10 minorities).
r: Earlier it had 342 seats; 272 was the old number of general seats.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 90) Which country is the second largest in the world by area?
f: By area the order is Russia first, Canada second, then the USA and China close together.
r: Russia covers about 17 million sq km and Canada about 10 million sq km.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 91) In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School upgraded to MAO College?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan began the school in 1875 and it was upgraded to MAO College in 1877.
r: The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 93) Which country won the 1998 FIFA Football World Cup?
f: France, the host nation, beat Brazil 3-0 in the 1998 final in Paris.
r: France won its second World Cup in 2018.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 94) Which angel is responsible for rain?
f: Hazrat Mikael (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and provision.
r: Jibrael brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Azrael takes souls.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 95) In which year did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic?
f: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic on 23 March 1956 when the first Constitution came into force.
r: Iskander Mirza became the first President under that Constitution.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 96) Who was the cousin of Hazrat Khadija (RA) and a Christian scholar who confirmed the Prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Waraqa bin Naufal, cousin of Hazrat Khadija (RA), told the Prophet (PBUH) that the angel of Moses had come to him.
r: He died soon after the first revelation.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 97) Tarbela Dam, near Haripur Hazara, is built on which river?
f: Tarbela Dam stands on the River Indus in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.
r: Tarbela was completed in 1976 and Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 98) On which date was the United Nations Organization formally established?
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, which is celebrated as UN Day.
r: The Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 99) Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at present?
f: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq was elected Speaker in February 2024 after the general elections.
r: Dr Fehmida Mirza, named in the note, was the first woman Speaker (2008-2013).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 100) Who is the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at present?
f: Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah of the PPP was elected Deputy Speaker in March 2024.
r: Faisal Karim Kundi, named in the note, held the post earlier (2012-2013).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 101) Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan at present?
f: Khawaja Muhammad Asif is the Defence Minister (again since March 2024; he also held the post in 2013-2017 and 2022-2023).
r: Ch Ahmed Mukhtar, named in the note, held the post in 2008-2012.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 102) Who is the Interior Minister of Pakistan at present?
f: Mohsin Naqvi became Interior Minister in March 2024.
r: Rehman Malik, named in the note, was Interior Minister under the PPP government (2008-2013).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 103) Who is the Foreign Minister of Pakistan at present (also serving as Deputy Prime Minister)?
f: Ishaq Dar was appointed Foreign Minister in 2024 and also holds the office of Deputy Prime Minister.
r: Shah Mehmood Qureshi, named in the note, was Foreign Minister in 2008-2011 and 2018-2022.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 104) Who is the Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan at present?
f: Jameel Ahmad has been Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan since August 2022.
r: Dr Shahid Hafiz Kardar, named in the note, was Governor in 2010-2012.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 107) Who was elected President of Pakistan in 2008 and was elected to the office again in 2024?
f: Asif Ali Zardari became President in September 2008 and again in March 2024.
r: The notes call him the 15th President, but counts differ: he is usually the 11th (2008) and 14th (2024) President.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 108) How many seats does the Punjab Provincial Assembly have?
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats, the largest of the four provincial assemblies.
r: Sindh has 168 and Balochistan 65 seats.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 108) How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly have at present?
f: After the 2018 merger of FATA the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly increased from 124 to 145 seats.
r: The note gives 124, which was the figure before the merger.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 110) How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan has five: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Broad Peak and Gasherbrum II.
r: The world has 14 peaks above 8000 m, and K2 at 8,611 m is the second highest.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 111) Who was the first Muslim to shoot an arrow in the way of Allah?
f: Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) was the first Muslim to shoot an arrow in the cause of Allah.
r: The note names Zubair bin Awam (RA), who is known as the first to draw his sword in Islam.

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 112) In which year of Hijrah did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam?
f: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) embraced Islam in 8 AH, shortly before the Conquest of Makkah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) gave him the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

q: (Forces Academy Academic · Line 113) Which is the smallest continent of the world?
f: Australia is the smallest of the seven continents, with an area of about 7.7 million sq km.
r: Asia is the largest continent and Africa the second largest.

q: What is 90% of 90? (2350)
r: Taking 90% of a number 90 gives 81, which equals 9 x 9.

q: Why do we boil milk? (1761)
f: Boiling heats milk enough to kill harmful germs and bacteria and makes it safe to drink and keep for longer.
r: Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, is the industrial process of heating milk to destroy germs.

q: Why do parents send their children to school? (1695)
f: Schools provide education, which develops knowledge, skills and character in children.
r: Education is a fundamental right of children under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.

f: Division comes before addition (BODMAS), so 2/2 = 1 and 2 + 1 = 3.
r: BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (311)
f: Percentage present = 1200 / 1500 x 100 = 80%.
r: The absent students are 300, which is 20%.

q: How many months of the year have 31 days? (382)
f: The months are January, March, May, July, August, October and December, which makes 7.
r: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year).

q: What is the antonym of wild? (969)
f: Wild describes an animal or place not under human control. Tame means gentle and domesticated, its opposite.
r: Domestic is another common antonym of wild.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have? (128)
f: A triangular prism has two triangular bases and three rectangular side faces: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.
r: It also has 9 edges and 6 vertices. Candidates gave different answers (3, 4, 5, 6) because the paper did not name the prism type; the triangular prism is the usual one.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations? (75)
f: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
r: The UN itself was founded in 1945.

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120? (349)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12, and a quarter of 12 is 3. Working in the other order gives 30 and then 3.
r: One quarter of one tenth equals 1/40, so the answer is 120/40.

q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (151)
f: Absent students = 500 - 340 = 160. Percentage absent = 160 / 500 x 100 = 32%.
r: The present students make up 68%, which is the number many people wrongly give.

q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (85)
f: If yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday. The day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
r: The day after tomorrow is always two days after today.

q: If today is Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow? (31)
f: Tomorrow is Saturday, so the day after tomorrow is Sunday.
r: The day after tomorrow means two days from today.

q: What is the national drink (juice) of Pakistan? (92)
f: Sugarcane juice is regarded as the national juice or drink of Pakistan.
r: Pakistan is among the world's top producers of sugarcane.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (212)
f: If yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday. The day after tomorrow is Saturday plus 2 days, which is Monday.
r: The day after tomorrow is always three days after yesterday.

q: In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Battle of Uhud fought? (107)
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD) near Mount Uhud, a year after Badr.
r: The archers left their post on the hill, which let the Quraish attack from behind.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan? (423)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
r: He was assassinated at Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (73)
f: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA) married the Prophet (PBUH) about 15 years before the first revelation.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) did not marry again during her lifetime.

q: If yesterday was Saturday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (21)
f: If yesterday was Saturday, today is Sunday and tomorrow is Monday. The day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
r: Candidates remembered Monday, which is tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (81)
f: Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He was also close in age and a foster brother.
r: Hazrat Hamza was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.

q: A pen is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage? (233)
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League? (142)
f: Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, at the persuasion of Allama Iqbal, Wazir Hasan and others. He remained a member of the Indian National Congress at the same time.
r: He left the Congress in 1920 over differences with Gandhi's policies.

q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 90? (88)
r: 1/10 of a number is the same as 10% of it.

q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan? (169)
f: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan in 1947 and served until 1954.
r: He later served as a judge and President of the International Court of Justice.

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed? (129)
f: Abu Jahl, a leader of the Quraysh, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. He was struck down by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.
r: Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred? (191)
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. He was killed by Wahshi, a slave of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.
r: Hazrat Hamza (RA) is known as Asadullah and Sayyid ush-Shuhada (Chief of the Martyrs).

q: In which year was the OIC founded? (153)
f: The OIC was founded in September 1969 at Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
r: Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: Which country lies to the east of Pakistan? (64)
f: India shares Pakistan's long eastern border.
r: Pakistan borders Iran to the west, Afghanistan to the north-west, China to the north and India to the east.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 90? (143)
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and one third of 9 is 3. The same value results from taking one tenth of one third of 90 or one third of 10% of 90.
r: Fractions of a number can be taken in any order because multiplication is commutative.

q: What is 1/10 of 120? (33)
r: One tenth is the same as 10 percent.

q: What is the largest lake of the world by area? (67)
f: The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square km, is the largest inland body of water and is classed as a lake.
r: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest.

q: What is the longest (largest) river of Asia? (109)
f: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest river in Asia.
r: It is the third longest river in the world.

q: What is the length of the Indus River according to Pakistani textbooks? (18)
f: Pakistani textbooks give the length of the Indus as about 3,180 km.
r: Sources differ: some give about 2,880 km (Britannica) or 2,900 km.

q: What is the national bird of the USA? (33)
f: The bald eagle was chosen as the national bird and emblem of the United States.
r: It appears on the Great Seal of the United States adopted in 1782.

q: A book is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit? (46)
f: Profit = selling price - cost price = 40 - 30 = Rs 10.
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar? (160)
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958 for about 3 million US dollars, and it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
r: Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon was in office at the time.

q: How many pillars of Islam are there? (49)
f: The five pillars are Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
r: Salah is the pillar performed five times daily.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)? (15)
f: Pakistan became a member of NAM in 1979 at the Havana summit.
r: NAM was founded in 1961 at Belgrade.

q: What is the length of the Canada-United States border? (12)
f: The border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles), the longest international land border in the world.
r: Note that 5,525 is the length in miles, not kilometres.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam become president of the All India Muslim League for the first time? (12)
f: Jinnah was elected president of the Muslim League at the Lucknow session in December 1916. This was the session at which the Lucknow Pact was agreed.
r: He later served as president again in the 1920s and 1930s and led the League until Pakistan was created.

q: Who among the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (31)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law, having married Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

q: Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan? (39)
f: After the death of Quaid-e-Azam in September 1948, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor General of Pakistan. He held the post until 1951.
r: Nazimuddin was followed as Governor General by Malik Ghulam Muhammad in 1951.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha? (34)
f: Waris Shah wrote the best known version of Heer in 1766.
r: Earlier versions of the story were written by Damodar Gulati.

q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have? (40)
f: The permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each holding veto power.
r: Russia took the Soviet Union's seat in 1991 and China's seat passed from Taiwan to the PRC in 1971.

q: In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Madinah? (18)
f: The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH on the advice of Salman Farsi. It stopped the Quraysh and their allies from attacking the city.
r: The Battle of Khandaq is also called the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab).

q: Which is the highest pass of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks? (29)
f: Khunjerab Pass, at about 4,693 m on the Pakistan-China border, is the highest pass usually cited for Pakistan.
r: Sources differ because some lists name Mintaka Pass, also on the China border, as slightly higher; Khunjerab is the highest paved international border crossing.

q: Which word is a synonym of wild? (194)
f: Wild means living or growing in nature, not controlled by humans, which is untamed. The other options are its opposites.
r: Its antonym is tame or domesticated.

q: What was Fatima Jinnah's profession? (62)
f: Fatima Jinnah trained as a dentist and qualified from the University of Calcutta in 1923. She ran her own dental clinic in Bombay.
r: She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation) and contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.

q: In which district is the Khewra salt mine located? (35)
f: The Khewra salt mine is in Jhelum district, Punjab, in the Salt Range.
r: It is among the largest salt mines in the world.

q: Who was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025, succeeding Ali Amin Gandapur? (145)
f: Sohail Afridi of PTI was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025.
r: Since 11 October 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under governor's rule (Governor Faisal Karim Kundi), so the province has no sitting Chief Minister at the moment. In 2021-22 the answer was Mahmood Khan.

q: What is one tenth of 120? (75)
f: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place left, so 120 becomes 12.
r: One tenth is the same as 10%.

q: In which year did Pakistan join SEATO? (322)
f: Pakistan joined the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in 1954 when the Manila Pact was signed in September 1954.
r: Some sources give 1955 (ratification), and Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (CENTO) in 1955.

q: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed? (171)
f: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru, with the World Bank as a party.
r: It gave Pakistan the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers.

q: In which year was the Nehru Report presented? (73)
f: The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru, was presented in 1928.
r: Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed? (231)
f: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963.
r: It settled the border in the Karakoram region and led to the Karakoram Highway cooperation.

q: What is the currency of Armenia? (9)
f: Armenia uses the dram.
r: Georgia uses the lari and Azerbaijan the manat.

q: What is the currency of Azerbaijan? (11)
f: Azerbaijan uses the Azerbaijani manat.
r: Turkmenistan also uses a currency called the manat.

q: What is the currency of Bangladesh? (48)
f: Bangladesh uses the taka.
r: Pakistan, India and Nepal use rupees, while Bhutan uses the ngultrum.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab? (193)
f: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024.
r: She is the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab; her predecessor in 2021-22 was Usman Buzdar.

q: Who was the first Governor General of independent India in 1947? (19)
f: Lord Mountbatten became Governor General of the Dominion of India on 15 August 1947.
r: Sources differ because Warren Hastings and William Bentinck are also called the first Governor General in earlier British India, but for 1947 it is Mountbatten.

q: Who wrote the novel Raja Gidh? (19)
f: Bano Qudsia wrote Raja Gidh, a novel about the concept of haram and halal food and its effect on the mind.
r: She was married to the writer Ashfaq Ahmed.

q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (66)
f: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
r: At about 4693 m it is among the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (38)
f: Hazrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib was a sister of Hazrat Hamza and thus a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: She was the mother of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).

q: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of which prophet? (81)
f: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), who was born without a father by Allah's command.
r: Surah Maryam, the 19th surah of the Quran, is named after her.

q: How many daughters did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) have? (119)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA).
r: All of his daughters except Hazrat Fatima (RA) died during his lifetime.

q: How many non-permanent members does the UN Security Council have? (21)
f: The Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
r: Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.

q: In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam? (34)
f: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH (629 CE), before the conquest of Makkah. Some sources give 7 AH, so sources differ, but 8 AH is the common textbook answer.
r: He was later given the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

q: On which prophet was the Injeel (Bible) revealed? (33)
f: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S). Zabur was given to Dawood, Taurat to Musa and the Quran to Muhammad.
r: Hazrat Isa (A.S) is also known as Ruhullah.

q: On which river is Simly Dam (Simla Dam) built? (8)
f: Simly Dam near Islamabad is an earthen dam on the Soan River. It supplies water to Islamabad.
r: It was completed in 1983; Khanpur Dam, by contrast, is on the Haro River.

q: What is the value of sin 90 degrees? (32)
f: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1) and sine is the y-coordinate, which equals 1.
r: The value of cos 90 degrees is 0.

q: On what date was the Nehru Report presented? (67)
f: The Nehru Report was presented at the All Parties Conference at Lucknow on 28 August 1928.
r: Motilal Nehru headed the committee that prepared it.

q: What is the largest district of Pakistan by area? (104)
f: Chagai in Balochistan covers about 44,748 square km, the largest district of Pakistan by area.
r: Chagai is where Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998 (Ras Koh hills).

q: Who was the first child to accept Islam? (63)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA), the cousin of the Prophet, accepted Islam as a boy of about 10 years old. He was raised in the Prophet's household.
r: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man to accept Islam.

q: Which is the biggest sea of the world by area? (20)
f: The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square km, the largest sea in the world. The South China Sea is about 3.5 million square km.
r: The Arabian Sea is the largest of the other options and lies next to Pakistan's coast.

q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of a Jewish leader? (19)
f: Hazrat Safiyya bint Huyayy was from the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir and married the Prophet (PBUH) after Khaybar.
r: She accepted Islam before the marriage.

q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan? (131)
f: Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.
r: Muhammad Munir succeeded him as Chief Justice in 1954.

q: Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan? (156)
f: The lyrics of Qaumi Tarana were written by the poet Abul Asar Hafeez Jalandhari. It was officially adopted in 1954.
r: The music of the national anthem was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla.

q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup? (52)
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
r: Pakistan is the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Jafar Tayyar (RA) martyred? (29)
f: Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) was one of the three commanders martyred in the Battle of Mutah in 8 AH. He is called Tayyar (the flyer) because he is said to have been given wings in Paradise.
r: The other two commanders at Mutah were Zaid bin Haritha and Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA).

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit America? (26)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the United States in May 1950, the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
r: His visit came after he chose Washington over an invitation from Moscow.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (162)
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
r: The Khyber Pass is about 53 km long and has been an invasion and trade route for centuries.

q: The Dorah Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (11)
f: The Dorah Pass lies on the Chitral border and leads from Pakistan into Afghanistan (Badakhshan).
r: Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the Pakistani side of the Dorah Pass.

q: Hazrat Hajra (Hajar) was the mother of which prophet? (55)
f: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ismail (AS).
r: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates her search for water.

q: How many original members did the United Nations have when it was founded in 1945? (37)
f: The UN began in 1945 with 51 original member states (Poland signed later and is counted among them).
r: The UN now has 193 members.

q: How many planets are there in the solar system? (69)
f: There are eight planets since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
r: The planets in order from the Sun start with Mercury and end with Neptune.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points? (131)
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim League reply to the Nehru Report.
r: They demanded safeguards for Muslims such as separate electorates and a federal system.

q: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan are famous players of which sport? (62)
f: Both Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan of Pakistan were world champions in squash.
r: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times in a row and Jansher Khan won the World Open eight times.

q: On which prophet was the Zabur (Psalms) revealed? (37)
f: The Zabur was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).
r: Hazrat Sulaiman (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (A.S).

q: What causes swine flu? (8)
f: Swine flu is caused by influenza A viruses, most notably the H1N1 strain.
r: The 2009 H1N1 pandemic was declared by the WHO in June 2009.

q: What is the capital of Austria? (215)
f: Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria. Canberra is the capital of Australia, not Austria.
r: Austria and Australia are often confused because of their similar names.

q: What is the capital of Bulgaria? (11)
f: Sofia is the capital and largest city of Bulgaria.
r: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.

q: What is the largest river of Pakistan? (185)
f: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan.
r: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

q: What is the length of the Suez Canal? (69)
f: The Suez Canal is about 193 km, which is roughly 120 miles.
r: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and opened in 1869.

q: Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world? (27)
f: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
r: Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer.

q: Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world? (72)
f: China produces more tea than any other country, with India second.
r: Kenya and Sri Lanka are the next major producers.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by surface area? (10)
f: Lake Superior in North America has a surface area of about 82,000 square kilometres, the largest among freshwater lakes.
r: Lake Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake and holds the most fresh water by volume.

q: Which woman accepted Islam first? (84)
f: Hazrat Khadija (R.A), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.
r: Hazrat Sumayya was the first martyr of Islam.

q: Who was the first president of the All India Muslim League? (25)
f: Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was the first president of the All India Muslim League, founded in Dhaka in 1906.
r: The League was founded at Dhaka during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

q: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'? (156)
f: 'Friends Not Masters: A Political Autobiography' was written by Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan. It was published in 1967.
r: Ayub Khan was Pakistan's second President and ruled from 1958 to 1969.

q: Zakat is which pillar of Islam? (7)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj, so Zakat is third.
r: Candidates wrote 4, but in the standard order Zakat comes third.

q: A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what? (278)
f: Snakes have no external ears and cannot hear airborne sound well; they sense ground vibrations instead.
r: Bats find their way by echolocation using high-pitched sounds.

q: What type of government was set up by the 1962 constitution of Pakistan? (75)
f: The 1962 constitution concentrated executive power in the President, so it created a presidential form of government.
r: The 1973 constitution replaced it with a parliamentary system.

q: How many member states does the European Union (EU) have? (52)
f: The EU has 27 member states, and the number has not changed since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020.
r: Before Brexit the EU had 28 members; Croatia was the last to join, in 2013.

q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located? (8)
f: The Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
r: Mian Mir is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple at Amritsar at the invitation of Guru Arjan.

q: In which month did the 1965 Pakistan-India war take place and how long did it last? (14)
f: The war began on 6 September 1965 when India crossed the international border at Lahore, and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
r: Pakistan celebrates 6 September every year as Defence Day.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress? (33)
f: Jinnah left Congress in 1920 over the Nagpur session and its non-cooperation policy.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: In which year was the Tashkent Agreement signed? (73)
f: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed on 10 January 1966 under Soviet mediation.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri.

q: Oil wrestling is the national sport of which country? (6)
f: Oil wrestling (Yagli Gures) is the national sport of Turkey.
r: The Kirkpinar festival in Edirne, Turkey, is the oldest wrestling competition in the world.

q: On which river is Warsak Dam built? (41)
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar.
r: Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.

q: Which is the fifth pillar of Islam? (39)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is fifth.
r: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able to afford it.

q: What is the capital of Azad Kashmir? (82)
f: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: Muzaffarabad lies at the confluence of the Jhelum and Neelum rivers.

q: What is the capital of Belarus? (31)
f: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
r: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.

q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan? (126)
f: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: Gilgit-Baltistan is home to K2, the second highest mountain in the world.

q: What is the capital of Ukraine? (52)
f: Kyiv (also spelled Kiev) is the capital of Ukraine.
r: Kyiv sits on the Dnieper river.

q: What is the currency of Egypt? (63)
f: Egypt uses the Egyptian pound.
r: Egypt controls the Suez Canal.

q: What is the currency of Indonesia? (7)
f: Indonesia uses the rupiah.
r: Malaysia uses the ringgit and Thailand the baht.

q: On what date was the Tashkent Agreement signed? (27)
f: India and Pakistan signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966, ending the 1965 war.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, who died in Tashkent the next day.

q: What is the largest lake of Europe? (21)
f: Lake Ladoga in Russia, about 17,700 square km, is the largest lake entirely within Europe.
r: The Caspian Sea is larger but is usually not counted as a European lake.

q: What is the largest river of Afghanistan? (14)
f: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km, is the longest river wholly within Afghanistan.
r: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border and is not entirely within Afghanistan.

q: What is the length of the Pakistan-India border (including the Line of Control and Working Boundary)? (11)
f: The combined length of the international boundary, Working Boundary and Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
r: The Radcliffe Line of 1947 defined the border between the two countries.

q: What is the national bird of Pakistan? (60)
f: The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
r: The Shaheen (falcon) is the national symbol of Pakistan's air force and a popular emblem, but not the national bird.

q: Which word is a synonym of attire? (7)
f: Attire means clothes or dress, so clothing is the synonym.
r: Another synonym of attire is apparel.

q: What is the title of Liaqat Ali Khan? (49)
f: Liaqat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was given the title Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
r: He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: In which year was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) founded? (39)
f: SAARC was founded at a summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The idea was proposed by Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.
r: SAARC has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located (on the Indus, in Mianwali district)? (13)
f: Kalabagh is in Mianwali district of Punjab, on the Indus near the boundary with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: The dam has never been built because of political opposition from some provinces.

q: Which country awards the Nobel Prizes (apart from the Peace Prize)? (13)
f: The Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature are awarded in Sweden, in line with Alfred Nobel's will.
r: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)? (10)
f: The SCO has ten full members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus. Turkey is only a dialogue partner.
r: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024; Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.

q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population? (80)
f: Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population (about 127 million in the 2023 census).
r: Sindh is the second most populous province.

q: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar? (22)
f: The Islamic year has twelve months and Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and last.
r: Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah and Muharram is the first month.

q: Which Sahabi married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum? (29)
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married Ruqayyah first and, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
r: He is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

q: Which was the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the first mosque of Islam in Madina? (17)
f: Masjid Quba was built by the Prophet (PBUH) on his arrival near Madina during the Hijrah.
r: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built soon afterwards in Madina.

q: Who is the current Chairman of NAB (National Accountability Bureau)? (99)
f: Lt Gen (retd) Nazir Ahmad became NAB chairman in 2023 and received a three-year extension from March 2026.
r: Earlier chairmen were Javed Iqbal (2017-22) and Aftab Sultan (2022-23).

q: Who is the President of Turkey? (13)
f: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.
r: The capital of Turkey is Ankara.

q: Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)? (9)
f: Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.
r: Their father Waleed bin Mughirah was a leader of the Banu Makhzum of Quraish.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal? (88)
f: The best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal is attributed to Fazal Shah (Sayyid Fazal Shah). Waris Shah is known for Heer Ranjha.
r: Sources differ on tellers of this tale, but Fazal Shah is the usual textbook answer.

q: A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes? (153)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed multiplied by time.

q: Which sea lies between Greece and Italy? (27)
f: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
r: The Aegean Sea lies east of Greece, between Greece and Turkey.

q: What is one third of 90? (51)
f: 90 divided by 3 is 30.
r: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

q: Which country is the second largest in the world by area? (48)
f: Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.
r: China and the United States follow closely as third and fourth.

q: According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected? (41)
o: By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
f: The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.
r: The Electoral College initially had 80,000 members, later raised to 120,000 (equally from East and West Pakistan).

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought? (112)
f: The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.
r: Hazrat Ali conquered the fort of Qamus in this battle.

q: Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country? (17)
f: Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.
r: Some candidates thought it was Egyptian, but it is Qatari.

q: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom? (43)
f: Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).
r: Her mother was Umm Ruman.

q: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom? (78)
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA).
r: The first written compilation of the Quran was kept with her during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA) and later.

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there? (29)
f: They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
r: Their combined rule lasted about 30 years (632 to 661 AD).

q: How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have? (45)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
r: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was born to Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq (AS) to Hazrat Sarah.

q: In which Ghazwa were the blessed teeth of the Prophet (PBUH) martyred? (42)
f: The Prophet's (PBUH) front tooth was broken and he was wounded in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
r: The Battle of Uhud took place near Mount Uhud close to Madinah.

q: In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed? (36)
f: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraysh in Dhul Qadah 6 AH (628 CE).
r: The Quran calls it a clear victory (Fath-e-Mubin) in Surah Al-Fath.

q: In which province is Khanpur Dam located? (18)
f: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: In which year did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina? (47)
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 AD, the 13th year of prophethood.
r: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)? (12)
f: Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.
r: The OIC was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die? (27)
f: Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.
r: He is buried at Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.

q: Kaleemullah is the title of which prophet? (78)
f: Kaleemullah means the one who spoke with Allah, the title of Hazrat Musa (A.S).
r: The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (A.S).

q: Which organism causes malaria? (19)
f: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, spread to humans by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
r: The deadliest malaria parasite is Plasmodium falciparum.

q: What is the area of Punjab (Pakistan) in square kilometres? (19)
f: Punjab covers about 205,344 square kilometres.
r: Punjab is the second largest province by area but the largest by population.

q: What is the capital of Chile? (7)
f: Santiago is the capital of Chile.
r: Valparaiso, where the national congress sits, is a major port city but not the capital.

q: What is the meaning of the word alter? (19)
f: To alter means to change something or make it different.
r: The related noun is alteration, meaning a change.

q: What is the currency of Cuba? (7)
f: Cuba uses the Cuban peso (CUP).
r: Cuba formerly had a second currency, the convertible peso (CUC), which was abolished in 2021.

q: What is the currency of Russia? (99)
f: Russia uses the ruble.
r: Ukraine uses the hryvnia and Kazakhstan the tenge.

q: On what date did the War of Independence of the Subcontinent begin? (9)
f: The 1857 War of Independence began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
r: The British call it the Sepoy Mutiny.

q: On what date did the Chauri Chaura incident happen? (48)
f: A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh on 4 February 1922.
r: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after this incident.

q: Which is the highest plateau in the world? (12)
f: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 m above sea level and is called the Roof of the World.
r: The Pamir region is also known as the Roof of the World.

q: What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket? (19)
f: The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.
r: The maximum width of the blade is 4.25 inches.

q: What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan? (119)
f: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.
r: It is shared between Sindh (about 270 km) and Balochistan (about 770 km).

q: What is the national tree of Pakistan? (22)
f: The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.
r: Its name comes from Sanskrit and means timber of the gods.

q: What is the relation of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) with Hazrat Ismail (AS)? (54)
f: Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).
r: Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra and Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (49)
f: Abdul Muttalib was the father of Abdullah, the Prophet's father, so he was the paternal grandfather. He looked after the Prophet after the death of his mother Hazrat Amina.
r: Abdul Muttalib was the chief of Quraysh and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

q: What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel? (78)
f: Ababeel is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,200 km, as announced by ISPR after its first test.
r: Ababeel is stated to have MIRV (multiple warhead) capability and was first tested in January 2017.

q: Which word is a synonym of evident? (7)
f: Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.
r: Another synonym is apparent.

q: Which word is a synonym of prevalent? (5)
f: Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.
r: Its opposite is rare or uncommon.

q: What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab? (68)
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
r: The National Assembly has 336 seats, of which Punjab has 141 general seats.

q: Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded? (7)
f: The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.
r: The failed invasion took place during the presidency of John F. Kennedy and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy? (106)
f: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.
r: Pakistan has won the Champions Trophy only once; India won the 2025 edition.

q: In which year did Swat merge fully into Pakistan? (80)
f: Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.
r: Swat is now part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

q: In which year was the first constitution of Pakistan enforced? (29)
f: The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
r: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day until the 1962 constitution replaced it.

q: In which province is Manchar Lake located? (26)
f: Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.
r: It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located? (15)
f: The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.
r: It is famous for its blue tile work and for having no minarets.

q: Which country was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet? (15)
f: Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.
r: The JF-17 is jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

q: Which is the largest country in the world by area? (93)
f: Russia covers about 17.1 million square km, more than any other country.
r: Canada is the second largest country by area.

q: Which is the month of Allah (Shahrullah) in the Islamic calendar? (11)
f: Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.
r: Some sources also apply the title Shahrullah to Muharram or Rajab, so sources differ.

q: Which is the outermost planet of the solar system? (5)
f: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
r: Pluto was considered the ninth planet until 2006.

q: Which is the smallest continent? (96)
f: Australia (Oceania) has an area of about 7.7 million square km, the smallest of the continents.
r: Australia is the only continent that is also a single country.

q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly? (102)
f: Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.
r: He is also called Dhun-Nun and Surah Younus is named after him.

q: Who was the first man to embrace Islam? (46)
f: Among adult free men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first to accept Islam.
r: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child to accept Islam.

q: Who inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan? (17)
f: Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.
r: The first governor of the State Bank was Zahid Hussain.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh? (208)
f: Syed Murad Ali Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party has been Chief Minister of Sindh since 2016 and won a third consecutive term in 2024.
r: He succeeded Qaim Ali Shah, who had held the post from 2008 to 2016.

q: Who is the national poet of Pakistan? (7)
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.
r: His birthday, 9 November, is observed as Iqbal Day.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest? (80)
f: Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1999 as the first Pakistani to do so.
r: Samina Baig became the first Pakistani woman to climb Everest in 2013.

q: Who wrote the book Das Kapital? (56)
f: Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism, was written by the German thinker Karl Marx. The first volume appeared in 1867.
r: Friedrich Engels edited and published the second and third volumes after Marx died.

q: Who wrote The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam? (7)
f: Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.
r: It was first published in 1930 and expanded in 1934.

q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you (taking me as male)? (55)
f: My brother's sister is my sister, so your mother is my sister. I am therefore your mother's brother, that is your maternal uncle.
r: A mother's brother is called mamu in Urdu, and a father's brother is called chacha.

q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 120? (19)
r: Taking 1/3 of 1/10 is the same as taking 1/30 of the number.

q: Who was the commander of the Muslim army in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk? (33)
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk (9 AH) was a campaign in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army of about 30,000. A Ghazwa is by definition a battle in which the Prophet personally took part.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) was left in charge of Madina during the Tabuk expedition.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan? (83)
f: Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally regarded as Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.
r: Keenjhar Lake near Thatta is the second largest and a major drinking water source for Karachi.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed? (43)
f: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916. It was an agreement in which the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam was the main architect of the pact and was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (37)
f: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%.
r: The absent students are 200, which is 13.33%.

q: What is one tenth of 90? (34)
f: 90 divided by 10 is 9.
r: One tenth of a number is the same as 10% of it.

q: Abdul Qadir was a famous player of which sport? (11)
f: Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.
r: Abdul Qadir played 67 Tests for Pakistan and died in 2019.

q: The Khilafat Movement started after which event? (11)
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.
r: Its leaders included Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali.

q: Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi? (79)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.
r: Khalid bin Waleed is known as Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

q: Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place? (91)
f: The Bolan Pass is a natural route in Balochistan linking Quetta with the plains of Sibi and Dadhar.
r: Khojak Pass, not Bolan, links Quetta with Chaman and Afghanistan.

q: From which institution did Quaid-e-Azam obtain his law degree? (7)
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.
r: He was the youngest Indian to be called to the bar at that time.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of ghusl are there (Hanafi fiqh)? (27)
f: The three faraiz of ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.
r: The faraiz of wudu are four in Hanafi fiqh.

q: How many Makki surahs are there in the Quran? (41)
f: Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.
r: Sources differ slightly on the exact numbers, but 86 and 28 are the figures most Pakistani textbooks give.

q: How many seats of the National Assembly of Pakistan are reserved for women? (85)
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.
r: Another 10 seats are reserved for non-Muslims.

q: In which city of India is Jallianwala Bagh located? (18)
f: Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden in Amritsar, Punjab, India. British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd there on 13 April 1919.
r: The massacre took place on Baisakhi day in 1919.

q: In which country were the Olympic Games postponed from 2020 and held in 2021 hosted? (22)
f: The Tokyo Olympics, scheduled for 2020, were postponed because of Covid-19 and held in Japan in July-August 2021.
r: The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris in 2024.

q: In which Hijri year did the tragedy of Karbala take place? (20)
f: The martyrdom of Hazrat Hussain (RA) at Karbala took place on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE).
r: Yazid ibn Muawiya was the Umayyad ruler at that time.

q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered? (44)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
r: The conquest followed the Quraysh breaking the Treaty of Hudaibiya.

q: In which language did Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai write poetry? (64)
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.
r: His famous collection of poetry is called Shah Jo Risalo.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Azha celebrated? (16)
f: Eid ul Azha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
r: Eid ul Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

q: In which Islamic month was the Quran first revealed? (20)
f: The Quran began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on Laylat ul Qadr, in the cave of Hira.
r: The first revealed verses are the opening of Surah Al-Alaq.

q: In which province is Keenjhar Lake located? (7)
f: Keenjhar Lake is near Thatta in Sindh.
r: Keenjhar is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan and a main water source for Karachi.

q: In which year did India carry out its first nuclear test? (57)
f: India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.
r: India carried out further tests, Pokhran-II, in May 1998.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Khyber (Khaybar) fought? (54)
f: The Battle of Khaybar was fought in 7 AH (628 AD) against the Jewish fortresses of Khaybar.
r: Hazrat Ali is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus in this battle.

q: Riyadh is the capital of which country? (70)
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
r: Saudi Arabia hosts the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah.

q: Safiullah is the title of which prophet? (56)
f: Safiullah means the chosen one of Allah and is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).
r: Other titles: Khalilullah for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Ruhullah for Isa (A.S).

q: Tirana is the capital of which country? (4)
f: Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania in the Balkans.
r: Albania's neighbours include Greece, North Macedonia, Kosovo and Montenegro.

q: Tripoli is the capital of which country? (4)
f: Tripoli is the capital of Libya on the Mediterranean coast of North Africa.
r: There is also a city named Tripoli in Lebanon, but it is not the capital.

q: Turkey is surrounded by the Aegean Sea, the Black Sea and which other sea? (4)
f: Turkey has the Black Sea to the north, the Aegean to the west and the Mediterranean to the south.
r: The Sea of Marmara lies entirely within Turkey and links the Black and Aegean Seas.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) does Hajj have according to the Hanafi school? (22)
f: The three faraiz are Ihram, standing at Arafat (Wuquf) and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.
r: Schools of thought differ slightly in counting Hajj faraiz, but the Hanafi count of three is common in Pakistani textbooks.

q: What does PEMRA stand for? (14)
o: Pakistan Education and Media Regulatory Authority
f: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, which regulates TV and radio broadcasting.
r: PEMRA was established in 2002.

q: What does POF stand for? (9)
f: POF stands for Pakistan Ordnance Factories, which make arms and ammunition.
r: POF is headquartered at Wah Cantt.

q: What is observed on 8 March every year? (7)
f: 8 March is International Women's Day, celebrating women's achievements and rights.
r: International Labour Day is on 1 May.

q: What is Pakistan's rank in the world by population (2026)? (45)
f: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, the United States and Indonesia.
r: Pakistan's population is estimated at over 250 million and may overtake Indonesia by around 2050.

q: What is sin X divided by cos X equal to? (23)
f: By definition, tan X equals sin X over cos X.
r: The reciprocal, cos X over sin X, is cot X.

q: What is the product of the three cube roots of unity? (40)
f: The cube roots of unity are 1, w and w squared, and w cubed equals 1. Their product is 1 x w x w squared = w cubed = 1.
r: The sum of the three cube roots of unity is 0.

q: What is the currency of Turkey? (40)
f: Turkey uses the Turkish lira.
r: Istanbul, the largest Turkish city, is not the capital; Ankara is.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present his Fourteen Points? (26)
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at Delhi in March 1929, answering the Nehru Report.
r: The Fourteen Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, such as separate electorates and one third seats in the central legislature.

q: Which is the hottest city of Pakistan? (29)
f: Jacobabad in Sindh regularly records the highest temperatures in Pakistan, often over 50 degrees Celsius.
r: Jacobabad is among the hottest inhabited places on Earth.

q: What is the integration of 1 with respect to x? (12)
f: The derivative of x is 1, so the integral of 1 dx is x + C.
r: The constant C is the constant of integration.

q: Which is the largest airport of Pakistan by area? (37)
f: Islamabad International Airport opened in 2018 and is the largest in Pakistan by area (about 19 square km).
r: Karachi Jinnah International is the busiest airport, which is why candidates answered Karachi; sources can differ on what largest means.

q: What is the largest city of Punjab by population? (9)
f: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and its largest city.
r: Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.

q: What is the second pillar of Islam? (17)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Salah is the second.
r: Salah was made obligatory five times a day during the Night Journey (Miraj).

q: The Treaty of Versailles, which ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year? (6)
f: The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 at the Palace of Versailles in France.
r: It imposed heavy reparations on Germany and created the League of Nations.

q: What was the relation of Abu Talib with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (50)
f: Abu Talib was the son of Abdul Muttalib and a brother of the Prophet's father Abdullah. He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.
r: Abu Talib was the father of Hazrat Ali (RA) and protected the Prophet during the early years in Makkah.

q: What was the old (previous) name of Makkah mentioned in the Holy Quran? (41)
f: The Holy Quran (Surah Al-Imran, verse 96) calls the place of the first house of worship Bakkah, which is an old name of Makkah. It was also known as Umm al-Qura.
r: Yathrib was the old name of Madina, not Makkah.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC T20 World Cup? (10)
f: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the final at Lord's in 2009 under captain Younis Khan. It is their only T20 World Cup title.
r: Pakistan were runners-up in 2007 and 2022; India won the 2024 and 2026 editions.

q: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madina take place, marking the start of the Hijri calendar? (15)
f: The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which is 1 AH. The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from this event.
r: The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar and its first month is Muharram.

q: Between which two parties was the Lucknow Pact signed? (23)
o: Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Khaksar movement
f: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. Both parties agreed to a joint demand for self-government.
r: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Quaid-e-Azam were the main leaders involved in making the pact.

q: In which city was the OIC established at the first Islamic summit in 1969? (28)
f: The first Islamic summit, which created the OIC, was held at Rabat in Morocco in 1969. Jeddah is the permanent headquarters of the OIC, not the place of its founding.
r: The Islamic Summit held in Lahore in 1974 was the second summit of the OIC.

q: In which country is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj? (4)
f: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia.
r: Pilgrims stone the Jamarat (pillars symbolising Satan) at Mina during Hajj.

q: In which province is Ranikot (Rani Fort) located? (6)
f: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills near Sann in Jamshoro district, Sindh.
r: It is often called the Great Wall of Sindh because of its long walls.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters? (25)
f: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.
r: The main naval base and Fleet Command are at Karachi.

q: Where is the shrine of Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar? (4)
f: Baba Farid Ganj Shakar is buried in Pakpattan, Punjab.
r: He was a major Chishti Sufi saint of the 12th and 13th centuries.

q: Which country hosted the first Football World Cup in 1930? (30)
f: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.
r: Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.

q: Which is the biggest province of Pakistan by area? (26)
f: Balochistan covers about 347,000 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan.
r: Punjab is the largest province by population.

q: Which SAARC country has the highest literacy rate? (4)
f: The Maldives has a literacy rate of about 98 to 99 percent, the highest among SAARC countries, with Sri Lanka close behind.
r: Afghanistan and Pakistan are among the lowest in SAARC for literacy.

q: Which Sahabi served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years? (33)
f: Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet as a servant at Madina as a boy and served him for about ten years.
r: He narrated over 2,000 hadiths.

q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan? (117)
f: The national flag was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kedwaii on the basis of the Muslim League flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947.
r: The green part of the flag stands for the Muslim majority and the white strip for minorities.

q: Who gave the name Pakistan? (53)
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
r: Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

q: Who is the President of Iran? (81)
f: Masoud Pezeshkian won the 2024 snap election and took office in July 2024.
r: His predecessor Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in May 2024.

q: Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider? (39)
f: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas was only 20 when he died in 1971 stopping a traitor pilot, and got the award.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

q: Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942? (6)
f: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call Do or Die.
r: The Muslim League opposed the movement.

q: Who rebuilt the Holy Kaaba with his son? (28)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) rebuilt the Kaaba with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS).
r: The Quraysh also rebuilt it before the Prophet's prophethood, and the Prophet (PBUH) placed the Black Stone.

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army? (17)
f: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948.
r: Douglas Gracey succeeded him, and Ayub Khan was the first native Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951.

q: Who was the world's first woman Prime Minister? (4)
f: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Sri Lanka became the world's first woman Prime Minister in 1960.
r: Indira Gandhi became India's Prime Minister in 1966.

q: Who was the President of the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan? (19)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.
r: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan later served as its Speaker.

q: Which team won the cricket World Cup in 1999? (6)
f: Australia beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the 1999 final at Lord's.
r: Pakistan was the runner-up in 1999 and champion in 1992.

q: A man going towards north turns left after some time, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing? (82)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
r: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

q: What is one third of 10% of 120? (54)
f: 10% of 120 is 12, and one third of 12 is 4.
r: One third of one tenth equals 1/30, so the answer is 120/30.

q: What is 90% of 70? (6)
r: To find 90% of a number, subtract one tenth of it from the number.

q: What is the derivative of a constant? (9)
f: A constant does not change as x changes, so its rate of change is zero.
r: The derivative of x with respect to x is 1.

q: Which one is different from the others: monkey, panda, baboon, chimpanzee? (188)
f: Monkey, baboon and chimpanzee are primates, while the panda is a bear.
r: Giant pandas feed mainly on bamboo.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution? (31)
f: The 1956 Constitution declared the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, ending its dominion status.
r: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, now celebrated as Pakistan Day.

q: Under the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by: (29)
o: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
f: The 1956 Constitution provided for the President to be elected by the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
r: Iskander Mirza became the first President under this Constitution.

q: In whose house in Madinah did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat? (38)
f: The Prophet's camel Qaswa knelt near the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (Khalid bin Zayd), and he stayed there until his own quarters and mosque were built.
r: Abu Ayyub Ansari died during the Muslim siege of Constantinople and is buried near its walls.

q: In which battle was the tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) broken? (32)
f: The Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded on the face during the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH, after the archers left their post.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Madinah in March 625 CE.

q: In which year did the United Nations come into being? (44)
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding members.
r: United Nations Day is observed every year on 24 October.

q: With which wife of the Prophet (PBUH) was the compiled copy of the Quran kept after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected? (20)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Quran compiled in book form; it passed to Hazrat Umar (RA) and then was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA), the Prophet's wife. Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare copies.
r: Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) led the compilation team under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record of the fastest century in ODIs (37 balls, 1996)? (9)
f: New Zealand's Corey Anderson scored a century off 36 balls against the West Indies in January 2014 and broke Afridi's 17-year-old record.
r: AB de Villiers later broke Anderson's record with a 31-ball century against the West Indies in January 2015, and it still stands.

q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (45)
f: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 90 x 1/5 = 18 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

q: In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located? (103)
f: The Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the walled city of Lahore. It was built in 1634-35 in the Mughal era.
r: It is famous for its Kashi tile work.

q: On which river is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built? (69)
f: The Diamer Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River in Gilgit-Baltistan, near Chilas.
r: Tarbela Dam is also on the Indus River.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) with Hazrat Abdul Muttalib? (4)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, and Abu Talib was a son of Abdul Muttalib. So Hazrat Ali was his grandson.
r: Abdul Muttalib was also the grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), which made the two cousins.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China? (166)
f: The Khunjerab Pass in the Karakoram links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang in China.
r: At about 4,693 m it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built? (38)
f: Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.
r: Its foundation stone was laid in 1973 and production began in 1981.

q: In which district is Khanpur Dam located? (11)
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River near Khanpur town in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and was completed in 1983.

q: In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born? (39)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, taken as 570 AD in Pakistani textbooks.
r: Some sources give 571 AD.

q: After how many years of independence did Pakistan get its first constitution? (116)
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, nearly 9 years later.
r: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day, and the 1956 constitution was abrogated in 1958 by Ayub Khan.

q: At what age (approximately) did the last revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (17)
f: Revelation began when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 and continued for about 23 years, so the last revelation came at about age 63.
r: Most scholars say the last verses were revealed a few weeks before his death at 63.

q: Boris Johnson served as Prime Minister (2019-2022) of which country? (3)
f: Boris Johnson led the Conservative Party and was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from July 2019 to September 2022.
r: He is no longer in office, having resigned in 2022 and been followed by Liz Truss.
