r: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, close to Madinah, in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: On what date did the Australian cricketer Shane Warne die? (10)
f: Shane Warne died of a suspected heart attack in Koh Samui, Thailand, on 4 March 2022 at the age of 52.
r: Warne took 708 wickets in Test cricket, a record for a leg-spinner.

q: The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed after which war? (24)
f: After the 1971 war and the separation of East Pakistan, Pakistan and India met at Shimla in 1972 and signed the agreement.
r: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 war.

q: One degree of an angle is equal to how many minutes? (11)
f: A degree is divided into 60 minutes, and a minute into 60 seconds.
r: A full circle measures 360 degrees.

q: Who was the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan? (22)
f: Shamshad Akhtar became the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2005.
r: She later served as Caretaker Finance Minister in 2023.

q: In how many years was the revelation of the Holy Quran completed? (19)
f: The Quran was revealed gradually to the Prophet (PBUH) over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Hira until shortly before his death.
r: About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.

q: In which year was the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) established? (22)
f: ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
r: RCD (Regional Cooperation for Development) was formed in 1964.

q: On what date did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start? (21)
f: The Pakistan Army launched Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad on 22 February 2017 against terrorism after a wave of attacks. It was a nationwide operation.
r: Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 was an earlier operation in North Waziristan.

q: In which year was the film Jinnah, on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released? (28)
f: The film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998.
r: It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.

q: Which city is known as the City of Gold? (32)
f: Johannesburg in South Africa is called the City of Gold because it grew after gold was discovered in the Witwatersrand in 1886.
r: South Africa has long been one of the largest gold producers in the world, though sources differ on later rankings.

q: Which plant is commonly named as the fastest growing plant (tree) in the world? (9)
f: Some bamboo species can grow almost one metre in a single day, which is why bamboo is commonly named the fastest growing plant.
r: Bamboo is technically a grass, and the Paulownia is often called the fastest growing true tree, so sources differ.

q: Habba Khatoon was a famous poet of which language? (31)
f: Habba Khatoon (Zoon) was a 16th century Kashmiri poet known for her lyrical songs.
r: She is often called the Nightingale of Kashmir.

q: About what percentage of Antarctica is covered by ice? (9)
f: About 98 percent of Antarctica is covered by an ice sheet, and only about 2 percent is bare rock. Some sources give 97.6 or 99 percent.
r: The ice sheet is on average about 2 km thick.

q: On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed? (13)
f: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 15 March as International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC.
r: 15 March was chosen as the anniversary of the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks.

q: Who is the Pakistani Nobel Prize winner in Physics, and how many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize in Physics? (16)
f: Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory. He is the only Pakistani to win a Nobel in Physics.
r: Pakistan's other Nobel laureate is Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city of Afghanistan? (36)
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul through the Torkham border crossing and Jalalabad.
r: The pass lies in the Safed Koh range.

q: What is the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census? (44)
f: The 2023 digital census recorded Pakistan's population as about 241.49 million.
r: The 2017 census had recorded about 207.7 million, and candidates in 2022 used estimates of about 220 million.

q: Which was the first private television channel of Pakistan? (23)
f: Shalimar Television Network, which began in 1990 as People's Television Network, was the first channel to break the monopoly of state-run PTV. It is the answer most textbooks give.
r: Sources differ on the word private: ARY Digital (2001) and Indus TV (2000) are often called the first fully independent channels.

q: Who was the first poet of the Punjabi language? (26)
f: Hazrat Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (1188-1266) is regarded as the first poet of Punjabi, and his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.
r: His shrine is in Pakpattan.

q: A quadratic equation is an equation of which degree? (17)
f: The highest power of the variable in a quadratic equation is 2, so it is a second degree equation.
r: The general form is ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, where a is not 0.

q: In which year was SUPARCO, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established? (17)
f: SUPARCO was formally established on 16 September 1961 by an executive order, with Dr Abdus Salam as its first chairman.
r: Some sources trace a precursor committee to 1961 as well; candidate answers such as 1955 and 1959 are incorrect.

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper? (42)
f: 5 papers take 5 minutes, so 1 paper takes 5 / 5 = 1 minute.
r: A rate of 1 paper per minute means that 60 papers would take an hour.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of the students are absent (to two decimal places)? (9)
r: The percentage present is 86.67%, which together with 13.33% makes 100%.

q: According to the 1956 Constitution, what was the minimum age to become President of Pakistan? (44)
f: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim of not less than 40 years of age.
r: Some candidates remembered 45, but 40 is the age given in the Constitution of 1956.

q: Who dismissed (abrogated) the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan? (16)
f: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
r: The 1962 Constitution had lasted about seven years.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be? (21)
f: From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days. 15 days is 2 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be? (35)
f: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Tuesday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: At what age did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, die? (8)
f: He was born on 1 April 1936 and died on 10 October 2021, which makes him 85 years old.
r: He died in Islamabad and was buried in the H-8 graveyard.

q: What is the antonym of sublime? (13)
f: Sublime means of very high excellence or beauty, so its opposite is ridiculous or lowly.
r: Magnificent, grand and noble are close in meaning to sublime.

q: On which side of Pakistan does the Arabian Sea lie? (35)
f: Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km runs along the Arabian Sea in the south, in Sindh and Balochistan.
r: Iran and Afghanistan lie to the west, China to the north-east and India to the east.

q: In which province and city is the BRT (Zu Peshawar) transport system located? (10)
f: The BRT Zu Peshawar is a bus rapid transit system of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It serves the city of Peshawar.
r: Lahore has the Orange Line Metro Train and Metro Bus, which are different projects.

q: Which country is the current men's Hockey World Cup champion (2026 edition)? (8)
f: Germany beat Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026 in Wavre, Belgium, to retain the title.
r: Belgium won the 2018 World Cup, and Germany won in 2023; Pakistan has four titles, the same as Germany.

q: What is the derivative of sin x with respect to x? (21)
f: The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.
r: The derivative of cos x is -sin x.

q: In which year was the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) agreement signed and launched? (27)
f: CPEC was launched in April 2015 when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pakistan and agreements worth about 46 billion dollars were signed.
r: A preliminary MoU on the corridor had been signed in 2013 during the visit of Premier Li Keqiang, which is why some sources give 2013.

q: On which date was the Lahore Declaration signed by the prime ministers of Pakistan and India? (12)
f: Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore.
r: Months later the Kargil conflict broke out in 1999.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) came to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr? (25)
f: The Makkan army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were about 313.
r: In the Battle of Uhad the Makkan army was about 3000 strong.

q: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine? (8)
f: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
r: Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine.

q: Which country hosted the extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on the Afghan crisis in December 2021? (8)
f: Pakistan hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Islamabad on 19 December 2021 to discuss the Afghan humanitarian crisis.
r: The 47th regular CFM was held in Niamey, Niger, in November 2020.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Israel (as of October 2026, before the 27 October election)? (8)
f: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel's government since December 2022, and he is campaigning for the election due on 27 October 2026.
r: Candidates in 2022 wrote Naftali Bennett, who was PM from June 2021 to June 2022, followed by Yair Lapid.

q: Which country has the largest number of lakes in the world? (9)
f: Canada has the most lakes in the world, with several hundred thousand, more than the rest of the world combined by most estimates.
r: Finland is known as the land of a thousand lakes but has far fewer lakes than Canada.

q: Which is the longest river lying entirely within Afghanistan? (8)
f: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km long, is the longest river that flows wholly in Afghanistan.
r: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border with Central Asia, so it is not counted as entirely Afghan; some sources differ.

q: Whose motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline? (47)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah gave the motto Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem) to the nation.
r: It is the national motto of Pakistan.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: L, M, N, ? (19)
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, so O follows N.
r: L, M, N, O are the 12th to 15th letters of the alphabet.

q: Who is the chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)? (31)
f: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has been PPP chairman since 2007 and was re-elected in April 2025.
r: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the party.

q: Who started the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement? (13)
f: The Reshmi Rumal Tehreek was organised by Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi together with Shaikh-ul-Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan of Deoband. Secret messages were written on silk cloth to seek help against British rule.
r: The plot was discovered in 1916 and Maulana Mahmud Hasan was imprisoned in Malta.

q: The Suez Canal separates Africa from which continent? (17)
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates the African mainland from the Sinai Peninsula, which is part of Asia. It also joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
r: The canal was opened in 1869.

q: Under which Prime Minister was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan framed and enforced? (22)
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the constitution in 1956, and it came into force on 23 March 1956.
r: 23 March is the day later celebrated as Republic Day, and Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.

q: What is the antonym of applaud? (7)
f: To applaud is to show approval or praise, so its opposite is to criticize or condemn.
r: Praise, cheer and admire are synonyms of applaud.

q: Bashar al-Assad was the president of which country? (7)
f: Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until his government fell in December 2024.
r: He succeeded his father Hafez al-Assad, who ruled Syria from 1971 to 2000.

q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan? (9)
f: Zahid Hussain was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, appointed in 1948.
r: The bank was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam on 1 July 1948.

q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth? (19)
f: Temperature increases with depth, so the inner core is the hottest layer at around 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius.
r: The inner core is solid due to the immense pressure even though it is so hot.

q: Which country developed the Sinopharm vaccine against Covid-19? (7)
f: Sinopharm is a state-owned Chinese pharmaceutical company, and its BBIBP-CorV vaccine was developed in China.
r: Pakistan used the Chinese Sinopharm and CanSino vaccines in its Covid-19 vaccination drive.

q: What is the antonym of 'demise'? (8)
f: Demise means death or end, so its opposite is birth or beginning.
r: Death, end and collapse are all synonyms of demise.

q: Which desert is located in Sindh? (7)
f: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is in the Tharparkar region of Sindh and is the largest desert of Sindh.
r: Thar is also home to the largest coal reserves of Pakistan.

q: Completely is to what, as a synonym? Choose the word closest in meaning to 'entirely'. (12)
f: Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.
r: Wholly and totally are also synonyms.

q: Who is the President of Israel? (7)
f: Isaac Herzog was elected the 11th President of Israel in June 2021 and is still in office.
r: His predecessor was Reuven Rivlin, and the presidency is largely ceremonial.

q: How many members does SAARC have? (19)
f: SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
r: SAARC began in 1985 with seven founding members, and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

q: In which city is Mughalpura (famous for its railway workshops) located? (26)
f: Mughalpura is an area of Lahore and is known for its large railway workshops and station.
r: Lahore Junction is the main railway station of the city.

q: Which Sahabi narrated the largest number of Ahadith? (17)
f: Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) narrated about 5,374 Ahadith, the highest number among the Companions.
r: He is known as Abu Huraira, meaning father of the kitten.

q: NASA, the space agency, belongs to which country? (35)
f: NASA stands for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, a United States government agency.
r: NASA was founded in 1958 and landed the first humans on the Moon in 1969.

q: On which date did the partition of Bengal take effect? (22)
f: The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.
r: Muslims celebrated it, while Hindus observed the day as a day of mourning.

q: Which planet is nearest to the Sun? (34)
f: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km.
r: Mercury is also the smallest planet of the solar system.

q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 120? (13)
f: 1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.
r: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 120 divided by 12.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Russia? (8)
f: Mikhail Mishustin has been Prime Minister of Russia since January 2020, and he remains in office as of October 2026.
r: His predecessor as Prime Minister was Dmitry Medvedev.

q: How many senses do human beings have according to the traditional classification? (28)
f: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
r: Modern science recognises additional senses such as balance and body position awareness.

q: What is the antonym of 'tamed'? (61)
f: Tamed means made gentle and under control, so its opposite is wild or untamed.
r: Domesticated is a synonym of tamed.

q: After which event did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam? (14)
f: Khalid bin Waleed (RA), who fought against Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam after the Treaty of Hudaibiya in 7 AH.
r: He is known as Saifullah, the Sword of Allah.

q: The White House in Washington, D.C. is the official residence and workplace of whom? (8)
o: The President of the United States
The Chief Justice of the US
f: The White House is the official residence and main workplace of the President of the United States.
r: The official residence of the US Vice President is the Naval Observatory, not the White House.

q: Which President introduced the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan? (20)
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President and enforced the 1962 Constitution on 8 June 1962, framed by a commission headed by Justice Shahabuddin.
r: It introduced a presidential system with the President elected through Basic Democrats.

q: Which is the third largest city of Pakistan by population? (57)
f: By population Karachi is first, Lahore second and Faisalabad third, in both the 2017 and 2023 censuses.
r: Faisalabad was formerly called Lyallpur.

q: Which prophet confronted the king Namrood (Nimrod)? (32)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) invited Namrood to worship one Allah, and Namrood had him thrown into a fire, which Allah made cool.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun).

q: What is the antonym of autonomy? (8)
f: Autonomy means self-rule, so its opposite is dependence, being controlled by others.
r: Synonyms of autonomy include independence and self-government.

q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley. (32)
f: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains (cereals) eaten by people, while hay is dried grass kept as fodder for animals.
r: Wheat and rice are the two major food crops of Pakistan.

q: The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, Zu Peshawar, was built by which government? (11)
f: The Peshawar BRT was started in 2017 by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government under Chief Minister Pervez Khattak. It runs in Peshawar, the provincial capital.
r: The Peshawar BRT was formally inaugurated on 13 August 2020 and has a corridor of about 27.5 km.

q: What is the capital of China? (16)
f: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
r: Shanghai is China's largest city, but not its capital.

q: Who wrote the book 'The Conquest of Happiness'? (32)
f: The Conquest of Happiness (1930) was written by the British philosopher Bertrand Russell.
r: Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat ul Wida)? (12)
f: The Last Sermon was delivered in the valley of Uranah at the plain of Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
r: It was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah.

q: In which year was the Sui gas field in Balochistan discovered? (43)
f: Natural gas was discovered at Sui in Balochistan in 1952 and supply started in 1955.
r: Sui is the largest natural gas field of Pakistan by output historically.

q: Which country occupies the Golan Heights? (6)
f: Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the Six-Day War of 1967. It has held the area since then.
r: The Golan Heights overlook the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan valley.

q: In which year did the Urdu-Hindi controversy begin? (28)
f: The Urdu-Hindi controversy began in 1867 at Banaras (Varanasi), when Hindus demanded Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu.
r: The controversy led Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to conclude Hindus and Muslims could not progress together.

q: How many sugar mills did Pakistan have at the time of independence in 1947? (6)
f: Most colonial-era sugar mills lay on the Indian side of the border, and Pakistan inherited only two.
r: The first new sugar mill after independence was set up at Tando Muhammad Khan in Sindh in 1961.

q: Lat, Manat and Uzza were what? (16)
f: Lat, Manat and Uzza were the three chief idols worshipped by the pagan Arabs before Islam.
r: The Quran mentions them in Surah An-Najm.

q: Which is the latest confirmed fighter jet inducted by the Pakistan Air Force? (16)
f: The Chinese-made J-10C multirole fighter was inducted by the PAF in March 2022 and is the latest confirmed fighter type.
r: Reports about the Chinese J-35 stealth fighter for Pakistan remain unconfirmed.

q: Which type of medicine is used to relieve pain? (6)
f: Analgesics such as paracetamol and aspirin are painkillers. They reduce pain without making the person lose consciousness.
r: Anaesthetics are different because they cause loss of sensation before surgery.

q: In which city of Pakistan was the first Metro Bus service inaugurated? (7)
f: The Metro Bus Service was inaugurated in Lahore in February 2013. It runs between Gajju Matta and Shahdara.
r: Rawalpindi-Islamabad followed in 2015 and Multan in 2017.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.01? (6)
r: Zero has no multiplicative inverse.

q: Which elements are found in the first period of the periodic table? (10)
f: The first period has only one shell, which can hold two electrons, so it contains just hydrogen (H) and helium (He).
r: The second period begins with lithium and ends with neon.

q: By what other name is the Pakistan Resolution known? (35)
f: The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was passed at Lahore, so it is also called the Lahore Resolution. It demanded independent states for the Muslims of India.
r: The Allahabad Address of 1930 by Allama Iqbal first outlined the idea of a Muslim state.

q: What is the antonym of 'stagnant'? (6)
f: Stagnant means not flowing or moving, as in stagnant water. Its opposite is flowing.
r: Stagnant can also describe an economy that is not growing.

q: In football, what did BPL originally stand for in the English league? (6)
f: The English top division was sponsored by Barclays from 2001 to 2016 and was called the Barclays Premier League (BPL). Today it is simply the Premier League.
r: BPL also stands for the Bangladesh Premier League in cricket.

q: What does the word venerate mean? (6)
f: To venerate is to regard someone or something with deep respect and reverence. Its synonyms are revere and honour.
r: The adjective venerable describes a person worthy of great respect, often because of age or wisdom.

q: Which of the following vitamins is NOT water soluble? (12)
f: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.
r: Fat soluble vitamins can be stored in the body, while water soluble ones are mostly excreted.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km? (30)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.
r: His speed is 20 km in 100 minutes, which is 12 km per hour.

q: Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) at the time of independence in 1947? (13)
f: The ministry of Dr Khan Sahib, which belonged to the Indian National Congress (backed by the Khudai Khidmatgars), was in power in the province in August 1947.
r: The Governor dismissed the Khan Sahib ministry on 22 August 1947, and Abdul Qayyum Khan of the Muslim League then became Chief Minister.

q: For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought? (36)
f: The war began in early September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days. It is remembered as the 17-day war.
r: Pakistan celebrates 6 September as Defence Day in memory of the 1965 war.

q: In which year was the Mangla Dam completed? (17)
f: Construction of Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River began in the early 1960s and it was completed in 1967. Sources differ slightly on the start year but agree on 1967.
r: Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed later, in 1974.

q: Which battle of the Muslims, fought in 3 AH, is counted as the second major battle after Badr? (25)
f: The major battles in order are Badr (2 AH), Uhud (3 AH) and Khandaq (5 AH), so Uhud is the second.
r: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

q: Which prophet was sent to the nation (Qaum) of Aad? (11)
f: Allah sent Hazrat Hud (AS) to guide the people of Aad, who lived in Al-Ahqaf in southern Arabia.
r: Hazrat Salih (AS) was sent to the nation of Thamud.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 constitution of Pakistan? (43)
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
r: Ayub Khan, the army chief, removed Iskander Mirza only 20 days later.

q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (58)
f: His name was Abdullah bin Abi Quhafa, and he received the title Siddiq and Atiq.
r: Some narrations say his pre-Islamic name was Abd al-Kaba, which the Prophet (PBUH) changed to Abdullah.

q: SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field? (11)
f: SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.
r: It was founded in 1961.

q: How many votes in the 336-member National Assembly are needed to pass a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister? (6)
f: A no-confidence resolution needs a majority of the total membership of the House. Half of 336 is 168, so 169 votes are needed.
r: Article 95 of the Constitution deals with the vote of no confidence against the Prime Minister. The National Assembly had 342 seats before 2018.

q: What is cos(90 degrees - x) equal to? (9)
f: By the complementary angle identity, cos(90 - x) = sin x.
r: Similarly sin(90 - x) = cos x.

q: Which document paved the way for the constitution of Pakistan? (5)
f: The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.
r: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

q: In a village the population in 2000 was 4600 and it doubles every five years. What was the population in 1995? (5)
f: Going back five years halves the population: 4600 / 2 = 2300.
r: Population in 2005 would be 9200 at the same rate.

q: Which province of Pakistan was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)? (5)
f: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018, the first province to do so.
r: Punjab issued licences to 62 transgender drivers in June 2023.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960? (13)
f: Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.
r: The World Bank mediated the treaty.

q: How many doors (gates) does Jannah (Paradise) have according to hadith? (11)
f: Authentic hadith state that Paradise has eight gates, one of them being Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
r: Hell has seven gates.

q: What does FATF stand for? (26)
f: FATF is the Financial Action Task Force, an international body that sets standards against money laundering and terror financing.
r: Pakistan was placed on the FATF grey list in June 2018 and removed in October 2022.

q: Which woman is mentioned by name in the Quran? (26)
f: Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.
r: A complete Surah of the Quran, Surah Maryam, is named after her.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'forestall'? (6)
f: To forestall means to prevent something from happening by taking action ahead of time.
r: Forestall is often confused with forest but has no connection with trees.

q: Who sold the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh in 1846? (10)
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 7.5 million rupees.
r: Gulab Singh became the first Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Who was the first Hafiz of the Holy Quran? (56)
f: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it first, so he is called the first Hafiz.
r: Among the Companions, Hazrat Ali, Ubayy bin Kab and Zaid bin Thabit were also famous Huffaz.

q: Who issues an ordinance at the federal level in Pakistan? (16)
f: Under Article 89 of the 1973 Constitution, the President can promulgate an ordinance when the National Assembly is not in session.
r: Governors issue ordinances in the provinces when the provincial assembly is not in session.

q: In which year was Pakistan's first postage stamp issued? (18)
f: Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.
r: Before that, stamps of British India overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Uhud? (49)
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hazrat Hamza (RA).
r: In the Battle of Badr only 14 Muslims were martyred.

q: How many times did Jansher Khan win the World Open squash title? (10)
f: Jansher Khan won the World Open squash championship eight times between 1987 and 1996.
r: He also won the British Open six times, while Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times.

q: Who was the king (Najashi) of Habsha (Abyssinia) who gave shelter to the Muslim migrants? (8)
f: The Christian king of Abyssinia, known by the title Najashi (Negus), was Ashama ibn Abjar. He protected the early Muslims who migrated there.
r: Abraha was the Abyssinian governor of Yemen who marched against the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.

q: What does KRL stand for? (8)
f: KRL stands for Khan Research Laboratories, named after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan. It is located at Kahuta.
r: It was originally set up in 1976 as the Engineering Research Laboratories and renamed in 1981.

q: What is the legislature of Pakistan called? (21)
f: Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shura (Parliament), made up of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: India's lower house is called the Lok Sabha.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Neelum Valley and the Neelum River located? (24)
f: The Neelum Valley and the Neelum River lie in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: The river flows through Muzaffarabad and joins the Jhelum, and its capital valley town is Athmuqam.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old? (10)
f: The sister is 15 years old when Ali is 5, so she is 10 years older than him. When Ali is 10, she is 10 + 10 = 20 years old.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: In which city is Ayub National Park located? (12)
f: Ayub National Park is a large public park on Murree Road in Rawalpindi, named after President Ayub Khan.
r: It has a lake, a zoo-like area and recreation facilities for families.

q: What is the meaning of the word prescribe? (7)
o: To recommend or order as a remedy or rule
f: To prescribe means to advise or order something, such as a medicine or a rule. Its synonyms include recommend, advise and ordain.
r: A doctor writes a prescription to prescribe medicine.

q: Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) is located near which city? (16)
f: Jabal-e-Rehmat is a hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stand at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered his Farewell Sermon near this area in 10 AH.

q: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed? (13)
f: The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919. It allowed arrest and detention without trial.
r: The Act was named after Justice Sidney Rowlatt, and it led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919.

q: What was the Rowlatt Act? (15)
o: A law allowing arrest and detention without trial
f: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the British government power to imprison suspects without trial and to limit press freedom. Indians called it the Black Act.
r: Gandhi launched a nationwide protest against it.

q: Which prophet is known for suffering patiently from a long skin disease? (8)
f: Hazrat Ayyub (AS) bore a long illness, said to be a skin disease, with great patience and is the model of sabr (patience).
r: The Quran mentions his prayer in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.

q: In which year was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra under the Treaty of Amritsar? (22)
f: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British signed the Treaty of Amritsar on 16 March 1846 and sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
r: The price was 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees.

q: How many sons did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have? (94)
f: He had three sons, Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyab and Tahir) and Ibrahim, and all of them died in infancy.
r: Ibrahim was the son of Hazrat Maria Qibtiyya and the others were sons of Hazrat Khadija.

q: What is the capital of Turkey? (117)
f: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, chosen by Ataturk in 1923 when the republic was founded.
r: Istanbul is the largest city of Turkey but not its capital.

q: In which province does the Upper Indus Plain mainly lie? (24)
f: The Upper Indus Plain, north of Mithankot, covers most of Punjab, where the five rivers join the Indus.
r: The Lower Indus Plain to the south lies mainly in Sindh.

q: What is the original meaning of the word Urdu? (35)
f: Urdu comes from the Turkish word ordu, meaning camp or army, as the language grew in the military camps and bazaars.
r: It is also called Lashkari zaban, the language of the army.

q: What is 80% of 90? (19)
r: 10% of 90 is 9, so 80% is 8 x 9.

q: What is 1/10th of 90? (6)
f: One tenth of 90 is 90 divided by 10, which is 9.
r: Dividing by 10 simply moves the decimal point one place to the left.

q: What did the British call the War of 1857 that Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent called the War of Independence? (4)
f: The British described the uprising of 1857 as a mutiny of their Indian soldiers (sepoys), calling it the Sepoy Mutiny or Indian Mutiny.
r: Indian and Pakistani historians call it the War of Independence; the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar was exiled to Rangoon afterwards.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan in October 1958? (4)
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958, dissolved the assemblies and imposed martial law.
r: Iskander Mirza himself was removed by General Ayub Khan only 20 days later.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th be? (4)
f: From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: Who is generally listed as the first Governor-General of India (of Bengal, 1774)? (9)
f: Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 and is commonly called the first Governor-General of India in textbooks.
r: Sources differ: Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of all India in 1833, and Lord Mountbatten was the first of independent India.

q: Which is counted as the third major Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after Badr and Uhud? (8)
f: The major battles in order are Badr, Uhud and Khandaq (Ahzab), fought in 5 AH. The Muslims dug a trench on the advice of Salman Farsi.
r: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan in the absence of the President? (12)
f: Under Article 49 of the constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
r: If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.

q: Which prophet (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun)? (14)
f: Allah sent Hazrat Musa (AS), together with his brother Hazrat Harun (AS), to invite Pharaoh to the truth and to free Bani Israel.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kaleem-ullah (one who spoke to Allah).

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of ADVERSITY? (12)
f: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, so its opposite is prosperity, meaning good fortune and success.
r: The plural form adversities is used for repeated difficulties.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to ADVERSITY? (4)
f: Adversity means a state of serious difficulty or misfortune. Hardship is the nearest synonym.
r: The proverb says that adversity is the test of true friends.

q: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla is famous for composing what? (4)
o: The tune of the national anthem of Pakistan
The words of the national anthem of Pakistan
The design of the flag of Pakistan
f: Ahmed Ghulam Ali Chagla (1902-1953) was a Pakistani musician who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan.
r: The words of the anthem were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

q: Which is the national airline of Pakistan? (7)
f: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the national flag carrier of Pakistan, established in 1955.
r: PIA operated its first flight in 1955 and is headquartered in Karachi.

q: Syed-ul-Ansar was the title of which Sahabi? (11)
f: Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA), chief of the Aws tribe of Madina, was given the title Syed-ul-Ansar.
r: Sources may differ on the title holder, but most Pakistani textbooks give Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

q: In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan officially approved and adopted? (15)
f: The national anthem was officially approved by the government of Pakistan in August 1954.
r: Its tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla in 1949 and the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

q: What is the walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj called? (5)
f: Sa'i is the ritual walk between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).
r: The Zamzam well appeared near the Kaaba after this search.

q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)? (6)
f: The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.
r: The dog is traditionally named Qitmir.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies? (23)
f: Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.
r: A Senator's term is six years, with half retiring every three years.

q: Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr? (12)
f: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
r: It was the first major battle of Islam.

q: What is the antonym of the word biased? (9)
f: Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.
r: Unbiased and neutral are other opposites.

q: What is the border line between Pakistan and India (drawn in 1947) called? (4)
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by the Boundary Commission headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe at the partition of India in 1947.
r: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border and the McMahon Line is the India-China boundary.

q: In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female? (7)
f: Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
r: Females are 1/3 of the bus because the two fractions add up to 1.

q: How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship? (26)
f: Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.
r: He also won the British Open ten times in a row from 1982 to 1991.

q: Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age? (14)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.
r: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also given a son, Hazrat Yahya (AS), in old age.

q: The circumference of a circle of radius r is equal to (4)
f: Circumference = 2 x pi x r, which is the same as pi x diameter.
r: The area of a circle is pi r squared.

q: What are two circles called that have three points in common? (4)
f: Three non-collinear points determine exactly one circle. If two circles share three points, they must be the same circle, so they coincide.
r: Two different circles can meet in at most two points.

q: What are sets that have no common element called? (11)
f: Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.
r: Sets that have the same number of elements are called equivalent sets.

q: Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan? (31)
f: The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
r: The anthem was officially adopted in 1954.

q: A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion? (8)
f: Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
r: He was known for his scholarship and integrity.

q: Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan? (15)
f: Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.
r: Cotton is the major cash crop of Pakistan, but it is grown on a smaller area than wheat.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of India? (59)
f: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.
r: He is the longest-serving Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi in total years.

q: What is a decimal called in which the digits repeat again and again? (4)
f: A decimal in which a digit or block of digits repeats endlessly, like 0.333..., is called a recurring (repeating) decimal.
r: Every recurring decimal can be written as a fraction of two integers, so it is a rational number.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam declare in Dhaka that Urdu would be the state language of Pakistan? (4)
f: On 21 March 1948 at Dhaka, Quaid-e-Azam declared that Urdu alone would be the state language of Pakistan.
r: Urdu was formally made the national language in the 1973 Constitution, so some sources give a different answer.

q: A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what? (9)
f: A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.
r: A matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.

q: On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today? (7)
f: Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
r: Before the 18th Amendment of 2010 the President could also dissolve it on his own discretion under Article 58(2)(b).

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (25)
f: Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan? (7)
f: The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.
r: A Senator has a term of six years.

q: What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today? (28)
f: Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.
r: In earlier decades thermal (oil and gas) plants produced most of Pakistan's electricity.

q: How many articles are there in the English language? (6)
f: The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.
r: Candidates often wrongly say 2, forgetting that a and an are separate forms.

q: A train travels twice as fast as a car. If the car covers 30 km in 60 minutes, in what time will the train cover 30 km? (4)
f: The car's speed is 30 km per hour, so the train's speed is 60 km per hour. The train covers 30 km in 30 / 60 hour = 30 minutes.
r: Time = distance / speed.

q: Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal? (7)
f: The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.
r: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in a dive.

q: How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)? (6)
f: FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
r: There were also frontier regions (FRs) attached to FATA.

q: In which year was the Bogra Formula presented? (8)
f: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.
r: It was announced in the Constituent Assembly in October 1953.

q: What was the Bogra Formula? (12)
o: A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
f: It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.
r: It was named after Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra.

q: In which galaxy does the Earth lie? (9)
f: Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.
r: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is Andromeda.

q: The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities? (16)
f: Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.
r: Sources differ on exact limits, but Taxila and Peshawar are its best-known centres.

q: In which country do the Golan Heights lie? (4)
f: The Golan Heights is a rocky plateau in south-western Syria. Most of it has been occupied by Israel since 1967.
r: Israel annexed the Golan Heights in 1981, but this is not recognised by most of the world.

q: If Hamza is three times as old as Ali, what will be the age of Hamza when Ali is 7 years old? (4)
f: Hamza's age is 3 times Ali's age, so 3 x 7 = 21 years.
r: Age problems are solved by first writing the ratio between the ages.

q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim? (6)
f: The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.
r: The boycott took place from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.

q: What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad? (24)
f: In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.
r: The renaming was done on the first anniversary of India's revocation of Article 370 in 2019.

q: Where was the ICC Men's T20 World Cup of 2021 played? (4)
f: The 2021 T20 World Cup, officially hosted by the BCCI of India, was moved because of COVID-19 and played in the UAE and Oman in October and November 2021.
r: Australia won the 2021 final against New Zealand in Dubai.

q: Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience? (10)
f: Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.
r: Allah cured him after he prayed, as mentioned in the Quran.

q: What does the adjective intimate mean? (8)
f: Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.
r: Intimate can also be a verb meaning to hint at something indirectly, pronounced differently.

q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have? (7)
f: According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
r: Jahannam, by contrast, has seven gates.

q: Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China? (5)
f: The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
r: Its Chinese designation is FC-1 Xiaolong.

q: Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'? (27)
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.
r: Fatima Jinnah wrote 'My Brother' and Hector Bolitho wrote 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.

q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi? (4)
f: Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.
r: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.

q: What kind of number is 5/7? (6)
f: A number that can be written as a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator is rational. 5/7 is such a ratio.
r: Numbers such as pi and the square root of 2 cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so they are irrational.

q: What is the capital of North Korea? (5)
f: Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.
r: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

q: Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan? (7)
f: Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.
r: Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue in Pakistan.

q: Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet? (6)
f: The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M? (5)
f: The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.
r: M is the 13th letter, exactly in the middle of the alphabet.

q: Who is Mark Zuckerberg? (7)
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.
r: Facebook was renamed as Meta Platforms in 2021.

q: On which date did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) arrive in Madina after the Hijrat? (4)
f: After staying at Quba, the Prophet (PBUH) entered Madina on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal, 1 AH (September 622 AD). He had left Makkah a few days earlier.
r: Some sources give slightly different days for the departure and arrival, but 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal is the common Pakistani textbook date.

q: What is the median of the data 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8? (4)
f: The data is already in order and has 9 values, so the median is the 5th value. The 5th value is 5.
r: The median is the middle value of ordered data, and for an even count it is the mean of the two middle values.

q: What is the midpoint of the points (3, 1) and (-3, 1)? (4)
r: The midpoint formula is the average of the x values and the average of the y values.

q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km? (14)
f: Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320. For 400 km, 400 x 50 / 320 = 62.5 gallons.
r: This is a direct proportion question.

q: In which night was Namaz (the five daily prayers) made obligatory? (17)
o: Shab-e-Mi'raj (the night of Isra and Mi'raj)
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Isra and Mi'raj (placed by tradition around the 10th-12th year of Prophethood).
r: Sources differ on the exact year of Miraj; some say the 11th or 12th Nabawi year.

q: In which Nabawi year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate from Makkah to Madina? (12)
f: The Hijrat took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year of prophethood.
r: This Hijrat marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

q: In which city is the head office (secretariat) of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located? (4)
f: The ECO secretariat is located in Tehran, Iran.
r: ECO was founded in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.

q: What does OGRA stand for? (7)
f: OGRA stands for the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, which regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.
r: OGRA was established in 2002 and has its head office in Islamabad.

q: In which year did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman? (7)
f: Pakistan bought the Gwadar enclave from the Sultan of Oman in 1958, and it was formally handed over on 8 December 1958.
r: Gwadar became part of Balochistan province in 1977.

q: Who originally built the Kaaba? (12)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), with the help of his son Hazrat Ismail (AS), raised the walls of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks.
r: Some traditions say the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS) or the angels, so sources differ.

q: Geographically, into how many main regions is Pakistan divided according to most textbooks? (16)
f: Pakistan is usually divided into six regions: Northern Highlands, Western Highlands, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and Salt Range, Indus Plain, and Deserts.
r: Some books group them into three or five regions, so sources differ.

q: Where was the Battle of Plassey fought? (71)
f: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey in Bengal, on the bank of the Bhagirathi river.
r: Plassey is in present-day West Bengal, India.

q: According to Pakistani textbooks, how many prophets were sent by Allah in total? (6)
f: A well-known hadith, as taught in Pakistani textbooks, gives the number of prophets as 124,000.
r: Only 25 prophets are named in the Quran, and some narrations give 224,000.

q: Under which treaty did Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir from the British? (12)
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846) the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 7.5 million rupees.
r: This created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra rule.

q: What is the meaning of the word refute? (7)
f: To refute a claim is to prove it wrong. Synonyms include disprove, rebut and counter.
r: Refute is sometimes wrongly used to mean simply deny.

q: Which country does not have a regular army? (49)
f: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 after a civil war. It relies on police forces for security.
r: Dominica, Iceland and Panama are other countries without a standing army.

q: What does SUPARCO stand for and what is it related to? (4)
o: Pakistan's space and upper atmosphere research agency
f: SUPARCO is the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency. It was founded in 1961.
r: Pakistan launched its first satellite Badr-1 in 1990.

q: Is the square root of 7 a rational or an irrational number? (5)
f: 7 is not a perfect square, so its square root is a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal and cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Hence it is irrational.
r: The square root of any prime number is irrational.

q: On what date was the Rowlatt Act passed in 1919? (4)
f: The Imperial Legislative Council passed the Rowlatt Act on 18 March 1919.
r: Some sources give 21 March 1919, the date of the Viceroy's assent, so sources differ slightly.

q: In which part of Punjab is the Salt Range located? (6)
f: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum River and the Indus River south of Potohar Plateau. Khewra salt mine is in the range.
r: Mount Sakesar is the highest peak of the Salt Range.

q: In which year was the Scientific Society founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur? (5)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 at Ghazipur to translate Western scientific works into Urdu.
r: The society later moved to Aligarh in 1866, where it published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.

q: In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born? (15)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817.
r: He founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh, which later became Aligarh Muslim University.

q: What is the value of tan 90 degrees? (15)
f: tan 90 = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1 / 0, and division by zero is undefined.
r: tan 45 degrees equals 1 and tan 0 degrees equals 0.

q: At what age of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the last revelation (wahi) revealed? (13)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and the last verses shortly before his death at the age of 63.
r: He passed away in 11 AH (632 CE).

q: Ali is 4 years old and he is 4 years younger than his sister. When Ali is 8 years old, how old will his sister be? (4)
f: Sister is 4 + 4 = 8 years old now, so she is 4 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she will be 8 + 4 = 12.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: What is the value of any non-zero number raised to the power zero? (4)
f: By the law of exponents a^0 = a^n / a^n = 1 for any non-zero number a.
r: The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in basic algebra.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 1st of that month? (6)
f: From the 1st to the 15th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both fall on the same weekday, Monday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: What is the value of sin 180 degrees? (16)
f: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and sine is the y-coordinate, which is 0.
r: Also cos 180 degrees = -1 and sin 90 degrees = 1.

q: What is the value of cos 180 degrees? (4)
f: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and cosine is the x-coordinate, which is -1.
r: cos 0 degrees = 1, cos 90 degrees = 0 and cos 180 degrees = -1.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (6)
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: The 1956 Constitution also used the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan, while the 1962 Constitution used Republic of Pakistan.

q: How many seats are reserved for non-Muslim minorities in the National Assembly of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (9)
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves ten seats in the National Assembly for non-Muslims.
r: Minority members are chosen on reserved seats in proportion to the seats won by each party.

q: Which country hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics? (3)
f: The 2022 Winter Olympics were held in Beijing, China, in February 2022. There was no Summer Olympics in 2022.
r: The 2020 Summer Olympics were held in Tokyo in 2021, and the 2024 Summer Games in Paris.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is male? (6)
f: 340 divided by 500 times 100 gives 68 percent.
r: The remaining 32 percent are female.

q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan? (12)
f: The Governors-General were Quaid-e-Azam, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55) and then Iskander Mirza.
r: Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.

q: If a helicopter covers 320 miles using 80 gallons of fuel, how many gallons are needed for 700 miles? (32)
f: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 miles: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
r: Such questions are solved with direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

q: For which field is Abdur Rehman Chughtai famous? (6)
f: Abdur Rehman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a famous Pakistani painter and artist known for his Mughal-influenced style.
r: He is also known for designing Pakistan's early postage stamps.

q: What is the meaning of abhor? (4)
f: Abhor means to regard with disgust and hatred.
r: The noun form is abhorrence.

q: What is a synonym of acute? (7)
f: Acute can mean sharp or intense, as in acute pain, and severe is the closest synonym.
r: Acute angle means an angle less than 90 degrees.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League? (40)
f: Allama Iqbal gave his Allahabad Address in 1930, in which he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
r: He gave a series of lectures at Madras and other places in 1928-29, which became Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam.

q: What is the meaning of the word ADHERE? (4)
f: To adhere means to stick or hold fast to something, such as a surface, a rule or a belief. Its synonyms include stick, cling and follow.
r: The related noun adherent means a supporter or follower of a cause.

q: What does the Arabic word Alfeel mean? (6)
f: Alfeel means elephant. Surah Al-Fil of the Quran tells of Abraha's army with elephants that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Year of the Elephant (about 570 CE).

q: When was the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) founded? (7)
f: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded at the Belgrade Summit in September 1961 by leaders such as Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno.
r: The movement grew out of the 1955 Bandung Conference.

q: Which act of worship is mentioned in the Quran together with Zakat in many verses? (3)
f: The Quran repeatedly commands to establish Salat and pay Zakat together, for example in Surah Al-Baqarah.
r: Salat is the second and Zakat the third pillar of Islam in the usual list (after Shahada).

q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 24 balls. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep? (8)
f: Let Ahmad keep x balls, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 24, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
r: Amjad therefore kept 18 balls, and 18 is three times 6.

q: What is the antonym of defile? (3)
f: To defile means to make dirty or impure, so its opposite is to purify.
r: Pollute, stain and spoil are close to defile in meaning.

q: What is the antonym of dilate? (3)
f: To dilate is to become wider or larger, so its opposite is to constrict or contract.
r: The pupil of the eye dilates in dim light.

q: Saudi riyal is the currency of which country? (5)
f: The riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia, issued by the Saudi Central Bank.
r: Qatar and Oman also use a currency called riyal, but the Saudi riyal belongs to Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the circling (going around) of the Kaaba during Hajj and Umrah called? (3)
f: Tawaf is the act of walking seven times around the Kaaba in an anticlockwise direction.
r: Tawaf begins and ends at the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad).

q: How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have? (25)
f: The 1962 Constitution given by Ayub Khan had 250 articles.
r: It was suspended when martial law was imposed in 1969.

q: Baltistan is also known as which of the following? (9)
f: Baltistan, in Gilgit-Baltistan, is called Little Tibet (Tibet-e-Khurd) because of its culture and mountain landscape similar to Tibet.
r: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.

q: Where did the Quraish tribe belong? (15)
f: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Kaaba.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.

q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability to understand the language of birds and animals? (20)
f: The Quran says that Allah taught Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) the speech of birds, and he talked with the hoopoe and the ant.
r: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) also ruled over the jinn and the wind, and he was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).

q: On which date of the Islamic month was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born, according to the view most followed in Pakistan? (14)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, which is about 570 AD in Makkah.
r: Some scholars and the Shia tradition give 17 Rabi-ul-Awwal, so sources differ on the exact day.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word brilliant? (7)
f: Brilliant means very bright or very intelligent, and its opposite is dull.
r: Synonyms of brilliant include bright, radiant and gifted.

q: On which river did India build the Baglihar dam? (33)
f: The Baglihar hydroelectric dam is built by India on the Chenab river in Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab flows on into Pakistan.
r: Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 the Chenab is one of the three western rivers allotted to Pakistan.

q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946? (9)
o: A British mission sent to India to discuss the transfer of power
A Muslim League mission sent to London
A Congress mission sent to the Viceroy
A United Nations mission to Kashmir
f: The Cabinet Mission was a delegation of three British cabinet ministers sent to India in 1946. It proposed a plan for the transfer of power and a united India with a weak centre.
r: The Muslim League first accepted the plan and later withdrew its acceptance.

q: Who was the third caliph of Islam? (7)
f: The order of the Rightly Guided Caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. So the third was Hazrat Uthman (RA).
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called Ghani and Zun-Noorain.

q: If set A has 3 elements and set B has 4 elements, how many elements are in the Cartesian product A x B? (6)
f: The number of elements in A x B is the product of the sizes: 3 x 4 = 12.
r: The number of elements of A x B equals that of B x A.

q: How many players play in a game of chess? (15)
f: Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.
r: Each player starts with 16 pieces on a board of 64 squares.

q: Which is the coldest inhabited place of Pakistan? (6)
f: Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan records the lowest winter temperatures among Pakistan's inhabited places; it recorded about minus 21 degrees Celsius in December 2019.
r: Ziarat and Gilgit are also among the coldest places in winter.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 + 7i? (3)
f: In a + bi the real part is a, so for 6 + 7i the real part is 6 and the imaginary part is 7.
r: The modulus of 6 + 7i is the square root of 85.

q: In which year AD was Makkah conquered by the Muslims? (3)
f: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH, which corresponds to January 630 AD.
r: The conquest was almost bloodless and the Prophet (PBUH) announced a general amnesty.

q: How many copies of the Quran were prepared by Hazrat Usman (RA) and sent to different regions? (7)
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies prepared from the Abu Bakr copy and sent them to major centres; most Pakistani textbooks say five copies.
r: Some sources say seven copies, including one kept in Madina, so sources differ.

q: What is the meaning of the word crude? (3)
f: Crude means in a natural or raw state, not yet processed, or rough and lacking refinement.
r: Crude oil is petroleum before it is refined into petrol and diesel.

q: Against whom did Nawab Siraj ud Daula fight the Battle of Plassey in 1757? (7)
f: The British East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
r: The battle marked the beginning of British rule in India.

q: Pakistan's friendship with which neighbouring country is described as higher than the mountains and deeper than the oceans? (3)
f: Pakistani leaders describe the Pakistan-China friendship as higher than the Himalayas and deeper than the oceans.
r: The Karakoram Highway and CPEC link the two countries.

q: Roughly what fraction of the Earth's land surface is covered by deserts (arid regions)? (8)
f: Deserts and arid lands cover roughly one third of the Earth's land surface.
r: Sources differ depending on how a desert is defined.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'ecstasy'? (4)
f: Ecstasy means overwhelming joy, so its opposite is deep unhappiness, which is misery. Rapture, elation and delight are its synonyms.
r: Agony and despair are also opposites of ecstasy.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan? (12)
o: An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies
f: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.
r: Asif Ali Zardari was elected President for a second time in March 2024.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word excuse (as a verb)? (32)
f: To excuse someone means to forgive or pardon a fault. Blame, punish and accuse have the opposite sense.
r: As a noun, excuse means a reason offered to justify a fault, for example a pretext.

q: According to Islam, fasting (Roza) protects a person from what? (4)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that fasting is a shield. It teaches self-control and keeps a person away from sins and evil deeds.
r: The Quran says fasting was prescribed so that you may become pious (taqwa).

q: What happened on 27 February 2019 when the Pakistan Air Force responded to an Indian incursion? (3)
o: Pakistan shot down two Indian aircraft and captured a pilot
f: On 27 February 2019 the PAF shot down Indian aircraft inside Pakistani airspace and the Indian pilot Wing Commander Abhinandan was captured.
r: Pakistan named its response Operation Swift Retort and returned the pilot to India on 1 March 2019.

q: What was the name of the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (28)
f: Halima Sadia of the Banu Saad tribe nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert.
r: Thuwaiba, a freed slave of Abu Lahab, nursed him briefly before Halima.

q: Which is the fourth source of Islamic law (Shariah) in the usual order? (3)
f: The four sources in order are the Holy Quran, the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus of scholars) and Qiyas (analogy).
r: Hanafi fiqh, followed by most Pakistanis, accepts all four sources.

q: What is the capital of France? (10)
f: Paris, on the River Seine, is the capital and largest city of France.
r: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.

q: The Friendship Gate (Bab-e-Dosti) at Chaman is a border crossing between which two countries? (9)
f: The Friendship Gate stands at Chaman in Balochistan on the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
r: It is on Pakistan's western border, the Durand Line, opposite Spin Boldak in Afghanistan.

q: In which year of prophethood (Nabwi) was the Year of Grief (Aam-ul-Huzn)? (4)
f: The Year of Grief was the 10th year of prophethood, when the Prophet (PBUH) lost his wife Hazrat Khadija (RA) and his uncle Abu Talib within a short time.
r: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.

q: What is Hajr-e-Aswad? (11)
o: The Black Stone fixed in the Kaaba
A gate of the Prophet's Mosque
f: Hajr-e-Aswad is the Black Stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.
r: Pilgrims try to kiss or point to it at the start of each Tawaf.

q: What is the HCF of 6 and 12? (3)
f: 6 divides 12 exactly, so the largest number dividing both is 6.
r: When one number divides the other, the smaller number is the HCF and the larger is the LCM.

q: At what age is Hazrat Isa (AS) commonly said to have been raised to the heavens? (24)
f: The commonly stated age at which Hazrat Isa (AS) was raised to the heavens is 33 years.
r: Sources differ on the exact age, but 33 is the figure most commonly given.

q: Which is the highest mountain in the world? (8)
f: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, is the highest mountain above sea level.
r: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: Which is an important river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)? (3)
f: The Kabul River flows from Afghanistan through Peshawar and joins the Indus near Attock. Swat river is also a major river of the province.
r: The Hub River lies on the border of Sindh and Balochistan.

q: What is the most important event of 10 Hijri? (19)
o: The Farewell Hajj and Last Sermon of the Prophet (PBUH)
f: In 10 AH the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Hajjatul Wida, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
r: The Conquest of Makkah took place in 8 AH.

q: Which Chinese fighter jets did Pakistan Air Force formally induct in March 2022? (3)
f: The PAF commissioned its first six J-10C multirole fighters from China in March 2022.
r: China's stealth fighter J-35 has been reported as a possible future PAF purchase, but no delivery has been officially confirmed.

q: What is the integral of ln x with respect to x? (4)
f: Integrating by parts with u = ln x and dv = dx gives x ln x - integral of (x times 1/x) dx = x ln x - x + C.
r: The derivative of ln x is 1/x.

q: What is the meaning of the word interim? (6)
f: Interim describes something provided or done for the time between two events, that is, temporary.
r: An interim government rules only until a regular government is elected.

q: Inzamam-ul-Haq, one of Pakistan's best batsmen, played which sport for the Pakistan national team? (3)
f: Inzamam-ul-Haq played Test and One Day cricket for Pakistan from 1991 to 2007 and captained the team.
r: He scored 8830 Test runs and 11701 ODI runs.

q: Who is regarded as the first martyr of Islam? (34)
f: Hazrat Sumayyah (RA), mother of Hazrat Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is the first martyr of Islam.
r: Some sources name Harith bin Abi Hala as the first male martyr, so sources differ.

q: How many Jewish tribes lived in Madina when the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated there? (13)
f: The three main Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir and Banu Quraizah.
r: The Charter of Madina (Misaq-e-Madina) was made with them after the Hijrah.

q: Which was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan? (4)
f: Bahawalpur was the first princely state to accede to Pakistan, in October 1947.
r: Its ruler, the Nawab Sadiq Muhammad Khan Abbasi V, acceded on 5 October 1947.

q: Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, belonged to which country? (6)
f: Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa was a Pakistani girl from Faisalabad who became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.
r: She died in January 2012 at the age of 16, and Lahore has a software technology park tower named after her.

q: Kathmandu is the capital of which country? (7)
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.
r: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

q: On which river is the Khanpur Dam built? (20)
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River in the Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6? (5)
f: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12 and multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first common multiple is 12.
r: LCM times HCF of two numbers equals their product (12 x 2 = 24).

q: What is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) called? (11)
f: When a liquid gains heat and its molecules escape into the air as vapour, the change is called evaporation or vaporization.
r: The reverse process, vapour changing into liquid, is called condensation.

q: What is the value of log 1 (to any valid base)? (6)
f: Any base b raised to the power 0 equals 1, so the logarithm of 1 is 0.
r: The logarithm of 0 is undefined.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'loved'? (3)
f: Loved means felt strong affection for, and its opposite is hated.
r: Loathed and detested are other close opposites.

q: What was the approximate strength of the Muslim army sent against Musailma Kazzab in the Battle of Yamama? (3)
f: Hazrat Khalid bin Walid (RA) led about 13,000 Muslims against the army of Musailma Kazzab at Yamama in 633 CE (11 AH).
r: Musailma's army is usually given as about 40,000, though sources differ on exact numbers.

q: In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located? (18)
f: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) in Madina after the Hijrat.
r: It also contains the blessed grave of the Prophet (SAW).

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Navy? (16)
o: Vice Admiral H. M. S. Choudri
f: Vice Admiral James Wilfred Jefford of the Royal Navy became the first head of the Royal Pakistan Navy in 1947.
r: The first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Navy was Vice Admiral Muhammad Siddiq Choudri.

q: A person walks 7 miles towards the north, then turns left, then turns left again. In which direction is he going now? (3)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. Turning left again from west makes him face south.
r: Two successive left turns make a total turn of 180 degrees.

q: What is a matrix with only one row called? (9)
f: A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix; its order is 1 x n.
r: A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will one man write in 5 minutes? (36)
f: 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes.
r: The rate is 1 page per man per 5 minutes, or 0.2 pages per minute.

q: Complete the sentence: The prices of clothes are too ___. (3)
f: Prices are described as high or low, so high is the correct word.
r: We use tall and long for height and length, not for prices.

q: What is the antonym of provoke? (7)
f: Provoke means to make someone angry or stir them up; the opposite is to pacify or calm them.
r: Appease and soothe are also antonyms of provoke.

q: What is a quarter of 12? (4)
f: A quarter means one fourth. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
r: A quarter of 120 is 30, ten times the answer here.

q: Which political party launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942? (3)
f: The Indian National Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay in August 1942 under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi. The Muslim League opposed the movement.
r: The Quit India Movement demanded an immediate end to British rule in India.

q: Why do people read newspapers? (12)
o: To get information and knowledge about current events
f: Newspapers report news and information about local and world events. People read them mainly to gain knowledge and stay informed.
r: The first printed newspapers appeared in Europe in the early 1600s.

q: What is the real part of the complex number -i(4i + 6)? (3)
f: -i(4i + 6) = -4i squared - 6i = 4 - 6i since i squared = -1. The real part is 4.
r: The imaginary part of this number is -6.

q: Who wrote the book Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War? (5)
f: Dead Reckoning (2011) was written by Sarmila Bose and discusses the 1971 war and its casualty figures. It is often confused with works by authors with similar names.
r: Shrabani Basu wrote Victoria and Abdul, a different book.

q: What does the word refund mean? (5)
f: Refund means to give back money that was paid, for example for a returned item. Its synonym is reimburse.
r: Refund can be a noun (a refund) or a verb (to refund).

q: What is the meaning of the word reluctant? (6)
f: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A reluctant person does not want to act.
r: The noun form is reluctance.

q: Which two hadith books are called the Sahihain? (5)
f: Sahihain means the two Sahih books: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Bukhari and Sahih Muslim by Imam Muslim.
r: These two are considered the most authentic books of hadith.

q: My brother's son's sister is my what? (7)
f: My brother's son is my nephew, and his sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
r: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

q: The Sun is currently in which stage of a star's life? (3)
f: The Sun fuses hydrogen into helium in its core, which is the main sequence stage. It has been in this stage for about 4.6 billion years.
r: In about 5 billion years the Sun will become a red giant.

q: Which is the largest railway station of Pakistan, according to most sources? (16)
f: Lahore Junction is most commonly named as the largest railway station of Pakistan by area.
r: Sources differ on this point, and Karachi Cantonment and Rohri are also described as very large.

q: What is the closest meaning of 'strenuous'? (4)
f: Strenuous means needing great effort or energy. Arduous has the same meaning.
r: The opposite of strenuous is effortless or easy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "normally"? (3)
f: Normally means in the usual way, which is usually.
r: Its opposite is abnormally.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "retrieve"? (6)
f: To retrieve is to get something back, which is to recover.
r: A retriever dog is named for fetching game.

q: With what is Tayammum performed? (15)
f: Tayammum is done by striking the hands on clean earth or dust and wiping the face and arms.
r: It is allowed instead of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful to use.

q: What is the antonym of the word timid? (9)
f: Timid means lacking courage, so its opposite is bold.
r: Shy, fearful and meek are synonyms of timid.
