q: Jami at-Tirmidhi (Tirmizi Sharif) is a book of what? (5)
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of the sayings and actions (ahadith) of the Prophet (PBUH) compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
r: It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sitta.

q: In which language was the Holy Quran first translated in the subcontinent (India)? (19)
f: Shah Waliullah made the well-known first full translation into Persian in 1738, which is the usual textbook answer.
r: Sources differ, as an early Sindhi translation is also claimed; Shah Abdul Qadir later did the first Urdu translation.

q: Change into passive voice: Soldiers are digging trenches. (3)
o: Trenches are being dug by soldiers.
Trenches have been dug by soldiers.
f: The present continuous active becomes am/is/are being plus the past participle in the passive.
r: The past continuous 'were digging' becomes 'were being dug'.

q: In which year was Urdu declared the national language of Pakistan, as commonly taught? (15)
f: Quaid-e-Azam declared Urdu the state language at Dhaka in March 1948, and this is the usual textbook answer.
r: The 1973 Constitution also names Urdu as the national language of Pakistan.

q: Who was the first Viceroy of India? (10)
f: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown.
r: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, and Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.

q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus? (3)
f: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses. Tuberculosis and cholera are caused by bacteria and malaria by a protozoan parasite.
r: Antibiotics do not work against viral diseases.

q: Which is the highest waterfall in the world? (6)
f: Angel Falls in Venezuela has a total height of about 979 metres, with an uninterrupted drop of about 807 metres, making it the highest waterfall in the world.
r: Angel Falls is located in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, and is named after the pilot Jimmie Angel.

q: What does WWW stand for in internet addresses? (3)
f: WWW stands for World Wide Web, the system of linked pages accessed over the internet.
r: The World Wide Web was invented by Tim Berners-Lee in 1989.

q: In which direction of Pakistan does the Chinese region of Xinjiang lie? (3)
f: Xinjiang lies to the north (north-east) of Pakistan and meets Gilgit-Baltistan at the Khunjerab Pass.
r: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with Xinjiang through the Khunjerab Pass.

q: What is 90 divided by 90 (90/90)? (6)
f: Any non-zero number divided by itself equals 1, so 90/90 = 1.
r: Division of zero by a non-zero number gives 0, but division by zero is undefined.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will be the 13th of that month? (3)
f: The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Sunday + 2 days = Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 14th of that month? (4)
f: The 14th is 13 days after the 1st, and 13 = 7 + 6. Monday + 6 days = Sunday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: Which term comes next in the series: 3z, 6y, 9x, 15w, ? (6)
f: The numbers 3, 6, 9, 15 follow the rule that each is the sum of the two before it (3+6=9, 6+9=15), so the next is 9+15=24. The letters go backwards from z, y, x, w to v.
r: A series where each term is the sum of the previous two is called a Fibonacci-type series.

q: What is the square root of 1600? (4)
f: 40 x 40 = 1600, so the square root of 1600 is 40.
r: The square root of 16 is 4, so the square root of 1600 is 4 x 10 = 40.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah receive the title of Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader), as most Pakistani textbooks state? (26)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks say that Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed gave the title Quaid-e-Azam to Jinnah in 1938.
r: Sources differ on the exact year, and some mention 1936 or other dates.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be? (5)
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be? (2)
f: From the 3rd to the 19th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Sunday, which is Tuesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 24th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 3rd be? (3)
f: From the 3rd back to the 24th is 21 days. 21 days is 3 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Tuesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: Which constitution was enforced in Pakistan in April 1972 after the separation of East Pakistan? (2)
f: After 1971 a temporary Interim Constitution was adopted in April 1972, which ended martial law and ran until the permanent constitution of 1973.
r: The permanent Constitution of Pakistan was passed in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

q: Under whose government was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan framed and passed? (2)
f: The 1973 Constitution was drafted by a parliamentary committee and passed by the National Assembly during the premiership of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. It was adopted in April 1973.
r: Abdul Hafeez Pirzada, the law minister, played a leading role in drafting it.

q: What is 2 x 2 divided by 2? (2)
f: Work left to right: 2 x 2 is 4, and 4 divided by 2 is 2.
r: Multiplication and division have equal priority and are done left to right.

q: In a school of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is female? (6)
f: Females are 500 minus 340, which is 160. Then 160 divided by 500 times 100 gives 32 percent.
r: Males make up 68 percent.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What percentage of students is absent? (15)
f: Absent students are 500 minus 360, which is 140. Then 140 divided by 500 times 100 gives 28 percent.
r: Present students here are 72 percent.

q: What is 3x4 + 2x4 (also written 3x4 + 4x2)? (5)
f: Multiply first: 3x4 = 12 and 2x4 = 8 (4x2 is also 8). Then add: 12 + 8 = 20.
r: In arithmetic, multiplication is done before addition (BODMAS).

q: How many columns does a matrix of order 5x4 have? (5)
f: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns. For 5x4 there are 5 rows and 4 columns.
r: The total number of elements in a 5x4 matrix is 20.

q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 8th day of that month? (5)
f: From the 8th to the 28th is 20 days, and 20 = 2 weeks + 6 days. Going back 6 days from Monday gives Tuesday.
r: Going back 6 days is the same as going forward 1 day in a week cycle.

q: In which Hijri year was Aam-ul-Wafood (Year of Delegations)? (11)
f: Delegations from many Arab tribes came to Madina to accept Islam in 9 AH, after the conquest of Makkah. This year is called Aam-ul-Wafood.
r: The year 9 AH is also when the Battle of Tabuk took place.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of abolish? (7)
f: To abolish a law or system means to formally put an end to it, which is to do away with it.
r: Annul, scrap and repeal are other synonyms of abolish.

q: Who was the first among slaves to accept Islam, according to most Pakistani textbooks? (4)
f: Textbooks list Abu Bakr among men, Khadija among women, Ali among children and Zaid bin Haritha among freed slaves as the first to accept Islam.
r: Some sources name Hazrat Bilal (RA) as the first slave to accept Islam, so sources differ.

q: How many acute angles are there in an acute triangle? (9)
f: In an acute triangle all three angles are less than 90 degrees, so all three are acute.
r: A right triangle has two acute angles and an obtuse triangle has two acute angles as well.

q: When was the Indian Independence Act passed? (5)
f: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947 and created the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.
r: It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of ADHERE? (5)
f: Adhere means to stick to something, so its opposite is detach, meaning to separate or loosen.
r: Adhesive is a substance that makes things adhere to each other.

q: What does an adjective describe or explain? (6)
f: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun by telling its quality, quantity or kind, as in a tall boy.
r: An adverb, in contrast, modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.

q: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan? (95)
f: The Durand Line was fixed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and the Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, and it forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
r: The Radcliffe Line separates Pakistan and India, and the McMahon Line is between India and China.

q: Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro. (4)
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents, while Euro is the currency of many European countries.
r: The word Europe, not Euro, is the name of the continent.

q: What is the (executive) capital of South Africa? (9)
f: Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital of South Africa. The country has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
r: Cape Town is the legislative capital and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital.

q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ahmed is 9? (3)
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ahmed becomes 9 after 6 years, so she will be 9 + 6 = 15 years.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 6 years).

q: Who is the current President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026? (2)
f: PML-N's Dr Najeeb Naqi was elected and sworn in as the 25th President of AJK on 24 September 2026 for a five-year term.
r: His predecessor Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry died on 31 January 2026, and acting presidents served until the new election.

q: Which letter comes next after O in the English alphabet? (2)
f: The alphabet runs ... M, N, O, P, Q, so P comes right after O.
r: N comes just before O.

q: Which letter comes first in alphabetical order in the word MANAGEMENT? (3)
f: The letters of MANAGEMENT are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. Arranged alphabetically they begin with A, so A comes first.
r: Arranged fully, the word becomes A A E E G M M N N T.

q: After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last? (14)
f: MANAGEMENT has the letters M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. In alphabetical order: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. Counting from the end: T (1st), N (2nd), N (3rd), so the third letter from the last is N.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters: A, E, M and N appear twice each.

q: What is the national mammal of the United States of America? (2)
f: The American bison was declared the national mammal of the USA in 2016.
r: The bald eagle is the national bird and emblem of the USA, which many people loosely call its national animal.

q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 20 balloons. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balloons did Ahmad keep? (2)
f: Let Ahmad keep x balloons, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 20, so 4x = 20 and x = 5.
r: Amjad therefore kept 15 balloons, and 15 is three times 5.

q: Which word is a synonym of anarchy? (2)
f: Anarchy means a state of disorder due to the absence of authority, which is the same as lawlessness.
r: The opposite of anarchy is order or good government.

q: Which Sahabi was appointed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as governor of Yemen? (7)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor, judge and teacher of the people.
r: Before he left, the Prophet (PBUH) asked him how he would judge, and he replied that he would use the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning.

q: Which of the following is another name of the Holy Quran? (4)
f: Furqan, meaning the criterion that separates right from wrong, is one of the names of the Holy Quran.
r: Other names of the Quran are Al-Kitab, Al-Dhikr and Al-Noor; Zabur, Injeel and Tauraat are other revealed books.

q: What is the antonym of excrete? (2)
f: To excrete is to get rid of waste matter from the body, so the opposite is to absorb or retain.
r: Kidneys excrete urea from the human body.

q: What is the antonym of prohibited? (2)
f: Prohibited means not permitted, so its opposite is allowed.
r: Forbidden, banned and barred are synonyms of prohibited.

q: Which word is a synonym of applaud? (4)
f: To applaud is to show approval, which means the same as to praise.
r: The opposite of applaud is to criticize or condemn.

q: What is the approximate total area of Pakistan? (26)
f: Pakistan covers about 796,095 square kilometres, the 33rd largest country by area.
r: Balochistan is the largest province, covering about 44 percent of the country.

q: Around which body does the Earth revolve? (6)
f: The Earth orbits the Sun, completing one revolution in about 365.25 days.
r: The Moon revolves around the Earth, not the Sun directly.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares Islam as the State religion? (32)
f: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
r: Article 1 names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: In which part of Asia is India located? (5)
f: India lies in South Asia, forming most of the Indian subcontinent.
r: SAARC was formed in 1985 by the countries of South Asia.

q: Aslam was 28 years old in 1945. How old will he be in 1965? (2)
f: From 1945 to 1965 is 20 years, so his age is 28 + 20 = 48.
r: Age problems come down to adding the difference in years.

q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically? (8)
f: Alphabetical order is A D E E G M N T U, so the third letter is E.
r: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E appearing twice.

q: Sahih Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book? (6)
f: Muslims regard the Holy Quran as the most authentic book, followed in authenticity by Sahih Bukhari among the hadith books.
r: Imam Bukhari compiled his collection over about 16 years.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away? (11)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH (632 AD) at the age of 63 years.
r: He passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in Madina.

q: In the coordinate plane, the y-axis is the (2)
f: The y-axis is the vertical number line of the plane, and the y-coordinate is called the ordinate.
r: The x-axis and y-axis meet at the origin (0, 0).

q: In the coordinate plane, the x-axis is the (2)
f: The x-axis is the horizontal number line of the plane, and the x-coordinate is called the abscissa.
r: The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants.

q: Against whom was the War of Independence of 1857 (Jang-e-Azadi) fought by the people of the subcontinent? (8)
f: The 1857 revolt was an uprising of Indian soldiers and people against British East India Company rule.
r: The British called it the Mutiny, while Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent call it the War of Independence.

q: Who is the author of the famous book Hujjatullah-il-Baligha? (4)
f: Hujjatullah-il-Baligha is a famous work on Islamic wisdom by Shah Waliullah Muhaddith Dehlvi.
r: Shah Waliullah also translated the Quran into Persian.

q: Ali and Ahmed have 25 balls in all. If Ali has 4 times as many as Ahmed, how many balls does Ahmed have? (2)
f: Let Ahmed have x. Then x + 4x = 25, so 5x = 25 and x = 5.
r: Ali then has 20 balls.

q: Who is the Governor of Balochistan (as of 2026)? (7)
f: Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is serving as Governor of Balochistan in 2026.
r: Sarfraz Bugti is the Chief Minister, not the Governor.

q: Which barrage is commonly described as the biggest and the first barrage of Pakistan on the Indus? (9)
f: Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932, is the one Pakistani textbooks name as the first and biggest barrage on the Indus.
r: Sources differ on size; Guddu and Taunsa are other large barrages on the Indus.

q: What is the area of a triangle with base 3 cm and height 6 cm? (2)
f: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 3 x 6 = 9 square cm.
r: Candidates often forget the half and give 18, which is the area of the rectangle.

q: On which document is the Constitution of Pakistan based? (2)
f: The Objectives Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles and was made a preamble and later a substantive part (Article 2A) of the Constitution.
r: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly.

q: Pakistan's economy is predominantly based on which sector? (7)
f: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, supporting a large share of employment and exports like textiles from cotton.
r: Services now form the largest share of GDP, but agriculture remains the traditional base.

q: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought? (25)
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, which started the Mughal Empire in India.
r: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556 and the Third in 1761.

q: Where is the Bay of Riga located? (2)
f: The Gulf (Bay) of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea lying between Latvia and Estonia.
r: The city of Riga, the capital of Latvia, stands on this bay.

q: Where is the Bay of Siam located? (2)
f: The Bay of Siam is an old name for the Gulf of Thailand, an arm of the South China Sea.
r: Siam was the former name of Thailand.

q: Choose the correct statement about air at higher altitude. (2)
o: Air becomes lighter (thinner) as we go upward
Air becomes heavier as we go upward
Air density does not change with height
f: Atmospheric pressure and density decrease with height, so air becomes thinner and lighter as we go up.
r: This is why mountaineers use oxygen cylinders at great heights.

q: To which religion did Rana Bhagwan Das belong? (5)
f: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu who served as a judge of the Supreme Court and as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
r: He was the first non-Muslim to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.

q: Which type of brick was used in the buildings of the Indus Valley Civilization? (2)
f: Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa were built with uniform baked clay bricks, usually in a ratio of about 1:2:4.
r: Baked bricks made the drainage and the Great Bath waterproof and durable.

q: What name did the British give to the War of Independence of 1857? (8)
f: The British called the events of 1857 the Sepoy Mutiny (or Indian Mutiny) because it began with Indian soldiers in the Company army.
r: Muslims and Indian nationalists call it the War of Independence.

q: Change the first word into a pronoun: Sana broke her pen. (2)
f: Sana is a female name, so the pronoun that replaces it is She.
r: A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun.

q: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which dynasty? (7)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid bin Abdul Malik. The Mughals came centuries later.
r: Hajjaj bin Yusuf was the Umayyad governor of Iraq who sent him.

q: The Panama Canal separates which two continents? (2)
f: The Panama Canal cuts through the Isthmus of Panama, dividing North America from South America. It connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
r: The canal opened in 1914.

q: What is the capital of the country Georgia? (2)
f: Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia, a country in the Caucasus. Atlanta is the capital of the US state of Georgia.
r: Yerevan is the capital of Armenia.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela? (3)
f: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.
r: Bogota is the capital of Colombia.

q: On which date was the Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman captured in Pakistan? (5)
f: Wing Commander Abhinandan's aircraft was shot down on 27 February 2019, a day after the Balakot air strike. He was returned to India on 1 March 2019.
r: The Pakistan Air Force shot down two Indian aircraft that day.

q: In which year was the Baghdad Pact (later renamed CENTO) signed? (4)
f: The Baghdad Pact was signed in 1955 and was renamed CENTO in 1959 after Iraq withdrew.
r: Pakistan was a member of both CENTO and SEATO.

q: Through which point does the line x = 6y pass? (2)
f: Putting x = 0 and y = 0 gives 0 = 0, so the line satisfies the equation at the origin. The same is true for y = 5x.
r: Any line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.

q: Which device converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy? (6)
f: A battery or electric cell uses chemical reactions to produce an electric current.
r: A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy, and a solar panel converts light energy.

q: Who was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army (1949)? (2)
f: General Kodandera Madappa Cariappa took over as Commander-in-Chief from the British officer Sir Francis Butcher on 15 January 1949.
r: Sources differ on the phrase first army chief, since the British general Rob Lockhart briefly led the army after 1947; most textbooks give Cariappa.

q: The Chauri Chaura incident of 1922 took place during which movement? (2)
f: On 4 February 1922 a mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura and killed policemen, so Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: Chauri Chaura is in Uttar Pradesh, India.

q: What is 5 o'clock in the afternoon in 24-hour time? (4)
f: For afternoon hours add 12: 5 + 12 = 17, so 5 PM is 1700 hours.
r: Military time uses the 24-hour clock from 0000 to 2359.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'immense'? (3)
f: Immense means extremely large or great.
r: Its opposite is tiny or minute.

q: What does the word 'cohesion' mean? (2)
o: Act of sticking together as a united whole
f: Cohesion is the state of sticking together or forming a united whole, as in a cohesive group.
r: The opposite of cohesion is disunity or disintegration.

q: What is the transpose of a column matrix? (3)
f: Transposing a matrix swaps its rows and columns. A column matrix of order n x 1 becomes a matrix of order 1 x n, which is a row matrix.
r: The transpose of a row matrix is a column matrix.

q: What was the Simon Commission? (11)
o: A British commission sent to India in 1927 to review the Government of India Act 1919, with no Indian member
A commission for partition of Bengal
A Muslim League committee for Pakistan
A commission for dividing Punjab in 1947
f: The Simon Commission, led by Sir John Simon, arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform. It had only British members, so Indian parties boycotted it.
r: It was announced in November 1927 and its slogan of protest was Simon Go Back.

q: In which city was the East India Company established? (4)
f: The East India Company was formed in London and received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I.
r: Its first Indian trading post was set up at Surat in 1612.

q: In which year was the East India Company first established? (7)
f: The English East India Company received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
r: The Company won control of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

q: Complete the sentence: If he had called me, I ___ come. (3)
f: This is the third conditional (if + past perfect), which needs would have + past participle in the main clause.
r: Past unreal conditions use 'if + had + past participle', then 'would have + past participle'.

q: What kind of number is a - ib (where a and b are real and b is not zero)? (2)
f: A number written in the form a + ib with real a and b is a complex number; a - ib is its conjugate, which is also complex.
r: A complex number has a real part and an imaginary part.

q: What is the antonym of 'composite'? (2)
f: Composite means made up of several parts, and its opposite is simple, made of a single part.
r: In number theory the opposite of a composite number is a prime number.

q: Which are the two largest continents of the world by area? (2)
f: Asia is the largest continent and Africa is the second largest by area.
r: Asia is also the most populous continent.

q: Which organization controls and develops Pakistan's water and electric power system? (2)
f: WAPDA (Water and Power Development Authority) develops the country's water and hydropower resources.
r: IRSA, in contrast, distributes river water among the provinces.

q: What is cos(-x) equal to? (2)
f: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.
r: Sine is an odd function: sin(-x) = -sin x.

q: What is sec x multiplied by cos x equal to? (17)
f: Sec x = 1/cos x, so sec x . cos x = 1.
r: Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.

q: What is cosec x multiplied by tan x equal to? (7)
f: Cosec x . tan x = (1/sin x)(sin x/cos x) = 1/cos x = sec x.
r: Tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located? (60)
f: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
r: It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

q: What is the opposite of the word crude? (10)
f: Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined, meaning processed or polished.
r: In manners, the opposite of crude is cultured or polite.

q: On which date is Pakistan Day celebrated? (15)
f: Pakistan Day is celebrated on 23 March to mark the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of 1940.
r: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.

q: Where is the deepest hole (borehole) drilled by humans in the world? (2)
f: The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached about 12,262 metres in 1989.
r: It is deeper than the Mariana Trench is deep, which is about 10,935 metres.

q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's surface? (25)
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific is the deepest known point, at about 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.
r: Mount Everest, the highest point, would be covered by more than 2 km of water if placed in the Challenger Deep.

q: What does the word 'delight' mean? (2)
f: Delight means great pleasure or joy; as a verb it means to please greatly.
r: A synonym of delight is joy, and an antonym is sorrow.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert located? (10)
f: The Cholistan Desert lies in southern Punjab, near Bahawalpur.
r: It is locally called Rohi and is an extension of the Thar Desert.

q: Which of the following is a desert of Pakistan? (2)
f: Cholistan in Punjab is a desert of Pakistan, along with Thar, Thal and Kharan.
r: Gobi is in Asia (Mongolia and China), and Sahara and Kalahari are in Africa.

q: In a diagonal matrix, if all the non-zero diagonal elements are equal, what is the matrix called? (2)
f: A diagonal matrix with equal diagonal entries is called a scalar matrix.
r: A scalar matrix whose diagonal entries are all 1 is the identity matrix.

q: In which year (CE) did the mother of the Holy Prophet (SAW) pass away? (2)
f: The Prophet (SAW) was born in 570 CE and his mother died when he was about six, around 577 CE.
r: The exact year is given slightly differently in some sources.

q: Which district of Pakistan has the largest population according to the census? (3)
f: Lahore district had about 11.1 million people in 2017 and about 13.0 million in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.
r: Karachi is larger as a whole city, but it is divided into seven separate districts.

q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to what? (3)
f: A bitch is the female dog; the female horse is a mare.
r: A male horse is called a stallion and a young horse a foal.

q: According to a hadith, how many good deeds (nekis) are earned by reciting one letter of the Holy Quran? (6)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good deed is rewarded tenfold, so one letter of the Quran earns ten good deeds.
r: This hadith is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)? (2)
f: ECO members are Pakistan, Iran, Turkey, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Saudi Arabia is not among them.
r: ECO has ten members and its secretariat is in Tehran.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of the word 'ecstasy'? (5)
f: Ecstasy is a state of intense happiness or delight. Rapture is a close synonym.
r: The adjective form is ecstatic, meaning extremely happy.

q: Where was Abdul Sattar Edhi born? (8)
f: Edhi was born in 1928 in Bantva in Gujarat, British India, and migrated to Pakistan after Partition.
r: His family belonged to the Memon community.

q: In whose government were the non-party based elections held in Pakistan in 1985? (12)
f: General Zia-ul-Haq held non-party elections in February 1985. Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after them.
r: The 1985 assemblies passed the Eighth Amendment.

q: What is the antonym of the word 'embellish'? (2)
f: To embellish is to make something more attractive by adding decoration. Its opposite is to disfigure or spoil.
r: Embellish can also mean to add exaggerated details to a story.

q: What is the synonym of 'enigmatic'? (4)
f: Enigmatic describes something puzzling and hard to understand, which is mysterious.
r: The noun enigma means a puzzle or riddle.

q: In whose era was the Battle of Yamama fought? (6)
f: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11-12 AH against the false prophet Musaylima during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
r: Many Huffaz died there, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.

q: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belongs to the descendants of which prophet? (3)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) descended from Hazrat Ismail (AS), son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), through the Quraysh.
r: Hazrat Essa (AS) had no father and no direct descendants.

q: On what date did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests? (37)
f: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Chagai hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998 (five tests, Chagai-I), followed by one more on 30 May 1998. This was a reply to India's tests earlier that month.
r: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: How many Nobel Prizes in Physics has Pakistan received so far? (7)
f: Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. No other Pakistani has won in Physics.
r: Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate and Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

q: Who started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal? (16)
f: Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal in the early 19th century to make Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
r: After him, his son Dudu Miyan led the movement.

q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Namaz have according to the Hanafi school? (8)
f: Namaz has 13 farz: 6 outside the prayer (conditions such as cleanliness, covering the body, facing the Qibla, time and intention) and 7 inside it (such as takbeer, qiyam, qira'at, ruku, sajdah, qa'da akhira).
r: Wajibat of Namaz are different from farz, and leaving a farz makes the prayer invalid.

q: On which date of Ramadan was Makkah conquered (Fath-e-Makkah) in 8 AH? (7)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 CE) for the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims entered the city peacefully.
r: Some sources give other dates in Ramadan such as 10 or 17.

q: What was the name of the father of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah? (15)
f: The father of Quaid-e-Azam was Jinnahbhai Poonja, a merchant in Karachi. His mother was Mithibai.
r: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) of Pakistan, according to the latest available reports? (2)
f: Rashid Mahmood Langrial was appointed FBR Chairman in August 2024 and the latest reports found show him still in office.
r: He succeeded Amjad Zubair Tiwana, who resigned in July 2024; the FBR chairmanship changes often, so check the latest news.

q: A man walks a few steps towards the north, then turns right and walks, and then turns right again. In which direction is he now going? (4)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east; a second right turn makes him face south.
r: Two consecutive right turns always reverse the original direction.

q: If 3x - 9 = 2x + 7, find x. (2)
f: Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 9 = 7, so x = 16.

q: Who was the founder of the USSR (Soviet Union)? (3)
f: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917 and headed the new state when the USSR was formally created in 1922.
r: Joseph Stalin ruled the USSR after Lenin's death in 1924.

q: What kind of fraction is 9/3? (2)
f: In 9/3 the numerator 9 is larger than the denominator 3, so it is an improper fraction. It simplifies to the whole number 3.
r: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, such as 5/7.

q: A plane uses 160 gallons of fuel to cover 330 nautical miles. About how many gallons will it use to cover 700 nautical miles? (2)
f: Fuel per mile is 160 divided by 330, and 700 times 160 divided by 330 is 112000 divided by 330, which is about 339.4 gallons.
r: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.

q: Robert E. Lee was a famous general of which war? (2)
f: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army of Northern Virginia in the American Civil War (1861-1865). His main opponent on the Union side was Ulysses S. Grant.
r: Lee surrendered to Grant at Appomattox Court House in April 1865.

q: What was the gift given to the Muslims on the night of Miraj? (3)
f: On the night of Miraj, Allah made five daily prayers obligatory for the Muslims. The number was reduced from fifty to five.
r: Salah is often called the gift of Miraj.

q: A brother is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when the brother is 12? (4)
f: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15 years old now. The brother becomes 12 after 7 years, so the sister will be 15 + 7 = 22.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

q: Who was the first Governor of the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) after the creation of Pakistan? (8)
f: Sir George Cunningham was appointed Governor of NWFP in August 1947 at the creation of Pakistan.
r: Cunningham also served as governor before independence, in 1937-1946.

q: Who was the first Governor of Punjab after the creation of Pakistan? (2)
f: Sir Francis Mudie was the first Governor of West Punjab in 1947.
r: He served until 1949 and was succeeded by Sir Abdur Rab Nishtar.

q: What was the name of the paternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (7)
f: The Prophet's father was Abdullah, and Abdullah's father was Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal grandfather.
r: Abdul Muttalib was the son of Hashim and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

q: In which province does the Green Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system run? (10)
f: The Green Line BRT runs in Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh province.
r: The Peshawar BRT (Zu Peshawar) is the equivalent system in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: What is the HCF of 12 and 28? (4)
f: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 28 = 2 x 2 x 7. The common part is 2 x 2 = 4.
r: The LCM of 12 and 28 is 84.

q: Bait ul Mamoor is located in which heaven? (2)
f: In the narration of the Miraj, the Prophet (PBUH) saw Bait ul Mamoor in the seventh heaven.
r: Seventy thousand angels enter it each day and never return to it again.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have? (7)
f: The word hexagon comes from the Greek hex meaning six, so it has six sides.
r: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is 720 degrees.

q: For how many years did the Prophet (PBUH) preach Islam in Makkah before the Hijrat to Madina? (2)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and migrated at 53, so he preached in Makkah for about 13 years.
r: He then lived about 10 years in Madina.

q: In which month of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed (6 AH)? (8)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH and the treaty was signed with Quraysh at Hudaibiya in that month.
r: The treaty set a ten-year truce and Muslims performed Umrah the following year.

q: What is the multiplicative identity of a complex number, written as an ordered pair? (4)
f: The complex number 1 + 0i is written (1, 0), and (a, b) times (1, 0) = (a, b) for every complex number.
r: The additive identity is (0, 0).

q: Who wrote the book 'Culture and Imperialism'? (3)
f: Culture and Imperialism (1993) was written by the Palestinian-American scholar Edward Said.
r: Said is also famous for his book Orientalism (1978).

q: In which country did the first Industrial Revolution begin? (2)
f: The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the second half of the 18th century, with steam power and mechanised textile production.
r: James Watt's improved steam engine (1769 patent) was a key invention of this revolution.

q: Complete the sentence: Smoking is injurious ___ health. (2)
f: The adjective injurious is followed by the preposition to, so the correct phrase is injurious to health.
r: The same pattern is used in harmful to, and detrimental to.

q: According to the Holy Quran and hadith, killing one innocent person is equal to what? (3)
f: Surah Al-Maidah (5:32) says that whoever kills one innocent soul is as if he had killed all of mankind.
r: The same verse says that saving one life is as if one had saved all of mankind.

q: Is the number 5/7 rational or irrational? (2)
f: A rational number can be written as p/q with integers p and q and q not zero. 5/7 has this form, so it is rational.
r: The square root of 2 and pi are famous irrational numbers.

q: Is 22/7 a rational or an irrational number? (2)
o: Irrational, because it is close to pi
Rational, because it is a ratio of two integers
f: 22/7 is a fraction of two integers, so it is rational. It is only an approximation of pi, which is irrational.
r: 22/7 is about 3.142857 while pi is about 3.141593.

q: Where is Jabal Arafat (Jabal-e-Rahmat), the hill where pilgrims stand on 9 Dhul Hijjah? (3)
o: Near Makkah, in the plain of Arafat
f: Jabal Arafat, also called Jabal-e-Rahmat, stands in the plain of Arafat about 20 km southeast of Makkah.
r: Standing at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah is the most important rite (rukn) of Hajj.

q: Change into passive voice: He said, "I have done my job." (2)
o: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.
It was said by him that he had done his job.
His job was done by him.
It is said by him that I have done my job.
f: In indirect passive form the statement becomes: It was said by him that his job had been done by him.
r: In reported speech, the present perfect changes to the past perfect after a past tense reporting verb.

q: Change the narration: He says, "I did not care about my job." (2)
o: He says that he had not cared about his job.
He said that he did not care about his job.
He says that he did not care about his job.
He says that I did not care about my job.
f: The reporting verb says is in the present tense, so the tense of the reported speech does not change; only the pronouns change.
r: If the reporting verb were past (said), the verb inside would shift back to the past perfect.

q: Which one is different from the others: chimpanzee, ape, baboon, kangaroo, monkey? (2)
f: Chimpanzee, ape, baboon and monkey are all primates, while the kangaroo is a marsupial.
r: Kangaroos are native to Australia and carry their young in a pouch.

q: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with which country? (3)
f: The Karakoram Highway runs from Hasan Abdal in Pakistan to Kashgar in China through the Khunjerab Pass.
r: The Khunjerab Pass, at about 4693 metres, is the highest paved border crossing in the world.

q: Which of these is another name for the Karakoram Highway? (28)
f: The Karakoram Highway is also called the Pakistan-China Friendship Highway and is numbered N-35.
r: It is sometimes called the Eighth Wonder of the World because of the difficulty of building it.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the karez system of irrigation mainly used? (4)
f: A karez is an underground channel that carries water from a hillside, and it is widely used in dry Balochistan.
r: Karez is also known as qanat in Iran and is used across Central Asia.

q: Who described Kashmir as the jugular vein of Pakistan? (3)
f: The statement is credited to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, who stressed the strategic importance of Kashmir.
r: Pakistan marks Kashmir Solidarity Day on 5 February each year.

q: What is the antonym of the word justify? (5)
f: To justify means to defend as right, and the opposite is to condemn or blame.
r: Another opposite of justify is to criticise.

q: In which year AD was the Battle (Ghazwa) of Khyber fought? (2)
f: The Battle of Khyber took place in 7 AH, which corresponds to 628 AD. It ended with the conquest of the Jewish fortresses of Khyber.
r: Some sources place the exact month between spring and mid 628 AD, but the year 628 AD (7 AH) is agreed.

q: Foot is to knee as hand is to what? (6)
f: The knee is the main joint of the leg above the foot, and the elbow is the main joint of the arm above the hand. So hand is to elbow.
r: The elbow joins the upper arm to the forearm.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) fought against the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud? (6)
f: The Makkan army at Uhud numbered about 3000 men, while the Muslims were about 1000 at the start and about 700 after 300 hypocrites withdrew.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: What is the capital of Sri Lanka as commonly given in textbooks? (9)
f: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka and the usual textbook answer.
r: The official legislative capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, near Colombo.

q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth's atmosphere? (4)
f: In the thermosphere, absorption of solar radiation can heat the thin air to over 1,000 degrees Celsius.
r: The mesosphere above the stratosphere is the coldest layer.

q: What is the process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of a plant? (7)
f: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.
r: It helps pull water up the plant and cools the leaves.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LENIENT? (9)
f: Lenient means merciful or not strict, so tolerant is the closest.
r: The opposite of lenient is strict or harsh.

q: Which mountain range lies between Pakistan and China? (4)
f: The Karakoram range along the north of Pakistan forms its border with China, crossed by the Karakoram Highway.
r: K2 lies in the Karakoram.

q: Which pillar of Islam was made obligatory on the Prophet (PBUH) during the Mairaj? (2)
f: Five daily prayers were gifted to the Muslims on the night of Mairaj, after being reduced from fifty.
r: The journey from Makkah to Bait-ul-Muqaddas is called Isra and the ascension to the heavens is called Mairaj.

q: Which party won a majority of seats in East Pakistan in the 1970 general elections? (8)
f: The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 of the 162 East Pakistan seats.
r: The Pakistan People's Party won the most seats in West Pakistan.

q: What is the capital of Malaysia? (113)
f: Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia.
r: Putrajaya is the administrative capital where government offices are located.

q: In a class of 30 students, 24 are male. What is the percentage of females? (2)
f: Females = 30 - 24 = 6. Percentage = 6/30 x 100 = 20%.
r: Males are 80% of this class.

q: What is the height of Mangla Dam (commonly quoted)? (2)
f: Mangla Dam is about 147 metres (482 feet) high according to commonly cited figures.
r: Some sources give slightly different heights, as the dam was raised in the 2000s.

q: What is the mean of -5 and -5? (5)
r: The mean of identical numbers equals that number.

q: What is the mean of 1, 4, 5, 6? (3)
r: Mean is the sum of values divided by their count.

q: What is the migration of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) from Makkah to Madina called? (2)
f: The migration from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD is called Hijrat (Hijrah). The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.
r: The Hijri calendar was introduced in the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan? (48)
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the total fell to 336 seats. These are 266 general, 60 women and 10 minority seats.
r: Before this change the National Assembly had 342 seats.

q: Who is the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional from Pakistan? (8)
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa became a Microsoft Certified Professional at the age of nine in 2004. She was the youngest in the world at that time.
r: She died in 2012 and the Arfa Karim Software Technology Park in Lahore is named after her.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan? (7)
f: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old. A voter must be 18.
r: Candidates for the Senate must be at least 30 years old.

q: Which planet has the largest moon in the Solar System? (17)
f: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the Solar System. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury.
r: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is second in size.

q: Who was the first man to land on the Moon? (9)
f: Neil Armstrong of the Apollo 11 mission stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
r: Buzz Aldrin followed him, while Michael Collins stayed in orbit.

q: Which pronoun is most suitable for the word mom? (2)
f: Mom is a female parent, so the feminine subject pronoun she is used.
r: Her is the object form and herself is the reflexive form.

q: What is the motto given by the Quaid-e-Azam to the nation? (5)
f: The Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline (Ittehad, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam, Nazm). This is the order used in his speeches and in Pakistani textbooks.
r: In Urdu the motto is often written as Ittehad, Tanzeem, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam; Unity, Faith, Discipline is the standard English form.

q: How many companions are called the Ashra Mubashra? (4)
f: Ashra Mubashra are ten Companions who were given the glad tidings of Paradise in their lifetime.
r: They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.001? (2)
f: The inverse of a number is 1 divided by it. 1 / 0.001 = 1000.
r: A number times its multiplicative inverse equals 1.

q: Who is the author of the book Indian Musalmans (1871)? (3)
f: Indian Musalmans: Are They Bound in Conscience to Rebel Against the Queen? was written by Sir William Wilson Hunter.
r: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and others wrote replies to Hunter's book.

q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran? (41)
f: The Holy Quran mentions the names of 25 prophets.
r: The commonly quoted total number of prophets is 124,000, though the Quran does not state it.

q: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I am sorry." (3)
o: She said that she is sorry.
She said that she was sorry.
She said that I was sorry.
She said that she had been sorry.
f: In indirect speech after a past reporting verb the present tense changes to past, and the pronoun I changes to she, so am becomes was.
r: Quotation marks and the comma are dropped and that is added in indirect speech.

q: How many nautical miles is the territorial sea of Pakistan under the UN Law of the Sea? (2)
f: Under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, a country's territorial sea extends 12 nautical miles from its coast, and Pakistan claims this limit.
r: Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone extends 200 nautical miles.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of the Netherlands as of 2026? (2)
f: Rob Jetten of the D66 party became Prime Minister on 23 February 2026, succeeding Dick Schoof.
r: Mark Rutte, who was PM in 2022, later became the Secretary General of NATO in 2024.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: O, K, H, F, ? (2)
f: The positions are 15, 11, 8, 6. The gaps are 4, 3, 2, so the next gap is 1 and 6 - 1 = 5, which is E.
r: The gaps decrease by 1 each time.

q: How many nights did the Prophet (PBUH) spend in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat? (3)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three nights before going on to Madina.
r: The Cave of Thawr is near Makkah, on the way to Madina.

q: Which type of noun is Islamabad? (4)
f: A proper noun is the name of a particular person, place or thing. Islamabad is the name of one specific city, so it is a proper noun and it is written with a capital letter.
r: A common noun such as city names any one of a class.

q: An obtuse angle measures more than 90 degrees and less than how many degrees? (3)
f: An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees (a right angle) but less than 180 degrees (a straight angle).
r: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, and an angle of exactly 180 degrees is called a straight angle.

q: What was the official name of the country under the 1962 constitution of Pakistan? (2)
f: The 1962 constitution named the country the Republic of Pakistan.
r: The word Islamic was added back in 1963 by the First Amendment, and the 1973 constitution uses Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: Ali is older than Waqas, and Usman is younger than Waqas. Who is the oldest of the three? (4)
f: Ali is older than Waqas and Waqas is older than Usman, so the order from oldest is Ali, Waqas, Usman.
r: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a single line of order.

q: Which is generally considered the oldest civilization of the world? (4)
f: The Mesopotamian (Sumerian) civilization, which arose between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers around 3500 BC, is usually regarded as the oldest.
r: The Indus Valley civilization of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa flourished around 2500 BC.

q: What is the currency of Oman? (3)
f: The official currency of Oman is the Omani rial.
r: The Omani rial is one of the highest-valued currencies in the world.

q: What is meant by the order of a matrix? (4)
o: Number of rows by number of columns
f: The order of a matrix is stated as rows x columns, for example a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns is of order 2 x 3.
r: The order is also called the size or dimension of the matrix.

q: Which of the following is a principal organ of the United Nations? (2)
f: The six principal organs of the UN are the General Assembly, Security Council, Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council, International Court of Justice and the Secretariat. The others listed are agencies or funds.
r: The International Court of Justice sits at The Hague and is the only principal organ not based in New York.

q: Out of 15000 students, 12000 are present. What is the percentage of students present? (2)
r: The percentage absent is 100 - 80 = 20%, which is 3000 students.

q: Mark Zuckerberg is the founder and head of which company? (12)
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the chairman and CEO of its parent company, Meta Platforms.
r: Facebook Inc. renamed itself Meta Platforms in October 2021; the company also owns Instagram and WhatsApp.

q: 6 is what percent of 20? (11)
f: Percentage = 6/20 x 100 = 30%.
r: Similarly, 30% of 20 is 6.

q: With what is Tayammum performed when water is not available? (2)
f: Tayammum is performed by striking the hands on clean earth, dust or sand and wiping the face and the arms.
r: Tayammum is permitted when water is not available or its use would harm health.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word PERPETUAL? (4)
f: Perpetual means never ending or continuing forever, which matches everlasting.
r: Its antonym is temporary or transient.

q: What is the study of geometrical shapes in a plane called? (4)
f: Plane geometry (Euclidean geometry) studies two-dimensional shapes such as lines, triangles and circles.
r: Solid geometry deals with three-dimensional figures.

q: Between whom was the Battle of Plassey (1757) fought? (10)
o: The British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal
f: At Plassey the East India Company force under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
r: The battle laid the foundation of British rule in India.

q: Through which point does the line y = 5x pass? (2)
f: Putting x = 0 gives y = 5 times 0 = 0, so the line passes through (0, 0). The other points do not satisfy y = 5x.
r: Any line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.

q: Who is the co-chairperson of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)? (2)
f: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the PPP.
r: He is also the President of Pakistan, serving his second term since March 2024.

q: Choose the correct preposition: My father died ___ the war. (2)
f: We say died in a war, because the war is the event during which he died.
r: We say died of an illness but died in an accident or war.

q: Who is the head of state of Jordan? (8)
f: Jordan is a monarchy and King Abdullah II is its head of state, so it has no president.
r: King Abdullah II has ruled since 1999 after the death of his father King Hussein.

q: What is the probability of a sure (certain) event? (3)
f: A sure event is one that is certain to happen, so its probability is 1. Probability always lies between 0 and 1.
r: An impossible event has probability 0.

q: Is 2x^2 + 3x + 2 a quadratic expression? (2)
f: The highest power of x is 2, with a non-zero coefficient 2, so it has the form ax^2 + bx + c of a quadratic.
r: Its discriminant 9 - 16 = -7 is negative, so it has no real roots.

q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 90? (2)
f: 1/3 of 90 is 30. A quarter of 30 is 30 divided by 4, which equals 7.5.
r: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 90 divided by 12.

q: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Rabb? (17)
f: Rabb means Lord, Sustainer and Nourisher, the One who brings up and provides for all creation. It is used in the Quran for Allah, as in Rabbul Alameen.
r: Rabbul Alameen, meaning Lord of all the worlds, appears in Surah Al-Fatiha.

q: The Radcliffe Line is the boundary between which two countries? (4)
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 to divide Punjab and Bengal between India and Pakistan. It is the border between Pakistan and India.
r: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: Which angel is appointed by Allah to bring rain? (3)
f: Hazrat Mikael (AS) is the angel in charge of rain and sustenance. This is the commonly taught view in Islamic books.
r: Hazrat Jibril (AS) brought revelation, and Hazrat Israfil (AS) will blow the Trumpet on the Day of Judgment.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 - 9i? (7)
f: In a + bi form, the real part is the term without i. Here it is 6.
r: The conjugate of 6 - 9i is 6 + 9i.

q: What was the real name of Iblis (Shaitan) before he was cursed? (2)
f: Iblis is said in many Islamic traditions to have been called Azazil before he refused to bow to Adam (AS). He was a jinn and was cursed for his pride.
r: Some narrations give his earlier name as Harith, so sources differ.

q: What is a decimal number that neither terminates nor repeats called? (2)
f: A non-terminating, non-recurring decimal cannot be written as a fraction p over q. Such a number is called irrational.
r: Pi and the square root of 2 are common irrational numbers.

q: A decimal in which one or more digits repeat endlessly in the same pattern is called: (2)
f: In a recurring decimal, a digit or a block of digits repeats forever, such as 0.333... or 0.142857142857... Such numbers are rational.
r: 1 divided by 3 gives 0.333..., a recurring decimal.

q: What did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduce in the provinces? (5)
f: The 1919 reforms divided provincial subjects into transferred (under elected ministers) and reserved (under the Governor). This system was called dyarchy.
r: Dyarchy was ended by the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy.

q: Between which two regions does the Rann of Kutch lie? (3)
f: The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh in the Thar desert area on the border between Sindh in Pakistan and Gujarat in India. A border dispute there was settled by tribunal in 1968.
r: The 1965 war began with clashes in the Rann of Kutch in April 1965.

q: According to the Quran, which religion is accepted by Allah? (3)
f: The Quran states that the religion with Allah is Islam (Surah Al-Imran 3:19). It also says no other religion will be accepted from anyone.
r: The Quran was completed with the verse declaring Islam as the chosen religion (Surah Al-Maidah 5:3).

q: Nankana Sahib is a famous holy site of which religion? (6)
f: Nankana Sahib is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. It is in Punjab, Pakistan.
r: Guru Nanak was born there in 1469.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to whose challenge? (3)
f: Lord Birkenhead, the Secretary of State for India, challenged Indian leaders to draft a constitution acceptable to all communities. The Nehru Report was the Congress-led answer to that challenge.
r: Quaid-e-Azam rejected the Nehru Report and presented his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan? (6)
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: Article 2 declares Islam to be the State religion of Pakistan.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan first used? (8)
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.
r: The 1962 Constitution changed the name to the Republic of Pakistan, and the 1973 Constitution restored Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: Which country has the largest official gold reserves in the world? (2)
f: The United States holds about 8,133 tonnes of official gold reserves, roughly double that of second-placed Germany.
r: Germany is second with about 3,350 tonnes, followed by Italy and France.

q: In which city did the tribes of Aus and Khazraj reside? (3)
f: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later called Madina. They became the Ansar after welcoming the Prophet (PBUH).
r: The two tribes had long been at war before Islam united them.

q: On which date was the Pakistan Resolution (Lahore Resolution) presented? (27)
f: The resolution was presented on 23 March 1940 at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League, having been moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and passed on 24 March.
r: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day.

q: According to the commonly given order of revelation, which Surah was the third to be revealed? (2)
f: The usual order is Al-Alaq first, Al-Qalam second and Al-Muzzammil third.
r: Sources differ; some lists place Al-Muddaththir ahead of Al-Muzzammil.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word reward? (3)
f: A reward is something given in return for good work or conduct, that is, a recompense.
r: The opposite of reward is punishment.

q: Which word is the synonym of rich? (2)
f: Rich means having a great deal of money, and wealthy has the same meaning.
r: Affluent is also a synonym of rich.

q: Which river is the largest in the world by volume of water discharged? (6)
f: The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.
r: The length of the Nile and the Amazon is disputed, so some sources name the Nile as longest.

q: The name Punjab means the land of how many rivers? (5)
f: Punjab is from the Persian words punj (five) and ab (water), meaning five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
r: Of these, the Beas and Sutlej are mainly in India after the Indus Waters Treaty.

q: The Reshmi Romal (Silk Letter) Tehreek was started by Maulana Mahmud Hasan and which colleague? (2)
f: The Silk Letter Movement of about 1913 to 1920 was organised by Shaikhul Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan with Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi.
r: Letters were written on silk cloth to communicate with allies abroad against British rule.

q: What is the square root of 196? (9)
f: 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.
r: 196 is a perfect square, being 14 squared.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 7? (7)
f: 2.6 x 2.6 = 6.76 and 2.7 x 2.7 = 7.29, so the root lies between them; 2.65 x 2.65 = 7.02 so it is about 2.65.
r: The square root of 7 is an irrational number, about 2.6458.

q: How many roots does a quadratic equation have? (12)
f: A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.
r: A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0.

q: In which battle were about 70 Sahaba martyred? (3)
f: About 70 Sahaba were martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 Hijri.
r: Only 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr.

q: In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics? (18)
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.
r: He was the first Pakistani and first Muslim from Pakistan to win a Nobel Prize.

q: Which of the following countries is a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as of 2026? (2)
f: Iran became a full member in 2023 and Belarus in 2024, bringing the SCO to ten full members. Turkey is only a dialogue partner, while Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.
r: The ten full members are China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran and Belarus.

q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)? (12)
f: The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.
r: The fleshy red part of a strawberry is the swollen receptacle of the flower rather than a true fruit.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (5)
o: An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
f: Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.
r: The President serves a five-year term.

q: What is the measure of an angle inscribed in a semicircle? (2)
f: By Thales' theorem, an angle inscribed in a semicircle subtends the diameter and is always a right angle, 90 degrees.
r: The central angle on a diameter is 180 degrees, which is exactly double the inscribed angle.

q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s? (8)
f: Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
r: Sindh was actually separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936 and became a separate province.

q: For what is the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) best known? (5)
o: A treaty with the Jews of Madinah
f: In the Last Sermon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared the equality of all people, the sanctity of life, property and honour, the rights of women and the abolition of interest and old blood feuds. It is therefore regarded as the first great charter of human rights.
r: The Last Sermon was delivered in the 10th year of Hijrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver the Last Sermon? (3)
o: In the valley of Uranah on the plain of Arafat
f: During the Farewell Hajj the Holy Prophet (PBUH) addressed more than one hundred thousand Muslims on the 9th of Dhul Hijjah in the valley of Uranah at Arafat.
r: Part of the sermon was also given at Mina on the days after Arafat.

q: Choose the correct preposition: She shouted ____ him. (2)
f: The verb shout takes at when it means to speak angrily to someone, so the correct sentence is She shouted at him.
r: Shout to someone means to call out so that the person can hear you, with no anger.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Siraat' (as in Siraat-e-Mustaqeem)? (2)
f: 'Siraat' is an Arabic word meaning a path or way. In Surah Al-Fatiha, Siraat-e-Mustaqeem means the straight path.
r: The Siraat on the Day of Judgement is also described as a bridge over Hell that everyone must cross.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will the age of his sister be when Adil is 15 years old? (3)
f: The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

q: Where is Gwadar situated? (12)
o: On the Makran coast of Balochistan
On the coast of Sindh near Karachi
f: Gwadar is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast of the Makran region in Balochistan.
r: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

q: In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start? (13)
f: The hashtag and movement began in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
r: It spread worldwide in 2020 after the death of George Floyd.

q: Who sold the Kashmir valley and to whom? (3)
o: The British East India Company to Gulab Singh Dogra
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh, the Dogra ruler of Jammu.
r: Gulab Singh became the first Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

q: What is the trivial solution of a homogeneous system of linear equations in three unknowns x, y and z? (3)
f: In a homogeneous system every right-hand side is 0, so putting every unknown equal to 0 always satisfies it. This is called the trivial solution (0, 0, 0).
r: A homogeneous system always has at least the trivial solution, so it is never inconsistent.

q: Solve the proportion 8 : 4 :: X : 16. What is X? (2)
r: The ratio 8 : 4 simplifies to 2 : 1.

q: Solve for x: 4x - 1 = x + 2 (2)
f: Subtract x from both sides: 3x - 1 = 2. Add 1: 3x = 3, so x = 1.

q: Ahsan Ramzan, who became the youngest world champion in 2022, is a player of which sport? (19)
f: Ahsan Ramzan of Lahore won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in Doha in 2022 at the age of 16. He became the youngest ever winner.
r: He beat Iran's Amir Sarkosh in that final.

q: Tiananmen Square is situated in which city? (2)
f: Tiananmen Square lies in the centre of Beijing, the capital of China. It is named after the Gate of Heavenly Peace.
r: It is one of the largest public squares in the world.

q: In which city was the first television station of Pakistan set up? (16)
f: Pakistan Television started its first broadcast from Lahore on 26 November 1964. It was a pilot station.
r: Karachi and Dhaka stations followed in 1966.

q: Marvi, the famous folk tale, belongs to which province of Pakistan? (2)
f: Umar Marvi is one of the seven famous folk heroines of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's Sindhi poetry. The story belongs to Sindh.
r: Marvi was a village girl of Tharparkar who refused the offers of the ruler Umar Soomro.

q: How many Muslim soldiers marched in the army for the Ghazwa of Tabuk? (2)
f: The Prophet (SAW) led about 30,000 Muslim fighters to Tabuk in 9 AH. It was the largest Muslim army up to that time.
r: The campaign is also called the Army of Hardship (Jaish-ul-Usrah).

q: What is the antonym of 'subversion'? (2)
f: Subversion means weakening an authority, so its opposite is supporting or upholding it. Support is the best opposite among the options.
r: Subversion usually refers to secret acts against a government.

q: After which event did Hazrat Abu Sufyan (RA) accept Islam? (14)
f: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.
r: Before this he had led the Quraysh in several battles against the Muslims.

q: In which Hijri year did Abu Sufyan accept Islam? (12)
f: Abu Sufyan embraced Islam on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, which took place in 8 AH.
r: Some candidates remember 6 AH, but the Conquest of Makkah was in 8 AH.

q: Which surah is known as Arus-ul-Quran (the Bride of the Quran)? (30)
f: Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran because of its beauty and its repeated refrain.
r: Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran.

q: How many surahs of the Holy Quran are named after prophets, according to the commonly given list? (9)
f: The commonly counted ones are Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Nuh and Muhammad, giving six.
r: Counts differ between sources depending on which names are included.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "evidence"? (4)
f: Evidence is the facts or signs that show something is true, which is proof.
r: The adjective evident means obvious.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "negotiate"? (5)
f: To negotiate is to discuss terms in order to reach agreement, which is to bargain.
r: A negotiator mediates between parties.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "replenish"? (2)
f: To replenish is to fill up again, which is to refill.
r: Its antonym is deplete.

q: Who is the President of Syria as of October 2026? (2)
f: Ahmed al-Sharaa became president of the Syrian transitional government in January 2025 after Bashar al-Assad was overthrown in December 2024.
r: Bashar al-Assad was president from 2000 until December 2024, and the post of prime minister was abolished in March 2025.

q: What is the other name of the Ghazwa of Tabuk? (5)
f: Tabuk is also called Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Army of Hardship, because of the heat, distance and shortage of supplies.
r: It is the last expedition led by the Prophet (SAW) himself.

q: A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing? (18)
f: Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
r: A right turn from north would point to the east.

q: Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now? (7)
f: Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
r: A left turn from north would point him to the west.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'tame' (or 'tamed')? (25)
f: To tame means to make an animal gentle and used to humans, so tame or tamed means domesticated.
r: Its antonym is wild.

q: Ali is ten years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali is 20 years old, what will be his sister's age? (2)
f: The sister is 20 when Ali is 10, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 20, she is 20 + 10 = 30.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 120? (31)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
r: The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.

q: In set theory, what does the letter Z denote? (2)
f: Z stands for the set of integers, that is, all positive and negative whole numbers and zero (from the German word Zahlen).
r: N is natural numbers, Q is rational numbers and R is real numbers.

q: Which pronoun is used for a thing? (2)
f: 'It' is the singular pronoun used for things and animals; he and she are for persons.
r: 'They' or 'them' are plural pronouns.

q: What was the real (birth) name of Tipu Sultan? (2)
f: Tipu Sultan was born as Sultan Fateh Ali Khan Tipu, son of Haider Ali of Mysore.
r: He was known as the Tiger of Mysore.

q: Zun-Noon is the title of which prophet? (2)
f: Zun-Noon means the one of the fish and is the title of Hazrat Yunus (AS).
r: He was swallowed by a fish and prayed Laa ilaha illa anta subhanaka.

q: If today is Friday, what day will it be after 12 days? (3)
f: 12 days is 1 week plus 5 days, and 5 days after Friday is Wednesday.
r: The week has 7 days, so only the remainder after dividing by 7 matters.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (2)
f: The 2nd is Friday, so the 3rd is Saturday and the 4th is Sunday. The day after tomorrow means the 4th.
r: Day after tomorrow means two days after today.

q: Xinjiang, a province of China, touches which side of Pakistan? (6)
f: Xinjiang borders Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan across the Karakoram.
r: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with Xinjiang.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 15th of that month? (8)
f: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Tuesday, which is Saturday.
r: Counting the difference in dates and taking the remainder after dividing by 7 solves every such day question.

q: Umar's age is 4 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when Umar is 11 years old? (3)
f: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now, so she is 8 years older than Umar. When Umar is 11, she is 11 + 8 = 19.
r: After 7 years both ages increase by 7, so 12 + 7 = 19.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Ukraine? (2)
f: Serhii Koretskyi, formerly head of Naftogaz, was confirmed as Prime Minister by the Verkhovna Rada on 16 July 2026.
r: Yulia Svyrydenko served as Prime Minister from July 2025 before him, and Denys Shmyhal before her.

q: Who was the first President of Ukraine? (2)
f: Leonid Kravchuk became the first President of independent Ukraine in December 1991 after the Soviet Union broke up.
r: He served until 1994, when Leonid Kuchma succeeded him.

q: Bakar is older than Ali and Umair is younger than Ali. Which statement is correct? (2)
f: Bakar is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Umair, so the order is Bakar, Ali, Umair. Bakar is the oldest and Umair the youngest.
r: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a line from oldest to youngest.

q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud? (12)
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA), called Asadullah (Lion of Allah), was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
r: He is also known as Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, the chief of the martyrs.

q: What is a matrix whose number of rows is not equal to its number of columns called? (5)
f: A matrix with unequal numbers of rows and columns (m x n with m not equal to n) is a rectangular matrix.
r: If rows and columns are equal, it is a square matrix.

q: In which city is the International Islamic University (IIUI) located? (14)
f: The International Islamic University is in Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
r: It was established in 1980 and given its present status in 1985.

q: Who lives and works in the White House in Washington, D.C.? (2)
f: The White House is the official residence and workplace of the President of the United States.
r: The White House has been the residence of every US President since John Adams in 1800.

q: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza were names of what in pre-Islamic Arabia? (4)
f: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat were the three chief idols worshipped by the Arabs before Islam.
r: Al-Lat was worshipped at Taif and Al-Uzza near Makkah; Manat was worshipped near Madinah.

q: If x = (1/3) y and y = 9, what is the value of x? (5)
f: Substitute y = 9: x = (1/3) x 9 = 3.
r: Multiplying by 1/3 is the same as dividing by 3.

q: How many vowels are in ASGJIOYTBUF? (2)
f: The vowels are A, I, O and U, so there are 4. Y is counted as a consonant here.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)? (13)
f: The WTO has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT.

q: By what other name is Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) known? (8)
f: Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, meaning servant of Allah, and his descendants are the Bani Israel.
r: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS).

q: What is the meaning of the word 'zenith' (also its synonym)? (2)
f: Zenith means the highest point, peak or summit of something.
r: In astronomy the zenith is the point in the sky directly above the observer.

q: If x = 9y + 1 and y = 1/3, what is x? (4)
r: Always do multiplication before addition.

q: What is 25% of 75? (2)
f: 25% is one quarter: 75 / 4 = 18.75.

q: What is 25% of 80? (2)
f: 25% is one quarter: 80 / 4 = 20.
r: 25% equals 1/4.

q: What is 70% of 80? (10)
r: 70% of 80 equals 80% of 70.

q: What is 120 multiplied by 7?
r: Multiplying by 7 is the same as multiplying by 10 and subtracting three times the number.

q: What is 30% of 1/10 of 120?
f: One tenth of 120 is 12. Then 30% of 12 = 0.3 x 12 = 3.6.
r: Candidates sometimes remembered 3, but the exact answer is 3.6.

q: If Monday is the 12th day of a month, what day will be the 1st of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 12th is 11 days, and 11 = 7 + 4. So the 1st is 4 days before Monday, which is Thursday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what days are the 12th and the 14th?
f: The 12th is 10 days after the 2nd, and 10 = 7 + 3, so it is Sunday + 3 = Wednesday. The 14th is 12 days after, 12 = 7 + 5, so Sunday + 5 = Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 12th of that month? (5)
f: The 12th is 11 days after the 1st, and 11 = 7 + 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 13th of that month? (3)
f: The 13th is 9 days after the 4th, and 9 = 7 + 2. Monday + 2 days = Wednesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 13th of that month? (10)
f: The 13th is 11 days after the 2nd, and 11 = 7 + 4. Monday + 4 days = Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 25th of that month?
f: The 25th is 11 days after the 14th, and 11 = 7 + 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Friday, what day was the 4th of that month? (2)
f: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days, and 11 = 7 + 4. So the 4th is 4 days before Friday, which is Monday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 15th of that month?
f: The 15th is 14 days after the 1st, which is exactly two weeks, so it is also a Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: What is sin(180 - x) equal to? (4)
f: Angles 180 - x and x lie on the same horizontal level of the unit circle, so they have the same sine: sin(180 - x) = sin x.
r: In the same way, cos(180 - x) = -cos x.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at the outbreak of the Second World War in 1939?
f: Neville Chamberlain was Prime Minister from 1937 to May 1940 and declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.
r: The UK has no president; Winston Churchill replaced Chamberlain in May 1940, and Boris Johnson (named by a candidate) was PM only in 2019 to 2022.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th be? (7)
f: From the 1st to the 19th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th be? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Sunday, which is Wednesday.
