r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 20th be? (3)
f: From the 4th to the 20th is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Friday, which is Sunday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 days is 2 full weeks plus 6 day(s), so the day is 6 day(s) after Sunday, which is Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 5th to the 21st is 16 days. 16 days is 2 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be? (4)
f: From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 days is 2 full weeks plus 6 day(s), so the day is 6 day(s) after Friday, which is Thursday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be? (9)
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 days is 2 full weeks plus 5 day(s), so the day is 5 day(s) after Friday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 26th be? (30)
f: From the 12th to the 26th is 14 days. 14 days is 2 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) after Friday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be? (5)
f: From the 4th to the 27th is 23 days. 23 days is 3 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 27th be?
f: From the 5th to the 27th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 28th be? (2)
f: From the 3rd to the 28th is 25 days. 25 days is 3 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 28th be? (5)
f: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days. 24 days is 3 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 29th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 4th be? (4)
f: From the 4th back to the 29th is 25 days. 25 days is 3 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) before Tuesday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 29th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 29th is 26 days. 26 days is 3 full weeks plus 5 day(s), so the day is 5 day(s) after Friday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 6th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 29th be?
f: From the 6th to the 29th is 23 days. 23 days is 3 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: Which form of government was in force in Pakistan during the 1971 war?
o: Martial law (military government under Yahya Khan)
f: General Yahya Khan had taken over in March 1969 and imposed martial law, so Pakistan was under military rule in 1971. Power passed to Zulfikar Ali Bhutto in December 1971.
r: Ayub Khan, who ruled before Yahya Khan, had resigned in March 1969.

q: A village had 1600 people in 2000, and its population doubles every five years. What was its population in 1980? (2)
f: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings, so the population in 2000 is 16 times that of 1980. Hence 1600 divided by 16 gives 100.
r: Going back in time with doubling growth means halving the number once for every period.

q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct in total in May 1998? (13)
f: Pakistan conducted five tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I) and one more on 30 May 1998 (Chagai-II), a total of six. Some sources mention only the five of 28 May.
r: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-weapon state and the first in the Muslim world.

q: Which war took place between Pakistan and India in 1999?
f: The Kargil War was fought in the Kargil sector of Kashmir between May and July 1999.
r: The Lahore Declaration had been signed earlier in 1999 between Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 200 are absent. What percentage of students is present? (2)
f: Present students are 1500 minus 200, which is 1300. Then 1300 divided by 1500 times 100 gives 86.67 percent.
r: Percentage equals part divided by whole times 100.

q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2019?
f: According to UNHCR, Turkey hosted about 3.6 million refugees in 2019, mostly Syrians, which was the highest in the world.
r: In 2023 and 2024 Iran overtook Turkey as the largest refugee-hosting country.

q: Which number comes next in the series 115, 55, 170, 65, 225, ?
f: There are two series mixed together. The odd places 115, 170, 225 rise by 55 each time, and the even places 55, 65, next rise by 10, so the next term is 75.
r: Alternating series are solved by separating the odd and even positions.

q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution, Pakistan's second constitution, in 1969? (14)
f: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
r: Iskander Mirza abrogated the first constitution (1956) in October 1958.

q: Which is the second longest river in the world according to common textbooks?
f: The Nile is usually named first at about 6650 km and the Amazon, flowing mainly through Brazil, second at about 6400 km.
r: Sources differ: some recent measurements make the Amazon longer than the Nile, though the Amazon is the largest river by volume.

q: What is 4 x 3 + 2 x 3?
f: Multiply first: 4 x 3 is 12 and 2 x 3 is 6. Then 12 plus 6 gives 18.
r: In BODMAS, multiplication is done before addition.

q: In a class of 1200 students, 300 are absent. What percentage of students is present? (2)
f: Present students are 1200 minus 300, which is 900. Then 900 divided by 1200 times 100 gives 75 percent.
r: Absent percentage here is 25, and present plus absent always make 100 percent.

q: In a class of 500 students, 320 are present. What percentage of students is absent? (4)
f: Absent students are 500 minus 320, which is 180. Then 180 divided by 500 times 100 gives 36 percent.
r: Present students here are 64 percent.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 360 are boys. What percentage of the students is girls? (2)
f: Girls are 1500 minus 360, which is 1140. Then 1140 divided by 1500 times 100 gives 76 percent.
r: Boys here are 24 percent.

q: In a class of 400 students, 360 are boys. What percentage of the students is girls?
f: Girls are 400 minus 360, which is 40. Then 40 divided by 400 times 100 gives 10 percent.
r: Boys here are 90 percent.

q: Who was the 3rd Prime Minister of Pakistan? (6)
f: The order of Pakistan's early prime ministers was Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Muhammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali and H. S. Suhrawardy. So the third was Muhammad Ali Bogra.
r: Muhammad Ali Bogra took office in April 1953 after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.

q: Who was the 5th Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: The first five prime ministers were Liaquat Ali Khan, Nazimuddin, Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali and then H. S. Suhrawardy. Fazal Elahi Chaudhry was a President, not a Prime Minister.
r: Suhrawardy served from September 1956 to October 1957 and was followed by I. I. Chundrigar.

q: What is 4 + 4x4? (7)
f: Multiplication comes first: 4x4 = 16. Then 4 + 16 = 20.
r: Following BODMAS, 4 + 4x4 is not (4 + 4)x4 which would be 32.

q: What is one-fourth of 10% of 120? (16)
r: One-fourth of 120 itself is 30.

q: What is the transpose of a matrix of order 4x3? (2)
f: The transpose swaps rows and columns, so a 4x3 matrix becomes a 3x4 matrix.
r: The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 8th day be?
f: From the 2nd to the 8th is 6 days. Friday plus 6 days is Thursday.
r: Six days after any day equals one day before it.

q: In a school of 3000 students, 2700 are present. What percentage of students are absent?
r: Present students are 90% of the total.

q: By which title is Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) well known? (9)
f: Abdullah ibn Abbas was a great scholar of Quranic interpretation, so he is called Tarjuman-ul-Quran (interpreter of the Quran). He is also called Hibr-ul-Ummah.
r: Saifullah is the title of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).

q: Who was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abbas (RA) in relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (2)
f: He was the son of Hazrat Abbas (RA), the uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), so he was the Prophet's cousin.
r: He was born about three years before the Hijrat.

q: Who was Hazrat Halima Sadia (RA) in relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (2)
f: Hazrat Halima Sadia of Banu Saad nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert, so she was his foster mother.
r: The Prophet's real mother was Hazrat Amina.

q: In which year was the 1962 constitution of Pakistan abrogated? (19)
f: General Yahya Khan took over after Ayub Khan resigned and abrogated the 1962 constitution in March 1969 by imposing martial law.
r: The 1962 constitution had been introduced by Ayub Khan.

q: Insert the correct form of the verb: Lightning ____ across the bridge last night. (3)
f: The words last night show past time, so the simple past tense flashed is needed.
r: The past participle of flash is also flashed.

q: Change to active voice: Why was the thief seen by Ali?
o: Why did Ali see the thief?
Why had Ali seen the thief?
Why was Ali seeing the thief?
f: The past simple passive was seen becomes did ... see in the active, with Ali as the subject and the thief as the object.
r: In the active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.

q: On what date did Allama Iqbal deliver his Allahabad Address? (34)
f: The Allahabad session of the All India Muslim League was held in December 1930 and Iqbal delivered his address on 29 December 1930.
r: The idea of a separate Muslim state he gave there led to the Pakistan Resolution of 1940.

q: What is the antonym of accept?
f: To accept means to receive or agree to something, and its opposite is to reject or refuse.
r: Decline and refuse are also antonyms of accept.

q: Adnan is 12 years old and his sister is 2 times his age. What will be the age of the sister after 8 years?
f: The sister's age now is 2 x 12 = 24 years. After 8 years she will be 24 + 8 = 32 years.
r: Age problems are solved by first finding present ages and then adding the years that pass.

q: FSB is the intelligence agency of which country? (2)
f: The FSB (Federal Security Service) is the main security and counter-intelligence agency of the Russian Federation. It replaced the Soviet-era KGB's domestic functions.
r: The foreign intelligence agency of Russia is the SVR.

q: MI5 is the security agency of which country? (2)
f: MI5, the Security Service, is the domestic counter-intelligence and security agency of the United Kingdom.
r: MI6 (the Secret Intelligence Service) handles British foreign intelligence.

q: MOIS is the intelligence agency of which country?
f: MOIS is the Ministry of Intelligence of the Islamic Republic of Iran, also known as VAJA.
r: Pakistan's main intelligence agency is the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI).

q: Faiq and Ahmad were born in 1970 and 1977 respectively. What are their ages in 1999?
f: Faiq: 1999 - 1970 = 29 years. Ahmad: 1999 - 1977 = 22 years.
r: Age equals the given year minus the birth year.

q: Which is the national airline of Russia?
f: Aeroflot is the flag carrier and largest airline of Russia, based in Moscow.
r: Lufthansa is from Germany and Emirates from the UAE.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) as of October 2026? (3)
f: Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani of PML-N was elected the 17th Prime Minister of AJK on 28 August 2026 after the July-August 2026 elections.
r: Faisal Mumtaz Rathore was the previous prime minister before the 2026 elections.

q: Who was the President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir before Dr Najeeb Naqi?
f: Sultan Mehmood Chaudhry was President of AJK from 2021 until his death on 31 January 2026. Acting presidents served until Dr Najeeb Naqi took oath in September 2026.
r: Chaudhry Latif Akbar acted as president for part of that interim period.

q: Who was the first President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir? (16)
f: Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan became the first President of Azad Kashmir in October 1947 after the Poonch uprising.
r: He served four non-consecutive terms and is called Ghazi-e-Millat.

q: Akbar is older than Zarnab, and Ali is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
f: Ali is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Zarnab, so the order from oldest is Ali, Akbar, Zarnab. Zarnab is the youngest.
r: Ranking questions are solved by placing the names in a single line from oldest to youngest.

q: Akram is 3 times as old as Zahra, whose age is 4 years. What will be Akram's age after 22 years?
f: Akram's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 22 years he will be 12 + 22 = 34 years.
r: Always find the present age first, then add the number of years.

q: The expression 3y - 2x + 3 is an algebraic what?
f: It has variables, constants and operations but no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression, not an equation.
r: This expression has three terms: 3y, -2x and 3.

q: Who is Ali Sadpara? (6)
f: Muhammad Ali Sadpara was a famous Pakistani high-altitude mountaineer from Skardu who climbed eight-thousanders such as Nanga Parbat in winter.
r: He went missing on K2 in February 2021 during a winter attempt.

q: In the sentence 'Aliya is going to school', what part of speech is the word Aliya?
f: Aliya is the name of a person, so it is a proper noun.
r: A pronoun such as she would replace the name Aliya in the sentence.

q: Khalil-ullah is the title of which prophet? (10)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalil-ullah, meaning friend of Allah.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is Kaleem-ullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is Ruh-ullah.

q: On what date was Allama Muhammad Iqbal born? (3)
f: Allama Iqbal was born in Sialkot on 9 November 1877.
r: He died in Lahore on 21 April 1938.

q: What is the position of the letter O in the English alphabet?
f: Counting A=1 to O gives A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, so O is the 15th letter.
r: The 26 letters have 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

q: In which country does the world's largest volunteer ambulance service operate? (15)
f: The Edhi Foundation of Pakistan runs the largest volunteer ambulance network in the world, recognised by Guinness World Records.
r: The Edhi Foundation was founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi, known as the Angel of Mercy.

q: Boxer Amir Khan, a former world champion, belongs to which country?
f: Amir Khan was born in Bolton, England, and represented Great Britain; he is of Pakistani descent.
r: He won an Olympic silver medal in 2004 at Athens.

q: Which word is the antonym of anarchy? (4)
f: Anarchy means a state of disorder and absence of government, so its opposite is order.
r: Chaos, disorder and lawlessness are synonyms of anarchy.

q: How many interior angles does a square have?
f: A square is a quadrilateral with four corners, so it has four angles, each of 90 degrees.
r: The four angles of a square add up to 360 degrees.

q: Which is the largest animal in the world? (20)
f: The blue whale grows up to about 30 metres in length and weighs up to nearly 200 tonnes, bigger than any other animal.
r: The African elephant is the largest living land animal.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah announce his 14 Points? (9)
f: Jinnah presented his 14 Points in March 1929 in Delhi as a reply to the Nehru Report.
r: The 14 Points set out the minimum constitutional demands of the Muslims of India.

q: On which date was the plan for the partition and independence of India announced?
f: Lord Mountbatten announced the Partition Plan, known as the 3 June Plan, on 3 June 1947.
r: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament on 18 July 1947.

q: What is the solution of the equation 3x - 7 = -x + 9?
f: Move x terms to the left: 3x + x = 9 + 7, so 4x = 16 and x = 4.
r: Check: 3(4) - 7 = 5 and -4 + 9 = 5, so both sides are equal.

q: What is the antonym of perfect?
f: Perfect means without any fault, so the opposite is faulty or imperfect.
r: Flawless, ideal and exact are synonyms of perfect.

q: What is the antonym of abuse? (2)
f: Abuse means to treat badly or insult, so its opposite is to respect or treat well.
r: Mistreat, insult and harm are close in meaning to abuse.

q: What is the antonym of arbitrary?
f: Arbitrary means based on random choice rather than reason, so its opposite is reasoned.
r: Random and whimsical are synonyms of arbitrary.

q: What is the antonym of blunt?
f: Blunt means not sharp or having no fine edge, so the opposite is sharp.
r: Blunt can also mean frank and outspoken in speech.

q: What is the antonym of callousness?
f: Callousness is cruel lack of feeling for others, and its opposite is compassion.
r: Callous is an adjective and comes from the Latin word for hard skin.

q: What is the antonym of elated?
f: Elated means very happy and proud, and its opposite is depressed or downcast.
r: Joyful, excited and cheerful are close in meaning to elated.

q: What is the antonym of error? (7)
f: An error is a mistake, so the opposite is accuracy or correctness.
r: Mistake, fault and blunder are synonyms of error.

q: What is the antonym of evident? (2)
f: Evident means clearly seen or understood, so its opposite is obscure or unclear.
r: Obvious, clear and plain are synonyms of evident.

q: What is the antonym of frugal?
f: Frugal means careful in spending money, and its opposite is extravagant or wasteful.
r: Thrifty, careful and economical are synonyms of frugal.

q: What is the antonym of imminent?
f: Imminent means about to happen soon, so its opposite is remote or distant.
r: Do not confuse imminent with eminent, which means famous.

q: What is the antonym of liberal? (3)
f: Liberal means open to new ideas and tolerant of others, so its opposite is conservative or narrow-minded.
r: Liberal can also mean generous in giving.

q: What is the antonym of magnanimous?
f: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving, especially toward a rival, so its opposite is petty or mean-spirited.
r: Selfish is also given as an opposite in some word lists.

q: What is the antonym of wail?
f: To wail is to cry loudly in grief, so the opposite is to rejoice.
r: Cry, lament and weep are close in meaning to wail.

q: Where is Masjid Aqsa located? (2)
f: Masjid Aqsa stands in the old city of Jerusalem in Palestine.
r: It was the first qibla of the Muslims and is the third holiest mosque in Islam.

q: The Rann of Kutch is a marshy region lying between Sindh (Pakistan) and which Indian state?
f: The Rann of Kutch is a large salt marsh between the Sindh province of Pakistan and the Indian state of Gujarat.
r: A 1965 border dispute over the Rann was settled by an international tribunal in 1968.

q: If 6 is the arithmetic mean between 4 and B, what is the value of B?
f: Mean = (4 + B) / 2 = 6, so 4 + B = 12 and B = 8.
r: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 18 and 36? (5)
r: The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by their number.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of (y + 3) and (y - 2)?
f: Sum = (y + 3) + (y - 2) = 2y + 1; dividing by 2 gives y + 0.5.
r: Check with y = 1: the numbers are 4 and -1, whose mean is 1.5, which equals 1 + 0.5.

q: Boxing is called the noble art of what?
f: Boxing has long been called the noble art of self-defence.
r: Modern boxing rules are based on the Marquess of Queensberry rules of 1867.

q: In which year was Benazir Bhutto assassinated? (3)
f: Benazir Bhutto was assassinated on 27 December 2007 in Rawalpindi after an election rally.
r: She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country.

q: Who promulgates ordinances in Pakistan when the National Assembly is not in session?
f: Under Article 89 of the Constitution, the President may promulgate an ordinance when Parliament is not in session.
r: An ordinance must be laid before Parliament and lapses after 120 days unless extended or approved.

q: What is the currency of Australia? (6)
f: Australia uses the Australian dollar (AUD).
r: Australia used the Australian pound until decimal currency was introduced in 1966.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Australia (as of 2026)?
f: Anthony Albanese of the Labor Party has been Prime Minister since May 2022.
r: His predecessor Scott Morrison served from 2018 to 2022.

q: Who is the author of the book In the Line of Fire? (5)
f: In the Line of Fire (2006) is the memoir of General Pervez Musharraf.
r: It was published when Musharraf was President of Pakistan.

q: Who is the author of the book Mein Kampf? (31)
f: Mein Kampf (My Struggle) was written by Adolf Hitler, partly while he was in prison in 1924.
r: It was published in two volumes in 1925 and 1926.

q: What is the meaning of the word autonomy?
f: Autonomy means the right or ability of a person, group or region to govern itself and make its own decisions.
r: An autonomous region is one that has its own local government within a larger country.

q: A boy has an average of 50 marks in 5 tests. How many marks must he score in the 6th test to raise his average to 70?
f: Total of 5 tests = 50 x 5 = 250. Total needed for 6 tests = 70 x 6 = 420, so the next score is 420 - 250 = 170.
r: Average = sum of all values divided by the number of values.

q: The line x = 5 is parallel to which axis?
o: It is parallel to no axis
f: All points on x = 5 have the same x value, so it is a vertical line parallel to the y-axis.
r: The equation x = 0 is the y-axis itself.

q: The line y = 6 is parallel to which axis? (5)
f: All points on y = 6 have the same y value, so it is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at (0, 6).
r: The equation y = 0 is the x-axis itself.

q: What is the name of the autobiography of Field Marshal Ayub Khan? (6)
f: Ayub Khan wrote Friends Not Masters, published in 1967.
r: In the Line of Fire is the autobiography of Pervez Musharraf.

q: Who is Azazeel, according to Islamic tradition?
f: Azazeel is the name by which Iblis (Shaitan) was known before he refused to prostrate to Hazrat Adam (AS).
r: Iblis was a jinn who lived among the angels.

q: Rehman Baba was a famous poet of which language? (35)
f: Rehman Baba (17th century) is a celebrated Sufi poet of the Pashto language.
r: His shrine is in Peshawar.

q: A boy walks 10 miles north, turns back and walks 10 miles, then turns right and again turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
f: After turning back he walks south and faces south. Turning right from south he faces west, and turning right again he faces north.
r: A right turn is a 90 degree clockwise turn.

q: In which city of Pakistan is Liaquat Bagh located?
f: Liaquat Bagh is a park in Rawalpindi where Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated in 1951.
r: It is also known for the 2007 assassination of Benazir Bhutto nearby.

q: On which date did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place? (2)
f: British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd in Amritsar on 13 April 1919, the Baisakhi day.
r: The massacre led to a wave of anti-British feeling in India.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh (as of 2026)? (26)
f: Tarique Rahman of the BNP became Prime Minister on 17 February 2026 after the general election.
r: Before him Muhammad Yunus led the interim government after Sheikh Hasina left in 2024.

q: In which year was the World Bank established? (2)
f: The World Bank was set up at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944 and began operations in 1946.
r: Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C.

q: Who were Banu Quraiza? (6)
o: A branch of the Quraish of Makkah
f: Banu Quraiza were a Jewish tribe living near Madinah. They broke their agreement with the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq).
r: After the Trench, the Muslims besieged their fortress and the matter was settled by the judgement of Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

q: What do the names of Surah Al-Fatiha and Surah Al-Baqarah mean in English?
f: Al-Fatiha means The Opening and Al-Baqarah means The Cow.
r: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran, and Al-Fatiha is its first.

q: Where is the Sukkur Barrage located? (2)
f: Sukkur Barrage is built on the River Indus at Sukkur in the province of Sindh.
r: It was completed in 1932 and feeds seven major canals.

q: What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 24 cm? (3)
f: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 6 x 24 = 72 square cm.
r: The area of a triangle is always half of the rectangle with the same base and height.

q: What is the height of a triangle whose base is 6 cm and area is 24 square cm?
f: Area = half x base x height, so 24 = 0.5 x 6 x h = 3h. Therefore h = 8 cm.
r: Height = 2 x area divided by base.

q: Is the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan based on a parliamentary or a presidential system? (16)
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary form of government with the Prime Minister as chief executive and the President as head of state.
r: The 1962 Constitution, by contrast, was presidential.

q: On which basis was Pakistan created, according to the resolution passed in 1940?
f: The Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940, based on the Two-Nation Theory, demanded separate Muslim states and led to Pakistan.
r: It was presented by A. K. Fazlul Haq and seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

q: Who is known as Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya (best of mankind after the prophets)?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA) is called Afzalul Bashar Ba'd al-Anbiya, the best of mankind after the prophets.
r: He was the first Caliph of Islam and the closest companion of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali becomes 8 years old, how old will his sister be? (2)
f: Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now. Ali needs 4 more years to be 8, so sister will be 8 + 4 = 12.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: Change into active voice: The rooms are being decorated by the students.
o: The students were decorating the rooms.
The students are decorating the rooms.
The students have decorated the rooms.
f: The passive present continuous (are being decorated) becomes the active present continuous (are decorating).
r: In active voice the doer becomes the subject.

q: Fill in the blank: Did the students ----- a lot of work in class?
f: After the auxiliary did the verb takes its base form, so have is correct.
r: In questions with did, the main verb never takes the past form.

q: To what name was Islamabad's Kashmir Highway changed in August 2020?
f: In August 2020 the government renamed Kashmir Highway in Islamabad as Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris.
r: It was done ahead of Youm-e-Istehsal on 5 August.

q: Which constitution was in force in Pakistan before the 1973 Constitution?
f: The 1962 Constitution, given by Ayub Khan, remained until it was abrogated in 1969 by Yahya Khan, apart from a brief interim period.
r: An Interim Constitution was in force in 1972 before the 1973 Constitution.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty belongs to whom? (14)
f: The Preamble and Objectives Resolution state that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, exercised by the people as a sacred trust.
r: The authority is exercised through chosen representatives within limits set by Allah.

q: In which place was Benazir Bhutto buried? (4)
f: Benazir Bhutto was buried in the family mausoleum at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana, Sindh, beside her father.
r: She was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 27 December 2007.

q: What was the name of Benazir Bhutto's mother?
f: Begum Nusrat Bhutto, of Iranian-Kurdish origin, was the wife of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and mother of Benazir.
r: She was also known as Mader-e-Jamhooriat (Mother of Democracy).

q: Between whom was the brotherhood (Mukhawat) established after the migration to Madinah? (6)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) created brotherhood between the Muhajirin who came from Makkah and the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah.
r: It helped settle the Muhajirin economically in Madinah.

q: Near which town is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built?
f: Diamer Bhasha Dam is on the Indus River about 40 km downstream of Chilas on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is planned as a very large dam for water storage and electricity.

q: What is the meaning of biased? (2)
o: Prejudiced in favour of one side
f: A biased person unfairly favours or opposes someone or something.
r: Bias means prejudice.

q: What is a bicameral legislature? (3)
o: A legislature chosen by the army
f: Bicameral means two chambers; the word camera means chamber.
r: Pakistan's Parliament has the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: Which was the first bicameral legislature of Pakistan, consisting of a National Assembly and a Senate?
f: The 1956 and 1962 Constitutions provided a single House (unicameral legislature). The 1973 Constitution created Parliament with two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: The Bogra Formula of 1953 had proposed a two-house legislature, but it was never adopted; some sources differ on how the first bicameral body is described.

q: Where is the Black Sea located? (2)
o: Between southeastern Europe and western Asia
f: The Black Sea lies between southeastern Europe and western Asia, bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia.
r: It connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles straits.

q: In which year did Muhammad Ali Bogra become Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: Governor-General Ghulam Muhammad dismissed Khawaja Nazimuddin in April 1953 and appointed Muhammad Ali Bogra, then ambassador to the USA, as Prime Minister.
r: Bogra remained Prime Minister until August 1955 and was succeeded by Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.

q: Who bowled the fastest recorded delivery in cricket history at 161.3 km per hour?
f: Shoaib Akhtar bowled a delivery of 161.3 km per hour against England in the 2003 World Cup, which is still the official record.
r: He is known as the Rawalpindi Express.

q: In a class the number of girls is 7 more than the number of boys and the total is 33. How many boys are there? (3)
f: Let boys be x, so girls are x + 7 and 2x + 7 = 33, giving x = 13. Girls are therefore 20.

q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan in March 1969?
f: When Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969, General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
r: Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution in 1958.

q: Which reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India? (11)
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted separate electorates to Muslims.
r: The Simla Deputation of 1906 had demanded separate electorates from Lord Minto.

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes? (8)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: In a bus of 24 people, 3/4 are male. What percentage are female?
f: Males are 3/4 of 24 = 18, so females are 24 - 18 = 6. Percentage = 6/24 x 100 = 25 percent.
r: The female share is 1 - 3/4 = 1/4, which is 25 percent.

q: Fill in the blank: We have business classes ______ night. (7)
f: The preposition 'at' is used with night in the phrase 'at night'.
r: We say in the morning, in the evening, but at night.

q: From which country did Pakistan acquire the J-10C fighter aircraft? (3)
f: The J-10C is a Chinese fighter built by Chengdu Aircraft Corporation. Pakistan Air Force inducted it from China.
r: Pakistan also operates the JF-17 Thunder, which it co-developed with China.

q: How many days are there in a common (non-leap) calendar year?
f: A common year has 12 months totalling 365 days. A leap year has 366 days.
r: A leap year comes every four years and adds 29 February.

q: What is the complex number 4 - 2i called?
f: A number of the form a + bi with i the square root of minus 1 is a complex number. Here a = 4 and b = -2.
r: Its conjugate is 4 + 2i.

q: Approximately how many prophets came to the world in total, according to popular Islamic tradition? (9)
f: A popular narration says that about 124,000 prophets were sent. The number is not given in the Quran.
r: Sources differ on the exact number, and 313 is commonly given for the Rasuls (messengers).

q: Who was the ruler of Sindh when Muhammad bin Qasim invaded it in 711 AD? (4)
f: Raja Dahir of the Brahman dynasty ruled Sindh from Aror. Muhammad bin Qasim defeated him in 712 AD.
r: The Sindh campaign took place under Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf.

q: Zakat becomes obligatory on a minimum of how many camels? (4)
f: The nisab for camels is five. One goat is due on 5 to 9 camels.
r: Zakat on gold has a nisab of 7.5 tola, and on silver 52.5 tola.

q: Which canal separates Asia from Africa?
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates Africa from the Sinai Peninsula in Asia. It links the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
r: The canal opened in 1869.

q: What is the capital of Argentina? (6)
f: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.
r: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay.

q: What is the capital of Bahrain? (56)
f: Manama is the capital of Bahrain, an island country in the Persian Gulf.
r: Doha is the capital of Qatar.

q: What is the capital of Cuba? (12)
f: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.
r: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica.

q: What is the capital of Denmark? (5)
f: Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark.
r: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

q: What is the capital of India? (5)
f: New Delhi is the capital of India.
r: Capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

q: What is the capital of Thailand?
f: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.
r: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.

q: On which date is International Women's Day celebrated? (2)
f: International Women's Day is observed every year on 8 March.
r: International Labour Day falls on 1 May.

q: How many centimetres are there in one metre?
f: The prefix centi means one hundredth, so 1 metre equals 100 centimetres.
r: 1 kilometre equals 1000 metres.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026? (79)
f: Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate and sworn in on 9 April 2024.
r: Sadiq Sanjrani was Senate chairman from 2018 to 2024.

q: Who is the Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as of October 2026? (3)
f: Mauritania's Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed was elected OIC Secretary General on 27 August 2026 in Jeddah, succeeding Hissein Brahim Taha of Chad.
r: Hissein Brahim Taha held the post from 2021, which was the answer in 2022.

q: In mathematics, a quantity whose value can change is called a (6)
f: A variable is a symbol that can take different values, unlike a constant whose value is fixed.
r: In the expression 3x + 5, x is the variable and 3 is the coefficient.

q: Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani C-in-C in January 1951, after British generals Messervy and Gracey.
r: Ayub Khan later became President of Pakistan after the 1958 coup.

q: According to Islamic teaching, what is recited in the ear of a newborn baby?
f: It is Sunnah to recite the Azan in the baby's right ear soon after birth.
r: Iqamah is recited in the left ear according to many scholars.

q: Which of the following is a Chinese COVID-19 vaccine?
f: Sinopharm is made in China; the other three were developed in the USA, Germany and the UK.
r: Sinovac and CanSino are other Chinese vaccines used in Pakistan.

q: Choose the correct word: Who did you take this book ____?
f: The sentence means from whom the book was taken, so the preposition from is correct.
r: Formally the sentence would be: From whom did you take this book?

q: In which US state is the Grand Canyon located?
f: The Grand Canyon, carved by the Colorado River, is in northern Arizona.
r: It is about 446 km long and up to 1.8 km deep.

q: In which period did the American Civil War take place?
f: The American Civil War between the Union and the Confederacy was fought from 1861 to 1865.
r: It ended slavery in the USA with the 13th Amendment in 1865.

q: Who led the Union side in the American Civil War?
f: Abraham Lincoln was President of the Union (the Northern states) during the war.
r: Jefferson Davis led the Confederacy and Robert E. Lee was its top general.

q: Mohenjo-daro, a famous site of the Indus Valley Civilization, is located in which province of Pakistan?
f: Mohenjo-daro lies in Larkana district of Sindh on the bank of the Indus.
r: Harappa, the other major city, is in Punjab.

q: Who were the first people to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953?
f: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.
r: Mallory and Irvine vanished near the summit in 1924 and their success is unproven.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'precious'?
f: Precious means of great value or highly prized.
r: Gold and diamonds are called precious metals and stones.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'breach'? (5)
f: To breach something is to break or violate it, such as a rule or a contract.
r: A breach can also mean a gap made in a wall.

q: Which line is the de facto boundary between India and China? (10)
f: The India-China frontier is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
r: The McMahon Line is the 1914 boundary in the east that China does not accept.

q: What is the antonym of 'coercive'? (17)
f: Coercive means forcing someone to act by pressure or threat, so its opposite is voluntary, done by free choice.
r: The noun form is coercion, meaning the use of force or threats to make someone do something.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'coercive'? (3)
f: Coercive means using force or pressure to make someone obey, which is close in meaning to compulsory.
r: Its antonym is voluntary.

q: In a matrix of order 5 x 4, how many elements are there in each column? (6)
f: The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.
r: The total number of elements in a 5 x 4 matrix is 20.

q: Which letter and number come next in the series: Z1, X3, V5, T7, ?
f: The letters move back by 2 each time (Z, X, V, T, R) and the numbers increase by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is R9.
r: Letter series that skip every other letter are common in verbal tests.

q: What is the synonym of 'command'?
f: To command means to give an authoritative instruction, which is the same as to order.
r: Command also means control over a unit, as in the command of an army.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission? (6)
f: The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.
r: Quaid-e-Azam later put forward his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: What is common in the series 4, 8, 12, 16? (2)
f: 4 = 4 x 1, 8 = 4 x 2, 12 = 4 x 3 and 16 = 4 x 4, so every term is a multiple of 4 with a common difference of 4.
r: A series with a constant difference is called an arithmetic progression.

q: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 gave benefits to which community? (3)
f: It created the Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam, giving Muslims better chances in education, jobs and politics.
r: Hindu agitation led the British to annul the partition in 1911.

q: 900 employees work in a company and 480 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
r: The percentage of men is 53.33%, and the two percentages add up to 100.

q: In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab? (16)
f: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.
r: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had ruled the Punjab until his death in 1839.

q: Who compiled the hadith collection Musnad Ahmad? (3)
f: Musnad Ahmad was compiled by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, founder of the Hanbali school of fiqh.
r: It contains tens of thousands of hadith arranged by narrator.

q: What is the largest composite number from 1 to 99?
f: 97 is prime, 98 = 2 x 49 and 99 = 9 x 11 has factors other than 1 and itself. So 99 is the largest composite number.
r: A composite number has more than two factors.

q: On what date was the Indian National Congress established? (15)
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.
r: Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD? (12)
f: Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.
r: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) conquered Damascus region, not Jerusalem.

q: How many members did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan originally have?
f: The first Constituent Assembly formed in 1947 had 69 members.
r: Its membership was later raised to 79 after the addition of more members.

q: In which year did the construction of Tarbela Dam begin? (2)
f: The contract was awarded in May 1968 and main construction ran from 1968 to 1976.
r: Tarbela Dam is built on the Indus River and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: In which year was Rawal Dam built (completed)?
f: Rawal Dam on the Korang River in Islamabad is listed as completed in 1962.
r: Some sources give 1962 as the start of construction, so sources differ.

q: Who performs the duties of the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to act?
f: Article 49 of the Constitution says the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
r: If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.

q: Convert 60 degrees into radians. (11)
f: Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
r: 180 degrees equals pi radians.

q: Convert to passive voice: He told me about the accident.
o: I was told about the accident by him.
I am told about the accident by him.
The accident was told by him to me about.
I had told about the accident by him.
f: The past simple active becomes was/were plus past participle in passive, with the object I becoming the subject.
r: Passive voice puts the receiver of the action at the start of the sentence.

q: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
f: A generator (dynamo) turns a coil in a magnetic field and produces electric current from mechanical motion.
r: An electric motor does the opposite and converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.

q: What does SUPARCO stand for?
o: Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission
Satellite and Upper Atmosphere Research Corporation
Space Utilization and Planetary Research Commission
Science and Upper Atmosphere Research Council
f: SUPARCO is Pakistan's national space agency, called the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission.
r: It was established in 1961.

q: The Wakhan Corridor connects Pakistan to which province of Afghanistan?
f: The Wakhan Corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan province of north-eastern Afghanistan.
r: It separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.

q: Between which two countries is the longest international border in the world? (2)
f: The Canada-USA border is about 8,900 km long including the Alaska border, the longest in the world.
r: It is also the longest undefended border.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes? (5)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
r: At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.

q: A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (2)
f: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.
r: Speed in km per minute is distance in km/h divided by 60, here 2 km per minute.

q: A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.
r: The same train covers 1.5 km every minute.

q: If a car covers 20 km in an hour, what distance does it cover in 30 minutes?
f: 30 minutes is half an hour. So the distance is 20 / 2 = 10 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.
r: The car's speed is 54 km/h.

q: Which of the following British reforms introduced separate electorates for the Muslims of the subcontinent?
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted Muslims separate electorates, which was a key demand of the Simla Deputation of 1906.
r: The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates, while the Cripps Mission came in 1942.

q: Which is the major rabi (winter) crop of Pakistan? (3)
f: Wheat is sown in October to December and harvested in April to May, which makes it the main rabi crop.
r: Cotton, rice and sugarcane are kharif (summer) crops.

q: On which date is World Red Cross and Red Crescent Day celebrated?
f: It is observed on 8 May, the birthday of Henry Dunant, the founder of the Red Cross.
r: Henry Dunant won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

q: After the 2026 tournament, which country or countries will host the next FIFA World Cup in 2030?
f: FIFA awarded the 2030 World Cup to Spain, Portugal and Morocco, with opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the centenary.
r: The 2026 World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, and Qatar hosted in 2022.

q: What is the currency of Belgium (Brussels) and Finland? (2)
f: Both Belgium and Finland are members of the Eurozone and use the euro.
r: Belgium used the Belgian franc before adopting the euro in 2002.

q: What is the currency of Uganda? (2)
f: Uganda's national currency is the Ugandan shilling.
r: The capital of Uganda is Kampala.

q: What is the name of China's currency? (8)
f: China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.
r: The word renminbi means the people's currency.

q: Who is the current Director General of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) of Pakistan?
f: Fuad Asadullah Khan has led the IB since 2022 and in May 2026 the Prime Minister approved a four-year extension for him.
r: He was the first officer from the intelligence cadre to head the IB.

q: Who is the current Chancellor of Germany? (7)
f: Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.
r: His predecessor was Olaf Scholz (2021 to 2025), and before him Angela Merkel served from 2005 to 2021.

q: If a circle is divided into 360 equal parts, what is each part called?
f: A full circle measures 360 degrees, so each of 360 equal parts is one degree.
r: A quadrant is a quarter of a circle, or 90 degrees.

q: Which country announced the cutting of funding to the World Health Organization in 2020 and later withdrew from it?
f: In 2020 President Trump halted US funding to the WHO, and in 2025 the United States started its withdrawal.
r: The United States had been the largest single donor to the WHO.

q: In which country is the Khanpur (Kahnpur) Dam located?
f: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Haripur in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: Hazrat Asma (R.A), known as Dhat un-Nitaqayn, was the daughter of which Sahabi? (3)
f: Asma bint Abu Bakr was the elder sister of Hazrat Aisha (R.A) and helped the Prophet (PBUH) during the Hijrah.
r: She was the mother of Abdullah ibn Zubair (R.A).

q: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), who was married to Hazrat Uthman (R.A), was the daughter of whom? (2)
f: Umm Kulthum was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and married Hazrat Uthman after the death of her sister Ruqayyah.
r: This is why Hazrat Uthman is called Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Ali (R.A) and Hazrat Fatima (R.A)?
f: Hazrat Zainab bint Ali was a daughter of Hazrat Ali and Hazrat Fatima and sister of Hasan and Husain.
r: Their other daughter was Umm Kulthum bint Ali.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
f: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February, so it has 365 + 1 = 366 days.
r: A leap year comes every four years, for example 2024 and 2028.

q: What is the definition of a noun?
o: A word that describes an action
A word that names a person, place, thing or idea
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
f: A noun is a naming word: it names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
r: A verb shows action, an adjective describes a noun, and a conjunction joins words or clauses.

q: What is a square matrix? (2)
o: A matrix with equal number of rows and columns
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with only one column
f: A square matrix has the same number of rows as columns, for example 3 by 3.
r: Only square matrices have determinants and can have inverses.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'demise'? (4)
f: Demise means death or the end of something.
r: Its antonym is birth.

q: In which body were the Basic Democrats of Ayub Khan's system mainly represented?
o: Electoral college for President and assemblies
f: Basic Democrats, elected from union councils, formed the electoral college that elected the President and members of the assemblies.
r: The system was announced in 1959 and used in the 1965 presidential election.

q: How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)? (5)
f: Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.
r: The number was later raised to 120,000, but 80,000 was the original figure.

q: What is the derivative of tan x with respect to x?
f: d/dx (tan x) = d/dx (sin x / cos x) = (cos^2 x + sin^2 x) / cos^2 x = sec^2 x.
r: The derivative of cot x is minus cosec squared x.

q: Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake? (8)
f: Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.
r: It is a very alkaline lake in the Great Rift Valley.

q: What is the determinant of a diagonal matrix? (3)
f: For a diagonal matrix all off-diagonal entries are zero, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal elements.
r: The sum of diagonal elements is called the trace.

q: What is a diagonal matrix? (12)
o: A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
f: A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.
r: Scalar and identity matrices are special diagonal matrices.

q: If the side of a square is a, what is the length of its diagonal?
f: By Pythagoras, diagonal = square root of (a^2 + a^2) = a times root 2.
r: The diagonals of a square are equal and bisect each other at right angles.

q: What is the diameter of a circle whose radius is 28?
f: Diameter = 2 x radius = 2 x 28 = 56.
r: Circumference equals pi times diameter.

q: What is the radius of a circle with diameter 52 cm?
f: Radius = diameter / 2 = 52 / 2 = 26 cm.
r: Area of this circle is pi x 26 x 26.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary? (31)
f: Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
r: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.

q: On which date did the singer Lata Mangeshkar die?
f: Lata Mangeshkar, the Indian playback singer, died in Mumbai on 6 February 2022.
r: She was born on 28 September 1929.

q: Where was democracy first practised in the world?
f: Democracy began in the ancient Greek city-state of Athens around the 5th century BC.
r: The word democracy comes from the Greek words demos (people) and kratos (rule).

q: The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices? (5)
f: Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.
r: The advice is given by Hazrat Luqman to his son in Surah Luqman.

q: What is the opposite of the word diversity? (6)
f: Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.
r: Diversity is a synonym of variety.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
f: One pencil costs 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils cost 5 x 5 = Rs 25.
r: One dozen means 12 items.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils? (2)
f: Four pencils are one third of a dozen, so the cost is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.
r: One pencil costs Rs 2.25.

q: What is the national dress of Pakistan?
f: Shalwar Kameez is worn across all provinces and is recognised as the national dress of Pakistan.
r: Sherwani is the national dress for formal wear of men and is linked with Quaid-e-Azam.

q: What is the cutting of hair by a pilgrim at the end of Hajj called? (4)
f: Halq means shaving the head, and qasr means trimming the hair; one of them is done to leave the state of Ihram.
r: Women only trim a fingertip length of hair.

q: What is the measure in degrees of each angle (corner) of a square? (4)
f: A square has four equal angles and they sum to 360 degrees, so each is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees.
r: A rectangle also has four right angles.

q: What does ECO stand for?
f: ECO stands for Economic Cooperation Organization, a regional group of Asian countries.
r: It succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of 1964.

q: Abdul Sattar Edhi, the famous humanitarian known as the Angel of Mercy, belonged to which country?
f: Edhi spent his life in Pakistan and founded the Edhi Foundation in Karachi. He is regarded as one of the greatest humanitarians of Pakistan.
r: Edhi died in Karachi on 8 July 2016.

q: If one egg takes 2 minutes to boil, how many minutes will 5 eggs take when boiled together in the same pot?
f: Eggs boil at the same time in the same pot, so the time does not depend on the number of eggs. All 5 eggs take 2 minutes.
r: This is a classic logic puzzle where the obvious multiplication is wrong.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest? (8)
f: Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
r: Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.

q: If Akbar is elder than Ahmad and Adnan is elder than Akbar, then who is the eldest?
f: Adnan is elder than Akbar, and Akbar is elder than Ahmad. So Adnan is the eldest.
r: The youngest in this chain is Ahmad.

q: In which pact were separate electorates for Muslims granted? (2)
f: Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress accepted the Muslim League's demand for separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Separate electorates were first given in the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.

q: What is a set that has no element called? (3)
f: A set with no element is called the null set or empty set and is written as a circle with a slash or as curly brackets with nothing inside.
r: The empty set is a subset of every set.

q: What is a set with exactly one element called? (4)
f: A set containing only one element, such as the set containing 5 alone, is called a singleton set.
r: A singleton set has exactly two subsets.

q: If every element of set A is also an element of set B, then A is called what of B? (2)
f: When all elements of A belong to B, A is a subset of B, written A is contained in B.
r: B is then called a superset of A.

q: Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
f: Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.
r: Mammals are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'embellish'?
o: To make more attractive by adding decoration
f: Embellish means to decorate or beautify something, or to add extra details to a story.
r: Adorn and ornament are synonyms of embellish.

q: When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon? (16)
f: Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Which of the following are the vowels of the English alphabet? (2)
f: The five vowel letters of English are A, E, I, O and U.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters, so 21 are consonants.

q: If RAT is coded as TAR (letters reversed), then what is FAT equal to?
f: RAT becomes TAR by reversing the order of letters. Reversing FAT gives TAF.
r: Reversal codes are the simplest letter codes.

q: In trigonometry, what is tan x equal to? (4)
o: cos x divided by sin x
sin x divided by cos x
f: Tangent is the ratio of sine to cosine, so tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.
r: Cot x is the reciprocal of tan x.

q: What is cosecant x equal to? (4)
o: sin x divided by cos x
f: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec x = 1 / sin x.
r: Sec x = 1 / cos x and cot x = 1 / tan x.

q: What type of equation is 6x - 5x - 7 = 0?
f: Simplifying gives x - 7 = 0, which has highest power 1 of x, so it is linear and gives x = 7.
r: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.

q: Who headed the committee for the collection of the Holy Quran in the era of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (3)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit, the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran into one volume.
r: Zaid also led the committee in the era of Hazrat Usman (RA).

q: How many end points does a ray have? (2)
f: A ray starts at one fixed point and extends endlessly in one direction, so it has one end point.
r: A line segment has two end points and a line has none.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was among his bitter enemies?
f: Abu Lahab (Abdul Uzza) strongly opposed the Prophet (PBUH) and a Surah of the Quran is named after him. Abu Jahal was not his uncle.
r: Surah Al-Masad condemns Abu Lahab.

q: Which event did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) take part in after the Harb-e-Fijar? (4)
f: After the Harb-e-Fijar, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in Hilf-ul-Fudul, a pact formed in Makkah to help the oppressed and protect travellers and the weak. He was a young man at the time.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) later said that he would still accept such a pact even in Islam.

q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular hexagon? (3)
f: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. A hexagon has 6 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 6 = 60 degrees.
r: Each internal angle of a regular hexagon is 120 degrees.

q: What is the measure of each external angle of a regular octagon?
f: The sum of the external angles of any polygon is 360 degrees. An octagon has 8 sides, so each external angle is 360 divided by 8 = 45 degrees.
r: Each internal angle of a regular octagon is 135 degrees.

q: What is meant by Laissez-faire in economics?
o: Minimum government interference in the economy
f: Laissez-faire is a French term meaning let do. It is the policy that the government should interfere as little as possible in economic affairs and leave markets free.
r: Adam Smith is the economist most associated with ideas of free markets.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
f: All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.
r: Dictionary order compares letters one by one from the left.

q: Hazrat Ali (RA) belonged to which family (clan) of Quraish? (2)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, who was a son of Abdul Muttalib of Banu Hashim. He was thus a cousin of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) also belonged to Banu Hashim.

q: For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous? (5)
f: Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.
r: Gaddani lies in Lasbela District.

q: For which product is Sialkot famous? (12)
f: Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.
r: Footballs made in Sialkot have been used in FIFA World Cups.

q: For what is Ziyarat in Balochistan famous? (2)
f: Ziyarat is a hill town famous for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days in 1948, and for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.
r: The Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.

q: A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
f: The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: Son is to father as nephew is to what? (2)
f: A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.
r: The female counterpart of a nephew is a niece.

q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: The father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was Hazrat Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
r: His mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahab.

q: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name? (13)
f: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.
r: It is also called Sab'a Mathani and is recited in every rakat of Namaz.

q: For which crime was Fatimah bint Aswad (a woman of Banu Makhzum) punished in the time of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (3)
f: Fatimah bint Aswad of Banu Makhzum was found guilty of theft, and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) ordered the punishment for theft. He refused to let rank or family influence the decision.
r: He said that nations before them were destroyed because they punished the poor but spared the rich.

q: Which day is observed in Pakistan on 5th February every year? (2)
f: Pakistan observes 5 February as Kashmir Solidarity Day to express support for the people of Indian-administered Kashmir.
r: Pakistan Day is on 23 March and Defence Day on 6 September.

q: Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan? (70)
f: Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.
r: Asim Munir was promoted to Field Marshal in May 2025, making him the second.

q: Find x if 3x - 9 = x + 7. (6)
f: Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.

r: Cross multiplying gives 14x = 56, which also gives x = 4.

q: What is the mean of 1, 3, 5 and 6?
f: Sum = 1 + 3 + 5 + 6 = 15; divided by 4 numbers gives 3.75.
r: The mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.

q: Which letter comes after M in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs L, M, N, so N follows M.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
f: Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.
r: An anagram uses all the given letters exactly once.

q: Which is the largest fort of Pakistan? (15)
f: Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.
r: It is also known as the Great Wall of Sindh.

q: Between whom was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought? (2)
o: The Muslims of Madinah and the Quraish of Makkah
The Muslims and the Jews of Khyber
The Muslims and the Byzantine army
The Muslims and the tribe of Thaqif at Taif
f: Badr was fought in 2 AH between the small Muslim army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and the much larger army of the Quraish of Makkah.
r: Badr is called Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day that separated right from wrong.

q: Near which city is the mountain where the Battle of Uhud was fought? (2)
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought at the foot of Mount Uhud, a few kilometres north of Madinah.
r: The battle took place in 3 AH between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

q: Which fraction comes next in the series: 3/5, 5/8, 8/12, 12/17, ?
f: Numerators are 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 with differences 2, 3, 4, 5, so the next is 17. Each denominator equals the next numerator, and the denominators 5, 8, 12, 17 continue with 17+6 = 23.
r: Each fraction's numerator equals the previous fraction's denominator.

q: What is the currency of France? (4)
f: France uses the euro, which replaced the French franc in 2002.
r: The euro is shared by most countries of the European Union eurozone.

q: If the first day of a month is Friday, which day will the 17th be? (2)
f: The 15th is 14 days (two full weeks) after the 1st, so it is also a Friday. The 17th is two days later, a Sunday.
r: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.

q: Change the narration (direct speech) of: He bade farewell to his friends.
o: He said to his friends that good-bye.
He told his friends, "Farewell to you."
f: To bid farewell means to say good-bye, so in direct speech it becomes: He said to his friends, "Good-bye."
r: Similar idioms: bade welcome becomes said, "Welcome", and wished becomes said, "Good luck."

q: What is the full form of PIA?
f: PIA stands for Pakistan International Airlines, the national flag carrier of Pakistan.
r: PIA began as Orient Airways in 1946 and took its present name in 1955.

q: In which city were the Olympic Games named Tokyo 2020 held?
f: The 2020 Summer Olympics were awarded to Tokyo, Japan. Because of COVID-19 they were postponed and held in Tokyo from July to August 2021.
r: Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics.

q: How many doors (gates) does the Holy Kaaba have? (2)
f: The Kaaba has a single door, on its north-east wall, about two metres above ground level.
r: The door is made of gold-plated material and is opened only on special occasions.

q: Who served as both Governor General and Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor General from 1948 to 1951 and then Prime Minister from 1951 to 1953.
r: He became Governor General after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.

q: Who is the President of Germany? (2)
f: Frank-Walter Steinmeier has been the Federal President of Germany since March 2017 and was re-elected in 2022. His second term ends in March 2027.
r: The President is the head of state, while the Chancellor (currently Friedrich Merz) is the head of government.

q: In which Ghazwa was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) wounded?
f: In the Battle of Uhad (3 AH) the Prophet (PBUH) was wounded in the face and his blessed tooth was broken.
r: The Muslim archers left their post on the hill during Uhad, which let the Quraish attack from behind.

q: What is jute commonly known as?
f: Jute is called the golden fibre because of its shiny golden-brown colour and its high value as a cash crop.
r: Bangladesh and India are the largest producers of jute.

q: Who was the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb, so her father Wahb bin Abd Manaf was his maternal grandfather.
r: Wahb belonged to the Banu Zuhra clan of Quraish.

q: The sign greater than or equal to is used in which type of mathematical statement? (2)
f: The sign for greater than or equal to compares two quantities without saying that they are exactly equal, so it forms an inequality.
r: The sign for less than or equal to is also used in inequalities.

q: Sindhi belongs to which language family?
f: Sindhi is an Indo-Aryan language that developed from Sanskrit and Prakrit.
r: Sindhi is the official language of Sindh province and is written in a Perso-Arabic script.

q: What is the first group of the periodic table called? (5)
f: Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium, which are called alkali metals.
r: Hydrogen sits at the top of Group 1 but is not an alkali metal.

q: Choose the correct word: They ___ seeds in flowers.
f: The subject They is plural, so the simple present plural verb grow is needed.
r: The verb grows is used with singular subjects such as he, she or it.

q: The old fort of Gwadar/Chabahar region lies on the coast of the Gulf of which?
f: Gwadar and Chabahar lie on the coast near the Gulf of Oman, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
r: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.

q: Which hadith is called Muttafaq Alaih?
o: A hadith narrated by both Imam Bukhari and Imam Muslim
A hadith narrated by only one companion
A hadith narrated by Imam Tirmidhi
f: Muttafaq Alaih (agreed upon) is a hadith recorded in both Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.
r: Such hadith are considered to be of the highest authenticity.

q: Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil War of 1999? (16)
f: Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery in Kargil.
r: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed also received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.

q: What is the straight line that divides a circle into two equal halves called?
f: A chord passing through the centre of a circle is the diameter and it cuts the circle into two equal semicircles.
r: The diameter equals twice the radius.

q: Who is the author of the novel The Pursuit of Happiness (2001)?
f: The novel The Pursuit of Happiness was written by the author Douglas Kennedy.
r: Do not confuse it with The Conquest of Happiness by Bertrand Russell.

q: What is the HCF of 12 and 16?
f: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3 and 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. The common factors are 2 x 2, so the HCF is 4.
r: The LCM of 12 and 16 is 48.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Labour Organization (ILO) located?
f: The ILO, a specialised agency of the United Nations, has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: The ILO was founded in 1919 and became a UN agency in 1946.

q: Where is the headquarters of the African Union located? (8)
f: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
r: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.

q: According to the Quran, who will be in the lowest depths of the Fire? (4)
f: Surah An-Nisa says the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire.
r: Hypocrites outwardly claimed faith while hiding disbelief.

q: With the help of which country did Pakistan carry out the Saindak project? (8)
f: The Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan was developed with Chinese help by the Metallurgical Corporation of China.
r: Saindak is in Chagai district, Balochistan.

q: Which is the highest mountain range in the world? (6)
f: The Himalayas contain Mount Everest and most of the world's highest peaks.
r: The Andes are the longest continental mountain range.

q: On which hills is the city of Islamabad situated? (7)
f: Islamabad lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills, part of the Himalayan foothills.
r: Faisal Mosque is at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old? (2)
f: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10 she will be 20.
r: The age difference between two people stays the same over time.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old is his sister?
f: 3 x 5 = 15 years.
r: She is 10 years older than Ali.

q: On which date of Rabi ul Awwal is the birthday of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) commonly observed?
f: Most Sunni Muslims observe the birth of the Prophet (PBUH) on 12 Rabi ul Awwal.
r: Shia scholars commonly observe it on 17 Rabi ul Awwal.

q: Fill in the blank: The children ___ the honey on bread. (2)
f: The plural subject children takes the plural verb eat.
r: Children is an irregular plural.

q: Choose the correct word: Nadia's father ___ honey.
f: Father is singular and the sentence is active present, so the verb is buys.
r: A singular third person subject takes a verb ending in s in the simple present.

q: Boy is to girl as horse is to what?
f: A girl is the female of a boy; the female of a horse is a mare.
r: A young horse is a foal.

q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour at a constant speed. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: 90 km takes 60 minutes, so 1 km takes 60 divided by 90 = 2/3 minute, which is 40 seconds.
r: Speed 90 km per hour equals 1.5 km per minute.

q: Infections in the human body are caused by which of the following? (9)
o: Germs (pathogens such as bacteria and viruses)
f: Infections occur when disease-causing germs such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites enter the body and multiply.
r: Antigens are substances that trigger the immune system, while antibodies are made to fight them.

q: What was the old name of Hyderabad (Sindh)? (3)
f: Hyderabad in Sindh was built on the site of the old fort town called Neerunkot (Nerunkot), which was ruled by the Kalhora dynasty later.
r: Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhora founded the modern city of Hyderabad in 1768.

q: If the eccentricity e of a conic is greater than 1, the conic is a: (2)
f: A conic has e = 0 for a circle, e less than 1 for an ellipse, e = 1 for a parabola and e greater than 1 for a hyperbola.
r: A circle is the special case of an ellipse with zero eccentricity.

q: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is known for his confrontation with which tyrant ruler?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) challenged the idol worship and the claim of divinity of King Namrood, who had him thrown into a fire that Allah made cool.
r: Pharaoh was the opponent of Hazrat Musa (AS).

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) to Hazrat Yaqub (AS)? (2)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was father of Ishaq (AS), who was the father of Yaqub (AS), so Ibrahim was the grandfather of Yaqub.
r: Yaqub (AS) is also called Israel and his twelve sons were the tribes of Bani Israel.

q: About what percentage of the world's ice is found in Antarctica?
f: Antarctica holds about 90 percent of all the ice on Earth, and about 70 percent of the world's fresh water.
r: Greenland holds most of the remaining ice.

q: What is the first source of Islamic law (Shariah)?
f: The Quran is the primary source of Islamic law, followed by the Sunnah (Hadith), Ijma (consensus) and Qiyas (analogy).
r: Ijtehad is the effort of scholars to derive rulings from these sources.

q: What are the real part and the imaginary part of the complex number -3 + 4i?
f: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. Here a = -3 and b = 4.
r: i is defined by i squared = -1.

q: What is the imaginary part of the complex number 7 - 2i?
f: Write 7 - 2i as 7 + (-2)i. The imaginary part is the coefficient of i, which is -2.
r: The conjugate of 7 - 2i is 7 + 2i.

q: For which sport is Imam-ul-Haq famous?
f: Imam-ul-Haq is a left-handed Pakistani cricketer who plays as an opening batsman for the national team.
r: He is the nephew of former Pakistan captain Inzamam-ul-Haq.

q: In which year was the International Monetary Fund (IMF) established? (2)
f: The IMF was formally established in December 1945 after the Bretton Woods conference of July 1944, and began operations in 1947.
r: Some sources say 1944 because the agreement was drawn up at Bretton Woods that year.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)? (81)
f: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington DC, United States, close to the World Bank.
r: The UN headquarters is in New York and the WTO is in Geneva.

q: When was the third martial law imposed in Pakistan? (34)
f: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977 by removing the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
r: The earlier martial laws were in 1958 (Ayub Khan) and 1969 (Yahya Khan); General Musharraf took power in 1999 without declaring martial law.

q: What was the Kargil incident? (2)
o: A 1999 conflict between Pakistan and India in the Kargil sector of Kashmir
The 1965 war in the Rann of Kutch
f: In 1999 fighting took place in the Kargil district of Kashmir after infiltration across the Line of Control, ending in July 1999.
r: The Kargil conflict took place during the premiership of Nawaz Sharif.

q: In a village the population was 16000 in the year 2000. If the population becomes 5 times every year, what was the population in 1998?
f: Each year the population is multiplied by 5. So 1999 was 16000 / 5 = 3200, and 1998 was 3200 / 5 = 640.
r: Going back in time means dividing by the growth factor.

q: On what date did India get independence? (5)
f: India became independent from British rule on 15 August 1947, one day after Pakistan.
r: India celebrates Republic Day on 26 January because its constitution came into force in 1950.

q: In which years did Israel and Singapore get independence respectively? (2)
f: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, and Singapore became independent from Malaysia on 9 August 1965.
r: Singapore first got self-government in 1959.

q: Which law was adopted as the interim constitution of Pakistan after independence in 1947?
f: Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935, with amendments, as its interim constitution until the 1956 constitution came into force.
r: The Objectives Resolution was passed in March 1949.

q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle? (2)
f: In Euclidean geometry the three interior angles of any triangle always add up to 180 degrees.
r: The interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees.

q: What is the integral of sin x with respect to x?
f: The derivative of cos x is -sin x, so the derivative of -cos x is sin x. Hence the integral of sin x is -cos x + C.
r: The integral of cos x is sin x + C.

q: What is the integral of tan x with respect to x? (3)
f: Write tan x as sin x over cos x and put u = cos x; the integral becomes -ln |cos x| + C, which equals ln |sec x| + C.
r: The derivative of tan x is sec squared x.

q: What is the antonym of interim? (2)
f: Interim means temporary, so its opposite is permanent.
r: Provisional and temporary are synonyms of interim.

q: How far does Pakistan's territorial sea extend from its baseline?
f: Pakistan's Territorial Waters and Maritime Zones Act of 1976 fixed the territorial sea at 12 nautical miles, in line with international law.
r: Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 200 nautical miles.
