q: On which date in 1933 was the name Pakistan first put forward by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in the pamphlet Now or Never? (22)
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali issued the pamphlet Now or Never on 28 January 1933 and proposed the name Pakistan in it.
r: The Lahore Resolution came later, on 23 March 1940.

q: Which of the following is the multiplicative inverse form of the 2 by 2 matrix with entries a, b in the first row and c, d in the second row?
o: Matrix with d, -b in the first row and -c, a in the second row, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with a, c and b, d, multiplied by 1/(ad - bc)
Matrix with d, b and c, a, multiplied by (ad - bc)
f: For a 2 by 2 matrix, swap a and d, change the signs of b and c, and divide by the determinant ad - bc.
r: The inverse exists only when the determinant is not zero.

q: The inverse of a square matrix exists only if what condition holds?
f: The inverse equals the adjoint divided by the determinant, so the determinant must not be zero; such a matrix is called non-singular.
r: A matrix with zero determinant is called singular.

q: What is the additive inverse of the ordered pair (-a, -b)? (7)
f: The additive inverse is the pair that gives (0, 0) when added. (-a, -b) + (a, b) = (0, 0), so the answer is (a, b).
r: The additive identity of ordered pairs is (0, 0).

q: What is the capital of Iran? (7)
f: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.
r: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan.

q: Which type of number is 9/2? (10)
f: 9/2 is a ratio of two integers, so it is rational, and every rational number is also a real number.
r: As a decimal, 9/2 equals 4.5, which terminates.

q: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is known by which title? (5)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice, in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim's (AS) dream.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah.

q: Which battle was fought by the Muslims after the Battle of Badr, as the second major battle of Islam?
f: Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Battle of Uhud followed in Shawwal 3 AH.
r: Uhud is a mountain near Madinah.

q: Which is the 7th month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar?
f: The months are Muharram, Safar, Rabi-ul-Awwal, Rabi-ul-Sani, Jamadi-ul-Awwal, Jamadi-ul-Sani, then Rajab as the seventh.
r: Rajab is one of the four sacred months, and Shab-e-Meraj is observed in it.

q: What is the capital of Israel as declared by Israel? (2)
f: Israel declares Jerusalem as its capital, although most countries keep their embassies in Tel Aviv and the status of Jerusalem is disputed.
r: Pakistan does not recognise Israel.

q: If the National Assembly and the Senate disagree on a bill, who resolves the issue under the Constitution of Pakistan? (3)
o: A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament
f: Under Article 70 of the 1973 Constitution, a disputed bill is put before a joint sitting of both Houses and is passed by a majority of the total members present and voting.
r: The joint sitting is summoned by the President.

q: What is the capital of Italy? (4)
f: Rome is the capital and largest city of Italy.
r: Vatican City, the smallest country in the world, lies inside Rome.

q: Who is the President of Italy? (2)
f: Sergio Mattarella has been President of Italy since 2015 and was re-elected for a second term in 2022.
r: Giorgia Meloni is the Prime Minister of Italy, not the President.

q: Where is Jannat-ul-Mualla (Jannatul Mula), the famous graveyard?
f: Jannat-ul-Mualla is the historic cemetery of Makkah, where Hazrat Khadijah (RA) is buried.
r: The famous graveyard of Madina is Jannat-ul-Baqi.

q: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a famous book of what?
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of hadith compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
r: It is counted among the Sihah Sittah, the six authentic books of hadith.

q: Which of the following is a member of SAARC?
f: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member, while Iran, Japan and China are only observers.
r: The other members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

q: Banu Quraizah, a tribe of Madina, belonged to which religion? (3)
f: Banu Quraizah was a Jewish tribe of Madina.
r: They broke their pact during the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab).

q: Fill in the blank: ____ MA degree is requisite to get a job. (4)
f: MA is pronounced em-ay, which begins with a vowel sound, so the article an is used.
r: The article depends on the sound, not the spelling, as in an hour and a university.

q: Which defence organization did Pakistan join in 1954?
f: Pakistan joined the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) in September 1954.
r: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact, later CENTO, in 1955.

q: According to hadith, about which act will a person be questioned first on the Day of Judgment in matters of worship?
f: The Prophet (SAW) said the first deed for which a servant will be called to account is his prayer (Salah).
r: Among matters between people, the first judgment will be about bloodshed.

q: In which Hijri year was Abu Jahl killed? (2)
f: Abu Jahl was killed in the Battle of Badr, which took place in Ramadan 2 AH.
r: He was killed by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.

q: Kabul is the capital of which country? (2)
f: Kabul is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan.
r: Kabul lies on the Kabul River and is close to the Khyber Pass route to Pakistan.

q: On which river is the city of Kabul located? (8)
f: The city of Kabul stands on the banks of the Kabul River.
r: The Kabul River flows into Pakistan and joins the Indus near Attock.

q: Kaghan Valley is located in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (3)
f: Kaghan Valley lies in the Mansehra district of Hazara in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: Babusar Pass at the head of the valley connects it to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: Hilal-e-Kashmir, the highest military gallantry award of Azad Kashmir, was awarded to whom?
f: Naik Saif Ali Janjua received it after dying in the 1947-48 war in Kashmir, and he is its only recipient.
r: It was declared equal to the Nishan-e-Haider in 1995.

q: Which of these countries is not a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
f: Turkmenistan has never joined the SCO, while Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, China and Pakistan are members.
r: Pakistan and India became full SCO members in 2017.

q: Between the Muslims and whom was the Ghazwa Khandaq (Battle of the Trench) fought?
f: The Quraish of Makkah joined with other Arab tribes and Jewish tribes to attack Madinah in 5 AH.
r: The battle is also called Ghazwa Ahzab, meaning the battle of the confederates.

q: Against whom was the Khilafat Movement in India directed? (15)
f: The movement, led by Muslims of India, opposed British treatment of the Ottoman Caliph after World War I.
r: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.

q: What is the synonym of the word justify? (2)
f: To justify means to show something to be right or reasonable, and vindicate has a similar meaning.
r: Justification is the noun form of justify.

q: Who led the Khilafat Movement in India? (6)
f: The Khilafat Movement (1919 to 1924) was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and his brother Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
r: Mahatma Gandhi of the Indian National Congress also supported the Khilafat Movement.

q: What was the main theme of the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (SAW)? (2)
o: Human rights, equality and the abolition of all discrimination
f: In the Last Sermon the Prophet (SAW) declared that all humans are equal and that no Arab is superior to a non-Arab except by piety. He also stressed the sanctity of life, property and the rights of women.
r: It is regarded as one of the earliest charters of human rights.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver his first Friday sermon (khutba) after migrating to Madina?
o: Valley of Ranuna (Banu Salim bin Auf)
f: On the way to Madina the Prophet (SAW) led the first Jumuah prayer and delivered the first khutba in the valley of Ranuna, in the territory of Banu Salim bin Auf.
r: The first mosque built in Islam was the Quba mosque, where he stayed for some days before entering Madina.

q: Where was the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat-ul-Wida) delivered?
f: The Last Sermon was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah 10 AH during the Farewell Pilgrimage, at the plain of Arafat in the valley of Uranah.
r: The Prophet (SAW) passed away about three months after the Farewell Pilgrimage.

q: What type of fraction is 11/9? (2)
f: In 11/9 the numerator 11 is greater than the denominator 9, so it is an improper fraction. It equals 1 and 2/9 as a mixed number.
r: Every fraction of two integers, including 11/9, is also a rational number.

q: What was the old name of the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)? (3)
f: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was formerly called the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP). It was renamed through the 18th Amendment in 2010.
r: The province was given its present name in April 2010.

q: KRL (Khan Research Laboratories) is best known in Pakistan for work on which field?
o: Uranium enrichment and nuclear and missile technology
f: KRL at Kahuta developed uranium enrichment using centrifuges and also worked on missiles such as the Ghauri.
r: Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan is regarded as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme.

q: What is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range? (19)
f: Tirich Mir, in Chitral, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush at about 7708 metres.
r: K2 and Nanga Parbat belong to the Karakoram and Himalaya ranges respectively.

q: Which of the following is a land-locked country?
f: Nepal has no sea coast and is surrounded by India and China. The other three countries all have a coastline.
r: Afghanistan, Bhutan and Uzbekistan are other land-locked countries of Asia.

q: How many official languages does the United Nations (UNO) have? (2)
f: The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.
r: English and French are the two working languages of the UN Secretariat.

q: About how many languages are spoken in the world today?
f: Language surveys such as Ethnologue count roughly 7,100 living languages in the world.
r: The exact number changes slightly every year as languages are documented or die out.

q: Hazrat Ali (RA) is known by which of these titles? (3)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) is called Asadullah (Lion of Allah). Saifullah is Khalid bin Waleed, Siddiq is Abu Bakr and Farooq is Umar (RA).
r: He is also known as Haidar-e-Karrar and Abu Turab.

q: Which is the largest island in the world? (10)
f: Greenland covers about 2.16 million square kilometres, more than any other island. Australia is counted as a continent.
r: New Guinea is the second largest island.

q: What is the LCM of 12 and 24?
f: 24 is a multiple of 12 and of itself, and no smaller number is a multiple of 24. So LCM is 24.
r: If one number divides the other, the larger number is the LCM.

q: What is the LCM of 6 and 8? (5)
f: 6 = 2 x 3 and 8 = 2 x 2 x 2, so LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 24.
r: HCF of 6 and 8 is 2, and 24 x 2 = 48 = 6 x 8.

q: Which was the first short-range ballistic missile developed and tested by Pakistan? (2)
f: Hatf-I was Pakistan's first indigenous short-range ballistic missile, tested in 1989.
r: Ghauri and Shaheen are medium-range missiles and Babur is a cruise missile.

q: In which year was Instagram launched? (2)
f: Instagram was launched in October 2010 by Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger.
r: Facebook bought Instagram in 2012.

q: Which country launched the Tianhe core module of its space station into space?
f: China launched the Tianhe core module of the Tiangong space station in April 2021.
r: Tianhe means Heavenly Harmony.

q: Who led the enemy forces against the Muslims in the Battle of Yamama?
f: Musailima the Liar claimed to be a prophet and was defeated and killed at the Battle of Yamama in 632 CE under Khalid bin Waleed.
r: The battle took place in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: The maple leaf is shown on the flag of which country?
f: The red maple leaf in the centre of the white square is the national emblem of Canada.
r: The Canadian flag was adopted in 1965.

q: The Parliament of Pakistan is of which type? (5)
f: It has two houses: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).
r: Pakistan has a parliamentary form of government under the 1973 Constitution.

q: Which letter comes after H in the English alphabet?
f: The order is G, H, I, so I follows H.
r: The English alphabet has 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

q: Points that all lie on the same straight line are called what? (2)
f: Collinear points lie on one straight line.
r: Coplanar points lie in the same plane.

q: How many midpoints does a line segment have? (2)
f: A line segment has exactly one midpoint, the point equidistant from both ends.
r: A full line extends infinitely and has no midpoint.

q: The straight line given by the equation y = 6x passes through which point?
f: Putting x = 0 gives y = 6 times 0 = 0, so the line passes through (0, 0). Every line of the form y = mx passes through the origin.
r: In y = mx, the number m is the slope of the line, which is 6 here.

q: Is the expression 2x + 3x + 1 = 0 a linear equation?
o: No, because it has three terms
No, because it has two x terms
f: Adding the like terms gives 5x + 1 = 0. The highest power of x is 1, so it is a linear equation.
r: A linear equation in one variable has exactly one root.

q: What is the degree of a linear equation? (2)
f: In a linear equation the highest power of the variable is 1, so its degree is 1.
r: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is a straight line.

q: Which region of Pakistan is commonly called Little Tibet? (3)
f: Baltistan, with its capital Skardu, resembles Tibet in culture, language and landscape, so it is called Little Tibet.
r: Ladakh in India is also sometimes called Little Tibet.

q: Which is the longest river entirely in England?
f: The Thames, about 346 km long, is the longest river wholly in England.
r: The Severn is longer overall (354 km) but part of it flows through Wales.

q: Who was Lord Curzon at the time of the partition of Bengal in 1905? (22)
f: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy and Governor-General of India from 1899 to 1905 and he carried out the partition of Bengal in 1905.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Who designed the Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore?
f: The Minar-e-Pakistan was designed by the Russian-born architect Nasreddin Murat-Khan.
r: It was built in Iqbal Park, Lahore, where the Lahore Resolution was passed in 1940.

q: What is the main religion of Pakistan? (2)
f: About 96 percent of Pakistanis are Muslims, so Islam is the main religion and the state religion.
r: Article 2 of the Constitution declares Islam the state religion of Pakistan.

q: On which date is the Mairaj (Shab-e-Mairaj) commemorated? (2)
f: The night journey and ascension of the Prophet (PBUH) is observed on the night of 27 Rajab.
r: Shab-e-Barat is on 15 Shaban.

q: Which Sahabi is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran? (19)
f: Surah Al-Ahzab (verse 37) mentions Zaid bin Harithah (RA) by name.
r: The Quran mentions Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by name four times.

q: Which Air Force rank is equivalent to the Army rank of Major?
f: Squadron Leader equals Major in the Army and Lieutenant Commander in the Navy.
r: Wing Commander equals Lieutenant Colonel.

q: Who was the first woman promoted to the rank of Major General in the Pakistan Army?
f: Dr Shahida Malik, a medical doctor, became the first woman Major General in 2002.
r: Nigar Johar became the first woman Lieutenant General in 2020.

q: A tangent to a circle makes what angle with the radius drawn to the point of contact? (6)
f: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the angle is 90 degrees.
r: From an external point two tangents of equal length can be drawn to a circle.

q: On which river is Dushanbe, the capital of Tajikistan, located?
f: Dushanbe lies in the Gissar valley on the Varzob River, which is called Dushanbinka within the city.
r: Dushanbe is the capital of Tajikistan, not a European city.

q: In which mountain range is the Siachen Glacier located? (3)
f: The Siachen Glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram range in the disputed Kashmir region.
r: It is about 76 km long and is among the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

q: In a class of 24 people, 2/3 are male. How many females are there?
f: Males = 2/3 of 24 = 16. Females = 24 - 16 = 8.
r: Females here are 1/3 of the class.

q: In a class of 24 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of females?
f: Females are 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the class. 1/3 of 100 is 33.33%.
r: The percentage of females does not depend on the class size when the fraction is given.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Malta (2026)?
f: Robert Abela (Labour Party) has been Prime Minister since 2020 and was sworn in again in June 2026 after the general election.
r: Joseph Muscat was Prime Minister of Malta before Abela, from 2013 to 2020.

q: Who is the President of Malta (2026)?
f: Myriam Spiteri Debono has been President of Malta since April 2024.
r: Her predecessor George Vella served from 2019 to 2024.

q: Which is the famous man-made forest of Pakistan, located in Punjab?
f: Changa Manga near Lahore is one of the largest hand-planted forests, created in the 1860s by the British.
r: Changa Manga is in Kasur district, Punjab.

q: Which letter is the third from the end (last) in the word MANAGEMENT? (4)
f: The word ends with E, N, T. Counting from the end: T is 1st, N is 2nd, E is 3rd.
r: Counting from the end gives E while counting from the start gives N.

q: In which country is Manchar Lake located?
f: Manchar Lake is in Sindh province, Pakistan, west of the Indus river.
r: It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.

q: Manchar Lake in Sindh lies near which town?
f: Manchar Lake is located near Sehwan Sharif in the Dadu and Jamshoro area of Sindh.
r: Manchar Lake is Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.

q: Mangla Dam is located near which city?
f: Mangla Dam is built near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: Mangla Dam is the second largest dam of Pakistan.

q: Mangla Dam is built on which river? (9)
f: Mangla Dam stands on the river Jhelum.
r: Tarbela Dam, in contrast, is on the Indus.

q: How many kilometres long is a marathon race? (2)
f: The official marathon distance is 42.195 km, which equals 26 miles and 385 yards.
r: The marathon is named after the legendary run from Marathon to Athens.

q: What was the name of the father of Hazrat Maryam (AS)?
f: The Quran calls her 'Maryam daughter of Imran', and her father is named Imran.
r: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was her guardian, not her father.

q: Which is the highest individual ODI score by a Pakistani batsman?
f: Fakhar Zaman made 210 not out against Zimbabwe at Bulawayo in July 2018, beating Saeed Anwar's 194.
r: Saeed Anwar's 194 against India in 1997 had been the Pakistan record for 21 years.

q: Which word fills the blank: He teaches us English ___ mathematics.
f: Besides means in addition to, which suits the sentence. Beside means next to.
r: Besides is also used as an adverb meaning moreover.

q: Two matrices A and B are inverse of each other when:
f: Matrices A and B are inverses if their product in both orders equals the identity matrix I.
r: Only square matrices can have an inverse.

q: A matrix having the same number of rows and columns (m = n) is called: (3)
f: When the number of rows equals the number of columns, the matrix is a square matrix.
r: A matrix with one row only is called a row matrix.

q: What are the vertical lines of entries in a matrix called? (4)
f: Vertical lines of entries are columns, and horizontal lines are rows.
r: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns.

q: In which country was the phrase Black Lives Matter first used (as a hashtag in 2013)?
f: It began as the hashtag #BlackLivesMatter in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
r: The movement became global after the death of George Floyd in 2020.

q: What is the meaning of 'emancipation'? (11)
f: Emancipation means being set free from legal, social or political restrictions, such as slavery.
r: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863.

q: What is the meaning of the Arabic word 'Hikmah'? (10)
f: Hikmah means wisdom, sound judgement.
r: Al-Hakim, a name of Allah, comes from the same root.

q: What is the meaning of 'Sirat'? (6)
f: Sirat means a path or road, as in Sirat-al-Mustaqeem, the straight path.
r: Surah Al-Fatihah asks Allah to guide us to the straight path.

q: What is the meaning of 'subsequently'? (2)
f: Subsequently means at a later time, afterwards.
r: Its opposite is previously.

q: What is the meaning of 'amicability'?
f: Amicability means a friendly and peaceful attitude.
r: Its adjective is amicable.

q: What is the meaning of 'Ansari'? (2)
o: Helper (descendant of the Ansar of Madinah)
f: Ansar means helpers, the people of Madinah who helped the Muslim emigrants. Ansari relates to them.
r: The emigrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.

q: What is the meaning of 'antique'? (2)
f: An antique is an old object, usually valuable because of its age.
r: Antiques are generally at least 100 years old.

q: What is the meaning of 'cohesive'?
o: Sticking together as a united whole
f: Cohesive means holding together firmly and united.
r: The noun is cohesion.

q: What is the meaning of 'doubt'? (2)
f: Doubt means a feeling of uncertainty about something.
r: Its opposite is certainty or confidence.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'mitigate'? (5)
o: To make less severe or serious
f: To mitigate means to reduce the severity, seriousness or harm of something. For example, planting trees mitigates the effect of floods.
r: Mitigation is a common word in disaster management, as in flood mitigation.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'recalcitrant'?
f: A recalcitrant person obstinately refuses to obey rules or accept control. It is used for uncooperative people or animals.
r: Its synonyms include defiant, unruly and obstinate.

q: What is the meaning of the verb 'rob'?
o: To take property unlawfully, often by force
f: To rob means to steal from a person or place, usually using force or threat. A person who does this is called a robber.
r: Robbery differs from burglary because robbery involves force or threat against a person.

q: What is the meaning of the Urdu/Arabic word 'Seerat'? (7)
f: Seerat means a person's life, conduct and character, and is used mainly for the biography of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). It is also written as Seerah.
r: The earliest well-known Seerat of the Prophet (PBUH) was written by Ibn Ishaq and edited by Ibn Hisham.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Zamzam'? (17)
f: Zamzam is the name of the sacred well in Makkah, and the word is linked to plentiful, gushing water. The well sprang near the Kaaba for Hazrat Ismail (AS) and his mother Hazrat Hajra.
r: Pilgrims drink Zamzam water during Hajj and Umrah, and Sai is performed between Safa and Marwa near it.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Iltijaa'?
f: Iltijaa is an Urdu word of Arabic origin meaning a humble request, plea or entreaty. It is used for earnestly asking someone for help.
r: Related words are darkhwast, arzi and dua, all meaning a request or prayer.

q: What is the median of 2, 3, 5, 7?
f: There are 4 values, so the median is the mean of the two middle values 3 and 5. (3 + 5) / 2 = 4.
r: The mean of 2, 3, 5, 7 is 4.25, which differs from the median.

q: What is the median of 3, 4, 7, 8, 6?
f: Arrange in order: 3, 4, 6, 7, 8. There are 5 values, so the median is the 3rd value, which is 6.
r: The mean of these numbers is 5.6, not the median.

q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of SAARC? (8)
f: Pakistan was one of the seven founding members of SAARC at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985. It did not join later.
r: Afghanistan became the eighth member in April 2007.

q: How many member states does the United Nations have? (38)
f: The UN has 193 member states. South Sudan was the latest to join, in 2011.
r: The Holy See and Palestine are non-member observer states.

q: Which names of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) are mentioned in the Quran? (2)
f: The Quran directly uses the names Muhammad (four times) and Ahmad (once, in Surah As-Saff). Other titles like Taha and Yasin are separate.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) is also addressed in the Quran with titles such as Nabi and Rasool.

q: How many metres are there in 2 km? (15)
r: One kilometre is about 0.62 miles.

q: What is the midpoint of the points (4, 6) and (2, 6)?
r: Both points have the same y value, so the segment is horizontal.

q: What is the meaning of 'broke down' in the sentence: The car broke down one mile away from home?
f: To break down means a machine or vehicle stops working because of a fault. So the car stopped working one mile from home.
r: Break down can also mean to lose emotional control or to analyse something in parts.

q: Which country has the largest number of active military personnel in the world? (18)
f: China's People's Liberation Army has about two million active personnel, the most in the world. India and the United States follow.
r: Rankings change slowly, and India has the second-largest active force in most recent lists.

q: Which of the following is a military alliance?
f: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) is a collective defence military alliance founded in 1949. SAARC is regional cooperation, OPEC deals with oil and WTO with trade.
r: Its Article 5 says an attack on one member is an attack on all.

q: What is the minimum age to become President of Pakistan? (8)
f: Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution says the President must be a Muslim, qualified to be a National Assembly member and at least 45 years old.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue of Pakistan?
f: Muhammad Aurangzeb took charge as Finance Minister in March 2024 and presented the FY2026-27 budget. He is still in office in October 2026.
r: In 2022 the finance minister was Miftah Ismail, followed by Ishaq Dar.

q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. About how much distance does it cover in 1 minute? (2)
f: 1 hour is 60 minutes, so distance per minute is 20 divided by 60, which is 0.33 km. This is about 333 metres.
r: Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives km per minute.

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how many papers does he write in one minute? (8)
f: Rate is 5 papers divided by 5 minutes, which is 1 paper per minute.
r: Rate equals work divided by time.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, how much time will 1 man take to write 1 page?
f: 5 men write 5 pages in 1 minute, so each man writes 1 page in 1 minute. One man therefore needs 1 minute for 1 page.
r: If each worker works at the same rate, work per worker is total work divided by number of workers.

q: What was the real name of the Bengali freedom fighter Tito Mir?
f: Tito Mir's real name was Syed Mir Nisar Ali. He led a peasant uprising against landlords and the British in Bengal in 1831.
r: He built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia and died fighting in 1831.

q: If a helicopter needs 80 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km? (5)
f: Fuel per km is 80 divided by 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 400 km, 400 x 0.25 = 100 gallons.
r: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th be?
f: The 9th is 7 days after the 2nd. After a full week the day repeats, so it is Monday.
r: Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.

q: In which year did Lord Mountbatten arrive in India as the last Viceroy?
f: Lord Mountbatten arrived in India in March 1947 to oversee the transfer of power. He announced the Partition plan on 3 June 1947.
r: He later became the first Governor General of independent India.

q: A train moves at 120 km/h. What distance does it cover in 120 minutes?
f: 120 minutes is 2 hours. Distance = 120 x 2 = 240 km.
r: Convert minutes to hours by dividing by 60.

q: A train is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes? (3)
f: 10 minutes is 1/6 hour. Distance = 60 x 1/6 = 10 km.
r: At 60 km/h a train covers 1 km each minute.

q: In which year was Islamabad officially made the capital of Pakistan, replacing Rawalpindi as interim capital? (12)
f: Karachi was first capital, then Rawalpindi served as interim capital while Islamabad was built. Islamabad officially became the capital in 1967.
r: Sources differ on the exact year, since the decision was taken in 1959-60 and the shift happened in stages.

q: Who moved the Objective Resolution in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1949?
f: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objective Resolution, and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
r: It later became the preamble of the 1973 Constitution.

q: Which of the following is one of the Ashra Mubashra?
f: Hazrat Talha bin Ubaidullah (RA) is among the ten Companions given the glad tidings of Paradise. The others listed are not in the group.
r: The ten include Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah.

q: What is the relation between multiplication and division? (4)
f: Division undoes multiplication, so they are inverse operations. For example, 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 / 4 = 6.
r: Addition and subtraction are also inverse operations.

q: What is the title of Hazrat Musa (AS)? (3)
f: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah because Allah spoke to him directly.
r: Khalilullah is Ibrahim, Safiullah is Adam and Ruhullah is Isa.

q: Who was the mother of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (3)
f: The Holy Prophet's mother was Hazrat Amina bint Wahb. Halima Sadia was his wet nurse.
r: Hazrat Amina passed away when he was about 6 years old.

q: Which one is different from the following: actor, director, music, producer?
f: Actor, director and producer are all people who work on a film, while music is a thing, not a person.
r: Odd-one-out questions are solved by finding the item of a different category.

q: Who was the Habshi (Abyssinian) king Najashi, who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants?
f: Najashi was the title of the Abyssinian king, whose real name was Ashama bin Abjar.
r: When he died in 9 AH, the Prophet (SAW) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.

q: What is Namaz-e-Ishraq?
o: An optional prayer offered after sunrise
A prayer offered during an eclipse
f: Ishraq is an optional (nafl) prayer offered about 15 to 20 minutes after sunrise, after the Fajr prayer.
r: Namaz-e-Istisqa is the prayer for rain.

q: Where is the National Museum of Pakistan located? (17)
f: The National Museum of Pakistan is in Karachi, in the Burnes Garden area.
r: The Lahore Museum is a separate and older museum.

q: How many member countries does NATO have at present? (6)
f: NATO has 32 members, after Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.
r: NATO was founded in 1949 with 12 members.

q: Is sin x positive or negative in the first quadrant?
f: In the first quadrant the y-coordinate is positive and sin x equals y divided by r, so it is positive.
r: In the first quadrant all six trigonometric ratios are positive.

q: The line x = 3 is ______ to the X axis. (4)
f: The line x = 3 is a vertical line, and a vertical line meets the horizontal X axis at a right angle.
r: The line x = 3 is parallel to the Y axis.

q: Fill in the blank: Mrs. Rehan is not pleased ___ the new servant.
f: The adjective pleased is followed by the preposition with when it refers to a person. So the correct sentence is: not pleased with the new servant.
r: Other common adjective and preposition pairs are angry with, good at and afraid of.

q: What is a bill called after it has been passed by Parliament and approved by the President of Pakistan?
f: A bill passed by both houses and assented to by the President becomes an Act of Parliament, which is law. An ordinance is a temporary law issued by the President when Parliament is not in session.
r: Under Article 75 of the Constitution the President has ten days to assent to a bill or return it.

q: What comes next in the series: 3A, 5C, 7E, ? (3)
f: The numbers increase by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9) and the letters skip one letter each time (A, C, E, G). So the next term is 9G.
r: The letters A, C, E, G are the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the alphabet.

q: What comes next in the series: 3x+4, 4x+2, ?
f: The coefficient of x increases by 1 each time (3, 4, 5) and the constant decreases by 2 (4, 2, 0). So the next term is 5x+0 = 5x.
r: Such a pattern is two arithmetic progressions running together.

q: What comes next in the series: B2, C3, D4, E5, F?
f: Each letter moves one step forward and each number increases by 1. F pairs with 6, so the next term is F6.
r: B is the 2nd letter, C the 3rd, and so on, so each letter pairs with its own position number.

q: What comes next in the series: 3W, 6X, 9Z, ?
f: The numbers increase by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). The letters move forward by 1, then 2, then 3: W to X to Z to C (after Z the alphabet starts again). So the next term is 12C.
r: In such letter series, the alphabet is treated as a circle, so Z is followed by A.

q: Which number comes next: 1, 4, 9, 16, ? (2)
f: These are the squares 1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4. The next is 5x5 = 25.
r: The gaps between squares are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9.

q: Which number comes next: 155, 65, 165, 75, ?
f: The terms in odd positions go 155, 165 and the terms in even positions go 65, 75, each rising by 10. So the next term is 165 + 10 = 175.
r: This is an alternating series made of two separate series.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 6, 8, ?
f: Each number is 2 more than the one before it. So 8 + 2 = 10.
r: These are the first even natural numbers.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, 12, ? (5)
f: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 12 + 3 = 15.
r: This is the table of 3.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, ?
f: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 9 + 3 = 12.
r: This is the table of 3.

q: Which number comes next: 5, 10, 15, ?
f: Each number is 5 more than the one before. So 15 + 5 = 20.
r: This is the table of 5.

q: Which number comes next: 66, 63, 57, 45, 21, ? (2)
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12, 24, each double the last. The next difference is 48, so 21 - 48 = -27.
r: The same series appears as 66, 63, 57, 45, 21 where the next term after 45 is 21.

q: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar served as the Governor of which province of Pakistan? (8)
f: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement, was Governor of Punjab from 1949 to 1951.
r: Nishtar Medical University in Multan is named after him.

q: In which Hijri year was Zakat made obligatory? (8)
f: According to the commonly taught view, Zakat became obligatory in the second year of Hijri, around the time Ramadan fasting was ordained. Some scholars give slightly different years.
r: Sources differ a little on the exact year of Zakat.

q: School is a noun. Which pronoun can be used in its place? (5)
f: A school is a singular, non-living thing, so the pronoun it is used for it.
r: The plural pronoun for schools is they.

q: What is the word used in place of a noun called?
f: A pronoun is used in place of a noun to avoid repeating it, such as he, she, it and they.
r: Words like he, she and it are personal pronouns.

q: What is the total number of nuclear-armed countries in the world today?
f: Nine countries have nuclear weapons: the USA, Russia, the UK, France, China, India, Pakistan, Israel (undeclared) and North Korea.
r: Pakistan is the only Muslim country with nuclear weapons.

q: 13, 15, 17 and 19 are what type of numbers?
f: Each of these numbers leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
r: The only even prime number is 2.

q: If a set has two elements, how many elements are in its power set? (3)
f: The power set of a set with n elements has 2 to the power n elements. For n = 2 this is 4: the empty set, two single-element subsets, and the set itself.
r: A set with 3 elements has a power set of 8 elements.

q: Which languages were declared official languages of Pakistan by the 1962 constitution?
f: The 1962 constitution recognised Urdu and Bengali as the national languages of Pakistan.
r: The 1956 constitution had also named Urdu and Bengali as state languages.

q: Which is generally regarded as the oldest city of Pakistan according to Pakistani textbooks? (3)
f: Peshawar is commonly described as the oldest living city of Pakistan, inhabited for over 2,500 years.
r: Sources differ, as Multan is also claimed to be among the oldest cities in South Asia.

q: For whom are the Special Olympics held? (2)
f: The Special Olympics are sports competitions for people with intellectual disabilities.
r: The Paralympic Games are held for athletes with physical disabilities.

q: What is the capital of Oman? (3)
f: Muscat is the capital and largest city of Oman.
r: Oman is ruled by a Sultan and is located on the south-eastern coast of the Arabian Peninsula.

q: Change into passive voice: Open the door. (2)
f: An imperative sentence is changed into the passive using Let + object + be + past participle, giving Let the door be opened.
r: Imperative sentences express commands, requests or advice.

q: What does Allama Iqbal Open University mainly promote? (2)
f: Allama Iqbal Open University in Islamabad provides distance and open education to students who cannot attend regular institutions.
r: It was established in 1974 as the People's Open University and renamed in 1977.

q: Fill in the blank: She opened the door ____. (2)
f: A word describing how an action is done must be an adverb, so slowly is correct.
r: Most adverbs of manner are formed by adding ly to an adjective.

q: What is the opposite of contiguous?
f: Contiguous means sharing a border or touching, so its opposite is separated or detached.
r: Contiguous comes from the Latin contingere, meaning to touch.

q: What is 14 - 6 - 4?
r: Subtraction is carried out from left to right.

q: What is the order of a square matrix having n rows?
f: A square matrix has equal rows and columns, so its order is n x n.
r: A 3 x 3 matrix is a square matrix of order 3.

q: What are the coordinates of the origin on a Cartesian graph? (2)
f: The origin is the point where the x-axis and y-axis cross, so both its x and y values are zero.
r: The two axes divide the plane into four quadrants that meet at the origin.

q: Who built the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam? (5)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) laid the foundation of the Quba Mosque near Madinah on his Hijrah, and the Companions helped build it.
r: The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) refers to a mosque founded on piety from the first day, which scholars identify as Quba.

q: In which period was the first war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir fought? (3)
f: The first Indo-Pak war over Kashmir began in October 1947 after tribal and Pakistani forces entered the state and India sent troops. It ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire on 1 January 1949.
r: The ceasefire line later became the Line of Control after the Simla Agreement of 1972.

q: The Dawn newspaper is owned by which family-run group? (2)
f: Dawn is published by Dawn Media Group, which is controlled by the Haroon family (with the Saigol family). The Haroon family bought majority shares in 1946.
r: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi in 1941.

q: What was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931? (2)
o: An agreement that ended the Civil Disobedience Movement and let Gandhi attend the Second Round Table Conference
A pact between Congress and the Muslim League
f: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy Lord Irwin. Congress suspended civil disobedience and the government released political prisoners.
r: Gandhi then attended the Second Round Table Conference in London in 1931.

q: Which area of Pakistan is called the Switzerland of Pakistan?
f: Swat valley is known as the Switzerland of Pakistan for its mountains, rivers and green scenery.
r: Faisalabad, by contrast, is known as the Manchester of Pakistan.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, which institution is supreme?
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Parliament is the supreme law-making body and the Prime Minister heads the government.
r: In practice the Constitution itself is supreme, and Parliament must act within it.

q: What is the parliament of Israel called?
f: The Israeli parliament is called the Knesset and it has 120 members.
r: The Knesset sits in Jerusalem.

q: On what date was the Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament?
f: The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and created the two dominions of Pakistan and India.
r: The 3 June 1947 plan was announced by Lord Mountbatten before the Act.

q: What is the Kunyat (kuniyyat) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (2)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was called Abu al-Qasim after his eldest son Qasim.
r: Abu Turab was the kunyat of Hazrat Ali (RA), and Abu Hafs of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: What is the perimeter of a circle called? (6)
f: The distance around a circle is called its circumference, equal to 2 x pi x radius.
r: The diameter is twice the radius.

q: What is the period of the function sin x?
f: The sine function repeats its values after every 2 pi radians (360 degrees), so sin(x + 2 pi) = sin x.
r: The period of tan x is pi.

q: Aleem Dar is a famous personality in which field? (2)
f: Aleem Dar is a Pakistani international cricket umpire, who won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times.
r: He officiated in more than 130 Test matches.

q: If 5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days, how many papers will 1 person write in 5 days?
f: Each person writes 1 paper in 5 days (5 persons write 5 papers in 5 days). So 1 person writes 1 paper in 5 days.
r: In 25 days, 1 person would write 5 papers.

q: Which pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan? (22)
f: The Khyber Pass, with the Torkham crossing, connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.
r: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Afghanistan and the Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan with China.

q: Which pillar of Islam is related to the event of Meraj?
f: Five daily prayers were made obligatory during the Meraj (Night Journey).
r: Originally 50 prayers were prescribed and were reduced to five.

q: Badr, where the first major battle of Islam was fought, is the name of what? (9)
o: A plain with wells near Madinah
f: Badr is a plain valley with wells about 150 km from Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
r: Mount Uhud, in contrast, is a mountain near Madinah.

q: Which is the brightest planet in the sky? (2)
f: Venus is the brightest planet as seen from Earth because it is close and its thick clouds reflect much sunlight.
r: It is often called the morning or evening star.

q: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a famous player of which game? (6)
f: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a former Pakistan cricket captain and batter.
r: He was a member of the 1992 World Cup winning Pakistan team.

q: What is the land of the pure people (Sarzamin-e-Pak) a name for? (2)
f: The name Pakistan means land of the pure, from Urdu pak (pure) and stan (land).
r: The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

q: Khushal Khan Khattak is a famous poet of which language? (2)
f: Khushal Khan Khattak (1613-1689) was a warrior-poet who wrote in Pashto.
r: He is regarded as the national poet of the Pashtuns.

q: Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar is regarded as the first major poet of which language? (21)
f: Baba Farid (1173-1266) of Pakpattan is considered the first major poet of the Punjabi language.
r: Some of his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: Which of the following points lies on the line y = 6x?
f: For (2, 12): 6 times 2 = 12, so it satisfies y = 6x. The others do not.
r: The line y = 6x has slope 6 and passes through the origin.

q: What is the population of Punjab province according to the 2023 census?
f: The 2023 census counted about 127.7 million people in Punjab, the most populous province.
r: Punjab holds roughly half of Pakistan's population.

q: Which of the following is a major port of Sri Lanka?
f: Colombo is the largest and busiest port of Sri Lanka.
r: Hambantota is another important port of Sri Lanka.

q: When did Pakistan issue its first postage stamps? (11)
f: Pakistan's first set of postage stamps was issued on 9 July 1948.
r: Before that, British Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

q: What is the value of x to the power 0 (for x not equal to 0)? (2)
f: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1, because x to the power n divided by x to the power n equals x to the power 0, which equals 1.
r: The expression 0 to the power 0 is treated as undefined or indeterminate in many contexts.

q: Which countries hold veto power in the UN Security Council? (14)
f: The five permanent members of the Security Council (P5) have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
r: A single veto from any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.

q: Which regional organization was the predecessor of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO)? (3)
f: RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was revived and expanded as ECO in 1985.
r: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of both RCD and ECO.

q: How many compiled copies of the Quran were prepared in the time of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (4)
f: Under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the Quran was collected into one single compiled copy, kept with him and then with Hazrat Umar and Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
r: Copies were multiplied and sent to different regions later, during the time of Hazrat Uthman (RA).

q: Which is the present constitution of Pakistan? (22)
f: Pakistan is currently governed by the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973.
r: It has been amended many times, including the 18th Amendment in 2010.

q: If the price of 3 eggs is 4 rupees, what is the price of 18 eggs?
f: 18 eggs is 6 times 3 eggs, so the price is 6 times 4 = 24 rupees.
r: This is a direct proportion problem solved by the unitary method.

q: Which country produces the most olives in the world? (2)
f: Spain is the largest producer of olives and olive oil, mainly from the region of Andalusia.
r: Spain produces roughly half of the world's olive oil in a good year.

q: What is the value of i x i, where i is the imaginary unit? (6)
f: The imaginary unit is defined by i squared equals -1, so i x i = -1.
r: Higher powers repeat in a cycle: i cubed is -i and i to the fourth power is 1.

q: What is the antonym of the word prohibit?
f: To prohibit means to forbid something, so its opposite is to permit or allow it.
r: Prohibit comes from the Latin prohibere, meaning to hold back.

q: Which word is a synonym of prohibit?
f: Prohibit means to officially stop something from being done, which is the same as forbid.
r: Ban and bar are other synonyms of prohibit.

q: Kharan is a district of which province of Pakistan? (3)
f: Kharan is a district and town in the west of Balochistan province.
r: The Kharan Desert, where Pakistan tested nuclear devices in 1998 near Chagai, lies in this region of Balochistan.

q: How many seats does the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Provincial Assembly have? (2)
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP in 2018, the assembly grew from 124 to 145 seats (115 general, 26 women, 4 non-Muslim).
r: Before the merger the assembly had 124 seats.

q: Which word is a synonym of provoke? (7)
f: To provoke means to stir up a strong reaction, which is the same as to incite.
r: Instigate and arouse are other synonyms of provoke.

q: What was the age of Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan at the time of Pakistan's first nuclear tests in May 1998?
f: Born on 1 April 1936, he was 62 years old on 28 May 1998.
r: The tests were carried out at Chagai in Balochistan.

q: From whom did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh? (72)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Hindu ruler of Sindh, in 711-712 AD.
r: Raja Dahir was defeated near Raor.

q: Where is Qila Derawar located?
f: Derawar Fort is a large fort in the Cholistan Desert near Ahmedpur East in Bahawalpur district, Punjab.
r: The fort was built by Rajput Bhatti rulers and is now on Pakistan's tentative UNESCO list.

q: Where was Masjid Quba, the first mosque in Islam, built?
f: Masjid Quba was built in the village of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) laid its foundation when he arrived there during the Hijrat.
r: Masjid Quba is regarded as the first mosque built in Islam.

q: The Khojak Pass connects Quetta with which Afghan city? (2)
f: The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies on the route from Quetta to Chaman and on to Kandahar in Afghanistan. The Khojak Tunnel runs beneath it.
r: The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi and the plains of Sindh and Punjab.

q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah socially and economically boycott the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Banu Hashim?
f: The Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib for about three years, and the family stayed in Shib Abi Talib. The boycott ended in the tenth year of prophethood.
r: Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadija (RA) both died soon after the boycott ended.

q: Who is said to have been the first to memorise the whole Quran (hifz)?
f: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it as it came and recited it to Hazrat Jibril (AS). He is therefore regarded as the first hafiz.
r: Among the companions, sources name several early huffaz, so this answer refers to the first hafiz overall.

q: What is a circle with zero radius called?
f: If the radius is zero, all points of the circle coincide with the centre, so it is a single point called a point circle.
r: A circle with radius 1 is called a unit circle.

q: If my age is 10 years and my brother's age is 2 times my age, what will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years? (2)
f: My brother is 2 x 10 = 20 years old now. After 10 years I will be 20 and he will be 30, so the ratio is 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.
r: The ratio of ages moves closer to 1 : 1 as both people grow older.

q: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was an organisation of which three countries? (4)
f: RCD was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic, technical and cultural cooperation.
r: RCD was later renamed ECO, which expanded in 1992 to include Central Asian states and Afghanistan.

q: Change into active voice: The book is being read by her.
f: The passive form is being read becomes the active is reading, and the agent her becomes the subject she. The tense stays present continuous.
r: In active voice the doer of the action is the subject of the sentence.

q: Change into passive voice: We are reading a book. (2)
o: A book was being read by us.
A book is read by us.
A book is being read by us.
A book has been read by us.
f: Present continuous passive uses is or are being plus the past participle. The object a book becomes the subject and we becomes by us.
r: Passive voice puts the focus on the action or receiver rather than the doer.

q: What is the value of the real number -(4! + 6)?
r: The factorial of 5 is 120.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 7 - 2i? (3)
f: In a + bi form with a = 7 and b = -2, the real part is 7.
r: Real numbers are complex numbers whose imaginary part is zero.

q: Rearrange the letters E T W A R to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
f: The letters form the word WATER. Its letters are W, A, T, E, R so the second last letter is E.
r: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen, and its formula is H2O.

q: How many Pakistani Nobel Prize winners have won in the field of physics?
f: Only Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1979 for the electroweak theory. Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.
r: Abdus Salam shared the 1979 physics prize with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg.

q: Which of the following is one of the eight categories of zakat recipients (masarif) mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah?
f: Surah At-Tawbah (verse 60) lists the fakir, miskin, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, fi sabilillah and travellers. Debtors (Al-Gharimin) are one of them.
r: Zakat cannot be given to the Prophet's family (Bani Hashim) according to the majority view.

q: What is dead reckoning in navigation?
o: Sailing only at night using the stars
Estimating current position from a known starting point, speed, time and direction
Measuring the depth of the sea
f: Dead reckoning calculates the present position by using a previously known position and adding the distance travelled on a known course. It does not need external signals.
r: Before GPS, ships and aircraft relied heavily on dead reckoning.

q: In which year did China recognize Pakistan?
f: The People's Republic of China was proclaimed in 1949 and Pakistan recognized it in 1950, among the first countries to do so. Diplomatic relations began on 21 May 1951.
r: Pakistan was among the first Muslim countries to recognize the People's Republic of China.

q: Where is the Red Sea located? (4)
f: The Red Sea lies between northeast Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). It connects to the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal.
r: The Red Sea joins the Indian Ocean through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (7)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was a cousin. He married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

q: What is the antonym of reluctant?
f: Reluctant means unwilling, so its opposite is willing or eager. The other options are synonyms.
r: Eager and keen are also antonyms of reluctant.

q: For how many days did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) stay in the Cave of Thawr (Ghar-e-Saur) during the Hijrat?
f: During the migration to Madinah the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) hid in the Cave of Thawr for three days. They then continued to Madinah.
r: The cave is near Makkah, south of the city.

q: According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be a member of the National Assembly?
f: The 1962 Constitution required a member of the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old.
r: Sources differ slightly on some qualification details; the minimum age of the President under the 1962 Constitution is commonly given as 35 years.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age required to be elected President of Pakistan? (2)
f: Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution requires the President to be a Muslim, qualified to be a member of the National Assembly, and not less than 45 years old.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies for a five-year term.

q: How many seats were reserved for women in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution provided a National Assembly of 300 general seats plus 10 seats reserved for women for ten years.
r: Under the 1973 Constitution today, 60 National Assembly seats are reserved for women.

q: How many seats are reserved for women in the Punjab Assembly? (3)
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general seats, 66 seats for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
r: Punjab has the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.

q: At which place in Lahore was the Lahore Resolution presented in 1940?
f: The session of the All India Muslim League was held at Minto Park, now Iqbal Park, where Minar-e-Pakistan stands.
r: Minar-e-Pakistan was built to commemorate the resolution.

q: Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming? (12)
f: Carbon dioxide, released by burning fossil fuels, traps heat in the atmosphere as a greenhouse gas.
r: Methane is another important greenhouse gas.

q: What is the meaning of retaliation? (3)
f: Retaliation means paying back an injury or wrong with a similar action, that is, revenge.
r: Its verb form is retaliate.

q: What is the antonym of retaliation?
f: Retaliation means revenge, so its opposite is forgiveness or pardon.
r: Revenge, vengeance and reprisal are synonyms of retaliation.

q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are written in reverse order, which is the last letter?
f: BEAUTY reversed is YTUAEB, so the last letter is B.
r: The first letter of the reversed word is Y.

q: According to the Hadith Qudsi on fasting, who will Himself give the reward of fasting? (2)
f: In the Hadith Qudsi Allah says: Fasting is for Me and I shall reward it Myself.
r: Fasting is the third pillar of Islam in some counts and the fourth in the commonly taught Pakistani order.

q: In which direction does the sun rise?
f: The Earth rotates from west to east, so the sun appears to rise in the east.
r: The sun sets in the west.

q: Who has scored the most runs in Test cricket? (25)
f: Sachin Tendulkar of India scored 15,921 runs in 200 Tests, and no one has passed this total as of October 2026.
r: Joe Root of England is second, having passed 14,000 Test runs in 2026.

q: What is the capital of Russia? (25)
f: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.
r: Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire until 1918.

q: Saleem is 3 years old and his sister is three times as old as him. How old will his sister be when Saleem is 12?
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now, so she is 6 years older than Saleem. When he is 12, she will be 12 + 6 = 18.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: What is the synonym of foe?
f: Foe means an enemy or opponent.
r: The antonym of foe is friend or ally.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old? (2)
f: When Ali is 3, Sara is 3 x 3 = 9, so Sara is 6 years older than Ali. The age gap stays the same, so when Ali is 8, Sara is 8 + 6 = 14.
r: The difference between two people's ages never changes with time.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 15 years old? (2)
f: When Ali is 3, Sara is 9, so she is 6 years older. When Ali is 15, Sara is 15 + 6 = 21.
r: The age gap of 6 years stays fixed for life.

q: How many seats does the Provincial Assembly of Sindh have in total?
f: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats: 130 general seats, 29 reserved for women and 9 reserved for non-Muslims.
r: The Punjab Assembly is the largest provincial assembly with 371 seats.

q: How many general seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have in the National Assembly of Pakistan after the 2023 delimitation?
f: After the merger of FATA and the 2023 delimitation, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has 45 general seats in the National Assembly.
r: Before the merger of FATA the province had 35 general seats, while Punjab now has 141 general seats.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word selfless?
f: Selfless means putting others before oneself, so its opposite is selfish, meaning concerned only with oneself.
r: Unselfish and altruistic are synonyms of selfless.

q: Under which Act was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936? (2)
f: The Government of India Act 1935 created Sindh as a separate province, which came into effect on 1 April 1936.
r: The demand for separating Sindh from Bombay was part of the Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929.

q: How many vowels are there in this sequence: A Q W S T R H J C B D Y K L O?
f: The only vowels in the sequence are A and O, so the count is 2. Y is treated as a consonant here.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are there in the sequence: a d i u l k m e?
f: The vowels in the sequence are a, i, u and e, which makes 4.
r: The English alphabet has five vowels and twenty-one consonants.

q: Complete the series: 1z, 2y, 3x, ?
f: The numbers go up by 1 each time and the letters go backwards through the alphabet (z, y, x, w). So the next term is 4w.
r: Z is the 26th letter and W is the 23rd letter of the alphabet.

q: Complete the series: a, c, f, ? (4)
f: The gaps increase by 1: a to c is +2, c to f is +3, so the next is +4. F is the 6th letter and 6 + 4 = 10, which is j.
r: J is the 10th letter of the English alphabet.

q: What is the next term in the series: A1, C3, D4, G7, ?
f: The number is the position of the letter in the alphabet, and the numbers 1, 3, 4, 7 each equal the sum of the two before (3 + 4 = 7). The next number is 4 + 7 = 11, which is K.
r: The numbers 1, 3, 4, 7, 11 are known as the Lucas numbers.

q: Fill in the blank: ____ sun sets in the west.
f: There is only one sun, so the definite article the is used before it.
r: The definite article is also used with unique things such as the moon, the earth and the sky.

q: In which year was the Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India signed? (3)
f: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
r: It converted the ceasefire line of Kashmir into the Line of Control.

q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, what is the official name of the Parliament of Pakistan?
f: Article 50 of the Constitution says the Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses, the National Assembly and the Senate, and it is called Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).
r: The two houses of the Majlis-e-Shoora are the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: In which direction of Pakistan does the port city of Gwadar lie?
f: Gwadar lies on the Arabian Sea coast in the south-west corner of Pakistan in the province of Balochistan.
r: Pakistan purchased Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

q: Which type of triangle has all three sides of different lengths? (3)
f: A scalene triangle has no two sides equal, while an isosceles triangle has two equal sides and an equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
r: The angles of a scalene triangle are also all different.

q: What is sin(-y) equal to?
f: Sine is an odd function, so reflecting the angle across the x-axis changes the sign of the sine. Therefore sin(-y) = -sin y.
r: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-y) = cos y.

q: Which tense is normally used with the words 'since' and 'for' (for example, 'I have lived here since 2010')?
f: 'Since' and 'for' show how long an action or state has continued up to now, which is expressed by the present perfect (or present perfect continuous) tense. Example: She has worked here for five years.
r: 'Since' is used with a point in time and 'for' with a length of time.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die? (10)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died at Aligarh on 27 March 1898.
r: He was born in 1817, so he lived about 80 years.

q: Which type of brackets is used to write a solution set? (2)
f: Sets, including solution sets, are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
r: Round and square brackets are used for intervals.

q: Solve the proportion 2 : x :: 14 : 28. What is x?
f: In a proportion the product of extremes equals the product of means: 2 x 28 = x x 14. So 56 = 14x and x = 4.
r: A proportion a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d.

q: Solve for x: 3x - 9 = 9 - x
f: Add x and 9 to both sides: 4x = 18, so x = 18/4 = 9/2 = 4.5.

q: Who was the son of Hazrat Sarah (AS), the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)? (3)
f: Hazrat Sarah was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), born when she was very old.
r: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra.

q: The sound of which animal is mentioned in the Quran as the most unpleasant of sounds?
f: Surah Luqman (31:19) says the harshest of sounds is surely the braying of the donkey.
r: This verse is part of Luqman's advice to his son to lower his voice.

q: When was the Soviet Union (USSR) established? (4)
f: The USSR was formally created on 30 December 1922 by the union of Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian and Transcaucasian republics.
r: It was dissolved in December 1991.

q: Iqbal's famous 1930 speech at the annual session of the All India Muslim League is known as which address? (4)
f: Allama Iqbal delivered his Presidential Address at Allahabad in December 1930. In it he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
r: The Allahabad Address is considered the intellectual root of the Pakistan idea.

q: What is the last sermon of the Holy Prophet (SAW) called?
f: The Prophet (SAW) delivered his final sermon during the Farewell Hajj at Arafat. It is called Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida.
r: The Farewell Hajj took place in 10 AH.

q: A car runs at 60 km/hr and a train runs at twice the speed of the car. What is the speed of the train?
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/hr. Speed does not change with the time taken, so it is still 120 km/hr after 30 minutes.
r: In 30 minutes this train would cover 60 km.

q: What does OPAC stand for in library science?
f: OPAC means Online Public Access Catalogue. It is a computerised database that lets users search a library's holdings.
r: It replaced the traditional card catalogue.

q: Fill in the blank: She arrived ___ the station. (3)
f: We use the preposition at with a specific point or place such as a station. So the sentence is: She arrived at the station.
r: We use arrive in for large places such as cities and countries.

q: After which battle did the Quraysh stop their attacks on Madina, as the Prophet (SAW) said they would no longer attack?
f: After the failed siege of Madina in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH, the Prophet (SAW) said that the Quraysh would not attack again and the Muslims would march against them.
r: The Battle of Khandaq was won mainly by the trench dug on the advice of Salman Farsi (RA).

q: The graphical representation of which type of equation is a straight line? (3)
f: A linear equation such as y = mx + c has degree one in its variables. Its graph is always a straight line.
r: A quadratic equation gives a parabola.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'strange'?
f: Strange means unusual or unexpected, and odd has the same meaning. The other options mean the opposite.
r: Other synonyms of strange are peculiar and queer.

q: What is the central subject of the Holy Quran?
f: The Quran is a book of guidance addressed to mankind. Its main subject is man and his success in this world and the Hereafter.
r: The Quran has 114 surahs and 30 paras.

q: What is a synonym of 'subversion'? (3)
f: Subversion means an attempt to weaken or overthrow an established authority from within. Undermining carries the same sense.
r: Sabotage is another close synonym.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to reach the summit of K2? (3)
f: Ashraf Aman reached the summit of K2 in 1977 as part of a Japanese-led expedition.
r: Nazir Sabir was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest, in 2000, and sources differ slightly on the exact K2 summit date in August 1977.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 16th of that month? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 16th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 16th falls on the same day as the 2nd, Sunday.
r: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.

q: What is the meaning of the name of Surah Al-Ankabut?
f: Ankabut means spider, and the surah is named after the spider's web used as an example in it.
r: Al-Ankabut is the 29th surah of the Quran.

q: Which two surahs are known as Muawwazatain?
f: Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas are called Muawwidhatayn because they seek refuge in Allah.
r: They are the last two surahs of the Quran, 113 and 114.

q: What is the capital of Sweden? (3)
f: Stockholm is the capital and largest city of Sweden.
r: Sweden is a Scandinavian country in northern Europe.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "abate"?
f: To abate means to become less intense, which is to subside.
r: Abatement is the noun form.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquiesce"?
f: To acquiesce is to accept or go along with something without protest, so comply is closest.
r: Its noun form is acquiescence.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "acquisition"?
f: An acquisition is something gained or bought, close to purchase.
r: Companies use the word for takeovers.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "awful"?
f: Awful means very bad, same as terrible.
r: The word originally meant inspiring awe.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "brute"?
f: A brute is a savage or cruel creature, so beast is closest.
r: Brutal is the related adjective.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "exceptional"? (5)
f: Exceptional means unusually good or rare, like extraordinary.
r: Its antonym is ordinary.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "irksome"? (5)
f: Irksome means causing irritation, so annoying is closest.
r: To irk means to annoy.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "magistrate"?
f: A magistrate is a civil officer who acts as a judge in lower courts.
r: In Pakistan, judicial magistrates hear minor criminal cases.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "puzzled"?
f: Puzzled means confused, the same as perplexed.
r: Bewildered is another synonym.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "wield"? (4)
f: To wield is to hold and use something such as a tool or power, so handle is closest.
r: One can wield a sword or wield influence.

q: What is the capital of Tajikistan? (11)
f: Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan.
r: Tajikistan borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

q: If 1 km takes 100 minutes, how many km can be covered in 12 minutes at the same rate?
f: Rate is 1/100 km per minute, so in 12 minutes the distance is 12 x 1/100 = 0.12 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: Which of the following was NOT among the Ashra Mubashra (the ten Companions given glad tidings of Paradise)?
f: Hazrat Talha is one of the ten given the glad tidings of Paradise, while Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) is not on that list.
r: The ten include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.

q: Which is the tallest building in Pakistan? (19)
f: Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi is generally listed as Pakistan's tallest building, though its stated height varies by source (about 273 to 300 metres).
r: Habib Bank Plaza was long considered the tallest before the Icon Tower was built.

q: Tarbela Dam is located in which district and province of Pakistan? (19)
f: Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus near Tarbela in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Tayammum have according to the Hanafi school? (3)
f: The three farz of Tayammum are making the intention, striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face, and wiping both arms up to the elbows.
r: Tayammum is performed when water is not available or cannot be used.

q: On which date is International Tea Day observed?
f: The United Nations designated 21 May as International Tea Day, first observed in 2020.
r: Earlier, tea-producing countries had celebrated an International Tea Day on 15 December.

q: A soldier's mother ____ her emotions as he left for the front. Choose the correct word.
f: The phrasal verb 'bottled up' means kept feelings hidden, and 'teared' is not the right form in this sense.
r: 'Bottle up' is the phrasal verb; the past tense is 'bottled up'.

q: What is 20% of one tenth of 90?
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and 20% of 9 is 1.8.
r: 20% is the same as one fifth.

q: What is one tenth of 1/20?
r: Multiplying by one tenth moves the decimal point one place left.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 9? (7)
f: One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
r: Equivalently 9 divided by 30 equals 0.3.

q: What is cosec theta equal to?
f: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, so cosec theta = 1 / sin theta.
r: Sec theta is 1 / cos theta and cot theta is 1 / tan theta.

q: In a right-angled triangle, sin theta is equal to which ratio? (2)
f: Sine of an angle is the length of the opposite side (perpendicular) divided by the hypotenuse.
r: Cos theta is base / hypotenuse and tan theta is perpendicular / base.

q: Which is the third surah of the Holy Quran? (7)
f: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, so the third surah is Al-Imran.
r: An-Nisa is the fourth surah.

q: A number whose three times is 6 has 2 added to it. What is the result?
f: If 3 times the number is 6, the number is 2. Adding 2 gives 2 + 2 = 4.
r: The candidate answer 2 is only the number itself, not the final result.

q: Through which point does the line y = 6x pass? (2)
f: Putting x = 0 gives y = 0, so the line passes through the origin (0, 0).
r: A line of the form y = mx always passes through the origin.

q: Watch is to time as barometer is to what? (3)
f: A watch measures time and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
r: A thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.

q: What was the approximate age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Fujjar war? (4)
f: The Fujjar war was fought in the sacred months and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part by handing arrows to his uncles at about the age of 15 years.
r: Some narrations give an age between 14 and 20 years, so sources differ slightly; 15 is the common textbook answer.

q: When did Tipu Sultan die? (3)
f: Tipu Sultan was killed defending Seringapatam against the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War on 4 May 1799.
r: The Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792 ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

q: Which title is used for Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA)? (3)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known by the title Attiq, meaning freed from the fire of Hell, besides Siddiq.
r: Farooq is the title of Hazrat Umar (RA) and Murtaza of Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: Habibullah (beloved of Allah) is the title of whom?
f: Habibullah is a famous title of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah.

q: If today is Friday, what day will it be after 14 days?
f: 14 days is exactly 2 weeks, so the day is the same: Friday.
r: Any multiple of 7 days brings the same weekday.

q: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 5 days?
f: Counting 5 days after Monday gives Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
r: Saturday and Sunday form the weekend.

q: What is the line that touches a circle at exactly one point called? (7)
f: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, while a secant cuts it at two points.
r: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

q: How many tournaments make up the Grand Slam in tennis?
f: The four Grand Slam tennis tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
r: Wimbledon is the oldest of the four.

q: What is the transpose of a row matrix called? (2)
f: Transposing swaps rows and columns, so a 1 by n row matrix becomes an n by 1 column matrix.
r: The transpose of a square matrix is also a square matrix.

q: What was the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) about?
o: Sale of Kashmir by the British to Gulab Singh
End of the First Anglo-Sikh War handing Punjab to the Mughals
f: Under the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 7.5 million rupees.
r: It followed the First Anglo-Sikh War and created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir.

q: Ali's present age is 3 years and his sister is twice his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 8 years old?
f: Sister's age now is 2 x 3 = 6, so she is 3 years older than Ali. When Ali is 8, she is 8 + 3 = 11.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice the age of Salman. When Salman is 12 years old, what will be the age of Ali? (7)
f: Ali is 2 x 4 = 8 now, so he is 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16.
r: Do not double the later age; only the present ages are in the ratio 2 to 1.

q: What type of constitution was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan? (21)
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, set up a federal parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly.
r: It was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed.

q: Beauty is to ugliness as adversity is to what?
f: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of adversity (hardship) is prosperity.
r: Hardship, misfortune and difficulty are synonyms of adversity, not opposites.

q: Beauty is to ugliness as diversity is to what? (2)
f: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of diversity (variety) is uniformity.
r: Variety, difference and range are close in meaning to diversity.

q: Unscramble the word SAPIR. Is it the name of a bird, a country or a city?
f: The letters of SAPIR form PARIS, which is a city, the capital of France.
r: Paris stands on the River Seine.

q: In which Hijri year was Hazrat Usman (RA) martyred?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA), the third caliph, was besieged in his house and martyred in Dhul Hijjah 35 AH (656 CE).
r: He was succeeded as caliph by Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: If Y = 4x - 2 and x = 2, what is the value of Y?
f: Substitute x = 2: Y = 4 x 2 - 2 = 8 - 2 = 6.
r: Multiplication is done before subtraction in the order of operations.

q: If y = 2x - 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y?
f: Substitute x = 2: y = 2 x 2 - 1 = 4 - 1 = 3.
r: Substitution means replacing a variable by its given value.

q: What comes next in the series Z1, Y2, X3, ...?
f: The letters move backwards through the alphabet (Z, Y, X, W) while the numbers go up by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4). So the next term is W4.
r: Letter pairs like this often combine a reverse alphabet with an increasing number.

q: On what date was the Treaty of Versailles signed? (3)
f: The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors at the Palace of Versailles.
r: It came into force on 10 January 1920, the same day the League of Nations first met.

q: What was the Treaty of Versailles?
o: A peace treaty ending World War I with Germany
A treaty ending World War II
An alliance between Britain and France
A treaty founding the United Nations
f: The Treaty of Versailles was the peace settlement between Germany and the Allied Powers after World War I.
r: It forced Germany to accept war guilt, pay reparations and lose territory.

q: According to the commonly accepted count, how many verses (ayat) does the Holy Quran have? (3)
f: The Hafs count most widely followed gives 6236 verses across 114 surahs.
r: Counts differ slightly between recitation traditions; 6666 is a popular but not the standard figure.

q: Fill in the blank: He was very grateful that he ----- my computer promptly.
f: The sentence is in the past tense (was grateful), so the past tense repaired is correct.
r: Tense should stay consistent between the clauses of a sentence.

q: Who was the last Viceroy of British India? (20)
f: Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy from March to August 1947 and then became the first Governor-General of independent India.
r: His predecessor was Lord Wavell.

q: In which year did Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan make his official visit to the United States?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 at the invitation of President Truman.
r: This visit is seen as the start of close Pakistan-US relations.

q: How many vowels are in the letter string AEDIPOUDLEC (Aedipoudlec)?
f: The vowels are A, E, I, O, U, E, which makes 6.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are in AZPQTVSJFIU?
f: The vowels are A, I and U, giving 3.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are in AdebccTEvIxyz?
f: The vowels are A, e, E and I, giving 4.
r: Capital and small letters count equally.

q: Which country does India import the largest share of its weapons from, according to SIPRI data?
