o: The cats are always chased by dogs.
The cats were always chased by dogs.
The cats are always being chased by dogs.
The cats always chase the dogs.
f: The sentence is present simple, so the passive is 'am/is/are + past participle': the cats are always chased by dogs.
r: The 'being' form is used only for the present continuous passive.

q: What causes earthquakes, including those under the ocean? (4)
f: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates slip or collide and release energy along faults, on land or the sea floor.
r: A big undersea earthquake can cause a tsunami.

q: What is the center of a circle called? (5)
o: Point from which all boundary points are equidistant
f: The center is the fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from every point on the circle.
r: The fixed distance is called the radius.

q: What is the centre of a circle? (2)
o: A fixed point equidistant from every point on the circle
The longest chord of the circle
f: The centre is the single fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from all points on the circumference. A circle has exactly one centre.
r: The fixed distance from the centre to the circle is called the radius.

q: What was the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922? (8)
o: A mob burned a police station and killed policemen, after which Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement
A massacre of unarmed people at a garden in Amritsar
A mutiny of Indian soldiers in Meerut
A salt march to the sea
f: On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh a crowd set fire to a police station, killing about 22 policemen. Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened earlier, in 1919.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'stagnancy'? (2)
f: Stagnancy is the state of not moving, flowing or developing, so it means inactivity.
r: Stagnant water is water that does not flow and often becomes foul.

q: What is a composite number? (7)
o: A number with exactly two factors
A positive integer greater than 1 with more than two factors
A number that is not divisible by 2
A number with only one factor
f: A composite number has at least one factor other than 1 and itself, so it has more than two factors. Examples are 4, 6, 8 and 9.
r: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

q: What is the meaning of 'contentment'? (2)
o: Satisfaction and happiness with what one has
f: Contentment is a state of being happy and satisfied with what one has.
r: The related adjective is content, and its opposite is discontent.

q: In which year AD was Khyber conquered by the Muslims? (2)
f: The Battle of Khyber took place in Muharram 7 AH, which corresponds to about 628 AD.
r: The conquest of Makkah took place later, in 8 AH.

q: Sahih Muslim is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book? (3)
f: Scholars rank Sahih Bukhari first and Sahih Muslim second in authenticity among the hadith collections.
r: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are called the Sahihain.

q: What is the official currency of Iran? (21)
f: The official currency of Iran is the Iranian rial. Ordinary people often quote prices in toman, which equals 10 rials.
r: Iran has passed a law to remove four zeros from the rial, and parliament kept the name rial rather than toman.

q: Which river is the deepest river in the world? (7)
f: The Congo River in Africa has been measured at depths of more than 220 metres, making it the deepest known river.
r: The Amazon carries the largest volume of water, while the Nile is often listed as the longest river.

q: Who delivered the famous Allahabad Address of 1930 in which a separate Muslim state in the north-west of India was envisioned? (3)
f: Allama Iqbal delivered this address as President of the All India Muslim League session at Allahabad in December 1930.
r: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933.

q: Which of the following is closest in meaning to the word development? (2)
f: Development means gradual growth or advancement, so improvement is the closest meaning.
r: Progress and advancement are also synonyms of development.

q: What is a synonym of 'difficult'? (2)
f: Difficult means needing much effort. Hard has the same meaning.
r: Easy and simple are antonyms of difficult.

q: Which of the following is a division of Punjab? (3)
f: Sahiwal is one of the divisions of Punjab. Hyderabad is in Sindh, Quetta in Balochistan and Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: Other Punjab divisions include Lahore, Multan, Faisalabad and Rawalpindi.

q: How many minutes are there in 10 degrees in the DMS (degrees, minutes, seconds) system? (4)
f: One degree is 60 minutes, so 10 degrees = 10 x 60 = 600 minutes.
r: One minute is 60 seconds, so one degree is 3600 seconds.

q: Pakistan's economy has traditionally been described as predominantly what kind of economy? (2)
f: Pakistani textbooks describe the country as agricultural because agriculture supports most of the rural population and provides raw material to industry.
r: Today the services sector gives the largest share of GDP, while agriculture still employs about a third or more of the workforce.

q: By whom is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected under the 1973 Constitution? (4)
f: The Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, usually the leader who has a majority there.
r: The President then appoints the elected member as Prime Minister.

q: The algebraic expression 4a - 5b - 6 is what kind of expression? (2)
f: Each variable has power 1, so the degree of the expression is 1 and it is a linear expression.
r: The expression 8y - 6x + 7 is also linear.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'eventually'? (3)
f: 'Eventually' means at last, after a long time or a series of events. 'Ultimately' carries the same sense.
r: Another synonym of 'eventually' is 'finally'.

q: What are all the factors of 10? (3)
f: The factors of a number are the numbers that divide it exactly. 10 divided by 1, 2, 5 and 10 leaves no remainder.
r: 10 has the prime factors 2 and 5.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in 60 minutes, how far does the train cover in the same time? (3)
f: The car's speed is 60 km in 1 hour = 60 km/h. The train moves at twice this speed, 120 km/h, so it covers 120 km in 60 minutes.
r: 60 minutes equal 1 hour.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car, and the train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does the car travel in 15 minutes? (2)
f: The train's speed is 120 km/h, so the car's speed is 120 / 2 = 60 km/h. In 15 minutes (a quarter of an hour) the car covers 60 / 4 = 15 km.
r: 15 minutes are one quarter of an hour.

q: Which is the fastest animal on earth? (2)
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, which is faster than any other animal. The cheetah is the fastest land animal at about 110 km/h.
r: The cheetah can keep its top speed only for short distances.

q: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the wife of whom? (2)
f: Hazrat Fatima (RA) married Hazrat Ali (RA) in 2 AH.
r: Their children were Hazrat Hasan, Hazrat Husain, Hazrat Zainab and Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

q: Who made the first successful powered aeroplane flight in 1903? (2)
f: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew the first powered, controlled aeroplane at Kitty Hawk, USA, on 17 December 1903.
r: The Montgolfier brothers made the first hot air balloon flight in 1783.

q: What is the formula of the discriminant of the quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0? (2)
f: The discriminant is D = b^2 - 4ac, the expression under the square root in the quadratic formula. It decides the nature of the roots.
r: If D is positive the roots are real and distinct, if D is zero they are equal, and if D is negative they are complex.

q: What is the meaning of futility? (2)
f: Futility is the quality of having no useful result, so it means pointlessness or uselessness.
r: The adjective form is futile.

q: Which general imposed the NRO (National Reconciliation Ordinance) in Pakistan in 2007? (2)
f: The National Reconciliation Ordinance was issued by President General Pervez Musharraf in October 2007. It gave amnesty in many corruption cases.
r: The Supreme Court of Pakistan declared the NRO unconstitutional in December 2009.

q: A class has 1500 students and 1200 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls? (5)
f: Girls = 1500 - 1200 = 300. Percentage = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20 percent.
r: Boys make up the other 80 percent of this class.

q: What is the height of a standard football goal (inside the posts, from ground to crossbar)? (2)
f: The crossbar of a standard football goal is 8 feet (2.44 m) above the ground.
r: The candidate answer of 24 inches is wrong; 24 feet is the width of the goal.

q: Who is the current Governor of Sindh (as of October 2026)? (13)
f: Nehal Hashmi of the PML-N took oath as Governor of Sindh on 13 March 2026.
r: He replaced Kamran Khan Tessori of the MQM-P, who was governor in 2022.

q: Who said that the life of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the best example? (2)
f: Allah says in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:21) that the Messenger of Allah is an excellent example for those who hope in Allah.
r: The Quran also describes the Prophet's character as of the highest standard in Surah Al-Qalam (68:4).

q: Which is the greatest number among 5, 4, 6, 9, 7 and 3? (2)
f: Comparing all the numbers, 9 is larger than 5, 4, 6, 7 and 3.
r: The smallest number in this list is 3.

q: After the death of which caliph was the compiled copy of the Quran passed to Hazrat Hafsa (RA) for safekeeping? (2)
f: The copy compiled under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) passed to Hazrat Umar (RA), and after his death it was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA).
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) later borrowed this copy from Hafsa (RA) to prepare standard copies of the Quran.

q: What is the HCF of 16 and 40? (4)
f: 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 and 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5, so the common part is 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.
r: HCF is also called the greatest common divisor (GCD).

q: Fill in the blank: Ali ____ himself against a horde of ruffians. (2)
f: The idiom is to pit oneself against someone, meaning to compete or struggle against them. The past tense is pitted.
r: Pit against means to set one person or force in a contest with another.

q: Who wrote the book Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind (Causes of the Indian Revolt)? (3)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it in 1859 to explain the causes of the War of Independence of 1857 and defend Muslims against blame.
r: It was originally written in Urdu and later translated into English.

q: Who was Hinda (Hind bint Utba) who accepted Islam? (2)
f: Hinda was the wife of Abu Sufyan and the mother of Hazrat Muawiyah (RA). She accepted Islam after the Conquest of Makkah.
r: She was also the one who had mutilated the body of Hazrat Hamza (RA) at Uhud before she embraced Islam.

q: Which is the higher mountain range, the Hindu Kush or the Himalaya? (2)
f: The Himalaya is higher: Mount Everest is 8,849 m while the Hindu Kush peak Tirich Mir is 7,708 m.
r: The Himalaya has more than a hundred peaks above 7,200 m.

q: Which country hosted the first Asian Games in 1951? (20)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
r: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: Which city hosted the Summer Olympic Games in 2012? (3)
f: The 2012 Summer Olympics were held in London, United Kingdom.
r: London became the first city to host the modern Olympics three times (1908, 1948 and 2012).

q: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896? (5)
f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
r: The ancient Olympics were also held in Greece, at Olympia.

q: What are the real and imaginary parts of the complex number 4 + 9i? (2)
f: In a + bi, a is the real part and b is the imaginary part. So the real part is 4 and the imaginary part is 9.
r: The imaginary part is the real coefficient b, not bi.

q: Who is generally credited as a co-founder of Twitter (now X) and its first chief executive? (2)
f: Twitter was founded in 2006 by Jack Dorsey, Noah Glass, Biz Stone and Evan Williams. Jack Dorsey is the best known and was its first CEO.
r: Twitter was renamed X in 2023 after it was bought by Elon Musk in 2022.

q: What is the capital of Ireland? (2)
f: Dublin is the capital and largest city of the Republic of Ireland. It lies on the east coast.
r: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, which is part of the United Kingdom.

q: In which year did the USSR veto a UN Security Council resolution on Kashmir, supporting India? (2)
f: On 22 June 1962 the Soviet Union vetoed a Security Council resolution on Kashmir backed by Pakistan. This was one of several Soviet vetoes on the issue.
r: The USSR had also used its veto on Kashmir in 1957.

q: Where is Jabal Tariq (Mount of Tariq) located? (2)
f: Jabal Tariq is the Arabic name from which the word Gibraltar comes. It is named after Tariq bin Ziyad, who landed there in 711 AD.
r: Tariq bin Ziyad began the Muslim conquest of Spain.

q: Which Muslim community of Kerala (Malabar coast), India, is well known? (2)
f: The Moplah (Mappila) are the Muslim community of the Malabar coast of Kerala, descended from Arab traders and local converts.
r: The Moplah Rebellion of 1921 took place in the Malabar region.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Khewra salt mine located? (3)
f: The Khewra salt mine lies in the Salt Range near Khewra in Jhelum district, in northern Punjab.
r: Khewra is one of the largest and oldest salt mines in the world.

q: Amir Khusro is regarded as the first poet of which language (in its early form)? (3)
f: Amir Khusro (1253-1325) composed verse in Hindavi, the early form of Urdu, and is called its first poet.
r: Amir Khusro also wrote in Persian and was a disciple of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya.

q: In which valley is Ansoo Lake located? (2)
f: Ansoo (Lake Ansoo) is a tear-shaped high-altitude lake in the Kaghan Valley of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: Lake Saif-ul-Malook is also in the Kaghan Valley.

q: Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite launched into space, was launched in which year? (2)
f: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 on 4 October 1957, which started the space age.
r: The first crewed spaceflight was Vostok 1 carrying Yuri Gagarin on 12 April 1961.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to lethal? (3)
f: Lethal means capable of causing death, which is the same as deadly.
r: Lethal injection is a method of execution in some countries.

q: Which is the last heavenly (divine) book? (2)
f: The Holy Quran was revealed to the last Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and is the final divine book. No book will come after it.
r: The other heavenly books are the Torah, Zaboor and Injeel.

q: In which unit is latitude measured? (2)
f: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the Equator, so it is measured in degrees.
r: The Equator is 0 degrees latitude and the poles are 90 degrees north and south.

q: How does the word MTVWVTM look when reflected in a mirror placed beside it (lateral reflection)? (2)
f: The letters M, T, V and W are each symmetrical about a vertical line, and the word reads the same from both ends. So its mirror image is identical.
r: Letters such as A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X and Y are symmetrical about a vertical axis.

q: Who discovered X-rays and developed the X-ray machine? (10)
f: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 in Germany.
r: He received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.

q: Fill in the blank: He lives ___ United States. (2)
f: The preposition in is used with the name of a country or large place where someone lives.
r: The preposition at is used for specific points such as at home or at school.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Mangla Dam located? (2)
f: Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum River near Mirpur in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: Mangla is one of the largest dams in Pakistan and was completed in 1967.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of marginal in the sense of minor or slight? (3)
f: Marginal means small or of little importance. The opposite is significant, meaning large or important.
r: Marginal can also mean at the edge, and then its opposite is central.

q: What is a Field Marshal? (8)
o: The highest rank in an army
A rank in the navy only
A police officer in charge of a district
f: Field Marshal is the highest (five-star) rank in the army of many countries. It is often given as an honour and is rarely awarded.
r: Ayub Khan became the first and only Field Marshal of Pakistan Army in 1959.

q: What is the median of 36 and 18? (2)
f: For two values the median is their average: (18 + 36) / 2 = 54 / 2 = 27.
r: For an even number of values the median is the mean of the two middle values.

q: Which prophet (AS) was granted the ability by Allah to mould (soften) iron? (2)
f: The Quran says that Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawud (AS) so he could make armour (Surah Saba).
r: Hazrat Dawud (AS) was given the holy book Zabur.

q: According to Greek mythology, who flew too close to the sun with wings of wax and fell into the sea? (2)
f: Icarus ignored his father's warning, flew too close to the sun, the wax melted and he fell.
r: His father Daedalus built the wings and the labyrinth of Crete.

q: Which number comes next: 12, 55, 14, 65, 16, 75, ? (2)
f: There are two interleaved series: 12, 14, 16 (add 2) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10). The term after 75 belongs to the first series, so it is 16 + 2 = 18.
r: The next term after 18 would be 85.

q: Which number comes next: 55, 65, 75, ? (5)
f: Each number increases by 10, so 75 + 10 = 85.
r: This is an arithmetic progression with common difference 10.

q: On whom is Hajj obligatory (farz)? (8)
o: Every sane, adult Muslim who has the means to travel and afford it
f: Hajj is farz once in a lifetime on a sane, adult (baligh) Muslim who is physically and financially able (istita'at) to make the journey.
r: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam.

q: Which of the following is a farz (obligatory act) of Hajj? (4)
f: The faraiz of Hajj in the Hanafi school are Ihram, Wuquf-e-Arafah and Tawaf-e-Ziyarah. Stoning and shaving are wajib, not farz.
r: Missing Wuquf-e-Arafah invalidates the Hajj.

q: Which word is a synonym of pacify? (10)
f: To pacify means to bring peace or to calm someone down. Calm has the same meaning.
r: Appease and soothe are other synonyms of pacify.

q: In which year was the second constitution of Pakistan enforced? (5)
f: Pakistan's first constitution came in 1956 and was abrogated in 1958. The second constitution, given by Ayub Khan, was enforced in 1962.
r: The third constitution of 1973 is still in force today with amendments.

q: What is a quarter of 10 percent of 12? (2)
f: 10 percent of 12 = 1.2. A quarter of 1.2 = 0.3.
r: A quarter means dividing by 4.

q: Which of the following lists the five pillars of Islam correctly? (2)
f: The five pillars are the declaration of faith (Kalima/Shahada), prayer (Salah), fasting (Sawm), charity (Zakat) and pilgrimage (Hajj).
r: In the order taught in Pakistan the pillars are Kalima, Salah, Roza, Zakat and Hajj.

q: Convert to passive voice: The pilot landed the plane safely. (2)
o: The plane is landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landed safely by the pilot.
The plane had landed safely by the pilot.
The plane was landing safely by the pilot.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were plus the past participle. The object plane becomes the subject: The plane was landed safely by the pilot.
r: Passive voice formula for simple past: object + was/were + third form of verb + by + subject.

q: Where were the first Asian Games held in 1951? (9)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
r: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: Sadequain, a famous name in Pakistani art, is known as a (3)
f: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a renowned Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known especially for his calligraphy of Quranic verses and verses of Allama Iqbal and Ghalib.
r: He also painted murals, including the ceiling of the Frere Hall in Karachi.

q: What is the approximate population of the Philippines in 2026? (2)
f: Current estimates put the population of the Philippines at about 118 million in 2026, which ranks it around 14th in the world.
r: The 2020 census of the Philippines counted about 109 million people.

q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won? (77)
f: Pakistan has two Nobel laureates: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
r: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate in history.

q: In which year was the One Unit scheme established in West Pakistan? (21)
f: The provinces of West Pakistan were merged into one unit in 1955.
r: One Unit was dissolved by Yahya Khan in 1970.

q: Past is to present as preceding is to: (4)
f: Past and present are opposites, and the opposite of preceding is following.
r: Preceding means coming before.

q: Who is the chairman of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) as of 2026? (2)
f: Barrister Gohar Ali Khan was elected PTI chairman unopposed in December 2023 as a temporary arrangement. He is still reported as chairman in 2026.
r: Imran Khan was chairman before 2023 and the party's founder; his camp still calls him the real chairman.

q: What is a quarter of 1/20? (2)
r: Multiplying two fractions means multiplying numerators together and denominators together.

q: Overexposure to ultraviolet rays from the sun is most harmful to which part of the human body? (4)
f: Ultraviolet rays damage skin cells and the eyes, causing sunburn, skin cancer and cataracts.
r: The ozone layer in the atmosphere absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

q: Which city or territory of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate according to the 2023 census? (19)
f: The 2023 census showed Islamabad Capital Territory with the highest literacy rate, about 84 percent, ahead of all provinces.
r: The national literacy rate was about 60.7 percent for people aged 10 and above.

q: Which is the largest religion in the world by number of followers? (13)
f: Christianity has about 2.4 billion followers, more than any other religion.
r: Islam is the second largest religion and is the fastest growing.

q: What was the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940? (10)
o: A demand for separate independent states for the Muslims of India
A demand for a united India
A plan to boycott the elections of 1946
f: At the Lahore session of the All-India Muslim League, the resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped into independent states.
r: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and later called the Pakistan Resolution.

q: What is the cube root of 8? (2)
f: 2 x 2 x 2 = 8, so the cube root of 8 is 2.
r: The cube root of 27 is 3 and the cube root of 64 is 4.

q: What is the cube root of 92, approximately? (2)
f: 4 cubed is 64 and 5 cubed is 125, so the cube root of 92 lies between 4 and 5. Since 4.5 cubed is 91.1, the value is about 4.5.
r: A perfect cube close to 92 is 91.125, which is 4.5 cubed.

q: For how many years did Hazrat Usman (RA) rule as Caliph? (3)
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) was Caliph from 23 AH to 35 AH, which is about 12 years.
r: He was the third Caliph and his rule was the longest among the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.

q: What is the presiding officer who runs the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan called? (2)
f: The National Assembly is presided over and run by its Speaker, who is elected by its members. In his absence the Deputy Speaker presides.
r: The Senate, by contrast, is presided over by the Chairman.

q: Famous footballer Mohamed Salah belongs to which country? (38)
f: Mohamed Salah was born in Nagrig, Egypt, and captains the Egyptian national team.
r: He is best known for his years at Liverpool in the English Premier League.

q: Which is the busiest seaport in the world (by container traffic)? (3)
f: Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port for 16 years in a row, handling about 55 million TEU in 2025. Singapore is second.
r: Ningbo-Zhoushan is the busiest port by total cargo tonnage.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word security? (2)
f: Security means the state of being protected from danger, which is safety.
r: Another close word is protection.

q: For how many terms can the Secretary-General of the United Nations normally serve? (2)
o: Two terms of five years each
Three terms of four years each
f: The UN Charter sets no limit, but by established practice the Secretary-General serves a five-year term that can be renewed once, so two terms.
r: The General Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on the recommendation of the Security Council.

q: Who started the Pan-Islamism movement in the Muslim world? (2)
f: Syed Jamaluddin Afghani called for the unity of all Muslims against European domination and is regarded as the founder of the Pan-Islamic movement.
r: In the subcontinent the Khilafat Movement was also influenced by Pan-Islamic ideas.

q: In which year was the Simla Conference between the British, the Congress and the Muslim League held? (9)
f: The Simla Conference was convened by Viceroy Lord Wavell in 1945 to discuss the Wavell Plan for an interim government.
r: The conference failed mainly because Congress refused to accept that the Muslim League alone represented the Muslims.

q: On which date was the Simla Conference of 1945 held (it began on this date)? (4)
f: Lord Wavell opened the Simla Conference on 25 June 1945 and it ended on 14 July 1945 without agreement.
r: The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India of 1972 is a different event.

q: On which date was the Simla (Shimla) Agreement between Pakistan and India signed? (14)
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.
r: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 after the 1965 war.

q: If one side of a square is 6 cm, what is its perimeter? (2)
f: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 6 = 24 cm.
r: The area of this square would be 36 square cm.

q: What is the value of sin 190 degrees? (2)
f: 190 degrees lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, so sin 190 = -sin 10 = -0.174.
r: The candidate answer 0.997 is not correct for degrees.

q: Who is the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan as of 2026? (6)
f: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has been Chief of Army Staff since November 2022 and was also named Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025.
r: General Qamar Javed Bajwa was the previous army chief from 2016 to 2022.

q: What does WHO stand for? (6)
f: WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency for international public health.
r: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word sublime? (2)
f: Sublime means of very high excellence or grandeur, so majestic is closest.
r: Its antonym is a word like ordinary or lowly.

q: Which vitamin do we get from sunlight? (3)
f: Sunlight on the skin helps the body make vitamin D.
r: Lack of vitamin D causes rickets in children.

q: What is the synonym of stagnant? (2)
f: Stagnant describes water or conditions that are still and not moving or developing.
r: Stagnate is the verb form, meaning to become inactive or still.

q: What is the synonym of might? (3)
f: As a noun, might means great strength or power.
r: Might is also a modal verb expressing possibility, but the noun sense is meant here.

q: What is the synonym of synopsis? (4)
f: A synopsis is a brief summary of a book, film or plot.
r: An abstract is a synopsis of a research paper.

q: In which Hijri month and year did the Ghazwa of Tabuk take place? (13)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards Tabuk in Rajab of 9 AH, which is about October 630 CE.
r: It is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship.

q: Who is the current T20I captain of the Pakistan cricket team (October 2026)? (2)
f: Pakistan named Sahibzada Farhan T20I captain in October 2026, ahead of the home series against Sri Lanka.
r: Salman Ali Agha led the side from March 2025 until this change, and Shaheen Shah Afridi remains ODI captain.

q: Which bowler of the Pakistan women's team became the first Pakistani player to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals? (2)
f: Nida Dar became the first Pakistan player, male or female, to reach 100 T20I wickets in July 2021.
r: Sana Mir took over 150 ODI wickets, and Dar has since passed 140 T20I wickets.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Thar desert mainly located? (9)
f: The Pakistani part of the Thar desert lies in the south-east of Sindh, mainly in Tharparkar district.
r: The Thar desert extends into the Indian state of Rajasthan and is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

q: What is the order of the transpose of a matrix of order m x n? (8)
f: The transpose is obtained by interchanging rows and columns, so an m x n matrix becomes n x m.
r: The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.

q: Who conquered Sindh during the Umayyad period? (4)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD under the Umayyad governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf and Caliph Walid I.
r: Raja Dahir was the ruler of Sindh at the time.

q: In set theory, the universal set is what of every set under consideration? (2)
f: The universal set contains all the elements of the sets under discussion, so every set is a subset of it and it is a superset of each.
r: The universal set is usually denoted by U.

q: What is the complement of the universal set? (3)
f: The complement of U contains the elements not in U, and there are none, so it is the empty set.
r: Likewise the complement of the empty set is the universal set.

q: What is the approximate value of pi? (4)
f: Pi is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, approximately 3.14159. It is commonly written as 3.14 or 22/7.
r: Pi is an irrational number, so its decimal expansion never ends or repeats.

q: Vehicle is to road as ship is to ___ ? (18)
f: A vehicle travels on a road, and a ship travels on the sea. The analogy links a vehicle or vessel with the surface it moves on.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: Which animal uses sound waves (echolocation) to find its way, like eyes? (2)
f: Bats emit high-frequency ultrasonic sounds and use the returning echoes to locate objects and prey in the dark. This is called echolocation.
r: Dolphins also use echolocation, and humans copy the idea in sonar.

q: What does the white band in the flag of Pakistan represent? (13)
f: The white stripe of the flag stands for the religious minorities of Pakistan, while the green stands for the Muslim majority.
r: The crescent in the flag represents progress and the star represents light and knowledge.

q: How many wives did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have at the time of his death, according to the commonly taught account? (3)
f: At the time of his death the Holy Prophet (PBUH) had 9 wives living. In total he married 11 wives; Hazrat Khadija (RA) and Hazrat Zainab bint Khuzaima (RA) had died before him.
r: The wives of the Prophet (PBUH) are called Ummahat-ul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers).

q: In the sentence 'Wow! This is my book', what part of speech is 'Wow'? (2)
f: 'Wow' expresses a sudden feeling of surprise, and a word that does this is an interjection.
r: An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.

q: What is the capital of New Zealand? (4)
f: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, although Auckland is its largest city.
r: New Zealand has no president; its head of state is the British monarch.

q: What is (3 + i)(3 - i)? (2)
r: The product of a complex number and its conjugate is always a real number.

q: What is 1/3 of 20? (2)
f: One third of 20 is 20 divided by 3, which is 20/3 or about 6.67.
r: A mixed form of 20/3 is 6 and 2/3.

q: What is 2 + 1/3? (2)
r: 7/3 is an improper fraction.

q: What is 1/10 of 1/5 of 120?
r: Taking 1/10 of a number just moves the decimal point one place to the left.

q: What is one third of 25% of 120?
f: 25% of 120 = 30. One third of 30 = 10.
r: 25% is the same as one quarter.

q: What is 125% of 25?
If the 13th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 27th day of that month be?
f: From the 13th to the 27th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the day is the same, Sunday.
r: A gap of 7, 14, 21 or 28 days always gives the same weekday.

q: If the 23rd of a month falls on Friday, what day will the 14th of that month be?
f: From the 14th to the 23rd is 9 days. 9 = 7 + 2, so the 14th is 2 days before Friday, which is Wednesday.
r: When going backward, subtract the extra days after removing full weeks.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th be? (2)
f: From the 3rd to the 14th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. The 14th is Tuesday.
r: Remove full weeks first, then count the remaining days.

q: If the 29th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 15th be?
f: From the 15th to the 29th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both are Monday.
r: Dates that are 14 days apart fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 15th be? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.
r: Thirteen days ahead is the same as one day behind.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Monday, which is Sunday.
r: Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Monday becomes Sunday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 17th of the month? (2)
f: From the 1st to the 17th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 17th is 2 days after Monday, which is Wednesday.
r: The 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th of a month always share the same weekday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 17th be?
f: From the 4th to the 17th is 13 days. 13 = 7 + 6, so the 17th is 6 days after Sunday, which is Saturday.
r: Six days ahead equals one day behind, so Sunday becomes Saturday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 18th of the month be? (4)
f: From the 2nd to the 18th is 16 days. 16 = 14 + 2, so the 18th is 2 days after Friday, which is Sunday.
r: Subtract full weeks (multiples of 7) and count only the remainder.

q: What is one tenth of 10% of 140?
f: 10% of 140 = 14. One tenth of 14 = 1.4.
r: 10% and one tenth are the same value, so this is 140 x 0.1 x 0.1 = 1.4.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)? (2)
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1340 = 160. Percentage = 160 / 1500 x 100 = 10.67%.
r: The percentage of present students here is 89.33%.

q: Out of 2000 students, 1600 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
r: The percentage of present students is 80%.

q: The population of a city was 1600 in 1960 and it doubles every year. What will the population be in 1967?
f: From 1960 to 1967 is 7 years, so the population doubles 7 times: 1600 x 2^7 = 1600 x 128 = 204800.
r: 2^7 = 128 and 2^10 = 1024 are useful powers of two to remember.

q: A car runs at a speed of 180 km/h. How much distance does it travel in 20 minutes?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 180 x 1/3 = 60 km.
r: To convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18, so 180 km/h is 50 m/s.

q: According to the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan, what was the minimum age to be elected President?
f: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim and at least 35 years old.
r: Under the 1973 Constitution the minimum age for President is 45 years, and the 1956 Constitution required 40 years.

q: Ali was born in 1974 and Azhar was born in 1970. Bilal is 2 years younger than Azhar. In which year was Bilal born?
f: Younger by 2 years means born 2 years later, so Bilal was born in 1970 + 2 = 1972.
r: Born later means younger; born earlier means older.

q: What position did Pakistan achieve in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan reached the final of the 1999 World Cup in England but lost to Australia at Lord's.
r: Pakistan won the World Cup once, in 1992.

q: Akbar was born in 1970 and Ammar in 1977. Bilal is older than Ammar. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Bilal is older than Ammar, so Ammar is younger than Bilal. Ammar (1977) is also younger than Akbar (1970), so Ammar is the youngest.
r: A later birth year means a younger person.

q: What is 2% of 200?
r: 1% of 200 is 2, so 2% is double that.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 21st be? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 21st is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 8th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 8th to the 21st is 13 days. 13 = 1 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Tuesday to reach Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st be?
f: From the 1st to the 21st is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be? (7)
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 23rd be?
f: From the 3rd to the 23rd is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Monday to reach Sunday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be? (2)
f: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 3rd to the 24th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 24th be?
f: From the 1st to the 24th is 23 days. 23 = 3 weeks and 2 extra days, so count 2 days forward from Sunday to reach Tuesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th be? (3)
f: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days. 21 = 3 weeks and 0 extra days, so count 0 days forward from Monday to reach Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Friday to reach Thursday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be?
f: From the 5th to the 25th is 20 days. 20 = 2 weeks and 6 extra days, so count 6 days forward from Sunday to reach Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Saturday, what day will the 26th be?
f: From the 7th to the 26th is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Saturday to reach Thursday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be? (3)
f: From the 1st to the 27th is 26 days. 26 = 3 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 25th be? (2)
f: From the 7th to the 25th is 18 days. 18 = 2 weeks and 4 extra days, so count 4 days forward from Sunday to reach Thursday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th be?
f: From the 7th to the 12th is 5 days. 5 = 0 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Monday to reach Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: The 24th of a month is Friday. What day is the 2nd of the same month?
f: The 2nd is 22 days before the 24th. 22 = 3 weeks and 1 extra day, so it is one day before Friday, which is Thursday.
r: Going back exactly 7 days always gives the same weekday.

q: Which country hosted the largest number of refugees in 2016? (2)
f: According to UNHCR figures for 2016, Turkey hosted about 2.9 million refugees, mostly Syrians, which was the largest number in the world.
r: Pakistan was the second largest host in 2016 with about 1.4 million refugees, mostly Afghans.

q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
f: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Indonesia, in the cities of Jakarta and Palembang.
r: The 2022 Asian Games, held in 2023, were hosted by Hangzhou in China.

q: On which date did the 2018 Asian Games begin?
f: The 18th Asian Games opened in Jakarta on 18 August 2018 and ended on 2 September 2018.
r: Indonesia's Jakarta and Palembang shared hosting of that edition.

q: Where were the 2018 Winter Olympic Games held? (2)
f: The 2018 Winter Olympics took place in Pyeongchang, South Korea, in February 2018.
r: The 2018 Summer Olympics did not exist: the Summer Games were held in Rio in 2016 and Tokyo in 2021.

q: Which country hosted the 2018 Asia Cup cricket tournament?
f: The 2018 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, in September 2018.
r: India won the 2018 Asia Cup by beating Bangladesh in the final.

q: What is the value of the percentage of absent students if 300 out of 500 students are present? (2)
f: Absent students = 500 - 300 = 200. Percentage absent = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.
r: Percentage present plus percentage absent always equals 100%.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 300 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (2)
r: The percentage present here is 20%.

q: There are 1500 students in a class, 1200 are boys and 300 are girls. What is the percentage of girls?
f: Percentage of girls = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%.
r: Boys make up the remaining 80%.

q: Out of 1200 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students, to two decimal places?
r: The percentage present is 340 / 1200 x 100 = 28.33%.

q: A helicopter flies at 340 km/h. About how much time does it take to cover 700 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 700 / 340 = 2.06 hours, which is about 2 hours 4 minutes.
r: Speed = distance / time is the basic formula behind such questions.

q: In a class of 500 students, 360 are present. How many students are absent? (7)
f: Absent students = 500 - 360 = 140.
r: As a percentage, 140 out of 500 is 28%.

q: A plane uses 80 gallons of fuel to cover 320 miles. How many gallons will 800 miles need?
f: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon. For 800 miles: 800 x 0.25 = 200 gallons.
r: The same method works with kilometres and litres.

q: A car travels at 78 km/h. How far will it travel in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 12 / 60 = 0.2 hour. Distance = 78 x 0.2 = 15.6 km.
r: To change minutes into hours, divide by 60.

q: How many elements are there in each row of a matrix of order 4x3?
f: A matrix of order 4x3 has 4 rows and 3 columns, so each row has 3 elements.
r: The total number of elements in a 4x3 matrix is 12.

q: A matrix is of order 4x3. How many rows does it have?
f: The order of a matrix is written as rows x columns, so a 4x3 matrix has 4 rows.
r: It has 3 columns.

q: In which year was the first martial law in Pakistan lifted?
f: General Ayub Khan imposed martial law in October 1958 and it was lifted on 8 June 1962 when the new constitution came into force.
r: The 1962 Constitution gave Pakistan a presidential system with Ayub Khan as President.

q: Which word is the antonym of abrogate?
f: To abrogate means to repeal or do away with a law. Its opposite is to enact or establish a law.
r: Repeal, annul and revoke are synonyms of abrogate.

q: Which word is a synonym of abrogate?
f: To abrogate means to formally cancel or repeal a law or agreement, so repeal has the same meaning.
r: The word comes from the Latin abrogare, meaning to repeal a law.

q: On which date was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan abrogated? (4)
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law on 25 March 1969 after Ayub Khan resigned, and the 1962 Constitution was abrogated.
r: Ayub Khan resigned on 25 March 1969 and handed power to the army chief Yahya Khan.

q: On which date was the first Constitution of Pakistan (1956) adopted by the Constituent Assembly? (7)
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the 1956 Constitution on 29 February 1956.
r: It came into force on 23 March 1956, which is why that day was celebrated as Republic Day.

q: What is the title of Imam Abu Hanifa's well-known book on beliefs?
f: Al-Fiqh al-Akbar is the creed work traditionally attributed to Imam Abu Hanifa.
r: Al-Muwatta is by Imam Malik and Kitab-ul-Umm is by Imam Shafi'i; some scholars debate how much of Fiqh-e-Akbar is by Abu Hanifa himself.

q: What is the commutative property of addition?
o: a x (b + c) = a x b + a x c
f: The commutative property says that changing the order of the numbers being added does not change the sum, so a + b = b + a.
r: Addition and multiplication are commutative, but subtraction and division are not.

q: Who was the first black President of South Africa? (2)
f: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first black President in May 1994 after the first fully democratic elections.
r: He spent 27 years in prison and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 jointly with F. W. de Klerk.

q: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya (1870) in reply to which book?
o: A Life of Mahomet by William Muir
f: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya was written to answer the objections raised against the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in William Muir's book A Life of Mahomet. Sir Syed wrote it after visiting England in 1869.
r: Sir Syed's own book on the 1857 war was Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind.

q: Who wrote the book Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya?
f: Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya is a work in defence of Islam written by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan. It was published in 1870.
r: Sir Syed founded the Aligarh Muslim (MAO) College in 1875.

q: Ahmed is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ahmed is 14 years old, what will be his sister's age?
f: Sister's age now is 6 x 3 = 18 years, so she is 12 years older than Ahmed. When Ahmed is 14, she is 14 + 12 = 26.
r: In age problems the difference in ages stays fixed while both ages increase equally.

q: On which date did Allama Muhammad Iqbal die? (17)
f: Allama Iqbal died in Lahore on 21 April 1938. He is buried near the Badshahi Mosque.
r: Iqbal's birth date is 9 November 1877 in Sialkot, which is observed as Iqbal Day.

q: Complete the analogy: Sailor is to Navy as Airman is to ____.
f: A sailor serves in the Navy, in the same way an airman serves in the Air Force.
r: Soldier, sailor and airman are the ranks-and-file terms for the Army, Navy and Air Force.

q: How many sons did Hazrat Aisha (RA) have?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), had no children. She is called Ummul Momineen.
r: She was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and is known for narrating many hadiths.

q: On which date was the Jammu and Kashmir State Subject Rule issued?
f: The State Subject Rule defining who was a permanent resident of Jammu and Kashmir was issued by Maharaja Hari Singh on 20 April 1927. It limited land ownership and state jobs to state subjects.
r: Maharaja Hari Singh ruled Jammu and Kashmir from 1925 to 1947.

q: If Ahmad is older than Akbar and Akbar is older than Ali, then Ali is ____.
f: The order of age is Ahmad, then Akbar, then Ali, so Ali is the youngest. Therefore Ali is younger than Ahmad (and Akbar).
r: Such statements can be solved by writing the names in order from oldest to youngest.

q: Is 5x - 4y + 6 = 0 an algebraic expression or an equation?
f: It has an equals sign with an expression on each side (the right side is 0), so it is an equation. It is a linear equation in two variables.
r: An algebraic expression, such as 5x - 4y + 6, has no equals sign.

q: The product of two algebraic expressions is ____ the product of their LCM and HCF.
f: For any two expressions (or numbers) f and g, f x g = LCM x HCF. So the product is equal to the product of LCM and HCF.
r: For numbers, 12 x 18 = 216 and LCM 36 x HCF 6 = 216.

q: What comes next in the series: X3, Y2, Z?
f: The letters move forward X, Y, Z while the numbers go down 3, 2, 1. So the next term is Z1.
r: Letter-number series usually move the letters and numbers by fixed steps.

q: If the letters of the word ARGUMENT are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter is third? (3)
f: The letters of ARGUMENT in alphabetical order are A, E, G, M, N, R, T, U. The third letter is G.
r: ARGUMENT has 8 letters and 3 vowels: A, U and E.

q: By what other name is Pakistan Day, observed on 23 March, also known? (2)
f: Pakistan Day commemorates the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) passed on 23 March 1940, so it is also called Resolution Day. It also marks the adoption of the first constitution in 1956.
r: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.

q: Who is the angel of death (Malak-ul-Maut) in Islamic belief? (2)
f: Hazrat Izrail (AS) is the angel entrusted with taking souls at death. The Quran refers to him as the angel of death in Surah As-Sajdah.
r: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel who will blow the trumpet on the Day of Judgement.

q: Two adjacent angles which together form a right angle are called what?
f: Two angles whose sum is 90 degrees are complementary. Together they make one right angle.
r: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, which is a straight line.

q: What is the antonym of the word abolish? (2)
f: To abolish is to put an end to something officially. Its opposite is to establish, meaning to set up.
r: Abolish, cancel, remove and end are all close in meaning to each other.

q: What is the antonym of the word accumulated?
f: Accumulated means gathered together over time. The opposite is dispersed, meaning scattered.
r: Accumulate is a synonym of amass and collect.

q: Find the missing number in the analogy 2 : X :: 4 : 16.
f: Since 4 : 16 shows that 16 is the square of 4 (4 x 4 = 16), the same rule applies to 2, so X = 2 x 2 = 4.
r: Square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on.

q: Anemia is mainly caused by the deficiency of which element?
f: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells. Without enough iron the blood cannot carry enough oxygen, which causes anemia.
r: Iodine deficiency causes goitre.

q: Area of a parallelogram = base x ______.
f: The area of a parallelogram is its base multiplied by its perpendicular height, also called its altitude.
r: The area of a triangle is half of base times altitude.

q: What is the antonym of despite?
f: Despite means in spite of something; the opposite idea is because of, which gives a cause.
r: Despite, in spite of and notwithstanding all mean the same thing.

q: What is the antonym of eliminated?
f: Eliminated means removed or left out; the opposite is included or retained.
r: Eliminate comes from the Latin eliminare, meaning to drive out of doors.

q: What is the antonym of evidently?
f: Evidently means in a clear and obvious way; the opposite is obscurely, meaning in an unclear way.
r: Evidently, obviously and clearly are synonyms of each other.

q: What is the antonym of foe?
f: A foe is an enemy; the opposite is a friend.
r: Foe and enemy are synonyms, as are ally and friend.

q: What is the antonym of improvement?
f: Improvement means becoming better; the opposite is deterioration, meaning becoming worse.
r: Progress and betterment are synonyms of improvement.

q: What is the antonym of impudent?
f: Impudent means rude and disrespectful; the opposite is respectful or polite.
r: Impudent, insolent and cheeky are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of multitude?
f: A multitude is a very large number of people or things; the opposite is a handful, a very small number.
r: Multitude, crowd and throng are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of nourishment?
f: Nourishment is the food needed for life and growth; the opposite is starvation, the lack of food.
r: Nutrition and sustenance are synonyms of nourishment.

q: What is the antonym of pragmatic? (3)
f: Pragmatic means dealing with things in a practical way; the opposite is idealistic, based on ideals rather than reality.
r: Pragmatic, practical and realistic are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of purification?
f: Purification means making something clean; the opposite is contamination, making it impure.
r: Pollution is another antonym of purification.

q: What is the antonym of recalcitrant?
f: Recalcitrant means stubbornly resisting authority; the opposite is obedient or compliant.
r: Candidates remembered willing or ready, which are also close in meaning to obedient.

q: What is the antonym of refuse?
f: To refuse is to say no to something offered; the opposite is to accept.
r: Refuse as a noun means rubbish, but in this question it is the verb.

q: What is the antonym of shameful?
f: Shameful means causing shame; the opposite is honourable, deserving respect.
r: Shameful, disgraceful and scandalous are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of strict?
f: Strict means demanding obedience to rules; the opposite is lenient, meaning easy-going or merciful.
r: Strict, stern and rigid are synonyms.

q: What is the antonym of underhand?
f: Underhand means done in a secret or dishonest way; the opposite is honest or open.
r: Aboveboard is the usual one-word opposite of underhand.

q: What is the antonym of virtue?
f: Virtue means moral goodness; the opposite is vice, meaning immoral behaviour.
r: The pair virtue and vice is a classic antonym pair.

q: What is the supreme law (apex law) of Pakistan?
f: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, adopted in 1973, is the supreme law of the country and all other laws must conform to it.
r: The 1973 Constitution was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and has 280 Articles.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 26? (3)
r: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly halfway between them.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 24 and 36?
r: The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 8 and 36?
r: The geometric mean of 8 and 36 is different: it is the square root of 288, about 16.97.

q: Who were the Ashra-e-Mubashara? (10)
o: Ten Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) given the glad tidings of Paradise in one lifetime
The ten wives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Ten Muslim commanders of the Battle of Badr
f: The Ashra-e-Mubashara are ten Companions whom the Prophet (PBUH) named as people of Paradise while they were alive. They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.
r: Their names are listed in a famous hadith narrated by Abdur Rahman bin Awf and Sa'id bin Zaid.

q: When did the USA drop atom bombs on Japan? (8)
f: The USA dropped the atom bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
r: Japan announced its surrender soon afterwards, ending the Second World War.

q: What is the national game of Australia, as commonly stated?
f: Cricket is commonly given as the national game of Australia. It is the most popular summer sport there.
r: Australia has no officially declared national game, so sources differ; Australian rules football is also very popular.

q: After the Quran, what is the most authentic source of Islamic teachings? (2)
f: The Hadith and Sunnah, the sayings and actions of the Prophet (PBUH), explain and complete the Quran. They are the second source of Islamic law.
r: Ijma and Qiyas are usually counted as the third and fourth sources.

q: What is the average of 23 and 32?
f: Add the numbers: 23 + 32 = 55. Divide by 2: 55 / 2 = 27.5.
r: Average equals the sum of values divided by the number of values.

q: What is the average of 28 and 36?
f: Add the numbers: 28 + 36 = 64. Divide by 2: 64 / 2 = 32.
r: The average of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

q: What is the average of 32 and 20? (2)
f: Add the numbers: 32 + 20 = 52. Divide by 2: 52 / 2 = 26.
r: Average is also called the arithmetic mean.

q: What is the y-axis also called in the coordinate plane?
f: The vertical y-axis is called the ordinate axis and the y-coordinate is the ordinate. The horizontal x-axis is the abscissa axis.
r: The point where both axes meet is called the origin.

q: How many times is the name of Hazrat Ayesha (RA) mentioned in the Quran?
f: The Quran does not mention Hazrat Ayesha (RA) by name. She is referred to indirectly in some verses about the Prophet's household.
r: The Prophet's wives are addressed as the Mothers of the Believers in Surah Al-Ahzab.

q: In which Surah was the incident of slander (Ifk) against Hazrat Ayesha (RA) addressed and her innocence declared?
f: Verses 11 to 20 of Surah An-Nur declare Hazrat Ayesha (RA) innocent of the false accusation. This is known as the incident of Ifk.
r: The incident took place after the expedition of Banu Mustaliq.

q: According to the 14 Points of Quaid-e-Azam, what form of government should India have? (2)
o: A federation with residuary powers vested in the provinces
A unitary system with a strong centre
f: The 14 Points demanded that the future constitution of India be federal. The residuary powers were to remain with the provinces.
r: Quaid-e-Azam presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: Muslim Bagh in Balochistan is famous for which mineral? (7)
f: Muslim Bagh in Zhob district of Balochistan is known for its chromite (chromium ore) deposits. Chromite is mined there on a large scale.
r: Chamalang in Balochistan is known for coal and Saindak for copper and gold.

q: On which date was the Baghdad Pact first signed between Turkey and Iraq?
f: Turkey and Iraq signed the Baghdad Pact in Baghdad on 24 February 1955. Britain, Pakistan and Iran joined later in 1955.
r: After Iraq left in 1959 the pact was renamed CENTO.

q: Who founded the city of Baghdad? (2)
f: The Abbasid caliph Al-Mansur founded Baghdad in 762 AD. He made it his capital and named it the City of Peace.
r: Baghdad reached its golden age under Haroon-ur-Rasheed and Mamun-ur-Rasheed.

q: What is the approximate area of Balochistan province? (12)
f: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km, which is about 44 percent of Pakistan. It is the largest province by area.
r: Punjab covers about 205,344 square km and Sindh about 140,914 square km.

q: Which was the first commercial bank of Pakistan, as commonly stated?
f: Habib Bank Limited (HBL), founded in 1941 and moved to Karachi after 1947, is generally called the first commercial bank of Pakistan.
r: Sources differ somewhat, but most Pakistani textbooks name Habib Bank.

q: In which city is the head office of the State Bank of Pakistan located?
f: The State Bank of Pakistan has its head office on I.I. Chundrigar Road in Karachi. It began operations on 1 July 1948.
r: The State Bank has a main branch in Islamabad too.

q: Who were the Banu Quraysh?
o: The ruling tribe of Makkah to which the Prophet (PBUH) belonged
f: Quraysh (Quraish) was the leading tribe of Makkah and the custodian of the Kaaba. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to its clan Banu Hashim.
r: Banu Quraiza, Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were Jewish tribes of Madina.

q: By what other name is the Sukkur Barrage known?
f: The Sukkur Barrage on the Indus was opened in 1932 and named the Lloyd Barrage after the Governor of Bombay, Sir George Lloyd.
r: It irrigates millions of acres in Sindh through seven canals.

q: The area of a triangle is 24 square cm and its base is 4 cm. What is its height?
f: Area = (1/2) x base x height, so 24 = (1/2) x 4 x h = 2h. Therefore h = 12 cm.
r: The height of a triangle is the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

q: Akbar is 3 times as old as his sister. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 15 years old?
f: Akbar's age is 3 times his sister's age, so sister = 15 divided by 3 = 5 years.
r: In ratio questions, divide the larger age by the multiple to get the smaller age.

q: Ali's sister is 3 times as old as Ali. How old will Ali's sister be when Ali becomes 14 years old?
f: Sister's age = 3 times Ali's age = 3 x 14 = 42 years.
r: Here the sister is the older one, so multiply Ali's age by 3.

q: On which date did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic under the 1956 Constitution? (14)
f: The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on 23 March 1956 and the country became the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

q: In which year did the revelation (wahi) first begin to descend on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira? (2)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old when Angel Jibreel brought the first revelation, in 610 AD during Ramadan.
r: The first revelation consisted of the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

q: Which countries jointly hosted the 2026 FIFA World Cup? (3)
f: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and Mexico, from June to July 2026.
r: The previous World Cup in 2022 was held in Qatar.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Belgium as of October 2026?
f: Bart De Wever became Prime Minister of Belgium on 3 February 2025 and remains in office.
r: Charles Michel, the answer given by candidates in 2022, was PM from 2014 to 2019, and Alexander De Croo held office from 2020 to 2025.

q: What is the Urdu meaning of the word Momin?
f: Momin means a believer, one who has faith (iman).
r: The plural Momineen is used in the title Ameer-ul-Momineen, meaning Commander of the Faithful.

q: In which quadrant of the coordinate plane does the point (-5, 6) lie? (2)
f: The x value is negative and the y value is positive, which is the second quadrant.
r: The signs by quadrant are (+,+), (-,+), (-,-) and (+,-) for the first to fourth quadrants.

q: Microsoft, the technology company, belongs to which country?
f: Microsoft is headquartered in Redmond, Washington, in the United States.
r: Microsoft was founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen.

q: The river Tigris mainly flows through which country?
f: The Tigris rises in Turkey and flows through Iraq, joining the Euphrates to form the Shatt al-Arab.
r: Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, stands on the Tigris.

q: Which is the best month mentioned in the Quran by name?
f: Ramadan is the only month named in the Quran, and the Quran was revealed in it.
r: Laylatul Qadr, better than a thousand months, falls in Ramadan.

q: Which is the longest tunnel of Pakistan?
f: The Lowari Tunnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, linking Dir and Chitral, has a main bore of about 8.5 km and is the longest in Pakistan.
r: The Khojak Tunnel in Balochistan is a railway tunnel about 3.9 km long.

q: Which is the longest river of India? (2)
f: The Ganga is the longest river of India, about 2,525 km.
r: The Indus and Brahmaputra are longer overall but rise outside India.

q: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was a slave in the custody of which Quraish chief before he was freed? (4)
f: Umayyah bin Khalaf tortured Hazrat Bilal (RA) for accepting Islam, until Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.
r: Hazrat Bilal (RA) became the first muazzin of Islam.

q: What is the national bird of India?
f: The Indian peafowl (peacock) was declared the national bird of India in 1963.
r: The national bird of Pakistan is the chukar partridge.

q: Choose the correct word: He has gone to ___ UK.
f: The name United Kingdom is a plural union of states, so UK takes the definite article: the UK.
r: Names like the USA, the UAE and the Netherlands also take the.

q: Sky is to blue as blood is to what?
f: The sky is blue in colour and blood is red in colour, so the analogy is by colour.
r: Haemoglobin in red blood cells gives blood its red colour.

q: On which date was the atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki? (2)
f: The United States dropped the atomic bomb on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945, three days after the bomb on Hiroshima.
r: Japan announced its surrender on 15 August 1945 and signed the surrender document on 2 September 1945.

q: On which date was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born? (3)
f: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi. He died on 11 September 1948.
r: His birthplace is Wazir Mansion, Karachi.

q: General Pervez Musharraf was born in which city?
f: Pervez Musharraf was born on 11 August 1943 in Delhi, British India. His family migrated to Pakistan in 1947.
r: He ruled Pakistan from the 1999 military takeover until he resigned in 2008.

q: In which city was Prophet Muhammad (SAW) born? (2)
f: The Holy Prophet (SAW) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, about 570 or 571 AD.
r: He migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which began the Hijri calendar.

q: The Maginot Line was a line of fortifications built along the border between which two countries?
f: France built the Maginot Line in the 1930s along its eastern border with Germany (and Italy) to stop a German invasion.
r: Germany bypassed it in 1940 by invading France through Belgium.

q: Which country has the longest bridge in the world? (6)
f: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, about 164.8 km long, is the longest bridge in the world by total length. It carries the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed railway.
r: The second longest is the Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan.

q: What is the son of my brother called in relation to me?
f: A brother's son is a nephew to his uncle or aunt.
r: A brother's daughter is called a niece.

q: What is the approximate average lactation period of a buffalo? (8)
f: A buffalo gives milk for about 270 to 305 days after calving, so about 300 days is the usual figure. It varies with breed and feeding.
r: Nili-Ravi is a famous Pakistani buffalo breed known for high milk yield.

q: Which is the tallest building in the world? (2)
f: Burj Khalifa in Dubai, 828 m high, is the tallest completed building in the world as of October 2026.
r: Jeddah Tower in Saudi Arabia is under construction and is expected to surpass it around 2028.

q: Gun is to bullet as pitcher is to ___.
f: A gun fires a bullet, and in baseball a pitcher throws a ball. The relationship is a tool or person to the object it sends.
r: A bat is used by the batter to hit the ball.

q: In a bus of 40 people, 30 are men. What percentage of the people are women?
f: Women = 40 - 30 = 10. Percentage = 10 / 40 x 100 = 25%.
r: The men make up the remaining 75%.

q: In which month and Hijri year was the Treaty (Sulah) of Hudaibia signed?
f: The Prophet (SAW) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH, was stopped at Hudaibia, and signed the treaty there with the Quraish.
r: The treaty is called a clear victory in Surah Al-Fath, and it was followed by the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

q: The compilation of the Quran in book form was done under which caliph, who accepted Hazrat Umar's (RA) suggestion after the Battle of Yamama?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) ordered Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to collect the Quran after many Huffaz were martyred at the Battle of Yamama.
r: Hazrat Usman (RA) later had standard copies made and sent to the main cities.

q: Lusaka is the capital of which country?
f: Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia.
r: Zambia was formerly called Northern Rhodesia and became independent in 1964.

q: What is the official capital of Benin?
f: Porto-Novo is the official capital of Benin, although the government sits in Cotonou.
r: Cotonou is the largest city and economic centre of Benin.

q: What is the constitutional capital of Bolivia?
f: Bolivia's constitution names Sucre as its capital.
r: The government and legislature sit in La Paz, which is the seat of government.

q: What is the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina?
f: Sarajevo is the capital and largest city of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
r: The 1914 assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo triggered World War I.

q: What is the capital of Egypt? (5)
f: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt, on the River Nile.
r: Egypt is building a New Administrative Capital east of Cairo.

q: What is the capital of Great Britain (the United Kingdom)? (2)
f: London is the capital of the United Kingdom and England.
r: Edinburgh, Cardiff and Belfast are capitals of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

q: What is the capital of Liberia? (3)
f: Monrovia is the capital of Liberia and is named after US President James Monroe.
r: Liberia was founded by freed African American slaves.

q: What is the capital of Madagascar?
f: Antananarivo is the capital and largest city of Madagascar.
r: Madagascar is the fourth largest island in the world.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia? (10)
f: Ulaanbaatar (Ulan Bator) is the capital of Mongolia.
r: Ulaanbaatar is one of the coldest capital cities in the world.

q: What is the capital of Morocco? (2)
f: Rabat is the capital of Morocco.
r: Casablanca is the largest city of Morocco.

q: What is the capital of Turkmenistan? (4)
f: Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan.
r: Turkmenistan is a Central Asian country bordering Iran and Afghanistan.

q: What is the capital of Uzbekistan? (3)
f: Tashkent is the capital and largest city of Uzbekistan.
r: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration between Pakistan and India was signed in this city.

q: What is the capital of Vietnam? (2)
f: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.
r: Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) is the largest city of Vietnam.

q: In which years was the FIFA World Cup not held because of World War II?
f: The World Cup was held in 1938 and then next in 1950, so the 1942 and 1946 tournaments were cancelled.
r: Brazil hosted the 1950 World Cup, the first after the war.

q: What is the currency of Canada? (4)
f: Canada uses the Canadian dollar (CAD).
r: The Canadian one dollar coin is nicknamed the loonie.

q: Which dam in Pakistan was built with the help of Canada under the Colombo Plan?
f: Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was built in the 1950s with Canadian aid under the Colombo Plan.
r: Mangla Dam was built on the Jhelum River and Tarbela Dam on the Indus River.

q: Who is the captain of the Pakistan women's cricket team in 2026? (2)
f: Fatima Sana leads Pakistan women's team, including at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.
r: Before Fatima Sana, Nida Dar and Bismah Maroof had captained the side.

q: Change the narration: The captain said to his men, "Stand at ease."
o: The captain told his men that they stood at ease.
The captain commanded his men to stand at ease.
The captain asked his men if they stood at ease.
The captain said to his men that stand at ease.
f: The quoted sentence is an order, so the reporting verb becomes commanded and the order is turned into an infinitive.
r: Imperative sentences in indirect speech use words such as ordered, commanded, requested or advised.

q: Choose the part of speech of the word 'but' in: I ran fast to catch the train but I was late.
f: Here 'but' joins two clauses showing contrast, so it is a coordinating conjunction.
r: The coordinating conjunctions are for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so.

q: Change the voice: Dogs always chased cats.
o: Cats are always chased by dogs.
Cats have always been chased by dogs.
Cats were always chased by dogs.
Cats were always being chased by dogs.
f: The sentence is past simple, so the passive uses 'was/were + past participle': cats were always chased by dogs.
r: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

q: In which city is the World Trade Center located?
f: The World Trade Center complex is in Lower Manhattan, New York City.
r: The original Twin Towers were destroyed in the attacks of 11 September 2001.

q: What was the name of the camel of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (5)
f: The Prophet's well-known camel was named Qaswa, which he rode during the Hijrat.
r: Sources also mention the name Adba for his camel, and Duldul was his mule.

q: In which year did Pakistan join CENTO (the Baghdad Pact)? (3)
f: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact in 1955, which was renamed CENTO in 1959.
r: Pakistan left CENTO in 1979 after Iran withdrew.

q: On a farm, the cows are 5, the camels are three times the cows and the goats are three times the camels. How many animals are there in total?
f: Cows = 5, camels = 3 x 5 = 15, goats = 3 x 15 = 45. Total = 5 + 15 + 45 = 65.
r: Always compute each group step by step before adding.

q: Which is the correct spelling?
f: The word is spelt circum-fer-ence, from Latin meaning carrying around.
r: Circumference comes from the Latin words circum (around) and ferre (to carry).

q: Which are the three largest cities of Pakistan by population?
f: In the 2023 census the most populous cities were Karachi, then Lahore, then Faisalabad.
r: Karachi is the largest city and the capital of Sindh.

q: Basel is a city of which country? (4)
f: Basel lies on the River Rhine in north-west Switzerland, near the French and German borders.
r: Basel is home to the Bank for International Settlements.

q: In which city is the Shahi Qila (Lahore Fort) located? (9)
f: The Shahi Qila, also called the Lahore Fort, stands in the Walled City of Lahore. It was rebuilt in the Mughal era, notably under Akbar.
r: The Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens were listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1981.

q: What is the characteristic of the logarithm (base 10) of 2458.4?
f: The characteristic is the number of digits before the decimal point minus one. 2458.4 has 4 digits before the point, so the characteristic is 3.
r: The decimal part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.

q: What is the characteristic of log 99.96?
f: 99.96 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so its characteristic is 2 - 1 = 1.
r: Since log 100 = 2, log 99.96 is just under 2, that is 1 plus a mantissa close to 1.

q: What is the characteristic of log 99.6?
f: 99.6 has 2 digits before the decimal point, so its characteristic is 2 - 1 = 1.
r: For numbers less than 1 the characteristic is negative.

q: In the sentence 'The movie was amazing', what part of speech is the word 'amazing'?
f: The word 'amazing' describes the noun 'movie', so it is an adjective.
r: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun.

q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey Champions Trophy? (7)
f: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy three times, in 1978, 1980 and 1994.
r: Australia is the most successful team in the tournament history, with 14 titles.

q: Which country topped the medal table of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta?
f: China won the most gold medals (132) and the most medals overall at the 2018 Asian Games.
r: Japan finished second and South Korea third in 2018.

q: Which country is the current FIFA World Cup champion (2026)?
f: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the 2026 final on 19 July 2026.
r: The previous champion was Argentina in 2022, and Germany won in 2014.

q: Who is the Premier (Prime Minister) of China? (3)
f: Li Qiang has been Premier of the State Council of China since March 2023.
r: His predecessor was Li Keqiang, who served from 2013 to 2023.

q: What is the closest meaning of 'up to date'?
f: Up to date means current or modern, including the latest information or style.
r: Its opposite is outdated or obsolete.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'cordial'?
f: Cordial means warm, friendly and polite.
r: Cordial can also be a noun meaning a sweet fruit drink.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'cute'?
f: Cute means pleasingly attractive or charming, especially in a small or sweet way.
r: Synonyms include adorable and lovely.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'distraction'? (3)
f: A distraction is something that pulls attention away from what one is doing, so diversion (also deviation of attention) is closest.
r: The opposite of distraction is concentration.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'installed'?
f: To install something is to put or fix it in position ready for use, so installed means fitted in place.
r: The opposite of install is uninstall or remove.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'lubricant'?
f: A lubricant such as oil or grease is applied to moving parts to reduce friction between them.
r: Engine oil is a common lubricant used in vehicles.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'predicament'?
f: A predicament is an unpleasant or awkward situation that is hard to get out of, so difficult situation or dilemma fits best.
r: Synonyms of predicament include plight, dilemma and quandary.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'proceeding' as used in 'The work is proceeding well'? (7)
f: To proceed means to go on or move forward, so proceeding means advancing or continuing.
r: As a noun, proceedings means the events of a meeting or a legal action.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'propel'?
f: To propel is to push or drive something forward with force.
r: A propeller is the device that propels a ship or aeroplane.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'purge'?
f: To purge means to rid something of unwanted things or people, in other words to cleanse or remove.
r: Purge is also used for a medicine that clears the bowels.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'safety'?
f: Safety means being protected from harm or danger, which is the same as security.
r: Danger, risk and threat are antonyms of safety.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'comic'?
f: Comic means causing laughter, so funny is the closest meaning.
r: Comical and humorous are also synonyms of comic.

q: What is the international telephone country code of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's international dialling code is +92.
r: +91 is India, +93 is Afghanistan and +98 is Iran.

q: Which is the largest and coldest place on Earth?
f: Antarctica is the coldest, driest and windiest continent and is larger than Europe and Australia.
r: The lowest natural temperature recorded on Earth, about minus 89 degrees Celsius, was at Vostok Station in Antarctica.

q: The common endpoint of two non-collinear rays forming an angle is called its what?
f: Two rays that start from the same point form an angle, and that shared endpoint is the vertex of the angle.
r: The two rays forming the angle are called its arms or sides.

q: Which two colours are found on the national flag of Pakistan?
f: The flag has a dark green field with a vertical white stripe at the hoist, and a white crescent and star on the green.
r: The flag was designed by Syed Amir-uddin Kedwaii based on the Muslim League flag.

q: Does a column matrix have an inverse?
o: No, because it is not a square matrix
Yes, it is always a row matrix
Yes, it is the identity matrix
Only if all entries are zero
f: Only a square matrix with a non-zero determinant can have an inverse, and a column matrix has one column but several rows, so it is not square.
r: A column matrix can be turned into a row matrix by taking its transpose.

q: How many rows and columns does the matrix [2 3] have?
f: The matrix is written in a single line, so it has 1 row, and it has two entries, so 2 columns. Its order is 1 x 2.
r: A matrix with only one row is called a row matrix.

q: What is the common difference of the series 12, 16, 20, 24, 28?
f: 16 - 12 = 4, 20 - 16 = 4, and so on, so each term increases by 4.
r: A series with a constant common difference is an arithmetic progression.
