r: The Khewra salt mine was discovered in the time of Alexander the Great, according to local tradition.

q: In which city is the shrine of the Sufi poet Bulleh Shah located? (8)
f: Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur, in Punjab.
r: Bulleh Shah wrote his Sufi poetry (kafis) in Punjabi.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word spurn? (8)
f: To spurn means to refuse something with scorn. Reject is the nearest meaning.
r: Spurn can also be used as a noun in old English for a kick, but the common meaning is to refuse.

q: If the 13th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th of that month? (6)
f: 28 - 13 = 15 days later. 15 = 14 + 1, so move 1 day forward from Monday, which is Tuesday.
r: Two full weeks (14 days) bring back the same weekday.

q: If the 27th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th day be? (6)
f: From the 9th to the 27th is 18 days. 18 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.
r: The 13th would be Monday, as 27 - 14 = 13.

q: Saeed Anwar, famous in Pakistan, was a player of which sport? (6)
f: Saeed Anwar was a left-handed opening batsman of the Pakistan cricket team.
r: He scored 194 against India in 1997, which was then the highest ODI score.

q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 PM? (6)
f: At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3. Three hour marks of 30 degrees each make 90 degrees.
r: Each hour mark on a clock face is 30 degrees apart.

q: Who is the head of the cabinet in a parliamentary system? (7)
f: In a parliamentary system the Prime Minister leads the cabinet and the government.
r: In Pakistan the President is the head of state, not of the cabinet.

q: In which present-day country did Islam originate? (9)
f: Islam began in Makkah in the Arabian Peninsula, in what is now Saudi Arabia.
r: The first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira near Makkah.

q: Is the cosine function an even or an odd function? (6)
f: cos(-x) = cos x for every x, which is the definition of an even function.
r: Sine and tangent are odd functions because sin(-x) = -sin x and tan(-x) = -tan x.

q: In which year was Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin dismissed? (6)
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed on 17 April 1953.
r: He had become Prime Minister after the assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1951.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'doomed'? (6)
f: Doomed means destined for misfortune, so its opposite is blessed or fortunate.
r: Fated and condemned are synonyms of doomed.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to furtive? (6)
f: Furtive means done in a secret or sneaky way to avoid being noticed. Stealthy has the same meaning.
r: Other synonyms of furtive are secretive, sly and surreptitious.

q: A car travels 60 km. A train with double the speed of the car travels for half the time. What distance does the train cover? (6)
f: Distance = speed x time. Doubling the speed and halving the time gives 2 x 1/2 = 1 times the car's distance, which is 60 km.
r: Speed doubled and time halved leaves the distance unchanged.

q: On which date is the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India commonly said to have begun in 1999? (20)
f: The conflict is commonly dated from 3 May 1999, when intrusions were first reported in the Kargil sector.
r: Indian sources mark 26 July 1999 as the end of the conflict, and sources differ slightly on exact dates.

q: In which year was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged? (7)
f: Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979, after being removed from power by General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.
r: He was the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party.

q: Between which longitudes does Pakistan lie? (6)
f: Pakistan lies approximately between 61 degrees east and 75 degrees east longitude.
r: Pakistan lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres.

q: Where is the Noor Mahal located? (6)
f: Noor Mahal is a palace built by the Nawab of Bahawalpur in 1872 in the city of Bahawalpur.
r: It is now under the care of the Pakistan Army.

q: What is the full name of Imam Malik, founder of the Maliki school of fiqh? (6)
f: Imam Malik is Malik ibn Anas, who lived in Madinah. He is also called Imam of Madinah.
r: His famous book is Al-Muwatta.

q: Pakistan provides a sea route to the landlocked countries of which region? (6)
f: Pakistan's ports, Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, offer the shortest sea access for Afghanistan and the Central Asian states. These states have no coastline of their own.
r: Afghanistan has long used Karachi port under the Afghan Transit Trade agreement.

q: Under which constitution is Pakistan currently being run? (6)
f: Pakistan is run under the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973 and has been amended many times.
r: The earlier constitutions of 1956 and 1962 were abrogated.

q: What is the tenure (term) of the National Assembly of Pakistan, unless it is dissolved earlier? (8)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the National Assembly lasts five years from its first meeting. After that it stops working automatically.
r: The Senate is a permanent house and is never dissolved.

q: Who was the Governor General of India during the War of Independence of 1857 and became the first Viceroy in 1858? (5)
f: Lord Canning was Governor General from 1856 to 1858. After the Government of India Act 1858 he became the first Viceroy.
r: Lord Dalhousie was his predecessor and introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan during the 1971 war with India? (5)
f: General Yahya Khan was President from March 1969 until 20 December 1971, so he was President during the December 1971 war.
r: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took over as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971.

q: Which country won the 1974 FIFA World Cup? (5)
f: West Germany beat the Netherlands 2-1 in the final in Munich to win the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
r: West Germany had also won the World Cup in 1954.

q: In the point (3, 4), what is the number 3 called? (5)
f: In an ordered pair (x, y) the first number x is the abscissa. The second number y is the ordinate.
r: The abscissa is measured along the x-axis.

q: Which province of the subcontinent did the British occupy first? (5)
f: The British won the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and took control of Bengal first.
r: Sindh was conquered in 1843 and Punjab in 1849.

q: In which year was the Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology (Islamic Council) established in Pakistan? (5)
f: The Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology was set up under the 1962 Constitution, on 1 August 1962.
r: In the 1973 Constitution it continued as the Council of Islamic Ideology under Articles 228 to 230.

q: What is the synonym of 'disastrous'? (5)
f: Disastrous means causing great harm or damage, which is the same as catastrophic.
r: The noun form is disaster.

q: What is the synonym of 'doomed'? (5)
f: Doomed means destined to a bad outcome, which is the same as fated.
r: The noun doom means a terrible fate.

q: Which country is the largest exporter of tea in the world by volume? (5)
f: Kenya exports more tea by volume than any other country. India is second, and Sri Lanka and China follow.
r: China is the largest tea producer, but it keeps much of its tea for home use, and sources differ if ranked by value.

q: In which country was FIFA founded in 1904? (5)
f: FIFA was founded in Paris, France, on 21 May 1904 by seven European associations.
r: FIFA headquarters are today in Zurich, Switzerland.

q: Which is the largest glacier of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks? (6)
f: Pakistani textbooks name the Siachen Glacier, about 76 km long, as the largest in the Karakoram and in the region.
r: Sources differ because Siachen is under Indian control, and Biafo and Baltoro are the longest glaciers inside Pakistan-administered areas.

q: The Gobi Desert lies in southern Mongolia and in which other country? (6)
f: The Gobi Desert stretches across southern Mongolia and northern China.
r: It is a cold desert and the largest desert in Asia.

q: What is the currency of Hungary? (5)
f: Hungary uses its own currency, the forint (HUF). It has not adopted the euro.
r: Poland uses the zloty and the Czech Republic uses the koruna.

q: The United States entered World War II after which event? (5)
o: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
f: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
r: Germany and Italy then declared war on the US a few days later.

q: Which group of gases is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer? (5)
f: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, and these break down ozone molecules.
r: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 phased out the use of CFCs.

q: What is the antonym of the word liberty? (5)
f: Liberty means freedom, so its opposite is slavery or bondage.
r: Captivity and servitude are also antonyms of liberty.

q: In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are male. How many are female? (11)
f: Males = 2/3 of 30 = 20. Females = 30 - 20 = 10.
r: Females are 1/3 of the total, which is about 33.33 percent.

q: What is the name of the force that opposes the motion between two bodies in contact? (8)
f: Friction acts between touching surfaces and opposes their relative motion.
r: Friction produces heat.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, a Federal Minister must be a member of which body? (5)
f: Article 92 says Federal Ministers are appointed from the members of Majlis-e-Shoora, which means the National Assembly or the Senate.
r: Not more than one-fourth of the Federal Ministers can be taken from the Senate.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy War College located? (7)
f: The Pakistan Navy War College is in Lahore.
r: The Pakistan Navy headquarters is in Islamabad.

q: What is a synonym of oppression? (6)
f: Oppression means cruel and unjust use of power, which is the same as tyranny.
r: Persecution is another synonym of oppression.

q: In which constitutional amendment were Qadianis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan? (5)
f: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, declared Qadianis (Ahmadis) non-Muslims. It was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
r: The amendment added clause 3 to Article 260.

q: The product of two real numbers is always which kind of number? (6)
f: Real numbers are closed under multiplication, so multiplying two real numbers always gives a real number.
r: Real numbers are also closed under addition and subtraction.

q: Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929 were presented in reply to which report? (5)
f: The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates and other Muslim demands. Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.
r: The Fourteen Points also demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency.

q: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior is a renowned Pakistani player of which game? (5)
f: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior was a famous Pakistani hockey midfielder and captain. He was part of the team that won Olympic gold in 1984.
r: Pakistan has won the Olympic hockey gold medal three times.

q: In a class of 33 students, the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many girls are there? (6)
f: Let girls = g, then boys = g + 7. So g + g + 7 = 33, 2g = 26 and g = 13.
r: There are 20 boys in this class.

q: Who was the father of the Mughal emperor Humayun? (8)
f: Humayun was the second Mughal emperor and the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.
r: Humayun's son Akbar became the third Mughal emperor.

q: Which word is pronounced differently from the rest: white, wait, wrong? (5)
f: In wrong the w is silent and the word begins with the r sound. In white and wait the w is pronounced.
r: Other words with a silent w are write, wrist and wrap.

q: Which Muslim leader was given the title of knighthood (Sir) by the British in 1888? (4)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was awarded the title KCSI (Knight Commander of the Star of India) in 1888.
r: Allama Iqbal was knighted later, in 1923.

q: Who was the Speaker (President) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan from 1948, after Quaid-e-Azam? (4)
f: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan became President (Speaker) of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in 1948 and held the post until 1954.
r: In 1954 Tamizuddin Khan challenged the dissolution of the Assembly by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad in court.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan under the 1962 constitution in 1962? (4)
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President of Pakistan from 1958 to 1969, and he introduced the 1962 constitution.
r: Ayub Khan was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army.

q: What is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note? (5)
f: The State Bank of Pakistan describes the back of the Rs 5000 note as showing the Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.
r: The front of the note carries the portrait of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

q: What is the antonym of the word sympathetic? (5)
f: Sympathetic means feeling pity and care for others, so its opposite is callous or unfeeling.
r: Merciless and heartless are also opposites.

q: What was the date of birth of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan? (5)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born on 17 October 1817 in Delhi.
r: He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.

q: Which of these countries has a coastline on the Black Sea? (4)
f: The Black Sea is bordered by Turkey, Bulgaria, Romania, Ukraine, Russia and Georgia. Ukraine is the only one among the options.
r: The Black Sea connects to the Mediterranean through the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles.

q: In which language did Baba Bulleh Shah write his poetry? (6)
f: Bulleh Shah, the Sufi poet of Kasur, wrote mainly in Punjabi (kafis).
r: Bulleh Shah lived from about 1680 to 1757.

q: Which region of China borders Pakistan in the north? (4)
f: The Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China touches Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan.
r: The Karakoram Highway crosses the Khunjerab Pass to link Pakistan with Xinjiang.

q: In which city is Clifton Beach located? (4)
f: Clifton Beach, also called Sea View, is on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.
r: Karachi is the capital of Sindh province.

q: What is the process called in which a gas changes directly into a liquid? (6)
f: Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid, for example water vapour forming water drops.
r: Condensation is the opposite of evaporation.

q: What is the currency of Bhutan? (4)
f: Bhutan's currency is the ngultrum, which is pegged to the Indian rupee.
r: The Indian rupee is also accepted in Bhutan.

q: Which word is a synonym of efficiency? (4)
f: Efficiency means doing a job well with little waste, which is the same as competence.
r: Another close word is effectiveness.

q: In which year was the draft constitution of the European Union presented? (4)
f: The European Convention presented the draft Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe in 2003.
r: The treaty was signed in 2004 but was never enforced, because France and the Netherlands rejected it in 2005.

q: Change the voice: By whom is the child being fed? (4)
o: Who is being fed by the child?
f: The sentence is in the present continuous passive. The active form is "Who is feeding the child?", with the same tense.
r: For "by whom" questions in passive voice, the active form starts with "who".

q: Which river do Hindus in India regard as sacred? (4)
f: Hindus consider the Ganges (Ganga) the holiest river and bathe in it at places like Varanasi and Haridwar. It is worshipped as the goddess Ganga.
r: The Ganges flows from the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal.

q: Who is the current President of Iraq (as of October 2026)? (4)
f: Iraq's parliament elected Nizar Amidi (Amedi) as President on 11 April 2026.
r: His predecessor Abdul Latif Rashid held the office from October 2022 to 2026.

q: In which country are the Olympic Mountains located? (4)
f: The Olympic Mountains are in the state of Washington in the north-west United States.
r: They are on the Olympic Peninsula and contain Olympic National Park.

q: Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the War of Independence of 1857? (5)
f: Lord Canning was Governor-General from 1856 and became the first Viceroy of India in 1858.
r: Lord Dalhousie was his predecessor.

q: Gypsum is the main source of which two elements? (5)
f: Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate (CaSO4.2H2O), so it supplies calcium and sulfur.
r: Heated gypsum gives plaster of Paris.

q: Which is the correct spelling? (4)
f: The correct spelling is malevolence, from Latin male (ill) and volens (wishing).
r: Its adjective is malevolent.

q: A train moves at twice the speed of a car, and the car moves at 60 km/h. How far will the train go in 12 minutes? (4)
f: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 12 minutes (12/60 = 0.2 hour) it covers 120 x 0.2 = 24 km.
r: To change minutes to hours, divide by 60.

q: What was the Tashkent Pact (Declaration) of 1966? (7)
o: A peace agreement between Pakistan and India after the 1965 war
A trade treaty between Pakistan and China
A defence pact between Pakistan and the USA
A water treaty on the Indus rivers
f: It was a peace agreement signed on 10 January 1966 in which both sides agreed to withdraw to pre-war positions.
r: The Soviet Union mediated the agreement.

q: Who signed the Tashkent Declaration on behalf of India? (4)
f: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it and died in Tashkent the next day.
r: Ayub Khan signed it for Pakistan.

q: If 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to type 1 page? (18)
f: 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man types 1 page in 5 minutes.
r: Work equals number of workers multiplied by time, divided by the number of pages.

q: Peshawar has traditionally been known as the city of what? (4)
f: Peshawar was traditionally called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.
r: Peshawar is also called the City of Grain and is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan were Islamic provisions first included? (5)
f: The 1956 Constitution was the first constitution of Pakistan and made the country an Islamic Republic. It included Islamic provisions.
r: The Objectives Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble.

q: Which team won the PSL trophy two times in a row? (4)
f: Lahore Qalandars won PSL 7 in 2022 and PSL 8 in 2023, back to back. No other team has won consecutive titles.
r: Lahore Qalandars also won in 2025, and Peshawar Zalmi won PSL 11 in 2026.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam go into self-imposed exile in London? (4)
f: After the Round Table Conferences, Jinnah was disappointed with Indian politics and settled in London around 1930. He returned in 1934.
r: Some sources say 1931; most Pakistani textbooks give 1930.

q: In which game is a free throw used? (10)
f: A free throw is an unopposed shot at the basket given to a player after a foul in basketball. It is worth one point.
r: A basket scored from inside the three-point line in open play is worth two points.

q: What is the height of the Eiffel Tower in Paris, including antennas, in metres? (4)
f: The Eiffel Tower is about 330 metres tall including its antenna, which is about 1,083 feet.
r: Sources differ slightly: the older figure of 324 m was used before antenna changes.

q: Who is generally regarded as the first poet of the Urdu language? (5)
f: Amir Khusrow (1253-1325) is commonly taught as the first poet who used early Urdu (Hindavi) in verse.
r: Sources differ, and some name Wali Deccani as the first major Urdu poet.

q: On what date was the Wavell Plan announced? (4)
f: Lord Wavell broadcast his plan on 14 June 1945. The Simla Conference to discuss it started on 25 June 1945.
r: The Simla Conference ended without agreement in July 1945.

q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya located? (7)
f: The shrine of the Sufi saint Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya is in Multan.
r: Multan is known as the City of Saints.

q: What is 65% of 100? (5)
r: Percent of 100 is always the same number as the percent itself.

q: Which battle was fought in 1757 between Nawab Siraj ud Daula and the British East India Company? (3)
f: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 in Bengal, where Robert Clive defeated Siraj ud Daula.
r: Mir Jafar's betrayal helped the British win Plassey, and the Battle of Buxar followed in 1764.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the December 1971 war? (3)
f: Nurul Amin was appointed Prime Minister on 7 December 1971 and held office during the war, which ended on 16 December.
r: He later served as Vice President of Pakistan under Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Who was the fifth Mughal emperor of India? (3)
f: The order was Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, then Shah Jahan. So Shah Jahan was fifth.
r: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal, and Aurangzeb was the sixth emperor.

q: What is the square root of 900? (3)
f: 30 x 30 = 900, so the square root of 900 is 30.
r: The square root of 9 is 3 and of 100 is 10, so 3 x 10 = 30.

q: What is the absolute value of a number? (3)
o: Its distance from zero, always non-negative
f: The absolute value is the distance of a number from zero on the number line, so it ignores the sign. For example |-5| = 5 and |5| = 5.
r: The absolute value of zero is zero.

q: What is the value of absolute zero on the Celsius scale? (3)
f: Absolute zero is 0 Kelvin, which equals -273.15 degrees Celsius. It is the lowest possible temperature.
r: On the Fahrenheit scale it is about -459.67 degrees.

q: Who founded Aligarh College (MAO College)? (3)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh.
r: He also founded the Scientific Society in 1864.

q: Which organization runs the world's largest volunteer ambulance service, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi? (3)
f: The Edhi Foundation, founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi in Pakistan, is recognised by Guinness World Records as having the largest volunteer ambulance service.
r: Abdul Sattar Edhi was known as the Angel of Mercy and died in 2016.

q: What is the antonym of the word mighty? (3)
f: Mighty means very strong, so its opposite is weak.
r: Feeble is another opposite of mighty.

q: What is the antonym of the word opaque? (3)
f: Opaque means that light cannot pass through, so its opposite is transparent.
r: Glass is transparent, while wood is opaque.

q: Choose the correct word: We are going to the beach ___ car. (3)
f: With a means of transport used without an article, the correct preposition is by: by car.
r: We say by bus, by train and by air in the same way.

q: Was the Constitution of Pakistan of 1956 bicameral or unicameral? (3)
o: Bicameral with a National Assembly and a Senate
Unicameral with a single National Assembly
f: The 1956 Constitution created a single house, the National Assembly. The 1962 Constitution was also unicameral.
r: The 1973 Constitution introduced the bicameral Parliament of National Assembly and Senate.

q: What is the binding force (unifying factor) of the people of Pakistan? (3)
f: Pakistan was created on the basis of the Two-Nation Theory, and the common religion Islam binds its diverse peoples together.
r: Pakistan has many languages and ethnic groups, such as Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto, Balochi and Urdu speakers.

q: What are the approximate length and breadth of Pakistan? (3)
f: Pakistan stretches about 1,600 km from north to south and about 885 km from east to west at its widest.
r: Figures differ slightly between sources; these are the common textbook values.

q: Ali buys a book for 40 rupees and sells it for 50 rupees. What is his profit percentage? (3)
f: Profit = 50 minus 40 = 10 rupees. Profit percent = 10/40 x 100 = 25%.
r: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price.

q: In which years were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of the world wars? (6)
f: The 1916 Games were cancelled due to World War 1, and the 1940 and 1944 Games due to World War 2.
r: The Games were not held at all in these years, but they still count in the numbering of the Olympiads.

q: Hazara is the name of an ethnic group mainly found in which country? (3)
f: The Hazara are a Persian-speaking ethnic group living mostly in central Afghanistan (Hazarajat).
r: A large Hazara community also lives in Quetta, Balochistan.

q: In which district of Punjab is the main part of the Kala Chitta Range located? (3)
f: The Kala Chitta Range is a low mountain range in northern Punjab, mainly in Attock district and partly in Rawalpindi district.
r: The range lies south of the Margalla Hills and north of the Soan River region.

q: On which two Japanese cities did the USA drop atomic bombs in August 1945? (3)
f: The USA dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and another on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
r: Japan announced its surrender soon after, ending World War 2.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word tenure? (3)
f: Tenure means the period or term during which a person holds an office or position.
r: For example, a President serves a tenure of five years in Pakistan.

q: Which letter completes the series: L, _, N, O? (3)
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, and M comes between L and N.
r: The alphabet has 26 letters from A to Z.

q: What does the Parliament of Pakistan consist of? (3)
f: Under Article 50 of the 1973 Constitution, Parliament consists of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: The National Assembly is the lower house and the Senate is the upper house.

q: What is the value of sin 0 degrees multiplied by cos 90 degrees? (3)
f: sin 0 = 0 and cos 90 = 0, so the product is 0 x 0 = 0.
r: Even if one of the two values were nonzero, the product would still be 0 because sin 0 is 0.

q: Which constitution is currently in force in Pakistan? (3)
f: The Constitution of 1973 is the current constitution of Pakistan.
r: It was enforced on 14 August 1973 and has 280 articles.

q: Who is the current Director General of ISI (Pakistan)? (3)
f: Lt Gen Muhammad Asim Malik has been DG ISI since September 2024.
r: He also serves as National Security Adviser; his predecessor was Nadeem Anjum.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Pakistan? (3)
f: Shehbaz Sharif has been Prime Minister since March 2024.
r: Anwaar ul Haq Kakar was caretaker PM from August 2023 to March 2024.

q: Which is the lowest point on land in Asia, about 430 metres below sea level? (3)
f: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land elevation on Earth, about 430 metres below sea level. It lies between Jordan and Israel or the West Bank.
r: Death Valley is the lowest point in North America, not Asia.

q: What type of democracy does Pakistan have under the 1973 Constitution? (3)
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a federal parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.
r: The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.

q: What is the derivative of 9 with respect to x? (3)
f: 9 is a constant and the derivative of any constant is zero.
r: The derivative of x is 1.

q: What is the Tour de France? (3)
f: The Tour de France is an annual multi-stage men's bicycle race held mainly in France. It usually lasts about three weeks in July.
r: The winner wears the famous yellow jersey.

q: In which continent is the Cape of Good Hope located? (3)
f: The Cape of Good Hope is a rocky headland on the Atlantic coast of South Africa.
r: Vasco da Gama rounded it in 1497 on the sea route to India.

q: Choose the correct word: He was good ___ math. (3)
f: The correct preposition after the adjective good, when talking about a skill or subject, is at.
r: We also say bad at, clever at and expert at.

q: Who proposed the heliocentric (sun-centred) model of the solar system? (14)
f: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun is at the centre and the planets move around it. Ptolemy and Aristotle supported an Earth-centred model.
r: Galileo later supported the Copernican model using telescope observations.

q: What is the approximate range of Pakistan's short-range ballistic missile Hatf-I? (3)
f: Hatf-I is Pakistan's first short-range, solid-fuel missile with a range of about 70 km, later improved to about 100 km in the Hatf-IA version.
r: Sources give slightly different figures for Hatf-I, between 70 and 100 km.

q: Justice Musarrat Hilali took oath in 2023 as the first woman Chief Justice of which high court? (3)
f: Justice Musarrat Hilali took oath as the first woman Chief Justice of the Peshawar High Court on 1 April 2023, in an acting capacity as per some reports. She later became a Supreme Court judge.
r: Justice Tahira Safdar of the Balochistan High Court was the first woman chief justice of any high court in Pakistan (2018).

q: What is iota (i) in mathematics? (3)
f: Iota is the imaginary unit and is defined as i = square root of -1, so i squared = -1.
r: Numbers of the form a + ib are called complex numbers.

q: Choose the correct word: There is ____ water in a jar. (3)
f: Water is uncountable, so it takes 'a lot of'. 'Many', 'several' and 'few' are used only with countable nouns.
r: 'Much' and 'a little' are also used with uncountable nouns.

q: In which city was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged? (3)
f: Bhutto was hanged in Rawalpindi Central Jail, and he was buried at Garhi Khuda Bakhsh near Larkana.
r: He was executed on 4 April 1979.

q: What is the LCM of 3 and 8? (3)
f: 3 and 8 have no common factor, so LCM = 3 x 8 = 24.
r: For two numbers, LCM x HCF equals their product.

q: Which is the largest lake of North America by area? (3)
f: Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes and the largest freshwater lake in North America by surface area.
r: Lake Michigan is the largest Great Lake lying wholly inside the USA.

q: If the sentence is completed in reported speech, which word fills the blank? Ali said that he ___ to London last year. (3)
f: The event happened last year, so the simple past form went is correct.
r: A time word like last year needs a past tense verb.

q: What is the smallest unit of life? (3)
f: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things.
r: Robert Hooke first observed and named cells in 1665.

q: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan served as President (Speaker) of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly from 1948 until which year? (3)
f: He held the office from 1948 until the Assembly was dissolved by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad in 1954.
r: His case, Federation of Pakistan v. Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan, is a famous constitutional case.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Hadith'? (3)
o: A saying or tradition of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
f: Hadith means a report, saying or tradition. In Islam it is the record of the sayings, actions and approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: The Sunnah and Hadith are the second main source of Islamic law after the Quran.

q: What is the meaning of the word obscure? (3)
f: Obscure means hard to understand or see, or not well known.
r: Its antonym is clear or obvious.

q: Which number is different from the others: 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 17, 19? (3)
f: All the numbers except 12 are prime numbers. 12 is divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6.
r: 2 is the only even prime number.

q: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences, Physics and Chemistry? (3)
f: Marie Curie won the Physics prize in 1903 (shared) and the Chemistry prize in 1911. She is the only person to win in two different sciences besides Linus Pauling, who won Chemistry and Peace.
r: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

q: Who wrote the folk romance Sassi Punnu in verse? (3)
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai told the tale of Sassui Punhun in his Shah Jo Risalo.
r: It is one of the seven tragic romances of Sindh.

q: In which city is Shalimar Bagh (Shalimar Gardens) located? (5)
f: The Shalimar Gardens are in Lahore, Pakistan. They were built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan around 1641.
r: The Shalimar Gardens and Lahore Fort are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: What is sin(270 degrees minus theta) equal to? (3)
f: Sine of 270 minus theta lies in the third quadrant where sine is negative, and the function changes to cosine at 270. So the result is minus cos theta.
r: Sin(90 minus theta) is equal to plus cos theta.

q: What is the currency of Spain? (3)
f: Spain uses the Euro, which replaced the peseta in 2002.
r: The Euro is used by 20 or more European Union countries known as the Eurozone.

q: Who was the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan at the time of the 1956 Constitution? (3)
f: Abdul Wahab Khan was the Speaker from 1955 and was in office when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
r: Tamizuddin Khan was the earlier President of the Constituent Assembly; sources differ on the numbering of the Speakers.

q: Which city of Pakistan is world famous for sports goods? (3)
f: Sialkot is the centre of Pakistan's sports goods industry, especially footballs.
r: Sialkot made the footballs used in several FIFA World Cups.

q: When did World War 1 start? (7)
f: World War 1 began in July 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
r: It ended in November 1918.

q: Which part of Asia is called the subcontinent? (3)
f: The subcontinent means South Asia, the region of Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and nearby countries.
r: It is called a subcontinent because it is separated from the rest of Asia by the Himalayas.

q: Which symbol denotes the union of two sets? (4)
f: The symbol ∪ means union, the set of all elements that are in A or in B or in both.
r: The symbol ∩ means intersection.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'console'? (4)
f: To console means to give comfort to someone who is sad.
r: The noun is consolation.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'consumer'? (3)
f: A consumer is a person who buys and uses goods or services, like a customer.
r: The opposite of consumer in economics is producer.

q: When did the Gandhi-Jinnah talks take place in Bombay? (3)
f: Gandhi met Quaid-e-Azam Jinnah at his house in Bombay from 9 to 27 September 1944. The talks failed because they did not agree on the Pakistan demand.
r: Gandhi's proposal was based on the Rajagopalachari formula.

q: What is Pakistan's top export product group? (3)
f: Textiles and clothing make up more than half of Pakistan's total exports.
r: Rice is Pakistan's biggest food export.

q: Ernest Hemingway was a writer of which country? (3)
f: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist who wrote The Old Man and the Sea.
r: He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.

q: Which word is the opposite of zeal? (3)
f: Zeal means strong enthusiasm, while apathy means lack of interest.
r: Apathy and indifference are common antonyms of enthusiasm.

f: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 12 + 1 = 13.
r: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

q: What is 2/3 + 3? (3)
r: 11/3 is an improper fraction equal to about 3.67.

q: What is 4 + 4/4? (3)
f: Division first: 4/4 = 1. Then 4 + 1 = 5.
r: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

q: The speed of a train is twice that of a car. If the car travels 100 km in one hour, how far does the train travel in 30 minutes? (2)
f: Train speed is 2 x 100 = 200 km/h. In half an hour it covers 200 / 2 = 100 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: Which number is different: 104, 106, 108, 110, 103? (2)
f: 104, 106, 108 and 110 are all even numbers, while 103 is odd.
r: An even number is divisible by 2 with no remainder.

q: If the 2nd of a month is Monday, what day is the 16th of that month? (2)
f: 16 - 2 = 14 days, which is exactly two weeks, so the day is the same: Monday.
r: Dates 7 apart always fall on the same weekday.

q: If a car covers 200 km in one hour, how many km will it cover in one minute? (2)
f: One hour has 60 minutes, so distance in one minute is 200 divided by 60 = 3.33 km (10/3 km).
r: Speed is distance divided by time.

q: Who was the Chief Justice of Pakistan in 2018? (2)
f: Mian Saqib Nisar was Chief Justice of Pakistan from December 2016 until January 2019, which covers all of 2018.
r: Asif Saeed Khosa succeeded him in January 2019.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th of that month be? (2)
f: From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days later. 15 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) forward from Sunday to reach Monday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 22nd of that month be? (2)
f: From the 4th to the 22nd is 18 days later. 18 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Thursday, what day will the 25th of that month be? (2)
f: From the 3rd to the 25th is 22 days later. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) forward from Thursday to reach Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 27th of that month be? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 27th is 25 days later. 25 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: In a class of 1000 students, 850 are present. What is the percentage of absentees? (2)
r: Present students are 85% of the class.

q: What is the cube of 900? (2)
r: The square of 900 is 810,000.

q: In which year were the Geneva Accords on Afghanistan signed, leading to the Soviet troop withdrawal? (4)
f: The Geneva Accords were signed on 14 April 1988 by Pakistan, Afghanistan, the USA and the USSR.
r: Soviet forces completed their withdrawal from Afghanistan in February 1989.

q: Which word is a synonym of accuse? (2)
f: To accuse is to charge someone with a fault or crime, which means to blame.
r: A related noun is accusation.

q: Aliza is 12 years older than Asad. When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 times his age. How old will Aliza be when Asad is 14? (2)
f: When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 x 6 = 18, so the gap is 18 - 6 = 12 years, which never changes. When Asad is 14, Aliza is 14 + 12 = 26.
r: The age gap between two people stays the same all their lives.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'ally'? (2)
f: An ally is a friend or partner who supports you, so 'partner' is the closest meaning.
r: The antonym of ally is enemy or opponent.

q: In which year were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan? (4)
f: The Second Amendment of 1974 declared Ahmadis non-Muslim.
r: Ordinance XX of 1984 added further restrictions.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim? (2)
f: The change came through the Second Amendment of 1974 to the 1973 Constitution.
r: The 1973 Constitution is the third constitution of Pakistan.

q: What is the antonym of the word broadly? (2)
f: Broadly means in a wide way, so its opposite is narrowly.
r: Broad and narrow are common opposites.

q: What is the antonym of the word industrious? (4)
f: Industrious means hardworking, so its opposite is lazy.
r: Diligent is a synonym of industrious.

q: What is the antonym of the word relinquish? (2)
f: Relinquish means to give up, so its opposite is retain or keep.
r: Surrender and abandon are synonyms of relinquish.

q: At what age did Arfa Karim become the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional in the world? (2)
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa passed the Microsoft Certified Professional exam in 2004 at the age of 9. This made her the youngest MCP in the world at that time.
r: She died in January 2012 and the Arfa Karim Software Technology Park in Lahore is named after her.

q: What is the currency of Argentina? (4)
f: Argentina uses the Argentine peso as its official currency. The real belongs to Brazil and the bolivar to Venezuela.
r: Argentina has faced very high inflation in recent years, which has weakened the peso.

q: Who is known as Baba-e-Sahafat (Father of Journalism) in Pakistan? (2)
f: Maulana Zafar Ali Khan, editor of the daily Zamindar, is most commonly given this title in Pakistani textbooks.
r: Sources differ, as some also use this title for other pioneer journalists.

q: Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) wrote his famous book Kashf-ul-Mahjoob in which language? (2)
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, a classic work on Sufism, was written in Persian.
r: Data Ganj Bakhsh is buried in Lahore.

q: What is the meaning of the idiom 'beat about the bush'? (2)
o: To avoid coming to the main point
f: The idiom means talking around a subject without addressing it directly.
r: The opposite idea is to get straight to the point.

q: What is the last letter of the word BEAUTY? (20)
f: B-E-A-U-T-Y ends with the letter Y.
r: BEAUTY has six letters.

q: Which event caused the United States to enter the Second World War, and which country attacked it? (2)
o: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941
f: On 7 December 1941 Japan launched a surprise air attack on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. The next day the United States declared war on Japan.
r: Germany and Italy then declared war on the United States a few days later.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali becomes 10? (2)
f: Sister's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. Ali gains 7 years (10 - 3), so the sister also gains 7 years: 12 + 7 = 19.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali becomes 8? (2)
f: Sister's age now is 5 x 3 = 15. Ali gains 3 years (8 - 5), so she is 15 + 3 = 18.
r: Both people grow older by the same number of years.

q: Fill in the blank: I ___ to Lahore in August. (2)
f: The sentence refers to a finished past time (August), so the simple past tense went is correct.
r: Go is irregular: go, went, gone.

q: Fill in the blank: She was afraid ___ dogs. (2)
f: The adjective afraid is followed by the preposition of.
r: Other common pairs are fond of, proud of and scared of.

q: How many times has Brazil won the FIFA World Cup? (2)
f: Brazil won the World Cup in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002, which makes 5 titles. It did not win in 2026.
r: Spain won the 2026 World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 in the final.

q: What is the capital of Kuwait? (2)
f: Kuwait City is the capital.
r: Kuwait City is the capital of Kuwait.

q: What is the characteristic of the common logarithm of 99? (2)
f: 99 lies between 10 and 100, so log 99 is between 1 and 2 (about 1.9956). The whole number part, the characteristic, is 1.
r: The decimal part of a logarithm is called the mantissa.

q: Grass is to ground as chimney is to what? (2)
f: Grass grows on the ground, in the same way a chimney stands on top of the roof of a house.
r: A chimney carries smoke from a fireplace or furnace out of the building.

q: Florida is a what? (2)
f: Florida is a state in the south-eastern United States.
r: Tallahassee is the capital of Florida.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission (PAEC)? (2)
f: The PAEC, Pakistan's main nuclear agency, has its headquarters in Islamabad.
r: The PAEC was set up in 1956 and Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan's KRL is based at Kahuta.

q: Complete the series: 1, 3, 7, 13, ? (2)
f: The differences are 2, 4, 6, so the next difference is 8. Then 13 + 8 = 21.
r: The differences in this series form an even number sequence.

q: The Torkham border crossing connects Pakistan with which country? (2)
f: Torkham is at the western end of the Khyber Pass and joins Pakistan's Khyber district with Nangarhar in Afghanistan.
r: It is the busiest crossing between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: A book is bought for 30 and sold for 40. What is the percentage profit? (11)
f: Profit = 40 - 30 = 10. Profit percent = 10 / 30 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
r: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price unless stated otherwise.

q: Balochistan covers roughly what percentage of the total area of Pakistan? (3)
f: Balochistan has about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km, which is about 44 percent.
r: Balochistan is the largest province by area but the smallest by population.

q: What is the most frequently occurring value in a set of data called? (2)
f: The mode is the value that is repeated the most times in the data.
r: Mean is the average and median is the middle value of ordered data.

q: Which team won two consecutive Pakistan Super League titles? (2)
f: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and again in 2023.
r: They also won in 2025; Peshawar Zalmi won the 2026 edition.

q: What is the national currency of Pakistan? (2)
f: Pakistan's currency is the Pakistani rupee, issued by the State Bank of Pakistan.
r: Its code is PKR.

q: What is the sum of the number of days in March and December? (2)
f: March has 31 days and December has 31 days. So 31 + 31 = 62.
r: The months with 31 days are January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

q: In which year was the Simla (Shimla) Deputation held? (2)
f: A Muslim delegation led by Sir Aga Khan met Viceroy Lord Minto at Simla on 1 October 1906. This led to the founding of the Muslim League in December 1906.
r: The deputation demanded separate electorates for Muslims.

q: After how many years of Pakistan's creation did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh? (2)
f: Pakistan came into being in 1947 and East Pakistan separated in December 1971, which is 24 years later.
r: Bangladesh became independent on 16 December 1971.

q: Which element in haemoglobin is necessary for carrying oxygen in the blood? (3)
f: Haemoglobin contains iron, and the iron binds oxygen in the red blood cells. Lack of iron causes anaemia.
r: Haemoglobin is the red pigment in red blood cells.

q: Which Egyptian footballer is famous as Mo Salah? (3)
f: Mohamed Salah is the well known Egyptian forward who plays for Liverpool and is nicknamed the Egyptian King.
r: Salah has won the Premier League Golden Boot several times.

q: Which word is a synonym of envious? (2)
f: Envious means feeling resentment about another person's success or belongings, which is the same as jealous.
r: The noun form of envious is envy.

q: At which port city did the British first set up a trading base in India? (2)
f: The British East India Company set up its first factory at Surat in Gujarat in 1613.
r: Captain William Hawkins reached Surat in 1608 to seek trading rights from Emperor Jahangir.

q: How many faces does a hexagonal prism have? (2)
f: A hexagonal prism has 6 rectangular side faces and 2 hexagonal faces (top and bottom), so 6 + 2 = 8.
r: A hexagonal prism has 12 vertices and 18 edges.

q: For what is Al-Razi (Rhazes) famous? (2)
f: Al-Razi was a great Muslim physician and chemist, who described measles and smallpox in his medical works.
r: His famous medical encyclopedia is Kitab al-Hawi.

q: Which team was the runner-up in the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar? (2)
f: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the 2022 final, so France was the runner-up.
r: Croatia finished third in 2022 after beating Morocco.

q: Against which power did Tipu Sultan of Mysore fight his main wars? (2)
f: Tipu Sultan fought the Anglo-Mysore wars against the British East India Company and was martyred defending Seringapatam in 1799.
r: He is known as the Tiger of Mysore.

q: A jet uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly at 320 km per hour (80 gallons per 320 km). How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km? (2)
f: Fuel per km = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 km: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
r: Fuel needed is directly proportional to distance when the rate of use stays the same.

q: Which form of government was provided by the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan? (2)
f: The 1956 Constitution made Pakistan an Islamic Republic with a federal, parliamentary system and a single-house legislature.
r: The 1962 Constitution that followed was presidential.

q: Where was the United Nations founded in 1945? (2)
f: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 at the conference that created the organization.
r: The UN headquarters are in New York, and the UN officially came into existence on 24 October 1945.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Mediterranean Sea with which water body? (2)
f: The Strait of Gibraltar is a narrow channel between Spain and Morocco that joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean.
r: The strait is only about 13 km wide at its narrowest point.

q: A person walks 6 km towards the north, then turns right and walks some distance, then turns right again. Which direction is he now heading? (2)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Another right turn from east makes him face south.
r: Two right turns in a row always reverse the original direction.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination of Pakistan (health minister) as of 2026? (2)
f: Syed Mustafa Kamal of the MQM-P holds the federal health portfolio in the government formed after the February 2024 elections.
r: Dr Nadeem Jan was the caretaker federal health minister in 2023 to 2024.

q: Ahmed is 5 years old and his sister is four times his age. When Ahmed is 12 years old, what is his sister's age? (2)
f: Sister is 4 x 5 = 20 years now, so the gap is 15 years. When Ahmed is 12, sister is 12 + 15 = 27 years.
r: After 7 years both ages rise by 7 (20 + 7 = 27).

q: What is the highest peak of the Himalayas? (3)
f: Mount Everest, on the Nepal-China border, is the highest peak of the Himalayas and of the world. Its official height is about 8849 m.
r: Everest is called Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet.

q: In which battle were the most Huffaz (memorisers) of the Quran martyred? (2)
f: Many Huffaz were martyred at Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailma. This led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran in one book.
r: Reports of the number martyred in this battle vary by source (commonly about 70 Huffaz).

q: What is the capital of Hungary? (5)
f: Budapest is the capital and largest city of Hungary. It lies on the River Danube.
r: Budapest was formed in 1873 by joining Buda, Pest and Obuda.

q: Who were the four Rightly Guided Caliphs (Khulafa-e-Rashideen) of Islam, in order? (2)
f: After the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the caliphs were Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Uthman and Hazrat Ali (RA) in that order.
r: Their combined rule lasted about 30 years, from 632 AD to 661 AD.

q: In which year did the USA and its allies invade Iraq? (4)
f: The US-led invasion of Iraq began in 2003 to remove the government of Saddam Hussein.
r: The 1991 Gulf War was a different conflict, fought after Iraq invaded Kuwait.

q: Where is the historic Jamrud Fort located? (2)
o: Peshawar, at the entrance of the Khyber Pass
f: Jamrud Fort stands near Peshawar at the eastern mouth of the Khyber Pass in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It was built in 1836 by the Sikh general Hari Singh Nalwa.
r: Hari Singh Nalwa was killed in a battle at Jamrud in 1837.

q: What is the capital of Japan? (4)
f: Tokyo is the capital and largest city of Japan.
r: Kyoto was the old imperial capital of Japan until 1868.

q: Who wrote the book Asrar-e-Khudi (Secrets of the Self)? (2)
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Asrar-e-Khudi in Persian, and it was published in 1915.
r: Its companion work is Rumuz-e-Bekhudi (1918).

q: Approximately how many people died in World War II (soldiers and civilians together)? (2)
f: Most estimates put the total deaths of World War II, including civilians, at roughly 70 to 85 million.
r: It was the deadliest conflict in human history.

q: The Kohat Tunnel connects Kohat with which city? (2)
f: The Kohat Tunnel links Kohat with Peshawar through the Kohat Pass road, which makes the journey shorter.
r: It was opened in 2003 and is about 1.9 km long.

q: Which landlocked country can use Pakistan's seaports (Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar) for its sea trade? (3)
f: Afghanistan has no coastline, so it uses Pakistan's ports under the Afghan Transit Trade arrangement. Central Asian states are also linked to these ports by road routes.
r: Iran has its own coast, and Nepal and Bhutan are not connected to Pakistan.

q: Which language is mainly spoken in Chitral? (2)
f: Khowar (also called Chitrali) is the main local language of Chitral district.
r: Khowar is the lingua franca of Chitral and is also spoken in parts of Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: At which Inn of Court in London did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah study law and qualify as a barrister? (2)
f: Jinnah joined Lincoln's Inn in 1893 and was called to the bar in 1896, at the age of 19.
r: He was the youngest Indian to be called to the bar at that time.

q: What type of legislature did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan provide? (2)
f: The 1956 Constitution created a single-house (unicameral) National Assembly of 300 members.
r: A bicameral legislature came with the 1973 Constitution (National Assembly and Senate).

q: What is the date of birth of Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was born on 1 October 1895 in Karnal, in present-day Haryana, India.
r: He was assassinated on 16 October 1951 in Rawalpindi.

q: What is a synonym of the word liberty? (2)
f: Liberty means the state of being free, so its synonym is freedom.
r: The opposite words are bondage, slavery and captivity.

q: Where is the Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque, one of the oldest mosques in Pakistan, located? (3)
f: The Mahmud Ghaznavi Mosque stands at Odigram (Udegram) in Swat District, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It dates from the Ghaznavid period, around 1048-49 AD.
r: It is often described as the oldest mosque in northern Pakistan, near Raja Gira Castle.

q: In which year was the Nishan-e-Haider awarded to Major Aziz Bhatti? (2)
f: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred in the 1965 war near the BRB canal at Lahore and was honoured with the Nishan-e-Haider for it that year.
r: He is one of the recipients of Pakistan's highest military award for gallantry.

q: Who was the first Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan in 1958? (2)
f: Martial law was imposed on 7 October 1958 by President Iskander Mirza, who made General Ayub Khan the Chief Martial Law Administrator.
r: Ayub Khan became Pakistan's first Field Marshal in 1959.

q: What is the geometric mean of 4 and 16? (2)
f: GM = square root of (4 x 16) = square root of 64 = 8.
r: For positive numbers, GM is never greater than the arithmetic mean.

q: How many member countries does SAARC have? (2)
f: SAARC has eight members: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
r: Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

q: What is the mode of the numbers 3, 3, 4, 5, 6? (3)
f: The mode is the value that appears most often. The number 3 appears twice and all others appear once.
r: The median of this set is 4.

q: To which age do the people of the Indus Valley Civilization belong? (4)
f: The Indus Valley people used copper and bronze tools, so the civilization belongs to the Bronze Age.
r: The civilization is also called the Harappan Civilization.

q: For what were the people of Mohenjo-daro and Harappa famous? (2)
o: Well-planned cities with a drainage system
f: Their cities had straight streets, brick houses and covered drains. This shows advanced town planning.
r: The Great Bath is a famous building of Mohenjo-daro.

q: If the first day of a month is Monday, what day will the 21st day be? (2)
f: The 21st is 20 days after the 1st. 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, and Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.

q: Suo motu notice by the Supreme Court of Pakistan is taken under which article of the Constitution? (2)
f: Article 184(3) gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction on matters of public importance involving fundamental rights.
r: Suo motu is a Latin term meaning on its own motion.

q: On which date was NATO founded? (2)
f: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington on 4 April 1949.
r: The Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955 as the Soviet response to NATO.

q: In 1999 General Pervez Musharraf replaced Nawaz Sharif and became what? (2)
f: After the coup of 12 October 1999 Musharraf took the title Chief Executive.
r: He became President in June 2001.

q: Which was the first battle of the Muslims against a non-Arab power? (3)
f: The Battle of Muta in 8 AH (629 CE) was fought against the Byzantine (Roman) army, a non-Arab power.
r: Zaid bin Haritha was the first commander of the Muslim army at Muta.

q: Which word is a synonym of obvious? (2)
f: Obvious means easy to see or understand, which is the same as evident.
r: Other synonyms are clear, plain and apparent.

q: In which year did the Third Battle of Panipat take place? (2)
f: The Third Battle of Panipat was fought in 1761 between the Marathas and the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali.
r: Ahmad Shah Abdali won the battle, which ended Maratha power in North India.

q: About what percent of the total area of Pakistan is covered by Balochistan? (2)
f: Balochistan has about 347,190 square km out of about 796,095 square km, which is about 43.6 percent.
r: Balochistan is the largest province by area but the smallest by population share.

q: What is the value of 3P2 (permutation of 3 things taken 2 at a time)? (2)
r: Permutations count ordered arrangements, so order matters.

q: In which type of cricket match is the pink ball used? (2)
o: Only one-day matches played in the morning
f: The pink ball is easier to see under floodlights, so it is used in day-night Test matches.
r: The first day-night Test was played in Adelaide in 2015 between Australia and New Zealand.

q: On which date was the first cricket World Cup played (started)? (3)
f: The first Cricket World Cup, the Prudential Cup, began on 7 June 1975 in England.
r: West Indies won the first World Cup, beating Australia in the final at Lord's.

q: What is the capital of Poland? (2)
f: Warsaw is the capital and largest city of Poland. It lies on the Vistula river.
r: Krakow was the capital of Poland until the late 16th century.

q: Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note? (2)
f: The State Bank of Pakistan states that the reverse of the Rs 5000 note carries a picture of Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.
r: The portrait of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is on the front of all Pakistani banknotes.

q: Under which article of the 1973 Constitution is the definition of a Muslim and non-Muslim given, as added by the Second Amendment? (2)
f: The Second Amendment added clause 3 to Article 260 and defined who is a Muslim. Qadianis were thus declared non-Muslim.
r: Article 2 declares Islam the State religion.

q: In which year was the Radcliffe Award announced? (2)
f: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission award was announced on 17 August 1947, after independence. It fixed the Punjab and Bengal boundaries.
r: Sir Cyril Radcliffe headed the commission.

q: Who received the first Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded in 1901? (2)
f: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901, and the Physics prize went to Wilhelm Rontgen for discovering X-rays.
r: Marie Curie won the Physics prize in 1903 and was the first woman Nobel winner.

q: In which province is the Rekodiq mining project (copper and gold) located? (2)
f: Rekodiq is a copper-gold deposit in Chagai district of Balochistan.
r: Saindak and Reko Diq are both in Chagai district.

q: For what work did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize? (2)
o: Unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak unification theory.
r: He was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate.

q: Which phrase does the Quran use for the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as a mercy for all? (2)
f: Surah Al-Anbiya says the Prophet was sent as Rahmatul lil Alamin, a mercy for all the worlds.
r: Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.

q: What is the gap in years between the first (1956) and second (1962) constitution of Pakistan? (2)
f: The first constitution came into force in March 1956 and the second in June 1962. 1962 minus 1956 is 6 years.
r: The 1973 Constitution is the third and current constitution of Pakistan.

q: Which letter is used to denote the set of rational numbers? (4)
f: Rational numbers are written as quotients (fractions) of integers, so the set is denoted by Q.
r: N is natural numbers, Z is integers and R is real numbers.

q: What is the domain of the function sin x? (2)
f: Sine is defined for every real value of x. Its range, not its domain, is from minus 1 to 1.
r: The period of sin x is 360 degrees (2 pi).

q: What is the determinant of a singular matrix? (2)
f: A square matrix is called singular exactly when its determinant is zero. Such a matrix has no inverse.
r: A matrix with non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.

q: If the sum of two angles of a triangle is 90 degrees, what is the third angle? (2)
f: The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. So the third angle is 180 - 90 = 90 degrees.
r: A triangle with one 90 degree angle is called a right-angled triangle.

q: Ship is to captain as car is to what? (2)
f: A captain is the person who controls a ship. In the same way a driver controls a car.
r: A pilot controls an aircraft.

q: How many countries are there in South Asia (the SAARC region)? (2)
f: South Asia has eight countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
r: Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member.

q: Spain is located in which continent? (3)
f: Spain lies in the south-west of Europe on the Iberian Peninsula.
r: Spain and Portugal share the Iberian Peninsula.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'strength'? (2)
f: Strength means the quality of being strong, which is the same as power or force.
r: The opposite (antonym) of strength is weakness.

q: What is the sum of 2 and 8? (2)
r: Addition is commutative, so 2 + 8 gives the same answer as 8 + 2.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'momentary'? (2)
f: Momentary means lasting only a very short time, which is the same as brief.
r: The opposite (antonym) of momentary is permanent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'fragile'? (3)
f: Fragile means easily broken, which is the same as delicate.
r: Glass is a common example of a fragile material.

q: In which district and province is the Tanda Dam located? (7)
f: Tanda Dam is a small dam built near Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It supplies drinking and irrigation water.
r: Kohat is also known for its tunnel, the Kohat Pass and its cantonment.

q: In which district of Punjab is Tandlianwala located? (2)
f: Tandlianwala is a city and tehsil in Faisalabad district of Punjab.
r: Faisalabad was earlier named Lyallpur.

q: Tarbela Dam construction began in 1968 during whose rule? (2)
f: Work on Tarbela Dam started in 1968 when Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President. It followed the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.
r: The dam was completed in 1976 during the time of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Fill in the blank: He is too weak ___ walk. (2)
f: The pattern is too + adjective + to + verb, so the correct word is to.
r: The sentence means that he is so weak that he cannot walk.

q: Which PSL team won the title in two consecutive seasons, 2022 and 2023? (2)
f: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL final in 2022 and again in 2023, the only back-to-back titles in PSL history.
r: Peshawar Zalmi are the champions of the 2026 season; Lahore also won in 2025.

q: Which tribe of Pashtuns did Sher Shah Suri belong to? (2)
f: Sher Shah Suri belonged to the Sur tribe of the Pashtuns, which is why he is called Suri.
r: His birth name was Farid Khan.

q: Sher Shah Suri belonged to which ethnic group? (2)
f: Sher Shah Suri was a Pashtun (Afghan) from the Sur tribe.
r: He defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun and ruled India from 1540 to 1545.

q: Who was the leader of the hypocrites (Munafiqeen) in the Battle of Uhud? (2)
f: Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul withdrew with about 300 men before the battle began.
r: This left the Muslims with about 700 men.

q: What does the expression Bird's Eye View mean? (3)
o: A view from a high point looking down
f: A bird's eye view means a wide view from high above, as a bird would see it.
r: The phrase is also used for a general overview of a subject.

q: Which famous book was written by the Punjabi poet Waris Shah? (2)
f: Waris Shah wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer (Heer Ranjha) around 1766.
r: Saif-ul-Malook was written by Mian Muhammad Bakhsh.

q: On what date did Pakistan win the Cricket World Cup final in 1992? (5)
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.
r: It is Pakistan's only ODI World Cup title.

q: Fill in the blank: He writes ____ blue ink. (2)
f: We say write in ink, writing in blue ink, when the colour of the writing is meant. With is also used for the pen, but in is the standard choice here.
r: We say write with a pen but write in ink.

q: Who wrote the book Pakistan: The Formative Phase? (3)
f: Pakistan: The Formative Phase was written by the political scientist Khalid B. Sayeed.
r: The book covers the early years of Pakistan from 1857 to 1948.

q: What is 2/2? (2)
f: A number divided by itself equals 1.
r: Zero divided by any non-zero number is 0.

q: What is 9/2? (2)
f: 9 divided by 2 is 4.5.
r: 9/2 is an improper fraction, equal to 4 1/2.

q: A train covers 20 km in 100 minutes. How long will it take to cover 1 km?
f: 100 minutes divided by 20 km gives 5 minutes for each km.
r: At this pace the train's speed is 12 km per hour.

q: Which number is different: 103, 104, 105, 116, 106?
f: 103, 104, 105 and 106 are consecutive numbers, but 116 does not fit in the sequence.
r: Consecutive numbers differ by exactly 1.

q: Today is Monday and it is the 12th day of the month. What day will the 10th of the same month be?
f: The 10th is 2 days before the 12th. Two days before Monday is Saturday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days.

q: Which number comes next: 65, 115, 75, 175, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series. The 1st, 3rd and 5th terms go 65, 75, so the next is 75 + 10 = 85. The even-place terms go 115, 175.
r: In alternating series, look at odd and even positions separately.

q: Total students are 1500 and 1300 are absent. What is the percentage of present students (approximately)? (2)
f: Present students = 1500 - 1300 = 200. Percentage = 200/1500 x 100 = 13.33%.
r: Present % plus absent % always equals 100%.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th of that month?
f: 12 - 3 = 9 days later. 9 = 7 + 2, so move 2 days forward from Sunday, which is Tuesday.
r: Only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th of that month?
f: 13 - 1 = 12 days later. 12 = 7 + 5, so move 5 days forward from Sunday, which is Friday.
r: Sunday plus 5 days: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri.

q: If the 24th date of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month?
f: 24 - 14 = 10 days earlier. 10 = 7 + 3, so go back 3 days from Friday: Thursday, Wednesday, Tuesday.
r: Going back 3 days equals going forward 4 days in a week.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th of that month? (2)
f: 14 - 4 = 10 days later. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days forward from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.
r: The 11th and 18th would also be Monday if the 4th is Friday.

q: Find the odd one out: 150, 261, 372, 594, 695
f: The series goes up by 111: 150, 261, 372, 483, 594, then 705. The term 695 does not fit (it should be 705).
r: 483 is missing from the list but the 111 pattern still holds.

q: Which reforms were introduced in British India in 1919? (2)
f: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were enacted as the Government of India Act 1919 and introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
r: The Morley-Minto Reforms were earlier, in 1909.

q: Who launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in 1946 against the Dogra Maharaja?
f: Sheikh Abdullah and his National Conference launched the Quit Kashmir Movement in May 1946 against Maharaja Hari Singh.
r: He was arrested soon after the movement began.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan was made in 1956? (2)
f: The Constituent Assembly passed the first constitution of Pakistan in 1956, which made the country an Islamic Republic.
r: It was abrogated by President Iskander Mirza in October 1958.

q: What was the first amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan about?
o: Recognition of Bangladesh by changing the definition of the territories of Pakistan
Allowing the President to dissolve the Assembly
Changing the name of the country
f: The First Amendment of 1974 changed Article 1 so that the territories of Pakistan no longer included East Pakistan, after Bangladesh was recognized.
r: The Second Amendment of 1974 declared Ahmadis non-Muslims for the purposes of the Constitution.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan during the 1999 Kargil conflict? (3)
f: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister from 1997 until October 1999, so he was in office during the Kargil conflict.
r: General Pervez Musharraf removed him in a coup on 12 October 1999.

q: On which date was the first Cricket World Cup final played in 1975?
f: The first Cricket World Cup was played in England in June 1975 and its final was held at Lord's on 21 June 1975.
r: West Indies won that final by beating Australia.

q: A plane uses 60 gallons of fuel to cover 90 km. How many gallons are needed to cover 200 km?
f: Fuel per km is 60/90 = 2/3 gallon. For 200 km: 200 x 2/3 = 133.33 gallons.
r: Fuel needed is directly proportional to the distance covered.

q: Who won the 2014 ICC World Twenty20 (T20 World Cup)?
f: Sri Lanka beat India by six wickets in the final at Dhaka in April 2014.
r: Pakistan's only T20 World Cup win was in 2009.

q: Who won the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup? (4)
f: Australia beat hosts India by six wickets in the final at Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023.
r: It was Australia's sixth World Cup title.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2 x 3?
f: By BODMAS, multiplication comes first: 2 x 3 = 6. Then 2 + 6 = 8.
r: Brackets, orders, division and multiplication, then addition and subtraction is the correct order of operations.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th of that month be? (2)
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 4th to the 20th is 16 days later. 16 divided by 7 leaves remainder 2, so move 2 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Wednesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 20th is 18 days later. 18 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) forward from Friday to reach Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 25th of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 25th is 6 days earlier. 6 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so move 6 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 29th of that month be?
f: From the 12th to the 29th is 17 days later. 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3, so move 3 day(s) forward from Monday to reach Thursday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 20th is 11 days earlier. 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4, so move 4 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Thursday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 31st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 2nd of that month be?
f: From the 31st to the 2nd is 29 days earlier. 29 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so move 1 day(s) backward from Monday to reach Sunday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: In a class of 450 students, 350 are male. What is the percentage of females?
r: The male percentage in this class is 350 / 450 x 100 = 77.78%.

q: In a class of 500 students, 350 were present. What is the percentage of absent students?
r: Present students are 70% of the class.

q: Out of 4500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
r: Present students are only 340 / 4500 x 100 = 7.56% of the total.

q: Out of 4500 students, 3400 are present. What is the percentage of absent students (to two decimal places)?
r: Present students are 3400 / 4500 x 100 = 75.56%.

q: If 260 out of 500 students are present, what is the percentage of absent students?
r: Present students are 52% of the total.

q: A class has 600 students and 420 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
r: Present students are 70% of the class.

q: In a school 500 students study and 320 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
r: Present students are 64% of the total.

q: What is 28% of 500?
r: 10% of 500 is 50, so 28% is a little more than half of 250.

q: The 3rd June Plan, which announced the partition of British India, was announced in which year?
f: Lord Mountbatten announced the plan on 3 June 1947. It decided the partition of India into India and Pakistan.
r: It is also called the Mountbatten Plan, and India Independence Act followed in July 1947.

q: Who was the third wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), in order of marriage?
f: In order of marriage the wives were Khadija, Sawda, then Aisha (RA). So Aisha (RA) was the third.
r: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA); sources may differ on later order.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 14th day be?
f: From the 4th to the 14th is 10 days. 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 days = Thursday.
r: Dates that differ by 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 4th of that month? (2)
f: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.
r: Going back 4 days is the same as going forward 3 days in a week.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 18th of the month?
f: From the 5th to the 18th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves 6, so Sunday + 6 days = Saturday.
r: The 12th of this month would be Sunday too.

q: If the 9th of a month is Sunday, what day is the 26th of the month?
f: From the 9th to the 26th is 17 days. 17 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday + 3 days = Wednesday.
r: The 23rd of this month would be Sunday.

q: What is the abscissa of a point also called?
f: The abscissa is the horizontal distance of a point, which is its x-coordinate.
r: The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

q: Where did Maulana Syed Abul Ala Maududi die?
f: Maududi died in Buffalo, New York, USA, on 22 September 1979 while seeking medical treatment.
r: He founded Jamaat-e-Islami in 1941 and was buried in Lahore.

q: If the force on an object is doubled while its mass stays the same, what happens to its acceleration?
f: By Newton's second law, F = ma, so a = F / m. Acceleration is directly proportional to force when mass is fixed.
r: If the mass is doubled instead, the acceleration halves.

q: What is acceleration?
f: Acceleration is how fast the velocity of an object changes with time, a = change in velocity / time.
r: The SI unit of acceleration is metre per second squared.

q: What is the additive identity of 5?
f: The additive identity is the number which leaves a number unchanged when added. 5 + 0 = 5.
r: The multiplicative identity is 1.

q: What is the additive inverse of 65?
f: The additive inverse is the number which gives zero when added. 65 + (-65) = 0.
r: The multiplicative inverse of 65 is 1/65.

q: On which date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan adopted by the National Assembly?
f: The National Assembly adopted the Constitution on 10 April 1973. It was enforced later, on 14 August 1973.
r: The Constitution was framed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: In the sentence 'He fought bravely', what part of speech is the word 'bravely'? (2)
f: 'Bravely' tells how he fought, so it modifies a verb. Words that modify verbs and end in -ly like this are adverbs.
r: The adjective form of this word is 'brave'.

q: What type of adverb is the word 'often'?
f: 'Often' tells how many times something happens. Adverbs that answer 'how often' are adverbs of frequency.
r: Other adverbs of frequency are always, never, sometimes and rarely.

q: The age of Ahmad is three times the age of his sister, and his sister is 4 years old. What will Ahmad's age be after 10 years?
f: Ahmad is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now. After 10 years he will be 12 + 10 = 22 years old.
r: Age problems are solved by first finding the present age, then adding the years.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is double his age. What is his sister's age?
f: Double of 4 is 2 x 4 = 8, so the sister is 8 years old.
r: The difference in their ages is 4 years and it always stays the same.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmed and Bilal is younger than Akbar. Who is the oldest of the three? (2)
f: Akbar is older than both Ahmed and Bilal, so he is the oldest.
r: Comparison questions are easiest with a line of names from oldest to youngest.

q: Which airline belongs to Italy and is its national flag carrier since 2021?
f: ITA Airways is the national airline of Italy. It took over from Alitalia in October 2021.
r: Alitalia was the former national airline of Italy.

q: Which is the intelligence agency of Israel?
f: Mossad is the national intelligence agency of Israel, responsible for foreign intelligence.
r: RAW is the foreign intelligence agency of India and ISI is that of Pakistan.

q: Abul Ala Maududi, the founder of Jamaat-e-Islami, was born in which city?
f: Maududi was born in 1903 in Aurangabad in the Deccan, British India.
r: He later moved to Pakistan and led Jamaat-e-Islami.

q: In which year did Abul Ala Maududi die?
f: Maududi died in 1979 in Buffalo, USA, and was buried in Lahore.
r: He founded Jamaat-e-Islami in 1941.

q: In which country is the city of Allahabad (now Prayagraj) located?
f: Allahabad is in the state of Uttar Pradesh in India. Its name was changed to Prayagraj in 2018.
r: Allama Iqbal gave his famous address at the Muslim League session held here in 1930.

q: Allama Iqbal did his graduation (BA) from which college?
f: Iqbal passed his BA in 1897 from Government College Lahore, and later his MA there in 1899.
r: He later got a PhD from Munich in Germany.

q: Complete the series: 4Z, 5Y, ?
f: The numbers go up by 1 (4, 5, 6) and the letters go backwards (Z, Y, X). So the next term is 6X.
r: Z is the last and A is the first letter of the English alphabet.

q: Altaf Hussain Hali was a famous poet of which language?
f: Altaf Hussain Hali (1837-1914) was a well-known Urdu poet and critic.
r: His long poem Musaddas-e-Hali is famous in Urdu literature.

q: Ali is older than Hammad but younger than Amir. Hammad is younger than Amir. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Amir is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Hammad. So the order from oldest is Amir, Ali, Hammad, and Hammad is the youngest.
r: In such questions, draw the people in a line from oldest to youngest.

q: Muhammad Amir is a famous fast bowler of which country?
f: Muhammad Amir is a left-arm fast bowler who plays cricket for Pakistan.
r: He first played international cricket for Pakistan in 2009.

q: Which country annexed Sindh in 1843?
f: The British East India Company, under General Charles Napier, defeated the Talpur Mirs at Miani in 1843 and annexed Sindh.
