f: DMAS stands for Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction, and the operations are done in this order.
r: BODMAS adds Brackets and Of before Division.

q: Which country attacked the Soviet Union (Russia) in World War 2 in 1941?
f: Germany invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 under Operation Barbarossa.
r: The Soviet Union then joined the Allies against Germany.

q: What is the full name of the hadith book Sahih Bukhari?
f: Imam Bukhari named his book Al-Jami al-Sahih (the Authentic Collection).
r: It is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after the Quran.

q: What was the old name of the city of Sahiwal? (2)
f: Sahiwal was called Montgomery during British rule and was renamed in 1967.
r: Lyallpur, now Faisalabad, was another city renamed after a British officer.

q: Saleem has an average of 60 in 4 subjects. After the next test his average falls to 58. How many marks did he score in the next test?
f: Total of 4 subjects = 4 x 60 = 240. Total of 5 tests = 5 x 58 = 290. Next score = 290 - 240 = 50.
r: Average equals total marks divided by the number of tests.

q: Change the narration into indirect speech: Sara said, "I am sorry."
o: Sara said that she is sorry.
Sara said that she was sorry.
Sara said that I was sorry.
Sara said that she had been sorry.
f: In indirect speech the present tense changes to past after a past reporting verb, and I becomes she.
r: Pronouns in indirect speech change to match the reporter's point of view.

q: Which two countries surround the Aral Sea?
f: The Aral Sea lies between Kazakhstan in the north and Uzbekistan in the south.
r: It has shrunk greatly since the 1960s.

q: The Caucasus region lies between which two seas?
f: The Caucasus mountain region lies between the Black Sea in the west and the Caspian Sea in the east.
r: Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus is the highest peak in Europe.

q: Which two seas does the Suez Canal connect?
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt links the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
r: It opened in 1869.

q: What is sec 2x equal to?
f: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, so sec of any angle is 1 divided by cos of that angle. For the angle 2x this gives sec 2x = 1 / cos 2x.
r: Sec 2x is not the same as 2 sec x.

q: Fill in the preposition: A private secretary has no authority ___ his boss.
f: The correct phrase is authority over someone, meaning power to control them.
r: We say authority over a person but authority on a subject.

q: What is the total number of women seats in the Senate of Pakistan? (3)
f: Each of the four provinces has 4 seats for women, which is 16, and Islamabad has 1 women seat. The total is 17.
r: The Senate has 96 members in all.

q: In a class of 33 students, 7 are boys. What is the percentage of girls (approximately)?
r: Boys are 7 / 33 x 100 = 21.21%, and the two add to 100%.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Shaheen-III missile? (2)
f: Shaheen-III is a surface-to-surface ballistic missile with a range of about 2750 km.
r: Shaheen-I has a range of about 750 km.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: b5, g8, l11, q14, ?
f: Letters move 5 steps each time (b, g, l, q, v) and the numbers go up by 3 (5, 8, 11, 14, 17). So the next term is v17.
r: Skipping 4 letters between terms gives a step of 5.

q: Find the next letter in the series: A C G M ?
f: Positions are 1, 3, 7, 13. The gaps are 2, 4, 6, so the next gap is 8, giving position 21, which is U.
r: The gaps in this series are even numbers rising by 2.

q: What comes next in the series: Z3, Y6, X9, ?
f: Letters go backward by one (Z, Y, X, W) and numbers go up by 3 (3, 6, 9, 12). So the next term is W12.
r: Z is the 26th letter and goes down one position each time.

q: In which year was Colonel Sher Khan (Nishan-e-Haider) martyred?
f: Captain (later Colonel) Karnal Sher Khan was martyred in the Kargil conflict in July 1999. He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.
r: He is the only Pakistan Army officer of Kargil to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: What is the value of sin 45 degrees?
f: In a right isosceles triangle with equal sides 1, the hypotenuse is square root of 2, so sin 45 is 1 divided by square root of 2, about 0.707.
r: Cos 45 degrees has the same value as sin 45 degrees.

q: Sidra is 6 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old will her brother be when Sidra becomes 11?
f: Brother is 6 x 2 = 12 now. Sidra becomes 11 after 5 years, so the brother will be 12 + 5 = 17.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is 2 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 8 years old?
f: Sister is 6 x 2 = 12 now. Ali becomes 8 after 2 years, so she will be 12 + 2 = 14.
r: Here the sister is 6 years older than Ali, and the gap never changes.

q: What is Sihah Sitta?
f: Sihah Sitta means the six most reliable books of hadith: Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.
r: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are together called the Sahihain.

q: Why did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan receive the title of Sir?
o: He was knighted by the British Government in 1888 for his services
He was elected president of the Muslim League
He founded the city of Aligarh
f: The British Government honoured him with a knighthood (KCSI) in 1888 in recognition of his public and educational services.
r: He had earlier been given the title Javad-ud-Daula by the Mughal emperor.

q: What was the slogan of the Pakistan National Alliance (PNA) movement of 1977?
f: The PNA, an alliance of nine parties against Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, campaigned for the enforcement of the system of the Prophet (PBUH), called Nizam-e-Mustafa.
r: The movement began after the March 1977 elections, and General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977.

q: A pen is bought for Rs 50 and sold for Rs 70. What is the percentage of profit?
f: Profit = 70 - 50 = Rs 20. Profit percentage = 20/50 x 100 = 40%.
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price.

q: A car has a speed of 120 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12.5 minutes?
f: 12.5 minutes = 12.5/60 hour. Distance = 120 x 12.5/60 = 25 km.
r: At 120 km/h a car covers 2 km every minute.

q: Which ocean lies to the south of India?
f: The Indian Ocean surrounds the southern tip of the Indian peninsula, with the Bay of Bengal to the east and the Arabian Sea to the west.
r: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean in the world.

q: In World War 2 (1939), which country did the Soviet Union attack first?
f: On 17 September 1939 the Soviet army invaded eastern Poland, soon after Germany invaded from the west.
r: The Soviet Union attacked Finland in the Winter War a few weeks later, in November 1939.

q: Which is the correct spelling of this military rank?
f: The correct spelling is Lieutenant.
r: In Pakistan Army the rank of Lieutenant is the first commissioned rank after passing out from PMA.

q: What is the area of a square whose side is 5 units? (2)
f: Area of a square = side x side = 5 x 5 = 25 square units.
r: The perimeter of this square would be 4 x 5 = 20 units.

q: What is the square of 12?
r: 12 squared is also called one gross, which is 144 items.

q: What is the square of 13?
r: 169 equals 144 + 25, which is 12 squared plus 5 squared.

q: In which city is Tahrir Square located?
f: Tahrir Square is in the centre of Cairo, the capital of Egypt.
r: It was the main centre of the Egyptian revolution of 2011.

q: Who is the legendary squash player of Pakistan who won the World Open six times?
f: Jahangir Khan is regarded as the greatest squash player ever and won the World Open six times.
r: He was unbeaten in 555 consecutive matches from 1981 to 1986.

q: In which year were the Engineering Research Laboratories (later Khan Research Laboratories) of Dr A. Q. Khan established at Kahuta? (3)
f: Dr A. Q. Khan founded the laboratory in 1976 to build uranium enrichment capability.
r: It was renamed Khan Research Laboratories in 1981 by President Zia-ul-Haq.

q: Fill in the preposition: He waited ___ the station.
f: We use at with a place regarded as a point, such as a station.
r: Waited for is used with the thing or person awaited, such as waited for the train.

q: Which is the highest railway station in Pakistan, at about 2,224 metres above sea level?
f: Kan Mehtarzai on the Zhob Valley Railway in Balochistan is cited as Pakistan's highest railway station.
r: The line is closed since 1986 and Kan Mehtarzai is no longer in use.

q: Out of 540 students, 160 are present. What is the approximate percentage of students present?
f: Percentage = 160 / 540 x 100 = 29.63, which is about 29.6%.
r: The number of absent students is 540 - 160 = 380, which is about 70.4%.

q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed (Barelvi), leader of the Mujahideen movement, was a student of whom?
f: Syed Ahmad Shaheed studied in Delhi under Shah Abdul Aziz Dehlawi, son of Shah Waliullah.
r: Syed Ahmad Shaheed was martyred at Balakot in 1831 fighting the Sikhs.

q: Which battle is generally called the first major battle of the British in the subcontinent that gave them rule in Bengal?
f: In the Battle of Plassey (1757) the East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah.
r: Some sources count the earlier Carnatic wars as the first fights, but textbooks give Plassey.

q: Which two water bodies does the Suez Canal connect?
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt joins the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
r: It was opened in 1869 and shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia.

q: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was the son of which prophet?
f: The Quran mentions Sulaiman (AS) as the son and heir of Prophet Dawud (AS).
r: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was given control over the winds and the jinn.

q: Takht-e-Sulaiman is the highest peak of which mountain range?
f: Takht-e-Sulaiman, about 3,487 metres high, is the highest peak of the Sulaiman Range in Balochistan.
r: The Sulaiman Range lies in the west of Pakistan along the Balochistan and KP border.

q: What is a Madni (Madani) surah of the Quran?
o: A surah revealed before the Hijrah
A surah revealed after the Hijrah
A surah revealed in Makkah only
A surah with the fewest verses
f: Surahs revealed after the Prophet's migration (Hijrah) to Madinah are called Madni surahs.
r: Madni surahs mostly deal with laws, society and the state.

q: Which surah of the Quran contains the Bismillah twice? (5)
f: Surah An-Naml has Bismillah at the start and again inside verse 30, in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS).
r: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that has no Bismillah at its start.

q: According to the common textbook count, how many Makki and Madni surahs does the Quran have?
f: The common Pakistani textbook count is 86 Makki surahs and 28 Madni surahs, which total 114.
r: Scholars differ slightly in the count of some surahs.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'apology'?
f: An apology is an expression of regret for a wrong done.
r: To apologise means to say sorry.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'clever'?
f: Clever means quick to learn and understand, which is the same as intelligent.
r: The opposite (antonym) of clever is foolish or dull.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'ferocious'?
f: Ferocious means savage and violent, which is the same as fierce.
r: Ferocity is the noun form of ferocious.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'God'?
f: A deity is a god or divine being.
r: The word deity comes from the Latin deus, meaning god.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'retreat'?
f: To retreat means to move back or withdraw, especially from danger or an enemy.
r: The opposite (antonym) of retreat is advance.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'stereotypical'?
f: Stereotypical means following a fixed, common pattern, which is close to conventional.
r: A stereotype is an over-simplified fixed idea about a type of person or thing.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'talkative'?
f: Talkative means fond of talking a lot, which is the same as garrulous.
r: The opposite (antonym) of talkative is reserved or silent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'garrulous'?
f: Garrulous means excessively talkative.
r: The noun form is garrulity.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'expunge'?
f: To expunge means to wipe out or erase completely.
r: Expunge is often used for removing names or remarks from a record.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'literally'? (2)
f: Literally means in the exact, actual sense of the words.
r: The opposite idea is figuratively.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'lowly'?
f: Lowly means of low rank or status, which is close to humble.
r: The opposite (antonym) of lowly is exalted.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'boast'?
f: To boast means to talk proudly about oneself, which is the same as to brag.
r: A person who boasts too much is called boastful.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disaster'?
f: A disaster is a sudden event causing great damage, which is a catastrophe.
r: Earthquakes and floods are examples of natural disasters.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'indescribable'?
f: Indescribable means too great or strange to be put into words, which is inexpressible.
r: The prefix in- here means not.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word insurgence?
f: Insurgence means an uprising or revolt against an authority. Rebellion has the same meaning.
r: An insurgent is a person who rises in revolt against a government.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word normal?
f: Normal means usual and as expected. Ordinary has the same meaning.
r: The opposite of normal is abnormal or unusual.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word pragmatic?
f: A pragmatic person deals with things in a sensible and realistic way. Practical has the same meaning.
r: The opposite of pragmatic is idealistic or impractical.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word tamper?
f: To tamper means to interfere with something in order to damage or change it without permission. Interfere is the nearest meaning.
r: Tampering with evidence is a crime in most countries.

q: Which tense is used in the sentence: They are watching TV?
f: The verb group are watching uses is/am/are plus verb-ing, which shows an action happening now. This is the present continuous tense.
r: The past continuous form would be: They were watching TV.

q: If 1 = 7 and 3 = 9, then 13 = ?
f: Each number is 6 more than the given number: 1 + 6 = 7 and 3 + 6 = 9. So 13 + 6 = 19.
r: In such code questions first find the rule that fits all the given examples.

q: What is one third of 20% of 60?
f: 20% of 60 = 12. One third of 12 = 4.
r: To find a percentage, multiply by the percent and divide by 100.

q: What is one third of 30% of 120?
f: 30% of 120 = 36. One third of 36 = 12.
r: 30% of a number equals three tenths of it.

q: What is one third of 95?
f: 95 divided by 3 = 31 with remainder 2, so the answer is 31 and 2/3 (31.67).
r: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3; 9 + 5 = 14 is not.

q: Ali's age is 5 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be his sister's age when Ali is 20?
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 20, she will be 20 + 10 = 30.
r: The age difference between two persons always stays the same.

q: Hania is 4 years old and her sister is three times her age. What will her sister's age be when Hania is 10? (2)
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12, so she is 8 years older. When Hania is 10, the sister will be 10 + 8 = 18.
r: The age difference between two persons always stays the same.

q: Who gave the first Azan inside the Kaaba after the conquest of Makkah?
f: On the day Makkah was conquered, the Prophet (PBUH) asked Hazrat Bilal (RA) to call the Azan from the roof of the Kaaba.
r: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the first Muezzin of Islam.

q: Who inaugurated the Mazar-e-Quaid (Quaid-e-Azam Mausoleum) in Karachi?
f: The mausoleum was opened to the public by President Yahya Khan in January 1971.
r: Its construction was completed in 1970 and the architect was Yahya Merchant.

q: How many oceans are there in the world? (2)
f: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic Oceans.
r: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

q: In which year of prophethood did the Muslims first migrate to Habsha (Abyssinia)?
f: The first migration to Abyssinia took place in the 5th year of prophethood, around 615 CE.
r: The Muslims were given shelter by the just king Najashi.

q: A train covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the train covers 20 / 100 = 0.2 km each minute. In 5 minutes it covers 5 x 0.2 = 1 km.
r: The speed of this train is 12 km per hour.

q: The speed of a car is 60 km/h and a train goes at double that speed. How far does the train travel in 100 minutes?
f: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 100 minutes (5/3 hour) it covers 120 x 5/3 = 200 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km? (2)
f: Total time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so time for 1 km = 100/90 = 1.11 minutes.
r: His speed is 54 km per hour.

q: What type of number is 0?
f: Whole numbers are 0, 1, 2, 3 and so on, so 0 is a whole number but not a natural number.
r: Natural numbers start from 1.

q: After rearranging the letters of the word UEABYIFT, what is the last letter of the new word? (2)
f: The letters make the word BEAUTIFY, which ends with Y.
r: BEAUTIFY means to make something beautiful.

q: Who was the Man of the Tournament in the 1999 Cricket World Cup?
f: South African all-rounder Lance Klusener was named Man of the Tournament in 1999.
r: Australia won that World Cup, beating Pakistan in the final.

q: Ali is shorter than Umar and Umar is shorter than Abdullah. What is the relation of Ali and Umar?
o: Ali and Umar are of equal height
f: The first statement says directly that Ali is shorter than Umar.
r: From both statements, Abdullah is the tallest and Ali is the shortest of the three.

q: Umer is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old will his sister be when Umer is 9?
f: The sister is 6 now, so she is 3 years older than Umer. When Umer is 9, she will be 9 + 3 = 12.
r: The age difference between two people stays the same for life.

q: What is the unit of lens power?
f: The power of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres, and its unit is the dioptre (D).
r: A converging lens has positive power and a diverging lens has negative power.

q: Who was the President of the USA for most of the Second World War? (5)
f: Franklin D. Roosevelt was President from 1933 until his death in April 1945, covering most of the war.
r: Harry Truman succeeded him and ordered the atomic bombings of Japan in August 1945.

q: An airplane uses 80 gallons of fuel to travel 320 km. How many gallons will it use to travel 700 km?
f: It uses 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallon per km. For 700 km: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
r: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance when the rate is constant.

q: At which place did India conduct its nuclear bomb tests in 1974 and 1998?
f: India tested its nuclear devices at Pokhran in the Rajasthan desert.
r: Pakistan conducted its tests in the Chagai hills in May 1998.

q: What is a refrigerator (fridge) mainly used for?
f: A fridge keeps the inside cool so that food stays fresh and does not spoil quickly.
r: A refrigerator works by removing heat from its inside and releasing it outside.

q: If Ali is older than Usman and Noman is older than Ali, who is the eldest?
f: Noman is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Usman, so the order is Noman, Ali, Usman.
r: Usman is the youngest of the three.

q: What does USSR stand for?
f: USSR stands for the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, the communist state formed in 1922.
r: The USSR broke up in December 1991 into 15 independent countries.

q: Where is the Kalash Valley located?
f: The Kalash valleys (Bumburet, Rumbur and Birir) lie in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: The Kalash people follow their own ancient religion and culture.

q: What is the value of i^5, where i is the imaginary unit?
f: i^2 = -1 and i^4 = 1, so i^5 = i^4 x i = 1 x i = i.
r: The powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.

q: What is velocity?
o: Rate of change of displacement with time
f: Velocity is a vector quantity: displacement divided by the time taken, so it has both speed and direction.
r: The SI unit of velocity is metre per second.

q: What is the vertical arrangement of numbers in a matrix called?
f: Entries written from top to bottom form a column, while entries written left to right form a row.
r: A matrix with m rows and n columns is said to be of order m x n.

q: Change the voice: You praised her very much.
o: She is praised very much by you.
She was praised very much by you.
She had praised you very much.
She has been praised very much by you.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was or were with the past participle: She was praised very much by you.
r: In passive voice the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1913?
f: Lord Hardinge served as Viceroy from 1910 to 1916, which includes 1913.
r: The capital of British India was moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911 during his time.

q: What is the meaning of the name Pakistan? (4)
f: Pak means pure and stan means land, so Pakistan means Land of the Pure.
r: The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.

q: How many vowels are in the letter string AHGRUOVE?
f: The vowels in AHGRUOVE are A, U, O and E. That makes 4 vowels.
r: The five English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are in the letter string AHJKFSREKHVCIBKMNEI?
f: Going through the letters, the vowels are A, E, I, E and I. That makes 5 vowels.
r: Y is treated as a consonant in these verbal tests unless the question says otherwise.

q: How many vowels are there in the word Tuesday?
f: The vowels in Tuesday are U, E and A. The letter Y is a consonant here, so the total is 3.
r: The word Tuesday has 7 letters, of which 4 are consonants.

q: In which year did Shah Waliullah of Delhi die? (2)
f: Shah Waliullah Dehlawi died in Delhi in 1762 (1176 AH).
r: He was born in 1703 and is famous for his book Hujjat Allah al-Baligha.

q: A man walks 1 m north, turns right, walks 1 m and then turns back. In which direction is he facing now?
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Turning back reverses the direction, so he faces west.
r: Turning back means turning through 180 degrees.

q: Ali walked 20 km in 120 minutes. How much distance will Ali cover in 5 minutes at the same speed?
f: Speed is 20 km per 120 minutes, which is 1/6 km per minute. In 5 minutes he covers 5/6 km, about 0.83 km (833 m).
r: 20 km in 2 hours means a speed of 10 km/h.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He walked ___ school.
f: The preposition towards shows the direction of movement, so 'He walked towards school' is correct.
r: The preposition to is also used with walk, as in 'walked to school'.

q: In which years did the two World Wars take place?
f: World War I was fought from 1914 to 1918 and World War II from 1939 to 1945.
r: World War II began with the German invasion of Poland in September 1939.

q: Change into passive voice: She said to me that she was watching TV.
o: I was told by her that she was watching TV.
I told her that she was watching TV.
She was told by me that she was watching TV.
TV was being watched by her to me.
f: In the passive form the object (me) becomes the subject, and said to becomes was told by. The reported clause stays the same.
r: The verb tell is used in the passive instead of say for reported speech.

q: What was the Wavell Plan?
o: A plan to reconstitute the Viceroy's Executive Council with equal Hindu and Muslim representation
A plan to partition India into two states
A plan to give India dominion status immediately
A plan to hold elections for a Constituent Assembly
f: Wavell proposed an Executive Council in which all members except the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief were Indians, with parity between caste Hindus and Muslims.
r: The plan failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over who could nominate Muslim members.

q: Choose the correct word: She is ___ weak in maths.
f: The adverb very is used before an adjective such as weak to give strength. Much, many and more do not fit here.
r: Very is an adverb of degree.

q: Which symbol is used for the set of whole numbers? (2)
f: The set of whole numbers (0, 1, 2, 3, ...) is written W.
r: N is for natural numbers, Z for integers and Q for rational numbers.

q: What is the synonym of the word widely?
f: Widely means over a large area or among many people, which is the same as extensively.
r: Narrowly is the opposite of widely.

q: What is the area of a rectangle with length 5 and width 4?
f: Area of a rectangle is length times width, so 5 x 4 = 20 square units.
r: The perimeter of this rectangle would be 2 x (5 + 4) = 18 units.

q: What is the synonym of the word wildly?
f: Wildly means in an uncontrolled or fierce way, which is close to violently.
r: Calmly is its opposite.

q: What is the antonym of the word wildly?
f: Wildly means in an uncontrolled way, so the opposite is calmly.
r: Wild (adjective) has the opposite tame.

q: If 1 man writes 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will 5 men write in 25 minutes?
f: One man writes 1 page per minute. So 5 men write 5 pages per minute, and in 25 minutes they write 5 x 25 = 125 pages.
r: Work problems are solved by first finding the rate of one worker.

q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day is it today?
f: The day after Sunday is Monday.
r: Monday is the first working day after the weekend in many countries.

q: What is the chemical symbol of zinc?
f: The symbol of zinc is Zn.
r: Zinc is used to galvanise iron to prevent rusting.

q: What is 1 + 2/2 + 2?
f: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 1 + 1 + 2 = 4.
r: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

q: What is 1 + 1/2?
r: 1.5 can also be written as 3/2.

q: What is 10% of 33?
r: To find 10%, divide by 10.

q: What is 20% of 41?
r: 20% equals one fifth.

q: What is 22 + 2/2?
f: Division first: 2/2 = 1. Then 22 + 1 = 23.
r: BODMAS says division comes before addition.

q: What is 3x + 3y written in factor form?
f: Both terms have the common factor 3, so 3x + 3y = 3(x + y).
r: Taking out a common factor is called factorisation.

q: What is 60% of 60?
r: 60% equals 3/5.

q: What is 65% of 70?
r: 10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 42 and 5% is 3.5.

q: What is 72% of 80?
r: 10% of 80 is 8, so 70% is 56 and 2% is 1.6.

q: What is 80 x 80?
f: 8 x 8 = 64, and two zeros are added, giving 6400.
r: 80 squared is 6400.

q: What is 81% of 81?
What is 90 x 90?
f: 9 x 9 = 81, and two zeros are added, giving 8100.
r: 90 squared is 8100.

q: What is 90% of 89?
What does KG stand for?
f: KG is the short form of kilogram, the SI unit of mass.
r: One kilogram equals 1000 grams.

q: What is the H.C.F of 4 and 16?
f: Factors of 4 are 1, 2, 4. All of these divide 16, so the highest common factor is 4.
r: If one number divides the other, it is the HCF.

q: What was the Islamic date of the independence of Pakistan (14 August 1947)? (9)
f: 14 August 1947 fell on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, the blessed night of Laylat ul Qadr as commonly believed.
r: Because of this date, Pakistan is often called a gift of the holy month of Ramadan.

q: Arrange the letters of PLOEADR to make the name of an animal. (8)
f: The letters P, L, O, E, A, D, R make the word LEOPARD, a big cat. It uses all seven letters once.
r: The leopard is a spotted big cat found in Asia and Africa.

q: On what date did the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) receive royal assent? (6)
f: The Act got royal assent on 23 December 1919 and the reforms started in 1921. They introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
r: The 20 August 1917 date is Montagu's announcement in the House of Commons.

q: What is the value of 3 factorial (3!)? (6)
r: By definition, 0! = 1.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the ancient site of Kot Diji located? (6)
f: Kot Diji is in Khairpur district of Sindh, near the Indus River. Its fort and Indus Valley site are well known.
r: The Kot Diji culture is an early phase of the Indus Valley civilization, before Mohenjo-daro.

q: Qantas is the national airline of which country? (4)
f: Qantas is the flag carrier of Australia. The name comes from Queensland and Northern Territory Aerial Services.
r: It was founded in 1920.

q: According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'between'? (4)
f: 'Between' shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word, as in 'between the two trees'. A word that does this is a preposition.
r: 'Between' is normally used for two things, while 'among' is used for more than two.

q: Who is the author of the book India, My Love? (4)
f: India, My Love is a book by the French author Dominique Lapierre about his travels in India. The French title is India Mon Amour.
r: Lapierre also wrote City of Joy and, with Larry Collins, Freedom at Midnight; a different book called India My Love: A Spiritual Journey also exists.

q: What is the commonly stated range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) short-range ballistic missile? (4)
f: Nasr is a short-range, nuclear-capable missile with a reported range of 60 to 70 km, with the upgraded version given as 70 km. It is meant as a battlefield weapon.
r: Early reports gave 60 km, so sources differ depending on the variant.

q: Which planet is called the sister planet of the Earth because of its similar size? (4)
f: Venus is almost the same size and mass as Earth, so it is called Earth's sister.
r: Venus is the hottest planet of the solar system.

q: A car is used for what purpose? (4)
f: A car is a road vehicle used to travel from one place to another.
r: The first practical petrol car was built by Karl Benz in 1885.

q: About how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain? (3)
f: An average adult has about 5 litres of blood, which is roughly 7 to 8 percent of body weight.
r: Blood is pumped around the body by the heart.

q: Which ancient city is regarded as the centre of Buddhist learning in Pakistan? (3)
f: Taxila, in the Gandhara region near Rawalpindi, was a famous centre of Buddhist learning and art.
r: Taxila was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

q: Hawaii is a state of the USA. What is its capital? (4)
f: The capital of Hawaii is Honolulu, on the island of Oahu.
r: Hawaii became the 50th US state in 1959.

q: In which year did the first All Pakistan Educational Conference take place in Karachi? (3)
f: The conference was held in Karachi from 27 November to 1 December 1947, just after independence. It was opened by Quaid-e-Azam's message on education policy.
r: Its date is the 27th of November 1947 as the start of the conference.

q: Mahatma Gandhi was the leader of which political party? (3)
f: Gandhi led the Indian National Congress in the freedom movement against British rule. He led campaigns such as Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah led the All India Muslim League.

q: What is the average life span of a red blood cell in the human body? (5)
f: Red blood cells live for about 120 days and are then broken down in the spleen and liver.
r: Red blood cells are made in the bone marrow.

q: Approximately how many litres of blood does an average adult human body contain? (3)
f: An average adult has roughly 4.5 to 5.5 litres of blood, usually given as about 5 litres. This is around 7 percent of body weight.
r: Women usually have slightly less blood volume than men.

q: The famous Leaning Tower of Pisa is located in which country? (3)
f: The Leaning Tower stands in the city of Pisa in Tuscany, Italy.
r: It is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral and its construction started in 1173.

q: Which British commander defeated Tipu Sultan in the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92)? (3)
f: Lord Cornwallis led the British forces and Tipu had to sign the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792.
r: Tipu Sultan was finally killed in 1799 in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War, when Lord Wellesley was Governor-General.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 17th be? (2)
f: From the 3rd to the 17th is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 17th is also a Monday.
r: A gap that is a multiple of 7 days gives the same weekday.

q: The 24th of January is celebrated as the day of what? (5)
f: The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education in 2018.
r: The day highlights the role of education in peace and development.

q: A helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to cover 320 km. How many gallons does it need to cover 700 km? (2)
f: Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallons. For 700 km: 0.15625 x 700 = 109.375, about 109.4 gallons.
r: Fuel used is directly proportional to the distance covered.

q: What part of speech is the word 'against' in the sentence 'He leaned against the wall'? (2)
f: 'Against' shows the relation between 'leaned' and 'the wall', so it is a preposition.
r: A preposition is normally followed by a noun or pronoun.

q: What part of speech is the word 'eat' in the sentence 'Children eat fruit'? (3)
f: 'Eat' names an action, so it is a verb.
r: A verb expresses an action, a state or an occurrence.

q: Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is a famous Pakistani player of which sport? (2)
f: Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi is Pakistan's best-known tennis player, famous for doubles.
r: He reached the US Open men's doubles final in 2010 with Rohan Bopanna.

q: How did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah respond to the Nehru Report of 1928? (2)
o: He rejected it and later presented his Fourteen Points
He asked the British to enforce it
He ignored it and left politics
f: The Nehru Report did not protect Muslim rights such as separate electorates, so Jinnah rejected it. In 1929 he gave his Fourteen Points as the Muslim demands.
r: Jinnah's earlier Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 had been turned down by the Congress.

q: What is the logarithm of unity (1) to any base? (2)
f: Any base raised to the power 0 gives 1, so log of 1 to any base is 0.
r: The logarithm of a negative number is not defined in real numbers.

q: Peshawar is associated with which ancient civilisation? (2)
f: Peshawar, once called Purushapura, was a capital of the Gandhara civilisation in Kushan times. Gandhara art blended Greek and Buddhist styles.
r: Taxila was another important Gandhara city.

q: Choose the correct sentence. (2)
o: The Principal has accepted my application.
The Principal have accepted my application.
The Principal has accept my application.
f: Principal is singular, so it takes has, and the present perfect needs the past participle accepted.
r: Principal means head of a school, while principle means a rule.

q: What is the date of birth of Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar? (2)
f: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar was born on 10 December 1878 in Rampur, India.
r: He edited the newspapers Comrade and Hamdard and was a leader of the Khilafat Movement.

q: Which disease is caused by the bite of an infected dog? (2)
f: Rabies is a viral disease passed to humans through the saliva of an infected animal, usually a dog.
r: Rabies can be prevented by vaccination given soon after a bite.

q: On which date is World Hepatitis Day observed every year? (2)
f: World Hepatitis Day is observed on 28 July, the birthday of Dr Baruch Blumberg who discovered the hepatitis B virus.
r: World Health Day is on 7 April and World AIDS Day is on 1 December.

q: Under the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan, the office of Governor General was replaced by which office? (2)
f: The Constitution of 1956 made Pakistan a republic, so the post of Governor General was replaced by the President.
r: Iskander Mirza, the last Governor General, became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.

q: Fill in the blank: She sits ___ the tree. (2)
f: The preposition under shows she is below the tree, which gives a meaningful sentence.
r: Under is a preposition of place, like above, beside and near.

q: Which comes next in the series: 1Z, 3X, 5V, ? (2)
f: Numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7) and letters go back by 2 (Z, X, V, T). So the next term is 7T.
r: Z is the 26th letter and T is the 20th.

q: Complete the series: 3/2, 6/4, 10/8, 15/16, ? (2)
f: Numerators increase by 3, 4, 5, 6 (3, 6, 10, 15, 21). Denominators double (2, 4, 8, 16, 32). So the next term is 21/32.
r: The numerators are triangular numbers.

q: What is the total number of members of the UN Security Council? (2)
f: There are 5 permanent members and 10 non-permanent members, so 5 + 10 = 15.
r: Non-permanent members are elected for two years.

q: Choose the correct verb: My mother ___ at the hospital. (2)
f: The subject my mother is third person singular, so the simple present verb takes -s: works.
r: In simple present tense, he, she and it take a verb ending in -s or -es.

q: What is iota (i) in mathematics called, and what is its value? (2)
o: The imaginary unit, equal to the square root of -1
f: Iota i is the imaginary unit defined by i squared = -1, so i is the square root of -1.
r: Powers of i repeat in a cycle of four: i, -1, -i, 1.

q: Change into passive voice: The pilot landed the aeroplane safely. (2)
o: The aeroplane was landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane is landed safely by the pilot.
The aeroplane has been landed safely by the pilot.
The pilot was landed safely by the aeroplane.
f: The sentence is in simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: the object becomes the subject.
r: Passive voice is formed as: object + form of be + past participle + by + subject.

q: How many centimetres are there in one inch? (2)
f: By international definition, one inch is exactly 2.54 centimetres.
r: One foot is 12 inches, which is about 30.48 centimetres.

q: PEMRA is the regulatory authority for which type of media in Pakistan? (2)
f: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority. It regulates and licenses television and radio channels.
r: PEMRA was established in 2002.

q: If one person writes one page in one minute, how many pages will 5 persons write in 5 minutes? (2)
f: One person writes 1 page per minute. 5 persons write 5 pages per minute, so in 5 minutes they write 25 pages.
r: Rate times people times time gives the total work.

q: According to the 2023 digital census, what is the population of Pakistan (approximately)? (2)
f: The 2023 census, approved by the CCI, recorded 241.49 million people.
r: The 2017 census had recorded 207.7 million.

q: What is the value of 1 raised to any power n? (2)
f: 1 multiplied by itself any number of times is always 1.
r: Any non-zero number raised to power zero is also 1.

q: If the diameter of a circle is 35, what is its radius? (2)
f: Radius is half of the diameter, so 35 divided by 2 = 17.5.
r: The diameter is twice the radius and the longest chord of a circle.

q: When did the United Nations General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights? (3)
f: The General Assembly adopted the Declaration in Paris on 10 December 1948.
r: 10 December is celebrated every year as Human Rights Day.

q: What is the common short form (abbreviation) of Saudi Arabia? (2)
f: Saudi Arabia is officially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, so its short form is KSA.
r: SAR is the code for the Saudi riyal, the currency of Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the value of cosec x multiplied by sin x? (2)
f: Cosec x is 1 divided by sin x, so cosec x times sin x equals 1 over sin x times sin x, which is 1.
r: Similarly sec x times cos x is 1 and cot x times tan x is 1.

q: Which place in Pakistan is famous for making small arms (weapons) in home industry? (2)
f: Darra Adam Khel, south of Peshawar in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is well known for its local small arms workshops.
r: Sialkot is instead famous for sports goods and surgical instruments.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'affection'? (2)
f: 'Affection' means almost the same as 'fondness'.
r: Its opposite is 'dislike' or 'hatred'.

q: The Victoria Cross is the highest military award of which country? (2)
f: The Victoria Cross is the highest British award for bravery in the face of the enemy. It was created by Queen Victoria in 1856.
r: The highest American military award is the Medal of Honor.

q: What is the meaning of the word wild? (2)
o: Untamed or living in a natural state
f: Wild describes animals or plants living in their natural state, not tamed or cultivated.
r: The opposite of wild is tame or domestic.

q: Who wrote the book Kitab ul Umm? (2)
f: Kitab ul Umm is a major work of fiqh written by Imam Muhammad bin Idris al-Shafi'i.
r: Imam Malik wrote Al-Muwatta and Imam Ahmad compiled the Musnad.

q: What is 60 percent of 100?
r: Percent means per hundred, so any percent of 100 equals the same number.

q: The population of a town in the year 2000 is 1600 and it doubles every 5 years. What was the population in 1980?
f: From 1980 to 2000 is 20 years, which is 4 doublings. So the 1980 population = 1600 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 = 100.
r: Going back in time with doubling means halving at each step.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Monday, which day will the 24th be?
f: From the 14th to the 24th is 10 days. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days ahead of Monday: Thursday.
r: Divide the gap by 7 and move forward by the remainder.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, which day will the 24th be?
f: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days. 20 = 14 + 6, so move 6 days ahead of Sunday: Saturday.
r: Moving 6 days ahead is the same as moving 1 day back.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, which day will the 28th be?
f: From the 2nd to the 28th is 26 days. 26 = 21 + 5, so move 5 days ahead of Monday: Saturday.
r: Weekdays repeat every 7 days.

q: If the 16th day of a month is Sunday, which day is the 5th of the same month?
f: From the 5th to the 16th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the 5th is 4 days before Sunday: Saturday, Friday, Thursday, Wednesday. So it is Wednesday.
r: For earlier dates, move backwards by the remainder of the gap divided by 7.

q: If the 5th day of a month is Friday, which day is the 23rd?
f: From the 5th to the 23rd is 18 days. 18 = 14 + 4, so move 4 days ahead of Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday. So it is Tuesday.
r: Two full weeks bring the same weekday back.

q: Akbar and Khalid were born in 1970 and 1975 respectively, and Ikram is older than Khalid. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Khalid (1975) is younger than Akbar (1970), and Ikram is older than Khalid. So Khalid is younger than both and is the youngest.
r: In age puzzles, a later birth year means a younger person.

q: A bus carries 500 passengers, of which 350 are men and the rest are women. What percentage of the passengers are women?
r: Men are 70% and women 30%, so the two add up to 100%.

q: Out of 1200 students, 800 boys are present. What percentage of the students are present?
f: Percentage present = 800/1200 x 100 = 2/3 x 100 = 66.67%.
r: 2/3 as a percentage is about 66.67%.

q: In which year CE did Abu Jahal die?
f: Abu Jahal was killed in the Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
r: Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.

q: In which year was the national flag of Pakistan adopted?
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the flag on 11 August 1947, a few days before independence.
r: The flag was designed on the basis of the Muslim League flag, with a white stripe for minorities.

q: An adverb is a word that mainly modifies a what?
f: An adverb mainly modifies a verb. It can also modify an adjective or another adverb.
r: Adjectives, in contrast, modify nouns and pronouns.

q: Which name of Allah means the Most Merciful?
f: Ar-Rahim means the Most Merciful (the Ever-Merciful).
r: Ar-Rahman is usually translated as the Most Gracious or the Beneficent.

q: Ahmed is 5 years old and Sara is three times his age. How old will Sara be when Ahmed is 11? (2)
f: Sara is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmed becomes 11 after 6 years, so Sara will be 15 + 6 = 21.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: Akbar is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 8?
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 now. Akbar becomes 8 after 5 years, so she will be 9 + 5 = 14.
r: Both people age by the same number of years.

q: Why did the United States enter World War II in December 1941? (2)
o: Japan attacked its naval base at Pearl Harbor
f: Japan carried out a surprise air attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
r: Germany and Italy then declared war on the United States a few days later.

q: What is the spread of cultural traits from one society to another called?
f: Cultural diffusion is the transfer of ideas, customs and technology from one society to another. Cultural diversity only means many cultures exist together.
r: Cultural lag means material culture changes faster than beliefs and values.

q: What is the antonym of 'delight'?
f: Delight means great pleasure, so its opposite is sorrow or misery. The other options are synonyms.
r: Another opposite of delight is displeasure.

q: What is the antonym of 'fragile'?
f: Fragile means easily broken, so the opposite is sturdy or strong. Delicate, brittle and weak are close in meaning to fragile.
r: The word fragile comes from the Latin fragilis, meaning easily broken.

q: What is the antonym of 'secret'?
f: Secret means kept hidden from others, so the opposite is public or open. The other options are synonyms.
r: Overt is another opposite of secret in formal English.

q: What is the antonym of 'terrifying'?
f: Terrifying means causing great fear, so the opposite is comforting or soothing. The others are synonyms.
r: Reassuring is another good opposite of terrifying.

q: What is the antonym of 'condensed'?
f: Condensed means made shorter or more compact, so the opposite is expanded. The other options mean the same as condensed.
r: In science, condensation is the change of a gas into a liquid.

q: What is the antonym of 'idleness'?
f: Idleness means doing no work, so the opposite is industry, meaning hard work. Laziness and sloth are synonyms.
r: The proverb says an idle mind is the devil's workshop.

q: The Arabian Sea is a part of which ocean?
f: The Arabian Sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean. It lies between India, Pakistan, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.
r: Pakistan's coastline along the Arabian Sea is about 1000 kilometres long.

q: The separation of Bangladesh in 1971 benefited which neighbouring country the most?
f: India supported the separation and fought the 1971 war, which weakened its rival Pakistan. India therefore gained strategically.
r: The 1971 war ended with the surrender of about 90000 Pakistani personnel.

q: What does ADB stand for?
f: ADB is the Asian Development Bank, which lends money to Asian countries for development. Pakistan is one of its members.
r: The ADB headquarters is in Manila, Philippines.

q: What is the logarithm of a number to its own base?
f: By definition, log base a of a equals 1 because a raised to the power 1 is a. For example, log 10 to base 10 is 1.
r: The logarithm of 1 to any base is 0.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, who is the head of government?
o: The Speaker of the National Assembly
f: Pakistan has a parliamentary system. The Prime Minister heads the government and the President is the head of state.
r: The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly.

q: On which date of Ramadan was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH, which is March 624 CE.
r: It is also called Youm-e-Furqan.

q: How many population censuses had Pakistan held up to the 2023 census, including it?
f: Censuses were held in 1951, 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998, 2017 and 2023, which makes seven.
r: The 2023 census was the first fully digital census of Pakistan.

q: Salman said that Ali ___ ill. Which option correctly completes this reported speech sentence?
f: In reported speech, a past reporting verb (said) changes the present tense of the original statement to the past tense, so is becomes was.
r: Direct speech: Salman said, "Ali is ill"; reported speech: Salman said that Ali was ill.

q: Which event led the United States to enter World War 2 in December 1941?
o: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
f: On 7 December 1941 Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor in Hawaii, and the US declared war on Japan the next day.
r: The war in Europe had already begun in September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.

q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: I hate being laughed ___.
f: The phrasal verb is laugh at, so the passive form is being laughed at.
r: Similar verb and preposition pairs are look at, listen to and depend on.

q: When was Chaudhry Rahmat Ali, who coined the name Pakistan, born?
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali was born on 16 November 1897 in Balachaur, in East Punjab.
r: He published the pamphlet Now or Never in 1933 in which the name Pakistan was proposed.

q: In linear programming, what is a point of the solution region where two of its boundary lines intersect called?
f: A vertex of the feasible region, where two boundary lines meet, is called a corner point.
r: The maximum or minimum of the objective function always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region.

q: Fill in the blank: Go there ___ bus.
f: We use by with a means of transport when no article is used, as in by bus, by train, by car.
r: With an article we say on the bus or in the car.

q: What is the capital of Gambia?
f: Banjul is the capital of Gambia, a small West African country.
r: Gambia is surrounded on land by Senegal.

q: What is the capital of Switzerland?
f: Bern is the federal city and seat of the Swiss government, although many people wrongly think Geneva or Zurich is the capital.
r: Geneva hosts many international organisations such as the UN European office.

q: Fill in the blank: That was ___ I was born.
f: The year is correct because the sentence refers to one specific year, so the definite article is needed.
r: The article an is used only before a vowel sound, so an year is always wrong.

q: On which date did Makkah fall to the Muslims in the Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)? (2)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 AD) for the conquest. The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah peacefully.
r: Sources differ slightly, some give 10 or 17 Ramadan 8 AH.

q: On which date did Pakistan come into being according to the Islamic calendar?
f: Pakistan was created on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, a Friday. It was also the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) in many accounts.
r: The date 27 Rajab is Shab-e-Miraj, not Pakistan's birth.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 12, 24, ?
f: Each number is double the previous one: 3x2=6, 6x2=12, 12x2=24, so 24x2=48.
r: This is a geometric series with common ratio 2.

q: Which number comes next: 80, 70, 62, 56, ?
f: The differences are -10, -8, -6, so the next difference is -4. Thus 56 - 4 = 52.
r: The differences themselves form an arithmetic series.

q: A helicopter covers 240 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons are needed for the next 400 km?
f: Fuel per km is 50/240 gallons. For 400 km: 400 x 50 / 240 = 83 1/3 gallons.
r: This is a direct proportion question.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of all the armed forces of Pakistan?
o: The Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
f: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces. The Prime Minister runs the government.
r: The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.

q: In which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
f: The Sahara lies across North Africa. It is the largest hot desert in the world.
r: It covers an area of about 9 million square kilometres.

q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning a person who does something for pleasure and not as a job?
f: The correct spelling is amateur. It comes from the French word for lover.
r: The opposite word is professional.

q: In which part of Pakistan is K2 located?
f: K2 is in the Karakoram range in Gilgit-Baltistan, on the border with China. It is 8611 metres high.
r: K2 is the second highest peak in the world.

q: What is the currency of North Korea?
f: North Korea uses the North Korean won. South Korea uses the South Korean won.
r: Its capital is Pyongyang.

q: Change into passive voice: I take exercise daily.
o: Exercise is taken by me daily.
Exercise was taken by me daily.
Exercise is being taken by me daily.
Exercise has been taken by me daily.
f: The sentence is in the simple present, so the passive uses is or are plus the past participle. So it becomes Exercise is taken by me daily.
r: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.

q: The Darling is a famous what, located in Australia?
f: The Darling is a river in Australia that joins the Murray River. It is about 1,500 km long.
r: The Murray-Darling basin is Australia's main river system.

q: A is the father of B, but B is not a daughter. What is B to A?
f: B is a child of A and is not a daughter, so B is a son.
r: The relation of A to B is father.

q: Who wrote the book Daughter of Destiny? (4)
f: Daughter of Destiny is the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, published in 1989. It was later reissued as Daughter of the East.
r: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan.

q: Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration signed in 1966?
f: It ended the 1965 war between India and Pakistan. The Soviet Union mediated it.
r: It was signed in January 1966.

q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of a province of Pakistan?
f: Maryam Nawaz became Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024, the first woman to hold the post in any province. She belongs to PML-N.
r: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman Prime Minister.

q: Which is the largest river of China?
f: The Yangtze is about 6,300 km long and is the longest river in China and Asia. The Yellow River is second.
r: It flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.

q: Lyallpur is the old name of which Pakistani city? (2)
f: Lyallpur was renamed Faisalabad in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia. It was named after Sir James Lyall.
r: Faisalabad is famous for textiles.

q: The city of Savannah is located in which country?
f: Savannah is a historic port city in Georgia, United States. It lies on the Savannah River.
r: A savannah is also a type of grassland.

q: What is the term for a line that meets another line at an angle of 90 degrees?
f: Two lines that meet at a right angle (90 degrees) are called perpendicular lines. Parallel lines never meet.
r: Perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is minus 1.

q: In a geometric progression, the constant ratio between consecutive terms is denoted by which letter?
f: In a geometric progression each term is the previous term multiplied by a fixed number called the common ratio, written r. The nth term is a times r to the power n minus 1.
r: In an arithmetic progression the common difference is denoted by d.

q: What is the derivative of cos(2x) with respect to x?
f: By the chain rule, the derivative of cos(u) is -sin(u) times du/dx. With u = 2x, du/dx = 2, so the answer is -2 sin(2x).
r: The derivative of sin(2x) is 2 cos(2x).

q: A decimal number that ends after a finite number of digits (for example 0.25) is called what?
f: A decimal with a finite number of digits after the point is a terminating decimal. It can always be written as a fraction.
r: A recurring decimal such as 0.333... has digits that repeat forever.

q: Change into direct speech: He told me that he was playing a game.
o: He said to me, "I was playing a game."
He said to me, "He is playing a game."
He said to me, "I am playing a game."
He said to me, "I will play a game."
f: In direct speech the reported past continuous tense changes back to the present continuous, and 'he' becomes 'I'. So the sentence is: He said to me, "I am playing a game."
r: When changing indirect to direct speech, 'told' usually becomes 'said to'.

q: Change into direct speech: She said to me that she was watching TV.
o: She said to me, "I am watching TV."
She said to me, "She was watching TV."
She said to me, "I will watch TV."
She said to me, "I have watched TV."
f: The past continuous 'was watching' goes back to the present continuous 'am watching', and 'she' becomes 'I'.
r: Direct speech is always written inside quotation marks.

q: Rearrange the jumbled letters 'EBAUYT' to make a meaningful English word.
f: The six letters E, B, A, U, Y, T can be arranged to spell BEAUTY.
r: Beauty is a noun meaning the quality of being pleasing to the eye or mind.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves twice as fast as the car. How much time will the train take to cover 30 km?
f: Speed of train = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. Time = 30 / 120 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.
r: Time equals distance divided by speed.

q: Which gas is mostly named as the main greenhouse gas causing global warming in textbooks? (2)
f: Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels is the main greenhouse gas added by human activity. It traps heat in the atmosphere.
r: Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas, but its amount is controlled by temperature, so sources can differ on which is primary.

q: There are 24 students in a class and the number of boys is double the number of girls. How many girls are there?
f: Let girls = x, then boys = 2x, so 3x = 24 and x = 8. There are 8 girls and 16 boys.
r: Ratio boys to girls here is 2:1, so girls are one third of the class.

q: The total number of students is 1500 and 340 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
r: Boys are 340/1500 x 100 = 22.67%, and the two percentages add up to 100.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st day of that month be?
f: From the 7th to the 21st is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. After whole weeks the day stays the same, so it is Friday.
r: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.

q: Perpendicular divided by hypotenuse gives which trigonometric ratio?
f: In a right-angled triangle, sin of an angle = perpendicular / hypotenuse. Cos = base / hypotenuse and tan = perpendicular / base.
r: A memory aid is SOH CAH TOA: Sin = Opposite/Hypotenuse, Cos = Adjacent/Hypotenuse, Tan = Opposite/Adjacent.

q: Which is greater: -15 or -20?
f: On the number line, a number further to the right is greater. -15 lies to the right of -20, so -15 is greater.
r: Among negative numbers, the one closer to zero is the greater number.

q: Arrange the letters AGRMYNE to form the name of a country.
f: The letters A, G, R, M, Y, N, E can be rearranged to spell GERMANY, a country in Europe.
r: The capital of Germany is Berlin.

q: Who started the FIFA World Cup, as the FIFA president who proposed the tournament?
f: Jules Rimet, a Frenchman and FIFA president from 1921 to 1954, drove the idea of the World Cup. The first tournament was held in Uruguay in 1930.
r: The original World Cup trophy was named the Jules Rimet Trophy.

q: According to grammar, what part of speech is the word 'hey'?
f: 'Hey' is a word used to express sudden feeling or to get attention, so it is an interjection.
r: Other interjections are 'oh', 'wow', 'alas' and 'hurrah'.

q: A car runs at half the speed of a train that travels at 60 km/h. How far will the car go in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 30 x 1/2 = 15 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, so time must be in hours when speed is in km/h.

q: What is half of 1/90?
r: Taking half of a fraction doubles its denominator.

q: The Hazara people of Afghanistan and Pakistan are commonly said to be descended from whom?
f: The most common view is that the Hazara descend from Mongol (and Turkic) troops of Genghis Khan who settled in central Afghanistan in the 13th century.
r: Sources differ on exact origins, and the Hazara speak Hazaragi, a dialect of Persian.

q: What is Hilal-e-Imtiaz?
o: The second highest civil award of Pakistan
The highest military gallantry award of Pakistan
The highest civil award of Pakistan
f: Hilal-e-Imtiaz is the second highest civil award of Pakistan, given for excellence in fields such as arts, sports, science and public service.
r: The highest civil award of Pakistan is Nishan-e-Pakistan.

q: Which city is considered the hottest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: Dera Ismail Khan in the southern plains of KPK regularly records the highest summer temperatures in the province, around 45 to 50 degrees Celsius.
r: The hottest city of Pakistan overall is usually given as Jacobabad in Sindh.

q: What is 24 minutes past 10 pm in 24-hour format?
f: 10 pm = 22:00 in 24-hour time. Adding 24 minutes gives 22:24, written 2224.
r: To convert pm time to 24-hour format, add 12 to the hour (except 12 pm).

q: Who was Habba Khatoon?
o: A Kashmiri poetess known as the Nightingale of Kashmir
A queen of the Mughal Empire
f: Habba Khatoon was a 16th century Kashmiri poetess and the wife of Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak. She is known for her songs of love and longing.
r: She is called the Nightingale of Kashmir.

q: What is the date of Independence Day of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947 as a result of the Indian Independence Act 1947.
r: India celebrates its Independence Day on 15 August.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word justice?
f: Justice means fair treatment, so its opposite is injustice, which means unfair treatment.
r: The prefix in- is often added to a word to make its opposite.

q: On which date did the 1999 Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India end?
f: The fighting in the Kargil sector began in early May 1999 and ended on 26 July 1999 when the last operations were over.
r: 26 July is observed in India as Kargil Vijay Diwas.

q: Mount Godwin-Austen is another name of which mountain?
f: K2 was named Mount Godwin-Austen after the British surveyor Henry Haversham Godwin-Austen who explored the area.
r: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8611 metres.

q: Which country is called the Land of the Midnight Sun?
f: In summer, parts of northern Norway have daylight all night, so it is called the Land of the Midnight Sun.
r: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun.

q: Which country has the largest number of islands in the world?
f: Sweden has about 267,000 islands, the most of any country, though most are very small.
r: Indonesia has the most islands among large island nations, about 17,000.

q: Which is the largest city of Japan?
f: Tokyo is the capital and the most populous city of Japan.
r: Osaka and Yokohama are other large Japanese cities.

q: According to the Economic Survey of Pakistan 2025-26, what is Pakistan's literacy rate (population aged 10 and above)?
f: The Economic Survey 2025-26, released in June 2026, gave the literacy rate as 63 percent, up from about 61 percent the year before.
r: Older reports gave around 60 percent in 2023 and 53 percent in earlier years; Punjab has the highest provincial rate.

q: The Margalla Hills of Islamabad are an extension of which mountain range? (2)
f: The Margalla Hills are the foothills at the western end of the Himalayas.
r: Margalla Hills National Park lies in the north of Islamabad.

q: What is a matrix called in which all the entries are zero?
f: A matrix whose every entry is zero is called a zero matrix or null matrix. It is the additive identity for matrices of the same order.
r: Adding a zero matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.

q: In statistics, what is the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value of a data set called?
f: Range is the largest value minus the smallest value in the data. For example, in 3, 7, 12 the range is 12 - 3 = 9.
r: Range is the simplest measure of how spread out data is.

q: What does the idiom 'call it a day' mean?
f: To call it a day means to stop what you are doing and finish for the time being. It is used when one has done enough work.
r: A similar idiom is 'call it a night'.

q: What is an interjection in English grammar?
o: A word that expresses sudden emotion, such as Wow or Alas
A word that names a person or place
A word that describes a noun
A word that joins two sentences
f: An interjection is a word or short phrase that shows sudden feeling like surprise, joy or pain. Examples are Oh, Hurrah and Alas.
r: An interjection is usually followed by an exclamation mark.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Monday, which day is the 25th of that month?
f: From the 12th to the 25th is 13 days. 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6, so Monday plus 6 days is Sunday.
r: Any two dates 7 days apart fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Monday, which day is the 15th of that month?
f: From the 3rd to the 15th is 12 days. 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
r: The 10th and 17th of that month are also Mondays.

q: Who built the Mohabbat Khan Mosque in Peshawar?
o: Nawab Mohabbat Khan, Mughal governor of Peshawar
f: The mosque was built around 1630 by Nawab Mohabbat Khan, the Mughal governor of Peshawar under Emperor Shah Jahan.
r: It is one of the best known Mughal-era mosques of Peshawar.

q: On which date was the Quit India resolution passed by the Indian National Congress in 1942?
f: The Quit India resolution was passed at Bombay on 8 August 1942 and the movement began the next day. It demanded an end to British rule in India.
r: Gandhi gave the call Do or Die during this movement.

q: What is 6 multiplied by 5?
f: 6 x 5 means five sixes: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 30.
r: The multiplication table of 6 is 6, 12, 18, 24, 30.

q: Which countries are the five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council?
o: USA, UK, France, Russia and China
USA, UK, France, Germany and Japan
USA, UK, Russia, India and China
USA, France, Germany, Russia and China
f: The five permanent members (P5) are the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia and China. Each has the power of veto.
r: Pakistan has been elected a non-permanent member of the Security Council several times, most recently for 2025-2026.

q: Which country has won the most Olympic medals of all time? (3)
f: The United States has the highest total of medals in the history of the Summer Olympic Games, well ahead of any other country.
r: Some tables count the former Soviet Union separately, but it still stays behind the United States.

q: What was the capital of the Ottoman Empire after 1453?
f: Sultan Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 and made it the Ottoman capital. It remained the capital until the empire ended in 1922.
r: Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923.

q: Who coined the name Pakistan? (2)
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in his pamphlet Now or Never.
r: Allama Iqbal had given the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

q: What is negative two divided by negative two?
f: A negative number divided by a negative number gives a positive result. So (-2) divided by (-2) = 1.
r: Any non-zero number divided by itself is equal to 1.

q: What is the scattering (spread) of a set of numbers called in statistics?
f: Dispersion means how much the values are spread out. Range, variance and standard deviation are measures of dispersion.
r: Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency.

q: A function in which different elements of the domain have different images in the range is called what?
f: In a one-one function, no two different inputs give the same output. Such a function is also called injective.
r: A function that is both one-one and onto is called bijective.

q: Hens and cows together have 48 heads and 140 legs. How many hens are there? (3)
f: Let hens be h and cows c. h + c = 48 and 2h + 4c = 140, so h + 2c = 70. Subtracting gives c = 22, so h = 48 - 22 = 26.
r: Check: 26 hens have 52 legs and 22 cows have 88 legs, which total 140.

q: In which mountain range is Broad Peak located?
f: Broad Peak (8,051 m) lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border, near K2.
r: Broad Peak is the 12th highest mountain in the world.

q: If 40 percent of a number is 56, what is the number?
f: 40 percent of x = 56, so x = 56 times 100 divided by 40 = 140.
r: Check: 40 percent of 140 is 56.

q: A period of ten years is also known as what?
f: A decade means ten years.
r: A century is 100 years and a millennium is 1000 years.

q: How many Pakistanis have won the Nobel Prize in Physics?
f: Only Dr Abdus Salam won it, in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg.
r: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.

q: From which substance do plants obtain hydrogen for making food?
f: In photosynthesis, water splits and gives hydrogen, which is used with carbon dioxide to make glucose.
r: Plants take in water through their roots.

q: Between which two teams was the first Test cricket match played?
f: The first Test was played at Melbourne in 1877 between Australia and England.
r: Australia won that match by 45 runs.

q: What is the lowest point of Pakistan?
o: Sea level at the Arabian Sea coast
f: The lowest point is the coast of the Arabian Sea at 0 m.
r: The highest point of Pakistan is K2.

q: What is the probability of getting a tail when a fair coin is tossed once? (2)
f: There are 2 equally likely outcomes and one is a tail, so probability is 1/2.
r: The probability of a sure event is 1.

q: Which Prophet (AS) was swallowed by a whale (big fish)?
f: The Quran tells that Hazrat Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a big fish and he prayed to Allah for forgiveness.
r: He is also called Dhun-Nun, the one of the fish.

q: Which authority provides water supply and sewerage services in big cities such as Lahore?
f: WASA is the Water and Sanitation Agency of the city development authorities.
r: WAPDA looks after water and power development at national level.

q: A book is bought for 40 rupees and sold for 40 rupees. What is the profit?
f: Profit = selling price minus cost price = 40 - 40 = 0.
r: When selling price equals cost price there is no profit and no loss.

q: In which year did Queen Victoria die?
f: Queen Victoria died on 22 January 1901.
r: She became Empress of India in 1876.

q: Which pass connects Quetta with Sibi?
f: The Bolan Pass lies in Balochistan between Quetta and Sibi.
r: Khojak Pass connects Quetta with Kandahar in Afghanistan.

q: Who was the first woman pilot of Pakistan? (2)
f: Shukriya Khanum earned a commercial pilot licence in 1959 and was the first Pakistani woman pilot.
r: Ayesha Farooq became the first woman fighter pilot of the PAF in 2013.

q: The Hunza River is located in which region of Pakistan?
f: The Hunza River flows through the Hunza valley in Gilgit-Baltistan and joins the Gilgit River.
r: The Karakoram Highway runs along the Hunza valley up to the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Who presides over the sessions of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The Speaker is the presiding officer who runs the business and sessions of the National Assembly.
r: In the absence of the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker presides.

q: Change into passive voice: Mary said that she was sorry.
o: It was said by Mary that she was sorry.
Mary was said that she was sorry.
That she was sorry has said Mary.
f: For reported speech, the passive form starts with It was said by, followed by the that clause unchanged.
r: The reporting verb said changes to was said in the passive.

q: What is the meaning of the name Muhammad (SAW)? (2)
f: Muhammad comes from the Arabic root h-m-d and means the one who is praised again and again.
r: Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), also comes from the same root.

q: On which date did Pakistan become a full member of the SCO?
f: Pakistan, along with India, became a full member at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.
r: Pakistan had been an observer since 2005.

q: How many full member countries does the SCO have after Belarus joined in 2024?
f: The members are China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus, which makes ten.
r: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in July 2024.

q: Who scored the first Test double century for Pakistan?
f: Wicketkeeper Imtiaz Ahmed scored 209 against New Zealand at Lahore in October 1955.
r: Hanif Mohammad later made 337 against West Indies in 1958.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats in the National Assembly are reserved in total (women and non-Muslims)?
f: 60 seats are reserved for women and 10 for non-Muslim minorities, so 60 plus 10 = 70.
r: Reserved seats are filled through proportional representation of the parties.

q: Which legislative assembly in Pakistan has the highest number of seats?
f: The Punjab Provincial Assembly has 371 seats, more than the National Assembly (336) and all other assemblies.
r: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five senses of a human being?
f: The five traditional senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Balance is not counted in them.
r: Balance is sensed by the inner ear.

q: What comes next in the series: X1, YY3, ZZZ5, ?
f: The letters go X, Y, Z, A in order and each letter is repeated one more time (1, 2, 3, 4 times). The numbers go up by 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next term is AAAA7.
r: After Z the alphabet starts again from A in such series.

q: What comes next in the series: Z1, X3, U6, Q10, L15, ?
f: Letters move back by 2, 3, 4, 5 and then 6 places: Z, X, U, Q, L, F. Numbers go up by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, so the next term is F21.
r: The numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.

q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
f: The word pentagon comes from the Greek penta meaning five, so it has five sides.
r: The sum of the interior angles of a pentagon is 540 degrees.

q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old is the sister?
f: Sister's age = 2 x 6 = 12 years.
r: The age difference between them is 6 years and it never changes.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'embellish'?
f: 'Embellish' means almost the same as 'adorn'.
r: Its opposite is a word such as 'disfigure'.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'specify'?
f: 'Specify' means almost the same as 'state clearly'.
r: The noun form is 'specification'.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'weird'?
f: 'Weird' means almost the same as 'strange'.
r: Its opposite is 'normal'.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'contemporary'?
f: 'Contemporary' means almost the same as 'modern'.
r: It can also mean living or existing at the same time.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'dearth'?
f: 'Dearth' means almost the same as 'scarcity'.
r: Its opposite is 'abundance'.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'absolute'?
f: 'Absolute' means almost the same as 'complete'.
r: An absolute monarch has complete power.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'spontaneous'?
f: 'Spontaneous' means almost the same as 'impulsive'.
r: Its opposite is 'planned' or 'deliberate'.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (synonym) to 'supervision'?
f: 'Supervision' means almost the same as 'oversight'.
r: The person who supervises is called a supervisor.

q: On which river is the Tanda Dam (Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa) built?
f: Tanda Dam is in Kohat District and is filled with water of the Kohat Toi stream. It supplies irrigation water to nearby villages.
r: Tanda Dam was declared a Ramsar wetland site in 1976.

q: Find the next term in the series: 3/6, 6/9, 10/15, 15/24, ?
f: Numerators 3, 6, 10, 15 increase by 3, 4, 5, so next is 15 + 6 = 21. Denominators 6, 9, 15, 24 increase by 3, 6, 9, so next is 24 + 12 = 36. The term is 21/36.
r: The numerators 3, 6, 10, 15, 21 are called triangular numbers.

q: Ali is 5 years old and Ayesha is twice his age. What will be Ayesha's age when Ali is 15 years old?
f: Ayesha's present age = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali becomes 15 after 10 years, so Ayesha will be 10 + 10 = 20 years.
r: Ayesha is 5 years older than Ali, so she is always 5 years older.

q: In which year did Turkey become a republic and gain its modern independent status under Mustafa Kemal Ataturk?
f: The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in July 1923, and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923.
r: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk was the first President of Turkey and died in 1938.

q: What type of equation is 2y = 1 + x?
f: Both x and y have power 1 only, so the highest degree is one. Such an equation is linear and its graph is a straight line.
r: A quadratic equation has a highest power of 2.

q: Which is considered the oldest university in the world still in operation?
f: Al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco was founded in 859 AD by Fatima al-Fihri. UNESCO and the Guinness World Records recognise it as the oldest.
r: Some sources name Al-Azhar (970 AD) or Bologna (1088) depending on the definition used.

q: When did the Indus Valley Civilization flourish, according to commonly taught dates? (2)
f: Pakistani textbooks give the period of the Indus Valley Civilization as about 2500 BC to 1500 BC. Its main cities were Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro.
r: Some modern sources give the mature phase as 2600 BC to 1900 BC, so dates differ between sources.

q: Between which two values does probability always lie?
f: Probability of an impossible event is 0 and of a certain event is 1. Every other event lies between these two values.
r: Probability is often also written as a percentage between 0 percent and 100 percent.

q: What is the range of the values 15, 7, 11, 10, 2, 3?
f: Range = largest value minus smallest value = 15 - 2 = 13.
r: Range is a measure of spread of data.

q: What type of verb is 'could'?
f: Could is a modal auxiliary (helping) verb. It is the past form of can and shows ability or possibility.
r: Other modal verbs are can, may, might, must, shall, should, will and would.

q: Choose the correct word: This jacket is very ___.
f: Very is followed by an adjective, and expensive is the correct adjective here. Much cheap and high do not fit the sentence.
r: Much is normally used with uncountable nouns, not directly before adjectives.

q: How many vowels are there in the letters: A E Z Y U A W O L U E?
f: The vowels are A, E, U, A, O, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are there in: A G I F O M E J I U Y X E?
f: The vowels are A, I, O, E, I, U, E. That makes 7 vowels.
r: Y is counted as a consonant in such counting questions.

q: Under whose government was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960?
f: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by President Ayub Khan of Pakistan and Prime Minister Nehru of India.
r: The World Bank was a signatory as the broker of the treaty.

q: Which bowler has taken the most wickets for Pakistan in international cricket (all formats combined)?
f: Wasim Akram took 414 Test and 502 ODI wickets, about 916 in international cricket, which is the most by any Pakistani bowler.
r: Wasim Akram is a left-arm fast bowler who captained Pakistan to the 1992 World Cup win as a key player.

q: Which movement launched in 1920 asked Indians to refuse to cooperate with British rule?
f: The Non-Cooperation Movement, led by Gandhi with Khilafat support, asked people to boycott British schools, courts and goods.
r: The Quit India Movement came later, in 1942.

q: Who wrote the famous travel book Rehla?
f: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan traveller, dictated his travels in the Rihla (Rehla) around 1355.
