r: Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq.

q: Ammar is older than Amjad, and Ali is younger than Ammar. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Ammar is older than both Amjad and Ali, so Ammar is the oldest.
r: The order of Amjad and Ali cannot be known from this information.

q: Saba is twice as old as her sister, and her sister is 8 years younger than Saba. How old will Saba be when her sister is 15?
f: Let sister be x, so Saba is 2x and 2x - x = 8, giving x = 8 and Saba = 16. Sister reaches 15 after 7 years, so Saba is 16 + 7 = 23.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

q: What is the result when zero is multiplied by any number?
f: Any number multiplied by zero gives zero.
r: This is called the zero property of multiplication.

q: What is the value of 2 + 1/2?
r: 2.5 can also be written as 5/2.

q: What is 80/80?
f: Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
r: Division of a number by 1 gives the same number.

q: What happened in the First Battle of Panipat? (4)
o: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi on 21 April 1526
Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas in 1761
f: On 21 April 1526 Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat, which began Mughal rule in India.
r: Babur used cannons and matchlocks, which gave him the victory.

q: Articles (a, an, the) are used mainly before which part of speech? (2)
f: An article is a word that comes before a noun (or its adjective) to show whether it is specific or general.
r: The word the is the definite article, while a and an are indefinite articles.

q: In which ghazwa (battle campaign) did the Muslims return to Madinah without any fighting? (2)
f: In Ghazwa Tabuk (9 AH) the Byzantine army withdrew, so the Muslim army returned to Madinah without a battle.
r: Tabuk was the last ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH) himself.

q: Who became the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in Pakistan (Balochistan High Court, 2018)? (2)
f: Justice Syeda Tahira Safdar took oath as Chief Justice of the Balochistan High Court on 1 September 2018, the first woman to hold such a post in Pakistan.
r: She was also the first woman civil judge in Balochistan.

q: What was the currency of France before the Euro? (2)
f: France used the French franc until it was replaced by the Euro (notes and coins from 2002).
r: The mark was the German currency and the lira was the Italian currency before the Euro.

q: What is the capital of Sierra Leone? (2)
f: Freetown is the capital and largest city of Sierra Leone.
r: Monrovia is the capital of neighbouring Liberia.

q: Since which year has Pakistan celebrated Defence Day on 6 September? (2)
f: The war with India took place in September 1965. The first Defence Day was observed on 6 September 1966, one year after the war.
r: Defence Day honours the armed forces for defending the country on 6 September 1965.

q: Which keyboard key is used for spell check in Microsoft Word? (2)
f: Pressing F7 starts the spelling and grammar check in Word.
r: F12 opens the Save As dialog in Word.

q: Where do the Jhelum and Chenab rivers meet? (3)
f: The Jhelum joins the Chenab at Trimmu near Jhang in Punjab.
r: The combined Chenab later meets the Ravi and Sutlej to form the Panjnad.

q: What are the ambassadors of Commonwealth countries to each other called? (2)
f: Commonwealth members exchange High Commissioners instead of ambassadors.
r: Pakistan has a High Commissioner in London.

q: In which country was the 1955 Bandung (Asian-African) conference, the forerunner of the Non-Aligned Movement, held? (2)
f: The Asian-African Conference of April 1955 was held in Bandung, Indonesia.
r: The Non-Aligned Movement itself was formally founded in Belgrade in 1961.

q: In a room, males are 3/2 of the females and the room has 30 people. How many females are in the room? (2)
f: Let females be F. Males are 1.5F, so F + 1.5F = 2.5F = 30. Then F = 12 and males = 18.
r: The male to female ratio here is 3 to 2.

q: What is the integral of cot x with respect to x? (3)
f: cot x = cos x / sin x. Put u = sin x, then du = cos x dx, so the integral is ln|u| + C = ln|sin x| + C.
r: The integral of tan x is -ln|cos x| + C.

q: Which three countries are known as the Baltic states? (2)
f: The Baltic states are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea.
r: All three joined NATO and the European Union in 2004.

q: What is the process of cutting away the unwanted area of an image called? (2)
f: Cropping removes the outer unwanted parts of a picture.
r: Resizing changes the whole size of a picture without removing parts.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Mirani Dam located? (2)
f: Mirani Dam is on the Dasht River in Kech district near Turbat, Balochistan.
r: It supplies water to Turbat and Gwadar areas.

q: Who founded the Urdu Defence Association in 1900? (2)
f: Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk formed the Urdu Defence Association in 1900 to protect Urdu during the Hindi-Urdu controversy.
r: The controversy began when UP governor Anthony MacDonnell favoured Hindi in 1900.

q: What is the circumference of the Earth at the equator? (2)
f: The Earth's equatorial circumference is about 40,075 km.
r: Its circumference through the poles is slightly smaller, about 40,008 km.

q: Which nutrient is the best source of quick energy for an athlete? (2)
f: Carbohydrates are broken into glucose, which the body can use fastest for energy.
r: Fats give more energy per gram but release it slowly.

q: In which Hijri year did fasting in Ramadan (Roza) become farz? (2)
f: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in 2 AH, in Madinah.
r: The first Ramadan fasts were kept in the same year as the Battle of Badr.

q: Which of the following is a main function of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)? (2)
o: Promoting exchange rate stability and giving short-term loans to countries with balance of payments problems
Printing the currency of member countries
Fixing the price of oil for member countries
Giving military aid to member countries
f: The IMF works for international monetary cooperation and stable exchange rates, and lends to countries facing balance of payments difficulties.
r: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington D.C. and was established in 1944 at Bretton Woods.

q: Which vitamin helps in the healing of wounds? (2)
f: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is needed to make collagen, which repairs skin and wounds.
r: Deficiency of vitamin C causes scurvy.

q: Kalam Valley is located in which district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (2)
f: Kalam is a popular valley at the top of the Swat valley in Swat district.
r: The Swat river starts near Kalam from the Ushu and Utror streams.

q: The Khojak Pass in Balochistan lies in Qila Abdullah district and leads towards which border town? (2)
f: The Khojak Pass in the Khwaja Amran range leads from Qila Abdullah to Chaman on the Afghan border.
r: The Khojak Rail Tunnel is one of the longest railway tunnels in Pakistan.

q: Which country has the lengthiest written constitution in the world? (3)
f: The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.
r: It was adopted in 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

q: In which year was the Badshahi Mosque of Lahore built? (5)
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.
r: For centuries it was the largest mosque in the world by capacity, and it stands opposite Lahore Fort.

q: In which area of Pakistan is the largest coal reserve found? (2)
f: The Thar coalfield in Sindh holds about 175 billion tonnes of lignite coal, the largest reserve in Pakistan.
r: Thar coal is now used to generate electricity near Islamkot.

q: What were the old names of India? (2)
f: India has been called Hindustan, Bharat and Bharatvarsha since ancient times.
r: The name India comes from the River Indus (Sindhu).

q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution presented in the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan? (2)
f: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented the Objectives Resolution on 7 March 1949.
r: It was passed on 12 March 1949.

q: Pakistan opposed the entry of India into which group? (2)
f: India applied for NSG membership in 2016 and Pakistan opposed it, saying it should be treated equally with India.
r: The NSG is a group of countries that controls exports of nuclear material.

q: Pakistan became a full member of which organization in 2017? (2)
f: Pakistan and India became full members of the SCO at the Astana summit in June 2017.
r: Pakistan had been an observer in the SCO since 2005.

q: What is the Pentagon? (2)
o: Headquarters of the US Department of Defense
The residence of the US President
f: The Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia is the headquarters of the United States Department of Defense.
r: It is named after its five-sided shape.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to Prescribe? (2)
f: To prescribe means to order or lay down a rule, which is close to dictate.
r: A doctor prescribes medicine by ordering it for a patient.

q: What does the Saindak Project produce? (2)
f: The Saindak Project in Chagai, Balochistan produces copper, gold and some silver.
r: It is run with Chinese help.

q: The Ziarat Residency in Balochistan is associated with which leader? (2)
f: Quaid-e-Azam spent the last days of his life at the Ziarat Residency in 1948 for rest and treatment.
r: Ziarat is also famous for its juniper forests, among the oldest in the world.

q: Between which two rivers does the Bari Doab lie? (2)
f: A doab is the land between two rivers. The Bari Doab lies between the Ravi and the Beas, with the Sutlej forming its lower boundary.
r: The name Bari Doab comes from the first letters of Beas and Ravi.

q: Which is the longest national highway of Pakistan? (2)
f: The N-5 runs from Karachi to Torkham, about 1,819 km, and is the longest highway in Pakistan.
r: It follows much of the old Grand Trunk Road route.

q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly? (2)
f: Rahila Hameed Khan Durrani was elected Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly in 2008, the first woman in this post.
r: Fehmida Mirza was the first woman Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan.

q: What is the space between the margin and the start of the first line of a paragraph called? (2)
f: Indentation is the blank space left at the start of a line to mark a new paragraph.
r: In justified text, both left and right edges are aligned.

q: How many times is the name of Hazrat Jibrael (AS) mentioned in the Quran? (2)
f: The name Jibreel appears three times, in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:97 and 2:98) and Surah At-Tahrim (66:4).
r: Some counts differ because he is also mentioned as Ruh-ul-Ameen without the name.

q: Atique is the title of which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH)? (2)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is known as Atique, meaning freed from the fire, and also as Siddique.
r: He was the first Caliph of Islam.

q: What is the main purpose of the World Trade Organization (WTO)? (2)
f: The WTO sets and enforces rules for trade between nations and settles trade disputes.
r: The WTO was set up in 1995 and replaced GATT.

q: If a train covers 120 km per hour, how far will it cover in 18 minutes? (2)
f: 18 minutes is 18/60 = 0.3 hour. Distance = 120 x 0.3 = 36 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, and the time must be in hours when the speed is in km per hour.

q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan in 1999?
f: General Pervez Musharraf became Chief of Army Staff in October 1998 and held the post in 1999, including the Kargil conflict and the October 1999 takeover.
r: He remained army chief until November 2007, and his predecessor was General Jahangir Karamat.

q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1971 war?
f: General Yahya Khan was army chief from 1966 and also President in 1971, when the war with India took place.
r: General Gul Hassan Khan took over as army chief on 20 December 1971.

q: Which two soldiers received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the 1999 Kargil conflict?
o: Havaldar Lalak Jan and Captain Karnal Sher Khan
Major Raja Aziz Bhatti and Major Tufail
Sawar Muhammad Hussain and Major Shabbir Sharif
Lance Naik Muhammad Mahfuz and Major Akram
f: Havaldar Lalak Jan (Northern Light Infantry) and Captain Karnal Sher Khan (27 Sindh) were awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil 1999.
r: Karnal Sher Khan was a Captain at the time of his martyrdom and was promoted to Colonel after death.

q: Who persuaded Hazrat Usman (RA) to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) presented Islam to Hazrat Usman (RA), who then accepted it at an early stage of the Prophet's mission.
r: Hazrat Usman (RA) is known as Zun-Noorain because he married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which instrument is used to measure the altitude (angle above the horizon) of the sun?
f: A sextant measures the angle between the horizon and a celestial body such as the sun, which gives its altitude.
r: Sailors use the sextant for navigation by finding their latitude.

q: Near which city did the plane crash that killed General Zia ul Haq in 1988 take place?
f: General Zia ul Haq died on 17 August 1988 when his aircraft crashed shortly after take-off near Bahawalpur.
r: US Ambassador Arnold Raphel and several Pakistani generals also died in the crash.

q: What is the touching or kissing of the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) during Tawaf called?
f: Istilam means touching or kissing the Black Stone, or pointing towards it when the crowd is too large.
r: Tawaf is the circling of the Kaaba seven times.

q: Who is the author of the play Hamlet? (2)
f: Hamlet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare around 1600.
r: Other famous tragedies by Shakespeare are Macbeth, Othello and King Lear.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present the Delhi Proposals?
f: The Delhi Muslim Proposals were put forward by Jinnah in March 1927 as a way to settle Hindu-Muslim differences on the constitution.
r: The year 1916 is that of the Lucknow Pact, and the 14 Points came in 1929.

q: In which city is the cemetery Jannat ul Baqi located?
f: Jannat ul Baqi is the main cemetery of Madinah, close to the Prophet's Mosque.
r: Many family members and Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) are buried there.

q: How many players are there in a baseball team on the field?
f: A baseball team puts nine players on the field at a time.
r: Cricket and football teams have 11 players each.

q: What is the date of birth of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the Gregorian calendar, as commonly given in Pakistani textbooks?
f: Pakistani textbooks commonly give 22 April 571 AD, in the Year of the Elephant, as the birth date.
r: Sources differ slightly, with some giving 20 April 571 AD, and the Islamic date is 12 Rabi ul Awwal in the commonly followed view.

q: Sofia is the capital of which country?
f: Sofia is the largest city and capital of Bulgaria.
r: Bulgaria is a Balkan country on the Black Sea.

q: What is the capital of Haiti?
f: Port-au-Prince is the capital and largest city of Haiti.
r: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, whose capital is Santo Domingo.

q: What is the capital of Honduras?
f: Tegucigalpa is the capital of Honduras.
r: Managua is the capital of Nicaragua.

q: What is the capital of Qatar?
f: Doha is the capital and largest city of Qatar.
r: Qatar hosted the FIFA World Cup in 2022.

q: On which date was the Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline agreement signed in 2010?
f: Iran and Pakistan signed the gas pipeline agreement on 16 March 2010.
r: A formal gas export contract followed in June 2010, and Pakistan's section was inaugurated in March 2013.

q: Which country is well known for having no official capital city?
f: Nauru has no official capital. Its government offices are in the Yaren district, which is treated as the de facto capital.
r: Nauru is the smallest island nation and the smallest republic in the world.

q: Rickets in children is caused by the lack of which vitamin?
f: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium. Without it the bones of children stay soft and bend, which is called rickets.
r: The adult form of this bone softening is called osteomalacia.

q: Which type of cell has no true nucleus?
f: Prokaryotic cells such as bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus. Their DNA lies free in the cytoplasm.
r: Mature red blood cells of humans also lose their nucleus.

q: What is the land area between the Chenab and Jhelum rivers called?
f: The doab between the Jhelum and Chenab is called Chaj Doab, a name made from the first letters of Chenab and Jhelum.
r: The doab between the Ravi and Chenab is called Rachna Doab.

q: In which Chinese city was the first China International Import Expo (CIIE) held in November 2018, which Prime Minister Imran Khan attended?
f: The first CIIE was held in Shanghai from 5 to 10 November 2018. Pakistan took part and Imran Khan visited China at that time.
r: The CIIE is held in Shanghai every November.

q: Where is the headquarters (Secretariat) of the Commonwealth of Nations?
f: The Commonwealth Secretariat is at Marlborough House in London, United Kingdom.
r: The Commonwealth has its own Secretary-General.

q: The Simla Conference, held by Viceroy Lord Wavell to discuss self-government, took place in which year?
f: Lord Wavell called the Simla Conference in June 1945. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League did not agree on Muslim representation.
r: The Wavell Plan was the proposal discussed at the conference.

q: The Tochi Pass links North Waziristan in Pakistan with which Afghan province?
f: The Tochi Pass runs from Bannu and North Waziristan towards Ghazni in Afghanistan.
r: The Tochi River flows through this pass.

q: The Malakand Pass links the Peshawar valley with which regions?
f: The Malakand Pass lies in Malakand district and is the gateway from the Peshawar plain to Swat, Dir and Chitral.
r: The Malakand Pass was the scene of the British campaign of 1897.

q: Which continent consists of only one country?
f: The continent of Australia is one single country, the Commonwealth of Australia.
r: Antarctica has no countries and Europe has more than 40.

q: Which team won the 2003 Cricket World Cup?
f: Australia beat India in the final in Johannesburg, South Africa, in March 2003.
r: Australia was captained by Ricky Ponting.

q: Which of these is a Kharif crop of Pakistan?
f: Kharif crops are sown in summer (April to June) and harvested in autumn. Rice, cotton, maize and sugarcane are Kharif crops.
r: Wheat, gram and mustard are Rabi (winter) crops.

q: Under whose captaincy did Pakistan win the 1992 Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne in 1992 under the captaincy of Imran Khan.
r: This is Pakistan's only Cricket World Cup title so far.

q: Which country won the 2020 Kabaddi World Cup (circle style) held in Lahore?
f: Pakistan beat India 43-41 in the final at Punjab Stadium, Lahore, on 16 February 2020.
r: It was Pakistan's first Kabaddi World Cup title.

q: Kip is the currency of which country?
f: The kip is the national currency of Laos.
r: Cambodia uses the riel and Myanmar uses the kyat.

q: Pound sterling is the currency of which country?
f: Pound sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom.
r: It is one of the oldest currencies still in use.

q: What is the currency of Vatican City?
f: Vatican City uses the euro, although it issues its own euro coins.
r: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world.

q: What is the currency of Vietnam?
f: The Vietnamese dong is the official currency of Vietnam.
r: Hanoi is the capital of Vietnam.

q: On which river is the Ghazi Brotha Dam (barrage) located?
f: Ghazi Barotha is on the Indus River, below Tarbela Dam, in Attock district.
r: It is a run-of-the-river hydropower project of about 1450 MW.

q: On what date did the USSR formally break up?
f: The Supreme Soviet declared the USSR dissolved on 26 December 1991, a day after Gorbachev resigned on 25 December.
r: Russia became the main successor state.

q: In which country is the Great Victoria Desert?
f: The Great Victoria Desert is the largest desert in Australia.
r: It lies in Western and South Australia.

q: Who wrote the book A Discipline Divided: Schools and Sects in Political Science?
f: Gabriel Almond wrote A Discipline Divided in 1988 about the divisions inside political science.
r: Almond is also known for his work on political culture.

q: Who wrote the book The Dividing Discipline: Hierarchy and Diversity in International Theory?
f: K. J. Holsti wrote The Dividing Discipline in 1985 on the state of international relations theory.
r: Holsti is a Finnish-Canadian scholar of international relations.

q: Modern badminton developed from the game Poona played by British army officers in which country?
f: British officers in India (at Pune, called Poona) played it in the 1870s and took it to England, where it was named after Badminton House.
r: Sources differ on small details of the early history of the game.

q: Fort Munro is a hill station in which district?
f: Fort Munro lies in the Sulaiman Mountains in Dera Ghazi Khan district, Punjab.
r: It is one of the few hill stations of Punjab.

q: Which party won the most seats in the 2008 general election in Pakistan?
f: The Pakistan Peoples Party won the most seats in February 2008, and Yousuf Raza Gilani became Prime Minister.
r: The election was held after the death of Benazir Bhutto in December 2007.

q: In which year was the Israeli intelligence agency Mossad established?
f: Mossad was founded on 13 December 1949 and took its present name in 1951.
r: Its full name is the Institute for Intelligence and Special Operations.

q: On what date was the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) established? (2)
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP at a meeting in Lahore on 30 November 1967.
r: The PPP first came to power after the 1970 election.

q: What is the full name of the conqueror of Sindh, Muhammad bin Qasim?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim belonged to the Banu Thaqif tribe of Taif, so he is known as al-Thaqafi.
r: He invaded Sindh in 711-712 AD during the Umayyad rule under governor Hajjaj bin Yusuf.

q: Kahuta Research Laboratories (the Engineering Research Laboratories) were established during the government of which leader?
f: The nuclear programme was started by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, and the Engineering Research Laboratories at Kahuta were set up in 1976 during his government.
r: The laboratories were later renamed Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) in 1981 after Dr A. Q. Khan.

q: Where is the headquarters of the CIA (Central Intelligence Agency) located?
f: The CIA headquarters is in Langley (McLean area), Virginia, near Washington D.C.
r: The CIA was established in 1947 under the National Security Act.

q: In which country is the city of Heidelberg located?
f: Heidelberg is a city in south-western Germany in the state of Baden-Wuerttemberg on the Neckar river.
r: Heidelberg University, founded in 1386, is the oldest university in Germany.

q: Which country has the highest number of satellites in orbit?
f: The United States owns by far the largest number of active satellites, mainly because of large constellations such as Starlink.
r: Sputnik 1 of the Soviet Union in 1957 was the first artificial satellite.

q: In which year (Nabwi) did the first Hijrat (migration) of Muslims to Habsha (Abyssinia) take place?
f: The first migration to Abyssinia took place in the 5th year of prophethood (about 615 AD) to escape the persecution of Quraish.
r: The king Najashi (Negus) gave shelter to the Muslims; some sources differ on the date of the second migration.

q: What is the capital of the Holy See?
f: The Holy See is the government of the Catholic Church and is based in Vatican City.
r: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world and lies inside Rome.

q: Which of the following was a paternal aunt (Phuphi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Safiyya was a daughter of Abdul Muttalib and so a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Other paternal aunts include Atika, Arwa, Umm Hakim al-Bayda, Barra and Umaima.

q: Which idol was worshipped by the people of Taif?
f: Al-Lat was the main idol of the Thaqif tribe of Taif.
r: Al-Uzza was worshipped near Nakhla and Manat near Qudayd, and Hubal was the chief idol inside the Kaaba.

q: On which date did India conduct its Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998?
f: India carried out the first of its Pokhran-II tests on 11 May 1998, followed by more tests on 13 May.
r: Pakistan answered with its tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998; India's first test was in 1974.

q: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is also known as what?
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909 was introduced by Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy), so it is called the Morley-Minto Reforms.
r: It gave Muslims separate electorates.

q: How many barrages are built on the River Indus in Pakistan?
f: The six barrages on the Indus are Jinnah, Chashma, Taunsa, Guddu, Sukkur and Kotri.
r: Sukkur Barrage, completed in 1932, is the oldest of them.

q: What is the approximate length of the Indus Highway (N-55) in Pakistan?
f: The Indus Highway runs from Karachi to Peshawar along the Indus river and is about 1264 km long.
r: It is numbered N-55 in the national highway network.

q: How many Muslims and how many disbelievers (Kuffar) took part in the Ghazwa of Khandaq?
f: About 3000 Muslims defended Madina against a combined army of about 10000 from the Quraish and their allies.
r: The trench was dug on the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

q: Who was the leader of the Quraish (disbelievers) army in the Ghazwa of Khandaq?
f: Abu Sufyan, who had not yet accepted Islam, led the Quraish in the Battle of Khandaq. Abu Jahl had been killed earlier at Badr.
r: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

q: In which district of Punjab is Namal (Numal) Lake located?
f: Namal Lake is an artificial lake in Mianwali district near the Namal Valley.
r: It lies in the Salt Range area.

q: What is the meaning of the word Urdu in the Turkish language?
f: The word Urdu comes from Turkish ordu which means army or military camp.
r: Urdu developed in the army camps and bazaars of the Mughal period.

q: What is the approximate length of the Line of Control (LOC) between Pakistan and India in Kashmir?
f: The Line of Control is about 740 km long, as commonly stated.
r: It was established after the 1971 war by the Simla Agreement of 1972; sources give slightly different lengths.

q: Which strait lies between Greenland and Iceland?
f: The Denmark Strait separates Greenland from Iceland and links the Arctic and Atlantic oceans.
r: Davis Strait lies between Greenland and Canada.

q: Kachura Lake is located near which city? (2)
f: Upper and Lower Kachura Lakes are near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: Lower Kachura is also called Shangrila Lake.

q: Rawal Lake is located in which city?
f: Rawal Lake is an artificial reservoir in Islamabad that supplies water to Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
r: It is fed by the Korang River.

q: On which date was Hazrat Ali (RA) martyred?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was attacked by Abdur Rahman bin Muljam while praying in Kufa and was martyred on 21 Ramzan 40 Hijri.
r: This date matches about 30 January 661 AD.

q: Where is Masjid Khaif located?
f: Masjid Khaif is a historic mosque in the valley of Mina near Makkah. Many prophets are said to have prayed there.
r: Mina is where pilgrims stay and perform the stoning of the Jamarat during Hajj.

q: What is the full form of IRDA?
f: IRDA stands for Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, the body that regulates the insurance sector in India.
r: It was set up under an Act of the Indian Parliament in 1999.

q: What is the meaning of the word Islam?
f: The word Islam comes from the Arabic root s-l-m, meaning submission to Allah and peace.
r: A person who follows Islam is called a Muslim, meaning one who submits.

q: What does the word Miraath mean?
f: Miraath is an Arabic word meaning inheritance, the property left by a dead person.
r: The rules of inheritance are given in Surah An-Nisa of the Quran.

q: Which two Surahs of the Quran are called Muawwidhatain (Moaztain)?
f: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114) teach us to seek refuge with Allah, so they are called Muawwidhatain.
r: They are the last two surahs of the Quran.

q: What is the highest mountain of the Balochistan plateau? (3)
f: Zarghun Ghar near Quetta is the highest peak in Balochistan at about 3,578 metres.
r: Takatu mountain overlooks Quetta city and is a well known nearby peak.

q: Where is Mount Whitney located?
f: Mount Whitney, about 4,421 metres, is in the Sierra Nevada range in California.
r: It is the highest peak in the contiguous United States.

q: Who appointed Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of Yemen?
f: The Holy Prophet (SAW) sent Hazrat Muaz bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and teacher in 10 Hijri.
r: He is known as the most knowledgeable Companion about halal and haram.

q: Which of the following was NOT a daughter of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
f: The four daughters of the Prophet (SAW) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA). Aisha (RA) was his wife.
r: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest and married Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: Hub Dam and Hub Lake are near which city?
f: Hub Dam is on the Hub River on the border of Sindh and Balochistan, and it supplies water to Karachi.
r: The Hub River forms part of the border between Sindh and Balochistan.

q: If nP2 = 20, what is the value of n?
r: nPr = n! divided by (n-r)!.

q: On which date was the League of Nations founded?
f: The League of Nations came into being on 10 January 1920 after the Treaty of Versailles, with its headquarters in Geneva.
r: It was replaced by the United Nations in 1945.

q: Who defeated Hemu in the Second Battle of Panipat (5 November 1556)?
f: The army of the young Akbar, led by Bairam Khan, defeated Hemu (Hemachandra Vikramaditya) at Panipat in 1556.
r: Akbar was only 13 years old at the time.

q: Whom did Ahmad Shah Abdali defeat in the Third Battle of Panipat (14 January 1761)?
f: Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani) defeated the Marathas led by Sadashiv Rao Bhau at Panipat in 1761.
r: The defeat greatly weakened Maratha power in north India.

q: Where is the permanent secretariat of SAARC?
f: The SAARC Secretariat was set up in Kathmandu in 1987.
r: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985.

q: In which year was interest (riba) finally prohibited in Islam, as commonly taught?
f: The final prohibition of riba came near the end of the Prophet's life and was announced in the Farewell Hajj sermon in 10 Hijri.
r: Sources differ on the exact stage dates of the prohibition of riba.

q: How many sajdas (places of prostration) are there in the Quran according to the Hanafi school?
f: The Quran has 14 verses of sajda according to the commonly taught view.
r: The Shafi school counts 15 by including one in Surah Al-Hajj.

q: Which Companion of the Prophet (SAW) has the title Jami ul Quran?
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) is called Jami ul Quran because he had copies of the Quran made in one standard text.
r: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first collected the Quran in a book form.

q: Between which two places was the first railway line in present Pakistan opened?
f: The first railway line in the area now Pakistan ran from Karachi to Kotri and opened in 1861.
r: It was part of the Scinde Railway.

q: What is the length of the Mariana Trench?
f: The Mariana Trench is about 2,550 km long and about 69 km wide.
r: It is in the western Pacific Ocean near the Mariana Islands.

q: What is the Mariana Trench?
o: The deepest part of the Earth's oceans, in the Pacific
The highest plateau in the world
f: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known place in the oceans, and its deepest point is called Challenger Deep.
r: Challenger Deep is about 10,900 metres deep.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Committee of the Red Cross located?
f: The Red Cross was founded in Geneva by Henry Dunant, and its headquarters is still in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

q: What was the approximate duration of the revelation of the Quran?
f: The Quran was revealed gradually over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Makkah to the last in Madinah.
r: About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.

q: On which river is Balakot located?
f: Balakot is a town in Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on the bank of the Kunhar River.
r: Balakot was badly hit by the October 2005 earthquake.

q: On which river is Wular Lake located?
f: Wular Lake in Kashmir is fed by the Jhelum River, which flows through it.
r: Wular Lake is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.

q: Sadiq Sanjrani held which office in Pakistan from 2018 to 2024?
f: Sadiq Sanjrani, from Balochistan, was elected Chairman of the Senate in March 2018 and served until 2024.
r: Since April 2024 the Chairman of the Senate is Yousaf Raza Gilani.

q: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
f: Sher Shah Suri is buried in a large tomb in the middle of a lake at Sasaram in Bihar, India.
r: Sher Shah built the Grand Trunk Road and introduced the rupee.

q: Titu Meer, the leader of the Bengal peasants' movement, was the son of whom?
f: Titu Meer (Mir Nisar Ali) was born in 1782 to Syed Mir Hassan Ali and Abida Ruqayya Khatoon in West Bengal.
r: He built a bamboo fort at Narkelberia and fought the British and landlords in 1831.

q: Who was the eldest son of Zaheeruddin Babur?
f: Humayun was the eldest son of Babur and succeeded him as the second Mughal emperor in 1530.
r: Babur's other sons were Kamran, Askari and Hindal.

q: What does HIT stand for?
f: HIT stands for Heavy Industries Taxila, a defence production complex in Taxila near Rawalpindi.
r: HIT makes Al-Khalid tanks and other armoured vehicles.

q: For which period did the Congress ministries remain in power in the provinces of British India?
f: After the 1937 elections the Congress formed ministries in 7 provinces, and they resigned in 1939 when India was dragged into World War II.
r: Muslims celebrated a Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the resignations.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in the subcontinent?
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
r: The empire lasted formally until 1857.

q: Amjad and Ahmed kept 24 balloons in total, and Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmed. How many balloons did Amjad keep?
f: Let Ahmed have x, then Amjad has 3x. So 4x = 24, x = 6, and Amjad has 18.

q: Fill in the blank: They are three brothers, Ali is ______ of the three.
f: The superlative degree is used when one person is compared with more than two, so cleverest is correct.
r: The comparative degree is used for two persons only.

q: Who wrote the book Construction of Religious Boundaries?
f: Harjot Oberoi wrote The Construction of Religious Boundaries (1994) about Sikh identity.
r: The book is a well-known study of Sikh tradition and culture.

q: Who wrote the Persian poetry book Zabur-e-Ajam?
f: Zabur-e-Ajam (1927) is a Persian book of poetry by Allama Iqbal.
r: It contains the famous Gulshan-e-Raz-e-Jadid and Bandagi Nama.

q: What is the relation of Hazrat Asma (RA) with Hazrat Zubair (RA)?
f: Hazrat Asma bint Abu Bakr (RA) was the wife of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam (RA).
r: Their son was Abdullah bin Zubair (RA).

q: Which sea has the saltiest water among the well-known seas of the world?
f: The Dead Sea has about 34 percent salt, nearly ten times that of ocean water, so people float easily in it.
r: Strictly it is a salt lake, and its shore is the lowest land on Earth.

q: Which pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League? (5)
f: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League on joint political demands. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity for his role in this pact.

q: Who imposed martial law in Pakistan in July 1977 and served as Chief Martial Law Administrator? (5)
f: General Zia ul Haq, the Chief of Army Staff, removed Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on 5 July 1977 (Operation Fair Play) and imposed martial law.
r: Zia ul Haq ruled until his death in an air crash on 17 August 1988.

q: Who dismissed the first government of Benazir Bhutto in August 1990? (5)
f: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan used the power of Article 58(2)(b) to dismiss her government in August 1990 on charges of corruption and misrule.
r: Nawaz Sharif became Prime Minister after the October 1990 elections.

q: If 300 out of 500 students are present, what is the percentage of present students? (4)
f: Percentage present = 300 divided by 500 times 100 = 60 percent.
r: The percentage of absent students in this case would be 40 percent.

q: Who wrote the novel The Alchemist? (4)
f: The Alchemist was written by the Brazilian author Paulo Coelho and published in 1988.
r: It is one of the best-selling books in the world and has been translated into over 80 languages.

q: Which continent has the largest number of countries? (5)
f: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations, the most of any continent.
r: Asia has about 48 to 49 countries and Europe about 44 to 50, depending on the source.

q: A car travels at 30 km/h and a train travels twice as fast. What is the speed of the train? (4)
f: Twice the car's speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h, so the train covers 60 km in one hour.
r: In 30 minutes the same train would cover 30 km.

q: On what date did Field Marshal Ayub Khan resign as President of Pakistan? (4)
f: Ayub Khan resigned on 25 March 1969 after mass protests and handed power to General Yahya Khan.
r: Yahya Khan then imposed martial law.

q: Which famous leaning tower is located in Italy? (3)
o: Tower of Pisa (Leaning Tower of Pisa)
f: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower of the cathedral in Pisa, Italy, and leans because of soft ground.
r: Its construction began in 1173.

q: Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore commemorates which historical event? (3)
f: Minar-e-Pakistan was built at Iqbal Park (Minto Park) to mark the passing of the Lahore Resolution on 23 March 1940.
r: Its construction was completed in 1968.

q: In which year did Pervez Musharraf resign as President of Pakistan? (3)
f: Musharraf resigned on 18 August 2008 to avoid impeachment.
r: He had come to power by a coup on 12 October 1999.

q: Who dismissed the first Nawaz Sharif government in 1993? (3)
f: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed the government in April 1993 using Article 58(2)(b).
r: The Supreme Court restored it in May 1993, but both Nawaz Sharif and the President resigned in July 1993.

q: On what date did Khawaja Nazimuddin, the second Prime Minister of Pakistan, take office? (3)
f: After Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Prime Minister on 17 October 1951.
r: He was dismissed by Governor General Ghulam Muhammad on 17 April 1953.

q: What is the product of sec and cos (of the same angle)? (3)
f: sec theta = 1 / cos theta, so sec theta x cos theta = 1.
r: Cosecant is the reciprocal of sine, and cotangent is the reciprocal of tangent.

q: Who gave the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech, and in which country was it delivered? (3)
f: Martin Luther King Jr delivered the speech in Washington DC at the Lincoln Memorial on 28 August 1963.
r: The speech was given during the March on Washington for civil rights.

q: A train travels at twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 20 km in one hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (3)
f: Train speed = 2 x 20 = 40 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 40 x 1/2 = 20 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan after the non-party general elections of 1985? (2)
f: After the 1985 non-party elections, General Zia ul Haq nominated Muhammad Khan Junejo, who became Prime Minister in March 1985.
r: Zia dismissed the Junejo government in May 1988.

q: Who ended the second government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif in October 1999? (2)
f: General Pervez Musharraf, the army chief, took over power in a bloodless coup on 12 October 1999 and ended Nawaz Sharif's government.
r: Musharraf first took the title of Chief Executive and became President in June 2001.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan in 2002 after the general elections? (2)
f: Mir Zafarullah Khan Jamali was elected Prime Minister on 23 November 2002 after the October 2002 general elections.
r: He resigned in June 2004 and Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain served briefly before Shaukat Aziz.

q: Under which article of the 1973 Constitution does the President appoint the Chief of Army Staff? (2)
f: Article 243 deals with command of the armed forces, and under it the President appoints the Chief of Army Staff on the advice of the Prime Minister.
r: This article was amended by the 27th Amendment of November 2025, which also created the post of Chief of Defence Forces.

q: In which country did Mahatma Gandhi start his non-violent (satyagraha) struggle? (2)
f: Gandhi developed satyagraha in South Africa from 1906 while protesting against discriminatory laws against Indians.
r: He returned to India in 1915.

q: Which book was written by Adolf Hitler? (2)
f: Mein Kampf (My Struggle) was written by Hitler while in prison in 1924-25 and sets out his political ideas.
r: Hitler led Nazi Germany from 1933 until 1945.

q: On what date did Amnesty International receive the Nobel Peace Prize? (2)
f: Amnesty International was awarded the 1977 Nobel Peace Prize, and the prize was presented on 10 December 1977 in Oslo.
r: The award was announced on 10 October 1977.

q: Which city is called the gold capital of the world in many Pakistani textbooks? (2)
f: Johannesburg in South Africa grew from a gold rush in 1886 and is known as the City of Gold.
r: Sources differ, as Dubai is also nicknamed the City of Gold for its gold trade.

q: All planets rotate on which of the following? (2)
f: Every planet spins (rotates) on its own axis, while it revolves around the Sun along its orbit.
r: Earth's rotation on its axis causes day and night.

q: Who dismissed the first government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto in 1990? (2)
f: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan dismissed her government on 6 August 1990 under Article 58(2)(b) on charges of corruption.
r: Her second government was dismissed in 1996 by President Farooq Leghari.

q: What is the factorial of 2? (2)
f: 2 factorial is 2 x 1 = 2.
r: 0 factorial and 1 factorial are both equal to 1.

q: Who designed the national flag of Pakistan according to most Pakistani sources? (2)
f: The flag was designed by Syed Amiruddin Kidwai, based on the flag of the All India Muslim League, and adopted on 11 August 1947.
r: Some sources also mention Master Altaf Hussain as the one who prepared the first flag, so sources differ.

q: A helicopter uses 120 gallons of fuel to travel 60 km. How far will it travel on 700 gallons at the same rate? (2)
f: Distance per gallon is 60 / 120 = 0.5 km. So 700 gallons cover 700 x 0.5 = 350 km.
r: This is a direct proportion question: more fuel gives more distance.

q: After which pact was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity? (2)
f: Jinnah worked to bring the Muslim League and Congress together in the Lucknow Pact of 1916, and was then called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity.
r: The title is commonly credited to Sarojini Naidu.

q: In which Hijri year did Pakistan come into being (14 August 1947)? (2)
f: 14 August 1947 fell in Ramadan 1366 AH.
r: It was the 27th of Ramadan, though some candidates remember it as 17 Ramadan.

q: What is the area of a triangle with base 6 cm and height 5 cm? (2)
f: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 6 x 5 = 15 sq cm.
r: A triangle has half the area of a rectangle with the same base and height.

q: What does GHQ stand for, and in which city is it located? (2)
f: GHQ means General Headquarters, the headquarters of the Pakistan Army, located in Rawalpindi.
r: The Chief of Army Staff works from GHQ.

q: Who is the Director General of ISI (Inter-Services Intelligence) of Pakistan as of 2026? (2)
f: Lt Gen Muhammad Asim Malik has been DG ISI since September 2024 and was still in the post in 2026.
r: His predecessor was Lt Gen Nadeem Anjum.

q: Who is credited with the famous saying "Knowledge is power"? (2)
f: The phrase "knowledge itself is power" is credited to the English philosopher Francis Bacon (1597).
r: Thomas Hobbes also used a similar phrase later, but Bacon is the usual answer in textbooks.

q: In mathematics, what is a row matrix? (2)
o: A matrix with only one column
A matrix with only one row (1 x n)
A matrix with equal rows and columns
A matrix with all zero entries
f: A row matrix has exactly one row and n columns, so its order is 1 x n.
r: A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.

q: In which year was the Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore completed? (2)
f: Construction of Minar-e-Pakistan started in 1960 and it was completed in 1968.
r: It stands in Iqbal Park, Lahore, where the Lahore Resolution was passed in 1940.

q: Which name did Pakistan give to its military response to India in May 2025? (2)
f: Pakistan named its response Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, meaning a solid wall (from Surah As-Saff, verse 4).
r: The operation was launched on 10 May 2025.

q: Kamal is older than Jamal, Jamal is older than Hussain, and Hussain is older than Waqar. Who is the oldest? (2)
f: The order from oldest is Kamal, Jamal, Hussain, Waqar. So Kamal is the oldest.
r: Waqar is the youngest in this chain.

q: Which one is the odd man out: Socrates, Handel, Beethoven, Mozart? (2)
f: Handel, Beethoven and Mozart were famous composers of music. Socrates was a Greek philosopher.
r: Socrates was the teacher of Plato, who was the teacher of Aristotle.

q: On what date did the second government of Benazir Bhutto take office as Prime Minister? (2)
f: Benazir Bhutto won the 1993 election and took oath as Prime Minister for the second time on 19 October 1993.
r: Her first term started on 2 December 1988, and she was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country.

q: Which parallel divides South Korea and North Korea? (2)
f: After the Second World War, Korea was divided along the 38th parallel north into North and South.
r: The 17th parallel divided North and South Vietnam.

q: What is the derivative of x to the power 5 with respect to x? (2)
f: By the power rule d/dx of x^n = n x^(n-1), so the derivative of x^5 is 5x^4.
r: The derivative of a constant is zero.

q: What did the Pakistan Resolution of 23 March 1940 demand, and who moved it? (2)
o: Separate electorates for Muslims, moved by Allama Iqbal
Full provincial autonomy within India, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan
Independent Muslim states in the north-western and eastern zones of India, moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq
A united India with a Muslim president, moved by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
f: The resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League and demanded independent states in the Muslim-majority zones. It was moved by Bengal Chief Minister A. K. Fazlul Huq.
r: It was seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman and is also called the Lahore Resolution.

q: Which is the largest river of South Africa? (2)
f: The Orange River is the longest river in South Africa, about 2,200 km long.
r: It flows west into the Atlantic Ocean and forms part of the border with Namibia.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'defer'? (2)
f: To defer means to put off until a later time, which is to postpone.
r: Defer can also mean to yield to someone's opinion.

q: Who dismissed the second government of Benazir Bhutto in November 1996?
f: President Farooq Leghari, a former member of her own party, dismissed her government on 5 November 1996 on charges of corruption and the killing of Murtaza Bhutto.
r: Her first government had been dismissed in 1990 by Ghulam Ishaq Khan.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day is the 18th day of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 18th is 17 days. 17 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 3, so the day is 3 days after Friday, which is Monday.
r: Days repeat every 7 days, so dates 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29 fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 20th day of that month?
f: From the 1st to the 20th is 19 days. 19 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 5, so the day is 5 days after Monday, which is Saturday.
r: If the 1st is Monday, then the 15th is also Monday, so the 20th is five days later.

q: In which country was the G20 Leaders' Summit of 2025 held? (4)
f: The 2025 G20 summit was held in Johannesburg, South Africa, in November 2025. It was the first G20 summit hosted in Africa.
r: The United States holds the G20 presidency for 2026, with the summit planned at Doral, Miami, in December 2026.

q: What is the full form of the abbreviation LLB?
f: LLB comes from the Latin Legum Baccalaureus and means Bachelor of Laws, the basic law degree.
r: The master's degree in law is abbreviated LLM.

q: What is the full form of OIC?
f: OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, a group of 57 member states. It was formerly named the Organisation of the Islamic Conference.
r: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the full form of PMA?
f: PMA stands for Pakistan Military Academy, the institution that trains officers for the Pakistan Army.
r: The Pakistan Military Academy is located in Kakul, Abbottabad.

q: What is the full form of PTA in Pakistan's telecom sector?
f: PTA is the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, the regulator of telecom services in Pakistan, set up in 1996.
r: PEMRA regulates electronic media, while PTA regulates telecommunications.

q: Through which amendment to the 1973 Constitution was NWFP renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: The 18th Amendment, passed in April 2010, renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: The same amendment removed the President's power to dismiss the assembly under Article 58(2)(b) and gave more powers to the provinces.

q: Who started the Aligarh Movement in the subcontinent?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan started the Aligarh Movement to promote modern education among Muslims after 1857.
r: He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.

q: In which year was Amnesty International established?
f: Amnesty International was founded in London in 1961 by the British lawyer Peter Benenson.
r: It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977 for its work for human rights.

q: What is the antonym of the word medieval?
f: Medieval refers to the Middle Ages and old times, so its opposite is modern.
r: The Middle Ages in Europe lasted roughly from the 5th to the 15th century.

q: Aslam walks towards the east, after some time he turns left, and some steps later he turns right. In which direction is he now moving?
f: Facing east, a left turn makes him face north. Turning right from north makes him face east again.
r: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

q: Who dissolved the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan in October 1954?
f: Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly on 24 October 1954. The Federal Court upheld this in the Maulvi Tamizuddin case.
r: The dissolution is seen as a key blow to democracy in early Pakistan.

q: Who is Data Ganj Bakhsh?
o: A Sufi saint of Lahore, Hazrat Ali Hujwiri
f: Data Ganj Bakhsh is the title of Hazrat Ali bin Usman Al-Hujwiri, an 11th-century Sufi saint who settled in Lahore. His shrine in Lahore is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
r: He wrote the famous Persian book on Sufism, Kashf-ul-Mahjoob.

q: Who was the first Governor of Balochistan after it became a province in 1970?
f: Balochistan became a province on 1 July 1970 when One Unit was dissolved, and Lt Gen Riaz Hussain was its first Governor.
r: Ghous Bakhsh Raisani, who followed him, is described as the first civilian Governor of Balochistan.

q: Who served as Chief Adviser of Bangladesh's interim government from August 2024 until February 2026?
f: After Sheikh Hasina left in August 2024, Nobel laureate Dr Muhammad Yunus led the interim government as Chief Adviser. His term ended when Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister on 17 February 2026.
r: Today Bangladesh has an elected Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, so there is no Chief Adviser now.

q: On which date did Benazir Bhutto first become Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1988?
f: After the November 1988 elections her PPP was the largest party, and she took oath as Prime Minister on 2 December 1988.
r: She was the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.

q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan after the death of General Zia ul Haq in 1988?
f: Zia died in a plane crash on 17 August 1988. Elections were held in November 1988 and Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988.
r: Ghulam Ishaq Khan, the Senate Chairman, became acting President after Zia's death.

q: Who became Prime Minister of Pakistan in April 2022 after Imran Khan lost a no-confidence vote?
f: Imran Khan was removed by a no-confidence vote in the National Assembly on 10 April 2022, and Shehbaz Sharif was elected Prime Minister the next day.
r: Imran Khan was the first Pakistani Prime Minister removed through a no-confidence vote.

q: In which month and year did the United States declare its independence?
f: The Declaration of Independence was adopted by the Continental Congress on 4 July 1776.
r: Britain formally recognised American independence in the Treaty of Paris in 1783.

q: Which law governed the constitutional setup of British India just before independence in 1947?
f: The Government of India Act 1935 was the last major constitutional law of British India and was used with changes as Pakistan's interim constitution.
r: Pakistan worked under the amended 1935 Act until its first Constitution came in 1956.

q: Between which two values do the sine and cosine functions always lie? (2)
f: On the unit circle, sine and cosine are the y and x coordinates of a point, so they can never go below -1 or above 1.
r: Tangent, unlike sine and cosine, has no upper or lower limit.

q: Complete the proverb: The early bird catches the ____.
f: The proverb says that a person who starts early gets the best chance of success, like a bird that finds the worm first.
r: A similar saying is Early to bed and early to rise makes a man healthy, wealthy and wise.

q: Why is milk boiled before drinking?
f: Heating milk to boiling point kills harmful bacteria and makes it safe to drink.
r: The process of heating milk to kill germs and then cooling it is named pasteurisation after Louis Pasteur.

q: What is the name of the house in Karachi where Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born?
f: Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 at Wazir Mansion, Kharadar, Karachi.
r: Wazir Mansion is now a protected national monument and a museum.

q: In a class of 30 students, 2/4 are boys. What percentage of the class are girls?
f: 2/4 of 30 is 15 boys, so girls are 30 minus 15 which is 15. Girls percentage is 15 divided by 30 times 100, which is 50 percent.
r: 2/4 is the same as 1/2, so half the class is girls.

q: On which date did the Cabinet Mission arrive in India in 1946?
f: The British Cabinet Mission reached India on 24 March 1946 to discuss transfer of power.
r: It announced its plan on 16 May 1946, proposing a loose federation with three groups of provinces.

q: What is the alimentary canal?
o: The long tube of the digestive system from mouth to anus
The tube that carries air to the lungs
The vessel that carries blood to the heart
The tube that carries urine from the kidneys
f: The alimentary canal, also called the gut, runs from the mouth through the oesophagus, stomach and intestines to the anus, and digests and absorbs food.
r: The small intestine is where most absorption of food takes place.

q: In which country is the Suez Canal located and which two seas does it join?
o: Egypt; Mediterranean Sea and Red Sea
Egypt; Red Sea and Arabian Sea
Saudi Arabia; Red Sea and Persian Gulf
f: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway in Egypt joining the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
r: It was opened in 1869 and shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia.

q: What is the capital of Iraq?
f: Baghdad, on the River Tigris, is the capital and largest city of Iraq.
r: Baghdad was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate from 762 CE.

q: Which team has won the ICC Champions Trophy the most times?
f: India has won three titles: 2002 (shared with Sri Lanka), 2013 and 2025.
r: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy once, in 2017, beating India in the final.

q: Which team won the ICC Champions Trophy in 2025?
f: India beat New Zealand in the final played in Dubai on 9 March 2025.
r: The 2025 tournament was hosted by Pakistan, but India played its matches in Dubai.

q: What is the diameter of a unit circle?
f: A unit circle has radius 1, so its diameter is 2 times the radius, which is 2.
r: The circumference of a unit circle is 2 times pi.

q: What is the circulatory system?
o: The system that moves blood around the body
The system that controls breathing only
f: The circulatory system carries blood, oxygen and nutrients to all body parts and takes waste away.
r: William Harvey described blood circulation in 1628.

q: What are the main parts of the human circulatory system?
f: The heart pumps blood, blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries) carry it, and blood is the fluid that moves in them.
r: Arteries carry blood away from the heart and veins bring it back.

q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan in 1977?
f: General Zia ul Haq was Army Chief from 1976 and took over power through martial law on 5 July 1977.
r: He remained Army Chief until his death in August 1988.

q: Complete the sentence: Practice makes us ____.
f: The saying is Practice makes perfect, meaning regular practice improves skill.
r: Another similar saying is Slow and steady wins the race.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She did returned back from London.
f: Returned already means came back, so the word back is repeated and wrong (redundant).
r: Similar repeated phrases are reply back and revert back.

q: Under which article of Pakistan's 1973 Constitution is a Qadiani (Ahmadi) defined as a non-Muslim?
f: Article 260(3) defines who is a Muslim and who is a non-Muslim. It was added by the Second Amendment of 1974.
r: The Second Constitutional Amendment was passed in September 1974 under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Which company first launched the PlayStation game console?
f: Sony Computer Entertainment launched the original PlayStation in Japan in December 1994.
r: Microsoft later entered the console market with the Xbox in 2001.

q: On what date was the first session of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan held in Karachi?
f: The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan met on 10 August 1947 in Karachi. On 11 August 1947 it elected Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as its President.
r: The Objectives Resolution was passed by this Assembly on 12 March 1949.

q: What is the integral of cos inverse (1/x) with respect to x, for x greater in size than 1?
o: x sec inverse(x) minus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C
x sec inverse(x) plus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C
x cos inverse(x) minus sqrt(1 - x^2) + C
sec inverse(x) divided by x + C
f: cos inverse(1/x) equals sec inverse(x). Integrating by parts, the integral of sec inverse(x) dx is x sec inverse(x) minus the integral of 1 / sqrt(x^2 - 1) dx, which gives x sec inverse(x) minus ln|x + sqrt(x^2 - 1)| + C.
r: The derivative of sec inverse(x) is 1 / (|x| sqrt(x^2 - 1)).

q: In which country is the Amazon rainforest and most of the Amazon River basin located?
f: Brazil holds about 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest and most of the river basin.
r: The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean and carries the largest volume of water of any river.

q: What does INTERPOL stand for in full?
f: INTERPOL is the International Criminal Police Organization, which helps police forces of its member countries to cooperate.
r: Its headquarters are in Lyon, France.

q: If a man covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does he cover in 20 minutes at the same speed?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so speed is 20 / 100 = 0.2 km per minute. In 20 minutes he covers 0.2 x 20 = 4 km.
r: Speed in km per hour here is 12 km/h.

q: If a train covers 100 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes. Distance per minute is 100 km / 100 minutes = 1 km.
r: The train's speed is 60 km per hour.

q: Which two provinces were created when Lord Curzon divided Bengal in 1905?
o: Eastern Bengal and Assam, and Western Bengal
f: The 1905 partition created the new Muslim-majority province of Eastern Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as capital, leaving Western Bengal with Calcutta.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911 after Hindu protests.

q: What is the superlative degree of the adjective good?
f: Good is an irregular adjective: good, better, best. Best is the superlative form.
r: Better is the comparative degree.

q: Which of these is a vector quantity, unlike speed?
f: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Speed has only magnitude, so it is a scalar.
r: Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

q: On what date was SUPARCO established?
f: SUPARCO, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, was set up on 16 September 1961 with Dr Abdus Salam as its first head.
r: Pakistan launched its first rocket, Rehbar-I, in 1962.

q: Which country is called the Cockpit of Europe?
f: Belgium has been the battlefield of many European wars, so it is called the Cockpit of Europe.
r: Its capital Brussels is also the headquarters of the European Union and NATO.

q: After how many years did Pakistan host an ICC event again with the Champions Trophy in 2025?
f: Pakistan last hosted an ICC event in 1996 (the World Cup, shared with India and Sri Lanka). The 2025 Champions Trophy came 29 years later.
r: India played its matches in Dubai under a hybrid model.

q: Finland is famous as a country of many what?
f: Finland is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes and has about 188,000 lakes.
r: Its capital is Helsinki.

q: How many inches are in one foot?
f: One foot is defined as 12 inches.
r: One yard is 3 feet, which equals 36 inches.

q: What is the full form of GDP?
f: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, the total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year.
r: GNP (Gross National Product) also counts income earned by citizens abroad.

q: What is the full form of NEPRA in Pakistan?
o: National Energy Production and Research Agency
National Electricity Pricing and Revenue Authority
f: NEPRA stands for National Electric Power Regulatory Authority, which regulates the power sector of Pakistan.
r: NEPRA was established in 1997 and its head office is in Islamabad.

q: Where is the headquarters of the National Radio and Telecommunication Corporation (NRTC) of Pakistan?
f: NRTC is a defence production organisation based in Haripur, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: In 2021 the government handed Telephone Industries of Pakistan over to NRTC.

q: Who gave the Six Points formula of 1966 demanding autonomy for East Pakistan?
f: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman presented the Six Points at a conference of opposition parties in Lahore in February 1966.
r: The Six Points became the base of the Awami League movement that led to Bangladesh in 1971.

q: In which year was UNESCO founded?
f: UNESCO was founded in 1945 when its constitution was adopted in London, as the United Nations agency for education, science and culture.
r: Its constitution came into force in November 1946 and its headquarters is in Paris.

q: On which date is Human Rights Day observed every year?
f: Human Rights Day is observed on 10 December, the day the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.
r: 24 October is United Nations Day.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the 3rd June Plan of 1947?
f: Lord Mountbatten, the last Viceroy, announced the 3rd June Plan which proposed the partition of India.
r: He became the first Governor General of independent India after independence.

q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 took place in protest against which act?
f: People gathered in Amritsar to protest the Rowlatt Act, which allowed arrest without trial, and General Dyer fired on them.
r: The massacre took place on 13 April 1919.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in 1919?
f: Lord Chelmsford was Viceroy and Governor General of India from 1916 to 1921.
r: Lord Reading succeeded him in 1921.

q: What was the original name of the Mughal emperor Jahangir?
f: Jahangir was born as Prince Salim (Nur-ud-Din Muhammad Salim) and took the title Jahangir when he became emperor.
r: His son Prince Khurram later became Emperor Shah Jahan.

q: What is the negative form of a past indefinite (simple past) sentence?
o: Subject + did not + base form of verb
Subject + does not + base form of verb
Subject + was not + verb with ing
f: In the simple past, the negative is made with did not plus the first form of the verb, for example: He did not go.
r: Past indefinite verbs in the positive use the second form, such as went.

q: If 4 June is Sunday, what day of the week will 15 June be?
f: From 4 June to 15 June is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Sunday, which is Thursday.
r: The days repeat every 7 days.

q: Nanga Parbat is also known by which name?
f: Nanga Parbat is called Killer Mountain because of the many climbers who died on it in early attempts.
r: K2 is the one known as the Savage Mountain.

q: In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan join the All India Muslim League?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan joined the Muslim League in 1923.
r: He became its General Secretary in 1936 and was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan.

q: The McMahon Line is the border line between which two countries?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 as the boundary between British India and Tibet and is now the disputed border of India and China in the east.
r: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

q: The Himalayas mountain range is located in which continent?
f: The Himalayas stretch across Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bhutan and China, all in Asia.
r: The Himalayas contain Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world.

q: What is the main source of the economy of Pakistan?
f: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy because it employs a large share of the workforce and supports exports like cotton and rice.
r: Cotton, wheat, rice and sugarcane are Pakistan's major crops.

q: Which resolution passed in March 1949 is regarded as the basis (foundation) of the constitutions of Pakistan?
f: The Objectives Resolution laid down the guiding principles for Pakistan's constitution and later became its preamble.
r: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

q: What is the meaning of the word "abhorrence"?
f: Abhorrence means a feeling of strong hatred or disgust towards something.
r: The verb form is "abhor", which means to hate strongly.

q: What is the meaning of the word "sensible"?
f: Sensible describes a person or choice that shows good judgement and is practical.
r: Do not confuse it with "sensitive", which means easily hurt or affected.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
f: Attaullah Tarar holds the information and broadcasting portfolio and was still in office in October 2026.
r: He was earlier Minister of State for Law and Justice.

q: In which year did Martin Luther King Jr. receive the Nobel Prize?
f: Martin Luther King Jr. was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964.
r: He was the youngest person to receive the Nobel Peace Prize at that time (aged 35).

q: On which date did Martin Luther King Jr. receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Oslo?
f: He received the prize in Oslo on 10 December 1964, which is Nobel Prize ceremony day.
r: His famous speech "I Have a Dream" was on 28 August 1963.

q: Who started the Home Rule Movement in India in 1916?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant
Sir Syed and Altaf Hussain Hali
f: Tilak launched his Home Rule League in April 1916 and Annie Besant launched hers in September 1916.
r: Its aim was self-government for India within the British Empire.

q: In which year was the Muhammadan Educational Conference formed by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan?
f: Sir Syed formed the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886 to spread modern education among Muslims.
r: It held its first meeting at Aligarh.

q: Which comes next in the series: A1, C3, E5, G7, ?
f: Letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers go up by 2 (1, 3, 5, 7, 9). So the next term is I9.
r: Alternating letter-number series are solved by finding the rule for letters and numbers separately.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ?
f: Each term is double the previous one: 32 x 2 = 64.
r: This is a geometric series with common ratio 2.

q: Which comes next in the series: A9, C12, E15, G18, ?
f: Letters skip one each time (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers go up by 3 (9, 12, 15, 18, 21). So the next term is I21.
r: In such series the letter rule and number rule are independent.

q: Which number comes next: 112, 55, 225, 65, ?
f: This is two alternating series. Terms 1, 3, 5: 112, 225 (112 x 2 + 1), then 225 x 2 + 1 = 451. The other series is 55, 65 (plus 10).
r: When terms jump up and down, split the series into odd and even positions.

q: Ali is 4 years old and Ahmad is twice his age. What will Ahmad's age be when Ali is 15?
f: Ahmad is 8 when Ali is 4, so he is 4 years older. When Ali is 15, Ahmad is 15 + 4 = 19.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: Which pair is the odd one out: CE, IJ, AC, GI, EG?
f: In CE, AC, GI and EG the second letter is 2 places after the first. In IJ, J is only 1 place after I, so IJ is odd.
r: Check the gap between letters in each pair to find the odd one.

q: What is the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
o: A military alliance of Western states
A group of states not formally aligned with any major power bloc
A trade union of oil producers
f: NAM is a group of states that chose not to join either the US-led or the Soviet-led bloc during the Cold War.
r: NAM was founded in Belgrade in 1961, after the 1955 Bandung conference.

q: In the 1956 constitution of Pakistan, Urdu and which other language were given the status of national language?
f: The 1956 constitution made both Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
r: The language issue was strong in East Pakistan, and the 1952 Language Movement was about Bengali.

q: Alaska is part of which country?
f: Alaska is a state of the USA. The USA bought it from Russia in 1867.
r: Alaska became the 49th US state in 1959.

q: Under the partition plan, what share of the cash balance of undivided India was agreed for Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's share of the cash balances was set at Rs 75 crore. India paid Rs 20 crore and withheld the remaining Rs 55 crore.
r: Gandhi fasted in January 1948 partly to press India to release the balance.

q: What was the Partition of Bengal of 1905?
o: Bengal was divided into East Bengal and Assam, and West Bengal, by Lord Curzon
Bengal was given to the French
Bengal was made a separate country
f: Viceroy Lord Curzon divided the Bengal Presidency into Eastern Bengal and Assam (capital Dhaka) and the rest of Bengal.
r: It was annulled in 1911 after strong Hindu protests.

q: Which British Indian province was partitioned in 1905?
f: In 1905 the Bengal Presidency was split into two parts.
r: The partition was announced by Lord Curzon.

q: What is a preposition?
o: A word that shows the relation of a noun or pronoun with another word
A word that names a person
A word that describes a verb
A word that joins two sentences
f: A preposition shows the relation of a noun or pronoun to another word, for example in, on, at.
r: A preposition is normally followed by a noun or pronoun.

q: Which is the busiest port of Pakistan?
f: Karachi Port handles the largest share of Pakistan's sea trade.
r: Port Qasim is the second major port and Gwadar is a deep sea port on the Makran coast.

q: What is a polynomial?
o: An expression with variables having whole number powers, joined by plus or minus signs
An expression with a variable in the denominator only
f: A polynomial is a sum of terms like a x to the power n, where n is a whole number, for example x^2 + 3x + 2.
r: The highest power of the variable is called the degree of the polynomial.

q: Who was the first President of the United States?
f: George Washington was the first President of the USA, serving from 1789 to 1797.
r: John Adams was the second President.

q: Which Iranian nuclear sites did the United States strike in June 2025?
f: On 21-22 June 2025 the US attacked the Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan nuclear sites in Operation Midnight Hammer.
r: It was the first combat use of the GBU-57 bunker-buster bomb, and Iran disputed the extent of damage.

q: Which player has won the most men's singles titles at the Australian Open in the Open era?
f: Novak Djokovic has won the Australian Open 10 times, more than any other man in the Open era.
r: Carlos Alcaraz beat Djokovic in the 2026 final, so Djokovic's total stayed at 10.

q: On what date did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Malala was announced as a Nobel Peace Prize winner on 10 October 2014 and received the prize at the ceremony in Oslo on 10 December 2014.
r: She shared the 2014 prize with Kailash Satyarthi of India and is the youngest Nobel laureate ever.

q: In which movement was Chaudhry Rehmat Ali mainly involved?
f: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali was a student leader at Cambridge who worked for a separate Muslim homeland, which became the Pakistan Movement.
r: He coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.

q: Where is the Sadpara Dam located?
f: Sadpara Dam is built on the Sadpara stream near Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: It supplies drinking water to Skardu city and is near Sadpara Lake.

q: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: Article 59 of the 1973 Constitution requires a Senate candidate to be at least 30 years old.
r: The minimum age for the National Assembly is 25 years.

q: What are the values of sin 0 degrees and cos 0 degrees?
f: From the standard trigonometric table, sin 0 = 0 and cos 0 = 1.
r: Sin 90 = 1 and cos 90 = 0, which is the reverse.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 10 times his age. What will be Ali's age after 12 years?
f: Ali is 4 now, so after 12 years he will be 4 + 12 = 16 years old.
r: His sister's age after 12 years would be 40 + 12 = 52 years.

q: A person bought a pen for Rs 20 and sold it for Rs 30. What is the percentage of profit?
f: Profit = 30 - 20 = Rs 10. Profit percent = 10 / 20 x 100 = 50 percent.
r: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price.

q: In Washington DC, what does DC stand for?
f: Washington DC is the capital of the USA and DC stands for District of Columbia.
r: The city is not part of any US state.

q: What does ASRC stand for in the Pakistan Army?
f: ASRC is the centre where candidates for the Pakistan Army appear for the initial tests. Its full form is Army Selection and Recruitment Centre.
r: ISSB is the later selection board that tests officer candidates.

q: What does CPU stand for in computing?
f: The CPU is the main chip that carries out instructions in a computer, so it is the Central Processing Unit.
r: It is often called the brain of the computer.

q: What does U.A.E stand for?
f: U.A.E is the short form of United Arab Emirates, a country made of seven emirates.
r: Its capital is Abu Dhabi and its largest city is Dubai.

q: How many types of swimming strokes are there in competitive swimming?
f: The four competitive strokes are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly.
r: The individual medley combines all four strokes in one race.

q: Who introduced the Doctrine of Lapse in the subcontinent?
f: Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.
r: Under it, a princely state without a natural male heir was annexed by the British.

q: In which continent is Sudan located?
f: Sudan lies in north-eastern Africa and borders Egypt and the Red Sea.
r: Its capital is Khartoum.

q: What is the sum of the roots of the equation x^2 - 5x + 1 = 0?
f: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is -b/a. Here a = 1 and b = -5, so the sum is 5.
r: The product of the roots is c/a = 1.

q: What is a synonym?
o: A word with the opposite meaning
A word with a similar meaning to another word
A word that sounds the same but is spelled differently
f: A synonym is a word that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word.
r: A word with the opposite meaning is called an antonym.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'vital'? (3)
f: Vital means absolutely necessary, which is the meaning of essential.
r: Vital comes from the Latin word vita, meaning life.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'optimistic'?
f: An optimistic person expects good outcomes, so hopeful is the closest word.
r: The antonym of optimistic is pessimistic.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'venerate'?
f: To venerate means to respect deeply, which is to revere.
r: Veneration is often used for saints, elders and religious figures.

q: What type of government system does Pakistan follow?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution Pakistan is a federal parliamentary republic in which the Prime Minister heads the government.
r: The President is the ceremonial head of state.

q: What do plants take in and release at night?
o: They take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide
They take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen
They take in nitrogen and release oxygen
They take in hydrogen and release carbon dioxide
f: At night there is no light for photosynthesis, so plants only respire. They take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide.
r: During the day photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so plants release net oxygen.

q: Which one is different from the rest: EH, AD, MP, QS?
f: Letter gaps: E to H is 3 (5 to 8), A to D is 3 (1 to 4), M to P is 3 (13 to 16), but Q to S is only 2 (17 to 19).
r: In odd-one-out letter pairs, always compare the gaps in alphabet positions.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 11?
f: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ali needs 8 more years to reach 11, so she will be 9 + 8 = 17.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same over time.

q: Umair is 5 years older than Amir, and Amir is 15 years old. How old will Umair be after 7 years?
f: Umair is 15 + 5 = 20 now. After 7 years he will be 20 + 7 = 27.
r: Add the years to the present age to find the future age.

q: Who served as Prime Minister of Pakistan three times?
f: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister in 1990, 1997 and 2013, so three terms.
r: Benazir Bhutto and Shehbaz Sharif each served twice as Prime Minister.

q: Which male tennis player has won the most singles titles in the Open Era?
f: Jimmy Connors holds the record with 109 ATP singles titles. Federer has 103.
r: Djokovic has passed 100 titles and is third, so rankings by titles can change; sources differ on his exact count.

q: What is the total area of Islamabad?
f: Islamabad Capital Territory covers about 906 square kilometres.
r: Islamabad became the capital of Pakistan in the 1960s, replacing Karachi.

q: Is the flu (influenza) caused by a virus or by bacteria?
f: Influenza is caused by influenza viruses, not by bacteria.
