r: Antibiotics do not work against viruses such as flu.

q: How many vowels are in these letters: A, c, I, t, v, a, e, o, u?
f: The vowels are A, I, a, e, o, u, which makes 6. The letters c, t and v are consonants.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: How many vowels are there in AIUDAUOEZXBGH?
f: The vowels are A, I, U, A, U, O, E, which makes 7. D, Z, X, B, G and H are consonants.
r: The English alphabet has 5 vowels and 21 consonants.

q: Which athlete has won the most Olympic gold medals in history?
f: American swimmer Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals, the most ever.
r: Phelps won 28 Olympic medals in total, also a record.

q: Who wrote the book My Experiments with Truth?
f: My Experiments with Truth is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi.
r: It was first written in Gujarati and later translated into English.

q: What is 2 + 2/1?
f: Division first: 2/1 = 2. Then 2 + 2 = 4.
r: By BODMAS, division is done before addition.

q: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet? (8)
f: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare in the 1590s.
r: Shakespeare also wrote Hamlet, Macbeth and Othello.

q: Which currency is used in Denmark? (4)
f: Denmark uses the Danish krone (DKK) and has not adopted the euro.
r: Sweden uses the Swedish krona and Norway the Norwegian krone.

q: About how many people lived in the Gaza Strip before the war that began in October 2023? (3)
f: Before October 2023 the Gaza Strip had around 2.1 to 2.2 million people, according to Palestinian and UN estimates.
r: Gaza is only about 365 square km, so it is one of the most densely populated places on earth; sources differ slightly on the exact number.

q: Emperor Hirohito was the emperor of which country during World War II? (3)
f: Hirohito was the emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989 and ruled during World War II.
r: Japan surrendered in August 1945 after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

q: Who wrote the book The Story of the Malakand Field Force (1898)? (3)
f: Winston Churchill wrote it as a young army officer and war correspondent after the 1897 Malakand campaign.
r: The book was Churchill's first published work on war.

q: How many foci does an ellipse have? (3)
f: An ellipse is defined by two fixed points called foci; the sum of distances from any point on it to the two foci is constant.
r: A circle is a special ellipse in which both foci coincide at the centre.

q: Which cricketer scored 13,000 runs in One Day Internationals in 2023, doing it faster than anyone before? (2)
f: Virat Kohli reached 13,000 ODI runs in September 2023 against Pakistan in the Asia Cup. He took only 267 innings, the fastest ever.
r: Sachin Tendulkar reached 13,000 ODI runs in 321 innings, which was the earlier record.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the Chief Justice of Pakistan appointed? (2)
f: Article 175A deals with the appointment of judges of the Supreme Court, and it covers the appointment of the Chief Justice of Pakistan.
r: Article 175A was inserted by the 18th Amendment (2010) and changed by the 26th Amendment (October 2024), which lets a parliamentary committee pick the Chief Justice from the three senior-most judges.

q: Which city was the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate? (2)
f: The Abbasids moved the capital from Damascus to the new city of Baghdad, founded by Caliph al-Mansur in 762 AD.
r: The Umayyad Caliphate before them had its capital at Damascus.

q: Which is the largest country of Africa by area? (2)
f: Algeria has an area of about 2.38 million square km, the largest in Africa since South Sudan separated from Sudan in 2011.
r: Before 2011 Sudan was the largest country in Africa.

q: The Rafah crossing connects the Gaza Strip with which country? (2)
f: Rafah is the border crossing between the southern Gaza Strip and Egypt's Sinai region.
r: It is the only crossing of Gaza that does not open directly into Israel.

q: Karl (Carl) Benz is known as the inventor of which machine? (2)
f: Karl Benz built the Benz Patent-Motorwagen in 1885 to 1886, regarded as the first practical petrol-powered automobile.
r: The company he founded later joined Daimler to form Mercedes-Benz.

q: Fill in the blank: She left her keys ___ the table. (2)
f: Keys resting on a flat surface such as a table take the preposition on.
r: In is used for enclosed spaces, for example in the drawer.

q: What is the name of the Pakistani military operation launched against India in May 2025? (2)
f: Pakistan named its military response to India in May 2025 Bunyan-um-Marsoos.
r: The name means a solid structure, taken from a verse of the Quran (Surah As-Saff).

q: Which country launched the Chandrayaan-3 mission in 2023? (2)
f: India launched Chandrayaan-3 on 14 July 2023 and landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023.
r: India became the first country to land near the south pole of the Moon.

q: Who is known as the father of chemistry? (2)
f: Jabir bin Hayyan (Geber) is called the father of chemistry in most Pakistani textbooks because of his early experimental work.
r: Some sources call Antoine Lavoisier the father of modern chemistry, so sources differ.

q: What is the currency of Mongolia? (2)
f: The currency of Mongolia is the tugrik (togrog), code MNT.
r: Its capital is Ulaanbaatar.

q: Who is known as the Daughter of the East? (2)
f: Daughter of the East is the title of the autobiography of Benazir Bhutto, and it is also used for her.
r: Benazir Bhutto was the first woman prime minister of a Muslim-majority country.

q: In which city was the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) formed by signing the treaty in 1949? (2)
f: The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington DC on 4 April 1949.
r: NATO headquarters are today in Brussels, Belgium.

q: Who were the founders of YouTube? (2)
o: Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim
f: YouTube was started in 2005 by three former PayPal employees: Chad Hurley, Steve Chen and Jawed Karim.
r: Google bought YouTube in 2006.

q: Which Pakistani athlete won an Olympic gold medal at Paris 2024 with a throw of 92.97 metres? (2)
f: Arshad Nadeem won the javelin throw gold at Paris 2024 with an Olympic record of 92.97 metres.
r: It was Pakistan's first individual Olympic gold medal and its first Olympic gold since 1984.

q: What is the length of the Gaza Strip? (2)
f: The Gaza Strip is a narrow coastal strip about 41 km long and 6 to 12 km wide.
r: Its total area is roughly 365 square kilometres.

q: Who won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for work on mRNA vaccines? (2)
f: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman for nucleoside base modifications that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19.
r: Their work made the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines possible.

q: What are people who deny Allah and do not believe in Him called in Islamic terminology? (2)
f: A Kafir is a person who rejects belief in Allah. A Munafiq is a hypocrite and a Fasiq is a sinner.
r: A Muttaqi is a God-fearing person.

q: Who is the owner of X (formerly Twitter)? (2)
f: Elon Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 and renamed it X in July 2023.
r: Jack Dorsey was a co-founder of Twitter.

q: Which Pakistani scientist received the Khwarizmi International Award from Iran in 2024? (2)
f: Prof Dr M. Raza Shah of the University of Karachi won the 37th Khwarizmi International Award, an Iranian science prize, in January 2024.
r: Dr Atta-ur-Rahman is another well-known Pakistani chemist and received the UNESCO Science Prize.

q: Which country hosted the 2023 Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Heads of State summit? (2)
f: India chaired the SCO in 2023 and hosted the summit virtually in July 2023.
r: Pakistan hosted the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Islamabad in October 2024.

q: A train covers 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
f: Speed = distance divided by time = 120 / 2 = 60 km/h.
r: To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by 5/18, so 60 km/h is about 16.7 m/s.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 12th of that month be?
f: From the 2nd to the 12th is 10 days. 10 = 7 + 3, so move 3 days forward from Friday: Saturday, Sunday, Monday.
r: The same weekday repeats every 7 days, so the 2nd, 9th, 16th and 23rd are all Fridays here.

q: What is 1369 x 1369?
r: 1369 is a perfect square, because 37 x 37 = 1369.

q: What is 45% of 300?
How many parts does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have?
f: The 1973 Constitution is divided into 12 parts, containing 280 articles and several schedules.
r: The 1973 Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and came into force on 14 August 1973.

q: What are the capitals of Australia, Canada and Japan, in that order?
f: The capital of Australia is Canberra, of Canada is Ottawa and of Japan is Tokyo.
r: Sydney, Toronto and Osaka are bigger or famous cities but they are not capitals.

q: According to Pakistan's official stand, which city should be the capital of Palestine?
f: Pakistan supports a two-state solution with an independent Palestine on the pre-1967 borders and East Jerusalem (Al-Quds Al-Sharif) as its capital.
r: Ramallah is the administrative seat of the Palestinian Authority, but it is not the claimed capital.

q: What is the chemical formula of the ammonium ion?
f: The ammonium ion is formed when ammonia (NH3) gains a hydrogen ion, giving NH4 with a positive charge.
r: Ammonium salts such as ammonium nitrate and ammonium sulphate are widely used as fertilizers.

q: Which instrument is used to measure the area of an irregular figure on a map or drawing?
f: A planimeter is a mechanical instrument that measures area by tracing the outline of a shape.
r: An odometer measures distance travelled, and a hygrometer measures humidity.

q: Army is to soldier as navy is to what?
f: A soldier is a member of the army, in the same way a sailor is a member of the navy.
r: A member of the air force is called an airman.

q: Who is the author of the book On the Origin of Species?
f: Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, explaining evolution by natural selection.
r: Alfred Russel Wallace developed a similar idea of natural selection independently.

q: Who is the author of the political book The Prince?
f: The Prince was written by the Italian thinker Niccolo Machiavelli, around 1513.
r: The book advises rulers to be practical in politics, which gave rise to the word Machiavellian.

q: What was the educational qualification of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah?
f: Jinnah studied law at Lincoln's Inn in London and qualified as a barrister at a very young age.
r: He was called to the Bar in 1896 and was among the youngest Indians to be a barrister.

q: Who was Baba Bulleh Shah?
f: Baba Bulleh Shah (1680 to 1757) was a famous Sufi poet who wrote in Punjabi, known for his kafis.
r: His shrine is in Kasur, Punjab.

q: Emperor Hirohito belonged to which country?
f: Hirohito was the Emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989, including the whole period of World War II.
r: His reign was the longest of any historical Japanese emperor.

q: Which country was the top source of workers' remittances to Pakistan in 2024 and also in FY2026?
f: State Bank of Pakistan data show Saudi Arabia as the largest source, with about 9.78 billion US dollars in FY2026, ahead of the UAE at about 8.81 billion.
r: Total remittances reached a record of about 41.6 billion US dollars in FY2026.

q: Who won the men's Ballon d'Or in 2023?
f: Lionel Messi won the 2023 Ballon d'Or, his eighth, after Argentina won the 2022 World Cup.
r: Ousmane Dembele is the reigning winner (2025), and the 2026 award is due on 26 October 2026.

q: Is the area of a figure always positive or negative?
f: Area measures the size of a surface, so it is always a positive quantity.
r: Area is measured in square units such as square metres.

q: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee all belong to which group of animals?
f: Monkeys, apes and chimpanzees are all members of the order Primates.
r: Humans also belong to the primates.

q: Which is the biggest country in the world by population?
f: India overtook China as the most populous country in 2023, with more than 1.4 billion people.
r: China was the most populous country until 2022, and Pakistan ranks among the top six.

q: Fill in the blank with a preposition: He is kind ___ slaves.
f: The adjective kind takes the preposition to, so the correct phrase is kind to.
r: Similar adjective-preposition pairs are cruel to, good at and fond of.

q: Fill in the blank: They said that Adil ___ ill.
f: The reporting verb said is in the past tense, so the reported clause also moves to the past: was.
r: In reported speech, present tense usually shifts one step back into the past tense.

q: In which year did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests at Chagai?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998, after India tested in May 1998.
r: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: Who wrote the book The Republic?
f: The Republic is a famous philosophical work written by the Greek philosopher Plato.
r: Plato was a student of Socrates and the teacher of Aristotle.

q: What are the capital and currency of Mexico?
f: The capital of Mexico is Mexico City and its currency is the Mexican peso (MXN).
r: Mexico City is one of the largest cities in North America.

q: Who was the captain of the Pakistan ODI cricket team at the 2023 World Cup?
f: Babar Azam captained Pakistan in ODIs at the 2023 ODI World Cup in India, and resigned as captain after it.
r: The current ODI captain is different from Babar Azam, so the 2023 answer is not the answer for today.

q: The speed of a train is twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed = 60 km in half an hour = 120 km/h. Train speed = 2 x 120 = 240 km/h, so in 30 minutes it covers 120 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A car runs at 90 km/h and the train runs at double the car speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 180 / 2 = 90 km.
r: To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

q: Change into passive voice: Parents send their children to school.
o: Children were sent to school by their parents.
Children are sent to school by their parents.
Children is sent to school by parents.
Children have been sent to school by their parents.
f: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive uses are plus the past participle: are sent.
r: Passive form for the simple present is: is/am/are plus past participle.

q: Change into passive voice: They constructed a wall.
o: A wall is constructed by them.
A wall has been constructed by them.
A wall was constructed by them.
A wall were constructed by them.
f: The sentence is in the simple past tense, so the passive uses was plus the past participle: was constructed.
r: Passive form for the simple past is: was/were plus past participle.

q: Change into passive voice: We boil the milk.
o: The milk was boiled by us.
The milk is boiled by us.
The milk is being boiled by us.
f: The sentence is in the simple present tense, so the passive is: The milk is boiled by us.
r: The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

q: Which ray is negatively charged?
f: Beta rays are streams of electrons, so they carry a negative charge.
r: Alpha rays are positively charged helium nuclei, and gamma rays have no charge.

q: Hen is to chicken as cow is to what?
f: A chicken is the young one of a hen, and a calf is the young one of a cow.
r: A lamb is the young of a sheep, a foal of a horse and a kid of a goat.

q: What is the name of the border between India and China?
f: The effective border between India and China is called the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
r: The McMahon Line is the traditional boundary in the eastern sector.

q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Ali runs more faster than Akram.
Ali runs most faster than Akram.
f: Faster is already a comparative, so more must not be added before it.
r: Double comparatives such as more better or more faster are always wrong.

q: What is the correct indirect speech of: He said, "We won the match."?
o: He said that they won the match.
He said that they had won the match.
He said that we had won the match.
He said that they have won the match.
f: We changes to they, and the simple past won changes to the past perfect had won.
r: In indirect speech after a past reporting verb, the simple past becomes the past perfect.

q: What is the least count of a standard screw gauge?
f: A standard screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 circular divisions, so least count = 1 / 100 = 0.01 mm.
r: A vernier caliper usually has a least count of 0.1 mm.

q: Which country won the Cricket World Cup in 1992?
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.
r: It remains Pakistan's only ODI World Cup title.

q: How many days are there in a week?
f: A week has seven days, Monday to Sunday.
r: A normal year has 52 weeks and one extra day.

q: What is a poem written on the death of a beloved person or friend called?
f: A poem of mourning written for someone who has died is called an elegy.
r: An ode praises a person or thing, and a sonnet has fourteen lines.

q: What is the definition of a radian?
o: The angle at the centre of a circle made by an arc equal in length to the radius
The angle made by an arc equal to the diameter
The angle of a full circle
f: One radian is the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length equals the radius.
r: A full circle is 2 pi radians, which equals 360 degrees.

q: Torque depends on which two quantities?
o: Force and distance from the axis
f: Torque is force multiplied by the perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.
r: The SI unit of torque is the newton metre.

q: Which one is different from the rest: Mango, Carrot, Apple, Banana?
f: Mango, apple and banana are fruits, while carrot is a vegetable.
r: Carrot is a root vegetable rich in vitamin A.

q: Who discovered hydrogen?
f: Henry Cavendish identified hydrogen as a distinct substance in 1766.
r: Lavoisier later gave hydrogen its name.

q: What is the unit of acceleration due to gravity?
f: Acceleration is change in velocity per unit time, so its unit is metre per second squared.
r: Near Earth's surface g is about 9.8 m/s squared.

q: What is the biggest source of fresh water on Earth?
f: About two thirds of the world's fresh water is locked in glaciers and ice caps.
r: Only about 3 percent of all water on Earth is fresh water.

q: On which sector does the economy of Pakistan mainly depend?
f: Agriculture is the largest employer and the backbone of Pakistan's economy, with cotton, wheat and rice as major crops.
r: Textiles, based on cotton, are the largest export sector.

q: What is the degree (highest power) of a quadratic equation?
f: A quadratic equation has the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, so its highest power is 2.
r: A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

q: Which country issued the world's first adhesive postage stamp, the Penny Black, in 1840?
f: The Penny Black was issued in Great Britain in May 1840.
r: Pakistan issued its first postage stamps in 1947.

q: In which year was the Palestinian group Hamas founded?
f: Hamas was founded in 1987 during the first Palestinian intifada.
r: The Palestine Liberation Organization was founded earlier, in 1964.

q: In which year was the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) founded?
f: The PLO was founded in 1964 at a meeting of the Arab League in Jerusalem.
r: Hamas was founded much later, in 1987.

q: Where was the G20 summit of 2023 held, and where was the one of 2025 held?
o: Rio de Janeiro, then New Delhi
f: The 2023 summit was in New Delhi, India, and the 2025 summit was in Johannesburg, South Africa.
r: It was the first G20 summit held on African soil.

q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2024?
f: The 2024 G20 summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
r: Brazil held the G20 presidency from December 2023 to November 2024.

q: In which sport is the word love used for a zero score?
f: In tennis, a score of zero is called love.
r: Other tennis scores run 15, 30, 40 and then game.

q: How many general seats are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: After the merger of FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the National Assembly has 266 general seats, plus 60 women and 10 minority seats.
r: The total strength is 336 seats; before the merger it was 342 with 272 general seats.

q: Who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2023?
f: The 2023 Nobel Peace Prize went to Narges Mohammadi of Iran for her fight against the oppression of women.
r: She was jailed in Iran at the time of the award.

q: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023?
f: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Norwegian writer Jon Fosse.
r: Annie Ernaux of France won in 2022.

q: Which country hosted the Hajj in 2024?
f: Hajj is performed in Makkah and nearby places in Saudi Arabia, which hosts it every year.
r: Hajj 2024 took place in June 2024.

q: What is the highest temperature officially recorded in Pakistan, at Turbat in 2017?
f: Turbat in Balochistan recorded 53.7 C on 28 May 2017, accepted as Pakistan's highest reliable temperature.
r: Jacobabad is commonly known as the hottest city of Pakistan.

q: Which country hosted the COP28 climate summit in 2023?
f: COP28 was held in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, from November to December 2023.
r: COP27 was in Egypt in 2022 and COP29 in Azerbaijan in 2024.

q: Which country brought a genocide case against Israel before the International Court of Justice in December 2023?
f: South Africa filed the case at the ICJ in December 2023, under the Genocide Convention.
r: The ICJ sits in The Hague, Netherlands.

q: Which international organization's 1947 partition plan (Resolution 181) paved the way for the creation of Israel?
f: The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 181 in November 1947, proposing separate Arab and Jewish states.
r: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948.

q: Who is the Supreme Leader of Iran as of October 2026?
f: Ali Khamenei was killed on 28 February 2026, and the Assembly of Experts chose his son Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader in March 2026.
r: Ali Khamenei had held the post since 1989; Masoud Pezeshkian is the President, not the Supreme Leader.

q: Which of these countries became a full member of BRICS in January 2024?
f: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined BRICS as full members on 1 January 2024.
r: Indonesia joined later, in January 2025.

q: What does KPK stand for?
f: KPK is the short form of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a province of Pakistan.
r: The province was renamed from North-West Frontier Province in 2010.

q: What is the approximate area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa covers about 101,741 square kilometres.
r: Balochistan is the largest province, with about 347,190 sq km.

q: Which is the largest city of Israel by population?
f: Jerusalem has the largest population of any Israeli city, about one million people.
r: Tel Aviv is the largest commercial centre, and most countries keep their embassies there.

q: What does Newton's second law of motion state?
o: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction
A body stays at rest unless a force acts on it
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
f: Newton's second law says F = ma: the force on a body equals its mass multiplied by its acceleration.
r: The unit of force, the newton, is named after him.

q: Which letter is missing in the sequence A, E, I, __, U?
f: The sequence lists the English vowels in order: A, E, I, O, U.
r: The English alphabet has five vowels.

q: Which is the lightest metal?
f: Lithium has the lowest density of all metals, about 0.53 g per cubic centimetre.
r: Lithium is used in rechargeable batteries.

q: What is the value of log 100 to base 10?
f: Since 10 raised to the power 2 equals 100, log 100 = 2.
r: The common logarithm of 10 is 1.

q: What is the value of log of 60 to the base 4, to two decimal places?
f: log4(60) = ln 60 divided by ln 4 = 4.0943 divided by 1.3863, which is about 2.95. It lies between 2 (log4 16) and 3 (log4 64).
r: log4(64) is exactly 3, so log4(60) must be a little less than 3.

q: About how long does sunlight take to reach the Earth?
f: The Sun is about 150 million km away and light travels at about 300,000 km per second. This gives about 500 seconds, or 8 minutes 20 seconds.
r: Moonlight takes only about 1.3 seconds to reach the Earth.

q: What is the property of a skew-symmetric matrix A?
o: A transpose equals the inverse of A
f: A matrix is skew-symmetric when its transpose is the negative of itself, A^T = -A. Because of this all its diagonal elements are zero.
r: A transpose equal to A is the property of a symmetric matrix.

q: What does the word 'optimistic' mean?
f: An optimistic person has a positive outlook and expects good outcomes.
r: The opposite of optimistic is pessimistic.

q: If Ali's sister is your mother, then what is Ali to you?
f: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mama). Ali is the brother of your mother, so he is your maternal uncle.
r: A father's brother is called a paternal uncle (chacha).

q: In which country does the Kanchenjunga mountain lie?
o: On the border of India and Nepal
f: Kanchenjunga lies on the border between Nepal and Sikkim (India) in the Himalayas.
r: At 8,586 m it is the third highest mountain in the world after Everest and K2.

q: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
f: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.
r: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa.

q: Which is the largest country in North America by area?
f: Canada is about 9.98 million square km, slightly larger than the United States, and the largest country in North America.
r: Canada is the second-largest country in the world after Russia.

q: Why has Pakistan not recognised Israel?
o: It supports Palestinian rights and wants a Palestinian state first
Because Israel is too far away
Because of a border war with Israel
f: Pakistan says it will not recognise Israel until a fair solution gives Palestinians an independent state based on the 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah also opposed the creation of Israel.

q: Is zero included in the natural numbers? Choose the textbook answer.
f: Natural numbers are counting numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on. Adding zero gives the whole numbers.
r: Some modern books include zero in natural numbers, so definitions differ.

q: What is the difference between rational and irrational numbers?
o: A rational number can be written as p over q, an irrational number cannot
A rational number has no decimals
An irrational number is always negative
Rational numbers are always whole numbers
f: Rational numbers can be written as a fraction p over q with q not zero. Irrational numbers like root 2 and pi cannot, and their decimals never end or repeat.
r: The square root of 2 was among the first numbers proven irrational.

q: Ali is six years older than his sister. When Ali's sister is 12 years old, how old is Ali?
f: Ali's age is the sister's age plus 6, so 12 + 6 = 18 years.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

q: How many medals did Pakistan win at the 2024 Paris Olympics?
f: Pakistan won one medal, the gold medal of Arshad Nadeem in javelin throw.
r: Arshad Nadeem threw an Olympic record 92.97 m.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1340 are male. What is the percentage of females?
r: Male students are 89.33% of the total.

q: What was the name of Pakistan's military operation against India in May 2025, in reply to India's Operation Sindoor?
f: Pakistan named its response Operation Bunyan-um-Marsoos, meaning a wall of lead.
r: Swift Retort was the name used for the February 2019 response.

q: The Simla Agreement of 1972 between Pakistan and India took place after which war?
f: The Simla Agreement was signed after the 1971 war that led to the creation of Bangladesh.
r: It was signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.

q: Who is generally called the pioneer of Artificial Intelligence, having coined the term in 1956?
f: John McCarthy coined the term Artificial Intelligence at the 1956 Dartmouth conference.
r: Alan Turing is also called a founder of AI for his earlier work.

q: Where is the deepest point of the Pacific Ocean?
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 10,900 m deep, the deepest known point of the oceans.
r: The Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific near Guam.

q: What is the present status of Palestine at the United Nations?
f: Since 2012 Palestine has been a non-member observer state at the UN. Full membership is blocked in the Security Council by a US veto.
r: In May 2024 the General Assembly gave Palestine extra rights, but not a vote.

q: Which Palestinian organisation is resisting Israel and controls the Gaza Strip?
f: Hamas is a Palestinian group that has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007.
r: Hezbollah is based in Lebanon.

q: Which country gives the most military aid to Israel?
f: The United States is the largest provider of military aid to Israel, about 3.8 billion dollars each year under a 2016 agreement.
r: Germany is usually named as the second-largest arms supplier.

q: Which border did Pakistan support for a Palestinian state at the UN?
o: The 1967 borders with Al-Quds as capital
f: Pakistan supports a two-state solution with an independent Palestine on pre-1967 borders and Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital.
r: The Six-Day War of 1967 led to Israel occupying the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

q: What did Pakistan demand at the UN for Palestine and Gaza?
f: Pakistan has repeatedly demanded an immediate and lasting ceasefire in Gaza and humanitarian aid.
r: Pakistan has been a vocal supporter of Palestine at the OIC and UN.

q: Which letter and number come next in the series: B3, D5, F7, ?
f: Letters move by two (B, D, F, H, J) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So the next term is H9, followed by J11.
r: Such series follow two patterns at once, one for letters and one for numbers.

q: Z=3, X=5, V=7, T=9. What comes next?
f: Letters go back by two (Z, X, V, T, R) and numbers go up by two (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). So next is R=11.
r: The letters skipped are Y, W, U and S.

q: Who is the President of the State of Palestine (Palestinian Authority) as of October 2026?
f: Mahmoud Abbas has been President of the Palestinian Authority since 2005 and was re-elected Fatah leader in May 2026. Presidential elections have been announced for 2027 but may be delayed.
r: Abbas is also known as Abu Mazen and leads the Fatah movement.

q: What is the system called in which one person holds absolute power over a country?
f: In an autocracy, one person has unlimited power and is not bound by elections or a legislature. A monarchy can be an autocracy only if the monarch rules absolutely.
r: Rule by a small group is called oligarchy, while rule by the people is democracy.

q: If 15 pencils cost Rs 175, what is the price of 12 pencils?
f: Price of 12 pencils = 175 x 12 / 15 = 2100 / 15 = Rs 140.
r: This is a direct proportion question: fewer items cost proportionally less.

q: A man buys a pen for Rs 30 and sells it at a 40 percent profit. What is the selling price?
f: Profit = 40 percent of 30 = 12 rupees. Selling price = 30 + 12 = Rs 42.
r: Selling price = cost price x (100 + profit percent) / 100.

q: Which two regions does the Khunjerab Pass connect?
f: The Khunjerab Pass lies on the Karakoram Highway and links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
r: At about 4,693 metres it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Warsak Dam situated?
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar, which is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It was built in the 1960s with Canadian help under the Colombo Plan.

q: How many vowel letters are in the series: A b d A U C M A u E?
f: The vowels are A, A, U, A, u and E, which makes 6.
r: The English vowels are A, E, I, O and U.

q: Who was the first woman Governor of Sindh?
f: Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan became Governor of Sindh in 1973, the first woman to hold the post in Pakistan.
r: She was the wife of Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan.

q: Solve for x: 4x + 5 = 6.
r: Always move the constant to the other side first, then divide by the coefficient of x.

q: On which date did the current Gaza war begin?
f: The war began on 7 October 2023 after Hamas attacked southern Israel and Israel launched a military campaign in Gaza.
r: A ceasefire framework was agreed in October 2025, but fighting and disputes continued afterwards.

q: What are the capital and currency of the United States?
f: The capital of the United States is Washington D.C. and its currency is the US Dollar (USD).
r: Washington D.C. is named after the first President, George Washington.

q: What are the capital and currency of the United Kingdom?
f: The capital of the United Kingdom is London and its currency is the Pound Sterling (GBP).
r: The pound is one of the oldest currencies still in use in the world.

q: What is the Sun?
f: The Sun is a star, a huge glowing ball of hot gas that produces energy by nuclear fusion.
r: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres from the Earth.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 12 years old?
f: The sister is 12 when Ali is 4, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 12 she will be 12 + 8 = 20.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: Which billionaire bought Twitter, which was later renamed X?
f: Elon Musk bought Twitter in October 2022 for about 44 billion US dollars and renamed it X in 2023.
r: Musk is also the head of Tesla and SpaceX.

q: What is the SI unit of the modulus of elasticity (Young's modulus)?
f: Young's modulus is stress divided by strain. Strain has no unit, so the unit is that of stress, N/m squared, called the pascal.
r: Strain itself is a pure ratio and has no unit.

q: Which isotope is used to treat goiter and thyroid disorders?
f: The thyroid gland absorbs iodine, so radioactive iodine-131 is used to shrink an overactive thyroid or goiter.
r: Cobalt-60 is used mainly in cancer radiotherapy.

q: A man walks 20 km in 40 minutes. How long does he take to walk 1 km?
f: Time per km = 40 / 20 = 2 minutes.
r: Speed here is 30 km per hour.

q: Whom did the British blame most for the War of 1857?
f: After 1857 the British held the Muslims mainly responsible, as the last Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar had led the revolt.
r: Muslims paid a heavy price, and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind to explain the causes.

q: If 5 men complete a piece of work in 11 days, how many days will 1 man take to do it?
f: Total work = 5 x 11 = 55 man-days. One man needs 55 days.
r: Fewer workers need proportionally more days, which is inverse proportion.

q: Who wrote the science fiction novel Dune?
f: Dune was written by the American author Frank Herbert and published in 1965.
r: Frank Patrick Herbert Jr. wrote several sequels to Dune.

q: The 2023 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to Claudia Goldin for her work on what?
f: Claudia Goldin was honoured for improving our understanding of women's earnings and labour market participation over the centuries.
r: She was the third woman to win the economics Nobel prize.

q: Which country won the FIFA Women's World Cup in 2023?
f: Spain beat England 1-0 in the 2023 final held in Sydney, Australia.
r: It was Spain's first women's World Cup title, and the 2023 event was co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand.

q: Rearrange the letters BUYAET to form a word. What is the last letter of the word?
f: The letters BUYAET form the word BEAUTY, which ends with the letter Y.
r: Unscrambling words is a common verbal intelligence question.

q: For what work was the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded?
o: Nucleoside base modifications that enabled mRNA vaccines against COVID-19
f: Katalin Kariko and Drew Weissman won it for discoveries about nucleoside base modifications that made effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19 possible.
r: Their work helped develop the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna vaccines.

q: A rectangle has a width of 8 and a length of 4. What is its area?
f: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 4 x 8 = 32.
r: Perimeter of this rectangle would be 2 x (4 + 8) = 24.

q: Into which river does the Ravi River fall?
f: The Ravi joins the Chenab near Ahmad Pur Sial in Punjab, Pakistan.
r: The Chenab later joins the Sutlej and then the Indus.

q: Boat is to water as aeroplane is to what?
f: A boat moves through water, and an aeroplane moves through air, the medium it travels in.
r: Analogy questions test the same relation in both pairs.

q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place in India?
f: The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district. A mob burned a police station, after which Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: The Non-Cooperation Movement was suspended soon after the incident.

q: If AX = B, where A is an invertible matrix, what is X?
f: Multiply both sides on the left by the inverse of A. This gives (A inverse)(A)X = (A inverse)B, so X = A inverse times B.
r: Matrix multiplication is not commutative, so the order of A inverse and B matters.

q: What is the value of (x^2 times x^2) divided by x^2?
f: x^2 times x^2 = x^4 by adding powers. Then x^4 divided by x^2 = x^2 by subtracting powers.
r: When multiplying powers of the same base you add exponents, and when dividing you subtract them.

q: What is the value of 2 square root 8 plus 3 square root 8?
f: Both terms have the same radical, so add the coefficients: 2 + 3 = 5. The result is 5 square root 8, which equals 10 square root 2.
r: Only like radicals (same number under the root) can be added directly.

q: What is 70% of 70?
What is 90% of 90? (2350)
r: Taking 90% of a number 90 gives 81, which equals 9 x 9.

q: Why do we boil milk? (1761)
f: Boiling heats milk enough to kill harmful germs and bacteria and makes it safe to drink and keep for longer.
r: Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, is the industrial process of heating milk to destroy germs.

q: Why do parents send their children to school? (1695)
f: Schools provide education, which develops knowledge, skills and character in children.
r: Education is a fundamental right of children under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.

f: Division comes before addition (BODMAS), so 2/2 = 1 and 2 + 1 = 3.
r: BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

q: What is the antonym of wild? (969)
f: Wild describes an animal or place not under human control. Tame means gentle and domesticated, its opposite.
r: Domestic is another common antonym of wild.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan? (423)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
r: He was assassinated at Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: How many months of the year have 31 days? (382)
f: The months are January, March, May, July, August, October and December, which makes 7.
r: February has 28 days (29 in a leap year).

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120? (349)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12, and a quarter of 12 is 3. Working in the other order gives 30 and then 3.
r: One quarter of one tenth equals 1/40, so the answer is 120/40.

q: In which year did Pakistan join SEATO? (322)
f: Pakistan joined the South-East Asia Treaty Organization in 1954 when the Manila Pact was signed in September 1954.
r: Some sources give 1955 (ratification), and Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (CENTO) in 1955.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (311)
f: Percentage present = 1200 / 1500 x 100 = 80%.
r: The absent students are 300, which is 20%.

q: A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what? (278)
f: Snakes have no external ears and cannot hear airborne sound well; they sense ground vibrations instead.
r: Bats find their way by echolocation using high-pitched sounds.

q: Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan? (243)
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah took the oath as the first Governor General of Pakistan on 15 August 1947.
r: He held the office until his death on 11 September 1948.

q: A pen is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage? (233)
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed? (231)
f: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963.
r: It settled the border in the Karakoram region and led to the Karakoram Highway cooperation.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Cricket World Cup? (216)
f: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand under Imran Khan, beating England in the final at Melbourne.
r: It remains Pakistan's only 50-over World Cup title.

q: What is the capital of Austria? (215)
f: Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria. Canberra is the capital of Australia, not Austria.
r: Austria and Australia are often confused because of their similar names.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (212)
f: If yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday. The day after tomorrow is Saturday plus 2 days, which is Monday.
r: The day after tomorrow is always three days after yesterday.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh? (208)
f: Syed Murad Ali Shah of the Pakistan Peoples Party has been Chief Minister of Sindh since 2016 and won a third consecutive term in 2024.
r: He succeeded Qaim Ali Shah, who had held the post from 2008 to 2016.

q: Which word is a synonym of wild? (194)
f: Wild means living or growing in nature, not controlled by humans, which is untamed. The other options are its opposites.
r: Its antonym is tame or domesticated.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab? (193)
f: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024.
r: She is the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab; her predecessor in 2021-22 was Usman Buzdar.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred? (191)
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet (PBUH), was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH. He was killed by Wahshi, a slave of Jubayr ibn Mut'im.
r: Hazrat Hamza (RA) is known as Asadullah and Sayyid ush-Shuhada (Chief of the Martyrs).

q: Which one is different from the others: monkey, panda, baboon, chimpanzee? (188)
f: Monkey, baboon and chimpanzee are primates, while the panda is a bear.
r: Giant pandas feed mainly on bamboo.

q: What is the capital of Nepal? (186)
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal. It lies in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayan region.
r: Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, lies on the border of Nepal and China.

q: What is the largest river of Pakistan? (185)
f: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan.
r: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

q: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed? (171)
f: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Ayub Khan and Nehru, with the World Bank as a party.
r: It gave Pakistan the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers.

q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan? (169)
f: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan in 1947 and served until 1954.
r: He later served as a judge and President of the International Court of Justice.

q: Which surah is called the heart (Qalb) of the Quran? (168)
f: A hadith narrated in the books of Hadith describes Surah Yaseen as the heart of the Quran.
r: Surah Yaseen is the 36th surah and has 83 verses.

q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball? (167)
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket, while football is played with the feet and no bat.
r: Football is the most widely played sport in the world.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China? (166)
f: The Khunjerab Pass in the Karakoram links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang in China.
r: At about 4,693 m it is one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: Where is the headquarters of NATO? (166)
f: NATO has its headquarters in Brussels, Belgium.
r: NATO was founded in 1949, and its headquarters was in Paris before 1967.

q: Which city is commonly called the heart of Pakistan? (163)
f: Lahore is popularly called the heart (Dil) of Pakistan because of its culture and history.
r: Sources differ, as Punjab province is also sometimes described as the heart of Pakistan.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (162)
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
r: The Khyber Pass is about 53 km long and has been an invasion and trade route for centuries.

q: From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar? (160)
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958 for about 3 million US dollars, and it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
r: Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon was in office at the time.

q: Total students in a class are 1500 and 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (158)
r: Present and absent percentages add up to 100%.

q: Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan? (156)
f: The lyrics of Qaumi Tarana were written by the poet Abul Asar Hafeez Jalandhari. It was officially adopted in 1954.
r: The music of the national anthem was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla.

q: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'? (156)
f: 'Friends Not Masters: A Political Autobiography' was written by Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan. It was published in 1967.
r: Ayub Khan was Pakistan's second President and ruled from 1958 to 1969.

q: What is the capital of Somalia? (154)
f: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia on the Indian Ocean coast.
r: Hargeisa is the capital of the self-declared Somaliland.

q: In which year was the OIC founded? (153)
f: The OIC was founded in September 1969 at Rabat, Morocco, after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
r: Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes? (153)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed multiplied by time.

q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (151)
f: Absent students = 500 - 340 = 160. Percentage absent = 160 / 500 x 100 = 32%.
r: The present students make up 68%, which is the number many people wrongly give.

q: Who was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025, succeeding Ali Amin Gandapur? (145)
f: Sohail Afridi of PTI was elected Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025.
r: Since 11 October 2026 Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has been under governor's rule (Governor Faisal Karim Kundi), so the province has no sitting Chief Minister at the moment. In 2021-22 the answer was Mahmood Khan.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 90? (143)
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and one third of 9 is 3. The same value results from taking one tenth of one third of 90 or one third of 10% of 90.
r: Fractions of a number can be taken in any order because multiplication is commutative.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League? (142)
f: Jinnah formally joined the Muslim League in 1913, at the persuasion of Allama Iqbal, Wazir Hasan and others. He remained a member of the Indian National Congress at the same time.
r: He left the Congress in 1920 over differences with Gandhi's policies.

q: What is the capital of Bhutan? (141)
f: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.
r: Bhutan is a landlocked Himalayan kingdom between India and China.

q: Who was the first President of Pakistan? (140)
f: Under the 1956 Constitution, Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956. Before this, the head of state was the Governor General.
r: Quaid-e-Azam and Ghulam Muhammad had served as Governor General, not as President.

q: Who was the first captain of the Pakistan cricket team? (137)
f: Abdul Hafeez Kardar captained Pakistan in its first Test series in India in 1952.
r: Under Kardar, Pakistan won its first Test on English soil at The Oval in 1954.

q: How many articles does the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan have? (134)
f: The 1973 Constitution, Pakistan's third constitution, contains 280 articles.
r: It has 12 parts and 7 schedules and was enforced on 14 August 1973.

q: Saifullah (Sword of Allah) was the title of whom? (133)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) gave the title Saifullah to the great general Khalid bin Waleed (R.A).
r: He commanded the Muslim armies in the conquest of Syria and the battle of Yarmouk.

q: Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan? (133)
f: Khawaja Muhammad Asif of the PML-N is the Federal Minister for Defence in the current government.
r: Pervez Khattak, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Defence Minister from 2018 to 2022.

q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan? (131)
f: Sir Abdul Rashid became the first Chief Justice of the Federal Court of Pakistan in 1949.
r: Muhammad Munir succeeded him as Chief Justice in 1954.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points? (131)
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim League reply to the Nehru Report.
r: They demanded safeguards for Muslims such as separate electorates and a federal system.

q: In which year was the Kargil war fought? (130)
f: The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan took place from May to July 1999.
r: It followed the 1998 nuclear tests of both countries.

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed? (129)
f: Abu Jahl, a leader of the Quraysh, was killed in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. He was struck down by two young Ansari brothers, Muadh and Muawwidh.
r: Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have? (128)
f: A triangular prism has two triangular bases and three rectangular side faces: 2 + 3 = 5 faces.
r: It also has 9 edges and 6 vertices. Candidates gave different answers (3, 4, 5, 6) because the paper did not name the prism type; the triangular prism is the usual one.

q: Your mother is my brother's sister. What is the relation between you and me? (128)
f: My brother's sister is my own sister, so your mother is my sister. Therefore I am your maternal uncle.
r: A mother's brother is called the maternal uncle (mamu in Urdu).

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Education of Pakistan? (128)
f: Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui holds the Federal Education and Professional Training portfolio in 2026.
r: Shafqat Mahmood held the post in 2021-22 when candidates sat the test.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located? (128)
f: The UN headquarters is on the east side of Manhattan in New York City, USA.
r: The UN also has major offices at Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.

q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan? (126)
f: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: Gilgit-Baltistan is home to K2, the second highest mountain in the world.

q: In which year did the Khilafat Movement start in India? (126)
f: The movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliph and the Muslim holy places after the First World War. Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.
r: The movement ended after Turkey abolished the caliphate in 1924.

q: Who founded the newspaper Dawn? (124)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941 to voice the Muslim League view.
r: Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

q: How many daughters did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) have? (119)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) had four daughters: Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima (RA).
r: All of his daughters except Hazrat Fatima (RA) died during his lifetime.

q: What is the length of the coastline of Pakistan? (119)
f: Pakistan's Arabian Sea coastline is officially about 1,046 km.
r: It is shared between Sindh (about 270 km) and Balochistan (about 770 km).

q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan? (117)
f: The national flag was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kedwaii on the basis of the Muslim League flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted it on 11 August 1947.
r: The green part of the flag stands for the Muslim majority and the white strip for minorities.

q: What is the capital of Turkey? (117)
f: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, chosen by Ataturk in 1923 when the republic was founded.
r: Istanbul is the largest city of Turkey but not its capital.

q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan? (117)
f: Astana is the capital of Kazakhstan; it replaced Almaty as capital in 1997.
r: Astana was renamed Nur-Sultan in 2019 and returned to the name Astana in 2022.

q: After how many years of independence did Pakistan get its first constitution? (116)
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, nearly 9 years later.
r: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day, and the 1956 constitution was abrogated in 1958 by Ayub Khan.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)? (116)
f: The OIC secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
r: Its intended permanent seat is East Jerusalem once it is liberated.

q: On what date did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points, and in reply to which report? (114)
o: 28 March 1929, reply to the Nehru Report
23 March 1940, reply to the Cripps Mission
28 March 1929, reply to the Simon Report
12 December 1930, reply to the Lahore Resolution
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presented his 14 Points in Delhi on 28 March 1929 as an answer to the Nehru Report of 1928.
r: The 14 Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, including separate electorates and one-third seats in the central legislature.

q: What is the capital of Malaysia? (113)
f: Kuala Lumpur is the capital and largest city of Malaysia.
r: Putrajaya is the administrative capital where government offices are located.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khyber fought? (112)
f: The Battle of Khyber (7 AH) was fought by the Muslims against the Jewish tribes living in the fortresses of Khyber.
r: Hazrat Ali conquered the fort of Qamus in this battle.

q: What is the largest ocean in the world? (112)
f: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square km, roughly a third of the Earth.
r: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is the deepest point on Earth.

q: What is the longest (largest) river of Asia? (109)
f: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the longest river in Asia.
r: It is the third longest river in the world.

q: Which is the shortest surah of the Quran? (108)
f: Surah Al-Kausar has only 3 verses and 10 words, making it the shortest surah.
r: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah with 286 verses.

q: In which year of the Hijri calendar was the Battle of Uhud fought? (107)
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (625 AD) near Mount Uhud, a year after Badr.
r: The archers left their post on the hill, which let the Quraish attack from behind.

q: Who was the commander of the Quraish army in the Battle of Badr? (107)
f: Abu Jahl (Amr bin Hisham) led the Quraish army at Badr in 2 AH and was killed in the battle.
r: Abu Sufyan led the trade caravan that the Quraish army came to protect.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy? (106)
f: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval in London on 18 June 2017 under captain Sarfraz Ahmed.
r: Pakistan has won the Champions Trophy only once; India won the 2025 edition.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan (as of 2026)? (105)
f: Mir Sarfraz Bugti took office as Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and was still serving in mid-2026.
r: His predecessors included Abdul Quddus Bizenjo (2021-2023) and Jam Kamal Khan (2018-2021).

q: What is the largest district of Pakistan by area? (104)
f: Chagai in Balochistan covers about 44,748 square km, the largest district of Pakistan by area.
r: Chagai is where Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998 (Ras Koh hills).

q: In which year was the first Cricket World Cup held? (104)
f: The first Cricket World Cup (the Prudential Cup) was played in England and began on 7 June 1975.
r: West Indies won the first two tournaments, in 1975 and 1979.

q: In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located? (103)
f: The Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the walled city of Lahore. It was built in 1634-35 in the Mughal era.
r: It is famous for its Kashi tile work.

q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia? (103)
f: Saudi Arabia uses the Saudi riyal.
r: The UAE uses the dirham and Kuwait the dinar.

q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish and stayed in its belly? (102)
f: Hazrat Younus (A.S) was swallowed by a large fish and prayed to Allah from within its belly.
r: He is also called Dhun-Nun and Surah Younus is named after him.

q: Ali walks towards north, then turns left, and after some time turns left again. In which direction does he face now? (100)
f: North then left is west. A second left from west is south.
r: Candidates wrote North, but two left turns make a 180 degree turn.

q: In which year did the Minto-Morley Reforms (Indian Councils Act) come into effect? (100)
f: The Indian Councils Act of 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Lord Minto was Viceroy and Lord Morley was Secretary of State for India.
r: The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms followed in 1919.

q: Who is the current Chairman of NAB (National Accountability Bureau)? (99)
f: Lt Gen (retd) Nazir Ahmad became NAB chairman in 2023 and received a three-year extension from March 2026.
r: Earlier chairmen were Javed Iqbal (2017-22) and Aftab Sultan (2022-23).

q: What is the currency of Russia? (99)
f: Russia uses the ruble.
r: Ukraine uses the hryvnia and Kazakhstan the tenge.

q: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted as the Government of India Act? (97)
f: The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, which introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
r: The Government of India Act 1935 later introduced provincial autonomy.

q: Which is the smallest continent? (96)
f: Australia (Oceania) has an area of about 7.7 million square km, the smallest of the continents.
r: Australia is the only continent that is also a single country.

q: What is the highest civil award of Pakistan? (96)
f: Nishan-e-Pakistan is the highest civil award given by the state of Pakistan.
r: Hilal-e-Imtiaz ranks below Nishan-e-Pakistan among civil awards.

q: If 5 boys write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how much time will one boy take to write one page? (96)
f: Each boy writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 boys write 5 pages, one page each, in 5 minutes).
r: Rate per boy is 1 page per 5 minutes.

q: What is the capital of Australia? (95)
f: Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
r: Sydney is Australia's largest city.

q: What is the name of the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan? (95)
f: The Durand Line was fixed in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand and the Afghan ruler Amir Abdur Rahman Khan, and it forms the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
r: The Radcliffe Line separates Pakistan and India, and the McMahon Line is between India and China.

q: What is the height of K2, the second highest mountain in the world? (94)
f: K2 is about 8,611 m high (some sources give 8,609 m).
r: K2 lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border and is also called Mount Godwin-Austen.

q: How many sons did the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have? (94)
f: He had three sons, Qasim, Abdullah (also called Tayyab and Tahir) and Ibrahim, and all of them died in infancy.
r: Ibrahim was the son of Hazrat Maria Qibtiyya and the others were sons of Hazrat Khadija.

q: Which is the largest country in the world by area? (93)
f: Russia covers about 17.1 million square km, more than any other country.
r: Canada is the second largest country by area.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world? (93)
f: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of about 1,642 metres.
r: Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake.

q: In which city is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO) located? (93)
f: The WHO is a specialised agency of the United Nations and has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: The International Olympic Committee is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

q: What is the national drink (juice) of Pakistan? (92)
f: Sugarcane juice is regarded as the national juice or drink of Pakistan.
r: Pakistan is among the world's top producers of sugarcane.

q: Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon. (92)
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a shape but a measure formed by two rays.
r: A hexagon has six sides.

q: On which date was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan? (92)
f: President Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958 and General Ayub Khan became the Chief Martial Law Administrator. Ayub Khan then removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.
r: The second martial law came in 1969 under Yahya Khan and the third in 1977 under Zia-ul-Haq.

q: Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place? (91)
f: The Bolan Pass is a natural route in Balochistan linking Quetta with the plains of Sibi and Dadhar.
r: Khojak Pass, not Bolan, links Quetta with Chaman and Afghanistan.

q: Which city in Pakistan is known as the City of Flowers? (91)
f: Peshawar is called the City of Flowers because of its many gardens.
r: Lahore is known as the City of Gardens.

q: What is a quarter of 120? (90)
f: 120 divided by 4 is 30.
r: A quarter of a number is the same as 25% of it.

q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah die? (90)
f: Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah died in Karachi on 9 July 1967 and was buried near the mausoleum of Quaid-e-Azam.
r: She is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: In which country did Pakistan open its first embassy? (89)
f: Pakistan opened its first embassy in Iran, which was also among the first countries to recognise Pakistan in 1947.
r: Some sources differ on early diplomatic firsts, but Iran is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks and tests.

q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 90? (88)
r: 1/10 of a number is the same as 10% of it.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi qissa (folk romance) Sohni Mahiwal? (88)
f: The best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal is attributed to Fazal Shah (Sayyid Fazal Shah). Waris Shah is known for Heer Ranjha.
r: Sources differ on tellers of this tale, but Fazal Shah is the usual textbook answer.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought? (88)
f: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
r: It was the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraysh.

q: Which is the largest hot desert of the world? (88)
f: The Sahara in North Africa covers about 9 million square kilometres and is the largest hot desert.
r: Counting cold deserts, Antarctica is the largest desert in the world.

q: Who is the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)? (87)
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP in Lahore in 1967.
r: Benazir Bhutto later became the first woman prime minister of a Muslim country.

q: What is the capital of Canada? (87)
f: Ottawa is the capital of Canada, although Toronto is the largest city.
r: Ottawa lies on the Ottawa River in the province of Ontario.

q: Who is the author of the book India of My Dreams? (86)
f: India of My Dreams is a collection of the writings of Mahatma Gandhi on his vision for India, compiled by R. K. Prabhu.
r: Gandhi's autobiography is titled The Story of My Experiments with Truth.

q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (85)
f: If yesterday was Sunday, today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday. The day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
r: The day after tomorrow is always two days after today.

q: How many seats of the National Assembly of Pakistan are reserved for women? (85)
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves 60 seats for women, filled by proportional representation.
r: Another 10 seats are reserved for non-Muslims.

q: Which woman accepted Islam first? (84)
f: Hazrat Khadija (R.A), wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the first person and first woman to accept Islam.
r: Hazrat Sumayya was the first martyr of Islam.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan? (83)
f: Manchar Lake in Sindh is generally regarded as Pakistan's largest freshwater lake.
r: Keenjhar Lake near Thatta is the second largest and a major drinking water source for Karachi.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Badr? (83)
f: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr, six from the Muhajirun and eight from the Ansar. About 70 of the Quraish were killed.
r: About 70 Sahaba were martyred later in the Battle of Uhud.

q: What is the capital of Azad Kashmir? (82)
f: Muzaffarabad is the capital of Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: Muzaffarabad lies at the confluence of the Jhelum and Neelum rivers.

q: A man going towards north turns left after some time, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing? (82)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
r: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

q: Which is the highest mountain range of Pakistan? (82)
f: The Karakoram range contains K2 (8,611 m), the highest peak in Pakistan.
r: Pakistan's mountain ranges include Himalaya, Karakoram, Hindu Kush, Sulaiman and Kirthar.

q: In which year did the Quit India Movement start? (82)
f: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.
r: The Muslim League opposed it and its slogan was Divide and Quit.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (81)
f: Hazrat Hamza was a son of Abdul Muttalib, so he was a paternal uncle of the Prophet (PBUH). He was also close in age and a foster brother.
r: Hazrat Hamza was martyred in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH and is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada.

q: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of which prophet? (81)
f: Hazrat Maryam (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Isa (AS), who was born without a father by Allah's command.
r: Surah Maryam, the 19th surah of the Quran, is named after her.

q: Who is the President of Iran? (81)
f: Masoud Pezeshkian won the 2024 snap election and took office in July 2024.
r: His predecessor Ebrahim Raisi died in a helicopter crash in May 2024.

q: What was the Cripps Mission? (81)
o: A 1942 British mission offering India post-war dominion status
A 1946 plan for a united India
f: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 with proposals to win Indian support in World War II; both Congress and the Muslim League rejected them.
r: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 is a different mission.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)? (81)
f: The IMF has its headquarters in Washington DC, United States, close to the World Bank.
r: The UN headquarters is in New York and the WTO is in Geneva.

q: Which is the largest province of Pakistan by population? (80)
f: Punjab has more than half of Pakistan's population (about 127 million in the 2023 census).
r: Sindh is the second most populous province.

q: In which year did Swat merge fully into Pakistan? (80)
f: Swat acceded to Pakistan in 1947 but remained a princely state. It was merged fully on 28 July 1969, when the state was abolished.
r: Swat is now part of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest? (80)
f: Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest in 1999 as the first Pakistani to do so.
r: Samina Baig became the first Pakistani woman to climb Everest in 2013.

q: Asadullah (Lion of Allah) is the title of which Sahabi? (79)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was given the title Asadullah for his bravery. Hazrat Hamza is also called Asadullah.
r: Khalid bin Waleed is known as Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

q: Who is the President of France? (79)
f: Emmanuel Macron was first elected President of France in 2017 and re-elected in 2022; he is still in office.
r: The French President is elected for a five-year term.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Senate of Pakistan as of October 2026? (79)
f: Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani of the PPP was elected Chairman of the Senate and sworn in on 9 April 2024.
r: Sadiq Sanjrani was Senate chairman from 2018 to 2024.

q: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of whom? (78)
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA).
r: The first written compilation of the Quran was kept with her during the caliphate of Hazrat Umar (RA) and later.

q: Kaleemullah is the title of which prophet? (78)
f: Kaleemullah means the one who spoke with Allah, the title of Hazrat Musa (A.S).
r: The Torah (Taurat) was revealed to Hazrat Musa (A.S).

q: What is the range of the Pakistani surface-to-surface missile Ababeel? (78)
f: Ababeel is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of 2,200 km, as announced by ISPR after its first test.
r: Ababeel is stated to have MIRV (multiple warhead) capability and was first tested in January 2017.

q: In which year were the modern Olympic Games first held? (78)
f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Baron Pierre de Coubertin revived the Games.
r: The International Olympic Committee was founded in 1894.

q: Zabihullah (the one sacrificed for Allah) is the title of which prophet? (78)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah because he was offered for sacrifice by his father Ibrahim (AS) in obedience to Allah.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Ismail (AS) is the ancestor of the Arab tribes.

q: Israel is the title of which prophet? (77)
f: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (A.S). The Children of Israel are his descendants.
r: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (A.S) and the father of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S).

q: Who wrote the book My Brother, about Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah? (77)
f: Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, wrote My Brother, which was published after her death.
r: Fatima Jinnah is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won? (77)
f: Pakistan has two Nobel laureates: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
r: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate in history.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls? (76)
f: Girls = 500 - 360 = 140. Percentage of girls = 140 / 500 x 100 = 28%.
r: The boys make up 72% of the students.

q: How many member countries does the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) have? (76)
f: The OIC has 57 member states spread over four continents.
r: It is the second largest intergovernmental organisation after the United Nations.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations? (75)
f: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
r: The UN itself was founded in 1945.

q: What is one tenth of 120? (75)
f: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place left, so 120 becomes 12.
r: One tenth is the same as 10%.

q: What type of government was set up by the 1962 constitution of Pakistan? (75)
f: The 1962 constitution concentrated executive power in the President, so it created a presidential form of government.
r: The 1973 constitution replaced it with a parliamentary system.

q: In which Surah does the phrase Bismillah occur twice (once at the start and once within a verse)? (75)
f: In Surah Al-Naml the Bismillah appears at the start and again in verse 30 in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS) to the Queen of Sheba.
r: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah without Bismillah at its start.

q: In which year did the USA invade Afghanistan? (75)
f: US-led forces began strikes on Afghanistan on 7 October 2001 after the 9/11 attacks.
r: The US withdrawal from Afghanistan was completed in August 2021.

q: What is the national flower of Pakistan? (74)
f: Jasmine (Chambeli) is the national flower of Pakistan.
r: Its Latin name is Jasminum officinale.

q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (73)
f: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid (RA) married the Prophet (PBUH) about 15 years before the first revelation.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) did not marry again during her lifetime.

q: In which year was the Nehru Report presented? (73)
f: The Nehru Report, drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru, was presented in 1928.
r: Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: In which year was the Tashkent Agreement signed? (73)
f: The Tashkent Declaration ending the 1965 war was signed on 10 January 1966 under Soviet mediation.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri.

q: Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world? (72)
f: China produces more tea than any other country, with India second.
r: Kenya and Sri Lanka are the next major producers.

q: Which country is called the Land of the Rising Sun? (72)
f: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun; its name Nippon means origin of the sun.
r: Its capital is Tokyo.

q: From whom did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh? (72)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir, the Hindu ruler of Sindh, in 711-712 AD.
r: Raja Dahir was defeated near Raor.

q: What was the profession of Mother Teresa? (71)
f: Mother Teresa was a Roman Catholic nun who founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950 to serve the poor and the sick.
r: She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and was declared a saint by the Catholic Church in 2016.

q: Who accompanied the Prophet (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah? (71)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH) and they hid in the cave of Thawr.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) stayed behind in Makkah to return the trusts kept with the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Where was the Battle of Plassey fought? (71)
f: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Plassey in Bengal, on the bank of the Bhagirathi river.
r: Plassey is in present-day West Bengal, India.

q: Riyadh is the capital of which country? (70)
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
r: Saudi Arabia hosts the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah.

q: How many Muslims were in the army at the Battle of Uhad (Uhud) in the end? (70)
f: About 1000 set out, but Abdullah bin Ubayy withdrew with about 300 men, leaving about 700 Muslims.
r: The Quraish army at Uhad numbered about 3000.

q: Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan? (70)
f: Muhammad Ayub Khan promoted himself to the rank of Field Marshal in 1959.
r: Asim Munir was promoted to Field Marshal in May 2025, making him the second.

q: How many planets are there in the solar system? (69)
f: There are eight planets since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
r: The planets in order from the Sun start with Mercury and end with Neptune.

q: What is the length of the Suez Canal? (69)
f: The Suez Canal is about 193 km, which is roughly 120 miles.
r: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and opened in 1869.

q: On which river is the Diamer Bhasha Dam being built? (69)
f: The Diamer Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River in Gilgit-Baltistan, near Chilas.
r: Tarbela Dam is also on the Indus River.

q: In which city is the Pakistan Steel Mills located? (69)
f: Pakistan Steel Mills was built at Pipri near Karachi with Soviet help.
r: It began production in the early 1980s.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Bank located? (69)
f: The World Bank has its headquarters in Washington, D.C., USA. It was set up in 1944 at the Bretton Woods conference.
r: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is also headquartered in Washington, D.C.

q: Which is considered the largest desert of Pakistan? (69)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks name the Thar Desert in Sindh as the largest desert of Pakistan. It is shared with India.
r: Sources differ: some measure only the Pakistani portion, where Cholistan is also large.

q: What is the total number of seats of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab? (68)
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 reserved for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
r: The National Assembly has 336 seats, of which Punjab has 141 general seats.

q: Which city of Pakistan is called the Manchester of Pakistan? (68)
f: Faisalabad is the centre of Pakistan's textile industry, like Manchester in England.
r: Faisalabad was formerly called Lyallpur.

q: Who founded Facebook? (68)
f: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 from Harvard University with his college roommates.
r: The company was renamed Meta Platforms in 2021.

q: In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are men and the rest are girls. What is the percentage of girls? (68)
f: Men = 2/3 x 30 = 20, so girls = 30 - 20 = 10. Percentage of girls = 10/30 x 100 = 33.33%.
r: Girls are 1/3 of the passengers.

q: What is the largest lake of the world by area? (67)
f: The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 square km, is the largest inland body of water and is classed as a lake.
r: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest.

q: On what date was the Nehru Report presented? (67)
f: The Nehru Report was presented at the All Parties Conference at Lucknow on 28 August 1928.
r: Motilal Nehru headed the committee that prepared it.

q: Where is the headquarters of SAARC located? (67)
f: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987.
r: SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka.

q: Who was the second Prime Minister of Pakistan? (67)
f: Liaqat Ali Khan was the first Prime Minister. After his assassination in 1951, Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second.
r: Nazimuddin had been Governor-General before becoming Prime Minister.

q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (66)
f: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan in Pakistan with Xinjiang in China.
r: At about 4693 m it is among the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: Who has taken the most Test wickets for Pakistan? (66)
f: Wasim Akram took 414 Test wickets, the highest by any Pakistani bowler, and the record still stands in 2026.
r: Waqar Younis is second for Pakistan with 373 Test wickets.

q: In which mountain range is K2, the second highest peak in the world, located? (65)
f: K2 (8,611 m) lies on the Pakistan-China border in the Karakoram range.
r: K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen and Chogori.

q: What is the highest military award of Pakistan? (65)
f: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest gallantry award of Pakistan, given for extraordinary bravery in battle.
r: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed was the first recipient in 1948.

q: Rooh Ullah (Ruhullah) is the title of which prophet? (65)
f: Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, the Spirit of Allah, because he was born by Allah's command without a father.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kalimullah and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) Khalilullah.

q: What is the currency of Japan? (65)
f: Japan's currency is the yen. Its code is JPY.
r: The Bank of Japan issues the yen.

q: Which country lies to the east of Pakistan? (64)
f: India shares Pakistan's long eastern border.
r: Pakistan borders Iran to the west, Afghanistan to the north-west, China to the north and India to the east.

q: In which language did Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai write poetry? (64)
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai (1689-1752) is the great Sufi poet of the Sindhi language.
r: His famous collection of poetry is called Shah Jo Risalo.

q: How old was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (SAW) when his mother, Hazrat Amina, passed away? (64)
f: Hazrat Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet (SAW) was about six years old.
