r: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then cared for him until he died when the Prophet (SAW) was eight.

q: Who is the President of China as of October 2026? (64)
f: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013 and also leads the Communist Party.
r: The head of government, the Premier, is Li Qiang, so the office of PM is not held by Xi.

q: Who was the first child to accept Islam? (63)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA), the cousin of the Prophet, accepted Islam as a boy of about 10 years old. He was raised in the Prophet's household.
r: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) the first free adult man to accept Islam.

q: What is the currency of Egypt? (63)
f: Egypt uses the Egyptian pound.
r: Egypt controls the Suez Canal.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Army? (63)
f: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
r: The President appoints the service chiefs on the advice of the Prime Minister.

q: What was Fatima Jinnah's profession? (62)
f: Fatima Jinnah trained as a dentist and qualified from the University of Calcutta in 1923. She ran her own dental clinic in Bombay.
r: She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation) and contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.

q: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan are famous players of which sport? (62)
f: Both Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan of Pakistan were world champions in squash.
r: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times in a row and Jansher Khan won the World Open eight times.

q: Which company is responsible for inventing the iPhone, launched in 2007 under its co-founder Steve Jobs? (62)
f: Apple Inc. launched the first iPhone in 2007, with Steve Jobs presenting it.
r: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple with Steve Wozniak in 1976.

q: How many countries have veto power in the United Nations Security Council? (62)
f: Only the five permanent members have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
r: The Security Council also has 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms, who have no veto.

q: Who is the Secretary General of the United Nations? (61)
f: Antonio Guterres has held the post since 2017 and his term ends on 31 December 2026.
r: The selection of his successor is under way in 2026.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Ghotki located? (61)
f: Ghotki is a city and district in northern Sindh, on the border with Punjab.
r: Ghotki lies on the Indus highway between Sukkur and Rahim Yar Khan.

q: Which is the smallest country in the world by area? (61)
f: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square km, the smallest independent state in the world. Monaco is the second smallest.
r: Vatican City is an enclave inside the city of Rome, Italy.

q: To which country does Olympic Airlines (now Olympic Air) belong? (61)
f: Olympic Airlines was the national flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis. It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009.
r: Olympic Airways was nationalised in 1975 and ceased operating as the flag carrier in 2009.

q: What is the antonym of 'tamed'? (61)
f: Tamed means made gentle and under control, so its opposite is wild or untamed.
r: Domesticated is a synonym of tamed.

q: What is the national bird of Pakistan? (60)
f: The chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
r: The Shaheen (falcon) is the national symbol of Pakistan's air force and a popular emblem, but not the national bird.

q: By whom was the Objectives Resolution passed? (60)
f: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 12 March 1949.
r: It later became the preamble of the 1956, 1962 and 1973 constitutions in some form.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2/3? (60)
f: Division comes first: 2/3. Then 2 + 2/3 = 6/3 + 2/3 = 8/3, which is 2 and 2/3.
r: In BODMAS, division is performed before addition.

q: Which one is different: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta, Karachi, Rawalpindi? (60)
f: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta and Karachi are all provincial capitals. Rawalpindi is not a provincial capital, so it is the odd one out.
r: Islamabad, not Rawalpindi, is the federal capital of Pakistan.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice located? (60)
f: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace in The Hague, Netherlands.
r: It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

q: What does the green colour in the national flag of Pakistan represent? (60)
f: The dark green field of the flag stands for the Muslim majority of Pakistan, while the white stripe stands for religious minorities.
r: The crescent symbolises progress and the star symbolises light and knowledge; the flag was adopted on 11 August 1947.

q: What does LOC stand for in the context of Kashmir? (59)
f: LOC stands for Line of Control, the military control line dividing Indian- and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
r: The LOC was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.

q: In which year did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh? (59)
f: East Pakistan broke away after the 1971 war, and the Dhaka surrender took place on 16 December 1971.
r: The Hamoodur Rehman Commission investigated the causes of the 1971 debacle.

q: Who founded the technology company Microsoft? (59)
f: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft on 4 April 1975.
r: Microsoft began in Albuquerque, New Mexico, before moving to Washington State.

q: In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) founded? (59)
f: The SCO was formally founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai, China, by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
r: Its predecessor was the Shanghai Five of 1996, and Pakistan and India became full members in 2017.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of India? (59)
f: Narendra Modi has been Prime Minister since 2014 and began his third consecutive term in June 2024.
r: He is the longest-serving Prime Minister of India after Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi in total years.

q: What is one third of 120? (58)
f: One third of 120 is 120 / 3 = 40.
r: A number divisible by 3 has digits whose sum is divisible by 3; 1+2+0 = 3.

q: Sultan Bahu and Bulleh Shah are poets of which language? (58)
f: Both Sufi poets wrote in Punjabi.
r: Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur and Sultan Bahu in Jhang.

q: What is the smallest bone in the human body? (58)
f: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone, about 3 mm long.
r: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest bone in the body.

q: Who invented the electric bulb (practical incandescent lamp)? (58)
f: Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent bulb in 1879.
r: Joseph Swan in Britain developed a similar lamp at about the same time.

q: Umm Kalsoom (Umm Kulthum) was what of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (58)
f: Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
r: She married Hazrat Usman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).

q: Which is the longest river in the world according to most textbooks? (58)
f: Most textbooks give the Nile as the longest river, at about 6,650 kilometres.
r: Some sources measure the Amazon as longer, so sources differ.

q: Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan? (58)
f: Sardar Ayaz Sadiq of the PML-N was elected Speaker on 1 March 2024 and is the current Speaker.
r: Asad Qaiser, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Speaker from 2018 to 2022.

q: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (58)
f: His name was Abdullah bin Abi Quhafa, and he received the title Siddiq and Atiq.
r: Some narrations say his pre-Islamic name was Abd al-Kaba, which the Prophet (PBUH) changed to Abdullah.

q: In which year did India carry out its first nuclear test? (57)
f: India conducted its first nuclear test (Smiling Buddha) at Pokhran in May 1974.
r: India carried out further tests, Pokhran-II, in May 1998.

q: For which achievement did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize in 2014? (57)
f: She received the Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for the right of children and girls to education.
r: At 17 she is the youngest Nobel laureate in history and shared the prize with Kailash Satyarthi.

q: Nelson Mandela was the leader and later President of which country? (57)
f: Mandela led the struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black President in 1994.
r: He was imprisoned for 27 years and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

q: Ruh-ul-Qudus is the title of which angel? (57)
f: Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit) is a title of the angel Hazrat Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.
r: Hazrat Jibreel (AS) is also called Ameen.

q: Which number comes next: 66, 63, 57, 45, ? (57)
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12, doubling each time, so the next difference is 24. Hence 45 - 24 = 21.
r: Series with doubling differences are common in verbal reasoning tests.

q: Which is the third largest city of Pakistan by population? (57)
f: By population Karachi is first, Lahore second and Faisalabad third, in both the 2017 and 2023 censuses.
r: Faisalabad was formerly called Lyallpur.

q: Who wrote the book Das Kapital? (56)
f: Das Kapital, a critique of capitalism, was written by the German thinker Karl Marx. The first volume appeared in 1867.
r: Friedrich Engels edited and published the second and third volumes after Marx died.

q: Safiullah is the title of which prophet? (56)
f: Safiullah means the chosen one of Allah and is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).
r: Other titles: Khalilullah for Ibrahim, Kaleemullah for Musa and Ruhullah for Isa (A.S).

q: Which country is known as the land of a thousand lakes? (56)
f: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes, giving it this nickname.
r: Canada has the largest total number of lakes in the world.

q: In a bus 30 passengers are travelling and 2/3 of them are male. How many males are in the bus? (56)
r: The remaining 10 passengers (1/3) are female.

q: What is the upper house of the Parliament of Pakistan called? (56)
f: Pakistan's Parliament has two houses, and the upper house is the Senate.
r: The lower house is the National Assembly.

q: Who was the first Hafiz of the Holy Quran? (56)
f: The Quran was revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH), who memorised it first, so he is called the first Hafiz.
r: Among the Companions, Hazrat Ali, Ubayy bin Kab and Zaid bin Thabit were also famous Huffaz.

q: What is the capital of Bahrain? (56)
f: Manama is the capital of Bahrain, an island country in the Persian Gulf.
r: Doha is the capital of Qatar.

q: Hazrat Hajra (Hajar) was the mother of which prophet? (55)
f: Hazrat Hajra was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and gave birth to Hazrat Ismail (AS).
r: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates her search for water.

q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you (taking me as male)? (55)
f: My brother's sister is my sister, so your mother is my sister. I am therefore your mother's brother, that is your maternal uncle.
r: A mother's brother is called mamu in Urdu, and a father's brother is called chacha.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu are there (Hanafi fiqh)? (55)
f: The four faraiz are washing the face, washing the arms up to and including the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing the feet up to the ankles.
r: The faraiz of ghusl are three.

q: Which letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ? (55)
f: The gaps between letters are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter and the 21st is U.
r: The differences in this series increase by 1 each time.

q: What is the relation between Hazrat Musa (AS) and Hazrat Haroon (AS)? (55)
f: Hazrat Haroon (AS) was the elder brother of Hazrat Musa (AS) and was also a prophet.
r: Musa (AS) asked Allah to make Haroon (AS) his helper, as mentioned in the Quran.

q: What is the relation of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) with Hazrat Ismail (AS)? (54)
f: Both were sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), so they were brothers (half-brothers, by different mothers).
r: Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Hajra and Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Sarah.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Khyber (Khaybar) fought? (54)
f: The Battle of Khaybar was fought in 7 AH (628 AD) against the Jewish fortresses of Khaybar.
r: Hazrat Ali is famous for conquering the fort of Qamus in this battle.

q: What is one third of 10% of 120? (54)
f: 10% of 120 is 12, and one third of 12 is 4.
r: One third of one tenth equals 1/30, so the answer is 120/30.

q: Who wrote the poems Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa? (54)
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa in 1909 and Jawab-e-Shikwa in 1913.
r: Both poems were later included in his Urdu collection Bang-e-Dra.

q: Who gave the name Pakistan? (53)
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.
r: Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

q: Which is the fastest bird in the world (in a dive)? (53)
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth.
r: The ostrich is the fastest running bird at about 70 km/h.

q: When did the Cripps Mission come to India? (53)
f: Sir Stafford Cripps reached India in March 1942 with proposals for dominion status after World War II.
r: The Muslim League and Congress both rejected the proposals.

q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC located? (53)
f: OPEC moved from Geneva to Vienna, Austria in 1965 and has been headquartered there since.
r: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960.

q: On which date was the Liaquat-Nehru Pact signed? (53)
f: The Liaquat-Nehru (Delhi) Pact was signed on 8 April 1950 by Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru to protect minorities in both countries.
r: It is also called the Delhi Pact.

q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup? (52)
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times: 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
r: Pakistan is the most successful team in Hockey World Cup history.

q: How many member states does the European Union (EU) have? (52)
f: The EU has 27 member states, and the number has not changed since the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020.
r: Before Brexit the EU had 28 members; Croatia was the last to join, in 2013.

q: What is the capital of Ukraine? (52)
f: Kyiv (also spelled Kiev) is the capital of Ukraine.
r: Kyiv sits on the Dnieper river.

q: Where and when was the All-India Muslim League founded? (52)
f: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 in Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference, at the house of Nawab Salimullah Khan.
r: Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were among its early leaders, and Sir Aga Khan was its first president.

q: Ruble is the currency of which country? (52)
f: The ruble is the currency of Russia.
r: The Russian capital is Moscow.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range? (52)
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, about 7,708 metres high.
r: Some Pakistani textbooks give 7,690 m, so sources differ slightly.

q: Who wrote Humayun Nama, an account of the reign of Emperor Humayun? (52)
f: Gulbadan Begum, a daughter of Babur and aunt of Akbar, wrote Humayun Nama.
r: Akbar had asked her to record her memories for Abul Fazl's Akbarnama.

q: In which city and country is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank located? (52)
f: The Asian Development Bank was founded in 1966 and has its headquarters in Mandaluyong City, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.
r: Japan and the United States are its largest shareholders, and Pakistan is a founding member.

q: What is one third of 90? (51)
f: 90 divided by 3 is 30.
r: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

q: Who suggested the name of the United Nations (UNO)? (51)
f: US President Franklin D. Roosevelt suggested the name United Nations, first used in the Declaration of 1 January 1942.
r: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which three rivers were allotted to Pakistan? (51)
f: The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty gave the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to Pakistan.
r: The treaty gave the eastern rivers Ravi, Beas and Sutlej to India and was brokered by the World Bank.

q: Which country was the first to recognise Pakistan after its creation in 1947, according to most Pakistani textbooks? (51)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks state that Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan. Iran also sent the first ambassador.
r: Sources differ, as some also credit Turkey, and Afghanistan opposed Pakistan's UN membership.

q: What was the relation of Abu Talib with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (50)
f: Abu Talib was the son of Abdul Muttalib and a brother of the Prophet's father Abdullah. He raised the Prophet after the death of Abdul Muttalib.
r: Abu Talib was the father of Hazrat Ali (RA) and protected the Prophet during the early years in Makkah.

q: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International? (50)
f: Amnesty International has its international secretariat in London.
r: It was founded in London in 1961 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

q: Boxer Muhammad Ali belonged to which country? (50)
f: Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer from Louisville, Kentucky.
r: He won the Olympic light heavyweight gold medal in Rome in 1960.

q: Who is the President of Russia? (50)
f: Vladimir Putin is the President of Russia, in office since 2012 after earlier terms from 2000 to 2008.
r: He was re-elected in March 2024 for a term of six years.

q: Krone is the currency of which country? (50)
f: The Danish krone is the currency of Denmark. Norway also uses a krone.
r: Sweden uses the krona and Finland uses the euro.

q: How many pillars of Islam are there? (49)
f: The five pillars are Shahadah (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
r: Salah is the pillar performed five times daily.

q: What is the title of Liaqat Ali Khan? (49)
f: Liaqat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was given the title Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
r: He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Abdul Muttalib with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (49)
f: Abdul Muttalib was the father of Abdullah, the Prophet's father, so he was the paternal grandfather. He looked after the Prophet after the death of his mother Hazrat Amina.
r: Abdul Muttalib was the chief of Quraysh and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

q: What is the total number of surahs in the Holy Quran? (49)
f: The Quran has 114 surahs.
r: Surah Al-Fatiha is the first and Surah An-Nas is the last.

q: Which city was the first capital of Pakistan? (49)
f: Karachi served as the capital from 1947 when Pakistan was created. The capital was shifted to Rawalpindi in 1959 and then to Islamabad in the 1960s.
r: Islamabad was built as the new capital and replaced Rawalpindi, which was the interim capital.

q: Who proposed digging the trench in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab)? (49)
f: Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A) suggested digging a trench, a Persian defence method, to protect Madina.
r: The battle took place in 5 AH.

q: If the 2nd of a month is Saturday, what day is the 28th of that month? (49)
f: The gap is 26 days. 26 mod 7 = 5, so Saturday plus 5 days is Thursday.
r: The 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th would all be Saturdays in this month.

q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded? (49)
f: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A. O. Hume.
r: The All-India Muslim League was formed later, in 1906 at Dhaka.

q: How many articles did the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan have? (49)
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first constitution, had 234 articles.
r: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated in October 1958.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Uhud? (49)
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, including Hazrat Hamza (RA).
r: In the Battle of Badr only 14 Muslims were martyred.

q: Which country does not have a regular army? (49)
f: Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 after a civil war. It relies on police forces for security.
r: Dominica, Iceland and Panama are other countries without a standing army.

q: What is the currency of Bangladesh? (48)
f: Bangladesh uses the taka.
r: Pakistan, India and Nepal use rupees, while Bhutan uses the ngultrum.

q: Which country is the second largest in the world by area? (48)
f: Russia is the largest country and Canada, with about 9.98 million square km, is second.
r: China and the United States follow closely as third and fourth.

q: On what date did the Chauri Chaura incident happen? (48)
f: A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh on 4 February 1922.
r: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after this incident.

q: Which was the first battle fought by the Muslims? (48)
f: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
r: About 313 Muslims faced an army of nearly 1000 Quraish at Badr and won a decisive victory.

q: Which prophet was given a great kingdom, including rule over the jinn and the winds? (48)
f: Allah gave Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) a unique kingdom, with jinn, birds and winds under his command.
r: Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawud (AS), who was also a prophet and king.

q: How many continents are there in the world? (48)
f: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia (Oceania).
r: Asia is the largest continent and Australia the smallest.

q: What is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)? (48)
f: Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Quetta, which one candidate wrote, is the capital of Balochistan.
r: Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities in South Asia.

q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan? (48)
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the total fell to 336 seats. These are 266 general, 60 women and 10 minority seats.
r: Before this change the National Assembly had 342 seats.

q: In which year did Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina? (47)
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 AD, the 13th year of prophethood.
r: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this event.

q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Zun-Noorain (Possessor of Two Lights)? (47)
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW), one after the other, so he was called Zun-Noorain.
r: His wives from the Prophet's family were Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

q: In which city is the Badshahi Mosque located? (47)
f: The Badshahi Mosque stands in Lahore opposite the Lahore Fort.
r: It was built by Emperor Aurangzeb in 1673.

q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which tribe? (47)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) belonged to the Quraish tribe, to its clan Banu Hashim.
r: Banu Aws and Banu Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina who became the Ansar.

q: In which direction of Pakistan is Iran located? (47)
f: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan, bordering Balochistan.
r: Pakistan also shares borders with Afghanistan in the west and north-west and China in the north.

q: On which date was the Battle of Badr fought? (47)
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, the first major battle between Muslims and the Quraish.
r: It is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

q: On what date did Pakistan get its first constitution? (47)
f: Pakistan's first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and the country became an Islamic Republic.
r: It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law on 7 October 1958 and 23 March is now Pakistan Day.

q: Whose motto is Faith, Unity, Discipline? (47)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah gave the motto Faith, Unity, Discipline (Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem) to the nation.
r: It is the national motto of Pakistan.

q: A book is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit? (46)
f: Profit = selling price - cost price = 40 - 30 = Rs 10.
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: Who was the first man to embrace Islam? (46)
f: Among adult free men, Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the first to accept Islam.
r: Hazrat Khadija (RA) was the first woman and Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child to accept Islam.

q: What is the total number of Ghazwat (battles in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part personally)? (46)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 27 Ghazwat. Sources differ, as some list 26 or 29.
r: The expeditions he did not attend personally are called Sariyya.

q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr? (46)
f: The Muslim army at Badr numbered about 313 men, against roughly 1000 Quraish soldiers.
r: Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).

q: If the letters BEYTUA are rearranged to make a correct word, what is the last letter of that word? (46)
f: The letters rearrange to BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
r: Beauty is a six-letter English word and the scrambled form BEYTUA uses exactly the same letters.

q: Which Sahabi is known by the title Jame ul Quran (compiler of the Quran)? (46)
f: Hazrat Uthman (RA) had the Quran copied into one standard text and sent copies to the major cities.
r: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) first gathered the Quran into one volume after the Battle of Yamama.

q: Which country opposed Pakistan's admission to the United Nations in 1947? (46)
f: Afghanistan was the only country that voted against Pakistan's membership of the UN in September 1947. It later withdrew its objection.
r: Pakistan became the 56th member of the United Nations on 30 September 1947.

q: Who is the son of Hazrat Hajira (A.S)? (46)
f: Hazrat Hajira was the wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S).
r: The well of Zamzam sprang up near the infant Ismail (A.S) in Makkah.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)? (46)
f: The IAEA has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. It promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy.
r: The IAEA is an independent organization that reports to the UN General Assembly and Security Council.

q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup? (46)
f: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3-3 draw in the final held in Qatar on 18 December 2022.
r: Lionel Messi captained Argentina to this win, their third World Cup title.

q: How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) have? (45)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (AS) and Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
r: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was born to Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq (AS) to Hazrat Sarah.

q: What is Pakistan's rank in the world by population (2026)? (45)
f: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, the United States and Indonesia.
r: Pakistan's population is estimated at over 250 million and may overtake Indonesia by around 2050.

q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (45)
f: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 90 x 1/5 = 18 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are boys. How many girls are there? (45)
r: Girls are 1/3 of the class, which is 10 students.

q: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran? (45)
f: Hazrat Musa (AS) is named about 136 times in the Quran, more than any other prophet.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is the next most frequently mentioned prophet.

q: What is an angle less than 90 degrees called? (45)
f: An angle smaller than 90 degrees is called an acute angle.
r: Two acute angles can add up to 90 degrees, in which case they are complementary.

q: Which Sahabi did the Prophet (PBUH) call the door of knowledge? (45)
f: A hadith reports the Prophet (PBUH) saying: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its door.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

q: Which languages were declared official languages in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan? (45)
f: The 1956 Constitution made Urdu and Bengali the state languages of Pakistan.
r: The Bengali language movement of 1952 forced this recognition.

q: Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan? (45)
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 runs in Tests and is Pakistan's leading Test run scorer. He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.
r: Javed Miandad (8,832) and Inzamam-ul-Haq (8,829) come next.

q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered? (44)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
r: The conquest followed the Quraysh breaking the Treaty of Hudaibiya.

q: In which year did the United Nations come into being? (44)
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945 after ratification by the main founding members.
r: United Nations Day is observed every year on 24 October.

q: K2, the second highest mountain in the world, is also known as what? (44)
f: K2 is also known as Mount Godwin-Austen, after the British surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen, and as Chogori.
r: K2 lies in the Karakoram range on the Pakistan-China border and is 8,611 metres high.

q: On which date was the Battle of Uhud fought? (44)
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE) near Mount Uhud, close to Madina.
r: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred in this battle.

q: Waris Shah is a famous poet of which language? (44)
f: Waris Shah (1722-1798) wrote the Punjabi romantic epic Heer Ranjha.
r: Waris Shah is buried in Jandiala Sher Khan, Sheikhupura district.

q: How many months are there in the Islamic calendar? (44)
f: The Islamic (Hijri) calendar is lunar and has 12 months, starting with Muharram.
r: It began with the Hijra of the Prophet (PBUH) in 622 CE.

q: In which year was the first census of Pakistan held? (44)
f: The first census of Pakistan was held in 1951. Later censuses were held in 1961, 1972, 1981, 1998 and 2017.
r: The 2017 census was the first one after nearly 19 years since the 1998 census.

q: In which city was Benazir Bhutto assassinated? (44)
f: Benazir Bhutto was killed after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
r: She was the first woman to head the government of a Muslim-majority country.

q: At what age did the first revelation (wahi) come to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (44)
f: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, came at the age of 40 in the Cave of Hira.
r: Gabriel (Jibreel) delivered the revelation in the month of Ramadan.

q: In which city is Warsak Dam located? (44)
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River about 30 km north-west of Peshawar, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: Warsak Dam was constructed in the 1960s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.

q: Which country mediated the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 between Pakistan and India? (44)
f: The Soviet Union under Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated the Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.
r: Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri died in Tashkent soon after signing.

q: Thimphu is the capital of which country? (44)
f: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
r: Bhutan is a Himalayan kingdom between China and India.

q: In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) deliver his Last (Farewell) Sermon? (44)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered the Last Sermon during the Farewell Hajj on 9 Dhul Hijjah, 10 AH (632 CE), at Arafat. He passed away in 11 AH.
r: The sermon was delivered at Mount Arafat in the valley of Uranah.

q: Which city is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya)? (44)
f: Multan is called the City of Saints because of its many shrines of Sufi saints, such as Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.
r: Multan is also known as the City of Mangoes.

q: Which is the largest salt mine of Pakistan? (44)
f: The Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district is the largest salt mine in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
r: Khewra salt is mostly rock salt, known as Himalayan pink salt.

q: What is the population of Pakistan according to the 2023 census? (44)
f: The 2023 digital census recorded Pakistan's population as about 241.49 million.
r: The 2017 census had recorded about 207.7 million, and candidates in 2022 used estimates of about 220 million.

q: According to the 1956 Constitution, what was the minimum age to become President of Pakistan? (44)
f: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be a Muslim of not less than 40 years of age.
r: Some candidates remembered 45, but 40 is the age given in the Constitution of 1956.

q: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of whom? (43)
f: Hazrat Ayesha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA).
r: Her mother was Umm Ruman.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed? (43)
f: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916. It was an agreement in which the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam was the main architect of the pact and was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity.

q: Who was the founder of the Indian National Congress? (43)
f: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885.
r: Its first session in Bombay was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: The OIC is an organization of which countries? (43)
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation is the collective voice of Muslim countries of the world.
r: The OIC was founded in 1969 in Rabat and its headquarters are in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 was made with the mediation of which organization? (43)
f: The treaty between Pakistan and India was brokered by the World Bank and signed in Karachi in September 1960.
r: India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan rejects this move.

q: In which year was the Sui gas field in Balochistan discovered? (43)
f: Natural gas was discovered at Sui in Balochistan in 1952 and supply started in 1955.
r: Sui is the largest natural gas field of Pakistan by output historically.

q: Who abrogated the 1956 constitution of Pakistan? (43)
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
r: Ayub Khan, the army chief, removed Iskander Mirza only 20 days later.

q: Who discovered X-rays in 1895? (43)
f: Wilhelm Conrad Rontgen, a German physicist, discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode ray tubes.
r: Rontgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.

q: What is the boundary line between India and China called? (43)
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and is the boundary India claims with China in the east.
r: China does not accept the McMahon Line.

q: In which Ghazwa were the blessed teeth of the Prophet (PBUH) martyred? (42)
f: The Prophet's (PBUH) front tooth was broken and he was wounded in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
r: The Battle of Uhud took place near Mount Uhud close to Madinah.

q: Babusar Pass connects the Kaghan Valley with which town? (42)
f: Babusar Pass links Kaghan Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: The pass is about 4,173 metres high and is usually open only in summer.

q: Who is the President of the United States in October 2026? (42)
f: Donald Trump won the 2024 election and was sworn in as the 47th President on 20 January 2025.
r: Joe Biden was President from January 2021 to January 2025, which is the answer candidates gave in 2022; the USA has a President and no Prime Minister.

q: What percentage of the total area of Pakistan is covered by forest? (42)
f: Pakistan's forest cover is about 4.8 percent of its land area according to commonly quoted figures.
r: This is low compared with the world average of about 30 percent; sources differ slightly.

q: Who is the author of the book India Wins Freedom? (42)
f: India Wins Freedom is the autobiographical account of the Indian independence struggle by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
r: Maulana Azad was the first Education Minister of independent India.

q: In which year was the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP) renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (42)
f: The 18th Amendment passed in April 2010 renamed NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Pakistan's parliament approved it that year.
r: The former FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 through the 25th Amendment.

q: Which was the first ghazwa (expedition led personally by the Holy Prophet SAW) of Islam? (42)
f: The first ghazwa, in Safar 2 AH, was Abwa, also called Waddan, in which the Prophet (SAW) himself went out but no fighting occurred.
r: The first major battle of Islam was Badr in Ramadan 2 AH.

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper? (42)
f: 5 papers take 5 minutes, so 1 paper takes 5 / 5 = 1 minute.
r: A rate of 1 paper per minute means that 60 papers would take an hour.

q: On which river is Warsak Dam built? (41)
f: Warsak Dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar.
r: Warsak Dam was built in the 1950s with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.

q: According to the 1962 constitution, how was the President of Pakistan elected? (41)
o: By an Electoral College of Basic Democrats
By the Governors of the provinces
f: The 1962 constitution introduced indirect election of the President by an Electoral College made up of the elected Basic Democrats.
r: The Electoral College initially had 80,000 members, later raised to 120,000 (equally from East and West Pakistan).

q: How many Makki surahs are there in the Quran? (41)
f: Commonly 86 surahs are counted as Makki (revealed before the Hijrah) and 28 as Madani.
r: Sources differ slightly on the exact numbers, but 86 and 28 are the figures most Pakistani textbooks give.

q: What was the old (previous) name of Makkah mentioned in the Holy Quran? (41)
f: The Holy Quran (Surah Al-Imran, verse 96) calls the place of the first house of worship Bakkah, which is an old name of Makkah. It was also known as Umm al-Qura.
r: Yathrib was the old name of Madina, not Makkah.

q: Near which city is the Rohtas Fort located? (41)
f: Rohtas Fort is near Dina in Jhelum district, Punjab. Sher Shah Suri built it in the 16th century.
r: Rohtas Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: How many ayats are there in total in Surah Al-Baqarah? (41)
f: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest surah, has 286 ayats.
r: It is the second surah of the Quran.

q: On what date was the OIC established? (41)
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation was established at the Rabat summit on 25 September 1969.
r: It was set up after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque on 21 August 1969, and its headquarters are in Jeddah.

q: Which province of Pakistan is known as Bab-ul-Islam (Gateway of Islam)? (41)
f: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam because Islam first entered the subcontinent there with Muhammad bin Qasim in 712 AD.
r: The question was asked about a city, but the standard answer is the province Sindh.

q: In which year was Tarbela Dam completed? (41)
f: Construction of Tarbela Dam on the Indus began in 1968 and the dam was completed in 1976.
r: Sources differ: civil works finished around 1974 and the full power project in 1984; 1976 is the usual textbook answer.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize? (41)
f: Dr Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg, for the electroweak theory. He was the first Pakistani and the first Muslim Nobel laureate in science.
r: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 and is the youngest Nobel laureate.

q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will come last? (41)
f: Alphabetical order of the letters is A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
r: Y is the 25th letter of the English alphabet.

q: How many prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran? (41)
f: The Holy Quran mentions the names of 25 prophets.
r: The commonly quoted total number of prophets is 124,000, though the Quran does not state it.

q: Who is known by the title Quaid-e-Millat? (41)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, is known as Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
r: He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed under which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan? (41)
f: Article 19 gives every citizen the right to freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable restrictions.
r: Article 19A of the 1973 Constitution, added in 2010, gives the right to information.

q: Which city of Pakistan is known as the City of Gardens? (41)
f: Lahore is called the City of Gardens because of its many Mughal and public gardens such as Shalimar and Jinnah Garden.
r: Lahore is also called the cultural capital of Pakistan.

q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have? (40)
f: The permanent members are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China, each holding veto power.
r: Russia took the Soviet Union's seat in 1991 and China's seat passed from Taiwan to the PRC in 1971.

q: What is the product of the three cube roots of unity? (40)
f: The cube roots of unity are 1, w and w squared, and w cubed equals 1. Their product is 1 x w x w squared = w cubed = 1.
r: The sum of the three cube roots of unity is 0.

q: What is the currency of Turkey? (40)
f: Turkey uses the Turkish lira.
r: Istanbul, the largest Turkish city, is not the capital; Ankara is.

q: Who is the fastest man on earth (100 m world record holder)? (40)
f: Usain Bolt of Jamaica holds the 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009.
r: He also holds the 200 m record of 19.19 seconds.

q: What is the capital of Balochistan? (40)
f: Quetta is the provincial capital and largest city of Balochistan.
r: Quetta is known as the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.

q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk fought? (40)
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk took place in 9 AH (630 CE) against the Byzantine threat on the northern frontier. The Prophet (PBUH) led about 30,000 Muslims, but no fighting occurred.
r: Tabuk is also called Ghazwa-e-Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship, because of the heat and shortage of supplies.

q: With the help of which country did Pakistan build the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet? (40)
f: The JF-17 Thunder was developed jointly by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
r: JF-17 stands for Joint Fighter 17.

q: Who was the first Ameer-ul-Momineen (Commander of the Faithful) in Islamic history? (40)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was called Khalifa-tu-Rasul Allah, while Hazrat Umar (RA) was the first to be addressed as Ameer-ul-Momineen. Most Islamic history books record this.
r: The title was adopted by later caliphs such as Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: With whom is the theory of relativity associated? (40)
f: The theory of relativity was developed by Albert Einstein.
r: He published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous Presidential Address at the Allahabad session of the Muslim League? (40)
f: Allama Iqbal gave his Allahabad Address in 1930, in which he proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.
r: He gave a series of lectures at Madras and other places in 1928-29, which became Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam.

q: How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan? (40)
f: Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.
r: The whole world has 14 peaks above 8000 m, and K2 at 8611 m is the second highest.

q: Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan? (39)
f: After the death of Quaid-e-Azam in September 1948, Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor General of Pakistan. He held the post until 1951.
r: Nazimuddin was followed as Governor General by Malik Ghulam Muhammad in 1951.

q: Which is the fifth pillar of Islam? (39)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is fifth.
r: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who are able to afford it.

q: In which year was SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) founded? (39)
f: SAARC was founded at a summit in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The idea was proposed by Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman.
r: SAARC has its secretariat in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.

q: Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider? (39)
f: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas was only 20 when he died in 1971 stopping a traitor pilot, and got the award.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

q: In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born? (39)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant, taken as 570 AD in Pakistani textbooks.
r: Some sources give 571 AD.

q: Near which city in Punjab are the ruins of the Indus Valley site of Harappa? (39)
f: The ruins of Harappa lie near the town of Harappa in Sahiwal district of Punjab, Pakistan. The site was first excavated in the 1920s.
r: Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus Valley city, is in Larkana district of Sindh.

q: In which year was the Pakistan Resolution passed? (39)
f: The Resolution was passed at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League on 23 March 1940.
r: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka? (39)
f: Sri Lanka uses the Sri Lankan rupee (code LKR).
r: The taka is the currency of Bangladesh and the rufiyaa that of the Maldives.

q: What is the capital of Malta? (39)
f: Valletta is the capital of Malta and a UNESCO World Heritage city.
r: Mdina was the old capital of Malta before Valletta.

q: Where and in which year were the first Asian Games held? (39)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951. Eleven countries took part.
r: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Safiyyah (RA) with the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (38)
f: Hazrat Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib was a sister of Hazrat Hamza and thus a paternal aunt of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: She was the mother of Hazrat Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).

q: In whose house in Madinah did the camel of the Prophet (PBUH) stop after the Hijrat? (38)
f: The Prophet's camel Qaswa knelt near the house of Hazrat Abu Ayyub Ansari (Khalid bin Zayd), and he stayed there until his own quarters and mosque were built.
r: Abu Ayyub Ansari died during the Muslim siege of Constantinople and is buried near its walls.

q: With the help of which country was Pakistan Steel Mills built? (38)
f: Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical and financial assistance in the 1970s.
r: Its foundation stone was laid in 1973 and production began in 1981.

q: For what purpose was the Khilafat Movement started? (38)
f: Indian Muslims started it to save the Ottoman Caliph and the Ottoman Empire after World War I.
r: It began in 1919 and ended after Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.

q: In which direction of Pakistan is India located? (38)
f: India lies along the eastern border of Pakistan.
r: The Pakistan-India border is about 2,900 km long.

q: Which is the correct spelling? (38)
f: The correct word has a double c and a double m: accommodation.
r: Accommodate follows the same pattern with double c and double m.

q: Who was the first person in space? (38)
f: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth aboard Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.
r: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space in 1963.

q: What was the old name of Faisalabad? (38)
f: Faisalabad was called Lyallpur after Sir James Lyall.
r: It was renamed in 1979 in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.

q: According to the Quran, on which mountain did the ark of Prophet Noah (AS) come to rest? (38)
f: Surah Hud (verse 44) says the ark settled on Al-Judi, a mountain in the Kurdistan region.
r: The Bible names the mountains of Ararat, so sources differ.

q: On which river is Tarbela Dam built? (38)
f: Tarbela Dam is an earth-filled dam on the Indus River in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world, completed in 1974.

q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib passed away? (38)
f: Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (PBUH) after his mother died and passed away when the Prophet was 8 years old. Afterwards his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother Hazrat Amina at the age of 6.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Reko Diq mine project located? (38)
f: Reko Diq is a large copper and gold deposit in Chagai district in the west of Balochistan.
r: Reko Diq is one of the largest undeveloped copper-gold deposits in the world.

q: How many member states does the United Nations have? (38)
f: The UN has 193 member states. South Sudan was the latest to join, in 2011.
r: The Holy See and Palestine are non-member observer states.

q: Famous footballer Mohamed Salah belongs to which country? (38)
f: Mohamed Salah was born in Nagrig, Egypt, and captains the Egyptian national team.
r: He is best known for his years at Liverpool in the English Premier League.

q: Kiwi, a flightless bird, is the national symbol of which country? (38)
f: The kiwi is the national bird of New Zealand, and New Zealanders are often called Kiwis.
r: The kiwi fruit is also linked to New Zealand but it originally came from China.

q: When did World War 2 start? (38)
f: World War 2 began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland.
r: It ended in 1945 with the surrender of Germany in May and Japan in September.

q: How many original members did the United Nations have when it was founded in 1945? (37)
f: The UN began in 1945 with 51 original member states (Poland signed later and is counted among them).
r: The UN now has 193 members.

q: On which prophet was the Zabur (Psalms) revealed? (37)
f: The Zabur was revealed to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).
r: Hazrat Sulaiman (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (A.S).

q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (37)
f: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%.
r: The absent students are 200, which is 13.33%.

q: Which is the largest airport of Pakistan by area? (37)
f: Islamabad International Airport opened in 2018 and is the largest in Pakistan by area (about 19 square km).
r: Karachi Jinnah International is the busiest airport, which is why candidates answered Karachi; sources can differ on what largest means.

q: In which year was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency? (37)
f: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935.
r: Karachi was made its capital.

q: Mahatma Gandhi was a famous leader of which country? (37)
f: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi led the Indian independence movement and the Indian National Congress.
r: Gandhi was assassinated in January 1948 in New Delhi.

q: Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which is the 3rd letter? (37)
f: The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The third letter is E.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

q: What system of government did the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan establish? (37)
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister heads the government and the President is head of state.
r: The 1973 Constitution was passed on 10 April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

q: In which country was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) formed in 1969? (37)
f: The OIC was founded at the Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969.
r: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: In which Hijri year was Hajj made obligatory (according to the most commonly taught view)? (37)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks teach that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH. The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Abu Bakr to lead the Hajj that year.
r: Sources differ, as some scholars give 6 AH or 10 AH; the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 AH.

q: Which is the highest peak of Pakistan? (37)
f: K2 (Mount Godwin-Austen) is 8,611 metres high, the highest peak in Pakistan and the second highest in the world.
r: Nanga Parbat at 8,126 metres is the second highest peak in Pakistan.

q: Which of these countries has only a maritime border with Pakistan and no land border? (37)
f: Pakistan has land borders with Afghanistan, China, India and Iran. Oman has no land border with Pakistan but shares a sea boundary in the Arabian Sea.
r: The Pakistan-Oman maritime boundary agreement came into force in 2000.

q: On what date did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests? (37)
f: Pakistan carried out its first nuclear tests in the Chagai hills, Balochistan, on 28 May 1998 (five tests, Chagai-I), followed by one more on 30 May 1998. This was a reply to India's tests earlier that month.
r: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed? (36)
f: The Treaty of Hudaibiya was signed between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraysh in Dhul Qadah 6 AH (628 CE).
r: The Quran calls it a clear victory (Fath-e-Mubin) in Surah Al-Fath.

q: On which side of Asia is Pakistan located? (36)
f: Pakistan lies in South Asia (the Indian subcontinent).
r: Some sources place Pakistan in South-West Asia, but it is usually counted as a South Asian country.

q: What is the capital of Punjab (Pakistan)? (36)
f: Lahore is the provincial capital of Punjab.
r: Maryam Nawaz is the current Chief Minister of Punjab, succeeding Usman Buzdar.

q: What does the word Pakistan mean? (36)
f: Pakistan is a Persian and Urdu word made of pak (pure) and stan (land), so it means land of the pure. It is not related to truth.
r: The name was proposed by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933 in the pamphlet Now or Never.

q: Where is Jabal-e-Noor (the mountain containing the Cave of Hira) located? (36)
f: Jabal al-Noor is a mountain near Makkah in Saudi Arabia and holds the Cave of Hira where the first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH).
r: The first revelation, the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq, was received in this cave.

q: In which battle were a large number of Hafiz-e-Quran Sahaba martyred? (36)
f: Many Qurra (Hafiz) companions were martyred at Yamama against the false prophet Musaylima in 632 AD.
r: This loss led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to have the Quran compiled in one book.

q: What is the new name of the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD)? (36)
f: RCD, formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey, was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.
r: ECO has its secretariat in Tehran.

q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ? (36)
f: Terms at odd places: 115, 170, 235 (adding 55, then 65). Terms at even places: 55, 65, 75 (adding 10 each time).
r: Series with two interleaved patterns should be split into alternate terms.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city of Afghanistan? (36)
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul through the Torkham border crossing and Jalalabad.
r: The pass lies in the Safed Koh range.

q: For how many days was the 1965 Pakistan-India war fought? (36)
f: The war began in early September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days. It is remembered as the 17-day war.
r: Pakistan celebrates 6 September as Defence Day in memory of the 1965 war.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how many pages will one man write in 5 minutes? (36)
f: 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes.
r: The rate is 1 page per man per 5 minutes, or 0.2 pages per minute.

q: Which is the oldest sport in the world according to most textbooks? (36)
f: Wrestling is usually named as the oldest sport, as cave paintings and ancient records show it thousands of years ago.
r: Sources differ, as some also name running, archery or chess among the oldest.

q: In which district is the Khewra salt mine located? (35)
f: The Khewra salt mine is in Jhelum district, Punjab, in the Salt Range.
r: It is among the largest salt mines in the world.

q: Where does the Karakoram Highway (KKH) start in Pakistan? (35)
f: In Pakistan the Karakoram Highway is commonly described as starting at Hassan Abdal and running north through Abbottabad, Gilgit and Sost to the Khunjerab Pass.
r: Some sources start it at Havelian, but Pakistani textbooks usually give Hassan Abdal.

q: How many players are there in a football team on the field? (35)
f: A football team fields eleven players including the goalkeeper.
r: A standard football match lasts 90 minutes.

q: The Olympic Games were cancelled in which year of World War 1? (35)
f: The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of the war; the games are held every four years, so 1914 was not an Olympic year.
r: The Olympics were cancelled again in 1940 and 1944 during World War 2.

q: Which country helped the USA build relations with China in 1971? (35)
f: Pakistan under Yahya Khan arranged the secret visit of Henry Kissinger to Beijing in July 1971.
r: President Nixon visited China in February 1972.

q: How many manzils (stages) is the Holy Quran divided into? (35)
f: The Quran is divided into seven manzils so that it can be recited in one week. Each manzil is read on one day of the week.
r: The Quran is also divided into 30 paras (juz).

q: Which is the largest city of Pakistan by population? (35)
f: Karachi is the most populous city of Pakistan, with over 14 million people at the 2017 census and about 20 million at the 2023 census.
r: Lahore is the second largest city.

q: What is the capital of Lebanon? (35)
f: Beirut is the capital and largest city of Lebanon.
r: Damascus is the capital of Syria.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ? (35)
f: The positions are 2, 5, 10, 17. The gaps are 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26, which is Z.
r: The positions are one more than the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 + 1 = 26.

q: Whose mother was Hazrat Sara (AS)? (35)
f: Hazrat Sara (AS), wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
r: Hazrat Hajra (AS) was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th be? (35)
f: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 days is 3 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Tuesday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: On which side of Pakistan does the Arabian Sea lie? (35)
f: Pakistan's coastline of about 1,046 km runs along the Arabian Sea in the south, in Sindh and Balochistan.
r: Iran and Afghanistan lie to the west, China to the north-east and India to the east.

q: NASA, the space agency, belongs to which country? (35)
f: NASA stands for the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, a United States government agency.
r: NASA was founded in 1958 and landed the first humans on the Moon in 1969.

q: By what other name is the Pakistan Resolution known? (35)
f: The Pakistan Resolution of 1940 was passed at Lahore, so it is also called the Lahore Resolution. It demanded independent states for the Muslims of India.
r: The Allahabad Address of 1930 by Allama Iqbal first outlined the idea of a Muslim state.

q: What is the original meaning of the word Urdu? (35)
f: Urdu comes from the Turkish word ordu, meaning camp or army, as the language grew in the military camps and bazaars.
r: It is also called Lashkari zaban, the language of the army.

q: Rehman Baba was a famous poet of which language? (35)
f: Rehman Baba (17th century) is a celebrated Sufi poet of the Pashto language.
r: His shrine is in Peshawar.

q: Who discovered bacteria? (35)
f: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria through his handmade microscope in the 1670s. He called them animalcules.
r: Louis Pasteur proved the germ theory of disease and Robert Koch identified the bacteria causing anthrax and tuberculosis.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi romance Heer Ranjha? (34)
f: Waris Shah wrote the best known version of Heer in 1766.
r: Earlier versions of the story were written by Damodar Gulati.

q: In which Hijri year did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam? (34)
f: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accepted Islam in 8 AH (629 CE), before the conquest of Makkah. Some sources give 7 AH, so sources differ, but 8 AH is the common textbook answer.
r: He was later given the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah).

q: What is one tenth of 90? (34)
f: 90 divided by 10 is 9.
r: One tenth of a number is the same as 10% of it.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many houses does the Parliament of Pakistan have? (34)
f: The Parliament consists of the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house), plus the President.
r: The Senate has 96 members after the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP.

q: For the Khilafat Movement, Muslims of India migrated towards which country? (34)
f: During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, thousands of Muslims left India for Afghanistan as a protest against British rule.
r: The migration failed because the Afghan government could not support so many people.

q: In which province is the Kharan Desert located? (34)
f: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan.
r: Pakistan's first nuclear test site, Chagai, is also in Balochistan close to this desert region.

q: Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan and the world? (34)
f: The Shandur polo ground at Shandur Pass is about 3,700 metres high and is called the highest polo ground in the world.
r: A famous polo festival between Chitral and Gilgit-Baltistan is held at Shandur every year.

q: Who is the current President of India? (34)
f: Droupadi Murmu took oath as the 15th President of India on 25 July 2022.
r: Her predecessor Ram Nath Kovind, the answer given in 2022, served from 2017 to 2022.

q: Which planet is nearest to the Sun? (34)
f: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun, at about 58 million km.
r: Mercury is also the smallest planet of the solar system.

q: Who is regarded as the first martyr of Islam? (34)
f: Hazrat Sumayyah (RA), mother of Hazrat Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is the first martyr of Islam.
r: Some sources name Harith bin Abi Hala as the first male martyr, so sources differ.

q: On what date did Allama Iqbal deliver his Allahabad Address? (34)
f: The Allahabad session of the All India Muslim League was held in December 1930 and Iqbal delivered his address on 29 December 1930.
r: The idea of a separate Muslim state he gave there led to the Pakistan Resolution of 1940.

q: When was the third martial law imposed in Pakistan? (34)
f: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed martial law on 5 July 1977 by removing the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
r: The earlier martial laws were in 1958 (Ayub Khan) and 1969 (Yahya Khan); General Musharraf took power in 1999 without declaring martial law.

q: Who discovered the neutron? (34)
f: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 by bombarding beryllium with alpha particles.
r: Chadwick received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935 for this discovery.

q: What is 1/10 of 120? (33)
r: One tenth is the same as 10 percent.

q: What is the national bird of the USA? (33)
f: The bald eagle was chosen as the national bird and emblem of the United States.
r: It appears on the Great Seal of the United States adopted in 1782.

q: On which prophet was the Injeel (Bible) revealed? (33)
f: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S). Zabur was given to Dawood, Taurat to Musa and the Quran to Muhammad.
r: Hazrat Isa (A.S) is also known as Ruhullah.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress? (33)
f: Jinnah left Congress in 1920 over the Nagpur session and its non-cooperation policy.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: Who was the commander of the Muslim army in the Ghazwa (Battle) of Tabuk? (33)
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk (9 AH) was a campaign in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army of about 30,000. A Ghazwa is by definition a battle in which the Prophet personally took part.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) was left in charge of Madina during the Tabuk expedition.

q: Which Sahabi served the Holy Prophet (PBUH) for ten years? (33)
f: Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet as a servant at Madina as a boy and served him for about ten years.
r: He narrated over 2,000 hadiths.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Tabuk fought? (33)
f: In 9 AH the Prophet (PBUH) led an army to Tabuk to face the Byzantine force, but no fighting took place.
r: It was the last military expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Desert Fox is the title of whom? (33)
f: Field Marshal Erwin Rommel earned the name Desert Fox for his skilled command of the German Afrika Korps in North Africa.
r: He was defeated by Montgomery at El Alamein in 1942.

q: In which year was the partition of Bengal annulled? (33)
f: The partition of Bengal, made in 1905, was annulled in 1911 after Hindu agitation.
r: The 1911 decision disappointed Muslims of East Bengal.

q: What is the meaning of Badr? (33)
f: Badr in Arabic means the full moon.
r: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) near a well named Badr.

q: Who was the last Mughal emperor of India? (33)
f: Bahadur Shah Zafar was deposed by the British after the War of Independence of 1857.
r: He was exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.

q: How many Hafiz (memorisers) of the Quran are reported to have been martyred in the Battle of Yamama? (33)
f: In the Battle of Yamama (12 AH) against the false prophet Musailima, about 70 Huffaz of the Quran were martyred, according to the commonly given account.
r: Some narrations give higher numbers, but this event led Hazrat Umar (RA) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran in one book.

q: What was the name of Pakistan's first satellite? (33)
f: Badr-1, launched on 16 July 1990 from China, was the first satellite of Pakistan.
r: It was built by SUPARCO.

q: Which mountain is known as the Killer Mountain? (33)
f: Nanga Parbat is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it in early attempts.
r: Nanga Parbat means Naked Mountain and is the ninth highest mountain in the world.

q: When did the Al-Khalid main battle tank enter service with the Pakistan Army? (33)
f: The Al-Khalid (MBT-2000), developed by Pakistan with Chinese help, entered service in 2001.
r: Some sources mention 2004 for its formal presentation, and the upgraded Al-Khalid-I was inducted in July 2020.

q: On which river did India build the Baglihar dam? (33)
f: The Baglihar hydroelectric dam is built by India on the Chenab river in Jammu and Kashmir. The Chenab flows on into Pakistan.
r: Under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 the Chenab is one of the three western rivers allotted to Pakistan.

q: By which process do green plants prepare their food? (33)
f: Plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make glucose in photosynthesis.
r: Oxygen is released as a by-product of photosynthesis.

q: What is the value of sin 90 degrees? (32)
f: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1) and sine is the y-coordinate, which equals 1.
r: The value of cos 90 degrees is 0.

q: In which battle was the tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) broken? (32)
f: The Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded on the face during the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH, after the archers left their post.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Madinah in March 625 CE.

q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River according to common textbooks? (32)
f: Most textbooks give the Amazon length as about 6,400 km.
r: Sources differ: some measurements give up to about 6,990 km, and the Nile is often listed as longest at about 6,650 km.

q: Which is the world's third longest river? (32)
f: By length the Nile and Amazon are first and second, and the Yangtze in China is third at about 6,300 km.
r: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.

q: How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (SAW) perform after his migration to Madina? (32)
f: He performed only one Hajj, in 10 AH, known as Hajjat-ul-Wada (the Farewell Pilgrimage).
r: He delivered his Farewell Sermon on the plain of Arafat during this Hajj.

q: The Hindu Kush mountain range connects Pakistan with which country? (32)
f: The Hindu Kush extends from central Afghanistan into northern Pakistan.
r: Tirich Mir (7708 m), the highest peak of the Hindu Kush, is in Chitral, Pakistan.

q: What is the national fruit of Pakistan? (32)
f: The mango is the national fruit of Pakistan.
r: Pakistan is among the largest producers of mangoes in the world.

q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country? (32)
f: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister of Pakistan in 1988, the first woman to head a Muslim country's government.
r: She was Prime Minister twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.

q: Which prophet built the ark (boat) at the command of Allah before the great flood? (32)
f: Allah commanded Hazrat Nuh (AS) to build the ark to save the believers from the flood.
r: Surah Nuh of the Quran is named after this prophet.

q: Who wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob? (32)
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob is the oldest Persian book on Sufism and was written by Hazrat Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
r: His shrine is in Lahore.

q: Which region is called the Land of Prophets? (32)
f: Palestine is called the Land of Prophets because many prophets, including Ibrahim, Dawud, Sulaiman, Isa and others, lived or preached there.
r: Jerusalem (Al-Quds) in Palestine holds Masjid al-Aqsa, the first qibla of Muslims.

q: Which area is known as the Roof of the World? (32)
f: The Pamir Plateau in Central Asia is called the Roof of the World because of its great height.
r: Tibet is also sometimes given this name.

q: Which city is known as the City of Gold? (32)
f: Johannesburg in South Africa is called the City of Gold because it grew after gold was discovered in the Witwatersrand in 1886.
r: South Africa has long been one of the largest gold producers in the world, though sources differ on later rankings.

q: Which prophet confronted the king Namrood (Nimrod)? (32)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) invited Namrood to worship one Allah, and Namrood had him thrown into a fire, which Allah made cool.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun).

q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley. (32)
f: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains (cereals) eaten by people, while hay is dried grass kept as fodder for animals.
r: Wheat and rice are the two major food crops of Pakistan.

q: Who wrote the book 'The Conquest of Happiness'? (32)
f: The Conquest of Happiness (1930) was written by the British philosopher Bertrand Russell.
r: Russell won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950.

q: If a helicopter covers 320 miles using 80 gallons of fuel, how many gallons are needed for 700 miles? (32)
f: Fuel per mile = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 miles: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
r: Such questions are solved with direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word excuse (as a verb)? (32)
f: To excuse someone means to forgive or pardon a fault. Blame, punish and accuse have the opposite sense.
r: As a noun, excuse means a reason offered to justify a fault, for example a pretext.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares Islam as the State religion? (32)
f: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
r: Article 1 names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: Near which place in Pakistan does the Kabul River join the Indus River? (32)
f: The Kabul River meets the Indus near Attock at Khairabad, where the clear Kabul water and the muddy Indus water can be seen side by side.
r: The Kabul River rises in Afghanistan and enters Pakistan near the Khyber area.

q: If today is Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow? (31)
f: Tomorrow is Saturday, so the day after tomorrow is Sunday.
r: The day after tomorrow means two days from today.

q: Who among the following was a son-in-law of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (31)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) was also a son-in-law, having married Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).

q: What is the capital of Belarus? (31)
f: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
r: Belarus is a landlocked country in Eastern Europe.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution? (31)
f: The 1956 Constitution declared the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, ending its dominion status.
r: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956, now celebrated as Pakistan Day.

q: With which surah does the Holy Quran begin? (31)
f: The Quran opens with Surah Al-Fatihah, which has seven verses.
r: Surah An-Nas is the last surah of the Quran.

q: What is the real name of Imam Bukhari? (31)
f: Imam Bukhari's full name was Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari. He compiled the collection Sahih al-Bukhari.
r: Imam Bukhari was born in 810 CE in Bukhara and his Sahih is regarded as the most authentic hadith collection.

q: What is the value of cos 0 degrees? (31)
f: At 0 degrees the adjacent side equals the hypotenuse, so cos 0 = 1.
r: sin 0 = 0 and tan 0 = 0.

q: When was the All India Muslim League established? (31)
f: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka during the Muhammadan Educational Conference. Nawab Salimullah Khan hosted the meeting.
r: Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk presided and Sir Agha Khan was the first honorary president.

q: In which year did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Peace Prize? (31)
f: Malala was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, jointly with Kailash Satyarthi.
r: At age 17 she became the youngest Nobel laureate ever.

q: What is the base of the natural logarithm? (31)
f: The natural logarithm ln x is the logarithm to base e, where e is approximately 2.71828.
r: Common logarithms use base 10, and computer science often uses base 2.

q: Who announced the partition of Bengal in 1905? (31)
f: Lord Curzon, the Viceroy of India, announced the partition of Bengal on 19 July 1905 and it took effect on 16 October 1905, creating a Muslim-majority eastern province.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911, and the All India Muslim League was formed in 1906 partly in reaction to these events.

q: Habba Khatoon was a famous poet of which language? (31)
f: Habba Khatoon (Zoon) was a 16th century Kashmiri poet known for her lyrical songs.
r: She is often called the Nightingale of Kashmir.

q: Who is the chairman of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)? (31)
f: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari has been PPP chairman since 2007 and was re-elected in April 2025.
r: Asif Ali Zardari is the co-chairperson of the party.

q: Who composed the music of the national anthem of Pakistan? (31)
f: The tune of the anthem was composed by Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla, while the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.
r: The anthem was officially adopted in 1954.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 120? (31)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
r: The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.

q: Who is the author of the book Mein Kampf? (31)
f: Mein Kampf (My Struggle) was written by Adolf Hitler, partly while he was in prison in 1924.
r: It was published in two volumes in 1925 and 1926.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary? (31)
f: Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
r: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.

q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa of Hunain fought? (31)
f: The Battle of Hunain was fought against the tribes of Hawazin and Thaqif in Shawwal 8 AH, soon after the Conquest of Makkah.
r: The Muslims were first pushed back by an ambush but then won the battle.

q: How many countries are there in Central Asia? (31)
f: Central Asia has five countries: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.
r: All five were part of the Soviet Union until 1991.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan gives the right to education? (31)
f: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes education a right of children.
r: Article 37 also speaks about the promotion of education as a principle of policy.

q: In which province is the Lower Indus plain mostly located? (31)
f: The Lower Indus plain lies in Sindh, from near Sukkur down to the Arabian Sea.
r: The Upper Indus plain lies mainly in Punjab.

q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2023 (New Delhi)? (31)
f: The 2023 G20 summit was held in New Delhi, India, in September 2023. India held the G20 presidency that year.
r: Indonesia hosted in 2022 and Brazil in 2024.

q: In which year did Pakistan play its first Test match? (31)
f: Pakistan's first Test was played against India in Delhi in October 1952.
r: Pakistan's first Test win came against India at Lucknow in the same series.

q: Car is to wheel as clock is to what? (31)
f: A wheel is a part of a car, and hands are a part of a clock.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: Which country hosted the first Football World Cup in 1930? (30)
f: The first FIFA World Cup was held in 1930 in Uruguay, which also won it.
r: Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.

q: Which is the longest river of Europe? (30)
f: The Volga in Russia is about 3,530 km long and is the longest river in Europe.
r: The Danube is the second longest river in Europe and flows through ten countries.

q: What is the length of a marathon race? (30)
f: The standard marathon distance is 26 miles 385 yards, which is 42.195 km.
r: The distance was fixed at the 1908 London Olympics.

q: Which surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah? (30)
f: Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) is the only surah that does not begin with Bismillah.
r: Bismillah appears twice in Surah An-Naml, once at the start and once inside verse 30.

q: What is 80% of 80? (30)
r: 80% is the same as the fraction 4/5.

q: How many Nishan-e-Haider awards have been given so far, according to the commonly cited count? (30)
f: The commonly cited current count is 11 recipients, all awarded posthumously. Older sources say 10, and the status of the eleventh name is sometimes disputed.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award of Pakistan.

q: Which country is shaped like a long boot on the map? (30)
f: Italy is a peninsula that looks like a long boot kicking the island of Sicily.
r: Rome, the capital of Italy, was the centre of the ancient Roman Empire.

q: Masjid Zarar (Dirar) was built by which group? (30)
f: A group of hypocrites built it near Quba to divide the Muslims, and the Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) condemned it.
r: The Prophet ordered it to be demolished after returning from Tabuk.

q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness? (30)
f: Vitamin A is needed to make the light-sensitive pigment in the retina. Its lack makes it hard to see in dim light.
r: Carrots, liver and green leafy vegetables are good sources of vitamin A.

q: In which year was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in Pakistan? (30)
f: The Pakistan Army launched Radd-ul-Fasaad in February 2017 as a nationwide intelligence-based operation against terrorism.
r: It followed Operation Zarb-e-Azb, which began in June 2014.

q: About how many times is the command of Namaz (Salah) mentioned in the Holy Quran, according to common textbooks? (30)
f: Salah and its related commands are repeated about 700 times in the Quran, showing its great importance.
r: Sources differ on the exact count, but 700 is the figure given in most Pakistani textbooks.

q: Who was the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator of Pakistan? (30)
