f: On 20 December 1971 Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto took over as President and became the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator after Yahya Khan stepped down.
r: Martial law was lifted in Pakistan in 1972 and the 1973 Constitution was adopted under Bhutto.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km? (30)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.
r: His speed is 20 km in 100 minutes, which is 12 km per hour.

q: Which surah is known as Arus-ul-Quran (the Bride of the Quran)? (30)
f: Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran because of its beauty and its repeated refrain.
r: Surah Yaseen is called the heart of the Quran.

q: If the 12th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 26th be? (30)
f: From the 12th to the 26th is 14 days. 14 days is 2 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) after Friday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: Which of the following countries does NOT share a border with Pakistan? (30)
f: Pakistan borders India, China, Afghanistan and Iran. Tajikistan is separated from Pakistan by the narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan.
r: The Wakhan Corridor is only about 14 to 15 km wide at its narrowest point.

q: Who is credited with discovering the proton? (30)
f: Ernest Rutherford identified the proton as a particle in 1917-1919.
r: Thomson discovered the electron and Chadwick discovered the neutron.

q: Which is the second highest mountain of Pakistan? (30)
f: K2 is the highest peak in Pakistan and Nanga Parbat, at about 8,126 m, is the second highest.
r: Nanga Parbat is nicknamed the Killer Mountain and is in Gilgit-Baltistan.

q: Who is traditionally credited in Pakistani textbooks with inventing the telescope? (30)
f: Galileo Galilei built and used an improved telescope in 1609 to observe the Moon, Jupiter's moons and the planets. Textbooks therefore credit him with the telescope.
r: Sources differ: the Dutch spectacle maker Hans Lippershey filed the first known patent for a telescope in 1608.

q: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL located? (30)
f: The General Secretariat of INTERPOL is in Lyon, France.
r: INTERPOL was earlier headquartered in Paris before moving to Lyon in 1989.

q: Which is the highest pass of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks? (29)
f: Khunjerab Pass, at about 4,693 m on the Pakistan-China border, is the highest pass usually cited for Pakistan.
r: Sources differ because some lists name Mintaka Pass, also on the China border, as slightly higher; Khunjerab is the highest paved international border crossing.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Jafar Tayyar (RA) martyred? (29)
f: Hazrat Jafar ibn Abi Talib (RA) was one of the three commanders martyred in the Battle of Mutah in 8 AH. He is called Tayyar (the flyer) because he is said to have been given wings in Paradise.
r: The other two commanders at Mutah were Zaid bin Haritha and Abdullah bin Rawaha (RA).

q: Which Sahabi married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and Hazrat Umm Kulthum? (29)
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married Ruqayyah first and, after her death, Umm Kulthum.
r: He is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashideen (rightly guided caliphs) are there? (29)
f: They are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (RA).
r: Their combined rule lasted about 30 years (632 to 661 AD).

q: In which year was the first constitution of Pakistan enforced? (29)
f: The first constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. It was abrogated by Ayub Khan's martial law in October 1958.
r: 23 March was celebrated as Republic Day until the 1962 constitution replaced it.

q: Which is the hottest city of Pakistan? (29)
f: Jacobabad in Sindh regularly records the highest temperatures in Pakistan, often over 50 degrees Celsius.
r: Jacobabad is among the hottest inhabited places on Earth.

q: Under the 1956 Constitution, the President of Pakistan was elected by: (29)
o: An electoral college of members of the National and Provincial Assemblies
f: The 1956 Constitution provided for the President to be elected by the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
r: Iskander Mirza became the first President under this Constitution.

q: Which is the second most populous country of the world? (29)
f: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, so China is now second.
r: In 2021-22 China was the most populous and India second.

q: What is 60% of 90? (29)
r: The product is the same for 90% of 60, since percentages are multiplicative.

q: Which Companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) is known as Sahib-e-Sirr (keeper of the secrets) of the Prophet? (29)
f: Hazrat Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman (R.A) was entrusted with the Prophet's secrets, including the names of the hypocrites.
r: Hazrat Umar (R.A) used to ask him whether his own name was among the hypocrites.

q: Which is the biggest continent in the world by area? (29)
f: Asia covers about 44.6 million square kilometres, which is the largest of all continents.
r: Asia is also the most populous continent.

q: Who wrote the pamphlet Now or Never (1933)? (29)
f: Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever? was written by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in 1933.
r: In it he proposed the name Pakistan for a separate Muslim homeland.

q: What is the value of cos 90 degrees? (29)
f: On the unit circle, the point at 90 degrees is (0, 1), and its x-coordinate, the cosine, is 0.
r: Sin 90 degrees equals 1.

q: What is the capital of the Philippines? (29)
f: Manila is the capital of the Philippines.
r: Quezon City is the largest city of the country by population.

q: Which country has won the most Cricket World Cup titles? (29)
f: Australia has won the men's Cricket World Cup six times (1987, 1999, 2003, 2007, 2015 and 2023).
r: India has won it twice and Pakistan once, in 1992.

q: Diamond is an allotrope of which element? (29)
f: Diamond is made of carbon atoms joined in a rigid tetrahedral crystal structure.
r: Graphite is another allotrope of carbon, and diamond is the hardest natural substance.

q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War II? (29)
f: Adolf Hitler led Germany as Chancellor and Fuhrer from 1933 until his death in 1945.
r: Churchill led Britain, Mussolini led Italy and Stalin led the Soviet Union.

q: In which city was the OIC established at the first Islamic summit in 1969? (28)
f: The first Islamic summit, which created the OIC, was held at Rabat in Morocco in 1969. Jeddah is the permanent headquarters of the OIC, not the place of its founding.
r: The Islamic Summit held in Lahore in 1974 was the second summit of the OIC.

q: Who rebuilt the Holy Kaaba with his son? (28)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) rebuilt the Kaaba with his son Hazrat Ismail (AS).
r: The Quraysh also rebuilt it before the Prophet's prophethood, and the Prophet (PBUH) placed the Black Stone.

q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 90? (28)
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and a quarter of 9 is 9 / 4 = 2.25.
r: A quarter of one tenth is 1/40 of the number.

q: By whose hand was Hazrat Hamza martyred in the Battle of Uhud? (28)
f: Wahshi bin Harb, a slave of Jubayr bin Mutim, killed Hazrat Hamza with a spear on the order of Hind.
r: Wahshi later accepted Islam.

q: What does OIC stand for? (28)
f: OIC stands for Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, the collective voice of the Muslim world.
r: It was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011 and is headquartered in Jeddah.

q: What is the largest bird in the world? (28)
f: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird, up to about 2.7 m tall.
r: The ostrich cannot fly but is the fastest running bird.

q: After how many years did East Pakistan (Bangladesh) separate from West Pakistan? (28)
f: Pakistan was created in 1947 and Bangladesh emerged in December 1971, which is 24 years later.
r: The separation followed the 1971 war and the fall of Dhaka on 16 December 1971.

q: How many times is the name Muhammad mentioned in the Holy Quran? (28)
f: The name Muhammad occurs in Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:144), Al-Ahzab (33:40), Muhammad (47:2) and Al-Fath (48:29), so four times.
r: The name Ahmad, another name of the Holy Prophet (SAW), appears once, in Surah As-Saff (61:6).

q: Who wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan? (28)
f: Hayat-e-Javed, a biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, was written by Khawaja Altaf Hussain Hali in 1901.
r: Hali also wrote the Musaddas, and Dr Javed Iqbal wrote the Iqbal biography Zinda Rood.

q: A man walks towards north, after some time turns right and then turns left. In which direction is he moving now? (28)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. A left turn from east makes him face north again.
r: A right turn followed by a left turn cancels out.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)? (28)
f: Harini Amarasuriya of the National People's Power became Prime Minister in September 2024 and was reappointed after the November 2024 election.
r: Earlier answers were Mahinda Rajapaksa (2019 to 2022) and Ranil Wickremesinghe (briefly in 2022).

q: Which is the longest railway tunnel in Pakistan? (28)
f: The Khojak Tunnel, built in 1891 in the Khojak Pass of Balochistan on the Quetta-Chaman line, is about 3.9 km long and is Pakistan's longest railway tunnel.
r: The Lowari Tunnel in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is longer, but it is a road tunnel, not a railway tunnel.

q: According to Islamic tradition, who first built the Kaaba? (28)
f: Islamic tradition says the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS), and later rebuilt by Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) with his son Ismail (AS). Many candidates and sources give this answer for the first building.
r: Sources differ, and some Pakistani textbooks credit Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) with building it, but they rebuilt it on its old foundations.

q: In which surah of the Quran is the name Ahmad (for the Holy Prophet PBUH) mentioned? (28)
f: The name Ahmad appears in Surah As-Saff (61:6), where Hazrat Isa (AS) gives the good news of a messenger named Ahmad coming after him.
r: The name Muhammad is mentioned four times in the Quran, in Al-Imran, Al-Ahzab, Muhammad and Al-Fath.

q: In which year was the film Jinnah, on the life of Quaid-e-Azam, released? (28)
f: The film Jinnah, starring Christopher Lee as Jinnah, was released in 1998.
r: It was directed by Jamil Dehlavi.

q: How many senses do human beings have according to the traditional classification? (28)
f: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
r: Modern science recognises additional senses such as balance and body position awareness.

q: In which year did the Urdu-Hindi controversy begin? (28)
f: The Urdu-Hindi controversy began in 1867 at Banaras (Varanasi), when Hindus demanded Hindi in Devanagari script replace Urdu.
r: The controversy led Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to conclude Hindus and Muslims could not progress together.

q: What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan today? (28)
f: Recent data for 2025 show hydel power as the largest single source, around 39 percent in some months. RLNG and nuclear follow.
r: In earlier decades thermal (oil and gas) plants produced most of Pakistan's electricity.

q: What was the name of the foster mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (28)
f: Halima Sadia of the Banu Saad tribe nursed and raised the infant Prophet (PBUH) in the desert.
r: Thuwaiba, a freed slave of Abu Lahab, nursed him briefly before Halima.

q: Which of these is another name for the Karakoram Highway? (28)
f: The Karakoram Highway is also called the Pakistan-China Friendship Highway and is numbered N-35.
r: It is sometimes called the Eighth Wonder of the World because of the difficulty of building it.

q: On which date was the Battle of Plassey fought? (28)
f: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company under Robert Clive and Nawab Siraj ud Daula of Bengal.
r: The Battle of Plassey is seen as the start of British political rule in India.

q: In which city is the National Library of Pakistan located? (28)
f: The National Library of Pakistan is located in Islamabad on Constitution Avenue in the same complex as other national institutions.
r: It was established in 1951 in Karachi and later moved to Islamabad.

q: Which large water body lies to the south of Pakistan? (28)
f: Pakistan has a coastline of about 1,046 km along the Arabian Sea in the south.
r: Karachi and Gwadar are the main ports on this coast.

q: Muhammad Ali Bogra held which office in Pakistan? (28)
f: Muhammad Ali Bogra served as the third Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955, after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.
r: He is remembered for the Bogra Formula of 1953 on constitution making.

q: Who wrote the novel Ice Candy Man? (28)
f: Ice Candy Man (1988) was written by the Pakistani novelist Bapsi Sidhwa. It tells the story of Partition through a Parsi girl in Lahore.
r: The novel was published in the USA as Cracking India and was filmed as 1947 Earth.

q: Which country is the largest producer of coffee in the world? (27)
f: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer for over 150 years.
r: Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer.

q: On what date was the Tashkent Agreement signed? (27)
f: India and Pakistan signed the Tashkent Declaration on 10 January 1966, ending the 1965 war.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri, who died in Tashkent the next day.

q: Which sea lies between Greece and Italy? (27)
f: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
r: The Aegean Sea lies east of Greece, between Greece and Turkey.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam die? (27)
f: Quaid-e-Azam died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.
r: He is buried at Mazar-e-Quaid in Karachi.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) of ghusl are there (Hanafi fiqh)? (27)
f: The three faraiz of ghusl are rinsing the mouth, rinsing the nose and washing the whole body.
r: The faraiz of wudu are four in Hanafi fiqh.

q: What is the normal term of office of the Secretary General of the United Nations? (27)
f: The Secretary General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council for a five-year term, which can be renewed.
r: The current Secretary General is Antonio Guterres of Portugal, in office since 2017, and his term ends on 31 December 2026.

q: How many Madani surahs does the Holy Quran contain, according to the common Pakistani textbook count? (27)
f: Of the 114 surahs, 86 are Makki and 28 are Madani. Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrat.
r: Scholars differ slightly on a few surahs, so some books give slightly different counts.

q: In which country were the 2016 Olympic Games held? (27)
f: The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
r: They were the first Summer Olympics held in South America.

q: Which is known as the highest battlefield of the world? (27)
f: Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram, where Pakistani and Indian troops face each other at around 6,000 m, is the highest battlefield.
r: Siachen is about 76 km long, one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

q: Which strip of land separates Pakistan from Central Asia (Tajikistan)? (27)
f: The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan from Tajikistan and Central Asia.
r: The corridor was created as a buffer between British India and Russian Empire in the 19th century.

q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan? (27)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly, then appointed by the President.
r: A candidate needs a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.

q: In which year was the war of independence (the Mutiny) fought in the subcontinent? (27)
f: The War of Independence broke out at Meerut in May 1857 against East India Company rule.
r: It ended with the British Crown taking direct control of India in 1858.

q: Which is the largest airport in the world by area? (27)
o: King Fahd International Airport (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
f: King Fahd International Airport near Dammam covers about 776 to 780 square kilometres, far more than any other airport.
r: Denver International Airport is second largest at about 136 square kilometres.

q: What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line)? (27)
f: The Durand Line, agreed in 1893, is most commonly given as about 2,640 km long.
r: Sources differ slightly (figures from about 2,600 to 2,670 km are quoted), and Afghanistan does not formally recognise the line.

q: What is the total number of members of the Senate of Pakistan? (27)
f: The Senate has 96 members: 23 from each of the four provinces (92) plus 4 from the Islamabad Capital Territory. A November 2025 report still describes a 96-member Senate
r: The Senate had 104 members until the FATA seats were phased out after FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018.

q: What does the United Nations observe on 24 January? (27)
f: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 24 January as International Day of Education in December 2018. It was first observed in 2019.
r: International Literacy Day is on 8 September and World Teachers Day on 5 October.

q: Which word is nearest in meaning to 'diversity'? (27)
f: Diversity means a range of different things, which is what variety means. Uniformity and similarity are its opposites.
r: Its adjective form is 'diverse', meaning varied or different in kind.

q: In which year of the Hijri calendar did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Umrat-ul-Qaza? (27)
f: After the Treaty of Hudaibiya the Muslims performed the Umrah they were stopped from in 6 AH. They did it the next year, in 7 AH.
r: It is called Umrat-ul-Qaza because it made up for the Umrah missed in 6 AH.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the IBSF World Snooker Championship for the first time? (27)
f: Muhammad Yousuf won the world amateur snooker title for Pakistan in 1994.
r: Muhammad Sajid won the world amateur title in 2006, Pakistan's second.

q: Which is the last completely revealed surah of the Holy Quran? (27)
f: Surah An-Nasr is regarded as the last complete surah to be revealed.
r: Sources differ about the last verse revealed, with Al-Baqarah verse 281 or Al-Maidah verse 3 often mentioned.

q: In which year was the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) agreement signed and launched? (27)
f: CPEC was launched in April 2015 when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Pakistan and agreements worth about 46 billion dollars were signed.
r: A preliminary MoU on the corridor had been signed in 2013 during the visit of Premier Li Keqiang, which is why some sources give 2013.

q: Who wrote the famous biography 'Jinnah of Pakistan'? (27)
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' in 1984.
r: Fatima Jinnah wrote 'My Brother' and Hector Bolitho wrote 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.

q: On which date was the Pakistan Resolution (Lahore Resolution) presented? (27)
f: The resolution was presented on 23 March 1940 at the Lahore session of the All India Muslim League, having been moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and passed on 24 March.
r: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day.

q: In which year did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal? (27)
f: Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the hockey final at the Rome Olympics of 1960 to win its first gold.
r: The other golds came in 1968 at Mexico City and 1984 at Los Angeles.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Canada today (October 2026)? (27)
f: Mark Carney became Prime Minister of Canada on 14 March 2025 and leads the Liberal Party. Canada has no president; the Prime Minister is head of government.
r: Justin Trudeau was Prime Minister before Carney (2015 to 2025), and King Charles III is Canada's head of state.

q: In which year did Aligarh College (MAO College) become Aligarh Muslim University? (27)
f: The MAO College was given university status in 1920 and became Aligarh Muslim University.
r: The MAO school began in 1875 and became a college in 1877, and sources differ slightly on these dates.

q: Who was known as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity in the subcontinent? (27)
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah worked for Hindu-Muslim unity in the early part of his career, including the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Sarojini Naidu gave him this title.
r: Jinnah was a member of the Indian National Congress before he led the Muslim League.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit America? (26)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the United States in May 1950, the first Pakistani Prime Minister to do so.
r: His visit came after he chose Washington over an invitation from Moscow.

q: In which province is Manchar Lake located? (26)
f: Manchar Lake is in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus.
r: It is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah present his Fourteen Points? (26)
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points at Delhi in March 1929, answering the Nehru Report.
r: The Fourteen Points demanded safeguards for Muslims, such as separate electorates and one third seats in the central legislature.

q: Which is the biggest province of Pakistan by area? (26)
f: Balochistan covers about 347,000 square km, roughly 44 percent of Pakistan.
r: Punjab is the largest province by population.

q: Lira is the currency of which country? (26)
f: The Turkish lira is the official currency of Turkey.
r: Italy used the lira before adopting the euro.

q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS)? (26)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
r: The Sa'i between Safa and Marwa during Hajj commemorates Hajra's search for water.

q: What is the first pillar of Islam? (26)
f: The first pillar is the declaration of faith (Shahada), which affirms Tauheed and the Prophethood of Muhammad (SAW).
r: The order of the pillars is Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.

q: Which is the longest freshwater lake in the world? (26)
f: Lake Tanganyika in Africa is about 676 km long, the longest freshwater lake in the world.
r: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world.

q: Which is the second largest continent by area? (26)
f: Asia is the largest and Africa is second largest with about 30.3 million square km.
r: Africa is also the second most populous continent.

q: Who was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel? (26)
f: Hazrat Isa (AS) was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
r: Hazrat Isa (AS) was given the Injeel.

q: In which month and Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah (Fatah Makkah) take place? (26)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah with an army of about ten thousand in Ramadan 8 AH, traditionally dated 20 Ramadan.
r: The conquest took place almost without bloodshed and the Prophet (PBUH) granted a general amnesty.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom? (26)
f: Andy Burnham became UK Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer stepped down as Labour leader.
r: Boris Johnson, the answer candidates gave in 2021-22, was Prime Minister from 2019 to 2022.

q: Between which two leaders was the Indus Waters Treaty signed in 1960? (26)
f: The treaty was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960 by Pakistan's President Ayub Khan and India's Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
r: The World Bank also signed it as a party to the treaty.

q: Campbellpur is the old name of which city of Pakistan? (26)
f: The city of Attock in Punjab was called Campbellpur during British rule, after Sir Colin Campbell. It was renamed Attock in 1978.
r: Attock is named after the famous Attock Fort on the Indus River.

q: The census of Pakistan is conducted by which organization? (26)
f: Population and housing censuses in Pakistan are carried out by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics. NADRA and the Election Commission only use the data or registers.
r: The 2017 and the digital 2023 censuses were both conducted by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

q: What is the other name of the Battle of Ahzab? (26)
f: The Battle of Ahzab (the Confederates) is also called the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) because the Muslims dug a trench around Madinah. It was fought in 5 AH.
r: The trench was dug on the suggestion of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

q: Youm-ul-Furqan is the name given to the day of which battle? (26)
f: The Battle of Badr, fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH, is called Youm-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
r: Badr was the first major battle between the Muslims and the Quraish.

q: Which surah of the Holy Quran is named after the ant? (26)
f: Surah Al-Naml (the Ant), the 27th surah, takes its name from the story of the ant that warned its colony about Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) and his army.
r: Al-Nahl is the surah named after the bee and Al-Ankabut the one named after the spider.

q: Between which two countries was the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 signed? (26)
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed by Pakistan and India to end the 1965 war.
r: The Soviet Union under Premier Kosygin mediated, and Indian PM Shastri died in Tashkent right after signing.

q: In which year was Bengal partitioned by the British? (26)
f: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905 into East Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Between which two countries does the Line of Control (LOC) lie? (26)
f: The Line of Control is the de facto military border dividing Indian-administered and Pakistan-administered Kashmir.
r: It was established by the Simla Agreement of 1972.

q: Who was the first poet of the Punjabi language? (26)
f: Hazrat Baba Fariduddin Ganjshakar (1188-1266) is regarded as the first poet of Punjabi, and his verses appear in the Guru Granth Sahib.
r: His shrine is in Pakpattan.

q: In which city is Mughalpura (famous for its railway workshops) located? (26)
f: Mughalpura is an area of Lahore and is known for its large railway workshops and station.
r: Lahore Junction is the main railway station of the city.

q: What does FATF stand for? (26)
f: FATF is the Financial Action Task Force, an international body that sets standards against money laundering and terror financing.
r: Pakistan was placed on the FATF grey list in June 2018 and removed in October 2022.

q: Which woman is mentioned by name in the Quran? (26)
f: Hazrat Maryam (AS), the mother of Prophet Isa (AS), is the only woman named in the Quran.
r: A complete Surah of the Quran, Surah Maryam, is named after her.

q: How many times did Jahangir Khan win the World Open squash championship? (26)
f: Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times, the last in 1988.
r: He also won the British Open ten times in a row from 1982 to 1991.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah receive the title of Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader), as most Pakistani textbooks state? (26)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks say that Maulana Mazharuddin Shaheed gave the title Quaid-e-Azam to Jinnah in 1938.
r: Sources differ on the exact year, and some mention 1936 or other dates.

q: What is the approximate total area of Pakistan? (26)
f: Pakistan covers about 796,095 square kilometres, the 33rd largest country by area.
r: Balochistan is the largest province, covering about 44 percent of the country.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh (as of 2026)? (26)
f: Tarique Rahman of the BNP became Prime Minister on 17 February 2026 after the general election.
r: Before him Muhammad Yunus led the interim government after Sheikh Hasina left in 2024.

q: Saint John's is the capital of which country? (26)
f: Saint John's is the capital of Antigua and Barbuda, on the island of Antigua.
r: Antigua and Barbuda became independent from Britain in 1981.

q: Which is the longest river of Pakistan, also called the Sindh river? (26)
f: The Indus River is about 2,900 km long and is the longest river of Pakistan. It is also called Sindh or Abaseen.
r: It starts near Mount Kailash in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi.

q: Who was the first president of the All India Muslim League? (25)
f: Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was the first president of the All India Muslim League, founded in Dhaka in 1906.
r: The League was founded at Dhaka during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy headquarters? (25)
f: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.
r: The main naval base and Fleet Command are at Karachi.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) were killed in the Battle of Badr? (25)
f: About 70 Quraish fighters were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr.
r: Fourteen Muslims were martyred at Badr.

q: Who was the first Mughal emperor of India? (25)
f: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
r: Sher Shah Suri was not a Mughal; he briefly defeated Humayun.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (25)
f: Percentage present = 360 / 500 x 100 = 72%.
r: The absent students are 140, which is 28%.

q: What is the kunniyat (kunyah) of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW)? (25)
f: The Prophet (SAW) was called Abu al-Qasim after his first son Qasim.
r: His other sons Abdullah and Ibrahim also died in infancy.

q: What was the old name of Attock city? (25)
f: Attock city was known as Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell.
r: Its old name was restored to Attock in 1978.

q: What was the caliphate number of Hazrat Umar (RA) among the Rashidun caliphs? (25)
f: The order of the Rashidun caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (may Allah be pleased with them). Umar was therefore the second.
r: Hazrat Umar (RA) ruled from 634 to 644 AD and is called Al-Farooq.

q: What is a triangle with all sides equal called? (25)
f: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles of 60 degrees each.
r: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and a scalene triangle has no equal sides.

q: For what is Ziarat famous? (25)
f: Ziarat in Balochistan is known for the Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days in 1948.
r: Ziarat is also known for one of the largest juniper forests in the world.

q: What is the highest court of Pakistan? (25)
f: The Supreme Court of Pakistan, in Islamabad, is the apex court of the country.
r: The Federal Shariat Court examines whether laws conform to Islamic injunctions.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 23rd day of that month? (25)
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: Who is the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK)? (25)
f: Faisal Karim Kundi of the PPP has been Governor of KPK since May 2024. He took over from Haji Ghulam Ali.
r: Shah Farman, the answer given in 2022, was governor from 2019 to 2023.

q: According to the 2023 census, about what percentage of Pakistan's population is Muslim? (25)
f: The 2023 census recorded Muslims at about 96.35 percent of the population of Pakistan.
r: The 2017 census figure was 96.47 percent, and candidates often quote 97 percent.

q: What is 1/3 of 90? (25)
f: 90 divided by 3 = 30.
r: A third of 90 is ten times a third of 9.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) came to fight the Muslims in the Battle of Badr? (25)
f: The Makkan army at Badr was about 1000 strong, while the Muslims were about 313.
r: In the Battle of Uhad the Makkan army was about 3000 strong.

q: Which battle of the Muslims, fought in 3 AH, is counted as the second major battle after Badr? (25)
f: The major battles in order are Badr (2 AH), Uhud (3 AH) and Khandaq (5 AH), so Uhud is the second.
r: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (25)
f: Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have? (25)
f: The 1962 Constitution given by Ayub Khan had 250 articles.
r: It was suspended when martial law was imposed in 1969.

q: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought? (25)
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526, which started the Mughal Empire in India.
r: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556 and the Third in 1761.

q: Which is the deepest known point of the Earth's surface? (25)
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench of the western Pacific is the deepest known point, at about 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.
r: Mount Everest, the highest point, would be covered by more than 2 km of water if placed in the Challenger Deep.

q: What is the synonym of the word 'tame' (or 'tamed')? (25)
f: To tame means to make an animal gentle and used to humans, so tame or tamed means domesticated.
r: Its antonym is wild.

q: Who has scored the most runs in Test cricket? (25)
f: Sachin Tendulkar of India scored 15,921 runs in 200 Tests, and no one has passed this total as of October 2026.
r: Joe Root of England is second, having passed 14,000 Test runs in 2026.

q: What is the capital of Russia? (25)
f: Moscow is the capital and largest city of Russia.
r: Saint Petersburg was the capital of the Russian Empire until 1918.

q: Where is the headquarters of the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (UN Human Rights)? (25)
f: The OHCHR (UN Human Rights) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. The UN Human Rights Council also meets in Geneva.
r: The UN Headquarters itself is in New York.

q: Which is the largest desert in the world by area? (25)
f: A desert is an area with very little precipitation, and Antarctica, at about 14 million square km, is the largest. The Sahara is the largest hot desert.
r: The Arctic Desert is the second largest and the Sahara is third.

q: When did Namaz (salah) become farz (obligatory) for Muslims? (24)
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Miraj, roughly five years before the Hijrat. Before this, the Muslims offered some prayers without a fixed five-time rule.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) received the command of five daily prayers directly from Allah during the Miraj.

q: Which city is known as the city of mosques? (24)
f: Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh, is known as the City of Mosques because of its thousands of mosques.
r: Dhaka is also known as the city of rickshaws.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, who resolves a dispute between the National Assembly and the Senate? (24)
f: Under Article 70, a bill on which the two houses disagree is settled by a joint sitting of both houses, decided by a majority of the total members present.
r: The President summons the joint sitting.

q: What does Saif mean in Arabic? (24)
f: Saif is the Arabic word for sword.
r: The Arabic word for shield is dir.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Urwa bin Zubair with Hazrat Ayesha (RA)? (24)
f: Urwa was the son of Hazrat Zubair bin Awwam and Hazrat Asma, who was the sister of Hazrat Ayesha. This made Urwa her nephew.
r: Urwa bin Zubair is one of the seven famous jurists of Madina and a major narrator of hadith from his aunt Hazrat Ayesha.

q: In which year of the Hijra was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem) to the Kaaba? (24)
f: The command to turn towards the Kaaba came in 2 AH, about sixteen to seventeen months after the Hijra, while the Prophet (PBUH) was leading prayer in Madina.
r: The mosque where this happened is known as Masjid Qiblatain.

q: Who is Hazrat Jibrael (AS)? (24)
f: Jibrael (AS) is the angel who brought the revelation of Allah to the prophets.
r: He first brought the Quran to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in the cave of Hira.

q: Chess originated in which country? (24)
f: Chess developed from an Indian game called chaturanga around the 6th century AD. It then spread to Persia and the Muslim world.
r: The Arabic and Persian word shatranj comes from the Sanskrit chaturanga.

q: From where do plants mainly obtain nitrogen for growth? (24)
f: Plants absorb nitrogen through their roots from the soil as nitrates and ammonium. Atmospheric nitrogen is made usable by bacteria and lightning.
r: Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules that fix nitrogen.

q: In which city was the Indian National Congress founded in 1885? (24)
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under W. C. Bonnerjee.
r: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, was the main founder of the Congress.

q: Which countries does the 38th parallel divide? (24)
f: The 38th parallel north was the dividing line between North and South Korea after 1945.
r: The present border, the Demilitarized Zone, was set by the 1953 armistice and runs near the 38th parallel.

q: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) appointed Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal (RA) as governor of which place? (24)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal to Yemen as governor and teacher of the people.
r: Hazrat Maaz bin Jabal was known as the most knowledgeable of the Companions in halal and haram.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Ismail (AS)? (24)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra.
r: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was his younger half-brother.

q: Who gave the first Azan in Islam? (24)
f: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA) was appointed by the Prophet (PBUH) as the first muezzin and called the first Azan in Madinah.
r: Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the Azan in a dream, and the Prophet (PBUH) taught them to Bilal (RA).

q: How many wajibat of Namaz are there according to the Hanafi school? (24)
f: The Hanafi school counts 14 wajibat of Namaz, such as reciting Surah Fatiha and a further surah.
r: The fard acts of Namaz are 13 in number.

q: The Shimla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed after which war? (24)
f: After the 1971 war and the separation of East Pakistan, Pakistan and India met at Shimla in 1972 and signed the agreement.
r: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed after the 1965 war.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Neelum Valley and the Neelum River located? (24)
f: The Neelum Valley and the Neelum River lie in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: The river flows through Muzaffarabad and joins the Jhelum, and its capital valley town is Athmuqam.

q: In which province does the Upper Indus Plain mainly lie? (24)
f: The Upper Indus Plain, north of Mithankot, covers most of Punjab, where the five rivers join the Indus.
r: The Lower Indus Plain to the south lies mainly in Sindh.

q: What is the new name of the Kashmir Highway in Islamabad? (24)
f: In August 2020 Pakistan renamed Islamabad's Kashmir Highway as Srinagar Highway in solidarity with Kashmiris.
r: The renaming was done on the first anniversary of India's revocation of Article 370 in 2019.

q: At what age is Hazrat Isa (AS) commonly said to have been raised to the heavens? (24)
f: The commonly stated age at which Hazrat Isa (AS) was raised to the heavens is 33 years.
r: Sources differ on the exact age, but 33 is the figure most commonly given.

q: What is the capital of Latvia? (24)
f: Riga is the capital and largest city of Latvia.
r: Latvia is one of the three Baltic states.

q: In which Islamic month is Hajj performed? (24)
f: Hajj rites are performed from the 8th to the 12th or 13th of Dhul Hijjah, the last month of the Islamic calendar.
r: Eid-ul-Adha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah.

q: In which year was the first Round Table Conference held in London? (24)
f: The first Round Table Conference was held in London from November 1930 to January 1931.
r: Three Round Table Conferences were held between 1930 and 1932.

q: Which is the hottest planet of the solar system? (24)
f: Venus is the hottest planet, about 465 degrees Celsius, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
r: Mercury is closer to the Sun but has almost no atmosphere to hold heat.

q: What is sin X divided by cos X equal to? (23)
f: By definition, tan X equals sin X over cos X.
r: The reciprocal, cos X over sin X, is cot X.

q: Between which two parties was the Lucknow Pact signed? (23)
o: Muslim League and the British Government
Muslim League and the Khaksar movement
f: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League. Both parties agreed to a joint demand for self-government.
r: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Quaid-e-Azam were the main leaders involved in making the pact.

q: What is the full form of OPEC? (23)
o: Organization of Producing and Exporting Countries
Organization of Power and Energy Countries
f: OPEC stands for Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a group of oil producing nations.
r: OPEC was founded in 1960 in Baghdad and is headquartered in Vienna.

q: Who was the second caliph (Khalifa) of Islam? (23)
f: Hazrat Umar bin Khattab (RA) became the second caliph in 13 AH after being nominated by Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA). He ruled for about ten years.
r: He was martyred in 23 AH by Abu Lulu Firoz and was succeeded by Hazrat Usman (RA).

q: In which city is the historic Bala Hisar Fort located? (23)
f: Bala Hisar Fort stands in Peshawar, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It overlooks the old city.
r: The fort was rebuilt by the Sikhs in the early 19th century.

q: In which surah is Ayat-ul-Kursi found? (23)
f: Ayat-ul-Kursi is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah.
r: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran with 286 verses.

q: What was the religion of Najashi, the king of Abyssinia (Habsha) who gave shelter to the early Muslim migrants? (23)
f: Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia was a Christian king. He protected the Muslim emigrants and refused to hand them over to the Quraish.
r: The Muslims made their first migration to Abyssinia in 5th year of the Prophethood.

q: Which country is the place of origin of the game of squash? (23)
f: Squash originated in England at Harrow School in the 19th century.
r: Pakistan dominated world squash through Hashim Khan, Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan.

q: Another name for the Manila Pact of 1954 is: (23)
f: The Manila Pact created the South East Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO), signed in Manila in September 1954.
r: SEATO was dissolved in 1977.

q: The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from which country? (23)
f: The narrow Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan lies between Pakistan on the south and Tajikistan on the north.
r: The corridor also touches China at its eastern end.

q: What is Bait ul Muqaddas? (23)
f: Bait ul Muqaddas means the Holy House and refers to Jerusalem and its Masjid al-Aqsa.
r: It was the first Qibla of Muslims before the change to the Kaaba.

q: What is the nisab (minimum threshold) of gold for zakat, in tola? (23)
f: The nisab of gold is 7.5 tola (about 87.48 grams). The 52.5 tola figure is the nisab of silver.
r: Zakat on wealth at or above the nisab is 2.5 percent.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of France as of October 2026? (23)
f: Sebastien Lecornu was appointed Prime Minister in September 2025 and reappointed in October 2025, and was still in office in October 2026.
r: Elisabeth Borne (2022-2024), whom candidates wrote in 2022, was later followed by Attal, Barnier and Bayrou; Emmanuel Macron is the President, not the PM.

q: Who was the first Pakistani woman cricketer to take 100 ODI wickets? (23)
f: Sana Mir became the first Pakistani woman to take 100 ODI wickets in February 2017 against Bangladesh in the World Cup Qualifier.
r: She finished her ODI career with about 150 ODI wickets, the most by a Pakistani woman, and was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame.

q: What was the code name of Pakistan's first nuclear tests of 28 May 1998? (23)
f: Pakistan's tests of 28 May 1998 at Chagai in Balochistan were code-named Chagai-I.
r: India's 1974 test was Smiling Buddha and its 1998 tests were Shakti; Pakistan's second test on 30 May 1998 was Chagai-II.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yousuf (AS)? (23)
f: Hazrat Yousuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).
r: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) is also known as Israel.

q: Which was the first private television channel of Pakistan? (23)
f: Shalimar Television Network, which began in 1990 as People's Television Network, was the first channel to break the monopoly of state-run PTV. It is the answer most textbooks give.
r: Sources differ on the word private: ARY Digital (2001) and Indus TV (2000) are often called the first fully independent channels.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the term of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies? (23)
f: Unless dissolved earlier, the National and Provincial Assemblies serve a term of five years from their first meeting.
r: A Senator's term is six years, with half retiring every three years.

q: In which year was the Suez Canal completed and opened? (23)
f: The Suez Canal was opened to traffic on 17 November 1869 after about ten years of construction.
r: It was built under the French engineer Ferdinand de Lesseps and links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.

q: What does SCO stand for? (23)
f: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a Eurasian political, economic and security grouping.
r: Its permanent bodies are the Secretariat in Beijing and the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure in Tashkent.

q: In which year was the second general election held in Pakistan? (23)
f: Pakistan's first general election on adult franchise was held in 1970 and the second in March 1977.
r: The 1977 election led to protests and the martial law of General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.

q: Which country lies to the west of Pakistan? (23)
f: Iran borders Pakistan on the west, mainly along Balochistan.
r: Afghanistan lies to the north-west of Pakistan.

q: In which year did Balochistan become a province of Pakistan? (23)
f: When the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan was dissolved on 1 July 1970, Balochistan became a full province.
r: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.

q: Who is credited with inventing the electric motor? (23)
f: Michael Faraday demonstrated the first electric motor in 1821, and most textbooks credit him.
r: Other inventors such as Jedlik, Jacobi and Davenport also built early motors, so sources differ.

q: Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bal-e-Jibreel (Gabriel's Wing)? (23)
f: Bal-e-Jibreel was written by Allama Muhammad Iqbal and published in 1935.
r: Iqbal's other Urdu books include Bang-e-Dara and Zarb-e-Kaleem.

q: What was the first book of poetry of Allama Iqbal? (23)
f: Asrar-e-Khudi, a Persian poetry book, was published in 1915 and is usually called his first poetry book.
r: His first prose book was Ilm-ul-Iqtisad (1903), so sources differ depending on the question.

q: Where were all the Round Table Conferences (1930 to 1932) held? (23)
f: The three Round Table Conferences were held in London to discuss constitutional reforms for India. They took place in 1930, 1931 and 1932.
r: The Muslim League was represented by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and Allama Iqbal attended the second session.

q: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar? (22)
f: The Islamic year has twelve months and Dhul Hijjah is the twelfth and last.
r: Hajj is performed in Dhul Hijjah and Muharram is the first month.

q: What is the national tree of Pakistan? (22)
f: The Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is the national tree of Pakistan.
r: Its name comes from Sanskrit and means timber of the gods.

q: In which country were the Olympic Games postponed from 2020 and held in 2021 hosted? (22)
f: The Tokyo Olympics, scheduled for 2020, were postponed because of Covid-19 and held in Japan in July-August 2021.
r: The next Summer Olympics after Tokyo were held in Paris in 2024.

q: How many faraiz (obligatory acts) does Hajj have according to the Hanafi school? (22)
f: The three faraiz are Ihram, standing at Arafat (Wuquf) and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.
r: Schools of thought differ slightly in counting Hajj faraiz, but the Hanafi count of three is common in Pakistani textbooks.

q: What was the old name of Madina? (22)
f: Madina was known as Yathrib before the Prophet (PBUH) migrated there in 622 CE.
r: Madina means the city of the Prophet.

q: Who gave the idea of SAARC? (22)
o: J. R. Jayewardene of Sri Lanka
f: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh proposed regional cooperation in South Asia in 1980, leading to SAARC.
r: SAARC was formally founded in Dhaka in December 1985.

q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet (SAW) live in Madina after the Hijrah? (22)
f: He migrated to Madina in 622 AD (1 AH) and passed away there in 632 AD (11 AH), about ten years later.
r: He lived about 13 years in Makkah after receiving the first revelation.

q: Under the Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to India? (22)
f: The 1960 treaty gave the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.
r: India announced in April 2025 that it was holding the treaty in abeyance, but the treaty allocation itself is unchanged.

q: What is the meaning of Al-Feel? (22)
f: Al-Feel is Arabic for the elephant and is the name of Surah 105 of the Quran.
r: The surah describes the army of Abraha with elephants that attacked the Kaaba in the year of the Prophet's birth.

q: On which occasion did Hinda (wife of Abu Sufyan) accept Islam? (22)
f: Hinda bint Utbah, who had opposed Islam at Uhud, accepted Islam when Makkah was conquered in 8 AH.
r: Her son Hazrat Muawiya (RA) later founded the Umayyad dynasty.

q: Who recited Surah Maryam before the king Najashi of Abyssinia? (22)
f: Hazrat Jaffar bin Abi Talib spoke for the Muslim migrants and recited verses of Surah Maryam, which moved Najashi and the bishops.
r: Hazrat Jaffar was later martyred at the Battle of Mutah and is known as Tayyar.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Furqan? (22)
o: The criterion that separates right from wrong
f: Furqan comes from an Arabic root meaning to separate or distinguish. It therefore means the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
r: Al-Furqan is a name of the Holy Quran and the title of the 25th surah.

q: In which country is the Wakhan Corridor situated? (22)
f: The Wakhan Corridor is a strip of land in the north-east of Afghanistan in Badakhshan province.
r: It was created as a buffer between the British and Russian empires in the 19th century.

q: Which was the first Muslim country to become a nuclear power? (22)
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998 and became the first Muslim country with nuclear weapons.
r: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-armed country in the world, after India's tests earlier in May 1998.

q: Who was the commander of the Quraysh army in the Battle of Uhud? (22)
f: Abu Sufyan bin Harb led the Makkan army of about 3,000 in 3 AH, because Abu Jahl had been killed at Badr. Khalid bin Walid commanded the cavalry wing.
r: Abu Sufyan later accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

q: Aleem Dar is a famous umpire of which game? (22)
f: Aleem Dar, from Lahore, is a famous Pakistani cricket umpire who stood in over 100 Test matches and won the ICC Umpire of the Year award three times in a row (2009-2011).
r: He served on the ICC Elite Panel of Umpires for many years.

q: Vienna is the capital of which country? (22)
f: Vienna is the capital and largest city of Austria on the Danube River.
r: Budapest, the capital of Hungary, is also on the Danube.

q: Who was the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan? (22)
f: Shamshad Akhtar became the first woman Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan in 2005.
r: She later served as Caretaker Finance Minister in 2023.

q: In which year was the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) established? (22)
f: ECO was established in 1985 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey as the successor of RCD.
r: RCD (Regional Cooperation for Development) was formed in 1964.

q: Under which Prime Minister was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan framed and enforced? (22)
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the constitution in 1956, and it came into force on 23 March 1956.
r: 23 March is the day later celebrated as Republic Day, and Iskander Mirza became the first President under it.

q: On which date did the partition of Bengal take effect? (22)
f: The partition of Bengal came into effect on 16 October 1905.
r: Muslims celebrated it, while Hindus observed the day as a day of mourning.

q: In which year was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh Dogra under the Treaty of Amritsar? (22)
f: After the First Anglo-Sikh War the British signed the Treaty of Amritsar on 16 March 1846 and sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh.
r: The price was 75 lakh Nanak Shahi rupees.

q: On which date in 1933 was the name Pakistan first put forward by Choudhry Rahmat Ali in the pamphlet Now or Never? (22)
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali issued the pamphlet Now or Never on 28 January 1933 and proposed the name Pakistan in it.
r: The Lahore Resolution came later, on 23 March 1940.

q: Who was Lord Curzon at the time of the partition of Bengal in 1905? (22)
f: Lord Curzon was the Viceroy and Governor-General of India from 1899 to 1905 and he carried out the partition of Bengal in 1905.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Which pass connects Peshawar with Afghanistan? (22)
f: The Khyber Pass, with the Torkham crossing, connects Peshawar with Afghanistan.
r: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with Afghanistan and the Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan with China.

q: Which is the present constitution of Pakistan? (22)
f: Pakistan is currently governed by the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973.
r: It has been amended many times, including the 18th Amendment in 2010.

q: What do the five rings of the Olympic flag represent? (22)
o: Five inhabited continents of the world
f: The five interlocked rings stand for the five inhabited continents joined by Olympism: Africa, the Americas, Asia, Europe and Oceania.
r: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background, designed in 1913 and first flown in 1920.

q: How many member countries does the Commonwealth of Nations have? (22)
f: The Commonwealth of Nations has 56 member states, the latest being Gabon and Togo who joined in June 2022.
r: Before 2022 the Commonwealth had 54 members.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current? (22)
f: Electric current is measured in amperes (amps), the flow of charge per second.
r: An ammeter, connected in series, measures current.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to fragment? (22)
f: A fragment is a small broken part or piece of something larger.
r: The opposite of fragment is whole or complete.

q: Who wrote the work The Loyal Muhammadans of India? (22)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan wrote it around 1860 to show that most Muslims were loyal to the British during the events of 1857.
r: Sir Syed also wrote Asar-us-Sanadid and founded the Aligarh movement.

q: In which year was the Durand Line, the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, agreed? (22)
f: The Durand Line agreement was signed in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan of Afghanistan.
r: Afghanistan has not formally accepted the Durand Line as an international border.

q: Which element is the most abundant in the universe? (22)
f: Hydrogen makes up about 75 percent of the ordinary matter in the universe by mass.
r: Helium is the second most abundant element, and oxygen is the most abundant in the Earth crust.

q: For what is the city of Multan famous? (22)
f: Multan is known as the City of Saints (Madinat-ul-Auliya) because it has many famous shrines of Sufi saints.
r: Multan is also called the City of Pirs and is famous for its mangoes and blue pottery.

q: If yesterday was Saturday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (21)
f: If yesterday was Saturday, today is Sunday and tomorrow is Monday. The day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
r: Candidates remembered Monday, which is tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow.

q: How many non-permanent members does the UN Security Council have? (21)
f: The Council has 15 members: 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent members.
r: Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.

q: What is the largest lake of Europe? (21)
f: Lake Ladoga in Russia, about 17,700 square km, is the largest lake entirely within Europe.
r: The Caspian Sea is larger but is usually not counted as a European lake.

q: Which is the last surah of the Holy Quran? (21)
f: Surah An-Nas is number 114 and is the last surah in the order of the Quran.
r: The first surah in order is Al-Fatihah.

q: In which year was NATO founded? (21)
f: NATO was founded by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington in April 1949.
r: The Soviet-led rival Warsaw Pact was formed in 1955.

q: What does Saifullah mean? (21)
f: Saif means sword and Allah is God, so Saifullah means Sword of Allah.
r: Saifullah was the title given to Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) by the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which surah contains the first verses of the Quran to be revealed? (21)
f: The first five verses revealed to the Prophet (SAW) in the Cave of Hira were from Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
r: Surah Al-Muddaththir is commonly mentioned as the next revelation after a pause.

q: Where is the hottest recorded air temperature in the world, 56.7 degrees Celsius (1913)? (21)
f: The official record of 56.7 degrees Celsius (134 F) was measured at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, in July 1913.
r: Candidates answered Egypt, but Egypt does not hold the world record.

q: What is the meaning of Ijtihad? (21)
o: To exert effort to reach a legal ruling
f: Ijtihad means to strive or exert one's utmost effort, in Islamic law to derive a ruling from the Quran and Sunnah.
r: Allama Iqbal called ijtihad the principle of movement in Islam.

q: What is the national language of Pakistan? (21)
f: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan under the Constitution.
r: English and Urdu are the official languages.

q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located? (21)
f: Nishtar Hospital is a large teaching hospital in Multan, Punjab.
r: It is named after Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a Pakistan Movement leader.

q: Which country is the world's largest exporter of arms? (21)
f: According to SIPRI, the United States is the largest arms exporter and supplies around 40 percent of global arms exports.
r: France has recently overtaken Russia as the second largest arms exporter.

q: Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport? (21)
f: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a Pakistani cricketer and the first captain of Pakistan in Test cricket.
r: He captained Pakistan in its first Test victory, at The Oval in 1954.

q: On which date is Defence Day observed in Pakistan? (21)
f: Defence Day is observed on 6 September to commemorate the defence of Pakistan in the 1965 war.
r: The 1965 war with India was fought in September 1965.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Hadith? (21)
f: In Arabic, Hadith means speech, statement, report or narration.
r: Technically, a Hadith is a report of the words, actions or approvals of the Prophet (SAW).

q: What is the meaning of Riba in Islam? (21)
f: Riba means increase and refers to interest or usury on loans, which Islam prohibits.
r: The prohibition of riba is stated in Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: What was the Nehru Report (1928)? (21)
o: Constitutional proposals for India drafted by a committee under Motilal Nehru
f: The Nehru Report of 1928 was a set of constitutional proposals drafted by a committee headed by Motilal Nehru. It rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Muhammad Ali Jinnah responded with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: Approximately what percentage of the adult human body is water? (21)
f: Water makes up about 60 percent of an adult's body weight.
r: Infants have a higher share, around 75 percent.

q: Why is the colour of the sky blue? (21)
o: Scattering of sunlight by air molecules
Absorption of blue light by clouds
f: Air molecules scatter short wavelength light (blue) much more than long wavelengths (red). This is called Rayleigh scattering.
r: At sunrise and sunset the sky looks red because light travels through more air and blue is scattered away.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 4th day of that month? (21)
f: The 14th is 10 days after the 4th. 10 mod 7 = 3, so go back 3 days from Monday: Sunday, Saturday, Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart always fall on the same weekday.

q: How many books are included in the Sihah Sittah (Sahih Sitta), the six authentic collections of hadith? (21)
f: Sihah Sittah literally means the six correct books. The six collections are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi, Nasai and Ibn Majah.
r: Sahih Bukhari, compiled by Imam Bukhari, is regarded as the most authentic of them.

q: On which date did the United Nations officially come into existence? (21)
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after ratification by China, France, the USSR, the UK, the USA and most other signatories. This date is celebrated as United Nations Day.
r: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.

q: Who is the youngest Nobel Prize winner in history? (21)
f: Malala Yousafzai was 17 years old when she received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, the youngest laureate ever.
r: Lawrence Bragg, aged 25, was the youngest laureate in a science field (Physics, 1915).

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When the boy is 11 years old, how old will his sister be? (21)
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 3 = 9 years, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11 she will be 11 + 6 = 17 years.
r: The age difference between two people never changes with time.

q: For what is Sher Shah Suri best known? (21)
o: Grand Trade Road and administrative reforms
f: Sher Shah Suri (1540-45) rebuilt the Grand Trade Road, introduced the silver rupee and reformed revenue administration.
r: He defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa and Kannauj.

q: Which angel will blow the trumpet (Sur) on the Day of Judgement? (21)
f: Hazrat Israfil (AS) is the angel appointed to blow the Sur to end the world and again to raise the dead.
r: Hazrat Azrail (AS) is the angel of death.

q: Who is the head of state of the United Kingdom? (21)
f: The UK is a monarchy with no president, and King Charles III is the head of state.
r: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister in July 2026, and in 2022 candidates named Boris Johnson in this role.

q: In which year was FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (21)
f: The 25th Constitutional Amendment was passed in May 2018 and merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which was completed after the President signed it.
r: Candidates often confuse this with 2021, but the merger law was passed in 2018.

q: Which one is different from the others: Circle, Square, Triangle, Angle? (21)
f: Circle, square and triangle are closed geometric figures, while an angle is not a closed figure.
r: An angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common point.

q: On what date did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start? (21)
f: The Pakistan Army launched Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad on 22 February 2017 against terrorism after a wave of attacks. It was a nationwide operation.
r: Operation Zarb-e-Azb in 2014 was an earlier operation in North Waziristan.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be? (21)
f: From the 4th to the 19th is 15 days. 15 days is 2 full weeks plus 1 day(s), so the day is 1 day(s) after Friday, which is Saturday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: What is the derivative of sin x with respect to x? (21)
f: The standard derivative of sin x is cos x.
r: The derivative of cos x is -sin x.

q: What is the legislature of Pakistan called? (21)
f: Pakistan's federal legislature is the Majlis-e-Shura (Parliament), made up of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: India's lower house is called the Lok Sabha.

q: Baba Fariduddin Ganj Shakar is regarded as the first major poet of which language? (21)
f: Baba Farid (1173-1266) of Pakpattan is considered the first major poet of the Punjabi language.
r: Some of his verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

q: What type of constitution was the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan? (21)
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, set up a federal parliamentary republic with a unicameral National Assembly.
r: It was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which town of Pakistan? (21)
f: The Khyber Pass runs from near Peshawar through Jamrud and Landi Kotal to the Torkham border with Afghanistan.
r: Landi Kotal is the highest point of the pass and lies close to the Afghan border.

q: Which is the smallest ocean in the world? (21)
f: The Arctic Ocean has an area of about 14 million square kilometres and is the smallest and shallowest ocean.
r: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.

q: Electric current is due to the flow of what? (21)
f: In a metallic conductor, the free electrons drift under a potential difference, and this flow of charge is the electric current.
r: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere.

q: What is the SI unit of temperature? (21)
f: The kelvin (K) is the base SI unit of temperature. Celsius and Fahrenheit are not SI units.
r: 0 K is called absolute zero, equal to minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

q: What is the official currency of Iran? (21)
f: The official currency of Iran is the Iranian rial. Ordinary people often quote prices in toman, which equals 10 rials.
r: Iran has passed a law to remove four zeros from the rial, and parliament kept the name rial rather than toman.

q: In which year was the One Unit scheme established in West Pakistan? (21)
f: The provinces of West Pakistan were merged into one unit in 1955.
r: One Unit was dissolved by Yahya Khan in 1970.

q: Find the odd one out: Pindi, Lahore, Karachi, Quetta, Peshawar. (21)
f: Lahore, Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar are the capitals of the four provinces of Pakistan, while Pindi (Rawalpindi) is not a provincial capital.
r: Rawalpindi is the neighbour of Islamabad and hosts the General Headquarters of the Pakistan Army.

q: Why do parents give education to their children? (21)
f: Parents educate children to groom them, that is, to prepare and train them for a successful life.
r: Groom means to prepare someone for a future role.

q: Which game is known as the Gentleman's Game? (21)
f: Cricket is called the gentleman's game because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship.
r: Cricket originated in England.

q: Which word is closest to the opposite of envious? (21)
f: Envious means wanting what others have. A content person is satisfied with what they have, so content is the opposite.
r: The noun envy is opposed by contentment.

q: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan? (21)
f: The Hindu Kush range lies in the north-west of Pakistan, along the border with Afghanistan.
r: Some sources also mention the Sulaiman Range, which lies to the west.

q: Which is the biggest sea of the world by area? (20)
f: The Philippine Sea covers about 5.7 million square km, the largest sea in the world. The South China Sea is about 3.5 million square km.
r: The Arabian Sea is the largest of the other options and lies next to Pakistan's coast.

q: In which Hijri year did the tragedy of Karbala take place? (20)
f: The martyrdom of Hazrat Hussain (RA) at Karbala took place on 10 Muharram 61 AH (680 CE).
r: Yazid ibn Muawiya was the Umayyad ruler at that time.

q: In which Islamic month was the Quran first revealed? (20)
f: The Quran began to be revealed in the month of Ramadan, on Laylat ul Qadr, in the cave of Hira.
r: The first revealed verses are the opening of Surah Al-Alaq.

q: With which wife of the Prophet (PBUH) was the compiled copy of the Quran kept after Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had it collected? (20)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) had the Quran compiled in book form; it passed to Hazrat Umar (RA) and then was kept with his daughter Hazrat Hafsa (RA), the Prophet's wife. Hazrat Usman (RA) later borrowed it to prepare copies.
r: Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) led the compilation team under Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).

q: Zun-Noorain (Zunnurain), meaning 'possessor of two lights', is the title of which Companion of the Prophet (PBUH)? (20)
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Ruqayyah and later Hazrat Umm Kulthum (R.A), one after the other. For this reason he is called Zun-Noorain.
r: Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the third Caliph of Islam and is also known as Ghani.

q: The Coastal Highway connects Gwadar with which city? (20)
f: The Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) runs along the Arabian Sea coast from Karachi to Gwadar.
r: It is about 653 km long and was completed in 2004.

q: How many ayats were revealed in the first revelation (Surah Al-Alaq) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (20)
f: The first revelation in the Cave of Hira consisted of the first five ayats of Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
r: The first revelation came in the month of Ramadan.

q: The Thomas Cup is associated with which sport? (20)
f: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team championship of badminton, contested between national teams.
r: The women's equivalent of the Thomas Cup is the Uber Cup.

q: What is the lower house of the Parliament of Pakistan called? (20)
f: The National Assembly is the lower house and its members are directly elected by the people.
r: The upper house of Pakistan's Parliament is the Senate.

q: What is the border line between Pakistan's Punjab and India's Punjab called? (20)
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947 and divides Punjab between Pakistan and India.
r: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

q: With the help of which country was Warsak Dam built? (20)
f: Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was built in the 1950s with Canadian aid under the Colombo Plan.
r: Candidates often said China, but the dam was Canadian-assisted.

q: Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526? (20)
f: Babur defeated the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat on 21 April 1526, which began Mughal rule in India.
r: Babur used artillery and field tactics learned from the Ottomans.

q: Deficiency of vitamin D causes which disease? (20)
f: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bones. Its lack causes soft, bent bones in children, called rickets.
r: Sunlight helps the skin make vitamin D.

q: On what date was the State Bank of Pakistan established? (20)
f: The State Bank of Pakistan began working on 1 July 1948 and was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam.
r: Its first Governor was Zahid Hussain.

q: On which date did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan die? (20)
f: Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan, known as the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021.
r: He was awarded Nishan-e-Imtiaz and Hilal-e-Imtiaz.

q: What is the opposite of 'tame'? (20)
f: Tame means domesticated and not dangerous, so its opposite is wild. Gentle, docile and domestic are close to tame in meaning.
r: Tame can also describe something dull, such as a tame film.

q: Which is the coldest desert in the world? (20)
f: The Antarctic Desert is the coldest and largest desert on Earth, with extremely low rainfall and temperatures far below freezing.
r: The Gobi is the best known cold desert of Asia, but it is much warmer than Antarctica.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month? (20)
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Monday gives Monday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th day of that month? (20)
f: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days, and 24 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: What is the official capital of Indonesia? (20)
f: Jakarta is Indonesia's legal capital. A new capital, Nusantara in East Kalimantan, was planned by a 2022 law, but Jakarta stays the capital until a formal transfer decree is issued.
r: Nusantara is now planned only as a political capital (target 2028), so candidates who wrote Nusantara in 2022 were anticipating a move that has not formally happened.

q: What was the real (original) name of Titu Mir? (20)
f: Titu Mir, the Bengali leader of the Barasat uprising, was born as Mir Nisar Ali.
r: He was killed in 1831 by British forces at his bamboo fort in Narkelbaria.

q: Which President introduced the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan? (20)
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan was President and enforced the 1962 Constitution on 8 June 1962, framed by a commission headed by Justice Shahabuddin.
r: It introduced a presidential system with the President elected through Basic Democrats.

q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability to understand the language of birds and animals? (20)
f: The Quran says that Allah taught Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) the speech of birds, and he talked with the hoopoe and the ant.
r: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) also ruled over the jinn and the wind, and he was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).

q: On which river is the Khanpur Dam built? (20)
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River in the Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: Which is the largest animal in the world? (20)
f: The blue whale grows up to about 30 metres in length and weighs up to nearly 200 tonnes, bigger than any other animal.
r: The African elephant is the largest living land animal.

q: Who was the last Viceroy of British India? (20)
f: Lord Mountbatten served as the last Viceroy from March to August 1947 and then became the first Governor-General of independent India.
r: His predecessor was Lord Wavell.

q: With which neighbouring country does Pakistan share a border of about 2,400 km? (20)
f: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border, the Durand Line, is about 2,430 km long and is commonly quoted as about 2,400 km.
r: Pakistan's border with India is about 3,300 km, with Iran about 900 km and with China about 520 km.

q: What does the name Moen jo Daro (Mohenjo-daro) mean? (20)
f: Mohenjo-daro is a Sindhi name meaning Mound of the Dead. It was a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization.
r: It is located in Larkana district of Sindh and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Which country hosted the first Asian Games in 1951? (20)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
r: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'disruption'? (20)
f: Disruption means a break or interruption in the normal course of something. Disturbance has the same meaning.
r: The opposite of disruption is continuity.

q: What is the chemical symbol of gold in the periodic table? (20)
f: The symbol Au comes from the Latin name aurum, meaning gold.
r: Ag is the symbol of silver, from the Latin argentum.

q: Who conquered Sindh in 712 AD? (20)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim, a young Arab general of the Umayyad caliphate, defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh.
r: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam, the Gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.

q: On which date is the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India commonly said to have begun in 1999? (20)
f: The conflict is commonly dated from 3 May 1999, when intrusions were first reported in the Kargil sector.
r: Indian sources mark 26 July 1999 as the end of the conflict, and sources differ slightly on exact dates.

q: What is the last letter of the word BEAUTY? (20)
f: B-E-A-U-T-Y ends with the letter Y.
r: BEAUTY has six letters.

q: Who was the first Governor General of independent India in 1947? (19)
f: Lord Mountbatten became Governor General of the Dominion of India on 15 August 1947.
r: Sources differ because Warren Hastings and William Bentinck are also called the first Governor General in earlier British India, but for 1947 it is Mountbatten.

q: Who wrote the novel Raja Gidh? (19)
f: Bano Qudsia wrote Raja Gidh, a novel about the concept of haram and halal food and its effect on the mind.
r: She was married to the writer Ashfaq Ahmed.

q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of a Jewish leader? (19)
f: Hazrat Safiyya bint Huyayy was from the Jewish tribe Banu Nadir and married the Prophet (PBUH) after Khaybar.
r: She accepted Islam before the marriage.

q: Which organism causes malaria? (19)
f: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites, spread to humans by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
r: The deadliest malaria parasite is Plasmodium falciparum.

q: What is the area of Punjab (Pakistan) in square kilometres? (19)
f: Punjab covers about 205,344 square kilometres.
r: Punjab is the second largest province by area but the largest by population.

q: What is the meaning of the word alter? (19)
f: To alter means to change something or make it different.
r: The related noun is alteration, meaning a change.

q: What is the maximum length of a cricket bat under the laws of cricket? (19)
f: The Laws of Cricket limit a bat to 38 inches (96.52 cm) in length.
r: The maximum width of the blade is 4.25 inches.

q: What is 1/3 of 1/10 of 120? (19)
r: Taking 1/3 of 1/10 is the same as taking 1/30 of the number.

q: Who was the President of the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan? (19)
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.
r: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan later served as its Speaker.

q: The Lowari Pass connects Chitral with which place? (19)
f: The Lowari Pass links Chitral with Dir, and so with the rest of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: The Lowari Tunnel, opened in 2017, now gives all-weather access to Chitral.

q: What is the height of Mount Everest? (19)
f: The 2020 joint Nepal-China survey gave Everest a height of 8,848.86 m, commonly rounded to 8,849 m.
r: Before 2020 the accepted height was 8,848 m.

q: At what age did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) place the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) in the Kaaba? (19)
f: When the Quraish rebuilt the Kaaba, they disputed who would put the Black Stone in place. The Prophet, aged 35, settled the matter by placing it on a cloth carried by all the tribal chiefs.
r: The Quraish called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and accepted his decision.

q: Where did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests on 28 May 1998? (19)
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh hills of Chagai district, Balochistan.
r: 28 May is observed every year as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 13th? (19)
f: The gap is 12 days. 12 mod 7 = 5, so Monday plus 5 days is Saturday.
r: The 8th, 15th, 22nd and 29th fall on the same weekday as the 1st.

q: Which word is formed by the alphabet positions 18, 5, 19, 20? (19)
f: Positions 18, 5, 19, 20 are R, E, S, T.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters, with Z at position 26.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month? (19)
f: From the 2nd to the 12th is 10 days, and 10 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Monday gives Thursday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan as of 2026? (19)
