f: The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and the 27th Amendment was passed by Parliament in November 2025. A 28th amendment was still only under discussion in mid-2026.
r: The 27th Amendment created the post of Chief of Defence Forces and a Federal Constitutional Court.

q: In which Islamic month did Pakistan gain independence on 14 August 1947? (19)
f: Pakistan came into being on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, which was 14 August 1947, a Friday.
r: 27 Ramadan is also known as Laylat al-Qadr in popular belief.

q: In which mountain range of Pakistan is Tirich Mir located? (19)
f: Tirich Mir lies in Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, in the Hindu Kush range.
r: At about 7,708 metres it is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

q: The Battle of Furqan is the name of which ghazwa? (19)
f: The Quran calls the day of Badr Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction between truth and falsehood. So the Battle of Furqan is the Battle of Badr.
r: Badr was fought in 2 AH (624 CE) and about 313 Muslims faced roughly 1000 Makkan soldiers.

q: What is the integral part of a logarithm called? (19)
f: A logarithm has two parts: the integer part is the characteristic and the decimal part is the mantissa.
r: The mantissa of a common logarithm is always kept positive.

q: Which was the first qiblah of the Muslims? (19)
o: Bait ul Muqaddas (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem
f: Muslims prayed towards Bait ul Muqaddas for about 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah. The qiblah was then changed to the Kaaba.
r: The change took place in 2 AH in the Masjid Qiblatain in Madinah.

q: Who was the Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army during the 1965 war with India? (19)
f: General Muhammad Musa Khan was Commander-in-Chief from 1958 to 1966 and led the army in the 1965 war.
r: Yahya Khan succeeded him as Commander-in-Chief in 1966.

q: There are 24 students and 1/4 of them are male. What is the percentage of females? (19)
f: Males are 1/4 = 25%, so females are 100 - 25 = 75% (18 of 24).
r: 1/4 equals 25 percent.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Japan? (19)
f: Sanae Takaichi became Japan's first woman Prime Minister in October 2025 and was re-designated after the February 2026 election.
r: Japan has no president; its head of state is Emperor Naruhito, and Fumio Kishida was PM in 2022.

q: Where were the FIFA World Cup matches of 2022 played? (19)
f: The 2022 FIFA World Cup was hosted by Qatar from November to December 2022. Argentina won it.
r: It was the first FIFA World Cup held in an Arab and Muslim-majority country.

q: In which constitution was the bicameral (two-house) legislature introduced in Pakistan? (19)
f: The 1973 Constitution created a bicameral Parliament of the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: The Senate was first formed in 1973 and the 1956 and 1962 constitutions had one house.

q: In how many years was the revelation of the Holy Quran completed? (19)
f: The Quran was revealed gradually to the Prophet (PBUH) over about 23 years, from the first revelation in Hira until shortly before his death.
r: About 13 years of this period were in Makkah and about 10 years in Madinah.

q: Which letter comes next in the series: L, M, N, ? (19)
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, so O follows N.
r: L, M, N, O are the 12th to 15th letters of the alphabet.

q: Which is the hottest layer of the Earth? (19)
f: Temperature increases with depth, so the inner core is the hottest layer at around 5,000 to 6,000 degrees Celsius.
r: The inner core is solid due to the immense pressure even though it is so hot.

q: How many members does SAARC have? (19)
f: SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Afghanistan joined as the eighth member in 2007.
r: SAARC began in 1985 with seven founding members, and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

q: What is 80% of 90? (19)
r: 10% of 90 is 9, so 80% is 8 x 9.

q: What is the most important event of 10 Hijri? (19)
o: The Farewell Hajj and Last Sermon of the Prophet (PBUH)
f: In 10 AH the Prophet (PBUH) performed his only Hajj, the Hajjatul Wida, and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
r: The Conquest of Makkah took place in 8 AH.

q: In which language was the Holy Quran first translated in the subcontinent (India)? (19)
f: Shah Waliullah made the well-known first full translation into Persian in 1738, which is the usual textbook answer.
r: Sources differ, as an early Sindhi translation is also claimed; Shah Abdul Qadir later did the first Urdu translation.

q: Ahsan Ramzan, who became the youngest world champion in 2022, is a player of which sport? (19)
f: Ahsan Ramzan of Lahore won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in Doha in 2022 at the age of 16. He became the youngest ever winner.
r: He beat Iran's Amir Sarkosh in that final.

q: In which year was the 1962 constitution of Pakistan abrogated? (19)
f: General Yahya Khan took over after Ayub Khan resigned and abrogated the 1962 constitution in March 1969 by imposing martial law.
r: The 1962 constitution had been introduced by Ayub Khan.

q: What is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range? (19)
f: Tirich Mir, in Chitral, is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush at about 7708 metres.
r: K2 and Nanga Parbat belong to the Karakoram and Himalaya ranges respectively.

q: Which Sahabi is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran? (19)
f: Surah Al-Ahzab (verse 37) mentions Zaid bin Harithah (RA) by name.
r: The Quran mentions Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) by name four times.

q: Which is the tallest building in Pakistan? (19)
f: Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi is generally listed as Pakistan's tallest building, though its stated height varies by source (about 273 to 300 metres).
r: Habib Bank Plaza was long considered the tallest before the Icon Tower was built.

q: Tarbela Dam is located in which district and province of Pakistan? (19)
f: Tarbela Dam is built on the River Indus near Tarbela in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: Which person led the launch of the iPhone, which Apple introduced in 2007? (19)
f: Steve Jobs, co-founder and then CEO of Apple, unveiled the first iPhone in January 2007. Apple is the company that made it.
r: Steve Jobs died in 2011 and Tim Cook became Apple's CEO.

q: The Olympic Games take their name from Olympia and Mount Olympus. In which country did the Olympic Games originate? (19)
f: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece, and Mount Olympus is also in Greece. The modern Olympics are named after these ancient games.
r: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.

q: Who described Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah as the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity? (19)
f: Sarojini Naidu gave Jinnah this title, praising his work for unity at the time of the 1916 Lucknow Pact. Her 1918 book on him is titled Mohomed Ali Jinnah: An Ambassador of Unity.
r: Gopal Krishna Gokhale had earlier made a similar remark about Jinnah, so some sources trace the phrase to him.

q: Which city or territory of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate according to the 2023 census? (19)
f: The 2023 census showed Islamabad Capital Territory with the highest literacy rate, about 84 percent, ahead of all provinces.
r: The national literacy rate was about 60.7 percent for people aged 10 and above.

q: Which product is Pakistan's largest export by value? (19)
f: Textiles, including cotton cloth, yarn, bed linen and readymade garments, make up more than half of Pakistan's exports by value. Rice is the largest food export but is much smaller.
r: Pakistan is among the top cotton-producing countries in the world.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to zest? (19)
f: Zest means great energy and enjoyment, which is enthusiasm.
r: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car. If the car travels 60 km in 1 hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (19)
f: The car speed is 60 km per hour, so the train speed is 120 km per hour. In 30 minutes (half an hour) the train covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
r: In the same 30 minutes the car covers 30 km.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a nuclear (atomic) power? (19)
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai hills on 28 May 1998 and so became a declared nuclear power.
r: 28 May is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer in Pakistan.

q: What is 1/4 of 1/10 of 120? (19)
r: A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.

q: On which date did the full-scale 1965 war between Pakistan and India begin, according to Pakistani textbooks? (19)
f: India attacked Lahore across the international border on 6 September 1965, which started the full-scale war. A ceasefire came on 23 September 1965.
r: Operation Gibraltar had begun earlier, in early August 1965, which is why some candidates remember 5 August.

q: Approximately what percentage of Pakistan's area does Balochistan cover? (19)
f: Balochistan has about 347,000 square km, which Pakistani textbooks give as roughly 44% of the country.
r: Sources differ slightly, as some give about 40 percent depending on the total area used.

q: What is the length of the Indus River according to Pakistani textbooks? (18)
f: Pakistani textbooks give the length of the Indus as about 3,180 km.
r: Sources differ: some give about 2,880 km (Britannica) or 2,900 km.

q: In which battle did the Muslims dig a trench around Madinah? (18)
f: The Muslims dug a trench around Madinah in the Battle of Khandaq (Ahzab) in 5 AH on the advice of Salman Farsi. It stopped the Quraysh and their allies from attacking the city.
r: The Battle of Khandaq is also called the Battle of the Confederates (Ahzab).

q: In which province is Khanpur Dam located? (18)
f: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River near Khanpur in Haripur district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

q: In which city of India is Jallianwala Bagh located? (18)
f: Jallianwala Bagh is a public garden in Amritsar, Punjab, India. British troops under General Dyer fired on a crowd there on 13 April 1919.
r: The massacre took place on Baisakhi day in 1919.

q: On what date is Youm-e-Takbeer observed in Pakistan? (18)
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998, observed yearly as Youm-e-Takbeer.
r: Nawaz Sharif was Prime Minister at the time.

q: In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan? (18)
f: The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973 and the first general elections under it were held in March 1977.
r: Those elections were followed by allegations of rigging and the imposition of martial law on 5 July 1977.

q: In which Ghazwa did angels come to help the Muslims? (18)
f: The Quran says that angels helped the Muslims in the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
r: About 313 Muslims faced an army of roughly 1,000 Quraysh at Badr.

q: In which war was Major Aziz Bhatti martyred? (18)
f: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred on 12 September 1965 defending the BRB canal sector near Lahore.
r: He was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: Which pamphlet did Chaudhry Rehmat Ali write in 1933? (18)
f: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali wrote the pamphlet Now or Never; Are We to Live or Perish Forever in 1933.
r: In it he coined the name Pakistan.

q: What was the most important event of 8 AH in Islamic history? (18)
f: The Muslims conquered Makkah peacefully in Ramadan 8 AH (630 AD). The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah and cleansed the Kaaba of idols.
r: The Battle of Hunain and the siege of Taif followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in the same year.

q: In which city is the Mahabat Khan Mosque located? (18)
f: The Mahabat Khan Mosque is a Mughal-era mosque in the old walled city of Peshawar, built in the 17th century.
r: It was built by Mahabat Khan, a governor of Peshawar under Shah Jahan.

q: Which angel brought revelation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (18)
f: Hazrat Jibrael (Gabriel, AS) conveyed the revelation of the Quran to the Prophet (PBUH).
r: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.

q: Which country is regarded as the birthplace of modern football (soccer)? (18)
f: Modern football rules were codified in England in 1863 when the Football Association was formed.
r: Ancient ball games such as the Chinese cuju existed earlier, so sources differ on the earliest origin.

q: Which of the following countries is a member of SAARC? (18)
f: Bhutan is one of the eight SAARC members.
r: SAARC members are Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.

q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran? (18)
f: Abu Lahab is named in Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) which condemns him.
r: He was the only enemy of the Prophet named in the Quran.

q: Adolf Hitler was a politician of which country? (18)
f: Hitler led Germany as head of the Nazi Party and became Chancellor in 1933.
r: Hitler was born in Austria in 1889 but gained political power in Germany.

q: Dr. Ruth Pfau is remembered for her work against which disease? (18)
f: Dr. Ruth Pfau, a German doctor, spent her life in Pakistan treating leprosy patients and helped control the disease.
r: She died in Karachi in August 2017 and was given a state funeral.

q: What does the word Akhuwat mean? (18)
f: Akhuwat is an Arabic and Urdu word meaning brotherhood. It is the name of a Pakistani organisation that gives interest-free loans.
r: The Akhuwat concept is based on the brotherhood between the Muhajirin and the Ansar of Madinah.

q: What is the value of 0! (zero factorial)? (18)
f: By definition 0! = 1, because there is exactly one way to arrange no objects. This also keeps the formula n! = n x (n-1)! true for n = 1.
r: The number of ways to choose 0 items from n, nC0, equals 1 for this reason.

q: What is the value of tan(-x)? (18)
f: Tangent is an odd function, because sin(-x) = -sin x and cos(-x) = cos x, so tan(-x) = -tan x.
r: Cosine is an even function, so cos(-x) = cos x.

q: What is the capital of Bangladesh? (18)
f: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.
r: Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan in 1971.

q: What was the name of the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) who was married to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (18)
f: Hazrat Ayesha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) and a wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: What is the shaving of the head during Hajj called? (18)
f: Halq is shaving the whole head, and Qasr is trimming the hair. One of them is done to come out of the state of Ihram.
r: Women only trim a small portion of their hair (Taqsir).

q: Which cricket league is played in Pakistan? (18)
f: The Pakistan Super League (PSL) is the professional Twenty20 league of Pakistan. It started in 2016.
r: Lahore Qalandars won the PSL in 2022 and 2023.

q: Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in India in 1920? (18)
f: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920, supported by the Khilafat Movement.
r: It was called off in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

q: On which date did Muhammad Ali Bogra present the Bogra Formula? (18)
f: Muhammad Ali Bogra presented his constitutional formula on 7 October 1953.
r: The formula was never implemented because the Constituent Assembly was dissolved in 1954.

q: What is the name of the angel in charge of Hell (Jahannam)? (18)
f: The Quran (Surah Az-Zukhruf) mentions Malik as the keeper of Hell.
r: Ridwan is the angel who is the keeper of Paradise.

q: In which country are the headquarters of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) located? (18)
f: The ECO secretariat is in Tehran, the capital of Iran.
r: Pakistan, Iran and Turkey were the founding members of ECO.

q: What is the antonym of intimate (adjective)? (18)
f: Intimate means close and familiar, so the opposite is distant.
r: Close, familiar and dear are synonyms of intimate.

q: In which year was Pakistan's first postage stamp issued? (18)
f: Pakistan issued its first set of four postage stamps on 9 July 1948.
r: Before that, stamps of British India overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

q: In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located? (18)
f: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built by the Holy Prophet (SAW) in Madina after the Hijrat.
r: It also contains the blessed grave of the Prophet (SAW).

q: In which year did Dr Abdus Salam win the Nobel Prize in Physics? (18)
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for the electroweak theory.
r: He was the first Pakistani and first Muslim from Pakistan to win a Nobel Prize.

q: A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing? (18)
f: Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
r: A right turn from north would point to the east.

q: Which country has the largest number of active military personnel in the world? (18)
f: China's People's Liberation Army has about two million active personnel, the most in the world. India and the United States follow.
r: Rankings change slowly, and India has the second-largest active force in most recent lists.

q: Napoleon Bonaparte belonged to which country? (18)
f: Napoleon Bonaparte was a French general who became Emperor of the French. He was born on the island of Corsica, which was a French territory.
r: Napoleon was finally defeated at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

q: Who introduced the system of Basic Democracies in Pakistan? (18)
f: Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies through the Basic Democracies Order of 1959. Ordinary citizens elected Basic Democrats from local union councils, who then acted as the electoral college.
r: The system was ended by General Yahya Khan's government and replaced under the 1973 Constitution.

q: Vehicle is to road as ship is to ___ ? (18)
f: A vehicle travels on a road, and a ship travels on the sea. The analogy links a vehicle or vessel with the surface it moves on.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: Which country suffered the most deaths in World War II? (18)
f: The Soviet Union lost an estimated 24 to 27 million people, mostly on the Eastern Front against Germany.
r: China also lost a very large number of people in the war.

q: Who has taken the most wickets in Test cricket? (18)
f: Muttiah Muralitharan of Sri Lanka took 800 Test wickets, the highest ever.
r: Shane Warne is second with 708 and James Anderson third with 704; Wasim Akram took 414.

q: Who wrote the book Pakistan: A Hard Country? (18)
f: Pakistan: A Hard Country (2011) was written by the British author Anatol Lieven.
r: Ahmed Rashid wrote Taliban and Descent into Chaos.

q: If 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to type 1 page? (18)
f: 5 men type 5 pages in 5 minutes, so each man types 1 page in 5 minutes.
r: Work equals number of workers multiplied by time, divided by the number of pages.

q: Which was the first mosque built by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the first mosque of Islam in Madina? (17)
f: Masjid Quba was built by the Prophet (PBUH) on his arrival near Madina during the Hijrah.
r: Masjid-e-Nabawi was built soon afterwards in Madina.

q: Al Jazeera TV channel belongs to which country? (17)
f: Al Jazeera is an Arabic news channel founded in 1996 and funded by the Qatari state, based in Doha.
r: Some candidates thought it was Egyptian, but it is Qatari.

q: Who inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan? (17)
f: Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated the State Bank of Pakistan in Karachi on 1 July 1948.
r: The first governor of the State Bank was Zahid Hussain.

q: What is the second pillar of Islam? (17)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj. So Salah is the second.
r: Salah was made obligatory five times a day during the Night Journey (Miraj).

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army? (17)
f: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948.
r: Douglas Gracey succeeded him, and Ayub Khan was the first native Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951.

q: At what age (approximately) did the last revelation descend upon Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (17)
f: Revelation began when the Prophet (PBUH) was 40 and continued for about 23 years, so the last revelation came at about age 63.
r: Most scholars say the last verses were revealed a few weeks before his death at 63.

q: What is the largest city of Balochistan by population? (17)
f: Quetta is the provincial capital and the most populous city of Balochistan.
r: Quetta is known as the Fruit Garden of Pakistan.

q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical form of the Quran? (17)
f: When asked about the Prophet's character, Hazrat Ayesha replied that his character was the Quran.
r: This report is found in Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad.

q: If today is Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow? (17)
f: Tomorrow is Tuesday, so the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
r: The day after tomorrow is always two days ahead of today.

q: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded? (17)
f: The first Nobel Prizes were awarded in 1901 in the original five categories.
r: Alfred Nobel died in 1896 and left his fortune to create the prizes.

q: What is the National Finance Commission (NFC) used for? (17)
o: Distributing federal divisible revenue between the federation and the provinces
f: The NFC Award decides how the divisible pool of federal taxes is shared between the centre and the four provinces.
r: The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.

q: What is the largest city of Sindh by population? (17)
f: Karachi is the capital of Sindh and the largest city in Pakistan.
r: Hyderabad is the second largest city of Sindh.

q: What is the meaning of Islam? (17)
o: Submission to the will of Allah
f: Islam means submission and obedience to Allah, and the root also gives the sense of peace.
r: A person who submits to Allah is called a Muslim.

q: What is the national game of Canada? (17)
f: Canada officially declared lacrosse its national summer sport and ice hockey its national winter sport in 1994.
r: Ice hockey is also an official national sport, so questions may accept either depending on the options.

q: Who was the first to translate the Holy Quran into Urdu? (17)
f: Shah Abdul Qadir Dehlvi produced the first idiomatic Urdu translation, Mudih-ul-Quran, in the 1790s.
r: Sources differ: his brother Shah Rafiuddin made an earlier literal Urdu translation, but most Pakistani textbooks credit Shah Abdul Qadir.

q: What does wuzu (wudu) mean? (17)
f: Wuzu is the ritual ablution in which the face, arms, head and feet are washed or wiped before prayer. It is a condition for offering Salah.
r: Wuzu comes from an Arabic word connected with cleanliness and brightness.

q: What is the special unstitched cloth worn by pilgrims during Hajj called? (17)
f: Ihram is the two-piece unstitched white cloth worn by male pilgrims during Hajj and Umrah. Wearing it begins the state of ihram.
r: Women pilgrims wear ordinary modest clothing and do not wear a special unstitched sheet.

q: Which city hosted the 2018 Asian Games? (17)
f: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.
r: The 2022 Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China, in 2023 after a postponement.

q: At which place did Pakistan conduct its nuclear tests in May 1998? (17)
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills of Balochistan on 28 and 30 May 1998.
r: 28 May is observed in Pakistan as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Fitr celebrated? (17)
f: Eid ul Fitr is celebrated on 1 Shawwal after the month of fasting ends.
r: Eid ul Fitr was first celebrated in 2 AH.

q: Is the number pi a rational or an irrational number? (17)
f: Pi cannot be written as a fraction of two integers and its decimal expansion never ends or repeats. Hence it is irrational.
r: Fractions such as 22/7 are only approximations of pi (3.14159...).

q: Pakistan is located in which continent? (17)
f: Pakistan lies in South Asia, part of the continent of Asia.
r: Pakistan borders Afghanistan, China, India and Iran.

q: The Panama Canal connects the Pacific Ocean with which ocean? (17)
f: The canal cuts across Panama and joins the Pacific Ocean with the Atlantic Ocean through the Caribbean Sea.
r: The Panama Canal was opened in 1914 while the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

q: To whom was the Nishan-e-Haider last awarded? (17)
f: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed received the award for gallantry in the 1999 Kargil conflict; no later award is recorded.
r: Lalak Jan belonged to Yasin valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and is the 11th recipient.

q: Uhad (Uhud) is the name of what? (17)
f: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madina, near which the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.

q: What does the Arabic word Mantiq mean? (17)
f: Mantiq is the Arabic word for logic, the science of correct reasoning. It is taught in Dars-e-Nizami madrassas.
r: Muslim philosophers such as Al-Farabi and Ibn Sina wrote extensively on Mantiq.

q: Where is the Zhob River situated? (17)
f: The Zhob River rises in Balochistan and flows through the Zhob district, joining the Gomal River.
r: The Gomal River later flows into the Indus River system through Dera Ismail Khan.

q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record for the fastest century in One Day Internationals? (17)
f: Afridi scored a century off 37 balls in 1996. Corey Anderson of New Zealand reached a hundred in 36 balls against West Indies in January 2014 and broke it.
r: AB de Villiers later took the record with a 31-ball century against West Indies in 2015.

q: Which is the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan? (17)
f: Pashtuns form the largest ethnic group of Afghanistan, roughly 40 percent of the population.
r: Tajiks are the second largest ethnic group of Afghanistan.

q: Who is called the Hawari (special helper) of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (17)
f: On the day of Khandaq the Prophet (PBUH) said that every prophet has a Hawari and his Hawari is Zubair (RA), as recorded in Sahih Bukhari.
r: The word Hawari is also used in the Quran for the disciples of Prophet Isa (AS).

q: With the help of which country was the KANUPP-1 nuclear power plant at Karachi constructed? (17)
f: KANUPP-1 is a CANDU heavy water reactor supplied by Canada and started operating in 1972.
r: Pakistan's later plants at Chashma were built with Chinese help.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month? (17)
f: From the 2nd to the 24th is 22 days, and 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Monday gives Tuesday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: Which planet has the largest number of moons? (17)
f: Saturn has the most confirmed moons of any planet, about 293 as of 2026. Jupiter is second with about 115.
r: Saturn's count was 83 in 2022 and rose sharply after new discoveries, so older answers differ.

q: Which was the second major battle (ghazwa) fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah, after the Battle of Badr? (17)
f: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle of Islam and the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH was the second.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought near Mount Uhud, close to Madinah, in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: A quadratic equation is an equation of which degree? (17)
f: The highest power of the variable in a quadratic equation is 2, so it is a second degree equation.
r: The general form is ax squared plus bx plus c equals 0, where a is not 0.

q: In which year was SUPARCO, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, established? (17)
f: SUPARCO was formally established on 16 September 1961 by an executive order, with Dr Abdus Salam as its first chairman.
r: Some sources trace a precursor committee to 1961 as well; candidate answers such as 1955 and 1959 are incorrect.

q: The Suez Canal separates Africa from which continent? (17)
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt separates the African mainland from the Sinai Peninsula, which is part of Asia. It also joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
r: The canal was opened in 1869.

q: Which Sahabi narrated the largest number of Ahadith? (17)
f: Hazrat Abu Huraira (RA) narrated about 5,374 Ahadith, the highest number among the Companions.
r: He is known as Abu Huraira, meaning father of the kitten.

q: In which year was the Mangla Dam completed? (17)
f: Construction of Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River began in the early 1960s and it was completed in 1967. Sources differ slightly on the start year but agree on 1967.
r: Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed later, in 1974.

q: In which night was Namaz (the five daily prayers) made obligatory? (17)
o: Shab-e-Mi'raj (the night of Isra and Mi'raj)
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Isra and Mi'raj (placed by tradition around the 10th-12th year of Prophethood).
r: Sources differ on the exact year of Miraj; some say the 11th or 12th Nabawi year.

q: What is sec x multiplied by cos x equal to? (17)
f: Sec x = 1/cos x, so sec x . cos x = 1.
r: Cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x.

q: Which planet has the largest moon in the Solar System? (17)
f: Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the largest moon in the Solar System. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury.
r: Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is second in size.

q: What is the literal meaning of the Arabic word Rabb? (17)
f: Rabb means Lord, Sustainer and Nourisher, the One who brings up and provides for all creation. It is used in the Quran for Allah, as in Rabbul Alameen.
r: Rabbul Alameen, meaning Lord of all the worlds, appears in Surah Al-Fatiha.

q: What is the antonym of 'coercive'? (17)
f: Coercive means forcing someone to act by pressure or threat, so its opposite is voluntary, done by free choice.
r: The noun form is coercion, meaning the use of force or threats to make someone do something.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'Zamzam'? (17)
f: Zamzam is the name of the sacred well in Makkah, and the word is linked to plentiful, gushing water. The well sprang near the Kaaba for Hazrat Ismail (AS) and his mother Hazrat Hajra.
r: Pilgrims drink Zamzam water during Hajj and Umrah, and Sai is performed between Safa and Marwa near it.

q: Where is the National Museum of Pakistan located? (17)
f: The National Museum of Pakistan is in Karachi, in the Burnes Garden area.
r: The Lahore Museum is a separate and older museum.

q: Reykjavik is the capital of which country? (17)
f: Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland.
r: Reykjavik is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state in the world.

q: Which country won the 2018 FIFA World Cup? (17)
f: France beat Croatia 4-2 in the final in Moscow in July 2018.
r: Russia hosted the 2018 tournament, and Argentina won the next one in 2022.

q: Which is the highest peak of the Salt Range? (17)
f: Sakesar, in district Khushab, is the highest peak of the Salt Range at about 1522 m.
r: The Salt Range lies between the Jhelum and Indus rivers in Punjab.

q: Which Islamic Summit of the OIC was held in Pakistan (Lahore) in 1974? (17)
f: The Second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC was hosted in Lahore in February 1974. The first summit was held in Rabat in 1969.
r: The Lahore summit was attended by many Muslim heads of state and led to Bangladesh being recognised by Pakistan.

q: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad, the name of the Pakistan Army operation launched in 2017, mean? (17)
f: Radd-ul-Fasaad is Arabic and means rejecting or eliminating discord and mischief. The operation was launched in February 2017 to remove the remaining terrorism and strengthen border security.
r: Operation Zarb-e-Azb (2014) was the earlier major operation in North Waziristan.

q: On which date did Allama Muhammad Iqbal die? (17)
f: Allama Iqbal died in Lahore on 21 April 1938. He is buried near the Badshahi Mosque.
r: Iqbal's birth date is 9 November 1877 in Sialkot, which is observed as Iqbal Day.

q: In which year did Queen Elizabeth II first visit Pakistan? (17)
f: The Queen first visited Pakistan in February 1961 during a Commonwealth tour.
r: Her second visit was in 1997.

q: Who discovered penicillin? (17)
f: Alexander Fleming, a Scottish scientist, discovered penicillin in 1928 from the mould Penicillium.
r: Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Florey and Chain.

q: In which year did the Second World War start? (17)
f: The Second World War began on 1 September 1939 when Germany invaded Poland, and ended in 1945.
r: Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939.

q: In which game has Pakistan won Olympic gold medals? (17)
f: Pakistan won Olympic gold three times in hockey, in 1960, 1968 and 1984.
r: Pakistan also won a bronze in Tokyo 1964 in hockey.

q: Which ruler is known as the Tiger of Mysore (Sher-e-Mysore)? (17)
f: Tipu Sultan fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore wars and is called the Tiger of Mysore.
r: He was martyred in 1799 defending Seringapatam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

q: Into how many main physical regions is Pakistan commonly divided in Pakistan Studies textbooks? (17)
f: Textbooks usually list six regions: Northern Mountains, Western Mountains, Potohar Plateau, Balochistan Plateau, Indus Plains and Deserts.
r: Sources differ, and some books group these into five regions.

q: Who is regarded as the oldest (first) poet of the Pashto language? (17)
f: Amir Kror Suri, a ruler of Ghor in the 8th century, is regarded as the earliest known Pashto poet.
r: Rahman Baba and Khushal Khan Khattak are famous later Pashto poets.

q: Which is the largest dam of Pakistan? (17)
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is the largest earth filled dam in Pakistan and one of the largest in the world.
r: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum is the second largest.

q: Who is the author of the book Pakistaniat (What is Pakistaniat?)? (17)
f: Pakistaniat is the idea of Pakistani national identity, and Javed Jabbar wrote a book on it titled What is Pakistaniat. He lists many elements that shape the identity of the Pakistani nation.
r: Javed Jabbar is a Pakistani politician, writer and former senator who also wrote Pakistan: Unique Origins, Unique Destiny.

q: Butterfly is a technique (stroke) of which sport? (17)
f: Butterfly stroke is one of the four main competitive swimming strokes.
r: The other strokes are freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid ul Azha celebrated? (16)
f: Eid ul Azha is celebrated on 10 Dhul Hijjah, the twelfth month of the Islamic calendar, to remember the sacrifice of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
r: Eid ul Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal.

q: Abdul Sattar Edhi is associated with which city of Pakistan? (16)
f: Edhi made Karachi the base of his welfare work, and the Edhi Foundation is headquartered there.
r: Edhi was born in Bantva, Gujarat (India) in 1928 and died in 2016.

q: Which Sahabi was married to two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), earning the title Dhun-Nurayn? (16)
f: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) and, after her death, Hazrat Umm Kulthum (RA).
r: Dhun-Nurayn means 'possessor of two lights'.

q: What is the currency of Brazil? (16)
f: Brazil uses the real.
r: Brazil is the largest country in South America.

q: Which word is a synonym of curious? (16)
f: Curious means eager to know or learn, which is the meaning of inquisitive.
r: Its opposite is incurious or indifferent.

q: For what purpose is Namaz-e-Istisqa offered? (16)
f: Istisqa means asking for water. Muslims offer this special prayer when there is drought and ask Allah for rain.
r: The prayer for a solar or lunar eclipse is called Namaz-e-Kusuf or Khusuf.

q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar Farooq (R.A)? (16)
f: Hazrat Hafsa bint Umar (R.A) married the Prophet (PBUH) in 3 AH.
r: Hazrat Aisha was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A).

q: In which Islamic month was the Ghazwa (Battle) of Badr fought? (16)
f: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.
r: It is called Yaum ul Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.

q: What is 28 May, the day Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in 1998, known as? (16)
f: On 28 May 1998 Pakistan carried out nuclear tests at Chagai, and the day is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer. Takbeer means proclaiming the greatness of God.
r: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear power and the first Muslim nuclear state.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word voyage? (16)
f: A voyage is a long journey, especially by sea or in space. Journey is the closest meaning.
r: The word voyage comes from Old French voiage.

q: Which agreement was signed between Pakistan and India in January 1966 after the 1965 war? (16)
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri. It ended the 1965 war and restored the earlier positions.
r: The Soviet Prime Minister Alexei Kosygin mediated the talks.

q: Which batsman scored 400 not out in a Test innings? (16)
f: Brian Lara of the West Indies scored 400 not out against England at Antigua in 2004. It is the highest individual score in Test cricket.
r: Matthew Hayden's 380 was the previous record before Lara's 400.

q: Who was the opponent of Field Marshal Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election of Pakistan? (16)
f: Miss Fatima Jinnah, sister of the Quaid-e-Azam, contested as the joint candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties in January 1965. Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats electoral college.
r: She was known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: Who was the first muezzin (caller to prayer) of Islam? (16)
f: Hazrat Bilal bin Rabah (RA), an Abyssinian companion, gave the first adhan in Madina after the Prophet approved it. Hazrat Abdullah bin Zaid (RA) saw the words of the adhan in a dream.
r: Hazrat Bilal (RA) also gave the adhan from the roof of the Kaaba on the day Makkah was conquered.

q: Banu Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa were tribes of which religion? (16)
f: Banu Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayzah were the Jewish tribes living around Madinah in the Prophet's time.
r: All three were later expelled or punished for breaking their agreements with the Muslims.

q: From which country did Allama Iqbal obtain his PhD? (16)
f: Iqbal received his PhD from the University of Munich in Germany in 1908. He studied at Cambridge in England but his doctorate was from Munich.
r: His thesis was The Development of Metaphysics in Persia.

q: What does the Arabic word Ansar mean? (16)
f: Ansar means helpers. It refers to the people of Madina who sheltered and helped the Muslims migrating from Makkah.
r: The migrants from Makkah are called Muhajirin.

q: What does NFC stand for in Pakistan's finance system? (16)
f: NFC stands for National Finance Commission. It decides how federal tax revenue is shared between the federation and the provinces.
r: The 7th NFC Award of 2010 gave the provinces 57.5 percent of the divisible pool.

q: On which date is American Independence Day celebrated? (16)
f: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted on 4 July 1776, and that day is celebrated as Independence Day.
r: The Declaration was mainly drafted by Thomas Jefferson.

q: Which city was the capital of the ancient Gandhara civilization in Pakistani textbooks? (16)
f: Taxila (Takshashila) is the capital of Gandhara most often given in Pakistani textbooks.
r: Sources differ: Pushkalavati and later Peshawar (Purushapura) also served as Gandhara capitals.

q: What is the meaning of the name Israel? (16)
f: Israel is a Hebrew name, the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), meaning servant of God (Abdullah).
r: The descendants of Hazrat Yaqub (AS) are called Bani Israel.

q: Which is the highest capital city of the world? (16)
f: La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, stands at about 3,640 metres above sea level, higher than any other capital.
r: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia, and Quito is the highest official capital.

q: In the Islamic calendar, which is the year called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)? (16)
f: In the 10th year of Prophethood, both Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
r: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) travelled to Taif.

q: Who was the first caliph of Islam? (16)
f: After the Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH, the Muslims chose Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA) as their first caliph at Saqifa Bani Saida.
r: The four Rashidun caliphs ruled in the order Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman and Ali (RA).

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ali is 11 years old, what is his sister's age? (16)
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15 years, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 10 = 21 years.
r: After 6 years both of them are 6 years older: 15 + 6 = 21.

q: Who is the Chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) as of October 2026? (16)
f: Mohsin Naqvi was elected PCB chairman unopposed on 6 February 2024 for a three-year term.
r: Ramiz Raja was PCB chairman from 2021 to December 2022, which was the answer in 2022.

q: Who is the current Prime Minister of Malaysia (October 2026)? (16)
f: Anwar Ibrahim became the 10th Prime Minister of Malaysia in November 2022 and is still in office in 2026.
r: Ismail Sabri Yaakob was PM from 2021 to 2022, when candidates took the test.

q: Which companion (Sahabi) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was his adopted son? (16)
f: Hazrat Zaid bin Haritha (RA) was freed and adopted by the Prophet (PBUH) before prophethood, and was known as Zaid bin Muhammad until adoption was abolished.
r: Zaid is the only companion whose name is mentioned in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab).

q: Rough is to smooth as crude is to what? (16)
f: Rough and smooth are opposites, so the opposite of crude (unrefined) is polished (refined).
r: Crude oil is oil that has not yet been refined.

q: Who benefited from the Partition of Bengal in 1905? (16)
f: The partition created a Muslim-majority province of East Bengal and Assam with Dhaka as its capital, which helped Muslims in education and jobs.
r: Hindus opposed it strongly and it was annulled in 1911.

q: Who recited verses of the Quran in the court of King Najashi of Abyssinia? (16)
f: Hazrat Jafar (RA) led the Muslim migrants to Abyssinia and recited the opening verses of Surah Maryam before Najashi. The king was moved and refused to hand the Muslims over to Quraish.
r: Hazrat Jafar (RA) is also known as Jafar Tayyar and was martyred at the Battle of Mutah.

q: Who is the Pakistani Nobel Prize winner in Physics, and how many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize in Physics? (16)
f: Dr. Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics for work on the electroweak theory. He is the only Pakistani to win a Nobel in Physics.
r: Pakistan's other Nobel laureate is Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).

q: Who dismissed (abrogated) the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan? (16)
f: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
r: The 1962 Constitution had lasted about seven years.

q: What is the capital of China? (16)
f: Beijing is the capital of the People's Republic of China.
r: Shanghai is China's largest city, but not its capital.

q: Lat, Manat and Uzza were what? (16)
f: Lat, Manat and Uzza were the three chief idols worshipped by the pagan Arabs before Islam.
r: The Quran mentions them in Surah An-Najm.

q: Which is the latest confirmed fighter jet inducted by the Pakistan Air Force? (16)
f: The Chinese-made J-10C multirole fighter was inducted by the PAF in March 2022 and is the latest confirmed fighter type.
r: Reports about the Chinese J-35 stealth fighter for Pakistan remain unconfirmed.

q: Who issues an ordinance at the federal level in Pakistan? (16)
f: Under Article 89 of the 1973 Constitution, the President can promulgate an ordinance when the National Assembly is not in session.
r: Governors issue ordinances in the provinces when the provincial assembly is not in session.

q: Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) is located near which city? (16)
f: Jabal-e-Rehmat is a hill on the plain of Arafat, about 20 km southeast of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stand at Arafat on 9 Dhul Hijjah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) delivered his Farewell Sermon near this area in 10 AH.

q: The ancient region of Gandhara lay mainly between which two modern cities? (16)
f: Gandhara covered the Peshawar valley and the Potohar plateau around Taxila, roughly from Peshawar to Rawalpindi in north-west Pakistan.
r: Sources differ on exact limits, but Taxila and Peshawar are its best-known centres.

q: Geographically, into how many main regions is Pakistan divided according to most textbooks? (16)
f: Pakistan is usually divided into six regions: Northern Highlands, Western Highlands, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and Salt Range, Indus Plain, and Deserts.
r: Some books group them into three or five regions, so sources differ.

q: What is the value of sin 180 degrees? (16)
f: On the unit circle, 180 degrees is the point (-1, 0), and sine is the y-coordinate, which is 0.
r: Also cos 180 degrees = -1 and sin 90 degrees = 1.

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Navy? (16)
o: Vice Admiral H. M. S. Choudri
f: Vice Admiral James Wilfred Jefford of the Royal Navy became the first head of the Royal Pakistan Navy in 1947.
r: The first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Navy was Vice Admiral Muhammad Siddiq Choudri.

q: Which is the largest railway station of Pakistan, according to most sources? (16)
f: Lahore Junction is most commonly named as the largest railway station of Pakistan by area.
r: Sources differ on this point, and Karachi Cantonment and Rohri are also described as very large.

q: Who started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal? (16)
f: Haji Shariatullah started the Faraizi Movement in Bengal in the early 19th century to make Muslims follow the obligatory duties (faraiz) of Islam and give up un-Islamic customs.
r: After him, his son Dudu Miyan led the movement.

q: In which city was the first television station of Pakistan set up? (16)
f: Pakistan Television started its first broadcast from Lahore on 26 November 1964. It was a pilot station.
r: Karachi and Dhaka stations followed in 1966.

q: What is one-fourth of 10% of 120? (16)
r: One-fourth of 120 itself is 30.

q: Who was the first President of Azad Jammu and Kashmir? (16)
f: Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan became the first President of Azad Kashmir in October 1947 after the Poonch uprising.
r: He served four non-consecutive terms and is called Ghazi-e-Millat.

q: Is the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan based on a parliamentary or a presidential system? (16)
f: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary form of government with the Prime Minister as chief executive and the President as head of state.
r: The 1962 Constitution, by contrast, was presidential.

q: In which year did the East India Company annex the Punjab? (16)
f: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Punjab was annexed to the Company's territories in 1849.
r: Maharaja Ranjit Singh had ruled the Punjab until his death in 1839.

q: When was the partition of Bengal enforced by Lord Curzon? (16)
f: Lord Curzon divided Bengal into East Bengal and Assam and West Bengal, and the partition took effect on 16 October 1905.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Who received the Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil War of 1999? (16)
f: Captain Karnal Sher Khan Shaheed was awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for his bravery in Kargil.
r: Havaldar Lalak Jan Shaheed also received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.

q: What is the capital of Ghana? (16)
f: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana, on the Gulf of Guinea coast.
r: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.

q: To which country did Winston Churchill, the famous leader of World War II, belong? (16)
f: Winston Churchill was British and served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and again from 1951 to 1955.
r: Churchill won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, how many seats does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) have in the Senate of Pakistan? (16)
f: After the 2018 merger of FATA and the 2024 changes, KPK has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat and 1 non-Muslim.
r: Before the merger of FATA, KPK had 22 seats and the Senate had 104 members.

q: What was the name of the foster sister of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (16)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was nursed by Halima Sadia, whose daughter Shaima was his foster sister. She helped to care for him as a child.
r: Halima Sadia belonged to the tribe of Banu Saad.

q: Gwadar Port is linked through CPEC with which country? (16)
f: Gwadar Port is the centrepiece of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, which links it with China's Xinjiang region.
r: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958.

q: What is the meaning of the word vague? (16)
f: Vague describes something that is unclear or lacks precise detail. Its synonyms are unclear and indefinite.
r: The opposite of vague is clear or precise.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Shina (Sheena) language mainly spoken? (16)
f: Shina is the main language of the Gilgit area and nearby valleys of Gilgit-Baltistan. It belongs to the Dardic group of languages.
r: Shina is also spoken in parts of Indian-administered Kashmir and in Kohistan.

q: Which vegetable is regarded as the national vegetable of Pakistan? (16)
f: Okra, known locally as bhindi or lady finger, is commonly listed as Pakistan's national vegetable.
r: Lists of national symbols differ between sources because there is no well-known official notification.

q: Who built the Red Fort of Delhi? (16)
f: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Red Fort in Delhi, completed in 1648.
r: Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal and the Badshahi Mosque was built by Aurangzeb.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)? (15)
f: Pakistan became a member of NAM in 1979 at the Havana summit.
r: NAM was founded in 1961 at Belgrade.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque of Pakistan located? (15)
f: The Shah Jahan Mosque was built in Thatta, Sindh, in the 17th century.
r: It is famous for its blue tile work and for having no minarets.

q: Which country was the first foreign buyer of the JF-17 Thunder fighter jet? (15)
f: Myanmar was the first export customer of the JF-17, signing its deal around 2015 and receiving aircraft from 2018.
r: The JF-17 is jointly developed by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex and China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.

q: In which year did the Hijrat (migration) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) to Madina take place, marking the start of the Hijri calendar? (15)
f: The Prophet migrated from Makkah to Madina in 622 AD, which is 1 AH. The Hijri calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from this event.
r: The Hijri calendar is a lunar calendar and its first month is Muharram.

q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and whom? (15)
f: After the 1971 war, Bhutto and the Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi signed the agreement at Shimla on 2 July 1972.
r: The agreement turned the cease-fire line in Kashmir into the Line of Control.

q: What is the meaning of Jihad? (15)
f: Jihad comes from an Arabic root meaning to strive or struggle in the way of Allah.
r: Scholars divide it into the struggle against one's own desires and the struggle in defence of the faith.

q: Mohenjo-daro is located near which city of Sindh? (15)
f: Mohenjo-daro, a city of the Indus Valley Civilisation, lies in Larkana District on the right bank of the Indus.
r: Mohenjo-daro means Mound of the Dead and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: What is 1/3 of 120? (15)
r: One third of 120 is ten times larger than one third of one tenth of 120, which is 4.

q: In how many fields is the Nobel Prize awarded today? (15)
f: The Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics, which is six fields.
r: Originally there were five; the Economics prize was added in 1969.

q: The year 1995 was the golden jubilee (50th anniversary) of which international organisation? (15)
f: The United Nations was founded in 1945, so 1995 marked its 50 years.
r: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, now celebrated as United Nations Day.

q: What was the Lucknow Pact of 1916? (15)
o: An agreement between the Muslim League and Congress accepting separate electorates for Muslims
A treaty between Britain and Afghanistan
An agreement ending the War of Independence 1857
f: The Lucknow Pact was signed in December 1916 by the All India Muslim League and the Indian National Congress, and Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for his role in it.

q: Which province of Pakistan has the largest number of National Assembly seats? (15)
f: Punjab has 141 of the 266 general seats of the National Assembly, far more than any other province.
r: The National Assembly has 336 seats in total, including 60 for women and 10 for non-Muslims.

q: By whom was Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal appointed governor of Yemen? (15)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor and judge around 10 AH.
r: The Prophet praised him as the most knowledgeable of the Ummah in halal and haram.

q: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of which Prophet? (15)
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS), who was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).
r: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, and his son was Hazrat Yusuf (AS).

q: In which city is the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) situated? (15)
f: PIMS is a large public teaching hospital located in sector G-8 of Islamabad.
r: Federal Government Polyclinic and PIMS are the main federal hospitals of Islamabad.

q: In which Nabawi year did the Year of Grief (Aam ul Huzn) occur? (15)
f: In the 10th year of prophethood both Hazrat Abu Talib and Hazrat Khadijah (RA) passed away within a short time.
r: The year corresponds to about 619 CE.

q: In which part of Pakistan is Mirpur located? (15)
f: Mirpur is a city and district in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (the question is often worded as province, though AJK is not a province).
r: Mangla Dam is built near Mirpur on the Jhelum River.

q: Ping pong is another name for which game? (15)
f: Ping pong is the popular name for table tennis.
r: Table tennis has been an Olympic sport since 1988.

q: Which is the world's most populous country today? (15)
f: India overtook China in 2023 to become the most populous country, according to the United Nations.
r: Before 2023 China was the most populous country.

q: Which two oceans does the Panama Canal connect? (15)
f: The Panama Canal cuts across the Isthmus of Panama and joins the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean. This saves ships the long voyage around South America.
r: The Panama Canal was opened in 1914.

q: Who signed the Simla Agreement of 1972 on behalf of Pakistan? (15)
f: President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Simla Agreement with the Indian Prime Minister in July 1972.
r: The agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day is the 14th day of that month? (15)
f: From the 2nd to the 14th is 12 days, and 12 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Friday gives Wednesday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: What is the height of the Diamer Bhasha Dam? (15)
f: The Diamer Bhasha Dam on the Indus is 272 metres high, per WAPDA.
r: It is a roller-compacted concrete dam and one of the tallest of its kind in the world.

q: In the word MANAGEMENT, arranged alphabetically, which letter is second last? (15)
f: Alphabetical order is A A E E G M M N N T. The last letter is T and the second last is N.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each appearing twice.

q: What was the Rowlatt Act? (15)
o: A law allowing arrest and detention without trial
f: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 gave the British government power to imprison suspects without trial and to limit press freedom. Indians called it the Black Act.
r: Gandhi launched a nationwide protest against it.

q: In which year was the national anthem of Pakistan officially approved and adopted? (15)
f: The national anthem was officially approved by the government of Pakistan in August 1954.
r: Its tune was composed by Ahmed G. Chagla in 1949 and the words were written by Hafeez Jalandhari.

q: Which crop is grown on the largest area in Pakistan? (15)
f: Wheat is the staple food and covers the largest cropped area, about 9 million hectares.
r: Cotton is the major cash crop of Pakistan, but it is grown on a smaller area than wheat.

q: In which year was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born? (15)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817.
r: He founded the M.A.O. College at Aligarh, which later became Aligarh Muslim University.

q: What is the value of tan 90 degrees? (15)
f: tan 90 = sin 90 / cos 90 = 1 / 0, and division by zero is undefined.
r: tan 45 degrees equals 1 and tan 0 degrees equals 0.

q: Where did the Quraish tribe belong? (15)
f: The Quraish were the leading tribe of Makkah and custodians of the Kaaba.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) was born into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish.

q: How many players play in a game of chess? (15)
f: Chess is played between two players, one with white pieces and one with black.
r: Each player starts with 16 pieces on a board of 64 squares.

q: With what is Tayammum performed? (15)
f: Tayammum is done by striking the hands on clean earth or dust and wiping the face and arms.
r: It is allowed instead of wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable or harmful to use.

q: In which year was Urdu declared the national language of Pakistan, as commonly taught? (15)
f: Quaid-e-Azam declared Urdu the state language at Dhaka in March 1948, and this is the usual textbook answer.
r: The 1973 Constitution also names Urdu as the national language of Pakistan.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are present. What percentage of students is absent? (15)
f: Absent students are 500 minus 360, which is 140. Then 140 divided by 500 times 100 gives 28 percent.
r: Present students here are 72 percent.

q: On which date is Pakistan Day celebrated? (15)
f: Pakistan Day is celebrated on 23 March to mark the Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution of 1940.
r: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956 when its first constitution came into force.

q: What was the name of the father of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah? (15)
f: The father of Quaid-e-Azam was Jinnahbhai Poonja, a merchant in Karachi. His mother was Mithibai.
r: Quaid-e-Azam was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.

q: In which country does the world's largest volunteer ambulance service operate? (15)
f: The Edhi Foundation of Pakistan runs the largest volunteer ambulance network in the world, recognised by Guinness World Records.
r: The Edhi Foundation was founded by Abdul Sattar Edhi, known as the Angel of Mercy.

q: On what date was the Indian National Congress established? (15)
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay on 28 December 1885.
r: Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee.

q: Which is the largest fort of Pakistan? (15)
f: Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 26 km long and is often called the largest fort in the world.
r: It is also known as the Great Wall of Sindh.

q: Against whom was the Khilafat Movement in India directed? (15)
f: The movement, led by Muslims of India, opposed British treatment of the Ottoman Caliph after World War I.
r: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali were its main leaders.

q: How many metres are there in 2 km? (15)
r: One kilometre is about 0.62 miles.

q: Which prophet (AS) was given the ability by Allah to soften and melt iron? (15)
f: The Quran says Allah made iron soft for Hazrat Dawood (AS), so he could make armour from it. He is the prophet who received the Zabur.
r: Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was the son of Hazrat Dawood (AS).

q: What is the antonym of the word plentiful? (15)
f: Plentiful means more than enough, and its opposite is scarce, meaning in short supply.
r: Other antonyms of plentiful are rare, sparse and insufficient.

q: In which region of Pakistan is Attabad Lake located? (15)
f: Attabad Lake lies in the Hunza valley of Gilgit-Baltistan near Karimabad. It was formed by a landslide that blocked the Hunza River.
r: The landslide happened in January 2010 and the lake submerged part of the Karakoram Highway.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train is twice as fast. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (15)
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: Who is the current ODI captain of Pakistan (as of October 2026)? (15)
f: Shaheen Shah Afridi was appointed Pakistan's ODI captain and was still leading the side in 2026.
r: Babar Azam was ODI captain in 2022 to 2023 and Mohammad Rizwan led briefly after him.

q: Which Mughal emperor built the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore? (15)
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.
r: It was the largest mosque in the world for about 300 years and is among the largest in the world today.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared by a committee headed by whom? (15)
f: The All Parties Committee that drafted the 1928 Nehru Report was chaired by Motilal Nehru.
r: Jawaharlal Nehru, his son, served as secretary of the committee.

q: Which building is shown on the back of the Pakistani 100 rupee note? (15)
f: The reverse of the Rs 100 note shows the Quaid-e-Azam Residency in Ziarat, Balochistan.
r: The Rs 5000 note shows the Faisal Mosque on its back.

q: Pablo Picasso, the famous painter, belonged to which country? (15)
f: Pablo Picasso was born in Malaga, Spain, in 1881.
r: He spent most of his adult life in France and co-founded the Cubist art movement.

q: On which date did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die? (15)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh. He was born on 17 October 1817.
r: He is buried in the compound of the Jama Masjid at Aligarh Muslim University.

q: In which month did the 1965 Pakistan-India war take place and how long did it last? (14)
f: The war began on 6 September 1965 when India crossed the international border at Lahore, and ended with a ceasefire on 23 September 1965, a total of 17 days.
r: Pakistan celebrates 6 September every year as Defence Day.

q: What is the largest river of Afghanistan? (14)
f: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km, is the longest river wholly within Afghanistan.
r: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border and is not entirely within Afghanistan.

q: What does PEMRA stand for? (14)
o: Pakistan Education and Media Regulatory Authority
f: PEMRA is the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority, which regulates TV and radio broadcasting.
r: PEMRA was established in 2002.

q: What is the capital of Sindh? (14)
f: Karachi is the capital of Sindh province.
r: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.

q: Which is the deepest known part of the earth's oceans? (14)
o: Puerto Rico Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean
Java Trench in the Indian Ocean
Tonga Trench in the Atlantic Ocean
f: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific holds the deepest point, Challenger Deep. The candidate answer wrongly placed it in the Atlantic.
r: Challenger Deep is roughly 10,900 metres deep.

q: What is the meaning of Ayat? (14)
f: Ayat is the plural of ayah, which means a sign or a verse of the Quran.
r: The Quran has 114 surahs and 6,236 ayat according to the common count.

q: What is the meaning of Quran? (14)
f: Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite, so it means that which is recited.
r: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.

q: How many masarif (heads of expenditure) of zakat are mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah? (14)
f: Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) names eight categories of zakat recipients: the poor, the needy, zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, slaves, debtors, the cause of Allah and the wayfarer.
r: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th day of that month? (14)
f: From the 1st to the 12th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Monday gives Friday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: How many idols were placed in and around the Kaaba before the conquest of Makkah? (14)
f: Traditional sources say 360 idols stood around the Kaaba when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah in 8 AH. He had them removed and the Kaaba cleansed.
r: The idol Hubal was the chief idol of the Quraysh inside the Kaaba.

q: In the Quaid-e-Azam's 14 Points (1929), Sindh was to be separated from which province? (14)
f: The 14 Points demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency and made a separate province.
r: Sindh actually became a separate province in 1936.

q: In which year did Britain annex Sindh? (14)
f: Sir Charles Napier defeated the Talpur Mirs at the Battle of Miani in 1843 and Sindh was annexed.
r: Punjab was annexed later, in 1849.

q: Musailma Kazzab was killed in which battle? (14)
f: Musailma, the false claimant of prophethood, was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Yamama in 632-633 CE in the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
r: Many Huffaz of the Quran were martyred at Yamama, which led to the compilation of the Quran.

q: What is the literal meaning of Tayammum? (14)
o: To intend or aim at something
f: Tayammum literally means to intend or to aim at something. In Islamic law it means purifying oneself with clean earth when water is unavailable.
r: Tayammum is allowed in place of wudu or ghusl when water is not available or its use would be harmful.

q: In which year did the Cabinet Mission visit India? (14)
f: The British Cabinet Mission arrived in India in March 1946 and announced its plan in May 1946. It proposed a loose federation, which the Congress and the Muslim League accepted only briefly.
r: The Cabinet Mission consisted of Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.

q: Around which year did the Ottoman Sultanate begin under Osman I? (14)
f: Osman I founded the Ottoman state in Anatolia around 1299. It lasted until the sultanate was abolished in 1922.
r: The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453 under Sultan Muhammad II (Mehmed the Conqueror).

q: Which was the last Ghazwa in which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) personally took part? (14)
f: The Ghazwa of Tabuk in 9 AH was the last military expedition led personally by the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Tabuk is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the expedition of hardship.

q: Which planet comes closest to the Earth? (14)
f: Venus approaches Earth to about 38 million km, closer than any other planet.
r: Some recent calculations show Mercury is nearest on average over time, but textbooks give Venus.

q: Who served the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) for ten years in Madinah? (14)
f: Hazrat Anas bin Malik (R.A) was given to the Prophet (S.A.W) as a boy by his mother and served him for about ten years.
r: He narrated over 2000 Hadith.

q: Who was the first Pakistani woman to climb K2? (14)
f: Samina Baig reached the summit of K2 on 22 July 2022, a few hours before Naila Kiani. She was the first Pakistani woman to do so.
r: Samina Baig had earlier climbed Mount Everest in 2013 and completed the Seven Summits in 2014.

q: Who was the first woman officer of the Pakistan Army to be promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General (three-star)? (14)
f: Lt Gen Nigar Johar of the Army Medical Corps was promoted in June 2020 and became the first woman in the Pakistan Army to reach three-star rank. She was also appointed the first female Surgeon General of the Pakistan Army.
r: She is from Swabi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of New Zealand (as of October 2026)? (14)
f: Christopher Luxon of the National Party has been Prime Minister since November 2023 and is still in office in October 2026.
r: Jacinda Ardern (until January 2023) and Chris Hipkins (until November 2023) held the post earlier; the next election is on 7 November 2026.

q: What is the capital of South Korea? (14)
f: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea.
r: Pyongyang is the capital of North Korea.

q: What is the capital of the Netherlands? (14)
f: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government and parliament sit in The Hague.
r: The International Court of Justice is located in The Hague.

q: On which date was the Pakistan-China boundary agreement signed? (14)
f: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement on 2 March 1963 and settled the border of Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang.
r: The Karakoram Highway linking the two countries was later built and opened to traffic in 1978.

q: For how many years is the President of Pakistan elected? (14)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the President holds office for a term of five years.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies.

q: After which event did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA) accept Islam? (14)
f: Khalid bin Waleed (RA), who fought against Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam after the Treaty of Hudaibiya in 7 AH.
r: He is known as Saifullah, the Sword of Allah.

q: Which prophet (AS) was sent to Pharaoh (Firaun)? (14)
f: Allah sent Hazrat Musa (AS), together with his brother Hazrat Harun (AS), to invite Pharaoh to the truth and to free Bani Israel.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is called Kaleem-ullah (one who spoke to Allah).

q: Which prophet was blessed with a son in his old age? (14)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) was granted Hazrat Ismail (AS) and later Hazrat Ishaq (AS) in his old age.
r: Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was also given a son, Hazrat Yahya (AS), in old age.

q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km? (14)
f: Fuel per km is 50 divided by 320. For 400 km, 400 x 50 / 320 = 62.5 gallons.
r: This is a direct proportion question.

q: On which date of the Islamic month was the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born, according to the view most followed in Pakistan? (14)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born on Monday, 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant, which is about 570 AD in Makkah.
r: Some scholars and the Shia tradition give 17 Rabi-ul-Awwal, so sources differ on the exact day.

q: After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last? (14)
f: MANAGEMENT has the letters M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. In alphabetical order: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. Counting from the end: T (1st), N (2nd), N (3rd), so the third letter from the last is N.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters: A, E, M and N appear twice each.

q: After which event did Hazrat Abu Sufyan (RA) accept Islam? (14)
f: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the time of the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.
r: Before this he had led the Quraysh in several battles against the Muslims.

q: In which city is the International Islamic University (IIUI) located? (14)
f: The International Islamic University is in Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
r: It was established in 1980 and given its present status in 1985.

q: Who abrogated the 1962 Constitution, Pakistan's second constitution, in 1969? (14)
f: General Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan in March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
r: Iskander Mirza abrogated the first constitution (1956) in October 1958.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty belongs to whom? (14)
f: The Preamble and Objectives Resolution state that sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, exercised by the people as a sacred trust.
r: The authority is exercised through chosen representatives within limits set by Allah.

q: Which countries hold veto power in the UN Security Council? (14)
f: The five permanent members of the Security Council (P5) have veto power: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
r: A single veto from any permanent member blocks a substantive resolution.

q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the United States House of Representatives? (14)
f: Nancy Pelosi of California became the first woman Speaker of the US House in January 2007. She held the post again from 2019 to 2023.
r: Pelosi was succeeded as Speaker by Kevin McCarthy in 2023, and later by Mike Johnson.

q: In the x,y coordinate system, what is the y-coordinate also called? (14)
f: In a point (x, y), the x-value is called the abscissa and the y-value is called the ordinate.
r: The point where both coordinates are zero is called the origin.

q: In which year did Pakistan launch its first satellite, Badr-1? (14)
f: Pakistan's first satellite, Badr-1, was launched on 16 July 1990 from China by SUPARCO. It was a low-earth-orbit experimental satellite.
r: Pakistan later launched Badr-B in 2001 and PakSat-1R in 2011.

q: Which is generally regarded as the oldest sea port of Pakistan? (14)
f: Karachi Port is the oldest and busiest port of Pakistan; modern port development there began in the 19th century.
r: Port Qasim is the second major port and Gwadar is the newest deep-sea port.

q: The girls are 33 and the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many boys are there? (14)
f: Boys = girls + 7 = 33 + 7 = 40.
r: The total number of boys and girls here is 73.

q: On which date was the Simla (Shimla) Agreement between Pakistan and India signed? (14)
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed the Simla Agreement on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.
r: The 1966 Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 after the 1965 war.

q: On which date did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic under the 1956 Constitution? (14)
f: The first Constitution of Pakistan came into force on 23 March 1956 and the country became the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to obligation? (14)
f: An obligation is something you must do, which means a duty.
r: In law, an obligation is a legal or moral duty that binds a person.

q: In which years was the Second World War fought? (14)
f: The Second World War began in 1939 when Germany invaded Poland and ended in 1945 with the defeat of Germany and Japan.
r: It was fought between the Allied Powers and the Axis Powers (Germany, Italy and Japan).

q: Which of the following is a greenhouse gas? (14)
f: Methane traps heat in the atmosphere, while oxygen, nitrogen and argon do not.
r: Carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide are the main greenhouse gases.

q: In which year was the present Constitution of Pakistan made? (14)
f: The present Constitution was passed by the National Assembly in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.
r: It was drafted under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Which person won two Nobel Prizes in his life, one of them the Nobel Peace Prize? (14)
f: Linus Pauling won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1954 and the Nobel Peace Prize in 1962.
r: He is the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage of the students are girls? (14)
r: The percentage of boys here is 68%, and the two percentages add up to 100%.

q: Which city is known as the City of Light? (14)
f: Paris is called the City of Light because it was an early centre of education and ideas and one of the first cities with gas street lighting.
r: Paris is the capital of France and stands on the River Seine.

q: Who proposed the heliocentric (sun-centred) model of the solar system? (14)
f: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed in 1543 that the Sun is at the centre and the planets move around it. Ptolemy and Aristotle supported an Earth-centred model.
r: Galileo later supported the Copernican model using telescope observations.

q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam located (on the Indus, in Mianwali district)? (13)
f: Kalabagh is in Mianwali district of Punjab, on the Indus near the boundary with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: The dam has never been built because of political opposition from some provinces.

q: Which country awards the Nobel Prizes (apart from the Peace Prize)? (13)
f: The Nobel Prizes in physics, chemistry, medicine and literature are awarded in Sweden, in line with Alfred Nobel's will.
r: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

q: Who is the President of Turkey? (13)
f: Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been President of Turkey since 2014 and was re-elected in 2023.
r: The capital of Turkey is Ankara.

q: Harappa, a major city of the Indus Valley Civilization, was situated on the bank of which river? (13)
f: Harappa lies in Sahiwal district of Punjab beside the (now partly dried) bed of the River Ravi.
r: Mohenjo-daro, the other great Indus city, stood on the bank of the Indus in Sindh.

q: In which battle did Allah help the Muslims with angels? (13)
f: The Quran (Surah Al-Imran and Al-Anfal) says Allah sent angels to help the Muslims at Badr.
r: Badr was fought in 2 AH with about 313 Muslims against about 1000 Quraish.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day is the 15th day of that month? (13)
f: From the 2nd to the 15th is 13 days, and 13 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: On what date was CPEC formed? (13)
f: Candidates and many Pakistani sources give 22 May 2013, when Pakistan and China signed the agreement on the economic corridor during Chinese Premier Li Keqiang's visit.
r: Sources differ: the 46 billion dollar CPEC package was announced in April 2015 during President Xi Jinping's visit.

q: Which word is a synonym of possession? (13)
f: Possession means the state of having or owning something, so ownership is a synonym.
r: The word can also mean a thing that is owned, such as property.

q: What is the total number of rukus in the Holy Quran? (13)
f: The Quran is divided into 558 rukus (sections), a division mainly used in the Indian subcontinent.
r: The Quran is also divided into 30 paras.

q: Which surah is described in the Quran as Ahsan-ul-Qasas (the best of stories)? (13)
f: Surah Yusuf tells the story of Hazrat Yusuf (A.S) and Allah calls it the best of stories.
r: Surah Yusuf is the 12th surah of the Quran.

q: Which name is given to the Battle of Khandaq (the Trench) in the Quran? (13)
f: The Battle of Khandaq (5 AH) is also called Ahzab (the Confederates), after the allied tribes who besieged Madinah.
r: The trench was dug on the advice of Salman al-Farsi.

q: The Tashkent Declaration of January 1966 was signed after which war? (13)
f: The Tashkent Declaration ended the September 1965 war between Pakistan and India.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri under Soviet mediation.

q: Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro belong to which civilization? (13)
f: Both are major cities of the Bronze Age Indus Valley Civilization.
r: Mohenjo-Daro is in Sindh and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

q: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) belonged to which clan (branch) of the Quraish tribe of Arabs? (13)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraish tribe. His grandfather was Abdul Muttalib, son of Hashim.
