r: His father was Hazrat Abdullah and his mother was Hazrat Amina.

q: What is the Zakat nisab of silver in tolas? (13)
f: The nisab of silver is 52.5 tolas, which is about 612.36 grams.
r: The nisab of gold is 7.5 tolas (about 87.48 grams), and the rate of Zakat is 2.5 percent.

q: In which year did the first Muslim commander, Muhammad bin Qasim, invade India (Sindh)? (13)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 AD.
r: Some sources give 711 AD for his arrival; most Pakistani textbooks give 712 AD.

q: What is the national animal of Pakistan? (13)
f: The Markhor, a wild mountain goat with spiral horns, is the national animal of Pakistan.
r: The Chukar partridge is the national bird, the Deodar the national tree and Jasmine the national flower of Pakistan.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to INDIFFERENCE? (13)
f: Indifference is a lack of interest or concern, which is apathy.
r: Its opposite is concern or enthusiasm.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TYRANT? (13)
f: A tyrant is a ruler who uses power in a cruel and unjust way, which is a despot.
r: Its opposite in sense is a benevolent ruler.

q: In which country is Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located? (13)
f: Angel Falls (Salto Angel) is in Canaima National Park in Bolivar state, Venezuela.
r: It is about 979 metres high.

q: Which commission, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, drew the boundary line between Pakistan and India in 1947? (13)
f: The Boundary Commission chaired by Sir Cyril Radcliffe demarcated the Punjab and Bengal borders, and the line is called the Radcliffe Line. The Radcliffe Award was announced on 17 August 1947.
r: The Radcliffe Award was announced after independence, on 17 August 1947.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Interior of Pakistan? (13)
f: Mohsin Naqvi is the Federal Interior Minister in the current government.
r: He is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and president of the Asian Cricket Council.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 11? (13)
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 4 = 12 years, so she is 8 years older. When Ali is 11 she will be 11 + 8 = 19 years.
r: The age difference stays constant, here always 8 years.

q: What is the value of tan 0 degrees? (13)
f: tan 0 = sin 0 / cos 0 = 0 / 1 = 0.
r: tan 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 = 0.

q: What is the antonym of abhor? (13)
f: To abhor means to hate strongly, so its opposite is to love or admire.
r: Loathe and detest are synonyms of abhor.

q: Which bridge in Turkey connects Asia and Europe over the Bosphorus Strait? (13)
f: The Bosphorus Bridge in Istanbul spans the Bosphorus Strait and joins the European and Asian sides of the city.
r: It was renamed 15 July Martyrs Bridge in 2016, and Istanbul has other Bosphorus bridges too.

q: Which of the following countries lies in both Europe and Asia? (13)
f: Turkey is divided by the Bosphorus strait, with a small part in Europe and most of its land in Asia.
r: Istanbul is the major city that lies on both continents.

q: Malaysia has a king instead of a president. Who is the head of state (Yang di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia in 2026? (13)
f: Malaysia is a constitutional monarchy with no president. Sultan Ibrahim of Johor has been the 17th Agong since 31 January 2024.
r: His predecessor was Sultan Abdullah of Pahang, who was Agong from 2019 to 2024.

q: What is the approximate total length of railway track in Pakistan? (13)
f: Pakistan Railways reports about 11,881 track kilometres, counting all tracks including double-track sections.
r: The route length is shorter, about 7,791 km, which is why sources differ.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Israel? (13)
f: Benjamin Netanyahu has been Prime Minister of Israel since December 2022 and was still in office in October 2026.
r: Naftali Bennett (2021-2022) was PM when candidates wrote in 2022, and Israel's next general election is scheduled for 27 October 2026.

q: On which date is the International Day to Combat Islamophobia observed? (13)
f: The UN General Assembly proclaimed 15 March as International Day to Combat Islamophobia in 2022, on a resolution moved by Pakistan on behalf of the OIC.
r: 15 March was chosen as the anniversary of the 2019 Christchurch mosque attacks.

q: What is the antonym of sublime? (13)
f: Sublime means of very high excellence or beauty, so its opposite is ridiculous or lowly.
r: Magnificent, grand and noble are close in meaning to sublime.

q: Who started the Reshmi Rumal (Silk Letters) Movement? (13)
f: The Reshmi Rumal Tehreek was organised by Maulana Ubaidullah Sindhi together with Shaikh-ul-Hind Maulana Mahmud Hasan of Deoband. Secret messages were written on silk cloth to seek help against British rule.
r: The plot was discovered in 1916 and Maulana Mahmud Hasan was imprisoned in Malta.

q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 120? (13)
f: 1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.
r: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 120 divided by 12.

q: Which party formed the government in the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) at the time of independence in 1947? (13)
f: The ministry of Dr Khan Sahib, which belonged to the Indian National Congress (backed by the Khudai Khidmatgars), was in power in the province in August 1947.
r: The Governor dismissed the Khan Sahib ministry on 22 August 1947, and Abdul Qayyum Khan of the Muslim League then became Chief Minister.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960? (13)
f: Jawaharlal Nehru signed the treaty with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan at Karachi on 19 September 1960.
r: The World Bank mediated the treaty.

q: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed? (13)
f: The Rowlatt Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919. It allowed arrest and detention without trial.
r: The Act was named after Justice Sidney Rowlatt, and it led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in April 1919.

q: At what age of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the last revelation (wahi) revealed? (13)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received his first revelation at 40 and the last verses shortly before his death at the age of 63.
r: He passed away in 11 AH (632 CE).

q: How many Jewish tribes lived in Madina when the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrated there? (13)
f: The three main Jewish tribes of Madina were Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir and Banu Quraizah.
r: The Charter of Madina (Misaq-e-Madina) was made with them after the Hijrah.

q: In which country did the Black Lives Matter slogan and movement first start? (13)
f: The hashtag and movement began in the USA in 2013 after the acquittal of the man who shot Trayvon Martin.
r: It spread worldwide in 2020 after the death of George Floyd.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO)? (13)
f: The WTO has its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing GATT.

q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan conduct in total in May 1998? (13)
f: Pakistan conducted five tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I) and one more on 30 May 1998 (Chagai-II), a total of six. Some sources mention only the five of 28 May.
r: Pakistan became the seventh nuclear-weapon state and the first in the Muslim world.

q: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called by which name? (13)
f: Surah Al-Fatiha is also called Umm-ul-Kitab (Mother of the Book) and Umm-ul-Quran because it sums up the message of the Quran.
r: It is also called Sab'a Mathani and is recited in every rakat of Namaz.

q: Who is the current Governor of Sindh (as of October 2026)? (13)
f: Nehal Hashmi of the PML-N took oath as Governor of Sindh on 13 March 2026.
r: He replaced Kamran Khan Tessori of the MQM-P, who was governor in 2022.

q: Which is the largest religion in the world by number of followers? (13)
f: Christianity has about 2.4 billion followers, more than any other religion.
r: Islam is the second largest religion and is the fastest growing.

q: In which Hijri month and year did the Ghazwa of Tabuk take place? (13)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) marched towards Tabuk in Rajab of 9 AH, which is about October 630 CE.
r: It is also called Ghazwa Usrah, the Expedition of Hardship.

q: What does the white band in the flag of Pakistan represent? (13)
f: The white stripe of the flag stands for the religious minorities of Pakistan, while the green stands for the Muslim majority.
r: The crescent in the flag represents progress and the star represents light and knowledge.

q: What is the capital city of Saudi Arabia? (13)
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
r: Jeddah is the main port city on the Red Sea coast.

q: Which event made the USA enter World War 2? (13)
f: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941, and the USA declared war the next day.
r: The USA dropped atom bombs on Japan in August 1945.

q: Insulin is used for the treatment of which disease? (13)
f: Insulin is a hormone that controls blood sugar, so it is used to treat diabetes.
r: Insulin is produced by the beta cells of the pancreas.

q: In which Amendment to the 1973 Constitution were Ahmadis declared non-Muslim? (13)
f: The Second Amendment, passed in 1974, declared Ahmadis non-Muslim for the purposes of the Constitution.
r: It was passed during the government of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

f: Division first: 3/3 = 1. Then 3 + 1 = 4.
r: BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

q: Jabir bin Hayyan (Geber) is known as the father of which science? (13)
f: Jabir bin Hayyan, a Muslim scientist of the eighth century, developed early laboratory methods such as distillation and crystallisation, so he is called the father of chemistry.
r: Ibn al-Haytham is known as the father of optics and Al-Khwarizmi as the father of algebra.

q: What is the lowest point on the surface of the earth on land? (13)
f: The shore of the Dead Sea, between Israel, Jordan and the West Bank, is about 430 m below sea level, the lowest land point.
r: The Dead Sea is also one of the saltiest lakes in the world.

q: What is the length of the Canada-United States border? (12)
f: The border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles), the longest international land border in the world.
r: Note that 5,525 is the length in miles, not kilometres.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam become president of the All India Muslim League for the first time? (12)
f: Jinnah was elected president of the Muslim League at the Lucknow session in December 1916. This was the session at which the Lucknow Pact was agreed.
r: He later served as president again in the 1920s and 1930s and led the League until Pakistan was created.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)? (12)
f: Pakistan was a founding member of the OIC, which was formed in 1969.
r: The OIC was called the Organisation of the Islamic Conference until 2011.

q: Which is the highest plateau in the world? (12)
f: The Tibetan Plateau averages over 4,500 m above sea level and is called the Roof of the World.
r: The Pamir region is also known as the Roof of the World.

q: What is the integration of 1 with respect to x? (12)
f: The derivative of x is 1, so the integral of 1 dx is x + C.
r: The constant C is the constant of integration.

q: Which agreement was signed after the 1971 war between Pakistan and India? (12)
f: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.
r: The Tashkent Agreement was signed after the 1965 war.

q: What is a Ruku in the Holy Quran? (12)
o: A section of verses marked in the text
f: A ruku in the Quran is a group of verses forming a section, marked with the letter ain in the margin.
r: In prayer, ruku also means bowing, but in the Mushaf it means a section.

q: In which city is the Arfa Karim Tower located? (12)
f: The Arfa Karim Tower is in Lahore, Punjab, near Gulberg. It is named after the young computer prodigy Arfa Karim.
r: Arfa Karim was the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional.

q: Which title of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) means Mercy for all the Worlds? (12)
f: Rahmatul-lil-Alameen means Mercy for the Worlds and is a title of the Prophet (PBUH) taken from the Quran, Surah Al-Anbiya.
r: Khatam-un-Nabiyyin means Seal of the Prophets.

q: Which Surah is known as Ash-Shifa (the cure)? (12)
f: Surah Al-Fatiha is known by many names including Ash-Shifa because it is recited for healing.
r: It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and Sab'a al-Mathani.

q: In which Surah does Allah swear by time? (12)
f: Surah Al-Asr begins with an oath by time (Wal-Asr).
r: Surah Al-Asr is the 103rd surah and has three verses.

q: What is Sahih Muslim? (12)
f: Sahih Muslim is a collection of authentic Hadith compiled by Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj.
r: Together with Sahih Bukhari it forms the Sahihain.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will be her age when Ali is 11 years old? (12)
f: Sister's age now = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali gets 6 years older, so she will be 10 + 6 = 16 years.
r: The difference of 5 years between them never changes.

q: The Cholistan Desert is located near which city? (12)
f: Cholistan lies in southern Punjab and stretches from Bahawalpur towards the Indian border. It is also called Rohi.
r: Derawar Fort is a famous landmark in the Cholistan Desert.

q: How many ayats (verses) are there in Surah Al-Kausar? (12)
f: Surah Al-Kausar (Surah 108) has 3 ayats, which makes it the shortest surah of the Quran.
r: It begins with the words Inna a'taina kal-Kausar.

q: To which land did the Muslims make their first migration (Hijrat) to escape persecution by the Quraish? (12)
f: In the fifth year of the Prophethood a group of Muslims crossed the Red Sea to Abyssinia, whose Christian king Negus gave them protection.
r: Hazrat Usman and his wife Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA) were among the first migrants.

q: To which place did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD? (12)
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib). This migration is the Hijrat.
r: The Hijri calendar begins from this migration.

q: What is the capital of Peru? (12)
f: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru.
r: Bogota is the capital of Colombia, Quito of Ecuador and Santiago of Chile.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word abundant? (12)
f: Abundant means existing in large quantities. Plentiful is the closest synonym.
r: The opposite of abundant is scarce.

q: What is the date of America's Independence Day? (12)
f: The Declaration of Independence of the United States was adopted on 4 July 1776, which is celebrated as Independence Day.
r: Americans celebrate it every year on 4 July.

q: What is the derivative of the exponential function e to the power x with respect to x? (12)
o: x times e to the power (x minus 1)
f: The function e^x is its own derivative, so d/dx of e^x equals e^x.
r: The derivative of a to the power x is a^x times ln a.

q: For what is Hakeem Luqman best known? (12)
f: Luqman was a sage whose wisdom and advice to his son are praised in the Quran.
r: Surah Luqman (Surah 31) is named after him.

q: Where did the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) receive the first revelation? (12)
f: The first revelation (the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq) came in the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Noor near Makkah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) was about 40 years old at that time.

q: Which acid is found in milk? (12)
f: Sour milk contains lactic acid, formed when bacteria ferment lactose. Fresh milk is only slightly acidic.
r: Citric acid is found in lemons and oranges.

q: Which is the largest country of Asia by population? (12)
f: India overtook China in 2023 and is now the most populous country in both Asia and the world, with about 1.45 billion people.
r: Earlier, China was the most populous country, which was the answer in 2021-22.

q: Who led the Simla Deputation of 1906 that presented Muslim demands to the Viceroy Lord Minto? (12)
f: The Simla Deputation of 1 October 1906 was led by Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah, Agha Khan III. It asked for separate electorates for Muslims.
r: The All India Muslim League was founded a few months later in Dhaka in December 1906.

q: What is 90% of 9? (12)
r: 90% of a number is the number minus 10% of it, so 9 - 0.9 = 8.1.

q: Who is the President of Sri Lanka (as of October 2026)? (12)
f: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won the September 2024 presidential election and took office as President.
r: Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President until 2022 and Ranil Wickremesinghe until 2024.

q: On which date was the Lahore Declaration signed by the prime ministers of Pakistan and India? (12)
f: Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore.
r: Months later the Kargil conflict broke out in 1999.

q: Completely is to what, as a synonym? Choose the word closest in meaning to 'entirely'. (12)
f: Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.
r: Wholly and totally are also synonyms.

q: Where did the Holy Prophet (SAW) deliver the Last Sermon (Khutba Hujjat ul Wida)? (12)
f: The Last Sermon was delivered in the valley of Uranah at the plain of Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
r: It was delivered on 9 Dhul Hijjah.

q: Which of the following vitamins is NOT water soluble? (12)
f: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat soluble and do not dissolve in water. The B vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble.
r: Fat soluble vitamins can be stored in the body, while water soluble ones are mostly excreted.

q: In which city is Ayub National Park located? (12)
f: Ayub National Park is a large public park on Murree Road in Rawalpindi, named after President Ayub Khan.
r: It has a lake, a zoo-like area and recreation facilities for families.

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan in the absence of the President? (12)
f: Under Article 49 of the constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the office is vacant or the President is absent.
r: If the Chairman is unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts as President.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of ADVERSITY? (12)
f: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, so its opposite is prosperity, meaning good fortune and success.
r: The plural form adversities is used for repeated difficulties.

q: Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr? (12)
f: The Battle of Badr in 2 AH was fought between the Muslims and the Quraish of Makkah.
r: It was the first major battle of Islam.

q: What was the Bogra Formula? (12)
o: A constitutional proposal for a two-house legislature with parity between East and West Pakistan
A plan to make Urdu the only national language
f: It proposed a bicameral legislature, with equal representation of the provinces in the upper house and representation by population in the lower house.
r: It was named after Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra.

q: In which Nabawi year did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate from Makkah to Madina? (12)
f: The Hijrat took place in 622 CE, which was the 13th year of prophethood.
r: This Hijrat marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

q: Who originally built the Kaaba? (12)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS), with the help of his son Hazrat Ismail (AS), raised the walls of the Kaaba by Allah's command. This is the answer given in most Pakistani textbooks.
r: Some traditions say the Kaaba was first built by Hazrat Adam (AS) or the angels, so sources differ.

q: Under which treaty did Gulab Singh purchase Kashmir from the British? (12)
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (March 1846) the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh of Jammu for 7.5 million rupees.
r: This created the princely state of Jammu and Kashmir under Dogra rule.

q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan? (12)
f: The Governors-General were Quaid-e-Azam, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55) and then Iskander Mirza.
r: Iskander Mirza became the first President of Pakistan in 1956.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan? (12)
o: An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies
f: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four provincial assemblies.
r: Asif Ali Zardari was elected President for a second time in March 2024.

q: Why do people read newspapers? (12)
o: To get information and knowledge about current events
f: Newspapers report news and information about local and world events. People read them mainly to gain knowledge and stay informed.
r: The first printed newspapers appeared in Europe in the early 1600s.

q: In whose government were the non-party based elections held in Pakistan in 1985? (12)
f: General Zia-ul-Haq held non-party elections in February 1985. Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after them.
r: The 1985 assemblies passed the Eighth Amendment.

q: Mark Zuckerberg is the founder and head of which company? (12)
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the chairman and CEO of its parent company, Meta Platforms.
r: Facebook Inc. renamed itself Meta Platforms in October 2021; the company also owns Instagram and WhatsApp.

q: How many roots does a quadratic equation have? (12)
f: A quadratic equation has degree 2, and an equation of degree n has n roots. So it has 2 roots, which may be real or complex.
r: A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0.

q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside of its body (on the surface of the skin)? (12)
f: The tiny seed-like dots on a strawberry are actually separate fruits (achenes) on the outer surface, each containing a seed. The other fruits keep their seeds inside.
r: The fleshy red part of a strawberry is the swollen receptacle of the flower rather than a true fruit.

q: Where is Gwadar situated? (12)
o: On the Makran coast of Balochistan
On the coast of Sindh near Karachi
f: Gwadar is a port city on the Arabian Sea coast of the Makran region in Balochistan.
r: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.

q: In which Hijri year did Abu Sufyan accept Islam? (12)
f: Abu Sufyan embraced Islam on the occasion of the Conquest of Makkah, which took place in 8 AH.
r: Some candidates remember 6 AH, but the Conquest of Makkah was in 8 AH.

q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was martyred in the Battle of Uhud? (12)
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA), called Asadullah (Lion of Allah), was killed by Wahshi in the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
r: He is also known as Sayyid-ush-Shuhada, the chief of the martyrs.

q: What is the capital of Cuba? (12)
f: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.
r: Kingston is the capital of Jamaica.

q: Which caliph received the surrender of Jerusalem (Bait-ul-Muqaddas) in 637 AD? (12)
f: Jerusalem was besieged by Muslim armies under Abu Ubaidah and Amr bin al-As and its people surrendered to Caliph Umar (RA) in person.
r: Khalid bin Waleed (RA) conquered Damascus region, not Jerusalem.

q: What is a diagonal matrix? (12)
o: A square matrix whose off-diagonal elements are all zero
A matrix with all elements equal
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose determinant is always 1
f: A diagonal matrix is a square matrix in which every element outside the main diagonal is zero.
r: Scalar and identity matrices are special diagonal matrices.

q: For which product is Sialkot famous? (12)
f: Sialkot is world famous for sports goods, such as footballs, and also for surgical instruments and leather goods.
r: Footballs made in Sialkot have been used in FIFA World Cups.

q: In which year was Islamabad officially made the capital of Pakistan, replacing Rawalpindi as interim capital? (12)
f: Karachi was first capital, then Rawalpindi served as interim capital while Islamabad was built. Islamabad officially became the capital in 1967.
r: Sources differ on the exact year, since the decision was taken in 1959-60 and the shift happened in stages.

q: Which gas is mainly responsible for global warming? (12)
f: Carbon dioxide, released by burning fossil fuels, traps heat in the atmosphere as a greenhouse gas.
r: Methane is another important greenhouse gas.

q: Moroni is the capital of which country? (12)
f: Moroni is the capital of the Union of the Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
r: Comoros lies between Mozambique and Madagascar.

q: Whose slave was Hazrat Bilal (RA) before he accepted freedom through Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (12)
f: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the slave of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who tortured him for accepting Islam. Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.
r: Hazrat Bilal (RA) became the first muezzin of Islam.

q: On which date was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) established? (12)
f: The SCO was formally established in Shanghai on 15 June 2001 by China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
r: Pakistan and India became full SCO members in 2017.

q: What is the antonym of fertile? (12)
f: Fertile land or a fertile mind produces plenty; the opposite is barren, which produces nothing.
r: Sterile is also accepted as an antonym of fertile, so sources may give either word.

q: Which country was the world's largest arms importer in the latest SIPRI data (2021-25)? (12)
f: SIPRI's March 2026 data for 2021-25 ranks Ukraine first, with about 9.7 percent of global arms imports, followed by India. The USA is a major exporter, not the top importer.
r: In the 2015-19 and earlier periods India or Saudi Arabia led, and India was second after Ukraine in 2020-24 data as well.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Gwadar Port located? (12)
f: Gwadar is a coastal city on the Arabian Sea in southwestern Balochistan, and its deep-sea port is there.
r: Gwadar Port is a key part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

q: Which of the following are the three types of blood cells? (12)
o: Red cells, white cells and platelets
Red cells, white cells and haemoglobin
f: Blood contains red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Plasma is the liquid part, not a cell.
r: Red blood cells carry oxygen using haemoglobin.

q: What is the approximate area of Balochistan province? (12)
f: Balochistan covers about 347,190 square km, which is about 44 percent of Pakistan. It is the largest province by area.
r: Punjab covers about 205,344 square km and Sindh about 140,914 square km.

q: Which is the oldest English newspaper of Pakistan still in publication? (12)
f: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in 1941 in Delhi and is the oldest widely cited English daily of Pakistan.
r: Dawn moved to Karachi after the creation of Pakistan in 1947.

q: On which date was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated? (12)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was shot at a public meeting in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. The assassin Said Akbar was killed on the spot.
r: The place of the assassination, Company Bagh, was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

q: In which city was the second Islamic Summit Conference of the OIC held in 1974? (12)
f: The second OIC Islamic Summit took place in Lahore in February 1974 and was hosted by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
r: The first Islamic Summit was held in Rabat, Morocco, in 1969.

q: Who won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy) award for 2022? (12)
f: Babar Azam of Pakistan won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for 2022.
r: Shaheen Shah Afridi won it for 2021.

q: What is the full form of ISPR? (12)
f: ISPR stands for Inter Services Public Relations, the media wing of the Pakistan Armed Forces.
r: It is headed by a Director General, a serving army officer.

q: Which dam of Pakistan is made of earth and rock fill and is the largest earth-filled dam in the world? (12)
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus River is mostly built of earth and rock fill and is called the largest earth-filled dam.
r: Tarbela was completed in 1976.

q: Who was the Viceroy of India in 1911 when the partition of Bengal was annulled? (12)
f: Lord Hardinge was Viceroy from 1910 to 1916. The annulment of the 1905 partition was announced at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911.
r: The capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

q: On which date did the USA drop the atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan? (12)
f: The first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945.
r: A second bomb hit Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.

q: On which date did Israel declare its independence? (12)
f: David Ben-Gurion declared the State of Israel on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate ended.
r: Israel celebrates its Independence Day by the Hebrew calendar, so the Gregorian date changes each year.

q: What is the currency of Azerbaijan? (11)
f: Azerbaijan uses the Azerbaijani manat.
r: Turkmenistan also uses a currency called the manat.

q: The Dorah Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (11)
f: The Dorah Pass lies on the Chitral border and leads from Pakistan into Afghanistan (Badakhshan).
r: Chitral district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is the Pakistani side of the Dorah Pass.

q: What is the capital of Bulgaria? (11)
f: Sofia is the capital and largest city of Bulgaria.
r: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026.

q: What is the length of the Pakistan-India border (including the Line of Control and Working Boundary)? (11)
f: The combined length of the international boundary, Working Boundary and Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
r: The Radcliffe Line of 1947 defined the border between the two countries.

q: Which is the month of Allah (Shahrullah) in the Islamic calendar? (11)
f: Ramadan is commonly called the month of Allah in Pakistani textbooks, because fasting is observed in it.
r: Some sources also apply the title Shahrullah to Muharram or Rajab, so sources differ.

q: Abdul Qadir was a famous player of which sport? (11)
f: Abdul Qadir was a Pakistani leg-spin bowler famous for his googly and wrist-spin.
r: Abdul Qadir played 67 Tests for Pakistan and died in 2019.

q: The Khilafat Movement started after which event? (11)
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire in World War I, which threatened the Caliphate.
r: Its leaders included Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali.

q: In which district is Khanpur Dam located? (11)
f: Khanpur Dam is built on the Haro River near Khanpur town in Haripur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It supplies drinking water to Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and was completed in 1983.

q: Jihad is a word of which language? (11)
f: Jihad is an Arabic word meaning striving or struggle.
r: The Quran was revealed in Arabic.

q: What is the land between two rivers called? (11)
f: A doab is the strip of land between two converging rivers.
r: The Punjab has five doabs such as Rachna Doab and Bari Doab.

q: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days, is located in which place? (11)
f: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. The Quaid stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.
r: Ziarat is famous for its juniper forests, and the Residency was damaged by a terrorist attack in 2013 and later rebuilt.

q: Which organization was formed by Turkey, Pakistan and Iran in 1964? (11)
f: Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was formed in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey.
r: RCD was renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

q: Who headed the committee that compiled the Holy Quran in one book during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)? (11)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA), on the advice of Hazrat Umar (RA) after the Battle of Yamama, assigned Hazrat Zaid bin Sabit (RA), the Prophet's scribe of revelation, to collect the Quran. He had memorised the Quran and written much of it down in the Prophet's lifetime.
r: Hazrat Usman (RA) later had standard copies prepared from this compilation.

q: According to the Islamic calendar, in which month did Pakistan become independent? (11)
f: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947, which was 27 Ramazan 1366 AH, a Friday and the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) according to common belief.
r: Ramazan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

q: Which is the oldest university of Pakistan? (11)
f: The University of the Punjab, Lahore was founded in 1882 and is the oldest in Pakistan.
r: The University of Karachi was founded in 1951.

q: Which is the smallest planet of the solar system? (11)
f: Mercury has a diameter of about 4,880 km, the smallest of the eight planets.
r: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.

q: Which country helped Pakistan build the Chashma nuclear power plant? (11)
f: The Chashma Nuclear Power Plants in Punjab were built with Chinese assistance.
r: China also built later units such as C-3 and C-4 at Chashma.

q: Which of the following Sahabah was NOT among the Ashra Mubashira (the ten companions given the glad tidings of Paradise)? (11)
f: Talha, Zubair and Abdur Rahman bin Auf are all in the list of ten promised Paradise in one hadith. Abu Hurairah, a great narrator of hadith, is not in that list.
r: The ten are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, Zubair, Abdur Rahman bin Auf, Saad bin Abi Waqqas, Saeed bin Zaid and Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (RA).

q: Hajj is which pillar of Islam? (11)
f: The five pillars are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj, so Hajj is the fifth.
r: Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime for those who can afford it.

q: How many Senate seats are allocated to each province of Pakistan? (11)
f: Each province has 23 Senate seats: 14 general, 4 for women, 4 for technocrats and 1 for non-Muslims.
r: The Senate is a permanent house; half of its members retire every three years.

q: In which province is Narowal district located? (11)
f: Narowal is a district in northeastern Punjab near the Indian border.
r: Narowal was made a separate district in 1991.

q: K2 lies on the border between Pakistan and which country? (11)
f: K2 stands in the Karakoram range on the border of Gilgit-Baltistan (Pakistan) and Xinjiang (China).
r: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world at about 8,611 m.

q: Stainless steel is an example of what? (11)
f: Stainless steel is an alloy of iron with chromium and often nickel.
r: Chromium of at least about 10.5 percent makes it resist rust.

q: To where did the Muslims first migrate? (11)
f: In 615 CE (5th year of the Prophethood) a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia to escape persecution in Makkah.
r: The king of Abyssinia, Negus (Najashi), gave them protection.

q: Which is the 3rd surah of the Holy Quran? (11)
f: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Ali Imran, so the third is Ali Imran.
r: Surah Ali Imran has 200 verses and is a Madani surah.

q: In Islam, which is the biggest sin? (11)
f: The Quran and Hadith describe shirk as the greatest sin, and Allah does not forgive it unless a person repents.
r: The Quran (Surah An-Nisa 4:48) says that Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives lesser sins.

q: What is the meaning of Ruku in prayer? (11)
f: Ruku means to bow, and in salah it is the posture of bowing with hands on the knees.
r: Sajdah, the prostration, is the posture that follows ruku.

q: What is the meaning of the word Tanzeel? (11)
f: Tanzeel comes from an Arabic root meaning to send down, and it is used for the revelation of the Quran.
r: The Quran says it is a Tanzeel from the Lord of the worlds.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of an identity matrix? (11)
f: Since I times I equals I, the inverse of an identity matrix is the identity matrix itself.
r: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.

q: In which year did the Second World War end? (11)
f: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan surrendered in August and September 1945. The war therefore ended in 1945.
r: The United Nations was founded in the same year, 1945.

q: Which is the deepest ocean in the world? (11)
f: The Pacific Ocean has the greatest average depth and contains the Mariana Trench, the deepest known point.
r: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is about 11,000 metres deep.

q: Which two surahs of the Holy Quran are together called Muawwazatain? (11)
f: Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah Al-Nas (114) both begin with a request to seek refuge (ta'awwuz) with Allah. That is why the pair is called Muawwazatain.
r: These are the last two surahs of the Quran and are commonly recited for protection.

q: Who is the writer of the book Becoming? (11)
f: Becoming (2018) is the memoir of Michelle Obama, former First Lady of the United States.
r: It became one of the best-selling memoirs of all time.

q: With which Indian prime minister did Pakistan sign the Lahore Declaration in 1999? (11)
f: The Lahore Declaration of February 1999 was signed by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
r: Soon after, the Kargil conflict of 1999 damaged the peace process.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, 75, ? (11)
f: Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.
r: The small numbers 55, 65, 75 increase by 10.

q: Amsterdam is the capital of which country? (11)
f: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital of the Netherlands. The government sits in The Hague.
r: Brussels is the capital of Belgium.

q: Lima is the capital of which country? (11)
f: Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru. It lies on the Pacific coast.
r: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

q: Who is the President of Ukraine? (11)
f: Volodymyr Zelensky has been President of Ukraine since May 2019 and still holds the office in 2026.
r: Petro Poroshenko was his predecessor, from 2014 to 2019.

q: One degree of an angle is equal to how many minutes? (11)
f: A degree is divided into 60 minutes, and a minute into 60 seconds.
r: A full circle measures 360 degrees.

q: The Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) project, Zu Peshawar, was built by which government? (11)
f: The Peshawar BRT was started in 2017 by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government under Chief Minister Pervez Khattak. It runs in Peshawar, the provincial capital.
r: The Peshawar BRT was formally inaugurated on 13 August 2020 and has a corridor of about 27.5 km.

q: Which prophet was sent to the nation (Qaum) of Aad? (11)
f: Allah sent Hazrat Hud (AS) to guide the people of Aad, who lived in Al-Ahqaf in southern Arabia.
r: Hazrat Salih (AS) was sent to the nation of Thamud.

q: SUPARCO is the national organization of Pakistan for which field? (11)
f: SUPARCO stands for Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, Pakistan's national space agency.
r: It was founded in 1961.

q: How many doors (gates) does Jannah (Paradise) have according to hadith? (11)
f: Authentic hadith state that Paradise has eight gates, one of them being Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
r: Hell has seven gates.

q: Syed-ul-Ansar was the title of which Sahabi? (11)
f: Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA), chief of the Aws tribe of Madina, was given the title Syed-ul-Ansar.
r: Sources may differ on the title holder, but most Pakistani textbooks give Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

q: What are sets that have no common element called? (11)
f: Sets with no element in common have an empty intersection, and such sets are called disjoint sets.
r: Sets that have the same number of elements are called equivalent sets.

q: What is Hajr-e-Aswad? (11)
o: The Black Stone fixed in the Kaaba
A gate of the Prophet's Mosque
f: Hajr-e-Aswad is the Black Stone set in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.
r: Pilgrims try to kiss or point to it at the start of each Tawaf.

q: What is the process by which a liquid changes into vapour (gas) called? (11)
f: When a liquid gains heat and its molecules escape into the air as vapour, the change is called evaporation or vaporization.
r: The reverse process, vapour changing into liquid, is called condensation.

q: In which Hijri year was Aam-ul-Wafood (Year of Delegations)? (11)
f: Delegations from many Arab tribes came to Madina to accept Islam in 9 AH, after the conquest of Makkah. This year is called Aam-ul-Wafood.
r: The year 9 AH is also when the Battle of Tabuk took place.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away? (11)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away in 11 AH (632 AD) at the age of 63 years.
r: He passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal in Madina.

q: What was the Simon Commission? (11)
o: A British commission sent to India in 1927 to review the Government of India Act 1919, with no Indian member
A commission for partition of Bengal
A Muslim League committee for Pakistan
A commission for dividing Punjab in 1947
f: The Simon Commission, led by Sir John Simon, arrived in India in 1928 to study constitutional reform. It had only British members, so Indian parties boycotted it.
r: It was announced in November 1927 and its slogan of protest was Simon Go Back.

q: 6 is what percent of 20? (11)
f: Percentage = 6/20 x 100 = 30%.
r: Similarly, 30% of 20 is 6.

q: Which reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims in British India? (11)
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909, known as the Minto-Morley Reforms, granted separate electorates to Muslims.
r: The Simla Deputation of 1906 had demanded separate electorates from Lord Minto.

q: Convert 60 degrees into radians. (11)
f: Radians = degrees x pi/180 = 60 x pi/180 = pi/3.
r: 180 degrees equals pi radians.

q: What is the meaning of 'emancipation'? (11)
f: Emancipation means being set free from legal, social or political restrictions, such as slavery.
r: Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863.

q: When did Pakistan issue its first postage stamps? (11)
f: Pakistan's first set of postage stamps was issued on 9 July 1948.
r: Before that, British Indian stamps overprinted with the word Pakistan were used in 1947.

q: What is the capital of Tajikistan? (11)
f: Dushanbe is the capital and largest city of Tajikistan.
r: Tajikistan borders Afghanistan, China, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

q: How many atmospheric layers does the Moon have? (11)
o: None, it has practically no atmosphere
f: The Moon is too small and its gravity too weak to hold an atmosphere. It has only an extremely thin exosphere that is almost a vacuum.
r: Because there is no air, sound cannot travel on the Moon and the sky looks black even in daytime.

q: In which surah of the Holy Quran are the faraiz (obligatory acts) of wudu mentioned? (11)
f: The faraiz of wudu are described in verse 6 of Surah Al-Maidah, which orders washing the face and arms, wiping the head and washing the feet.
r: The same verse also gives the command for tayammum when water is not available; Surah An-Nisa (4:43) also mentions tayammum.

q: During which months of 1999 was the Kargil conflict between Pakistan and India fought? (11)
f: The Kargil conflict began in early May 1999 and ended in late July 1999, after a ceasefire request following talks in Washington.
r: Kargil lies in the Ladakh region along the Line of Control.

q: What does CPEC stand for? (11)
f: CPEC stands for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, a package of infrastructure and energy projects linking Gwadar port with western China.
r: CPEC was formally launched in 2015 and its flagship port is Gwadar in Balochistan.

q: Which is the busiest sea (ocean) trade route of the world according to standard textbooks? (11)
f: The North Atlantic sea route links eastern North America with north-western Europe and carries the heaviest volume of ocean trade in most textbooks.
r: Modern shipping statistics sometimes rank Asian routes through the Strait of Malacca very high, so sources can differ.

q: Who first suggested the name Pakistan? (11)
f: Chaudhry Rehmat Ali, a Cambridge student, proposed the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
r: The name is made from the letters of Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan.

q: Which Muslim League leader responded to the Nehru Report (1928) with his famous Fourteen Points in 1929? (11)
f: The Nehru Report rejected separate electorates and Muslim demands, so Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929 as the Muslim reply.
r: Jinnah had earlier put forward his Delhi Muslim Proposals in 1927.

q: In which of Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points was the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency demanded? (11)
f: Point 9 of the Quaid's Fourteen Points (1929) demanded that Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency.
r: Sindh was finally separated from Bombay and made a separate province in 1936.

q: Who is traditionally credited with the creation of the Urdu language? (11)
f: Amir Khusro (1253-1325) is traditionally credited with using and promoting the early form of Urdu, then called Hindavi, in his poetry.
r: Sources differ: Urdu really developed over centuries from the mixing of Persian, Arabic and local languages in the army bazaars and courts.

q: What was the relationship between Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)? (11)
f: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah (AS). He was the younger brother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).
r: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: Who invented the printing press with movable type in Europe? (11)
f: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany invented the movable-type printing press around 1440.
r: His first major printed work was the Gutenberg Bible.

q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: He will not approve ___ your plan. (11)
f: The verb approve takes the preposition of when it means to think well of something.
r: Disapprove is also followed by of.

q: In which years was the First World War fought? (11)
f: The First World War began in July 1914 and ended with the armistice of November 1918.
r: The Treaty of Versailles with Germany was signed in 1919.

q: Who is the current President of Bangladesh (as of October 2026)? (11)
f: Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned in July 2026. Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected by Parliament on 20 August 2026 and sworn in as the 23rd President.
r: Earlier answers such as Mohammed Shahabuddin (from 2023) are now outdated; Tarique Rahman is the Prime Minister.

q: How many straight lines can pass through a single given point? (11)
f: Through one point we can draw a line in every possible direction, so there are infinitely many lines.
r: Exactly one straight line passes through two different points.

q: Where is the Thal desert located in Pakistan? (11)
o: Between the Indus and Jhelum rivers in Punjab
In the Chagai district of Balochistan
In the Cholistan region near Bahawalpur
f: The Thal desert lies in the Punjab province in the area between the Indus and Jhelum rivers, covering districts such as Bhakkar, Layyah, Khushab and Mianwali.
r: The Thar desert is a different desert and lies in Sindh.

q: Which organ of the human body pumps blood throughout the body? (11)
f: The heart is a muscular organ that contracts regularly and pushes blood through the blood vessels.
r: A normal adult heart beats about 72 times per minute at rest.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1300 are present. How many students are absent? (11)
f: Absent students = 1500 - 1300 = 200.
r: The percentage absent is 200/1500 x 100 = 13.33 percent.

q: Humayun was defeated by which ruler, forcing him to leave India in 1540? (11)
f: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at Chausa in 1539 and at Kannauj in 1540. Humayun then fled India.
r: Humayun regained his throne in 1555 after defeating the Suri ruler Sikandar Suri.

q: Germany invaded which country first in World War II in September 1939? (11)
f: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France then declared war on Germany.
r: The Soviet Union also invaded Poland from the east on 17 September 1939.

q: What type of fraction is 9/2? (11)
f: In 9/2 the numerator 9 is greater than the denominator 2, so it is an improper fraction. It equals the mixed number 4 and 1/2.
r: A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator, for example 2/9.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress? (11)
f: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906, when he attended its Calcutta session.
r: He joined the All India Muslim League later, in 1913.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a member of the International Labour Organization (ILO)? (11)
f: Pakistan has been an ILO member since 1947, the year of its independence.
r: The ILO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: Between which latitudes does Pakistan lie? (11)
f: Pakistan extends from about 24 degrees north in the south to about 37 degrees north in the north.
r: Pakistan's north-south extent is roughly 1,600 km.

q: Who is called the Traveller of Islam? (11)
f: Ibn Battuta, the Moroccan explorer, travelled about 120,000 km across Africa, Asia and Europe in nearly 30 years.
r: He wrote the famous travel book called the Rihla.

q: What is the date of Bangladesh's declaration of independence? (11)
f: Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971 and celebrates it as Independence Day. The war ended on 16 December 1971.
r: 16 December is celebrated in Bangladesh as Victory Day.

q: In a bus of 30 passengers, 2/3 are male. How many are female? (11)
f: Males = 2/3 of 30 = 20. Females = 30 - 20 = 10.
r: Females are 1/3 of the total, which is about 33.33 percent.

q: A book is bought for 30 and sold for 40. What is the percentage profit? (11)
f: Profit = 40 - 30 = 10. Profit percent = 10 / 30 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
r: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price unless stated otherwise.

q: Which city is the most populous in the world according to the UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025? (11)
f: The UN 2025 report ranks Jakarta first with about 42 million people, ahead of Dhaka and Tokyo.
r: Tokyo was named the largest city in earlier UN reports and has now dropped to third.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of the world by surface area? (10)
f: Lake Superior in North America has a surface area of about 82,000 square kilometres, the largest among freshwater lakes.
r: Lake Baikal is the deepest freshwater lake and holds the most fresh water by volume.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)? (10)
f: The SCO has ten full members: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus. Turkey is only a dialogue partner.
r: Iran joined in 2023 and Belarus in 2024; Afghanistan and Mongolia are observers.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC T20 World Cup? (10)
f: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the final at Lord's in 2009 under captain Younis Khan. It is their only T20 World Cup title.
r: Pakistan were runners-up in 2007 and 2022; India won the 2024 and 2026 editions.

q: The first five ayats revealed to the Prophet (PBUH) were from which surah? (10)
f: The first five ayats revealed in the cave of Hira belong to Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.
r: Surah Al-Muddaththir is commonly considered to follow after a pause in revelation.

q: What does the word ayat mean? (10)
f: Ayat is the plural of ayah, meaning a sign, and it is used for the verses of the Quran.
r: A chapter of the Quran is called a surah.

q: What does zakat mean literally? (10)
f: Zakat literally means purification and growth, as giving it purifies wealth and the soul.
r: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and is usually 2.5 percent on savings above nisab.

q: What is a scalar matrix? (10)
o: A diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal
A matrix with all elements zero
A matrix with one row only
A matrix whose rows and columns are interchanged
f: A scalar matrix is a square diagonal matrix in which all the main diagonal elements are the same and all other elements are zero.
r: A scalar matrix with diagonal elements equal to 1 is the identity matrix.

q: What is the meaning of Zakat? (10)
f: Zakat means purification and growth, as paying it purifies a person's wealth.
r: Zakat is paid at 2.5 percent of savings held above the nisab for a year.

q: Where is the shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam? (10)
f: The shrine of Hazrat Shah Rukn-e-Alam is in Multan.
r: It is famed for its Tughlaq-era architecture.

q: Who won the world amateur snooker championship in 1994 for Pakistan? (10)
f: Muhammad Yousaf won the IBSF World Amateur Snooker Championship in 1994.
r: Muhammad Asif later won the same title in 2012.

q: Ali walks 4 meters towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now? (10)
f: A left turn from north points him to the west.
r: Anticlockwise order of directions is North, West, South, East.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Saturday, what day is the 26th? (10)
f: The gap is 24 days. 24 mod 7 = 3, so Saturday plus 3 days is Tuesday.
r: Count only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 12th? (10)
f: The gap is 8 days. 8 mod 7 = 1, so Monday plus 1 day is Tuesday.
r: Dates exactly 8 days apart differ by one weekday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 23rd? (10)
f: The gap is 19 days. 19 mod 7 = 5, so Tuesday plus 5 days is Sunday.
r: Check: the 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th are Tuesdays, so the 23rd is two days before the 25th, a Sunday.

q: Who is the Pakistani who most recently won a Nobel Prize? (10)
f: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, which makes her the latest Pakistani Nobel laureate.
r: Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate, winning the Physics prize in 1979.

q: Up to approximately what depth (in metres) does sunlight penetrate in the ocean (the sunlit or euphotic zone)? (10)
f: Enough sunlight for photosynthesis reaches only to about 200 metres, which is called the sunlit (euphotic) zone.
r: Below it lies the twilight zone from about 200 m to 1000 m, and below 1000 m is the dark midnight zone.

q: In which country is the Suez Canal situated? (10)
f: The Suez Canal is an artificial waterway running through Egypt.
r: It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea and was opened in 1869.

q: In which Hijri year was the Ghazwa Ahzab (Khandaq) fought? (10)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks place the Battle of the Trench in Shawwal 5 AH (627 CE).
r: Some historians place it in 4 AH, so sources differ.

q: On which date was SAARC formed? (10)
f: SAARC was established at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985 by seven South Asian countries.
r: Its secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal, and Afghanistan joined in 2007.

q: To which tribe did Hazrat Ali (RA) belong? (10)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was born in Makkah into the Banu Hashim clan of the Quraysh tribe. He was the cousin of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Aws and Khazraj were the two main tribes of Madina.

q: What is the abscissa of a point in the Cartesian plane? (10)
f: In a point (x, y), the abscissa is the x-coordinate, the horizontal distance from the y-axis.
r: The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

q: What is the capital of Uganda? (10)
f: Kampala is the capital of Uganda.
r: Entebbe, near Kampala, hosts Uganda's main international airport.

q: Which currency is most used in world trade? (10)
f: The US dollar is the main currency for invoicing trade and for global reserves.
r: The euro is the second most used reserve currency.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LEISURE? (10)
f: Leisure is time free from work or duties, which is free time.
r: The word comes from the Old French leisir, meaning to be permitted.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TOTALLY? (10)
f: Totally means in every way or to the full extent, which is completely or entirely.
r: Utterly and wholly are other close words.

q: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world? (10)
f: Kazakhstan has an area of about 2.72 million square kilometres and no coastline on an ocean. It is the largest landlocked country.
r: Mongolia is the second largest landlocked country.

q: Who first proposed the name Pakistan? (10)
f: Choudhry Rahmat Ali, a Cambridge student, coined the name Pakistan in his 1933 pamphlet Now or Never.
r: Allama Iqbal's 1930 Allahabad address proposed a separate Muslim state but did not use the name Pakistan.

q: Who refused to accept the Nobel Prize in Literature? (10)
f: The French writer Jean-Paul Sartre declined the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, saying he refused official honours.
r: Boris Pasternak was forced by Soviet authorities to decline his 1958 Nobel Prize.

q: Who was the first woman to travel to space? (10)
f: Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union flew aboard Vostok 6 in June 1963. She orbited the Earth 48 times.
r: Sally Ride became the first American woman in space in 1983.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 21st day of that month? (10)
f: From the 4th to the 21st is 17 days, and 17 divided by 7 leaves remainder 3. Moving 3 day(s) forward from Friday gives Monday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: If log x = y (common logarithm, base 10), what is x? (10)
f: By definition, log x = y with base 10 means x = 10^y.
r: Natural logarithm uses base e, so ln x = y gives x = e^y.

q: What is a matrix whose entries are all zero called? (10)
f: A matrix with every element equal to zero is called a null (zero) matrix.
r: Adding a null matrix to any matrix of the same order leaves it unchanged.

q: On what date did the Australian cricketer Shane Warne die? (10)
f: Shane Warne died of a suspected heart attack in Koh Samui, Thailand, on 4 March 2022 at the age of 52.
r: Warne took 708 wickets in Test cricket, a record for a leg-spinner.

q: In which province and city is the BRT (Zu Peshawar) transport system located? (10)
f: The BRT Zu Peshawar is a bus rapid transit system of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It serves the city of Peshawar.
r: Lahore has the Orange Line Metro Train and Metro Bus, which are different projects.

q: Which elements are found in the first period of the periodic table? (10)
f: The first period has only one shell, which can hold two electrons, so it contains just hydrogen (H) and helium (He).
r: The second period begins with lithium and ends with neon.

q: Who sold the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh in 1846? (10)
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) the British East India Company sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 7.5 million rupees.
r: Gulab Singh became the first Dogra Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir.

q: How many times did Jansher Khan win the World Open squash title? (10)
f: Jansher Khan won the World Open squash championship eight times between 1987 and 1996.
r: He also won the British Open six times, while Jahangir Khan won the World Open six times.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 10 years old? (10)
f: The sister is 15 years old when Ali is 5, so she is 10 years older than him. When Ali is 10, she is 10 + 10 = 20 years old.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: Which prophet was tested by Allah with a long and severe illness and was known for his patience? (10)
f: Hazrat Ayub (AS) was tested with loss of wealth, family and a long illness and kept patience, so his name is a proverb for sabr.
r: Allah cured him after he prayed, as mentioned in the Quran.

q: What is the capital of France? (10)
f: Paris, on the River Seine, is the capital and largest city of France.
r: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.

q: Who was the first Viceroy of India? (10)
f: Lord Canning became the first Viceroy in 1858 after the Government of India Act transferred power from the East India Company to the Crown.
r: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal, and Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India.

q: What is the opposite of the word crude? (10)
f: Crude means raw or unrefined, so its opposite is refined, meaning processed or polished.
r: In manners, the opposite of crude is cultured or polite.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert located? (10)
f: The Cholistan Desert lies in southern Punjab, near Bahawalpur.
r: It is locally called Rohi and is an extension of the Thar Desert.

q: In which province does the Green Line Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) system run? (10)
f: The Green Line BRT runs in Karachi, which is the capital of Sindh province.
r: The Peshawar BRT (Zu Peshawar) is the equivalent system in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: Between whom was the Battle of Plassey (1757) fought? (10)
o: The British East India Company and Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal
f: At Plassey the East India Company force under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
r: The battle laid the foundation of British rule in India.

q: What is 70% of 80? (10)
r: 70% of 80 equals 80% of 70.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 13th of that month? (10)
f: The 13th is 11 days after the 2nd, and 11 = 7 + 4. Monday + 4 days = Friday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: Khalil-ullah is the title of which prophet? (10)
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalil-ullah, meaning friend of Allah.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is Kaleem-ullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is Ruh-ullah.

q: Which line is the de facto boundary between India and China? (10)
f: The India-China frontier is known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
r: The McMahon Line is the 1914 boundary in the east that China does not accept.

q: Which type of number is 9/2? (10)
f: 9/2 is a ratio of two integers, so it is rational, and every rational number is also a real number.
r: As a decimal, 9/2 equals 4.5, which terminates.

q: Which is the largest island in the world? (10)
f: Greenland covers about 2.16 million square kilometres, more than any other island. Australia is counted as a continent.
r: New Guinea is the second largest island.

q: What is the meaning of the Arabic word 'Hikmah'? (10)
f: Hikmah means wisdom, sound judgement.
r: Al-Hakim, a name of Allah, comes from the same root.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die? (10)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died at Aligarh on 27 March 1898.
r: He was born in 1817, so he lived about 80 years.

q: Which team won the Asia Cup cricket tournament in 2022? (10)
f: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by 23 runs in the final in Dubai in September 2022 to win the T20 format Asia Cup.
r: The 2022 Asia Cup was played in the United Arab Emirates after being moved from Sri Lanka.

q: Ghani Khan, the famous poet and philosopher, wrote mainly in which language? (10)
f: Ghani Khan (1914-1996) was a well known Pashto poet, painter and philosopher from Charsadda.
r: He was the son of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan and wrote the book The Pathans.

q: What is the capital of Zambia? (10)
f: Lusaka is the capital and largest city of Zambia.
r: Zambia is a landlocked country in southern Africa that was formerly Northern Rhodesia.

q: In which year was the construction of Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi started (established)? (10)
f: The foundation of Pakistan Steel Mills was laid in 1973 by Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto with Soviet help.
r: The mill began production in 1981.

q: In which year was the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) institution founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Aligarh? (10)
f: Sir Syed founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh on 24 May 1875, which later became MAO College.
r: The school was raised to MAO College in 1877 and became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920; some sources date the college itself to 1877.

q: Who was the mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)? (10)
f: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and his wife Hazrat Sarah. He was born when Sarah was very old.
r: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: What is the approximate length of the River Nile? (10)
f: The Nile is about 6,650 km (4,130 miles) long. It is traditionally given as the longest river in the world.
r: Sources differ, and some textbooks give figures near 6,400 to 6,700 km; the Amazon is also claimed as longer by some measurements.

q: Which is the oldest seaport of Pakistan, as given in Pakistani textbooks? (10)
f: Karachi Port is generally given as the oldest and main seaport of Pakistan, with the modern port working from the 19th century. Gwadar and Port Qasim are much newer.
r: Karachi Port Trust was established in 1887; some sources name the ancient port of Banbhore as older.

q: In what amount was the valley of Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846)? (10)
f: By the Treaty of Amritsar the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh Dogra for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. This began Dogra rule in Kashmir.
r: The treaty was signed on 16 March 1846 after the First Anglo-Sikh War.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word annihilate? (10)
f: To annihilate is to destroy something utterly so that nothing remains. Its closest meaning is to destroy completely.
r: The word comes from the Latin annihilare, meaning to reduce to nothing.

q: Who discovered X-rays and developed the X-ray machine? (10)
f: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 in Germany.
r: He received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901 for this discovery.

q: Which word is a synonym of pacify? (10)
f: To pacify means to bring peace or to calm someone down. Calm has the same meaning.
r: Appease and soothe are other synonyms of pacify.

q: What was the Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940? (10)
o: A demand for separate independent states for the Muslims of India
A demand for a united India
A plan to boycott the elections of 1946
f: At the Lahore session of the All-India Muslim League, the resolution demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped into independent states.
r: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq and later called the Pakistan Resolution.

q: Who were the Ashra-e-Mubashara? (10)
o: Ten Companions of the Prophet (PBUH) given the glad tidings of Paradise in one lifetime
The ten wives of the Prophet (PBUH)
Ten Muslim commanders of the Battle of Badr
f: The Ashra-e-Mubashara are ten Companions whom the Prophet (PBUH) named as people of Paradise while they were alive. They include the four Rightly Guided Caliphs.
r: Their names are listed in a famous hadith narrated by Abdur Rahman bin Awf and Sa'id bin Zaid.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia? (10)
f: Ulaanbaatar (Ulan Bator) is the capital of Mongolia.
r: Ulaanbaatar is one of the coldest capital cities in the world.

q: In which country does Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, mainly lie? (10)
f: Mount Everest lies in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and the Tibet region of China. The main summit is usually described as being in Nepal.
r: Everest is about 8,849 metres high; Nepal calls it Sagarmatha and Tibet calls it Chomolungma.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of India? (10)
f: Jawaharlal Nehru became India's first Prime Minister on 15 August 1947 and served until 1964.
r: Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second Prime Minister of India.

q: In which country is Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in its range and home of the gods in myth, located? (10)
f: Mount Olympus is located in northern Greece and is its highest mountain.
r: In Greek mythology it was the home of the twelve Olympian gods.

q: What is transpiration in plants? (10)
o: Loss of water vapour from the aerial parts, mainly leaves
f: Transpiration is the loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mostly through the stomata of leaves.
r: Transpiration helps pull water and minerals up from the roots and cools the plant.

q: Which river is considered sacred in India? (10)
f: The Ganges (Ganga) is regarded as the holiest river by Hindus, who bathe in it at places such as Varanasi and Haridwar.
r: The Ganges flows into the Bay of Bengal through Bangladesh.

q: Choose the correct word: The aeroplane flew ___ my head. (10)
f: The preposition over is used when something passes above a person or object. The other options do not suit the meaning.
r: Over means above, while across means from one side to the other.

q: What is the approximate area of Sindh province? (10)
f: Sindh covers about 140,914 square kilometres, which is about 17.7 percent of Pakistan.
r: Sindh is the third largest province of Pakistan by area after Balochistan and Punjab.

q: How many ayat (verses) does Surah Al-Ikhlas have? (10)
f: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) has 4 ayat. It describes the oneness of Allah.
r: Reciting it is said to equal one third of the Quran in reward.

q: How many letters does the Pashto alphabet have according to the most commonly cited reference count? (10)
f: The Pashto alphabet is written in an extended Arabic script and is most commonly cited as having 45 letters.
r: Some learner guides count 44 letters, so sources differ slightly; 45 is the figure candidates and many references use.

q: How many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize so far? (10)
f: Two Pakistanis have won it: Dr Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
r: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate in history.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to peril? (10)
f: Peril means serious danger or risk.
r: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

q: Between which two countries does the Durand Line lie? (10)
f: The Durand Line is the border drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan. Today it is the international border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
r: It was agreed between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to eminent? (10)
f: Eminent means famous and respected, which is prominent.
r: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

q: Who was the first Finance Minister of Pakistan? (10)
f: Malik Ghulam Muhammad was Finance Minister in the first cabinet of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1947. He later became the third Governor General.
r: He presented the first budget of Pakistan in 1948.

q: What does OS stand for in computing? (10)
f: In computers, OS stands for Operating System, the main software that runs the computer.
r: Windows, Linux, macOS and Android are well-known operating systems.

q: The Wagah border connects Pakistan with which country? (10)
f: Wagah, on the Grand Trunk Road between Lahore and Amritsar, is the main land crossing between Pakistan and India.
r: A daily flag-lowering ceremony is held there by both countries.

q: Which country is Pakistan's biggest trading partner today? (10)
f: China is Pakistan's largest trading partner, mainly because of large imports from China.
r: The United States is Pakistan's largest single export market, but China leads in total trade.

q: Who is the head of state of Pakistan according to the 1973 Constitution (currently in office, 2026)? (10)
f: The President is the head of state, and Asif Ali Zardari has held the office since 10 March 2024.
r: His predecessor was Arif Alvi (2018 to 2024); the Prime Minister is head of government.

q: What is the tenure of a member of the Senate of Pakistan? (10)
f: A Senator is elected for six years. Half of the members retire every three years.
r: The Senate is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.

q: Which sport is called the Game of Gentlemen? (10)
f: Cricket is known as the Game of Gentlemen because of its tradition of fair play and sportsmanship. The phrase comes from its English origins.
r: Cricket began in England and its laws are kept by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).

q: Who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar movement? (10)
f: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Bacha Khan) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God) movement around 1929 in the Pashtun areas.
r: Its members were known as Red Shirts and followed non-violence.

q: Who is Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York as of October 2026? (10)
f: Asim Iftikhar Ahmad heads the Pakistan Mission to the UN and issues its statements in 2026.
r: Munir Akram held this post before him.

q: In which game is a free throw used? (10)
f: A free throw is an unopposed shot at the basket given to a player after a foul in basketball. It is worth one point.
r: A basket scored from inside the three-point line in open play is worth two points.

q: What is an electric motor? (10)
o: A device that changes electrical energy into mechanical energy
A device that changes mechanical energy into electrical energy
f: An electric motor uses a current in a magnetic field to produce rotation. This turns electrical energy into mechanical energy.
r: A generator does the opposite job of a motor.

q: What is the currency of Armenia? (9)
f: Armenia uses the dram.
r: Georgia uses the lari and Azerbaijan the manat.

q: Who was the brother of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA)? (9)
f: Walid bin Walid (RA) was the brother of Khalid bin Waleed (RA) and accepted Islam before him.
r: Their father Waleed bin Mughirah was a leader of the Banu Makhzum of Quraish.

q: On what date did the War of Independence of the Subcontinent begin? (9)
f: The 1857 War of Independence began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
r: The British call it the Sepoy Mutiny.

q: What does POF stand for? (9)
f: POF stands for Pakistan Ordnance Factories, which make arms and ammunition.
r: POF is headquartered at Wah Cantt.

q: What is the largest city of Punjab by population? (9)
f: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and its largest city.
r: Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.

q: What is the derivative of a constant? (9)
f: A constant does not change as x changes, so its rate of change is zero.
r: The derivative of x with respect to x is 1.

q: Which cricketer broke Shahid Afridi's record of the fastest century in ODIs (37 balls, 1996)? (9)
f: New Zealand's Corey Anderson scored a century off 36 balls against the West Indies in January 2014 and broke Afridi's 17-year-old record.
r: AB de Villiers later broke Anderson's record with a 31-ball century against the West Indies in January 2015, and it still stands.

q: The rate of change is called what? (9)
f: In calculus the derivative measures the rate of change of a quantity with respect to another.
r: The derivative of distance with respect to time is velocity.

q: Which is the world's largest uranium producing country? (9)
f: Kazakhstan has been the top uranium producer since 2009 and supplied about 39 percent of world mine output in 2024.
r: Canada is second and Namibia third in recent World Nuclear Association data.

q: Is the sun a star or a planet? (9)
f: The sun is a star because it produces its own light and heat by nuclear fusion. Planets only reflect light.
r: The sun is a medium-sized yellow dwarf star at the centre of our solar system.

q: What is Sunnah? (9)
o: The way and practice of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
f: Sunnah literally means path or way, and in Islam it refers to the sayings, actions and approvals of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: Sunnah is the second source of Islamic law after the Quran.

q: When was Sindh separated from the Bombay Presidency? (9)
f: Sindh became a separate province on 1 April 1936 under the Government of India Act 1935. Sir Shah Nawaz Bhutto and others had campaigned for the separation.
r: The Quaid-e-Azam had included the separation of Sindh in his Fourteen Points of 1929.

q: When and where was the Red Cross founded? (9)
f: The International Committee of the Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 on the initiative of Henry Dunant.
r: Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

q: Who introduced the presidential system in Pakistan? (9)
f: Ayub Khan introduced the presidential system through the Constitution of 1962.
r: Ayub Khan became Pakistan's first military ruler in 1958.

q: How many months of the year have 30 days? (9)
f: April, June, September and November have 30 days, which makes 4.
r: Candidates wrote 7, but that is the number of 31-day months.

q: How many roots does a linear equation in one variable have? (9)
f: A linear equation ax + b = 0 with a not zero has exactly one solution x = -b / a.
r: A quadratic equation has at most two roots.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd? (9)
f: The gap is 22 days. 22 mod 7 = 1, so Monday plus 1 day is Tuesday.
r: The 22nd is also a Monday here since it is 21 days (3 weeks) after the 1st.

q: The first 5 verses revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) belong to which surah? (9)
f: The first five ayats revealed in the Cave of Hira begin with Iqra bismi rabbika and are from Surah Al-Alaq.
r: Surah Al-Alaq is also called Surah Iqra.

q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, belongs to which country? (9)
f: Antonio Guterres, the ninth UN Secretary-General, is a former Prime Minister of Portugal.
r: His term ends on 31 December 2026 and the selection of his successor is under way; before him Ban Ki-moon of South Korea held the post.

q: What is the first month of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar? (9)
f: The Hijri calendar begins with Muharram, and 1 Muharram is the Islamic New Year.
r: The calendar was introduced in the time of Hazrat Umar (RA) and counts from the Hijrah to Madina.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hafsa (RA) with the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (9)
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA), married the Prophet (PBUH) and is a Mother of the Believers.
r: The first compiled copy of the Quran was kept with Hazrat Hafsa (RA).

q: Which angels write down the good and bad deeds of every human being? (9)
f: Kiraman Katibin are the two noble recording angels on a person's shoulders who write the deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.
r: Munkar and Nakir are the angels who question a person in the grave.

q: After how many years does a leap year normally come? (9)
f: A leap year occurs once every 4 years, when the year is divisible by 4, and adds 29 February.
r: Century years such as 1900 are leap years only if divisible by 400.

q: In which Islamic month is Laylat ul Qadr (the Night of Power)? (9)
f: Laylat ul Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, especially the odd nights.
r: Surah Al-Qadr is devoted to this night, which is described as better than a thousand months.

q: In which province does the Soan River flow? (9)
f: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar plateau of Punjab (Rawalpindi area) to join the Indus.
r: The Soan valley is one of the oldest sites of early human tools in South Asia.

q: Among Muslim-majority countries, what is Pakistan's rank by population? (9)
f: Indonesia has the largest population among Muslim-majority countries and Pakistan is second.
r: Bangladesh is usually ranked third.

q: What is the capital of Germany? (9)
f: Berlin is the capital of Germany.
r: Bonn was the capital of West Germany before reunification in 1990.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word juvenile? (9)
f: Juvenile refers to a young person or something belonging to young people. Youthful is the closest meaning.
r: A juvenile court deals with offenders below the adult age.

q: What is the meaning of Hilf-ul-Fudul? (9)
f: Hilf-ul-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah by chiefs who promised to defend the oppressed and give justice to all. Its name means the pact of the virtuous.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) took part in it as a young man before prophethood and praised it later.

q: In which year was the state of Israel declared? (9)
f: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948, as the British Mandate over Palestine ended. The first Arab-Israeli war followed immediately.
r: The UN General Assembly adopted the Palestine partition plan in November 1947.

q: In which year did Choudhary Rahmat Ali write the pamphlet 'Now or Never'? (9)
f: Choudhary Rahmat Ali and his Cambridge colleagues issued the pamphlet 'Now or Never' in January 1933. It first proposed the name Pakistan for a Muslim homeland.
r: Rahmat Ali is known as the person who coined the name Pakistan.

q: In which region was the ancient Gandhara civilization centred? (9)
f: Gandhara flourished in the Peshawar valley and Potohar region of northwest Pakistan, with Taxila and Peshawar as major centres.
r: Gandhara art is famous for Greco-Buddhist sculpture.
