q: Which is the largest man-made lake (reservoir) of Pakistan? (9)
f: Tarbela Reservoir on the Indus has the largest surface area of any reservoir in Pakistan, about 250 square kilometres.
r: Tarbela Dam is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: A jet covers 320 km using 50 gallons of fuel. How many gallons will it use to cover 700 km? (9)
f: Fuel per km = 50/320 = 0.15625 gallon. For 700 km: 700 x 0.15625 = 109.375 gallons.
r: The same result comes from the proportion 50 x 700 / 320.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 13th day of that month? (9)
f: From the 2nd to the 13th is 11 days, and 11 divided by 7 leaves remainder 4. Moving 4 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Thursday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: What is cos x multiplied by tan x equal to? (9)
f: Since tan x = sin x / cos x, cos x times tan x = sin x.
r: Another identity: sin x divided by cos x equals tan x.

q: Which plant is commonly named as the fastest growing plant (tree) in the world? (9)
f: Some bamboo species can grow almost one metre in a single day, which is why bamboo is commonly named the fastest growing plant.
r: Bamboo is technically a grass, and the Paulownia is often called the fastest growing true tree, so sources differ.

q: About what percentage of Antarctica is covered by ice? (9)
f: About 98 percent of Antarctica is covered by an ice sheet, and only about 2 percent is bare rock. Some sources give 97.6 or 99 percent.
r: The ice sheet is on average about 2 km thick.

q: Out of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of the students are absent (to two decimal places)? (9)
r: The percentage present is 86.67%, which together with 13.33% makes 100%.

q: Which country has the largest number of lakes in the world? (9)
f: Canada has the most lakes in the world, with several hundred thousand, more than the rest of the world combined by most estimates.
r: Finland is known as the land of a thousand lakes but has far fewer lakes than Canada.

q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan? (9)
f: Zahid Hussain was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan, appointed in 1948.
r: The bank was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam on 1 July 1948.

q: What is cos(90 degrees - x) equal to? (9)
f: By the complementary angle identity, cos(90 - x) = sin x.
r: Similarly sin(90 - x) = cos x.

q: Who is generally listed as the first Governor-General of India (of Bengal, 1774)? (9)
f: Warren Hastings became Governor-General of Bengal in 1774 and is commonly called the first Governor-General of India in textbooks.
r: Sources differ: Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of all India in 1833, and Lord Mountbatten was the first of independent India.

q: What is the antonym of the word biased? (9)
f: Biased means unfairly favouring one side, so its opposite is impartial.
r: Unbiased and neutral are other opposites.

q: A square matrix whose determinant is zero is called what? (9)
f: A square matrix with determinant equal to zero has no inverse and is called a singular matrix.
r: A matrix with a non-zero determinant is called non-singular and has an inverse.

q: In which galaxy does the Earth lie? (9)
f: Our solar system and the Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy, a barred spiral galaxy.
r: The nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way is Andromeda.

q: How many seats are reserved for non-Muslim minorities in the National Assembly of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (9)
f: Article 51 of the Constitution reserves ten seats in the National Assembly for non-Muslims.
r: Minority members are chosen on reserved seats in proportion to the seats won by each party.

q: Baltistan is also known as which of the following? (9)
f: Baltistan, in Gilgit-Baltistan, is called Little Tibet (Tibet-e-Khurd) because of its culture and mountain landscape similar to Tibet.
r: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.

q: What was the Cabinet Mission of 1946? (9)
o: A British mission sent to India to discuss the transfer of power
A Muslim League mission sent to London
A Congress mission sent to the Viceroy
A United Nations mission to Kashmir
f: The Cabinet Mission was a delegation of three British cabinet ministers sent to India in 1946. It proposed a plan for the transfer of power and a united India with a weak centre.
r: The Muslim League first accepted the plan and later withdrew its acceptance.

q: The Friendship Gate (Bab-e-Dosti) at Chaman is a border crossing between which two countries? (9)
f: The Friendship Gate stands at Chaman in Balochistan on the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.
r: It is on Pakistan's western border, the Durand Line, opposite Spin Boldak in Afghanistan.

q: What is a matrix with only one row called? (9)
f: A matrix having only one row is called a row matrix; its order is 1 x n.
r: A matrix with only one column is called a column matrix.

q: What is the antonym of the word timid? (9)
f: Timid means lacking courage, so its opposite is bold.
r: Shy, fearful and meek are synonyms of timid.

q: How many acute angles are there in an acute triangle? (9)
f: In an acute triangle all three angles are less than 90 degrees, so all three are acute.
r: A right triangle has two acute angles and an obtuse triangle has two acute angles as well.

q: What is the (executive) capital of South Africa? (9)
f: Pretoria is the administrative (executive) capital of South Africa. The country has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
r: Cape Town is the legislative capital and Bloemfontein is the judicial capital.

q: Which barrage is commonly described as the biggest and the first barrage of Pakistan on the Indus? (9)
f: Sukkur Barrage, opened in 1932, is the one Pakistani textbooks name as the first and biggest barrage on the Indus.
r: Sources differ on size; Guddu and Taunsa are other large barrages on the Indus.

q: What is the capital of Sri Lanka as commonly given in textbooks? (9)
f: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka and the usual textbook answer.
r: The official legislative capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, near Colombo.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to LENIENT? (9)
f: Lenient means merciful or not strict, so tolerant is the closest.
r: The opposite of lenient is strict or harsh.

q: Who was the first man to land on the Moon? (9)
f: Neil Armstrong of the Apollo 11 mission stepped on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
r: Buzz Aldrin followed him, while Michael Collins stayed in orbit.

q: What is the square root of 196? (9)
f: 14 x 14 = 196, so the square root of 196 is 14.
r: 196 is a perfect square, being 14 squared.

q: How many surahs of the Holy Quran are named after prophets, according to the commonly given list? (9)
f: The commonly counted ones are Yunus, Hud, Yusuf, Ibrahim, Nuh and Muhammad, giving six.
r: Counts differ between sources depending on which names are included.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be? (9)
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 days is 2 full weeks plus 5 day(s), so the day is 5 day(s) after Friday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: By which title is Hazrat Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) well known? (9)
f: Abdullah ibn Abbas was a great scholar of Quranic interpretation, so he is called Tarjuman-ul-Quran (interpreter of the Quran). He is also called Hibr-ul-Ummah.
r: Saifullah is the title of Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA).

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah announce his 14 Points? (9)
f: Jinnah presented his 14 Points in March 1929 in Delhi as a reply to the Nehru Report.
r: The 14 Points set out the minimum constitutional demands of the Muslims of India.

q: Approximately how many prophets came to the world in total, according to popular Islamic tradition? (9)
f: A popular narration says that about 124,000 prophets were sent. The number is not given in the Quran.
r: Sources differ on the exact number, and 313 is commonly given for the Rasuls (messengers).

q: Infections in the human body are caused by which of the following? (9)
o: Germs (pathogens such as bacteria and viruses)
f: Infections occur when disease-causing germs such as bacteria, viruses, fungi or parasites enter the body and multiply.
r: Antigens are substances that trigger the immune system, while antibodies are made to fight them.

q: Mangla Dam is built on which river? (9)
f: Mangla Dam stands on the river Jhelum.
r: Tarbela Dam, in contrast, is on the Indus.

q: Badr, where the first major battle of Islam was fought, is the name of what? (9)
o: A plain with wells near Madinah
f: Badr is a plain valley with wells about 150 km from Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
r: Mount Uhud, in contrast, is a mountain near Madinah.

q: Where is the shrine of the famous Pashto poet Rehman Baba located? (9)
f: The mausoleum of Abdur Rehman Mohmand, known as Rehman Baba, is at Hazar Khwani near Peshawar.
r: Rehman Baba is called the Nightingale of Pashto poetry and lived in the 17th century.

q: What is the average height of the Potohar Plateau above sea level according to most Pakistani textbooks? (9)
f: The Potohar Plateau lies between the Indus and Jhelum rivers and has an average height of about 300 to 600 metres.
r: Sources differ slightly, with some giving the height in feet as about 1000 to 2000 feet.

q: What is the approximate maximum height of the Kirthar range (its highest point, Zardak Peak)? (9)
f: The highest point of the Kirthar range is Zardak Peak at roughly 2,260 metres, or about 7,400 feet.
r: Sources give slightly different figures, from about 2,260 to 2,267 metres.

q: Which is regarded as the first women's university in Pakistan, and in which city is it located? (9)
o: Kinnaird College for Women University, Lahore
Sardar Bahadur Khan Women's University, Quetta
f: Fatima Jinnah Women University was founded in 1998 in Rawalpindi and is generally regarded as Pakistan's first women's university. It is named after Fatima Jinnah, the sister of the Quaid-e-Azam.
r: Some sources call it the first public sector women's university, because Kinnaird College in Lahore was a much older women's college.

q: The Karakoram mountain range lies between Pakistan and which country? (9)
f: The Karakoram range runs along the northern border of Pakistan and separates Gilgit-Baltistan from the Xinjiang region of China.
r: The Karakoram Highway crosses this range through the Khunjerab Pass and links Pakistan with China.

q: According to the commonly given number in Pakistani textbooks, how many Companions served as Katib-e-Wahi (scribes of revelation) for the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (9)
f: Many Pakistani books state that about 40 Companions wrote down the revelation, including Hazrat Ali, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA).
r: Sources differ on the exact number, and Hazrat Zaid bin Thabit (RA) is the best known of the scribes.

q: Who conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD? (9)
f: The young Arab general Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the Umayyad caliphate. He defeated Raja Dahir.
r: Sindh is therefore called Bab-ul-Islam, the gateway of Islam, in the subcontinent.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'excuse' used as a verb meaning to forgive? (9)
f: To excuse means to forgive or let go without blame. Its opposite is to accuse or blame someone.
r: 'Condemn' and 'blame' are also opposites of excuse in this sense.

q: What is the antonym of isolation? (9)
f: Isolation means being alone and apart from others; the opposite is companionship or togetherness.
r: Isolation, seclusion and solitude are close synonyms.

q: Where were the first Asian Games held in 1951? (9)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, in 1951.
r: The Asian Games are held every four years under the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: In which year was the Simla Conference between the British, the Congress and the Muslim League held? (9)
f: The Simla Conference was convened by Viceroy Lord Wavell in 1945 to discuss the Wavell Plan for an interim government.
r: The conference failed mainly because Congress refused to accept that the Muslim League alone represented the Muslims.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Thar desert mainly located? (9)
f: The Pakistani part of the Thar desert lies in the south-east of Sindh, mainly in Tharparkar district.
r: The Thar desert extends into the Indian state of Rajasthan and is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.

q: In which city is the Shahi Qila (Lahore Fort) located? (9)
f: The Shahi Qila, also called the Lahore Fort, stands in the Walled City of Lahore. It was rebuilt in the Mughal era, notably under Akbar.
r: The Lahore Fort and Shalimar Gardens were listed as UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1981.

q: What is the highest point on the surface of the Earth above sea level? (9)
f: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal and China border, is about 8849 metres high and is the highest point above sea level.
r: K2 in Pakistan is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: Convert 90 degrees into radians. (9)
f: 1 degree = pi/180 radian. So 90 degrees = 90 x pi/180 = pi/2 radians.
r: A full circle of 360 degrees equals 2 pi radians.

q: In which city is the headquarters of the European Union (EU) located? (9)
f: The main institutions of the European Union, such as the European Commission and the Council, are based in Brussels, Belgium.
r: The European Parliament meets in Strasbourg, France, and has its secretariat in Luxembourg.

q: Who was the first president of the Indian National Congress in 1885? (9)
f: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in Bombay in December 1885 under the presidency of W. C. Bonnerjee.
r: A. O. Hume, the founder of the Congress, was its first general secretary.

q: In aviation, in which unit is altitude commonly measured internationally? (9)
f: International civil aviation standards use feet for altitude and flight levels.
r: A few countries, such as China and Russia, have used metres for altitude.

q: How many Prime Ministers did Pakistan have between 1947 and 1958? (9)
f: They were Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Mohammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Mohammad Ali, H. S. Suhrawardy, I. I. Chundrigar and Feroz Khan Noon, which makes 7.
r: Martial law was imposed in October 1958 by Iskander Mirza and Ayub Khan.

q: In which year was the C. R. (Rajagopalachari) Formula put forward? (9)
f: C. Rajagopalachari proposed the formula in 1944 as a basis for talks between Gandhi and Jinnah.
r: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks of September 1944 failed, partly because Jinnah rejected the formula.

q: In which city is Paradise Point located? (9)
f: Paradise Point is a famous rocky beach spot on the Arabian Sea coast in Karachi.
r: It is close to Cape Monze (Ras Muari) and has a natural arch in the rocks.

q: In which city of Pakistan is Iqbal Park located? (9)
f: Iqbal Park in Lahore is the park where Minar-e-Pakistan stands and the Pakistan Resolution was passed in 1940.
r: It was earlier called Minto Park.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam return to India after his self-imposed exile in England? (9)
f: Jinnah stayed in London for some years after the Round Table Conferences. He came back in 1934 at the request of Muslim leaders and was elected president of the Muslim League.
r: Some sources give 1935 for his final return, but 1934 is the common textbook year.

q: What does the crescent on the flag of Pakistan represent? (9)
f: According to the usual explanation, the crescent stands for progress.
r: The five pointed star stands for light and knowledge, and the white strip for minorities.

q: Where is the National College of Arts (NCA) located? (9)
f: The National College of Arts is a famous art and design institution in Lahore. It was founded in 1875 as the Mayo School of Art.
r: Its first principal was John Lockwood Kipling, the father of the writer Rudyard Kipling.

q: Which mammal lays eggs? (9)
f: The platypus and the echidna are monotremes, the only mammals that lay eggs.
r: Monotremes live in Australia and New Guinea.

q: In which present-day country did Islam originate? (9)
f: Islam began in Makkah in the Arabian Peninsula, in what is now Saudi Arabia.
r: The first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira near Makkah.

q: Which is the odd one out: panda, chimpanzee, bamboo? (9)
f: Panda and chimpanzee are animals, while bamboo is a plant.
r: Bamboo shoots and leaves are the main food of the giant panda.

q: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles? (9)
f: Brazil has won the men's World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002). No other team has more, including after the 2026 tournament.
r: Spain won the 2026 World Cup, beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time, for their second title.

q: What was the Islamic date of the independence of Pakistan (14 August 1947)? (9)
f: 14 August 1947 fell on 27 Ramadan 1366 AH, the blessed night of Laylat ul Qadr as commonly believed.
r: Because of this date, Pakistan is often called a gift of the holy month of Ramadan.

q: On which river is Simly Dam (Simla Dam) built? (8)
f: Simly Dam near Islamabad is an earthen dam on the Soan River. It supplies water to Islamabad.
r: It was completed in 1983; Khanpur Dam, by contrast, is on the Haro River.

q: What causes swine flu? (8)
f: Swine flu is caused by influenza A viruses, most notably the H1N1 strain.
r: The 2009 H1N1 pandemic was declared by the WHO in June 2009.

q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located? (8)
f: The Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir is buried in Lahore, in the Dharampura area.
r: Mian Mir is said to have laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple at Amritsar at the invitation of Guru Arjan.

q: What does WAPDA stand for? (8)
f: WAPDA stands for Water and Power Development Authority.
r: WAPDA was created in 1958 to develop Pakistan's water and hydropower resources.

q: What does yellow journalism mean? (8)
f: Yellow journalism is journalism that exaggerates or sensationalises news to attract readers rather than reporting facts carefully.
r: The term arose from the 1890s newspaper rivalry between Joseph Pulitzer and William Randolph Hearst.

q: In the usual order of the oceans by size, what is the number of the Indian Ocean? (8)
f: By size the order is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic, so the Indian Ocean is third.
r: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ismail (AS) with Hazrat Ibrahim (AS)? (8)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Hajra. He was the elder of Ibrahim's two sons.
r: Father and son together raised the foundations of the Kaaba in Makkah.

q: 340 out of 500: what is the percentage? (8)
r: Percent means per hundred.

q: In which city was the All India Muslim League founded in 1906? (8)
f: The All India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in December 1906 at the Muslim Educational Conference, hosted by Nawab Salimullah Khan.
r: Its first president was Nawab Viqar-ul-Mulk, and Sir Aga Khan was the first permanent president.

q: What is the literal meaning of the word Quran? (8)
o: That which is recited or read
f: The word Quran comes from the Arabic root qara'a, meaning to read or recite.
r: Al-Furqan (the Criterion) and Al-Huda (the Guidance) are other names of the Quran.

q: What is Hudaibiya? (8)
o: A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
f: Hudaibiya is a place near Makkah where the treaty between the Prophet (PBUH) and the Quraish was signed in 6 AH.
r: The Treaty of Hudaibiya set a ten-year truce and paved the way for the conquest of Makkah.

q: What are the Upper House (Senate) and Lower House (National Assembly) of Pakistan jointly called? (8)
f: Together with the President, the Senate and the National Assembly form the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora.
r: The Senate of Pakistan has 96 members.

q: Convert 30 degrees into radians. (8)
f: Radians = degrees x pi / 180 = 30 pi / 180 = pi / 6.
r: 180 degrees equals pi radians.

q: How many basic trigonometric functions are there? (8)
f: They are sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant and cotangent.
r: Cosecant, secant and cotangent are reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent.

q: What is the derivative of x with respect to x? (8)
f: By the power rule, d(x^1)/dx = 1 x x^0 = 1.
r: The derivative of x squared is 2x.

q: What is the formula for the area of a triangle? (8)
f: The area of a triangle is half the area of the parallelogram with the same base and height.
r: The area of a rectangle is length x width.

q: After which battle did the disbelievers become unable to attack Madinah (and Makkah-based enemies could no longer launch attacks)? (8)
f: After the failed siege in the Battle of Khandaq the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said the Quraysh would no longer attack the Muslims, and the Muslims would march against them.
r: The Battle of Khandaq took place in 5 AH and a trench was dug on the advice of Hazrat Salman Farsi (RA).

q: In which district of Pakistan is the Chashma nuclear power plant located? (8)
f: The Chashma Nuclear Power Complex stands near Chashma barrage on the Indus in Mianwali district, Punjab.
r: Chashma Nuclear Power Plant Unit 1 was built with Chinese help.

q: In which Islamic month did the tragedy of Karbala take place? (8)
f: Imam Hussain (RA) was martyred at Karbala on 10 Muharram 61 AH, the day of Ashura.
r: The year of the event, 61 AH, fell during the rule of Yazid.

q: What is the term of a Senator in Pakistan? (8)
f: Senators are elected for a six-year term, and half retire every three years.
r: The Senate itself is a permanent house and is never dissolved.

q: What is the period between a person's death and the Day of Judgment called in Islam? (8)
f: Barzakh is the intermediate stage between death and resurrection, in which the soul stays until the Day of Judgment.
r: Barzakh is also the Quranic word for a barrier, for example between two seas in Surah Ar-Rahman.

q: Why was Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad launched in February 2017? (8)
o: To eliminate the remaining terrorist threat across the country
f: It was a nationwide operation of the armed forces to eliminate the remaining terrorist threat, consolidate earlier gains and strengthen border security.
r: It followed earlier operations such as Zarb-e-Azb and was launched on 22 February 2017.

q: For addition of matrices, what must both matrices have? (8)
o: The same order (same number of rows and columns)
The same number of columns only
f: Matrices are added element by element, so they must have the same number of rows and columns.
r: Matrix multiplication needs columns of the first to equal rows of the second.

q: From which country does the TAPI gas pipeline start? (8)
f: TAPI stands for Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, and the gas comes from Turkmenistan.
r: The gas source is the Galkynysh field in Turkmenistan.

q: According to a hadith of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), lying is a sign of which kind of person? (8)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was known as Sadiq (truthful) and Ameen (trustworthy) even before prophethood.

q: How many players of one team are on the court at a time in basketball? (8)
f: Each basketball team plays with five players on the court at a time.
r: A team may have up to 12 players in total on its roster in international games.

q: Through which of these countries does the Tropic of Cancer not pass? (8)
f: The Tropic of Cancer (23.5 degrees north) crosses India, Bangladesh and Egypt, but Pakistan lies north of it.
r: It also passes through Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Libya and southern China.

q: What does Tayammum mean? (8)
o: Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
f: Tayammum is a substitute for wudu or ghusl performed with clean earth or dust when water is not available or cannot be used. It is taught in the Quran in Surah Al-Maidah.
r: Tayammum is made by striking the hands on clean earth and wiping the face and hands.

q: Which is the largest plateau of the world by area? (8)
f: The Tibetan Plateau covers about 2.5 million square kilometres and is the largest as well as the highest plateau.
r: It is often called the Roof of the World.

q: What is the meaning of the word Al-Noor? (8)
f: Noor is an Arabic word meaning light, and Al-Noor means The Light.
r: Surah An-Nur is the 24th surah of the Holy Quran and Al-Nur is one of the names of Allah.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to OPPRESS? (8)
f: To oppress is to keep people down by cruel or unjust use of power, which is to persecute.
r: Its opposite is to liberate.

q: What was the Simla Conference of 1945? (8)
o: A meeting of Wavell with Indian leaders on self-government that failed
The signing of the Pakistan-India peace agreement
The announcement of the Partition Plan
The first session of the Constituent Assembly
f: The Viceroy Lord Wavell called Indian leaders to Simla in June-July 1945 to discuss an Executive Council. It failed because Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on who nominates Muslim members.
r: The Wavell Plan was rejected as the Muslim League insisted on being the sole representative of Muslims.

q: Where was Benazir Bhutto assassinated in December 2007? (8)
f: Benazir Bhutto was killed on 27 December 2007 after addressing an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi. She was attacked as she left the venue.
r: She had been Prime Minister of Pakistan twice, in 1988-90 and 1993-96.

q: Which Pakistani batter holds the highest individual score in Test cricket for Pakistan? (8)
f: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958, still Pakistan's highest Test score.
r: Younis Khan's 313 against Sri Lanka in 2009 is the second highest by a Pakistani.

q: Which planet is named after the Roman equivalent of the Greek god Zeus? (8)
f: Jupiter is the Roman name of the king of the gods, whom the Greeks called Zeus.
r: Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system.

q: Who is the Chief of the Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy? (8)
f: Admiral Naveed Ashraf took over as Chief of the Naval Staff in October 2023 and is the serving chief in 2026.
r: His predecessors were Admiral Muhammad Zakaullah and, before him, Admiral Muhammad Amjad Khan Niazi.

q: Who is the father of Hazrat Usman (R.A)? (8)
f: Hazrat Usman (R.A) was the son of Affan bin Abi al-As of the Banu Umayya clan of Quraysh.
r: Abu Quhafa was the father of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Khattab the father of Hazrat Umar (R.A).

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan when the President is absent or unable to perform the functions of office? (8)
o: The Speaker of the National Assembly
f: Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President. If there is no Chairman, the Speaker of the National Assembly does so.
r: Muhammad Mian Soomro and Wasim Sajjad are among Senate Chairmen who have acted as President.

q: Who was the second President of Pakistan? (8)
f: Iskander Mirza was the first President under the 1956 Constitution. Ayub Khan removed him in 1958 and became the second.
r: Counts differ if the Governor-General office is included, but textbooks list Ayub Khan second.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 23rd day of that month? (8)
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days, and 19 divided by 7 leaves remainder 5. Moving 5 day(s) forward from Monday gives Saturday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 24th day of that month? (8)
f: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days, and 20 divided by 7 leaves remainder 6. Moving 6 day(s) forward from Monday gives Sunday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: Which letter comes next: A B C D E F G H ? (8)
f: The letters are in alphabetical order, and the one after H is I.
r: I is the 9th letter of the alphabet.

q: At what age did Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, the father of Pakistan's nuclear programme, die? (8)
f: He was born on 1 April 1936 and died on 10 October 2021, which makes him 85 years old.
r: He died in Islamabad and was buried in the H-8 graveyard.

q: Which country is the current men's Hockey World Cup champion (2026 edition)? (8)
f: Germany beat Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026 in Wavre, Belgium, to retain the title.
r: Belgium won the 2018 World Cup, and Germany won in 2023; Pakistan has four titles, the same as Germany.

q: Who developed the first successful polio vaccine? (8)
f: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated polio vaccine, announced in 1955.
r: Albert Sabin later developed the oral polio vaccine.

q: Which country hosted the extraordinary session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on the Afghan crisis in December 2021? (8)
f: Pakistan hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Islamabad on 19 December 2021 to discuss the Afghan humanitarian crisis.
r: The 47th regular CFM was held in Niamey, Niger, in November 2020.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Israel (as of October 2026, before the 27 October election)? (8)
f: Benjamin Netanyahu has led Israel's government since December 2022, and he is campaigning for the election due on 27 October 2026.
r: Candidates in 2022 wrote Naftali Bennett, who was PM from June 2021 to June 2022, followed by Yair Lapid.

q: Which is the longest river lying entirely within Afghanistan? (8)
f: The Helmand River, about 1,150 km long, is the longest river that flows wholly in Afghanistan.
r: The Amu Darya forms part of the northern border with Central Asia, so it is not counted as entirely Afghan; some sources differ.

q: What is the antonym of 'demise'? (8)
f: Demise means death or end, so its opposite is birth or beginning.
r: Death, end and collapse are all synonyms of demise.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Russia? (8)
f: Mikhail Mishustin has been Prime Minister of Russia since January 2020, and he remains in office as of October 2026.
r: His predecessor as Prime Minister was Dmitry Medvedev.

q: The White House in Washington, D.C. is the official residence and workplace of whom? (8)
o: The President of the United States
The Chief Justice of the US
f: The White House is the official residence and main workplace of the President of the United States.
r: The official residence of the US Vice President is the Naval Observatory, not the White House.

q: What is the antonym of autonomy? (8)
f: Autonomy means self-rule, so its opposite is dependence, being controlled by others.
r: Synonyms of autonomy include independence and self-government.

q: Who was the king (Najashi) of Habsha (Abyssinia) who gave shelter to the Muslim migrants? (8)
f: The Christian king of Abyssinia, known by the title Najashi (Negus), was Ashama ibn Abjar. He protected the early Muslims who migrated there.
r: Abraha was the Abyssinian governor of Yemen who marched against the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.

q: What does KRL stand for? (8)
f: KRL stands for Khan Research Laboratories, named after Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan. It is located at Kahuta.
r: It was originally set up in 1976 as the Engineering Research Laboratories and renamed in 1981.

q: Which prophet is known for suffering patiently from a long skin disease? (8)
f: Hazrat Ayyub (AS) bore a long illness, said to be a skin disease, with great patience and is the model of sabr (patience).
r: The Quran mentions his prayer in Surah Al-Anbiya and Surah Sad.

q: Which is counted as the third major Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), after Badr and Uhud? (8)
f: The major battles in order are Badr, Uhud and Khandaq (Ahzab), fought in 5 AH. The Muslims dug a trench on the advice of Salman Farsi.
r: Sources differ: early chronologies also list small expeditions such as Abwa and Buwat before Badr.

q: A. R. Cornelius, a Chief Justice of Pakistan, belonged to which religion? (8)
f: Justice Alvin Robert Cornelius was a Christian and served as Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
r: He was known for his scholarship and integrity.

q: In which year was the Bogra Formula presented? (8)
f: Prime Minister Muhammad Ali Bogra presented the formula in 1953 to solve the constitutional deadlock.
r: It was announced in the Constituent Assembly in October 1953.

q: What does the adjective intimate mean? (8)
f: Intimate describes a very close, familiar relationship or a detailed, deep knowledge of something.
r: Intimate can also be a verb meaning to hint at something indirectly, pronounced differently.

q: Amjad and Ahmad together kept 24 balls. Amjad kept three times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep? (8)
f: Let Ahmad keep x balls, so Amjad keeps 3x. Then x + 3x = 24, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
r: Amjad therefore kept 18 balls, and 18 is three times 6.

q: Roughly what fraction of the Earth's land surface is covered by deserts (arid regions)? (8)
f: Deserts and arid lands cover roughly one third of the Earth's land surface.
r: Sources differ depending on how a desert is defined.

q: Which is the highest mountain in the world? (8)
f: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China border, is the highest mountain above sea level.
r: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically? (8)
f: Alphabetical order is A D E E G M N T U, so the third letter is E.
r: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E appearing twice.

q: Against whom was the War of Independence of 1857 (Jang-e-Azadi) fought by the people of the subcontinent? (8)
f: The 1857 revolt was an uprising of Indian soldiers and people against British East India Company rule.
r: The British called it the Mutiny, while Muslims and Hindus of the subcontinent call it the War of Independence.

q: What name did the British give to the War of Independence of 1857? (8)
f: The British called the events of 1857 the Sepoy Mutiny (or Indian Mutiny) because it began with Indian soldiers in the Company army.
r: Muslims and Indian nationalists call it the War of Independence.

q: Where was Abdul Sattar Edhi born? (8)
f: Edhi was born in 1928 in Bantva in Gujarat, British India, and migrated to Pakistan after Partition.
r: His family belonged to the Memon community.

q: How many farz (obligatory acts) does Namaz have according to the Hanafi school? (8)
f: Namaz has 13 farz: 6 outside the prayer (conditions such as cleanliness, covering the body, facing the Qibla, time and intention) and 7 inside it (such as takbeer, qiyam, qira'at, ruku, sajdah, qa'da akhira).
r: Wajibat of Namaz are different from farz, and leaving a farz makes the prayer invalid.

q: Who was the first Governor of the North-West Frontier Province (now KPK) after the creation of Pakistan? (8)
f: Sir George Cunningham was appointed Governor of NWFP in August 1947 at the creation of Pakistan.
r: Cunningham also served as governor before independence, in 1937-1946.

q: In which month of the Hijri calendar was the Treaty of Hudaibiya signed (6 AH)? (8)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) set out for Umrah in Dhul Qadah 6 AH and the treaty was signed with Quraysh at Hudaibiya in that month.
r: The treaty set a ten-year truce and Muslims performed Umrah the following year.

q: Which party won a majority of seats in East Pakistan in the 1970 general elections? (8)
f: The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 of the 162 East Pakistan seats.
r: The Pakistan People's Party won the most seats in West Pakistan.

q: Who is the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional from Pakistan? (8)
f: Arfa Karim Randhawa became a Microsoft Certified Professional at the age of nine in 2004. She was the youngest in the world at that time.
r: She died in 2012 and the Arfa Karim Software Technology Park in Lahore is named after her.

q: Who is the head of state of Jordan? (8)
f: Jordan is a monarchy and King Abdullah II is its head of state, so it has no president.
r: King Abdullah II has ruled since 1999 after the death of his father King Hussein.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan was the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan first used? (8)
f: The 1956 Constitution, Pakistan's first, named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan. Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.
r: The 1962 Constitution changed the name to the Republic of Pakistan, and the 1973 Constitution restored Islamic Republic of Pakistan.

q: Who demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency in the Muslim proposals of the 1920s? (8)
f: Jinnah included the separation of Sindh from Bombay in the Delhi Muslim Proposals of 1927 and again in his Fourteen Points of 1929.
r: Sindh was actually separated from the Bombay Presidency in 1936 and became a separate province.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day is the 15th of that month? (8)
f: From the 4th to the 15th is 11 days. 11 = 7 + 4, so the day is 4 days after Tuesday, which is Saturday.
r: Counting the difference in dates and taking the remainder after dividing by 7 solves every such day question.

q: By what other name is Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) known? (8)
f: Yaqoob (AS) is also called Israel, meaning servant of Allah, and his descendants are the Bani Israel.
r: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS).

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes? (8)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: What is the name of China's currency? (8)
f: China's official currency is the renminbi, whose main unit is the yuan.
r: The word renminbi means the people's currency.

q: Which lake is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake? (8)
f: Lake Turkana in northern Kenya lies in a desert region and is the largest permanent desert lake, nicknamed the Jade Sea.
r: It is a very alkaline lake in the Great Rift Valley.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest? (8)
f: Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
r: Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.

q: Where is the headquarters of the African Union located? (8)
f: The African Union has its headquarters in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
r: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity in 2002.

q: With the help of which country did Pakistan carry out the Saindak project? (8)
f: The Saindak copper-gold project in Balochistan was developed with Chinese help by the Metallurgical Corporation of China.
r: Saindak is in Chagai district, Balochistan.

q: On which river is the city of Kabul located? (8)
f: The city of Kabul stands on the banks of the Kabul River.
r: The Kabul River flows into Pakistan and joins the Indus near Attock.

q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of SAARC? (8)
f: Pakistan was one of the seven founding members of SAARC at the Dhaka summit on 8 December 1985. It did not join later.
r: Afghanistan became the eighth member in April 2007.

q: What is the minimum age to become President of Pakistan? (8)
f: Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution says the President must be a Muslim, qualified to be a National Assembly member and at least 45 years old.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how many papers does he write in one minute? (8)
f: Rate is 5 papers divided by 5 minutes, which is 1 paper per minute.
r: Rate equals work divided by time.

q: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar served as the Governor of which province of Pakistan? (8)
f: Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement, was Governor of Punjab from 1949 to 1951.
r: Nishtar Medical University in Multan is named after him.

q: In which Hijri year was Zakat made obligatory? (8)
f: According to the commonly taught view, Zakat became obligatory in the second year of Hijri, around the time Ramadan fasting was ordained. Some scholars give slightly different years.
r: Sources differ a little on the exact year of Zakat.

q: In which city is the Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force located? (8)
f: The Air Headquarters of the Pakistan Air Force is in Islamabad. The PAF Air Command and Staff College is at Karachi.
r: The Pakistan Air Force Academy is at Risalpur.

q: In which year was the 18th Amendment to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan passed? (8)
f: The 18th Amendment was passed by Parliament in April 2010 and signed by President Zardari. It transferred many powers from the centre to the provinces.
r: It renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly under 58(2)(b).

q: What is the antonym of superiority? (8)
f: Superiority means being higher in quality or rank; the opposite is inferiority.
r: The terms inferiority complex and superiority complex were popularised by the psychologist Alfred Adler.

q: Into which sea does the Indus River flow? (8)
f: The Indus River flows through Pakistan and falls into the Arabian Sea near Karachi in Sindh.
r: The Indus delta is near Thatta.

q: What was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) of Pakistan, Iran and Turkey renamed as in 1985? (8)
f: The RCD was revived and renamed the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985 by its three founding members.
r: ECO later expanded in 1992 to include Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

q: Which is the largest temple in the world? (8)
f: Angkor Wat in Cambodia covers about 162 hectares and is the largest religious monument in the world.
r: Angkor Wat was built in the 12th century by King Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu and later a Buddhist temple.

q: In which city is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations located? (8)
f: The FAO has its headquarters in Rome, Italy. It leads international efforts against hunger and works on food and agriculture.
r: The FAO was founded in 1945 and its World Food Day is observed on 16 October.

q: In which year did the Muslims of the subcontinent get the right of separate electorates? (8)
f: Separate electorates were granted to the Muslims by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
r: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 later made the Congress accept separate electorates.

q: What is the antonym of protect? (8)
f: To protect is to keep safe from harm; the opposite is to endanger, to put in harm's way.
r: Defend, guard and shield are synonyms of protect.

q: Bani Israel (Children of Israel) are the descendants of which prophet, whose title was Israel? (8)
f: Israel was the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS), and his twelve sons formed the twelve tribes of Bani Israel. Hence the people are called Bani Israel.
r: Hazrat Musa (AS) is the most prominent prophet sent to Bani Israel.

q: The Flemish people are found mainly in which country? (8)
f: The Flemish are the Dutch-speaking people of Flanders, the northern region of Belgium.
r: The French-speaking people of southern Belgium are called Walloons.

q: To which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate in 622 AD? (8)
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, which was then called Yathrib.
r: This migration, the Hijrah, marks the start of the Islamic Hijri calendar.

q: Which is the second highest mountain in the world? (8)
f: K2, at about 8,611 m, is the second highest mountain in the world after Mount Everest.
r: K2 is the highest mountain of Pakistan and lies in the Karakoram range.

q: Rearrange the letters RAPIS to form the name of a famous capital city. Which city is it, and of which country is it the capital? (8)
f: The letters R, A, P, I, S rearrange to make PARIS. Paris is the capital of France.
r: Paris stands on the River Seine and is the capital of France.

q: What was the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922? (8)
o: A mob burned a police station and killed policemen, after which Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement
A massacre of unarmed people at a garden in Amritsar
A mutiny of Indian soldiers in Meerut
A salt march to the sea
f: On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh a crowd set fire to a police station, killing about 22 policemen. Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened earlier, in 1919.

q: What is a Field Marshal? (8)
o: The highest rank in an army
A rank in the navy only
A police officer in charge of a district
f: Field Marshal is the highest (five-star) rank in the army of many countries. It is often given as an honour and is rarely awarded.
r: Ayub Khan became the first and only Field Marshal of Pakistan Army in 1959.

q: On whom is Hajj obligatory (farz)? (8)
o: Every sane, adult Muslim who has the means to travel and afford it
f: Hajj is farz once in a lifetime on a sane, adult (baligh) Muslim who is physically and financially able (istita'at) to make the journey.
r: Hajj is the fifth pillar of Islam.

q: What is the order of the transpose of a matrix of order m x n? (8)
f: The transpose is obtained by interchanging rows and columns, so an m x n matrix becomes n x m.
r: The transpose of the transpose of a matrix gives back the original matrix.

q: When did the USA drop atom bombs on Japan? (8)
f: The USA dropped the atom bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945 and on Nagasaki on 9 August 1945.
r: Japan announced its surrender soon afterwards, ending the Second World War.

q: What is the approximate average lactation period of a buffalo? (8)
f: A buffalo gives milk for about 270 to 305 days after calving, so about 300 days is the usual figure. It varies with breed and feeding.
r: Nili-Ravi is a famous Pakistani buffalo breed known for high milk yield.

q: Which is the only even prime number? (8)
f: A prime number has exactly two factors. Every even number greater than 2 is divisible by 2, so it has more than two factors, which leaves 2 as the only even prime.
r: The number 1 is not a prime number.

q: What is the synonym of germinate? (8)
f: To germinate is to begin to grow from a seed, which is to sprout.
r: Germination is the process by which a seed develops into a seedling.

q: What does Makruh mean in Islamic law? (8)
o: A permitted act with no reward
A disliked act that is better avoided
An act that is strictly forbidden
f: A Makruh act is disliked and discouraged in Islam, but doing it is a lesser matter than a forbidden (Haram) act.
r: Makruh is one of the five categories of rulings: Fard, Mustahab, Mubah, Makruh and Haram.

q: In which month and year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Muslim League and the Indian National Congress? (8)
f: The Lucknow Pact was agreed at the joint sessions of the Congress and the Muslim League in Lucknow in December 1916.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is known as the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for this pact.

q: Pakistani people are equal because of which common bond? (8)
f: Pakistan was created in the name of Islam, and the Islamic teaching of equality unites its people despite different languages and cultures.
r: Pakistan has many languages and dresses but one common faith for the large majority.

q: According to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim, which prophet was a carpenter by profession? (8)
f: Sahih Muslim reports that Hazrat Zakariya (AS) was a carpenter.
r: Hazrat Dawud (AS) made iron armour, and Hazrat Idris (AS) is commonly said to have been a tailor.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and one third of them are men, the rest are women. What is the percentage of women? (8)
f: Women = 2/3 of the passengers. 2/3 x 100 = 66.67 percent.
r: Men are 10 of the 30 passengers and women are 20.

q: What is the meaning of veto power? (8)
o: The right to reject or block a decision
The right to call a meeting
The right to join the UN
f: Veto is Latin for I forbid. It is the power to stop a resolution or decision even if others support it.
r: In the UN Security Council any one of the five permanent members can block a resolution by veto.

q: Who wrote the Urdu poetry book Bang-e-Dara? (8)
f: Bang-e-Dara is the first Urdu poetry collection of Allama Muhammad Iqbal.
r: It was published in 1924.

q: Where is the famous Golden Gate Bridge located? (8)
f: The Golden Gate Bridge spans the Golden Gate strait and connects San Francisco with Marin County in California.
r: It opened in 1937 and is a suspension bridge painted in International Orange.

q: A train moves at a speed of 60 km/hour. How much time will it take to cover 150 km? (8)
f: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 60 = 2.5 hours.
r: 2.5 hours equals 2 hours 30 minutes.

q: Who prepared the Pirpur Report of 1938 on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces? (8)
o: Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur
f: The Pirpur Report was prepared by a Muslim League committee headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur.
r: Fazlul Haq issued a separate report in 1939 called the Sharif Report.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan was enforced in 1962? (8)
o: The second constitution, with a presidential system
The first constitution, with a parliamentary system
The third constitution, with a parliamentary system
f: The 1962 constitution was the second constitution of Pakistan and gave a presidential system with strong powers to the President.
r: It was given by President Ayub Khan and ended in 1969 when Yahya Khan imposed martial law.

q: Akbar is older than Khalid and Ahmed is younger than Khalid. Which statement is true? (8)
f: The order from oldest is Akbar, Khalid, Ahmed. So Akbar is older than Ahmed.
r: Chaining two comparisons gives a third one.

q: Who wrote the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'? (8)
f: Pakistan: The Heart of Asia is a collection of speeches made by Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, during his 1950 visit to the USA.
r: Ayub Khan wrote the autobiography Friends Not Masters.

q: In which district of Sindh is Ranikot Fort (Rani Fort) situated? (8)
f: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills of Jamshoro district in Sindh.
r: Ranikot is often called the largest fort in the world because its wall is about 26 km long.

q: Which two countries are known for the greatest rivalry in Test cricket? (8)
f: England and Australia play the Ashes series, the oldest and most famous rivalry in Test cricket.
r: The Ashes began in 1882 after Australia beat England at The Oval.

q: In which war was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed martyred? (8)
f: Captain Muhammad Sarwar was martyred in the 1948 Kashmir war near Uri in October 1948.
r: He was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: In which year was the Wavell Plan announced? (8)
f: Lord Wavell, the Viceroy, announced his plan in June 1945, and it was discussed at the Simla Conference.
r: The Cripps Mission came earlier, in 1942.

q: In which city is the shrine of the Sufi poet Bulleh Shah located? (8)
f: Bulleh Shah is buried in Kasur, in Punjab.
r: Bulleh Shah wrote his Sufi poetry (kafis) in Punjabi.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word spurn? (8)
f: To spurn means to refuse something with scorn. Reject is the nearest meaning.
r: Spurn can also be used as a noun in old English for a kick, but the common meaning is to refuse.

q: What is the tenure (term) of the National Assembly of Pakistan, unless it is dissolved earlier? (8)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the National Assembly lasts five years from its first meeting. After that it stops working automatically.
r: The Senate is a permanent house and is never dissolved.

q: What is the name of the force that opposes the motion between two bodies in contact? (8)
f: Friction acts between touching surfaces and opposes their relative motion.
r: Friction produces heat.

q: Who was the father of the Mughal emperor Humayun? (8)
f: Humayun was the second Mughal emperor and the son of Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire.
r: Humayun's son Akbar became the third Mughal emperor.

q: Arrange the letters of PLOEADR to make the name of an animal. (8)
f: The letters P, L, O, E, A, D, R make the word LEOPARD, a big cat. It uses all seven letters once.
r: The leopard is a spotted big cat found in Asia and Africa.

q: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet? (8)
f: Romeo and Juliet is a tragedy written by William Shakespeare in the 1590s.
r: Shakespeare also wrote Hamlet, Macbeth and Othello.

q: Zakat is which pillar of Islam? (7)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj, so Zakat is third.
r: Candidates wrote 4, but in the standard order Zakat comes third.

q: What is the currency of Indonesia? (7)
f: Indonesia uses the rupiah.
r: Malaysia uses the ringgit and Thailand the baht.

q: Which word is a synonym of attire? (7)
f: Attire means clothes or dress, so clothing is the synonym.
r: Another synonym of attire is apparel.

q: What is the capital of Chile? (7)
f: Santiago is the capital of Chile.
r: Valparaiso, where the national congress sits, is a major port city but not the capital.

q: What is the currency of Cuba? (7)
f: Cuba uses the Cuban peso (CUP).
r: Cuba formerly had a second currency, the convertible peso (CUC), which was abolished in 2021.

q: Which word is a synonym of evident? (7)
f: Evident means clearly seen or understood, which is obvious.
r: Another synonym is apparent.

q: Where does the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1961 belong, that is, which country was invaded? (7)
f: The Bay of Pigs (Bahia de Cochinos) is on the southern coast of Cuba. In April 1961 CIA-backed Cuban exiles landed there to overthrow Fidel Castro and failed.
r: The failed invasion took place during the presidency of John F. Kennedy and pushed Cuba closer to the Soviet Union.

q: Who is the national poet of Pakistan? (7)
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal is the national poet of Pakistan, called Shair-e-Mashriq.
r: His birthday, 9 November, is observed as Iqbal Day.

q: Who wrote The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam? (7)
f: Allama Iqbal wrote this book, which is based on his lectures delivered in 1928-29.
r: It was first published in 1930 and expanded in 1934.

q: From which institution did Quaid-e-Azam obtain his law degree? (7)
f: Muhammad Ali Jinnah studied at Lincoln's Inn in London and was called to the bar in 1896.
r: He was the youngest Indian to be called to the bar at that time.

q: In which province is Keenjhar Lake located? (7)
f: Keenjhar Lake is near Thatta in Sindh.
r: Keenjhar is one of the largest freshwater lakes in Pakistan and a main water source for Karachi.

q: What is observed on 8 March every year? (7)
f: 8 March is International Women's Day, celebrating women's achievements and rights.
r: International Labour Day is on 1 May.

q: In which year did Pakistan co-host the ICC Cricket World Cup together with India and Sri Lanka? (7)
f: The 1996 World Cup was jointly hosted by Pakistan, India and Sri Lanka.
r: Pakistan also co-hosted the 1987 World Cup with India only.

q: What is the closest meaning of selfless? (7)
f: A selfless person thinks of others before himself, which is what altruistic means.
r: The opposite of selfless is selfish.

q: Who wrote Shah Jo Risalo? (7)
f: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai composed the Sindhi poetry collection Shah Jo Risalo.
r: His shrine is at Bhit Shah in Sindh.

q: The Danube is the second longest river of which continent? (7)
f: The Danube, about 2,850 km long, is the second longest river in Europe after the Volga.
r: It flows into the Black Sea.

q: Which word is a synonym of elation? (7)
f: Elation means great joy or high spirits, so delight is a synonym.
r: Its opposite is dejection.

q: What is the meaning of the word obvious? (7)
f: Something obvious is easy to see or understand and is clear to everyone.
r: Its opposite is obscure or hidden.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)? (7)
f: Hazrat Ishaq (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and Hazrat Sarah.
r: Hazrat Yaqub (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: What was the old name of Sri Lanka? (7)
f: Sri Lanka was known as Ceylon until it was renamed in 1972.
r: Burma is the old name of Myanmar and Siam of Thailand.

q: In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India? (7)
f: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 during the Second World War. He offered dominion status after the war, which the Congress and the Muslim League rejected.
r: The Cabinet Mission was a different mission that came to India in 1946.

q: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC? (7)
f: SAARC has eight members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka. Myanmar is not a member.
r: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985 and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

q: Arrange the letters YEBATU into a meaningful word. (7)
f: The letters Y, E, B, A, T, U rearrange to BEAUTY.
r: BEAUTY has 6 letters, of which E, A and U are vowels.

q: Find the odd one out: Angle, Triangle, Square, Rectangle. (7)
f: Triangle, square and rectangle are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a closed figure.
r: A triangle has three sides and the sum of its angles is 180 degrees.

q: In which surah is the longest verse of the Holy Quran? (7)
f: The longest verse is Ayat ad-Dayn (verse 282) about written contracts of debt, in Surah Al-Baqarah.
r: Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255 of the same surah.

q: Under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty, which rivers were allotted to Pakistan? (7)
f: The treaty gave the three western rivers, Indus, Jhelum and Chenab, to Pakistan and the three eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej, to India.
r: The treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 and mediated by the World Bank.

q: What is the meaning of Wudu (Wuzu)? (7)
o: Ablution, the ritual washing before prayer
f: Wudu means ablution, the washing of the face, hands, head and feet before prayer, from a root meaning cleanliness.
r: In the Hanafi school wudu has four faraiz, as stated in Surah Al-Maidah.

q: In which region of Pakistan does the River Soan flow? (7)
f: The Soan rises in the Murree hills and flows through the Potohar Plateau near Rawalpindi and Islamabad before joining the Indus.
r: The Soan valley is known for Stone Age sites.

q: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which companion? (7)
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), the first Caliph.
r: Her mother was Umm Ruman and she is known as Siddiqa bint Siddiq.

q: ICAO is a specialized agency of which organization? (7)
f: The International Civil Aviation Organization is a specialized agency of the United Nations dealing with civil aviation standards.
r: ICAO is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.

q: In which city of Pakistan does the Orange Line Metro Train run? (7)
f: The Orange Line Metro Train is a rapid transit line in Lahore, built with Chinese financing under CPEC and opened in 2020.
r: It is Pakistan's first modern metro train system.

q: In which city did the tribes of Bani Aus and Bani Khazraj live? (7)
f: Aus and Khazraj were the two main Arab tribes of Yathrib, later named Madinah, and they accepted Islam after the Pledges of Aqaba.
r: They are known as the Ansar (helpers) of Madinah.

q: In which year did Pakistan last win the Hockey World Cup? (7)
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994, the last of these in Sydney in 1994.
r: Pakistan is the most successful team in World Cup history along with the Netherlands, with four titles each.

q: The Simla Conference of 1945 was held on 25 June 1945 under which Viceroy? (7)
f: Viceroy Lord Wavell called the conference at Simla to discuss his plan for an Executive Council with Indian members.
r: It failed because Congress and the Muslim League disagreed over the choice of Muslim members.

q: On whom was the Zaboor (Psalms) revealed? (7)
f: The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS).
r: Hazrat Dawud (AS) was also a king, and his son Hazrat Sulaiman (AS) was a prophet too.

q: The word Everyone is what part of speech? (7)
f: Everyone stands in place of a noun (all people), so it is an indefinite pronoun.
r: Other indefinite pronouns are someone, anybody and nobody.

q: Towards which place was the first Hijrat of the Muslims made? (7)
f: In 615 AD a small group of Muslims migrated from Makkah to Habsha (Abyssinia) to escape persecution by the Quraysh. Its Christian king, the Negus, gave them protection.
r: The migration to Madina came about seven years later, in 622 AD.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'evacuate'? (7)
f: To evacuate is to leave or empty a place, especially because of danger.
r: Evacuate comes from the Latin word vacuare, meaning to empty.

q: Which is the largest bone of the human body? (7)
f: The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone in the human body.
r: The smallest bone is the stapes in the middle ear.

q: Which continent is known as the Dark Continent? (7)
f: Africa was called the Dark Continent because its interior was unknown to Europeans for a long time.
r: The nickname became popular through the explorer Henry Morton Stanley.

q: Which strait separates Russia and the United States (Alaska)? (7)
f: The Bering Strait lies between the Chukchi Peninsula of Russia and Alaska in the United States.
r: It connects the Pacific and Arctic oceans and is about 85 km wide.

q: What is the rate of zakat on gold and silver (above nisab)? (7)
f: Zakat on gold, silver and cash savings above nisab is one-fortieth, which is 2.5 percent.
r: Nisab for gold is about 7.5 tola (87.48 grams) and for silver 52.5 tola.

q: Which country is called the largest democracy in the world? (7)
f: India has the largest electorate and the largest population of any democracy. It is called the world's largest democracy.
r: India overtook China as the world's most populous country in 2023.

q: Which Pakistani army operation was launched nationwide in February 2017? (7)
f: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was announced on 22 February 2017 after a wave of terror attacks across Pakistan.
r: Zarb-e-Azb began in June 2014 and Rah-e-Rast in 2009.

q: Which of the following was a daughter of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (7)
f: The four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (RA). Aisha, Hafsa and Khadija (RA) were his wives.
r: All the daughters were born to Hazrat Khadija (RA).

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day is the 25th day of that month? (7)
f: From the 4th to the 25th is 21 days, and 21 divided by 7 leaves remainder 0. Moving 0 day(s) forward from Friday gives Friday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: What is a chord that passes through the centre of a circle called? (7)
f: A chord through the centre is the longest chord of the circle and is called the diameter.
r: The diameter is twice the radius.

q: What is the antonym of applaud? (7)
f: To applaud is to show approval or praise, so its opposite is to criticize or condemn.
r: Praise, cheer and admire are synonyms of applaud.

q: Bashar al-Assad was the president of which country? (7)
f: Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until his government fell in December 2024.
r: He succeeded his father Hafez al-Assad, who ruled Syria from 1971 to 2000.

q: Which country developed the Sinopharm vaccine against Covid-19? (7)
f: Sinopharm is a state-owned Chinese pharmaceutical company, and its BBIBP-CorV vaccine was developed in China.
r: Pakistan used the Chinese Sinopharm and CanSino vaccines in its Covid-19 vaccination drive.

q: Which desert is located in Sindh? (7)
f: The Thar Desert, also called the Great Indian Desert, is in the Tharparkar region of Sindh and is the largest desert of Sindh.
r: Thar is also home to the largest coal reserves of Pakistan.

q: Who is the President of Israel? (7)
f: Isaac Herzog was elected the 11th President of Israel in June 2021 and is still in office.
r: His predecessor was Reuven Rivlin, and the presidency is largely ceremonial.

q: In which city of Pakistan was the first Metro Bus service inaugurated? (7)
f: The Metro Bus Service was inaugurated in Lahore in February 2013. It runs between Gajju Matta and Shahdara.
r: Rawalpindi-Islamabad followed in 2015 and Multan in 2017.

q: What is the meaning of the word prescribe? (7)
o: To recommend or order as a remedy or rule
f: To prescribe means to advise or order something, such as a medicine or a rule. Its synonyms include recommend, advise and ordain.
r: A doctor writes a prescription to prescribe medicine.

q: Which is the national airline of Pakistan? (7)
f: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) is the national flag carrier of Pakistan, established in 1955.
r: PIA operated its first flight in 1955 and is headquartered in Karachi.

q: In a bus of 24 people, 2/3 are male. What percentage are female? (7)
f: Males are 2/3 of 24 = 16, so females are 24 - 16 = 8. Percentage = 8/24 x 100 = 33.33 percent.
r: Females are 1/3 of the bus because the two fractions add up to 1.

q: On whose advice does the President of Pakistan dissolve the National Assembly under the Constitution as it stands today? (7)
f: Under Article 58 the President dissolves the National Assembly only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
r: Before the 18th Amendment of 2010 the President could also dissolve it on his own discretion under Article 58(2)(b).

q: What is the term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan? (7)
f: The National Assembly has a term of five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier.
r: A Senator has a term of six years.

q: Which is the fastest land (terrestrial) animal? (7)
f: The cheetah is the fastest land animal and can run at about 100 to 110 km per hour in short bursts.
r: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird in a dive.

q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have? (7)
f: According to authentic hadith, Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
r: Jahannam, by contrast, has seven gates.

q: Which language is the lingua franca (common link language) of Pakistan? (7)
f: Urdu is understood across all provinces and links people of different mother tongues. It is also the national language.
r: Punjabi is the most widely spoken mother tongue in Pakistan.

q: Who is Mark Zuckerberg? (7)
f: Mark Zuckerberg co-founded Facebook in 2004 and is the CEO of its parent company Meta.
r: Facebook was renamed as Meta Platforms in 2021.

q: What does OGRA stand for? (7)
f: OGRA stands for the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority, which regulates the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector of Pakistan.
r: OGRA was established in 2002 and has its head office in Islamabad.

q: In which year did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman? (7)
f: Pakistan bought the Gwadar enclave from the Sultan of Oman in 1958, and it was formally handed over on 8 December 1958.
r: Gwadar became part of Balochistan province in 1977.

q: What is the meaning of the word refute? (7)
f: To refute a claim is to prove it wrong. Synonyms include disprove, rebut and counter.
r: Refute is sometimes wrongly used to mean simply deny.

q: What is a synonym of acute? (7)
f: Acute can mean sharp or intense, as in acute pain, and severe is the closest synonym.
r: Acute angle means an angle less than 90 degrees.

q: When was the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) founded? (7)
f: The Non-Aligned Movement was formally founded at the Belgrade Summit in September 1961 by leaders such as Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Nkrumah and Sukarno.
r: The movement grew out of the 1955 Bandung Conference.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word brilliant? (7)
f: Brilliant means very bright or very intelligent, and its opposite is dull.
r: Synonyms of brilliant include bright, radiant and gifted.

q: Who was the third caliph of Islam? (7)
f: The order of the Rightly Guided Caliphs is Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. So the third was Hazrat Uthman (RA).
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) is called Ghani and Zun-Noorain.

q: How many copies of the Quran were prepared by Hazrat Usman (RA) and sent to different regions? (7)
f: Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies prepared from the Abu Bakr copy and sent them to major centres; most Pakistani textbooks say five copies.
r: Some sources say seven copies, including one kept in Madina, so sources differ.

q: Against whom did Nawab Siraj ud Daula fight the Battle of Plassey in 1757? (7)
f: The British East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, helped by the betrayal of Mir Jafar.
r: The battle marked the beginning of British rule in India.

q: Kathmandu is the capital of which country? (7)
f: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal.
r: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan.

q: What is the antonym of provoke? (7)
f: Provoke means to make someone angry or stir them up; the opposite is to pacify or calm them.
r: Appease and soothe are also antonyms of provoke.

q: My brother's son's sister is my what? (7)
f: My brother's son is my nephew, and his sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
r: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of abolish? (7)
f: To abolish a law or system means to formally put an end to it, which is to do away with it.
r: Annul, scrap and repeal are other synonyms of abolish.

q: Which Sahabi was appointed by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) as governor of Yemen? (7)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) sent Hazrat Muadh bin Jabal (RA) to Yemen as governor, judge and teacher of the people.
r: Before he left, the Prophet (PBUH) asked him how he would judge, and he replied that he would use the Quran, then the Sunnah, then his own reasoning.

q: Who is the Governor of Balochistan (as of 2026)? (7)
f: Jaffar Khan Mandokhail is serving as Governor of Balochistan in 2026.
r: Sarfraz Bugti is the Chief Minister, not the Governor.

q: Pakistan's economy is predominantly based on which sector? (7)
f: Agriculture is the backbone of Pakistan's economy, supporting a large share of employment and exports like textiles from cotton.
r: Services now form the largest share of GDP, but agriculture remains the traditional base.

q: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh during the rule of which dynasty? (7)
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 AD during the reign of the Umayyad caliph Walid bin Abdul Malik. The Mughals came centuries later.
r: Hajjaj bin Yusuf was the Umayyad governor of Iraq who sent him.

q: In which year was the East India Company first established? (7)
f: The English East India Company received its royal charter from Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.
r: The Company won control of Bengal after the Battle of Plassey in 1757.

q: What is cosec x multiplied by tan x equal to? (7)
f: Cosec x . tan x = (1/sin x)(sin x/cos x) = 1/cos x = sec x.
r: Tan x equals sin x divided by cos x.

q: How many Nobel Prizes in Physics has Pakistan received so far? (7)
f: Dr Abdus Salam received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. No other Pakistani has won in Physics.
r: Dr Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate and Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

q: On which date of Ramadan was Makkah conquered (Fath-e-Makkah) in 8 AH? (7)
f: Most Pakistani textbooks give 20 Ramadan 8 AH (January 630 CE) for the conquest of Makkah, when the Muslims entered the city peacefully.
r: Some sources give other dates in Ramadan such as 10 or 17.

q: What was the name of the paternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (7)
f: The Prophet's father was Abdullah, and Abdullah's father was Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's paternal grandfather.
r: Abdul Muttalib was the son of Hashim and the one who rediscovered the Zamzam well.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have? (7)
f: The word hexagon comes from the Greek hex meaning six, so it has six sides.
r: The sum of the interior angles of a hexagon is 720 degrees.

q: What is the process by which water vapour is lost from the leaves of a plant? (7)
f: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.
r: It helps pull water up the plant and cools the leaves.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan? (7)
f: Article 62 requires a candidate for the National Assembly to be at least 25 years old. A voter must be 18.
r: Candidates for the Senate must be at least 30 years old.

q: What is the real part of the complex number 6 - 9i? (7)
f: In a + bi form, the real part is the term without i. Here it is 6.
r: The conjugate of 6 - 9i is 6 + 9i.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 7? (7)
f: 2.6 x 2.6 = 6.76 and 2.7 x 2.7 = 7.29, so the root lies between them; 2.65 x 2.65 = 7.02 so it is about 2.65.
r: The square root of 7 is an irrational number, about 2.6458.

q: Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now? (7)
f: Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
r: A left turn from north would point him to the west.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th be? (7)
f: From the 1st to the 19th is 18 days. 18 days is 2 full weeks plus 4 day(s), so the day is 4 day(s) after Monday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: What is 4 + 4x4? (7)
f: Multiplication comes first: 4x4 = 16. Then 4 + 16 = 20.
r: Following BODMAS, 4 + 4x4 is not (4 + 4)x4 which would be 32.

q: What is the antonym of error? (7)
f: An error is a mistake, so the opposite is accuracy or correctness.
r: Mistake, fault and blunder are synonyms of error.

q: Fill in the blank: We have business classes ______ night. (7)
f: The preposition 'at' is used with night in the phrase 'at night'.
r: We say in the morning, in the evening, but at night.

q: Who is the current Chancellor of Germany? (7)
f: Friedrich Merz of the CDU became Chancellor in May 2025 and was still in office in October 2026.
r: His predecessor was Olaf Scholz (2021 to 2025), and before him Angela Merkel served from 2005 to 2021.

q: On which hills is the city of Islamabad situated? (7)
f: Islamabad lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills, part of the Himalayan foothills.
r: Faisal Mosque is at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

q: What is the additive inverse of the ordered pair (-a, -b)? (7)
f: The additive inverse is the pair that gives (0, 0) when added. (-a, -b) + (a, b) = (0, 0), so the answer is (a, b).
r: The additive identity of ordered pairs is (0, 0).

q: What is the capital of Iran? (7)
f: Tehran is the capital and largest city of Iran.
r: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan.

q: What is the meaning of the Urdu/Arabic word 'Seerat'? (7)
f: Seerat means a person's life, conduct and character, and is used mainly for the biography of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). It is also written as Seerah.
r: The earliest well-known Seerat of the Prophet (PBUH) was written by Ibn Ishaq and edited by Ibn Hisham.

q: Which word is a synonym of provoke? (7)
f: To provoke means to stir up a strong reaction, which is the same as to incite.
r: Instigate and arouse are other synonyms of provoke.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Ali (RA) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)? (7)
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle, so he was a cousin. He married the Prophet's daughter Hazrat Fatima (RA).
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 9? (7)
f: One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
r: Equivalently 9 divided by 30 equals 0.3.

q: Which is the third surah of the Holy Quran? (7)
f: The order is Al-Fatiha, Al-Baqarah, Al-Imran, so the third surah is Al-Imran.
r: An-Nisa is the fourth surah.

q: What is the line that touches a circle at exactly one point called? (7)
f: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, while a secant cuts it at two points.
r: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice the age of Salman. When Salman is 12 years old, what will be the age of Ali? (7)
f: Ali is 2 x 4 = 8 now, so he is 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16.
r: Do not double the later age; only the present ages are in the ratio 2 to 1.

q: What was the code name of Pakistan's nuclear tests conducted in May 1998? (7)
f: Pakistan's tests at Chagai in Balochistan were named Chagai-I (28 May 1998, five tests) and Chagai-II (30 May 1998, one test).
r: Pakistan observes 28 May as Youm-e-Takbeer; Smiling Buddha was the code name of India's 1974 test.

q: Who was the first ambassador of Pakistan to the United States? (7)
f: Mirza Abol Hassan Ispahani, a close associate of Jinnah, was the first Pakistani ambassador to the USA. He served until 1952.
r: Sources differ on whether he took up the post in 1947 or 1948; he later served as High Commissioner to Britain.

q: Tallinn is the capital of which country? (7)
f: Tallinn is the capital and largest city of Estonia, on the Gulf of Finland.
r: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are the three Baltic states.

q: In which country did noodles originate? (7)
f: The oldest known noodles, about 4000 years old, were found at the Lajia site in China, and China is generally credited with their origin.
r: Italy and China have long argued about the origin of pasta and noodles.

q: The word 'terrorism' was first used in connection with which historical event? (7)
f: The term came into use in the 1790s for the Reign of Terror of the Jacobins in revolutionary France.
r: Sources differ on the exact year, with 1794 and 1795 both quoted.

q: The determinant of the transpose of a square matrix A is equal to what? (7)
o: Negative of the determinant of A
The inverse of the determinant of A
f: Interchanging rows and columns does not change the determinant, so det(A transpose) = det(A).
r: Also det(AB) = det(A) x det(B) for square matrices of the same order.

q: Kalimullah (the one who spoke with Allah) is the title of which prophet? (7)
f: Hazrat Musa (AS) spoke directly with Allah on Mount Tur, so he is called Kalimullah.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah and Hazrat Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah.

q: According to the 2017 census, what was the population of Pakistan? (7)
f: The 6th Population and Housing Census of 2017 counted 207,684,626 people in Pakistan.
r: The next census, held in 2023, counted about 241.5 million people.

q: What is the antonym of appropriate? (7)
f: Appropriate means suitable for the situation; the opposite is inappropriate or unsuitable.
r: Suitable, fitting and proper are synonyms of appropriate.

q: In which direction is China located with respect to Pakistan? (7)
f: China lies to the north-east of Pakistan and borders Gilgit-Baltistan through the Khunjerab Pass.
r: The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan and China across the Khunjerab Pass.

q: The Kirthar Hills (Kirthar Range) lie along the border of which two provinces of Pakistan? (7)
f: The Kirthar Range runs north to south and forms the boundary between Sindh and Balochistan. It is the southern part of the Sulaiman-Kirthar system.
r: Zardak Peak (about 2,260 m) is generally named as its highest point, though sources differ slightly.

q: On which date is Labour Day (International Workers' Day) observed? (7)
f: Labour Day is observed every year on 1 May, including in Pakistan, where it is a public holiday.
r: The day commemorates the Haymarket affair of Chicago in 1886.

q: Near which city is Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay during Hajj, located? (7)
f: Mina is a valley about 5 km east of Makkah in Saudi Arabia. Pilgrims stay there and perform the stoning of the Jamarat.
r: Arafat and Muzdalifah are the other nearby sites of the Hajj rites.
