q: What is the height of Nanga Parbat, the ninth highest mountain in the world? (7)
f: Nanga Parbat rises to 8,126 metres (26,660 feet) above sea level. It is the ninth highest mountain in the world.
r: Nanga Parbat is also called Diamer, meaning huge mountain, and is the second highest peak in Pakistan after K2.

q: Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440? (7)
f: Johannes Gutenberg of Germany developed the movable-type printing press in the mid-1400s.
r: Movable type had earlier been used in China and Korea, but Gutenberg's press is the textbook answer.

q: Which of the following is a fard (obligatory) act of wudu according to the Hanafi school? (7)
o: Washing the hands up to the wrists
f: The four faraiz of wudu are washing the face, washing both arms up to the elbows, wiping a quarter of the head, and washing both feet up to the ankles. Gargling and rinsing the nose are sunnah.
r: The four faraiz of wudu are taken from verse 6 of Surah Al-Ma'idah.

q: What is a composite number? (7)
o: A number with exactly two factors
A positive integer greater than 1 with more than two factors
A number that is not divisible by 2
A number with only one factor
f: A composite number has at least one factor other than 1 and itself, so it has more than two factors. Examples are 4, 6, 8 and 9.
r: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite.

q: Which river is the deepest river in the world? (7)
f: The Congo River in Africa has been measured at depths of more than 220 metres, making it the deepest known river.
r: The Amazon carries the largest volume of water, while the Nile is often listed as the longest river.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd be? (7)
f: From the 4th to the 23rd is 19 days. 19 = 2 weeks and 5 extra days, so count 5 days forward from Sunday to reach Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: In a class of 500 students, 360 are present. How many students are absent? (7)
f: Absent students = 500 - 360 = 140.
r: As a percentage, 140 out of 500 is 28%.

q: On which date was the first Constitution of Pakistan (1956) adopted by the Constituent Assembly? (7)
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the 1956 Constitution on 29 February 1956.
r: It came into force on 23 March 1956, which is why that day was celebrated as Republic Day.

q: Muslim Bagh in Balochistan is famous for which mineral? (7)
f: Muslim Bagh in Zhob district of Balochistan is known for its chromite (chromium ore) deposits. Chromite is mined there on a large scale.
r: Chamalang in Balochistan is known for coal and Saindak for copper and gold.

q: How many times has Pakistan won the Hockey Champions Trophy? (7)
f: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy three times, in 1978, 1980 and 1994.
r: Australia is the most successful team in the tournament history, with 14 titles.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'proceeding' as used in 'The work is proceeding well'? (7)
f: To proceed means to go on or move forward, so proceeding means advancing or continuing.
r: As a noun, proceedings means the events of a meeting or a legal action.

q: In which district of Punjab is Kalabagh located? (7)
f: Kalabagh is a town on the Indus River in Mianwali district, Punjab.
r: The proposed Kalabagh Dam site is near this town.

q: What is the commonly quoted length of the Pakistan-Iran border? (7)
f: The Pakistan-Iran border is commonly given as about 909 km. It separates Balochistan from Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province.
r: Some sources give about 959 km, so figures differ slightly by source.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate from Makkah to Madina? (7)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in 570 AD and migrated in 622 AD, which is commonly given as 53 years of age in Pakistani textbooks.
r: Some sources say 52 years because of differences in counting the years.

q: What is the synonym of liberal? (7)
f: Liberal can mean giving freely or in large amounts, which is generous.
r: Liberal also means open to new ideas, so sources may give broad-minded as another synonym.

q: Who is Pakistan's highest run scorer in Test cricket? (7)
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs and is the leading Pakistani Test run scorer.
r: He passed Javed Miandad's 8,832 runs in 2015 and was the first Pakistani to reach 10,000 Test runs.

q: On which side of Punjab is the Cholistan Desert located? (7)
f: The Cholistan Desert lies in the south of Punjab near Bahawalpur, along the border with India.
r: It is also called Rohi, and it is part of the greater Thar Desert.

q: On which date was the Legal Framework Order (LFO) issued by President Yahya Khan? (7)
f: President General Yahya Khan issued the Legal Framework Order on 30 March 1970 to arrange the first general elections on the basis of one man one vote. It also ended the One Unit.
r: Some sources give 28 March 1970, the date of its announcement; a different LFO was issued by General Pervez Musharraf in 2002.

q: What is the meaning of the word ominous? (7)
o: Threatening, suggesting that something bad will happen
f: Ominous describes something that gives a sign of coming trouble or danger. For example, ominous dark clouds suggest a storm.
r: Synonyms of ominous include threatening, sinister and foreboding.

q: Which is the smallest of the five rivers of Punjab (Pakistan) in length? (7)
f: The Ravi is about 720 km long, the shortest of the five rivers, and is commonly called the smallest river of Pakistan in textbooks.
r: The Jhelum is only slightly longer, at about 725 km, so some sources give slightly different rankings.

q: Geographically, Greenland belongs to which continent? (7)
f: Greenland lies on the North American continental shelf, although politically it is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
r: Greenland is the largest island in the world.

q: In which year did the British occupy Punjab? (7)
f: The British defeated the Sikhs in the Second Anglo-Sikh War and annexed Punjab in 1849.
r: Sindh had been annexed earlier, in 1843.

q: What is the sum of two supplementary angles? (7)
f: Two angles are supplementary when they add up to 180 degrees, for example 110 and 70.
r: Two angles that add up to 90 degrees are called complementary angles.

q: Manchar Lake, the largest freshwater lake of Pakistan, is located in which district of Sindh? (7)
f: Manchar Lake lies in Dadu district of Sindh, west of the Indus River near Sehwan.
r: It is among the largest freshwater lakes in South Asia.

q: In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, die? (7)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated on 16 October 1951 at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
r: Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

q: What is the power set of the empty set? (7)
o: The set containing 0 and the empty set
The set containing the empty set
f: The empty set has one subset, itself, so its power set has 2 to the power 0 = 1 element, namely the set containing the empty set.
r: A set with n elements has 2 to the power n subsets.

q: What is the derivative of ln x with respect to x? (7)
f: The natural logarithm ln x has derivative 1/x for x greater than zero. This is a standard result of calculus.
r: The derivative of e to the power x is e to the power x itself.

q: Which group of vitamins does not dissolve in water? (7)
f: Vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble. They dissolve in fat and not in water.
r: Vitamins B-complex and C are water-soluble.

q: What is an identity matrix? (7)
o: A square matrix with all elements zero
A square matrix with 1 on the main diagonal and 0 elsewhere
A matrix with only one row
A matrix with all elements equal to 1
f: An identity matrix is a square matrix whose main diagonal elements are all 1 and all other elements are 0.
r: Multiplying any matrix by the identity matrix of a suitable size leaves it unchanged.

q: What is another name for the Lahore Resolution of 1940? (7)
f: The Lahore Resolution, passed on 23 March 1940, demanded separate Muslim states and is also called the Pakistan Resolution.
r: It was moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq at the Muslim League session at Minto Park, Lahore.

q: Who was the companion of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W.) in the Cave of Thawr during the Hijrat? (7)
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddiq (R.A.) accompanied the Prophet (S.A.W.) and hid with him in the Cave of Thawr during the migration to Madinah.
r: Hazrat Ali (R.A.) stayed in Makkah in the Prophet's bed that night.

q: In which direction from Karachi is Mohenjo-daro located? (7)
f: Mohenjo-daro is near Larkana in northern Sindh, which lies north-east of Karachi. It is on the right bank of the Indus river.
r: Mohenjo-daro was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980.

q: Who is the current Governor of Punjab (as of October 2026)? (7)
f: Sardar Saleem Haider Khan of the PPP took oath as Governor of Punjab on 10 May 2024 and still holds the post.
r: Before him the governor was Baligh-ur-Rehman, and earlier Chaudhry Muhammad Sarwar.

q: On what basis is the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chosen? (7)
o: Elected by the members of the Provincial Assembly, as the leader of the majority
Elected directly by the people of the province
f: Under Article 130 of the Constitution, the Provincial Assembly elects the Chief Minister, who must command the confidence of the majority of members.
r: The Governor of the province appoints the person elected by the assembly.

q: On a farm, goats are double the cows and camels are double the goats. If there are 10 goats, how many animals are on the farm? (7)
f: Goats are 10, so cows are 10 / 2 = 5 and camels are 10 x 2 = 20. Total is 5 + 10 + 20 = 35.
r: Always find the base quantity first, then work out the others.

q: Who was the Finance Minister in the interim government of British India in 1946, before independence? (7)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan held the finance portfolio in the interim government formed in October 1946. His budget was nicknamed the poor man's budget.
r: Liaquat Ali Khan later became the first Prime Minister of Pakistan.

q: If 7 books cost 3500 rupees, what is the price of 1 book? (7)
f: Price of 1 book = 3500 divided by 7 = 500 rupees.
r: This is the unitary method: find the price of one item first.

q: In a bus, 2/3 of the passengers are men. What is the percentage of women? (7)
f: Women are 1 minus 2/3 = 1/3 of the passengers. 1/3 of 100 = 33.33%.
r: Percentage = fraction multiplied by 100.

q: What is the meaning of 'doomed'? (7)
f: Doomed means certain to meet a bad end or failure.
r: Doom also refers to death or destruction.

q: Which of the following books was written by Altaf Hussain Hali? (7)
f: Altaf Hussain Hali wrote the long poem Musaddas, also called Madd-o-Jazr-e-Islam, in 1879. Bang-e-Dra and Shikwa are by Allama Iqbal, and Aab-e-Hayat is by Muhammad Hussain Azad.
r: Hali also wrote Hayat-e-Javed, Yadgar-e-Ghalib and Muqaddama Sher-o-Shayari.

q: The ancient Mehrgarh civilization site, one of the oldest farming settlements in South Asia, is located in which province of Pakistan? (7)
f: Mehrgarh lies on the Kachhi plain near the Bolan Pass in Balochistan.
r: Mehrgarh dates back to about 7000 BC and came before the Indus Valley civilization.

q: What was the real (original) name of Shah Waliullah of Delhi? (7)
f: Shah Waliullah was born as Qutbuddin Ahmad and later became known as Shah Waliullah.
r: He wrote the famous book Hujjat Allah al-Baligha.

q: Which place in Punjab is famous for its salt mountain and salt mine? (7)
f: Khewra in the Salt Range of Jhelum district is famous for the world's second largest salt mine.
r: The Khewra salt mine was discovered in the time of Alexander the Great, according to local tradition.

q: Who is the head of the cabinet in a parliamentary system? (7)
f: In a parliamentary system the Prime Minister leads the cabinet and the government.
r: In Pakistan the President is the head of state, not of the cabinet.

q: In which year was Zulfikar Ali Bhutto hanged? (7)
f: Bhutto was hanged on 4 April 1979, after being removed from power by General Zia ul Haq in July 1977.
r: He was the founder of the Pakistan Peoples Party.

q: Where is the Pakistan Navy War College located? (7)
f: The Pakistan Navy War College is in Lahore.
r: The Pakistan Navy headquarters is in Islamabad.

q: What was the Tashkent Pact (Declaration) of 1966? (7)
o: A peace agreement between Pakistan and India after the 1965 war
A trade treaty between Pakistan and China
A defence pact between Pakistan and the USA
A water treaty on the Indus rivers
f: It was a peace agreement signed on 10 January 1966 in which both sides agreed to withdraw to pre-war positions.
r: The Soviet Union mediated the agreement.

q: In which city is the shrine of Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya located? (7)
f: The shrine of the Sufi saint Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya is in Multan.
r: Multan is known as the City of Saints.

q: When did World War 1 start? (7)
f: World War 1 began in July 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
r: It ended in November 1918.

q: In which district and province is the Tanda Dam located? (7)
f: Tanda Dam is a small dam built near Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It supplies drinking and irrigation water.
r: Kohat is also known for its tunnel, the Kohat Pass and its cantonment.

q: Oil wrestling is the national sport of which country? (6)
f: Oil wrestling (Yagli Gures) is the national sport of Turkey.
r: The Kirkpinar festival in Edirne, Turkey, is the oldest wrestling competition in the world.

q: The Treaty of Versailles, which ended World War I with Germany, was signed in which year? (6)
f: The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919 at the Palace of Versailles in France.
r: It imposed heavy reparations on Germany and created the League of Nations.

q: In which province is Ranikot (Rani Fort) located? (6)
f: Ranikot Fort lies in the Kirthar foothills near Sann in Jamshoro district, Sindh.
r: It is often called the Great Wall of Sindh because of its long walls.

q: Who led the Quit India Movement of 1942? (6)
f: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942 with the call Do or Die.
r: The Muslim League opposed the movement.

q: Which team won the cricket World Cup in 1999? (6)
f: Australia beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the 1999 final at Lord's.
r: Pakistan was the runner-up in 1999 and champion in 1992.

q: What is 90% of 70? (6)
r: To find 90% of a number, subtract one tenth of it from the number.

q: Who was the first woman martyred in Islam? (6)
f: Hazrat Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to give up Islam.
r: Her husband Hazrat Yasir (RA) was also martyred.

q: Which game is played on a court enclosed by four walls? (6)
f: Squash is played in a closed court with four walls, and the ball may be hit off any wall except for out-of-play lines.
r: Squash was invented in England at Harrow School in the 19th century and Pakistan has been a champion nation in it.

q: What is the value of tan 45 degrees? (6)
f: At 45 degrees sin and cos are both 1 over root 2, so tan = sin/cos = 1.
r: The value of tan 60 degrees is root 3.

q: What is the highest point above sea level in Pakistan? (6)
f: K2 (8,611 m) is the highest peak in Pakistan.
r: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is the second highest mountain in Pakistan.

q: What is the meaning of Maghfirat? (6)
f: Maghfirat is Arabic for forgiveness or pardon.
r: Allah's name Al-Ghafoor means the Most Forgiving.

q: What is the sign of the product of a positive number and a negative number? (6)
f: A positive times a negative is always negative, for example 3 x (-2) = -6.
r: The product of two negative numbers is positive.

q: What is the sound made by an eagle called? (6)
f: An eagle's call is described as a screech or shrill cry.
r: Owls hoot while lions roar.

q: Lake Saif-ul-Malook is situated in which valley? (6)
f: Lake Saif-ul-Malook lies near Naran in the Kaghan Valley, Mansehra district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is at about 3,200 metres above sea level.

q: The United Nations recognises 12 July as which day? (6)
f: The UN declared 12 July Malala Day in 2013, Malala Yousafzai's birthday.
r: World Population Day falls on 11 July.

q: Who established the Mughal rule in India? (6)
f: Babar defeated Ibrahim Lodhi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.
r: Babar was a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan.

q: Which people lived at Khyber at the time of the Prophet (PBUH)? (6)
f: Khyber was a fortified oasis inhabited mainly by Jewish tribes, and the Muslims conquered it in 7 AH.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) is famous for his role in the conquest of the fort of Khyber.

q: How many dimensions does volume have? (6)
f: Volume measures space in length, width and height, so it is three dimensional.
r: Volume is measured in cubic units such as cubic metres.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 18th? (6)
f: The gap is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. So the 18th is also a Sunday.
r: Dates that are multiples of 7 apart share the same weekday.

q: From which city did the Holy Prophet (SAW) migrate in 622 AD? (6)
f: In 622 AD the Prophet (SAW) migrated from Makkah to Madina (then called Yathrib), which is called the Hijrat.
r: The Islamic Hijri calendar starts from this migration.

q: Is a Pakistan Navy Lieutenant equal in rank to a Pakistan Army Captain? (6)
o: No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Major
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Lieutenant
No, Navy Lieutenant is equal to Army Colonel
f: A Navy Lieutenant ranks with an Army Captain and a Pakistan Air Force Flight Lieutenant.
r: A Navy Lieutenant Commander is equal to an Army Major.

q: On what date was Benazir Bhutto assassinated? (6)
f: She was killed in a gun and bomb attack after an election rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
r: She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim-majority country.

q: In which river is the rare blind dolphin found? (6)
f: The Indus river dolphin (bhulan) is blind and lives in the Indus river system.
r: Its main protected stretch in Pakistan is between Guddu and Sukkur barrages.

q: By whom are the members of the Senate of Pakistan mainly elected? (6)
f: Senators from each province are elected by the members of that province's assembly through single transferable vote.
r: Senators serve a six-year term and half of them retire every three years.

q: Fill in the blank: ____ sun rises in the east. (6)
f: The sun is unique, so it takes the definite article the.
r: The article the is also used with unique things such as the moon and the earth.

q: Fill in the blank: Why are you so ____ with him? (6)
f: After the linking verb are, we need an adjective describing the subject, so angry.
r: Adverbs such as angrily describe verbs, not the subject after to be.

q: In which province is the Gomal Zam Dam located? (6)
f: Gomal Zam Dam is built on the Gomal River in South Waziristan, in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: It is a multipurpose dam completed in 2013.

q: On which river is Sukkur Barrage built? (6)
f: Sukkur Barrage was built across the Indus River at Sukkur in Sindh.
r: It was opened in 1932 and feeds seven major canals.

q: Under the Constitution of Pakistan, the President is bound to act on the advice of whom? (6)
f: Article 48 of the Constitution requires the President to act on the advice of the Prime Minister (or the Cabinet).
r: Pakistan has a parliamentary system in which the Prime Minister is the real executive head.

q: What is an angle of 90 degrees called? (6)
f: An angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle. Acute angles are smaller and obtuse angles are larger.
r: A straight angle measures 180 degrees.

q: In vector algebra, what is the value of j . j (dot product of the unit vector j with itself)? (6)
r: Dot products of different unit vectors such as i . j are 0.

q: An acute angle is how large compared with a right angle? (6)
f: A right angle is 90 degrees and an acute angle is any angle between 0 and 90 degrees, so it is smaller.
r: An angle larger than 90 and smaller than 180 degrees is called obtuse.

q: What is the meaning of the word defer? (6)
f: To defer means to put off something until a later time.
r: Another meaning is to yield to someone's opinion, as in defer to the elders.

q: What is the boundary line between Pakistan and India in Kashmir called? (6)
f: The Line of Control (LoC) separates Pakistan-administered and Indian-administered Kashmir.
r: It was established by the 1972 Simla Agreement, based on the 1949 ceasefire line.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to MALICIOUS? (6)
f: Malicious means intending to harm others, which is spiteful.
r: Its opposite is benevolent.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to TIMID? (6)
f: Timid means lacking courage or confidence, which is shy.
r: Its opposite is bold or daring.

q: In which year did the First World War end? (6)
f: The armistice with Germany took effect on 11 November 1918, ending the fighting. The Treaty of Versailles followed in 1919.
r: The First World War began in 1914.

q: In which year was the Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) established by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey? (6)
f: The RCD was formally established in 1964 by Pakistan, Iran and Turkey to promote economic cooperation. It replaced the earlier CENTO-linked arrangements in the economic field.
r: The RCD was succeeded by the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in 1985.

q: On what date was the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan enforced? (6)
f: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973, and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. It was authenticated by President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.
r: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto was the Prime Minister when the Constitution was enacted.

q: Where is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh (Hazrat Ali Hujwiri) located? (6)
f: Data Ganj Bakhsh, the author of Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, is buried in Lahore near Bhati Gate. His shrine is one of the most visited in Pakistan.
r: His death anniversary (Urs) is held every year at the shrine in Lahore.

q: In which city was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan, assassinated in 1951? (6)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot on 16 October 1951 while addressing a public meeting at Company Bagh in Rawalpindi.
r: Company Bagh was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

q: Which Pakistani scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1979? (6)
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics with Sheldon Glashow and Steven Weinberg for the unified electroweak theory.
r: Abdus Salam is the only Pakistani Nobel laureate in Physics; Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

q: Who was the second martial law administrator of Pakistan? (6)
f: Ayub Khan imposed the first martial law in October 1958. General Yahya Khan imposed the second in March 1969 when Ayub resigned.
r: General Zia-ul-Haq imposed the third martial law in July 1977.

q: A boy bought a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is his profit percentage? (6)
f: Profit = 700 - 500 = Rs 200. Profit percentage = 200 / 500 x 100 = 40%.
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: Odd one out: Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, Rawalpindi. (6)
f: Islamabad is the federal capital, Lahore is the capital of Punjab and Quetta is the capital of Balochistan. Rawalpindi is not a capital.
r: Rawalpindi is the headquarters of the Pakistan Army and neighbours Islamabad.

q: Rearrange the letters IAPRS to form a word. What does the word name? (6)
f: The letters I, A, P, R, S rearranged give PARIS, the capital of France.
r: Paris stands on the River Seine.

q: Which country occupies the Golan Heights? (6)
f: Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the Six-Day War of 1967. It has held the area since then.
r: The Golan Heights overlook the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan valley.

q: How many sugar mills did Pakistan have at the time of independence in 1947? (6)
f: Most colonial-era sugar mills lay on the Indian side of the border, and Pakistan inherited only two.
r: The first new sugar mill after independence was set up at Tando Muhammad Khan in Sindh in 1961.

q: Which type of medicine is used to relieve pain? (6)
f: Analgesics such as paracetamol and aspirin are painkillers. They reduce pain without making the person lose consciousness.
r: Anaesthetics are different because they cause loss of sensation before surgery.

q: What is the multiplicative inverse of 0.01? (6)
r: Zero has no multiplicative inverse.

q: What is the antonym of 'stagnant'? (6)
f: Stagnant means not flowing or moving, as in stagnant water. Its opposite is flowing.
r: Stagnant can also describe an economy that is not growing.

q: In football, what did BPL originally stand for in the English league? (6)
f: The English top division was sponsored by Barclays from 2001 to 2016 and was called the Barclays Premier League (BPL). Today it is simply the Premier League.
r: BPL also stands for the Bangladesh Premier League in cricket.

q: What does the word venerate mean? (6)
f: To venerate is to regard someone or something with deep respect and reverence. Its synonyms are revere and honour.
r: The adjective venerable describes a person worthy of great respect, often because of age or wisdom.

q: How many votes in the 336-member National Assembly are needed to pass a no-confidence motion against the Prime Minister? (6)
f: A no-confidence resolution needs a majority of the total membership of the House. Half of 336 is 168, so 169 votes are needed.
r: Article 95 of the Constitution deals with the vote of no confidence against the Prime Minister. The National Assembly had 342 seats before 2018.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'forestall'? (6)
f: To forestall means to prevent something from happening by taking action ahead of time.
r: Forestall is often confused with forest but has no connection with trees.

q: What is 1/10th of 90? (6)
f: One tenth of 90 is 90 divided by 10, which is 9.
r: Dividing by 10 simply moves the decimal point one place to the left.

q: Which animal was with the Ashab-e-Kahf (Companions of the Cave)? (6)
f: The Quran in Surah Al-Kahf mentions that their dog lay at the entrance of the cave with outstretched paws.
r: The dog is traditionally named Qitmir.

q: How many articles are there in the English language? (6)
f: The English articles are a, an and the. A and an are indefinite and the is definite.
r: Candidates often wrongly say 2, forgetting that a and an are separate forms.

q: How many agencies were there in the Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA)? (6)
f: FATA had seven agencies: Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North Waziristan and South Waziristan.
r: There were also frontier regions (FRs) attached to FATA.

q: For how many years did the Quraish of Makkah boycott Banu Hashim? (6)
f: The Quraish imposed a social and economic boycott on Banu Hashim for about three years in the valley of Shib Abi Talib.
r: The boycott took place from the 7th to the 10th year of prophethood.

q: What kind of number is 5/7? (6)
f: A number that can be written as a ratio of two integers with a non-zero denominator is rational. 5/7 is such a ratio.
r: Numbers such as pi and the square root of 2 cannot be written as a ratio of integers, so they are irrational.

q: Which letter comes after G in the English alphabet? (6)
f: The order is F, G, H, I, so H follows G.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: According to Pakistani textbooks, how many prophets were sent by Allah in total? (6)
f: A well-known hadith, as taught in Pakistani textbooks, gives the number of prophets as 124,000.
r: Only 25 prophets are named in the Quran, and some narrations give 224,000.

q: In which part of Punjab is the Salt Range located? (6)
f: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, between the Jhelum River and the Indus River south of Potohar Plateau. Khewra salt mine is in the range.
r: Mount Sakesar is the highest peak of the Salt Range.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 1st of that month? (6)
f: From the 1st to the 15th is 14 days, exactly two weeks, so both fall on the same weekday, Monday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: What was the official name of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (6)
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution names the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: The 1956 Constitution also used the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan, while the 1962 Constitution used Republic of Pakistan.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is male? (6)
f: 340 divided by 500 times 100 gives 68 percent.
r: The remaining 32 percent are female.

q: For which field is Abdur Rehman Chughtai famous? (6)
f: Abdur Rehman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a famous Pakistani painter and artist known for his Mughal-influenced style.
r: He is also known for designing Pakistan's early postage stamps.

q: What does the Arabic word Alfeel mean? (6)
f: Alfeel means elephant. Surah Al-Fil of the Quran tells of Abraha's army with elephants that tried to destroy the Kaaba in the Year of the Elephant.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) was born in the Year of the Elephant (about 570 CE).

q: If set A has 3 elements and set B has 4 elements, how many elements are in the Cartesian product A x B? (6)
f: The number of elements in A x B is the product of the sizes: 3 x 4 = 12.
r: The number of elements of A x B equals that of B x A.

q: Which is the coldest inhabited place of Pakistan? (6)
f: Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan records the lowest winter temperatures among Pakistan's inhabited places; it recorded about minus 21 degrees Celsius in December 2019.
r: Ziarat and Gilgit are also among the coldest places in winter.

q: What is the meaning of the word interim? (6)
f: Interim describes something provided or done for the time between two events, that is, temporary.
r: An interim government rules only until a regular government is elected.

q: Arfa Karim, the youngest Microsoft Certified Professional, belonged to which country? (6)
f: Arfa Abdul Karim Randhawa was a Pakistani girl from Faisalabad who became a Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.
r: She died in January 2012 at the age of 16, and Lahore has a software technology park tower named after her.

q: What is the value of log 1 (to any valid base)? (6)
f: Any base b raised to the power 0 equals 1, so the logarithm of 1 is 0.
r: The logarithm of 0 is undefined.

q: What is the meaning of the word reluctant? (6)
f: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant to do something. A reluctant person does not want to act.
r: The noun form is reluctance.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "retrieve"? (6)
f: To retrieve is to get something back, which is to recover.
r: A retriever dog is named for fetching game.

q: Which is the highest waterfall in the world? (6)
f: Angel Falls in Venezuela has a total height of about 979 metres, with an uninterrupted drop of about 807 metres, making it the highest waterfall in the world.
r: Angel Falls is located in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, and is named after the pilot Jimmie Angel.

q: What is 90 divided by 90 (90/90)? (6)
f: Any non-zero number divided by itself equals 1, so 90/90 = 1.
r: Division of zero by a non-zero number gives 0, but division by zero is undefined.

q: Which term comes next in the series: 3z, 6y, 9x, 15w, ? (6)
f: The numbers 3, 6, 9, 15 follow the rule that each is the sum of the two before it (3+6=9, 6+9=15), so the next is 9+15=24. The letters go backwards from z, y, x, w to v.
r: A series where each term is the sum of the previous two is called a Fibonacci-type series.

q: In a school of 500 students, 340 are male. What percentage of the students is female? (6)
f: Females are 500 minus 340, which is 160. Then 160 divided by 500 times 100 gives 32 percent.
r: Males make up 68 percent.

q: What does an adjective describe or explain? (6)
f: An adjective modifies a noun or pronoun by telling its quality, quantity or kind, as in a tall boy.
r: An adverb, in contrast, modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb.

q: Around which body does the Earth revolve? (6)
f: The Earth orbits the Sun, completing one revolution in about 365.25 days.
r: The Moon revolves around the Earth, not the Sun directly.

q: Sahih Bukhari is regarded as the most authentic book of hadith after which book? (6)
f: Muslims regard the Holy Quran as the most authentic book, followed in authenticity by Sahih Bukhari among the hadith books.
r: Imam Bukhari compiled his collection over about 16 years.

q: Which device converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy? (6)
f: A battery or electric cell uses chemical reactions to produce an electric current.
r: A generator converts mechanical energy to electrical energy, and a solar panel converts light energy.

q: According to a hadith, how many good deeds (nekis) are earned by reciting one letter of the Holy Quran? (6)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) said a good deed is rewarded tenfold, so one letter of the Quran earns ten good deeds.
r: This hadith is narrated in Sunan al-Tirmidhi.

q: In whose era was the Battle of Yamama fought? (6)
f: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11-12 AH against the false prophet Musaylima during the caliphate of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA).
r: Many Huffaz died there, which led to the first compilation of the Quran.

q: Foot is to knee as hand is to what? (6)
f: The knee is the main joint of the leg above the foot, and the elbow is the main joint of the arm above the hand. So hand is to elbow.
r: The elbow joins the upper arm to the forearm.

q: Approximately how many disbelievers (Quraish) fought against the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud? (6)
f: The Makkan army at Uhud numbered about 3000 men, while the Muslims were about 1000 at the start and about 700 after 300 hypocrites withdrew.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: Nankana Sahib is a famous holy site of which religion? (6)
f: Nankana Sahib is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism. It is in Punjab, Pakistan.
r: Guru Nanak was born there in 1469.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan declares that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan? (6)
f: Article 1 of the 1973 Constitution states that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: Article 2 declares Islam to be the State religion of Pakistan.

q: Which river is the largest in the world by volume of water discharged? (6)
f: The Amazon carries the greatest volume of water of any river in the world.
r: The length of the Nile and the Amazon is disputed, so some sources name the Nile as longest.

q: Xinjiang, a province of China, touches which side of Pakistan? (6)
f: Xinjiang borders Gilgit-Baltistan in the north of Pakistan across the Karakoram.
r: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with Xinjiang.

q: Who was the 3rd Prime Minister of Pakistan? (6)
f: The order of Pakistan's early prime ministers was Liaquat Ali Khan, Khawaja Nazimuddin, Muhammad Ali Bogra, Chaudhry Muhammad Ali and H. S. Suhrawardy. So the third was Muhammad Ali Bogra.
r: Muhammad Ali Bogra took office in April 1953 after Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed.

q: Who is Ali Sadpara? (6)
f: Muhammad Ali Sadpara was a famous Pakistani high-altitude mountaineer from Skardu who climbed eight-thousanders such as Nanga Parbat in winter.
r: He went missing on K2 in February 2021 during a winter attempt.

q: What is the currency of Australia? (6)
f: Australia uses the Australian dollar (AUD).
r: Australia used the Australian pound until decimal currency was introduced in 1966.

q: What is the name of the autobiography of Field Marshal Ayub Khan? (6)
f: Ayub Khan wrote Friends Not Masters, published in 1967.
r: In the Line of Fire is the autobiography of Pervez Musharraf.

q: Who were Banu Quraiza? (6)
o: A branch of the Quraish of Makkah
f: Banu Quraiza were a Jewish tribe living near Madinah. They broke their agreement with the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq).
r: After the Trench, the Muslims besieged their fortress and the matter was settled by the judgement of Hazrat Saad bin Muadh (RA).

q: Between whom was the brotherhood (Mukhawat) established after the migration to Madinah? (6)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) created brotherhood between the Muhajirin who came from Makkah and the Ansar, the helpers of Madinah.
r: It helped settle the Muhajirin economically in Madinah.

q: What is the capital of Argentina? (6)
f: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.
r: Montevideo is the capital of Uruguay.

q: In mathematics, a quantity whose value can change is called a (6)
f: A variable is a symbol that can take different values, unlike a constant whose value is fixed.
r: In the expression 3x + 5, x is the variable and 3 is the coefficient.

q: In a matrix of order 5 x 4, how many elements are there in each column? (6)
f: The order 5 x 4 means 5 rows and 4 columns. Each column runs down through all the rows, so it has 5 elements.
r: The total number of elements in a 5 x 4 matrix is 20.

q: The Nehru Report of 1928 was prepared in response to which commission? (6)
f: The Simon Commission of 1927 had no Indian member, and Lord Birkenhead challenged Indians to frame a constitution. The Nehru Report was the Indian reply.
r: Quaid-e-Azam later put forward his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.

q: What is the opposite of the word diversity? (6)
f: Diversity means variety; its opposite is uniformity, meaning sameness.
r: Diversity is a synonym of variety.

q: Find x if 3x - 9 = x + 7. (6)
f: Subtract x from both sides: 2x - 9 = 7, so 2x = 16 and x = 8.

q: Which is the highest mountain range in the world? (6)
f: The Himalayas contain Mount Everest and most of the world's highest peaks.
r: The Andes are the longest continental mountain range.

q: Who led the Khilafat Movement in India? (6)
f: The Khilafat Movement (1919 to 1924) was led by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and his brother Maulana Shaukat Ali. It aimed to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
r: Mahatma Gandhi of the Indian National Congress also supported the Khilafat Movement.

q: A tangent to a circle makes what angle with the radius drawn to the point of contact? (6)
f: A tangent is always perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so the angle is 90 degrees.
r: From an external point two tangents of equal length can be drawn to a circle.

q: What is the meaning of 'Sirat'? (6)
f: Sirat means a path or road, as in Sirat-al-Mustaqeem, the straight path.
r: Surah Al-Fatihah asks Allah to guide us to the straight path.

q: How many member countries does NATO have at present? (6)
f: NATO has 32 members, after Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden in 2024.
r: NATO was founded in 1949 with 12 members.

q: What is the perimeter of a circle called? (6)
f: The distance around a circle is called its circumference, equal to 2 x pi x radius.
r: The diameter is twice the radius.

q: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a famous player of which game? (6)
f: Inzamam-ul-Haq is a former Pakistan cricket captain and batter.
r: He was a member of the 1992 World Cup winning Pakistan team.

q: What is the value of i x i, where i is the imaginary unit? (6)
f: The imaginary unit is defined by i squared equals -1, so i x i = -1.
r: Higher powers repeat in a cycle: i cubed is -i and i to the fourth power is 1.

q: What is 2/2 + 1? (6)
r: Any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.

q: What is the antonym of friendly? (6)
f: Friendly means kind and welcoming; the opposite is hostile, meaning unfriendly or aggressive.
r: Hostile comes from the Latin hostis, meaning enemy.

q: The speed of a train is double that of a car. If the car's speed is 60 km/h, what is the speed of the train? (6)
f: Double of 60 km/h is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h.
r: Speed = distance divided by time.

q: What is the average gestation period of a cow? (6)
f: A cow carries her calf for about 283 days, which is roughly nine months. This is close to the human pregnancy length.
r: The gestation period of a buffalo is longer, about 310 to 315 days.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of the word 'utility'? (6)
f: Utility means the quality of being useful or serving a practical purpose. Usefulness is therefore its closest synonym.
r: The word 'utilize' means to make practical use of something.

q: What is the antonym of "embrace" in the sense of accepting an idea? (6)
f: To embrace an idea is to accept it eagerly, so its opposite is to reject it.
r: Embrace also means to hold someone in the arms, and in that sense a synonym is hug.

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Fatima (RA) to Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)? (6)
f: Hazrat Fatima (RA) was the youngest daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
r: She is known as Zahra and Sayyidat Nisa al-Alamin.

q: How many provinces does Pakistan have? (6)
f: Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
r: Islamabad Capital Territory, Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir are not provinces.

q: What is the base of the common logarithm? (6)
f: The common logarithm uses base 10, so log 100 = 2 because 10 squared is 100.
r: The natural logarithm uses base e, which is about 2.718.

q: In which year and at which city was the Lahore Declaration signed between Pakistan and India? (6)
f: The Lahore Declaration was signed on 21 February 1999 in Lahore by Nawaz Sharif and Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
r: It was signed a few months before the Kargil conflict of 1999.

q: The followers of Hazrat Isa (AS) are called what? (6)
f: The followers of Hazrat Isa (Jesus) are called Christians. Christianity is the largest religion in the world by followers.
r: The Quran calls them Nasara (Nazarenes).

q: Which country joined the United Nations in 2002 after its people approved membership in a referendum? (6)
f: Swiss voters approved UN membership in a referendum in March 2002, and Switzerland became the 190th member in September 2002.
r: Switzerland had earlier rejected UN membership in a 1986 referendum.

q: Who is the custodian of the House in the National Assembly of Pakistan? (6)
f: The Speaker presides over the sessions of the National Assembly and is regarded as the custodian of the House. He maintains order and decides points of procedure.
r: In the Speaker's absence the Deputy Speaker presides over the House.

q: Why do we boil water before drinking it? (6)
f: Boiling kills harmful bacteria and other germs that cause waterborne diseases.
r: Boiling for about one to three minutes is generally advised for unsafe water.

q: What is the approximate gestation period of a buffalo? (6)
f: A buffalo carries its calf for about 10 months, which is roughly 305 to 320 days.
r: A cow's gestation is shorter, about 280 days.

q: Who is the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan as of 2026? (6)
f: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir has been Chief of Army Staff since November 2022 and was also named Chief of Defence Forces in December 2025.
r: General Qamar Javed Bajwa was the previous army chief from 2016 to 2022.

q: What does WHO stand for? (6)
f: WHO is the World Health Organization, a United Nations agency for international public health.
r: WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: Which country has the longest bridge in the world? (6)
f: The Danyang-Kunshan Grand Bridge in China, about 164.8 km long, is the longest bridge in the world by total length. It carries the Beijing-Shanghai high-speed railway.
r: The second longest is the Changhua-Kaohsiung Viaduct in Taiwan.

q: What is sin x . cos x equal to? (6)
f: The double angle formula says sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x. Dividing both sides by 2 gives sin x cos x = (sin 2x) / 2.
r: The related formula cos 2x = cos squared x minus sin squared x is also widely used.

q: What does IMF stand for? (6)
f: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund. It is a UN-linked financial institution that supports global monetary cooperation.
r: The IMF was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference and is headquartered in Washington DC.

q: Who signed the Tashkent Declaration of 1966 on behalf of India? (6)
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan. The Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin mediated.
r: Shastri died in Tashkent a few hours after signing the declaration.

q: According to the Ahadith, what is said about a person who eats his fill while his neighbour sleeps hungry? (6)
o: He is not a true believer
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said that he is not a believer who eats his fill while his neighbour goes hungry by his side. This stresses the rights of neighbours.
r: Islam gives great importance to the rights of neighbours.

q: What is the probability of getting an odd number when a fair die is rolled once? (6)
f: The odd numbers are 1, 3 and 5, which is 3 outcomes out of 6, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
r: The probability of any event always lies between 0 and 1.

q: Sara is twice her brother's age and her brother is 5 years old. What will be Sara's age when her brother becomes 10? (6)
f: Sara is now 2 x 5 = 10 years old. The brother needs 5 more years to reach 10, so Sara will be 10 + 5 = 15.
r: The difference between two people's ages always stays the same as time passes.

q: What is the capital of the USA? (6)
f: Washington, D.C. is the federal capital of the United States and the seat of the White House and Congress. It lies on the Potomac River.
r: New York City hosts the United Nations headquarters but is not the capital.

q: What is the magnitude of a unit vector? (6)
f: A unit vector is defined as a vector of length one, so its magnitude is 1. It is used to indicate direction only.
r: The unit vectors along the x, y and z axes are i, j and k.

f: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 0.01 becomes 1.
r: 0.01 is the same as 1/100, so 0.01 x 100 = 1.

q: A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns, written inside square brackets, is called what? (6)
f: A rectangular array of numbers in rows and columns enclosed in brackets is called a matrix.
r: The size of a matrix is called its order, written as rows x columns.

q: Who was the father of Hazrat Yusuf (AS)? (6)
f: Hazrat Yusuf (AS) was the son of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS), who was also a prophet.
r: Hazrat Yaqoob (AS) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS) and the grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS).

q: What was Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (6)
f: Hazrat Umme Kulsum (RA) was a daughter of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (RA).
r: She was married to Hazrat Uthman (RA) after the death of her sister Hazrat Ruqayyah (RA).

q: Ahmed got 15 marks out of 60. What is his percentage? (6)
f: Percentage = 15/60 x 100 = 25%.
r: 15/60 simplifies to 1/4, which is 25%.

q: In which country is the headquarters of the Olympics (International Olympic Committee) located? (6)
f: The International Olympic Committee has its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.
r: The modern Olympic Games first began in Athens in 1896.

q: Which country was the third largest host of refugees in 2016 according to the Amnesty International report? (6)
f: Amnesty International's October 2016 report ranked Jordan first, Turkey second, Pakistan third (about 1.6 million) and Lebanon fourth.
r: The UNHCR figures of the same year ranked Turkey first, so rankings differ between organisations.

q: Which Quetta-area peak, also called Loe Sar Nekan, is generally given as the highest peak of Balochistan? (6)
f: Zarghun Ghar, near Quetta, at about 3,578 metres is generally given as the highest peak in Balochistan.
r: Sources differ a little on its exact height and name; Kuchnai Saar (about 3,404 m) is listed next.

q: Between which two countries was the Shimla Agreement of 1972 signed? (6)
f: The Shimla Agreement was signed by Pakistan and India in July 1972 after the 1971 war.
r: Under it both countries agreed to settle disputes peacefully and respect the Line of Control in Kashmir.

q: What is the product of 3/2 and 2/3? (6)
f: Multiply: (3 x 2) / (2 x 3) = 6/6 = 1. The two fractions are reciprocals of each other.
r: The product of a number and its reciprocal is always 1.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 26th be? (6)
f: From the 4th to the 26th is 22 days. 22 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1, so the day is Monday.
r: The 4th, 11th, 18th and 25th are all Sundays in this month.

q: Who is known as the founder of the technology company Apple? (6)
f: Steve Jobs co-founded Apple in 1976 with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne and led it for many years.
r: Apple launched the iPhone in 2007 under Steve Jobs.

q: Which word is made by arranging the letters POEARLD? (6)
f: The letters P, O, E, A, R, L, D can be rearranged to spell LEOPARD, using all seven letters.
r: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, including northern Pakistan.

q: Who was Hazrat Sarah (AS)? (6)
o: Wife of Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Hazrat Ishaq (AS)
f: Hazrat Sarah was the first wife of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS).
r: Hazrat Hajra (AS), the second wife of Ibrahim (AS), was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (AS).

q: On what date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations? (6)
f: Pakistan was admitted to the United Nations on 30 September 1947, a few weeks after independence.
r: Pakistan was the 56th member state of the UN.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Azad Jammu and Kashmir? (6)
f: Under the 1974 interim constitution the post of Prime Minister was created, and Abdul Hamid Khan was elected the first Prime Minister of AJK in 1975.
r: Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan was the first President of AJK, not the first Prime Minister.

q: What is the determinant of a non-square matrix? (6)
o: Equal to its number of rows
f: A determinant can be found only for a square matrix, with equal rows and columns. For a non-square matrix it does not exist.
r: A square matrix with determinant zero is called a singular matrix.

q: Which of the following are greenhouse gases? (6)
f: Carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and water vapour trap heat in the atmosphere and cause the greenhouse effect.
r: Oxygen and nitrogen make up about 99 percent of dry air but are not greenhouse gases.

q: Choose the correct sentence. (6)
o: We look forward to win the match.
We look forward to winning the match.
We look forward to won the match.
We look forward for win the match.
f: The phrase look forward to is followed by a gerund (verb plus ing), because to is a preposition here. So winning is correct.
r: Similar phrases are: used to doing, object to doing and in favour of doing.

q: In a class of 30 students, 2/3 are male. What is the percentage of males? (6)
f: Percentage = 2/3 x 100 = 66.67%.
r: The remaining 1/3 are females, which is 33.33%.

q: In which year was the Pirpur Report on the grievances of Muslims in Congress provinces published? (6)
f: The Pirpur Report, prepared by a committee of the Muslim League headed by Raja Syed Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur, came out in 1938.
r: It listed complaints against Congress rule in the provinces from 1937.

q: If the 13th day of a month is Monday, what day is the 28th of that month? (6)
f: 28 - 13 = 15 days later. 15 = 14 + 1, so move 1 day forward from Monday, which is Tuesday.
r: Two full weeks (14 days) bring back the same weekday.

q: If the 27th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 9th day be? (6)
f: From the 9th to the 27th is 18 days. 18 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 days = Thursday.
r: The 13th would be Monday, as 27 - 14 = 13.

q: Saeed Anwar, famous in Pakistan, was a player of which sport? (6)
f: Saeed Anwar was a left-handed opening batsman of the Pakistan cricket team.
r: He scored 194 against India in 1997, which was then the highest ODI score.

q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 PM? (6)
f: At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3. Three hour marks of 30 degrees each make 90 degrees.
r: Each hour mark on a clock face is 30 degrees apart.

q: Is the cosine function an even or an odd function? (6)
f: cos(-x) = cos x for every x, which is the definition of an even function.
r: Sine and tangent are odd functions because sin(-x) = -sin x and tan(-x) = -tan x.

q: In which year was Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin dismissed? (6)
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was dismissed on 17 April 1953.
r: He had become Prime Minister after the assassination of Liaquat Ali Khan in 1951.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'doomed'? (6)
f: Doomed means destined for misfortune, so its opposite is blessed or fortunate.
r: Fated and condemned are synonyms of doomed.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to furtive? (6)
f: Furtive means done in a secret or sneaky way to avoid being noticed. Stealthy has the same meaning.
r: Other synonyms of furtive are secretive, sly and surreptitious.

q: A car travels 60 km. A train with double the speed of the car travels for half the time. What distance does the train cover? (6)
f: Distance = speed x time. Doubling the speed and halving the time gives 2 x 1/2 = 1 times the car's distance, which is 60 km.
r: Speed doubled and time halved leaves the distance unchanged.

q: Between which longitudes does Pakistan lie? (6)
f: Pakistan lies approximately between 61 degrees east and 75 degrees east longitude.
r: Pakistan lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres.

q: Where is the Noor Mahal located? (6)
f: Noor Mahal is a palace built by the Nawab of Bahawalpur in 1872 in the city of Bahawalpur.
r: It is now under the care of the Pakistan Army.

q: What is the full name of Imam Malik, founder of the Maliki school of fiqh? (6)
f: Imam Malik is Malik ibn Anas, who lived in Madinah. He is also called Imam of Madinah.
r: His famous book is Al-Muwatta.

q: Pakistan provides a sea route to the landlocked countries of which region? (6)
f: Pakistan's ports, Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, offer the shortest sea access for Afghanistan and the Central Asian states. These states have no coastline of their own.
r: Afghanistan has long used Karachi port under the Afghan Transit Trade agreement.

q: Under which constitution is Pakistan currently being run? (6)
f: Pakistan is run under the Constitution of 1973, which came into force on 14 August 1973 and has been amended many times.
r: The earlier constitutions of 1956 and 1962 were abrogated.

q: Which is the largest glacier of Pakistan according to most Pakistani textbooks? (6)
f: Pakistani textbooks name the Siachen Glacier, about 76 km long, as the largest in the Karakoram and in the region.
r: Sources differ because Siachen is under Indian control, and Biafo and Baltoro are the longest glaciers inside Pakistan-administered areas.

q: The Gobi Desert lies in southern Mongolia and in which other country? (6)
f: The Gobi Desert stretches across southern Mongolia and northern China.
r: It is a cold desert and the largest desert in Asia.

q: What is a synonym of oppression? (6)
f: Oppression means cruel and unjust use of power, which is the same as tyranny.
r: Persecution is another synonym of oppression.

q: The product of two real numbers is always which kind of number? (6)
f: Real numbers are closed under multiplication, so multiplying two real numbers always gives a real number.
r: Real numbers are also closed under addition and subtraction.

q: In a class of 33 students, the boys outnumber the girls by 7. How many girls are there? (6)
f: Let girls = g, then boys = g + 7. So g + g + 7 = 33, 2g = 26 and g = 13.
r: There are 20 boys in this class.

q: In which language did Baba Bulleh Shah write his poetry? (6)
f: Bulleh Shah, the Sufi poet of Kasur, wrote mainly in Punjabi (kafis).
r: Bulleh Shah lived from about 1680 to 1757.

q: What is the process called in which a gas changes directly into a liquid? (6)
f: Condensation is the change of a gas or vapour into a liquid, for example water vapour forming water drops.
r: Condensation is the opposite of evaporation.

q: In which years were the modern Olympic Games cancelled because of the world wars? (6)
f: The 1916 Games were cancelled due to World War 1, and the 1940 and 1944 Games due to World War 2.
r: The Games were not held at all in these years, but they still count in the numbering of the Olympiads.

q: On what date did India conduct its first nuclear test? (6)
f: India carried out its first nuclear test, code named Smiling Buddha, at Pokhran on 18 May 1974.
r: India's second series of tests at Pokhran was in May 1998.

q: On what date did the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) receive royal assent? (6)
f: The Act got royal assent on 23 December 1919 and the reforms started in 1921. They introduced dyarchy in the provinces.
r: The 20 August 1917 date is Montagu's announcement in the House of Commons.

q: What is the value of 3 factorial (3!)? (6)
r: By definition, 0! = 1.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the ancient site of Kot Diji located? (6)
f: Kot Diji is in Khairpur district of Sindh, near the Indus River. Its fort and Indus Valley site are well known.
r: The Kot Diji culture is an early phase of the Indus Valley civilization, before Mohenjo-daro.

q: Which word is a synonym of prevalent? (5)
f: Prevalent means common or existing widely at a given time, which is widespread.
r: Its opposite is rare or uncommon.

q: Which is the outermost planet of the solar system? (5)
f: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
r: Pluto was considered the ninth planet until 2006.

q: In which months does the monsoon season occur in Pakistan? (5)
f: The monsoon rains reach Pakistan in July and last until about September.
r: Most of the monsoon rain falls in the northern and north-eastern parts of the country.

q: What is the national game of Pakistan? (5)
f: Field hockey is commonly given as the national game of Pakistan.
r: Pakistan has won the Hockey World Cup four times.

q: In which year was Basic Democracy introduced in Pakistan by Ayub Khan? (5)
f: President Ayub Khan introduced the Basic Democracies system through an order in October 1959. It had a five-tier structure with 80,000 Basic Democrats who elected the president.
r: The scheme was abolished after Ayub Khan resigned in 1969.

q: In which year were the first Commonwealth Games (then called the British Empire Games) held? (5)
f: The first British Empire Games were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930. They were later renamed the Commonwealth Games.
r: The Games are held every four years and were named the British Commonwealth Games in 1970 and the Commonwealth Games in 1978.

q: What are both houses of the Parliament of Pakistan (Senate and National Assembly) together called? (5)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution the Parliament, called Majlis-e-Shoora, consists of the President, the Senate and the National Assembly.
r: The Senate is the upper house and the National Assembly is the lower house.

q: If A and B are disjoint sets, what is A intersection B? (5)
f: Disjoint sets have no common element, so their intersection is the empty set.
r: The empty set is written as phi or { }.

q: Diphtheria is a disease of which part of the body? (5)
f: Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the throat and upper airways.
r: It is prevented by the DPT vaccine.

q: In which Chinese city did the Covid-19 outbreak first appear in December 2019? (5)
f: The first cases of Covid-19 were reported in Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, China, in December 2019.
r: The World Health Organization declared Covid-19 a pandemic in March 2020.

q: What is the antonym of persistent? (5)
f: Persistent means continuing firmly without stopping. Occasional, meaning happening only now and then, is the opposite.
r: Persistent and persevering are synonyms.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of x-3 and x+5? (5)
r: The arithmetic mean of two numbers lies exactly midway between them.

q: What is the most populated city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa? (5)
f: Peshawar is the provincial capital and the largest city of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by population.
r: Mardan is among the next largest cities of the province.

q: What is the name of Pakistan's unmanned combat aerial vehicle? (5)
f: Burraq is the armed drone developed by Pakistan and was first used in combat in 2015.
r: Shahpar is another Pakistani drone used mainly for surveillance.

q: Who introduced the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly? (5)
f: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented it on 7 March 1949 and the Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949.
r: The Objectives Resolution later became the preamble and then Article 2A of the Constitution.

q: Who was the last Governor General of Pakistan? (5)
f: Iskander Mirza was the last Governor General and became the first President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
r: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956.

q: A circle whose radius is 1 is called what? (5)
f: A circle with radius equal to 1 unit is called a unit circle.
r: The unit circle centred at the origin is used to define sine and cosine in trigonometry.

q: If the second day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 28th? (5)
f: The gap is 26 days. 26 mod 7 = 5, so Sunday plus 5 days is Friday.
r: The 2nd, 9th, 16th, 23rd and 30th are Sundays in this month.

q: If y = 2x + 1 and x = 2, what is the value of y? (5)
f: Substitute x = 2: y = 2 x 2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5.
r: An equation of the form y = mx + c represents a straight line with slope m.

q: Rearrange the letters PEOLARD to form a correct English word. (5)
f: The letters P, E, O, L, A, R, D rearrange to make LEOPARD, a big cat.
r: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, and it is a strong climber.

q: Pakistan won the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy final against which team? (5)
f: Pakistan beat India by 180 runs in the final at The Oval, London, on 18 June 2017.
r: Sarfraz Ahmed captained Pakistan and Fakhar Zaman scored 114 in the final.

q: In which year was the M.A.O. School at Aligarh raised to the status of a College? (5)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the school in 1875, and it became Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College in 1877.
r: The college became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: On which prophet was the Torah (Taurat) revealed? (5)
f: The Torah was revealed on Hazrat Musa (AS) for the Bani Israil.
r: The Zaboor was revealed on Hazrat Dawud (AS), the Injeel on Hazrat Isa (AS) and the Quran on Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

q: The Silk Road connects Pakistan with which country? (5)
f: The Karakoram Highway follows part of the ancient Silk Road and links Pakistan to China through the Khunjerab Pass.
r: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is a modern project built along this old route.

q: What does SAFTA stand for? (5)
f: SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area. It is a trade arrangement among the member states of SAARC to reduce customs duties.
r: SAFTA was signed in 2004 and came into force on 1 January 2006.

q: Definitely is to absolutely as totally is to what? (5)
f: Definitely and absolutely are synonyms, so the synonym of totally is entirely.
r: In analogy questions first find the relationship (here synonyms) and then apply it.

q: According to the 2023 census, which is the most populous district of Pakistan? (5)
f: Lahore district had about 13 million people in the 2023 census, the highest of any district.
r: Karachi is larger as a city but is divided into several districts.

q: The COVID-19 outbreak first started in which province of China? (5)
f: The first cases were reported in the city of Wuhan, the capital of Hubei province, in December 2019.
r: The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020.

q: Fill in the blank: He is ____ I am. (5)
f: Older takes than in comparisons, and the pronoun I am follows because it is a subject comparison.
r: Elder is used for family members, as in elder brother, and is not followed by than.

q: Fill in the blank: He is jealous ____ him. (5)
f: The adjective jealous takes the preposition of.
r: Similarly, we say envious of and afraid of.

q: Choose the correct word: I was tired, so I ____ to sleep. (5)
f: The sentence is in the past tense (I was tired), so the past form went is needed.
r: Went is the past tense of go, and gone is its past participle.

q: How many consecutive matches did the Pakistani squash legend Jahangir Khan win in his famous unbeaten run? (5)
f: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches between 1981 and 1986, until Ross Norman beat him in the 1986 World Open.
r: Some authors have questioned the exact count because records were poorly kept, but 555 is the figure officially cited.

q: In which Islamic month did the Battle (Ghazwa) of Uhad take place? (5)
f: The Battle of Uhad was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH near Mount Uhad close to Madina.
r: The Battle of Badr was fought in the previous year, in Ramadan 2 AH.

q: Pakistan is a gateway to which region? (5)
f: Pakistan lies between South Asia, Central Asia and the Arabian Sea, so its ports and routes give Central Asia access to the sea.
r: Gwadar Port is promoted as a trade outlet for landlocked Central Asian states.

q: Who started Pakistan's biggest ambulance service? (5)
f: Abdul Sattar Edhi founded the Edhi Foundation, which runs Pakistan's largest ambulance network.
r: Edhi is known as the Angel of Mercy and died in 2016.

q: What did Thomas Edison invent (practically)? (5)
f: Thomas Edison developed the first practical long-lasting incandescent electric light bulb in 1879. He also invented the phonograph.
r: The telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.

q: What does the word Al-Fatiha mean? (5)
f: Al-Fatiha means The Opening, because it opens the Quran and also opens the prayer.
r: It is also called Umm-ul-Kitab and has seven verses.

q: What does the abbreviation PSL stand for in Pakistani cricket? (5)
f: PSL stands for Pakistan Super League, the franchise Twenty20 cricket league of Pakistan. It began in 2016.
r: The PSL is run by the Pakistan Cricket Board.

q: Which word is a synonym of conceal? (5)
f: To conceal means to keep something out of sight, which is to hide it. Reveal, show and expose are antonyms.
r: The noun form is concealment.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'dormant'? (5)
f: Dormant means temporarily inactive or sleeping, as in a dormant volcano.
r: The opposite of dormant is active.

q: What was Hilful Fudul? (5)
o: A peace pact of Makkan tribes to protect the oppressed
A treaty between Muslims and Jews of Madinah
f: Hilful Fudul was a pact formed in Makkah to defend the wronged and help the weak, and the young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) later said he would still respond to such a pact in Islam.

q: Which is the most populous district of Punjab, Pakistan? (5)
f: Lahore has the largest population of any district in Punjab (about 13 million in the 2023 census).
r: Lahore is also the capital of Punjab.

q: What is the antonym of 'climb'? (5)
f: To climb is to go up, and the opposite is to descend (go down).
r: Descend comes from the Latin descendere.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to FLOURISH? (5)
f: To flourish is to grow and develop in a healthy, successful way, which is to thrive.
r: Its opposite is to decay or wither.

q: What is Uhud? (5)
f: Uhud is a mountain just north of Madinah where the Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) said that Uhud is a mountain that loves us and we love it.

q: Which is considered the first book of Hadith compiled? (5)
f: Imam Malik compiled the Muwatta in Madinah in the 8th century, and it is generally taken as the first book of Hadith.
r: Some sources mention earlier small collections such as Sahifa Hammam ibn Munabbih.

q: In which year was the Second Battle of Panipat fought between Akbar's army and Hemu? (5)
f: The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556, when Akbar's general Bairam Khan defeated Hemu. It secured the Mughal throne for Akbar.
r: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was won by Babur against Ibrahim Lodhi.

q: Where is the MAO College (founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan) located? (5)
f: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College was founded in 1875 at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
r: It later became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: In which city is the Margalla Hills National Park located? (5)
f: The Margalla Hills form the northern backdrop of Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan.
r: Faisal Mosque lies at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

q: Which country supplied S-400 air defence missile systems to India? (5)
f: India signed a deal in 2018 with Russia for S-400 Triumf air defence systems. Deliveries began in 2021.
r: The S-400 is a Russian long range surface to air missile system.

q: Which authority regulates the oil and gas sector in Pakistan? (5)
f: OGRA was established in 2002 to regulate the midstream and downstream oil and gas sector. NDMA handles disasters, WAPDA water and power, PEMRA electronic media.
r: OGRA also recommends the prices of petroleum products and natural gas.

q: Which mountain (peak) lies on the border between China and Pakistan? (5)
f: K2 in the Karakoram lies on the China-Pakistan border, between Gilgit-Baltistan and Xinjiang.
r: At 8,611 m, K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: Which preposition is used with 'laugh' when making fun of someone: 'laughed ___ someone'? (5)
f: To laugh at someone means to mock them; 'laugh at' is the correct phrasal form.
r: 'Laugh with someone' means to share the joke in a friendly way.

q: Who is known as the Traveler of Islam? (5)
f: Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan scholar, traveled across much of the Muslim world and beyond for about 30 years and is called the Traveler of Islam.
r: His travel account is known as the Rihla.

q: Who signed the Indus Waters Treaty on behalf of Pakistan in 1960? (5)
f: President Ayub Khan signed the treaty for Pakistan in Karachi on 19 September 1960. Jawaharlal Nehru signed it for India.
r: W. A. B. Iliff signed for the World Bank.

q: Yaum-ul-Furqan is the name of the day of which event? (5)
f: The Quran calls the day of the Battle of Badr Yaum-ul-Furqan, the day of distinction between truth and falsehood.
r: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.

q: What is the maximum number of right angles a triangle can have? (5)
f: Angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees, so two right angles (180) would leave nothing for the third angle. At most one right angle is possible.
r: A triangle with one right angle is called a right-angled triangle.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day is the 12th day of that month? (5)
f: From the 4th to the 12th is 8 days, and 8 divided by 7 leaves remainder 1. Moving 1 day(s) forward from Sunday gives Monday.
r: Days of the week repeat every 7 days, so dates that differ by a multiple of 7 fall on the same weekday.

q: If A is a subset of B, then A union B is equal to which set? (5)
f: Every element of A is already in B, so combining A and B gives just B.
r: In the same case, A intersection B equals A.

q: Into how many semicircles does a diameter divide a circle? (5)
f: A diameter passes through the centre and cuts the circle into two equal halves, each called a semicircle.
r: A semicircle subtends an angle of 180 degrees at the centre.

q: Rearrange the letters RSPAI to get the name of a city. (5)
f: The letters R, S, P, A, I rearrange to PARIS.
r: Paris is the capital of France, on the river Seine.

q: What are the two square roots of 64? (5)
f: 8 x 8 = 64 and (-8) x (-8) = 64, so the roots are +8 and -8.
r: Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.

q: Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)? (5)
o: Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
f: Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.
r: Letters like B, C, D, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line.

q: Which quantity has no unit? (5)
f: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, so the units cancel and it is dimensionless. The others all have units.
r: Velocity is measured in m/s, density in kg/m3 and pressure in pascals.

q: Which document paved the way for the constitution of Pakistan? (5)
f: The Objective Resolution of 1949 laid down the guiding principles for the constitutions of Pakistan and became their preamble.
r: It was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan in the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

q: In a village the population in 2000 was 4600 and it doubles every five years. What was the population in 1995? (5)
f: Going back five years halves the population: 4600 / 2 = 2300.
r: Population in 2005 would be 9200 at the same rate.

q: Which province of Pakistan was the first to issue driving licences to transgender persons (in 2018)? (5)
f: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa traffic police issued driving licences to transgender persons in March 2018, the first province to do so.
r: Punjab issued licences to 62 transgender drivers in June 2023.

q: What is the walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj called? (5)
f: Sa'i is the ritual walk between Safa and Marwa, commemorating Hazrat Hajra's search for water for Ismail (AS).
r: The Zamzam well appeared near the Kaaba after this search.

q: Which fighter jet has Pakistan produced jointly with China? (5)
f: The JF-17 Thunder is a light multirole fighter built by Pakistan Aeronautical Complex, Kamra, with China's Chengdu Aircraft Corporation.
r: Its Chinese designation is FC-1 Xiaolong.

q: What is the capital of North Korea? (5)
f: Pyongyang is the capital and largest city of North Korea.
r: Seoul is the capital of South Korea.

q: Which letter comes after the letter that is followed by M? (5)
f: The letter followed by M is L, and the letter after L is M.
r: M is the 13th letter, exactly in the middle of the alphabet.

q: Is the square root of 7 a rational or an irrational number? (5)
f: 7 is not a perfect square, so its square root is a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal and cannot be written as a fraction of integers. Hence it is irrational.
r: The square root of any prime number is irrational.

q: In which year was the Scientific Society founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur? (5)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 at Ghazipur to translate Western scientific works into Urdu.
r: The society later moved to Aligarh in 1866, where it published the Aligarh Institute Gazette.

q: Saudi riyal is the currency of which country? (5)
f: The riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia, issued by the Saudi Central Bank.
r: Qatar and Oman also use a currency called riyal, but the Saudi riyal belongs to Saudi Arabia.

q: What is the LCM of 4 and 6? (5)
f: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12 and multiples of 6 are 6, 12. The first common multiple is 12.
r: LCM times HCF of two numbers equals their product (12 x 2 = 24).

q: Who wrote the book Dead Reckoning: Memories of the 1971 Bangladesh War? (5)
f: Dead Reckoning (2011) was written by Sarmila Bose and discusses the 1971 war and its casualty figures. It is often confused with works by authors with similar names.
r: Shrabani Basu wrote Victoria and Abdul, a different book.

q: What does the word refund mean? (5)
f: Refund means to give back money that was paid, for example for a returned item. Its synonym is reimburse.
r: Refund can be a noun (a refund) or a verb (to refund).

q: Which two hadith books are called the Sahihain? (5)
f: Sahihain means the two Sahih books: Sahih al-Bukhari by Imam Bukhari and Sahih Muslim by Imam Muslim.
r: These two are considered the most authentic books of hadith.

q: Jami at-Tirmidhi (Tirmizi Sharif) is a book of what? (5)
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi is a collection of the sayings and actions (ahadith) of the Prophet (PBUH) compiled by Imam Tirmidhi.
r: It is one of the six major hadith collections known as Sihah Sitta.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th be? (5)
f: From the 2nd to the 19th is 17 days. 17 days is 2 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: What is 3x4 + 2x4 (also written 3x4 + 4x2)? (5)
f: Multiply first: 3x4 = 12 and 2x4 = 8 (4x2 is also 8). Then add: 12 + 8 = 20.
r: In arithmetic, multiplication is done before addition (BODMAS).

q: How many columns does a matrix of order 5x4 have? (5)
f: A matrix of order m x n has m rows and n columns. For 5x4 there are 5 rows and 4 columns.
r: The total number of elements in a 5x4 matrix is 20.

q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will be the 8th day of that month? (5)
f: From the 8th to the 28th is 20 days, and 20 = 2 weeks + 6 days. Going back 6 days from Monday gives Tuesday.
r: Going back 6 days is the same as going forward 1 day in a week cycle.

q: When was the Indian Independence Act passed? (5)
f: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947 and created the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.
r: It received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

q: Which word is the antonym (opposite) of ADHERE? (5)
f: Adhere means to stick to something, so its opposite is detach, meaning to separate or loosen.
r: Adhesive is a substance that makes things adhere to each other.

q: In which part of Asia is India located? (5)
f: India lies in South Asia, forming most of the Indian subcontinent.
r: SAARC was formed in 1985 by the countries of South Asia.

q: To which religion did Rana Bhagwan Das belong? (5)
f: Rana Bhagwandas was a Hindu who served as a judge of the Supreme Court and as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.
r: He was the first non-Muslim to serve as acting Chief Justice of Pakistan.

q: On which date was the Indian pilot Abhinandan Varthaman captured in Pakistan? (5)
f: Wing Commander Abhinandan's aircraft was shot down on 27 February 2019, a day after the Balakot air strike. He was returned to India on 1 March 2019.
r: The Pakistan Air Force shot down two Indian aircraft that day.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of the word 'ecstasy'? (5)
f: Ecstasy is a state of intense happiness or delight. Rapture is a close synonym.
r: The adjective form is ecstatic, meaning extremely happy.

q: What is the antonym of the word justify? (5)
f: To justify means to defend as right, and the opposite is to condemn or blame.
r: Another opposite of justify is to criticise.

q: What is the mean of -5 and -5? (5)
r: The mean of identical numbers equals that number.

q: What is the motto given by the Quaid-e-Azam to the nation? (5)
f: The Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto Unity, Faith, Discipline (Ittehad, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam, Nazm). This is the order used in his speeches and in Pakistani textbooks.
r: In Urdu the motto is often written as Ittehad, Tanzeem, Yaqeen-e-Muhkam; Unity, Faith, Discipline is the standard English form.

q: What did the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919) introduce in the provinces? (5)
f: The 1919 reforms divided provincial subjects into transferred (under elected ministers) and reserved (under the Governor). This system was called dyarchy.
r: Dyarchy was ended by the Government of India Act 1935, which introduced provincial autonomy.

q: The name Punjab means the land of how many rivers? (5)
f: Punjab is from the Persian words punj (five) and ab (water), meaning five rivers: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.
r: Of these, the Beas and Sutlej are mainly in India after the Indus Waters Treaty.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution? (5)
o: An Electoral College of the Senate, National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies
