f: Under Article 41 of the 1973 Constitution the President is elected by an Electoral College made up of members of the Senate, the National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.
r: The President serves a five-year term.

q: For what is the Last Sermon (Khutbah Hajjat-ul-Wida) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) best known? (5)
o: A treaty with the Jews of Madinah
f: In the Last Sermon the Holy Prophet (PBUH) declared the equality of all people, the sanctity of life, property and honour, the rights of women and the abolition of interest and old blood feuds. It is therefore regarded as the first great charter of human rights.
r: The Last Sermon was delivered in the 10th year of Hijrah during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "negotiate"? (5)
f: To negotiate is to discuss terms in order to reach agreement, which is to bargain.
r: A negotiator mediates between parties.

q: What is the other name of the Ghazwa of Tabuk? (5)
f: Tabuk is also called Ghazwat al-Usrah, the Army of Hardship, because of the heat, distance and shortage of supplies.
r: It is the last expedition led by the Prophet (SAW) himself.

q: What is a matrix whose number of rows is not equal to its number of columns called? (5)
f: A matrix with unequal numbers of rows and columns (m x n with m not equal to n) is a rectangular matrix.
r: If rows and columns are equal, it is a square matrix.

q: If x = (1/3) y and y = 9, what is the value of x? (5)
f: Substitute y = 9: x = (1/3) x 9 = 3.
r: Multiplying by 1/3 is the same as dividing by 3.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Friday, what day will be the 12th of that month? (5)
f: The 12th is 11 days after the 1st, and 11 = 7 + 4. Friday + 4 days = Tuesday.
r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 27th be? (5)
f: From the 4th to the 27th is 23 days. 23 days is 3 full weeks plus 2 day(s), so the day is 2 day(s) after Monday, which is Wednesday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 28th be? (5)
f: From the 4th to the 28th is 24 days. 24 days is 3 full weeks plus 3 day(s), so the day is 3 day(s) after Friday, which is Monday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: What is the arithmetic mean of 18 and 36? (5)
r: The arithmetic mean is the sum of the values divided by their number.

q: Who is the author of the book In the Line of Fire? (5)
f: In the Line of Fire (2006) is the memoir of General Pervez Musharraf.
r: It was published when Musharraf was President of Pakistan.

q: The line y = 6 is parallel to which axis? (5)
f: All points on y = 6 have the same y value, so it is a horizontal line parallel to the x-axis, crossing the y-axis at (0, 6).
r: The equation y = 0 is the x-axis itself.

q: What is the capital of Denmark? (5)
f: Copenhagen is the capital and largest city of Denmark.
r: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

q: What is the capital of India? (5)
f: New Delhi is the capital of India.
r: Capital moved from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word 'breach'? (5)
f: To breach something is to break or violate it, such as a rule or a contract.
r: A breach can also mean a gap made in a wall.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes? (5)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
r: At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.

q: How many Basic Democrats were there in Ayub Khan's system (40,000 in each wing)? (5)
f: Ayub Khan's Basic Democracies had 80,000 members, 40,000 in East Pakistan and 40,000 in West Pakistan.
r: The number was later raised to 120,000, but 80,000 was the original figure.

q: The voice of which animal is described in the Holy Quran as the worst of voices? (5)
f: Surah Luqman says the harshest of voices is surely the voice of the donkey.
r: The advice is given by Hazrat Luqman to his son in Surah Luqman.

q: For what industry is Gaddani in Balochistan famous? (5)
f: Gaddani, on the coast of Balochistan near Karachi, has one of the largest ship breaking yards in the world, where old ships are dismantled.
r: Gaddani lies in Lasbela District.

q: What is the first group of the periodic table called? (5)
f: Group 1 contains lithium, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium and francium, which are called alkali metals.
r: Hydrogen sits at the top of Group 1 but is not an alkali metal.

q: On what date did India get independence? (5)
f: India became independent from British rule on 15 August 1947, one day after Pakistan.
r: India celebrates Republic Day on 26 January because its constitution came into force in 1950.

q: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is known by which title? (5)
f: Hazrat Ismail (AS) is called Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice, in the story of Hazrat Ibrahim's (AS) dream.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah.

q: What is the LCM of 6 and 8? (5)
f: 6 = 2 x 3 and 8 = 2 x 2 x 2, so LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 = 24.
r: HCF of 6 and 8 is 2, and 24 x 2 = 48 = 6 x 8.

q: The Parliament of Pakistan is of which type? (5)
f: It has two houses: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).
r: Pakistan has a parliamentary form of government under the 1973 Constitution.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'mitigate'? (5)
o: To make less severe or serious
f: To mitigate means to reduce the severity, seriousness or harm of something. For example, planting trees mitigates the effect of floods.
r: Mitigation is a common word in disaster management, as in flood mitigation.

q: If a helicopter needs 80 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons are needed to cover 400 km? (5)
f: Fuel per km is 80 divided by 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 400 km, 400 x 0.25 = 100 gallons.
r: Fuel used is directly proportional to distance.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, 12, ? (5)
f: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 12 + 3 = 15.
r: This is the table of 3.

q: School is a noun. Which pronoun can be used in its place? (5)
f: A school is a singular, non-living thing, so the pronoun it is used for it.
r: The plural pronoun for schools is they.

q: Who built the Quba Mosque, the first mosque in Islam? (5)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) laid the foundation of the Quba Mosque near Madinah on his Hijrah, and the Companions helped build it.
r: The Quran (Surah At-Tawbah) refers to a mosque founded on piety from the first day, which scholars identify as Quba.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "exceptional"? (5)
f: Exceptional means unusually good or rare, like extraordinary.
r: Its antonym is ordinary.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to "irksome"? (5)
f: Irksome means causing irritation, so annoying is closest.
r: To irk means to annoy.

q: Which country is traditionally called the Land of the White Elephant? (5)
f: Thailand (formerly Siam) is known by this name because white elephants were sacred and symbols of royal power there.
r: Sources differ slightly, as Myanmar and Laos have also been linked to white elephants, but Thailand is the textbook answer.

q: In the expression 7X + 4, what is 7 called? (5)
f: The number multiplying the variable X is its coefficient; 4 is the constant term.
r: X is the variable of the expression.

q: Who made the first solo non-stop flight across the Atlantic Ocean in 1927? (5)
f: Charles Lindbergh flew the Spirit of St. Louis alone from New York to Paris in May 1927.
r: Alcock and Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight (not solo) in 1919, and Amelia Earhart was the first woman to fly it solo in 1932.

q: What is the antonym of the word advance? (5)
f: To advance means to move forward, and its opposite is to retreat or move backward.
r: Advance can also mean to lend money beforehand, in which case it is a noun meaning a loan paid early.

q: What is the baby (young one) of a frog called? (5)
f: A young frog hatches from an egg as a tadpole, which lives in water and breathes with gills. It later grows legs and lungs and becomes an adult frog.
r: The change from tadpole to frog is called metamorphosis.

q: Maputo is the capital of which country? (5)
f: Maputo, formerly Lourenco Marques, is the capital of Mozambique.
r: Mozambique gained independence from Portugal in 1975.

q: There are 24 members in a committee and 5 are men. What is the percentage of women? (5)
f: Women = 24 - 5 = 19. Percentage = 19 / 24 x 100 = 79.17 percent.
r: The men are 5/24 x 100 = 20.83 percent, and the two percentages add up to 100.

q: How many nations and territories belong to the Commonwealth Games Federation, which takes part in the Commonwealth Games? (5)
f: The Commonwealth Games Federation has 74 members (nations and territories), including dependent territories that compete under their own flags.
r: The Commonwealth of Nations has only 56 member states, and about 72 teams took part in the Glasgow 2026 Games according to some reports.

q: For what is Sadequain famous? (5)
f: Sadequain (1930-1987) was a famous Pakistani painter and calligrapher, known for his Quranic calligraphy and murals.
r: He painted the ceiling mural at the Mangla Dam power house and the Frere Hall murals in Karachi.

q: What is the width (length between the posts) of a standard football goal? (5)
f: The two posts of a standard football goal are 24 feet (7.32 m) apart.
r: The goal height is 8 feet (2.44 m).

q: What is the capital of Iceland? (5)
f: Reykjavik is the capital and largest city of Iceland. It is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state.
r: Iceland is a Nordic island country in the North Atlantic Ocean.

q: What is the length of the Panama Canal in nautical miles, approximately? (5)
f: The Panama Canal is about 82 km (51 miles) long. Since 1 nautical mile is 1.852 km, this is about 44 nautical miles.
r: The canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans and opened in 1914.

q: Which angel is in charge of rain and provision according to Islamic belief? (5)
f: Hazrat Mikail (AS) is the angel entrusted with rain, vegetation and sustenance. Jibrail brings revelation, Israfil blows the Trumpet and Izrail takes souls.
r: Mikail is also spelled Mika'il and is mentioned by name in Surah Al-Baqarah.

q: How many main blood groups are there in the ABO system? (5)
f: The main blood groups are A, B, AB and O, which makes four.
r: Each group can be Rh positive or Rh negative, giving eight common types.

q: What is the capital of Zimbabwe? (5)
f: Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.
r: Harare was formerly called Salisbury.

q: In a circle, what is the distance from the center to any point on the circle called? (5)
f: The distance from the center to a point on the circle is the radius.
r: The diameter is twice the radius.

q: Which of the following is a prime number: 7, 9, 18, 21? (5)
f: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 9 and 21 = 3 x 7 are composite.
r: 2 is the only even prime number.

q: What is the closest meaning (synonym) of genuine? (5)
f: Genuine means real and not imitation. Authentic has the same meaning.
r: Sincere is also used as a synonym of genuine when talking about feelings.

q: Who founded the political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI)? (5)
f: PTI was founded by Imran Khan in April 1996 in Lahore. He has remained its founder and leader since.
r: Imran Khan became Prime Minister of Pakistan in August 2018 and was removed through a no-confidence vote in April 2022.

q: Who said that the character of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the Quran, that is, he was the embodiment of the Quran? (5)
f: When asked about the character of the Prophet (PBUH), Hazrat Aisha (RA) replied that his character was the Quran.
r: This narration is recorded in Sahih Muslim and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad.

q: Which tennis Grand Slam tournament is still played on grass courts? (5)
f: Wimbledon in London is the only Grand Slam still played on grass.
r: The French Open is played on clay, while the US Open and Australian Open use hard courts.

q: What is the antonym of 'transparent'? (5)
f: Transparent means see-through, so its opposite is opaque, which does not let light through.
r: Wood and metal are opaque materials.

q: Which type of engine is used in jet aircraft? (5)
f: Jet aircraft are powered by gas turbine engines such as the turbojet and turbofan. They produce thrust by expelling a fast stream of hot gas backwards.
r: Frank Whittle of Britain patented the turbojet engine in 1930.

q: What is the capital of Norway? (5)
f: Oslo is the capital and largest city of Norway.
r: Norway is not a member of the European Union.

q: In which years were the Olympic Games cancelled because of World War II? (5)
f: The 1940 Games (Tokyo/Helsinki) and the 1944 Games (London) were cancelled due to the war.
r: The Olympics were also cancelled in 1916 because of World War I.

q: What is the meaning of the word 'kith' (as in 'kith and kin')? (5)
f: Kith means one's friends, neighbours and acquaintances, while kin means blood relatives.
r: Candidates often answered relatives, but that is the meaning of kin.

q: Mogadishu is the capital of which country? (5)
f: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia, on the Indian Ocean coast.
r: Somalia is located in the Horn of Africa.

q: 6 is what percentage of 20? (5)
f: Percentage = 6 / 20 x 100 = 30 percent.
r: Percentage = part divided by whole, multiplied by 100.

q: Who is the author of the book 'Jinnah of Pakistan'? (5)
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote 'Jinnah of Pakistan' (1984).
r: Hector Bolitho wrote another well-known biography titled 'Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan'.

q: Gautama Buddha, the founder of Buddhism, belonged to which country? (5)
f: Gautama Buddha was born at Lumbini, which lies in present-day Nepal. He later attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya in India.
r: In his time his Shakya clan lived near the present Nepal-India border.

q: What is the center of a circle called? (5)
o: Point from which all boundary points are equidistant
f: The center is the fixed point inside a circle that is at the same distance from every point on the circle.
r: The fixed distance is called the radius.

q: A class has 1500 students and 1200 of them are boys. What is the percentage of girls? (5)
f: Girls = 1500 - 1200 = 300. Percentage = 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20 percent.
r: Boys make up the other 80 percent of this class.

q: Which country hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896? (5)
f: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896.
r: The ancient Olympics were also held in Greece, at Olympia.

q: Which number comes next: 55, 65, 75, ? (5)
f: Each number increases by 10, so 75 + 10 = 85.
r: This is an arithmetic progression with common difference 10.

q: In which year was the second constitution of Pakistan enforced? (5)
f: Pakistan's first constitution came in 1956 and was abrogated in 1958. The second constitution, given by Ayub Khan, was enforced in 1962.
r: The third constitution of 1973 is still in force today with amendments.

q: What is the capital of Egypt? (5)
f: Cairo is the capital and largest city of Egypt, on the River Nile.
r: Egypt is building a New Administrative Capital east of Cairo.

q: What was the name of the camel of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (5)
f: The Prophet's well-known camel was named Qaswa, which he rode during the Hijrat.
r: Sources also mention the name Adba for his camel, and Duldul was his mule.

q: Which symbol is used to denote the set of integers in mathematics? (5)
f: The set of integers is written as Z, from the German word Zahlen meaning numbers.
r: N denotes natural numbers, Q rational numbers and R real numbers.

q: On which river is the Bhakra Dam of India built? (5)
f: The Bhakra Dam is built on the Sutlej River in Himachal Pradesh, India. It forms the Gobind Sagar reservoir.
r: The Sutlej was allotted to India under the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.

q: Who founded the All India Muslim League in 1906 at Dhaka, hosting the meeting where it was formed? (5)
f: The All India Muslim League was formed on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka at a meeting hosted by Nawab Khwaja Salimullah of Dhaka. Nawab Waqar-ul-Mulk and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk were also prominent in its formation.
r: Sir Sultan Muhammad Shah Aga Khan III was its first president.

q: Who was the first President of India? (5)
f: Dr Rajendra Prasad became India's first President in January 1950.
r: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

q: On which date did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan to become Bangladesh? (5)
f: The Pakistan army in Dhaka surrendered on 16 December 1971, after which East Pakistan became Bangladesh.
r: The war between Pakistan and India began on 3 December 1971, and Bangladesh celebrates 26 March as its Independence Day.

q: Which Pakistani player won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012, 2019 and 2024? (5)
f: Muhammad Asif of Faisalabad won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012, 2019 and 2024.
r: Muhammad Yousuf (1994) and Muhammad Sajjad (2006) were earlier Pakistani world amateur snooker champions.

q: What is a synonym of the word 'transparent'? (5)
f: Transparent means allowing light to pass through so things can be seen clearly. Clear is the closest synonym.
r: Translucent means light passes through but objects cannot be seen clearly.

q: Which country won the most medals at the Olympic Games held at Tokyo in 2020 (held in 2021)? (5)
f: The USA topped the medal table with 113 medals, including 39 gold.
r: China had 38 gold medals, one fewer than the USA.

q: On which date was the 1956 constitution of Pakistan abrogated? (5)
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 constitution on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
r: Ayub Khan took over as President on 27 October 1958.

q: In which valley is Attabad Lake located? (5)
f: Attabad Lake is in the Gojal area of the upper Hunza Valley in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: The lake was formed in January 2010 when a landslide blocked the Hunza River.

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan provides the right to free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16? (5)
f: Article 25A was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010. It obliges the State to give free and compulsory education to children from 5 to 16 years.
r: Article 37(b) also directs the State to remove illiteracy and provide free secondary education.

q: What is the value of sec 0 (secant of zero degrees)? (5)
f: Secant is the reciprocal of cosine, and cos 0 = 1, so sec 0 = 1/1 = 1.
r: Sec 90 degrees is undefined because cos 90 degrees is zero.

q: On which date did Fatima Jinnah die? (5)
f: Fatima Jinnah, the sister of Quaid-e-Azam, died in Karachi on 9 July 1967.
r: She was born on 31 July 1893 in Karachi and is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: What is the tense used to write about the future called? (5)
f: Future tense describes actions that will happen later, usually with will or shall, as in: I will go.
r: English has four forms of future tense: simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous.

q: Who was the first Pakistani cricketer to score a triple century in Test cricket? (5)
f: Hanif Mohammad scored 337 against the West Indies at Bridgetown in 1958. It was the first Test triple century by a Pakistani.
r: Hanif also scored 499 for Karachi in 1958-59, which was then the highest first-class score.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word lately? (5)
f: Lately means in the recent past, which is the same as recently.
r: Do not confuse lately with late, which means after the expected time.

q: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'restricted'. (5)
f: Restricted means kept within limits or not allowed freely, so the closest word is limited.
r: The antonym of restricted is unrestricted or free.

q: In which mountain range are Pakistan's famous salt mines, such as Khewra, located? (5)
f: The Salt Range in Punjab holds huge rock salt deposits, including the Khewra salt mine.
r: Khewra is one of the largest salt mines in the world.

q: Which word is closest in meaning (a synonym) to thy? (5)
f: Thy is an old English word meaning your (belonging to you).
r: A synonym is a word with almost the same meaning as another word.

q: What is the meaning of the word undaunted? (5)
f: Undaunted means not discouraged or frightened by difficulty or danger, so it means fearless.
r: Daunt means to make someone feel afraid or less confident.

q: In which year did Zakat become compulsory (enforced by law) in Pakistan? (5)
f: The Zakat and Ushr Ordinance was promulgated in 1980 under General Zia-ul-Haq, and Zakat deduction from bank accounts started that year.
r: Zakat is deducted from savings accounts on the first of Ramadan.

q: How many degrees are there in the angle around a full circle? (5)
f: A complete turn around the centre of a circle is 360 degrees.
r: A straight line makes 180 degrees and a right angle makes 90 degrees.

q: What is the closest meaning of the word chaos? (5)
f: Chaos means complete disorder and confusion. Its opposite is order.
r: The word chaos comes from the ancient Greek word for empty space.

q: What is the full form of SCO? (5)
f: SCO stands for Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, a political, economic and security group of Eurasian countries.
r: Pakistan became a full member of the SCO in 2017.

q: Which is the largest (longest) surah of the Holy Quran? (5)
f: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah of the Quran and has 286 ayat.
r: The shortest surah is Surah Al-Kausar with 3 ayat.

q: Who led the Muslim army in the Battle (Ghazwa) of Badr? (5)
f: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH and the Muslim army was commanded by the Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself. The Muslims were about 313 men.
r: The Quraish army at Badr was commanded by Abu Jahl.

q: How many princely states were there in British India at the time of partition in 1947? (5)
f: About 562 princely states existed in British India in 1947. Each had to join India or Pakistan or stay independent.
r: Some sources give 565 because counting methods differ.

q: Under which Article of the Constitution of Pakistan is free and compulsory education a fundamental right? (5)
f: Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment in 2010, makes free and compulsory education a right for children aged 5 to 16.
r: Article 19A gives the right to information.

q: In which type of brackets is a solution set written? (5)
f: A solution set is a set, and sets are written inside curly brackets, for example {2, 3}.
r: Square brackets are used for matrices and for closed intervals.

q: Fill in the blank: Children died ___ fever. (5)
f: We use the preposition of with a cause of death, such as died of fever.
r: We say died of a disease but died in an accident.

q: In which district of Punjab is Harappa located? (5)
f: The ruins of Harappa lie near the Ravi River in Sahiwal district, Punjab.
r: Harappa was first excavated in the 1920s.

q: Who is called Shaheed-e-Millat in Pakistan? (5)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister of Pakistan, was assassinated in Rawalpindi in 1951. He is therefore called Shaheed-e-Millat, the martyr of the nation.
r: Liaquat Ali Khan was shot at Company Bagh, which was later renamed Liaquat Bagh.

q: What is photosynthesis? (5)
o: Making food by green plants using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
f: In photosynthesis, plants use chlorophyll in chloroplasts and sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.
r: Photosynthesis releases the oxygen we breathe.

q: If the diameter of a circle is 56, what is its radius? (5)
f: Radius is half of the diameter. 56 / 2 = 28.
r: Diameter = 2 x radius.

q: On which date was the One Unit scheme enforced in West Pakistan? (5)
f: The West Pakistan One Unit scheme was enforced on 14 October 1955, merging the western provinces and states into one unit.
r: One Unit was abolished by General Yahya Khan on 1 July 1970.

q: An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force? (5)
f: The curved wings make air move faster over the top, creating lower pressure above and an upward force called lift. Lift must be greater than or equal to weight to fly.
r: The four forces on an aeroplane are lift, weight, thrust and drag.

q: Where is the Kot Diji fort located, in terms of district? (5)
f: Kot Diji is a town in Khairpur district of Sindh. Its fort was built by the Talpur rulers.
r: Kot Diji is also an important pre-Harappan archaeological site.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disgusting'? (5)
f: Disgusting means causing strong dislike or sickness. Revolting has nearly the same meaning.
r: Other synonyms are repulsive, nasty and foul.

q: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range? (5)
f: Mount Everest lies in the Mahalangur sub-range of the Himalayas on the Nepal and China (Tibet) border.
r: K2, the second highest peak, is in the Karakoram range.

q: Who was the caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab in 2023 to 2024? (5)
f: Mohsin Naqvi served as caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab from January 2023 until February 2024.
r: Maryam Nawaz became elected Chief Minister of Punjab in February 2024.

q: Who is the current President of Pakistan (as of October 2026)? (5)
f: Asif Ali Zardari was sworn in as the 14th President of Pakistan on 10 March 2024 and still holds the office. The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies.
r: Zardari's predecessor was Dr Arif Alvi, who served from 2018 to 2024.

q: Which sentence is correct? (5)
o: Making friends is more rewarding than to make enemies.
Making friend is more rewarding than making enemies.
Making friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
Make friends is more rewarding than making enemies.
f: Both parts of the comparison should have the same form, so both use the gerund: making friends and making enemies. Friends must also be plural.
r: This rule is called parallel structure.

q: Which type of energy is stored in fruits? (5)
f: Fruits store energy in food molecules such as sugars, which is chemical energy released during digestion.
r: Plants make this energy from sunlight through photosynthesis.

q: In which game did Pakistan win its first Olympic medal? (5)
f: Pakistan won its first Olympic medal, a silver in hockey, at Melbourne in 1956.
r: Pakistan has won three Olympic gold medals, all in hockey.

q: Who is the current Foreign Minister of Pakistan (2026)? (5)
f: Mohammad Ishaq Dar serves as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan. He was still in office in August 2026 according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
r: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari was Foreign Minister from 2022 to 2023 before Ishaq Dar took the post in 2024.

q: Which is the official language of Pakistan, used in government alongside the national language Urdu? (5)
f: The 1973 Constitution makes Urdu the national language and keeps English as the official language for government use.
r: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

q: How many rational numbers lie between 0 and 1? (5)
f: Between any two rational numbers there is another one, for example their average, so the set between 0 and 1 is infinite.
r: Examples are 1/2, 1/3, 2/5 and 3/4.

q: What is the sum of the first seven multiples of 5? (5)
r: The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n+1)/2.

q: Who was the Governor General of India during the War of Independence of 1857 and became the first Viceroy in 1858? (5)
f: Lord Canning was Governor General from 1856 to 1858. After the Government of India Act 1858 he became the first Viceroy.
r: Lord Dalhousie was his predecessor and introduced the Doctrine of Lapse.

q: Who was the President of Pakistan during the 1971 war with India? (5)
f: General Yahya Khan was President from March 1969 until 20 December 1971, so he was President during the December 1971 war.
r: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto took over as President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971.

q: Which country won the 1974 FIFA World Cup? (5)
f: West Germany beat the Netherlands 2-1 in the final in Munich to win the 1974 FIFA World Cup.
r: West Germany had also won the World Cup in 1954.

q: In the point (3, 4), what is the number 3 called? (5)
f: In an ordered pair (x, y) the first number x is the abscissa. The second number y is the ordinate.
r: The abscissa is measured along the x-axis.

q: Which province of the subcontinent did the British occupy first? (5)
f: The British won the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and took control of Bengal first.
r: Sindh was conquered in 1843 and Punjab in 1849.

q: In which year was the Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology (Islamic Council) established in Pakistan? (5)
f: The Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology was set up under the 1962 Constitution, on 1 August 1962.
r: In the 1973 Constitution it continued as the Council of Islamic Ideology under Articles 228 to 230.

q: What is the synonym of 'disastrous'? (5)
f: Disastrous means causing great harm or damage, which is the same as catastrophic.
r: The noun form is disaster.

q: What is the synonym of 'doomed'? (5)
f: Doomed means destined to a bad outcome, which is the same as fated.
r: The noun doom means a terrible fate.

q: Which country is the largest exporter of tea in the world by volume? (5)
f: Kenya exports more tea by volume than any other country. India is second, and Sri Lanka and China follow.
r: China is the largest tea producer, but it keeps much of its tea for home use, and sources differ if ranked by value.

q: In which country was FIFA founded in 1904? (5)
f: FIFA was founded in Paris, France, on 21 May 1904 by seven European associations.
r: FIFA headquarters are today in Zurich, Switzerland.

q: What is the currency of Hungary? (5)
f: Hungary uses its own currency, the forint (HUF). It has not adopted the euro.
r: Poland uses the zloty and the Czech Republic uses the koruna.

q: The United States entered World War II after which event? (5)
o: The Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
f: Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii, on 7 December 1941. The US declared war on Japan the next day.
r: Germany and Italy then declared war on the US a few days later.

q: Which group of gases is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer? (5)
f: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere, and these break down ozone molecules.
r: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 phased out the use of CFCs.

q: What is the antonym of the word liberty? (5)
f: Liberty means freedom, so its opposite is slavery or bondage.
r: Captivity and servitude are also antonyms of liberty.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan, a Federal Minister must be a member of which body? (5)
f: Article 92 says Federal Ministers are appointed from the members of Majlis-e-Shoora, which means the National Assembly or the Senate.
r: Not more than one-fourth of the Federal Ministers can be taken from the Senate.

q: In which constitutional amendment were Qadianis declared non-Muslim in Pakistan? (5)
f: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution, passed in 1974, declared Qadianis (Ahmadis) non-Muslims. It was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
r: The amendment added clause 3 to Article 260.

q: Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points of 1929 were presented in reply to which report? (5)
f: The Nehru Report of 1928 rejected separate electorates and other Muslim demands. Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.
r: The Fourteen Points also demanded the separation of Sindh from the Bombay Presidency.

q: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior is a renowned Pakistani player of which game? (5)
f: Shahbaz Ahmed Senior was a famous Pakistani hockey midfielder and captain. He was part of the team that won Olympic gold in 1984.
r: Pakistan has won the Olympic hockey gold medal three times.

q: Which word is pronounced differently from the rest: white, wait, wrong? (5)
f: In wrong the w is silent and the word begins with the r sound. In white and wait the w is pronounced.
r: Other words with a silent w are write, wrist and wrap.

q: What is shown on the back of the Pakistani 5000 rupee note? (5)
f: The State Bank of Pakistan describes the back of the Rs 5000 note as showing the Faisal Mosque, Islamabad.
r: The front of the note carries the portrait of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.

q: What is the antonym of the word sympathetic? (5)
f: Sympathetic means feeling pity and care for others, so its opposite is callous or unfeeling.
r: Merciless and heartless are also opposites.

q: What was the date of birth of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan? (5)
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born on 17 October 1817 in Delhi.
r: He founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875.

q: Who was the Governor-General of India at the time of the War of Independence of 1857? (5)
f: Lord Canning was Governor-General from 1856 and became the first Viceroy of India in 1858.
r: Lord Dalhousie was his predecessor.

q: Gypsum is the main source of which two elements? (5)
f: Gypsum is hydrated calcium sulfate (CaSO4.2H2O), so it supplies calcium and sulfur.
r: Heated gypsum gives plaster of Paris.

q: In which constitution of Pakistan were Islamic provisions first included? (5)
f: The 1956 Constitution was the first constitution of Pakistan and made the country an Islamic Republic. It included Islamic provisions.
r: The Objectives Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble.

q: Who is generally regarded as the first poet of the Urdu language? (5)
f: Amir Khusrow (1253-1325) is commonly taught as the first poet who used early Urdu (Hindavi) in verse.
r: Sources differ, and some name Wali Deccani as the first major Urdu poet.

q: What is 65% of 100? (5)
r: Percent of 100 is always the same number as the percent itself.

q: In which city is Shalimar Bagh (Shalimar Gardens) located? (5)
f: The Shalimar Gardens are in Lahore, Pakistan. They were built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan around 1641.
r: The Shalimar Gardens and Lahore Fort are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: What is the capital of Hungary? (5)
f: Budapest is the capital and largest city of Hungary. It lies on the River Danube.
r: Budapest was formed in 1873 by joining Buda, Pest and Obuda.

q: On what date did Pakistan win the Cricket World Cup final in 1992? (5)
f: Pakistan beat England in the final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on 25 March 1992 under Imran Khan.
r: It is Pakistan's only ODI World Cup title.

q: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan? (5)
f: Bishkek is the capital.
r: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan.

q: On which date was the first ever Test cricket match played? (5)
f: The first Test was Australia against England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, starting on 15 March 1877.
r: Australia won that match by 45 runs.

q: Which surah of the Quran contains the Bismillah twice? (5)
f: Surah An-Naml has Bismillah at the start and again inside verse 30, in the letter of Prophet Sulaiman (AS).
r: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that has no Bismillah at its start.

q: Who was the President of the USA for most of the Second World War? (5)
f: Franklin D. Roosevelt was President from 1933 until his death in April 1945, covering most of the war.
r: Harry Truman succeeded him and ordered the atomic bombings of Japan in August 1945.

q: What is the average life span of a red blood cell in the human body? (5)
f: Red blood cells live for about 120 days and are then broken down in the spleen and liver.
r: Red blood cells are made in the bone marrow.

q: The 24th of January is celebrated as the day of what? (5)
f: The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education in 2018.
r: The day highlights the role of education in peace and development.

q: In which year was the Badshahi Mosque of Lahore built? (5)
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb Alamgir and completed in 1673.
r: For centuries it was the largest mosque in the world by capacity, and it stands opposite Lahore Fort.

q: Which pact was signed in 1916 between the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League? (5)
f: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League on joint political demands. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was called the Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity for his role in this pact.

q: Who imposed martial law in Pakistan in July 1977 and served as Chief Martial Law Administrator? (5)
f: General Zia ul Haq, the Chief of Army Staff, removed Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on 5 July 1977 (Operation Fair Play) and imposed martial law.
r: Zia ul Haq ruled until his death in an air crash on 17 August 1988.

q: Who dismissed the first government of Benazir Bhutto in August 1990? (5)
f: President Ghulam Ishaq Khan used the power of Article 58(2)(b) to dismiss her government in August 1990 on charges of corruption and misrule.
r: Nawaz Sharif became Prime Minister after the October 1990 elections.

q: Which continent has the largest number of countries? (5)
f: Africa has 54 countries recognised by the United Nations, the most of any continent.
r: Asia has about 48 to 49 countries and Europe about 44 to 50, depending on the source.

q: The Constitution of 1956 was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on which date? (7)
f: The Constituent Assembly adopted the first Constitution on 29 February 1956 (1956 was a leap year).
r: It came into force on 23 March 1956, later celebrated as Republic Day.

q: Which Prime Minister played the leading role in framing the Constitution of 1956? (22)
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the 1956 Constitution.
r: He also served as Finance Minister and Secretary General of the government earlier.

q: On which date did the Constitution of 1956 come into force? (14)
f: The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.
r: 23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the 1940 Lahore Resolution.

q: The Constitution of 1956 was framed by the Constituent Assembly in the name of whom?
f: The Constitution was adopted in the name of the people of Pakistan, as the preamble says.
r: The Objective Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble basis.

q: The Constitution of 1956 received its assent from which office holder?
f: The Governor General (Iskander Mirza) gave assent to the Constitution passed by the Constituent Assembly. He became the first President on 23 March 1956.
r: The office of Governor General was replaced by the President.

q: What name did the Constitution of 1956 give to the country? (31)
f: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic, the first in the world.
r: The 1962 Constitution first dropped the word Islamic from the name.

q: Which part of the Constitution of 1956 dealt with Fundamental Rights?
f: Fundamental Rights were placed in Part II of the 1956 Constitution.
r: The Directive Principles of State Policy came in the following part.

q: Which form of government was provided by the Constitution of 1956? (2)
f: The 1956 Constitution set up a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister and cabinet responsible to the National Assembly.
r: The 1962 Constitution changed this to a presidential system.

q: According to the Constitution of 1956, who was the Head of State?
f: The President replaced the Governor General as constitutional Head of State.
r: Iskander Mirza was the first President of Pakistan.

q: What was the minimum age to become President under the Constitution of 1956? (44)
f: The 1956 Constitution required the President to be at least 40 years old and a Muslim.
r: The 1962 Constitution lowered the minimum age to 35.

q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1956 provide? (3)
f: It provided a single-house National Assembly of 300 members, equally divided between East and West Pakistan.
r: Pakistan's first bicameral legislature came with the 1973 Constitution.

q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1956?
f: The 1956 Constitution created the Supreme Court of Pakistan, replacing the Federal Court that existed since 1948. The source marked Federal Court, which is wrong.
r: The Federal Shariat Court was created much later, in 1980.

q: Which languages were made national languages by the Constitution of 1956?
f: Urdu and Bengali were declared the state languages in the 1956 Constitution, with English used officially for 20 years.
r: Bengali was recognised after the 1952 Language Movement.

q: Which type of federal structure did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
f: It provided a federation of two wings, East and West Pakistan, with federal, provincial and concurrent lists.
r: Powers were distributed through three lists.

q: How many Articles and Parts did the Constitution of 1956 contain? (49)
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles, 13 Parts and 6 Schedules.
r: The 1973 Constitution has 280 Articles.

q: For about how long did the Constitution of 1956 remain in force? (2)
f: It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated on 7 October 1958, about two and a half years.
r: It was the shortest-lived of Pakistan's three constitutions.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1956 abrogated? (5)
f: President Iskander Mirza abrogated it on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
r: Ayub Khan became Chief Martial Law Administrator and removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.

q: Which body enacted the Constitution of 1956?
f: The second Constituent Assembly passed it, as the first one had been dissolved in 1954.
r: Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in October 1954.

q: What was the total strength of the National Assembly under the Constitution of 1956?
f: It had 300 members, 150 from each wing, plus 10 seats reserved for women, so 310. The Constitution also kept parity between the wings.
r: Today the National Assembly has 336 seats.

q: How were members of the National Assembly elected under the Constitution of 1956?
f: The Constitution provided direct elections to the National Assembly, though no general election was held before it was abrogated.
r: The first direct adult-franchise general election was held in 1970.

q: What type of citizenship did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
f: Pakistan had a single citizenship for all citizens, as in a federation like India but unlike the USA.
r: The 1973 Constitution also has a single citizenship.

q: Under the Constitution of 1956, how were powers divided in the federation?
f: Powers were shared through a Federal List, a Provincial List and a Concurrent List.
r: The 1962 Constitution had only Central and Provincial subjects.

q: Under the Constitution of 1956, to whom was the Cabinet collectively responsible?
f: In the parliamentary system the Cabinet led by the Prime Minister was answerable to the National Assembly.
r: The Prime Minister was the head of government.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1962 enforced? (4)
f: President Ayub Khan promulgated it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force on 8 June 1962. Note the source gave 28 February, which is not the correct date.
r: Martial law was lifted when it came into force.

q: In how many Parts was the Constitution of 1962 divided (it had 250 Articles)?
f: The 1962 Constitution had 250 Articles, 12 Parts and 3 Schedules.
r: The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles and 13 Parts.

q: Which form of government did the Constitution of 1962 provide? (75)
f: It created a strong presidential system with the President as Chief Executive.
r: There was no Prime Minister in the 1962 Constitution as originally framed.

q: How was the President elected under the Constitution of 1962? (41)
f: The President was elected indirectly by an electoral college of Basic Democrats.
r: Ayub Khan won the 1965 election against Fatima Jinnah this way.

q: The electoral college under the Constitution of 1962 was originally formed of how many Basic Democrats?
f: Originally 80,000 Basic Democrats (40,000 per wing) formed the electoral college.
r: It was later raised to 120,000 before the 1965 election.

q: What was the voting age under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution set the minimum voting age at 21 years.
r: The voting age was lowered to 18 in 1973 and is now 18.

q: What was the minimum age for a person to be elected President under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution required the President to be at least 35 years of age and a Muslim.
r: Under the 1956 Constitution it was 40 years.

q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who had the power to dissolve the National Assembly?
f: The President held the power to dissolve the Assembly, one of his wide powers. The source asked the Article number, which could not be verified.
r: Under the 1973 Constitution this power is in Article 58.

q: Under the Constitution of 1962, who could be impeached by the National Assembly?
f: The Constitution provided a process for impeaching the President, though it was very difficult to use.
r: In the 1973 Constitution the President is removed under Article 47.

q: The Constitution of 1962 provided a federation of the centre and how many provinces?
f: The federation consisted of two provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.
r: West Pakistan was a single province created through One Unit in 1955.

q: What was the original name of the country under the Constitution of 1962? (2)
f: The 1962 Constitution dropped the word Islamic and called the country the Republic of Pakistan.
r: The word Islamic was restored by an amendment.

q: In which month of 1963 did the National Assembly pass the amendment restoring the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
f: The first Amendment Act was passed in December 1963 and restored the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: The amendment was formally assented in January 1964.

q: Who was the Chief Executive of the country under the Constitution of 1962? (2)
f: The President was both head of state and chief executive.
r: Ayub Khan was the first President under this Constitution.

q: What was the term of office of the President under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The President held office for five years.
r: The 1973 Constitution also gives a five-year term.

q: Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The Supreme Court remained the apex court of the country.
r: The Supreme Court was first created by the 1956 Constitution.

q: What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
f: It provided a single-house National Assembly.
r: The Senate came only with the 1973 Constitution.

q: Up to which age could a Supreme Court judge serve under the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution set retirement of Supreme Court judges at 65 years.
r: Under the 1973 Constitution it is also 65 years.

q: Which languages were national languages under the Constitution of 1962?
f: Urdu and Bengali were national languages, while English remained in official use.
r: Bengali was first recognised in 1956.

q: Which system of local government did Ayub Khan make the base of the Constitution of 1962?
f: The Basic Democracies system of 1959 created union councils whose members formed the electoral college.
r: The Devolution Plan was introduced later, in 2001.

q: Which city was named as the capital of Pakistan in the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution named the newly built city of Islamabad as the capital, with Rawalpindi serving as the interim capital while it was being built.
r: Ayub Khan chose the site of Islamabad near General Headquarters at Rawalpindi.

q: Under which Article of the 1962 Constitution could the President promulgate Ordinances when the National Assembly was not in session?
f: Article 29 of the 1962 Constitution allowed the President to make an Ordinance with the same force as an Act when the Assembly was dissolved or not in session and immediate legislation was needed.
r: Such an Ordinance covered only matters within the competence of the Central Legislature.

q: Under Article 226 of the 1962 Constitution, who was treated as the first President of Pakistan under that Constitution?
f: Article 226 (transitional provisions) provided that, following the referendum of February 1960, Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan was to be the first President under the 1962 Constitution.
r: The 1962 Constitution came into force on 8 June 1962.

q: Which Order, issued by General Yahya Khan on 30 March 1970, set the framework for the first general elections and for making a new constitution?
f: The Legal Framework Order of 30 March 1970 laid down the basis for the December 1970 elections and required the elected Assembly to frame a constitution within 120 days.
r: The LFO also ended the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan on 1 July 1970.

q: In which month and year was the Constitution of 1962 abrogated? (4)
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
r: The 1962 Constitution had come into force on 8 June 1962.

q: For approximately how many years did the Constitution of 1962 remain in force?
f: It was in force from 8 June 1962 until 25 March 1969, which is about seven years (nearly six years and nine months).
r: It was Pakistan's second constitution.

q: Which system of government was introduced by the Constitution of 1962?
f: The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive power in the President, who was both head of state and head of government, so critics called it a one-man show.
r: The President was elected indirectly by Electoral College of Basic Democrats.

q: Who abrogated the Constitution of 1962? (16)
f: General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
r: Yahya Khan became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.

q: On which date was the Constitution of 1973 authenticated by the President of Pakistan?
f: The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973 and President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry authenticated it on 12 April 1973.
r: The President who authenticated it was Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.

q: On which date did the Constitution of 1973 come into force?
f: The Constitution was enforced on 14 August 1973, the Independence Day, after being authenticated on 12 April 1973.
r: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister under it.

q: How many Articles does the Constitution of 1973 contain?
f: The Constitution of 1973 has 280 Articles divided into 12 Parts.
r: Articles added by amendments carry letters, for example Article 140A and Article 10A.

q: On which date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The Objectives Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan.
r: It became the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to whom?
f: The Objectives Resolution states that sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone.
r: It adds that the authority is delegated to the State through its people as a sacred trust.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the authority exercised by the people of Pakistan within limits set by Allah is a what?
f: The Resolution says the authority to be exercised by the people within the limits prescribed by Allah is a sacred trust.
r: The Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers through the chosen representatives of the people.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, through whom shall the State exercise its powers and authority?
o: The chosen representatives of the people
f: The Objectives Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers and authority through the chosen representatives of the people.
r: It also promises democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice as enunciated by Islam.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, how shall Muslims be enabled to order their lives?
o: In accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam
f: The Resolution says Muslims shall be enabled to order their lives in the individual and collective spheres in accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam as set out in the Quran and Sunnah.
r: The Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, what freedom shall be given to minorities?
o: To profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures freely
To follow only the teachings of Islam
To live as decided by government policy
f: The Resolution says adequate provision shall be made for minorities freely to profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures.
r: It also promises to safeguard the legitimate interests of minorities and backward classes.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, the independence of the judiciary shall be what?
f: The Resolution states that the independence of the judiciary shall be fully secured.
r: It also says fundamental rights, including equality of status and opportunity, shall be guaranteed.

q: According to the Objectives Resolution, Pakistan will make its full contribution towards what?
o: International peace and progress and the happiness of humanity
f: The Resolution says the people of Pakistan should attain their rightful place among nations and make their full contribution towards international peace and progress and the happiness of humanity.
r: This is the closing aim stated in the Resolution and in the Preamble.

q: In what form was the Objectives Resolution placed in the Constitution of 1973 as originally enacted?
f: In the original 1973 Constitution the Objectives Resolution was the Preamble. It became a substantive part later through Article 2A.
r: Article 2A was inserted by the Eighth Amendment in 1985.

q: What name does Article 1 of the Constitution of 1973 give to Pakistan?
f: Article 1(1) says Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: The name Islamic Republic was first used in the 1956 Constitution.

q: After the 25th Amendment of 2018, what do the territories of Pakistan under Article 1 comprise?
o: Four provinces, FATA and the Federal Capital
The provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh, and the Islamabad Capital Territory (plus such other territories as may be included)
Four provinces, Azad Kashmir and Islamabad only
f: The 25th Amendment (2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed it from Article 1, so Article 1(2) now lists four provinces and the Islamabad Capital Territory. The older answer with FATA is outdated.
r: Article 1(2)(c) also covers such States and territories as are or may be included in Pakistan.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is Islam declared the State religion of Pakistan? (32)
f: Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
r: Article 2A makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution?
f: Article 2A states that the principles and provisions of the Objectives Resolution (Annex) are made substantive part of the Constitution and have effect accordingly.
r: It was inserted in 1985 through the Eighth Amendment.

q: Under Article 5(1) of the Constitution of 1973, loyalty to whom is the basic duty of every citizen?
f: Article 5(1) says loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen.
r: Article 5 is in Part I of the Constitution.

q: Article 5(2) of the Constitution of 1973 describes obedience to the Constitution and law as the what of every citizen?
f: Article 5(2) says obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be and of every other person within Pakistan.
r: Article 5(1) makes loyalty to the State the basic duty of every citizen.

q: A person who abrogates, subverts, suspends or holds in abeyance the Constitution by force or unconstitutional means is guilty of what under Article 6?
f: Article 6(1) says any person who abrogates or subverts the Constitution by use of force or show of force or other unconstitutional means is guilty of high treason.
r: The words 'suspends or holds in abeyance' were added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.

q: Under Article 6(3) of the Constitution, who is empowered to provide the punishment for persons found guilty of high treason?
f: Article 6(3) says the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) shall by law provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of high treason.
r: The High Treason (Punishment) Act 1973 was passed under this Article.

q: In which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the State defined for the purposes of Fundamental Rights?
f: Article 7 defines the State as the Federal Government, Parliament, a Provincial Government, a Provincial Assembly and local authorities.
r: Article 8 follows and deals with laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.

q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution contain the Principles of Policy?
f: Chapter 2 of Part II, Articles 29 to 40, sets out the Principles of Policy.
r: Principles of Policy are not enforceable in court, unlike the Fundamental Rights.

q: Under Article 8 of the 1973 Constitution, a law that is inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights is what?
o: Void to the extent of the inconsistency
f: Article 8 says any law inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
r: Article 8 itself falls in Chapter 1 of Part II.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law?
f: Article 9 (security of person) says no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.
r: The Supreme Court has read the right to life broadly to include a healthy environment.

q: Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution deal with the Fundamental Rights?
f: Chapter 1 of Part II, Articles 8 to 28, contains the Fundamental Rights.
r: Articles 29 to 40 contain the Principles of Policy.

q: What is Chapter 1 of Part II of the 1973 Constitution (Articles 8 to 28) called?
f: Chapter 1 of Part II is titled Fundamental Rights, the rights guaranteed by the Constitution and enforceable in court.
r: Chapter 2 of Part II is titled Principles of Policy.

q: Safeguards as to arrest and detention are provided in which Article of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 10 gives safeguards on arrest and detention, including the right to be told the grounds and to appear before a magistrate within 24 hours.
r: Article 10A adds the right to a fair trial.

q: Article 10A of the 1973 Constitution deals with which right?
o: Right to fair trial and due process
f: Article 10A guarantees the right to fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and criminal charges.
r: Article 25A deals with free and compulsory education.

q: Through which amendment was the right to fair trial (Article 10A) added to the Fundamental Rights?
f: Article 10A was inserted by the 18th Amendment of 2010.
r: The 18th Amendment also inserted Article 19A (right to information) and Article 25A (right to education).

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution are slavery and forced labour prohibited?
f: Article 11 prohibits slavery, forced labour and the employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work.
r: Article 11 also forbids trafficking in human beings.

q: Article 12 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
f: Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment, meaning no one can be punished for an act that was not an offence when it was done.
r: Article 13 protects against double punishment and self-incrimination.

q: Article 13 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
f: Article 13 says no person shall be punished more than once for the same offence nor be compelled to be a witness against himself.
r: Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment.

q: Under which provision of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be subjected to torture for extracting evidence?
f: Article 14(2) says no person shall be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.
r: Article 14(1) says the dignity of man and the privacy of home shall be inviolable.

q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 15 of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 15 guarantees every citizen the right to remain in, enter and move freely throughout Pakistan and settle in any part of it, subject to law.
r: Freedom of speech is in Article 19.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is freedom of assembly guaranteed?
f: Article 16 gives every citizen the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.
r: Article 17 covers freedom of association.

q: Which freedom is provided in Article 17 of the 1973 Constitution?
f: Article 17 gives every citizen the right to form associations or unions and to form or be a member of a political party, subject to restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of Pakistan.
r: Article 16 covers freedom of assembly.

q: Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 18 of the 1973 Constitution?
o: Freedom of trade, business or profession
f: Article 18 gives every citizen the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation and to conduct any lawful trade or business.
r: Article 20 covers freedom to profess religion.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution does every citizen have the right of access to information in matters of public importance?
f: Article 19A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives every citizen the right of access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.
r: Article 19 itself covers freedom of speech.

q: Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is there safeguard against taxation for the purposes of any particular religion?
f: Article 21 says no person shall be compelled to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.
r: Article 20 gives freedom to profess religion and to manage religious institutions.

q: If yesterday was Sunday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (85)
f: Yesterday Sunday means today is Monday; the day after tomorrow is Monday + 2 = Wednesday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: If the 4th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 19th day be? (21)
f: The gap is 19 - 4 = 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Friday + 1 = Saturday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: What is 90% of 90? (2350)
r: Shortcut: x% of y equals y% of x, so 90% of 90 is 9 x 9 = 81.

q: What is one third of 10% of 90?
f: 10% of 90 = 9, and one third of 9 = 3.
r: 10% of a number: move the decimal point one place to the left.

q: What is one third of 10% of 120? (54)
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one third of 12 = 4.
r: Work from the inside out: first the percentage, then the fraction.

q: How many months of a year have 31 days? (382)
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days, so there are seven.
r: Knuckle trick: every knuckle is a 31-day month and every gap is a shorter month (July and August are both 31).

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 paper? (42)
f: 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, so he writes 1 paper per minute.
r: Rate = work divided by time; find the rate of one worker first.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls? (76)
r: Percentage = part / total x 100; for a part of 500, divide the part by 5.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2/2? (984)
f: Division comes first: 2/2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
r: BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division and Multiplication, then Addition and Subtraction.

q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 120? (349)
f: One tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.
r: Quarter of a number is the number divided by 4; one tenth is divided by 10.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the percentage of women? (68)
r: If 2/3 is one group, the rest is 1/3, which is 33.33%.

q: Ali bought a pen for Rs 30 and sold it for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage? (233)
r: Profit % is always calculated on the cost price, not the selling price.

q: Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon. (92)
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed shapes (polygons); an angle is not a shape.
r: In odd-one-out questions, find the property that three items share.

q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball? (167)
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket; football is mainly played with the foot.
r: Look for the equipment or the way the game is played.

q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley. (32)
f: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains for humans; hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.
r: Group by use: grains for food versus fodder.

q: Which one is different from the others: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda, Baboon?
f: Monkey, ape, chimpanzee and baboon are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: Primates include monkeys, apes, baboons and humans.

q: Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro. (4)
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents; the Euro is a currency (the continent is Europe).
r: There are seven continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 26th day be? (35)
f: The gap is 26 - 4 = 22 days; 22 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. How many women are there? (11)
r: Find the fraction of the other group as 1 minus the given fraction.

q: A man walked towards the north, then turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction? (82)
f: North, then left gives West, then right from West gives North.
r: Left turn: N to W to S to E. Right turn: N to E to S to W.

q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ? (36)
f: Two series are mixed: 115, 170, 235 (add 55, then 65) and 55, 65, 75 (add 10), so the missing term is 75.
r: If a series looks random, separate the alternate terms into two series.

q: Complete the series: 66, 63, 57, 45, ? (57)
f: The differences are 3, 6, 12 (doubling), so the next difference is 24 and 45 - 24 = 21.
r: Check differences first; if they double, the series is a doubling-difference series.

q: Complete the series: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ? (3)
f: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.

q: Complete the series: B, E, J, Q, ? (35)
f: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9 and 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.
r: Letter series: convert letters to numbers (A=1 ... Z=26) and study the gaps.

q: Complete the series: A, C, F, J, O, ? (55)
f: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (gaps 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next gap is 6 and 15 + 6 = 21 = U.
r: Gaps that increase by 1 are the triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21.

q: Complete the series: L, M, N, ? (19)
f: The letters are consecutive in the alphabet, so after N comes O.
r: Simple consecutive series go forward one letter at a time.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 19th day be? (2)
f: The gap is 15 days; 15 divided by 7 leaves 1, so Sunday + 1 = Monday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 4th day be?
f: The gap is 10 days backwards; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Sunday - 3 = Thursday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: Why do parents give education to their children? (21)
f: Education develops and grooms a child into a capable and responsible person.
r: In such questions choose the most natural and purposeful answer.

q: Why do we boil milk? (1761)
f: Boiling kills harmful germs (bacteria), making the milk safe to drink.
r: Pasteurisation is a similar heating process used for packaged milk.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (212)
f: Yesterday Friday means today is Saturday; the day after tomorrow is Saturday + 2 = Monday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (19)
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h; in 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time; convert minutes into hours first.

q: A bat cannot see; a snake cannot what? (278)
f: A snake has no outer ears and cannot hear airborne sound well, so the answer is hear (note: in reality a bat can see; it also uses echolocation).
r: Snakes sense vibrations through the ground and use their tongue to smell.

q: What is the sound made by an eagle called?
f: The call of an eagle is described as a scream.
r: Other animal sounds: lion roars, owl hoots, dog barks.

q: What is half of 9/90?
f: 9/90 = 0.1, and half of 0.1 = 0.05 = 1/20 (so the source statement of 1/5 or 0.2 is wrong).
r: Simplify the fraction first: 9/90 = 1/10.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (158)
r: Present % + absent % = 100%, so 80% present means 20% absent.

q: My brother's sister is your mother. Taking me as a male, what am I to you? (55)
f: My brother's sister is my own sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, that is, your maternal uncle.
r: Brother's sister means own sister (or oneself if female).

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be? (14)
f: The gap is 11 days; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday + 4 = Friday (the source statement of Saturday is wrong).
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, how long will 1 man take to write 1 page?
f: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men write 5 pages in the same 5 minutes).
r: When workers and work are equal, each worker does one unit in the given time.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (25)
f: Train speed = 2 x 30 = 60 km/h; in half an hour it covers 30 km.
r: Distance = speed x time; 30 minutes is half an hour.

q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 1.11 minutes (the source value 0.9 is wrong).
r: Minutes per km = total minutes / total km.

q: What is 80% of 90? (19)
In a classroom, out of 1500 students 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (311)
r: Simplify first: 1200/1500 = 4/5 = 80%.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 12th day be? (19)
f: The gap is 10 days; 10 divided by 7 leaves 3, so Monday + 3 = Thursday (the source statement of Friday is wrong).
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 23rd day be?
f: The gap is 21 days, which is exactly 3 weeks, so the day stays Sunday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: What is the value of (2 + 2)?
f: Adding the numbers in the bracket gives 2 + 2 = 4 (the source statement of 8 is wrong).
r: Brackets are solved first.

q: What is one third of 120? (58)
r: A third is the number divided by 3.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, what is the price of 4 pencils? (2)
f: One dozen = 12 pencils; price of 1 pencil = 27 / 12 = 2.25; 4 pencils = Rs 9.
r: 4 pencils is a third of a dozen, so the price is a third of 27.

q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then turns left again. What is his present direction? (100)
f: North, then left gives West, then left again gives South.
r: Two left turns make a U-turn (opposite direction).

q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (151)
r: Present is 68%, so absent is 100 - 68 = 32%.

q: A train is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (45)
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 90 / 5 = 18 km.
r: Convert minutes to hours: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour.

q: A man covers 20 km in one hour and 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km? (30)
f: Total time is 100 minutes for 20 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 20 = 5 minutes (the source value 0.2 is wrong).
r: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 4th day be? (2)
f: The gap is 11 days backwards; 11 divided by 7 leaves 4, so Monday - 4 = Thursday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: In a class of 24 students, 1/4 are male. What is the percentage of females? (19)
r: If 1/4 are male, then 3/4 = 75% are female.

q: A man walks towards the north, then turns left, then turns right. What is his present direction? (82)
f: North, left gives West, then right from West gives North again.
r: A left turn followed by a right turn returns to the original direction.

q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically? (8)
f: Alphabetical order: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U; the third letter is E.
r: Write the letters in order and count carefully; repeated letters count twice.

q: An aeroplane flies in the air mainly because of which force? (5)
f: The shape of the wings produces lift, which overcomes weight so the aeroplane flies.
r: Four forces on a plane: lift, weight, thrust and drag.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as clock is to what? (18)
f: Wheels are a part of a vehicle, and hands are a part of a clock.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: After how many years does a leap year normally come? (9)
f: A leap year (366 days) comes every 4 years, for example 2024 and 2028.
r: Century years are leap years only if divisible by 400.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes (at the same speed)?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 120/100 = 1.2 km per minute; in 15 minutes: 1.2 x 15 = 18 km. The printed answer 30 km in the source is wrong.
r: Find the speed per minute first, then multiply by the minutes.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will tomorrow be?
f: Yesterday Friday means today is Saturday, so tomorrow is Sunday.
r: Yesterday, today and tomorrow are three consecutive days; tomorrow is 2 days after yesterday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, what day will the 14th day be?
f: The gap is 10 days and 10 mod 7 = 3, so the day moves 3 step(s) ahead of Sunday, which gives Wednesday. The source statement (14th is Monday) is wrong.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: A car is moving at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
f: 10 minutes = 1/6 hour, and 120 x 1/6 = 20 km.
r: Km per minute = km/h divided by 60 (120 km/h = 2 km per minute).

q: What is 120 x 7?
r: Multiply the non-zero part first, then add the zero back.

q: If the 28th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 8th day be? (5)
f: The 2nd date is 20 days earlier; 20 mod 7 = 6, so go back 6 day(s) from Monday (same as 1 ahead), which gives Tuesday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km? (30)
f: 100 minutes / 20 km = 5 minutes per km.
r: Time per km = total time divided by total km.

q: Ahmad walks towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now? (18)
f: Facing north, the left hand side is west.
r: Facing north: left is west, right is east. Facing south: left is east, right is west.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd day be? (25)
f: The gap is 21 days and 21 mod 7 = 0, so the day moves 0 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Friday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister Sidra is twice his age. How old will Sidra be when Ali is 11 years old?
f: Sidra is 10 now, so she is 5 years older than Ali. When Ali is 11, Sidra is 11 + 5 = 16.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, what day will the 13th day be? (19)
f: The gap is 12 days and 12 mod 7 = 5, so the day moves 5 step(s) ahead of Monday, which gives Saturday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: What is a quarter of 120? (90)
r: A quarter is 25 percent, and half of a half.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage are boys? (6)
r: Percentage = part/total x 100; out of 500, each student is 0.2 percent.

q: If 1 dozen pencils cost Rs 60, what is the cost of 5 pencils?
f: 1 dozen = 12 pencils, so one pencil costs 60/12 = Rs 5; 5 pencils cost Rs 25.
r: One dozen = 12, a half dozen = 6, a gross = 144.

q: A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (2)
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour, and 120/5 = 24 km.
r: 12 minutes is one fifth of an hour.

q: After arranging the letters of SIRAP, it becomes the name of a country, city, ocean or state. Which one is it?
f: The letters of SIRAP rearrange to PARIS, the capital city of France. So it is a city.
r: Anagram questions: look for a familiar name first, then check that every letter is used.

q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to what? (3)
f: A bitch is a female dog; the female horse is a mare.
r: Male horse: stallion; young horse: foal; young female: filly.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 18th day be?
f: The gap is 14 days and 14 mod 7 = 0, so the day moves 0 step(s) ahead of Monday, which gives Monday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 14th day be? (15)
f: The gap is 12 days and 12 mod 7 = 5, so the day moves 5 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Wednesday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: What will be the last letter of UTYEAB after arranging its letters alphabetically? (41)
f: Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.
r: Letters of the alphabet end with Z; Y is the later of the letters U, T, E, A, B, Y.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word Managment when its letters are arranged alphabetically? (37)
f: Letters of Managment: A, A, E, G, M, M, N, N, T in alphabetical order, so the 3rd letter is E. The source answer G is wrong (G is 4th). The same answer E applies to the correctly spelled MANAGEMENT.
