r: Write the letters in order, keeping repeated letters, and count carefully.

q: A person purchased a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. What is the profit percentage? (6)
r: Profit % is always calculated on the cost price.

q: What is one tenth of 90? (34)
r: One tenth means divide by 10, which moves the decimal one place left.

q: What is one tenth of 120? (75)
r: One tenth means divide by 10, which moves the decimal one place left.

q: If yesterday was Monday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?
f: Yesterday Monday means today is Tuesday; tomorrow is Wednesday and the day after tomorrow is Thursday.
r: Day after tomorrow is 3 days after yesterday.

q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons of fuel to move 320 km, how many gallons will it need to move 400 km? (14)
f: Fuel per km = 50/320; for 400 km: 50 x 400/320 = 62.5 gallons.
r: Direct proportion: more distance needs proportionally more fuel.

q: Amjad and Ahmad kept 24 balls together. Amjad kept 3 times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep? (8)
f: Let Ahmad have x; Amjad has 3x, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
r: For a ratio 1:3 the total has 4 parts; divide the total by 4.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when the boy is 11 years old? (21)
f: The sister is 9 now, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11, she is 17.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: What is 20% of one tenth of 90?
f: One tenth of 90 = 9; 20% of 9 = 1.8.
r: 20% is one fifth, so divide by 5.

q: What is the sister of my brother's son to me? (7)
f: My brother's son's sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
r: Brother's or sister's son is a nephew; daughter is a niece.

q: A boy has an average of 50 marks in 5 tests. How many marks must he score in the 6th test to raise his average to 70?
f: Total of 5 tests = 250. Total needed for 6 tests = 70 x 6 = 420. Next test = 420 - 250 = 170 (not possible if each test is out of 100, but this is the mathematical answer).
r: Needed score = new average x number of tests minus the current total.

q: My age is 10 years and my brother is 2 times my age. What will be the ratio of my age to my brother's age after 10 years? (2)
f: Brother is 20 now. After 10 years I am 20 and he is 30, so the ratio is 20:30 = 2:3 (the reverse order gives 3:2).
r: Add the same years to both ages before finding the ratio; never add years to the ratio itself.

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd day be? (4)
f: The gap is 20 days and 20 mod 7 = 6, so the day moves 6 step(s) ahead of Friday, which gives Thursday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 10 years old? (2)
f: The sister is 15 now, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10, she is 20.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, what day will the 12th day be?
f: The gap is 8 days and 8 mod 7 = 1, so the day moves 1 step(s) ahead of Tuesday, which gives Wednesday.
r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap between the two dates by 7 (gap 7, 14, 21 gives the same day).

q: Saleem has an average of 60 in 4 subjects. His average drops to 58 after the next test. How many marks did he score in that test?
f: Total of 4 = 240. Total of 5 = 58 x 5 = 290. Next test = 290 - 240 = 50. (The source asks to find the grade; the marks are the only value that can be worked out.)
r: New test marks = new average x new count minus old total.

q: 10 men dig a well in 5 days. How many days will 5 men take to dig it? (2)
f: Work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days; with 5 men: 50/5 = 10 days. The source answer 20 is wrong.
r: Fewer men take proportionally more days (inverse proportion): men x days = constant.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali's age is twice Salman's age. What will be Ali's age when Salman is 12 years old? (7)
f: Ali is 8 now, 4 years older than Salman. When Salman is 12, Ali is 16.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad. Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest? (8)
f: Order from eldest: Umair, Akbar, Ahmad.
r: Write the names in a line from oldest to youngest to solve ranking questions.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Adil is 15 years old? (3)
f: Sister is 15 now, 10 years older than Adil. When Adil is 15, she is 25.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: What is 80% of 80? (30)
r: 80% = 4/5, so divide by 5 and multiply by 4.

q: What is 90% of 70? (6)
r: 90% = whole minus 10 percent.

q: Write the word formed from the numbers 18, 5, 19, 20 (A=1, B=2, and so on). (19)
f: 18 = R, 5 = E, 19 = S, 20 = T, so the word is REST.
r: Position shortcuts: A=1, E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Z=26.

q: The sister of my brother is your mother. What is your relation to me?
f: My brother's sister is my sister (taking me as male), and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother and you are my nephew or niece.
r: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle; his children's relation to you is cousin, and you are his nephew or niece.

q: Adnan walks 10 meters towards the north, then towards the south. After this he turns back and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
f: After walking south he faces south; turning back he faces north; turning left from north he faces west.
r: Turning back means a 180 degree turn; left of north is west.

q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. How much distance does it cover in 1 minute? (2)
f: 20 km / 60 minutes = 1/3 km = 0.333 km. The printed answer 0.3 km is only a rounded value.
r: Km per minute = km/h divided by 60.

q: What is 60% of 9? (2)
What is 80% of 10?
r: Percent of 10: move the decimal one place and multiply (10% of 10 = 1).

q: What is 90% of 90?
r: 10% of 90 is 9, so 90% is 90 minus 9 = 81.

q: What is one-third of 10% of 120?
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one-third of 12 = 4.
r: 10% of a number is the number divided by 10.

q: What is one-third of 10% of 90?
f: 10% of 90 = 9, and one-third of 9 = 3.
r: One-third of a number is the number divided by 3.

q: What is one-fourth of 120?
f: 120 divided by 4 = 30.
r: One-fourth is the same as 25%.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what will be the 24th day of that month?
f: From the 4th to the 24th is 20 days; 20 mod 7 = 6, and Monday plus 6 days = Sunday.
r: A week has 7 days, so dates 7 apart fall on the same weekday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, what will be the 23rd day of that month?
f: From the 2nd to the 23rd is 21 days = exactly 3 weeks, so the day is again Sunday.
r: Dates 7, 14 or 21 days apart share the same weekday.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of the sister when the boy is 11 years old?
f: Sister is 9 when the boy is 3, so she is 6 years older. When the boy is 11, she is 11 + 6 = 17.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present and absent students?
f: 1200/1500 x 100 = 80% present, so absent = 300 students = 20%.
r: If 1300 were present, the percentage would be 86.67% present.

q: Amjad and Ahmad kept 25 balls. Amjad kept 4 times as many as Ahmad. How many balls did Ahmad keep?
f: Let Ahmad have x; then x + 4x = 25, so x = 5 (Amjad has 20).
r: Total shares = 1 + 4 = 5, and 25 divided by 5 = 5.

q: Ali bought a pen for Rs. 30 and sold it for Rs. 40. What is his profit percentage?
r: Profit percentage is always calculated on the cost price.

q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, how much time will he take to cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100/90 = 10/9 minutes, about 1.11 minutes.
r: His speed is 90 km per 100 minutes, i.e. 54 km per hour.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, in how many minutes will 1 man write 1 page?
f: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes (5 men x 5 minutes gives 5 pages, one page per man).
r: Rate per man is 1 page per 5 minutes.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 120 km/h; in half an hour it covers 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the number of women?
r: Women are 1/3 of the passengers.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the oldest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Umair is the oldest.
r: Chain comparisons can be written as a single ordered line.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Ahmad is the youngest.
r: The person who is older than nobody in the chain is the youngest.

q: Ali moves towards the north, after some time he turns left, then again turns left. What is his present direction?
f: Facing north, a left turn gives west, and another left turn gives south.
r: Two left turns (or two right turns) reverse the direction.

q: A man walked towards the north, then he turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
f: North, left turn gives west, right turn from west gives north again.
r: A left turn followed by a right turn cancel each other.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The 3rd letter is E.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

q: What will be the 3rd letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 3rd letter is E.
r: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E repeated twice.

q: The jumbled word UTYEAB is rearranged to form a word. What will be the last letter of that word when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: UTYEAB forms BEAUTY. Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.
r: Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet, the highest letter in this word.

q: Arrange the jumbled word OPERALD to form a word and identify its category.
f: OPERALD rearranges to LEOPARD, a big wild cat.
r: The leopard is a member of the big cat family.

q: According to the dictionary order, which word comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
f: All start with M; the second letters A, A, O put Mountain last. Between MACHINE and MARGALLA, C comes before R, so Machine is first.
r: Dictionary order compares letter by letter from the left.

q: What comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
f: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.
r: The gaps are consecutive odd numbers.

q: Find the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize.
f: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains for humans, while hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.
r: Wheat is the main staple crop of Pakistan.

q: Find the odd one out: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda.
f: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: Chimpanzees are apes, not monkeys.

q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you (taking me as a male)?
f: My brother's sister is also my sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, your maternal uncle.
r: Mother's brother is Mamu; father's brother is Chacha.

q: The sister of my brother's son is my what?
f: My brother's son is my nephew; his sister is my brother's daughter, i.e. my niece.
r: A nephew is a brother's or sister's son; a niece is a daughter.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as Sound is to ?
f: A vehicle moves by means of wheels, and sound travels by means of waves.
r: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it needs a medium for its waves.

q: Water is to flow as Air is to ?
f: Water flows and air blows.
r: Moving air is called wind.

q: A bat cannot see well and a snake cannot ?
f: The analogy is a sense that the animal lacks; snakes have no outer ears and are largely deaf to airborne sound.
r: Snakes sense ground vibrations and smell with their forked tongue.

q: How many months of the year have 31 days?
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days.
r: February has 28 or 29 days; April, June, September and November have 30.

q: What is the value of 3P2 (3 permutation 2)?
r: nPr = n!/(n-r)!

q: What is the area of a rectangle whose width is 3 and height is 8?
f: Area = width x height = 3 x 8 = 24.
r: Perimeter of this rectangle would be 2(3 + 8) = 22.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
f: A triangular prism has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces, 5 in total.
r: It has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

q: What is the eccentricity of a parabola?
f: A parabola is the conic section with eccentricity exactly 1.
r: Circle e = 0, ellipse e less than 1, hyperbola e greater than 1.

q: The probability of an event always lies between which values?
f: Probability is 0 for an impossible event and 1 for a certain event; all others lie in between.
r: Probabilities are sometimes expressed as percentages from 0% to 100%.

q: Which city is known as the heart of Pakistan?
f: Lahore is commonly called the heart of Pakistan (and the cultural capital).
r: Lahore is the capital of Punjab and is also called the City of Gardens.

q: What was the earlier capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
f: Karachi was the first capital from 1947; Rawalpindi was temporary capital and Islamabad became capital in the 1960s.
r: Islamabad was built in the 1960s at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

q: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?
f: Astana is the capital; it was called Nur-Sultan from 2019 to 2022 and then renamed Astana again.
r: Almaty was the earlier capital and is the largest city.

q: What is the capital of Ghana?
f: Accra is the capital and largest city of Ghana.
r: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from Britain, in 1957.

q: What is the capital of Austria?
f: Vienna is the capital of Austria.
r: Vienna lies on the River Danube.

q: What is the capital of Somalia?
f: Mogadishu is the capital of Somalia.
r: Somalia is in the Horn of Africa.

q: Who is the Foreign Minister of Iran?
f: Abbas Araghchi has been Iran's Foreign Minister since August 2024 and still held the post in late 2026 reports.
r: Javad Zarif was the earlier Foreign Minister who negotiated the 2015 nuclear deal.

q: Who is the President of China?
f: Xi Jinping has been President of China since 2013.
r: Li Qiang is the Premier of China, not the President.

q: Who was the leader of Germany in World War 2?
f: Adolf Hitler led Nazi Germany as Fuhrer from 1934 to 1945.
r: World War 2 began in 1939 with Germany's invasion of Poland.

q: What is the most important resource of the Arabian countries?
f: Oil (petroleum) is the main economic resource of the Arab Gulf countries.
r: Saudi Arabia has one of the world's largest proven oil reserves.

q: What is the currency of Japan?
f: The Japanese currency is the yen.
r: The Chinese currency is the yuan and the South Korean currency is the won.

q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
f: Australia (Oceania) is the smallest continent by land area.
r: Europe is the second smallest continent.

q: Which is the 2nd largest continent in the world?
f: Asia is the largest, and Africa is second with about 30.3 million sq km.
r: Africa has 54 recognised countries.

q: What is the main source of freshwater in the world?
f: About 68-69% of the world's freshwater is locked in glaciers and ice caps.
r: Only about 3% of all water on Earth is fresh.

q: Which country is the biggest coffee producer in the world?
f: Brazil is the largest coffee producer, supplying roughly a third of the world's coffee.
r: Vietnam is usually the second largest producer.

q: Which country is known as the Land of a Thousand Lakes?
f: Finland has about 188,000 lakes and is called the Land of a Thousand Lakes.
r: Minnesota in the USA is also nicknamed Land of 10,000 Lakes.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
f: Lake Baikal in Russia is about 1,642 m deep, the deepest lake on Earth.
r: Baikal holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater.

q: Which is the longest river in the world (by the traditional measurement)?
f: The Nile is traditionally ranked longest at about 6,650 km; the Amazon is the largest by water volume.
r: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

q: Which is the fastest bird in the world?
f: The peregrine falcon reaches over 320 km/h in its hunting dive.
r: The ostrich is the fastest running bird.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations (UNO)?
f: The UN headquarters is in New York City, USA.
r: The UN was founded in 1945.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank?
f: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.
r: The ADB was established in 1966.

q: At the end of 2016, which country was the third-largest refugee-hosting country in the world according to UNHCR?
f: UNHCR Global Trends 2016: Turkey (2.9 million) was first, Pakistan (1.4 million) second and Lebanon (1.0 million) third.
r: Most refugees in Pakistan are from Afghanistan.

q: Why did America take part in World War 2?
o: Because of the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor
Because of the sinking of the Titanic
Because of the Cuban Missile Crisis
f: The USA entered the war after Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941.
r: Pearl Harbor is in Hawaii.

q: The 2015 nuclear agreement between Iran and world powers (including the USA) is known as?
f: The JCPOA was agreed in July 2015 with Iran by the P5+1; the USA withdrew from it in 2018.
r: The JCPOA limited Iran's uranium enrichment in return for lifting sanctions.

q: In which year did India conduct its first nuclear test?
f: India's first test (Smiling Buddha) was on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran.
r: India's second series of tests, Pokhran-II, was in May 1998.

q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
f: Kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.
r: 0 K is absolute zero, about minus 273.15 degrees Celsius.

q: What is the antonym of Wild?
f: Tamed (domesticated) is the opposite of wild.
r: Fierce and savage are synonyms of wild.

q: What is a synonym of Gorgeous?
f: Gorgeous means very beautiful or stunning.
r: Its antonyms include ugly and plain.

q: Who is the author of Shikwa and Jawab-e-Shikwa?
f: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote Shikwa (1909) and Jawab-e-Shikwa (1913).
r: Both poems are included in his Urdu collection Bang-e-Dra.

q: Who wrote the book Friends Not Masters?
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan wrote his autobiography Friends Not Masters in 1967.
r: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto wrote The Myth of Independence.

q: Who wrote the book Jinnah of Pakistan?
f: Stanley Wolpert, an American historian, wrote Jinnah of Pakistan (1984).
r: Hector Bolitho wrote Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan.

q: What is the national bird of Pakistan?
f: The Chukar partridge is the national bird of Pakistan.
r: The Markhor is the national animal.

q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
f: The national flower of Pakistan is jasmine (Chambeli).
r: Jasmine is a symbol of grace and beauty in Pakistan.

q: Who designed the flag of Pakistan?
f: The national flag of Pakistan was designed by Syed Amir-ud-Din Kidwai, based on the Muslim League flag.
r: The flag was adopted on 11 August 1947.

q: In which region of Asia is Pakistan located?
f: Pakistan is a country of South Asia.
r: It borders Iran, Afghanistan, China and India.

q: Which is the largest river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is the longest and largest river of Pakistan, about 3,180 km long.
r: It rises near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

q: Which is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
f: Chagai in Balochistan is the largest district of Pakistan, with about 44,748 square km.
r: Pakistan's nuclear tests of 1998 were held in the Chagai hills.

q: How many peaks above 8000 metres are located in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan has five peaks above 8000 m: K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I, Gasherbrum II and Broad Peak.
r: K2 (8611 m) is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir, the highest peak of the Hindu Kush in Pakistan?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral is 7708 m high.
r: It is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range.

q: Which line is the boundary between China and India in the eastern sector?
f: The McMahon Line was drawn in 1914 and marks the China-India border in the eastern sector; China does not accept it.
r: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

q: The Wakhan border of Pakistan is shared with which country?
f: The Wakhan strip is part of Afghanistan and touches northern Chitral in Pakistan.
r: The Wakhan Corridor separates Pakistan from Tajikistan.

q: How was Attabad Lake in Gilgit-Baltistan formed?
f: A massive landslide in January 2010 blocked the Hunza River and formed the lake.
r: Attabad Lake is in the Hunza valley near Karakoram Highway.

q: In which province is Mohenjo-Daro located?
f: Mohenjo-Daro is in Larkana district, Sindh.
r: Harappa, the other Indus Valley city, is in Punjab.

q: Why do people visit Ziarat in Balochistan?
o: The tomb of Allama Iqbal is there
f: The Quaid-e-Azam Residency, where Jinnah spent his last days, is in Ziarat.
r: Ziarat is also famous for its juniper forests.

q: Why do we boil milk?
f: Boiling kills harmful germs and bacteria in milk.
r: Pasteurisation also kills germs using controlled heating.

q: Why do parents send children to school?
o: To groom them and give them education
To keep them away from home
f: Parents send children to school for education and character building.
r: Education is a fundamental right under Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan.

q: PEMRA is the regulatory body for which media?
f: The Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority regulates TV and radio.
r: PEMRA was established in 2002.

q: Which city started television broadcasting first in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan Television started in Lahore on 26 November 1964.
r: PTV later opened stations in Dhaka, Karachi, Rawalpindi and Peshawar.

q: When did Pakistan join the United Nations?
f: Pakistan became the 56th member of the UN on 30 September 1947.
r: Afghanistan, Yemen and Pakistan were admitted in that period.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam present his 14 Points?
f: Jinnah presented the 14 Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
r: The Nehru Report was of 1928.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
f: Iqbal gave his presidential address at the Muslim League session in Allahabad in December 1930.
r: He proposed a separate Muslim state in north-west India.

q: When did Muslims get the right of separate electorates?
f: Separate electorates for Muslims were granted by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
r: The Congress accepted them in the Lucknow Pact of 1916.

q: When did Quaid-e-Azam join the All India Muslim League?
f: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913.
r: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906.

q: What was the date of the Lahore Resolution?
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed on 23 March 1940, moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq.
r: It was seconded by Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman.

q: What was the official reason given for the Partition of Bengal in 1905?
f: Lord Curzon said Bengal was too big to govern, so it was divided for administrative reasons.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911.

q: Who became the Prime Minister of Pakistan after Liaquat Ali Khan?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin was Governor-General and then became Prime Minister in 1951 after Liaquat Ali Khan was killed.
r: Liaquat Ali Khan was Pakistan's first Prime Minister.

q: Who was the third Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: The order was Jinnah, Nazimuddin, then Malik Ghulam Muhammad (1951-55).
r: Iskander Mirza was the fourth Governor-General and later first President.

q: Which Act was used as the basis of Pakistan's first (interim) constitution?
f: Pakistan adopted the Government of India Act 1935 with changes as its interim constitution.
r: The first full constitution came in 1956.

q: The 1956 Constitution was framed under the Prime Ministership of which leader?
f: Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the first constitution was adopted on 23 March 1956.
r: Pakistan became an Islamic Republic on that day.

q: The 1962 Constitution of Pakistan was abrogated by whom?
f: General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated it in March 1969.
r: Ayub Khan had given the 1962 Constitution.

q: When were the first general elections held after the 1962 Constitution was abrogated?
f: General elections were held in December 1970 under Yahya Khan.
r: They were the first elections on the basis of one man one vote.

q: How many general seats did the Awami League win in the 1970 elections?
f: The Awami League of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman won 160 general seats, all in East Pakistan.
r: The PPP won 81 seats in West Pakistan.

q: The Shimla Agreement of 1972 was signed between which two leaders?
o: Liaquat Ali Khan and Jawaharlal Nehru
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Indira Gandhi
Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri
f: Bhutto and Indira Gandhi signed it in Shimla on 2 July 1972.
r: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 was signed by Ayub Khan and Shastri.

q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed?
f: Pakistan and China signed the boundary agreement in 1963.
r: Diplomatic relations began in 1951.

q: How many days did the 1965 Pakistan-India war last?
f: The war ran from 6 September to 23 September 1965, which is 17 days.
r: The Tashkent Declaration ended it in January 1966.

q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah die?
f: Fatima Jinnah, Madar-e-Millat, died on 9 July 1967.
r: She contested the 1965 presidential election against Ayub Khan.

q: What is the date of Pakistan's first nuclear test?
f: Pakistan conducted its first nuclear tests on 28 May 1998 (Chagai-I).
r: 28 May is observed as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: How many nuclear blasts did Pakistan conduct in 1998?
f: Five blasts on 28 May and one on 30 May 1998, a total of six.
r: India had tested earlier in May 1998.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Pakistan (and of the Muslim world)?
f: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in December 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.
r: She was elected again in 1993.

q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Punjab (Pakistan)?
f: Maryam Nawaz has been Chief Minister of Punjab since February 2024, the first woman in this post.
r: Shehbaz Sharif is the Prime Minister.

q: Who is the current Chief Minister of Balochistan?
f: Mir Sarfraz Bugti was elected Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024 and still holds the office.
r: He belongs to the PPP.

q: Pakistan created the post of Chief of Defence Forces through which constitutional amendment?
f: The 27th Amendment (November 2025) changed Article 243 and created the Chief of Defence Forces.
r: The post of Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee was abolished by the same amendment.

q: Which Chinese-made fighter jet was inducted by the Pakistan Air Force in 2022 and used in the May 2025 conflict?
f: The PAF inducted the Chinese J-10CE in 2022 and used it in May 2025.
r: JF-17 Thunder is jointly produced by Pakistan and China.

q: What is the Uraan Pakistan plan?
o: A plan to build a new airport
A military exercise of the Air Force
A national economic transformation plan launched in December 2024
f: Uraan Pakistan is the government's economic transformation plan led by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, with five pillars including exports and digital economy.
r: Its stated aim is a 3 trillion dollar economy by 2047.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize?
f: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979.
r: Malala Yousafzai won the Peace Prize in 2014.

q: Ahsan Ramzan is a famous player of which sport?
f: Ahsan Ramzan is a Pakistani snooker player who won the IBSF World Snooker Championship in 2012.
r: Muhammad Asif and Muhammad Sajjad are other Pakistani snooker world champions.

q: Jahangir Khan is famous for which sport?
f: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times and was unbeaten for about five years.
r: Jansher Khan was another great Pakistani squash player.

q: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a player of which sport?
f: Kardar was the first captain of Pakistan's Test cricket team.
r: Pakistan's first Test win came against India in 1952 in Lucknow.

q: Who has scored the most Test runs for Pakistan?
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs and is Pakistan's top Test run scorer.
r: He was the first Pakistani to pass 10,000 Test runs.

q: Which game is played with a racket and a shuttle?
f: Badminton uses rackets and a shuttlecock.
r: Squash uses a ball and a closed court.

q: Which ICC tournament did Pakistan host in 2025?
f: Pakistan hosted the ICC Champions Trophy in February-March 2025, its first ICC event in about 29 years.
r: India played its matches in Dubai.

q: Who said that the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is the practical interpretation of the Holy Quran?
f: When asked about his character, Hazrat Ayesha R.A said his character was the Quran.
r: She is among the main narrators of Ahadith.

q: Over what period was the Holy Quran revealed?
f: Revelation began in 610 CE and ended about 23 years later, around 632 CE.
r: About 13 years were in Makkah and about 10 in Madinah.

q: How many Ayats are in Surah Al-Baqarah?
f: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 Ayats.
r: It is the longest Surah of the Quran.

q: How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Holy Quran?
f: The Quran names 25 Prophets.
r: Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH) is the last of them.

q: What is the meaning of Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin?
f: Khatam-ul-Nabiyyin (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:40) means the Seal or Last of the Prophets.
r: No Prophet will come after Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH).

q: Who was the first martyr of Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah R.A was killed by Abu Jahl for her faith and is known as the first martyr of Islam.
r: Her husband Hazrat Yasir R.A was also martyred.

q: Who was the first woman to accept Islam? (2)
f: Hazrat Khadija R.A was the first person to accept Islam after the Prophet (PBUH).
r: She was the first wife of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Who narrated the largest number of Ahadith?
f: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A narrated about 5,374 Ahadith.
r: He was a companion of the Ahl-e-Suffa.

q: Which of the following lists names all four daughters of Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: The four daughters were Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatima R.A.
r: Hazrat Usman R.A married Ruqayyah and later Umm Kulthum.

q: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of which Sahabi?
f: Hazrat Ayesha R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A and wife of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Hazrat Hafsa R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Umar R.A.

q: Which of the following was a daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A?
f: Hazrat Ayesha R.A (and also Hazrat Asma R.A) were daughters of Hazrat Abu Bakr R.A.
r: Hazrat Hafsa R.A was the daughter of Hazrat Umar R.A.

q: Hazrat Ali R.A belonged to which clan?
f: Hazrat Ali R.A was from Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: He was the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Which was the first major battle of Islam, fought between Muslims and the Quraysh?
f: Badr in 2 AH was the first major battle; earlier expeditions such as Widdan had no fighting.
r: Widdan (Abwa) was the first ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Youm-e-Furqan is the title of which battle?
f: The Quran calls the day of Badr Youm-ul-Furqan, the day that separated truth from falsehood.
r: It was fought on 17 Ramadan.

q: In which year of Hijrah did the Battle of Badr take place?
f: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE).
r: Uhud was in 3 AH.

q: How many Muslims took part in the Battle of Badr?
f: About 313 Muslims fought against about 1000 Quraysh.
r: The Muslims had only 2 horses and about 70 camels.

q: How did Abu Jahl die?
o: Killed in the Battle of Uhud
Killed in the Battle of Badr, struck by two young boys Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh
f: Two young Ansari brothers, Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, struck him down at Badr and Abdullah ibn Mas'ud finished him.
r: Abu Jahl was the chief enemy of Islam among the Quraysh leaders.

q: What does the word Ahzab mean?
f: Ahzab means groups or confederates; the tribes allied against Madinah in 5 AH.
r: Surah Al-Ahzab is the 33rd Surah of the Quran.

q: Which companion suggested digging a trench in the Battle of Ahzab (Khandaq)?
f: Hazrat Salman Farsi R.A suggested the Persian idea of a trench to defend Madinah.
r: The trench was about 5 km long.

q: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed?
f: The treaty was signed in Dhul Qa'dah 6 AH (628 CE).
r: The Quran called it a clear victory in Surah Al-Fath.

q: Which special prayer is performed in the middle of the night?
f: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer offered after sleeping, in the last part of the night.
r: Surah Al-Muzzammil urges night prayer.

q: Where is Mina located?
f: Mina is a valley about 5 km from Makkah where pilgrims stay during Hajj and stone the Jamarat.
r: Arafat and Muzdalifah are the other Hajj sites near Makkah.

q: Where is Mina located?
o: Near Makkah (about 5 km east of it)
f: Mina is a valley a few kilometres east of Makkah where pilgrims stay and stone the Jamarat during Hajj.
r: Pilgrims spend the 8th to 13th Dhul Hijjah nights in the tents of Mina.

q: How many gates does Jannah (Paradise) have?
f: Authentic Ahadith state that Jannah has eight gates, one of which is Ar-Rayyan for those who fast.
r: Jahannam, in contrast, has seven gates.

q: Who will blow the Trumpet (Soor) on the Day of Judgment?
f: Angel Israfil A.S has been entrusted to blow the Soor to announce Qiyamat and again for resurrection.
r: Jibrail brings revelation, Mikail looks after rain and provision, Izrail takes souls.

q: According to Pakistani textbooks, in which year A.D. was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born (in Rabi-ul-Awwal, commonly given as 22nd April)?
f: The year of the Elephant is taken as 571 A.D in Pakistani textbooks, with the date given as 22nd April (12 Rabi-ul-Awwal). Some historians give 570 A.D.
r: He was born in Makkah in the Year of the Elephant.

q: What was the name of the father of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The father of the Prophet (PBUH) was Abdullah bin Abdul Muttalib, who died before the Prophet was born.
r: Abdullah died in Madina on a trade journey, while Amina was pregnant.

q: What was the name of the mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The mother of the Prophet (PBUH) was Amina bint Wahb of Banu Zuhra.
r: She died at Abwa when the Prophet was about six years old.

q: What was the name of the maternal grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Amina was the daughter of Wahb bin Abd Manaf, chief of Banu Zuhra, so he was the maternal grandfather.
r: Abdul Muttalib chose Amina for his son Abdullah.

q: What was the name of the maternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), as given in the list?
f: Amina's mother was Barrah bint Abd al-Uzza, which the list spells as Batarah.
r: Fatima bint Amr was the paternal grandmother, the mother of Abdullah.

q: What was the real name of Abdul Muttalib, grandfather of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abdul Muttalib's real name was Shaybah; he was called Abdul Muttalib because he was brought up by his uncle Muttalib.
r: He was the chief of Quraish and the custodian of Zamzam.

q: What was the name of the paternal grandmother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the mother of Abdullah?
f: Abdullah's mother was Fatima bint Amr of Banu Makhzum, so she was the Prophet's paternal grandmother.
r: Amina was his mother, not his grandmother.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) travel to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib?
f: At age 12 he went with Abu Talib on a trade caravan, where the monk Bahira recognised signs of prophethood.
r: His second trade trip to Syria, at 25, was for Khadija R.A.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) marry Hazrat Khadija R.A?
f: He married Khadija R.A at age 25, while she was about 40.
r: Khadija R.A was his first wife and all his children except Ibrahim were from her.

q: Among adult free men, who was the first to accept Islam?
f: Abu Bakr Siddiq R.A was the first adult free man to accept Islam.
r: He is titled Siddiq and was the first Caliph.

q: Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
f: Ali R.A, then about ten years old and living in the Prophet's house, was the first child to accept Islam.
r: Zaid bin Haritha R.A is counted as the first freed slave among the early Muslims.

q: After the first revelation, which relative of Hazrat Khadija R.A confirmed that the Prophet (PBUH) was the awaited Prophet?
f: Khadija R.A took the Prophet (PBUH) to her cousin Waraqa bin Naufal, a Christian scholar, who confirmed his prophethood.
r: Waraqa died soon afterwards and the revelation paused for a time (Fatrat-ul-Wahy).

q: How many children did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have, according to the common Seerah account?
f: The common account gives 3 sons (Qasim, Abdullah, Ibrahim) and 4 daughters (Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatima).
r: Ibrahim was the only child not born to Khadija R.A; his mother was Maria Qibtiyya.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) receive the first revelation (Wahy)?
f: The first revelation came in the cave of Hira when he was 40 years old.
r: The first verses were from Surah Al-Alaq, beginning with Iqra.

q: Who was the second wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: After Khadija R.A passed away, the Prophet (PBUH) married Sawda R.A, so she is his second wife. The name Zubaida in the list is not correct.
r: Ayesha R.A, daughter of Abu Bakr, married him soon after, in Makkah.

q: In which year A.D. did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) migrate to Madina?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 A.D, which is the start of the Islamic calendar.
r: The Hijri calendar was started in the time of Hazrat Umar R.A.

q: Which pair were among the foster mothers (wet nurses) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Thuwaybah (the freed slave of Abu Lahab) and Halima Sa'diyah both nursed the Prophet (PBUH). The list's Sobia is Thuwaybah.
r: Halima belonged to the tribe of Banu Sa'd.

q: Besides Hazrat Halima, whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) call his mother?
o: Hazrat Asma bint Abu Bakr R.A
f: The Prophet (PBUH) called Umm Ayman, who raised him after Amina's death, 'my mother after my mother'.
r: Her son was Usama bin Zaid R.A.

q: How many years after the birth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) did his mother Hazrat Amina die?
f: Amina died at Abwa while returning from Madina when the Prophet was about six years old.
r: After her, his grandfather Abdul Muttalib took care of him until he died when the Prophet was 8.

q: What was the name of the foster sister of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Shaima (Hudhafa bint Harith), daughter of Halima, used to carry and care for the Prophet (PBUH) as a child.
r: She was captured in the battle of Hunain and treated with great respect by the Prophet.

q: Which of these was a foster brother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), a son of Hazrat Halima?
f: Abdullah bin Harith, son of Halima and Harith, was nursed with the Prophet (PBUH) and is known as his foster brother.
r: The list gives the name as Abdullah bin Abu Sheema.

q: For how long, according to the common account, did Hazrat Halima look after the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The common Seerah account says the Prophet stayed with Halima in the desert for around four years (some say five).
r: Desert upbringing gave him pure Arabic and strong health.

q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of the Hajr-e-Aswad (Black Stone) incident?
f: When the Kaaba was rebuilt, the Prophet (PBUH), then 35, settled the dispute by placing the stone on a sheet carried by all tribal leaders.
r: He was called Al-Amin (the Trustworthy) before prophethood.

q: Who used to spread thorns in the way of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
o: Umm Jamil, wife of Abu Lahab
f: Umm Jamil bint Harb, wife of Abu Lahab, used to put thorns on the Prophet's path; Surah Al-Lahab mentions her as the carrier of firewood.
r: She was the sister of Abu Sufyan.

q: Whose house was used as the centre of secret preaching by the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
o: Hazrat Arqam bin Abi Arqam R.A
f: The house of Arqam on Mount Safa was Dar-e-Arqam, the first centre of Islamic teaching in Makkah.
r: Umar R.A accepted Islam and the Muslims then began to preach openly.

q: In which year of Prophethood did the boycott of Banu Hashim begin?
f: Quraish boycotted Banu Hashim and Banu Muttalib from the 7th year of prophethood and they stayed in Shib Abi Talib for about three years.
r: The boycott ended in the 10th Nabvi, the year of grief.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the first heaven during Miraj?
f: Authentic Ahadith of Bukhari and Muslim say he met Adam A.S in the first heaven.
r: Ibrahim A.S was met in the seventh heaven.

q: Which Prophets did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the second heaven during Miraj?
o: Hazrat Musa A.S and Hazrat Haroon A.S
Hazrat Isa A.S and Hazrat Yahya A.S
f: In the second heaven he met the cousins Isa A.S and Yahya A.S.
r: Isa and Yahya were maternal cousins.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the third heaven during Miraj?
f: Authentic Hadith says he met Yusuf A.S in the third heaven. The list's answer Yaqub is not correct.
r: Yusuf A.S was given half of all beauty.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fourth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Idris A.S in the fourth heaven.
r: Idris A.S is mentioned in the Quran as a truthful Prophet raised to a high place.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the fifth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Haroon A.S in the fifth heaven.
r: Haroon A.S was the elder brother of Musa A.S.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the sixth heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Musa A.S in the sixth heaven; Musa advised him to ask Allah to reduce the number of prayers.
r: The prayers were reduced from fifty to five.

q: Which Prophet did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) meet on the seventh heaven during Miraj?
f: He met Ibrahim A.S in the seventh heaven, leaning against Bait-ul-Mamoor.
r: Bait-ul-Mamoor is visited daily by seventy thousand angels.

q: What was the name of the camel on which the Holy Prophet (PBUH) traveled during the Hijrah?
f: The Prophet's well-known she-camel was Al-Qaswa, and he rode her to Madina.
r: Duldul was his white mule.

q: From whom did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) purchase the land for the mosque in Madina (Masjid-e-Nabawi)?
f: The land of Masjid-e-Nabawi belonged to two orphans, Sahl and Suhail, and the Prophet (PBUH) bought it from them.
r: The Prophet first stayed at the house of Abu Ayyub Ansari R.A.

q: In which Hijri year was the Charter of Madina (Meesaq-e-Madina) issued?
f: The Charter of Madina was made soon after the Hijrah, in 1 A.H, between Muslims, Jews and others of Madina.
r: It is often called the first written constitution of an Islamic state. The number of its articles differs in sources, so that part is not asked.

q: In which Hijri year was the change of Qibla (from Baitul Maqdis to Kaaba) ordered?
f: The order to turn towards the Kaaba came in the 2nd year after Hijrah, during prayer at Masjid-e-Qiblatain.
r: The Battle of Badr took place in the same year.

q: According to the common Seerah count, how many Ghazwat (expeditions led by the Prophet PBUH himself) are there?
f: Seerah books commonly count 27 Ghazwat, in which the Prophet (PBUH) took part himself; he actually fought in about nine of them.
r: Expeditions he did not lead are called Saraya, commonly counted as 56.

q: Which was the first Ghazwa of Islam?
f: The first Ghazwa led by the Prophet (PBUH) was Abwa, also called Waddan, in 2 A.H, and no fighting took place.
r: The first major battle of Islam was Badr.

q: Who was the first to compile Ahadith (Hadith) officially, on the order of Hazrat Umar bin Abdul Aziz?
f: Imam Ibn Shihab Zuhri is widely regarded as the first to compile Ahadith formally, at the order of Umar bin Abdul Aziz.
r: Imam Bukhari's Sahih Bukhari is the most authentic collection.

q: How many Ahadith are reported from Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A?
f: Hazrat Abu Hurairah R.A is credited with 5374 narrations, the highest among the Sahaba, according to Baqi bin Makhlad.
r: Abdullah bin Umar R.A and Anas bin Malik R.A follow him in the number of narrations.

q: Which Prophet is known as Shaikh-ul-Anbiya?
f: Hazrat Nuh A.S is called Shaikh-ul-Anbiya (Elder of the Prophets) because of his very long life of preaching.
r: Ibrahim A.S is called Khalilullah and Abul Anbiya.

q: Who was given the title Ameen-ul-Ummat?
o: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A
Hazrat Saad bin Abi Waqqas R.A
f: The Prophet (PBUH) gave Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah R.A the title Ameen-ul-Ummat (Trustworthy of the Ummah).
r: He was one of the ten Sahaba given the good news of Jannah.

q: What is the dome over the sacred grave of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) known as?
f: The dome over the Prophet's tomb in Masjid-e-Nabawi is known as the Green Dome (Gumbad-e-Khizra).
r: Gumbad-e-Sakhra is the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem.

q: Where is Bait-ul-Mamoor located?
f: Bait-ul-Mamoor is a house of worship of the angels in the seventh heaven, directly above the Kaaba.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) saw it during Miraj.

q: Which mosque was demolished on the order of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The hypocrites built Masjid-e-Dirar to harm Muslims, and the Prophet (PBUH) had it destroyed after Surah At-Tawbah revealed its purpose.
r: Masjid-e-Quba was the first mosque built in Islam.

q: Who conquered the fort of Qamus during the Battle of Khyber?
f: Hazrat Ali R.A, given the flag by the Prophet (PBUH), conquered the fort of Qamus and killed its champion Marhab.
r: Ali R.A is known by the title Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

q: Which woman tried to poison the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at Khyber?
f: A Jewish woman, Zainab bint Harith, served poisoned roasted goat meat to the Prophet (PBUH) after the conquest of Khyber.
r: Bishr bin Bara R.A died from eating it.

q: Which Surah did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) recite at the conquest of Makkah?
f: On entering Makkah, the Prophet (PBUH) was reciting Surah Al-Fath while riding his camel.
r: Surah Al-Fath was revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

q: In which year of Prophethood did the first migration to Abyssinia (Habshah) take place?
f: In Rajab of the 5th year of Prophethood (615 A.D), a small group went to Abyssinia to escape persecution.
r: They were protected by the Christian king Najashi (Negus).

q: How many people took part in the first migration to Abyssinia, according to Ibn Ishaq?
f: Ibn Ishaq's account gives 11 men and 4 women, in total 15.
r: Hazrat Usman R.A and his wife Ruqayyah R.A were among them.

q: In which year A.D. did the second migration to Abyssinia take place, according to the common account?
f: The second, bigger migration took place about a year after the first, around 616 A.D.
r: Hazrat Jafar bin Abi Talib R.A led the second group.

q: How many people in total took part in the second migration to Abyssinia?
f: The second migration had 83 men and 18 women, in total 101 people.
r: Hazrat Jafar R.A recited Surah Maryam before King Najashi.

q: What does Harb-e-Fijar mean?
o: A war fought in the prohibited (sacred) months
A war for the Kaaba key
f: Harb-e-Fijar was fought between Quraish and Banu Qais in the sacred months, in which fighting was forbidden, so it was called the sinful war.
r: The young Prophet (PBUH) took part in it by handing arrows to his uncles.

q: Which year is called Aam-ul-Huzn (Year of Grief)?
f: In the 10th year of Prophethood, Hazrat Khadija R.A and Abu Talib both passed away, so it is called the Year of Grief.
r: Soon after, the Prophet (PBUH) went to Taif.

q: What was the original name of Abu Jahl?
f: Abu Jahl was Amr bin Hisham, called Abul Hakam by Quraish; the Prophet (PBUH) called him Abu Jahl (father of ignorance). The list writes Omar bin Hisham.
r: He was killed in the Battle of Badr.

q: In which Hijri year did the conquest of Makkah take place?
f: Makkah was conquered peacefully in Ramadan of 8 A.H (630 A.D).
r: The Prophet (PBUH) forgave the people of Makkah.

q: In which Hijri year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform his (Farewell) Hajj?
f: He performed the only Hajj of his life, the Farewell Hajj, in 10 A.H and delivered the Last Sermon at Arafat.
r: He passed away about three months later.

q: Where was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) buried?
o: In the room (Hujra) of Hazrat Ayesha R.A
f: He passed away in the room of Ayesha R.A and was buried at the same spot, as Prophets are buried where they die.
r: Abu Bakr R.A and Umar R.A were later buried beside him.

q: Which king tore up the letter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) inviting him to Islam?
f: The Persian king Khusro Parvez tore the letter, and the Prophet (PBUH) said his kingdom would also be torn apart.
r: Heraclius received the letter politely and Muqawqis sent gifts.

q: Who was the Byzantine (Roman) emperor in the 7th Hijri year, when the Prophet PBUH sent him a letter?
f: Heraclius ruled the Byzantine Empire from 610 to 641 A.D and received the Prophet's letter in 7 A.H.
r: Abu Sufyan was questioned by Heraclius about the Prophet.

q: At what age did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) pass away?
f: He passed away on 12 Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 A.H at the age of 63 years.
r: Abu Bakr R.A, Umar R.A and Ali R.A also died at 63 years.

q: If Ali's present age is 5 years and Sidra is twice Ali's age, what will be Sidra's age when Ali is 11 years old?
f: Sidra is 10 now, so she is 5 years older than Ali. When Ali is 11, Sidra is 11 + 5 = 16. The age difference never changes, so 22 (double of 11) is wrong.
r: In age questions, first find the age difference: it stays the same for life.

q: A boy is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be his sister's age when the boy is 11?
f: Sister is 9, which is 6 years more than the boy. When he is 11 she is 11 + 6 = 17. 33 (3 x 11) is wrong because the 'times' rule is only true today.
r: Age ratios change every year, but the difference in years stays fixed.

q: My age is 10 years and my brother is 2 times my age. What will be the ratio of our ages after 10 years?
f: Now: 10 and 20. After 10 years: 20 and 30. 20 : 30 = 2 : 3. 1:2 is today's ratio, not the ratio after 10 years.
r: Add the same years to both ages before making the ratio.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be his sister's age when Ali is 10?
f: Sister is 15, so she is 10 years older. When Ali is 10 she is 10 + 10 = 20. 30 (3 x 10) wrongly keeps the 'times' rule.
r: Age difference = 15 - 5 = 10 years, and it never changes.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice Salman's age. When Salman is 12, what will be Ali's age?
f: Ali is 8, so he is 4 years older. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16. 24 wrongly doubles 12.
r: Twice the age is true only today; the gap of 4 years stays.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be his sister's age when Adil is 15?
f: Sister is 15, so she is 10 years older. When Adil is 15 she is 15 + 10 = 25. 45 (3 x 15) is wrong.
r: Always add the fixed age gap to the new age.

q: A man walked towards North, then turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
f: From North a left turn faces West; a right turn from West faces North again.
r: A left turn and then a right turn cancel each other.

q: Ali moves towards North. After some time he turns left and then again turns left. What is his present direction?
f: North, left = West, left again = South. Two left turns make a U-turn.
r: Two turns in the same direction (left-left or right-right) = facing the opposite way.

q: A man walks towards North, then turns left, then turns right. What is his present direction?
f: North, left = West, right = North. The two opposite turns cancel.
r: Left then right (or right then left) brings you back to your first direction.

q: Ahmad walks towards North and then turns left. What is his present direction?
f: When you face North, your left hand points West.
r: Facing North: right = East, left = West, behind = South.

q: Adnan walks 10 metres towards North, then towards South. After this he turns back and then moves towards his left. What is his present direction?
f: He faces South, turns back so he faces North, then turns left: facing North, left is West.
r: 'Turn back' means a 180 degree turn.

q: Frank is taller than John, and Ralph is taller than Frank. Who is the shortest?
f: Order: Ralph > Frank > John, so John is the shortest.
r: Write the names in one line from tallest to shortest to solve ranking questions.

q: Azhar was born in 2000 and Javed in 2005. Aslam is older than Javed but younger than Azhar. Who is the oldest?
f: The person born first is the oldest. Azhar (2000) is older than Aslam, and Aslam is older than Javed (2005).
r: Earlier year of birth = older person.

q: Ali is younger than Ahmad, and Yaqoob is older than Ahmad. Who is the youngest?
f: Order: Yaqoob > Ahmad > Ali, so Ali is the youngest.
r: Younger than the middle person who is himself younger than the oldest = youngest.

q: 90% of 90 is
r: Trick: 90% of a number = number minus 10% of it (90 - 9 = 81).

q: 80% of 90 is
80% of 80 is
90% of 70 is
60% of 9 is
r: Find 10% first (0.9), then multiply by 6.

q: 80% of 10 is
r: Any % of 10 = that % divided by 10.

q: One third of 10% of 90 is
f: 10% of 90 = 9; one third of 9 = 3.
r: Solve 'of' questions from the end: the last number first.

q: One third of 10% of 120 is
f: 10% of 120 = 12; one third of 12 = 4.
r: 'Of' means multiply.

q: 20% of one tenth of 90 is
f: One tenth of 90 = 9; 20% of 9 = 1.8.
r: 20% is the same as one fifth.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls?
f: Girls = 500 - 360 = 140. 140 / 500 x 100 = 28%. 72% is the percentage of boys.
r: Boys % + Girls % must always be 100%.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the percentage of women?
f: Women are 1/3 of the passengers, and 1/3 = 33.33%.

q: In a class of 500, 340 are boys. Find the percentage of boys.
r: Dividing by 500 and multiplying by 100 is the same as dividing by 5.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
f: Absent = 300. 300 / 1500 x 100 = 20%. 80% is the present percentage.
r: Present % + Absent % = 100%.

q: In a classroom of 1500 students, 1200 are present. Find the percentage of present students.
Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students?
r: First find the number absent, then the percentage.

q: Which word looks the same in a mirror?
f: T and I are symmetrical letters, and TITITIT reads the same from both sides, so its mirror image is the same word.
r: Letters that look the same in a mirror: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y.

q: Complete the series: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, ?
f: Two series: 55, 65, 75 (+10) and 115 + 55 = 170, 170 + 65 = 235. The missing term is 75.
r: Check alternate terms when a series jumps up and down.

q: Complete the series: 66, 63, 57, 45, ?
f: Differences are 3, 6, 12, then 24 (doubling). 45 - 24 = 21. The PDF wrote 24, which is the difference, not the next number.
r: Doubling differences: 3, 6, 12, 24.

q: Complete the series: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ?
f: Each term x 2 + 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.
r: Differences 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 also give 126.

q: What comes next: 3, 7, 14, 18, 36, 40, ?
r: Mixed patterns often repeat two steps.

q: Quarter of one tenth of 120 is
f: One tenth of 120 = 12; a quarter of 12 = 3.
r: Quarter = 1/4.

q: Quarter of 120 is
r: Quarter = divide by 4.

q: One tenth of 90 is
r: One tenth = divide by 10.

q: One tenth of 120 is
r: Move the decimal one place left.

q: One third of 120 is
r: One third = divide by 3.

q: Half of 9/90 is
r: Simplify the fraction first.
12 x 7 = 84, then add the zero.

f: Division first: 2/2 = 1, then 1 + 1 = 2.
r: BODMAS: Division comes before Addition.

f: Bracket first: 2 + 2 = 4, then 2 x 4 = 8.
r: BODMAS: Brackets first.

q: Half of a quarter is
r: 'Of' means multiply.

q: Complete the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
r: Write letter positions (A=1 ... Z=26) to solve letter series.

q: Complete the series: A, C, F, J, O, ?
r: Increasing gaps of 1 are common in letter series.

q: Complete the series: L, M, N, ?
f: Simple alphabetical order: L, M, N, O.
r: O is the 15th letter.

q: If Z = 2 and X = 5, then which comes next?
f: Letters go back with growing gaps (Z to X is 2 back, X to U is 3 back) and numbers grow with growing gaps (2 to 5 is +3, 5 to 9 is +4). So the next is U = 9.
r: In growing-gap series both the letter gap and the number gap go up by 1 each step.

q: Z = 3, X = 5, V = 7, T = 9. Find the next.
f: Letters go back by 2 (Z, X, V, T, R) and numbers go up by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11).
r: Check the letter rule and the number rule separately.

q: What comes next: A, E, K, ?
f: Positions 1, 5, 11: add 4, 6, then 8. 11 + 8 = 19 = S.
r: Gaps going up by 2 (4, 6, 8).

q: Complete the series: AB/A, BC/B, CD/C, ?
f: Each term moves one letter forward: DE / D.
r: Look at every part of the term separately.

q: Complete the series: H, F, D, ?
f: Each letter goes back by 2: H, F, D, B.
r: Backward series: subtract the same gap.

q: Complete the series: J, H, F, D, ?
f: Back by 2 each time: J, H, F, D, B.
r: Same rule as H, F, D, B.

q: Complete the series: A, E, K, ?
f: Same question as before: positions 1, 5, 11, gaps 4, 6, 8, so 19 = S. The PDF wrote R here, which does not fit the pattern.
r: Repeated in the notes twice with two answers; S is correct.

q: How many months have 31 days?
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December = 7 months.
r: Knuckle trick: every knuckle month has 31 days.

q: A leap year comes after how many years?
f: A year is about 365 days and 6 hours. 4 x 6 hours = 1 extra day, so every 4th year has 366 days.
r: In a leap year February has 29 days.

q: If yesterday was Sunday, then the day after tomorrow will be
f: Today is Monday, tomorrow Tuesday, the day after tomorrow Wednesday.
r: Find 'today' first in day questions.

q: If yesterday was Friday, tomorrow will be
f: Today is Saturday, so tomorrow is Sunday.
r: Yesterday + 2 days = tomorrow.

q: If the 28th day of a month is Sunday, then the 2nd day will be
f: 28 - 2 = 26 days back. 26 = 3 weeks + 5 days. 5 days before Sunday is Tuesday.
r: Remove full weeks (7 days) and count only the remainder.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Tuesday, then the 26th day will be
f: 26 - 4 = 22 = 3 weeks + 1 day. Tuesday + 1 = Wednesday.
r: Same weekday repeats every 7 days.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, the 19th day will be
f: 19 - 4 = 15 = 2 weeks + 1 day. Sunday + 1 = Monday.
r: 4, 11, 18 are Sundays, so 19 is Monday.

q: If the 14th day of a month is Sunday, the 4th day will be
f: 14 - 4 = 10 = 1 week + 3 days back. 3 days before Sunday is Thursday.
r: 7th is also Sunday, so 4th is 3 days before it.

q: If the 1st day of a month is Monday, then the 12th day will be
f: 12 - 1 = 11 = 1 week + 4 days. Monday + 4 = Friday. (The PDF wrote Saturday, which is one day off.)
r: 1st and 8th are Mondays, so the 12th is Friday.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, then the 12th day will be
f: 12 - 2 = 10 = 1 week + 3 days. Monday + 3 = Thursday.
r: 2nd and 9th are Mondays.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Sunday, the 23rd day will be
f: 23 - 2 = 21 = exactly 3 weeks, so the same day: Sunday.
r: Any gap of 7, 14, 21 or 28 days gives the same weekday.

q: If the 15th day of a month is Monday, the 4th day of the month is
f: 15 - 4 = 11 = 1 week + 4 days back. 4 days before Monday is Thursday.
r: 8th is Monday, so 4th is 4 days earlier.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, then the 23rd day will be
f: 23 - 2 = 21 = 3 full weeks, so the same day: Friday.
r: Exact weeks keep the same weekday.

q: If the 4th day of a month is Sunday, the 14th day is
f: 14 - 4 = 10 = 1 week + 3 days. Sunday + 3 = Wednesday.
r: 11th is Sunday, so 14th is Wednesday.

q: If one dozen pencils cost Rs 27, then the price of 4 pencils is
f: 4 is one third of 12, so the price is 27 / 3 = Rs 9.
r: 1 dozen = 12.

q: If 1 dozen pencils cost Rs 60, the price of 5 pencils will be
f: One pencil = 60 / 12 = Rs 5, so 5 pencils = Rs 25.
r: Find the price of one item first (unitary method).

q: If one dozen eggs cost Rs 24, then the price of 7 eggs is
f: One egg = 24 / 12 = Rs 2, so 7 eggs = Rs 14.
r: Unitary method: one item first, then multiply.

q: One dozen pencils cost Rs 15. What is the price of 72 pencils?
f: 72 pencils = 6 dozen. 6 x 15 = Rs 90.

q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you?
f: My brother's sister is my sister. My sister is your mother, so I am your mother's brother: your (maternal) uncle.
r: Mother's brother = maternal uncle (Mamun).

q: The sister of my brother's son is my
f: My brother's son's sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
r: Brother's or sister's daughter = niece.

q: My sister is your mother. What is your relation to me?
f: You are my sister's child, so you are my nephew (boy) or niece (girl).
r: Sister's son = nephew, sister's daughter = niece.

q: A is the father of B, but B is not A's son. What is B to A?
f: A child of a father who is not his son must be his daughter.
r: Read the 'not' carefully in relation questions.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 120 km/h. In half an hour it covers 120 / 2 = 60 km.
r: Distance = Speed x Time.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes it covers 30 km.
r: 30 minutes = half an hour.

q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour. 90 / 5 = 18 km.
r: Change minutes to hours by dividing by 60.

q: If a helicopter needs 50 gallons to fly 320 km, how many gallons does it need to fly 400 km?
r: Direct proportion: more distance, more fuel.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. 100 / 20 = 5 minutes per km.
r: Convert hours to minutes first.

q: A bus moves at 60 km/h and a train moves at twice that speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 120 km/h. In half an hour: 60 km. (The PDF does not show the answer.)
r: Same as the train and car question: double speed, half time.

q: Ali bought a pen for Rs 30 and sold it for Rs 40. What is his profit percentage?
r: Profit % is always on the cost price.

q: A person bought a book for Rs 500 and sold it for Rs 700. Find the profit percentage.
r: 28.57% would be wrongly using the selling price.

q: A bat cannot see, and a snake cannot
f: Snakes have no outer ears and cannot hear sound in the air the way we do; they feel vibrations.
r: Bats use echoes (echolocation) to move in the dark.

q: Find the odd one: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed shapes (polygons); an angle is not a shape.
r: A hexagon has 6 sides.

q: Find the odd one: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket; football is played with the feet.
r: Hockey is the national game of Pakistan.

q: Find the odd one: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize
f: Wheat, rice and maize are grains (food crops); hay is dried grass for animals.
r: Wheat is the main food crop of Pakistan.

q: Find the odd one: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda
f: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: The giant panda mainly eats bamboo.

q: Find the odd one: America, Africa, Asia, Euro
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents; the euro is a currency.
r: Asia is the largest continent.

q: The sound of an eagle is called a
f: An eagle screams (also called a screech). An owl hoots, a pigeon coos and small birds chirp.
r: Animal sounds are common in verbal tests.

q: An aeroplane flies due to
f: The wings make lift, the upward force that keeps the aeroplane in the air.
r: The four forces on a plane: lift, weight, thrust and drag.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as sound is to
f: A vehicle moves on wheels; sound travels as waves.
r: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum.

q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to
f: A female dog is a bitch; a female horse is a mare.
r: A young horse is a foal; a young male horse is a colt.

q: Parents give education to their children
f: The main aim of education is to groom children into good, skilled people.
r: In 'why' questions, choose the main and most sensible reason.

q: We boil milk
f: Boiling kills harmful germs and makes milk safe to drink.
r: Pasteurisation also heats milk to kill germs.

q: Why do people read newspapers?
f: Newspapers give news and knowledge about the world.
r: Choose the main purpose, not a side use.

q: Why do people use cars?
f: The main use of a car is travelling from one place to another.
r: Main purpose questions have one sensible answer.

q: Why do girls wear glasses?
f: Glasses are mainly worn to correct eyesight.
r: Short sight and long sight are corrected with lenses.

q: Why do women go to the bazaar?
f: A bazaar is a market, and people go there mainly for shopping.
r: Bazaar = market.

q: What will be the last letter of UTYEAB after arranging it alphabetically?
f: Arranged: A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
r: Write the letters in A to Z order before answering.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its different letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Different letters in order: A, E, G, M, N, T. The 3rd is G. (If every letter is counted, including repeats, the 3rd letter would be E.)
r: Read whether the question counts repeated letters.

q: What will be the second letter when AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Arranged: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 2nd letter is D. (The PDF wrote E, which is the 3rd letter.)
r: AUGMENTED has the letters A, U, G, M, E, N, T, E, D.

q: Arrange RAPIS. It is the name of a
f: RAPIS rearranged gives PARIS, a city (the capital of France).
r: Paris is on the River Seine.

q: Arrange OPERALD. In which category does it lie?
f: OPERALD rearranged gives LEOPARD, a wild animal.
r: The leopard is found in northern Pakistan and Azad Kashmir.

q: Find the odd one: Lahore, Rawalpindi, Karachi, Sindh, Quetta
f: Sindh is a province; the others are cities.
r: Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

q: Cold is to ice as hot is to
f: Very cold water becomes ice; very hot water becomes steam.
r: Water boils at 100 degrees C and freezes at 0 degrees C.

q: Which does not belong to the group: Cow, Dog, Leopard, Cat
f: Dog, leopard and cat eat meat (carnivores); the cow eats grass (herbivore).
r: Herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat meat.

q: Arrange E, H, M, O, R, T into a word.
f: E, H, M, O, R, T make the word MOTHER.
r: Jumbled-word questions usually make a common word.

q: According to the dictionary, which comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
f: All start with M. Second letters: A, A, O. Then third letters: C (MACHINE) comes before R (MARGALLA).
r: Compare letter by letter until they differ.

q: If 1 man writes 5 papers in 5 minutes, then 1 man will write 1 paper in
f: 5 papers in 5 minutes = 1 paper per minute.
r: Find the work done in one unit of time.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the number of women?
Amjad and Ahmad have 24 balls. Amjad has 3 times as many as Ahmad. How many does Ahmad have?
f: Ahmad = x, Amjad = 3x, so 4x = 24 and x = 6.
r: Total parts = 1 + 3 = 4.

q: If 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes, then 1 man will write 1 page in
f: Each man writes 1 page in 5 minutes, because 5 men write 5 pages in 5 minutes.
r: Classic trick question: the answer stays 5 minutes.

q: 10 men dig a well in 5 days. How many days will 5 men take?
f: Work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days. 50 / 5 = 10 days.
r: Fewer men = more days (inverse proportion).

q: Which figure completes the matrix (replaces the question mark)? (Complete the Sequence, Problem 56)
f: Count the crosses. Row 1: 5, 6, 7 (add 1). Row 2: 7, 9, 11 (add 2). Row 3: 8, 11, so add 3 to get 14. Option 3 has 5 + 5 + 4 = 14 crosses. Option 2 has only 13 and option 1 has 15.
r: In grids of dots or crosses, count them and look for an "add 1, add 2, add 3" pattern by row.

q: Current Chief Minister of Sindh (3)
f: As of Oct 2026, Syed Murad Ali Shah (PPP) is Chief Minister of Sindh; no change was found in searches.
r: The Governor of Sindh is a different office. Murad Ali Shah started his third term after the 2024 election.

q: Who was the first Muslim female Prime Minister?
f: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister of Pakistan in December 1988, the first woman to lead a government in a Muslim-majority country.
r: Her first term began in December 1988. She was the daughter of Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: Who is the new Prime Minister of Canada?
f: As of Oct 2026, Mark Carney is Prime Minister of Canada. He became Liberal leader in March 2025 and won the April 2025 election.
r: Justin Trudeau resigned as Liberal leader in 2025. Ottawa is Canada's capital.

q: In which country was FIFA founded?
f: FIFA was founded in Paris, France, on 21 May 1904.
r: FIFA headquarters is in Zurich, Switzerland. FIFA stands for Federation Internationale de Football Association.

q: When did Bangladesh gain independence? (2)
f: Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971, which is its Independence Day.
r: Victory came on 16 December 1971 when Pakistan surrendered in Dhaka. Bangladesh was formerly East Pakistan. Note: Ambiguous: 26 March is declaration, 16 December is Victory Day.

q: Who wrote Pakistan: A Hard Country?
f: Anatol Lieven wrote Pakistan: A Hard Country (2011).
r: The book looks at Pakistan's state, society, politics and security.

q: What does Radd-ul-Fasaad mean?
f: Radd means rejection and fasaad means disorder or strife, so the phrase means rejecting discord.
r: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017. It was a nationwide counter-terrorism operation.

q: Who was the first President of the United States?
f: George Washington was inaugurated on 30 April 1789 as the first US President.
r: He served two terms, 1789 to 1797. John Adams was the second President.

q: Who developed the theory of relativity?
f: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity.
r: Special relativity was published in 1905. General relativity reached its final form in 1915.

q: What are the two theories of relativity?
f: Einstein published Special Relativity in 1905 and General Relativity in 1915.
r: General relativity describes gravity as curvature of spacetime. Special relativity covers space, time and motion without gravity.

q: The Lucknow Pact was an agreement between which parties? (2)
o: Indian National Congress and Hindu Mahasabha
Indian National Congress and All-India Muslim League
f: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was signed by the Congress and the Muslim League.
r: It agreed on constitutional reforms and separate electorates. Jinnah is called the ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity for it.

q: Kot Diji is in which province?
f: Kot Diji is in Sindh, near Khairpur, with a historic fort and a pre-Harappan site.
r: The site shows early Indus Valley cultural phases. Khairpur is a district of Sindh.

q: Who was Babur’s son and successor?
f: Humayun succeeded his father Babur in 1530.
r: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526. Humayun ruled 1530-1540 and again from 1555.

q: When did Humayun rule?
f: Humayun ruled 1530-1540, lost to Sher Shah Suri, and regained Delhi in 1555.
r: He died in 1556 and was followed by Akbar. Sher Shah Suri displaced him in 1540.

q: What is cos 0°?
f: On the unit circle cosine is the x-coordinate, which is 1 at 0 degrees.
r: cos 90° = 0 and cos 180° = -1.

q: Who wrote Mein Kampf?
f: Mein Kampf was written by Adolf Hitler.
r: It was published in two volumes in the 1920s.

q: What is the currency of New Zealand?
f: New Zealand uses the New Zealand dollar (NZD), written NZ$.
r: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand. Auckland is its largest city.

q: Fill in the blank: “She is afraid ___ the dark.”
f: The standard pattern is 'afraid of'.
r: Other examples: afraid of heights, fond of, proud of.

q: Who joined the Muslim League in 1913? (2)
f: Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in 1913.
r: He had earlier worked with the Indian National Congress. He later led the Pakistan Movement.

q: When did Liaquat Ali Khan join the Muslim League?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan is commonly said to have joined the Muslim League in 1923.
r: He became Pakistan's first Prime Minister in 1947. He was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.

q: Which is Pakistan’s most populous province?
f: Punjab is the most populous province, about 127.7 million people in the 2023 census.
r: Sindh is second most populous. Balochistan is largest by area.

q: What was Sindh’s population in the 2023 census?
f: The 2023 census counted about 55.7 million people in Sindh (55,696,147).
r: The 2023 census was Pakistan's first digital census. Preliminary figure in May 2023 was about 57.9 million.

q: What was Gilgit-Baltistan’s population?
f: The 2023 census gave Gilgit-Baltistan a population of 1,709,049. The 2017 census figure was about 1.49 million.
r: Gilgit-Baltistan is not one of Pakistan's four provinces. Its capital is Gilgit. Note: Question has no date. Source gives 1.49 million (2017 census); latest 2023 census figure is 1.71 million, used here. Wrong options are far from both figures.

q: Which country is the world’s largest tea producer?
f: China is the world's largest tea producer.
r: India is second. Kenya is a major black tea exporter.

q: Which country produces large quantities of black tea?
f: Kenya is a leading producer and exporter of black tea.
r: China leads in total tea production. India is also a major tea producer. Note: Rankings vary; China/India lead overall tea, Kenya is top black tea exporter.

q: Where do the Indus and Kabul rivers meet?
f: The Kabul River joins the Indus near Attock Khurd in Punjab.
r: The Indus then flows south to the Arabian Sea.

q: What is Pakistan’s longest river?
f: The Indus is Pakistan's longest river and the backbone of its irrigation.
r: Major tributaries include Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Sutlej and Kabul.

q: What is the radius of a unit circle?
f: A unit circle has radius 1 and equation x² + y² = 1.
r: It is centred at the origin.

q: Where is the Asian Development Bank headquartered?
f: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.
r: ADB was established in 1966. It focuses on development in Asia and the Pacific.

q: What is the world’s second-largest country by area?
f: By total area Canada is the second-largest country after Russia.
r: Russia is the largest by total area. China and the USA rank close together at third and fourth.

q: Which country is commonly ranked third by total area?
f: As of Oct 2026, ranking third by area is disputed: China is commonly listed third in school lists, while the USA is third by total area in many sources (including water). Answer China is acceptable only as the exam-key convention.
r: Russia is the largest country by area. Rankings of 3rd and 4th (China, USA) vary by convention. Note: Ranking of 3rd place depends on convention (China or the United States); China chosen as per source.

q: What is the capital of Türkiye (Turkey)?
f: Ankara is the capital of Turkiye; Istanbul is the largest city but not the capital.
r: The Republic of Turkiye was proclaimed in 1923. Ataturk was its first president.

q: Where is NATO headquarters? (4)
f: NATO headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
r: NATO was founded on 4 April 1949. Its HQ is in the Haren area of Brussels.

q: What does NATO stand for? (2)
f: NATO stands for North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a collective-defence alliance.
r: Its founding treaty was signed in Washington, D.C. in 1949.

q: What is evaporation?
o: Change of a vapour into a liquid
Change of a liquid into vapour from its surface
Change of a solid directly into vapour
Change of a liquid into a solid
f: Evaporation turns liquid into vapour at the surface and can happen below boiling point.
r: Condensation is the reverse process.

q: What is condensation?
o: Change of water vapour into liquid
f: Condensation is when water vapour cools and turns into liquid water.
r: Clouds form by condensation. Evaporation is the opposite process.

q: What is the third pillar of Islam? (2)
f: The five pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.
r: Zakat is obligatory almsgiving when conditions are met.

q: What does the crescent and star on Pakistan’s flag represent?
o: Crescent: progress; star: light and knowledge
f: By the usual explanation, the crescent stands for progress and the star for light and knowledge.
r: The flag was adopted on 11 August 1947. Green stands for the Muslim majority and white for minorities. Note: Symbol meanings are conventional explanations, not official legal text.

q: Who won the first FIFA World Cup?
f: Uruguay won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930, beating Argentina 4-2 in the final.
r: The first tournament was held in Uruguay. It was held in 1930.

q: How many Nobel Prizes have been awarded to Pakistani laureates? (2)
f: Pakistan's two commonly counted Nobel laureates are Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
r: Malala was the youngest Nobel laureate at the time of her award. Abdus Salam was the first Pakistani laureate. Note: Count depends on definition; some lists add people born in British India in what is now Pakistan.

q: In which sport did Pakistan win Olympic gold medals?
f: Pakistan won Olympic hockey gold in 1960, 1968 and 1984.
r: Arshad Nadeem won Pakistan's first individual Olympic gold in javelin in 2024. Pakistan won hockey gold at Rome 1960, Mexico 1968 and Los Angeles 1984. Note: Pakistan also won individual gold in athletics (javelin) in 2024, so wording is loose; field hockey is the standard answer. Source note that Pakistan won no gold in 2024 is wrong: Arshad Nadeem won javelin gold in Paris 2024.

q: Who was Pakistan’s Army Commander-in-Chief during the 1965 war? (2)
f: Gen. Muhammad Musa Khan was Army Commander-in-Chief in the 1965 war.
r: The war began in September 1965. Ayub Khan was President.

q: Who received Nishan-e-Haider for the 1965 war?
f: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was awarded Nishan-e-Haider for defending the Lahore front (BRB canal) in September 1965.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

q: Who won the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup?
f: England won the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup, beating New Zealand in the final at Lord's.
r: The final was decided on boundary count after a tied Super Over. It was England's first World Cup title.

q: Who captained Pakistan to the 1992 Cricket World Cup title?
f: Imran Khan led Pakistan to the 1992 World Cup title.
r: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne.

q: Which languages/technologies are used to build websites?
f: HTML structures content, CSS styles it and JavaScript adds interactivity.
r: Java and JavaScript are different languages. PHP is commonly used on the server side. Note: Question is loosely worded; the standard core web technologies are used as the answer.

q: Where is the Golden Gate Bridge?
f: The Golden Gate Bridge connects San Francisco with Marin County.
r: It opened in 1937.

q: How many consecutive matches did Jahangir Khan win?
f: Jahangir Khan won 555 consecutive matches, a famous squash record.
r: He dominated squash from 1981 to 1986. He won the World Open six times.

q: Who coined the word “robot” in 1920/1921?
