f: Karel Capek popularized the word robot in his 1920 play R.U.R.; his brother Josef is often credited with suggesting it.
r: The play is Rossum's Universal Robots. Unimate, the first industrial robot, came later (George Devol, Joseph Engelberger). Note: Credit is shared: Karel popularized the word, Josef suggested it. Josef Capek is listed as a wrong option; standard exam answer is Karel Capek.

q: Who is known as the father of robotics?
f: Joseph Engelberger is called the father of industrial robotics because he commercialized the Unimate robot.
r: George Devol patented an early programmable robot. Karel Capek coined the word 'robot'.

q: Who was Pakistan’s first Prime Minister? (2)
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was Pakistan's first Prime Minister, serving 1947-1951.
r: Khawaja Nazimuddin succeeded him.

q: Who is the Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: As of Oct 2026, Shehbaz Sharif is Prime Minister of Pakistan, serving since March 2024.
r: The PM is elected by the National Assembly. Asif Ali Zardari is the President.

q: Which prophet is called Safiullah?
f: Adam (AS) is commonly given the title Safiullah, meaning the chosen one of Allah.
r: Nuh (AS) is Najiyullah, Ibrahim (AS) is Khalilullah, Musa (AS) is Kalimullah.

q: What is the title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)?
f: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) is called Khalilullah, the Friend of Allah.
r: The Quran mentions this in 4:125. Kalimullah is the title of Musa (AS) and Safiullah of Adam (AS).

q: Who wrote Khilafat-o-Mulukiyat?
f: Khilafat-o-Mulukiyat was written by Abul A'la Maududi.
r: It discusses the shift from caliphate to monarchy. Maududi founded Jamaat-e-Islami.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab?
f: As of Oct 2026, Maryam Nawaz is the Chief Minister of Punjab, in office since February 2024.
r: She is the first woman Chief Minister of Punjab. She is the daughter of Nawaz Sharif. Note: Search confirmed her as incumbent only from Wikipedia and early-2026 government items; no Oct 2026 dated report found. Re-verify near test date.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
f: As of Oct 2026, Mir Sarfraz Bugti (PPP) is Chief Minister of Balochistan, in office since March 2024.
r: Quetta is the provincial capital.

q: Which company owns PlayStation?
f: PlayStation is owned by Sony Interactive Entertainment, part of Sony Group.
r: The original PlayStation launched in Japan in 1994. Xbox belongs to Microsoft.

q: What is a zero matrix?
o: A matrix with all diagonal elements one
A matrix with only one row
A matrix whose determinant is one
A matrix in which every element is zero
f: A zero matrix has every element equal to zero.
r: Adding a zero matrix of the same size leaves a matrix unchanged.

q: What percentage of Pakistan is covered by forests?
f: As of Oct 2026, the Pakistan Economic Survey (2026) puts forest area at about 4.1 million hectares, around 4.7% of land.
r: Pakistan loses about 11,000 hectares of forest a year. Older and FAO figures such as 2.2% are also quoted. Note: No single figure: 2.2% (FAO, often in old MCQ keys), 4.7% (Economic Survey 2026), 5.1% (PFI) all appear. Check the exam's key.

q: Which is the largest forest in Pakistan?
f: Changa Manga is Pakistan's largest man-made (planted) forest; natural forests such as Ziarat juniper are also very large, so the wording is loose.
r: It lies in Punjab near Kasur. Note: 'Largest forest' depends on natural vs planted; Changa Manga is the commonly expected answer.

q: What is the world’s largest tropical rainforest?
f: The Amazon is the world's largest tropical rainforest, mostly in Brazil.
r: It spans several South American countries. The Congo basin is the second largest.

q: Who wrote Pakistan’s national anthem lyrics?
f: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the lyrics of Pakistan's national anthem.
r: The music was composed by Ahmad G. Chagla. The lyrics are in highly Persianized Urdu.

q: Who designed Pakistan’s national flag?
f: Amiruddin Kidwai designed Pakistan's national flag.
r: The flag was adopted on 11 August 1947. The white stripe stands for minorities.

q: Which language is used in Pakistan’s national anthem?
f: The anthem is written in highly Persianized Urdu with many Persian and Arabic-derived words.
r: Lyrics were written by Hafeez Jalandhari. Music was composed by Ahmad G. Chagla.

q: What symbol is used for the set of rational numbers?
f: Q is the symbol for rational numbers (quotient, p/q).
r: R is for real numbers, Z for integers, N for natural numbers.

q: What is Türkiye’s currency? (2)
f: Turkiye's currency is the Turkish lira (TRY).
r: Turkiye's central bank is in Ankara.

q: What is the old name of Türkiye?
f: The Republic of Turkey (Turkiye, name official in the UN since 2022) succeeded the Ottoman Empire in 1923; the question is loosely worded, and 'Ottoman Empire' is the only option that fits.
r: Anatolia (Asia Minor) is the region, not the state's old name. Türkiye's capital is Ankara. Note: Ambiguous: source says Anatolia is only the region; Ottoman Empire is the standard state predecessor.

q: What is the world’s largest sea?
f: The Philippine Sea is commonly cited as the largest sea (marginal sea).
r: It lies in the western North Pacific Ocean. Note: Ranking of seas depends on the definition used; Philippine Sea is the standard answer.

q: Complete: “He will ___ here by now.”
f: The future perfect uses will have plus past participle, so the answer is 'have reached'.
r: Future perfect: will have + past participle. 'Arrive' is often preferred over 'reach here' in formal usage. Note: Source notes 'have arrived' is more natural, but 'have reached' fits the blank.

q: What is Pakistan’s national flower? (3)
f: Jasmine (chambeli) is Pakistan's national flower.
r: Pakistan's national tree is deodar.

q: What is Pakistan’s national bird?
f: Pakistan's national bird is the chukar partridge (Chakor).
r: The chukar is a partridge species. Pakistan's national animal is the markhor.

q: What is Pakistan’s national animal?
f: The markhor, a wild mountain goat, is Pakistan's national animal.
r: The snow leopard is another well-known animal of Pakistan's mountains. The chukar is Pakistan's national bird.

q: What is Pakistan’s national tree?
f: Deodar (Himalayan cedar) is Pakistan's national tree.
r: Its scientific name is Cedrus deodara. It grows in the western Himalayas.

q: What is Pakistan’s national sport?
f: Field hockey is commonly cited as Pakistan's national sport.
r: Pakistan has won Olympic gold in men's hockey. Cricket is the most popular sport but not the commonly cited national sport. Note: Official status is debated; some sources cite no official national sport. Field hockey is the standard exam answer.

q: Who founded Dawn newspaper?
f: Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941.
r: Dawn later moved to Pakistan. It is a major English-language newspaper.

q: What is the world’s fastest bird?
f: The peregrine falcon is the fastest bird, exceeding 300 km/h in its hunting dive (stoop).
r: It is not the fastest in level flight.

q: What is the fastest-running bird?
f: The ostrich is the fastest-running bird, reaching about 70 km/h in short bursts.
r: Ostriches are flightless birds native to Africa. They are the largest living birds.

q: From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultanate of Oman and took possession in 1958.
r: Gwadar is a major CPEC port in Balochistan.

q: Which area is called Babul Islam? (3)
f: Sindh is called Babul Islam, the Gateway of Islam, because Islam first entered the subcontinent here.
r: Muhammad bin Qasim's campaign in Sindh took place in 711-712 CE.

q: How long did Prophet Yunus remain in the fish?
f: The Qur'an gives no exact duration for Prophet Yunus in the fish.
r: His supplication is in Qur'an 21:87. Note: Question has no single agreed duration; reports of 3 to 40 days are not established.

q: Where is the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) headquartered?
f: The ECO Secretariat is in Tehran, Iran.
r: ECO succeeded the Regional Cooperation for Development in 1985. Members are from West, Central and South Asia.

q: Who wrote Daughter of Destiny?
f: Benazir Bhutto wrote the memoir Daughter of Destiny, published in 1988.
r: She became Pakistan's first female Prime Minister in 1988. It is an autobiography.

q: What does SAARC stand for?
o: South Asian Alliance for Regional Cooperation
South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
Southern Asian Association for Regional Commerce
South Asian Association for Resource Cooperation
f: SAARC stands for South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation.
r: The charter was signed in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. The Secretariat is in Kathmandu.

q: Who developed the first practical visible LED?
f: Nick Holonyak Jr. demonstrated the first practical visible-spectrum (red) LED in 1962.
r: Shuji Nakamura, Akasaki and Amano won the 2014 Nobel Prize for blue LEDs. Oleg Losev observed LED effect in the 1920s.

q: What does CPEC stand for?
f: CPEC stands for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.
r: It is part of China's Belt and Road Initiative. It covers transport, energy and infrastructure.

q: Who passed the Objectives Resolution?
f: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the Objectives Resolution, and the Constituent Assembly passed it on 12 March 1949.
r: It was presented on 7 March 1949. It later became a preamble to Pakistan's constitutions.

q: What is another name for the Holy Quran?
f: Al-Furqan, meaning the Criterion, is one of the Quran's names.
r: Other names include Al-Kitab and Al-Dhikr. Al-Furqan separates truth from falsehood.

q: When were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted? (3)
f: The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
r: The reforms introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

q: How many major rivers are commonly listed for Balochistan?
f: Some general knowledge sources list seven major rivers for Balochistan.
r: Rivers include Hingol, Dasht, Porali, Hub, Zhob, Nari and Bolan. Many are seasonal. Note: Count depends on classification; 7 is the commonly quoted figure.

q: Which Surah is named after an ant?
f: Surah An-Naml (Surah 27) means 'The Ant'.
r: An-Nahl is the Bee and Al-Ankabut is the Spider.

q: When were Pakistan's first general elections held on the basis of adult franchise? (2)
f: Pakistan's first direct general elections on adult franchise were held on 7 December 1970.
r: The Awami League won a majority of seats, mostly in East Pakistan.

q: Which countries are the Baltic States? (2)
f: The three Baltic States are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
r: All three border the Baltic Sea. Finland, Poland, Germany and Russia are not counted among them.

q: When was the Pirpur Report published?
f: The Pirpur Report was published in 1938 for the All-India Muslim League.
r: It alleged Congress ministries mistreated Muslims after the 1937 elections. Raja Muhammad Mehdi of Pirpur headed the committee.

q: When did the Cabinet Mission come to India? (2)
f: The British Cabinet Mission came to India in 1946.
r: It had three members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander. It proposed a three-tier federation.

q: What is the real cube root of unity? (2)
f: The real cube root of 1 is 1.
r: x^3 = 1 has roots 1 and (-1 ± i√3)/2. The two complex roots are conjugates.

q: When did Khalid ibn al-Walid accept Islam? (3)
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid accepted Islam around 8 AH, before the Conquest of Makkah.
r: He was known as Sayfullah (Sword of Allah).

q: When did Abu Sufyan accept Islam?
f: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH.
r: He was the father of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan. Makkah was conquered largely without fighting.

q: Hazrat Muadh ibn Jabal was appointed governor/representative to which region? (2)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh ibn Jabal to Yemen to teach and judge.
r: This is a well-known report in hadith literature.

q: What is the inverse of a scalar matrix?
f: If A = aI with a not zero, then A inverse = (1/a)I, which is again scalar.
r: A zero scalar matrix has no inverse because its determinant is zero.

q: Simplify sin(180° − x).
f: Sine is positive in the second quadrant, so sin(180° - x) = sin x.
r: In radians, sin(π - x) = sin x.

q: What was the former name of Attock city?
f: Attock was formerly called Campbellpur and was renamed Attock in 1978.
r: Attock Fort stands near a strategic crossing of the Indus. Montgomery (now Sahiwal) and Lyallpur (now Faisalabad) are other renamed cities.

q: What is the length of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border?
f: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line) is commonly estimated at about 2,640 km.
r: The Durand Agreement was signed in 1893. Some sources give about 2,430 km. Note: Source gives varying figures (2,640 vs 2,430 km); 2,640 km is the common one.

q: When was the Geneva Accords/Pact on Afghanistan signed?
f: The Geneva Accords on Afghanistan were signed on 14 April 1988.
r: Soviet troop withdrawal finished by 15 February 1989. Pakistan, Afghanistan, USA and USSR were signatories.

q: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun? (2)
f: Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun because Nippon means origin of the sun.
r: Tokyo is Japan's capital.

q: How many agencies did the former FATA consist of?
f: Former FATA had seven tribal agencies: Bajaur, Khyber, Kurram, Mohmand, Orakzai, North and South Waziristan.
r: FATA merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 (25th Amendment).

q: What was the religion of the Negus (Najashi), king of Abyssinia, at the time of the early Muslim migration? (3)
f: By the traditional account, Najashi was a Christian who protected the Muslim migrants.
r: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke to him for the Muslims. Abyssinia is the historic Ethiopia.

q: Which is the most developed continent?
f: Europe ranks highest on many human-development measures.
r: The Human Development Index combines health, education and income. Note: No single official answer; North America also ranks high. Europe chosen as standard answer.

q: What is the last letter when “UTYEAB” is arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted alphabetically the letters are A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last is Y.
r: Alphabetical order puts Y after U and T.

q: What is the third letter when “MANAGEMENT” is arranged alphabetically?
f: MANAGEMENT sorts as A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T, so the third letter is E.
r: Sort repeated letters too.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
f: If yesterday was Friday, today is Saturday. Tomorrow is Sunday, so the day after tomorrow is Monday.
r: Day after tomorrow means two days from today. Always find today first.

q: How many months have 31 days? (4)
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days, so seven months.
r: April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 or 29.

q: There are 30 people in a room and the male:female ratio is 3:2. How many females are there?
f: 30 people split 3:2 gives 5 parts of 6 each, so females = 2 x 6 = 12.
r: Males = 18. Always divide the total by the sum of ratio parts first.

q: A book is bought for Rs 30 and sold for Rs 40. What is the profit percentage?
f: Profit is Rs 10 on cost Rs 30, so 10/30 x 100 = 33 1/3%.
r: Profit % = profit / cost price x 100. Loss % is also based on cost price.

q: Who is Pakistan's Federal Minister for Railways?
f: As of Oct 2026, Muhammad Hanif Abbasi is Federal Minister for Railways.
r: Bilal Azhar Kayani is listed as State Minister for Railways. Saad Rafique and Sheikh Rashid were earlier ministers.

q: Who is the Governor of Sindh?
f: As of Oct 2026, Nehal Hashmi (PML-N) is Governor of Sindh, sworn in on 13 March 2026, replacing Kamran Tessori.
r: The Governor is the constitutional head of the province; the Chief Minister leads the government.

q: What is the lowest point on Earth? (3)
f: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is the deepest known point of the ocean and Earth's lowest point.
r: It lies in the western Pacific Ocean. The Dead Sea shore is the lowest exposed land. Note: Ambiguous: Dead Sea shore is the lowest land point; Challenger Deep is the lowest point overall.

q: Who is known by the title “Jami-ul-Quran”?
f: Uthman (RA) is called Jami-ul-Quran because he standardized and distributed copies of the Quran.
r: Abu Bakr (RA) ordered the first collection after the Battle of Yamama. Note: Some sources also apply the title to Abu Bakr (RA); Uthman is the common answer.

q: Which is Pakistan's largest district by area? (2)
f: Chagai in Balochistan, about 44,748 sq km, is the largest district of Pakistan by area (some sources give about 50,545 sq km).
r: As of Oct 2026 Chagai is still listed as the largest. Its headquarters is Dalbandin.

q: Who wrote “The Loyal Muhammadans of India”?
f: Sir Syed wrote it after 1857 to show Muslims who stayed loyal to the British.
r: He founded the Aligarh college in 1875.

q: When was the China-Pakistan boundary agreement signed?
f: The China-Pakistan boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.
r: It delimited the northern boundary. The Karakoram Highway later improved links between the two countries.

q: Where did Pakistan conduct its first nuclear tests?
f: Pakistan's first nuclear tests were on 28 May 1998 at Ras Koh Hills, Chagai District, Balochistan.
r: 28 May is commemorated as Youm-e-Takbeer. More tests followed at Kharan on 30 May 1998. Note: Source answer is a long sentence; shortened. Kharan hosted the later tests, so it is a wrong option for the first test.

q: Basel is a city in which country?
f: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine, near the German and French borders.
r: Bern is the capital of Switzerland. Zurich is the largest Swiss city.

q: What is the smallest continent? (2)
f: In the seven-continent model, Australia is the smallest continent.
r: Oceania is a wider region including New Zealand and Pacific islands.

q: What is Pakistan's highest civil award?
f: Nishan-e-Pakistan is Pakistan's highest civil award.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is the highest military gallantry award, not civil.

q: Who was Pakistan's first woman Governor (of Sindh)?
f: Pakistan never had a woman Governor-General; Begum Ra'ana Liaquat Ali Khan was its first woman governor (Sindh, 1973-76).
r: Jinnah was the first Governor-General. The post ended when Pakistan became a republic in 1956.

q: Who was Pakistan's second Prime Minister?
f: Nazimuddin became PM in 1951 after Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated.
r: He had earlier been Governor-General of Pakistan.

q: What is an empty set?
o: A set with exactly one element
A set containing only the number zero
f: The empty set has no elements, so its cardinality is zero.
r: It is written as the symbol ∅ or { }. It is a subset of every set.

q: When did the Chauri Chaura incident occur? (4)
f: The Chauri Chaura incident happened on 4 February 1922 in Gorakhpur district.
r: Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement afterwards.

q: What is the longest river in Asia? (2)
f: The Yangtze in China is the longest river in Asia, about 6,300 km.
r: It flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai. The Yellow River is the second longest in China.

q: What does “Al-Saffah” mean?
f: Al-Saffah is commonly translated as the blood-shedder.
r: Abu al-Abbas al-Saffah was the first Abbasid caliph. The Abbasids overthrew the Umayyads in 750 CE.

q: What is the nisab of gold for zakat?
f: The Hanafi nisab of gold is 7.5 tola, about 87.48 grams.
r: Zakat is 2.5% after one lunar year. The silver nisab is 52.5 tola (about 612.36 g).

q: On what date did the 1857 uprising begin at Meerut?
f: The 1857 uprising began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
r: Mangal Pandey's revolt at Barrackpore was in March 1857. Rebels then marched to Delhi.

q: What was Hazrat Hamza's relationship to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)? (2)
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was the Prophet's paternal uncle and companion.
r: He was martyred at Uhud in 3 AH. He is called Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

q: Which words can be synonyms of “prescribe”?
f: Prescribe means to order or direct; it can also mean to authorize a medicine.
r: Prescribe means order; proscribe means forbid. Note: Several words fit 'prescribe'; Direct chosen. Question is ambiguous.

q: What is the cube root of −2?
f: The cube root of a negative number is negative, so the cube root of -2 is -∛2, about -1.26.
r: 1.26 cubed is about 2. Cube root of -8 is -2.

q: When was the Quit India Movement launched? (2)
f: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August 1942.
r: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call.

q: Who is known by the title “Kaleemullah”? (2)
f: Kaleemullah means one who spoke with Allah, a title of Prophet Musa.
r: Khalilullah is Prophet Ibrahim and Ruhullah is Prophet Isa.

q: Who is the Speaker of Pakistan's National Assembly? (3)
f: As of Oct 2026, Sardar Ayaz Sadiq is the Speaker; he was elected on 1 March 2024.
r: Asad Qaiser was Speaker 2018 to 2022. Ghulam Mustafa Shah is Deputy Speaker.

q: What is 90% of 90? (3)
r: Percentage means per hundred. 90% of 90 = 0.9 x 90.

q: “Israel” is a traditional title/name associated with which prophet? (3)
f: Israel is the title of Prophet Yaqub (AS), so his descendants are Bani Israel.
r: Israel means servant of Allah. Yusuf (AS) was his son.

q: Which region lies between Pakistan and Tajikistan? (2)
f: The Wakhan Corridor of Afghanistan separates Pakistan and Tajikistan, so they share no border.
r: The corridor is a narrow strip in Badakhshan. It was created as a buffer between British India and Russia. Note: Question is loosely worded; answer is the Wakhan Corridor (Afghanistan).

q: What are Laat and Uzza?
o: Names of two mountains near Makkah
Names of two wells of Makkah
f: Al-Lat and al-Uzza were idols worshipped in pre-Islamic Arabia.
r: They are named in Surah An-Najm (53:19-20). The third is Manat.

q: Who was Pakistan's first Foreign Minister? (3)
f: Sir Muhammad Zafrullah Khan was Pakistan's first Foreign Minister.
r: He later became President of the UN General Assembly and a judge of the ICJ.

q: Who advocated separating Sindh from the Bombay Presidency?
o: Sindhi Muslim leaders and the All-India Muslim League (Jinnah)
f: Sindhi Muslim leaders and the Muslim League backed separation; Jinnah included it in his Fourteen Points (1929).
r: Sindh became a separate province in 1936. The Government of India Act 1935 was then coming into force. Note: Source answer is vague; standard answer is Muslim League/Jinnah and Sindhi leaders.

q: Who won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
f: France beat Croatia 4-2 in the 2018 final.
r: Russia hosted the tournament.

q: Who was President when Pakistan's 1956 Constitution came into force?
f: Iskander Mirza became the first President when the 1956 Constitution came into force.
r: Pakistan became a republic on 23 March 1956. The constitution was abrogated in 1958.

q: When did Muhammad Ali Jinnah leave the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah broke with Congress in 1920 around the Nagpur session over Gandhi's methods.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: When was the Conquest of Makkah? (2)
f: Makkah was conquered in Ramadan 8 AH (630 CE).
r: It followed the breaking of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Badr was in 2 AH and Uhud in 3 AH.

q: Between whom was Mawakhat-e-Madinah established?
f: Mawakhat-e-Madinah (brotherhood) was set up between the Muhajirun of Makkah and the Ansar of Madinah.
r: Muhajirun means those who migrated. Ansar means helpers.

q: Who is known by the title “Asadullah”?
f: Hazrat Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) is known as Asadullah, Lion of Allah.
r: Hazrat Hamza (RA) is also called Asadullah. Khalid bin Walid (RA) is called Saifullah. Note: Both Ali (RA) and Hamza (RA) are called Asadullah; Ali chosen per source.

q: When was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah born?
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was born on 25 December 1876 in Karachi.
r: He died on 11 September 1948. He became Pakistan's first Governor-General.

q: When was the Nehru Report published? (2)
f: The Nehru Report was published on 30 August 1928 under Motilal Nehru.
r: Jinnah answered with his Fourteen Points in 1929.

q: Which continent has historically been called the “Dark Continent”?
f: Africa was called the Dark Continent in European colonial-era writing (a dated label).
r: Africa is the second-largest continent by area and population.

q: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
f: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan.
r: Kyrgyzstan is landlocked and its currency is the som.

q: Who partitioned Bengal in 1905?
f: Lord Curzon, the Viceroy, partitioned Bengal in 1905.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911. It stimulated the Swadeshi Movement.

q: What is the length of Pakistan's coastline? (4)
f: Pakistan's coast along the Arabian Sea is commonly given as about 1,046 km.
r: Major areas: Karachi, Makran coast, Gwadar. Note: Sources vary (about 990 to 1,050 km) depending on measurement; 1,046 km is the commonly cited figure.

q: What does “Badr” refer to, and what does the word mean? (2)
o: A mountain near Makkah; means light
A well in Makkah; means sword
A place near Madinah; means full moon
A valley near Taif; means victory
f: Badr is a settlement southwest of Madinah where the Battle of Badr took place. The word is glossed as full moon.
r: The battle was in 2 AH (624 CE). Muslims numbered about 313.

q: Which country is the largest producer of carpets?
f: Iran is commonly cited as the leading producer/exporter of handmade carpets, though China leads in total (mostly machine-made) volume; the question wording is ambiguous.
r: Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947. 'First to recognise' can mean formal recognition or diplomatic relations. Note: Disputed point; Iran is the most commonly cited answer, but sources vary on the exact date.

q: What is sin 90°?
f: The sine of 90 degrees is 1, the top point of the unit circle.
r: sin 0 = 0 and cos 90 = 0. In radians 90 degrees is pi/2.

q: In which year did Abdus Salam receive the Nobel Prize?
f: Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics.
r: He was the first Pakistani Nobel laureate. He shared it with Glashow and Weinberg for electroweak theory.

q: What is the capital of Sri Lanka?
f: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is Sri Lanka's legislative capital.
r: Colombo is the largest city and commercial centre. Sri Lanka is an island in the Indian Ocean. Note: Many quiz keys say Colombo, which is the commercial capital; Colombo is left out of the options because it is arguably also correct.

q: What is the name of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border?
f: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border, agreed in 1893.
r: Afghanistan disputes it.

q: Who is commonly credited with providing an intellectual vision for a separate Muslim-majority state in South Asia?
f: Allama Iqbal gave the vision in his Allahabad Address of December 1930.
r: Rahmat Ali coined the name Pakistan in 1933 in Now or Never. Iqbal is called the Poet of the East.

q: What was Allama Iqbal's first Persian philosophical book?
f: Asrar-e-Khudi (1915) was Iqbal's first Persian philosophical book.
r: Bang-e-Dara (1924) was his first major Urdu collection.

q: When did Abu Bakr (RA) lead the Hajj, and when was Hajj made obligatory? (2)
f: Abu Bakr (RA) led the Hajj in 9 AH.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH. Note: Question has two parts; the year Hajj became obligatory is disputed (commonly 6, 9 or 10 AH). Answer given is for the Hajj led by Abu Bakr.

q: What was the name of Hazrat Uthman ibn Affan's father?
f: Hazrat Uthman's father was Affan ibn Abi al-As.
r: Uthman was the third Rightly Guided Caliph and Dhun-Nurayn.

q: Which city is often described as one of Pakistan's oldest continuously inhabited cities?
f: Multan is often described as one of Pakistan's oldest continuously inhabited cities.
r: Multan is the City of Saints because of its Sufi shrines. Mohenjo-daro is older but not continuously inhabited. Note: The claim of being the single oldest depends on definition; Multan is the standard answer.

q: Which country is called the “Land of White Elephants”?
f: Thailand is called the Land of White Elephants.
r: The white elephant is linked to Thai royalty. Bangkok is the capital.

q: Who was the first Caliph of Islam?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) became the first Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH) in 632 CE.
r: The four Rightly Guided Caliphs were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali. Abu Bakr ruled about two years.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to travel to space?
f: Namira Salim flew on Virgin Galactic's Galactic 04 mission in October 2023 and was the first Pakistani in space.
r: The flight was suborbital. Pakistan has no government astronaut on an orbital mission yet.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan? (3)
f: Jinnah was the first Governor-General, from 14 August 1947 until his death on 11 September 1948.
r: Khawaja Nazimuddin succeeded him as Governor-General.

q: What was the first major war between Pakistan and India over Kashmir?
f: The first Indo-Pakistani war over Kashmir was fought in 1947-48.
r: A UN-arranged ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949. It began soon after Partition.

q: When was the Tashkent Declaration signed?
f: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Shastri and Ayub Khan.
r: It followed the 1965 Indo-Pakistani War.

q: When was the Badshahi Mosque built?
f: The Badshahi Mosque, commissioned by Aurangzeb, was completed in 1673.
r: It stands in Lahore opposite Lahore Fort. It was once among the world's largest mosques.

q: What is commonly listed as Pakistan's longest national highway?
f: N-5 runs from Karachi to Torkham and is the longest national highway.
r: The Karakoram Highway (N-35) is famous for altitude, not length.

q: How many idols were reportedly kept in the Kaaba before the Conquest of Makkah?
f: Traditional Islamic accounts say 360 idols were kept in the Kaaba.
r: They were removed after the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. The Kaaba is in Masjid al-Haram.

q: Who wrote the “Now or Never” pamphlet and when?
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali published Now or Never in 1933.
r: It used the name Pakistan. He was a student at Cambridge.

q: When did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations? (2)
f: Pakistan became a UN member on 30 September 1947.
r: It was the 56th member. The UN was founded on 24 October 1945.

q: When was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) born?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah around 570 CE, in the Year of the Elephant.
r: Some sources say 571 CE. The exact year is an estimate. Note: Exact year is 570 or 571 CE; 570 chosen as the standard answer.

q: Who is associated with the title “Atiq”?
f: Abu Bakr (RA) is traditionally given the title Atiq; he is best known as Al-Siddiq.
r: He was the first Caliph after the Prophet (PBUH).

q: When was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat on 21 April 1526.
r: This began Mughal rule in northern India. The Second Battle of Panipat was in 1556.

q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly?
f: Rahila Durrani was elected the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly in December 2015.
r: She served until August 2018; Abdul Quddus Bizenjo succeeded her.

q: Which country voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in 1947?
f: Afghanistan cast the only vote against Pakistan's admission to the UN.
r: Pakistan was admitted on 30 September 1947.

q: Which angel brought revelation to the Prophets?
f: Angel Jibril brought revelation to the Prophets.
r: He is also called Ruh al-Amin.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
f: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia.
r: Mongolia is landlocked between Russia and China. It is also spelled Ulan Bator.

q: Where were the 2016 Summer Olympics held?
f: The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
r: They ran from 5 to 21 August 2016. It was the first Summer Games in South America.

q: When did Jinnah present the Delhi Proposals?
f: Jinnah's Delhi Muslim Proposals were made in 1927.
r: The Lucknow Pact was 1916, not the Delhi Proposals. The Delhi Proposals led to Nehru Report responses and Jinnah's 14 Points in 1929. Note: Source notes that the 'Delhi Pact of 1916' wording is a confusion with the Lucknow Pact.

q: There are 48 heads and 140 legs among hens and cows. How many hens are there?
f: Let hens be h and cows c: h+c=48 and 2h+4c=140, so c=22 and h=26.
r: Hens have 2 legs and cows 4. Check: 52+88=140.

q: When was the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah signed? (2)
f: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed in 6 AH (628 CE).
r: It was a truce between Madinah and the Quraysh. It came before the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

q: For what did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize?
o: Peace (2014), for children's right to education
f: Malala won the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for the right of all children to education.
r: She shared it with Kailash Satyarthi and is the youngest Nobel laureate.

q: When did the Khilafat Movement begin?
f: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 and continued into the early 1920s.
r: It aimed to save the Ottoman Caliphate after WWI. It overlapped with Non-Cooperation.

q: Complete the sentence: “Ali was born ___ 20 August 1997.”
f: Use 'on' with a specific date, for example 'on 20 August 1997'.
r: Use 'in' with a month or year, like 'in August'.

q: What was the approximate Muslim force at the Battle of Badr? (2)
f: Traditional accounts say about 313 Muslims fought at Badr.
r: Badr took place in 2 AH (624 CE) against a much larger Quraysh force.

q: What is Sahifa al-Sadiqa?
o: Collection of letters of Hazrat Umar
Hadith collection of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As
A tafsir of Surah Al-Baqarah by Ibn Abbas
A book of Islamic law by Imam Malik
f: Sahifa al-Sadiqa was an early written hadith collection by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As.
r: It is often called the first hadith writing, depending on definition.

q: Which international organization did Pakistan join as a full member in 2017?
f: Pakistan became a full SCO member in June 2017 at the Astana summit.
r: Pakistan had been an SCO observer since 2005.

q: Which country is commonly said to have been the first to recognize Pakistan?
f: Iran is commonly cited as the first country to recognise Pakistan.
r: Pakistan became independent on 14 August 1947. Sources differ on exact recognition date. Note: Duplicate of the earlier 'first to recognise Pakistan' topic; commonly cited answer, sources vary.

q: Who was the first muezzin of Islam? (2)
f: Hazrat Bilal (RA) was the first muezzin of Islam.
r: The muezzin gives the adhan. Bilal suffered persecution before the Hijrah.

q: Which key opens spell check in Microsoft Word?
f: F7 opens spelling and grammar check in Microsoft Word.
r: F12 opens Save As. F1 opens Help.

q: What role did the World Bank play in the Indus Waters Treaty?
o: It mediated and helped broker the treaty
It was a signatory in place of Pakistan
It built the Tarbela Dam alone
f: The World Bank brokered the treaty, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960.
r: It was signed in Karachi on 19 September 1960. It divides the Indus system waters.

q: What percentage of Pakistan's land area is classified as forest?
f: The World Bank indicator gives Pakistan about 4.7% forest area for 2023.
r: Forest figures differ by source (FAO about 2.2%, national about 5%). Pakistan has one of the lowest forest covers in South Asia. Note: Source says 4.6%; World Bank mirror shows 4.7% (2023). Figures vary by source, so question is ambiguous.

q: During whose caliphate was the Battle of Yamama fought?
f: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 11 AH during Abu Bakr's caliphate against Musaylima.
r: Many Quran reciters died there. This led to the collection of the Quran.

q: Where are Pakistan's major coal reserves found?
f: Thar in Tharparkar district, Sindh, has Pakistan's largest coal resource.
r: Coal is also found in Balochistan, Punjab and KP.

q: In which Hijri year was zakat made obligatory?
f: Zakat is commonly dated as made obligatory in 2 AH.
r: Zakat is one of the Five Pillars of Islam. Note: Some scholars give other dates (e.g. 8 or 9 AH); 2 AH is the common exam answer.

q: How many daughters did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) have? (2)
f: Zaynab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah were the Prophet's four daughters.
r: Fatimah (RA) was the youngest.

q: Which prophet is mentioned most often by name in the Quran?
f: Prophet Musa (AS) is named most often in the Quran, about 136 times.
r: His story appears in Al-Baqarah, Al-A'raf and Ta-Ha. Counts vary by method. Note: Exact count depends on counting method, but Musa is the standard answer.

q: What is the integral of cot x?
f: cot x = cos x / sin x, so its integral is ln|sin x| + C.
r: The integral of tan x is -ln|cos x| + C. C is the constant of integration.

q: Who was the mother of Prophet Ishaq (Isaac), peace be upon him?
f: Sarah was the mother of Prophet Ishaq (AS) and wife of Ibrahim (AS).
r: Ibrahim (AS) was his father. Ismail (AS) was the son of Hajar.

q: Which pass connects Chitral with Afghanistan?
f: Dorah Pass connects Chitral with Badakhshan in Afghanistan.
r: Lowari Pass connects Dir and Chitral. Khunjerab connects Pakistan and China.

q: In which expedition did the Muslims return without a major battle?
f: At Tabuk (9 AH) the Muslims returned without a full battle.
r: Tabuk is in northwestern Saudi Arabia. It took place in heat and scarcity. Note: Other expeditions also ended without fighting; Tabuk is the standard MCQ answer.

q: Which planet is nearest to Earth?
f: As of Oct 2026 the school answer is Venus (closest approach), but a 2019 study showed Mercury is nearest to Earth on average, so check wording of the exam.
r: Mercury is the nearest planet on average over time. Note: Venus vs Mercury depends on definition; Venus is the usual exam answer.

q: Pakistan has opposed India's unconditional inclusion in which group?
f: Pakistan opposes India's unconditional inclusion in the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
r: Pakistan favours a criteria-based approach. The NSG coordinates nuclear export controls.

q: How is an earthquake's magnitude measured?
f: Modern earthquake magnitude is reported on the Moment Magnitude scale (Mw); Richter was the older scale.
r: Mercalli measures intensity (effects), not magnitude. Note: Richter scale is the traditional exam answer; Mw is the modern one.

q: When is friction between a tyre and the road at its maximum useful level?
o: When the wheels are fully locked and sliding
When the tyre is stationary and unloaded
When the road is wet with zero tyre pressure
Just before the tyre starts to skid
f: Friction is highest near the limit of static friction, just before sliding begins.
r: Locked sliding tyres have less friction than rolling tyres near peak grip. ABS prevents wheel lockup. Note: Question is vague; many MCQ keys say 'hard braking'. Answer chosen is the scientific one.

q: What are ambassadors of Commonwealth countries to one another commonly called?
f: Commonwealth members' envoys to one another are High Commissioners.
r: Their mission is a High Commission, not an embassy.

q: What is Earth's circumference?
f: Earth's equatorial circumference is about 40,075 km.
r: The polar circumference is about 40,008 km. Earth is an oblate spheroid.

q: What are the main functions of the IMF?
o: Promote international monetary cooperation, exchange stability and lend to members with balance-of-payments problems
Fund individual infrastructure projects and reduce poverty directly
Set world trade tariffs and settle trade disputes
f: The IMF promotes monetary cooperation and exchange stability, monitors economies and lends to members with balance-of-payments problems.
r: Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C. Trade disputes are handled by the WTO and long-term development lending by the World Bank. Note: Open-ended 'main functions' question; the core function is used as the answer.

q: What is the Pentagon?
o: Headquarters of the US Department of Defense
f: The Pentagon is the headquarters of the US Department of Defense in Arlington, Virginia.
r: It is five-sided. It lies across the Potomac from Washington, D.C.

q: What is the capital of Sierra Leone?
f: Freetown is the capital of Sierra Leone.
r: Monrovia is Liberia's capital. Sierra Leone is in West Africa.

q: Who led the opposing Meccan force at the Battle of Uhud?
f: Abu Sufyan led the Meccan army at Uhud. Khalid ibn al-Walid commanded the cavalry.
r: Uhud was in 3 AH (625 CE). Khalid later became Muslim. Note: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the cavalry, so he is not used as an option.

q: Who was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in Pakistan?
f: Syeda Tahira Safdar became Chief Justice of the Balochistan High Court in 2018, the first woman to head a Pakistani High Court.
r: Ayesha Malik later became the first woman judge of the Supreme Court (2022).

q: What is the space between a document margin and the start of a paragraph called?
f: Indentation is the inset of a paragraph from the margin.
r: First-line and hanging indents are common. Paragraph spacing is the vertical gap.

q: What is cutting away unwanted parts of an image called?
f: Cropping removes unwanted outer parts of an image.
r: Resizing changes dimensions, not the visible bounds.

q: Which Microsoft Word feature creates decorative text?
f: WordArt applies stylized, decorative effects to text.
r: It suits titles and headings, not long body text.

q: In which country was the 1955 Bandung Conference held, which helped inspire the Non-Aligned Movement?
f: The Bandung Conference was held in Bandung, Indonesia, in April 1955.
r: The Non-Aligned Movement was formed at Belgrade in 1961.

q: What minerals does the Saindak project produce?
f: Saindak is a copper-gold project, with silver also recovered.
r: It is in Chagai District, Balochistan. The lease was extended to 2037 for the Chinese company MCC.

q: What type of legislature does Pakistan have at the federal level?
f: Pakistan's Parliament has two chambers, the National Assembly and the Senate.
r: Bicameral means two chambers. Each province has a single-chamber provincial assembly.

q: What is Pakistan's largest operating oil refinery?
f: As of Oct 2026, PARCO calls its Mid-Country Refinery (120,000 bpd, Mahmoodkot) Pakistan's largest operating refinery. Some listings show Cnergyico with a higher nameplate capacity (about 156,000 bpd), so the answer depends on the word 'operating'.
r: PARCO means Pak-Arab Refinery Limited. MCR capacity was upgraded from 100,000 to 120,000 bpd in 2020. Note: 'Largest' is PARCO's own claim; a third-party dataset lists Cnergyico (Hub, about 156,000 bpd) as larger by capacity.

q: What is the purpose of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
o: To give loans to poor countries
To fix world currency exchange rates
To administer trade agreements and settle trade disputes
f: The WTO administers trade agreements, hosts trade negotiations, settles disputes and reviews trade policies.
r: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva. It replaced GATT in 1995.

q: Which vitamin supports wound healing?
f: Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, which helps wounds heal.
r: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Its deficiency causes scurvy. Note: Vitamin A and protein also help wound healing, but Vitamin C is the standard answer.

q: What is a major immediate energy source for an athlete?
f: Carbohydrates are a readily available energy source, stored as glycogen in muscles and liver.
r: Fat and protein also contribute to energy.

q: A book costs Rs 500 and is sold for Rs 700. What is the profit percentage?
r: Profit % is always on cost price. Loss % is calculated the same way.

q: Which battle is called Jang-e-Furqan?
f: Badr is called Jang-e-Furqan because it distinguished truth from falsehood.
r: It took place in 2 AH (624 CE).

q: Evaluate 2 + 2 ÷ 2. (3)
f: Division comes first: 2 ÷ 2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
r: BODMAS/PEMDAS sets the order of operations.

q: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud? (2)
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud.
r: Uhud was in 3 AH (625 CE). Hamza (RA) was among the martyrs.

q: What has historically been Pakistan's largest broad source category for electricity generation?
f: As of Oct 2026 thermal is still the largest source of installed capacity (55.7% in FY2025; about 49.2% in FY2026 per Economic Survey 2025-26), but its share is falling as solar/renewables grow.
r: Renewables reached about 20.3% of capacity in FY2026; hydel 23.4%, nuclear 7.1%.

q: In which direction is Iran from Pakistan? (2)
f: Iran lies to the west of Pakistan.
r: Iran borders Balochistan. Pakistan also borders Afghanistan, China and India.

q: How many Quran reciters (huffaz) are traditionally reported to have been martyred at the Battle of Yamama? (3)
f: About 70 Quran reciters are commonly reported martyred at Yamama (632 CE), which led to compiling the Quran.
r: Yamama was fought against the false prophet Musaylimah in Caliph Abu Bakr's time. Note: Accounts differ: some say about 700 reciters and total Muslim casualties were higher (about 1,200). Standard textbook answer is about 70 huffaz.

q: When was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's “Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind” (“The Causes of the Indian Revolt”) published?
f: Sir Syed's Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind was published in 1858.
r: The uprising began at Meerut on 10 May 1857. Sir Syed blamed British policies.

q: On what date was the Objectives Resolution introduced in the Constituent Assembly?
f: The Objectives Resolution was introduced on 7 March 1949 and passed on 12 March 1949.
r: Liaquat Ali Khan moved it.

q: Which pronoun can replace the singular noun “school” in a sentence?
f: A singular thing like a school is replaced by the pronoun "it".
r: Use "they" for plural schools. Example: The school is old. It needs repairs.

q: What does SAFTA stand for?
o: South Asian Finance and Trade Association
f: SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area.
r: It was signed in 2004 and took effect in 2006 under SAARC.

q: How many Muslims were initially present at the Battle of Uhud? (2)
f: About 1,000 Muslims set out for Uhud, and around 300 withdrew before the battle.
r: Uhud took place in 3 AH (625 CE). About 700 Muslims actually fought. Note: Ambiguous: about 700 actually fought; 700 left out of options to avoid confusion.

q: How many types of articles are there in English grammar?
f: English has two types of articles, definite (the) and indefinite (a/an).
r: 'A' goes before consonant sounds, 'an' before vowel sounds. Note: Source answer mixes 'two types' and 'three forms'; two types chosen as standard.

q: What does IMF stand for?
f: IMF stands for International Monetary Fund.
r: It was set up at Bretton Woods in 1944. Its headquarters are in Washington, D.C.

q: Who founded the Urdu Defence Association?
f: Mohsin-ul-Mulk is credited with organising the Urdu Defence Association in 1900.
r: It arose from the Urdu-Hindi controversy in the United Provinces. It is different from Anjuman-e-Taraqqi-e-Urdu.

q: How many times is the name Jibril explicitly mentioned in the Quran?
f: Jibril is named explicitly three times: Quran 2:97, 2:98 and 66:4.
r: Ruh al-Qudus and Ruh al-Amin are titles and not counted. Jibril brought revelation to the Prophet (PBUH).

q: Mount Olympus is in which country?
f: Mount Olympus, the highest mountain in Greece, is in Greece.
r: It is about 2,917 m high. In myth it was the home of the Greek gods.

q: Who was the last prophet sent to the Children of Israel, according to Islamic belief?
f: Isa (AS) was the last prophet sent to Bani Israel before Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).
r: Isa was born to Maryam. Muhammad (PBUH) is the final prophet.

q: What was France's currency before the euro?
f: France used the franc before the euro.
r: One euro equals 6.55957 francs. Euro notes and coins began in 2002.

q: What is one tenth of 90?
f: One tenth means dividing by 10, and 90 / 10 = 9.
r: One hundredth of 90 is 0.9. Ten percent equals one tenth.

q: What is one tenth of 120?
f: One tenth of 120 is 120 / 10 = 12.
r: One tenth means 10 percent.

q: Who enslaved Hazrat Bilal (RA) before his freedom?
f: Bilal (RA) was enslaved by Umayyah ibn Khalaf and tortured for accepting Islam.
r: Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed him.

q: Where do articles usually appear in an English noun phrase?
o: At the end of a sentence
f: Articles come before a noun or noun phrase, such as 'a book'.
r: They often come before adjectives: 'the old house'.

q: What is the literal meaning of Islam?
f: The literal meaning of Islam is submission or surrender to Allah.
r: The root is s-l-m, linked with peace and submission. A Muslim is one who submits to Allah.

q: Of 1,500 students, 1,200 are present. What percentage is present?
r: Absent students are 300, which is 20%. Percentage = part / whole x 100.

q: Of 500 students, 340 are present. What percentage is absent?
r: Present is 68%. Percentage = part/whole x 100.

q: What does Akhuwat/Mawakhat mean?
f: Akhuwat/Mawakhat means brotherhood; the Prophet (PBUH) paired Muhajirun and Ansar in Madinah.
r: The Muhajirun were migrants from Makkah and the Ansar were helpers of Madinah.

q: What was Hudaybiyyah?
o: A place near Makkah where a treaty was signed
f: Hudaybiyyah is a place near Makkah where the 6 AH treaty was concluded.
r: The treaty gave a truce between Muslims and Quraysh. It followed the Prophet's attempted pilgrimage.

q: Who is associated with the residency at Ziarat?
f: The Ziarat Residency is linked to Jinnah, who stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.
r: It is in Ziarat, Balochistan.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the Harb al-Fijar?
f: Traditional accounts say he was about 15 (some say 14-20) at Harb al-Fijar.
r: It was a series of pre-Islamic tribal conflicts. He did not fight as a main combatant. Note: Reports vary on exact age; 15 is the commonly given figure.

q: Who produced the first complete, published Urdu translation of the Quran?
f: Shah Abdul Qadir's idiomatic Urdu translation (1790, published 1829) is commonly credited as the first complete Urdu translation.
r: His brother Shah Rafiuddin made the first verbatim (word-by-word) Urdu translation. Note: Disputed: Shah Rafiuddin's verbatim translation is also called first complete; Shah Abdul Qadir is the common answer.

q: What is the McMahon Line?
o: Eastern China-India boundary line (1914 Simla Convention)
f: The McMahon Line is the eastern sector boundary between China and India drawn at the 1914 Simla Convention.
r: It is named after Henry McMahon. India accepts it but China disputes it.

q: According to a commonly cited hadith, what is the jihad of women?
f: A hadith describes a righteous Hajj as the jihad of women.
r: Wording depends on the hadith report.

q: They are three brothers. Ali is ___ of the three.
f: For three or more people the superlative is used, so 'the cleverest'.
r: Cleverer is comparative (two). Cleverest is superlative (three or more).

q: Complete the sentence: “He served us ___ breakfast.”
f: 'Breakfast' takes 'a' when it is described, so 'He served us a good breakfast' is correct.
r: 'He served us breakfast' is also correct. 'An' is used only before a vowel sound. Note: Source answer is a full sentence; the blank is taken as 'a good'.

q: Where are Pakistan's famous salt mines located?
f: Khewra Salt Mine in Punjab is Pakistan's famous salt mine.
r: It is in the Salt Range near Pind Dadan Khan, district Jhelum. It is a major tourist site.

q: When was the Conquest of Khaybar? (2)
f: The conquest of Khaybar took place in 7 AH (628 CE).
r: Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was in 6 AH. Fath Makkah was in 8 AH.

q: For what purpose is Salat al-Istisqa offered?
f: Salat al-Istisqa is offered to ask Allah for rain during drought.
r: It is usually prayed in congregation. Istisqa means seeking water.

q: When was the Jinnah Antarctic Research Station established?
f: Jinnah Antarctic Station was established on 18 January 1991.
r: Pakistan became an associate member of SCAR in 1992.

q: When was the Lahore Resolution adopted? (2)
f: The Lahore Resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940 at the Muslim League session in Lahore.
r: It is also called the Pakistan Resolution. 23 March is Pakistan Day.

q: In which year did World War I end?
f: World War I ended in 1918 with the Armistice on 11 November.
r: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.

q: What is the world's largest island?
f: Greenland is the world's largest island; Australia counts as a continent.
r: Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark.

q: What does OPEC stand for?
o: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
f: OPEC stands for Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
r: Founded in Baghdad in 1960; HQ in Vienna.

q: On which river is Diamer-Bhasha Dam being built?
f: Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River.
r: It lies in the Gilgit-Baltistan/KP region. It is for storage, irrigation and hydropower.

q: When was the Battle of Uhud fought? (3)
f: The Battle of Uhud was fought in 3 AH (625 CE) near Mount Uhud.
r: It followed the Battle of Badr in 2 AH. Uhud lies north of Madinah.

q: Where is the Jinnah Antarctic Research Station located?
f: Jinnah Antarctic Station is in East Antarctica, in the Queen Maud Land region as commonly described.
r: It was established in January 1991. It supports Pakistan's scientific work. Note: Exact location descriptions vary between sources; not independently confirmed.

q: Who is the only Companion of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) mentioned by name in the Quran?
f: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) is the only Companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab 33:37).
r: He was the adopted son of the Prophet (PBUH). He was martyred at Mu'tah.

q: The FSB is the security agency of which country?
f: The FSB is the Federal Security Service of Russia.
r: It is a domestic security and counterintelligence agency.

q: Who said of the Prophet (PBUH), “His character was the Quran”?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA) said this when asked about the Prophet's (PBUH) character (Sahih Muslim).
r: It means his character embodied the Quran.

q: Who is Pakistan's Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue?
f: As of Oct 2026, Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb is Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue, since March 2024.
r: He was in Bangkok for IMF-World Bank meetings in October 2026. Ishaq Dar is Deputy PM and Foreign Minister.

q: Who is known by the title “Ruhullah”? (2)
f: Prophet Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, meaning Spirit of Allah, in Islamic tradition.
r: Musa (AS) is Kalimullah and Ibrahim (AS) is Khalilullah.

q: To which prophet was the Zabur revealed?
f: The Zabur was revealed to Prophet Dawud.
r: Torah to Musa, Injil to Isa, Quran to Muhammad (PBUH).

q: What is the approximate length of the Line of Control (LoC) in Kashmir?
f: The LoC in Kashmir is commonly cited as about 740 km long.
r: It is not a final international border. Note: Estimates vary slightly (about 740 to 778 km).

q: On which river is Mangla Dam built?
f: Mangla Dam is built on the Jhelum River.
r: It is near Mirpur, AJK, and was completed in 1967. Tarbela is on the Indus.

q: Bari Doab lies between which rivers?
f: Bari Doab lies between the Ravi and Beas rivers.
r: A doab is land between two rivers. Rachna Doab lies between the Ravi and Chenab. Note: Some sources define Bari Doab as between Beas/Sutlej and Ravi; standard answer used.

q: Which Surahs are called Al-Mu'awwidhatayn? (2)
f: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are the last two surahs, Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114), used for seeking refuge.
r: Surah Al-Ikhlas is 112. An-Nas is the last surah of the Quran.

q: Which Surah was recited before Najashi by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib?
f: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited Surah Maryam before Najashi.
r: This was during the migration to Abyssinia. It speaks of Maryam and Isa.

q: Which well-known body of water is famous for its very high salinity?
f: The Dead Sea is famous for very high salinity; it is technically a hypersaline lake.
r: It lies between Jordan and Israel/West Bank and has the lowest land elevation on Earth.

q: Which country has the world's longest written national constitution?
f: India has the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.
r: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and took effect on 26 January 1950.

q: In which year did Shah Waliullah die?
f: Shah Waliullah died in 1762.
r: He was born in 1703. He translated the Quran into Persian.

q: In which mountain range is Siachen Glacier located?
f: Siachen Glacier lies in the eastern Karakoram.
r: It is among the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

q: A train travels at 120 miles per hour. How far does it travel in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes is 0.2 hour, so distance = 120 x 0.2 = 24 miles.
r: 24 miles is about 38.6 km.

q: Which Surah is traditionally called the “Heart of the Quran”?
f: Surah Ya-Sin (Surah 36) is traditionally called the Heart of the Quran.
r: It has 83 verses in the Hafs numbering. The hadith wording is debated by scholars. Note: Popular title based on a hadith whose grading is debated; still the standard exam answer.

q: If yesterday was Monday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
f: If yesterday was Monday, today is Tuesday, so the day after tomorrow is Thursday.
r: Tomorrow is Wednesday. Count forward from today.

q: A class has 500 students, of whom 360 are boys. What percentage are girls?
r: Boys are 72%. Percentage = part / whole x 100.

q: A helicopter uses 50 gallons to travel 320 km. How much fuel is needed for 400 km at the same rate?
f: Fuel per km is 50/320, so 400 km needs 50 x 400/320 = 62.5 gallons.
r: Fuel use is assumed proportional to distance.

q: Amjad and Ahmed have 24 balloons in total. If Amjad has three times as many as Ahmed, how many does Amjad have?
f: If Ahmed has x, Amjad has 3x, so 4x = 24 and x = 6. Amjad has 18.
r: Ahmed has 6 balloons.

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How far does it travel in 18 minutes?
f: 18 minutes is 0.3 hour, so distance = 120 x 0.3 = 36 km.
r: Distance = speed x time. 120 km/h means 2 km per minute.

q: What is the main reason children are sent to school?
o: For education, learning and social development
To make them obey their elders only
To keep them away from home
f: School gives children education, skills and social development.
r: Primary education is a basic right in Pakistan under Article 25-A of the Constitution.

q: Who is the Speaker of the Punjab Assembly?
f: Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan was elected Speaker of the Punjab Assembly in February 2024.
r: Maryam Nawaz is the Chief Minister of Punjab.

q: Why is milk usually boiled before drinking? (2)
f: Heating milk to boiling kills most harmful microbes, making it safer to drink.
r: Pasteurization, named after Louis Pasteur, heats milk to a set temperature to kill germs.

q: Who wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob?
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob was written by Syed Ali Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
r: It is one of the oldest Persian books on Sufism; Data Sahib's shrine is in Lahore.

q: Who wrote Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya?
f: Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya, a large history of Islam, was written by Ibn Kathir.
r: Ibn Kathir also wrote the famous Tafsir Ibn Kathir.

q: Who is credited with inventing the practical light bulb?
f: Thomas Edison developed the first practical, commercially successful incandescent light bulb in 1879.
r: Other inventors such as Joseph Swan also worked on electric lamps.

q: Who discovered X-rays?
f: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895.
r: Röntgen received the first Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901.

q: Where are the headquarters of the Pakistan Navy?
f: Naval Headquarters of the Pakistan Navy is in Islamabad.
r: Karachi is the Navy's main base and fleet headquarters.

q: Who were awarded the Nishan-e-Haider for the 1999 Kargil conflict?
o: Captain Karnal Sher Khan and Havildar Lalak Jan
Captain Sarwar and Naik Saif Ali Janjua
Major Aziz Bhatti and Major Shabbir Sharif
f: Captain Karnal Sher Khan and Havildar Lalak Jan received the Nishan-e-Haider for their bravery in Kargil in 1999.
r: Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

q: According to the Qur'an (2:127), who raised the foundations of the Kaaba? (2)
f: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:127 says Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) raised the foundations of the House.
r: Some traditions say an earlier Kaaba existed from the time of Adam (AS).

q: How many rukus are there in the Holy Qur'an (common count)?
f: The commonly taught count of rukus in the Qur'an is 540.
r: The Qur'an has 114 surahs and 30 paras.

q: In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India? (2)
f: The British government sent the Cripps Mission in March 1942 during World War II.
r: It offered dominion status after the war in return for Indian support in the war.

q: How many surahs of the Qur'an are Madani (common count)? (2)
f: By the common count, 28 surahs are Madani and 86 are Makki.
r: Madani surahs were revealed after the Hijrah to Madinah.

q: Which city is called the Manchester of Pakistan?
f: Faisalabad is called the Manchester of Pakistan because of its large textile industry.
r: Faisalabad was earlier named Lyallpur.

q: When was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE).
r: About 313 Muslims fought against the Quraysh of Makkah.

q: Who commanded the Muslim army at the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) himself led the Muslim army at Uhud in 3 AH.
r: Khalid ibn Walid fought on the Makkan side at Uhud before accepting Islam.

q: Who is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider? (2)
f: Pilot Officer Rashid Minhas was about 20 years old when he was martyred in 1971 and awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.
r: He is the only Pakistan Air Force officer to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: Who said, 'No power on earth can undo Pakistan'?
f: This famous statement is attributed to Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah after the creation of Pakistan.
r: Jinnah died on 11 September 1948 in Karachi.

q: Which title of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is given in the Qur'an (21:107)?
f: Surah Al-Anbiya 21:107 calls him a mercy to all the worlds (Rahmat-ul-lil-Alameen).
r: Khalilullah is the title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS).

q: In which year did Pakistan join the OIC as a founding member?
f: The OIC was founded at Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969, and Pakistan was a founding member.
r: Pakistan hosted the second Islamic Summit in Lahore in 1974.

q: Thimphu is the capital of which country?
f: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
r: Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.

q: What was the famous title of Hazrat Umar (RA)?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA) was called Al-Farooq, meaning the one who separates truth from falsehood.
r: He was also the first caliph called Amir-ul-Mu'mineen.

q: Who was Pakistan's first Test cricket captain?
f: Abdul Hafeez Kardar captained Pakistan in its first Test series in India in 1952.
r: Kardar is called the father of Pakistan cricket.

q: Who is Pakistan's highest run-scorer in Test cricket?
f: Younis Khan scored 10,099 Test runs, the most by a Pakistani batter.
r: He was the first Pakistani to score 10,000 Test runs.

q: In which district is the ancient site of Harappa located?
f: Harappa archaeological site is in Sahiwal District, Punjab.
r: Mohenjo-daro, another Indus Valley site, is in Larkana District, Sindh.

q: The yuan is the currency unit of which country?
f: The yuan is the main unit of China's currency, the renminbi.
r: Japan's currency is the yen.

q: In which Hijri year did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) perform his first Umrah?
f: The first completed Umrah was Umrat al-Qada in 7 AH, after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
r: In 6 AH the Muslims were stopped at Hudaybiyyah and could not perform Umrah.

q: Into how many physical (geographical) regions is Pakistan commonly divided in textbooks?
f: Many textbooks divide Pakistan into five physical regions such as northern mountains, western mountains, Balochistan Plateau, Potohar Plateau and the Indus Plain.
r: Some books add deserts as a separate region, giving six.

q: On which river is Warsak Dam built?
f: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River, about 30 km from Peshawar.
r: Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum River.

q: Who was the first President of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly?
f: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected the first President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.
r: Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan later became President of the Assembly.

q: Babusar Pass connects which two areas?
f: Babusar Pass joins Naran/Kaghan Valley (Mansehra) with Chilas in Diamer District.
r: Khunjerab Pass connects Hunza with China.

q: On what date did Pakistan become an Islamic Republic?
f: The first Constitution came into force on 23 March 1956 and named the country the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
r: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated in 1958.

q: When was Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founded?
f: Imran Khan founded PTI on 25 April 1996.
r: Pakistan Peoples Party was founded on 30 November 1967.

q: What is the name of the boundary line drawn between Pakistan and India in 1947?
f: Sir Cyril Radcliffe drew the partition boundary between Pakistan and India in 1947.
r: The Durand Line is the Pakistan-Afghanistan border.

q: When was the United Nations established? (3)
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, now celebrated as UN Day.
r: The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 in San Francisco.

q: Who is Pakistan's Federal Minister for National Health Services?
f: Syed Mustafa Kamal became Federal Minister for National Health Services in March 2025.
r: Mustafa Kamal was earlier the Mayor (Nazim) of Karachi.

q: When was the World Health Organization (WHO) founded?
f: WHO's constitution came into force on 7 April 1948.
r: 7 April is celebrated every year as World Health Day.

q: What was the old name of Madinah?
f: Before the Hijrah, Madinah was called Yathrib.
r: After the Hijrah it became Madinat-un-Nabi, the City of the Prophet.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar with Afghanistan through the Khyber District.
r: Torkham is the main border crossing on the Khyber route.

q: What system of government did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan give?
o: Federal parliamentary with a Prime Minister
f: The 1962 Constitution, made under Ayub Khan, introduced a presidential system.
r: The 1956 Constitution had a parliamentary system.

q: After textiles, which is Pakistan's second-largest export item?
f: Textiles are Pakistan's largest export group, and rice is commonly ranked second.
r: Basmati rice from Punjab is a famous Pakistani export.

q: What is Brazil's largest export crop?
f: Soybeans are Brazil's leading agricultural export.
r: Brazil is also the world's largest coffee producer.

q: Which team won the 1999 Cricket World Cup? (2)
f: Australia beat Pakistan in the final at Lord's to win the 1999 World Cup.
r: Pakistan won the Cricket World Cup in 1992.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his mother died?
f: His mother Hazrat Amina died at Abwa when he was about six years old.
r: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then took care of him.

q: What is the currency of Cuba? (3)
f: Cuba's official currency is the Cuban peso (CUP).
r: Cuba ended its dual-currency system in 2021.

q: What is the world's largest lake by surface area? (2)
f: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake by area, though its water is salty.
r: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by surface area.

q: Under the 1962 Constitution, who elected the President of Pakistan?
f: Under the 1962 Constitution, the President was elected indirectly by an electoral college of Basic Democrats.
r: There were 80,000 Basic Democrats, 40,000 from each wing.

q: What is the currency of Sri Lanka? (3)
f: Sri Lanka's currency is the Sri Lankan rupee.
r: Bangladesh's currency is the taka.

q: What is the capital of Albania?
f: Tirana is the capital and largest city of Albania.
r: Skopje is the capital of North Macedonia.

q: What is the capital of Bulgaria?
f: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria.
r: Bucharest is the capital of Romania.

q: What is Canada's official national winter sport?
f: By federal law (1994), ice hockey is Canada's national winter sport.
r: Lacrosse is Canada's national summer sport.

q: In his current term, Donald Trump is which numbered President of the United States?
f: Donald Trump began his second term on 20 January 2025 as the 47th President.
r: He was also the 45th President (2017-2021), as his terms are non-consecutive.

q: Which is commonly cited as the tallest building in Pakistan?
f: Bahria Icon Tower in Karachi, about 273 m tall, is commonly cited as Pakistan's tallest building.
r: Minar-e-Pakistan in Lahore is a famous national monument.

q: What is the currency of Bosnia and Herzegovina?
f: Bosnia and Herzegovina uses the convertible mark (BAM).
r: Its capital is Sarajevo.

q: What is the capital of Algeria? (2)
f: Algiers is the capital of Algeria.
r: Algeria is the largest country in Africa by area.

q: In which year was the Simla (Shimla) Conference held? (3)
f: The Simla Conference was held in June-July 1945 by Viceroy Lord Wavell.
r: It failed over the Muslim League's demand to nominate all Muslim members.

q: Who was the first (permanent) President of the All-India Muslim League? (3)
f: Sir Aga Khan III was the first permanent President of the All-India Muslim League.
r: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka on 30 December 1906.

q: What is the world's deepest lake? (2)
f: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake in the world, about 1,642 m deep.
r: Lake Baikal is also the oldest lake in the world.

q: Where is Shahi Qila (Royal Fort) located? (2)
f: Shahi Qila, or Lahore Fort, is in Lahore, next to the Badshahi Mosque.
r: Lahore Fort is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: Who is the President of Pakistan?
f: Asif Ali Zardari began his second term as President in March 2024.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.

q: In which year was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) established? (2)
f: The OIC was set up in 1969 after the first Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco.
r: The OIC headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

q: How many member states are in the European Union?
f: The EU has 27 member states.
r: The United Kingdom left the EU in 2020.

q: Who is the President of France? (2)
f: Emmanuel Macron has been President of France since 2017; his second term runs to 2027.
r: Paris is the capital of France.

q: Which country is the world's largest coffee producer?
f: Brazil produces the most coffee in the world.
r: Vietnam is the second-largest coffee producer.

q: What was Hazrat Umm Kulthum's (RA) relation to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Umm Kulthum (RA) was one of the four daughters of the Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadijah (RA).
r: She married Hazrat Uthman (RA) after the death of her sister Ruqayyah (RA).

q: Which river is often cited as the world's shortest river?
f: The Roe River in Montana, about 61 m long, is the river most often cited as the shortest in the world.
r: Shortest-river rankings depend on how a river's source and mouth are measured, so records differ.

q: Who led the disbelievers (Quraysh) at the Battle of Badr? (2)
f: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) was the leading commander of the Quraysh at Badr and was killed there.
r: The Battle of Badr was fought in 2 AH; about 313 Muslims took part.

q: Which is the second-largest continent by area? (2)
f: Asia is the largest continent and Africa is second by area.
r: Africa has 54 recognised countries, more than any other continent.

q: Which is the longest glacier in the Karakoram range (claimed by Pakistan)?
f: Siachen, about 76 km long, is the longest glacier in the Karakoram.
r: Siachen is among the longest glaciers outside the polar regions.

q: How many Nishan-e-Haider awards have been given in total?
f: The commonly listed total of Nishan-e-Haider recipients is 11 (including Saif Ali Janjua's Hilal-e-Kashmir).
r: The first recipient was Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed (1947-48 war).

q: Where is the headquarters of the UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR)?
f: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is based in Geneva.
r: The UN Human Rights Council also meets in Geneva.

q: Who is the Secretary-General of the Arab League?
f: Ahmed Aboul Gheit of Egypt has been Secretary-General of the Arab League since 2016.
r: The Arab League was founded in 1945 and has its headquarters in Cairo.

q: In which year was 'South Asian Aviation' founded?
f: The source gives 1998 as the founding year.
r: PIA, Pakistan's national airline, was formed in 1955 (incorporated 1956).

q: Against which team and where did Pakistan play its first Test match (October 1952)?
f: Pakistan's first Test was against India at Delhi, starting 16 October 1952.
r: Pakistan won its second Test at Lucknow; India won the 1952 series 2-1.

q: Which title is given to Liaquat Ali Khan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister, was assassinated in 1951 and is called Shaheed-e-Millat.
r: Madar-e-Millat is the title of Fatima Jinnah.

q: On which date is Youm-e-Takbeer observed in Pakistan?
f: Youm-e-Takbeer marks Pakistan's nuclear tests of 28 May 1998.
r: The tests were conducted in the Ras Koh Hills, Chagai, Balochistan.

q: Who was the foster mother (wet-nurse) of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in his childhood?
f: Halima Sa'diyah of the Banu Sa'd tribe nursed and raised the Prophet (PBUH) in the desert in his early years.
r: After his mother's death, his grandfather Abdul Muttalib and then his uncle Abu Talib cared for him.

q: What does 'Tanzil' mean? (3)
f: Tanzil means sending down; in Quranic usage it refers to the revelation of the Quran.
r: Tafsir means explanation of the Quran and Tilawat means recitation.

q: What is the literal meaning of 'Zakat'?
f: Zakat literally means purification and growth; in Islamic law it is obligatory almsgiving.
r: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam and was made obligatory in 2 AH.

q: In which year CE did the Hijrah take place, the event from which the Hijri calendar begins?
f: The Hijri calendar is counted from the Hijrah (migration) to Madinah in 622 CE.
r: Hazrat Umar (RA) formally adopted the Hijri calendar about 17 years after the Hijrah.

q: What is the currency of Egypt? (3)
f: Egypt's currency is the Egyptian pound (EGP).
r: Egypt's capital is Cairo.

q: What is the purpose of the NFC Award in Pakistan?
o: To distribute revenues between the federation and the provinces
To set the State Bank's interest rate
To allocate seats in the National Assembly
f: The National Finance Commission Award divides specified federal revenues between the federation and the provinces under Article 160 of the Constitution.
r: NFC stands for National Finance Commission; the 7th NFC Award was given in 2009-10.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906 (commonly cited year).
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913 and left the Congress in 1920.

q: According to Hanafi fiqh, how many fard (obligatory) acts are there in Hajj? (2)
f: Hanafi teaching lists three fara'id of Hajj: Ihram, staying at Arafat (Wuquf) and Tawaf al-Ziyarah.
r: Other schools of fiqh classify the pillars of Hajj differently.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
f: The IAEA is based at the Vienna International Centre, Austria.
r: The IAEA was founded in 1957.

q: Who is called 'Ruh-ul-Qudus' (the Holy Spirit) in Islam?
f: In Islamic interpretation Ruh-ul-Qudus refers to the angel Jibraeel (AS).
r: Jibraeel (AS) brought revelation to the prophets.

q: Which of the following are the five permanent members of the UN Security Council?
o: Japan, France, Russia, UK and USA
China, France, Russia, UK and USA
China, France, India, UK and USA
China, Germany, Russia, UK and USA
f: The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States.
r: Each permanent member has veto power over substantive resolutions.

q: In which year did the British annex Sindh?
f: The British annexed Sindh in 1843 after the battles of Miani and Dubbo.
r: Sir Charles Napier led the British campaign.

q: Where is the Shah Jahan Mosque located? (2)
f: The Shah Jahan Mosque, built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, is in Thatta, Sindh.
r: It is famous for its blue glazed tile work and many domes.

q: Which is the most populous city of Pakistan?
f: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city by population.
r: Lahore is the second most populous city.

q: In which district is Keenjhar Lake located?
f: Keenjhar Lake lies in Thatta District, Sindh.
r: It is one of Pakistan's largest freshwater lakes and supplies water to Karachi.

q: Which dam/hydropower project has India built on the Indus River in Ladakh (former Jammu & Kashmir state)?
f: India's Nimoo Bazgo hydropower project is built on the Indus River in Ladakh.
r: Baglihar is on the Chenab and Kishanganga is on the Neelum (Kishanganga) river.

q: Which country helped Pakistan build Warsak Dam? (2)
f: Warsak Dam was built with Canadian assistance under the Colombo Plan.
r: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River near Peshawar and was completed in 1960.

q: Which is the third surah of the Quran?
f: Surah Aal-e-Imran is the third surah in the standard order of the Quran.
r: It has 200 verses and is named after the family of Imran.

q: When did the five daily prayers (Salah) become obligatory?
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory during Isra and Mi'raj, before the Hijrah.
r: Mi'raj is commonly placed around the 10th-12th year of Prophethood.

q: What is the name of Japan's parliament?
f: Japan's parliament is the National Diet (Kokkai).
r: It has two houses: the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

q: Which is the largest district of Balochistan by area?
f: Chagai is the largest district of Balochistan by area.
r: Pakistan's 1998 nuclear tests were carried out in Chagai.

q: The Darling is a river in which country? (2)
f: The Darling River is in south-eastern Australia.
r: It joins the Murray River, Australia's longest river.

q: Which is the last surah of the Quran in its standard order? (2)
f: Surah An-Nas (114) is the final surah in the standard order of the Quran.
r: The last verse revealed is a separate question; many scholars name Al-Baqarah 2:281.

q: Multan is famous as the city of what?
f: Multan is known as the City of Saints because of its many Sufi shrines.
r: Lahore is called the City of Gardens.

q: Which land is often called the 'Land of Prophets'?
f: Palestine is often called the land of prophets because many prophets lived and preached there.
r: Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem was the first qibla of Muslims.

q: In which language did Bulleh Shah write his poetry?
f: Bulleh Shah was a famous Punjabi Sufi poet.
r: His shrine is in Kasur, Punjab.

q: Which is the largest lake of Germany by area?
f: Lake Constance (Bodensee) is the largest lake touching Germany by area.
r: It is shared with Switzerland and Austria; Müritz is the largest lake wholly in Germany.

q: How many years after independence did East Pakistan separate from Pakistan?
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and East Pakistan separated in 1971: 1971 - 1947 = 24.
r: East Pakistan became Bangladesh in 1971.

q: When was the state of Israel formed?
f: Israel declared independence on 14 May 1948.
r: 2 November 1917 is the date of the Balfour Declaration.

q: Which is the world's largest permanent desert lake? (2)
f: Lake Turkana in Kenya is known as the world's largest permanent desert lake.
r: It is also the world's largest alkaline lake.

q: Who was the second Caliph of Islam?
f: Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) succeeded Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) as the second Rightly Guided Caliph.
r: He is known by the title Al-Farooq.

q: Which is the second pillar of Islam?
f: The five pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj; Salah is second.
r: Zakat is the third pillar.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred? (2)
