f: Hazrat Hamza (RA) was martyred at the Battle of Uhud in 3 AH.
r: He is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs).

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed? (2)
f: Abu Jahl was killed at the Battle of Badr in 2 AH.
r: Badr is also called Yaum-ul-Furqan (Jang-e-Furqan).

q: Jahangir Khan is famous for which sport? (2)
f: Jahangir Khan is a Pakistani squash legend.
r: He won 555 matches in a row from 1981 to 1986.

q: Which river is commonly listed as the world's third-longest?
f: The Yangtze, about 6,300 km long, is usually listed as the third-longest river after the Nile and Amazon.
r: The Yangtze is also the longest river in Asia.

q: Which of the following seas does Turkey border?
f: Turkey borders the Black Sea in the north (as well as the Aegean, Mediterranean and Marmara seas).
r: Istanbul lies on the Bosphorus, which links the Black Sea with the Sea of Marmara.

q: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'?
f: 'Friends Not Masters' (1967) is the political autobiography of President Ayub Khan.
r: Pervez Musharraf's memoir is 'In the Line of Fire'.

q: Which pass in Pakistan is commonly cited as the highest paved international border crossing in the world?
f: Khunjerab Pass (about 4,693 m) on the Karakoram Highway is commonly cited as Pakistan's highest pass and the world's highest paved border crossing.
r: It links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang, China.

q: How many surahs are there in the Quran?
f: The Quran has 114 surahs.
r: The longest surah is Al-Baqarah and the shortest is Al-Kawthar.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
f: ICAO, the UN agency for civil aviation, is headquartered in Montreal, Canada.
r: ICAO was set up under the Chicago Convention of 1944.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)?
f: The WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948, now marked as World Health Day.

q: In which year were the Summer Olympics cancelled because of World War I?
f: The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled because of World War I; 1914 was not an Olympic year.
r: The 1940 and 1944 Games were cancelled because of World War II.

q: What is the capital of Colombia?
f: Bogotá is the capital of Colombia.
r: Caracas is Venezuela's capital, Lima is Peru's and Quito is Ecuador's.

q: Which gas is most abundant in the Sun?
f: The Sun is made mostly of hydrogen (about 73% by mass), with helium second.
r: The Sun gets its energy from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.

q: Who is known by the title 'Sardar-ul-Ansar' (leader of the Ansar)?
f: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA) was chief of the Aws tribe of the Ansar; the Prophet (PBUH) told the Ansar, 'Stand up for your leader' about him.
r: Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) was the chief of the Khazraj, the other Ansar tribe.

q: Which region is called the cradle of Islam?
f: Islam began in Makkah and Madinah, both in the Hijaz region of present-day Saudi Arabia.
r: The Hijaz lies along the Red Sea coast of the Arabian Peninsula.

q: In which year of Prophethood did the 'Year of Grief' (Aam-ul-Huzn) occur?
f: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) and Abu Talib both died in the 10th year of Prophethood, so it was called the Year of Grief.
r: The Year of Grief is usually dated to about 619 CE, before the Hijrah.

q: In which Surah does Allah swear by time?
f: Surah Al-Asr begins with 'Wal-Asr', an oath by time.
r: Surah Ash-Shams begins with an oath by the sun.

q: In which city is the shrine of Data Ganj Bakhsh located? (2)
f: The shrine of Hazrat Ali Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh) is in Lahore.
r: Data Ganj Bakhsh wrote Kashf-ul-Mahjoob, an early Persian book on Sufism.

q: Who was the first Mughal emperor?
f: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after winning the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
r: Babur wrote his memoirs, the Baburnama, in Chagatai Turkish.

q: What is the approximate length of the Makran Coastal Highway (N-10) between Karachi and Gwadar?
f: The Makran Coastal Highway along the Balochistan coast is commonly quoted as about 653 km long.
r: 1,046 km is the length of Pakistan's whole coastline.

q: Which Prophet built the Ark?
f: The Quran tells that Allah ordered Prophet Nuh (AS) to build the Ark before the great flood.
r: Surah Nuh (Surah 71) is named after him.

q: Whom did Babur defeat in the First Battle of Panipat?
f: Babur defeated Sultan Ibrahim Lodi of Delhi at Panipat in 1526.
r: Babur defeated Rana Sanga a year later at the Battle of Khanwa (1527).

q: From which Surah was the first revelation?
f: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq, starting with 'Iqra' (Read), were the first revelation in the Cave of Hira.
r: The first revealed word was 'Iqra', meaning 'Read' or 'Recite'.

q: What is the official height of Mount Everest? (2)
f: Nepal and China jointly announced Everest's height as 8,848.86 metres in 2020.
r: 8,611 m is the height of K2, the world's second-highest mountain.

q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River? (2)
f: The Amazon is commonly given as about 6,400 km long, though estimates vary.
r: The Amazon carries more water than any other river in the world.

q: What is the name of Turkey's (Türkiye's) parliament?
f: Türkiye's legislature is the Grand National Assembly (TBMM).
r: The Knesset is Israel's parliament and the Duma is Russia's.

q: Which sea lies between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean (Aegean) Sea?
f: The Black Sea joins the Sea of Marmara through the Bosporus, and Marmara joins the Aegean through the Dardanelles.
r: The Sea of Marmara lies entirely within Türkiye.

q: Fill in the blank: 'He went to the river ___ car.'
f: We use 'by' with means of transport: by car, by bus, by train.
r: We say 'on foot', not 'by foot'.

q: Mount Kigo is located in which country?
f: Kigo is in Wakiso District near Kampala, Uganda.
r: Lake Victoria borders Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.

q: Lake Victoria is shared by which countries?
f: Lake Victoria in East Africa is bordered by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
r: Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake and a main source of the White Nile.

q: Mount Whitney is located in which country?
f: Mount Whitney is in the Sierra Nevada, California, USA.
r: It is the highest peak in the contiguous United States (about 4,421 m).

q: What is the fifth (outermost) layer of Earth's atmosphere?
f: The layers are troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere; the exosphere is the fifth and outermost.
r: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere.

q: What percentage of air is nitrogen?
f: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen by volume.
r: Oxygen makes up about 21% of air, and argon about 0.93%.

q: The Kobo Hills are in which country?
f: The supplied source places the Kobo Hills in Tanzania.
r: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak.

q: What is the total area of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's total area including Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir is commonly given as 881,913 sq km.
r: Without GB and AJK, the area is often quoted as 796,096 sq km.

q: What is the approximate area of Pakistan's Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)?
f: Pakistan's EEZ, extending 200 nautical miles from the coast, covers about 240,000 sq km.
r: In 2015 the UN extended Pakistan's continental shelf by about 50,000 sq km, so total maritime area is about 290,000 sq km.

q: What is the area of Islamabad Capital Territory?
f: Islamabad Capital Territory covers about 906 sq km.
r: Islamabad became the capital in place of Karachi in the 1960s.

q: Which is the second-longest river in Africa?
f: The Congo is Africa's second-longest river after the Nile.
r: The Congo River crosses the Equator twice.

q: Who is the most recent recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Havildar Lalak Jan was martyred on 7 July 1999 in the Kargil conflict, the latest action for which Nishan-e-Haider was given.
r: Captain Karnal Sher Khan also received Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil; he was martyred on 5 July 1999.

q: Which is the deepest river in the world?
f: Parts of the Congo River are more than 220 m deep, the deepest measured in any river.
r: The Congo also has the second-largest discharge after the Amazon.

q: Where is Tanda Dam located?
f: Tanda Dam is near Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
r: Tanda Dam is used for irrigation and is also a picnic spot.

q: Under which law was the Punjab Police (colonial police system) established?
f: The Police Act 1861, passed after the 1857 uprising, set up the police system that became the Punjab Police.
r: Police Order 2002 later replaced the 1861 Act in Pakistan.

q: Which is the world's busiest container seaport?
f: Shanghai has handled the most containers (TEUs) of any port for many years.
r: Rotterdam is Europe's largest seaport.

q: In which language did Waris Shah write his poetry?
f: Waris Shah wrote the famous romance 'Heer' in Punjabi.
r: Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai wrote in Sindhi.

q: Which country is called the land of a thousand lakes?
f: Finland has around 188,000 lakes, giving it this nickname.
r: Thailand is called the Land of White Elephants.

q: Who nominates the Chief Justice of Pakistan under the 26th Amendment?
f: Since the 26th Amendment (2024), a Special Parliamentary Committee picks the CJP from the three most senior Supreme Court judges and the President formally appoints.
r: Before 2024, the most senior Supreme Court judge became Chief Justice automatically.

q: On which day of the week did the 1965 war begin (6 September 1965)?
f: 6 September 1965, when India attacked Lahore, was a Monday.
r: 6 September is celebrated in Pakistan as Defence Day.

q: When was NATO established? (2)
f: NATO was created by the North Atlantic Treaty signed in Washington on 4 April 1949.
r: NATO had 12 founding members.

q: When was the OIC established?
f: The OIC was founded at the first Islamic Summit in Rabat, Morocco, on 25 September 1969.
r: The second OIC summit was held in Lahore in February 1974.

q: Which drink is popularly called Pakistan's national juice?
f: Sugarcane juice is widely called Pakistan's national drink/juice.
r: The mango is Pakistan's national fruit.

q: When did the Arabs under Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 711-712 CE, defeating Raja Dahir.
r: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam (Gateway of Islam).

q: How many Muslims fought at the Battle of Uhud?
f: About 1,000 Muslims set out, but around 300 left with Abdullah ibn Ubayy, leaving about 700.
r: The Makkan army at Uhud was about 3,000 strong.

q: Who led the Muslim army in the Ghazwa of Tabuk?
f: A Ghazwa is an expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH) himself; he led Tabuk in 9 AH.
r: Tabuk was the Prophet's last expedition, and no battle was fought.

q: Who was the first adult free man to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is traditionally the first free adult man to accept Islam.
r: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was the first person overall, and Hazrat Ali (RA) the first child.

q: Which is conventionally taught as the world's longest river?
f: The Nile, about 6,650 km, is usually taught as the longest river.
r: Some studies argue the Amazon is longer, depending on how it is measured.

q: The Danube River is in which continent?
f: The Danube flows through central and eastern Europe into the Black Sea.
r: The Danube passes through four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.

q: Pakistan's non-party general elections of 1985 were held under whose government?
f: Non-party elections were held on 25 February 1985 under General Zia-ul-Haq.
r: Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after these elections.

q: Which of these organizations is NOT part of the United Nations?
f: NATO is a separate military alliance; UNESCO, WHO and UNICEF are UN bodies.
r: The UN was founded on 24 October 1945.

q: What is the distance between the points (0,1) and (1,1)?
f: Both points have y = 1, so the distance is the difference in x: 1 - 0 = 1.
r: The distance between (0,0) and (1,1) would be √2.

q: Who was the Iranian (Sasanian) king at the time of the Battle of Qadisiyyah?
f: Yazdegerd III was the last Sasanian king and ruled during Qadisiyyah (636 CE).
r: Rostam Farrokhzad was the Persian commander killed in the battle.

q: Who founded the Indian National Congress in 1885? (2)
f: A.O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Congress in 1885 to give educated Indians a platform.
r: The first Congress session was held in Bombay under W.C. Bonnerjee.

q: When did the Muslim League celebrate the Day of Deliverance? (2)
f: Jinnah called for the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939 after the Congress ministries resigned.
r: The Congress ministries ruled from 1937 to 1939.

q: Who won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Literature?
f: Belarusian writer Svetlana Alexievich won the 2015 Nobel Prize in Literature.
r: The 2015 Nobel Peace Prize went to the Tunisian National Dialogue Quartet.

q: Over how many years was the Holy Quran revealed? (2)
f: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years: about 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.
r: The Quran has 114 Surahs.

q: Which is the largest ocean?
f: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of Earth's surface.
r: The Arctic is the smallest ocean.

q: The Yangtze River is in which country?
f: The Yangtze flows west to east across China into the East China Sea.
r: The Three Gorges Dam is built on the Yangtze.

q: In which year did the Panama Canal open, and which oceans does it join?
f: The Panama Canal opened on 15 August 1914 and links the Atlantic (via the Caribbean) and the Pacific.
r: The Suez Canal (1869) links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.

q: Rawal Dam is built on which river, and when was it completed?
f: Rawal Dam on the Korang River near Islamabad was completed in 1962.
r: Rawal Dam supplies water to Rawalpindi and Islamabad.

q: From which city was Pakistan's first radio broadcast made on 14 August 1947?
f: Radio Pakistan's first announcement of independence was broadcast from Lahore on the night of 13-14 August 1947.
r: Mustafa Ali Hamdani made the famous announcement.

q: What is the approximate length of the Nile in miles?
f: The Nile is about 6,650 km long, which is about 4,130 miles.
r: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

q: From how many camels does zakat become due?
f: The nisab for camels starts at five, on which one goat is due.
r: The nisab for goats/sheep starts at 40.

q: Which river is commonly ranked the sixth-longest in the world?
f: By length, the Huang He (about 5,464 km) is usually ranked sixth after the Nile, Amazon, Yangtze, Mississippi-Missouri and Yenisei.
r: The Huang He is called 'China's Sorrow' because of its deadly floods.

q: Narowal District is part of which division?
f: Narowal is a district of Punjab within Gujranwala Division.
r: Kartarpur Corridor is in Narowal District.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Cuba from 1959 to 1976?
f: Fidel Castro became Prime Minister after the 1959 revolution and held the post until 1976.
r: Havana is the capital of Cuba.

q: What was Hazrat Luqman famous for?
f: Luqman is known as Luqman al-Hakim (the Wise) for the wise advice given in the Quran.
r: Surah Luqman (Surah 31) contains his advice to his son.

q: Which strait separates the USA (Alaska) from Russia?
f: The Bering Strait lies between Alaska and Russia's Chukotka region.
r: The Diomede Islands lie in the Bering Strait.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque located? (2)
f: Shah Jahan built this mosque in Thatta, Sindh, in the 1640s.
r: It is famous for its blue tile work and many domes.

q: What does WAPDA stand for?
f: WAPDA is the Water and Power Development Authority, set up in 1958.
r: WAPDA builds and runs big dams like Tarbela and Mangla.

q: Who was the first child to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) accepted Islam at about 10 years of age, the first child to do so.
r: Hazrat Ali (RA) is known by the title Asadullah.

q: What is the capital of Bhutan?
f: Thimphu is the capital and largest city of Bhutan.
r: Bhutan's currency is the ngultrum.

q: By whom is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected?
o: Electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies
f: Under the Constitution, the Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly from among its members.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament and the four Provincial Assemblies.

q: What is the main purpose of sending children to school?
o: To keep them busy at home
To make them earn money early
To get education and learn skills
To keep them away from friends
f: Schools give children knowledge, skills and social development for a useful life.
r: Article 25-A of Pakistan's Constitution makes free education a right for children aged 5 to 16.

q: What is the currency of Russia?
f: Russia's currency is the ruble (RUB).
r: Moscow is the capital of Russia.

q: Who became Pakistan's first woman fighter pilot qualified for combat duty?
f: Flight Lieutenant Ayesha Farooq became Pakistan's first female fighter pilot qualified for combat in 2013.
r: Women had served in other PAF roles before this milestone.

q: By whom is the President of Pakistan elected?
o: Electoral college of both Houses of Parliament and the four Provincial Assemblies
f: The Constitution says the President is elected by an electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and the four Provincial Assemblies.
r: The President's term is five years.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: The Battle of Badr took place in Ramadan, 2 AH (624 CE).
r: Badr is also called Jang-e-Furqan.

q: Where is the Badshahi Mosque located?
f: The Badshahi Mosque was built in Lahore by Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
r: It was completed in 1673.

q: The Yellow Sea lies between China and which peninsula?
f: The Yellow Sea lies between mainland China and the Korean Peninsula.
r: It supports important fisheries and shipping routes.

q: Abdul Qadir was a well-known player of which sport?
f: Abdul Qadir was a famous Pakistani leg-spin bowler.
r: He played for Pakistan mainly from the late 1970s to the early 1990s.

q: Where will the 2027 ICC Men's ODI Cricket World Cup be held?
f: The 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup is jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
r: It is scheduled from October to November 2027.

q: In which year did the English East India Company's ship first arrive at Surat?
f: Captain William Hawkins arrived at Surat on 24 August 1608.
r: The East India Company was chartered in 1600 by Queen Elizabeth I.

q: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were presented in response to which report?
f: The Nehru Report (1928) ignored Muslim demands, so Jinnah answered with his Fourteen Points in 1929.
r: The Nehru Report was published on 30 August 1928.

q: Which word comes first in dictionary order?
f: Comparing letters left to right, 'Aca' comes before 'Acc', 'Acq' and 'Act'.
r: Dictionary order compares words letter by letter from the left.

q: Who made an early working solar cell in 1883?
f: Charles Fritts made an early selenium solar cell in 1883.
r: Modern silicon solar cells were developed at Bell Labs in 1954.

q: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the Hijrah to Madinah?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) travelled with the Prophet (PBUH) to Madinah in 622 CE.
r: They stayed in the Cave of Thawr on the way.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela? (2)
f: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.
r: Venezuela is in northern South America with a Caribbean coastline.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of Pakistan's Armed Forces?
o: The Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
f: The Constitution makes the President the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
r: Asif Ali Zardari is the current President of Pakistan.

q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC?
f: OPEC's headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.
r: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in September 1960.

q: The Manila Pact is also known as what? (2)
f: The Manila Pact of 8 September 1954 is the Southeast Asia Collective Defense Treaty that created SEATO.
r: SEATO was dissolved in 1977.

q: In which Pakistani river is the blind Indus river dolphin found? (2)
f: The Indus river dolphin lives mainly in the Indus River system of Pakistan.
r: It is an endangered freshwater dolphin.

q: How many people have received the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Eleven brave soldiers have been awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.
r: It is Pakistan's highest military gallantry award.

q: Who wrote Tafsir al-Tabari?
f: Tafsir al-Tabari was written by Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari.
r: The work is also called Jami' al-Bayan.

q: What is the approximate length of the Indus River?
f: The Indus is about 3,180 km long.
r: It rises in Tibet and falls into the Arabian Sea.

q: Who wrote the Urdu novel 'Raja Gidh'?
f: 'Raja Gidh' (1981) is a famous Urdu novel by Bano Qudsia.
r: Bano Qudsia was the wife of writer Ashfaq Ahmed.

q: What is the capital of France?
f: Paris is the capital and largest city of France.
r: France is a permanent member of the UN Security Council.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points? (3)
f: Jinnah presented his Fourteen Points in March 1929.
r: They were a response to the Nehru Report of 1928.

q: When and where was the All-India Muslim League founded?
f: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka on 30 December 1906.
r: It was formed during the All-India Muhammadan Educational Conference session.

q: On what date did Israel declare independence?
f: Israel declared independence in Tel Aviv on 14 May 1948.
r: 2 November 1917 is the date of the Balfour Declaration.

q: Who is regarded as the founder of modern nursing?
f: Florence Nightingale set up modern nursing after her work in the Crimean War.
r: International Nurses Day (12 May) is her birthday.

q: Which country holds the G20 presidency in 2026?
f: The United States took over the G20 presidency on 1 December 2025.
r: South Africa held the G20 presidency in 2025.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)? (3)
f: The OIC General Secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
r: The OIC was founded in 1969 at the Rabat Islamic Summit.

q: How was the OIC founded?
o: By many Muslim countries together at the 1969 Rabat Summit
f: The OIC was set up jointly by the states at the 1969 Islamic Summit in Rabat; no single country founded it.
r: The summit was called after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque in 1969.

q: Which currency is used in Cuba?
f: The Cuban peso (CUP) is Cuba's official currency.
r: Cuba ended its dual-currency system in 2021.

q: Which Pakistani city is often called one of the hottest in the world?
f: Jacobabad in Sindh is often cited as one of the hottest cities due to extreme summer heat.
r: A single-day record and a yearly average are different measures of heat.

q: When did the five daily prayers (Salah) become obligatory?
o: On the night of Mi'raj, before the Hijrah
In the first year after Hijrah
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory during the Mi'raj, before the migration to Madinah.
r: The exact date of the Mi'raj is not agreed by all scholars.

q: Which is commonly cited as Pakistan's largest artificial freshwater lake?
f: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake in Thatta, Sindh is commonly cited as Pakistan's largest artificial freshwater lake.
r: Manchar Lake is called Pakistan's largest natural freshwater lake.

q: Which pass connects Quetta with Sibi?
f: The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi through Balochistan's hills.
r: Khojak Pass connects Quetta with Chaman.

q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
f: Nishtar Hospital is a large teaching hospital in Multan.
r: Multan is called the City of Saints.

q: Which Companion married Hazrat Fatimah (RA), the Prophet's daughter?
f: Hazrat Ali (RA) married Fatimah (RA), so he was the Prophet's son-in-law.
r: Hazrat Uthman (RA) married two of the Prophet's daughters and is called Dhun-Nurayn.

q: Which constitution of Pakistan introduced a presidential system?
f: The 1962 Constitution, made under Ayub Khan, gave Pakistan a presidential system.
r: The 1973 Constitution set up a parliamentary federal system.

q: What is the currency of Libya?
f: Libya's currency is the Libyan dinar (LYD).
r: It replaced the Libyan pound in 1971.

q: Where and when were the first Asian Games held?
f: The first Asian Games opened in New Delhi on 4 March 1951.
r: The Asian Games are run by the Olympic Council of Asia.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Cholistan Desert?
f: Cholistan lies in southern Punjab, mainly in the Bahawalpur region.
r: It is locally called Rohi.

q: Which is the largest city of Sindh by population?
f: Karachi is Sindh's capital and Pakistan's largest city.
r: Hyderabad is Sindh's second-largest city.

q: In which year was the first Nobel Prize awarded?
f: The first Nobel Prizes were given in 1901.
r: The Economics prize was added in 1969.

q: Which angel is called Ruh-ul-Qudus (the Holy Spirit)?
f: Ruh-ul-Qudus is a title of Angel Jibreel (AS), who brought revelation.
r: He is also called Ruh-ul-Amin (the trustworthy spirit).

q: What was the relationship between Asma bint Abu Bakr (RA) and Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA)?
f: Asma (RA) was the wife of Zubair ibn al-Awwam (RA).
r: Their son was Abdullah ibn al-Zubair (RA).

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 120? (2)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12, and one quarter of 12 is 3.
r: 120 / 10 / 4 = 3, which is the same as 120 / 40.

q: Who was the formal President of Cuba during the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962? (2)
f: Osvaldo Dorticos was Cuba's President in 1962; Fidel Castro was Prime Minister.
r: The crisis was between the USA and the Soviet Union over missiles in Cuba.

q: Which major battle came after the Battle of Badr?
f: After Badr (2 AH), the next major battle was Uhud in 3 AH.
r: Uhud was fought near Madinah in 625 CE.

q: Where is the Kharan Desert located?
f: The Kharan Desert lies in the arid western part of Balochistan, around Kharan and Chagai.
r: It should not be confused with the Thar Desert (Sindh) or the Cholistan Desert (Punjab).

q: On which continent is Lake Victoria? (2)
f: Lake Victoria lies in East Africa, shared by Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya.
r: Lake Victoria is a major source of the White Nile.

q: Which Caliph was the first to be called Amir-ul-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful)?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA), the second Caliph, was the first to take the title Amir-ul-Mu'minin.
r: The title means "Commander of the Faithful".

q: What are Canada's official national sports?
f: Canada's National Sports of Canada Act (1994) names lacrosse as the summer sport and ice hockey as the winter sport.
r: Ice hockey alone is an incomplete answer when the question asks for both national sports.

q: What is the world's largest cold desert?
f: A desert is defined by very low rainfall, and Antarctica is the largest such region with a cold climate.
r: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khaybar fought?
f: In 7 AH (628 CE), the Muslims fought the Jewish tribes in their fortresses at the oasis of Khaybar.
r: Khaybar is an oasis north of Madinah; the battle came after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

q: Who wrote "Kashf-ul-Mahjoob"?
o: Ali ibn Usman al-Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob was written by Ali ibn Usman al-Hujwiri, known as Data Ganj Bakhsh.
r: It is one of the earliest major Persian books on Sufism, and its author's shrine is in Lahore.

q: Which organization promotes the peaceful use of nuclear technology and applies nuclear safeguards?
f: The IAEA, set up in 1957, promotes peaceful nuclear technology and checks that nuclear material is not used for weapons.
r: IAEA headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.

q: When was New Delhi inaugurated as the capital of British India?
f: New Delhi was formally inaugurated by Viceroy Lord Irwin on 13 February 1931.
r: The decision to move the capital from Calcutta to Delhi was announced in 1911.

q: The Flint River (which joins the Chattahoochee) is located in which US state?
f: This Flint River flows south through Georgia and joins the Chattahoochee to form the Apalachicola River.
r: There is also a different Flint River in Michigan.

q: In which city is Heathrow Airport located?
f: Heathrow Airport is the main international airport of London, United Kingdom.
r: Heathrow is one of the busiest airports in the world.

q: Which two countries are separated by the 38th parallel?
f: After World War II, the 38th parallel was used as the dividing line between North and South Korea.
r: The Korean Demilitarized Zone (1953) follows the armistice line, which does not match the 38th parallel exactly.

q: Which Chinese autonomous region borders Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan borders the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of China.
r: Pakistan and China are connected through the Khunjerab Pass.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with China?
f: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang, China.
r: Khunjerab Pass is about 4,693 m high, one of the highest paved border crossings in the world.

q: Which city of Pakistan is popularly called the "City of Flowers"?
f: Peshawar is popularly known as the City of Flowers.
r: Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: In which city is the main campus of the National College of Arts (NCA)?
f: The National College of Arts has its main campus in Lahore.
r: NCA also has a campus in Rawalpindi.

q: Who was Pakistan's first Commander-in-Chief of the Army? (2)
f: General Sir Frank Messervy was the first C-in-C of the Pakistan Army, from August 1947 to February 1948.
r: Ayub Khan became the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief in 1951.

q: What is the fifth pillar of Islam?
f: The five pillars are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj; Hajj is the fifth.
r: Hajj is performed in the month of Dhul-Hijjah by those who are able.

q: In 622 CE, to which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrate?
f: In 622 CE the Prophet (PBUH) migrated from Makkah to Madinah, then called Yathrib.
r: The Hijrah marks the start of the Islamic (Hijri) calendar.

q: Which part of the body does diphtheria mainly affect?
f: Diphtheria is a bacterial infection that mainly affects the nose and throat.
r: Diphtheria is caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae and is prevented by vaccination.

q: What is the full name of Imam Bukhari?
f: Imam Bukhari's full name is Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari, and his kunya is Abu Abdullah.
r: He was born in Bukhara in 810 CE and compiled Sahih al-Bukhari.

q: Who compiled Sunan Abi Dawud?
f: Sunan Abi Dawud was compiled by Imam Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani.
r: It is one of the six major Sunni hadith books (Sihah Sittah).

q: What does the name "Pakistan" mean? (2)
f: In Persian/Urdu, "Pak" means pure and "stan" means land, so Pakistan means Land of the Pure.
r: The name was coined by Chaudhry Rahmat Ali in his 1933 pamphlet "Now or Never".

q: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of which Companion?
f: Hazrat Aisha (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA).
r: Hazrat Hafsa (RA), another wife of the Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: Where is Masjid-e-Nabawi located? (2)
f: Masjid-e-Nabawi, the Prophet's Mosque, is in Madinah, Saudi Arabia.
r: It was built by the Prophet (PBUH) after the Hijrah in 622 CE.

q: Bait-ul-Maqdis in Jerusalem is also known by which name?
f: Bait-ul-Maqdis refers to the holy sanctuary in Jerusalem containing Masjid al-Aqsa.
r: Al-Aqsa was the first Qibla of the Muslims.

q: In which province is the Thal Desert?
f: The Thal Desert lies in Punjab, between the Indus and Jhelum rivers.
r: It covers parts of Bhakkar, Khushab, Layyah and Mianwali districts.

q: Near which city is the Cholistan Desert?
f: The Cholistan Desert lies near Bahawalpur in southern Punjab.
r: Cholistan is also called Rohi, and Derawar Fort is its famous landmark.

q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: The Prime Minister is elected by the National Assembly from among its members.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and the provincial assemblies.

q: Which Indian Prime Minister visited Pakistan in February 1999?
f: Atal Bihari Vajpayee came to Lahore by bus in February 1999.
r: His visit led to the signing of the Lahore Declaration.

q: Which of these countries has no system of national orders or honours?
f: Swiss tradition forbids national orders and titles, so Switzerland has no award like Pakistan's Nishan-e-Haider.
r: The Swiss armed forces do give service and mission awards, but no national gallantry order.

q: What is the full form of ISPR?
f: ISPR stands for Inter-Services Public Relations.
r: ISPR is the media wing of Pakistan's armed forces.

q: Manama is the capital of which country?
f: Manama is the capital and largest city of Bahrain.
r: Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf.

q: What is the currency of Australia?
f: Australia's currency is the Australian dollar (AUD).
r: The Australian dollar replaced the Australian pound in 1966.

q: Which two oceans are connected by the Panama Canal?
f: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic Ocean (via the Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean.
r: The Panama Canal opened in 1914.

q: When was the World Trade Organization (WTO) established?
f: The WTO started work on 1 January 1995, replacing the GATT system.
r: WTO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
f: Buenos Aires is the capital and main port of Argentina.
r: Argentina is in the southern part of South America.

q: Who was Pakistan's second Governor-General?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor-General after Quaid-e-Azam's death in September 1948.
r: Nazimuddin later became Pakistan's second Prime Minister.

q: The Bay of Biscay lies along the coasts of which countries?
f: The Bay of Biscay lies along the western coast of France and the northern coast of Spain.
r: It is part of the north-eastern Atlantic Ocean and is known for rough seas.

q: When was the All-India Muslim League founded? (2)
f: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka on 30 December 1906.
r: The Lahore Resolution was passed by the Muslim League in 1940.

q: Who was the first wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was the first wife of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: She is traditionally regarded as the first person to accept Islam.

q: Where is the Kirthar Range located?
f: The Kirthar Range runs along the border between Sindh and Balochistan.
r: Kirthar National Park is in Sindh.

q: Which place in Pakistan is the birthplace of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism?
f: Guru Nanak was born at Nankana Sahib, Punjab, marked by Gurdwara Janam Asthan.
r: Kartarpur is linked with the later life and death of Guru Nanak.

q: About how many languages are spoken in Pakistan?
f: Surveys report more than 70 languages spoken in Pakistan.
r: Urdu is the national language and English is widely used for official work.

q: In which year was the Indian National Congress founded? (2)
f: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 in Bombay.
r: Its first president was Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee.

q: What is the UN status of Palestine and the Holy See (Vatican City)?
o: The Holy See is a full member; Palestine is an observer
Palestine is a full member; the Holy See is an observer
f: Neither is a full UN member; both have non-member observer state status in the General Assembly.
r: The UN has 193 member states.

q: Which party did Quaid-e-Azam join before joining the Muslim League?
f: Jinnah joined the Indian National Congress in 1906 and the Muslim League in 1913.
r: Jinnah left the Congress in 1920.

q: Which neighbouring country is separated from Pakistan by the Durand Line?
f: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
r: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border is about 2,640 km long.

q: How often does a leap year usually occur?
f: A leap year comes every 4 years, adding 29 February.
r: A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400, so 1900 was not but 2000 was.

q: A light-year is a unit of what?
f: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year.
r: One light-year is about 9.46 trillion km.

q: In which year did the War of Independence take place in the subcontinent?
f: The War of Independence (called the Mutiny by the British) broke out in 1857.
r: It began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the Scientific Society?
f: Sir Syed set up the Scientific Society at Ghazipur in 1864.
r: Its aim was to translate Western science books into Urdu; it later moved to Aligarh.

q: Which book did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan write in reply to William Muir's 'Life of Mahomet'?
f: Sir Syed wrote Khutbat-e-Ahmadiya to answer Muir's criticism of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Muir's biography was published in 1858-1861.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan establish the MAO School at Aligarh?
f: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental School at Aligarh was founded in 1875.
r: It became MAO College in 1877 and Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: In which year was Bengal partitioned?
f: The Partition of Bengal took effect in October 1905 under Lord Curzon.
r: It was annulled in 1911.

q: In which year did the Simla Deputation meet the Viceroy?
f: The Simla Deputation met Lord Minto on 1 October 1906.
r: It was led by Sir Aga Khan III and asked for separate electorates.

q: In which year were the Morley-Minto Reforms enacted?
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909 is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
r: These reforms gave Muslims separate electorates.

q: In which year was the Partition of Bengal annulled? (2)
f: The partition was cancelled at the Delhi Durbar on 12 December 1911.
r: In 1911 the capital was also shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All-India Muslim League? (2)
f: Jinnah joined the Muslim League in 1913 while still a Congress member.
r: He had joined the Indian National Congress in 1906.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed? (3)
f: The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916.
r: It was an agreement between the Congress and the Muslim League that accepted separate electorates.

q: When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
f: The massacre took place in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.
r: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered the troops to fire.

q: During which period did the Khilafat Movement take place?
f: The Khilafat Movement ran from about 1919 until the Caliphate was abolished in 1924.
r: It aimed to save the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver the Allahabad Address?
f: Iqbal delivered the Allahabad Address on 29 December 1930.
r: It proposed a consolidated Muslim state in north-west India.

q: During which years were the Round Table Conferences held in London?
f: Three Round Table Conferences were held in London between 1930 and 1932.
r: Congress attended only the second conference.

q: During which period did Congress ministries rule the provinces?
f: Congress formed ministries after the 1937 elections and resigned in 1939.
r: They resigned in protest at India being taken into World War II without consultation.

q: In which year were the Gandhi-Jinnah talks held?
f: The Gandhi-Jinnah talks were held in Bombay in September 1944.
r: The talks failed over the Pakistan demand.

q: In which year was the Wavell Plan announced?
f: Lord Wavell announced his plan in 1945.
r: It proposed reforming the Viceroy's Executive Council.

q: When were the last elections held in British India before independence?
f: The central and provincial elections were held in 1945-46.
r: The Muslim League won almost all Muslim seats.

q: When was the 3rd June Plan announced?
f: Lord Mountbatten announced the partition plan on 3 June 1947.
r: It provided for the division of British India into India and Pakistan.

q: On what date did Pakistan become independent?
f: Pakistan came into being on 14 August 1947.
r: Pakistan joined the United Nations on 30 September 1947.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many divisions does Punjab have?
f: The source lists 9 divisions for Punjab in the PBS 2023 census baseline.
r: Division counts can change when new divisions are notified.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many divisions does Sindh have?
f: Sindh has 6 divisions: Karachi, Hyderabad, Mirpurkhas, Sukkur, Larkana and Shaheed Benazirabad.
r: Manchar is Pakistan's largest natural freshwater lake, in Sindh.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many divisions does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have?
f: KP has 7 divisions: Malakand, Hazara, Mardan, Peshawar, Kohat, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan.
r: The former FATA districts are now part of KP divisions.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many divisions does Balochistan have?
f: Balochistan has 8 divisions in the 2023 census list.
r: Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many divisions does Pakistan have?
f: The source gives 30 divisions in the PBS 2023 census baseline.
r: The same source counts 136 districts including Islamabad.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many districts does Punjab have?
f: The source lists 36 districts for Punjab.
r: Punjab is Pakistan's most populous province.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many districts does Sindh have?
f: Sindh has 30 districts, including 7 districts of Karachi.
r: Keenjhar Lake in Sindh is a major source of water for Karachi.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many districts does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have?
f: The PBS 2023 table lists 35 districts for KP.
r: District counts change when new districts are created.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many districts does Balochistan have?
f: The source lists 34 districts for Balochistan.
r: Chagai is the largest district of Balochistan by area.

q: How many districts does Islamabad Capital Territory have?
f: Islamabad Capital Territory is counted as a single district.
r: ICT is federally administered and is not a province.

q: According to the 2023 census (PBS), how many districts does Pakistan have?
f: The source gives 136 districts including Islamabad in the PBS 2023 baseline.
r: District totals change as provinces create new districts.

q: What is the currency of Indonesia?
f: Indonesia's currency is the Indonesian rupiah (IDR).
r: Indonesia is building Nusantara as its new capital.

q: Who was the mother of Prophet Ismail (AS)?
f: Hazrat Hajra was the mother of Ismail (AS).
r: The well of Zamzam is linked with Hajra and Ismail (AS).

q: In which year did Pakistan win the Men's Hockey World Cup in Sydney?
f: Pakistan won its fourth Hockey World Cup in Sydney in 1994.
r: Pakistan also won the World Cup in 1971, 1978 and 1982.

q: Who wrote the famous Punjabi qissa 'Sohni Mahiwal'?
f: Fazal Shah is credited with the best-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal.
r: Waris Shah wrote the famous version of Heer Ranjha.

q: Who wrote 'Kashf-ul-Mahjoob'?
o: Ali bin Usman Hujwiri (Data Ganj Bakhsh)
f: Kashf-ul-Mahjoob was written by Ali bin Usman Hujwiri.
r: It is one of the earliest books on Sufism in Persian.

q: Which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA)?
f: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).
r: She kept the written copy of the Quran compiled under Abu Bakr (RA).

q: In which Hijri year was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Maqdis to the Kaaba?
f: The Qibla was changed in 2 AH, about 16-17 months after the Hijrah.
r: Masjid al-Qiblatain in Madinah is linked with this event.

q: What was the old name of Faisalabad?
f: Faisalabad was called Lyallpur until it was renamed in 1977.
r: It was renamed in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.

q: According to the 2023 census, which is Pakistan's most populous district?
f: Lahore District had the largest population (about 13 million) in the 2023 census.
r: Karachi is a bigger city, but it is split into several districts.

q: Who first proposed the idea of SAARC?
f: Bangladesh's President Ziaur Rahman proposed regional cooperation in 1980.
r: SAARC was formally established in Dhaka in December 1985.

q: How many books are included in the Sihah Sittah (Kutub al-Sittah)?
f: Kutub al-Sittah means 'the six books' of hadith.
r: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are the two most famous of them.

q: Who martyred Hazrat Hamza (RA) at the Battle of Uhud?
f: Wahshi ibn Harb killed Hamza (RA) with a spear at Uhud.
r: Wahshi later accepted Islam.

q: In analytic geometry, what is the x-coordinate of a point called?
f: In a point (x, y), the first coordinate x is called the abscissa.
r: The y-coordinate is called the ordinate.

q: On which occasion did the five daily prayers become obligatory?
f: Islamic tradition links the command of five daily prayers to the Night Journey and Ascension (Mi'raj).
r: The exact date of the Mi'raj (often said to be 27 Rajab) is disputed among scholars.

q: The Gulf of Riga is part of which sea?
f: The Gulf of Riga is an inlet of the Baltic Sea between Latvia and Estonia.
r: Riga, the capital of Latvia, lies at the southern end of the gulf.

q: What is the highest military order of the Netherlands?
f: The Military William Order (Militaire Willems-Orde) is the oldest and highest Dutch honour for military bravery.
r: The order was established in 1815.

q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam site located?
f: The proposed site is on the Indus River near Kalabagh in Mianwali District, Punjab.
r: The project is controversial and has not been built.

q: Which Caliph of Islam was Hazrat Umar (RA)?
f: Hazrat Umar (RA) succeeded Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) as the second Caliph.
r: His caliphate lasted from 634 to 644 CE.

q: In which direction is India from Pakistan?
f: India lies along Pakistan's eastern border.
r: Much of the Punjab boundary between the two countries follows the Radcliffe Line.

q: What type of government did Pakistan's 1962 Constitution set up?
f: The 1962 Constitution, introduced under Ayub Khan, created a presidential system.
r: The 1973 Constitution brought back a parliamentary system.

q: Where is the shrine of Hazrat Mian Mir located?
f: The Sufi saint Mian Mir lived in Lahore and his shrine is there.
r: Tradition says he laid the foundation stone of the Golden Temple in Amritsar.

q: Habba Khatoon was a poet of which language?
f: Habba Khatoon was a Kashmiri poet and queen famous for Kashmiri lyric poetry.
r: She is linked with Sultan Yusuf Shah Chak of Kashmir.

q: How many centres does a circle have?
f: A circle has exactly one centre, and every point on it is the same distance from that centre.
r: The distance from the centre to the circle is called the radius.

q: Which rivers were given to Pakistan under the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty?
f: The treaty gave the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan.
r: The eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) went mainly to India; the World Bank helped broker the treaty.

q: By what other name is the 1940 Lahore Resolution popularly known?
f: The Lahore Resolution of 23 March 1940 became popularly known as the Pakistan Resolution.
r: It was passed at the All-India Muslim League session in Lahore.

q: Which administrative region of Pakistan borders China?
f: Gilgit-Baltistan shares Pakistan's border with China's Xinjiang region.
r: The Khunjerab Pass on the Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China.

q: What is the capital of Belarus?
f: Minsk is the capital and largest city of Belarus.
r: Belarus is landlocked and its currency is the Belarusian ruble.

q: Which is the smallest ocean in the world by area?
f: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the five oceans.
r: It is also the shallowest ocean.

q: Where are the Ras Koh Hills located?
f: The Ras Koh Hills are in Chagai District of Balochistan.
r: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests there on 28 May 1998.

q: In which country is the Port of Rotterdam?
f: Rotterdam is a Dutch city and its port is the largest in Europe.
r: The port lies on the Rhine-Meuse-Scheldt delta.

q: What is the approximate length of CPEC from Kashgar to Gwadar?
f: CPEC from Kashgar in Xinjiang to Gwadar is commonly cited as about 3,000 km long.
r: CPEC includes road, rail, energy and port projects.

q: What is the approximate height of the highest peak of the Ras Koh Hills?
f: Common geographic sources give the highest point of the Ras Koh Hills as about 3,009 m.
r: Ras Koh is in Chagai, Balochistan, site of the 1998 nuclear tests.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Nasr (Hatf-IX) missile?
f: ISPR has stated the Nasr's range as about 70 km (first tested at 60 km).
r: Nasr is a short-range tactical ballistic missile.

q: What does Hazrat Usman's (RA) title Dhun-Nurayn mean?
f: He married two daughters of the Prophet (PBUH), Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum, one after the other, so he was called Possessor of the Two Lights.
r: Hazrat Usman (RA) was the third Caliph.

q: Which title is traditionally given to Prophet Ismail (AS)?
f: Muslim tradition calls Ismail (AS) Zabihullah, the one offered for sacrifice.
r: Khalilullah is the title of his father, Prophet Ibrahim (AS).

q: Which German general was nicknamed the Desert Fox?
f: Erwin Rommel earned the nickname while commanding German forces in North Africa in World War II.
r: He was defeated at the Second Battle of El Alamein in 1942.

q: Who built Masjid-e-Dirar in Madinah?
f: Masjid-e-Dirar was built by the hypocrites of Madinah, instigated by Abu Amir al-Rahib.
r: It is mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah (9:107-110).

q: In which year was Malala Yousafzai awarded the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Malala won the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize, shared with Kailash Satyarthi.
r: She was then the youngest-ever Nobel laureate, at age 17.

q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
f: 'Penta' means five, so a pentagon has five sides.
r: The interior angles of a pentagon add up to 540 degrees.

q: What is another name of K2?
f: K2 is also called Mount Godwin-Austen, after surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen.
r: K2 is the world's second-highest mountain, in the Karakoram.

q: Who contested against Ayub Khan in the 1965 presidential election?
f: Fatima Jinnah was the joint opposition candidate against Ayub Khan in 1965.
r: Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats electoral college.

q: Where is the Chashma Nuclear Power Plant located?
f: CHASNUPP is near Chashma Barrage in Mianwali District, Punjab.
r: The plant operates under IAEA safeguards.

q: Which Companion served Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) for about ten years?
f: Anas (RA) was brought to the Prophet as a boy and served him for about ten years in Madinah.
r: He is one of the main narrators of hadith.

q: What is the upper house of Pakistan's Parliament called?
f: Pakistan's Parliament has two houses; the upper house is the Senate.
r: The lower house is the National Assembly (Article 50).

q: What was Hazrat Safiyyah's (RA) relationship to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Safiyyah bint Huyayy (RA) was a wife of the Prophet and a Mother of the Believers.
r: She married the Prophet after the Battle of Khaybar.

q: Which is called the world's highest battlefield?
f: Siachen, in the eastern Karakoram, is the highest place where armies face each other.
r: Pakistan and India have kept troops there since 1984.

q: What is the world's largest desert?
f: A desert is defined by very low rainfall, so ice-covered Antarctica is the largest desert.
r: The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

q: What is the movement of people from one place to another called?
f: Moving from one place to another to live is called migration.
r: Leaving a country is emigration; entering one is immigration.

q: How many official copies of the Quran were prepared under Caliph Uthman (RA)?
f: Uthman (RA) had several standard copies made and sent to major cities; accounts give different totals, often 5 to 7.
r: This work standardized the written text of the Quran.

q: How many members did Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly have at its formation?
f: Pakistan's first Constituent Assembly started with 69 members (later raised to 79).
r: It first met on 10 August 1947 and elected Quaid-e-Azam its President on 11 August.

q: Counting from 1970, which general election of Pakistan was the 2018 election?
r: The 2018 election was held on 25 July 2018 and PTI won the most seats.

q: Which Companion suggested digging a trench in the Battle of the Trench?
f: Salman al-Farsi (RA) suggested the Persian method of defending Madinah with a trench.
r: The battle (Ghazwa-e-Khandaq) took place in 5 AH / 627 CE.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations? (2)
f: The UN headquarters is in Manhattan, New York City, on the East River.
r: The UN also has major offices in Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi.

q: Which country is UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres from?
f: Antonio Guterres is a Portuguese politician and former Prime Minister of Portugal.
r: He has been the ninth UN Secretary-General since 1 January 2017; his second term ends on 31 December 2026.

q: Where are the Black Hills located?
f: The Black Hills are a mountain range mainly in South Dakota, extending into Wyoming.
r: Mount Rushmore is carved in the Black Hills.

q: Who is known as the 'Father of Democracy' in Pakistan?
f: Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy, Pakistan's fifth Prime Minister, is commonly given the title Father of Democracy.
r: Jinnah is known as Quaid-e-Azam (Great Leader).

q: Which country is called the world's largest democracy?
f: India has the largest number of voters of any democracy.
r: India has a parliamentary system with a President and a Prime Minister.

q: Where is Nari Bolan Dam located?
f: Nari Bolan Dam is in Kachhi (Bolan) District of Balochistan.
r: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River and Tarbela Dam on the Indus.

q: Which languages did Pakistan's 1956 Constitution recognize as state languages?
f: The 1956 Constitution made both Urdu and Bengali state languages.
r: English was allowed for official use for a transition period.

q: In which district are the Khewra Salt Mines located?
f: Khewra, in the Salt Range, is in Jhelum District, Punjab.
r: It is one of the oldest and largest salt mines in the world.

q: Who was the main founding leader of the USSR?
f: Lenin led the Bolshevik Revolution, and the USSR was formed under him on 30 December 1922.
r: The USSR dissolved in 1991.

q: When was Pakistan's first martial law imposed?
f: President Iskander Mirza declared martial law on 7 October 1958 and made Ayub Khan Chief Martial Law Administrator.
r: Ayub Khan removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.

q: On which river is Jinnah Barrage built?
f: Jinnah Barrage is on the Indus River near Kalabagh, Mianwali District.
r: It is separate from the proposed Kalabagh Dam.

q: Where is the headquarters (Secretariat) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
f: The SCO Secretariat is located in Beijing, China. The organisation was established in 2001 to promote regional cooperation among its member states.
r: The SCO's anti-terrorism body (RATS) is based in Tashkent; Pakistan became a full member in 2017.

q: Who was the first Chief Justice of Pakistan?
f: Sir Abdul Rashid became Pakistan’s first Chief Justice in 1949, heading the Federal Court. He served in this position until 1954.
r: Justice Muhammad Munir succeeded him in 1954.

q: Who is the Deputy Prime Minister of Pakistan (as of October 2026)?
f: Ishaq Dar serves as Pakistan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister. Government appointments should be checked against the latest official records before publication.
r: Ishaq Dar was appointed Deputy Prime Minister in April 2024.

q: In which direction is Afghanistan located from Pakistan?
f: Afghanistan lies mainly to the northwest of Pakistan and shares a long international border with it, commonly known as the Durand Line.
r: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893.

q: In which year did the Kargil War take place?
f: The Kargil conflict took place between India and Pakistan in the summer of 1999 in the Kargil sector of the disputed Kashmir region.
r: Captain Karnal Sher Khan and Havildar Lalak Jan received the Nishan-e-Haider for Kargil.

q: What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia. It is an important political, administrative and economic centre.
r: Jeddah is Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea port city.

q: What is the official currency of Saudi Arabia?
f: The Saudi riyal is the official currency of Saudi Arabia. One riyal is divided into 100 halalas.
r: The UAE uses the dirham.

q: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan in the Khyber region?
f: The Khyber Pass connects northwestern Pakistan with Afghanistan. Historically, it has served as an important route for trade, travel and military movements.
r: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with China.

q: At what price did Pakistan purchase Gwadar from Oman?
f: Pakistan purchased Gwadar from Oman in 1958. The port later became strategically important because of its location on the Arabian Sea.
r: Gwadar became part of Pakistan on 8 September 1958, under Prime Minister Feroz Khan Noon.

q: Under which constitutional amendment was the post of Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) created in Pakistan?
f: The amendment changed Article 243 of Pakistan’s Constitution and restructured the higher defence command system.
r: The 26th Amendment (2024) changed how the Chief Justice of Pakistan is appointed.

q: Who was the father of Prophet Ibrahim (A.S.) according to the Quranic account commonly taught in Islamic Studies?
f: Surah Al-An'am (6:74) mentions Azar in connection with Prophet Ibrahim (A.S.) and his rejection of idol worship. Classical scholars have discussed the precise relationship described in this verse.
r: Prophet Ibrahim (A.S.) is known by the title Khalilullah.

q: Who was the first Muslim martyr in Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah (R.A.) was among the earliest Muslims persecuted in Makkah. She is widely recognised in Islamic history as the first martyr of Islam.
r: She was the mother of Hazrat Ammar bin Yasir (R.A.).

q: What is the eccentricity of a parabola?
f: Eccentricity describes the shape of a conic section. A parabola has an eccentricity exactly equal to 1.
r: A circle has e = 0, an ellipse 0 < e < 1, and a hyperbola e > 1.

q: Who holds the record for the most wickets in men's Test cricket? (2)
f: The Sri Lankan spin bowler retired from Test cricket with 800 wickets, the highest total in the format’s history.
r: Shane Warne is second with 708 Test wickets.

q: What is a synonym of "turbulent"?
f: “Turbulent” describes something marked by disorder, instability or violent movement. “Stormy” is an appropriate synonym when describing rough weather.
r: "Tranquil" is an antonym of turbulent.

q: What is the integral of 2x with respect to x?
f: The printed question was unclear; it most likely meant ∫2x dx. Since the derivative of x² is 2x, ∫2x dx = x² + c.
r: The derivative of any constant c is 0, which is why c is added.

q: What is the antonym of "wild"?
f: “Wild” describes an animal that is not domesticated,  whereas “tame” describes an animal that has been trained to live peacefully with humans.
r: "Domesticated" is another antonym of wild.

q: What is the antonym of "gracious"?
f: “Gracious” means courteous, kind and pleasant in behaviour. “Rude” describes someone who behaves impolitely or shows a lack of consideration for others.
r: "Cordial" is a synonym of gracious.

q: Who wrote the book "Jinnah of Pakistan"?
f: Stanley Wolpert was an American historian and author. His book Jinnah of Pakistan is a biography of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the founder of Pakistan.
r: Hector Bolitho wrote "Jinnah: Creator of Pakistan" (1954).

q: Which article of the Constitution of Pakistan guarantees the right to education?
f: Article 25-A makes it the state's responsibility to provide free and compulsory education to children aged 5–16 years, in the manner determined by law.
r: Article 25-A was added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather, Abdul Muttalib, passed away?
f: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born around 570 CE. His grandfather, Abdul Muttalib, took care of him after his mother's death and passed away when Muhammad ﷺ was approximately eight years old.
r: After Abdul Muttalib's death, his uncle Abu Talib took care of him.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he migrated from Makkah to Madinah?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was approximately 53 years old at the time of his migration to Madinah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) passed away in Madinah at about 63 years of age.

q: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was the father of which wife of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Hazrat Ayesha (R.A.) was the daughter of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A.), the first Caliph of Islam. She became one of the most important transmitters of Hadith and Islamic knowledge.
r: Hazrat Hafsa (RA) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (RA).

q: Who was the first woman martyr in Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah (R.A.) was among the earliest Muslims persecuted in Makkah. She is widely recognised as the first martyr in Islamic history.
r: She was the mother of Hazrat Ammar bin Yasir (RA).

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
f: A triangular prism has two triangular faces and three rectangular faces. Therefore, it has five faces in total.
r: A triangular prism has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

q: The China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) is a joint project between which two countries?
f: CPEC is an economic development initiative connecting Pakistan's Gwadar Port with China's Xinjiang region through transport, energy and infrastructure projects.
r: CPEC is part of China's Belt and Road Initiative, launched in 2013.

q: What is another name for the Karakoram Highway?
f: The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan with China through the mountainous Karakoram region. It is an important route for trade, travel and bilateral connectivity.
r: The Karakoram Highway (N-35) is often called the Eighth Wonder of the World.

q: Which two countries are connected by the Khunjerab Pass?
f: Khunjerab Pass lies in the Karakoram Mountains along the Pakistan–China border. It is the highest paved international border crossing in the world.
r: Khunjerab Pass is about 4,693 metres above sea level.

q: Hafeez Kardar was a famous player of which sport?
f: Abdul Hafeez Kardar was a prominent Pakistani cricketer and the country's first Test captain after independence. He played a major role in establishing Pakistan in international Test cricket.
r: Pakistan played its first Test match in 1952 against India.

q: Which is the highest plateau in Balochistan?
f: The Kalat region is an elevated area in central Balochistan. Plateau-related questions can sometimes use different geographical classifications, so the exact wording of the original test question matters.
r: The Potohar Plateau is in northern Punjab.

q: What was the former name of Karachi?
f: Karachi developed from a small fishing settlement traditionally associated with the name Kolachi. The settlement later grew into a major port city and Pakistan's largest city.
r: Karachi was Pakistan's first capital.

q: What is the capital of Hungary?
f: Budapest is the capital and largest city of Hungary. It was formed through the unification of Buda, Óbuda and Pest in 1873.
r: The River Danube flows through Budapest.

q: Where is the Dasht River located?
f: The Dasht River is located in southwestern Balochistan and flows through the region towards the Arabian Sea. It is associated with the Gwadar and Kech areas.
r: The Mirani Dam is built on the Dasht River.

q: Which country is the world's largest crude oil producer?
f: The United States remained the world's largest crude oil producer in 2025, averaging approximately 13.6 million barrels per day. The answer may differ if the original question refers specifically to oil exports or Pakistan's oil imports.
r: Saudi Arabia is the world's largest crude oil exporter.

q: Which country hosted the first Asian Games? (3)
f: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951.
r: Asian Games are held every 4 years. Pakistan first took part in 1951.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan? (3)
f: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar in Pakistan with Afghanistan.
r: Khunjerab connects Pakistan with China.

q: With the help of which country did Pakistan build its first steel mill (Pakistan Steel Mills, Karachi)?
f: Pakistan Steel Mills at Karachi was set up with Soviet technical help in the 1970s.
r: It started production in 1981. It is located at Pipri, Karachi.

q: How many Khulafa-e-Rashidin (Rightly Guided Caliphs) were there?
f: The four caliphs were Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali (R.A.).
r: Their rule lasted from 632 to 661 CE.

q: Which prophet built the ship (Ark)?
f: Hazrat Nuh (A.S.) built the ship by Allah's command before the great flood.
r: Surah Nuh (71) is named after him. Ark landed on Mount Judi.

q: What is the approximate length of the Amazon River? (2)
f: Common sources give the Amazon about 6,400 km; some measures give about 6,992 km.
r: Nile is about 6,650 km; Yangtze (6,300 km) is the longest river in Asia. Note: Same UN question printed again as 1013; Amazon length asked instead. Estimates vary.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the Muslim League? (2)
f: Jinnah joined the All India Muslim League in 1913.
r: The League was founded in Dhaka in 1906. The Lucknow Pact was in 1916.

q: In which city was Pakistan's first television station established (1964)?
f: PTV's first station started in Lahore on 26 November 1964.
r: Karachi and Islamabad centres opened later.

q: On which date was the Quit India resolution passed (Quit India Movement)?
f: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution on 8 August 1942 in Bombay; the movement began on 9 August.
r: Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die'.

q: What does 'alter' mean?
f: To alter is to make something different.
r: Antonym: preserve, keep.

q: What does 'obvious' mean?
f: Obvious means easy to see or understand; apparent.
r: Synonyms: evident, apparent, plain.

q: How many Farz (obligatory acts) are there in Hajj according to the Hanafi view? (2)
f: The Hanafi view counts three Farz: Ihram, standing at Arafat and Tawaf-e-Ziyarat.
r: Other schools count Sa'i as a pillar too. Wuquf at Arafat is the most important. Note: Counts differ between schools; the Hanafi count of 3 is used.

q: The first five verses revealed to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) belong to which surah?
f: The first five ayat of Surah Al-Alaq were revealed in the Cave of Hira.
r: Revelation began in Ramadan. The angel was Jibreel (A.S.).

q: Who wrote the Punjabi epic romance 'Heer Ranjha'? (2)
f: Waris Shah wrote Heer in 1766.
r: Waris Shah is buried at Jandiala Sher Khan.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of India (after the Charter Act of 1833)?
f: The Charter Act 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Bentinck was the first.
r: Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773). Lord Mountbatten was the last.

q: What is the total number of seats of the Punjab Assembly? (2)
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 for women and 8 for non-Muslims.
r: Punjab Assembly is the largest provincial assembly in Pakistan.

q: Which is regarded as the longest river of the world in standard exams?
f: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is the traditional exam answer for the longest river, though some measurements argue the Amazon is longer.
r: Some surveys say the Amazon is longer. The Amazon is largest by volume. Note: Amazon vs Nile length is debated; standard exam answer is Nile.

q: What is the name of the pamphlet/book of Chaudhry Rehmat Ali published in 1933?
f: Rehmat Ali issued 'Now or Never' in 1933 and proposed the name Pakistan.
r: He launched the Pakistan National Movement in Cambridge.

q: Which is the last month of the Islamic calendar? (3)
f: Dhul Hijjah is the 12th and last month; Hajj is performed in it.
r: Muharram is the first month.

q: What was the old name of Makkah?
f: Makkah is also called Bakkah in the Holy Quran (3:96).
r: The old name of Madinah was Yathrib.

q: Which is the smallest continent? (5)
f: Australia/Oceania is the smallest continent by area.
r: Asia is the largest.

q: In which battle was the blessed tooth of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) injured?
f: In Uhud the Holy Prophet's lower front tooth was broken and he was wounded.
r: Uhud was fought in 3 AH near Madinah.

q: How many plane faces does a triangular prism have?
f: A triangular prism has 2 triangular and 3 rectangular faces, which makes 5.
r: It has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

q: In which district of Pakistan is the Khewra salt range (biggest salt mine) located? (2)
f: Khewra Salt Mine lies in the Salt Range in Jhelum district.
r: It is the second largest salt mine in the world.

q: Injeel is the holy book of which Prophet?
f: Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S.).
r: Torah to Musa, Zabur to Dawood, Quran to Muhammad (PBUH).

q: In which year was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed? (6)
f: The boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.
r: The Karakoram Highway links the two countries.

q: Which province of Pakistan is known as 'Bab-ul-Islam' (Gateway of Islam)? (2)
f: Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam as Islam first came to the subcontinent here through Muhammad bin Qasim (712 CE).
r: Muhammad bin Qasim defeated Raja Dahir.

q: Convert 30 degrees into radians. (2)
f: Radians = degrees x pi/180, so 30 x pi/180 = pi/6 = 0.5236.
r: 180 degrees = pi radians.

q: India conducted its first nuclear test in which year?
f: India's first test, 'Smiling Buddha', was on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran.
r: Pakistan tested in May 1998 at Chagai.

q: Who succeeded Ali Amin Gandapur as Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in October 2025?
f: PTI's Sohail Afridi was elected KP chief minister on 15 October 2025.
r: As of Oct 2026, reports say governor's rule was imposed in KP on 11 Oct 2026, so there is no elected CM.

q: Which is the most populated city of Sindh? (2)
f: Karachi is the largest city of Sindh and Pakistan.
r: Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

q: When was the Battle of Uhud fought? (2)
f: Uhud was fought on 7 Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE).
r: Badr was 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

q: Who was the first captain of the Pakistan cricket team? (2)
f: A. H. Kardar led Pakistan in its first Test in 1952.
r: Pakistan's first Test was against India in 1952.

q: Where was the United Nations founded (charter signed)?
f: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco in June 1945; the UN came into being on 24 October 1945.
r: UN headquarters is in New York.

q: Which is the largest dam in the world (by power capacity) and where is it located?
o: Three Gorges Dam, Yangtze River, China
f: Three Gorges Dam in Hubei, China is the world's largest power station.
r: Tarbela is the largest earth-filled dam in the world. Note: 'Largest' depends on measure (power, size, height); Three Gorges is the standard answer.

q: Riyadh is the capital of which country?
f: Riyadh is the capital and largest city of Saudi Arabia.
r: Makkah and Madinah are the holy cities.

q: Where is the Mahabat Khan Mosque located? (3)
f: It was built in the 1670s by Mahabat Khan, a Mughal governor of Peshawar.
r: Wazir Khan Mosque is in Lahore.

q: Who was the last British Governor-General (Viceroy) of India? (2)
f: Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and later first Governor-General of independent India.
r: Jinnah was the first Governor-General of Pakistan.

q: In which region of Pakistan is the Shina (Sheena) language spoken? (3)
f: Shina is mainly spoken in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: Burushaski and Balti are other languages of the region.

q: In which sport has Pakistan won the Champions Trophy at world level (3 times)?
f: Pakistan won the Hockey Champions Trophy three times (1978, 1980, 1994), not four, and it is the only Asian winner; hockey is still the right answer.
r: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times (1971, 1978, 1982, 1994).

q: In which city is the Wazir Khan Mosque located? (4)
f: Wazir Khan Mosque stands in the Walled City of Lahore, built 1634-35.
r: It is famous for Mughal-era tile work.

q: What is the capital of Somalia? (7)
f: Mogadishu is the capital and largest city of Somalia.
r: Somalia is in the Horn of Africa.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: Benazir Bhutto became PM in 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.
r: She was PM in 1988-90 and 1993-96.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah left the Congress in 1920 over Gandhi's Non-Cooperation methods.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: What is the currency of Egypt? (3)
f: Egypt's currency is the Egyptian pound (EGP).
r: Cairo is the capital.

q: In mathematics, what does HCF stand for?
f: HCF is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers exactly.
r: LCM is the least common multiple.

q: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a poet of which language?
f: Shah Latif wrote Shah Jo Risalo in Sindhi.
r: His shrine is at Bhit Shah.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of India at the time of the Lahore Declaration (1999)?
f: Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif signed the Lahore Declaration on 21 February 1999.
r: Vajpayee travelled to Lahore by the Delhi-Lahore bus.

q: How many Articles are there in the Constitution of Pakistan 1973?
f: The 1973 Constitution has 280 Articles.
r: It came into force on 14 August 1973.

q: In which year did World War I start?
f: WWI began in July 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand.
r: It ended in 1918.

q: Which country suffered atomic bombings and massive destruction in World War II?
f: The USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945.
r: Japan surrendered on 15 August 1945. Note: Question is vague; Japan (atomic bombs) is the standard answer.

q: On which date was the Pakistan-China border agreement signed? (2)
f: The boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.
r: Signed by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Chen Yi.

q: Who is the Chairman of NAB (as of Oct 2026)?
f: As of Oct 2026, Nazir Ahmad is NAB chairman; his term was extended by 3 years from March 2026.
r: He took over in March 2023.

q: Who is the current President of France (as of Oct 2026)? (2)
f: As of Oct 2026, Macron is president; his second term runs until 2027.
r: He was first elected in 2017.

q: What is the capital of Malaysia? (2)
f: Kuala Lumpur is the capital; Putrajaya is the administrative centre.
r: Malaysia is in Southeast Asia.

q: What is the total length of Pakistan's coastline? (4)
f: Pakistan's coast along the Arabian Sea is about 1,046 km.
r: Sindh coast is about 270 km; Balochistan coast about 770 km.

q: How many countries have veto power in the UN Security Council?
f: The five permanent members are USA, UK, France, China and Russia.
r: There are 10 non-permanent members without veto.

q: Which surah of the Holy Quran contains Bismillah twice? (2)
f: Surah An-Naml has Bismillah at the start and also within verse 30.
r: Surah At-Tawbah has no Bismillah.

q: Which is the deepest ocean?
f: Pacific holds the Mariana Trench, the deepest point.
r: Challenger Deep is about 11,000 m deep.

q: Which is the lowest point on land in Asia?
f: The Dead Sea shore is about 430 m below sea level, the lowest land point.
r: It is between Jordan and Israel.

q: What is the border line between India and China called? (3)
f: The McMahon Line marks the eastern boundary of India with Tibet/China (1914).
r: The actual control is called the Line of Actual Control (LAC). The Durand Line is Pakistan-Afghanistan. Note: The border is disputed; McMahon Line is the standard answer.

q: Which country did Liaquat Ali Khan visit in 1950 on his famous first major state visit?
f: Liaquat visited the USA in May 1950 on Truman's invitation.
r: He chose Washington over Moscow's invitation. Note: Some sources say he had visited Iran in 1949 earlier; USA is the standard exam answer.

q: With which Indian Prime Minister did General Pervez Musharraf hold the 2001 Agra Summit?
f: Musharraf met Vajpayee in Agra in July 2001.
r: Simla Agreement (1972) was between Bhutto and Indira Gandhi.

q: Who discovered X-rays? (2)
f: Rontgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and won the first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901).
r: Marie Curie discovered polonium and radium.

q: Who was the caretaker Chief Minister of Punjab (Pakistan) in 2023-24?
f: Mohsin Naqvi was caretaker CM from Jan 2023 to Feb 2024.
r: As of Oct 2026, Maryam Nawaz is the elected Chief Minister.

q: Which major city of Pakistan has the highest literacy rate? (2)
f: Islamabad (capital territory) has the highest literacy rate.
r: Balochistan has the lowest provincial literacy. Note: Rankings vary by census; Islamabad is the standard answer.

q: Who founded Facebook?
f: Mark Zuckerberg launched Facebook in 2004 at Harvard.
r: Parent company is now Meta.

q: In which year did Fatima Jinnah formally enter the All India Muslim League (as commonly cited)? (2)
f: Many sources say she joined the League's Women's Central Sub-Committee in 1938.
r: She was called 'Madar-e-Millat'. Note: Source answer given was about Microsoft (Bill Gates, 1975), which is wrong. Sources differ (1934 / 1938); 1938 chosen.

q: What is the currency of Russia? (4)
f: Russia's currency is the ruble.
r: Moscow is the capital.

q: What does 'Hadith' mean in Islamic terms?
o: Life story of the four caliphs
Sayings, actions and approvals of the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
f: Hadith are the reports of the words, deeds and approvals of the Prophet (PBUH).
r: Sahih Bukhari is the most authentic collection.

q: Which city is known as the 'Heart of Pakistan'? (2)
f: Lahore is called the heart of Pakistan for its culture and history.
r: It is also called the Cultural Capital. Note: Nickname varies; Lahore is the usual answer.

q: Which country voted against Pakistan's admission to the UN in 1947? (2)
f: Afghanistan was the only country that opposed Pakistan's membership; Pakistan joined on 30 Sept 1947.
r: Afghanistan later reversed its stand.

q: Olympic Airlines (Olympic Airways) was the national airline of which country? (4)
f: Olympic Airways was the flag carrier of Greece, founded in 1957 by Aristotle Onassis.
r: It was replaced by Olympic Air in 2009. Aegean is now Greece's largest airline.

q: Who won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sobers Trophy) for 2022? (2)
f: Babar Azam won the ICC Men's Cricketer of the Year (Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy) for 2022. He also won the ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year for 2022.
r: Ben Stokes won the ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year for 2022. Shaheen Afridi won the Sobers Trophy for 2021.

q: On which date did Pakistan sign the SEATO (Manila) Pact?
f: Pakistan was an original signatory of the Manila Pact on 8 September 1954.
r: Pakistan joined CENTO (Baghdad Pact) in 1955 and left SEATO in 1972.

q: Multan is famous as the city of what? (2)
f: Multan is called 'City of Saints and Shrines' (Madinat-ul-Auliya).
r: Shrines include Bahauddin Zakariya and Shah Rukn-e-Alam.

q: Which is the smallest bone in the human body? (2)
f: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone (about 3 mm).
r: The femur is the longest bone.

q: From which ruler did Pakistan purchase Gwadar in 1958?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman for about 3 million US dollars; it joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958.
r: Gwadar port is key to CPEC.

q: How many member states does the UN have?
f: The UN has 193 member states; South Sudan joined in 2011 as the latest.
r: Palestine and Vatican are observers.

q: Which of these is the correct meaning of veto power in the UN?
o: Power to appoint the Secretary-General alone
Power of a permanent member to block any Security Council resolution
Right to vote twice in the General Assembly
Right to expel any member state
f: A single no vote from any of the five permanent members blocks a resolution.
r: The five are USA, UK, France, China and Russia.

q: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which area?
