f: Bolan Pass links Quetta (high Balochistan) to the Sindh plains via Dhadar and Sibi.
r: It was an old route from Central Asia to South Asia.

q: The Wagah border connects Pakistan with which country? (3)
f: Wagah (Lahore side) is the main road border crossing between Pakistan and India, near Amritsar.
r: The Beating Retreat ceremony is held daily at Wagah. Torkham connects Pakistan with Afghanistan.

q: The Indus Plain is divided into which two main parts?
o: Upper Indus Plain and Lower Indus Plain
f: The Upper (Punjab) and Lower (Sindh) Indus Plain are the two parts.
r: Plain is made by the Indus and its tributaries.

q: Choose the correct spelling.
f: Impetuous (acting quickly without thought) is the correct spelling.
r: Do not confuse with 'impetus'.

q: What is the antonym of 'broadly'?
f: Broadly means in a wide way; the opposite is narrowly.
r: Antonym of broad is narrow.

q: Who popularised the Sohni Mahiwal story in Punjabi poetry?
f: Fazal Shah Sayyad wrote the well-known Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal.
r: Heer Ranjha is by Waris Shah.

q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness (often linked to eye problems in MCQs)?
f: Vitamin A lack causes night blindness.
r: Colour blindness is genetic, not due to vitamin deficiency.

q: Which country mediated the Tashkent Agreement (1966) between India and Pakistan?
f: The Soviet PM Kosygin mediated; the treaty was signed on 10 January 1966.
r: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it.

q: Where is the headquarters of Amnesty International? (2)
f: Amnesty International is headquartered in London, UK.
r: It won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Punjab, Pakistan (as of Oct 2026)? (2)
f: As of Oct 2026, Maryam Nawaz has been CM since 26 Feb 2024.

f: Abu Sufyan commanded the Quraish at Uhud; Abu Jahl and the others had died at Badr.
r: Khalid bin Walid led the Quraish cavalry then.

q: In Ghazwa Uhud, Hazrat Ali (RA) was awarded with:
f: As reported in tradition, the Prophet gave Hazrat Ali (RA) the sword Zulfiqar at Uhud.
r: Saifullah was Khalid bin Walid's title. Note: This is a traditional report; sources differ.

q: Who is the Defence Minister of Pakistan? (3)
f: Khawaja Muhammad Asif has been Federal Minister for Defence since 2024. As of Oct 2026 no report of his replacement was found.
r: He is a PML-N leader from Sialkot. He also served as Defence Minister in 2022-23.

q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
f: Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan became Pakistan's first Foreign Minister in 1947.
r: He later became President of the UN General Assembly (1962) and a judge of the ICJ.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan? (6)
f: Liaqat Ali Khan became the first PM on 15 August 1947 and served until his assassination in 1951.
r: He was assassinated at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951. He is called Quaid-e-Millat.

q: Who is the founder of the iPhone (Apple, which launched it in 2007)?
f: Steve Jobs, co-founder and CEO of Apple, introduced the first iPhone in January 2007.
r: Apple was founded in 1976 by Jobs, Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Note: Phone has no single 'founder'; Steve Jobs is the standard exam answer.

q: The first recorded ancient Olympic Games were held in 776 BC in which place?
f: The first recorded ancient Olympics took place at Olympia in Greece in 776 BC.
r: The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.

q: In which year did Pakistan win its first Olympic gold medal in hockey?
f: Pakistan beat India 1-0 in the final at the Rome Olympics in 1960.
r: Pakistan won 3 Olympic hockey golds: 1960, 1968, 1984.

q: The Mughal Empire was founded by
f: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the empire.
r: Babur wrote his memoir Baburnama.

q: Who was the last Mughal emperor?
f: Bahadur Shah II 'Zafar' was removed by the British after the War of Independence 1857 and exiled to Rangoon.
r: He was also an Urdu poet.

q: How many Nobel Prizes has Pakistan won (counting Pakistani-origin laureates as per common exam answer)? (2)
f: Dr. Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014) are the two Pakistani Nobel laureates.
r: Salam was the first Muslim to win a science Nobel. Note: Count depends on definition; two is the standard answer.

q: In which year did Malala Yousafzai win the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Malala shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Kailash Satyarthi at the age of 17.
r: She is the youngest Nobel laureate ever.

q: Who wrote the national anthem of Pakistan? (2)
f: Abu-Al-Asar Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the lyrics of Qaumi Tarana.
r: The anthem is in Persian-heavy Urdu and has 3 stanzas.

q: In which year was the Qaumi Tarana officially adopted as Pakistan's national anthem in August?
f: The anthem was officially adopted in August 1954.
r: Its tune was composed earlier, in 1949.

q: Who composed the national anthem of Pakistan?
f: Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla composed the music in 1949.
r: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the words.

q: Who designed the national flag of Pakistan? (3)
f: Syed Amiruddin Kidwai designed the flag, based on the Muslim League flag.
r: The white stripe stands for minorities; green for Muslims.

q: Who was the first woman judge of a High Court in Pakistan?
f: Majida Rizvi was appointed to the Lahore High Court in 1974, the first woman High Court judge.
r: Justice Ayesha Malik became the first woman judge of the Supreme Court in 2022.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
f: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela.
r: Angel Falls, the highest waterfall, is in Venezuela.

q: Manama is the capital of which country?
f: Manama is the capital of Bahrain.
r: Bahrain is an island country in the Persian Gulf.

q: What is widely considered the greatest rivalry in Test cricket?
f: The Ashes began in 1882 and is the oldest and most famous Test rivalry.
r: The urn trophy is only a small replica kept at Lord's.

q: Which pass is associated with Kohat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (source says it links Kohat with Afghanistan)?
f: The Kohat Pass links Peshawar with Kohat; it is the Kohat-area pass, as given by the source.
r: Khyber Pass links Peshawar with Kabul.

q: Bangladesh separated from Pakistan after how many years?
f: Pakistan was created in 1947 and East Pakistan became Bangladesh in 1971, 24 years later.
r: The war ended on 16 December 1971.

q: In which year did Bangladesh separate from Pakistan? (4)
f: East Pakistan became Bangladesh after the war of 1971.
r: Dhaka fell on 16 December 1971. The Hamoodur Rahman Commission investigated the fall.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Education and Professional Training of Pakistan? (2)
f: As of 2026 reports, Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui holds this ministry.
r: He is from the MQM-Pakistan party.

q: Who is the Federal Minister for Health of Pakistan?
f: Syed Mustafa Kamal is Federal Health Minister, per reports to September 2026.
r: He is a former mayor of Karachi (MQM-P).

q: Which is the largest mosque in the world?
f: Masjid al-Haram in Makkah is the largest mosque by capacity and area.
r: Masjid-e-Nabawi in Madinah is the second largest.

q: In which city is Masjid-e-Nabawi located?
f: Masjid-e-Nabawi, built by the Prophet (PBUH), is in Madinah.
r: It contains the Prophet's tomb (Rawdah).

q: What is the currency of Australia?
f: Australia uses the Australian dollar (AUD).
r: Its capital is Canberra.

q: The Arabian Sea is located in which part of Pakistan?
f: Pakistan's coastline on the Arabian Sea lies in the south (Sindh and Balochistan).
r: Karachi and Gwadar are major ports.

q: In which language did Baba Bulleh Shah mainly write poetry?
f: Baba Bulleh Shah, the Sufi poet of Kasur, wrote mostly in Punjabi (kafis).
r: His shrine is in Kasur.

q: In which language does Kalsoom Begum write poetry?
f: As given in the source list, she writes in Urdu.
r: Urdu is Pakistan's national language.

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army? (2)
f: Messervy, a British officer, was the first C-in-C (1947-48).
r: Gracey succeeded him.

q: Who was the first Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee of Pakistan?
f: General Muhammad Shareef was the first CJCSC (1976-80). As of Oct 2026 the CJCSC post has been abolished by the 27th Amendment (Nov 2025), which created the Chief of Defence Forces.
r: 27th Amendment (Nov 2025) created the Chief of Defence Forces and the Federal Constitutional Court.

q: Who was the first Muslim (Pakistani) Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: Ayub Khan became the first native C-in-C in January 1951.
r: He later became President in 1958.

q: Which is the biggest desert of Pakistan? (2)
f: Thar is the largest desert in Pakistan by common exam answer.
r: It lies in Sindh and extends into India. Note: Cholistan and Thar are sometimes compared; Thar is the standard answer.

q: Which is the world's largest desert lake?
f: Lake Turkana in Kenya is the largest permanent desert lake.
r: It is also called the Jade Sea.

q: Which is the coldest desert in the world?
f: Antarctica is a polar desert with the lowest temperatures on Earth.
r: The Gobi is a cold desert but not the coldest.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
f: The Sahara in North Africa is the largest hot desert.
r: Antarctica is the largest desert overall. Note: Plain 'largest desert' is ambiguous (Antarctica is bigger); Sahara is the standard exam answer for hot desert.

q: Who was the first woman head (Governor) of the State Bank of Pakistan? (4)
f: Shamshad Akhtar became SBP Governor in 2005.
r: She served 2005-2006.

q: Who was the first Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan?
f: Zahid Hussain was the first SBP Governor (1948-60).
r: SBP began work on 1 July 1948.

q: The State Bank of Pakistan was inaugurated by Quaid-e-Azam in which month and year?
f: Jinnah inaugurated SBP on 1 July 1948 in Karachi.
r: It was his last major public speech event.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'disastrous'?
f: Disastrous means causing great harm; catastrophic means the same.
r: Devastating and ruinous are also synonyms.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'didactic'?
f: Didactic means intended to teach.
r: It comes from Greek didaktikos.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'dissipate'?
f: Dissipate means to disperse or fade away (also, to waste).
r: Dissipation can also mean wasteful living.

q: Who invented the (practical) electric light bulb? (2)
f: Edison developed the first long-lasting practical bulb in 1879.
r: Joseph Swan independently invented a bulb in England. Note: Often credited jointly with Joseph Swan; Edison is the standard answer.

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'? (3)
f: Finland has about 188,000 lakes.
r: Canada is known as the land of many lakes too, but this nickname is Finland's.

q: What is the capital of Finland?
f: Helsinki is Finland's capital.
r: It is on the Gulf of Finland.

q: What is the currency of Finland?
f: Finland adopted the euro in 1999 (notes in 2002).
r: Sweden and Norway keep their own currencies.

q: How many times has Brazil won the FIFA World Cup?
f: Brazil won in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002. As of Oct 2026 the count is still 5 (Spain won in 2026).
r: Brazil is the only team to play every World Cup.

q: What is Brazil's largest exported crop?
f: Brazil is the world's largest soybean exporter.
r: Brazil is also the top coffee producer.

q: Which country is the world's largest producer of coffee?
f: Brazil produces about a third of the world's coffee.
r: Vietnam is second.

q: What is the highest mountain in the Himalayas?
f: Mount Everest on the Nepal-Tibet border is the highest.
r: K2 is in the Karakoram, not the Himalayas.

q: What is the height of Mount Everest (as commonly taught)?
f: Everest is about 8,848 m (re-measured 8,848.86 m in 2020).

q: The Margalla Hills of Islamabad are an extension of which range?
f: Margalla Hills are the foothills of the Himalayas.
r: Faisal Mosque lies at their foot.

q: Who was martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
f: Hazrat Hamza (RA), uncle of the Prophet, was martyred at Uhud in 625 CE.
r: He was called Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

q: What was the relation of Hazrat Hamza (RA) with Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH)? (2)
f: Hamza was the son of Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather, so he was his paternal uncle (and foster brother).
r: He was also the Prophet's foster brother.

q: Who was the first commander of the Islamic Army (first military expedition)?
f: The first expedition (Sariyya Sif al-Bahr, 623 CE) was led by Hamza according to the standard account.
r: Some narrations credit Ubaydah ibn al-Harith. Note: Slight disagreement in sources; Hamza is the standard answer.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'curious'?
f: Curious means eager to learn; inquisitive means the same.
r: Interested and eager are also close.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'captious'?
f: Captious means tending to find fault over trivial matters.
r: Hypercritical and censorious are synonyms.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'cynical'?
f: A cynic believes people act only from selfish motives, so is distrustful or skeptical.
r: Antonym: optimistic. Note: Source listed misanthropic, moody, eccentric, which are loose; 'distrustful' is the standard meaning.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'spurn'?
f: To spurn is to reject with disdain.
r: Scorn and disdain are close synonyms.

q: Which word is the opposite of 'coherent' (source wrote 'doherent')?
f: Incoherent or disjointed is the antonym of coherent.
r: Cohesive means holding together.

q: In what year was the Lahore Resolution adopted?
f: The resolution was passed on 23 March 1940 at Minar-e-Pakistan grounds (Iqbal Park), Lahore.
r: Pakistan Day is on 23 March.

q: Who moved (presented) the Lahore Resolution in 1940? (2)
f: Sher-e-Bangal A.K. Fazlul Huq moved the resolution.
r: Chaudhry Khaliquzzaman seconded it.

q: Which country won the football World Cup in 2022? (3)
f: Argentina beat France on penalties in Qatar in December 2022.
r: Spain won the 2026 edition.

q: What is the capital of Argentina?
f: Buenos Aires is Argentina's capital.
r: It lies on the Rio de la Plata.

q: Which is the highest volcano in the world?
f: Ojos del Salado on the Argentina-Chile border is the highest active volcano at about 6,893 m.
r: Kilimanjaro is the highest in Africa.

q: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'? (2)
f: Japan's name 'Nippon' means 'origin of the sun'.
r: Its capital is Tokyo.

q: What is the name of Japan's parliament?
f: Japan's parliament is the National Diet (Kokkai).
r: It has two houses: House of Representatives and House of Councillors.

q: Where is the world's longest railway tunnel located?
f: The Gotthard Base Tunnel (about 57 km) is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
r: The Seikan Tunnel in Japan (about 54 km) is the longest with an undersea section.

q: When was NATO established?
f: NATO was founded by the Washington Treaty on 4 April 1949.
r: It started with 12 members.

q: When was the OIC formed?
f: The OIC was formed on 25 September 1969 after the Al-Aqsa arson in Jerusalem.
r: It was renamed Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in 2011; HQ is Jeddah.

q: When did Pakistan join the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)?
f: Pakistan was a founding member at the first conference in Rabat in September 1969.
r: The second summit was held in Lahore in 1974.

q: The current UN Secretary-General (António Guterres) is from which country?
f: Guterres, from Portugal, has served since 2017; his term ends 31 December 2026.
r: His successor is being selected in 2026.

q: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have? (3)
f: The five permanent members are the USA, Russia, China, UK and France.
r: There are 10 non-permanent members.

q: Which is the correct spelling of the word meaning 'rash, hasty'?
f: The correct spelling is 'impetuous'.
r: Impetuous means acting quickly without thought.

q: The length of the Pak-China border is about
f: The standard exam value for the Pak-China border is 595 km.
r: It crosses at Khunjerab Pass.

q: 'Safiullah' (chosen of Allah) is the title of which prophet?
f: Adam (AS) is called Safiullah.
r: Nuh is Najiullah; Ibrahim is Khalilullah; Musa is Kalimullah.

q: On which date did India conduct its first nuclear test? (2)
f: India's first test, 'Smiling Buddha', was at Pokhran on 18 May 1974.
r: India's later tests were in May 1998.

q: Which organisation works to prevent nuclear proliferation and promote safe nuclear energy, founded in 1957?
f: The International Atomic Energy Agency was founded in 1957.
r: Its HQ is in Vienna.

q: Who was the second Governor General of Pakistan?
f: Nazimuddin succeeded Jinnah in September 1948.
r: Ghulam Muhammad dismissed him as PM in 1953.

q: Who was the first Governor General of Pakistan? (2)
f: Jinnah took the oath on 15 August 1947.
r: He died on 11 September 1948.

q: The Shah Jahan Mosque is located in
f: Shah Jahan Mosque is in Thatta, Sindh, built about 1647.
r: It is famous for its brick and tile work and a UNESCO site.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'might'?
f: Might means great strength or power.
r: Puissance and force are synonyms.

q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'exigency'?
f: Exigency means an urgent need or emergency.
r: Distress and urgency are close.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency?
f: The IAEA is headquartered in Vienna.
r: It was set up in 1957.

q: The Tashkent Declaration was signed after which war?
f: The agreement was signed on 10 January 1966 to end the 1965 war.
r: Signed by Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri.

q: The Khilafat Movement started after which war?
f: It began about 1919 to save the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.
r: Leaders: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Shaukat Ali.

q: What is the sum of supplementary angles?
f: Two angles are supplementary if they add up to 180 degrees.
r: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees.

q: In which year was the British East India Company founded (arrived) in the subcontinent era?
f: The company received its royal charter on 31 December 1600.
r: It ruled India after the Battle of Plassey 1757 until 1858.

q: The 'Black Flag' (Abbasid) revolution started from which region?
f: The Abbasid revolution (747 CE) started in Khurasan under Abu Muslim and used black flags.
r: It ended Umayyad rule in 750.

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed? (4)
f: Abu Jahl was killed at Badr in 624 CE.
r: Badr was the first major battle of Islam.

q: Which Indian Prime Minister signed the Indus Waters Treaty (1960) with Pakistan's President Ayub Khan?
f: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the treaty in Karachi on 19 September 1960.
r: India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025.

q: What is the factorial of 1?
f: 1! equals 1.
r: 0! also equals 1.

q: The book 'Hayat-e-Javed' was written by (2)
f: Hali wrote Hayat-e-Javed, the biography of Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.
r: Hali also wrote Musaddas-e-Hali.

q: Pakistan's largest export group is
f: Textiles and apparel make about 60% of Pakistan's exports (USD 17.93 billion in FY2025-26).
r: Knitwear, bedwear and readymade garments lead.

q: What is the full form of LOC?
f: LoC is the military control line in Kashmir since 1972 (Simla Agreement).
r: It is about 740 km long.

q: Which is the longest river of Pakistan? (3)
f: The Indus (about 3,180 km) is Pakistan's longest and largest river.
r: It starts from Tibet near Lake Mansarovar and falls in the Arabian Sea.

q: In which province is Keenjhar Lake located?
f: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake is in Thatta district, Sindh.
r: It supplies drinking water to Karachi.

q: Which Chinese city lies close to the Pakistan border (near the Khunjerab Pass route)?
f: Kashgar in Xinjiang is the Chinese city nearest to the Pakistan border and the Karakoram Highway.
r: The Karakoram Highway links Kashgar (China) with Hasan Abdal (Pakistan). Khunjerab Pass (4,693 m) is the border crossing.

q: Which language did Sher Shah Suri speak?
f: Sher Shah Suri was a Pashtun (Sur tribe) and Pashto was his mother tongue.
r: He defeated Humayun in 1540 and built the Grand Trunk Road. He also used Persian for administration. Note: He also used Persian and Hindavi; standard exam answer is Pashto.

q: The Thar Desert in Pakistan is located in which province?
f: Pakistan's part of the Thar Desert lies in southeastern Sindh (Tharparkar district).
r: Cholistan is the desert in Punjab. Thar is among the largest subtropical deserts.

q: Who is the founder of Facebook? (4)
f: Mark Zuckerberg founded Facebook in 2004 with college friends at Harvard.
r: Facebook's parent company was renamed Meta in 2021.

q: Thomas Edison invented which of these?
f: Thomas Edison developed the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb in 1879.
r: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone. Edison also invented the phonograph.

q: How many rectangular side faces does a hexagonal prism have? (2)
f: A hexagonal prism has a hexagon base, so it has 6 rectangular side faces (8 faces in total).
r: A triangular prism has 3 side faces and 5 faces in total.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar to which city? (2)
f: Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan to Kabul in Afghanistan.
r: It is about 53 km long and passes through the Safed Koh range.

q: Who are the current Chief Ministers of Punjab and Sindh (Pakistan)?
o: Maryam Nawaz and Murad Ali Shah
Shehbaz Sharif and Murad Ali Shah
Usman Buzdar and Syed Qaim Ali Shah
f: As of Oct 2026, Maryam Nawaz is Punjab CM (since Feb 2024) and Murad Ali Shah is Sindh CM.
r: Maryam Nawaz is the first female CM of Punjab. Murad Ali Shah (PPP) has been Sindh CM since 2016.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi romance 'Sohni Mahiwal'? (2)
f: The popular Punjabi version of Sohni Mahiwal was written by Fazal Shah Sayyad.
r: Waris Shah wrote Heer Ranjha. Sohni Mahiwal is one of the Punjabi/Sindhi folk romances.

q: World War II began on which date?
f: WWII began when Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939.
r: Britain and France declared war on Germany on 3 September 1939. WWII ended in 1945.

q: A black horse is a sign of what in common saying?
f: In common belief, as in the source, a black horse is taken as a sign of good luck and strength.
r: In some traditions (the Bible, Revelation) a black horse stands for famine. Note: Symbol meaning depends on culture; source answer 'good luck' kept.

q: Which is the hottest planet in the solar system?
f: Venus has a thick CO2 atmosphere causing a runaway greenhouse effect, with about 465 C surface temperature.
r: Mercury is the closest to the Sun but cooler than Venus.

q: The process in which a gas changes directly into a liquid is called?
f: Condensation is the change of gas/vapour to liquid by cooling.
r: Direct solid to gas is sublimation. Gas directly to solid is deposition.

q: Who is credited with inventing the first electric motor (1821 demonstration)? (3)
f: Faraday demonstrated the first electromagnetic rotation device in 1821, the basis of the electric motor.
r: Tesla invented the practical AC induction motor in 1887. Note: Others (Jedlik, Davenport) are also credited; Faraday is the standard exam answer.

q: The process by which plants release water vapour into the atmosphere is called?
f: Transpiration is loss of water vapour through the stomata of leaves.
r: Stomata are opened and closed by guard cells.

q: The Babusar Pass connects which two areas?
f: Babusar Pass (4,173 m) links the Kaghan Valley (Mansehra) with Chilas in Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: It is a shorter route to Gilgit than the Karakoram Highway from Abbottabad.

q: Which is the largest dam in the world by installed power capacity?
f: As of Oct 2026 Three Gorges Dam (about 22,500 MW) is still the largest operating plant by installed capacity.
r: China's Medog (Yarlung Tsangpo) project, about 60,000 MW, began construction in July 2025 and is planned for about 2033.

q: The 2023 G20 summit was held in which city?
f: The 18th G20 summit was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 9-10 September 2023.
r: The 2022 summit was in Bali; the African Union became a permanent G20 member in 2023.

q: Choose the correct word: 'There ____ a computer on the table.'
f: 'Computer' is singular, so the singular verb 'is' is used with 'There'.
r: Use 'there are' with plural nouns.

q: What is the border line between Pakistan and Afghanistan called? (3)
f: The Durand Line is the 2,640 km border between Pakistan and Afghanistan, drawn in 1893.
r: The Radcliffe Line separates Pakistan and India; the McMahon Line is India-China.

q: K2 is in which mountain range?
f: K2 lies in the Karakoram Range on the Pakistan-China border.
r: K2 is the second highest mountain in the world.

q: The Salt Range (with the Khewra salt mine) is located in which province of Pakistan?
f: The Salt Range lies in northern Punjab, famous for the Khewra Salt Mine in Jhelum district.
r: Khewra is among the world's oldest and largest salt mines.

q: Bulleh Shah was a poet of which language?
f: Bulleh Shah (1680-1757) was a Sufi poet who wrote in Punjabi (kafis).
r: His shrine is in Kasur.

q: Rehman Baba wrote poetry in which language?
f: Rehman Baba (1650-1715) was a Sufi poet of Pashto, buried near Peshawar.
r: He is known as the Nightingale of Pashto.

q: NATO was established in which year? (2)
f: NATO was formed on 4 April 1949 by the Washington Treaty.
r: The Warsaw Pact (1955) was the Soviet bloc's response.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Shaheen-III missile?
f: Shaheen-III is a medium-range ballistic missile with a range of about 2,750 km.
r: Shaheen-I is about 750 km and Shaheen-II about 1,500 km.

q: Pakistan played its first ever Test cricket match against which country?
f: Pakistan's first Test was against India in Delhi in October 1952.
r: Pakistan became a Test nation in 1952.

q: Who became the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan?
f: Justice Ayesha Malik was elevated to the Supreme Court in January 2022 as its first woman judge.
r: She earlier served on the Lahore High Court.

q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place? (2)
f: The Chauri Chaura incident occurred on 4 February 1922, after which Gandhi ended the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: Gandhi suspended the movement on 12 February 1922.

q: On which cities was the atom bomb first used in history?
f: The USA dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima (6 Aug 1945) and Nagasaki (9 Aug 1945).
r: Japan surrendered on 15 August 1945.

q: What is the real name of Imam Bukhari?
f: Imam Bukhari's full name was Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari.
r: His collection is Sahih al-Bukhari.

q: Which city is known as the 'City of Gardens' in Pakistan?
f: Lahore is called the City of Gardens because of its Mughal and colonial gardens such as Shalimar Bagh.
r: Lahore is also known as the cultural capital of Pakistan.

q: Who is the President of Pakistan (head of Parliament)?
f: As of Oct 2026, Asif Ali Zardari is the 14th President of Pakistan (since March 2024).
r: The President is part of Parliament along with the National Assembly and Senate.

q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
f: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of temperature.
r: 0 K is absolute zero, about -273.15 C.

q: In which district is Rohtas Fort located? (3)
f: Rohtas Fort was built by Sher Shah Suri near Jhelum, Punjab.
r: It is a UNESCO World Heritage site (1997).

q: Who received an honorary British knighthood in 1988?
f: Caspar Weinberger, former US Defence Secretary, was given an honorary knighthood by Queen Elizabeth II (honorary GBE).
r: He served as US Secretary of Defense from 1981 to 1987.

q: Who is the President of China? (4)
f: As of Oct 2026, Xi Jinping is President (since 2013), and also CCP General Secretary.
r: Li Qiang is the Premier. Hu Jintao was President before Xi.

q: The 'Hero' award is the highest military honour of which country?
f: 'Hero of the DPRK' is North Korea's highest title for heroic military and national service.
r: Pakistan's highest gallantry award is Nishan-e-Haider.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Court of Justice?
f: The ICJ sits in the Peace Palace at The Hague, Netherlands.
r: It is the principal judicial organ of the UN.

q: In which year did the Kargil War take place? (2)
f: The Kargil conflict between India and Pakistan was fought in May-July 1999.
r: It took place in Kargil, Ladakh.

q: Where is the headquarters of the UN human rights office (OHCHR / Human Rights Council)?
f: The UN Human Rights Council and OHCHR are based in Geneva.
r: UN headquarters itself is in New York.

q: In which year did Major Aziz Bhatti receive the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was martyred at the Burki sector (Lahore front) in the 1965 war and awarded the Nishan-e-Haider.
r: Pakistan's first Nishan-e-Haider recipient was Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar (1948).

q: Which country is the largest tea producer in the world? (2)
f: China produces the most tea, followed by India.
r: Kenya is a major tea exporter.

q: What does the white colour in Pakistan's flag represent?
f: The white stripe stands for religious minorities; the green is for the Muslim majority.
r: The crescent shows progress and the star light and knowledge.

q: Which is the biggest bird in the world by size?
f: The ostrich is the largest living bird, up to 2.7 m tall.
r: Ostrich eggs are the largest of any living bird.

q: In which battle was Hazrat Hamza (RA) martyred? (2)
f: Hazrat Hamza was martyred at Uhud in 3 AH (625 CE).
r: He is known as Asadullah (Lion of Allah).

q: How many bones are there in the adult human body?
f: An adult human body has 206 bones.
r: A baby is born with about 300 bones, many of which fuse.

q: Which is the first group of the periodic table?
f: Group 1 (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr) are the alkali metals.
r: Group 17 is halogens; Group 18 is noble gases.

q: Which Pakistani player has taken the most Test wickets? (3)
f: Wasim Akram took 414 Test wickets, the most for Pakistan.
r: He also holds many ODI records for Pakistan.

q: Mohenjo-daro is located in which district of Sindh? (2)
f: Mohenjo-daro is in Larkana district, on the Indus River.
r: It is a UNESCO World Heritage site (1980).

q: Who wrote the book 'Friends Not Masters'? (4)
f: Ayub Khan wrote it as his political autobiography in 1967.
r: Ayub Khan ruled Pakistan 1958-1969.

q: In which year did Pakistan's Parliament declare Ahmadis non-Muslim through a constitutional amendment?
f: The Second Amendment to the 1973 Constitution (7 September 1974) declared Ahmadis non-Muslim.
r: It was passed under PM Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

q: What was Fatima Jinnah's profession? (2)
f: Fatima Jinnah trained and practised as a dentist in Calcutta.
r: She is known as Madar-e-Millat.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the Cricket World Cup? (2)
f: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup under Imran Khan, beating England in Melbourne.
r: Pakistan also won the 2009 T20 World Cup.

q: Who coined the name 'Pakistan'?
f: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali coined 'Pakistan' in the 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never'.
r: He studied at Cambridge.

q: Which is the fastest bird in the world? (3)
f: A peregrine falcon can dive at over 320 km/h.
r: The ostrich is the fastest bird on land.

q: Which country is the second largest gold producer in the world (as of 2025)?
f: Russia ranks second after China in 2025 gold mine output.
r: China is first; Australia is third.

q: How many Pakistanis have won a Nobel Prize?
f: Abdul Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014) are the two Nobel laureates of Pakistan.
r: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate.

q: Who received the first Nobel Peace Prize (1901)?
f: Henry Dunant (with Frederic Passy) won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.
r: Dunant founded the Red Cross.

q: For what did Malala Yousafzai win the Nobel Prize?
f: Malala shared the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize for her struggle for girls' education.
r: She shared it with Kailash Satyarthi.

q: What is the capital of Turkey? (4)
f: Ankara has been Turkey's capital since 1923.
r: Istanbul is the largest city.

q: Where were the 2016 Olympic Games held?
f: The 2016 Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
r: London hosted in 2012; Tokyo in 2021.

q: Which latitude and longitude passes through the central point of Pakistan (approx)?
f: Pakistan lies roughly between 24-37 N latitude and 61-75 E longitude, so its centre is about 30 N 70 E.
r: Pakistan lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres.

q: What is the range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile? (2)
f: Ababeel is a MIRV-capable ballistic missile with a range of about 2,200 km.
r: It was first tested in January 2017.

q: Which is the lowest place on land on Earth?
f: The Dead Sea shore is about 430 m below sea level.
r: Death Valley is the lowest in North America.

q: Which country has a sea border with Pakistan but no land border?
f: Pakistan and Oman share a maritime boundary in the Arabian Sea only.
r: Pakistan's land neighbours: India, Afghanistan, Iran and China.

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Champions Trophy? (2)
f: Pakistan beat India in the 2017 final at The Oval.
r: Sarfaraz Ahmed was captain.

q: In which year was the Durand Line agreed?
f: Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman signed the agreement in 1893.
r: It is about 2,640 km long.

q: Who is the author of the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'?
f: It is a collection of speeches by Liaquat Ali Khan (1950).
r: Liaquat was Pakistan's first Prime Minister.

q: As Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan made a historic 1950 visit to which country?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 on an invitation from President Truman.
r: He never visited Moscow despite an invitation. Note: Question reworded; 'first visit' is disputed (an Iran trip in 1949 is reported), USA kept as exam answer.

q: What is the currency of Japan?
f: The currency of Japan is the yen.
r: The yuan is China's currency.

q: What is the capital of Australia? (2)
f: Canberra is the capital of Australia.
r: Sydney is the largest city.

q: In which year was Dr Abdus Salam awarded the Nobel Prize?
f: Dr Abdus Salam shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics.
r: He shared it with Glashow and Weinberg for electroweak theory.

q: When did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations? (3)
f: Pakistan joined the UN on 30 September 1947.
r: As of Oct 2026 the UN has 193 members and its HQ is in New York.

q: What is the national vegetable of Pakistan? (2)
f: Okra is listed as Pakistan's national vegetable in common exam lists.
r: The national fruit is the mango; national flower is jasmine.

q: Sher Shah Suri belonged to which ethnic group? (2)
f: Sher Shah Suri was a Pashtun from the Sur tribe.
r: He founded the Sur Empire.

q: NASA is the space agency of which country?
f: NASA is the National Aeronautics and Space Administration of the USA.
r: Russia has Roscosmos; India has ISRO.

q: In which year did Pakistan play its first Test match? (2)
f: Pakistan played its first Test against India at Delhi in October 1952.
r: Pakistan's first Test win came at Lucknow in the same 1952-53 tour. Pakistan became a Test nation in 1952.

q: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan guarantees freedom of speech?
f: Article 19 gives every citizen freedom of speech and expression, subject to reasonable restrictions.
r: Article 19A gives the right to information. Article 17 is freedom of association.

q: Which Article of the Constitution of Pakistan provides the right to free and compulsory education?
f: Article 25A (added by the 18th Amendment, 2010) gives free and compulsory education to children aged 5 to 16.
r: The 18th Amendment was passed in April 2010. Article 22 deals with educational institutions. Note: Source says 'freedom of education'; the standard exam answer is the right to education, Article 25A.

q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is still standing today?
f: The Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is the only ancient wonder that still exists.
r: It was built for Pharaoh Khufu about 2560 BC. The Colossus and Lighthouse were destroyed by earthquakes.

q: Who proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system (Sun at the centre)?
f: Copernicus published his Sun-centred model in 1543 in 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium'.
r: Kepler later described elliptical orbits. Galileo supported the model with telescope evidence.

q: What is the currency of Denmark? (2)
f: Denmark uses the Danish krone (DKK) and not the euro.
r: Sweden uses the krona and Norway uses its own krone.

q: Syed Abul A'la Maududi, founder of Jamaat-e-Islami, died in which city?
f: Maududi died on 22 September 1979 in Buffalo, New York, USA, while receiving medical treatment.
r: He is buried in Lahore. His famous work is the Tafheem-ul-Quran.

q: On which date did the British first arrive in the subcontinent (ship Hector landing at Surat)?
f: Captain William Hawkins arrived at Surat on the ship Hector on 24 August 1608.
r: The East India Company was founded on 31 December 1600. Sir Thomas Roe reached Jahangir's court in 1615.

q: What is Pakistan's rank in the world by population? (4)
f: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country, after India, China, USA and Indonesia.
r: The 2023 census counted 241.49 million people. Pakistan is about to pass Indonesia in some estimates.

q: What is the term of a Senator in Pakistan? (2)
f: Senators are elected for 6 years; half retire every 3 years.
r: The Senate is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved. The Senate has 96 members.

q: In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his Allahabad Address? (3)
f: Iqbal presented the idea of a separate Muslim state in North-West India at the Muslim League session in Allahabad in December 1930.
r: The Lahore Resolution came in 1940. Iqbal was the Muslim League president in 1930.

q: Abdur Rahman Chughtai was a famous?
f: Abdur Rahman Chughtai (1894-1975) was a Pakistani painter known for Mughal and Islamic style art.
r: He designed the Pakistan Postal Stamps and Muraqqa-e-Chughtai. He was awarded Hilal-e-Imtiaz.

q: Which mountain range lies in the north-west of Pakistan?
f: The Hindu Kush range runs along north-west Pakistan (Chitral) into Afghanistan.
r: Tirich Mir (7,708 m) is its highest peak. The Karakoram lies in the north.

q: In which region of the world is Pakistan located?
f: Pakistan lies in South Asia, bordering India, Afghanistan, Iran and China.
r: Pakistan became a member of SAARC in 1985. Its capital is Islamabad.

q: Liaqat Ali Khan made his first state visit to which country in 1950?
f: He visited the USA in May 1950 after getting invitations from both the USSR and the USA.
r: This visit set Pakistan on a pro-West foreign policy. He addressed the US Congress.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah join the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah joined the Congress in 1906 and attended the Calcutta session as Dadabhai Naoroji's secretary.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913. He left the Congress in 1920.

q: In which province of Pakistan is the Kharan Desert located?
f: The Kharan Desert lies in Kharan district of Balochistan; the first nuclear tests were near Chagai.
r: Pakistan's other deserts are Thar (Sindh), Thal and Cholistan (Punjab).

q: In which year was the first Cricket World Cup held?
f: The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975; West Indies won.
r: Pakistan won the World Cup in 1992 under Imran Khan. Lord's hosted the 1975 final.

q: Who is the highest wicket-taker for the Pakistan cricket team?
f: Wasim Akram took 916 international wickets (414 Test, 502 ODI), the most for Pakistan.
r: He is called the Sultan of Swing. Waqar Younis is second among fast bowlers.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan die?
f: Sir Syed died on 27 March 1898 at Aligarh.
r: He founded the Aligarh Muslim University (MAO College in 1875). He was born in 1817.

q: On which date did East Pakistan separate to become Bangladesh?
f: Pakistan's army surrendered in Dhaka on 16 December 1971 and Bangladesh came into being.
r: Bangladesh declared independence on 26 March 1971. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman led the Awami League.

q: What was Pakistan's total population in the 2023 census?
f: The 7th Population and Housing Census (2023) counted 241.49 million people.
r: The 2017 census counted 207.68 million. The census is digital for the first time in 2023.

q: What was Allama Iqbal's first Persian book of poetry?
f: Asrar-e-Khudi was published in 1915 as Iqbal's first Persian poetry book.
r: Iqbal's first book overall was Ilm-ul-Iqtisad (1903) on economics. Bang-e-Dara (1924) was his first Urdu poetry book.

q: Which sea separates Morocco (Africa) from Europe?
f: Morocco faces Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar, which joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic.
r: The Strait of Gibraltar is only about 14 km wide at its narrowest. Morocco's capital is Rabat.

q: In which year did India conduct its nuclear tests at Pokhran that led to Pakistan's tests?
f: India conducted Pokhran-II tests on 11 and 13 May 1998; Pakistan answered on 28 May 1998.
r: India's first test (Smiling Buddha) was in 1974. Pakistan celebrates 28 May as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: KANUPP (Karachi Nuclear Power Plant) was built with the help of which country?
f: KANUPP-1 was a CANDU reactor supplied by Canada and started in 1972.
r: Pakistan's first nuclear power plant. Chashma plants were built with Chinese help.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh? (3)
f: Murad Ali Shah (PPP) was elected CM of Sindh for a 3rd term on 26 February 2024.
r: He first became CM in 2016 after Qaim Ali Shah. Karachi is Sindh's capital.

q: Which is the longest river in the world (traditional measurement)? (2)
f: The Nile (about 6,650 km) is traditionally taken as the longest river.
r: The Amazon carries the most water. Some studies claim the Amazon is longer. Note: 'Largest' is ambiguous; standard exam answer is Nile (longest).

q: What is the value of sin 0 degrees?
f: On the unit circle, the y-coordinate at 0 degrees is 0, so sin 0 = 0.
r: cos 0 = 1. sin 90 = 1.

q: Who gave the idea of SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation)?
f: Bangladesh President Ziaur Rahman proposed regional cooperation in 1977-80, leading to SAARC in 1985.
r: SAARC was founded in Dhaka on 8 December 1985. Its secretariat is in Kathmandu.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world? (2)
f: Lake Baikal in Russia is about 1,642 m deep, the deepest lake.
r: It holds about 20 percent of the world's fresh surface water. It is also the oldest lake.

q: In which country was the G-20 summit of 2023 held? (2)
f: The 2023 G20 summit was held in New Delhi on 9-10 September 2023.
r: Indonesia hosted in 2022 and Brazil in 2024. The African Union joined as a permanent member in 2023.

q: Which is considered the world's oldest sport?
f: Wrestling is commonly called the oldest sport, shown in cave paintings about 15,000 years old.
r: Wrestling was in the ancient Olympic Games from 708 BC. Note: Opinion-based; wrestling is the standard exam answer.

q: What is the approximate value of the square root of 14?
f: 3.74 squared is about 13.99, so the square root of 14 is about 3.74.
r: The square root of 16 is 4. The square root of 9 is 3.

q: Muhammad Ali, the legendary boxer, belonged to which country?
f: Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight champion.
r: He won gold at the 1960 Rome Olympics. He was called 'The Greatest'.

q: Major Aziz Bhatti was martyred in which war?
f: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti was killed on 12 September 1965 at the BRB Canal in Lahore sector.
r: He received the Nishan-e-Haider. He belonged to the 17 Punjab Regiment.

q: What does OS stand for in computing?
f: OS means operating system, the main software that runs a computer.
r: Examples are Windows, Linux and Android. DOS means Disk Operating System.

q: Which is considered the oldest seaport of Pakistan?
f: Karachi Port (opened 1887 in modern form) is Pakistan's oldest and busiest seaport.
r: Port Qasim was built in 1980s. Gwadar is a deep sea port in Balochistan. Note: Ancient ports like Banbhore also existed; Karachi is the standard exam answer.

q: Which symbol denotes the union of sets?
f: The symbol ∪ is read 'union' and joins all elements of both sets.
r: ∩ means intersection. ⊂ means subset.

q: How many member states does the OIC have? (2)
f: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation has 57 member states.
r: Its headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. It was founded in 1969.

q: In which Constitution of Pakistan were Islamic provisions first added?
f: The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic and included Islamic provisions.
r: The 1973 Constitution also made Islam the state religion. The 1962 Constitution first dropped 'Islamic' from the name.

q: In which city is the National Library of Pakistan located? (2)
f: The National Library of Pakistan is in Islamabad, on Constitution Avenue.
r: It was established in 1993. The Quaid-e-Azam Library is in Lahore.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank (ADB)?
f: ADB is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, Philippines.
r: ADB was founded in 1966. Japan and the USA are its largest shareholders.

q: Complete the common trivia: 'Bats cannot ___, snakes cannot ___.'
f: This is the common folk statement in the source: bats cannot see and snakes cannot hear.
r: Real science: bats can see and also use echolocation; snakes have no outer ear and sense ground vibrations.

q: The name 'India' and the word 'Hindu' come from which river?
f: Persians and Greeks pronounced Sindhu as Hindu/Indus; the Indus gave India its name.
r: The Indus is called Sindhu in Sanskrit. The Indus Valley Civilization grew along it.

q: In which city were the Round Table Conferences (1930-32) held?
f: Three Round Table Conferences were held in London between 1930 and 1932.
r: Allama Iqbal attended the 2nd conference. Jinnah had also attended the first.

q: Which city is called the 'Golden Gate of the World'?
f: San Francisco is known for the Golden Gate Strait and the Golden Gate Bridge.
r: The bridge opened in 1937. The city is in California.

q: What does 'Mohenjo-daro' mean?
f: In Sindhi, Mohenjo-daro means 'Mound of the Dead'.
r: The Indus Valley city dates to about 2500 BC. It is in Larkana, Sindh.

q: Who is the Supreme Commander of the Pakistan Armed Forces under the Constitution?
f: As of Oct 2026, the President is traditionally called Supreme Commander of the armed forces, but Article 243 gives control and command to the Federal Government; the 27th Amendment (Nov 2025) created the Chief of Defence Forces (Field Marshal Asim Munir).
r: The President appoints the army chief/CDF on the Prime Minister's advice.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
f: Sarfraz Bugti (PPP) has been CM since March 2024.
r: Quetta is the provincial capital. Bugti was elected unopposed.

q: Sher Shah Suri was a famous?
o: Ruler (Afghan emperor of the Sur dynasty)
f: Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun and ruled North India from 1540 to 1545.
r: He built the Grand Trunk Road and introduced the rupee.

q: Which is the largest district of Pakistan by area?
f: Chagai in Balochistan is the largest district, over 50,000 sq km.
r: Pakistan's nuclear tests were held at Chagai hills in 1998. Balochistan is the largest province.

q: How many faces does a pentagonal prism have?
f: A pentagonal prism has 5 rectangular side faces and 2 pentagonal bases, so 7 faces.
r: It has 15 edges and 10 vertices. A cuboid has 6 faces.

q: Which country lies to the east of Pakistan? (2)
f: India borders Pakistan on the east.
r: Iran is west, Afghanistan is west/north-west and China is north-east.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa as of October 2026?
o: No elected CM (Governor's rule since 11 October 2026)
f: KP has been under governor's rule since 11 October 2026, run by Governor Faisal Karim Kundi.
r: Sohail Afridi was CM from October 2025. Governor's rule is imposed under Article 234.

q: How many flat circular faces does a cylinder have?
f: A cylinder has two flat circular faces (top and bottom) and one curved surface.
r: A sphere has no flat face. A cone has one flat circular face.

q: Which is the deepest river in the world? (2)
f: The Congo River in Africa is over 220 m deep.
r: It is also Africa's second longest river. It crosses the equator twice.

q: Which prophet was swallowed by a fish (whale)? (3)
f: The Quran tells that Hazrat Yunus (AS) was swallowed by a big fish.
r: He is also called Dhun-Nun and Sahib al-Hut. Surah Yunus (10) is named after him.

q: Which is the smallest surah of the Holy Quran? (2)
f: Al-Kawthar (Surah 108) has only 3 verses and about 10 words.
r: Al-Baqarah is the longest surah. Al-Asr and An-Nasr also have 3 verses but are longer.

q: What is the value of sin 180 degrees?
f: On the unit circle, the y-coordinate at 180 degrees is 0.

q: What is the capital of Russia?
f: Moscow is Russia's capital and largest city.
r: St Petersburg was the capital in imperial times. The Kremlin is in Moscow.

q: Which is the national bird of Pakistan? (4)
f: The Chukar partridge is Pakistan's national bird.
r: The Markhor is the national animal. The Jasmine is the national flower.

q: What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-Iran border?
f: The Pakistan-Iran border is about 909 km long, between Balochistan and Sistan-Baluchestan.
r: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line) is about 2,640 km. Pakistan-India is about 3,323 km. Note: Source says 904 km; sources vary (905-959 km); 909 km is the most cited.

q: In which country is the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
f: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is in Pisa, Italy.
r: It began leaning during construction in the 12th century. It is a bell tower.

q: In which city is the Jinnah Bridge located?
f: Jinnah Bridge connects Karachi's city to Keamari and the port.
r: Karachi is Sindh's capital. Quaid's mausoleum is also in Karachi.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization (WHO)? (2)
f: WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
r: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948. The UN is headquartered in New York.

q: What is the currency of Canada?
f: Canada uses the Canadian dollar (CAD).
r: Ottawa is the capital. Its coin is nicknamed the 'loonie'.

q: Which is the highest polo ground in Pakistan?
f: The Shandur Polo Ground (about 3,700 m) is the highest polo ground in the world.
r: Shandur hosts the Shandur Polo Festival between Chitral and Gilgit teams.

q: In which year was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan? (2)
f: President Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958, then Ayub Khan took over.
r: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated. Zia imposed martial law in 1977.

q: Who was the last confirmed US ambassador to Pakistan?
f: Donald Blome served as US ambassador to Pakistan from 2022 until January 2025.
r: Natalie Baker became chargé d'affaires after him.

q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan? (3)
f: Gilgit is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: K2 lies in Gilgit-Baltistan. It was given provincial-like status in 2009.

q: How many plane faces does a rectangular prism (cuboid) have? (4)
f: A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.
r: A triangular prism has 5 faces.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points? (2)
f: Jinnah gave the Fourteen Points in March 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report.
r: The Fourteen Points demanded separate electorates and one-third seats for Muslims at the centre.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of the Muslim world?
f: Benazir Bhutto became Pakistan's PM in December 1988, the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country.
r: She was PM twice (1988-90, 1993-96). She was assassinated on 27 December 2007.

q: In which year was SEATO (South-East Asia Treaty Organization) founded?
f: SEATO was formed on 8 September 1954 by the Manila Pact.
r: Pakistan joined SEATO and CENTO. SEATO was dissolved in 1977.

q: How many articles did the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan have?
f: The 1962 Constitution had 250 articles, 12 schedules and 5 parts.
r: The 1973 Constitution has 280 articles. The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles.

q: Harappa, the Indus Valley site, is located about 20 km from which city?
f: Harappa is in Punjab, about 20 km west of Sahiwal city.
r: Harappa was discovered in 1920-21. Mohenjo-daro in Sindh is the other major Indus Valley site.

q: The German-Pakistani doctor Ruth Pfau devoted her life in Pakistan to treating which disease?
f: Dr. Ruth Pfau worked for leprosy patients in Karachi from 1960 and set up the Marie Adelaide Leprosy Centre.
r: She got a state funeral in Pakistan in 2017. Pakistan was declared leprosy-controlled by WHO in 1996.

q: What is the tenure (term) of a member of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: An NA member is elected for five years unless the Assembly is dissolved earlier.
r: Senate members serve 6 years. The President is elected for 5 years.

q: Who acts as the President of Pakistan in his absence?
f: Under Article 49 of the Constitution, the Chairman Senate acts as President when the President is absent or unable to work.
r: If the Chairman Senate is also unavailable, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts.

q: The Regional Cooperation for Development (RCD) was renamed as which organization?
f: RCD (Pakistan, Iran, Turkey) was revived and renamed ECO in 1985.
r: ECO headquarters is in Tehran. ECO now has 10 member states.

q: In which province is the proposed Kalabagh Dam site?
f: The Kalabagh dam site is on the Indus near Kalabagh in Mianwali district, Punjab.
r: The dam has not been built because of political disagreement among provinces. It is near the border with KP.

q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia? (3)
f: The Saudi riyal (SAR) is the official currency.
r: The UAE uses the dirham. Kuwait uses the dinar.

q: What is the capital of Indonesia?
f: As of Oct 2026, Jakarta is still the legal capital because no presidential decree has moved the status.
r: Nusantara on Borneo is being built as the new capital and is planned as political capital around 2028.

q: How many districts does Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have?
f: As of late 2025 listings, KP has 40 districts in seven divisions.
r: KP had about 35-36 districts before recent new districts were created. Peshawar is the capital. Note: Source says 36 which is an older count; recent listing (Wikipedia, Oct 2025) says 40. Counts vary by source.

q: Who wrote the novel 'Raja Gidh'?
f: Raja Gidh (1981) is the famous Urdu novel by Bano Qudsia.
r: Her husband Ashfaq Ahmed was also a writer. She received Sitara-e-Imtiaz and Hilal-e-Imtiaz.

q: The shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam is in which city?
f: Shah Rukn-e-Alam's tomb is in Multan and is a Tughlaq-era monument.
r: Multan is called the City of Saints. Baba Farid's shrine is in Pakpattan.

q: The Constitution of 1962 was approved during the rule of which leader?
f: Field Marshal Ayub Khan gave the 1962 Constitution, which had a presidential system.
r: It came into force on 8 June 1962. It was abrogated in 1969.

q: Tarbela Dam construction began during the rule of which leader?
f: Work on Tarbela started in 1968 under Ayub Khan after the Indus Waters Treaty.
r: It was completed in 1974 under Bhutto. It is on the Indus in Haripur district, KP. Note: Dam was started under Ayub (1968) and finished under Bhutto (1974); standard answer is Ayub Khan.

q: Humayun was the son of which Mughal emperor?
f: Humayun, second Mughal emperor, was the eldest son of Babur.
r: Humayun's son was Akbar. Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun in 1540.

q: At which port city did the British first land/settle in the Indian sub-continent?
f: The English East India Company first set up a trading post at Surat; Captain Hawkins arrived in 1608.
r: The Company was formed in 1600. Calcutta was founded by Job Charnock in 1690.

q: The Indian sub-continent lies in which continent?
f: The sub-continent (Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, etc.) lies in South Asia, part of Asia.
r: Countries include Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka.

q: Who discovered the rotation of the Earth (and the heliocentric theory)?
f: Copernicus proposed that the Earth rotates daily and goes around the Sun.
r: Galileo supported it with a telescope. Kepler gave the laws of planetary motion. Note: Source gave only 'Nicholas'; taken as Nicolaus Copernicus (standard answer).

q: Who made the first electric motor?
f: Faraday built the first simple electric motor in 1821.
r: Faraday also discovered electromagnetic induction. Tesla later developed the AC induction motor. Note: Credit is sometimes given to others (Jedlik, Davenport); exam answer is Faraday.

q: What is the SI unit of electric current? (2)
f: Electric current is measured in amperes (A).
r: Voltage is in volts. Resistance is in ohms.

q: Which of these quantities has no unit?
f: Strain is a ratio of change in length to original length, so it has no unit.
r: Stress is measured in pascals. Refractive index also has no unit.

q: Which animal is commonly called the 'desert fox'?
f: The fennec fox is a small desert fox of North Africa with big ears.
r: German general Erwin Rommel was also nicknamed the 'Desert Fox'.

q: Which sport is called the 'gentleman's game'? (2)
f: Cricket is known as the gentleman's game for its spirit and etiquette.
r: The Spirit of Cricket is written in the MCC Laws. Cricket began in England.

q: In which year did America invade Iraq? (2)

q: Who is the President of France? (2)

r: He was first elected in 2017 and re-elected in 2022.

q: What mainly causes earthquakes in the ocean?

r: Such quakes can cause tsunamis. The Pacific Ring of Fire has most quakes.

q: Which equation gives a straight line?

q: The upper part of the River Indus flows through which major city of Gilgit-Baltistan?

r: It is Pakistan's national aquatic mammal. It lives between Guddu and Sukkur barrages mostly.

q: What is the result when any number is multiplied by 0?

r: Any number divided by zero is undefined. Zero is the additive identity.

q: Who wrote the book 'India of My Dreams'?
f: 'India of My Dreams' is a collection of Gandhi's writings on his vision of India.
r: Gandhi's autobiography is 'My Experiments with Truth'.

r: The Attock Fort was built by Akbar. Panjnad is where the five rivers join.

q: Who is the Chief Justice of Pakistan?

q: Which pass connects Parachinar with Afghanistan?

q: Which is the capital of Austria? (4)

q: Which article of the 1973 Constitution declares Islam as the state religion?

q: Who was the first Field Marshal of Pakistan?

q: Syed Ahmad Shaheed carried forward the reform movement of which earlier scholar?

q: In which year was the Olympic Games cancelled because of World War I?
f: The 1916 Berlin Olympics were cancelled due to World War I.
r: Games were also cancelled in 1940 and 1944 due to World War II.

q: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with which place? (2)

r: It was an old route between Central Asia and the subcontinent.

q: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (3)

r: It is on the Karakoram Highway. It is among the highest paved border crossings.

q: What is the range of the Hatf-I missile?
f: Hatf-I is a short-range ballistic rocket with about 70-100 km range.
r: Hatf-III Ghaznavi has about 290 km range. Ghauri is Hatf-V.

q: Who received the Nishan-e-Haider in 1999?
f: Lalak Jan was awarded Nishan-e-Haider for bravery in the Kargil conflict of 1999.
r: Captain Karnal Sher Khan also received it for Kargil, in 1999.

q: In which year did India perform its second (Pokhran-II) atomic tests?
f: India carried out the Pokhran-II tests in May 1998.
r: Pakistan responded with Chagai tests on 28 May 1998. India's first test was in 1974.

q: The 1956 Constitution of Pakistan was of which form?
f: The 1956 Constitution created a federal parliamentary Islamic Republic.
r: It came into force on 23 March 1956. Ayub Khan abrogated it in 1958.

q: Which sea separates Greece from Italy?
f: The Ionian Sea lies between southern Italy and western Greece.
r: The Aegean Sea is east of Greece. The Adriatic is between Italy and the Balkans.

q: Who is the current President of Iran?
f: Pezeshkian became President in July 2024 and is in office as of Oct 2026 per latest reports found.
r: Iran has no Prime Minister; the post was abolished in 1989. Raisi died in a 2024 helicopter crash.

q: K2 is also known as?
f: K2 is named Godwin-Austen after the British surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen.
r: K2 was first climbed by an Italian team in 1954. It is also called Chogori.

q: Which scientist won Nobel Prizes in both Chemistry and Peace?
f: Pauling won the Chemistry prize in 1954 and the Peace prize in 1962.
r: Marie Curie won two Nobels, in Physics and Chemistry. John Bardeen won two in Physics.

q: The boundary line between India and Pakistan is called?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe in 1947.
r: The Durand Line is Pakistan-Afghanistan. The LoC divides Kashmir.

q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
f: Jasmine (Chambeli) is Pakistan's national flower.
r: Pakistan's national tree is the Deodar.

q: From which country did Pakistan buy Gwadar? (3)
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultan of Oman in 1958.
r: Gwadar formally joined Pakistan on 8 September 1958. Gwadar port is part of CPEC.

q: Where is the headquarters of the WHO? (2)
f: WHO is headquartered in Geneva.
r: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948.

q: The 'Hero' medal (Hero of the Soviet Union/Russian Federation) belongs to which country?
f: 'Hero of the Russian Federation' is Russia's highest title, following the old Soviet one.
r: Pakistan's highest award is Nishan-e-Haider.

q: In which year was the Government of India Act passed?
f: The big Government of India Act was passed in 1935 giving provincial autonomy.
r: It was the base for the later constitutions. Burma and Aden were separated. Note: Several Acts exist (1919, 1935); the 1935 Act is the standard answer.

q: In which year did the Cripps Mission come to India? (3)
f: Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in March 1942 with a proposal for dominion status after the war.
r: The Congress and the League rejected it. The Cabinet Mission was in 1946.

q: Which city is known as the 'City of Saints'?
f: Multan has many shrines of Sufi saints.
r: It is also called the City of Mangoes.

q: Which Pakistani city is called the 'Manchester of Pakistan'?
f: Faisalabad is known for its textile industry.
r: Its old name was Lyallpur. Sialkot is known for sports goods.

q: Which city is the legislative capital of South Africa?
f: South Africa's Parliament sits in Cape Town.
r: Pretoria is the executive capital. Bloemfontein is the judicial capital.

q: Which country lies to the north of Pakistan?

r: The Khunjerab Pass links Pakistan and China. Afghanistan lies to the north-west. Note: Direction is loose: Afghanistan is north-west; China is the standard exam answer.

q: On which date was Gwadar purchased by Pakistan from Oman?
f: Pakistan under PM Feroz Khan Noon bought Gwadar from Oman on 8 September 1958 for about 3 million US dollars.
r: Gwadar was formally handed over on 8 December 1958. It became part of Balochistan in 1977.

q: Which is the first mosque (house of worship) built on earth?

r: Quba Mosque is the first mosque built in Islam (Madinah, 622 AD).

q: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was the son of which prophet?
f: Sulaiman (AS) inherited the kingdom and knowledge from his father Dawud (AS).

f: Hajra was the wife of Ibrahim (AS) and mother of Ismail (AS).
r: Sa'i between Safa and Marwa remembers Hajra's search for water. Zamzam appeared for Ismail (AS).

r: The Quran has 114 surahs. Makki surahs are mostly short and deal with faith. Note: Counts differ slightly between scholars; 86 Makki and 28 Madni is the standard answer.

f: A hadith in Bukhari says Allah created Adam (AS) 60 cubits tall; a cubit is about 1.5 feet.

q: Nelson Mandela belonged to which country?
f: Mandela fought apartheid and became South Africa's first black president in 1994.
r: He spent 27 years in prison. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

q: On what date was the Lahore Resolution passed?

q: Who gave the motto 'Unity, Faith, Discipline'? (2)

r: It is the national motto of Pakistan. The order is Iman, Ittehad, Tanzeem.

q: In the Third Anglo-Mysore War (1792), Tipu Sultan was defeated by which British commander?

r: Tipu died in the Fourth Mysore War in 1799 at Seringapatam.

q: In which year did Pakistan last win the Hockey World Cup?

r: Pakistan finished outside the top 8 at the 2026 World Cup.

q: Which picture is printed on the back of the Pakistani 100 rupee note?

q: Where did Allama Iqbal deliver his famous address of 1930?

q: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with which country? (2)

q: What is the length of the Pakistan-China border?

q: In which Surah are wudu, ghusl and tayammum described? (2)

q: Under whose rule was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan introduced? (2)
