f: Pakistan joined SEATO in 1954.
r: It joined CENTO (Baghdad Pact) in 1955 and left SEATO in 1973.

q: How many members does the United Nations have?
f: The UN has 193 member states. South Sudan was the newest, joining in 2011.
r: Palestine and Vatican City are non-member observer states. The UN was founded in 1945.

q: What is the height of the Eiffel Tower (with antenna)?
f: The Eiffel Tower is about 330 m tall including its antenna.
r: It was built in 1889 in Paris by Gustave Eiffel. Original height was about 300 m.

q: In which country is the University of Benin?
f: The University of Benin is in Benin City, Edo State, Nigeria.
r: Do not confuse Benin City (Nigeria) with the country Benin.

q: What is the height of Tirich Mir?
f: Tirich Mir in Chitral, KPK, is 7,708 m high.
r: It is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range. K2 (8,611 m) is the highest in Pakistan.

q: Which is the largest lake in the world?
f: The Caspian Sea (Central Asia) is the largest inland water body by area, about 371,000 sq km.
r: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area. Lake Baikal is the deepest.

q: Which is the world's largest sea port?
f: As of Oct 2026, Shanghai is the world's busiest container port (about 55 million TEU in 2025), ahead of Singapore (44.7 million TEU). By total cargo tonnage, Ningbo-Zhoushan is the largest.
r: Ningbo-Zhoushan leads in total tonnage (over 1.4 billion tonnes in 2025).

q: Which of these is different from the rest: Rome, Paris, Berlin, New York?
f: Rome, Paris and Berlin are national capitals; New York is not a capital.
r: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the USA.

q: What is the capital of Italy?
f: Rome is the capital of Italy.
r: Vatican City is inside Rome.

q: What is the unit of magnetic flux?
f: The SI unit of magnetic flux is the weber (Wb).
r: Tesla is the unit of magnetic flux density.

q: One horsepower is equal to how many watts?
f: 1 horsepower equals about 746 watts.
r: 1 kilowatt = 1000 watts.

q: The pinhole camera was invented by?
f: Ibn al-Haytham (Alhazen) described the pinhole camera (camera obscura) in his Book of Optics.
r: He is called the father of modern optics.

q: Which is the deepest part of the Earth's oceans?
f: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is about 11,000 m deep.
r: Its deepest point is Challenger Deep.

q: The Earth is divided into how many continents?
f: The usual model has seven continents.
r: They are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

q: Water flows through pipes, and blood flows through?
f: Blood flows through blood vessels such as veins (and arteries).
r: Veins carry blood to the heart; arteries carry it away.

q: How many days are there in a leap year?
f: A leap year has 366 days because February has 29 days.
r: A leap year comes every 4 years.

q: Choose the correct word: There is no one else to hide ___.
f: We say 'hide behind' someone or something.
r: Preposition use is a common English test topic.

q: A light year is a unit of?
f: A light year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion km.
r: Light speed is about 3 lakh km per second.

q: What is the unit of force?
f: The SI unit of force is the newton (N).
r: 1 N = 1 kg m/s squared.

q: The kWh (kilowatt-hour) is a unit of?
f: kWh measures energy. Power is in watts or kilowatts.
r: 1 kWh = 3.6 million joules.

q: What is the area of a circle?
f: Area of a circle = pi x r x r.
r: Circumference = 2 pi r.

q: IMF stands for?
f: IMF is the International Monetary Fund, which helps countries with financial stability.
r: Its headquarters is in Washington, D.C.

q: NaCl is the chemical formula of?
f: NaCl is common salt, sodium chloride.
r: Washing soda is Na2CO3.

q: Who is the current Chief of the Naval Staff of Pakistan (as of Oct 2026)?
f: As of Oct 2026, Admiral Naveed Ashraf is CNS. He took charge on 7 October 2023.
r: He succeeded Admiral Amjad Khan Niazi.

q: The medium which carries signals from source to destination is called?
f: The channel (transmission medium) carries the signal from sender to receiver.
r: Examples are cable, fibre and air.

q: The highest mountain of the world, Mount Everest, is in which country?
f: Mount Everest (8,849 m) is on the Nepal-China border and is mainly credited to Nepal.
r: K2 is the highest mountain in Pakistan.

q: When did Pakistan join the UN?
f: Pakistan became a UN member on 30 September 1947.
r: Pakistan was the 56th member.

q: Which river flows along the Salt Range?
f: The Indus flows along the western side of the Salt Range.
r: The Jhelum also flows along its northern edge. Khewra has a famous salt mine. Note: Jhelum also touches the Salt Range; standard answer here is Indus.

q: In an n-p-n transistor, the p region works as the?
f: In an n-p-n transistor the middle p-type layer is the base.
r: The other two layers are emitter and collector.

q: Who was the first Chief of Naval Staff of the Pakistan Navy?
f: Vice Admiral Muhammad Siddiq Choudri was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief (Chief of Naval Staff) of the Pakistan Navy, 1953 to 1959.
r: The first Commander-in-Chief after independence was British: Rear Admiral James Wilfred Jefford.

q: How many metres are there in 2 km?
r: 1 mile is about 1.6 km.

q: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) headquarters is in which country?
f: ADB is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.
r: ADB was set up in 1966.

q: When were the first direct general elections (one person, one vote) held in Pakistan?
f: The first direct general elections based on adult franchise were held in December 1970.
r: Awami League won in East Pakistan; PPP won in West Pakistan. Note: Source answer text was mismatched ('Brussels and Luxembourg'); standard answer 1970 used.

q: Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto gave Pakistan which constitution?
f: The 1973 Constitution, Pakistan's third, was passed under Z. A. Bhutto.
r: It is still in force. The 1956 and 1962 constitutions came earlier.

q: How many agencies were there in FATA?
f: FATA had 7 tribal agencies (Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Orakzai, Kurram, North and South Waziristan).
r: FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 (25th Amendment).

q: How many member countries are in the European Union (EU)?
f: The EU has 27 members after the UK left in 2020.
r: The EU headquarters is Brussels, Belgium. The Maastricht Treaty took effect in 1993.

q: Which of these is not a member of the United Nations?
f: Vatican City is only a non-member observer state of the UN.
r: Palestine is also a non-member observer state. Switzerland joined in 2002.

q: Who founded the Dawn newspaper?
f: Jinnah founded Dawn in Delhi in 1941.
r: It began as a weekly newspaper.

q: The Muztagh Pass connects Baltistan with?
f: Muztagh Pass links Baltistan with Yarkand in Xinjiang, China.
r: Mintaka and Khunjerab also link Gilgit-Baltistan with China.

q: The Tochi Pass connects Bannu (Pakistan) with?
f: The Tochi Pass links Bannu in Pakistan with Ghazni in Afghanistan.
r: It lies in North Waziristan.

q: The Shandur Pass connects Gilgit with?
f: Shandur Pass links Chitral (KPK) with Gilgit-Baltistan.
r: The world's highest polo ground is at Shandur.

q: The Lowari Pass connects Dir and Peshawar region with?
f: Lowari Pass links Dir with Chitral.
r: The Lowari Tunnel is a major road tunnel there.

q: The Bolan Pass connects Quetta with?
f: Bolan Pass joins Quetta with Sibi and the Sindh plains.
r: It is in the Brahui range, Balochistan.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan to visit China?
f: Suhrawardy visited China in 1956 while he was the 5th PM (1956-57).
r: China-Pakistan ties began in 1951.

q: In the 1970 elections, who led the winning party in East Pakistan?
f: The Awami League led by Sheikh Mujib won almost all East Pakistan seats.
r: Z. A. Bhutto's PPP won most seats in West Pakistan.

q: The Warsak Dam is built on which river? (2)
f: Warsak Dam (KPK) is on the Kabul River.
r: Mangla is on the Jhelum, Tarbela on the Indus, Mirani on the Dasht.

q: Which country of the world lies in two continents?
f: Turkey lies in both Europe and Asia.
r: Istanbul is split by the Bosphorus. Russia and Egypt also span two continents. Note: More than one country spans two continents; Turkey is the standard exam answer.

q: From whom did Pakistan buy Gwadar, and in which year?
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from Oman in 1958 for about 3 million dollars.
r: Gwadar is on the Balochistan coast of the Arabian Sea.

q: Which continent is known as the 'Dark Continent'?
f: Africa was called the Dark Continent because it was little known to Europeans.
r: Africa is the second largest continent.

q: For how many years is the President of Pakistan elected?
f: The President is elected for a five-year term by an electoral college.
r: The 1973 Constitution sets this term.

q: Who had the longest tenure as President of Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan was President for about 10 years 5 months (1958-1969).
r: Zia-ul-Haq was President for about 9 years 11 months.

q: Campbellpur is the old name of which city of Pakistan?
f: Attock was earlier called Campbellpur.
r: The Attock Fort was built by Akbar.

q: Tirmizi (Jami at-Tirmidhi) is a book of?
f: Jami at-Tirmidhi is one of the six authentic Hadith books (Sihah Sitta).
r: The others are Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Nasai and Ibn Majah.

q: Nobel Prizes are given in how many fields today?
f: Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics (added 1969).
r: The prizes were first given in 1901.

q: How many Nobel Prizes does Pakistan have (as of Oct 2026)?
f: Pakistan has 2 Nobel laureates: Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014).
r: Malala is the youngest Nobel laureate.

q: What is the chemical symbol of gold?
f: Au comes from the Latin word Aurum.
r: Silver is Ag (Argentum).

q: Who gave the name 'United Nations'?
f: US President Roosevelt suggested the name; it was first used in the Declaration by United Nations (1 Jan 1942).
r: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.

q: Which is the smallest river of Pakistan among the main rivers?
f: The Ravi is the shortest of the five rivers of the Punjab (about 720 km).
r: The Ravi flows through Lahore. The five rivers of Punjab are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej. Note: Smallest depends on definition; standard exam answer is Ravi.

q: How many provinces does Pakistan have?
f: Pakistan has four provinces: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.
r: Islamabad is the Capital Territory; Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir are administered regions.

q: Which city is on the border of Sindh and Punjab provinces?
f: Kashmore is the northernmost district of Sindh and touches the Punjab border.
r: Kashmore also touches Balochistan. Sukkur is the third largest city of Sindh.

q: Who was the Prime Minister of Great Britain during the Second World War (1940-45)?
f: Churchill led Britain from May 1940 to July 1945, most of the war.
r: WWII lasted 1939 to 1945; WWI lasted 1914 to 1918. Chamberlain was PM only in the first months (1939-40). Note: Chamberlain was PM at the very start of the war; standard answer is Churchill.

q: After the 1965 war, which agreement did Pakistan sign with India?
f: The Tashkent Agreement was signed on 10 January 1966 to end the 1965 war.
r: It was signed by Ayub Khan and Indian PM Lal Bahadur Shastri, with USSR mediation.

q: Who wrote 'Das Kapital'?
f: Karl Marx wrote Das Kapital, the book that criticises capitalism (first volume 1867).
r: Marx also co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Friedrich Engels.

q: Breaking a promise is a sign of what?
f: A hadith lists breaking a promise as a sign of a hypocrite (munafiq).
r: Other signs of hypocrisy in the hadith: lying and betraying a trust. Note: Answer follows the hadith; Hypocrisy is the standard answer.

q: Masjid-e-Zarrar was built by whom?
f: The hypocrites of Madinah built it to harm Muslims, and the Prophet (SAW) had it destroyed.
r: It is mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah. Masjid Quba was the first mosque of Islam.

q: In which years was Tarbela Dam constructed?
f: Construction of Tarbela Dam started in 1968 and the dam was completed in 1976.
r: Tarbela is on the River Indus in Haripur, KPK; it is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: Who was the foster mother of Prophet Muhammad (SAW)?
f: Halima Sadia of Banu Saad nursed the Prophet (SAW) in his infancy.
r: His real mother was Hazrat Aminah, who died when he was six.

q: What does LOC stand for in the Kashmir issue?
f: LOC means Line of Control, the military line dividing Indian and Pakistani held Kashmir.
r: The LOC is about 740 km (460 miles) long and came after the Simla Agreement 1972.

q: The Theory of Relativity was given by whom?
f: Einstein published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.
r: Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.

q: When did Queen Elizabeth II tour Pakistan?
f: She visited twice, in 1961 (President Ayub Khan) and in 1997.
r: The 1997 visit was during Pakistan's 50th anniversary year.

q: The telescope was discovered (first used for astronomy) by whom?
f: Galileo built a telescope in 1609 and used it to study the sky.
r: Hans Lippershey first patented a telescope in 1608; Newton built the reflecting telescope. Note: Strictly Lippershey invented it; standard exam answer is Galileo.

q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (SAW)?
f: Hazrat Khadija bint Khuwaylid married the Prophet (SAW) before prophethood.
r: The Prophet did not marry again while she was alive.

q: Who was the first Khalifa (Caliph) of Islam?
f: Abu Bakr became caliph after the Prophet (SAW) passed away in 632 CE.
r: His caliphate lasted about 2 years and 3 months (source says 2 years 2 months 11 days).

q: In which year was the Indian National Congress established?
f: Congress was founded in December 1885.
r: Founder: Allan Octavian Hume. Muslim League was founded in 1906.

q: Who was the first President of India?
f: Rajendra Prasad served as first President from 1950 to 1962.
r: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

q: By which year does Pakistan plan to send its first astronaut into space?
f: As of Oct 2026, Pakistan's first astronaut (one of two candidates, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali or Khurram Daud) is expected to fly to China's Tiangong station in late 2026, probably on Shenzhou-24; the exact date is not firmly confirmed.
r: Pakistan's first person in space is still Namira Salim (2023, private flight).

q: In which region of Pakistan does the Neelum River flow?
f: The Neelum River flows through Neelum Valley in Azad Jammu and Kashmir.
r: The Neelum-Jhelum hydropower project is on this river; it joins the Jhelum near Muzaffarabad.

q: Sindh was conquered by whom?
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 CE at about age 17.
r: He defeated Raja Dahir. Sindh is called Bab-ul-Islam.

q: Who was the leader of the Muslims in the Ghazwa Tabuk?
f: The Prophet (SAW) personally led the army to Tabuk in 9 AH.
r: It is also called Ghazwa-e-Usrah (hardship), and no fighting took place.

q: The Kashmir Highway in Islamabad was renamed as what?
f: In 2018 the Kashmir Highway was renamed Srinagar Highway to show solidarity with Kashmiris.
r: It connects Islamabad with Rawalpindi side routes and the Faizabad area.

q: Fill in the blank: 'I am going ____ home.'
f: With 'home' used as an adverb, no preposition is used: 'I am going home'.
r: Similar: 'come home', 'go abroad' take no preposition.

q: Fill in the blank: 'Asad is swimming ____ one hour.'
f: 'For' is used with a period of time such as one hour.
r: 'Since' is used with a point in time (since 5 o'clock).

q: Why do we boil milk?
f: Boiling kills harmful bacteria in milk.
r: Pasteurisation (named after Louis Pasteur) also kills germs by heating.

q: One third of one tenth of 90 is?
f: One tenth of 90 = 9; one third of 9 = 3.
r: Fractions of a number are found step by step.

q: A quarter of one tenth of 120 is?
f: One tenth of 120 = 12; a quarter of 12 = 3.
r: Answer printed on page 114 as 3.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2/2 ?
f: By BODMAS division comes first: 2/2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
r: BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

q: Fill in the blank: 'Throw the pen ____ the dustbin.'
f: 'Into' shows movement from outside to the inside of the dustbin.
r: 'In' shows position, 'into' shows movement. Note: Answer not printed in the source; standard answer is into.

q: Fill in the blank: 'He is superior ____ me.'
f: Words like superior, inferior and senior take 'to' not 'than'.
r: Other 'to' words: prefer, junior, preferable.

q: Fill in the blank: 'I was amazed ____ his misbehaviour.'
f: 'Amazed at' is the correct phrase.
r: Similar: surprised at, shocked at.

q: Fill in the blank: 'He is responsible ____ his decision.'
f: We say 'responsible for' a thing and 'responsible to' a person.
r: Accountable also takes 'for' (a thing).

q: Fill in the blank: 'He is good ____ football.'
f: 'Good at' is used for skills.
r: Similar: bad at, clever at, weak at.

q: Fill in the blank: 'Usman is afraid ____ the dog.'
f: 'Afraid of' is the correct phrase.
r: Similar: fond of, proud of, full of.

q: Fill in the blank: 'She is jealous ____ my friend.'
f: 'Jealous of' is the correct phrase.
r: Similar: envious of.

q: What type of constitution was the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1962 Constitution gave all power to the President (Ayub Khan).
r: Pakistan has had constitutions in 1956, 1962 and 1973.

q: When did Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad start?
f: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad was launched in February 2017.
r: It followed the wave of terror attacks in early 2017 and was nationwide.

q: When was Operation Zarb-e-Azb launched?
f: Zarb-e-Azb began in June 2014 after the terrorist attack on Jinnah International Airport, Karachi.
r: It was carried out in North Waziristan.

q: How many roots does a linear equation have?
f: A linear equation (degree 1) has exactly one root.
r: A quadratic equation has two roots.

q: Hazrat Ismail (AS) was the son of whom?
f: Hazrat Ismail was the elder son of Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Hajra.
r: Ibrahim had 2 sons: Ismail and Ishaq.

q: What was the name of the son of Hazrat Zakariya (AS)?
f: Hazrat Yahya (John) was the son of Hazrat Zakariya.
r: Yahya was a cousin of Hazrat Isa (AS).

q: In which year did Pakistan introduce its first postage stamp?
f: Pakistan issued its first stamps on 9 July 1948.
r: The first stamp design was by Abdul Rehman Chughtai and was approved by Quaid-i-Azam.

q: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty signed?
f: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 in Karachi.
r: Signed by Nehru and Ayub Khan with the World Bank as a party. India got three eastern rivers, Pakistan the three western rivers.

q: With whose help was Pakistan Steel Mills built?
f: Pakistan Steel Mills in Karachi was built with Soviet Union help; work began in 1973.
r: It started production in 1981 near Bin Qasim.

q: Where did the boat of Hazrat Nuh (AS) stop?
f: The Quran says the Ark settled on Mount Judi.
r: Mount Judi is mentioned in Surah Hud.

q: Which of these countries has no army?
f: Iceland has no standing army; it relies on NATO membership and a coast guard.
r: Others without armies include Andorra, Dominica and Grenada. Note: Several countries qualify; Iceland is a standard answer.

q: What is the largest single source of electricity generation in Pakistan?
f: As of Oct 2026, hydropower is still Pakistan's largest single source of electricity generation (about 31% of output in FY2025 and FY2026), ahead of nuclear (about 17.7%). The 23.4% hydel figure in the Economic Survey is installed capacity share, not generation.
r: Nuclear is the second-largest generation source at roughly 17-18%.

q: In which year was the First Battle of Panipat fought?
f: The First Battle of Panipat (Babur vs Ibrahim Lodhi) was fought in 1526.
r: Second battle 1556, third 1761. Kashmir was sold to Gulab Singh by the British in 1846 for 7.5 million rupees.

q: How many Hockey World Cups has Pakistan won?
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup four times.

q: In which district is the ancient site of Harappa located?
f: Harappa is near Sahiwal in Punjab.
r: Mohenjo-daro is in Larkana, Sindh.

q: Pakistan has won the British Open squash title more than how many times?
f: Between 1950 and 1997 Pakistanis won over 30 British Open titles.
r: Jahangir Khan won 10 British Opens; Jansher Khan won 6. Note: Source says 23; sources are loose, over 30 is the commonly quoted figure.

q: Jahangir Khan was a player of which sport?
f: Jahangir Khan was a legendary squash champion.
r: He won 10 British Open titles and was unbeaten for about 5 years.

q: What does 'Israel' mean?
f: Israel is the title of Hazrat Yaqub (AS) and means servant of God (Abdullah).
r: His children are called Bani Israel.

q: What does 'Zam Zam' mean?
f: Hazrat Hajra said 'zam zam' (stop) to the gushing water.
r: Zamzam well is in Masjid al-Haram, Makkah, near the Kaaba.

q: The two daughters of the Holy Prophet (SAW) were married to whom, one after the other?
f: Hazrat Ruqayyah and then Hazrat Umm Kulthum were married to Hazrat Usman, so he is called Zun-Noorain.
r: Hazrat Fatima married Hazrat Ali (RA).

q: In which year did the Khilafat Movement start? (2)
f: The Khilafat Movement started in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
r: Leaders: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Maulana Shaukat Ali. Jang-e-Azadi was in 1857.

q: Famous boxer Muhammad Ali belongs to which country?
f: Muhammad Ali (born Cassius Clay) was an American heavyweight boxer.
r: He won the Olympic gold medal in 1960 and accepted Islam in 1964.

q: Who advised Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Holy Quran?
f: After many Huffaz were martyred in the Battle of Yamama, Hazrat Umar (RA) advised Abu Bakr (RA) to compile the Quran.
r: Zaid bin Thabit (RA) did the compilation work; Hazrat Uthman (RA) later made standard copies.

q: How many nuclear tests did Pakistan perform on 28 May 1998 at Chagai, Balochistan?
f: Pakistan conducted five nuclear tests on 28 May 1998 in the Chagai Hills.
r: A sixth test was done on 30 May 1998 at Kharan. 28 May is Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: Namaz-e-Istisqa is offered for what?
f: Salat al-Istisqa is the prayer asking Allah for rain during drought.
r: Salat al-Kusuf is offered at a solar eclipse.

q: Namaz-e-Kasoof is offered at the time of which event?
f: Salat al-Kusuf is the prayer offered during a solar eclipse.
r: Prayer for a lunar eclipse is called Salat al-Khusuf. Note: Some scholars use Kusuf/Khusuf for either eclipse; the standard exam answer is solar eclipse.

q: Which Sahabi served the Prophet (PBUH) for ten years?
f: Anas bin Malik (RA) was given to the Prophet (PBUH) as a boy and served him for ten years in Madinah.
r: He is among the Sahabah who narrated the most Ahadith.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
f: The IMF headquarters is in Washington DC, USA.
r: The IMF was set up in 1944 (Bretton Woods) and began work in 1945.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to climb Mount Everest?
f: Nazir Sabir reached the summit of Mount Everest on 17 May 1977, the first Pakistani to do so.
r: Samina Baig became the first Pakistani woman to climb Everest in 2013.

q: In which year was the Suez Canal completed (opened)?
f: The Suez Canal in Egypt opened in 1869 and is about 193 km long.
r: It was built under Ferdinand de Lesseps.

q: The Suez Canal connects which two seas?
f: The canal links the Mediterranean Sea in the north with the Red Sea in the south.
r: It separates Africa from Asia (Sinai Peninsula).

q: Which Prophet built the Ark (boat) for the great flood?
f: Hazrat Nuh (AS) built the Ark by Allah's command to save believers from the flood.
r: His people did not accept his message for about 950 years.

q: On which mountain did the Ark of Hazrat Nuh (AS) come to rest?
f: The Quran says the Ark settled on Mount Judi (Al-Judi), traditionally located in Turkey.
r: Tradition says the people stayed in the Ark for about 6 months.

q: Which Prophet worked as a carpenter?
f: A Hadith in Sahih Muslim says Zakariya (AS) was a carpenter.
r: Hazrat Dawud (AS) was known for making armour.

q: Where is Jabal-e-Noor located?
f: Jabal-e-Noor is the mountain near Makkah that holds the Cave of Hira.
r: The first revelation came to the Prophet (PBUH) in the Cave of Hira.

q: What is the meaning (synonym) of 'fondness'?
f: Fondness means a liking or love for someone or something, so affection is its meaning.
r: Related words: love, liking, tenderness.

q: In which country was the 2022 FIFA World Cup held?
f: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first in the Middle East.
r: The 2026 World Cup is hosted by the USA, Canada and Mexico.

q: On which date is Defence Day of Pakistan observed?
f: Defence Day marks the 6 September 1965 defence of Pakistan against India.
r: Youm-e-Takbeer is 28 May.

q: Who discovered bacteria?
f: Van Leeuwenhoek first observed bacteria through a microscope in 1676.
r: He is called the Father of Microbiology.

q: The word 'Jihad' belongs to which language?
f: Jihad is an Arabic word meaning struggle or striving.
r: Its root is j-h-d.

q: Which country invented the game of chess?
f: Chess began in India in the Gupta period as 'Chaturanga'.
r: It later spread to Persia and Europe.

q: In which year did Pakistan win its first Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup under Imran Khan in Australia and New Zealand.
r: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne.

q: 'Israel' is the title of which Prophet?
f: Israel was the title (name) of Hazrat Yaqoob (AS); his children are called Bani Israel.
r: He was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (AS).

q: What is the gestation (pregnancy) period of a buffalo?
f: A buffalo carries its calf for roughly 300 to 320 days.
r: A cow's pregnancy lasts about 280 days. Note: Exact figure varies by breed (about 300-320 days).

q: At the point of contact, a tangent to a circle makes what angle with the radius?
f: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
r: Two tangents from an outside point are equal in length.

q: The Battle of Plassey was fought between whom?
o: British East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah
f: The 1757 Battle of Plassey was won by the East India Company against Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab of Bengal.
r: Battles of Panipat: 1526, 1556 and 1761.

q: The Karakoram Highway is also called by which name?
f: The KKH follows part of the ancient Silk Route and is also called the Friendship Highway.
r: It links Hasan Abdal in Pakistan with Kashgar in China.

q: How many letters does the Pashto alphabet have?
f: The Pashto alphabet is usually counted as 44-45 letters.
r: Urdu has about 39 and English has 26 letters. Note: Counts vary slightly (44 to 45); 45 is the common exam answer.

q: What does the word 'Urdu' mean?
f: Urdu is a Turkish word meaning army or camp (Lashkar).
r: Urdu grew in army camps of the Mughal period.

q: Kot Diji is located in which province?
f: Kot Diji is in Khairpur district, Sindh, known for its fort and an early Indus-period site.
r: Kot Diji culture came before the Mohenjo-daro civilisation.

q: How many verses (ayat) does Surah Al-Baqarah have?
f: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 verses and is the longest surah.
r: It is the 2nd surah of the Quran.

q: What is the first pillar of Islam?
f: The first pillar is the declaration of faith in the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad (PBUH).
r: The five pillars are Kalima, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj.

q: How many heads (Masarif) of Zakat are mentioned in the Quran?
f: Surah At-Tawbah (9:60) names eight categories of those who may receive Zakat.
r: They include the poor, the needy, debtors and travellers.

q: Who is the Foreign Minister of Pakistan (As of Oct 2026)?
f: As of Oct 2026, Ishaq Dar is Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan (web check: listed in that role in 2026).
r: Bilawal Bhutto Zardari was Foreign Minister from April 2022 to August 2023 and again until the 2024 government change.

q: In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) established?
f: The SCO was formally founded on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai.
r: As of Oct 2026 it has 10 members (Belarus joined in 2024); HQ is Beijing.

q: What was the capital of Pakistan before Islamabad?
f: Karachi was the first capital; the capital moved to Rawalpindi (temporary) and then Islamabad in 1960s.
r: Islamabad was planned by Constantinos Doxiadis.

q: What was Mother Teresa's occupation?
f: Mother Teresa was a Catholic nun and missionary who served the poor in Kolkata.
r: She founded the Missionaries of Charity and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.

q: In which year was the Tarbela Dam completed?
f: Tarbela Dam on the River Indus was completed in 1976.
r: It is the largest earth-filled dam in the world.

q: Mohammad Ali Bogra was the ___ of Pakistan.
f: Mohammad Ali Bogra was Prime Minister of Pakistan from 1953 to 1955.
r: The first PM was Liaqat Ali Khan and the second was Khawaja Nazimuddin.

q: What is the process of water changing into steam (vapour) called?
f: Water turning into vapour on heating is called evaporation (vaporisation).
r: The reverse process is condensation. Note: Strictly, boiling is fast vaporisation; evaporation is the standard exam answer.

q: Translate this passage ___ English.
f: We say 'translate something into a language'.
r: 'Translate from Urdu into English' is the usual pattern.

q: His head is covered ___ hair.
f: 'Covered with' is the correct phrase.
r: 'Covered by' is used for agents, e.g. covered by insurance.

q: He was accused ___ theft.
f: The correct phrase is 'accused of'.
r: Also: charged with, convicted of.

q: Choose the correct word: 'I am going ___ home.'
f: 'Home' works as an adverb here, so no preposition is used after 'going'.
r: Say 'go home', not 'go to home'.

q: He is fond ___ drawing.
f: The correct phrase is 'fond of'.
r: Also: proud of, afraid of.

q: My sister is bad ___ Maths.
f: We say 'bad at' a subject or skill.
r: Also: good at, weak in.

q: We must bear ___ his pranks.
f: 'Bear with' means to be patient with something.
r: 'Bear' alone means to carry.

q: I am envious ___ them.
f: The correct phrase is 'envious of'.
r: Also: jealous of.

q: Harry is capable ___ doing anything.
f: The correct phrase is 'capable of'.
r: 'Able to' is followed by a verb.

q: My book is different ___ yours.
f: The standard phrase is 'different from'.
r: 'Different to' is used in British casual speech.

q: It was kind ___ you to help.
f: For adjectives describing a person's behaviour we use 'of', as in 'kind of you'.
r: Also: nice of, silly of.

q: Sana was staring ___ me.
f: The correct phrase is 'stare at'.
r: Also: look at, glare at.

q: I was astonished ___ his failure.
f: The correct phrase is 'astonished at'.
r: Also: surprised at, shocked at.

q: What does 'yearn' mean?
f: Yearn means to long for something deeply.
r: Synonyms: long, crave, pine.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'alert'?
f: Alert means quick to notice, so watchful is its synonym.
r: Synonyms: vigilant, attentive.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'precarious'?
f: Precarious means unsafe or uncertain, so insecure fits.
r: Synonyms: risky, unstable.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'blush'?
f: To blush is to turn red in the face, so redden is a synonym.
r: Blush is caused by shame or embarrassment.

q: What is the meaning of 'zeal'?
f: Zeal means great energy or eagerness.
r: Synonyms: passion, fervour.

q: What is the meaning of 'cordial'?
f: Cordial means warm and friendly.
r: Synonyms: warm, genial.

q: Choose the antonym of 'expand'.
f: Expand means to grow bigger; its opposite is condense (make smaller).
r: Synonyms of expand: enlarge, extend.

q: Choose the antonym of 'attract'.
f: Attract means to pull towards; repel means to push away.
r: Magnets attract and repel.

q: Choose the antonym of 'ductile'.
f: Ductile means able to be drawn into wire or bent easily; stiff (brittle) is the opposite.
r: Copper is a ductile metal.

q: Which word is a synonym of 'tyrant'?
f: A tyrant is a cruel, oppressive ruler, so despot is a synonym.
r: Synonyms: dictator, oppressor.

q: Choose the synonym of 'arrogant'.
f: Arrogant means having too high an opinion of oneself; conceited means the same.
r: Synonyms: haughty, proud.

q: What is the meaning of 'vagrant'?
f: A vagrant is a person who wanders without a home or job.
r: Synonyms: wanderer, drifter.

So every figure has two separate circles, one white and one black. Figure 2 has the arrow and panel in the right places, but it shows only one big black circle and no white circle. That is why figure 2 is the odd one out.
r: Count the small parts in every figure first (circles, arrows, panels). The figure with a missing or merged part is usually the odd one.

q: Which one is different from the rest? (Forces Academy Picture Test II, Q5)
f: All figures are the same flask: a round bulb, a straight neck and a small step on one side of the neck end. In options 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 the step is on the same side when you turn them to match. In option 3 the step is on the other side, so it is a mirror image.
r: Look at one small detail (here the step at the end of the neck) and check which side it is on after turning each figure.

q: Which one is different from the rest? (Forces Academy Picture Test II, Q6)
f: All five figures are the same blob shape with a pointed beak, just turned. Turn option 3 so its beak matches option 5 and the long and short parts beside the beak are swapped. That means option 3 is a mirror image, the odd one.
r: Note which side of the beak is longer; in a mirror image the long and short sides change places.

q: Which one is different from the rest? (Forces Academy Picture Test II, Q7)
f: Each figure is the same shoe-like shape: a round knob, a long bar and a hooked end. Options 1, 2, 3 and 5 are only turned versions of each other. Option 4 can only be matched by flipping it over, so it is the mirror image.
r: Turning never changes the hook's side relative to the knob; flipping does.

q: Which one is different from the rest? (Forces Academy Picture Test II, Q8)
f: Each triangle has three corner pieces: one black, one with lines and one white. Going round clockwise, options 1, 2, 3 and 5 always read lines, white, black. Option 4 reads lines, black, white, so it is the odd one.
r: With shaded corners, read the colours clockwise from any corner and compare the order, not the positions.

q: Which one is different from the rest? (Forces Academy Picture Test II, Q9)
f: Each figure is a half circle joined to a small tab at one end of its straight edge. Options 2, 3, 4 and 5 are the same shape only turned. Option 1 is a mirror image (flipped over): its tab is at the other end of the straight edge, so it is the odd one. Turning a shape never makes its mirror image.
r: Go round the shape clockwise: tab, straight edge, curve. A figure with a different order is a mirror image.

f: All four are the same meander (zigzag) line. Options 1, 2 and 4 are rotations of one drawing. Option 3 is the mirror image of option 4 (they reflect each other), so it cannot be made by turning.
r: When two figures look like reflections of each other, one of them is usually the odd one; test each against a third figure.

q: The first shape changes in some way to become the second shape. Which option replaces the question mark? (Pro Genius Analogy Q3)
f: Count the lines from the outside in. In figure 1 the outer two lines swap their corner style (square and round) and the inner two lines swap too, while thick and thin stay where they are. In figure 3 the 2nd line has a gap on the right arm and the 3rd line has a gap on the left arm, so swapping line 1 with line 2 and line 3 with line 4 moves the right gap to the outer line and the left gap to the innermost line, which is option 1. Option 2 is tempting, but it only swaps the outer pair; its left gap is still on the 3rd line.
r: Number the nested lines 1 to 4 from the outside and list each line's feature (gap, corner, thickness). Then check pair by pair which features moved.

f: From figure 1 to figure 2, both arrows turn around to point the opposite way (each arrow keeps its own head style), and the row of hexagons is read in reverse order, so black-white-black-white becomes white-black-white-black. Doing the same to figure 3 gives arrows pointing the other way and the stars changing from white-black-white-black to black-white-black-white, which is option 5. Option 3 is tempting because its arrows are reversed correctly, but its stars are in the same order as figure 3, so the pattern was not reversed.
r: Check each part separately: first the arrow directions and head styles, then the order of the shaded and unshaded shapes. Options that get only one part right are the usual traps.

The outside row moves one edge anticlockwise each step: top, upper left, lower left, bottom. Both rows meet again at the bottom in figure 4. So in the next figure the inside row goes to the lower left edge and the outside row goes to the lower right edge, with the order triangle, square, circle kept. Option 5 is wrong because its outside row has the order changed (square, circle, triangle). Options 2 and 4 are wrong because both rows sit on the same side.
r: Track each group of shapes separately and note which way it moves, one edge per step. Then use the order of shapes inside each row to remove options.

f: The circle and the small square always sit at the same height on opposite sides, and the pair moves down step by step. (This puzzle is hard to read: please also check with your answer key.)
r: Check height and left-right side of each small mark in every figure. A mark that swaps sides each step is easy to predict.

q: Find the figure that comes next in the series. (PDF Q11)
f: Look at the small black ball. It moves around the circle in the clockwise direction, about one step (45 degrees) each time: bottom-left, left, top-left, top. So next it must be at the top-right. The thick black bar also moves clockwise round the outside edge of the box: top-right, bottom-right, bottom, bottom-left, so next it goes to the left side. Only option 3 has the ball at top-right and the bar at the left. Option 5 has the bar on the left too, but its ball is outside the circle, so it is wrong.
r: Track each small object separately and note its direction and step size. Then match the answer by checking one object at a time and cutting wrong options.

q: Which figure completes the matrix (replaces the question mark)? (Complete the Sequence, Problem 56)
f: Count the crosses. Row 1: 5, 6, 7 (add 1). Row 2: 7, 9, 11 (add 2). Row 3: 8, 11, so add 3 to get 14. Option 3 has 5 + 5 + 4 = 14 crosses. Option 2 has only 13 and option 1 has 15.
r: In grids of dots or crosses, count them and look for an "add 1, add 2, add 3" pattern by row.

f: The short line (corner to centre) moves one corner clockwise each time: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, so next is bottom-left. The long diagonal switches direction every time, so next it must go from top-left to bottom-right. Option 1 has both. Options 2, 3 and 4 repeat earlier figures.
r: When two lines are inside a square, follow each line on its own.

r: A dot or oval moving round a circle keeps the same direction; check clockwise or anticlockwise.

f: Each figure is the one before it turned 90 degrees clockwise. The small box with the + goes top-left, top-right, bottom-right, so next it goes bottom-left, and the slanting line points to the top-right corner. Option 4 is the third figure turned once more. Option 2 also has + at bottom-left, but its lines are a flipped picture, not a turn.
r: Turn the whole figure in your head 90 degrees; check every line, not only the + sign.

r: Split the series into shape and shading, and compare each shape with its own earlier copy.

f: The two crossed boxes always sit side by side and move round: top, left, bottom, right. After the right side they return to the top. Option 1 has the two top boxes crossed. Options 4 and 5 use boxes that are not next to each other, which never happens in the series.
r: If a pair of shaded boxes moves round a 2x2 grid, after four steps it is back at the start.

f: In each pair, the small shape that was inside becomes the big outer shape, and the old outer shape becomes a small black shape sitting on top. The triangle with a square inside becomes a square with a small triangle on top. So the circle with a triangle inside becomes a triangle with a small circle on top: option 3. Option 4 has the circle on top of a square, the wrong big shape.
r: Ask: which shape was inside, and which was outside? Then swap their sizes.

f: Each figure adds one more line: 1 line, 2 lines, then 3 lines in the triangle. The next figure keeps the triangle and has 4 lines. Option 1 fits. Option 3 has 4 lines but goes back to the rectangle, and option 2 has only 2 lines.
r: Count the lines in each figure; the count usually goes up by one.

q: Which letter comes next in the following series: S, Q, N, L, I, ?
f: Gaps alternate -2, -3: S to Q is 2, Q to N is 3, N to L is 2, L to I is 3, then -2 gives G.
r: Tip: alternating gaps in letter series repeat in pairs; list the gaps.

q: Complete the series: A, C, F, J, O, ? (56)
f: Positions are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (gaps 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next gap is 6 and 15 + 6 = 21 = U.
r: Gaps that increase by 1 are the triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21.

q: Which number comes next: 42, 30, 20, 12, ?
f: Differences are -12, -10, -8, so the next is -6: 12 - 6 = 6.
r: Tip: these numbers are products of consecutive integers (7x6, 6x5, 5x4, 4x3, 3x2).

q: Complete the series: F, H, K, O, T, ?
f: The jumps are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next jump is +6. T is the 20th letter and 20 + 6 = 26, which is Z.
r: The jump between letters rises by 1 each time.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 225, 65, 335, ?
f: The odd places 115, 225, 335 rise by 110 each time. The even places 55, 65 rise by 10, so the next is 75.
r: The question asks for the next term, which falls in the even-place series.

q: Which letter comes next in the following series: D, H, M, P, U, ?
f: Split the series into two: D, M, U (gaps +9, +8) and H, P, then W (gaps +8, +7). The next letter is W.
r: Tip: in alternating letter series, separate the odd and even positions into two sequences.

q: What number comes next in the following series? 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, ?
f: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 2+1 = 3, 1+3 = 4, 3+4 = 7, so next is 4+7 = 11.
r: Tip: this is a Fibonacci-type series where each term is the sum of the previous two.

q: Which letter comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ? (110)
f: The gaps between letters are +2, +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6. O is the 15th letter and the 21st is U.
r: The differences in this series increase by 1 each time.

q: Which of the following is a prime number: 7, 9, 18, 21? (10)
f: 7 has only two factors, 1 and 7. 9 = 3 x 3, 18 = 2 x 9 and 21 = 3 x 7 are composite.
r: 2 is the only even prime number.

q: What number comes next in the following series: 40, 30, 35, 25, 30, 20, ?
r: Tip: two alternating steps make a zigzag series.

q: What will come next in the following series: 47, 40, 34, 29, 25, ?
f: Differences are -7, -6, -5, -4, so next is -3: 25 - 3 = 22.
r: Tip: if the gap reduces by one each time, continue the reducing gap.

q: Complete the series: 1A, 2D, 3H, ?
f: Numbers go 1, 2, 3, 4. Letters A, D, H, M move forward by 3, 4, 5, so the next letter is M.

q: What comes next in the series: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, ?
f: Each term has a capital letter and its small letter, moving one letter forward each time. After Dd comes Ee.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 6, 14, 30, 62, ? (3)
f: Each term is double the previous plus 2: 62 x 2 + 2 = 126.
r: The terms are also 2^2 - 2, 2^3 - 2, ... so the next is 2^7 - 2 = 126.

q: Which word is formed by the alphabet positions 18, 5, 19, 20? (38)
f: Positions 18, 5, 19, 20 are R, E, S, T.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters, with Z at position 26.

q: Which number comes next: 99, 80, 63, 48, ?
f: Differences are -19, -17, -15, so next is -13: 48 - 13 = 35.
r: Tip: differences that fall by 2 each time form a second-order series.

q: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ? (2)
f: Gaps increase by 1: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6 (O → U).

q: Are the numbers 1, 3, 9, 11, 13 even or odd numbers?
f: Each of these numbers leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, so they are odd numbers.
r: Two is the only even prime number.

q: Which number comes next: 35, 19, 11, 7, ?
f: Differences are -16, -8, -4, so the next is -2: 7 - 2 = 5.
r: Tip: halving differences point to a pattern of repeated division by 2.

q: Find the next letter in the series: A, C, F, J, ?
f: Gaps between letters increase by one each time: A+2=C, C+3=F, F+4=J, J+5=O.

q: What letter comes next in the following series: J, H, F, D, ?
f: Each letter is 2 places before the previous one: J, H, F, D, then B.
r: Tip: going backward in the alphabet by a fixed step is as common as going forward.

q: What is the median of the series 2, 4, 6, 7, 9?
f: The numbers are already in order and there are five of them, so the middle (third) value is 6.
r: The mean is 28 / 5 = 5.6, which differs from the median.

q: Which letter comes next: R, M, I, F, ?
f: Positions are 18, 13, 9, 6 with differences -5, -4, -3. Next is -2: 6 - 2 = 4, which is D.
r: Tip: write letters as numbers; the differences shrink by one each time.

q: Which letter comes next in the following series: B, E, G, J, L, ?
f: The gaps alternate +3, +2: B to E is 3, E to G is 2, G to J is 3, J to L is 2, so L + 3 = O.
r: Tip: alternating gaps of 3 and 2 repeat; add the next gap in turn.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 6, 9, ?
f: Each number is 3 more than the one before. So 9 + 3 = 12.
r: This is the table of 3.

q: Write the next number in the series: 1, 4, 10, 22, 46, ?
f: Each term is double the previous term plus 2: 1, 4, 10, 22, 46, then 46 x 2 + 2 = 94.
r: Tip: if terms roughly double, test multiply by 2 and add a constant.

q: Which number comes next: 6, 12, 9, 16, 12, ?
f: Alternate terms form two series: 6, 9, 12 (adding 3) and 12, 16, 20 (adding 4). The next term is 20.
r: Tip: when numbers go up and down, split them into odd-position and even-position series.

q: What number comes next in the following series? 3, 5, 3/5, 7, 11, ?
f: The terms come in groups of three: the first two numbers and then their fraction (3, 5, 3/5), then (7, 11, 7/11).
r: Tip: mixed series of whole numbers and fractions are often built from repeating groups.

q: Which number is different from the others: 3, 5, 7, 11, 12, 13, 17, 19? (3)
f: All the numbers except 12 are prime numbers. 12 is divisible by 2, 3, 4 and 6.
r: 2 is the only even prime number.

q: Which number comes next: 105, 55, 160, 65, 225, 75, ?
f: The numbers at odd places (105, 160, 225) rise by 55, then 65, so the next rise is 75: 225 + 75 = 300. The other numbers (55, 65, 75) rise by 10 each time.
r: Such interleaved series are solved by separating the odd and even places.

q: Which letter comes next: Y, S, N, J, G, ?
f: Positions are 25, 19, 14, 10, 7. The differences are -6, -5, -4, -3, so next is -2: 7 - 2 = 5, which is E.
r: Tip: shrinking differences (6, 5, 4, 3, 2) are common in letter series.

q: Which number comes next: 2500, 500, 100, 20, ?
f: Each number is divided by 5: 2500, 500, 100, 20, then 20 / 5 = 4.
r: Tip: when numbers fall fast, test division before subtraction.

q: Which number comes next: 115, 55, 170, 65, 235, 75, ? (22)
f: Each big number is the previous big number plus the small number after it: 115+55=170, 170+65=235, 235+75=310.
r: The small numbers 55, 65, 75 increase by 10.

q: Which number comes next in the following: 2, 4, 5, 10, 11, 22, ?
f: The pattern is multiply by 2, then add 1: 2x2=4, 4+1=5, 5x2=10, 10+1=11, 11x2=22, 22+1=23.
r: Tip: if the numbers jump up and then up slightly, test alternating multiply and add.

q: Which number comes next: 3, 8, 14, 21, ?
f: The differences are 5, 6, 7, so the next difference is 8: 21 + 8 = 29.
r: Tip: when differences increase by 1, the series is built from consecutive added numbers.

f: The number 3 appears four times, more than any other value (2 and 5 appear twice).
r: The mode is the most frequent value in a data set.

q: Which letter comes next: E, G, J, N, ?
f: Positions are 5, 7, 10, 14 with differences +2, +3, +4. Next is +5: 14 + 5 = 19, which is S.
r: Tip: if the gaps grow by one each time, keep adding the next bigger gap.

q: Complete the series: J, H, F, D, ?
f: Back by 2 each time: J, H, F, D, B.
r: Same rule as H, F, D, B.

q: Which number comes next: 28, 19, 12, 7, ?
f: Differences are -9, -7, -5, so the next is -3: 7 - 3 = 4.
r: Tip: the differences decrease by 2 each time, a typical second-order series.

q: What will be the next number: 11, 21, 40, 77, 150, ?
f: The differences are 10, 19, 37, 73, and each difference is double the previous minus 1. The next difference is 145, so 150 + 145 = 295.
r: Tip: when each term is roughly double the previous, check for double plus or minus a small number.

q: Which number comes next? 27, 20, 14, 9, ?
f: The differences are 7, 6, 5, so the next difference is 4: 9 - 4 = 5.
r: Tip: for number series, check the differences, then the ratios, then alternating patterns.

q: Which number comes next: 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, ?
f: The steps alternate +1, +2, +1, +2, so after 7 comes 7 + 1 = 8.
r: Tip: repeating step cycles like +1, +2 are common.

q: Which number comes next: 2, 5, 9, 14, ?
f: The differences are 3, 4, 5, so the next difference is 6. 14 + 6 = 20.
r: When the differences increase by 1 each time, the series is quadratic.

q: What is the median of the data 2, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8? (4)
f: The data is already in order and has 9 values, so the median is the 5th value. The 5th value is 5.
r: The median is the middle value of ordered data, and for an even count it is the mean of the two middle values.

q: What comes next in the series: B, E, J, Q, ?
f: Letter positions are 2, 5, 10, 17 with gaps 3, 5, 7, so the next gap is 9: 17 + 9 = 26 = Z.
r: The gaps are consecutive odd numbers.

q: What letter comes next in the following series? E, J, N, Q, ?
f: The steps are +5, +4, +3, so the next step is +2: Q + 2 = S.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: Which letter comes next in the following series? A, H, N, S, W, ?
f: The letter positions are 1, 8, 14, 19, 23 with gaps 7, 6, 5, 4. The next gap is 3: 23 + 3 = 26, which is Z.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: How does the word MTVWVTM look when reflected in a mirror placed beside it (lateral reflection)? (2)
f: The letters M, T, V and W are each symmetrical about a vertical line, and the word reads the same from both ends. So its mirror image is identical.
r: Letters such as A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X and Y are symmetrical about a vertical axis.

q: Which word looks the same in a mirror?
f: T and I are symmetrical letters, and TITITIT reads the same from both sides, so its mirror image is the same word.
r: Letters that look the same in a mirror: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y.

q: Which word remains the same when reflected in a mirror (vertical mirror)? (6)
f: T, W and M are symmetrical about the vertical axis; S, R and Q are not.

q: Which of the letters A, H, I, W, M, O, T, U, Y look the same in a mirror (vertical mirror held beside the letter)? (10)
o: Only A, H, I and O
Only H, I, O and W
Only M, T, U and Y
f: Every one of these letters is symmetric about a vertical line, so each looks the same when reflected.
r: Letters like B, C, D, E and K are symmetric only about a horizontal line.

q: Aslam walks towards the east, after some time he turns left, and some steps later he turns right. In which direction is he now moving?
f: Facing east, a left turn makes him face north. Turning right from north makes him face east again.
r: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

q: Adnan walks 10 meters towards the north, then towards the south. After this he turns back and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
f: After walking south he faces south; turning back he faces north; turning left from north he faces west.
r: Turning back means a 180 degree turn; left of north is west.

q: A person walks 7 miles towards the north, then turns left, then turns left again. In which direction is he going now? (3)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. Turning left again from west makes him face south.
r: Two successive left turns make a total turn of 180 degrees.

q: A man going towards north turns left after some time, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing? (164)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west. A right turn from west makes him face north again.
r: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise and a right turn is 90 degrees clockwise.

q: Ali walks 10 km north, then turns left and then turns right. Which direction is he facing now? (2)
f: Facing north, a left turn makes him face west; a right turn from west brings him back to face north.
r: A left turn followed by a right turn cancels out.

q: Talha is moving towards the north and then turns right. In which direction is he facing now? (14)
f: Facing north, a right turn points him towards the east.
r: A left turn from north would point him to the west.

q: A man walks towards north, after some time turns right and then turns left. In which direction is he moving now? (56)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. A left turn from east makes him face north again.
r: A right turn followed by a left turn cancels out.

q: A man walks towards North, then turns left, then turns right. What is his present direction? (83)
f: North, left = West, right = North. The two opposite turns cancel.
r: Left then right (or right then left) brings you back to your first direction.

q: Adnan walks 10 metres towards North, then towards South. After this he turns back and then moves towards his left. What is his present direction?
f: He faces South, turns back so he faces North, then turns left: facing North, left is West.
r: 'Turn back' means a 180 degree turn.

q: A man walked 1 km towards south and then turned right and walked another 1 km, in which direction is he?
f: Facing south, his right hand points west, so after turning right he walks west.
r: Tip: facing south, right is west and left is east.

q: Adnan walks 10 meters towards the north, then walks towards the south. After this he turns back and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now?
f: After walking south he faces south. Turning back makes him face north. Turning left from north makes him face west.
r: Left of north is west and right of north is east.

q: A person walks 6 km towards the north, then turns right and walks some distance, then turns right again. Which direction is he now heading? (2)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Another right turn from east makes him face south.
r: Two right turns in a row always reverse the original direction.

q: Ahmad walks towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now? (18)
f: Facing north, the left hand side is west.
r: Facing north: left is west, right is east. Facing south: left is east, right is west.

q: A man walks 1 m north, turns right, walks 1 m and then turns back. In which direction is he facing now?
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east. Turning back reverses the direction, so he faces west.
r: Turning back means turning through 180 degrees.

q: A person walks 20 km north, then turns right, then left, then right again. In which direction is he now facing?
f: Facing north, a right turn gives east. A left turn then gives north, and a right turn again gives east.
r: A right turn moves clockwise by 90 degrees and a left turn moves anticlockwise by 90 degrees.

q: Ali moves towards North. After some time he turns left and then again turns left. What is his present direction? (102)
f: North, left = West, left again = South. Two left turns make a U-turn.
r: Two turns in the same direction (left-left or right-right) = facing the opposite way.

q: A man walks north, then turns left, then turns right. In which direction is he now facing? (8)
f: North → left = West → right = North again.

q: A man walked 10 m towards east and then 5 m to North and then 10 m towards West, how far is he from the starting point?
f: The east and west moves cancel, so only the 5 m north remains. He is 5 m from the start.
r: Tip: opposite movements cancel on each axis.

q: Ali is going in the direction of west. He turns left and then turns right. In which direction is Ali going now? (3)
f: Facing west, a left turn points him south. Then a right turn from south points him west again.
r: Facing west, his left is south and his right is north.

q: A man walked towards North, then turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction? (83)
f: From North a left turn faces West; a right turn from West faces North again.
r: A left turn and then a right turn cancel each other.

q: A man walks a few steps towards the north, then turns right and walks, and then turns right again. In which direction is he now going? (4)
f: Facing north, a right turn makes him face east; a second right turn makes him face south.
r: Two consecutive right turns always reverse the original direction.

q: A watch reads half past nine. The minute hand points toward North. In which direction does the hour hand point?
f: At half past nine the minute hand points to 6 and the hour hand lies between 9 and 10. If the minute hand (6) points North, the clock is turned half a turn, so the 9-10 position (about 3) points East.
r: Tip: turn the whole dial so that the minute hand matches the given direction, then read the hour hand.

q: Ahmad walks towards North and then turns left. What is his present direction?
f: When you face North, your left hand points West.
r: Facing North: right = East, left = West, behind = South.

q: Ahmad walks North, then turns left. In which direction is he now facing?
f: Turning left while facing North makes you face West.

q: Ali walks towards north, then turns left, and after some time turns left again. In which direction does he face now? (200)
f: North then left is west. A second left from west is south.
r: Candidates wrote North, but two left turns make a 180 degree turn.

q: A man walked towards the north, then he turned left. After some time he turned right. What is his present direction?
f: North, left turn gives west, right turn from west gives north again.
r: A left turn followed by a right turn cancel each other.

q: Ali walks towards the north, turns left and walks 5 m, then turns left again. In which direction is he facing now?
f: Facing north, a left turn gives west. Another left turn from west gives south.

q: Ali walks 4 meters towards the north and then turns left. In which direction is he facing now? (20)
f: A left turn from north points him to the west.
r: Anticlockwise order of directions is North, West, South, East.

q: A man travels towards the north and then turns to his left. In which direction is he now facing? (36)
f: Facing north, a left turn points to the west.
r: A right turn from north would point to the east.

q: A boy walks 10 miles north, turns back and walks 10 miles, then turns right and again turns right. Which direction is he facing now?
f: After turning back he walks south and faces south. Turning right from south he faces west, and turning right again he faces north.
r: A right turn is a 90 degree clockwise turn.

q: Your mother is my brother's sister. What is the relation between you and me? (256)
f: My brother's sister is my own sister, so your mother is my sister. Therefore I am your maternal uncle.
r: A mother's brother is called the maternal uncle (mamu in Urdu).

q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you (taking me as male)? (165)
f: My brother's sister is my sister, so your mother is my sister. I am therefore your mother's brother, that is your maternal uncle.
r: A mother's brother is called mamu in Urdu, and a father's brother is called chacha.

q: X and Y are brothers, B is A's brother but A is the mother of X, what is B to Y?
f: A is the mother of X and Y, and B is her brother, so B is the maternal uncle of Y.
r: Tip: your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mama).

q: If Ali is brother of the son of Salman's son, what relation is Ali to Salman?
f: Salman's son has a son, and Ali is that boy's brother, so Ali is also a son of Salman's son. That makes him Salman's grandson.
r: Tip: work from the innermost relation outwards.

q: My brother's sister is your mother. What am I to you? (4)
f: My brother's sister is my sister; she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother — your maternal uncle.

q: If my mother is your sister, what am I to you? (4)
f: Your sister is my mother, so I am her child, which makes me your sister's child, that is your nephew or niece.
r: The child of your brother is also your nephew or niece.

q: The sister of my brother's son is my what? (16)
f: My brother's son is my nephew; his sister is my brother's daughter, i.e. my niece.
r: A nephew is a brother's or sister's son; a niece is a daughter.

q: My mother is your brother's sister. What am I to you?
f: Your brother's sister is your sister, so my mother is your sister and I am your nephew.
r: Tip: in relation puzzles, translate each phrase into a simple relation one step at a time.

q: A is the father of B, but B is not A's son. What is B to A?
f: A child of a father who is not his son must be his daughter.
r: Read the 'not' carefully in relation questions.

q: If your mother is my sister, what am I to you?
f: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle (mamoon).
r: Your father's brother is your paternal uncle (chacha).

q: My sister is your mother. What is your relation to me?
f: You are my sister's child, so you are my nephew (boy) or niece (girl).
r: Sister's son = nephew, sister's daughter = niece.

q: The sister of my brother is your mother. What is your relation to me?
f: My brother's sister is my sister (taking me as male), and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother and you are my nephew or niece.
r: Your mother's brother is your maternal uncle; his children's relation to you is cousin, and you are his nephew or niece.

q: What is the sister of my brother's son to me? (7)
f: My brother's son's sister is my brother's daughter, who is my niece.
r: Brother's or sister's son is a nephew; daughter is a niece.

q: Akmal and Jamal are brothers, Anjum and Ajmal are their sons. What is the relation between Anjum and Ajmal?
f: Anjum and Ajmal are sons of two brothers, so they are cousins.
r: Fact: children of two brothers are called paternal cousins.

q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you (taking me as a male)?
f: My brother's sister is also my sister, and she is your mother, so I am your mother's brother, your maternal uncle.
r: Mother's brother is Mamu; father's brother is Chacha.

q: Which statement is correct? A. A son is always better educated than his father, B. A son is always more healthier than his father, C. A son is always younger than his father, D. A son is always less tall than his father, E. A son is always wiser than his father
o: A son is always better educated than his father
A son is always more healthier than his father
A son is always younger than his father
A son is always less tall than his father
A son is always wiser than his father
f: A father is by definition born before his son, so the son is always younger. The other statements may be true sometimes but not always.
r: Tip: the word always makes a statement false if there is even one exception.

q: If my brother's sister is your mother, who am I to you?
f: My brother's sister is my sister. My sister is your mother, so I am your mother's brother: your (maternal) uncle.
r: Mother's brother = maternal uncle (Mamun).

q: Saleem is 12 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old is his sister?
f: Sister's age = 3 x 12 = 36 years.
r: Her age is 24 years more than Saleem's age.

q: Nazar is 2/3 times younger than his elder brother. His brother Rab Nawaz is 21 years old, what is the age of Nazar?
f: Nazar's age is 2/3 of 21 = 14 years.
r: Tip: 7 is one third of 21 and 14 is two thirds, so read the fraction carefully.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Adil is 15 years old? (3)
f: Sister is 15 now, 10 years older than Adil. When Adil is 15, she is 25.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 11?
f: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ali needs 8 more years to reach 11, so she will be 9 + 8 = 17.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same over time.

q: Ali's age is 5 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be his sister's age when Ali is 20?
f: Sister's age now = 3 x 5 = 15, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 20, she will be 20 + 10 = 30.
r: The age difference between two persons always stays the same.

q: Ali is 4 years old and Ahmad is twice his age. What will Ahmad's age be when Ali is 15?
f: Ahmad is 8 when Ali is 4, so he is 4 years older. When Ali is 15, Ahmad is 15 + 4 = 19.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali becomes 8? (2)
f: Sister's age now is 5 x 3 = 15. Ali gains 3 years (8 - 5), so she is 15 + 3 = 18.
r: Both people grow older by the same number of years.

q: Ahmed is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. When Ahmed is 14 years old, what will be his sister's age?
f: Sister's age now is 6 x 3 = 18 years, so she is 12 years older than Ahmed. When Ahmed is 14, she is 14 + 12 = 26.
r: In age problems the difference in ages stays fixed while both ages increase equally.

q: Akbar is 3 times as old as his sister. How old will his sister be when Akbar is 15 years old?
f: Akbar's age is 3 times his sister's age, so sister = 15 divided by 3 = 5 years.
r: In ratio questions, divide the larger age by the multiple to get the smaller age.

q: Ali is 10 years old and he is twice as old as his sister. How old will his sister be after 20 years?
f: His sister is 10 divided by 2 = 5 years old now. After 20 years she will be 5 + 20 = 25.
r: The age difference between two people never changes with time.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ali is 8 years old? (4)
f: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 years now, so the gap is 8 years. When Ali is 8, sister is 8 + 8 = 16 years.
r: Multiplying the new age by 3 (24) is a common mistake, as the gap stays fixed.

q: Sidra is 6 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old will her brother be when Sidra becomes 11?
f: Brother is 6 x 2 = 12 now. Sidra becomes 11 after 5 years, so the brother will be 12 + 5 = 17.
r: The age gap between two people always stays the same.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is four times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 10?
f: Sister is now 4 x 5 = 20. Ali needs 5 more years, so she will be 20 + 5 = 25.

q: Ali's age is 10 and his sister Aisha is double his age. When Ali is 15, how old will Aisha be?
f: Aisha is 20 now. Ali will be 15 after 5 years, so Aisha will be 20 plus 5 = 25.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: Ali is 6 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old is his sister?
f: Sister's age = 3 x 6 = 18 years.
r: Here times as old means multiply.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will be her age when Ali is 11 years old? (24)
f: Sister's age now = 2 x 5 = 10 years. Ali gets 6 years older, so she will be 10 + 6 = 16 years.
r: The difference of 5 years between them never changes.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib died?
f: Abdul Muttalib died when the Prophet (PBUH) was 8 years old. He was 6 when his mother died and about 12 on the Syria trip, so the other options are wrong.
r: After Abdul Muttalib, his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 8 years old? (2)
f: When Ali is 3, Sara is 3 x 3 = 9, so Sara is 6 years older than Ali. The age gap stays the same, so when Ali is 8, Sara is 8 + 6 = 14.
r: The difference between two people's ages never changes with time.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister Sidra is twice his age. When Ali is 11, how old will Sidra be?
f: Sidra is 5 × 2 = 10 now. Ali reaches 11 after 6 more years, so Sidra will be 10 + 6 = 16.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister Sidra is twice his age. How old will Sidra be when Ali is 11 years old?
f: Sidra is 10 now, so she is 5 years older than Ali. When Ali is 11, Sidra is 11 + 5 = 16.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: How old was Fatima Jinnah when she died in 1967?
f: Fatima Jinnah was born in July 1893 and died on 9 July 1967, so she was 73. She is known as Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: Ali is 3 years older than his brother. What will be Ali's age when his brother is 11 years old?
f: The age gap stays 3 years. When the brother is 11, Ali is 11 + 3 = 14 years.
r: In age problems, the difference in ages never changes with time.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 10 times his age. What will be Ali's age after 12 years?
f: Ali is 4 now, so after 12 years he will be 4 + 12 = 16 years old.
r: His sister's age after 12 years would be 40 + 12 = 52 years.

q: What is the age required to be qualified as a member (and so to become Speaker) of the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: Under Article 62 and 51 of the 1973 Constitution, a person must be at least 25 years old to be a member of the National Assembly, and the Speaker is elected from its members.
r: A person must be at least 35 years old to be elected President.

q: Akram is 3 times as old as Zahra, whose age is 4 years. What will be Akram's age after 22 years?
f: Akram's age now is 3 x 4 = 12 years. After 22 years he will be 12 + 22 = 34 years.
r: Always find the present age first, then add the number of years.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is twice his age. When Ali becomes 8 years old, how old will his sister be? (2)
f: Sister is 2 x 4 = 8 years now. Ali needs 4 more years to be 8, so sister will be 8 + 4 = 12.
r: The age difference between two people never changes.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he migrated from Makkah to Madinah?
f: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE. Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was approximately 53 years old at the time of his migration to Madinah.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) passed away in Madinah at about 63 years of age.

q: Ali's sister is 3 times as old as Ali. How old will Ali's sister be when Ali becomes 14 years old?
f: Sister's age = 3 times Ali's age = 3 x 14 = 42 years.
r: Here the sister is the older one, so multiply Ali's age by 3.

q: Umer is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. How old will his sister be when Umer is 9?
f: The sister is 6 now, so she is 3 years older than Umer. When Umer is 9, she will be 9 + 3 = 12.
r: The age difference between two people stays the same for life.

q: Salman is 4 years old and Ali is twice Salman's age. When Salman is 12, what will be Ali's age?
f: Ali is 8, so he is 4 years older. When Salman is 12, Ali is 12 + 4 = 16. 24 wrongly doubles 12.
r: Twice the age is true only today; the gap of 4 years stays.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is 4 times older than him. How old is his sister? (2)
f: 4 × 4 = 16 years.

q: Aliza is 12 years older than Asad. When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 times his age. How old will Aliza be when Asad is 14? (2)
f: When Asad was 6, Aliza was 3 x 6 = 18, so the gap is 18 - 6 = 12 years, which never changes. When Asad is 14, Aliza is 14 + 12 = 26.
r: The age gap between two people stays the same all their lives.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is three times his age. How old will the sister be when Ali is 10 years old?
f: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now. Ali needs 6 more years to reach 10, so the sister will be 12 + 6 = 18.

q: Ali is 4 years old and his sister is double his age. What is his sister's age?
f: Double of 4 is 2 x 4 = 8, so the sister is 8 years old.
r: The difference in their ages is 4 years and it always stays the same.

q: Saleem is 3 years old and his sister is three times as old as him. How old will his sister be when Saleem is 12?
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now, so she is 6 years older than Saleem. When he is 12, she will be 12 + 6 = 18.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: How old was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when his grandfather Hazrat Abdul Muttalib passed away? (76)
f: Abdul Muttalib took care of the Prophet (PBUH) after his mother died and passed away when the Prophet was 8 years old. Afterwards his uncle Abu Talib became his guardian.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) lost his mother Hazrat Amina at the age of 6.

q: Ali and Farooq are brothers. Ali is three times as old as Farooq, and Farooq is now 4 years old. How old will Farooq be when Ali is 13 years old?
f: Ali's age now = 3 x 4 = 12. Ali will be 13 after 1 year, when Farooq will be 4 + 1 = 5.
r: The difference between their ages always stays 8 years.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister Sara is 3 times his age. How old will Sara be when Ali is 15 years old? (2)
f: When Ali is 3, Sara is 9, so she is 6 years older. When Ali is 15, Sara is 15 + 6 = 21.
r: The age gap of 6 years stays fixed for life.

q: Ahmed is 10 years old and his brother is 5. What will his brother's age be after 3 years?
f: 5 + 3 = 8 years.

q: When Ali was 3, his sister's age was four times his age. How old is Ali's sister when Ali is 12? (2)
f: When Ali was 3 his sister was 12, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 12 she is 12 + 9 = 21.
r: The age difference between two people stays constant over time.

q: The age of Ali is 6 years and Sara is three times as old as Ali. What will Ali's age be after 6 years? (2)
f: Ali is 6 now, so after 6 years he will be 6 + 6 = 12. Sara's age does not matter for this question.
r: Sara is currently 18 years old.

q: Sidra is 5 years old and her brother is twice her age. How old is her brother?
f: Twice her age is 2 x 5 = 10 years. So the brother is 10 years old.
r: The age difference between them is 5 years.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the Harb al-Fijar?
f: Traditional accounts say he was about 15 (some say 14-20) at Harb al-Fijar.
r: It was a series of pre-Islamic tribal conflicts. He did not fight as a main combatant. Note: Reports vary on exact age; 15 is the commonly given figure.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his grandfather Abdul Muttalib passed away? (2)
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born around 570 CE and lost his mother at age 6. His grandfather Abdul Muttalib, who then cared for him, died when he was about 8.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is twice his age. What will his sister's age be when Ali is 12 years old? (3)
f: The sister is 2 x 3 = 6 when Ali is 3, so she is 3 years older. When Ali is 12, she is 12 + 3 = 15.
r: Age problems are solved by keeping the fixed age difference.

q: Ahmed is 3 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. How old will his sister be when Ahmed is 9? (3)
f: The sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old now. Ahmed becomes 9 after 6 years, so she will be 9 + 6 = 15 years.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 6 years).

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when his mother died?
f: His mother Hazrat Amina died at Abwa when he was about six years old.
r: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib then took care of him.

q: A brother is 5 years old and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when the brother is 12? (4)
f: The sister is 3 x 5 = 15 years old now. The brother becomes 12 after 7 years, so the sister will be 15 + 7 = 22.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

q: Umar's age is 4 years and his sister is three times his age. What will be the sister's age when Umar is 11 years old? (3)
f: Sister is 3 x 4 = 12 now, so she is 8 years older than Umar. When Umar is 11, she is 11 + 8 = 19.
r: After 7 years both ages increase by 7, so 12 + 7 = 19.

q: The age of Ahmad is three times the age of his sister, and his sister is 4 years old. What will Ahmad's age be after 10 years?
f: Ahmad is 3 x 4 = 12 years old now. After 10 years he will be 12 + 10 = 22 years old.
r: Age problems are solved by first finding the present age, then adding the years.

q: Ali is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will be the age of his sister when Ali is 10 years old? (2)
f: The sister is 15 now, so she is 10 years older than Ali. When Ali is 10, she is 20.
r: The age difference stays constant.

q: Aslam was 28 years old in 1945. How old will he be in 1965? (2)
f: From 1945 to 1965 is 20 years, so his age is 28 + 20 = 48.
r: Age problems come down to adding the difference in years.

q: Ali's sister is three times Ali's age. If Ali is 3 years old, how old will his sister be when Ali is 7 years old?
f: Sister is 3 x 3 = 9 years old when Ali is 3. The age gap is 6 years, so when Ali is 7 she is 7 + 6 = 13.
r: The difference between two people's ages always stays the same.

q: Ahmed is 5 years old and Sara is three times his age. How old will Sara be when Ahmed is 11? (2)
f: Sara is 3 x 5 = 15 now. Ahmed becomes 11 after 6 years, so Sara will be 15 + 6 = 21.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same.

q: Ali is 3 years old and his sister is 4 times his age. When Ali is 8 years old, what will his sister's age be? (2)
f: Sister's age now = 4 x 3 = 12 years, so she is 9 years older. When Ali is 8 she will be 8 + 9 = 17 years.
r: Solve age questions by finding the fixed difference first.

q: Adil is 5 years old and his sister is 3 times his age. What will the age of his sister be when Adil is 15 years old? (3)
f: The sister is now 3 x 5 = 15 years old. Adil needs 15 - 5 = 10 more years, so the sister will be 15 + 10 = 25.
r: The age difference between two people always stays the same (here 10 years).

q: What was the age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of Hijrat to Madinah?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) received the first revelation at 40 and spent 13 years preaching in Makkah, so he migrated at 53. 63 was his age at death, and 50 was his age in the Year of Grief.
r: Hijrat took place in 622 AD; Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) was with him in Cave Thawr.

q: If 15th of February in a leap year is Sunday, then what will be the 15th of the next month?
f: February has 29 days in a leap year, so 15 March is 29 days later. 29 = 4 x 7 + 1, so it is one day after Sunday, which is Monday.
r: Tip: a leap year has 366 days and a February with 29 days.

r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same day of the week.

q: If yesterday was Friday, what day will be the day after tomorrow? (636)

r: Days: shift by the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 (going back in the month means subtract the remainder).

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Monday, what day will the 19th of that month be? (2)

r: A week has 7 days, so the same weekday repeats every 7 days of the month.

q: If yesterday was Monday, what day will be the day after tomorrow?

q: If the 3rd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 23rd be? (4)

r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 2nd day of a month is Friday, what day will the 15th be? (2)

q: If the 4th day of a month is Monday, what day will the 20th of that month be?
