f: From the 12th to the 26th is 14 days. 14 days is 2 full weeks plus 0 day(s), so the day is 0 day(s) after Friday, which is Friday.
r: Dates that are 7 days apart always fall on the same weekday, so only the remainder after dividing the gap by 7 matters.

q: If the 7th day of a month is Friday, what day will the 21st day of that month be?
f: From the 7th to the 21st is 14 days, which is exactly two weeks. After whole weeks the day stays the same, so it is Friday.
r: Dates that differ by a multiple of 7 always fall on the same weekday.

q: If 2200 hours is 10 o'clock in the evening then write the answer as 4, and if not then write 5.
f: 2200 hours in the 24-hour clock is 22 - 12 = 10 in the evening, so the statement is true and the answer is 4.
r: Tip: for 24-hour times after 1300, subtract 12 to get the pm hour.

q: What is 5 o'clock in the afternoon in 24-hour time? (4)
f: For afternoon hours add 12: 5 + 12 = 17, so 5 PM is 1700 hours.
r: Military time uses the 24-hour clock from 0000 to 2359.

q: Time on Ali's watch is quarter to three. If the hour hand is pointing towards east, then where is the minute hand pointing?
f: At quarter to three the hour hand is almost at 3 and points east, while the minute hand is at 9, exactly opposite, so it points west.
r: Tip: the 3 and 9 on a clock face are opposite each other.

q: In 24-hour (military) time, how is 5 o'clock in the evening written?
f: In 24-hour time, add 12 to PM hours: 5 PM = 17:00 = 1700 hours.
r: 5 o'clock in the morning is written as 0500 hours.

q: If clock A goes faster than clock B and clock C keeps time with clock A, then: A. C is slower than B, B. B keeps time with C, C. C is faster than B, D. B may be faster or slower than C, E. B and C keeps time with A
o: B may be faster or slower than C
B and C keeps time with A
f: C keeps the same time as A, and A is faster than B, so C is faster than B.
r: Tip: replace equal items with each other and the comparison carries over.

q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3 PM? (12)
f: At 3 o'clock the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3. Three hour marks of 30 degrees each make 90 degrees.
r: Each hour mark on a clock face is 30 degrees apart.

q: Usman is older than Khalid, and Khalid is older than Kadir. Who is the eldest? (4)
f: Usman is older than Khalid and Khalid is older than Kadir, so the order is Usman, Khalid, Kadir.
r: Such ordering problems are solved by writing the persons in a line from oldest to youngest.

q: Ammar is older than Amjad, and Ali is younger than Ammar. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Ammar is older than both Amjad and Ali, so Ammar is the oldest.
r: The order of Amjad and Ali cannot be known from this information.

q: Amjad is taller than Asif, Akram is taller than Amjad. Who is the shortest?
f: Akram is taller than Amjad, who is taller than Asif, so Asif is the shortest.
r: Tip: write the names in order of height to see the shortest.

q: If the second of the following numbers is added to the shortest number and divided by the third number, what will the answer be? 2, 14, 4
f: Second number 14 plus shortest number 2 is 16. Dividing by the third number 4 gives 4.
r: Tip: identify the numbers by position first (first, second, third), then apply the operations in order.

q: Akbar is taller than Akmal, and Akmal is taller than Ali. Which statement is correct?
o: Akmal is taller than Ali but shorter than Akbar
f: The order of height is Akbar, then Akmal, then Ali. So Akmal is in the middle.
r: Such questions are solved by arranging the persons in order.

q: Which cricketer scored 13,000 runs in One Day Internationals in 2023, doing it faster than anyone before? (2)
f: Virat Kohli reached 13,000 ODI runs in September 2023 against Pakistan in the Asia Cup. He took only 267 innings, the fastest ever.
r: Sachin Tendulkar reached 13,000 ODI runs in 321 innings, which was the earlier record.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmed and Bilal is younger than Akbar. Who is the oldest of the three? (2)
f: Akbar is older than both Ahmed and Bilal, so he is the oldest.
r: Comparison questions are easiest with a line of names from oldest to youngest.

q: If Akram is taller than Saeed and Saeed is shorter than Kazim, may Kazim be as tall as Akram?
f: Both Akram and Kazim are taller than Saeed, but nothing says Kazim cannot match Akram, so it is possible.
r: Tip: may be asks whether something is possible, not certain.

q: Anwar is older than Ali, and Aslam is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest of the three?
f: Anwar is older than Ali and Ali is older than Aslam, so the order from oldest is Anwar, Ali, Aslam.
r: Aslam is the youngest of the three.

q: Who was the first person to fly faster than the speed of sound? (2)
f: US Air Force pilot Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier on 14 October 1947 flying the Bell X-1 rocket plane.
r: The speed of sound at sea level is about 1,235 km/h, called Mach 1.

q: If Akram is older than Kamal and Hamid is younger than Kamal but Amjad is older than Hamid, who is the youngest?
f: Hamid is younger than Kamal and Amjad, and Kamal is younger than Akram, so Hamid is the youngest.
r: Tip: write the names in a line from oldest to youngest to check ranking questions.

q: If Ahmed is older than Kamal and Kamal is younger than Imran, then Ahmed is:
f: Both Ahmed and Imran are older than Kamal, but Ahmed and Imran are not compared directly.
r: Tip: two people both above a third cannot be ranked against each other.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Aslam. Ahmad is younger than Aslam. Which statement is true?
o: Aslam is older than Ahmad and younger than Akbar
f: Akbar is older than both. Ahmad is younger than Aslam, so the order from oldest is Akbar, Aslam, Ahmad.
r: In ordering questions, write the names in a line from oldest to youngest to avoid mistakes.

q: Ali is older than Waqas, and Usman is younger than Waqas. Who is the oldest of the three? (4)
f: Ali is older than Waqas and Waqas is older than Usman, so the order from oldest is Ali, Waqas, Usman.
r: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a single line of order.

q: If A is as tall as D, C is shorter than A, B is taller than D, then: A. A is taller than B, B. C is as tall as D, C. B may be taller or shorter than C, D. C is shorter than D, E. B is shorter than A
o: C is as tall as D
B may be taller or shorter than C
f: A and D are equal in height and C is shorter than A, so C is shorter than D. Also B is taller than D, so B is taller than A as well.
r: Tip: substitute equal items and chain the comparisons.

q: Ali is shorter than Umar and Umar is shorter than Abdullah. What is the relation of Ali and Umar?
o: Ali and Umar are of equal height
f: The first statement says directly that Ali is shorter than Umar.
r: From both statements, Abdullah is the tallest and Ali is the shortest of the three.

q: Bakar is older than Ali and Umair is younger than Ali. Which statement is correct? (2)
f: Bakar is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Umair, so the order is Bakar, Ali, Umair. Bakar is the oldest and Umair the youngest.
r: Such questions are solved by arranging the names in a line from oldest to youngest.

q: If Arza is older than Munir and Munir is younger than Javaid, then Arza is:
f: Munir is below both Arza and Javaid, but nothing links Arza and Javaid directly, so their order cannot be known.
r: Tip: two people both older than a third cannot be compared with each other.

q: Akbar is older than Khalid and Ahmed is younger than Khalid. Which statement is true? (16)
f: The order from oldest is Akbar, Khalid, Ahmed. So Akbar is older than Ahmed.
r: Chaining two comparisons gives a third one.

q: If Aslam is taller than Hafeez and Hafeez is shorter than Mani, then Aslam is the tallest:
f: We know Aslam is above Hafeez and Mani is above Hafeez, but Aslam and Mani are not compared, so we cannot tell who is tallest.
r: Tip: a conclusion is certain only if every comparison needed is stated in the premises.

q: Akbar is older than Zarnab, and Ali is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
f: Ali is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Zarnab, so the order from oldest is Ali, Akbar, Zarnab. Zarnab is the youngest.
r: Ranking questions are solved by placing the names in a single line from oldest to youngest.

q: If Imran is older than Waseem and Kaleem is younger than Imran, which of the following statements is true?
o: Waseem and Kaleem are of equal age
f: Imran is older than both Waseem and Kaleem, so he is the oldest. The relative ages of Waseem and Kaleem are not known.
r: Tip: only accept statements that follow from the facts given.

q: Ali is older than Hammad but younger than Amir. Hammad is younger than Amir. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Amir is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Hammad. So the order from oldest is Amir, Ali, Hammad, and Hammad is the youngest.
r: In such questions, draw the people in a line from oldest to youngest.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the eldest? (24)
f: Umair is older than Akbar, and Akbar is older than Ahmad. So the order is Umair, Akbar, Ahmad and Umair is the eldest.
r: Chain the comparisons to rank all persons.

q: Ali was born in 1974 and Azhar was born in 1970. Bilal is 2 years younger than Azhar. In which year was Bilal born?
f: Younger by 2 years means born 2 years later, so Bilal was born in 1970 + 2 = 1972.
r: Born later means younger; born earlier means older.

q: Frank is taller than John, and Ralph is taller than Frank. Who is the shortest?
f: Order: Ralph > Frank > John, so John is the shortest.
r: Write the names in one line from tallest to shortest to solve ranking questions.

q: If Ahmad is older than Akbar and Akbar is older than Ali, then Ali is ____.
f: The order of age is Ahmad, then Akbar, then Ali, so Ali is the youngest. Therefore Ali is younger than Ahmad (and Akbar).
r: Such statements can be solved by writing the names in order from oldest to youngest.

q: Akbar is taller than Ali and Usman is shorter than Ali. Who is the tallest of the three?
f: Akbar is taller than Ali, and Ali is taller than Usman, so the order is Akbar, Ali, Usman. Akbar is the tallest.
r: Chain comparisons like this are solved by writing the names in order from greatest to least.

q: The speed of sound is faster than the speed of light:
f: Light travels at about 300,000 km per second, while sound in air travels at only about 343 metres per second.
r: Tip: this is why you see lightning before you hear thunder.

q: Kamal is older than Jamal, Jamal is older than Hussain, Hussain is older than Waqar. Who is the oldest? (3)
f: The order is Kamal, Jamal, Hussain, Waqar from oldest to youngest.
r: Tip: write the names in a line from oldest to youngest to check ranking questions.

q: Ali is younger than Hassan and Akbar is younger than Ali. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
f: Hassan is older than Ali, who is older than Akbar, so Hassan is the oldest and Akbar the youngest.
r: Ali is in the middle, so he is neither the oldest nor the youngest.

q: Ali is shorter than Bilal. Umer is taller than Ali but shorter than Bilal. Who is the tallest?
f: Ali < Umer < Bilal, so Bilal is tallest.

q: Akbar was born in 1970 and Ammar in 1977. Bilal is older than Ammar. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Bilal is older than Ammar, so Ammar is younger than Bilal. Ammar (1977) is also younger than Akbar (1970), so Ammar is the youngest.
r: A later birth year means a younger person.

q: Ali is younger than Ahmad, and Yaqoob is older than Ahmad. Who is the youngest?
f: Order: Yaqoob > Ahmad > Ali, so Ali is the youngest.
r: Younger than the middle person who is himself younger than the oldest = youngest.

q: Ali is older than Kashif and Kashif is older than Haris. Who is the oldest and who is the youngest?
f: Ali is older than Kashif, who is older than Haris, so Ali is the oldest and Haris the youngest.
r: Such ordering questions are solved fastest by writing the names in a single line from largest to smallest.

q: Akbar and Khalid were born in 1970 and 1975 respectively, and Ikram is older than Khalid. Who is the youngest of the three?
f: Khalid (1975) is younger than Akbar (1970), and Ikram is older than Khalid. So Khalid is younger than both and is the youngest.
r: In age puzzles, a later birth year means a younger person.

q: Akbar was born in 1980 and Aslam in 1987. Bilal is elder than Aslam but younger than Akbar. What is the order from eldest to youngest?
f: Akbar (1980) is eldest and Aslam (1987) is youngest. Bilal is younger than Akbar and elder than Aslam, so he is in the middle.

q: Ali is taller than Osama and Osama is taller than Faheem. Who is the tallest of all? (3)
f: Ali is taller than Osama, who is taller than Faheem, so Ali is the tallest.
r: Faheem is the shortest in this chain.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the youngest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Ahmad is the youngest.
r: The person who is older than nobody in the chain is the youngest.

q: If Ali is older than Usman and Noman is older than Ali, who is the eldest?
f: Noman is older than Ali, and Ali is older than Usman, so the order is Noman, Ali, Usman.
r: Usman is the youngest of the three.

q: Azhar was born in 2000 and Javed in 2005. Aslam is older than Javed but younger than Azhar. Who is the oldest?
f: The person born first is the oldest. Azhar (2000) is older than Aslam, and Aslam is older than Javed (2005).
r: Earlier year of birth = older person.

q: Akbar is older than Ahmad, and Umair is older than Akbar. Who is the oldest?
f: Umair is older than Akbar, who is older than Ahmad, so Umair is the oldest.
r: Chain comparisons can be written as a single ordered line.

q: Arrange the jumbled word OPERALD to form a word and identify its category.
f: OPERALD rearranges to LEOPARD, a big wild cat.
r: The leopard is a member of the big cat family.

q: What is the last letter of the word BEAUTY? (40)
f: B-E-A-U-T-Y ends with the letter Y.
r: BEAUTY has six letters.

q: Arrange the letters AGRMYNE to form the name of a country.
f: The letters A, G, R, M, Y, N, E can be rearranged to spell GERMANY, a country in Europe.
r: The capital of Germany is Berlin.

q: According to the dictionary order, which word comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
f: All start with M; the second letters A, A, O put Mountain last. Between MACHINE and MARGALLA, C comes before R, so Machine is first.
r: Dictionary order compares letter by letter from the left.

q: Rearrange NMERGAY to form the name of a country.
f: NMERGAY → GERMANY.

q: Arrange BROTHER in alphabetical order and then indicate the letter left of the middle letter.
f: In alphabetical order it is B, E, H, O, R, R, T. The middle (4th) letter is O and the letter to its left is H.
r: Tip: with 7 letters the middle is the 4th.

q: Which letter in the word PRODUCTION lies as far from the beginning of the word as it is from the beginning of the alphabet?
f: D is the 4th letter in PRODUCTION (P, R, O, D) and also the 4th letter of the alphabet.
r: Tip: check each letter position against its alphabet number.

q: Which would be the middle letter if the letters of the word SUBORDINATE are arranged in an alphabetical order?
f: The 11 letters in order are A, B, D, E, I, N, O, R, S, T, U. The 6th (middle) letter is N.
r: Tip: for 11 items the middle one is the 6th.

q: After arranging the letters of SIRAP, it becomes the name of a country, city, ocean or state. Which one is it?
f: The letters of SIRAP rearrange to PARIS, the capital city of France. So it is a city.
r: Anagram questions: look for a familiar name first, then check that every letter is used.

q: What will be the last letter of UTYEAB after arranging its letters alphabetically? (41)
f: Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.
r: Letters of the alphabet end with Z; Y is the later of the letters U, T, E, A, B, Y.

q: Re-arrange the letters ARTGN and find the middle letter.
f: ARTGN rearranges to GRANT, whose middle (third) letter is A.
r: Tip: unscramble the word first, then count to the centre.

q: Rearrange PRAIS to form the name of a city.
f: PRAIS rearranges to PARIS (the capital of France).

q: What is the third letter when “MANAGEMENT” is arranged alphabetically?
f: MANAGEMENT sorts as A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T, so the third letter is E.
r: Sort repeated letters too.

q: Rearrange the letters of LEAPORD to make the name of an animal. (3)
f: The letters L, E, A, P, O, R, D can be arranged to spell LEOPARD, which is a big cat.
r: The leopard is a big cat known for its spotted coat.

q: Arrange the letters YEBATU into a meaningful word. (14)
f: The letters Y, E, B, A, T, U rearrange to BEAUTY.
r: BEAUTY has 6 letters, of which E, A and U are vowels.

q: Rearrange the jumbled letters 'EBAUYT' to make a meaningful English word.
f: The six letters E, B, A, U, Y, T can be arranged to spell BEAUTY.
r: Beauty is a noun meaning the quality of being pleasing to the eye or mind.

q: What will be the 3rd letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 3rd letter is E.
r: AUGMENTED has 9 letters, with E repeated twice.

q: If the letters EAUTYB are rearranged into a meaningful word, what is its last letter?
f: EAUTYB rearranges to BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
r: The first letter of BEAUTY is B.

q: Arrange the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order. Which is the 3rd letter? (74)
f: The letters in order are A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The third letter is E.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter will come last? (82)
f: Alphabetical order of the letters is A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
r: Y is the 25th letter of the English alphabet.

q: Rearrange the letters E T W A R to make a word. What is the second last letter of that word?
f: The letters form the word WATER. Its letters are W, A, T, E, R so the second last letter is E.
r: Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen, and its formula is H2O.

q: Arrange the letters of MANAGEMENT alphabetically. Which is the 3rd letter? (4)
f: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T → 3rd letter is E (3rd last letter of the word is also E).

q: Arrange the letters of BEAUTY alphabetically. Which letter comes last? (10)
f: Alphabetical order: A, B, E, T, U, Y → last is Y.

q: Write the 4th letter before W, as counted from the end of the alphabet.
f: Going back from W: V, U, T, S, so the 4th letter before W is S.
r: Tip: the letter 4 places before W (23rd) is the 19th letter, S.

q: After rearranging the letters of the word UEABYIFT, what is the last letter of the new word? (2)
f: The letters make the word BEAUTIFY, which ends with Y.
r: BEAUTIFY means to make something beautiful.

q: If the letters of the word ARGUMENT are arranged in alphabetical order, which letter is third? (3)
f: The letters of ARGUMENT in alphabetical order are A, E, G, M, N, R, T, U. The third letter is G.
r: ARGUMENT has 8 letters and 3 vowels: A, U and E.

q: Arrange these words alphabetically: beauty, leopard. Which comes first?
f: B comes before L in the alphabet, so beauty comes first and leopard second.
r: Dictionary order compares words letter by letter from the left.

q: Rearrange the letters BUYAET to form a word. What is the last letter of the word?
f: The letters BUYAET form the word BEAUTY, which ends with the letter Y.
r: Unscrambling words is a common verbal intelligence question.

q: NECESSARY CUSTOM TO TRADE ROAD DEVELOPMENT. If one word is omitted from the above, the others could be arranged as one sentence. Write the second letter of the word to be omitted.
f: Without the word CUSTOM the rest forms the sentence 'Road development necessary to trade'. CUSTOM has U as its second letter.
r: Tip: try dropping each word in turn and see which remaining set makes a sensible sentence.

q: Rearrange the letters IAPRS to form a word. What does the word name? (12)
f: The letters I, A, P, R, S rearranged give PARIS, the capital of France.
r: Paris stands on the River Seine.

q: Arrange the letters of PLOEADR to make the name of an animal. (16)
f: The letters P, L, O, E, A, D, R make the word LEOPARD, a big cat. It uses all seven letters once.
r: The leopard is a spotted big cat found in Asia and Africa.

q: Which letter comes first alphabetically among the letters of the word MOTHER?
f: The letters of MOTHER in alphabetical order are E, H, M, O, R, T, so the first is E.
r: Tip: write out the letters in alphabetical order to find the first or last.

q: If the following are arranged in order of size, what would come in the middle? A. Book, B. Word, C. Chapter, D. Sentence, E. Paragraph
f: In increasing order: word, sentence, paragraph, chapter, book. The middle one is paragraph.
r: Tip: sort the full list first, then pick the centre item.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary? (62)
f: Compare the third letter: Addidas has d, which comes before i in Adiabatic, Adjust (j) and Adit (i).
r: Dictionary order compares letters from left to right.

q: Arrange the letters 'IYTC' to form a meaningful word.
f: Rearranging I, Y, T, C gives the word CITY.
r: An anagram uses all the given letters exactly once.

q: According to the dictionary, which comes first: MOUNTAIN, MARGALLA, MACHINE?
f: All start with M. Second letters: A, A, O. Then third letters: C (MACHINE) comes before R (MARGALLA).
r: Compare letter by letter until they differ.

q: What will be the second letter when AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically?
f: Arranged: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U. The 2nd letter is D. (The PDF wrote E, which is the 3rd letter.)
r: AUGMENTED has the letters A, U, G, M, E, N, T, E, D.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: back, racket, biscuit?
f: Words are arranged by their first letter: b comes before r. Between back and biscuit, the second letters a and i decide it, and a comes first, so the order is back, biscuit, racket.
r: If the first letters are the same, compare the second letter, then the third, and so on.

q: Rearrange the letters PEOLARD to form a correct English word. (10)
f: The letters P, E, O, L, A, R, D rearrange to make LEOPARD, a big cat.
r: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, and it is a strong climber.

q: If the letters BEYTUA are rearranged to make a correct word, what is the last letter of that word? (92)
f: The letters rearrange to BEAUTY, whose last letter is Y.
r: Beauty is a six-letter English word and the scrambled form BEYTUA uses exactly the same letters.

q: Rearrange the letters PHELTANE to make the name of an animal.
f: PHELTANE has the letters E, L, E, P, H, A, N, T, which spell ELEPHANT. Antelope, Panther and Leopard need letters (like O, R, D) that are not in PHELTANE.

q: Rearranging the letters AGREMYN gives the name of which country?
f: The letters A, G, R, E, M, Y, N can be arranged to spell GERMANY, using all seven letters exactly once.
r: Berlin is the capital of Germany.

q: In the word MANAGEMENT, arranged alphabetically, which letter is second last? (30)
f: Alphabetical order is A A E E G M M N N T. The last letter is T and the second last is N.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters, with A, E, M and N each appearing twice.

q: Rearrange the letters RAPIS to form the name of a famous capital city. Which city is it, and of which country is it the capital? (16)
f: The letters R, A, P, I, S rearrange to make PARIS. Paris is the capital of France.
r: Paris stands on the River Seine and is the capital of France.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word Managment when its letters are arranged alphabetically? (37)
f: Letters of Managment: A, A, E, G, M, M, N, N, T in alphabetical order, so the 3rd letter is E. The source answer G is wrong (G is 4th). The same answer E applies to the correctly spelled MANAGEMENT.
r: Write the letters in order, keeping repeated letters, and count carefully.

q: How many letters of the word CENTRAL are also found in the word DISCOVER?
f: DISCOVER contains C, E and R from CENTRAL; N, T, A and L are missing. So the answer is 3.
r: Tip: check each letter of the first word against the second, one by one.

q: After arranging the letters of the word MANAGEMENT in alphabetical order, which letter is the third from the last? (28)
f: MANAGEMENT has the letters M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. In alphabetical order: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. Counting from the end: T (1st), N (2nd), N (3rd), so the third letter from the last is N.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters: A, E, M and N appear twice each.

q: Which word comes first in dictionary order?
f: Comparing letters left to right, 'Aca' comes before 'Acc', 'Acq' and 'Act'.
r: Dictionary order compares words letter by letter from the left.

q: Rearrange the letters RSPAI to get the name of a city. (10)
f: The letters R, S, P, A, I rearrange to PARIS.
r: Paris is the capital of France, on the river Seine.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its different letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Different letters in order: A, E, G, M, N, T. The 3rd is G. (If every letter is counted, including repeats, the 3rd letter would be E.)
r: Read whether the question counts repeated letters.

q: Arrange E, H, M, O, R, T into a word.
f: E, H, M, O, R, T make the word MOTHER.
r: Jumbled-word questions usually make a common word.

q: Which word comes first alphabetically in a dictionary: Adidas or Addida? (2)
f: Both words start with AD. The third letter of Addida is D and of Adidas is I, and D comes before I, so Addida comes first.
r: Dictionaries compare words letter by letter from the left until the first difference.

q: What is the 2nd letter of the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet runs A, B, C, so the second letter is B.
r: The English alphabet has 26 letters.

q: If the letters of the word BEAUTY are written in reverse order, which is the last letter?
f: BEAUTY reversed is YTUAEB, so the last letter is B.
r: The first letter of the reversed word is Y.

q: The jumbled word UTYEAB is rearranged to form a word. What will be the last letter of that word when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: UTYEAB forms BEAUTY. Alphabetical order is A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last letter is Y.
r: Y is the 25th letter of the alphabet, the highest letter in this word.

q: What will be the last letter of UTYEAB after arranging it alphabetically?
f: Arranged: A, B, E, T, U, Y. The last letter is Y.
r: Write the letters in A to Z order before answering.

q: What will be the third letter when the word AUGMENTED is arranged alphabetically? (24)
f: Alphabetical order: A, D, E, E, G, M, N, T, U; the third letter is E.
r: Write the letters in order and count carefully; repeated letters count twice.

q: Which word comes first in the dictionary: False, Fallow, Faithful, Fallable, Falcon?
f: All words begin with Fa. The third letters are i (Faithful), l (the rest), so Faithful comes first. Then Falcon, Fallable, Fallow and False follow.
r: Dictionary order compares letters one by one from the left.

q: Arrange the letters of the word SAID in alphabetical order.
f: The letters are S, A, I, D. In alphabetical order they are A, D, I, S, so the word is ADIS.
r: Alphabetical order follows A to Z, so D comes before I and I before S.

q: Rearrange PARDLEO to make an animal. (10)
f: PARDLEO → LEOPARD.

q: Rearrange the letters of CHIKARA to make the name of a city. Which city is it?
f: The letters C H I K A R A can be arranged to spell KARACHI.
r: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.

q: Which word is made by arranging the letters POEARLD? (12)
f: The letters P, O, E, A, R, L, D can be rearranged to spell LEOPARD, using all seven letters.
r: The leopard is a big cat found in Africa and Asia, including northern Pakistan.

q: Which letter comes first in alphabetical order in the word MANAGEMENT? (3)
f: The letters of MANAGEMENT are M, A, N, A, G, E, M, E, N, T. Arranged alphabetically they begin with A, so A comes first.
r: Arranged fully, the word becomes A A E E G M M N N T.

q: What will be the 3rd letter of the word MANAGEMENT when its letters are arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted letters: A, A, E, E, G, M, M, N, N, T. The 3rd letter is E.
r: MANAGEMENT has 10 letters with A, E, M and N each repeated twice.

q: What is the last letter when “UTYEAB” is arranged alphabetically?
f: Sorted alphabetically the letters are A, B, E, T, U, Y, so the last is Y.
r: Alphabetical order puts Y after U and T.

q: Father is to son as mother is to ____.
f: A father and his male child are father and son. In the same way a mother and her female child are mother and daughter.
r: Analogy questions test the same relationship in both pairs.

q: Ring is to finger as watch is to what?
f: A ring is worn on the finger and a watch is worn on the wrist.
r: Analogy questions test the relation of an object to the body part where it is worn.

q: Train is to track as bus is to?
f: A train runs on a track and a bus runs on a road. Both pairs show a vehicle and the path it travels on.
r: Tip: in analogy questions state the relationship in a sentence, then apply it to the second pair.

q: Brain is to think as heart is to:
f: The brain's function is thinking; the heart's function is pumping blood.

q: Tobacco is to Pipe as Coal is to:
f: Tobacco is burned in a pipe, and coal is burned in an oven.
r: Tip: the relation is a material and the container or device where it is burned.

q: If London is to Thames then Lahore is to ____?
f: The River Thames flows through London and the River Ravi flows by Lahore.
r: Tip: the five rivers of Punjab are Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej.

q: Sky is to Earth as Ceiling is to:
f: The sky is above the earth; a ceiling is above the floor, so the pairing matches.
r: Tip: in analogies, state the relationship in a sentence first (above / below, part / whole) and then apply it.

q: WHEN is to TIME as WHERE is to:
f: WHEN asks about time and WHERE asks about place, which is SPACE.
r: Tip: question words map to concepts: when is time, where is place or space.

q: Complete the analogy: Man is to wallet as woman is to ____.
f: A man carries money in a wallet and a woman usually carries it in a purse.
r: Analogy questions test the relation between the first pair.

q: Cold is to ice as hot is to
f: Very cold water becomes ice; very hot water becomes steam.
r: Water boils at 100 degrees C and freezes at 0 degrees C.

q: Solve the proportion 8 : 4 :: X : 16. What is X? (2)
r: The ratio 8 : 4 simplifies to 2 : 1.

q: RED is to BLOOD as WHITE is to:
f: Blood is red and milk is white, so the pairing is an object and its colour.
r: Tip: this is a colour-association analogy.

q: POUND is to WEIGHT as METER is to:
f: Pound is a unit of weight and meter is a unit of length.
r: Tip: for unit analogies, ask what each unit measures.

q: SICK is to SACK as LICK is to:
f: SICK changes its vowel I to A to make SACK, so LICK becomes LACK.
r: Tip: in word analogies compare the letters one by one to find which letter changes.

q: HAPPINESS is to 415537299 as SHAPE is to:
f: From HAPPINESS = 415537299: H=4, A=1, P=5, I=3, N=7, E=2, S=9. SHAPE is S9 H4 A1 P5 E2, which is 94152.
r: Tip: build the letter table from the long word first.

q: Bird is to nest as human is to:
f: A nest is a bird's home; a house is a human's home.

q: Rough is to smooth as crude is to what? (32)
f: Rough and smooth are opposites, so the opposite of crude (unrefined) is polished (refined).
r: Crude oil is oil that has not yet been refined.

q: CLOCK is to DAY as CALENDAR is to:
f: A clock tracks the hours of a day, and a calendar tracks the days of a year.
r: Tip: a clock tracks the day, a calendar tracks the year.

q: SHELLS is to 251442 as LESS is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: Complete the analogy: Sailor is to Navy as Airman is to ____.
f: A sailor serves in the Navy, in the same way an airman serves in the Air Force.
r: Soldier, sailor and airman are the ranks-and-file terms for the Army, Navy and Air Force.

q: If a 20 feet long wire is to be cut so that one piece is 2/3 as long as the other piece, how long will be the shorter piece?
f: The pieces are in the ratio 2:3, so there are 5 parts in total, and each part is 20 / 5 = 4 feet. The shorter piece is 2 x 4 = 8 feet.
r: Tip: turn a ratio of 2 to 3 into 5 equal parts of the total.

q: NARROW is to WIDE as THIN is to:
f: Narrow and wide are opposites, and the opposite of thin is fat.
r: Tip: first decide whether the relation is synonym or antonym.

q: RACKET is to 314582 as CRATE is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: Flower is to fragrance as food is to:
f: A flower is known for fragrance; food for taste.

q: Foot is to knee as hand is to what? (12)
f: The knee is the main joint of the leg above the foot, and the elbow is the main joint of the arm above the hand. So hand is to elbow.
r: The elbow joins the upper arm to the forearm.

q: WHEEL is to BICYCLE as LEG is to:
f: A wheel is a part of a bicycle, and a leg is a part of the body.
r: Tip: LEG is also a part of a TABLE, so use the body-part sense for the closest match here.

q: Water is to ice as milk is to what? (4)
f: Ice is the solid form obtained from water, and cheese is the solid product obtained from milk.
r: Cheese is made by curdling milk and separating the solid curds from the whey.

q: Ink is to pen as blood is to:
f: Ink flows in a pen; blood flows in veins.

q: Cat is to Kitten as Dog is to?
f: A kitten is the young one of a cat, and a puppy is the young one of a dog.
r: Tip: animal-to-young analogies use the special word for the young of that animal (calf, lamb, cub).

q: NORTH is to SOUTH as EAST is to:
f: South is the direct opposite of north, and west is the direct opposite of east.
r: Tip: the four opposite pairs of compass directions are north and south, east and west.

q: Pakistan is to Islamabad as Japan is to ...?
f: Islamabad is the capital of Pakistan, and in the same way Tokyo is the capital of Japan.
r: Kyoto was the old imperial capital of Japan until 1868.

q: Nib is to Pen as Blade is to?
f: A nib is the writing part of a pen, and a blade is the cutting part of a knife.
r: Tip: this is a part-to-whole analogy.

q: If A is to E then C is to?
f: A to E is a jump of 4 letters (A=1, E=5), so C (3) plus 4 gives G (7).
r: Tip: convert letters to positions to find a fixed jump.

q: 1/3 is to 9 as 1/2 is to:
f: 1/3 becomes 9, which is the square of its reciprocal (3 squared). The reciprocal of 1/2 is 2, and 2 squared is 4.
r: Tip: try squares, cubes and reciprocals for pairs that link a fraction to a whole number.

q: MAN is to MASCULINE as WOMAN is to:
f: Masculine is the adjective for a man and feminine is the adjective for a woman.
r: Tip: match the type of word, here an adjective.

q: NEAR is to FAR as CLOSE is to:
f: Far is the opposite of near, and open is the opposite of close (shut).
r: Tip: close can mean near or shut; the first pair tells you to use the antonym of the word.

q: Finger is to hand as leaf is to what? (4)
f: A finger is a part attached at the end of the hand, just as a leaf is a part attached to a branch.
r: Analogy questions are solved by finding the relationship between the first pair and applying it to the second.

q: IRON is to HEAVY as FEATHER is to:
f: Iron is a heavy material, and a feather is light.
r: Tip: this analogy links an object to its typical quality.

q: INFANCY is to CHILDHOOD as ADOLESCENCE is to:
f: Stages of life follow in order: infancy, childhood, adolescence, then youth.
r: Tip: the sequence of human life stages is infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, old age.

q: EYE is to SEE as NOSE is to:
f: The eye is the organ used to see, and the nose is the organ used to smell.
r: Tip: the pattern is organ and its function.

q: List is to Last as Fist is to?
f: List becomes Last by changing the vowel I to A, so Fist becomes Fast.
r: Tip: when the words look alike, compare letter by letter to find which letter changes.

q: CLOCK is to TIME as THERMOMETER is to:
f: A clock is an instrument that measures time, and a thermometer measures temperature.
r: Tip: the pattern is instrument and the quantity it measures.

q: 63 is to 9 as 71 is to?
f: 63 gives 9 as the sum of its digits (6 + 3 = 9). So 71 gives 7 + 1 = 8.
r: Tip: the digit-sum relation is common in number analogies.

q: SEEING is to PICTURE as HEARING is to:
f: We see a picture and we hear a song, so the object of hearing is a SONG.
r: Tip: the pattern is sense and the object it perceives.

q: Dog is to bitch as horse is to what? (7)
f: A bitch is the female dog; the female horse is a mare.
r: A male horse is called a stallion and a young horse a foal.

q: Find the missing number in the analogy 2 : X :: 4 : 16.
f: Since 4 : 16 shows that 16 is the square of 4 (4 x 4 = 16), the same rule applies to 2, so X = 2 x 2 = 4.
r: Square numbers are 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 and so on.

q: COMPARE is to 7324615 as OPERA is to?
r: Tip: build a letter-to-digit table from the given word first.

q: Triangle is to Prism as Circle is to?
f: A prism is the three-dimensional solid built from a triangle, and a sphere is the solid form of a circle.
r: Tip: 2D-to-3D analogies pair a flat shape with its solid.

q: Fish is to swimming as Snake is to:
f: Fish swim; a snake crawls (it moves along the ground without legs).
r: Tip: this is an animal-and-movement analogy; match the animal to its typical way of moving.

q: HERE is to NOW as THERE is to:
f: HERE refers to place and NOW refers to time at the same point. THERE refers to a place, so its matching time word is THEN.
r: Tip: place and time words often pair up: here/now, there/then, where/when.

q: EF is to DG as JK is to?
f: E-1 = D and F+1 = G. Apply the same to JK: J-1 = I and K+1 = L.
r: Tip: letters moving outward from the centre form a mirror-like pair pattern.

q: LOCAL is to 51325 as CALL is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: FOUR is to ELEVEN as THREE is to?
f: FOUR means 4 and ELEVEN means 11, which is 7 more. THREE means 3, and 3 + 7 = 10, which is TEN.
r: Tip: convert number words into numbers before looking for the rule.

q: ARMY is to SOLDIER as NAVY is to: (2)
f: A soldier serves in the army and a sailor serves in the navy.
r: Tip: in this analogy the second word is the ordinary member of the first.

q: Tail is to ANIMAL as Beak is to:
f: A tail is a body part of an animal and a beak is a body part of a bird.
r: Tip: part-to-whole analogies pair a body part with the creature that has it.

q: DARK is to NIGHT as DAY is to:
f: Darkness is associated with night, and light is associated with day.
r: Tip: this is a characteristic-of analogy.

q: HEAR is to EAR as CLOSE is to:
f: Removing the first letter of HEAR gives EAR, and removing the first letter of CLOSE gives LOSE.
r: Tip: check for hidden words made by dropping a letter.

q: STONE is to HARD as COTTON WOOL is to:
f: A stone is characterised by being hard, and cotton wool by being soft.
r: Tip: in analogies, name the quality that links the first pair.

q: FINGER is to ELBOW as TOE is to:
f: The elbow is the joint in the middle of the arm, and the knee is the matching middle joint of the leg.
r: Tip: map the arm to the leg to find the matching joint.

q: Gun is to bullet as pitcher is to ___.
f: A gun fires a bullet, and in baseball a pitcher throws a ball. The relationship is a tool or person to the object it sends.
r: A bat is used by the batter to hit the ball.

q: If 6 : m :: 9 : 12, what is m?
f: Proportion gives 6/m = 9/12, so m = 6 x 12 / 9 = 8.
r: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (a x d = b x c).

q: BEGIN is to END as NORTH is to:
f: Begin and end are opposites, and the opposite direction of north is south.
r: Tip: the four cardinal directions form two opposite pairs: north and south, east and west.

q: Boy is to girl as horse is to what?
f: A girl is the female of a boy; the female of a horse is a mare.
r: A young horse is a foal.

q: Beauty is to ugliness as diversity is to what? (2)
f: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of diversity (variety) is uniformity.
r: Variety, difference and range are close in meaning to diversity.

q: CLOSE is to OPEN as NEAR is to:
f: CLOSE and OPEN are opposites, so the opposite of NEAR is FAR.
r: Tip: first name the relationship (opposite, synonym, part of) in the first pair, then apply it to the second.

q: RECEDE is to PROCEED as STOP is to:
f: Recede and proceed are opposites, and the opposite of stop is go.
r: Tip: recede means to move back, and proceed means to move forward.

q: Ship is to captain as car is to what? (2)
f: A captain is the person who controls a ship. In the same way a driver controls a car.
r: A pilot controls an aircraft.

q: STUN is to NUTS as POTS is to?
f: NUTS is STUN written backwards, so POTS reversed is STOP.
r: Tip: spelling a word backwards often produces another real word.

q: Tree is to branches as river is to:
f: Branches spread out from a tree, and canals are channels taken off a river. This matches the answer key (a delta could also be argued).
r: Tip: when two options seem close, pick the one that fits the relationship in the first pair most directly.

q: DINNER is to NIGHT as MORNING is to:
f: Dinner is the meal eaten at night, and breakfast is the meal eaten in the morning.
r: Tip: the pair is meal and time of day.

q: CATERING is to 21436895 as GREAT is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: CLEAR is to DIM as NEAT is to:
f: CLEAR and DIM are opposites, so we need the opposite of NEAT, which is DIRTY.
r: Tip: when a pair is opposites, pick the antonym and reject synonyms like TIDY.

q: Girl is to boy as woman is to what?
f: A girl is a young female and a boy is a young male. In the same way a woman is an adult female and a man is an adult male.
r: Analogy questions test the same relationship in both pairs, here female and male.

q: TRIANGLE is to PRISM as CIRCLE is to:
f: A prism is a triangle extended into three dimensions with the same cross-section, and a cylinder is a circle extended the same way.
r: Tip: the key sheet gives sphere here, but a prism has constant triangular cross-sections just as a cylinder has circular ones.

q: Tomorrow is to Yesterday as Thursday is to?
f: Yesterday is two days before tomorrow, so the matching day is two days before Thursday, which is Tuesday.
r: Tip: count the day gap in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: SPHERE is to CIRCLE as CUBE is to: A. Cuboid, B. Angle, C. Square, D. Point, E. None
f: A sphere is the three-dimensional form of a circle, so the matching two-dimensional form of a cube is a square.
r: Tip: the question prints SRHERE, which is a typing error for SPHERE.

q: Airplane is to Air as Whale is to:
f: An airplane travels in air, and a whale lives and travels in the ocean.
r: Tip: in analogies, name the relation (here: moving thing and its medium) and apply it to the second pair.

q: Completely is to what, as a synonym? Choose the word closest in meaning to 'entirely'. (24)
f: Entirely means in every part or fully, the same as completely.
r: Wholly and totally are also synonyms.

q: SOW is to SEED as REAP is to:
f: We sow seed, and we reap the crop.
r: Tip: GRAIN is only one kind of crop, so CROP is the best match for the pair.

q: BIRD is to CAGE as PRISONER is to:
f: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in a cell.
r: Tip: the pattern is captive and the place where it is kept.

q: ABD is to CBA as QRT is to?
f: ABD to CBA: first letter +2 (A to C), middle letter unchanged (B), last letter -3 (D to A). Apply this to QRT: Q+2 = S, R stays R, T-3 = Q, giving SRQ.
r: Tip: compare each letter position separately to find the shift for that position.

q: FISH is to SWIM as BIRD is to:
f: A fish moves by swimming, and a bird moves by flying.
r: Tip: this is an animal and its mode of movement.

q: Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to?
f: A bird is kept in a cage, and a prisoner is kept in jail.
r: Tip: the relation is 'confined living thing and its place of confinement'.

q: If Light is to Eye, then Sound is to?
f: The eye senses light, and the ear senses sound.
r: Tip: sense-organ analogies pair a stimulus with the organ that detects it.

q: Bird is to Cage as Prisoner is to: A. Chains, B. Court, C. Freedom, D. Cell, E. Police
f: A bird is kept in a cage and a prisoner is kept in a cell.
r: Tip: this is an object and its place of confinement.

q: A is to E as C is to:
f: A is the 1st letter and E is the 5th, so we move forward 4 places. C is the 3rd, and 3 + 4 = 7, which is G.
r: Tip: count the number of places between the first pair and repeat the same jump.

q: Tight is to Loose as Hard is to: (2)
f: Loose is the opposite of tight, so the opposite of hard is soft.
r: Tip: if the first pair are opposites (antonyms), choose the opposite of the third word.

q: Sky is to blue as blood is to what?
f: The sky is blue in colour and blood is red in colour, so the analogy is by colour.
r: Haemoglobin in red blood cells gives blood its red colour.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as clock is to what? (18)
f: Wheels are a part of a vehicle, and hands are a part of a clock.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: If Shoe is to Foot then Helmet is to ____.
f: A shoe is worn on the foot and a helmet is worn on the head.
r: Tip: in analogies, first state the relationship (here, worn on) and then apply it to the second pair.

q: Past is to present as preceding is to: (4)
f: Past and present are opposites, and the opposite of preceding is following.
r: Preceding means coming before.

q: Boat is to water as aeroplane is to what?
f: A boat moves through water, and an aeroplane moves through air, the medium it travels in.
r: Analogy questions test the same relation in both pairs.

q: BAIT is to FISH as GUN is to:
f: Bait is the thing used to catch a fish, and a bullet is the thing fired from a gun to hit a target.
r: Tip: this analogy links a tool to what it is used to capture.

q: Definitely is to absolutely as totally is to what? (10)
f: Definitely and absolutely are synonyms, so the synonym of totally is entirely.
r: In analogy questions first find the relationship (here synonyms) and then apply it.

q: OPEN is to CLOSE as FAR is to:
f: Open and close are opposites, and the opposite of far is near.
r: Tip: check whether an analogy is about opposites or about synonyms.

q: If L is to 1, T is to 2, E is to 3, R is to 4, add up the digits for the word LETTER, divide the total by 5 and give the result as your answer.
f: LETTER = L1 + E3 + T2 + T2 + E3 + R4 = 15, and 15 divided by 5 = 3.
r: Tip: write each letter's value under it before adding.

q: Pakistan is to Asia as England is to what?
f: Pakistan is a country in the continent Asia, and England is a country in the continent Europe.
r: England is part of the United Kingdom.

q: Son is to father as nephew is to what? (2)
f: A son is the child of his father, and a nephew is the child of the brother or sister of an uncle or aunt, so the relation is nephew to uncle.
r: The female counterpart of a nephew is a niece.

q: If sow is to seed then reap is to?
f: A farmer sows seed and reaps the crop, so the object that matches seed is crop.
r: Tip: in analogies the second word of the pair is the thing acted upon; sow acts on seed, reap acts on crop.

q: SINGLE is to DOUBLE as ONE is to:
f: SINGLE means one and DOUBLE means two, so the number matching ONE in the pair is TWO.
r: Tip: the pair moves from a count to the next count.

q: NORTH is to 51398 as THORN is to:
r: Tip: in coding questions, first write down the letter-to-digit table from the given word, then re-read it for the new word.

q: If 18:00 o'clock is to 6 o'clock, then 14:00 o'clock is to ____ o'clock.
f: 18:00 on the 24-hour clock is 6 on a 12-hour clock (18 - 12). Likewise 14:00 is 2 o'clock.
r: Tip: subtract 12 from any 24-hour time after 12:00 to get the 12-hour time.

q: DERANGE is to 4371563 as GRAND is to:
r: Tip: build the letter-digit table first, then translate the new word.

q: Solve the proportion 2 : x :: 14 : 28. What is x?
f: In a proportion the product of extremes equals the product of means: 2 x 28 = x x 14. So 56 = 14x and x = 4.
r: A proportion a : b :: c : d means a/b = c/d.

q: DARE is to 4172 as READ is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: Speak is to hear as look is to what?
f: Speaking is matched by hearing, and looking is matched by seeing, the result received.
r: Hearing is the sense of the ear and seeing is the sense of the eye.

q: Watch is to time as barometer is to what? (3)
f: A watch measures time and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
r: A thermometer measures temperature and an anemometer measures wind speed.

q: HIGH is to LOW as COWARD is to:
f: High and low are opposites; the opposite of coward is brave.
r: Tip: the opposite of coward is brave, whereas strong is a different quality.

q: Sheep is to wool as cat is to what?
f: Wool is the covering that grows on a sheep, and fur is the covering that grows on a cat.
r: Wool is obtained by shearing sheep.

q: P is to L as N is to?
f: P is the 16th letter and L is the 12th, which is 4 places back. N is the 14th, and 4 places back is J (10).
r: Tip: letter analogies depend on the fixed jump between the first pair.

q: SMEAR is to 31247 as REAMS is to:
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: Vehicle is to wheels as Sound is to ? (2)
f: A vehicle moves by means of wheels, and sound travels by means of waves.
r: Sound cannot travel in a vacuum because it needs a medium for its waves.

q: BOOK is to TITLE as MAN is to:
f: A book is identified by its title, and a man is identified by his name.
r: Tip: this pair links a thing to the label that identifies it.

q: MILE is to LAND as KNOT is to:
f: A mile is a unit of distance used on land, and a knot is a unit of speed used at sea.
r: Tip: one nautical mile equals 1.852 km, and a knot is one nautical mile per hour.

q: Vehicle is to road as ship is to ___ ? (36)
f: A vehicle travels on a road, and a ship travels on the sea. The analogy links a vehicle or vessel with the surface it moves on.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: If 9 : m :: 2 : 8, find the value of m. (2)
r: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means.

q: AGREED is to 157224 as GEARED is to:
r: Tip: repeated letters, like the two E's, must give the same digit.

q: Even is to Uneven as Violent is to: A. Aggressive, B. Friendly, C. Responsible, D. Sadest, E. Unkind
f: Even and uneven are opposites, so we need the opposite of violent, and friendly (gentle) is the best match. Aggressive and unkind are similar to violent.
r: Tip: identify whether the first pair is synonyms or antonyms.

q: 6 is to F as 11 is to? A. K, B. L, C. M
f: F is the 6th letter of the alphabet, so the pair is number to its letter. The 11th letter is K.
r: Tip: remember A=1, E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20 and Z=26 as quick anchors.

q: TIME is to EMIT as 4375 is to?
f: EMIT is TIME written backwards, so reverse 4375 to get 5734.
r: Tip: a reversal pattern applies equally to letters and digits.

q: 2 is to 5 as K is to?
f: The step from 2 to 5 is +3. Moving 3 letters on from K (L, M, N) gives N.
r: Tip: when numbers and letters are mixed, apply the same step to both.

q: OCTOBER is to NOVEMBER as SUNDAY is to:
f: November is the month that follows October, and Monday is the day that follows Sunday.
r: Tip: time-sequence analogies usually ask for the next item in the cycle.

q: Find X: 3 : X :: 4 : 12
f: The ratio 4:12 equals 1:3, so 3:X must also be 1:3. Therefore X = 3 x 3 = 9.
r: In a proportion a:b :: c:d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).

q: Book is to cover as picture is to what?
f: A cover goes around and protects a book, in the same way a frame goes around and holds a picture.
r: Analogy questions depend on finding the relation between the first pair and applying it to the second.

q: TRIP is to DAY as CALENDAR is to:
f: A trip is measured in days, and a calendar is measured in a year.
r: Tip: this is a unit-of-measure analogy; match the unit that the object covers.

q: Grass is to ground as chimney is to what? (2)
f: Grass grows on the ground, in the same way a chimney stands on top of the roof of a house.
r: A chimney carries smoke from a fireplace or furnace out of the building.

q: Engine is to Car as Cell is to:
f: An engine powers a car, and a cell (battery) powers a torch.
r: Tip: this analogy links a power source to the device it runs.

q: Car is to wheel as clock is to what? (62)
f: A wheel is a part of a car, and hands are a part of a clock.
r: Analogy questions: find the relationship in the first pair and apply it to the second.

q: Sweet is to sour as cold is to:
f: Sweet and sour are opposites, and the opposite of cold is hot.
r: Tip: check whether an analogy is about opposites or about synonyms.

q: HIGH is to LOW as BAD is to:
f: HIGH and LOW are opposites, and the opposite of BAD is GOOD.
r: Tip: EVIL is a synonym of BAD, not the opposite.

q: DEAL is to 7345 as LEAD is to:
f: D=7, E=3, A=4, L=5. LEAD is L, E, A, D = 5, 3, 4, 7, which gives 5347.
r: Tip: in word-code questions, write the code letter under each letter, then re-use the same mapping for the new word.

q: Horse is to mare as dog is to what?
f: A mare is a female horse. The female dog is called a bitch.
r: A young dog is a puppy.

q: Hand is to Touch as Nose is to?
f: The hand is the organ of touch, and the nose is the organ of smell.
r: Tip: the five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch, each tied to one organ.

q: Easy is to Light as Rough is to:
f: Easy and light both mean not hard or heavy to deal with, and rough is closest to hard (a rough surface feels hard and coarse). The paper's answer key gives Hard.
r: Tip: when the analogy is not obvious, look for the option that is the antonym of the third word.

q: FOOT is to LEG as HAND is to:
f: The foot is attached to the leg, and the hand is attached to the arm.
r: Tip: this is a body-part connection analogy.

q: Hen is to chicken as cow is to what?
f: A chicken is the young one of a hen, and a calf is the young one of a cow.
r: A lamb is the young of a sheep, a foal of a horse and a kid of a goat.

q: Bright is to Dim as Clear is to?
f: Dim is the opposite of bright, and vague is the opposite of clear.
r: Tip: antonym analogies: find the opposite of the third word in the answer options.

f: 2/4 is reduced to its simplest ratio 1:2, so 18/24 in simplest form is 3:4.
r: Tip: divide top and bottom by their highest common factor, here 6.

q: Shoe is to foot as helmet is to what?
f: A shoe is worn to protect the foot, and a helmet is worn to protect the head.
r: This is a type of analogy based on an object and the body part it protects.

q: ADVANCE is to FORWARD as INCREASE is to:
f: Advance and forward are synonyms, and the synonym of increase is raise.
r: Tip: decide whether the first pair is synonyms or opposites before choosing.

q: Finger is to Hand as Toe is to?
f: A finger is a part of the hand, and a toe is a part of the foot.
r: Tip: part-to-whole analogies are solved by naming the whole that holds the part.

q: Beauty is to ugliness as adversity is to what?
f: Ugliness is the opposite of beauty, and the opposite of adversity (hardship) is prosperity.
r: Hardship, misfortune and difficulty are synonyms of adversity, not opposites.

q: December is to October as June is to?
f: December is two months after October in reverse, so go two months back: June gives April.
r: Tip: count the months in the first pair and apply the same step.

q: MEDICAL is to 5132768 as DECIMAL is to:
f: From MEDICAL = 5132768: M=5, E=1, D=3, I=2, C=7, A=6, L=8. DECIMAL is D3 E1 C7 I2 M5 A6 L8, which gives 3172568.
r: Tip: write the letter-to-digit code under the first word, then read off the second word letter by letter.

q: BOTTLE is to CORK as BOX is to:
f: A cork closes a bottle, and a lid closes a box.
r: Tip: this is an object and its closing part.

q: Hot is to Burn as Cold is to?
f: Excessive heat makes things burn, and excessive cold makes things freeze.
r: Tip: this is a cause-and-effect analogy; ask what the extreme does.

q: Water is to flow as Air is to ?
f: Water flows and air blows.
r: Moving air is called wind.

q: Hospital is to patient as school is to:
f: A hospital serves patients; a school serves students.

q: Carpenter is to wood as mason is to:
f: A carpenter works with wood; a mason works with bricks/stone.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. STVU, B. HIJK, C. IJKL, D. OPQR, E. EFGH
f: The others are four consecutive letters of the alphabet. STVU has the order S, T, V, U, which is not consecutive.
r: Tip: look for a swapped or skipped letter.

q: Which is different in the following: Speech, Lecture, Oration, Sermon, Gossip?
f: Speech, lecture, oration and sermon are formal talks given to an audience, while gossip is casual talk about other people.
r: Tip: formal versus informal is a common basis for odd-one-out questions.

q: Which one is different from others: Selfish, Dishonest, Foolish, Ugly?
f: Selfish, dishonest and foolish describe character or behaviour, while ugly describes physical appearance.
r: Tip: separate qualities of character from qualities of looks.

q: Which one is different from the rest? QS, EH, IL, MP, AD
f: In EH, IL, MP and AD the second letter is 3 places after the first. In QS the gap is only 2.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Hot, B. Steam, C. Water, D. Ice, E. Vapour
f: Steam, water, ice and vapour are forms of water. Hot is only a quality.
r: Tip: water exists as solid (ice), liquid and gas (steam or vapour).

q: Find the odd one out: January, March, Friday, November
f: All others are months; Friday is a day.

q: Which one of the following is different from others?
f: Salmon, crab, shark and whale are all specific sea animals, while Fish is the general category name. This follows the answer key (whale is also not a true fish).
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Green, B. Red, C. Dark, D. Yellow, E. Brown
f: Green, red, yellow and brown are colours. Dark describes shade, not a particular colour.
r: Tip: dark and light are shades that can apply to any colour.

q: Find the odd one out: Cow, goat, horse, buffalo.
f: Cow, goat and buffalo are ruminants that are kept for milk, but the horse is not a ruminant and is mainly used for riding and work.
r: Ruminants chew the cud and have a stomach with four chambers.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. DBC, B. MLK, C. ONM, D. CBA, E. ZYX
f: MLK, ONM, CBA and ZYX are each three consecutive letters in backward order. DBC is not in a consecutive order.
r: Tip: check whether groups of letters run forwards or backwards.

q: Which is different from the rest: Donkey, Zebra, Horse, Giraffe?
f: Donkey, zebra and horse all belong to the horse family (Equidae), while the giraffe belongs to a different family.
r: The giraffe is the tallest land animal.

q: Which one is the odd man out: Socrates, Handel, Beethoven, Mozart? (2)
f: Handel, Beethoven and Mozart were famous composers of music. Socrates was a Greek philosopher.
r: Socrates was the teacher of Plato, who was the teacher of Aristotle.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Month, B. Season, C. Year, D. Day, E. Week
f: Month, year, day and week are fixed units of time measured by the calendar. A season is a part of the year with a particular climate and has no fixed number of days.
r: Tip: the four seasons are summer, autumn, winter and spring.

q: Which one is different from the rest: September, May, March, Tuesday?
f: September, May and March are months of the year, while Tuesday is a day of the week.

q: My book is different ___ yours.
f: The standard phrase is 'different from'.
r: 'Different to' is used in British casual speech.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Little, B. Rare, C. Less, D. Inferior, E. Few
f: Little, rare, less and few all refer to small quantity or amount. Inferior refers to lower quality.
r: Tip: separate words about quantity from words about quality.

q: Which one is different from the others: Ship, Bus, Train, Car, Truck?
f: Bus, train, car and truck travel on land, while a ship travels on water.
r: Tip: group items by where or how they work, then pick the one that falls outside the group.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Square, B. Line, C. Triangle, D. Circle, E. Rectangle
f: Square, triangle, circle and rectangle are closed shapes enclosing an area. A line does not enclose any area.
r: Tip: a closed shape has an inside and an outside.

q: Which word does not belong to this list: Foot, Inch, Yard, Acre, Mile?
f: Foot, inch, yard and mile measure length, but an acre measures area.
r: Tip: an acre is about 4047 square metres; in Pakistan land is also measured in kanal and marla.

q: Which of the following is different from others: Plate, Dish, Knife, Spoon, Sugar?
f: Plate, dish, knife and spoon are utensils, while sugar is a food item.
r: Tip: separate objects used for eating from things that are eaten.

q: Find the odd one out: Axe, Sword, Dagger, Fork, Knife
f: Axe, sword, dagger (and knife) are weapons/cutting arms; a fork is a table utensil.

q: Which word does not belong to the list?
f: BLACKSMITH, TAILOR and MASON are skilled manual craftsmen. A PROFESSOR is an academic.
r: Tip: split professions into manual trades and academic jobs.

q: Point out the odd one out: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon. (276)
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a shape but a measure formed by two rays.
r: A hexagon has six sides.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Play, B. Cricket, C. Swimming, D. Football, E. Child
f: Play, cricket, swimming and football are all sports or games. Child is a person.
r: Tip: look for the item that is not an activity.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Teacher, B. Patient, C. Lawyer, D. Doctor, E. Medicine
f: Teacher, patient, lawyer and doctor are all people. Medicine is a thing.
r: Tip: check for person versus thing.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Kingdom, B. State, C. Province, D. Citizen, E. Country
f: Kingdom, state, province and country are territories or political regions. A citizen is a person who lives in one.
r: Tip: a place and a person are different kinds of noun.

q: Which one is different from the rest? Cow, Hen, Duck, Bull, Mare
f: Cow, hen and mare are female animals, while bull is the only male.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Balochistan, Rawalpindi? (4)
f: Karachi, Lahore and Rawalpindi are cities, while Balochistan is a province.
r: Balochistan is the largest province of Pakistan by area.

q: Which is different from other: Radius, Diagonal, Diameter, Circumference?
f: Radius, diameter and circumference are all parts of a circle, but a diagonal belongs to polygons such as squares and rectangles.
r: Tip: circumference = 2 x pi x radius, and diameter = 2 x radius.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Live, B. Die, C. Exist, D. Be
f: Live, exist and be all mean to have life or being. Die means the opposite, to stop living.
r: Tip: look for an antonym hidden among synonyms.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Hand, B. Arm, C. Body, D. Wrist, E. Fingers
f: Hand, arm, wrist and fingers are all parts of the arm. Body is the whole that contains them.
r: Tip: whole versus part is a common way to make an odd one out.

q: Which one is different from the rest: Mango, Carrot, Apple, Banana?
f: Mango, apple and banana are fruits, while carrot is a vegetable.
r: Carrot is a root vegetable rich in vitamin A.

q: Which one is different from the rest? AC, DG, HK, LO
f: In DG, HK and LO the second letter is 3 places after the first. In AC it is only 2 places.
r: Tip: for letter series, convert letters to numbers (A=1 to Z=26) and look at the gaps.

q: Which term is different in this series: A3, C5, E7, G9, I12?
f: Letters move by 2 (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers also move by 2 (3, 5, 7, 9, 11). The last term should be I11, so I12 is wrong.
r: Such questions test both letter and number patterns together.

q: Which one is different from the rest?
f: Kabul, Delhi and Dhaka are national capitals. Karachi is not the capital of Pakistan.
r: Fact: Islamabad has been the capital of Pakistan since 1960s, before that Karachi was the capital.

q: Which one is different from the rest?
f: Relationship, kinship and friendship are all human bonds. Spaceship is a vehicle.
r: Tip: words with the same ending may still belong to different categories, so check the meaning.

q: Which one is different from the rest?
f: Confuse, puzzle, disturb and tense relate to being troubled or perplexed. Advancing means moving forward.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one is different from the rest?
f: AC, CE, EG and GI each skip one letter and the second letter of each pair becomes the first letter of the next. II repeats the same letter, so it is different.
r: Tip: in letter pairs, compare how the second letter relates to the first.

q: Which one is different from the rest?
f: PLEADER, MAGISTRATE, JUDGE and ADVOCATE all work in the legal system. A COOK does not.
r: Tip: group the options by profession field.

q: Find the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize.
f: Wheat, rice and maize are food grains for humans, while hay is dried grass used as animal fodder.
r: Wheat is the main staple crop of Pakistan.

q: Find the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Circle, Angle
f: The others are shapes; an angle is not a closed shape.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest? Infant, Adult, Child, Newborn, Baby
f: Infant, child, newborn and baby all describe young ones. Adult is a fully grown person.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one is the odd one out: Zebra, Donkey, Horse, Kangaroo?
f: Zebra, donkey and horse all belong to the horse family (Equidae). A kangaroo is a marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.
r: Kangaroos are native to Australia and move by hopping.

q: Odd one out: Islamabad, Lahore, Quetta, Rawalpindi. (12)
f: Islamabad is the federal capital, Lahore is the capital of Punjab and Quetta is the capital of Balochistan. Rawalpindi is not a capital.
r: Rawalpindi is the headquarters of the Pakistan Army and neighbours Islamabad.

q: Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: Brazil, Canada, Chile and Argentina are countries. New York is a city.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: Red, blue, green and yellow are specific colors. Color is the general category.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different from the others?
f: OBVIOUS, CLEAR and APPARENT all mean easy to see or understand. DUBIOUS means doubtful.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out words, find the three that are synonyms and pick the remaining one.

q: Which of these is different from the rest: Rome, Paris, Berlin, New York?
f: Rome, Paris and Berlin are national capitals; New York is not a capital.
r: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the USA.

q: Find the odd one: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Maize
f: Wheat, rice and maize are grains (food crops); hay is dried grass for animals.
r: Wheat is the main food crop of Pakistan.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Stationary, B. Eraser, C. Pen, D. Paper
f: Eraser, pen and paper are all items of stationery. The word given, stationary, means not moving and is a different word.
r: Tip: stationery with an e means writing materials, stationary with an a means not moving.

q: Which one is different from the rest: cow, snake, elephant, monkey?
f: Cow, elephant and monkey are mammals, while a snake is a reptile.
r: Mammals are warm-blooded and feed milk to their young.

q: Which is different in the following: Violin, Piano, String, Cutter, Banjo?
f: Violin, piano, string and banjo are all connected with music, while a cutter is a cutting tool.
r: Tip: the key word here is the category, musical instrument versus tool.

q: Choose the odd one out: Cricket, Football, Hockey, Chess.
f: Chess is an indoor board game, while the others are outdoor field sports.

q: Which one of the following is different from others: Shirts, Boots, Coats, Trousers, Necktie?
f: Shirts, coats, trousers and necktie are clothes worn on the body, while boots are footwear.
r: Tip: look for the item that belongs to a different category (footwear versus clothing).

q: Find the odd one out: Angle, Triangle, Square, Rectangle. (14)
f: Triangle, square and rectangle are closed plane figures (polygons), while an angle is not a closed figure.
r: A triangle has three sides and the sum of its angles is 180 degrees.

q: Which of the following is different from the rest?
f: Unearth, discover, find and locate all mean to come across something that already exists. Invention means to create something new.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which of the following is different from the rest?
f: Yacht, steamer and ship travel on water, while an aircraft travels in the air.
r: Tip: group items by the medium they operate in (land, water, air).

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Lion, B. Wolf, C. Cat, D. Goat, E. Tiger
f: Lion, wolf, cat and tiger are meat-eating (carnivorous) animals. A goat eats plants.
r: Tip: diet is a useful category for animal odd-one-out questions.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. KOOL, B. LOOM, C. NOOS, D. MOON, E. WOOX
f: In KOOL, LOOM, MOON and WOOX the first and last letters are consecutive in the alphabet (K L, L M, M N, W X). In NOOS, N and S are not consecutive.
r: Tip: look at the outer letters when the middle letters repeat.

q: Which group of letters is different from the others?
f: ACBC, XZYZ and JLK(L) follow the same pattern of one letter, one ahead, one in between, repeating the middle one; MCPO does not follow it.
r: Tip: compare the position patterns inside each group, not the letters themselves.

q: Which is different in the following: Lion, Wolf, Leopard, Lamb, Tiger?
f: Lion, wolf, leopard and tiger are carnivorous predators, while a lamb is a gentle animal that eats plants.
r: Tip: carnivores hunt other animals, herbivores eat plants; this split is common in odd-one-out questions.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Two, B. Double, C. Pair, D. Three, E. Couple
f: Two, double, pair and couple all mean 2. Three is a different number.
r: Tip: check whether most words share the same number.

q: Which one is different from the rest: A4, B5, C5, D7?
f: A, B, C, D are the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th letters. The number is the letter position plus 3 in A4, B5 and D7 (1+3, 2+3, 4+3), but C5 breaks it because 3+3 is 6.
r: In letter-number odd-one-out questions, convert letters to their alphabet positions first.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest? A. House, B. Mountain, C. River, D. Forest, E. Sea
f: Mountain, river, forest and sea are natural features. A house is man-made.
r: Tip: natural versus man-made is a common category split.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. South-West, B. North-East, C. North-West, D. East-West, E. South-East
f: South-West, North-East, North-West and South-East are the four intermediate (diagonal) directions. East-West is a pair of opposite cardinal directions, not a single direction.
r: Tip: the four intermediate directions lie halfway between the cardinal points.

q: Which one is different: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta, Karachi, Rawalpindi? (120)
f: Lahore, Peshawar, Quetta and Karachi are all provincial capitals. Rawalpindi is not a provincial capital, so it is the odd one out.
r: Islamabad, not Rawalpindi, is the federal capital of Pakistan.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Car, train, aircraft and ship are machines with engines, while a cart is pulled by an animal or by hand.
r: Tip: the Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: February, December, June and September are months, while Monday is a day of the week.
r: Tip: February is the shortest month, with 28 days (29 in a leap year).

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Brother, uncle, son and grandfather are male relatives, while a sister is female.
r: Tip: check gender first when the words are family relations.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Tennis, hockey, cricket and football are outdoor games, while billiard is an indoor game.
r: Tip: split games into indoor and outdoor groups.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Mango, lemon and orange are fruits, while tomato is generally treated as a vegetable in cooking.
r: Tip: botanically a tomato is a fruit, but in everyday classification it is a vegetable.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Two, four, twenty and fifty are even numbers, while five is odd.
r: Tip: parity (odd or even) is a quick odd-one-out check for numbers.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Cup, mug, glass and jug are containers, while a drink is what goes inside them.
r: Tip: separate containers from their contents.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Sword, knife, fork and axe are sharp tools or weapons, while a cup is a container with no sharp edge.
r: Tip: look at the main property (sharp or pointed) shared by most of the items.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Town, city, village and township are all human settlements on earth. Heaven is not.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Separation, split, divide and gap all involve parting. Union means joining together.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Dagger, sword and knife are cutting weapons. A fork is an eating tool without a blade.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Crow, parrot, owl and sparrow are birds, while a lion is a mammal.
r: Tip: check class (bird, mammal, fish) when animals are listed.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Pear, orange, banana and apple are fruits, while potato is a vegetable.
r: Tip: classify by food group when a list mixes fruits and vegetables.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: House, hut and villa are specific types of homes to live in, while building is a general term for any structure.
r: Tip: spot the word that is a general category rather than a specific kind.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Sing, call and speak are all ways of making sounds with the voice, while hear is a way of receiving sounds.
r: Tip: separate actions of producing from actions of receiving.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Smuggle, cheat, steal and bribe are illegal or dishonest acts, while selling is a normal lawful activity.
r: Tip: look for the lawful item among a list of crimes.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Ankle, knee, foot and toe are all parts of the leg, while the tongue is in the mouth.
r: Tip: group body parts by the area they belong to.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: Stem, root, branch and leaf are parts of a plant, while the tree is the whole plant.
r: Tip: look for the whole among a list of parts.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: WRIST, KNEE and ELBOW are body joints. BALD is a condition, not a body part.
r: Tip: check whether three items belong to one category (here joints) and one does not.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: WEAK, UGLY, SLOW and DULL are all negative qualities. BRIGHT is a positive one.
r: Tip: sort the options by positive and negative meaning.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest?
f: TRIANGLE, PARALLELOGRAM, SQUARE and RECTANGLE are made of straight sides and corners. A CIRCLE has a curved boundary and no corners.
r: Tip: a circle is the only common shape with no straight sides.

q: Which one is different in the following: Petrol, Oil, Water, Spirit?
f: Petrol, oil and spirit are flammable liquids, while water does not burn.
r: Tip: flammability is a quick test for fuels versus other liquids.

q: Which is different from the rest: Kangaroo, Horse, Deer, Cow?
f: The horse, deer and cow are all hoofed land mammals, while the kangaroo is a marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.
r: Kangaroos are native to Australia.

q: Find the odd one: America, Africa, Asia, Euro
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents; the euro is a currency.
r: Asia is the largest continent.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Young, B. Lovely, C. Beautiful, D. Handsome, E. Pretty
f: Lovely, beautiful, handsome and pretty all describe good looks. Young describes age.
r: Tip: group words by what they describe.

q: Which one is different: A12, B13, D15, E19, C14?
f: Letter position plus 11 gives the number: A(1)=12, B(2)=13, C(3)=14, D(4)=15. For E(5) it should be 16, but it is 19.
r: The odd one out breaks the pattern shared by all the others.

q: Which one is different from the rest: square, yard, meter, foot?
f: Yard, meter and foot are units of length. Square is a geometric shape.
r: One yard equals three feet, and one meter is about 3.28 feet.

q: Which one is different from the following: actor, director, music, producer?
f: Actor, director and producer are all people who work on a film, while music is a thing, not a person.
r: Odd-one-out questions are solved by finding the item of a different category.

q: What is different from the rest?
f: Swim, walk, run and gymnastic are physical exercises or movements, while game is a general term for a competitive activity.
r: Tip: look for the item that is a broader category than the rest.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Run, B. Flow, C. Swim, D. Fast, E. Move
f: Run, flow, swim and move are verbs of motion. Fast is an adjective or adverb describing speed.
r: Tip: look for a different part of speech.
