q: Which one of the following is different? A. Tobacco, B. Pipe, C. Cigarette, D. Cigar
f: Tobacco, cigarette and cigar are all made of tobacco. A pipe is only a device in which tobacco is smoked.
r: Tip: ask what each item is made of or what it is used for.

q: What is the probability of getting an odd number when a fair die is rolled once? (12)
f: The odd numbers are 1, 3 and 5, which is 3 outcomes out of 6, so the probability is 3/6 = 1/2.
r: The probability of any event always lies between 0 and 1.

q: Which one is different from the others: monkey, panda, baboon, chimpanzee? (376)
f: Monkey, baboon and chimpanzee are primates, while the panda is a bear.
r: Giant pandas feed mainly on bamboo.

q: Which is different: Triangle, Rectangle, Square, Circle?
f: Triangle, rectangle and square are polygons with straight sides. A circle is a curved shape with no sides.
r: Tip: look for curved versus straight edges.

q: Which does not belong to the group: Cow, Dog, Leopard, Cat
f: Dog, leopard and cat eat meat (carnivores); the cow eats grass (herbivore).
r: Herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat meat.

q: Which one is different? Camel, Donkey, Bull, Mare
f: Camel, donkey and bull are general or male animal names, while a mare is specifically a female horse.
r: Tip: the key for this test chose mare as the odd one.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. GHI, B. JKL, C. NOP, D. QST, E. UVW
f: The others are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. QST skips R.
r: Tip: check for a skipped letter in letter-group questions.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Silver, B. Mercury, C. Gold, D. Iron
f: Silver, gold and iron are solid metals at room temperature. Mercury is a liquid metal.
r: Tip: mercury is the only metal that is liquid at normal room temperature.

q: Find the odd one: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket; football is played with the feet.
r: Hockey is the national game of Pakistan.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. August, B. September, C. October, D. November
f: September, October and November all end in the letters ber. August does not.
r: Tip: September to December get their names from Latin numbers (septem, octo, novem, decem).

q: Which pair is the odd one out: CE, IJ, AC, GI, EG?
f: In CE, AC, GI and EG the second letter is 2 places after the first. In IJ, J is only 1 place after I, so IJ is odd.
r: Check the gap between letters in each pair to find the odd one.

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest? (2)
f: Yard, foot, mile and kilometer are units of measuring length, while length itself is the quantity being measured.
r: Tip: one mile is about 1.609 kilometres.

q: Which is the odd one out: panda, chimpanzee, bamboo? (18)
f: Panda and chimpanzee are animals, while bamboo is a plant.
r: Bamboo shoots and leaves are the main food of the giant panda.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Camel, B. Ox, C. Horse, D. Donkey, E. Mule
f: Camel, ox, horse and donkey are natural animal species. A mule is a hybrid, the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.
r: Tip: a hinny is the opposite cross, a male horse and a female donkey.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. PQO, B. KJL, C. UTV, D. SRT, E. FEG
f: KJL, UTV, SRT and FEG each go one step back then two steps forward (-1, +2). PQO goes forward then back (+1, -2), so it is the odd one.
r: Tip: write the step sizes between neighbouring letters, as in +1, -2, to spot the odd group.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Feathers, B. Hair, C. Grass, D. Wool
f: Feathers, hair and wool grow on the bodies of animals or birds. Grass is a plant.
r: Tip: classify by origin, such as animal, plant or mineral.

q: Which one is different from the rest: EH, AD, MP, QS?
f: Letter gaps: E to H is 3 (5 to 8), A to D is 3 (1 to 4), M to P is 3 (13 to 16), but Q to S is only 2 (17 to 19).
r: In odd-one-out letter pairs, always compare the gaps in alphabet positions.

q: Which is different in the following: Ounce, Pound, Ton, Maund?
f: Ounce, pound and ton belong to the same Western (imperial) system, while the maund is a traditional South Asian unit.
r: Tip: a maund is about 40 kg in Pakistan today (37.3 kg in the older system).

q: Find the odd one: Lahore, Rawalpindi, Karachi, Sindh, Quetta
f: Sindh is a province; the others are cities.
r: Karachi is the capital of Sindh.

q: Which one is different from the others: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda, Baboon?
f: Monkey, ape, chimpanzee and baboon are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: Primates include monkeys, apes, baboons and humans.

q: Which one is different: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Baseball? (501)
f: Cricket, tennis and baseball are played with a bat or racket, while football is played with the feet and no bat.
r: Football is the most widely played sport in the world.

q: Which is different from others: Whisper, Shout, Sing, Tell?
f: Whisper, shout and tell are ways of speaking words, while singing involves music and a tune.
r: Tip: look for the action that uses a different skill from the rest.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Hard, B. Stiff, C. Unbending, D. Flexible
f: Hard, stiff and unbending describe something rigid. Flexible means able to bend easily.
r: Tip: three synonyms and one antonym is a very common pattern.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. MNO, B. STW, C. XYZ, D. EFG, E. BCD
f: MNO, XYZ, EFG and BCD are three consecutive letters of the alphabet. STW skips a letter (S, T, then W).
r: Tip: in letter-group questions first check whether the letters are consecutive, then check gaps and direction.

q: Find the odd one: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda
f: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: The giant panda mainly eats bamboo.

q: Point out the odd one out: Wheat, Hay, Rice, Barley. (96)
f: Wheat, rice and barley are food grains (cereals) eaten by people, while hay is dried grass kept as fodder for animals.
r: Wheat and rice are the two major food crops of Pakistan.

q: Which word does not belong to this list: Less, Depart, Abate, Decrease?
f: Less, abate and decrease all mean to reduce, while depart means to leave.
r: Tip: look for the word whose meaning is not shared by the others.

q: Find the odd one out: Delhi, Ahmedabad, Mumbai, Sibbi.
f: Delhi, Ahmedabad and Mumbai are cities of India. Sibbi (Sibi) is a city of Balochistan, Pakistan.
r: Sibi is famous for its annual Sibi Mela and its very hot summers.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Sports, B. Teem, C. Game, D. Team
f: Sports, game and team all belong to the field of games and play. Teem (to be full of) is unrelated.
r: Tip: teem and team sound alike but have different meanings.

q: Which is the odd one out: India, Pakistan, China, Spain?
f: India, Pakistan and China are Asian countries, while Spain is in Europe.
r: Spain's capital is Madrid.

q: Find the odd one out: Lahore, Rawalpindi, Karachi, Quetta (4)
f: Lahore, Karachi and Quetta are provincial capitals; Rawalpindi is not.

q: What is different from the others?
f: Potato, cabbage, pea and lady finger are vegetables. Orange is a fruit.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: What is different from the others?
f: Stream, sea, river and lake are natural water bodies. A canal is man-made.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: What is different from the others?
f: Eye, hand, nose and leg are body parts. Smell is a sense or sensation.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Odd one out among: Musician, Movie, Director, Writer.
f: Musician, director and writer are all people with professions. A movie is a work, not a person.
r: In odd-one-out questions, look for the item that belongs to a different category from the rest.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Leprosy, B. Typhoid, C. Vomiting, D. Asthma
f: Leprosy, typhoid and asthma are diseases. Vomiting is a symptom, not a disease in itself.
r: Tip: distinguish a disease from a symptom of a disease.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Boy, B. Girl, C. Woman, D. Lady, E. Female
f: Girl, woman, lady and female all refer to the female sex. A boy is male.
r: Tip: in word odd-one-out questions look for a shared category such as gender, material or function.

q: Find the odd one: Angle, Rectangle, Square, Hexagon
f: Rectangle, square and hexagon are closed shapes (polygons); an angle is not a shape.
r: A hexagon has 6 sides.

q: Which one is different from the others: Circle, Square, Triangle, Angle? (42)
f: Circle, square and triangle are closed geometric figures, while an angle is not a closed figure.
r: An angle is formed by two rays meeting at a common point.

q: Point out the odd one out: America, Africa, Asia, Euro. (8)
f: America, Africa and Asia are continents; the Euro is a currency (the continent is Europe).
r: There are seven continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

q: Which one is different from the rest: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Sindh, Peshawar, Quetta? (2)
f: Rawalpindi, Lahore, Peshawar and Quetta are cities, while Sindh is a province.
r: Quetta is the capital of Balochistan and Peshawar is the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. ABCACB, B. NOPNPO, C. RSTSTR, D. GHIGIH, E. KLMKML
f: In the others, three consecutive letters are followed by the same three with the last two swapped (ABC ACB, NOP NPO, GHI GIH, KLM KML). RSTSTR repeats the letters as S T R, which is a rotation instead.
r: Tip: compare the second half of each string with the first half.

q: Which is the odd one out: iron, brass, tin, copper? (2)
f: Iron, tin and copper are pure metallic elements. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
r: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.

q: Which one is different from the others: Karachi, Lahore, Peshawar, Abbottabad?
f: Karachi, Lahore and Peshawar are the capitals of Sindh, Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Abbottabad is not a provincial capital.
r: Abbottabad is the home city of the Pakistan Military Academy at Kakul.

q: Which one is the odd one out: mango, guava, apple, potato?
f: Mango, guava and apple are fruits that grow on trees, while potato is a vegetable (an underground tuber).
r: Potato is a stem tuber that grows under the soil.

q: Which one is different from the others: chimpanzee, ape, baboon, kangaroo, monkey? (2)
f: Chimpanzee, ape, baboon and monkey are all primates, while the kangaroo is a marsupial.
r: Kangaroos are native to Australia and carry their young in a pouch.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. LLMN, B. UUVW, C. CCDE, D. GGHI, E. RRRS
f: The others repeat the first letter twice and then follow with the next two consecutive letters. RRRS repeats its first letter three times.
r: Tip: count repeated letters as well as the order of the alphabet.

q: Which one is different from the rest? Oxygen, Sulphur, Silver, Zinc, Protenium
f: Oxygen is a gas at room temperature, while sulphur, silver and zinc are solids (the printed Protenium is not a standard element name). The answer key also gives Oxygen.
r: Tip: if one item is a gas and the rest are solids, the gas is the odd one.

q: Which one of the following is different: Mile, Kanal, Marla, Acre?
f: Kanal, marla and acre are units of land area, while a mile is a unit of length.
r: Tip: one kanal equals 20 marla, and a marla is about 272 square feet.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Picture, B. Painting, C. Photography, D. Poster
f: Picture, painting and poster are finished visual items. Photography is the art or process of taking photographs, not an item.
r: Tip: separate objects from activities or processes when finding the odd one out.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. Circle, B. Square, C. Triangle, D. Hexagon
f: Square, triangle and hexagon are polygons with straight sides and corners. A circle has a curved boundary and no corners.
r: Tip: a polygon needs at least three straight sides.

q: Which one of the following is different: Cow, Goat, Sheep, Horse, Buffalo?
f: Cow, goat, sheep and buffalo are milk-giving farm animals, while a horse is not kept for milk.
r: Tip: think about the main purpose an animal is kept for.

q: Which one is different: 7D, 9G, 4A, 6C?
f: Letter positions are D=4, G=7, A=1, C=3. Number minus letter position gives 3, 2, 3, 3, so 9G breaks the pattern.
r: Position of a letter is its place in the alphabet (A=1, B=2 and so on).

q: Which one of the following is different from the rest? (3)
f: High, great, fat and big all suggest large size. Small is the opposite.
r: Tip: in odd-one-out questions, find the property shared by most words and pick the one that breaks it.

q: Find the odd one out: Pindi, Lahore, Karachi, Quetta, Peshawar. (42)
f: Lahore, Karachi, Quetta and Peshawar are the capitals of the four provinces of Pakistan, while Pindi (Rawalpindi) is not a provincial capital.
r: Rawalpindi is the neighbour of Islamabad and hosts the General Headquarters of the Pakistan Army.

q: Find the odd one out: Monkey, Ape, Chimpanzee, Panda. (12)
f: Monkey, ape and chimpanzee are primates; the panda is a bear.
r: Chimpanzees are apes, not monkeys.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. TSUS, B. NMOM, C. DCEC, D. HGJG, E. RQSQ
f: TSUS, NMOM, DCEC and RQSQ all follow -1, +2, -2 between letters. HGJG goes -1, +3, -3, so it is different.
r: Tip: the third letter in each group steps forward by 2 from the second letter in the other groups.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. RUS, B. FHG, C. MON, D. QSR, E. TVU
f: FHG, MON, QSR and TVU all follow the pattern +2, -1 between letters (F+2 = H, H-1 = G, and so on). RUS goes +3, -2.
r: Tip: write the jump between each pair of letters to find the common pattern.

q: Which one of the following is different? A. EVU, B. RHI, C. OLK, D. SHG, E. HSR
f: EVU, OLK, SHG and HSR all end with two letters in backward alphabetical order (V U, L K, H G, S R). RHI ends with H I, which goes forward.
r: Tip: compare the direction of movement inside each group, not only the letters themselves.

q: A man earned Rs. 28 and saved Rs. 7. What percent of his earning did he save?
f: Percent saved = 7 / 28 x 100 = 25%.
r: Tip: percent = part divided by whole, times 100.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present and absent students?
f: 1200/1500 x 100 = 80% present, so absent = 300 students = 20%.
r: If 1300 were present, the percentage would be 86.67% present.

q: What is one third of 20% of 60?
f: 20% of 60 = 12. One third of 12 = 4.
r: To find a percentage, multiply by the percent and divide by 100.

q: What is 70% of 80? (20)
r: 70% of 80 equals 80% of 70.

q: In a classroom, out of 1500 students 1200 are present. What is the percentage of present students? (311)
r: Simplify first: 1200/1500 = 4/5 = 80%.

q: If 12 is divided by 3, what is half of the result?
f: 12 divided by 3 gives 4, and half of 4 is 2.
r: Tip: first do the division, then take half of the answer.

q: What is 25% of 75? (2)
f: 25% is one quarter: 75 / 4 = 18.75.

q: What is one quarter of one third of 36?
f: One third of 36 is 36/3 = 12. One quarter of 12 is 12/4 = 3.
r: One quarter of one third is the same as 1/12 of the number.

q: Half of a quarter is
r: 'Of' means multiply.

q: What is 20% of one tenth of 90? (3)
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and 20% of 9 is 1.8.
r: 20% is the same as one fifth.

q: What is one quarter of 120?
f: 120 divided by 4 = 30.

q: What is 80% of 20?
r: 80% is equal to 4/5.

q: What is 80% of 10? (2)
r: Percent of 10: move the decimal one place and multiply (10% of 10 = 1).

q: What is 90% of 9? (24)
r: 90% of a number is the number minus 10% of it, so 9 - 0.9 = 8.1.

q: What percent of 6 is 2?
r: 2 out of 6 is the same as the fraction 1/3.

q: What is 7% of 80?
r: 10% of 80 is 8, so 7% must be a little less.

q: What is 20% of 50?
r: 20% equals one fifth.

q: What is a quarter of 1/3 of 120? (26)
f: 1/3 of 120 is 40. A quarter of 40 is 40 divided by 4, which equals 10.
r: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 120 divided by 12.

q: What is 90% of 81?
What is one quarter of one tenth of 120? (700)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12, and a quarter of 12 is 3. Working in the other order gives 30 and then 3.
r: One quarter of one tenth equals 1/40, so the answer is 120/40.

q: In a class of 500 students, 340 are boys. What percentage are boys? (7)
r: Percentage = part/total x 100; out of 500, each student is 0.2 percent.

q: What is 90% of 90? (7107)
r: 10% of a number = the number divided by 10. 50% of 90 = 45.

q: Of 500 students, 340 are present. What percentage is absent?
r: Present is 68%. Percentage = part/whole x 100.

q: A class has 500 students: 340 boys and 160 girls. What is the percentage of girls? (6)
What is a quarter of 12? (4)
f: A quarter means one fourth. 12 divided by 4 equals 3.
r: A quarter of 120 is 30, ten times the answer here.

q: What is 60% of 80?
r: 60% is the same as 3/5, and 3/5 of 80 is 48.

q: What is half of the diameter of a circle called? (4)
f: The diameter is twice the radius, so half of the diameter is the radius.
r: The radius is the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge.

q: If three is subtracted from 12, then what will be one third of the remaining?
f: 12 - 3 = 9, and one third of 9 is 3.
r: Tip: follow the order of operations given in the sentence.

q: In a classroom of 1500 students, 1200 are present. Find the percentage of present students.
What is one third of 120? (180)
f: One third of 120 is 120 / 3 = 40.
r: A number divisible by 3 has digits whose sum is divisible by 3; 1+2+0 = 3.

q: What is 54% of 90?
What is 80% of 40?
r: 80% equals 4/5.

q: What is one third of one tenth of 120? (62)
f: One tenth of 120 is 12 and one third of 12 is 4.
r: The order of taking fractions does not change the result: 120 x 1/3 x 1/10 is also 4.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1300 are present. What percentage of students is present?
f: Percentage present = 1300 / 1500 x 100 = 86.67%. 80% would need 1200 present, 13.33% is the absent percentage, and 87.5% would need 1312.5 present, which is not possible.

q: What is 90% of 89?
What is a quarter of 1/20? (2)
r: Multiplying two fractions means multiplying numerators together and denominators together.

q: What is 10% of 80? (3)
r: To find 10% of a number, divide it by 10.

q: What is one quarter of one tenth of 12?
f: One tenth of 12 is 1.2. One quarter of 1.2 is 1.2 / 4 = 0.3.
r: A quarter of a number is the same as dividing it by 4.

f: 32 percent of 25 is 32/100 x 25 = 8.
r: Tip: 25 is one quarter of 100, so 32% of 25 is 32 divided by 4 = 8.

q: What is 60 percent of 100?
r: Percent means per hundred, so any percent of 100 equals the same number.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. How many women are there? (11)
r: Find the fraction of the other group as 1 minus the given fraction.

q: What is one tenth of 120? (227)
f: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place left, so 120 becomes 12.
r: One tenth is the same as 10%.

q: In a class of 100 students, 40% failed in English and 70% in Urdu. Were there any who failed both in English and Urdu?
f: 40 + 70 = 110, which is more than 100 students, so at least 10 students must have failed both subjects.
r: Tip: if the percentages of two groups add up to more than 100, the groups must overlap.

q: What is one third of 10? (2)
f: One third of 10 = 10 / 3 = 3.33, which is 3 and 1/3.
r: Ten is not exactly divisible by 3, so the answer is a fraction.

q: A cake is cut so that one piece, which is half of the cake, is twice as large as one of the other pieces. How many pieces are there?
f: One piece is 1/2 of the cake, and each other piece is half of that, 1/4. The remaining 1/2 makes two pieces of 1/4, so there are 3 pieces in all.
r: Tip: draw the fractions out; the pieces must add up to one whole.

q: What is 90% of 70? (20)
r: To find 90% of a number, subtract one tenth of it from the number.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What percentage is present? (8)
What is one tenth of 30?
f: One tenth of 30 is 30 / 10 = 3.
r: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left.

q: What is 60% of 9? (5)
What is 75% of 200?
If 1/8 of a number is 6, what is the number? A. 14, B. 48, C. 42
f: The number is 6 x 8 = 48.
r: Tip: to find the whole from a fraction, multiply by the denominator.

q: What is 60% of 60?
r: 60% equals 3/5.

q: What is a quarter of 120? (271)
f: 120 divided by 4 is 30.
r: A quarter of a number is the same as 25% of it.

q: If two thirds of a group are men, what percentage of the group are women?
f: Women are 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 of the group. 1/3 x 100 = 33.33%.
r: One third is equal to 33.33 percent.

q: What is 65% of 70?
r: 10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 42 and 5% is 3.5.

q: What is 60% of 70? (2)
r: 10% of 70 is 7, so 60% is 6 x 7.

q: What is 90% of 99? (2)
f: 90% of 99 = 0.9 x 99 = 89.1. Equivalently, 10% of 99 is 9.9, and 99 minus 9.9 = 89.1.
r: 90% of 100 is 90, so 90% of 99 is 0.9 less than 90.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (159)
r: Present % + absent % = 100%, so 80% present means 20% absent.

q: What is one tenth of 10% of 140?
f: 10% of 140 = 14. One tenth of 14 = 1.4.
r: 10% and one tenth are the same value, so this is 140 x 0.1 x 0.1 = 1.4.

q: Half of 9/90 is
r: Simplify the fraction first.

q: One third of one half is equal to?
f: One third of one half is 1/3 x 1/2 = 1/6.
r: Tip: the word 'of' between fractions means multiply.

q: What is a quarter of 10 percent of 12? (2)
f: 10 percent of 12 = 1.2. A quarter of 1.2 = 0.3.
r: A quarter means dividing by 4.

q: A class has 500 students, of whom 360 are boys. What percentage are girls?
r: Boys are 72%. Percentage = part / whole x 100.

q: What is 28% of 500?
r: 10% of 500 is 50, so 28% is a little more than half of 250.

q: What is half of 9/90?
f: 9/90 = 0.1, and half of 0.1 = 0.05 = 1/20 (so the source statement of 1/5 or 0.2 is wrong).
r: Simplify the fraction first: 9/90 = 1/10.

q: What is 20 percent of 500?
f: 20% of 500 = 20 times 500 divided by 100 = 100.

q: What is one-fourth of 10% of 120? (32)
r: One-fourth of 120 itself is 30.

q: What is 80% of 80? (96)
r: 80% = 4/5, so divide by 5 and multiply by 4.

q: What is 81% of 81?
There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the number of women? (2)
r: Women are 1/3 of the passengers.

q: What is 30% of 1/10 of 120?
f: One tenth of 120 is 12. Then 30% of 12 = 0.3 x 12 = 3.6.
r: Candidates sometimes remembered 3, but the exact answer is 3.6.

q: What is one third of 30% of 120?
f: 30% of 120 = 36. One third of 36 = 12.
r: 30% of a number equals three tenths of it.

q: What is one tenth of 90? (104)
f: One tenth means dividing by 10, and 90 / 10 = 9.
r: One hundredth of 90 is 0.9. Ten percent equals one tenth.

q: What is one tenth of 1/20?
r: Multiplying by one tenth moves the decimal point one place left.

q: What is a quarter of one tenth of 120? (353)
f: One tenth of 120 = 12, and a quarter of 12 = 3.
r: Quarter of a number is the number divided by 4; one tenth is divided by 10.

q: What is one third of 1/80?
r: Multiplying fractions means multiplying the numerators and the denominators.

q: What is 100% of 200?
f: 100% means the whole amount, so 100% of 200 is 200.

q: What is half of 1/90?
r: Taking half of a fraction doubles its denominator.

q: What is one third of 25% of 120?
f: 25% of 120 = 30. One third of 30 = 10.
r: 25% is the same as one quarter.

q: What is 60% of 90? (58)
r: The product is the same for 90% of 60, since percentages are multiplicative.

q: What is 5% of 80?
In a group of 50 players, 30% play hockey and 80% play cricket. Are there any who play both hockey and cricket?
o: One cannot say without further detail
f: 30% of 50 is 15 and 80% of 50 is 40. Since 15 + 40 = 55 is more than 50, at least 5 players must play both.
r: Tip: if the two groups add up to more than the total, they must overlap.

q: What is a quarter of 1/10 of 1200?
r: A quarter of 1200 is 300, so one tenth of that is also 30.

q: In a class of 24 students, 1/4 are male. What is the percentage of females? (19)
r: If 1/4 are male, then 3/4 = 75% are female.

q: What is 70% of 70?
What is the quarter of 9?
f: A quarter of 9 = 9 divided by 4 = 2.25.
r: Half of 9 is 4.5, and half of that is 2.25.

q: What is a quarter of 1/10 of 9?
f: 1/10 of 9 = 0.9. A quarter of 0.9 = 0.9 divided by 4 = 0.225.
r: A quarter of a number means dividing it by 4.

q: What is 44% of 350?
f: 44% of 350 = 44 times 350 divided by 100 = 154.

q: What is one third of 10% of 90? (18)
f: 10% of 90 = 9, and one third of 9 = 3.
r: 10% of a number: move the decimal point one place to the left.

q: What is 90% of 91? (2)
f: 90% of 91 = 0.9 x 91 = 81.9. Equivalently, 10% of 91 is 9.1, and 91 minus 9.1 = 81.9.
r: Taking 90% of a number is the same as subtracting 10% of it.

q: What is 40% of 9?
r: 10% of 9 is 0.9, so 40% is four times that.

q: In a college, out of 200 students 45% study Physics and 65% study Maths. Are there any students who neither study Physics nor Maths?
f: Physics has 90 students and Maths 130, a total of 220, so at least 20 study both. If exactly 20 study both there are none who study neither, but if more study both there are some. The answer cannot be fixed (the paper key says Yes).
r: Tip: when overlap is unknown, the number outside both sets can vary.

q: What is one third of one fourth of 120?
f: One fourth of 120 = 30, and one third of 30 = 10.

q: What is 45% of 300?
What is 1/3 of 10% of 99?
r: 99 is divisible by 3, so 1/3 of 99 = 33.

q: What is half of 1/8? (5)
r: Halving a fraction doubles its denominator.

q: What is one third of 95?
f: 95 divided by 3 = 31 with remainder 2, so the answer is 31 and 2/3 (31.67).
r: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3; 9 + 5 = 14 is not.

q: What is one third of 90? (102)
f: 90 divided by 3 is 30.
r: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3.

q: What is 20% of 41?
r: 20% equals one fifth.

q: What is 10% of 33?
r: To find 10%, divide by 10.

q: What is 65% of 100? (10)
r: Percent of 100 is always the same number as the percent itself.

q: What is 80% of 90? (59)
What is a quarter of one tenth of 90? (56)
f: One tenth of 90 is 9, and a quarter of 9 is 9 / 4 = 2.25.
r: A quarter of one tenth is 1/40 of the number.

q: What is 2% of 200?
r: 1% of 200 is 2, so 2% is double that.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and one third of them are men, the rest are women. What is the percentage of women? (16)
f: Women = 2/3 of the passengers. 2/3 x 100 = 66.67 percent.
r: Men are 10 of the 30 passengers and women are 20.

q: In a class of 1500 students, 1200 are present. What percentage is absent? (2)
6 is what percentage of 20? (10)
f: Percentage = 6 / 20 x 100 = 30 percent.
r: Percentage = part divided by whole, multiplied by 100.

q: In a class of 500, 340 are boys. Find the percentage of boys.
r: Dividing by 500 and multiplying by 100 is the same as dividing by 5.

q: What is 1/3 of 90% of 90?
f: 90% of 90 is 81, and one third of 81 is 27.
r: A percent means per hundred, so 90% is 90/100.

q: Out of 500 students, 340 are present. What is the percentage of absent students? (152)
r: Present is 68%, so absent is 100 - 68 = 32%.

q: What is 30% of 20?
r: 30% of 20 is 3 times 10% of 20, which is 2.

q: What is 40% of 60?
What is 90% of 80?
What is a quarter of 1/10 of 1/120?
r: Taking a quarter of a number means dividing it by 4.

q: A quarter of 10% of 120 is: (8)
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one quarter of 12 = 3.

q: What is a quarter of 90? (4)
f: A quarter of 90 = 90 divided by 4 = 22.5.
r: A quarter equals 25%, so 25% of 90 is also 22.5.

q: 6 is what percent of 20? (22)
f: Percentage = 6/20 x 100 = 30%.
r: Similarly, 30% of 20 is 6.

q: What is 80% of 75?
r: 80% equals 4/5 and 75 x 4 / 5 = 60.

q: What is 25% of 80? (2)
f: 25% is one quarter: 80 / 4 = 20.
r: 25% equals 1/4.

q: What is 9% of 9?
What is one third of one tenth of 9? (14)
f: One tenth of 9 is 0.9 and one third of 0.9 is 0.3.
r: Equivalently 9 divided by 30 equals 0.3.

q: There are 30 passengers in a bus and 2/3 of them are men. What is the percentage of women? (73)
r: If 2/3 is one group, the rest is 1/3, which is 33.33%.

q: Out of 500 students, 360 are boys. What is the percentage of girls? (78)
r: Percentage = part / total x 100; for a part of 500, divide the part by 5.

q: What is 5% of 700?
f: 5% of 700 = 5 times 700 divided by 100 = 35.

q: Of 1,500 students, 1,200 are present. What percentage is present?
r: Absent students are 300, which is 20%. Percentage = part / whole x 100.

q: What is 72% of 80?
r: 10% of 80 is 8, so 70% is 56 and 2% is 1.6.

q: What is one third of 10% of 120? (169)
f: 10% of 120 = 12, and one third of 12 = 4.
r: Work from the inside out: first the percentage, then the fraction.

q: What is 125% of 25?
What is a quarter of 1/3 of 90? (2)
f: 1/3 of 90 is 30. A quarter of 30 is 30 divided by 4, which equals 7.5.
r: A quarter of 1/3 is 1/12, so the answer is 90 divided by 12.

q: What is 30% of 30? (3)
f: 30 percent of 30 is 0.30 x 30 = 9.
r: Tip: 10 percent of a number is that number divided by 10.

q: A man earns Rs. 2400 per month. He pays Rs. 1500 for office rent and Rs. 200 is spent as office expense. How much tax does he pay if the balance is taxed at the rate of 5%?
r: Tip: tax applies only to the balance left after the deductions named in the question.

q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. How much distance does it cover in 1 minute? (2)
f: 20 km / 60 minutes = 1/3 km = 0.333 km. The printed answer 0.3 km is only a rounded value.
r: Km per minute = km/h divided by 60.

q: A train covers 120 km in 2 hours. What is its speed?
f: Speed = distance divided by time = 120 / 2 = 60 km/h.
r: To convert km/h into m/s, multiply by 5/18, so 60 km/h is about 16.7 m/s.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How long will he take to cover 1 km? (3)
f: 100 minutes ÷ 20 km = 5 minutes per km.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How many km will it cover in 12 minutes?
f: Speed is 120 km/h, which is 2 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 2 times 12, which is 24 km.
r: 12 minutes is one fifth of an hour, and one fifth of 120 is 24.

q: A train covers 20 km in one hour. About how much distance does it cover in 1 minute? (2)
f: 1 hour is 60 minutes, so distance per minute is 20 divided by 60, which is 0.33 km. This is about 333 metres.
r: Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives km per minute.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does it go in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 120 × 1/5 = 24 km.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in 60 minutes, how far does the train cover in the same time? (3)
f: The car's speed is 60 km in 1 hour = 60 km/h. The train moves at twice this speed, 120 km/h, so it covers 120 km in 60 minutes.
r: 60 minutes equal 1 hour.

q: A train travels at 120 miles per hour. How far does it travel in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes is 0.2 hour, so distance = 120 x 0.2 = 24 miles.
r: 24 miles is about 38.6 km.

q: The speed of a train is twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed = 60 km in half an hour = 120 km/h. Train speed = 2 x 120 = 240 km/h, so in 30 minutes it covers 120 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A car is travelling at the speed of 120 km per hour. How many minutes will it take to travel 24 km?
f: 120 km per hour is 2 km per minute, so 24 km takes 24 / 2 = 12 minutes.
r: Tip: convert km per hour to km per minute by dividing by 60.

q: A train is moving at 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (91)
f: 12 minutes = 12/60 = 1/5 hour. Distance = 90 x 1/5 = 18 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

q: A car runs at a speed of 180 km/h. How much distance does it travel in 20 minutes?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 180 x 1/3 = 60 km.
r: To convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18, so 180 km/h is 50 m/s.

q: A train covers 120 km in one hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (4)
f: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour. So the distance is 120 / 5 = 24 km.
r: Speed in km per minute is distance in km/h divided by 60, here 2 km per minute.

q: Train A runs at 60 km/h and train B is twice as fast. How many km does train B cover in 30 minutes?
f: Speed of B = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.

q: If a car covers 90 km in one hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will it cover 1 km?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes for 90 km. So 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 10/9 minutes.
r: The car's speed is 54 km/h.

q: If a train covers 100 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes. Distance per minute is 100 km / 100 minutes = 1 km.
r: The train's speed is 60 km per hour.

q: The speed of a car is 60 km/h and a train goes at double that speed. How far does the train travel in 100 minutes?
f: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 100 minutes (5/3 hour) it covers 120 x 5/3 = 200 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: If a man covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes, how much distance does he cover in 20 minutes at the same speed?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so speed is 20 / 100 = 0.2 km per minute. In 20 minutes he covers 0.2 x 20 = 4 km.
r: Speed in km per hour here is 12 km/h.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes? (10)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the speed is 120 / 100 = 1.2 km per minute. In 15 minutes the train covers 1.2 x 15 = 18 km.
r: At this speed the train runs at 72 km/h.

q: A train moves at a speed of 60 km/hour. How much time will it take to cover 150 km? (16)
f: Time = distance / speed = 150 / 60 = 2.5 hours.
r: 2.5 hours equals 2 hours 30 minutes.

q: A car covers 30 km in 60 minutes. How far will it cover in 30 minutes at the same speed? (2)
f: Speed is 30 km per hour. In half an hour it covers 30 / 2 = 15 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A car travels 20 km in 1 hour 20 minutes. How many minutes will it take to cover 10 km?
f: 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes for 20 km. So 10 km, which is half the distance, takes 80 / 2 = 40 minutes.
r: The car's speed is 15 km per hour.

q: A train covers 20 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes is 100 minutes, so the train covers 20 / 100 = 0.2 km each minute. In 5 minutes it covers 5 x 0.2 = 1 km.
r: The speed of this train is 12 km per hour.

q: The speed of an aircraft is 720 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 1 minute?
f: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so distance in 1 minute = 720 / 60 = 12 km.

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 30 minutes? (16)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: A train moves twice as fast as a car. If the car moves at 90 km/h, how far will the train go in 30 minutes? (3)
f: Speed of the train = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 180 x 1/2 = 90 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A train covers 120 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 15 minutes (at the same speed)?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 120/100 = 1.2 km per minute; in 15 minutes: 1.2 x 15 = 18 km. The printed answer 30 km in the source is wrong.
r: Find the speed per minute first, then multiply by the minutes.

q: If a train covers 120 km per hour, how far will it cover in 18 minutes? (2)
f: 18 minutes is 18/60 = 0.3 hour. Distance = 120 x 0.3 = 36 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, and the time must be in hours when the speed is in km per hour.

q: A train covers 120 km per hour. How much time will it take to cover 20 km?
f: Time = 20 / 120 hour = 1/6 hour. 1/6 of 60 minutes = 10 minutes.
r: Time = distance divided by speed.

q: A train's speed is 100 km/h. How far does it cover in 1 minute (to two decimal places)?
f: 1 minute = 1/60 hour. Distance = 100 / 60 = 1.67 km (about 1667 metres).
r: 100 km/h is about 27.8 metres per second.

q: A car runs at half the speed of a train that travels at 60 km/h. How far will the car go in 30 minutes?
f: Car speed = 60 / 2 = 30 km/h. Distance in 30 minutes (half an hour) = 30 x 1/2 = 15 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, so time must be in hours when speed is in km/h.

q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, how much time will he take to cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100/90 = 10/9 minutes, about 1.11 minutes.
r: His speed is 90 km per 100 minutes, i.e. 54 km per hour.

q: A train runs at twice the speed of a car. The car covers 60 km in 30 minutes. How many km will the train cover in 30 minutes? (2)
f: In 30 minutes the car covers 60 km, so the train covers twice that distance in the same time: 2 x 60 = 120 km.

q: A car travels at 78 km/h. How far will it travel in 12 minutes?
f: 12 minutes = 12 / 60 = 0.2 hour. Distance = 78 x 0.2 = 15.6 km.
r: To change minutes into hours, divide by 60.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car. If the car travels 60 km in 1 hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (38)
f: The car speed is 60 km per hour, so the train speed is 120 km per hour. In 30 minutes (half an hour) the train covers 120 x 1/2 = 60 km.
r: In the same 30 minutes the car covers 30 km.

q: A car covers 60 km in 40 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
f: 60 km in 40 minutes means 30 km in 20 minutes, so in 60 minutes it covers 90 km: 90 km/h.

q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km? (2)
f: Total time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so time for 1 km = 100/90 = 1.11 minutes.
r: His speed is 54 km per hour.

q: A car has a speed of 120 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12.5 minutes?
f: 12.5 minutes = 12.5/60 hour. Distance = 120 x 12.5/60 = 25 km.
r: At 120 km/h a car covers 2 km every minute.

q: A train is moving at 45 km per hour. How far will it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 5 minutes is 5/60 = 1/12 hour. Distance = 45 x 1/12 = 3.75 km.
r: Speed in km/h divided by 60 gives the distance covered in one minute.

q: A train travels 15 km on 1 litre of fuel. How many litres are needed to travel 300 km?
f: Litres needed = 300 divided by 15 = 20.
r: Fuel consumption problems use the formula distance divided by distance per litre.

q: A man walks 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How much time will he take to cover 1 km? (91)
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Time for 1 km = 100 / 20 = 5 minutes.
r: His speed is 20 km in 100 minutes, which is 12 km per hour.

q: A car travels at 30 km/h and a train travels twice as fast. What is the speed of the train? (4)
f: Twice the car's speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h, so the train covers 60 km in one hour.
r: In 30 minutes the same train would cover 30 km.

q: A man covers 20 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes. How many km does he cover in one minute?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes. Distance per minute = 20 / 100 = 0.2 km.
r: 0.2 km equals 200 metres per minute, or 12 km per hour.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. If the car covers 60 km in one hour, how much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (21)
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h; in 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time; convert minutes into hours first.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car. The car covers 60 km in one hour. How far will the train go in 30 minutes? (3)
f: Train speed = 120 km/h; in half an hour = 60 km.

q: The speed of a train is twice that of a car. If the car travels 100 km in one hour, how far does the train travel in 30 minutes? (2)
f: Train speed is 2 x 100 = 200 km/h. In half an hour it covers 200 / 2 = 100 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: A train moves at twice the speed of a car, and the car moves at 60 km/h. How far will the train go in 12 minutes? (4)
f: Train speed is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 12 minutes (12/60 = 0.2 hour) it covers 120 x 0.2 = 24 km.
r: To change minutes to hours, divide by 60.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (50)
f: Car speed is 30 km/h, so train speed is 2 x 30 = 60 km/h. In 30 minutes the train covers 60 x 0.5 = 30 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: If 8 men can complete a piece of work in 6 days, how many men are needed to complete half of that work in the same 6 days?
f: Total work is 8 x 6 = 48 man-days, so half the work is 24 man-days. In 6 days this needs 24 / 6 = 4 men.
r: Work done equals number of workers multiplied by days.

q: A train covers 20 km in 100 minutes. How long will it take to cover 1 km?
f: 100 minutes divided by 20 km gives 5 minutes for each km.
r: At this pace the train's speed is 12 km per hour.

q: A train is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes? (45)
f: 12 minutes = 1/5 hour; 90 / 5 = 18 km.
r: Convert minutes to hours: 12 minutes is 1/5 of an hour.

q: A man walked 4 km in 30 minutes and another 11 km in one hour. What was his per hour speed to cover the whole distance?
f: The total distance is 4 + 11 = 15 km and the total time is 1.5 hours. Speed = 15 / 1.5 = 10 km per hour.
r: Tip: average speed = total distance divided by total time.

q: A train travelled for 30 minutes at a speed of 90 km per hour and for another 50 minutes at a speed of 120 km per hour. How much distance will it cover?
f: In 30 minutes at 90 km per hour it goes 45 km. In 50 minutes at 120 km per hour it goes 100 km. The total is 145 km.
r: Tip: convert minutes to hours before multiplying by speed.

q: A train travels 60 km in 20 minutes. What is its speed in km/h?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Speed = 60 / (1/3) = 180 km/h.
r: To change km per minute into km per hour, multiply by 60.

q: A train covers 100 km in 1 hour. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
f: 12 minutes is 12/60 = 1/5 of an hour. Distance = 100 x 1/5 = 20 km.
r: Speed in km per hour times time in hours gives distance in km.

q: A car travels at 60 km/h and a train at twice that speed (120 km/h). How far does the train travel in 30 minutes? (306)
f: 30 minutes is half an hour, so distance = 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed multiplied by time.

q: Water flows through pipes, and blood flows through?
f: Blood flows through blood vessels such as veins (and arteries).
r: Veins carry blood to the heart; arteries carry it away.

q: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 20 minutes?
f: 20 minutes is 20/60 = 1/3 of an hour. Distance = 60 x 1/3 = 20 km.
r: Distance equals speed times time.

q: A train travels 6 meters in 1/4 minutes. How much distance (in meters) does it travel in 5 minutes?
f: 5 minutes contain 20 quarter-minutes, so the distance is 20 x 6 = 120 meters.
r: Tip: convert the time into units of the given interval and then multiply.

q: A train's speed is double that of a car, and the car travels 30 km in 1 hour. How much distance will the train cover in 30 minutes? (26)
f: Train speed = 2 x 30 = 60 km/h; in half an hour it covers 30 km.
r: Distance = speed x time; 30 minutes is half an hour.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train is twice as fast. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (30)
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 120 x 0.5 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A man covers 20 km in one hour and 40 minutes. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km? (30)
f: Total time is 100 minutes for 20 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 20 = 5 minutes (the source value 0.2 is wrong).
r: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves at twice the speed of the car. How much time will the train take to cover 60 km? (2)
f: Train speed is 120 km/h. Time = 60 / 120 = 0.5 hour = 30 minutes.
r: Time = distance divided by speed.

q: A car travels 70 km in one hour. How much distance will it travel in 40 minutes at the same speed?
f: 40 minutes is 40/60 = 2/3 of an hour. Distance = 70 x 2/3 = 46.67 km.
r: Distance equals speed multiplied by time.

q: A train travels with twice the speed of a car. If the car travels 1 km, how far does the train travel in the same time?
f: In the same time, a train with double the speed covers double the distance, so 2 x 1 = 2 km.
r: At equal times, distance is directly proportional to speed.

q: If 5 men complete a piece of work in 11 days, how many days will 1 man take to do it?
f: Total work = 5 x 11 = 55 man-days. One man needs 55 days.
r: Fewer workers need proportionally more days, which is inverse proportion.

q: Ali walked 20 km in 120 minutes. How much distance will Ali cover in 5 minutes at the same speed?
f: Speed is 20 km per 120 minutes, which is 1/6 km per minute. In 5 minutes he covers 5/6 km, about 0.83 km (833 m).
r: 20 km in 2 hours means a speed of 10 km/h.

q: A car travels at 60 km per hour. How much distance will it cover in 40 minutes?
f: 40 minutes = 2/3 hour. Distance = 60 x 2/3 = 40 km.
r: To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

q: A car moves at 60 km/h and a train moves twice as fast as the car. How much time will the train take to cover 30 km?
f: Speed of train = 2 x 60 = 120 km/h. Time = 30 / 120 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.
r: Time equals distance divided by speed.

q: A train is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes? (3)
f: 10 minutes is 1/6 hour. Distance = 60 x 1/6 = 10 km.
r: At 60 km/h a train covers 1 km each minute.

q: A train travels 60 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. How much distance will it cover in 12 minutes at the same speed?
f: 1 hour 40 minutes = 100 minutes, so speed = 60/100 = 0.6 km per minute. In 12 minutes it covers 0.6 x 12 = 7.2 km.
r: Speed here is 36 km per hour.

q: A train travels at 60 km per hour. How much time will it take to cover 3 km?
f: Speed is 60 km per hour, which is 1 km per minute. So 3 km takes 3 minutes.
r: 60 km per hour equals 1 km per minute, a handy conversion.

q: A bus moves at 60 km/h and a train moves at twice that speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 120 km/h. In half an hour: 60 km. (The PDF does not show the answer.)
r: Same as the train and car question: double speed, half time.

q: A man travels 90 km in 1 hour at a constant speed. In how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: 90 km takes 60 minutes, so 1 km takes 60 divided by 90 = 2/3 minute, which is 40 seconds.
r: Speed 90 km per hour equals 1.5 km per minute.

q: How much distance will you cover in 3 and a half minutes if you are moving at the speed of 120 km/h?
f: 120 km/h is 2 km per minute, so in 3.5 minutes you cover 2 x 3.5 = 7 km.
r: Tip: dividing km/h by 60 gives km per minute.

q: A train travels at twice the speed of a car, and the car covers 20 km in one hour. How far will the train travel in 30 minutes? (3)
f: Train speed = 2 x 20 = 40 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 40 x 1/2 = 20 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: A car travels at 120 km/h and another car travels twice as fast. How far will the second car travel in 30 minutes?
f: The second car's speed is 2 x 120 = 240 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it travels 240 x 1/2 = 120 km.
r: Distance = speed x time.

q: If 10 men can dig a well in 5 days, how many days will 5 men take to dig it? (2)
f: Total work = 10 x 5 = 50 man-days. With 5 men, days = 50 / 5 = 10 days.
r: Fewer workers need proportionally more time, which is called inverse proportion.

q: A jet uses 80 gallons of fuel to fly at 320 km per hour (80 gallons per 320 km). How many gallons are needed to cover 700 km? (2)
f: Fuel per km = 80 / 320 = 0.25 gallons. For 700 km: 700 x 0.25 = 175 gallons.
r: Fuel needed is directly proportional to distance when the rate of use stays the same.

q: A helicopter flies at 340 km/h. About how much time does it take to cover 700 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 700 / 340 = 2.06 hours, which is about 2 hours 4 minutes.
r: Speed = distance / time is the basic formula behind such questions.

q: If a man travels 90 km in 1 hour and 40 minutes, in how many minutes will he cover 1 km?
f: Time is 100 minutes for 90 km, so 1 km takes 100 / 90 = 1.11 minutes (the source value 0.9 is wrong).
r: Minutes per km = total minutes / total km.

q: A car runs at 90 km/h and the train runs at double the car speed. How much distance does the train cover in 30 minutes?
f: Train speed = 2 x 90 = 180 km/h. In 30 minutes (half an hour) it covers 180 / 2 = 90 km.
r: To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

q: A car travels at 90 km per hour. How much distance does it cover in 40 minutes?
f: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, so distance = 90 x 2/3 = 60 km.
r: Distance = speed x time, with time converted into hours.

q: A train covers 90 km in 1 hour. How much time will it take to cover 120 km?
f: Time = distance / speed = 120 / 90 = 4/3 hours. 4/3 hours is 1 hour 20 minutes.
r: The same train covers 1.5 km every minute.

q: Travelling at a speed of 120 km/hour, how much time would be taken to cover a road that is 24 km long?
f: Time = distance / speed = 24 / 120 = 0.2 hour, which is 0.2 x 60 = 12 minutes.
r: Tip: remember time = distance divided by speed, and convert hours to minutes by multiplying by 60.

q: A car is moving at 120 km/h. How much distance does it cover in 10 minutes?
f: 10 minutes = 1/6 hour, and 120 x 1/6 = 20 km.
r: Km per minute = km/h divided by 60 (120 km/h = 2 km per minute).

q: A train moves at twice the speed of a car. If the car covers 120 km in 60 minutes, in how many minutes will the train cover 120 km?
f: Car speed is 120 km/h, so train speed is 240 km/h. Time for 120 km is 120 divided by 240, which is half an hour, or 30 minutes.
r: When speed doubles, the time for the same distance is halved.

q: The speed of a train is double that of a car. If the car's speed is 60 km/h, what is the speed of the train? (12)
f: Double of 60 km/h is 2 x 60 = 120 km/h.
r: Speed = distance divided by time.

q: A train travels at 120 km/h. How far does it travel in 18 minutes?
f: 18 minutes is 0.3 hour, so distance = 120 x 0.3 = 36 km.
r: Distance = speed x time. 120 km/h means 2 km per minute.

q: If a train covers a distance of 75 km in one hour, how much time will it take to cover 225 km?
f: Time = 225 / 75 = 3 hours.
r: Tip: time = distance divided by speed.

q: A train's speed is twice that of a car, and the train covers 120 km in 1 hour. How far does the car travel in 15 minutes? (2)
f: The train's speed is 120 km/h, so the car's speed is 120 / 2 = 60 km/h. In 15 minutes (a quarter of an hour) the car covers 60 / 4 = 15 km.
r: 15 minutes are one quarter of an hour.

q: A car runs at 60 km/hr and a train runs at twice the speed of the car. What is the speed of the train?
f: Train speed = 2 x 60 = 120 km/hr. Speed does not change with the time taken, so it is still 120 km/hr after 30 minutes.
r: In 30 minutes this train would cover 60 km.

q: A man covers 3 km in 1 hour. How much distance will he cover in 20 minutes at the same speed?
f: 20 minutes = 1/3 hour. Distance = 3 x 1/3 = 1 km.
r: At this speed he walks 1 km every 20 minutes.

q: A man travelled 65 km in a car. He travelled the first 35 km at the speed of 70 km per hour and the other 30 km at the speed of 90 km per hour. How many minutes did he take to travel the whole distance?
f: 35 km at 70 km per hour is 0.5 hour or 30 minutes. 30 km at 90 km per hour is one third of an hour or 20 minutes. The total is 50 minutes.
r: Tip: time = distance divided by speed, calculated for each part.
