f: The people of Makkah called him Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and As-Sadiq (the truthful). Al-Farooq is the title of Umar (RA), As-Siddiq of Abu Bakr (RA), and Saifullah of Khalid bin Walid (RA).
r: Because he was Al-Amin, the Quraysh accepted his decision on placing the Black Stone (Hajr-e-Aswad) in the Kaaba.

q: Which pact did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) participate in to support the oppressed?
f: Hilf al-Fudul was a pact made in Makkah before prophethood to help the oppressed, and he took part in it as a young man. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), the Pledges of Aqabah and the Charter of Madinah all came after prophethood.
r: Hilf al-Fudul was made in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an after the Harb al-Fijar wars.

q: How old was Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) when he married Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
f: He married Khadijah (RA) at the age of 25, and she was about 40. 40 was his age at the first revelation, so the other options are wrong.
r: Khadijah (RA) was his first wife, and he did not marry anyone else during her life. All his children except Ibrahim were from her.

q: Which Surah contains the first five verses identified as the first revelation?
f: The first revelation was the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq, starting with Iqra (Read), in the Cave of Hira. Al-Muddaththir came after the pause in revelation, and Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah came later.
r: Surah Al-Alaq is the 96th Surah. The first complete Surah revealed is commonly said to be Al-Fatihah.

q: Who was the first person to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Khadijah (RA) was the first person of all to accept Islam. Abu Bakr (RA) was the first free adult man, Ali (RA) the first child, and Zayd (RA) the first freed slave.
r: Khadijah (RA) died in the Year of Sorrow, the same year as Abu Talib.

q: Who is commonly identified as the first adult free man to accept Islam?
f: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (RA) was the first free adult man to accept Islam. Ali (RA) was a child then, Uthman (RA) accepted Islam through Abu Bakr (RA), and Umar (RA) accepted Islam years later.
r: Through Abu Bakr (RA), Uthman, Zubair, Talha, Abdur Rahman bin Auf and Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA) accepted Islam.

q: Who is commonly identified as the first child to accept Islam?
f: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) was about 10 years old when he accepted Islam, so he was the first child Muslim. Hasan, Husayn and Usama (RA) were born after that.
r: Ali (RA) lived in the Prophet's (PBUH) house as a child. He later married Fatimah (RA).

q: Who was the first freed slave commonly identified among the earliest Muslims?
f: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA), the freed slave and adopted son of the Prophet (PBUH), was among the first four Muslims. Bilal (RA) accepted Islam a little later, Ammar (RA) was not a freed slave of the Prophet, and Salman (RA) accepted Islam in Madinah.
r: Zayd (RA) is the only companion named in the Quran (Surah Al-Ahzab). He was martyred at the Battle of Mu'tah.

q: For approximately how many years was the Islamic message initially preached privately?
f: The secret preaching lasted about 3 years. Then Allah ordered open preaching, and the Prophet (PBUH) called the Quraysh from Mount Safa. 2, 5 and 7 years are not the accepted period.
r: Dar al-Arqam was the house used as the secret centre of the early Muslims.

q: Which Christian scholar did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) meet through Hazrat Khadijah (RA)?
f: After the first revelation, Khadijah (RA) took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who said the same angel (Namus) came to Musa (AS). Bahira was the monk met on the Syria trip, Heraclius was the Roman emperor, and Nestorius was an old church leader.
r: Waraqah was Khadijah's (RA) cousin and knew the Torah and Gospel.

q: From which hill did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) publicly call the Quraysh to Islam?
f: He stood on Mount Safa near the Kaaba and called the Quraysh openly to Islam. Uhud is in Madinah, Arafat is outside Makkah, and Marwah is the other hill of Sa'i, not this event.
r: Before that he invited his family to a dinner (Dawat-e-Dhul Ashira).

q: Which uncle opposed Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during his public warning at Mount Safa?
f: Abu Lahab cursed him at Mount Safa, and Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) was revealed about him. Abu Talib protected him, Hamza later accepted Islam, and Abbas did not oppose him there.
r: Abu Lahab's real name was Abdul Uzza. His wife Umm Jamil is also condemned in the same Surah.

q: Who is traditionally recognized as the first martyr of Islam?
f: Sumayyah (RA), mother of Ammar (RA), was killed by Abu Jahl and is the first martyr of Islam. Her husband Yasir (RA) was also martyred but after her, Bilal (RA) survived, and Hamza (RA) was martyred later at Uhud.
r: The first male martyr is commonly said to be Yasir (RA). Hamza (RA) is called Sayyid ush-Shuhada (leader of martyrs).

q: Which companion endured persecution while repeatedly declaring the oneness of Allah?
f: Bilal (RA) was tortured by his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf on hot sand but kept saying Ahad, Ahad (Allah is One). Ammar, Abu Dharr and Khabbab (RA) were also persecuted, but the Ahad Ahad story is of Bilal (RA).
r: Abu Bakr (RA) bought Bilal (RA) and set him free. Bilal (RA) later became the first Mu'adhdhin of Islam.

q: Where did the first migration of Muslims to escape persecution take place?
f: The first Hijrah was to Abyssinia (Habshah, now Ethiopia) in the 5th year of Prophethood. Hijrah to Yathrib (Madinah) was later, Taif was only a visit, and Yemen is wrong.
r: Uthman (RA) and his wife Ruqayyah (RA) were in the first group. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA) spoke before the Najashi in the second migration.

q: What title was used for the Christian ruler of Abyssinia who gave shelter to Muslims?
f: The king of Abyssinia was called Najashi (Negus); his name was Ashama. Heraclius was the Roman emperor, Chosroes (Kisra) the Persian king, and Muqawqis the ruler of Egypt.
r: Najashi Ashama later accepted Islam, and the Prophet (PBUH) offered his funeral prayer in absentia.

q: Which uncle and protector of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died during the Year of Sorrow?
f: Abu Talib died in the 10th year of Prophethood, called Aam al-Huzn (Year of Sorrow). Abu Lahab died after Badr, Hamza (RA) was martyred at Uhud, and Abbas (RA) lived long after.
r: Khadijah (RA) also died in the Year of Sorrow.

q: Which city did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) visit seeking support after facing opposition in Makkah?
f: After the Year of Sorrow he went to Taif to seek help, but its people stoned him. Madinah was the place of Hijrah later, and Khaybar and Tabuk are places of later expeditions.
r: Taif is the city of the Banu Thaqif tribe. On the way back, a Christian slave named Addas met him.

q: Which companion accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) on his journey to Taif?
f: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) went with him to Taif and was injured while protecting him. Abu Bakr (RA) was his companion in the Hijrah, not Taif; Ali and Umar (RA) did not go.
r: The Taif journey was in the 10th year of Prophethood.

q: What is the night journey from Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa called?
f: The night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem is called Isra. Mi'raj is the ascension from Al-Aqsa to the heavens, Hijrah is migration, and Ghazwah is a battle.
r: Surah Bani Israel (Al-Isra) begins with this journey. The Prophet (PBUH) rode Buraq.

q: What is the ascension of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) to the heavens called?
f: Mi'raj means the ascension from Masjid al-Aqsa up through the heavens. Isra is only the night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem. Ghazwah is a battle and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
r: Isra and Mi'raj happened about one year before Hijrah. Surah Bani Israil (Al-Isra) starts with the Isra.

q: Which fundamental act of worship was prescribed during the event of Mi'raj?
f: The five daily prayers (Salah) were made obligatory on the night of Mi'raj. Fasting and Zakat came in 2 AH in Madinah, and Hajj was made obligatory later (about 9 AH).
r: At first 50 prayers were ordered, then reduced to 5 with the reward of 50. Salah is the only worship made obligatory in the heavens.

q: From which sacred mosque did the night journey begin in Makkah?
f: The Isra began at Masjid al-Haram in Makkah, as Surah Al-Isra verse 1 says. Masjid al-Aqsa was the end point of the journey. Quba and Masjid an-Nabawi are in Madinah and were built after Hijrah.
r: Isra: Masjid al-Haram to Masjid al-Aqsa on the Buraq. Masjid al-Aqsa was the first Qiblah.

q: What were the pledges made between Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and people from Yathrib called?
f: The people of Yathrib gave their pledges at Aqabah near Mina, so they are called the Pledges of Aqabah. Hudaybiyyah (6 AH) was a treaty with Quraysh, the Charter of Madinah came after Hijrah, and Ridwan was under a tree at Hudaybiyyah.
r: First Aqabah: 12 men (621 CE). Second Aqabah: about 73 men and 2 women (622 CE).

q: What was the earlier name of Madinah?
f: Madinah was called Yathrib before Hijrah; it became Madinat-un-Nabi, the City of the Prophet. Bakkah is an old name of Makkah, Faran is a name linked to the Makkah area, and Khaybar is a separate oasis north of Madinah.
r: Madinah is also called Taybah. Makkah is also called Umm al-Qura.

q: Who was sent to Yathrib as an early Muslim teacher after the First Pledge of Aqabah?
f: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) was the first teacher (envoy) of Islam sent to Yathrib. Abu Bakr and Bilal stayed in Makkah, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a man of Madinah, later sent to Yemen.
r: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer martyred at Uhud. Mu'adh ibn Jabal was sent to Yemen as governor and teacher.

q: Who slept in Prophet Muhammad's (PBUH) bed on the night of Hijrah?
f: Ali (RA) slept in the Prophet's bed to trick the Quraysh and later returned people's trusts (amanat). Abu Bakr travelled with the Prophet, Umar had migrated openly earlier, and Uthman had gone to Abyssinia and Madinah.
r: Hijrah took place in 622 CE (Rabi al-Awwal, 1 AH era). Ali joined the Prophet in Quba a few days later.

q: Who accompanied Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) during the migration to Madinah?
f: Abu Bakr (RA) was the Prophet's companion on the Hijrah and in the cave (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40). Ali stayed back in Makkah, Umar migrated before, and Zayd went with the Prophet to Taif, not on Hijrah.
r: Abdullah ibn Urayqit was their guide. Asma bint Abi Bakr brought food and got the title Dhat an-Nitaqayn.

q: In which cave did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (RA) take refuge during Hijrah?
f: They hid for three nights in the Cave of Thawr, south of Makkah. Cave Hira is where the first revelation came, and Uhud and Quba are places in Madinah.
r: Cave Hira is on Jabal an-Nur. The spider web and the dove's nest at Thawr are famous stories.

q: Who was the leader of the hypocrites in Madinah commonly mentioned in Seerah?
f: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul led the hypocrites (Munafiqun) in Madinah. Abu Jahl was an open enemy in Makkah, Musaylimah was a false prophet, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was a Jewish poet.
r: Ibn Ubayy went back with about 300 men before Uhud. Surah Al-Munafiqun is about the hypocrites.

q: Which Jewish scholar of Madinah accepted Islam and became a companion?
f: Abdullah ibn Salam (RA), a rabbi of Banu Qaynuqa, accepted Islam soon after Hijrah. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Huyayy ibn Akhtab stayed enemies, and Abu Jahl was a pagan of Makkah.
r: Huyayy ibn Akhtab was a chief of Banu Nadir. Safiyyah (RA), his daughter, became a wife of the Prophet.

q: What title was given to the Muslims of Madinah who welcomed the emigrants?
f: Ansar means helpers; they were the Muslims of Madinah (Aws and Khazraj). Muhajirun were the emigrants from Makkah, Tabi'un came after the companions, and Ashab al-Suffah lived on the Suffah platform.
r: The Ansar came from two tribes: Aws and Khazraj. The Prophet made brotherhood (Mu'akhat) between Ansar and Muhajirun.

q: What was the platform in Masjid an-Nabawi associated with companions devoted to learning?
f: The Suffah was a shaded platform where poor companions lived and learned; it is called the first residential school of Islam. The Mihrab is the prayer niche, the Minbar is the pulpit, and the Rawdah is the area between the pulpit and the Prophet's house.
r: Abu Hurairah (RA) was one of the famous Ashab al-Suffah. Masjid an-Nabawi was built in 1 AH.

q: Which companion reported a dream containing the wording of the Adhan?
f: Abdullah ibn Zayd (RA) saw the words of the Adhan in a dream and told the Prophet, who approved them. Bilal was told to call it because of his strong voice. Uthman and Abu Bakr did not report this dream.
r: The Adhan began in 1 AH (some say 2 AH) in Madinah. Bilal (RA) was the first Mu'adhdhin.

q: Who became the most famous early Mu'adhdhin of Islam?
f: Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) was the first and most famous Mu'adhdhin of the Prophet. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was a second Mu'adhdhin but less famous, while Ammar and Salman were not Mu'adhdhins.
r: Bilal gave the Adhan on the Kaaba at the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH). His former master was Umayyah ibn Khalaf.

q: In which month of 2 AH was fasting in Ramadan made obligatory?
f: The order to fast in Ramadan came in Sha'ban of 2 AH, just before the first Ramadan in Madinah. Ramadan is the month of fasting itself, not the month the order came, and Rajab and Shawwal are wrong months.
r: The Qiblah was also changed in 2 AH (Rajab or Sha'ban). Battle of Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

q: In which year of Hijrah was the obligation of Ramadan fasting introduced?
f: Fasting in Ramadan became obligatory in 2 AH. In 1 AH Masjid an-Nabawi was built, 5 AH was the Battle of the Trench, and 9 AH is when Hajj became obligatory (per most scholars).
r: Zakat and Eid prayers also started in 2 AH. Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183 is the fasting verse.

q: In which direction did Muslims pray before the Qiblah was changed to the Kaaba?
f: Muslims first prayed toward Bait al-Maqdis (Masjid al-Aqsa) in Jerusalem for about 16-17 months after Hijrah. Damascus, Cairo and Mount Sinai were never the Qiblah.
r: The Qiblah changed to the Kaaba in 2 AH (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144). Masjid al-Aqsa is called the first Qiblah.

q: Which mosque is associated with the change of Qiblah during prayer?
f: Masjid al-Qiblatayn means the mosque of two Qiblahs, because the Qiblah changed during a prayer there. Quba is the first mosque built in Islam, Masjid an-Nabawi is the Prophet's mosque, and al-Ghamamah is linked to Eid prayer.
r: Masjid Quba is the first mosque of Islam. The Qiblah change came in 2 AH.

q: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) married Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)?
f: Fatimah (RA) married Ali (RA) in 2 AH. Zaynab married Abu al-As, and Ruqayyah and then Umm Kulthum married Uthman (RA).
r: Uthman (RA) is called Dhun-Nurayn because he married two daughters of the Prophet. Hasan and Husayn were sons of Ali and Fatimah.

q: Which expedition is regarded as the first Ghazwah led personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
f: Ghazwah al-Abwa (Waddan), in Safar 2 AH, was the first expedition the Prophet led himself. Buwat, Safwan (first Badr) and Ushayrah came after it in the same year.
r: Ushayrah led to a treaty with Banu Mudlij. Badr al-Kubra (17 Ramadan 2 AH) was the first big battle.

q: What is a military campaign attended personally by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) called?
f: A Ghazwah is a campaign in which the Prophet himself took part. A Sariyyah is one he sent without going himself, Hijrah is migration, and Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage.
r: Most counts give 27 Ghazwat and about 50 or more Saraya. The last Ghazwah was Tabuk (9 AH).

q: Which prominent Quraysh leader was killed at Badr?
f: Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham) was killed at Badr by the young Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, and finished by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah and Amr ibn al-Aas survived and later accepted Islam.
r: Abu Jahl was called the Pharaoh of this Ummah. Abu Sufyan led the Quraysh caravan before Badr.

q: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Badr according to accounts?
f: 14 Muslims were martyred at Badr (6 Muhajirun and 8 Ansar). 70 is the number of Quraysh killed at Badr and also of Muslims martyred at Uhud, so it is wrong here.
r: 313 Muslims fought about 1,000 Quraysh at Badr. 70 Quraysh were killed and 70 captured.

q: Approximately how many Quraysh fighters were killed at Badr?
f: About 70 Quraysh were killed and about 70 were taken prisoner at Badr. 14 is the number of Muslim martyrs, and 100 and 300 are not given in the accounts.
r: Badr was on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 CE). The Muslims were 313 against about 1,000.

q: Which daughter of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) died around the time of the Battle of Badr?
f: Ruqayyah (RA), wife of Uthman, died in Madinah while the Muslims were at Badr; Uthman stayed back to nurse her. Zaynab died in 8 AH, Umm Kulthum in 9 AH, and Fatimah after the Prophet.
r: Uthman then married Umm Kulthum and got the title Dhun-Nurayn. Uthman got a share of Badr booty though absent.

q: What educational condition was set for releasing certain literate prisoners after Badr?
o: Teach children to read and write
f: Literate prisoners who could not pay ransom were freed after each taught 10 Muslim children to read and write. Ransom was for those who could pay, no one was forced to convert, and building houses was not a condition.
r: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA) learned writing this way. Ransom per prisoner was about 1,000 to 4,000 dirhams.

q: What name does the Qur'an use for the day of the Battle of Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal 8:41 calls Badr Yaum al-Furqan, the Day of Criterion between truth and falsehood. Fath refers to the Conquest of Makkah, Ahzab to the Trench, and Jumu'ah is Friday.
r: Surah Al-Anfal was revealed about Badr. Surah Al-Ahzab is about the Battle of the Trench (5 AH).

q: According to the Qur'an, how many angels were initially promised as reinforcement at Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal 8:9 says Allah helped with a thousand angels one after another. 3,000 and 5,000 are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran as further promises, and 100 and 10,000 are not mentioned.
r: Surah Al-Imran 3:124-125 mentions 3,000 and 5,000 angels. 10,000 was the size of the Muslim army at the Conquest of Makkah.

q: Who was the former master of Bilal (RA) who was killed at Badr?
f: Umayyah ibn Khalaf tortured Bilal (RA) in Makkah and was killed at Badr. Utbah and Walid were killed in the first duels at Badr but were not Bilal's masters, and Abu Lahab did not go to Badr and died in Makkah.
r: Abu Bakr (RA) bought and freed Bilal. Hamza, Ali and Ubaydah fought the first duels at Badr.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was captured at Badr?
f: Abbas (RA) fought on the Quraysh side and was taken prisoner, then paid ransom. Abu Talib had died before Hijrah, Hamza fought for the Muslims, and Abu Lahab did not join the battle.
r: Abbas openly accepted Islam before the Conquest of Makkah. Abu Lahab died a few days after Badr.

q: Which Jewish tribe was expelled from Madinah after the conflict following Badr?
f: Banu Qaynuqa broke the treaty after Badr and were expelled in 2 AH. Banu Nadir were expelled in 4 AH, Banu Qurayzah were punished after the Trench in 5 AH, and Ghatafan was an Arab tribe, not Jewish.
r: The three Jewish tribes of Madinah: Qaynuqa, Nadir, Qurayzah. Surah Al-Hashr is about Banu Nadir.

q: Which cousin of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) distinguished himself in the fighting at Badr?
f: Ali (RA), the Prophet's cousin, won his duel against Walid ibn Utbah and fought bravely at Badr. Abu Bakr was not a cousin and stayed with the Prophet at the command shelter, Uthman was absent, and Mu'adh ibn Jabal was not a cousin.
r: Ali got the sword Dhul-Fiqar at Badr. Hamza (RA) killed Utbah ibn Rabi'ah in the duels.

q: Which Surah contains the final explicit Qur'anic prohibition of intoxicants?
f: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90-91 gave the final, complete ban on wine and gambling. Al-Baqarah 2:219 only said the harm is greater than the benefit, while Al-Fil and Al-Kawthar are short Makki surahs not about intoxicants.
r: Wine was banned in stages: Al-Baqarah 2:219, An-Nisa 4:43, then Al-Ma'idah 5:90. The final ban came around 3-4 AH.

q: Which expedition is commonly known as the Battle of Sawiq?
f: Ghazwah as-Sawiq (2 AH) was the chase of Abu Sufyan after his raid near Madinah; his men threw away bags of sawiq (barley flour) while fleeing. Uhud, Khandaq and Khaybar were different, bigger battles.
r: Sawiq means barley flour. Abu Sufyan made this raid to fulfil his oath after Badr.

q: In which Islamic month and year did the Battle of Uhud take place?
f: Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH (March 625 CE). Ramadan 2 AH was Badr, and the other dates do not match any of these battles.
r: Battle of the Trench: Shawwal/Dhul Qa'dah 5 AH. Badr: 17 Ramadan 2 AH.

q: How many Muslims initially set out toward Uhud before a group withdrew?
f: About 1,000 Muslims set out; Abdullah ibn Ubayy then left with about 300, leaving about 700. 313 was Badr, 3,000 was the Quraysh army, and 700 is the number left after the withdrawal.
r: About 700 Muslims fought at Uhud against 3,000 Quraysh. 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

q: Approximately how many Quraysh soldiers participated in the Battle of Uhud?
f: The Quraysh came to Uhud with about 3,000 soldiers under Abu Sufyan. 1,000 was their number at Badr, and 10,000 was the size of the allied army at the Trench (Ahzab).
r: The Quraysh had about 200 horses at Uhud. At the Trench the confederates had about 10,000.

q: How many archers were positioned to guard the Muslim army's rear at Uhud?
f: The Prophet placed 50 archers on the hill of Ainain (Jabal ar-Rumat) to guard the rear. About 10 stayed back when the others left, and 100 and 200 are wrong.
r: The archers' hill is called Jabal ar-Rumat (Hill of Archers). Their leader was Abdullah ibn Jubayr.

q: Who commanded the archers positioned at Uhud?
f: Abdullah ibn Jubayr (RA) led the 50 archers and stayed at his post until he was martyred. Mus'ab held the standard, Hamza fought in the main army, and Khalid was then on the Quraysh side.
r: Mus'ab ibn Umayr was the standard-bearer at Uhud. Khalid ibn al-Walid accepted Islam in 8 AH.

q: Which military commander exploited the opening left by archers at Uhud?
f: Khalid ibn al-Walid led the Quraysh cavalry around the hill and attacked from behind when the archers left. Abu Sufyan was the overall leader, and Ikrimah helped Khalid but did not lead the attack; Amr ibn al-Aas did not lead it.
r: Khalid later got the title Saifullah (Sword of Allah) at Mu'tah. He accepted Islam in 8 AH.

q: Which uncle of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the Lion of Allah, was martyred at Uhud?
f: Hamza (RA), Asadullah, was martyred at Uhud by Wahshi's spear. Abu Talib died before Hijrah, Abbas lived long after, and Ja'far was a cousin martyred at Mu'tah.
r: Hamza is called Sayyid ash-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs). Ja'far is called Ja'far at-Tayyar.

q: Who was the Muslim standard-bearer martyred at Uhud?
f: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) carried the flag at Uhud and was martyred holding it. Ali took the flag after him and survived, Hamza was martyred but not as flag-bearer, and Sa'd was an archer who survived.
r: Mus'ab was the first teacher sent to Yathrib. He looked like the Prophet, so some thought the Prophet was killed.

q: How many Muslims were martyred at the Battle of Uhud according to accounts?
f: About 70 Muslims were martyred at Uhud, most of them Ansar. 14 was Badr's number of martyrs, 313 was the Muslim army at Badr, and 100 is not given.
r: Quraysh lost about 22-23 men at Uhud. Martyrs of Uhud are buried near Jabal Uhud.

q: What injury did Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) sustain during the Battle of Uhud?
f: At Uhud a front tooth (lower right) of the Prophet was broken and two rings of his helmet went into his cheek. He did not break his arm, did not lose his sight, and was not unhurt.
r: Abu Ubaydah (RA) pulled out the helmet rings with his teeth. Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas threw the stone that hurt the Prophet.

q: Which companion is remembered for defending Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) at Uhud?
f: Talhah (RA) shielded the Prophet with his own body and his hand was paralysed by arrows. Abu Lahab was an enemy who died after Badr, Ibn Ubayy left before the battle, and Musaylimah was a false prophet.
r: Talhah is one of the Ashara Mubashara (ten promised Paradise). Abu Dujanah and Nusaybah bint Ka'b also shielded the Prophet at Uhud.

q: What major lesson is drawn from Uhud regarding the Muslim archers?
o: Obedience to the Prophet (PBUH) was essential
f: The archers left their post against the Prophet's clear order, and the Muslims lost the upper hand; so the lesson is obedience. Leaving early caused the loss, cavalry was in fact used against them, and returning to Makkah makes no sense.
r: Surah Al-Imran (verses 121-175) discusses Uhud. The archers were told not to leave even if birds snatched the army.

q: Who is the Chief Minister of Sindh? (2)
f: Syed Murad Ali Shah of the PPP is the Chief Minister of Sindh; he was re-elected after the February 2024 elections.
r: Sindh's provincial assembly sits in Karachi.

q: Which is the third Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Surah Aal-e-Imran comes third, after Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah.
r: Surah Aal-e-Imran has 200 verses and was revealed in Madinah.

q: What is the capital city of Sindh province?
f: Karachi is the provincial capital of Sindh. Hyderabad is a big city of Sindh but not its capital.
r: Karachi was also Pakistan's first federal capital.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'Wild'?
f: 'Wild' means not controlled by people; 'tame' means trained or domesticated.
r: Fierce, savage and untamed are synonyms of 'wild', not opposites.

q: What title was given to Liaquat Ali Khan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister, is called Quaid-e-Millat (Leader of the Nation).
r: Fatima Jinnah is called Madar-e-Millat (Mother of the Nation).

q: In which year did Pakistan join SEATO?
f: Pakistan signed the Manila Pact (SEATO) in September 1954.
r: Pakistan joined the Baghdad Pact (later CENTO) in 1955.

q: What is one-third of 120?
r: One-quarter of 120 is 30.

q: What is 90% of 90? (2)
Why do we boil milk before drinking it?
o: To add more vitamins to it
To make it digest more slowly
To kill harmful bacteria and germs
f: Boiling kills the harmful microorganisms in raw milk.
r: Pasteurisation heats milk to a lower temperature to kill germs without boiling it.

q: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to which Prophet?
f: Allah revealed the Injeel to Hazrat Isa (A.S).
r: The Taurat was revealed to Hazrat Musa (A.S) and the Zaboor to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).

q: Which is the last (12th) month of the Islamic calendar?
f: Dhul-Hijjah is the 12th month; Hajj and Eid-ul-Adha take place in it.
r: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar.

q: When was the Pakistan-China Border Agreement signed? (2)
f: The Sino-Pakistan boundary agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.
r: Pakistan and China set up diplomatic relations on 21 May 1951.

q: Hazrat Maryam (A.S) is the mother of which Prophet? (2)
f: Hazrat Maryam (A.S) gave birth to Hazrat Isa (A.S) without a father, by Allah's command.
r: Surah Maryam (Surah 19) is named after her.

q: In which year of Prophethood (Nabwi) were the five daily prayers made obligatory?
f: The five daily prayers were made obligatory on the night of Isra and Mi'raj, commonly dated to the 10th year of Prophethood.
r: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in 2 AH.

q: What is the synonym of 'Prevalent'? (2)
f: 'Prevalent' means common or widespread.
r: Its antonym is 'rare'.

q: Which is the longest river in Europe? (2)
f: The Volga (about 3,530 km) flows through Russia into the Caspian Sea.
r: The Danube is the second longest river in Europe.

q: Which is the smallest continent in the world?
f: Australia is the smallest continent by land area.
r: Asia is the largest continent.

q: Where and when was Liaquat Ali Khan assassinated?
f: He was shot at Company Bagh (now Liaquat Bagh), Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
r: Benazir Bhutto was also assassinated at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, in 2007.

q: The absolute value of any real number is always:
f: |x| is the distance from zero on the number line, so it is never negative.

q: In statistics, the 'average' is also called the:
f: The average (arithmetic mean) is the sum of values divided by their number.
r: The median is the middle value when data is arranged in order.

q: What is the current total strength of the Senate of Pakistan?
f: After the 25th Amendment merged FATA into KP, its 8 Senate seats ended, so the Senate went from 104 to 96 members.
r: The National Assembly has 336 seats.

q: How many general seats does each province have in the Senate?
f: Each province has 23 Senate seats in total: 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat/ulema and 1 non-Muslim.
r: All four provinces have equal seats in the Senate, whatever their population.

q: During the Khilafat Movement (Hijrat Movement of 1920), Muslims migrated to which country?
f: In 1920 many Indian Muslims, calling India Dar-ul-Harb, migrated to Afghanistan.
r: Afghanistan soon closed its border, and many migrants returned in great hardship.

q: Where did Hazrat Amina, mother of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), pass away?
f: She died at Abwa, between Makkah and Madinah, when the Prophet (PBUH) was about six.
r: She was returning from Madinah (Yathrib) after visiting relatives.

q: Who was the first Muazzin of Islam? (2)
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) chose Hazrat Bilal (R.A) to give the first Azan in Madinah.
r: Hazrat Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (R.A) also gave Azan in Madinah.

q: Who were the first to offer Namaz (prayer) in Islam?
o: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (R.A)
Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) and Hazrat Umar (R.A)
f: Hazrat Khadija (R.A) was the first to pray along with the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: Hazrat Khadija (R.A) was also the first person to accept Islam.

q: Which pass connects Chitral with Upper Dir?
f: The Lowari Pass links Dir and Chitral; the Lowari Tunnel now runs under it.
r: Shandur Pass links Chitral with Gilgit.

q: Who was the last Governor-General of Pakistan? (2)
f: Iskander Mirza became Governor-General in 1955 and then the first President in 1956.
r: Quaid-e-Azam was the first Governor-General.

q: Which day is observed internationally on 12 July? (3)
f: The UN declared 12 July, Malala Yousafzai's birthday, as Malala Day.
r: International Day of Education is on 24 January.

q: Who was the first captain of the Indian women's cricket team?
f: Shantha Rangaswamy led India in its first women's Test in 1976.
r: Mithali Raj is India's highest run-scorer in women's ODIs.

q: How many people have received the Nishan-e-Haider? (2)
f: 10 soldiers received it, and Naik Saif Ali Janjua's Hilal-e-Kashmir is treated as equal, making 11.
r: Captain Raja Muhammad Sarwar was the first recipient.

q: How many articles were in the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles in 13 parts and 6 schedules.
r: The 1962 Constitution had 250 articles; the 1973 Constitution originally had 280.

q: In which year were the first general elections held under the 1973 Constitution? (3)
f: Elections were held in March 1977; protests followed and martial law came in July 1977.
r: The 1985 elections were held on a non-party basis.

q: In which country is the Great Slave Lake located?
f: Great Slave Lake is in Canada's Northwest Territories.
r: It is the deepest lake in North America.

q: How many continents are there in the world?
f: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
r: Asia is the largest and Australia the smallest.

q: Ghazwa-e-Tabook was led against which empire?
f: In 9 AH the Holy Prophet (PBUH) led the army to Tabook against the Byzantine Romans.
r: Tabook was the last Ghazwa of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

q: When was the Tashkent Declaration between Pakistan and India signed?
f: Ayub Khan and Lal Bahadur Shastri signed it after the 1965 war.
r: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972.

q: Which is the most abundant chemical element in the universe?
f: Hydrogen makes up about 75% of the normal matter in the universe; helium is second.
r: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth's crust.

q: Who was the first President of Pakistan?
f: Iskander Mirza took oath as first President on 23 March 1956 under the first constitution.
r: Ayub Khan removed him in October 1958.

q: What was the relationship between Hazrat Asma (R.A) and Hazrat Aisha (R.A)?
f: Both were daughters of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (R.A), from different mothers.
r: Hazrat Asma (R.A) is called 'Zat-un-Nitaqain' (she of the two belts).

q: When was the Basic Democracies system introduced in Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan introduced Basic Democracies in 1959 with 80,000 elected members.
r: These Basic Democrats elected the President in 1960 and 1965.

q: Mangla Dam was built during whose government?
f: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River was completed in 1967 under the Indus Basin Project in Ayub Khan's era.
r: Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed in 1976.

q: Which is the longest river in North America?
f: The Missouri (about 3,767 km) is slightly longer than the Mississippi, which it joins.
r: The Mississippi-Missouri system together is the longest in North America.

q: By which treaty was Kashmir sold to Gulab Singh in 1846?
f: On 16 March 1846 the British sold Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees.
r: The Treaty of Lahore (9 March 1846) ended the First Anglo-Sikh War.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India?
f: Babur founded it after defeating Ibrahim Lodhi at Panipat in 1526.
r: Sher Shah Suri briefly drove out Humayun and founded the Sur dynasty.

q: Which country opposed Pakistan's UN membership in 1947?
f: Afghanistan cast the only vote against, over the Durand Line dispute.
r: Iran was the first country to recognise Pakistan.

q: How many member states does SAARC have?
f: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.
r: SAARC was founded in Dhaka in 1985 with 7 members; Afghanistan joined in 2007.

q: Which is the smallest continent by land area? (2)
f: Australia covers about 7.7 million sq km, the smallest of all continents.
r: Australia is also called the island continent.

q: Why is Sindh historically called 'Bab-ul-Islam'?
o: It was the capital of the Mughal Empire
Islam entered the subcontinent through it with Muhammad bin Qasim
It has the most mosques in Pakistan
The Pakistan Resolution was passed there
f: Muhammad bin Qasim conquered Sindh in 712 AD, so Islam entered South Asia through Sindh (the 'Gateway of Islam').
r: Sindh is also home to Mohenjo-daro of the Indus Valley Civilization.

q: Which book of Hadith is regarded as the most authentic after the Quran?
f: Imam Bukhari's collection is considered the most authentic book after the Quran; Sahih Muslim is second.
r: Together the two are called 'Sahihain'.

q: When is the International Day of Education observed? (2)
f: The UN General Assembly declared 24 January the International Day of Education.
r: 8 September is International Literacy Day; 5 October is World Teachers' Day.

q: Pakistan bought Gwadar from which country in 1958?
f: Gwadar was handed over by the Sultanate of Oman on 8 September 1958.
r: Gwadar is now the key port of CPEC.

q: Which city is known as the 'City of Mosques'?
f: Dhaka, Bangladesh, is famous for its many mosques.
r: Cairo is called the 'City of a Thousand Minarets'.

q: How many categories of Zakat recipients (Masarif-e-Zakat) are named in the Quran?
f: Surah At-Tawbah, verse 60, names eight categories, such as the poor (Fuqara) and the needy (Masakeen).
r: Zakat is usually 2.5% of savings held for one lunar year.

q: Which South American country is the longest from north to south?
f: Chile stretches over 4,300 km along the western coast of South America.
r: Chile's capital is Santiago.

q: Who was President of the 76th UN General Assembly?
f: Abdulla Shahid of the Maldives presided over the 76th session (2021-22).
r: Volkan Bozkir of Turkey presided over the 75th session.

q: Which city is known as the 'Heart of Pakistan'?
f: Lahore is called the heart of Pakistan for its culture and history.
r: Lahore is also called the 'City of Gardens'.

q: Which city is called the 'Manchester of Pakistan'? (2)
f: Faisalabad is called this because of its huge textile industry.
r: Faisalabad was earlier called Lyallpur.

q: What is the currency of Albania?
f: Albania's currency is the Lek.
r: The Lev is Bulgaria's currency.

q: What does the word 'Hikmah' mean?
f: Hikmah means wisdom or deep understanding.
r: Patience in Arabic is 'Sabr'.

q: How was Hazrat Abu Talib related to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abu Talib was the brother of the Prophet's father, Abdullah, and protected him in Makkah.
r: Hazrat Ali (R.A) was Abu Talib's son.

q: Who looked after the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the death of Hazrat Amina?
f: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib cared for him until he died when the Prophet was eight; then Abu Talib took over.
r: Hazrat Halima Sadia was his foster (nursing) mother.

q: When was the Nehru Report presented?
f: Motilal Nehru's report of August 1928 rejected separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.

q: For how long was Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (R.A) Caliph?
f: He ruled from 632 AD until his death in 634 AD.
r: Hazrat Umar (R.A) ruled for about 10 years after him.

q: Who wrote Pakistan's National Anthem?
f: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the lyrics; they were approved in 1954.
r: Ahmed G. Chagla composed the anthem's music.

q: When was the 26th Constitutional Amendment of Pakistan passed?
f: The 26th Amendment, passed in October 2024, changed how the Chief Justice is appointed and created constitutional benches.
r: The 25th Amendment (May 2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

q: What is the area of Gilgit-Baltistan?
f: Gilgit-Baltistan covers about 72,971 sq km in Pakistan's far north.
r: AJK covers about 13,297 sq km.

q: Which Pakistani city is known as 'Madinat-ul-Auliya' (City of Saints)?
f: Multan is famous for many Sufi shrines, such as that of Shah Rukn-e-Alam.
r: Multan is also called the 'City of Saints' in English.

q: In which war did Major Raja Aziz Bhatti Shaheed earn the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: He defended the Burki sector near Lahore in September 1965.
r: Captain Karnal Sher Khan earned it in Kargil in 1999.

q: Who introduced the 1962 Constitution of Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan's 1962 Constitution set up a presidential system.
r: It was abolished when Yahya Khan imposed martial law in 1969.

q: Which was the first major battle in Islamic history?
f: Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH (624 AD) and the Muslims won decisively.
r: Uhud followed in 3 AH and Khandaq in 5 AH.

q: Where is the battlefield of Badr located?
f: Badr lies southwest of Madinah, near the Red Sea coast.
r: Badr was a well-known stop on the trade route to Syria.

q: In which battle was Abu Jahl killed? (3)
f: Two young Ansari brothers, Mu'adh and Mu'awwidh, struck him down at Badr.
r: Abu Jahl's real name was Amr ibn Hisham.

q: Which pass connects Pakistan (Gilgit-Baltistan) with China (Xinjiang)?
f: The Karakoram Highway crosses into China at the Khunjerab Pass (4,693 m).
r: The Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan.

q: What is the provincial capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: Peshawar is the capital of KP.
r: Peshawar is one of the oldest living cities of South Asia.

q: Which is the largest and most populous city of Pakistan?
f: Karachi is Pakistan's biggest city, financial centre and main seaport.
r: Lahore is the second largest city.

q: What is the approximate total length of the Pakistan-India border (including the LoC)?
f: The border including the Line of Control is about 3,323 km.
r: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border (Durand Line) is about 2,640 km.

q: Which country shares the Durand Line border with Pakistan?
f: The Durand Line was drawn in 1893 between Sir Mortimer Durand and Amir Abdur Rahman Khan.
r: Pakistan's border with Iran is about 909 km long.

q: In which year was Pakistan first named an Islamic Republic in its constitution?
f: The 1956 Constitution named the state the 'Islamic Republic of Pakistan'.
r: The 1962 Constitution first used 'Republic of Pakistan'; 'Islamic' was added back in 1963.

q: What form of government did the 1962 Constitution provide?
f: The 1962 Constitution gave executive power to the President.
r: The 1956 and 1973 Constitutions were parliamentary.

q: How many sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) have who were Prophets?
o: Two: Hazrat Ishaq and Hazrat Yaqub
Two: Hazrat Ismail and Hazrat Ishaq
f: Hazrat Ismail (A.S) was born to Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq (A.S) to Hazrat Sarah.
r: Hazrat Yaqub (A.S) was the son of Hazrat Ishaq (A.S).

q: Who was President of Pakistan when the 1973 Constitution came into force?
f: Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became President on 14 August 1973, when Bhutto became Prime Minister.
r: The 1973 Constitution came into force on 14 August 1973.

q: What was the total number of members of the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan?
f: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) gave the Constituent Assembly 389 members.
r: Of these, 292 were from British provinces, 93 from princely states and 4 from Chief Commissioner areas.

q: The Arabian Sea is part of which ocean?
f: The Arabian Sea is the north-western part of the Indian Ocean.
r: Pakistan's coastline on the Arabian Sea is about 1,050 km.

q: Which Prophet has the title 'Safiullah'?
f: Safiullah means 'the chosen one of Allah'; it is the title of Hazrat Adam (A.S).
r: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) is called Khalilullah (friend of Allah).

q: Which Prophet has the title 'Kaleemullah'?
f: Kaleemullah means 'one who spoke with Allah'; Hazrat Musa (A.S) spoke with Allah at Mount Toor.
r: Hazrat Isa (A.S) is called Roohullah.

q: What is the provincial capital of Punjab?
f: Lahore has been the capital of Punjab for centuries.
r: Rawalpindi is home to the GHQ of the Pakistan Army.

q: On which date did Pakistan become a member of the United Nations?
f: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947.
r: The UN itself came into being on 24 October 1945.

q: Which region is known as the 'Roof of the World'?
f: The high Pamir region of Central Asia is called the 'Roof of the World'.
r: The Tibetan Plateau is also sometimes given this name.

q: Which is the highest plateau in Pakistan?
f: Deosai in Gilgit-Baltistan, about 4,100 m high, is one of the highest plateaus in the world.
r: Deosai is called the 'Land of Giants'.

q: Which is the third largest ocean in the world?
f: After the Pacific and the Atlantic, the Indian Ocean is the third largest.
r: The Arctic is the smallest ocean.

q: Which two Surahs are together called 'Al-Mu'awwidhatayn'?
f: Both begin with 'Qul a'udhu' (I seek refuge) and are recited for protection.
r: Surah Al-Baqarah and Aal-e-Imran are called 'Az-Zahrawain' (the two bright ones).

q: How many Grand Slam tennis tournaments are held each year?
f: The Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.
r: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam played on grass.

q: Mohenjo-daro is a site of which ancient civilization?
f: Mohenjo-daro in Larkana, Sindh, dates to about 2500 BC.
r: Harappa, in Sahiwal district, Punjab, is another major Indus Valley site.

q: What is the approximate distance from Islamabad/Rawalpindi to Peshawar on the M-1 Motorway?
f: The M-1 Motorway between Islamabad and Peshawar is about 155-160 km long.
r: The M-2 Motorway between Islamabad and Lahore is about 375 km long.

q: What is the antonym (opposite) of 'Opaque'?
f: Opaque things block light; transparent things let light pass through.
r: Frosted glass is translucent: it lets some light through.

q: How many Muslims fought in the Battle of Badr?
f: 313 poorly equipped Muslims defeated about 1,000 Quraish.
r: About 1,000 Quraish fought at Badr.

q: Fill in the blank: 'He died ___ malaria.'
f: We die 'of' a disease.
r: 'From' is used more for an injury or outside cause, e.g. 'died from his wounds'.

q: What is the other name of the Lahore Resolution (1940)?
f: It was passed on 23 March 1940 at Minto Park (now Iqbal Park) and is called the Pakistan Resolution.
r: The Objectives Resolution was passed in 1949.

q: How many founding member countries did the UN have in 1945? (2)
f: 50 countries signed the Charter in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 and Poland signed later, making 51.
r: The UN now has 193 member states.

q: Who is honoured as the founder of Pakistan?
f: Quaid-e-Azam led the political struggle that created Pakistan in 1947.
r: Allama Iqbal is called the 'Poet of the East' and gave the idea of a separate homeland in 1930.

q: Which constitutional document was the first passed in Pakistan's history?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan moved it and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
r: It was made a working part of the Constitution as Article 2-A in 1985.

q: Which organization did Pakistan, Iran and Turkey set up in 1985?
f: ECO replaced the RCD, which the same three countries formed in 1964.
r: ECO now has 10 members.

q: For how many years did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) live in Makkah?
f: He lived in Makkah from his birth until the Hijrah at the age of 53.
r: He lived about 10 years in Madinah after the Hijrah.

q: What was the old name of Madinah before Islam?
f: After the Hijrah, Yathrib became 'Madinat-un-Nabi' (City of the Prophet).
r: Bakkah is an old name of Makkah.

q: Who was elected President of Pakistan's First Constituent Assembly?
f: Quaid-e-Azam was elected unanimously on 11 August 1947 and gave his famous speech.
r: Jogendra Nath Mandal chaired the opening session on 10-11 August 1947.

q: What is a synonym of 'Mediate'?
f: To mediate is to step in between two sides to help them agree.
r: A person who mediates is called a mediator.

q: Where is the headquarters (General Secretariat) of the OIC?
f: The OIC Secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.
r: The OIC has 57 member states.

q: Where is the Quaid-e-Azam Residency in Balochistan located?
f: Quaid-e-Azam spent his last days at the Ziarat Residency in 1948.
r: Ziarat is famous for its ancient juniper forests.

q: What is the capital of Ukraine? (2)
f: Kyiv stands on the Dnieper River.
r: Kharkiv is Ukraine's second largest city.

q: Which country helped Pakistan build the Warsak Dam?
f: Canada funded and built it under the Colombo Plan; it was completed in 1960.
r: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River near Peshawar.

q: Which is the largest city of Punjab by population?
f: Lahore has over 13 million people.
r: Faisalabad is the second largest city of Punjab.

q: Which is the largest city of Sindh by population?
f: Karachi is Pakistan's largest city.
r: Hyderabad is Sindh's second largest city.

q: Who led the Quraish army in the Battle of Badr?
f: Abu Jahl led the Quraish at Badr and was killed there.
r: Abu Sufyan was leading the trade caravan at that time, not the army.

q: Who led the Quraish army in the Battle of Uhud?
f: Abu Sufyan led the Makkan army at Uhud in 3 AH; he accepted Islam later.
r: Khalid bin Waleed led the Quraish cavalry at Uhud.

q: In which country is the active volcano Mount Etna?
f: Mount Etna is on the island of Sicily, Italy.
r: Mount Vesuvius, which buried Pompeii, is also in Italy.

q: Which is the deepest lake in the world? (2)
f: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is about 1,642 m deep.
r: Lake Tanganyika in Africa is the second deepest.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
f: Lake Superior (about 82,100 sq km) lies between Canada and the USA. The Caspian Sea is bigger but salty.
r: Lake Baikal holds the most fresh water by volume.

q: Which two oceans are joined by the Panama Canal?
f: The 82 km canal crosses the Isthmus of Panama.
r: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.

q: In which year was the OIC founded?
f: The OIC was founded in 1969 after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
r: Pakistan hosted the 2nd OIC Summit in Lahore in 1974.

q: What is an angle of less than 90 degrees called? (2)
f: An angle between 0 and 90 degrees is acute.
r: An obtuse angle is between 90 and 180 degrees.

q: Who is the youngest winner of the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: Malala won it in 2014 at the age of 17.
r: She shared the 2014 prize with India's Kailash Satyarthi.

q: When was the Kargil conflict fought?
f: Fighting took place on the heights of Kargil in Kashmir from May to July 1999.
r: Captain Karnal Sher Khan and Havildar Lalak Jan earned the Nishan-e-Haider in Kargil.

q: Which is the longest river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus flows about 3,180 km from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.
r: Tarbela Dam is built on the Indus.

q: Which is the largest barrage in Pakistan? (2)
f: Sukkur (Lloyd) Barrage on the Indus, opened in 1932, feeds one of the largest irrigation systems in the world.
r: Kotri Barrage is near Hyderabad.

q: On which river did India build the Baglihar Dam?
f: Baglihar Dam is on the Chenab in Indian-held Jammu and Kashmir; Pakistan objected under the Indus Waters Treaty.
r: India's Kishanganga project is on the Neelum (Kishanganga) River.

q: What form of government did the 1973 Constitution adopt?
f: The Prime Minister holds executive power and Parliament has two houses.
r: The 1962 Constitution was presidential.

q: What is the literal meaning of 'Zakat'?
f: Zakat purifies wealth and makes it grow with blessings.
r: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam.

q: What is 'Rukoo' in Namaz?
f: In Rukoo one bows with hands on the knees.
r: Prostration is called Sajdah.

q: Where is the largest and oldest salt mine of Pakistan?
f: The Khewra Salt Mine in the Salt Range is the second largest in the world.
r: It is said to have been found by Alexander's army around 320 BC.

q: What is the approximate length of the Durand Line?
f: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border is about 2,640 km long.
r: It was drawn in 1893.

q: What is the capital of Chile?
f: Santiago is Chile's capital and largest city.
r: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.

q: Who was Chief Minister of Punjab from 2018 to 2022?
f: Usman Buzdar of PTI was CM from August 2018 to April 2022.
r: Maryam Nawaz became Punjab's first woman CM in 2024.

q: How many faces does a triangular prism have? (2)
f: It has 2 triangular faces and 3 rectangular faces.
r: A triangular prism has 9 edges and 6 vertices.

q: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (R.A) was the father of which Mother of the Believers?
f: Hazrat Aisha (R.A) was his daughter.
r: Hazrat Hafsa (R.A) was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (R.A).

q: The Wakhan Corridor, which separates Pakistan from Tajikistan, belongs to which country?
f: It is a narrow strip of north-eastern Afghanistan created in the 1890s.
r: Wakhan also touches China at its eastern end.

q: Who was Speaker of the National Assembly from 2018 to 2022?
f: PTI's Asad Qaiser was elected Speaker in August 2018.
r: Fehmida Mirza was the first woman Speaker.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution, whose advice must the President follow?
f: Article 48 says the President acts on the advice of the Cabinet or Prime Minister.
r: Article 41 deals with the office of the President.

q: In which province are the Chagai Hills located?
f: Pakistan's nuclear tests were held in the Chagai Hills on 28 May 1998.
r: 28 May is celebrated as Youm-e-Takbeer.

q: Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament (for example, during impeachment of the President)?
f: A joint sitting of both houses is chaired by the Speaker of the National Assembly.
r: Impeachment of the President is covered by Article 47.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the All-India Muslim League? (3)
f: He joined in 1913, persuaded by Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar and Syed Wazir Hasan.
r: The Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906.

q: Narowal district is in which division of Punjab?
f: Narowal is part of Gujranwala Division in north-eastern Punjab.
r: Kartarpur Corridor (Gurdwara Darbar Sahib) is in Narowal district.

q: In which year did Sir Syed Ahmad Khan set up the Scientific Society? (2)
f: He set it up at Ghazipur to translate modern Western books into Urdu.
r: He founded the MAO School at Aligarh in 1875.

q: Which is the largest and deepest ocean?
f: The Pacific covers about 30% of Earth's surface and contains the Mariana Trench.
r: The Mariana Trench is about 11 km deep.

q: Which is the smallest and shallowest ocean?
f: The Arctic Ocean surrounds the North Pole and is mostly covered by ice.
r: The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica.

q: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
f: The Sahara covers over 9 million sq km of North Africa.
r: Antarctica is the largest desert overall (a cold desert).

q: What is the dress worn by pilgrims during Hajj and Umrah called?
f: For men, Ihram is two plain white unstitched sheets, showing equality before Allah.
r: Pilgrims enter Ihram at fixed points called Miqat.

q: Who was Zaheer-ud-din Muhammad Babur?
o: The first Mughal emperor of India
The founder of the Ghaznavid dynasty
The founder of the Lodhi dynasty
f: Babur founded the Mughal dynasty in 1526 after the First Battle of Panipat.
r: Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor.

q: When does Pakistan celebrate Youm-e-Takbeer?
f: It marks the nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998.
r: 6 September is Defence Day.

q: When is Kashmir Solidarity Day observed in Pakistan?
f: Pakistan observes 5 February each year to show support for Kashmiris.
r: 27 October is observed as 'Black Day' by Kashmiris.

q: Which is the farthest planet from the Sun?
f: Neptune is the eighth planet. Pluto has been called a dwarf planet since 2006.
r: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

q: Which is the longest and strongest bone in the human body?
f: The femur (thigh bone) runs from the hip to the knee.
r: The stapes in the ear is the smallest bone.

q: When was the State Bank of Pakistan inaugurated?
f: Quaid-e-Azam inaugurated it on 1 July 1948.
r: Zahid Hussain was its first Governor.

q: What is the approximate length of the Pakistan-Iran border? (2)
f: The border (about 909-959 km) separates Balochistan from Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan.
r: The Pakistan-China border is about 596 km.

q: What was the name of the countrywide counter-terrorism operation launched in 2017?
f: Radd-ul-Fasaad began on 22 February 2017 to clear hidden terrorist cells.
r: Zarb-e-Azb was launched in North Waziristan in June 2014.

q: Which country paid for and built the Warsak Dam on the Kabul River?
f: Canada built it under the Colombo Plan; it was completed in 1960.
r: Warsak Dam is about 30 km from Peshawar.

q: Where is the Naval Headquarters of Pakistan located?
f: Naval HQ is in Islamabad, though the main naval bases are in Karachi.
r: Air HQ is also in Islamabad; Army GHQ is in Rawalpindi.

q: Nelson Mandela was the anti-apartheid leader of which country?
f: He spent 27 years in prison and became South Africa's first Black president in 1994.
r: He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993.

q: Hazrat Ismail (A.S) was the elder son of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Ismail (A.S) was born to Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) and Hazrat Hajra.
r: Hazrat Ibrahim and Hazrat Ismail (A.S) rebuilt the Kaaba together.

q: When was the Indus Waters Treaty signed?
f: Ayub Khan and Nehru signed it in Karachi with World Bank mediation.
r: It gave the eastern rivers to India and the western rivers to Pakistan.

q: What is the approximate total length of the CPEC route?
f: CPEC links Gwadar Port with Kashgar in Xinjiang, China, over roughly 3,000 km.
r: CPEC was launched in 2015.

q: Which is the longest river in Asia?
f: The Yangtze in China is about 6,300 km long, the third longest river in the world.
r: The Nile is the longest river in the world.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win a Nobel Prize? (2)
f: Dr. Abdus Salam won the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physics.
r: Malala was the second Pakistani, in 2014.

q: What is the capital of Mongolia?
f: Ulaanbaatar is the capital of Mongolia.
r: It is called the coldest national capital in the world.

q: In which years were the Colombo Plan and the Baghdad Pact started?
f: The Colombo Plan began in 1950; the Baghdad Pact (later CENTO) was signed in 1955.
r: Pakistan joined SEATO in 1954.

q: In which year were the Delhi Muslim Proposals presented?
f: In March 1927 Muslim leaders offered to accept joint electorates on certain conditions.
r: Quaid-e-Azam's Fourteen Points came in 1929.

q: What is 80% of 90?
What system of government does the 1973 Constitution set up?
f: Executive power is with the Prime Minister, who answers to Parliament.
r: Pakistan has a two-house Parliament: the National Assembly and the Senate.

q: Which is the world's largest hydroelectric dam by power output?
f: Three Gorges on the Yangtze has about 22,500 MW capacity.
r: Tarbela is the world's largest earth-filled dam.

q: Which Surah of the Quran does not begin with Bismillah?
f: Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'at) begins without Bismillah.
r: Surah An-Naml contains Bismillah twice.

q: Which is the shortest Surah of the Quran?
f: Surah Al-Kawthar has only 3 verses.
r: Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest Surah.

q: When was Pakistan admitted to the United Nations?
f: The General Assembly admitted Pakistan on 30 September 1947.
r: Afghanistan was the only country that voted against.

q: What is the capital of Balochistan?
f: Quetta is the provincial capital, about 1,680 m above sea level.
r: Quetta is called the 'Fruit Garden of Pakistan'.

q: What is the claimed range of Pakistan's Ababeel missile?
f: Ababeel is a surface-to-surface missile with a range of 2,200 km that can carry multiple (MIRV) warheads.
r: Shaheen-III has a range of about 2,750 km.

q: What is the area of Punjab province?
f: Punjab is the second largest province by area and the largest by population.
r: Balochistan is the largest province by area (347,190 sq km).

q: Which neighbouring country is linked with Pakistan by the ancient Silk Route?
f: The Karakoram Highway follows the old Silk Route to China through the Khunjerab Pass.
r: The Karakoram Highway is called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.

q: Which country has the largest population in the world?
f: India overtook China in 2023; both have over 1.4 billion people.
r: Pakistan is the fifth most populous country.

q: In which city was Benazir Bhutto assassinated?
f: She was killed after a rally at Liaquat Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 27 December 2007.
r: She was the first woman Prime Minister of a Muslim country.

q: What does the word 'Ayat' mean?
o: A sign, and a verse of the Quran
f: Ayat means sign or proof; each verse of the Quran is called an Ayah.
r: A chapter of the Quran is called a Surah.

q: What does 'Ahl al-Bayt' mean in Islam?
o: People of the House (family of the Holy Prophet PBUH)
f: It refers to the household and family of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: 'Ahl al-Kitab' means People of the Book (Jews and Christians).

q: Which Islamic month is called 'Shahrullah' (the Month of Allah)?
f: A hadith in Sahih Muslim calls Muharram 'the month of Allah' and praises fasting in it.
r: Muharram, Rajab, Dhul-Qa'dah and Dhul-Hijjah are the four sacred months.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid-ul-Adha celebrated?
f: Eid-ul-Adha is on 10 Dhul-Hijjah and remembers Hazrat Ibrahim's (A.S) sacrifice.
r: Eid-ul-Fitr is on 1 Shawwal.

q: In which country did the modern game of squash begin?
f: Squash began at Harrow School, England, around 1830.
r: Pakistan's Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan are squash legends.

q: In which years did Pakistan co-host the Cricket World Cup?
f: Pakistan co-hosted with India in 1987 and with India and Sri Lanka in 1996.
r: Pakistan won the 1992 World Cup in Australia.

q: Which language was made a national language along with Urdu in the 1956 and 1962 Constitutions?
f: Bengali got this status after the Bengali Language Movement.
r: The 1973 Constitution names Urdu as the national language.

q: What is Pakistan's official state news agency?
f: APP provides news to media outlets at home and abroad.
r: ISPR is the media wing of the armed forces.

q: Who was the last Prophet sent to the Bani Israel? (2)
f: Hazrat Isa (A.S) was the last Prophet sent to the Bani Israel.
r: The Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the last Prophet for all mankind.

q: Which social media company did Mark Zuckerberg found in 2004?
f: Zuckerberg started Facebook at Harvard in February 2004.
r: Facebook's parent company was renamed Meta in 2021.

q: What is cot(x) x tan(x) equal to?
f: cot(x) = 1/tan(x), so the product is 1.
r: Similarly, sin(x) x cosec(x) = 1.

q: How many quadrants does the Cartesian (x-y) plane have?
f: The x-axis and y-axis divide the plane into four quadrants.
r: In the first quadrant both x and y are positive.

q: Who wrote the play 'The Man of Destiny' about Napoleon?
f: Shaw wrote this one-act play in 1897.
r: Shaw won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1925.

q: Who was the first adult free man to accept Islam?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) accepted Islam at once. Hazrat Ali (R.A) was the first child and Hazrat Zaid (R.A) the first freed slave.
r: Hazrat Khadija (R.A) was the first person overall to accept Islam.

q: How many daughters did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have?
f: Hazrat Zainab, Ruqayyah, Umm Kulthum and Fatimah (R.A).
r: Hazrat Fatimah (R.A) was the youngest daughter.

q: Who suggested the name 'PAKISTAN' in 1933?
f: He gave it in his pamphlet 'Now or Never' in 1933.
r: Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.

q: Where did Pakistan's first Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan die?
f: He was shot at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, on 16 October 1951.
r: Company Bagh was renamed Liaquat Bagh after him.

q: What is the official length of a marathon race?
f: The marathon length of 42.195 km (26.2 miles) was set at the 1908 London Olympics.
r: The race remembers the Greek runner who ran from Marathon to Athens.

q: Jahangir Khan is a world champion of which sport?
f: He was unbeaten in 555 squash matches in a row (1981-1986).
r: Jansher Khan is another Pakistani squash legend.

q: Which is the oldest university in Pakistan?
f: The University of the Punjab, Lahore, was founded in 1882.
r: The University of Karachi was founded in 1951.

q: Who holds the record for the highest individual score in a Test match?
f: Brian Lara scored 400 not out against England in Antigua in 2004.
r: Hanif Mohammad's 337 is a famous Pakistani Test innings.

q: Where is the International Islamic University (IIUI) located?
f: IIUI, founded in 1980, has its main campus in H-10, Islamabad.
r: Faisal Mosque, Islamabad, once housed the university.

q: In which province of Pakistan are the Chagai Hills situated?
f: Pakistan carried out its nuclear tests in the Chagai Hills in May 1998.
r: Ras Koh in Chagai district was the test site on 28 May 1998.

q: In which year did Muhammad bin Qasim conquer Sindh? (2)
f: He defeated Raja Dahir and conquered Sindh in 712 AD for the Umayyads.
r: Mahmud of Ghazni began his raids on India in 1001 AD.

q: In how many fields is the Nobel Prize given?
f: Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics.
r: The Economics prize was added in 1968 and first given in 1969.

q: In which year did Malala Yousafzai win the Nobel Peace Prize?
f: She shared it with Kailash Satyarthi in 2014.
r: She was shot by the Taliban in Swat in 2012.

q: Which country lies to the east of Pakistan?
f: India is on Pakistan's eastern border.
r: Iran lies to the west, Afghanistan to the north-west and China to the north-east.

q: Which country lies to the south of Afghanistan?
f: Pakistan borders Afghanistan on the south and east.
r: Iran lies to the west of Afghanistan.

q: Where is the Kharan Desert?
f: Kharan Desert is in Balochistan; Pakistan's second test (Chagai-II, 30 May 1998) was held there.
r: The Thar Desert is in Sindh.

q: Hazrat Hafsa (R.A) was the daughter of which Companion?
f: Hazrat Hafsa (R.A), wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), was the daughter of Hazrat Umar (R.A).
r: The written Quran collected under Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) was kept with her.

q: Which Companion has the title 'Zun-Noorain' (Possessor of Two Lights)?
f: He married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH): Ruqayyah and Umm Kulthum (R.A).
r: Hazrat Umar (R.A) is called Al-Farooq.

q: In which year was the Khilafat Movement launched?
f: Maulana Muhammad Ali and Maulana Shaukat Ali launched it in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate.
r: It ended when Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.

q: Which is the main and largest river of Pakistan?
f: The Indus is the lifeline of Pakistan's farming and economy.
r: The Indus flows into the Arabian Sea near Thatta.

q: What is the capital city of Libya?
f: Tripoli is the capital and largest city of Libya, on the Mediterranean coast. Benghazi is Libya's second city, not the capital.
r: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia and Algiers is the capital of Algeria.

q: Which currency is the most traded in world financial markets?
f: The US Dollar is used in most foreign exchange deals and is the main reserve currency of central banks.
r: The Euro is the second most traded currency in the world.

q: Which is the largest natural freshwater lake in Pakistan?
f: Manchar Lake in Jamshoro/Dadu districts of Sindh, west of the Indus, is Pakistan's largest natural freshwater lake.
r: Keenjhar (Kalri) Lake in Thatta supplies drinking water to Karachi.

q: What is the official name of the sport commonly called Ping Pong?
f: Ping Pong is the popular name of Table Tennis, which is governed by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF).
r: Table tennis became an Olympic sport at the 1988 Seoul Olympics.

q: In which city is the Shah Jahan Mosque situated?
f: The Shah Jahan Mosque in Thatta, Sindh, was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century and is famous for its 93 domes.
r: The Makli Necropolis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is also near Thatta.

q: What is the capital city of Austria?
f: Vienna, on the Danube River, is the capital of Austria. Budapest is Hungary's capital and Prague is the Czech capital.
r: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and OPEC have their headquarters in Vienna.

q: Where is Jabal-e-Noor (Mountain of Light) located?
f: Jabal-e-Noor is in Makkah. It has the Cave of Hira, where the first revelation came to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
r: The first revealed verses were the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.

q: The term 'agricultural shot' is used in which sport?
f: In cricket, an 'agricultural shot' is a wild cross-bat swing with no proper technique, like swinging a scythe.
r: A 'cow corner' is the cricket fielding area where such shots usually go (deep mid-wicket).

q: In which year did Lord Curzon carry out the Partition of Bengal?
f: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, creating the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam. 1911 is when it was cancelled.
r: The partition was annulled in 1911 by King George V at the Delhi Darbar.

q: What was the religion of King Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia when the early Muslims migrated there?
f: Najashi was a Christian king who gave shelter to the Muslim emigrants; he later accepted Islam.
r: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) offered funeral prayer in absentia (Ghaibana) for Najashi.

q: What does the word 'Conceal' mean?
f: 'Conceal' means to hide something or keep it secret. 'Reveal' is its opposite.
r: The noun form is 'concealment'.

q: In which province of Pakistan is Chagai district located?
f: Chagai district is in Balochistan and borders both Iran and Afghanistan.
r: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests in the Ras Koh Hills of Chagai on 28 May 1998.

q: Who founded the English newspaper 'Dawn' in 1941?
f: Quaid-e-Azam founded Dawn in Delhi in October 1941 to put forward the Muslim League's point of view.
r: Maulana Muhammad Ali Jauhar ran the English weekly 'Comrade'.

q: What is the approximate total length of the Indus River?
f: The Indus is about 3,180 km long, rising near Lake Mansarovar in Tibet and falling into the Arabian Sea near Thatta.
r: 6,650 km is the length of the Nile, the world's longest river.

q: In which year did the Chauri Chaura incident take place? (2)
f: On 4 February 1922, protesters burned a police station at Chauri Chaura (UP), and Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
r: The Khilafat Movement lost much of its strength after Gandhi stopped the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q: Which drink is the national drink of Pakistan?
f: Sugarcane juice (ganne ka ras) was declared Pakistan's national drink in 2019 after a public poll.
r: Pakistan's national fruit is the mango.

q: In which year was Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) formed?
f: PIA was formed in 1955 when the government merged Orient Airways into the new national airline.
r: Orient Airways was founded in 1946 in Calcutta with the support of Quaid-e-Azam.

q: According to Islamic teaching, how many prophet sons did Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) have?
f: Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S) had two sons who were prophets: Hazrat Ismail (A.S) and Hazrat Ishaq (A.S).
r: Hazrat Ismail's mother was Hazrat Hajra and Hazrat Ishaq's mother was Hazrat Sarah.

q: In which year were non-party based general elections held in Pakistan?
f: General Zia-ul-Haq held the general elections of February 1985 on a non-party basis.
r: Muhammad Khan Junejo became Prime Minister after the 1985 elections.

q: Who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan? (2)
f: Under the 1973 Constitution, the Prime Minister is elected by a majority of the members of the National Assembly.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of both houses of Parliament and the four provincial assemblies.

q: How many times has Pakistan won the Men's Hockey World Cup?
f: Pakistan won the Hockey World Cup in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
r: Pakistan has won 3 Olympic gold medals in hockey (1960, 1968, 1984).

q: From which country did Pakistan buy Gwadar? (2)
f: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultanate of Oman in September 1958 during PM Feroz Khan Noon's government.
r: Gwadar port is a key part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).

q: In which year did Pakistan win the ICC Men's T20 World Cup?
f: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka in the 2009 final at Lord's under Younis Khan. In 2007 Pakistan lost the final to India.
r: Pakistan won the ICC Champions Trophy in 2017.

q: Why does the daytime sky look blue?
o: Reflection of light from the oceans
Scattering of sunlight by air molecules
Absorption of red light by the Sun
f: Air molecules scatter short blue wavelengths of sunlight much more than red ones (Rayleigh scattering), so blue light reaches us from all over the sky.
r: The same scattering makes sunsets look red, because blue light is scattered away over the long path.

q: How many months of the year have 31 days? (2)
f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December have 31 days, which makes 7 months.
r: February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

q: Boris Johnson was the Prime Minister of which country?
f: Boris Johnson was UK Prime Minister and Conservative Party leader from 2019 to 2022.
r: He was followed by Liz Truss, who served only about 7 weeks.

q: Hazrat Hajra (A.S) was the mother of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Hajra was the mother of Hazrat Ismail (A.S). Hazrat Ishaq's mother was Hazrat Sarah.
r: Her running between Safa and Marwah is remembered as Sa'i during Hajj and Umrah.

q: How many members does the UN Security Council have?
f: The Security Council has 15 members: 5 permanent members with veto power and 10 non-permanent members elected for 2 years.
r: Pakistan is a non-permanent member of the Security Council for 2025-2026.

q: Tripoli is the capital of which North African country?
f: Tripoli, on the Mediterranean coast, is the capital of Libya.
r: Rabat is the capital of Morocco and Cairo is the capital of Egypt.

q: The Khyber Pass connects Peshawar with which city?
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar in Pakistan with Jalalabad and Kabul in Afghanistan.
r: Torkham is the main border crossing at the Khyber Pass.

q: During the Hijrat Movement of 1920, Indian Muslims tried to migrate to which country?
f: Ulema declared India Dar-ul-Harb, and thousands of Muslims migrated to Afghanistan, which later closed its border to them.
r: The Hijrat Movement was part of the Khilafat Movement period.

q: Which is the largest lake on Earth?
f: The Caspian Sea is the largest enclosed inland body of water on Earth (about 371,000 sq km), even though it is called a sea.
r: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area, and Lake Baikal is the deepest lake.

q: Who gave Pakistan the motto 'Unity, Faith, Discipline'?
f: Quaid-e-Azam gave the nation the motto 'Unity, Faith and Discipline' (Ittehad, Yaqeen, Tanzeem).
r: The motto appears on the state emblem of Pakistan in Urdu.

q: In which month and year was the Nehru Report published?
f: The Nehru Report, prepared by a committee under Motilal Nehru, was published in August 1928.
r: Quaid-e-Azam answered it with his Fourteen Points in March 1929.

q: What was the old British name of Attock city?
f: Attock was called Campbellpur after Sir Colin Campbell; it was renamed Attock in 1978.
r: Lyallpur is now Faisalabad and Montgomery is now Sahiwal.

q: How many Madani Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
f: 28 Surahs were revealed after the Hijrah (Madani) and 86 before it (Makki), making 114 in total.
r: Surah Al-Baqarah, the longest Surah, is Madani.

q: How many Makki Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
f: 86 Surahs were revealed in Makkah before the Hijrah; the other 28 are Madani.
r: Makki Surahs mostly deal with Tauheed, the Hereafter and Prophethood.

q: Against whom did the Muslims fight the Battle of Badr?
f: Ghazwa-e-Badr (2 AH) was fought against the idol-worshipping Quraish of Makkah led by Abu Jahl.
r: 313 Muslims defeated about 1,000 Quraish fighters at Badr.

q: South Africa is famous worldwide as a leading producer of which mineral?
f: South Africa's Witwatersrand Basin has produced more gold than anywhere else in history.
r: South Africa is also the world's largest producer of platinum.

q: Which is the largest bay in the world?
f: The Bay of Bengal, about 2.17 million sq km in the northeastern Indian Ocean, is usually named the largest bay.
r: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, the world's largest delta, opens into the Bay of Bengal.

q: Which is the largest marginal sea in the world?
f: The Philippine Sea in the western Pacific covers about 5.7 million sq km, more than any other sea.
r: The Arabian Sea, on Pakistan's coast, is part of the Indian Ocean.

q: Which mountain range forms the border between Spain and France?
f: The Pyrenees run about 430 km from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean, between Spain and France.
r: The tiny country of Andorra lies in the Pyrenees.

q: Where is the western end (starting point) of the Himalayas?
f: The Himalayas stretch from Nanga Parbat in the west to Namcha Barwa in the east. K2 is in the Karakoram, not the Himalayas.
r: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is called the 'Killer Mountain'.

q: The boxing champion Muhammad Ali belonged to which country?
f: Muhammad Ali, born Cassius Clay in Louisville, Kentucky, USA, was a three-time world heavyweight champion.
r: He won an Olympic gold medal at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

q: Which city hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics?
f: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, hosted the 2016 Olympics, the first in South America. London hosted 2012 and Tokyo 2020.
r: Paris hosted 2024 and Los Angeles will host 2028.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwa-e-Khandaq) fought?
f: Ghazwa-e-Khandaq (also called Ahzab) was fought in 5 AH (627 AD). Badr was in 2 AH and Uhud in 3 AH.
r: The idea of digging the trench was given by Hazrat Salman Farsi (R.A).

q: Who took over power in Pakistan after General Yahya Khan resigned in 1971?
f: Z.A. Bhutto became President and the first civilian Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971.
r: Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became President in 1973 when Bhutto became Prime Minister.

q: What is the approximate length of Pakistan's coastline?
f: Pakistan's coastline on the Arabian Sea is about 1,046 km long; most of it is the Makran coast of Balochistan.
r: Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar are Pakistan's main seaports.

q: What is the currency of Turkey? (2)
f: Turkey's currency is the Turkish Lira, divided into 100 kurus.
r: The capital of Turkey is Ankara.

q: What is the capital city of Australia?
f: Canberra is Australia's planned federal capital. Sydney is the largest city but not the capital.
r: Canberra was chosen as a compromise between rival cities Sydney and Melbourne.

q: Which country is the world's largest producer and exporter of coffee?
f: Brazil has been the world's largest coffee producer and exporter for over 150 years. Vietnam is second.
r: Coffee is believed to have first been found in Ethiopia.

q: Which country is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'? (2)
f: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'; in fact it has over 180,000 lakes.
r: Norway is called the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'.

q: In which year and city was SAARC founded?
f: SAARC was founded on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Kathmandu is where its secretariat is.
r: SAARC's secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal.

q: What is the main source of electricity generation in Pakistan?
f: Most of Pakistan's electricity comes from thermal power plants using gas, oil and coal, followed by hydel power.
r: Tarbela is Pakistan's largest hydel power station.

q: Where is Jabal-e-Rehmat (Mount of Mercy) located?
f: Jabal-e-Rehmat stands in the plain of Arafat near Makkah, where the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave the Farewell Sermon.
r: Wuquf (standing) at Arafat on 9 Zil-Hajj is the main pillar of Hajj.

q: What is the currency of Japan?
f: Japan's currency is the Yen. The Won is Korean, the Yuan is Chinese and the Ringgit is Malaysian.
r: The Yen is one of the world's main reserve currencies.

q: Who was the first Foreign Minister of Pakistan?
f: Sir Zafarullah Khan was appointed the first Foreign Minister by Quaid-e-Azam; he later became President of the UN General Assembly and of the ICJ.
r: Malik Ghulam Muhammad was Pakistan's first Finance Minister.

q: In which city is Nishtar Hospital located?
f: Nishtar Hospital, one of Pakistan's biggest teaching hospitals, is in Multan, attached to Nishtar Medical University.
r: It is named after Sardar Abdur Rab Nishtar, a leader of the Pakistan Movement.

q: What is the currency of Poland?
f: Poland's currency is the Zloty, meaning 'golden'. The Forint is Hungarian and the Koruna is Czech.
r: Poland is in the EU but has not adopted the Euro.

q: Who compiled 'Sahih al-Bukhari'? (2)
f: Imam Bukhari, born in Bukhara (now Uzbekistan) in 194 AH, compiled Sahih al-Bukhari.
r: Sahih Bukhari and Sahih Muslim together are called 'Sahihain'.

q: During whose government was Mangla Dam built?
f: Mangla Dam on the Jhelum River in Mirpur (AJK) was completed in 1967 under Ayub Khan, as part of the Indus Basin works.
r: Tarbela Dam was completed in 1976 under Bhutto's government.

q: What does OPEC stand for?
o: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
Organization of Petroleum and Energy Cooperation
f: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, founded in Baghdad in 1960.
r: OPEC's headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.

q: About what percentage of Pakistan's population is Muslim?
f: Census figures show about 96 to 97% of Pakistanis are Muslims.
r: Christians and Hindus are the largest religious minorities of Pakistan.

q: What is the currency of Kuwait?
f: Kuwait's currency is the Kuwaiti Dinar, the highest-valued currency unit in the world.
r: Bahrain's Dinar and Oman's Rial are the next highest-valued currencies.

q: Who was the second Governor-General of Pakistan?
f: Khawaja Nazimuddin became Governor-General in September 1948 after the death of Quaid-e-Azam.
r: In 1951 Khawaja Nazimuddin became the second Prime Minister and Ghulam Muhammad became Governor-General.

q: About how many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of the Trench (Khandaq)?
