f: Only about 6 Muslims were martyred at Khandaq because the trench stopped direct fighting. 70 were martyred at Uhud.
r: Hazrat Saad bin Muaz (R.A) was wounded at Khandaq and later died of his wound.

q: How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Uhud?
f: About 70 Companions were martyred at Uhud, including the Prophet's uncle Hazrat Hamza (R.A). 14 were martyred at Badr.
r: Hazrat Hamza (R.A) is called Sayyid-ush-Shuhada (leader of the martyrs).

q: How many wives did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) have in his lifetime?
f: Most scholars count 11 wives, called Ummahat-ul-Momineen (Mothers of the Believers). He left behind 9 wives at his death.
r: Hazrat Khadija (R.A) was his first wife and Hazrat Maimuna (R.A) the last he married.

q: What was the religion of the Quraish before Islam?
f: The Quraish worshipped idols; the Kaaba had 360 idols before the Conquest of Makkah.
r: Hubal was the chief idol in the Kaaba.

q: What is the deepest known point in the oceans?
f: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, western Pacific, is about 10,900 m deep.
r: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean.

q: Which is the highest paved mountain pass in Pakistan?
f: Khunjerab Pass, 4,693 m high, joins Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang (China) on the Karakoram Highway.
r: Shandur Pass is famous for the world's highest polo ground.

q: Which is the tallest building in Pakistan?
f: Bahria Icon Tower in Clifton, Karachi, about 273 m tall, is Pakistan's tallest building.
r: Before it, the MCB Tower in Karachi was the tallest building in Pakistan.

q: Which highway links Pakistan with China?
f: The Karakoram Highway (N-35), built jointly by Pakistan and China, crosses into China at Khunjerab Pass.
r: It is often called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'.

q: In which year was the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) founded?
f: The OIC was founded in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969 after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque. 1974 was the Lahore summit.
r: Pakistan hosted the second OIC summit in Lahore in 1974.

q: Where is the headquarters of the World Bank? (2)
f: The World Bank's headquarters is in Washington, D.C., USA. It was set up at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference with the IMF.
r: The IMF's headquarters is also in Washington, D.C.

q: On which date were the 2018 general elections held in Pakistan?
f: The general elections were held on 25 July 2018, and PTI won the most seats. 18 August 2018 is when Imran Khan took oath as PM.
r: The next general elections were held on 8 February 2024.

q: In which year was the Battle of Yamama fought?
f: The Battle of Yamama was fought in 632 AD (11-12 AH) under Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) against the false prophet Musaylimah. 636 AD is Yarmouk.
r: Musaylimah was killed in this battle by Hazrat Wahshi (R.A).

q: The Battle of Yarmouk was fought against which empire?
f: Yarmouk (636 AD) was fought against the Byzantines under Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A). The Persians were defeated at Qadisiyyah.
r: The Battle of Qadisiyyah (636 AD) was against the Persian Empire.

q: Which old name of Makkah is used in Surah Aal-e-Imran?
f: Verse 96 of Surah Aal-e-Imran says the first House for mankind is at 'Bakkah'. Yathrib and Taiba are names of Madinah.
r: Ummul Qura (Mother of Towns) is another Quranic name for Makkah, used in Surah Al-An'am.

q: In which year did East Pakistan separate and become Bangladesh?
f: East Pakistan separated on 16 December 1971 at the end of the 1971 war with India.
r: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman became the first leader of Bangladesh.

q: In which year was the first ICC Champions Trophy held?
f: The first Champions Trophy was held in 1998 in Dhaka, Bangladesh, under the name 'ICC KnockOut'. South Africa won it.
r: Pakistan won the Champions Trophy in 2017, beating India in the final.

q: Who was President of Iran from 2021 until his death in 2024?
f: Ebrahim Raisi became President in 2021 and died in a helicopter crash in May 2024. Rouhani was before him and Pezeshkian after him.
r: Masoud Pezeshkian was elected President of Iran in July 2024.

q: What is the capital city of Japan?
f: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the world's most populated metropolitan area. Kyoto was the old capital.
r: Kyoto was Japan's imperial capital for over 1,000 years.

q: Which is the largest enclosed body of water on Earth?
f: The Caspian Sea, about 371,000 sq km, is the largest enclosed (inland) body of water.
r: The Dead Sea is the lowest point on land and one of the saltiest water bodies.

q: How many general seats are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: The National Assembly has 266 general seats; with 60 seats for women and 10 for minorities, the total is 336.
r: Before the FATA merger (25th Amendment) there were 272 general seats and 342 in total.

q: Which is the first Surah of the Holy Quran?
f: Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Quran; it has 7 verses and is recited in every rakat of prayer. Al-Alaq was the first revealed.
r: Surah Al-Fatihah is also called 'Ummul Kitab' (Mother of the Book).

q: What is the nisab of Zakat on gold, and the rate?
f: Zakat is due at 2.5% on gold of 7.5 tolas (about 87.48 g) or more, held for one lunar year. 52.5 tolas is the nisab for silver.
r: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam.

q: What is the nisab of Zakat on silver, and the rate?
f: Zakat on silver is 2.5% (1/40th) when it reaches 52.5 tolas (about 612.36 g). 7.5 tolas is the nisab for gold.
r: Ushr is the Zakat on farm produce, at 10% or 5% depending on irrigation.

q: Where is Simly Dam located?
f: Simly Dam is on the Soan River near Islamabad and is the main source of drinking water for the city.
r: Rawal Dam, on the Korang River, supplies water to Rawalpindi.

q: Fatima Jinnah contested which presidential election against Ayub Khan?
f: Fatima Jinnah was the candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties in the January 1965 presidential election and lost to Ayub Khan.
r: She is called 'Madar-e-Millat' (Mother of the Nation).

q: What was the age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) at the time of his death?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) passed away at the age of 63 (lunar years) in Madinah, in Rabi-ul-Awwal 11 AH (632 AD).
r: He received the first revelation at the age of 40.

q: Which is the fifth month of the Islamic calendar?
f: The order is Muharram, Safar, Rabi-ul-Awwal, Rabi-ul-Sani, then Jamadi-ul-Awwal as the fifth month.
r: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.

q: What is the currency of Russia?
f: Russia's currency is the Ruble, divided into 100 kopecks. The Hryvnia is Ukrainian and the Tenge is Kazakh.
r: Belarus also uses a currency called the ruble (Belarusian ruble).

q: What is the capital city of Turkey?
f: Ankara became the capital of the Republic of Turkey in 1923. Istanbul is the largest city but not the capital.
r: The Republic of Turkey was founded by Mustafa Kemal Ataturk in 1923.

q: Where is the Kareem Block market located?
f: Kareem Block market is a busy shopping area in Allama Iqbal Town, Lahore.
r: Allama Iqbal Town is in south-west Lahore.

q: How many days did the 1965 Pakistan-India war last? (3)
f: The war began on 6 September 1965 and the ceasefire came on 23 September, so it lasted 17 days. The 1971 war lasted about 13 days.
r: 6 September is celebrated as Defence Day in Pakistan.

q: What is a synonym of 'Diversity'?
f: 'Diversity' means variety or difference among things. 'Similarity' is close to its opposite.
r: The adjective form is 'diverse'.

q: When was the Pakistan Military Academy (PMA) Kakul established?
f: PMA Kakul, Abbottabad, was established in October 1947; Brigadier Francis Ingall was its first commandant.
r: Cadets who pass out of PMA are commissioned as Second Lieutenants.

q: Which two entities are Permanent Observer Non-Member States at the United Nations?
o: Palestine and the Holy See (Vatican City)
f: The State of Palestine and the Holy See are non-member observer states; they can take part in UN meetings but cannot vote on resolutions.
r: Switzerland was an observer state for many years before joining the UN as a full member in 2002.

q: What is the total length of the Pakistan-India border, including the Line of Control?
f: The Pakistan-India border is about 3,323 km long including the LoC in Kashmir. About 2,430 km is the length of the Pak-Afghan border (Durand Line).
r: The Wagah border near Lahore is the main crossing point between Pakistan and India.

q: What is a synonym of 'Zeal'?
f: 'Zeal' means great enthusiasm or passion for a cause. 'Laziness' is nearly its opposite.
r: A person full of zeal is called a 'zealot' (often used for an extreme supporter).

q: How many Caliphs are counted among the Khulafa-e-Rashideen (Rightly Guided Caliphs)?
f: The four Rightly Guided Caliphs are Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali (R.A).
r: The period of the Khulafa-e-Rashideen lasted about 30 years (632-661 AD).

q: What is the capital city of Estonia?
f: Tallinn, on the Gulf of Finland, is the capital of Estonia. Riga is Latvia's capital and Vilnius is Lithuania's.
r: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania are called the Baltic States.

q: Which Pakistani city is known as the 'City of Lights'?
f: Karachi is called the 'City of Lights' for its busy round-the-clock life and business.
r: Lahore is called the 'City of Gardens' and Faisalabad the 'Manchester of Pakistan'.

q: Who was the first Indian Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army?
f: General K. M. Cariappa took command on 15 January 1949, which India celebrates as Army Day. Lockhart and Bucher were British.
r: Cariappa and Sam Manekshaw were the only two Indian Army officers given the rank of Field Marshal.

q: Who was the first Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army? (2)
f: British General Sir Frank Messervy commanded the Pakistan Army from August 1947 to February 1948. Gracey came after him.
r: General Ayub Khan was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief (from January 1951).

q: Who was the first Pakistani Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Army?
f: General Ayub Khan took command on 17 January 1951, taking over from General Sir Douglas Gracey.
r: General Muhammad Musa succeeded Ayub Khan as Commander-in-Chief in 1958.

q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan from 1988 to 1991?
f: General Mirza Aslam Beg became COAS after General Zia-ul-Haq died in the Bahawalpur air crash in August 1988.
r: General Zia-ul-Haq was killed in the C-130 crash on 17 August 1988.

q: Who was the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan from 1991 to 1993?
f: General Asif Nawaz Janjua served as COAS from August 1991 until his sudden death in January 1993.
r: General Abdul Waheed Kakar became COAS after him in 1993.

q: How many member states does the United Nations have?
f: The UN has 193 member states; South Sudan became the 193rd member in July 2011.
r: The UN was founded on 24 October 1945 with 51 members.

q: What is the currency of Saudi Arabia?
f: Saudi Arabia's currency is the Riyal, fixed at about 3.75 Riyals to one US Dollar.
r: The UAE uses the Dirham and Kuwait uses the Dinar.

q: In which country is the Suez Canal located?
f: The Suez Canal cuts through the Isthmus of Suez in Egypt.
r: Egypt's President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the canal in 1956.

q: How many total seats are there in the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
f: The Punjab Assembly has 371 seats: 297 general, 66 for women and 8 for non-Muslims. 336 is the National Assembly.
r: The Sindh Assembly has 168 seats.

q: Which titles were given to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) in Makkah for his honesty?
f: The people of Makkah called him Al-Sadiq (the Truthful) and Al-Amin (the Trustworthy), and even his enemies kept their valuables with him.
r: Al-Farooq was the title of Hazrat Umar (R.A) and Al-Siddiq of Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A).

q: Which is the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun?
f: Mercury is the smallest planet and the nearest to the Sun; it goes round the Sun in 88 days and has no moons. Pluto is no longer a planet.
r: Venus is the hottest planet even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

q: What was the line dividing Pakistan and India in 1947 called?
f: The Radcliffe Line was drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, chairman of the Boundary Commissions. The Durand Line is the Pak-Afghan border.
r: The McMahon Line is the border line between India and China (Tibet).

q: Which companion is known by the title 'Asadullah' (Lion of Allah)?
f: Hazrat Ali (R.A) is called Asadullah and Haider-e-Karrar for his bravery, especially at Khaybar. Saifullah is Khalid bin Waleed's title.
r: Hazrat Ali (R.A) was the fourth Rightly Guided Caliph.

q: Who wrote the Punjabi epic 'Heer Ranjha' (1766)?
f: Sufi poet Waris Shah wrote 'Heer' in Punjabi in 1766. Mian Muhammad Bakhsh wrote 'Saiful Malook'.
r: Waris Shah's tomb is in Jandiala Sher Khan, Sheikhupura.

q: Vienna is the capital of which country?
f: Vienna is the capital of Austria. Berlin is Germany's capital, Bern is Switzerland's and Budapest is Hungary's.
r: Vienna is famous for musicians like Mozart and Beethoven.

q: Who wrote the book 'India of My Dreams'?
f: 'India of My Dreams' is a collection of Gandhi's writings about his vision of free India. Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India'.
r: Gandhi's autobiography is 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'.

q: Where did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place in 1919?
f: On 13 April 1919, British troops under General Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.
r: The protest was against the Rowlatt Act of 1919.

q: When did India carry out its first nuclear test, 'Smiling Buddha'?
f: India's first nuclear test was on 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. 11 May 1998 was its second set of tests.
r: Pakistan answered India's 1998 tests with its own tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998.

q: Which is the smallest country in the world? (2)
f: Vatican City, about 0.49 sq km and inside Rome, is the smallest country. Monaco is second.
r: Vatican City is the centre of the Roman Catholic Church and home of the Pope.

q: Which river carries the largest volume of water in the world?
f: The Amazon in South America carries more water than any other river. The Nile is the longest but carries much less water.
r: The Congo is the second-largest river by water flow.

q: In which sport is 147 the maximum break?
f: In snooker, a 147 maximum break means potting all 15 reds with 15 blacks and then all six colours.
r: Pakistan's Muhammad Yousuf won the IBSF World Amateur Snooker Championship in 1994.

q: In which province of Pakistan is most of the Thar Desert?
f: Most of Pakistan's Thar Desert is in south-eastern Sindh (Tharparkar), on the border with Rajasthan, India.
r: The Thar coalfield in Tharparkar holds one of the world's largest coal reserves.

q: What is the capital city of Belarus?
f: Minsk is the capital of Belarus. Kyiv is Ukraine's capital and Vilnius is Lithuania's.
r: Belarus's currency is the Belarusian ruble.

q: Where was the highest air temperature on Earth recorded?
f: Death Valley, California, recorded 56.7 C (134 F) in 1913, the official world record. The old Al Aziziyah record was cancelled in 2012.
r: Pakistan's highest recorded temperature is 53.7 C at Turbat (2017).

q: What is the currency of Armenia? (2)
f: Armenia's currency is the Dram, introduced in 1993. The Manat is Azerbaijan's and the Lari is Georgia's.
r: The capital of Armenia is Yerevan.

q: Who was Chairman of NAB from 2017 to 2022?
f: Former Supreme Court judge Justice (R) Javed Iqbal headed NAB from October 2017 to 2022. Qamar Zaman Chaudhry was before him.
r: NAB (National Accountability Bureau) was set up in 1999.

q: What is the capital city of Bhutan?
f: Thimphu is the capital of Bhutan. Kathmandu is Nepal's capital; Paro is a Bhutanese town with its only international airport.
r: Bhutan measures progress through 'Gross National Happiness'.

q: Which is the national sport of Pakistan?
f: Field hockey is Pakistan's national game; Pakistan has won 3 Olympic golds and 4 World Cups in it. Cricket is more popular but is not the national game.
r: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan made Pakistan famous in squash.

q: Who wrote the words of Pakistan's National Anthem?
f: Hafeez Jalandhari wrote the National Anthem in Persianised Urdu in 1952. Ahmed Ghulamali Chagla composed its music.
r: The anthem was officially approved in August 1954.

q: How many members are there in the National Assembly of Pakistan? (2)
f: The National Assembly has 336 members: 266 general seats, 60 for women and 10 for minorities. 342 was the total before the FATA merger.
r: The Senate of Pakistan has 96 members.

q: What are the two houses of Pakistan's Parliament (Majlis-e-Shoora)?
f: Under the 1973 Constitution, the Parliament has two houses: the Senate (upper house) and the National Assembly (lower house).
r: The Chairman of the Senate acts as President when the President is absent.

q: What is the capital city of Kuwait?
f: Kuwait City, on the Persian Gulf, is the capital of Kuwait. Doha is Qatar's capital, Manama is Bahrain's and Muscat is Oman's.
r: Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990, which led to the Gulf War of 1991.

q: Who designed the national flag of Pakistan?
f: Amir-ud-Din Kidwai designed the flag based on the Muslim League flag, with a crescent and five-pointed star.
r: The white part of the flag stands for minorities and the green for the Muslim majority.

q: In which year was SAARC founded?
f: SAARC was founded in December 1985 in Dhaka with 7 members; Afghanistan joined in 2007 as the 8th.
r: Pakistan hosted the 12th SAARC summit in Islamabad in 2004.

q: Which line marks much of the border between the USA and Canada?
f: The 49th Parallel North forms most of the western USA-Canada border. The 38th Parallel divides North and South Korea.
r: The USA-Canada border is the world's longest international land border.

q: Which five countries have veto power in the UN Security Council?
o: USA, UK, Russia, China and Germany
USA, UK, France, Japan and China
USA, Russia, China, India and France
USA, UK, Russia, China and France
f: The five permanent members (P5) with veto power are the USA, UK, Russia, China and France.
r: Germany, Japan, India and Brazil (the G4) are seeking permanent seats.

q: What does the Arabic word 'Badr' mean?
f: 'Badr' means full moon. The battle is named after the well and village of Badr, south-west of Madinah.
r: The Battle of Badr took place on 17 Ramadan, 2 AH.

q: Which city is known as the hottest place in Pakistan?
f: Jacobabad in Sindh often crosses 50 C in summer and is famous as Pakistan's hottest city.
r: The highest temperature in Pakistan, 53.7 C, was recorded at Turbat in 2017.

q: About how many languages are spoken in Pakistan?
f: More than 70 languages are spoken in Pakistan. Urdu is the national language; Punjabi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki and Balochi are major ones.
r: Punjabi is the mother tongue of the largest number of Pakistanis.

q: Which dam is built on the Kabul River near Peshawar?
f: Warsak Dam on the Kabul River near Peshawar was completed in 1960 with Canadian help. Tarbela is on the Indus and Mangla on the Jhelum.
r: Khanpur Dam is on the Haro River.

q: In which countries is the Hindu Kush mountain range located?
f: The Hindu Kush runs mainly through Afghanistan and northern Pakistan, south-west from the Pamir Knot.
r: Tirich Mir (7,708 m) in Chitral is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

q: What is the currency of Bangladesh?
f: Bangladesh's currency is the Taka. The Ngultrum is Bhutan's and the Kyat is Myanmar's.
r: The Taka is divided into 100 poisha.

q: What is the capital city of Azerbaijan?
f: Baku, on the west shore of the Caspian Sea, is the capital of Azerbaijan. Tbilisi is Georgia's and Yerevan is Armenia's.
r: Azerbaijan's currency is the Manat.

q: Which Maldivian served as President of the 76th UN General Assembly?
f: Maldives Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid was President of the 76th UNGA from September 2021 to September 2022.
r: Pakistan's Sir Zafarullah Khan was President of the 17th UN General Assembly (1962).

q: Which is the largest natural lake in Afghanistan?
f: The notes give Band-e-Amir, a chain of six deep blue lakes in the Hindu Kush (Bamyan).
r: Band-e-Amir became Afghanistan's first national park in 2009.

q: Which country helped build the Warsak Dam?
f: Canada gave money and engineering help for Warsak Dam under the Colombo Plan.
r: The World Bank helped arrange the Indus Waters Treaty of 1960.

q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was PM from 14 August 1947 until he was assassinated in Rawalpindi on 16 October 1951.
r: He is called 'Quaid-e-Millat'.

q: Who was the last Governor-General and the first President of Pakistan?
f: Iskander Mirza was Governor-General (1955-56) and became the first President under the 1956 Constitution (1956-58).
r: Iskander Mirza imposed martial law on 7 October 1958.

q: About how many times is Salah (prayer) mentioned in the Holy Quran?
f: The notes say Salah is mentioned (or commanded) about 700 times in the Quran.
r: Salah is the second pillar of Islam, and was made obligatory on the night of Miraj.

q: What is the approximate road distance between Peshawar and Rawalpindi?
f: Peshawar and Rawalpindi are about 170-190 km apart by the GT Road or the M-1 Motorway.
r: The M-1 Motorway links Islamabad and Peshawar.

q: Which mountain pass connects Pakistan with China?
f: Khunjerab Pass (4,693 m) in the Karakoram joins Pakistan and China. Khyber Pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan.
r: The Bolan Pass links Quetta with Sibi in Balochistan.

q: What is the total area of Punjab province?
f: Punjab covers about 205,344 sq km, roughly 26% of Pakistan's area. 347,190 sq km is Balochistan, the largest province.
r: Sindh covers about 140,914 sq km and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa about 101,741 sq km.

q: What is the capital city of Bulgaria?
f: Sofia, at the foot of Vitosha Mountain, is Bulgaria's capital. Bucharest is Romania's and Belgrade is Serbia's.
r: Bulgaria adopted the Euro on 1 January 2026, replacing the Lev.

q: In which city was leg-spinner Abdul Qadir born?
f: Abdul Qadir was born in Lahore in 1955; he brought leg-spin back into modern cricket in the 1970s-80s.
r: His best Test bowling was 9 wickets for 56 runs against England in 1987.

q: What is a synonym of 'Cease'?
f: 'Cease' means to stop or come to an end. 'Begin' and 'Continue' are its opposites.
r: A 'ceasefire' is an agreement to stop fighting.

q: Which is the largest continent by both area and population?
f: Asia covers about 44.6 million sq km and has about 60% of the world's people. Africa is second in both.
r: Australia is the smallest continent.

q: Which Prophet was swallowed by a big fish?
f: Hazrat Yunus (A.S) was swallowed by a fish and prayed 'La ilaha illa Anta Subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimeen'.
r: Hazrat Yunus (A.S) is called 'Zun-Noon' (the one of the fish) in the Quran.

q: What is the currency of France?
f: France uses the Euro; it replaced the French Franc (cash Euro came in 2002).
r: The European Central Bank, which manages the Euro, is in Frankfurt, Germany.

q: Which capital city does the River Thames flow through?
f: The Thames flows about 346 km through southern England and passes through London into the North Sea. The Seine flows through Paris.
r: Tower Bridge over the Thames is a famous London landmark.

q: Who is Robert King?
o: An American TV writer and producer
f: Robert King is an American screenwriter and producer who co-created the TV legal drama 'The Good Wife' with his wife Michelle King.
r: The Kings also created the follow-up series 'The Good Fight'.

q: About how many Muslims marched in the expedition of Tabuk?
f: About 30,000 Muslims joined the Tabuk expedition in 9 AH, the largest army led by the Holy Prophet (PBUH). 10,000 marched for the Conquest of Makkah.
r: The Tabuk expedition was against the Byzantines, and no battle was fought.

q: How many countries are members of the United Nations today?
f: There are 193 UN member states; South Sudan was the latest to join, in 2011.
r: Palestine and the Holy See are non-member observer states.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?
f: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773 and served till 1785. Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India.
r: Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India (1858).

q: In 1950, Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan made a famous official visit to which country?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan visited the USA in May 1950 on President Truman's invitation, instead of the Soviet Union.
r: His speeches on that tour were published as the book 'Pakistan: The Heart of Asia'.

q: What is a synonym of 'Bragging'?
f: 'Bragging' means boasting, or talking too proudly about oneself.
r: A person who brags is called a 'braggart'.

q: What is a synonym of 'Splendid'?
f: 'Splendid' means magnificent, grand or very impressive. 'Ordinary' and 'Dull' are its opposites.
r: The noun form is 'splendour'.

q: Which archangel is in charge of rain and sustenance?
f: Hazrat Mikail (A.S) is in charge of rain, clouds and provisions. Jibrail brought revelation, Israfil will blow the trumpet and Izrail takes souls.
r: Hazrat Jibrail (A.S) is called 'Ruh-ul-Amin' in the Quran.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam present his Fourteen Points?
f: Jinnah presented the Fourteen Points in March 1929 in Delhi in reply to the Nehru Report (1928).
r: Allama Iqbal gave his Allahabad Address in 1930.

q: What is the capital city of Russia?
f: Moscow is the capital of Russia and one of Europe's largest cities. Saint Petersburg was the capital before 1918.
r: The Kremlin in Moscow is the official home of the Russian President.

q: With which Indian Prime Minister did Ayub Khan sign the Indus Waters Treaty in 1960?
f: Ayub Khan and Nehru signed the Indus Waters Treaty in Karachi on 19 September 1960, with the World Bank's help. Ayub signed the Tashkent Declaration with Shastri.
r: Under the treaty, Pakistan got the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) and India the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).

q: When and where was Sir Syed Ahmad Khan born?
f: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in Delhi on 17 October 1817. Aligarh is where he founded his college.
r: He wrote 'Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind' (Causes of the Indian Revolt) about the 1857 war.

q: What was the title of Allama Iqbal's doctoral thesis, published as his first book in English?
o: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam
The Development of Metaphysics in Persia
f: Iqbal's PhD thesis 'The Development of Metaphysics in Persia' (1908) was submitted to Munich University. 'Reconstruction' is his later lectures (1930).
r: Iqbal's first Urdu poetry collection was 'Bang-e-Dra' (1924).

q: Which two seas are joined by the Suez Canal?
f: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, giving the shortest sea route between Europe and Asia.
r: The Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

q: For how long did Liaquat Ali Khan serve as Prime Minister?
f: Liaquat Ali Khan was PM from August 1947 until his assassination on 16 October 1951, about 4 years.
r: He was shot at Company Bagh, Rawalpindi, now called Liaquat Bagh.

q: How many pillars of Islam are there? (2)
f: The five pillars are Shahada, Salah, Zakat, Sawm (fasting) and Hajj.
r: The articles of faith (Iman-e-Mufassal) are seven.

q: Which Prophet was ordered by Allah to build the Ark?
f: Hazrat Nooh (A.S) built the Ark on Allah's command to save the believers from the Great Flood.
r: The Ark came to rest on Mount Judi, as stated in Surah Hud.

q: Hajj is which pillar of Islam?
f: Hajj is the fifth pillar, compulsory once in life for every Muslim who can afford it and is physically able.
r: Zakat is the third pillar and fasting is the fourth.

q: Who was Prime Minister of Iraq from 2020 to 2022?
f: Mustafa Al-Kadhimi, former intelligence chief, was Iraq's PM from May 2020 to October 2022. Al-Sudani came after him.
r: Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani became PM of Iraq in October 2022.

q: Who published the world's first printed weekly newspaper in 1605?
f: Johann Carolus published the 'Relation' in Strasbourg in 1605, seen as the first printed newspaper. Gutenberg invented the printing press about 150 years earlier.
r: William Caxton brought the printing press to England in 1476.

q: Who elects the President of Pakistan?
o: An electoral college of the Senate, National Assembly and four Provincial Assemblies
f: Under Article 41 of the Constitution, the President is elected by an electoral college of both houses of Parliament and all four provincial assemblies.
r: The President's term is 5 years.

q: Who developed the first effective polio vaccine in 1953?
f: Dr. Jonas Salk of the USA developed the injected (inactivated) polio vaccine in 1953. Sabin later made the oral vaccine.
r: Edward Jenner made the first vaccine, against smallpox, in 1796.

q: Which is the largest and widest river flowing through Bangladesh?
f: The Brahmaputra, called the Jamuna in Bangladesh, is the widest river there; it rises in Tibet as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
r: The Padma (Ganges) and Jamuna join and then meet the Meghna before reaching the Bay of Bengal.

q: In which country did General Wojciech Jaruzelski impose martial law in 1981?
f: Jaruzelski imposed martial law in Poland on 13 December 1981 to crush the Solidarity movement.
r: Solidarity was led by Lech Walesa, who later became President of Poland.

q: During whose government was Tarbela Dam completed?
f: Tarbela Dam on the Indus was completed in 1976 under Bhutto's government. Mangla Dam was completed under Ayub Khan.
r: Tarbela is the world's largest earth-filled dam.

q: Where and when were the first Commonwealth Games held?
f: The first Commonwealth Games, then called the British Empire Games, were held in Hamilton, Canada, in 1930.
r: The Commonwealth Games are held every four years.

q: On which date did Gandhi launch the Quit India Movement?
f: The Congress launched the Quit India Movement at its Bombay session on 8 August 1942, with the slogan 'Do or Die'.
r: The Muslim League replied with the slogan 'Divide and Quit'.

q: When was the Pakistan-China Boundary Agreement signed?
f: The boundary agreement was signed in Beijing on 2 March 1963 by Z.A. Bhutto and Chinese Foreign Minister Chen Yi.
r: Pakistan and China established diplomatic relations on 21 May 1951.

q: What is a synonym of 'Stationary'?
f: 'Stationary' means not moving. Do not confuse it with 'stationery', which means writing materials.
r: 'Stationery' (with 'e') means paper, pens and other office supplies.

q: For about how long did Hazrat Nooh's (A.S) Ark float during the Great Flood?
f: The notes say the Ark floated about 150 days (5 to 6 months) before resting on Mount Judi.
r: Mount Judi is mentioned in Surah Hud, verse 44.

q: What is the term of the President of the UN General Assembly?
f: The President of the UN General Assembly is elected for one year (one session). The UN Secretary-General serves 5-year terms.
r: The presidency rotates among the five regional groups of the UN.

q: Who built 'Masjid-e-Zirar'?
o: The hypocrites (Munafiqeen), urged by Abu Amir
f: Hypocrites built Masjid-e-Zirar at the urging of Abu Amir the monk, to divide Muslims; it was demolished on the Prophet's order after Tabuk.
r: Masjid-e-Zirar is mentioned in Surah At-Tawbah, verse 107.

q: When was Pakistan's first Constitution enforced?
f: Pakistan's first Constitution came into force on 23 March 1956 and made Pakistan an Islamic Republic. 12 March 1949 is the Objectives Resolution.
r: It was abrogated on 7 October 1958 by Iskander Mirza.

q: Who was the first human to travel into space in 1961?
f: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961. Armstrong was the first man on the Moon (1969).
r: Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space (1963).

q: In the order of the Holy Quran (Mushaf), which is the third Surah?
f: In the Mushaf order, Aal-e-Imran comes after Al-Fatihah and Al-Baqarah, so it is the third Surah. An-Nisa is fourth.
r: Surah Aal-e-Imran has 200 verses.

q: Who was the 13th President of Pakistan (2018-2024)?
f: Dr. Arif Alvi of PTI was President from 9 September 2018 to March 2024. Mamnoon Hussain was before him and Zardari after him.
r: Asif Ali Zardari became President for a second time in March 2024.

q: Around which period was the ancient city of Taxila founded?
f: Taxila grew as a city around the 6th century BCE (some date it earlier) and flourished under the Achaemenid, Mauryan and Kushan empires.
r: Taxila is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and was a famous centre of Buddhist learning.

q: Which companion was given the title 'Saifullah' (Sword of Allah)?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) called Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A) Saifullah after his leadership at the Battle of Mu'tah (8 AH).
r: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A) led the Muslims to victory at Yarmouk in 636 AD.

q: About how many Huffaz (memorisers of the Quran) were martyred in the Battle of Yamama?
f: The notes say about 70 Huffaz were martyred at Yamama. Their loss led Hazrat Umar (R.A) to urge Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) to compile the Quran.
r: Hazrat Zaid bin Sabit (R.A) was given the task of collecting the Quran in one book.

q: On which river is Diamer-Bhasha Dam being built?
f: Diamer-Bhasha Dam is being built on the Indus River in Gilgit-Baltistan, for water storage and about 4,500 MW of electricity.
r: Mohmand Dam is being built on the Swat River.

q: Which Prophet has the title 'Zabiullah'?
f: Hazrat Ismail (A.S) is called Zabiullah because he willingly agreed to be sacrificed for Allah. Hazrat Ibrahim is Khalilullah.
r: Eid-ul-Adha is celebrated in memory of this sacrifice.

q: Who started the Non-Cooperation Movement in British India in 1920?
f: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920; the Ali brothers and Khilafat leaders supported it.
r: Gandhi called off the movement in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident.

q: In statistics, what is another name for the average?
f: The mean is found by adding all values and dividing by the number of values.
r: The median is the middle value when data is arranged in order.

q: Which city hosted the 2018 Asian Games?
f: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, the first Asian Games co-hosted by two cities.
r: Incheon hosted the 2014 Asian Games and Hangzhou hosted the 2022 Games (held in 2023).

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
f: The IMF is headquartered in Washington, D.C., close to the World Bank.
r: The IMF and World Bank were created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944.

q: Who discovered the photovoltaic effect (the principle of solar cells) in 1839?
f: French physicist Alexandre-Edmond Becquerel saw that light falling on an electrode produced electricity.
r: Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize for explaining the photoelectric effect.

q: What is the capital of Venezuela?
f: Caracas is the capital and largest city of Venezuela.
r: Bogota is the capital of Colombia, Venezuela's western neighbour.

q: Which is the busiest container seaport in the world?
f: Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port every year since 2010.
r: Singapore is usually ranked second in the world for container traffic.

q: In which year was the Simla Conference held under Lord Wavell?
f: The Simla Conference met in June-July 1945 and failed over the question of Muslim representation.
r: The Cripps Mission came to India in 1942.

q: Where was the world's highest air temperature recorded?
f: 56.7 degrees C was recorded at Furnace Creek, Death Valley, on 10 July 1913.
r: Jacobabad and Mohenjo-daro are among the hottest places in Pakistan.

q: Who founded the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) in 1967?
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP in Lahore on 30 November 1967.
r: The PPP's slogan was 'Roti, Kapra aur Makaan' (bread, clothing and shelter).

q: In which years was nationwide martial law formally declared in Pakistan?
f: Martial law was imposed by Ayub Khan (via Iskander Mirza) in 1958, by Yahya Khan in 1969 and by Zia-ul-Haq in 1977.
r: In 1999 General Musharraf took power as 'Chief Executive' through an emergency and PCO, without formally declaring martial law.

q: How many centimetres are there in one metre?
f: 1 metre = 100 centimetres = 1,000 millimetres.
r: 1 metre is about 39.37 inches.

q: What is the total length of the border between the USA and Canada?
f: The US-Canada border is about 8,891 km (5,525 miles) long, the longest international border in the world.
r: The US-Mexico border is about 3,145 km long.

q: When did India take the Kashmir issue to the UN Security Council?
f: India lodged its complaint on 1 January 1948 under Article 35 of the UN Charter.
r: The UNCIP resolutions of 13 August 1948 and 5 January 1949 called for a plebiscite in Kashmir.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam leave the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah left Congress in 1920 at the Nagpur session because he disagreed with Gandhi's non-cooperation methods.
r: Jinnah joined the All-India Muslim League in 1913.

q: From which plateau does the Yangtze River rise?
f: The Yangtze rises in the Tanggula Mountains on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
r: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia, about 6,300 km.

q: Which Prophet was given the title 'Israel'?
f: Hazrat Yaqoob (Jacob) was called Israel; his descendants are called Bani Israel.
r: His twelve sons became the twelve tribes of Bani Israel.

q: Abdul Qadir was a famous Pakistani player of which game?
f: Abdul Qadir was a famous leg-spin bowler for Pakistan.
r: Hockey is Pakistan's national game.

q: Which country hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023?
f: India hosted the 2023 World Cup; Australia beat India in the final at Ahmedabad.
r: It was Australia's sixth ODI World Cup title.

q: When did the first English East India Company ship land in the subcontinent?
f: William Hawkins arrived at Surat on the ship 'Hector' on 24 August 1608.
r: The East India Company received its royal charter on 31 December 1600.

q: Where is the headquarters of OPEC? (2)
f: OPEC moved its headquarters from Geneva to Vienna in 1965.
r: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in 1960.

q: The Manila Pact of 1954 created which organisation?
f: The Manila Pact set up SEATO, a defence alliance against communism in Southeast Asia.
r: CENTO came from the Baghdad Pact of 1955.

q: In which river is the endangered blind dolphin (Bhulan) found?
f: The Indus blind dolphin lives mainly in the lower Indus River in Pakistan.
r: The Indus river dolphin is Pakistan's national mammal.

q: What does the Quranic word 'Tanzeel' mean?
f: Tanzeel means sending down; it refers to the gradual revelation of the Quran from Allah.
r: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years.

q: How many soldiers have been awarded the Nishan-e-Haider?
f: Ten Pakistan Armed Forces martyrs plus Naik Saif Ali Janjua (whose Hilal-e-Kashmir is treated as equal) make 11.
r: Captain Muhammad Sarwar Shaheed was the first to receive the Nishan-e-Haider.

q: What were the old names of Attock and Faisalabad?
f: Attock was called Campbellpur and Faisalabad was called Lyallpur; Charsadda is the ancient Pushkalavati.
r: Faisalabad was renamed in honour of King Faisal of Saudi Arabia.

q: Which historic trade route links Pakistan with China through the northern mountains?
f: The ancient Silk Road crossed these mountains; today the Karakoram Highway follows it to Khunjerab Pass.
r: The Grand Trunk Road runs from Kabul through Peshawar and Lahore to Bengal.

q: What is the synonym of 'Liberal'?
f: Liberal means open to other views, i.e. tolerant or broad-minded.
r: 'Liberal' can also mean generous, as in a liberal donation.

q: Under the 1973 Constitution, who elects the Prime Minister of Pakistan?
f: The Prime Minister is elected by the members of the National Assembly.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses and the four Provincial Assemblies.

q: When was the Government of India Act 1935 passed?
f: The Act got royal assent on 2 August 1935; its provincial part came into force in 1937.
r: It served as the interim constitution of Pakistan after 1947.

q: When did Hind bint Utbah, mother of Amir Muawiyah, accept Islam?
o: 8 AH, at the Conquest of Makkah
f: Hind accepted Islam at the Conquest of Makkah in 8 AH, after her husband Abu Sufyan.
r: Abu Sufyan accepted Islam just before the Muslims entered Makkah.

q: Which country is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
f: Japan's name, Nippon or Nihon, means 'origin of the sun'.
r: Norway is called the 'Land of the Midnight Sun'.

q: How many Makki and Madani Surahs are there in the Quran?
f: By the common count, 86 Surahs are Makki and 28 are Madani, a total of 114.
r: Makki Surahs mostly deal with faith and Tawheed; Madani Surahs deal more with laws.

q: Which barrage is on the Indus River near Kashmore?
f: Guddu Barrage near Kashmore was completed in 1962 and supplies Sindh and Balochistan.
r: Kotri Barrage is near Hyderabad.

q: Where is the headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
f: The IAEA, set up in 1957, is based at the Vienna International Centre.
r: OPEC is also headquartered in Vienna.

q: When was Operation Zarb-e-Azb launched in North Waziristan?
f: Zarb-e-Azb began on 15 June 2014, a week after the attack on Karachi airport.
r: Operation Radd-ul-Fasaad began on 22 February 2017.

q: In which year were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms introduced?
f: They became the Government of India Act 1919, which brought 'diarchy' to the provinces.
r: The Morley-Minto Reforms came in 1909.

q: Which country is the world's largest exporter of weapons?
f: According to SIPRI, the USA supplies around 40% of all major arms exports.
r: France has recently been ranked the second largest arms exporter.

q: Which team won the 2019 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup?
f: England beat New Zealand at Lord's on boundary count after the match and Super Over were tied.
r: It was England's first ODI World Cup title.

q: Which is the deepest river in the world?
f: Parts of the Congo River are more than 220 m deep.
r: The Amazon carries the most water of any river.

q: In which year was the Holy Prophet (PBUH) born?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) was born in Makkah in the 'Year of the Elephant', about 570-571 AD.
r: 610 AD is the year of the first revelation and 622 AD is the year of the Hijrah.

q: How many amendments have been made to the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan (as of 2026)?
f: The 27th Amendment was passed in November 2025, after the 26th Amendment of October 2024.
r: The 18th Amendment (2010) gave more powers to the provinces.

q: Who took over the government of Pakistan after General Yahya Khan resigned?
f: Bhutto became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator on 20 December 1971.
r: Fazal Elahi Chaudhry became President in 1973 when Bhutto became Prime Minister.

q: Where is the headquarters of Olympic Air?
f: Olympic Air is a Greek airline based at Athens International Airport in Spata.
r: Olympic Air is a subsidiary of Aegean Airlines.

q: Which is the largest railway workshop in Pakistan?
f: The Mughalpura (Moghalpura) workshops in Lahore are the biggest railway workshops in Pakistan.
r: The Pakistan Railways headquarters is in Lahore.

q: How many sense organs do human beings have?
f: The five sense organs are eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin.
r: The skin is the largest organ of the human body.

q: In which Hijri year was Makkah conquered?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) entered Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH (630 AD) with about 10,000 companions.
r: The Treaty of Hudaibiyah was signed in 6 AH.

q: Who was the first Caliph of Islam?
f: Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) was Caliph from 632 to 634 AD.
r: He compiled the Quran into one book after the Battle of Yamama.

q: About how many Muslims fought in the Battle of Uhud?
f: About 1,000 set out, but 300 hypocrites left with Abdullah ibn Ubayy, leaving about 700.
r: 313 Muslims fought at Badr.

q: When did Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (R.A) accept Islam?
o: 8 AH, before the Conquest of Makkah
5 AH, after the Battle of the Trench
f: He accepted Islam in Safar 8 AH (629 AD) in Madinah with Amr ibn al-Aas and Usman bin Talha.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) gave him the title 'Saifullah' (Sword of Allah).

q: In which year were the Morley-Minto Reforms introduced?
f: The Indian Councils Act 1909 gave Muslims separate electorates.
r: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka in 1906.

q: Who introduced the Basic Democracies system in Pakistan?
f: Ayub Khan introduced it through the Basic Democracies Order of October 1959.
r: The 80,000 Basic Democrats also acted as the electoral college for the presidential election.

q: On the bank of which river is Harappa located?
f: Harappa lies near an old course of the Ravi River in Sahiwal district.
r: Mohenjo-daro is on the bank of the Indus in Larkana district.

q: Which country made the modern rules of football?
f: The Football Association in London wrote the modern rules in 1863.
r: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904.

q: In which country did the game of cricket start?
f: Cricket started in south-east England in the Middle Ages.
r: The first Test match was played between Australia and England in 1877.

q: Which team has won the Men's Hockey World Cup the most times?
f: Pakistan won in 1971, 1978, 1982 and 1994.
r: The Netherlands and Australia have each won 3 titles; Germany and Belgium have also won.

q: Who was Chief Minister of Balochistan from 2021 to 2023?
f: Abdul Quddus Bizenjo of the Balochistan Awami Party (BAP) took over from Jam Kamal in October 2021.
r: Sarfraz Bugti became Chief Minister of Balochistan in March 2024.

q: Against which team did Sachin Tendulkar score his first ODI century (1994)?
f: He scored 110 against Australia in Colombo on 9 September 1994.
r: Tendulkar was the first man to score a double century in ODIs (2010).

q: Which country is generally considered to have the most powerful military in the world?
f: The USA has the largest defence budget, advanced technology and bases all over the world.
r: China has the largest active-duty army in the world.

q: Who was Chief of Army Staff (COAS) of Pakistan from 2016 to 2022?
f: General Bajwa was COAS from November 2016 to November 2022 (with an extension).
r: General Asim Munir became COAS in November 2022.

q: From which PMA Long Course did General Qamar Javed Bajwa pass out?
f: Bajwa was commissioned from the 62nd Long Course into 16 Baloch Regiment in 1980.
r: The Pakistan Military Academy is at Kakul, Abbottabad.

q: When was Operation Rah-e-Haq launched in Swat?
f: Rah-e-Haq began in late 2007 against militants of Maulana Fazlullah in Swat.
r: Operation Rah-e-Rast in Swat was launched in May 2009.

q: When was Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan born?
f: Dr. A.Q. Khan was born on 1 April 1936 in Bhopal, British India.
r: He set up Khan Research Laboratories (KRL) at Kahuta.

q: In which part of Pakistan is Hunza Valley?
f: Hunza Valley is in Gilgit-Baltistan, famous for Baltit and Altit forts.
r: Attabad Lake in Hunza formed after a landslide in 2010.

q: In which year was the Battle of Yamama fought?
f: Yamama was fought under Caliph Abu Bakr against the false prophet Musaylimah, who was killed.
r: Many Huffaz were martyred there, which led to the compilation of the Quran.

q: Where is the Red Sea located?
o: Between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula
Between north-east Africa and the Arabian Peninsula
f: The Red Sea separates Africa from Arabia.
r: It joins the Mediterranean through the Suez Canal and the Gulf of Aden through Bab-el-Mandeb.

q: Which Egyptian city is known as the 'City of the Pyramids'?
f: Giza, next to Cairo, has the Great Pyramid and the Great Sphinx.
r: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing.

q: Which Italian city is called the 'Queen of the Adriatic'?
f: Venice is built on islands in a lagoon of the Adriatic Sea.
r: Venice is also called the 'City of Canals'.

q: What is the currency of Cuba?
f: Cuba's official currency is the Cuban Peso (CUP).
r: The Bolivar is the currency of Venezuela.

q: The holy book Injeel was revealed to which Prophet?
f: The Injeel (Gospel) was revealed to Hazrat Isa (A.S).
r: The Taurat was revealed to Hazrat Musa (A.S) and the Zabur to Hazrat Dawood (A.S).

q: When did the Gandhi-Jinnah talks take place in Bombay?
f: The talks failed because Gandhi did not accept the Muslims as a separate nation.
r: The talks were held at Jinnah's house in Bombay.

q: What is the length of the Pakistan-China border?
f: The Pakistan-China border is about 596 km, fixed by the 1963 boundary agreement.
r: The Pak-Afghan border (Durand Line) is about 2,640 km long.

q: In which city is Iqbal Park (Greater Iqbal Park) located?
f: The Lahore Resolution was passed there on 23 March 1940; Minar-e-Pakistan stands in it.
r: Iqbal Park was earlier called Minto Park.

q: Warsak Dam is built on which river? (2)
f: Warsak Dam is on the Kabul River about 30 km north-west of Peshawar.
r: Tarbela Dam is on the Indus River.

q: Who was Speaker of the Punjab Assembly from 2018 to 2022?
f: Pervaiz Elahi was Speaker until he became Chief Minister of Punjab in 2022.
r: Pervaiz Elahi was also Chief Minister of Punjab from 2002 to 2007.

q: In which Islamic month was the Battle of Badr fought?
f: Badr was fought on 17 Ramadan 2 AH; the Quran calls it Youm-ul-Furqan.
r: The Battle of Uhud was fought in Shawwal 3 AH.

q: In which month did the revelation of the Quran begin?
f: The Quran says, 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed' (2:185).
r: The Quran was revealed on Laylat-ul-Qadr, which is in the last ten nights of Ramadan.

q: In which year did Pakistan become a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO)?
f: Pakistan and India became full members at the Astana summit on 9 June 2017.
r: Pakistan had been an observer in the SCO since 2005.

q: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word 'Israel', the title of Hazrat Yaqoob (A.S)?
o: One who strives with God (servant of God)
f: 'Israel' is explained as 'one who strives with God'; Muslim scholars often say 'Abdullah' (servant of God).
r: 'Khalilullah' (Friend of God) is the title of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S).

q: Which is the second most populous country in the world?
f: India passed China in 2023 to become the most populous; China is now second with about 1.4 billion.
r: The USA is third in population.

q: In which Hijri year was the Treaty of Hudaibiyah signed?
f: It was signed in 6 AH (628 AD); the Quran calls it 'Fath-um-Mubeen' (a clear victory).
r: The treaty was for 10 years, but the Quraish broke it, leading to the Conquest of Makkah.

q: For a parabola, what is the fixed straight line called?
f: A parabola is the set of points at equal distance from the focus and the directrix.
r: The focus is the fixed point of a conic.

q: What is the fixed point of a conic section called?
f: Each point on a conic is related by a fixed ratio of its distances from the focus and directrix.
r: An ellipse and a hyperbola each have two foci.

q: What is the constant ratio of the distance from the focus to the distance from the directrix in a conic called?
f: This ratio e is the eccentricity: e = 1 parabola, e < 1 ellipse, e > 1 hyperbola.
r: A circle has eccentricity 0.

q: Who led the Muslim army in the expedition of Tabuk?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) himself led about 30,000 Muslims to Tabuk in 9 AH.
r: Tabuk was the last expedition led by the Prophet (PBUH).

q: In which year was the state of Swat merged into Pakistan?
f: Swat, Dir and Chitral were merged into Pakistan in 1969 under Yahya Khan.
r: The last Wali of Swat was Miangul Jahanzeb.

q: Who was the first female martyr of Islam?
f: Hazrat Sumayyah, mother of Ammar bin Yasir, was killed by Abu Jahl for refusing to leave Islam.
r: Her husband Yasir (R.A) was also martyred, making them the first martyr couple of Islam.

q: Which was the first commercial bank of Pakistan in 1947?
f: Habib Bank moved its head office from Bombay to Karachi in 1947 on Quaid-e-Azam's advice.
r: National Bank of Pakistan was set up in 1949.

q: Where is the Amazon River mainly located?
f: The Amazon flows through Peru, Colombia and mainly Brazil to the Atlantic.
r: The Amazon carries more water than any other river.

q: When did the United Nations officially come into existence?
f: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945; it was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
r: 24 October is celebrated as UN Day every year.

q: In which year was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) founded?
f: The OIC was founded in Rabat, Morocco, in September 1969 after the arson attack on Al-Aqsa Mosque.
r: Pakistan hosted the 2nd OIC Summit in Lahore in 1974.

q: Which is the longest river in North America?
f: The Missouri is about 3,767 km long and joins the Mississippi near St. Louis.
r: The Mississippi-Missouri together form the largest river system in North America.

q: When did Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan pass away?
f: Dr. A.Q. Khan died in Islamabad on 10 October 2021 at the age of 85.
r: He was buried in the H-8 graveyard, Islamabad, with state honours.

q: Which Surah is called 'Uroos-ul-Quran' (Bride of the Quran)?
f: Surah Ar-Rahman is called the Bride of the Quran for its beauty and repeated verse 'Fabi ayyi ala-i Rabbikuma tukazziban'.
r: Surah Yaseen is called the 'Heart of the Quran'.

q: What was Abu Talib's relation to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Abu Talib raised the Prophet (PBUH) after Abdul Muttalib died and protected him in Makkah.
r: Hazrat Ali (R.A) was the son of Abu Talib.

q: According to the 1973 Constitution, sovereignty over the whole universe belongs to whom?
f: The Objectives Resolution (now in the Preamble and Article 2A) says sovereignty belongs to Allah alone.
r: The Objectives Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949.

q: Which of these countries has been one of the biggest importers of weapons in recent years?
f: India has been among the top arms importers in SIPRI reports for many years, along with Saudi Arabia.
r: Ukraine became the biggest arms importer in 2020-24 because of the war with Russia.

q: Who proposed the Quit India resolution in August 1942?
f: Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement with the call 'Do or Die'.
r: The British arrested Congress leaders soon after the resolution was passed.

q: How many general seats does each province have in the Senate of Pakistan?
f: Each province has 14 general seats; with 4 women, 4 technocrat/ulema and 1 minority seat, the total per province is 23.
r: After the 25th Amendment (FATA merger) the Senate has 96 members.

q: Which is the largest living bird in the world?
f: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird and lays the largest eggs.
r: The emu of Australia is the second largest bird.

q: Which hills lie just north of Islamabad?
f: The Margalla Hills are foothills of the Himalayas and include Daman-e-Koh and Pir Sohawa.
r: Margalla Hills National Park was declared in 1980.

q: In which district of Punjab is Harappa located?
f: Harappa lies about 24 km south-west of Sahiwal city.
r: Harappa was first excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921.

q: Justice A.R. Cornelius is famous as which of these?
o: 4th Chief Justice of Pakistan and a renowned jurist
f: Cornelius was Chief Justice from 1960 to 1968 and was the only judge to dissent in the 1955 Tamizuddin case.
r: Justice Muhammad Munir was Chief Justice when the Tamizuddin Khan case was decided.

q: What was the approximate total population of Pakistan (West and East) at independence?
f: The 1951 census counted about 75 million: about 33.7 million in West and 42 million in East Pakistan.
r: East Pakistan had more people than West Pakistan.

q: Who were the main candidates in the 1965 presidential election of Pakistan?
o: Ayub Khan and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto
f: Ayub Khan defeated Fatima Jinnah in the indirect election by the Basic Democrats.
r: Fatima Jinnah was the candidate of the Combined Opposition Parties (COP).

q: What is the last public sermon of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) called?
f: It was delivered at Arafat on 9 Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH (632 AD).
r: It is often called the first charter of human rights in Islam.

q: Which is the highest peak on Earth?
f: Mount Everest is 8,848.86 m high, on the Nepal-China border.
r: K-2 (8,611 m) in Pakistan is the second highest peak.

q: Who was the first female Prime Minister of Pakistan and the Muslim world?
f: Benazir Bhutto took oath on 2 December 1988 at the age of 35.
r: Khaleda Zia became Bangladesh's first woman Prime Minister in 1991.

q: What is the capital of Gilgit-Baltistan? (2)
f: Gilgit city is the seat of the Gilgit-Baltistan government.
r: Skardu is the main town of Baltistan.

q: What is the capital of China?
f: Beijing is the political and cultural centre of China.
r: Shanghai is China's largest city by population.

q: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Russia?
f: The Lena (about 4,400 km) flows into the Arctic Ocean and lies wholly in Russia.
r: The Volga is the longest river in Europe.

q: Who has been the longest-serving president of the Indian National Congress?
f: Sonia Gandhi led Congress from 1998 to 2017 and again from 2019 to 2022.
r: Mallikarjun Kharge became Congress president in 2022.

q: In which year was Bengal partitioned by the British?
f: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905.
r: The partition was cancelled in 1911 by King George V.

q: In which Islamic month is Eid-ul-Fitr celebrated?
f: Eid-ul-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal, after Ramadan ends.
r: Eid-ul-Adha is celebrated on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.

q: What is the maximum allowed length of a cricket bat?
f: Under the MCC Laws a bat may be at most 38 inches (96.52 cm) long.
r: The bat's blade may be at most 4.25 inches wide.

q: Which is traditionally considered the longest river in the world?
f: The Nile is about 6,650 km long and flows into the Mediterranean Sea.
r: Some studies claim the Amazon is slightly longer.

q: Which game started at Harrow School, England, in about 1830?
f: Squash grew from the older game of rackets, played with a soft ball that 'squashes'.
r: Jahangir Khan and Jansher Khan of Pakistan are squash legends.

q: Who was the first Pakistani to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (1979)?
f: Abdus Salam shared the prize for unifying the electromagnetic and weak forces.
r: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.

q: Where is Pakistan Steel Mills located?
f: Pakistan Steel Mills was built at Port Qasim with help from the Soviet Union.
r: Heavy Mechanical Complex is at Taxila.

q: In which district is the Khewra Salt Mine located?
f: The Khewra Salt Mine is in Jhelum district, in the Salt Range.
r: It is the second largest salt mine in the world and produces pink rock salt.

q: Which is the main river of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
f: The Kabul River enters from Afghanistan, flows past Peshawar and joins the Indus at Attock.
r: The Swat River is a tributary of the Kabul River.

q: What is the length of the Suez Canal?
f: The Suez Canal is about 193 km long, from Port Said to Suez.
r: The Panama Canal is about 82 km long.

q: Which war was fought from 1861 to 1865?
f: The Union (North) fought the Confederacy (South) over slavery and unity.
r: Abraham Lincoln was US President during the Civil War.

q: Which country hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
f: Qatar hosted the first World Cup in the Arab world; Argentina won it.
r: Russia hosted the 2018 FIFA World Cup.

q: Which is the longest river along northern Afghanistan?
f: The Amu Darya forms much of Afghanistan's northern border.
r: The Helmand is the longest river flowing entirely inside Afghanistan.

q: Where was the first revelation (Wahi) sent to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: In Ramadan 610 AD, Jibraeel (A.S) brought the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq in the Cave of Hira.
r: The Prophet (PBUH) and Abu Bakr (R.A) hid in the Cave of Thaur during the Hijrah.

q: Who became Chief Minister of Punjab after the 2018 elections?
f: Usman Buzdar was elected Chief Minister on 19 August 2018.
r: Hamza Shehbaz became Chief Minister in April 2022.

q: Who was the first wife of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: The Prophet (PBUH) married Hazrat Khadija when he was 25; she was his only wife while she lived.
r: Hazrat Khadija was also the first person to accept Islam.

q: How many permanent members with veto power does the UN Security Council have?
f: The P5 are the USA, UK, France, Russia and China.
r: The Security Council has 15 members in total.

q: In which year did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
f: Pakistan joined at the Havana summit in 1979 after leaving CENTO.
r: NAM was founded in Belgrade in 1961.

q: In which year was the Lucknow Pact signed between the Congress and the Muslim League?
f: In the Lucknow Pact (1916), worked out by Jinnah, Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.
r: Sarojini Naidu called Jinnah the 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity'.

q: The Hindu Kush range extends across which countries?
f: The Hindu Kush runs about 800 km from central Afghanistan to northern Pakistan and Tajikistan.
r: Tirich Mir (7,708 m) in Chitral is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush.

q: When did India carry out its first nuclear test (Pokhran-I)?
f: India's first test, code-named 'Smiling Buddha', was on 18 May 1974.
r: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests at Chagai on 28 May 1998.

q: Who was the first Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William (Bengal)?
f: Warren Hastings became Governor-General in 1773 under the Regulating Act.
r: Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India in 1833.

q: Hazrat Uzair (Ezra) is known in Islamic tradition as which of these?
o: A righteous Prophet/scholar of Bani Israel
A companion of the Holy Prophet (PBUH)
f: Uzair is named in Surah At-Tawbah (9:30); tradition links him to the story of a man whom Allah caused to die for 100 years and then raised (2:259).
r: He is credited with restoring the Taurat for Bani Israel.

q: Who was Chairman of the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) from 2017 to 2022?
f: Justice (R) Javed Iqbal headed NAB from October 2017 to mid-2022.
r: NAB was created in 1999 under General Musharraf.

q: What is the name of the travel book of Ibn Battuta?
f: Ibn Battuta's Rihla describes his travels of about 30 years across Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
r: Kitab-ul-Hind was written by Al-Biruni.

q: Habba Khatoon, the 'Nightingale of Kashmir', was a poetess of which language?
f: Habba Khatoon was a 16th-century Kashmiri poetess and queen of Yusuf Shah Chak.
r: Lal Ded is another famous Kashmiri mystic poetess.

q: When did Pakistan join SEATO?
f: Pakistan signed the Manila Pact (SEATO) on 8 September 1954.
r: Pakistan left SEATO in 1973 after the separation of East Pakistan.

q: South Africa is the world's largest producer of which precious metal?
f: South Africa produces about 70% of the world's platinum.
r: South Africa was once the top gold producer, but today China produces more gold.

q: What was the old name of Quetta?
f: Quetta was called Shalkot (or Shal) in the past.
r: Quetta means 'fort' (from the Pashto word 'kwatkot').

q: Which country is the world's largest producer of uranium?
f: Kazakhstan produces over 40% of the world's mined uranium.
r: Australia has the largest known uranium reserves.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam join the Indian National Congress?
f: Jinnah joined Congress at the Calcutta session in 1906 as secretary to Dadabhai Naoroji.
r: He joined the Muslim League in 1913.

q: Which famous pass connects Peshawar (Pakistan) with Afghanistan?
f: The Khyber Pass links Peshawar with Jalalabad and Kabul.
r: The Broghil Pass in the Hindu Kush links Chitral with Afghanistan's Wakhan corridor.

q: Hazrat Yaqoob (A.S) was the son of which Prophet?
f: Hazrat Yaqoob was the son of Hazrat Ishaq and grandson of Hazrat Ibrahim (A.S).
r: Hazrat Yusuf (A.S) was a son of Hazrat Yaqoob (A.S).

q: Zakat is which pillar of Islam?
f: The pillars in order are Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.
r: Zakat is usually 2.5% of savings held for one lunar year.

q: In which Hijri year was the Battle of Hunain fought?
f: Hunain was fought shortly after the Conquest of Makkah against the Hawazin and Thaqif tribes.
r: The siege of Taif followed the Battle of Hunain.

q: Which Pakistani batsman scored Pakistan's first ODI century (and early ODI fifties)?
f: Majid Khan scored Pakistan's first ODI hundred (109 vs England, 1974) and also made 60 vs West Indies in the 1975 World Cup.
r: Javed Miandad did not score a fifty in the 1975 World Cup.

q: Who wrote the memoir 'Becoming' (2018)?
f: 'Becoming' is the memoir of former US First Lady Michelle Obama.
r: Barack Obama wrote 'A Promised Land' (2020).

q: Where is the headquarters of NATO?
f: NATO moved its headquarters from Paris to Brussels in 1967.
r: NATO was founded in 1949.

q: According to Surah Al-Anfal (8:9), how many angels did Allah send to help the Muslims at Badr?
f: Surah Al-Anfal says Allah helped with a thousand angels, one after another.
r: Surah Aal-e-Imran (3:124-125) mentions 3,000 and 5,000 angels.

q: Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with which country?
f: Khunjerab Pass links Gilgit-Baltistan with Xinjiang, China.
r: At about 4,693 m it is the highest paved international border crossing.

q: Mirpur is a district of which part of Pakistan?
f: Mirpur is in AJK; it is called 'Little England' because many of its people live in the UK.
r: Mangla Dam is located in Mirpur district.

q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in Europe?
f: Lake Ladoga in Russia, near St. Petersburg, covers about 17,700 sq km.
r: Lake Onega, also in Russia, is the second largest in Europe.

q: On which date is Saudi Arabia's National Day celebrated?
f: It marks the unification of the Kingdom by King Abdulaziz in 1932.
r: 22 February is Saudi Founding Day.

q: What is the synonym of 'Hierarchy'?
f: A hierarchy is a system where people or things are arranged by rank.
r: The army chain of command is an example of a hierarchy.

q: What is the synonym of 'Curious'?
f: Curious means eager to know or learn; inquisitive means the same.
r: The antonym of curious is indifferent.

q: What is the synonym of 'Tempted'?
f: To be tempted is to be attracted or enticed to do something.
r: The noun form is 'temptation'.

q: What are the entries of a null (zero) matrix?
o: Diagonal entries are one, others zero
f: A null matrix has every entry equal to 0 and is written O.
r: A matrix with 1s on the diagonal and 0s elsewhere is the identity matrix.

q: Which is the largest landlocked country in the world?
f: Kazakhstan covers about 2.72 million sq km with no access to the open ocean.
r: Mongolia is the second largest landlocked country.

q: Where is the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS)?
f: PIMS is a major hospital in sector G-8/3, Islamabad.
r: The Aga Khan University Hospital is in Karachi.

q: Against whom was the Battle of Khaibar fought in 7 AH?
f: The Muslims captured the Jewish forts of Khaibar; Hazrat Ali (R.A) conquered the fort of Qamus.
r: Hazrat Ali (R.A) got the title 'Fateh-e-Khaibar'.

q: Which region is known as the 'Land of the Prophets'?
f: Many Prophets such as Ibrahim, Ishaq, Yaqoob, Dawood, Sulaiman and Isa (A.S) lived in Palestine.
r: Masjid-e-Aqsa in Jerusalem was the first Qibla of Muslims.

q: In which district was the Kalabagh Dam proposed?
f: Kalabagh Dam was planned on the Indus River at Kalabagh in Mianwali district.
r: The project has not been built because of disagreement between provinces.

q: What is the antonym of 'Obnoxious'?
f: Obnoxious means very unpleasant, so pleasant is its opposite.
r: Synonyms of obnoxious include offensive and repulsive.

q: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
f: The UN headquarters is in Manhattan, New York, along the East River.
r: Geneva hosts the UN's main European office.

q: In which year was the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) founded?
f: The ICRC was founded in Geneva in 1863 by Henry Dunant and others.
r: The ICRC has won the Nobel Peace Prize three times (1917, 1944, 1963).

q: Where did the US-Afghan Taliban peace talks take place, leading to the 2020 agreement?
f: The Doha Agreement was signed on 29 February 2020 and led to the withdrawal of foreign troops.
r: The Taliban took Kabul in August 2021.

q: What core values form the foundation of the European Union?
o: A single army and foreign policy
Rule of law, democracy and human rights
f: Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union lists values such as democracy, rule of law and human rights.
r: The euro is used by 20 EU member states.

q: Which part of Pakistan shares a border with China?
f: Gilgit-Baltistan borders Xinjiang, China, through the Karakoram range.
r: The Karakoram Highway crosses into China at Khunjerab Pass.

q: Rotterdam is the main seaport of which country?
f: Rotterdam is the largest port in Europe, at the mouth of the Rhine-Meuse delta.
r: Antwerp is the main port of Belgium.

q: About how many books did Shah Waliullah Dehlvi write?
f: Shah Waliullah wrote over 50 books, including 'Hujjatullah-il-Baligha'.
r: He translated the Quran into Persian.

q: What is a matrix with every entry zero called?
f: A null matrix O has all entries 0, and A + O = A for any matrix A of the same order.
r: An identity (unit) matrix has 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

q: What is a triangle with two equal sides called?
f: An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the angles opposite them are also equal.
r: An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal.

q: What is tan(270 degrees - x) equal to?
f: 270 - x lies in the 3rd quadrant where tan is positive, and at 270 tan changes to cot, so it equals cot x.
r: tan(270 + x) = -cot x, because 270 + x lies in the 4th quadrant.

q: For an acute angle x, in which quadrant does (270 degrees - x) lie?
f: If 0 < x < 90, then 270 - x is between 180 and 270, which is the third quadrant.
r: In the third quadrant only tan and cot are positive.

q: What is the capital of Colombia?
f: Bogota lies on a high plateau in the Andes at about 2,640 m.
r: Quito is the capital of Ecuador and Lima of Peru.

q: Who wrote the Urdu novel 'Raja Gidh' (1981)?
f: 'Raja Gidh' by Bano Qudsia is about the idea of halal and haram (lawful and unlawful) earnings.
r: Bano Qudsia was the wife of writer Ashfaq Ahmed.

q: What is the national winter sport of Canada? (2)
f: Ice hockey is Canada's official national winter sport.
r: Lacrosse is Canada's national summer sport.

q: What is a diagonal matrix with all diagonal entries equal called?
f: A scalar matrix has the form kI, with the same number k on the diagonal.
r: An identity matrix is a scalar matrix with k = 1.

q: In which city was the Orange Line Metro Train opened?
f: Lahore's Orange Line started commercial service in October 2020 as a CPEC project.
r: Peshawar has a BRT bus system and Karachi has the Green Line BRT.

q: What is the value of 6P3?
r: 6C3 = 20, because combinations ignore order.

q: What is the derivative of a constant?
f: A constant does not change, so its rate of change is zero.
r: The derivative of x is 1.

q: Which set is a subset of every set?
f: The empty set has no elements, so it is a subset of every set.
r: Every set is an improper subset of itself; the empty set is a proper subset of every non-empty set.

q: What is the value of cot(theta) x tan(theta)?
f: cot(theta) = 1/tan(theta), so their product is 1.
r: sin(theta) x cosec(theta) = 1 too.

q: What is the value of 1/0?
f: Division by zero is not defined in real numbers.
r: 0 divided by any non-zero number is 0.

q: How many articles did the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan originally have?
f: The original 1973 Constitution had 280 articles arranged in 12 parts.
r: The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles.

q: The Strait of Gibraltar connects the Atlantic Ocean with which sea?
f: It separates Spain (Europe) from Morocco (Africa).
r: Tariq bin Ziyad crossed it in 711 AD; Gibraltar means 'Jabal-ut-Tariq'.

q: In which year did Balochistan become a full province?
f: Balochistan became a province on 1 July 1970 when Yahya Khan ended One Unit.
r: Quetta is the capital of Balochistan.

q: When was the One Unit scheme set up in West Pakistan?
f: One Unit joined all western provinces into one province on 14 October 1955.
r: One Unit was ended on 1 July 1970.

q: Where does the Indus River rise?
f: The Indus rises in western Tibet near Mount Kailash and Lake Mansarovar.
r: The Indus is about 3,180 km long and falls into the Arabian Sea.

q: In which year did Quaid-e-Azam resign from the Indian National Congress (Nagpur session)?
f: Jinnah left Congress at the Nagpur session in 1920, opposing Gandhi's non-cooperation methods.
r: He joined Congress in 1906.

q: Who was the first Defence Minister of Pakistan?
f: As Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan also held the defence portfolio.
r: Iskander Mirza was the first Defence Secretary of Pakistan.

q: Which is the longest bone in the human body?
f: The femur is the longest and strongest bone in the body.
r: The stapes in the ear is the smallest bone.

q: When was the State Bank of Pakistan established?
f: Quaid-e-Azam opened the State Bank in Karachi on 1 July 1948.
r: Its first Governor was Zahid Hussain.

q: Which is the coldest planet in the solar system?
f: Uranus has the lowest recorded temperature, about -224 degrees C, even though Neptune is farther away.
r: Venus is the hottest planet.

q: What is the antonym of 'Diligence'?
f: Diligence means steady hard work, so laziness is its opposite.
r: The adjective form is 'diligent'.

q: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
f: Light travels at 299,792,458 m/s, about 3 x 10^8 m/s.
r: Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air.

q: When did Pakistan join the Non-Aligned Movement?
f: Pakistan joined at the 1979 Havana summit after leaving CENTO.
r: Pakistan left CENTO in March 1979.

q: Who was the British Prime Minister at the time of independence in 1947?
f: Labour PM Attlee announced the transfer of power to India and Pakistan.
r: Churchill was PM during most of World War II.

q: Which city is called the 'Gateway of Pakistan'?
f: Karachi has the main seaport and busiest international airport.
r: Karachi was Pakistan's first capital (1947-1959).

q: What is the national flower of Pakistan?
f: Jasmine (Chambeli) is Pakistan's national flower.
r: Deodar is Pakistan's national tree.

q: When were the first major democratic reforms introduced in Pakistan, according to the notes?
f: The notes link the first democratic reforms to 1972, when an elected civilian government under Z.A. Bhutto replaced martial law and began reforms.
r: Pakistan's present constitution was passed in 1973.

q: How many Hajj did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform?
f: The Holy Prophet (PBUH) performed only one Hajj, the Farewell Hajj (Hajjatul Wida) in 10 A.H.
r: He performed more than one Umrah (four are reported).

q: Which mountain is known as the 'Killer Mountain'?
f: Nanga Parbat (8,126 m) is called the Killer Mountain because many climbers died on it.
r: K2 is called the 'Savage Mountain'.

q: In 24-hour (military) time, how is 5 o'clock in the evening written?
f: In 24-hour time, add 12 to PM hours: 5 PM = 17:00 = 1700 hours.
r: 5 o'clock in the morning is written as 0500 hours.

q: If yesterday was Saturday, what day will it be the day after tomorrow?
f: If yesterday was Saturday, today is Sunday, tomorrow is Monday, so the day after tomorrow is Tuesday.
r: Two days before Sunday is Friday.

q: Which letter comes after N in the English alphabet?
f: The alphabet order is ...M, N, O, P...; so O comes after N.
r: N is the 14th letter and O is the 15th letter.

q: In how many years was the Holy Quran revealed?
f: The Quran was revealed over about 23 years: about 13 years in Makkah and 10 years in Madinah.
r: The first revelation came in the Cave of Hira.

q: In which year did Pakistan and China sign their border agreement?
f: The Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement was signed on 2 March 1963.
r: Pakistan and China set up diplomatic relations in 1951.

q: In how many fields is the Nobel Prize given? (2)
f: Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, Peace and Economics (6 fields).
r: The Economics prize was added in 1968 and first given in 1969.

q: What was Hazrat Umm-e-Kulsoom (R.A.) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
f: Umm-e-Kulsoom (R.A.) was a daughter of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) and Hazrat Khadija (R.A.).
r: She married Hazrat Usman (R.A.) after her sister Ruqayyah (R.A.) died, so he is called Zun-Nurain.

q: How many years after independence did Pakistan get its first constitution?
f: Pakistan became independent in 1947 and its first constitution came in 1956, 9 years later.
r: Until 1956, Pakistan was run under the Government of India Act 1935 (with changes).

q: Tirich Mir is the highest peak of which mountain range?
f: Tirich Mir (7,708 m) in Chitral is the highest peak of the Hindu Kush range.
r: K2 is the highest peak of the Karakoram range.

q: In a class of 24 students, 1/4 are male. What percentage are female?
f: If 1/4 (25%) are male, the rest, 3/4, are female = 75%.
r: 1/4 of 24 = 6 male students, so 18 are female.

q: Which uncle of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) is mentioned by name in the Quran?
f: Surah Al-Lahab (Al-Masad) names Abu Lahab, the Prophet's uncle who opposed Islam.
r: Abu Lahab's real name was Abdul Uzza.

q: With which country does Pakistan share its longest border? (2)
f: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border is about 2,640 km long, Pakistan's longest border.
r: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border line was drawn in 1893 by Sir Mortimer Durand.

q: Which is the largest (longest-walled) fort of Pakistan?
f: Ranikot Fort in Sindh has walls about 32 km long, making it the largest fort in Pakistan.
r: Ranikot is called the 'Great Wall of Sindh'.

q: What is the total number of seats in the National Assembly of Pakistan?
f: There are 336 seats in the National Assembly, including reserved seats for women and minorities.
r: The Senate has 96 seats.

q: Who founded the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP)? (2)
f: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto founded the PPP in Lahore in 1967.
r: PPP's slogan was 'Roti, Kapra aur Makan'.

q: Who acts as President of Pakistan when the President is absent?
f: Under Article 49, the Chairman of the Senate acts as President; if he is not available, the Speaker of the National Assembly acts.
r: The President is elected by an electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies.

q: In which province is Gwadar located?
f: Gwadar is a port city on the Makran coast of Balochistan.
r: Gwadar port is a key part of CPEC.

q: When was the Qibla changed from Bait-ul-Muqaddas to the Kaaba?
f: The Qibla was changed in 2 A.H. (Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 144).
r: The mosque where this happened is called Masjid al-Qiblatain in Madinah.

q: Bashar al-Assad was the president of which country?
f: Bashar al-Assad ruled Syria from 2000 until he was removed in December 2024.
r: Damascus is the capital of Syria.

q: In which year did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) perform Hajj?
f: The Prophet's only Hajj, the Farewell Hajj, was in 10 A.H.
r: The Farewell Sermon (Khutba Hajjatul Wida) was given at Arafat.

q: Pakistan is NOT a member of which organization?
f: Pakistan is not a member of NATO; it is a member of OIC, SCO and SAARC.
r: Pakistan is a 'Major Non-NATO Ally' of the USA (since 2004). It is also not in G20 or BRICS.

q: 'BIN' is the intelligence agency of which country?
f: BIN (Badan Intelijen Negara) is Indonesia's State Intelligence Agency.
r: Pakistan's main intelligence agency is the ISI.

q: 'Tenge' is the currency of which country?
f: The tenge is the currency of Kazakhstan.
r: Uzbekistan's currency is the som.

q: What is the value of 2 + 2 / 2?
f: By BODMAS, divide first: 2 / 2 = 1, then 2 + 1 = 3.
r: (2 + 2) / 2 would be 2, because brackets come first.

q: Why do we boil milk?
f: Boiling kills harmful bacteria and germs, making milk safe to drink.
